title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) in Berlin: booking an appointment (Termin) via service.berlin.de
tldr: You search for a registration appointment (Termin) for your residence registration (Anmeldung) in Berlin on service.berlin.de — new slots appear unpredictably and are often gone within minutes. Registration is free, the deadline is 14 days under §17 BMG, and the late-filing fine can reach 1000€. Tip: book any appointment (even one 2 months out) and keep the confirmation — in practice the Berlin authorities treat an early booking as a good-faith attempt to meet the deadline.

steps.title: Where and how to look for an appointment (Termin)

content.text: In Berlin, all residence registration (Anmeldung) is handled by a network of district citizens' offices (Bürgerämter) — about 40 offices across 12 districts. You can only book online or by phone at 115. The booking site is service.berlin.de. According to the site (checked 03.06.2026), the service is listed as 'Wohnsitz - Alleinige Wohnung oder Hauptwohnung anmelden', Dienstleistung code 120686.

items: Main link: service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/120686/
Alternative: service.berlin.de/terminvereinbarung/
Phone 115 — the Berlin Service city hotline
You can register at ANY district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) in Berlin, not just the one for your district
Booking the appointment is free, and the registration service itself is 0€

content.text: Scroll down to the 'Termin berlinweit suchen' button. The site will show a calendar with all the available slots across every district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) in Berlin.

items: New slots are released unpredictably — most often on weekday mornings (7:00–10:00)
Refresh the page every 1–2 minutes — slots are taken within seconds
Don't limit yourself to the central districts (Mitte, Pankow) — try Spandau, Reinickendorf, Marzahn
Don't use automated bots (such as Terminland bots) — Berlin Service blocks the IP
Alternative: legal monitoring services — Termin-Bot Berlin, BürgeramtBot — cost 10–30€ for finding a slot

content.text: Enter your email and phone number. The confirmation arrives by email — save it as a PDF. This is your registration appointment confirmation (Anmeldebestätigungs-Termin), and it protects you legally even if the actual visit is 2 months away.

items: Completed registration form (Anmeldeformular) — download it from service.berlin.de or pick one up on site
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from your landlord (Vermieter) — §19 BMG, mandatory
Passport + residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel), if you have one
Marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) / birth certificates (Geburtsurkunden) — for first-time registration in Berlin
Appointment confirmation (email or printout)

content.text: The most common misunderstanding: the 14-day deadline under §17 BMG runs from the date you MOVE IN (Einzug), not from the appointment date. The law itself requires you to file the residence registration (Anmeldung) within two weeks, but because of the slot shortage the Berlin authorities in practice treat a timely appointment booking as a good-faith attempt to meet the deadline, even if the visit is a couple of months later. This is administrative practice (Kulanz), not an explicit provision of §17 BMG, so there's no guarantee — but in reality it almost always settles the question of a fine.

Save the PDF of the appointment confirmation showing the booking date. If the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) does issue an administrative fine (Bußgeld), this confirmation is your main argument in an objection (Einspruch) and usually helps to cancel or reduce the fine.

Don't confuse 'Wohnsitz - Hauptwohnung anmelden' (Dienstleistung 120686) with 'Wohnsitz - Zweitwohnsitz' (351783) or with re-registration to a new address (Ummeldung). Residence registration (Anmeldung) is only for your first registration in Berlin or a move from another city.

If you're late, book as soon as you can. The district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) in Berlin usually doesn't fine you for a delay of up to 1–2 months, but for a delay of more than 3 months or for repeat violations a fine of 30–100€ is issued regularly.

Online registration (elektronische Wohnsitzanmeldung, eWA) via BundID and eID is available in Berlin: by May 2026 the wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de service covers most of Germany's population. But it requires a document with an activated eID chip (a German national identity card (Personalausweis), an EU eID card, or a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) with eID). Anyone who has just arrived and doesn't yet have such a document must do their first registration in person.

title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) in Cologne via the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt)
tldr: In Cologne, residence registration (Anmeldung) is handled by a network of 10 citizens' service centres (Kundenzentren; formerly Bürgerämter). You book an appointment (Termin) at termine-online.stadt-koeln.de — slots are often 6–10 weeks out. The service is free and the deadline is 14 days under §17 BMG. Alternative: online via wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de.

steps.title: Cologne's system of citizens' service centres (Kundenzentren)

content.text: Cologne has no single central district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) — instead there is a network of district citizens' service centres (Kundenzentren): Innenstadt, Lindenthal, Nippes, Ehrenfeld, Mülheim, Porz, Kalk, Chorweiler, Rodenkirchen and others. You can do your residence registration (Anmeldung) at any of them, regardless of which district you live in. The service is free.

items: Main portal: stadt-koeln.de
Booking: termine-online.stadt-koeln.de
Registration is free
Deadline: 14 days from the move-in date (§17 BMG)
Online alternative: wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de (with BundID and a German eID)

content.text: This is the single Stadt Köln booking portal. Select 'Kundenzentren — An- und Ummeldung'.

items: 'Anmeldung einer Wohnung' — for registering your address
'An- und Ummeldung' — if you've already lived in another German city
Don't confuse it with 'Ausweisangelegenheiten' (ID documents)

content.text: The site will show the nearest available dates across all the citizens' service centres. In Cologne the appointment is usually 6–10 weeks out — that's normal. In practice, a timely appointment booking is treated as good-faith compliance with the deadline under §17 BMG, although this is administrative practice rather than an explicit provision of the law.
The confirmation arrives by email. One day before the appointment you'll get a reminder. Print it out or save the PDF.

items: Registration form (Anmeldeformular) — download it from stadt-koeln.de or fill it in on site
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from your landlord (Vermieter) — §19 BMG, mandatory since 2015
Passport and/or national identity card (Personalausweis) of everyone moving in
Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — if you have a residence title
Marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) / birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) — for first-time registration in Germany or for a family registration
Appointment confirmation

content.text: Without the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung), registration is impossible — the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) in Cologne checks strictly. A rental contract (Mietvertrag) does NOT replace this confirmation under §19 BMG.
Don't confuse termine-online.stadt-koeln.de (official) with termine-reservieren.de and terminli.de — these are third-party services. They don't do the registration for you; they only monitor slots.

Cologne has a dog tax (Hundesteuer) — if you register an address with a dog, then within 1–2 months of the residence registration (Anmeldung) you'll automatically receive a letter from the city tax office (Steueramt). Don't ignore it.

Registering a second residence (Anmeldung Zweitwohnsitz) in Cologne is subject to the second-home tax (Zweitwohnsteuer) — under the local statute (Satzung) this is about 10% of the annual rent excluding utilities (Nettokaltmiete); the city can change the rate and the base. If you're already registered in another city and are only renting a flat in Cologne for study or work, work out whether it wouldn't be better to make Cologne your main residence (Hauptwohnsitz).

title: The 14-day deadline: what counts as the move-in date
tldr: Under §17 Abs. 1 BMG the deadline for residence registration (Anmeldung) is 14 days from the date of move-in (Einzug), not from the date you get the keys or sign the contract. In practice a timely appointment (Termin) booking is usually treated as good-faith compliance with the deadline, even if the visit is later (this is administrative practice (Verwaltungspraxis), not a provision of the law). The late-filing fine is up to 1000€ under §54 Abs. 2 BMG; in Berlin and Munich it is actually charged for a delay of several months.

content.text: §17 Abs. 1 Bundesmeldegesetz: 'Wer eine Wohnung bezieht, hat sich innerhalb von zwei Wochen nach dem Einzug bei der Meldebehörde anzumelden.' The key word is 'Einzug' (moving in). This is the actual day you started using the flat as your home: sleeping there, keeping your belongings there, spending your nights there. Not the date you signed the rental contract (Mietvertrag), not the date you got the keys, not the date you booked the moving company.

items: Counted from the move-in date (Einzug) — the actual day you moved in
NOT counted from signing the contract (Mietvertragsabschluss)
NOT counted from getting the keys (Schlüsselübergabe)
If you got the keys on April 1 but moved in on April 15, the deadline is April 29
If you got the keys in March but your first night in the flat was April 10, the deadline is April 24

steps.title: Exactly how the 14 days are counted

content.text: Under the general rules for calculating deadlines (§187 BGB, applied by analogy to the registration deadline) the move-in day (Einzugstag) itself usually does not count toward the deadline — the count starts the next day. If the last day of the deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, it is usually extended to the next business day (§193 BGB). In disputed cases it's best to check with the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) itself.
Move-in (Einzug) — Monday April 6, 2026. The deadline starts on Tuesday April 7. The 14th day is Monday April 20. The residence registration (Anmeldung) must be filed by the end of that day.

items.title: Example 2: the last day is a weekend

content.text: Move-in (Einzug) — Saturday April 4. The 14th day is Saturday April 18. Under §193 BGB the deadline is extended to Monday April 20.

items.title: An appointment booking = meeting the deadline

content.text: By the established practice of Berlin and many other authorities, a confirmed appointment (Termin) booking at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) within 14 days is treated as good-faith compliance with §17 BMG, even if the visit itself is later. This is administrative practice (Kulanz), not an explicit provision of the law, so there's no guarantee — but in reality it almost always settles the question of a fine. Save the PDF of the confirmation.

items: Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) showing the move-in date — the main document
Flat handover protocol (Übergabeprotokoll) — with a dated stamp
Invoice from the moving company (Umzugsunternehmen Rechnung) — showing the moving date
Rental contract (Mietvertrag) with the rental start date (Mietbeginn) — less reliable, since it often doesn't match the actual move-in
If you're contesting a fine, all of these documents help

content.text: §54 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 BMG: failing to file the residence registration (Anmeldung) on time is an administrative offence (Ordnungswidrigkeit) carrying a fine of up to 1000€. Actual amounts: Berlin — 0–100€ for a delay of up to 2 months, 100–300€ for a delay of 3–6 months, 500–1000€ for repeated violations. Munich and Hamburg are tougher — a fine of 30–80€ for the first weeks of delay. Cologne and Frankfurt are usually milder, often just a warning (Verwarnung) without a fine for a first delay.

If you're late, book an appointment (Termin) as soon as you can anyway. Bring a free-form explanation (Begründung) to the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt): the reason for the delay, your attempts to find an appointment (screenshots), and the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) with a late issue date. The authority is often accommodating.

If a fine has already been issued (a fine notice, Bußgeldbescheid, has arrived in the mail), you have 14 days to file an objection (Einspruch). After 14 days the fine takes effect and can end up at the credit bureau SCHUFA.

costs.note: Free in most cities

costs.label: Administrative fine (Bußgeld) for late filing
costs.note: Under §54 BMG. In practice: Berlin 0–300€, München 30–150€, Köln/Frankfurt often 0€ for a first delay

costs.label: Lawyer (Rechtsanwalt) for an objection (optional)
costs.note: If the fine is large — a lawyer can help with the appeal

title: Complete document package for residence registration (Anmeldung)
tldr: For residence registration (Anmeldung) at any German district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) you'll need: the registration form (Anmeldeformular), the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung; §19 BMG, mandatory since 2015), and a passport. For a family, add a marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) and birth certificates (Geburtsurkunden). The service is free in most cities and the deadline is 14 days under §17 BMG.

content.text: These documents are required regardless of city and marital status. Without them, residence registration (Anmeldung) is impossible.

items: Registration form (Anmeldeformular) — the completed form (download it from the website of the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) or pick it up on site). In Berlin it's the 'Meldeschein', in Munich the 'Anmeldung bei der Meldebehörde'

Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) — from your landlord (Vermieter) under §19 BMG. It must include: the full name of the housing provider (Wohnungsgeber), the full name of the owner (Eigentümer) if they differ, the flat's address, the move-in date (Einzug), the full names of everyone moving in, and a signature
A valid passport (Reisepass) OR national identity card (Personalausweis) OR an EU country ID card
Appointment (Termin) confirmation — a printout of the email confirming the booking

steps.title: Documents for a family residence registration

content.text: If you're registering with a spouse and/or children, you'll need additional documents to prove the family ties. The district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) in Berlin, Munich and Frankfurt requires them only for the first residence registration (Anmeldung) in that city.

items: Marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) — original + apostille (Apostille) + certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) into German
Children's birth certificates (Geburtsurkunden) — original + apostille + translation
Divorce certificate (Scheidungsurkunde) — if divorced and it's relevant to the children's status
Spouse's death certificate (Sterbeurkunde) — if widowed
Consent of the other parent — if a minor is being registered with one parent under joint custody (Sorgerecht)
Visa (Visum) or residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — if you already have one. If you entered on a D visa and don't yet have a residence permit, the passport with the visa is enough
Temporary proof of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) — if you're extending your visa/residence permit and have temporary permission
Confirmation of arrival (Bestätigung der Ankunft) — for Ukrainians under §24 AufenthG (temporary protection)

content.text: The appointment lasts 5–15 minutes. The official checks your documents, scans your passport and the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung), enters the data into the registration system (Meldewesen), and prints out the registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung). You can order a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) on the spot for an extra fee.

items: Registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung) — the main document; keep the original
A sticker/stamp in your passport noting the registration (optional, not in all cities)
A letter with your tax identification number (Steuer-ID) within 2–4 weeks from the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (if it's your first registration in Germany)
A letter about the public broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag, GEZ) within 1–2 months requiring you to pay 18,36€/month

content.text: The district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) won't issue the registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung) and will ask you to book again. You'll have to look for a slot from scratch — and that's critical, because appointments are often 1–2 months out. Better to double-check the package 3 times before the visit.

The landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) is specifically the special form under §19 BMG, not a free-form letter from your landlord (Vermieter). Use your city's official template (download it from the website of the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt)). Free-form letters are often not accepted.
A rental contract (Mietvertrag) does NOT replace the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung). Since 2015 (the BMG reform) these have been strictly separate documents.

A certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) into German is required for all foreign documents relating to marital status. The translation must be done by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) — it costs 25–70€ per page. Check the list of translators at justiz.de → Dolmetscher- und Übersetzerdatenbank.

If the documents are in Russian, Ukrainian, Arabic, etc., an apostille (Apostille) or legalisation is needed to use them in Germany. This is done in the country that issued the document, not in Germany.

After the residence registration (Anmeldung) you'll receive a tax identification number (Steuer-ID) within 2–4 weeks. If it doesn't arrive, contact the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (online form at bzst.de). Without the tax number an employer can't withhold tax correctly.

costs.note: Free in Berlin, München, Frankfurt, Köln, Hamburg. The Anmeldung itself is free everywhere.

costs.label: Simple registration certificate (einfache Meldebescheinigung)
costs.note: The cost varies by city

costs.label: Certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung), per page
costs.note: From a vereidigter Übersetzer — from 25€ per page

costs.label: Apostille (Apostille) in the document-issuing country
costs.note: Depends on the country and document type

costs.label: Certified copy (beglaubigte Kopie), per page
costs.note: Certified copy — at the Bürgeramt or a notary

title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) in Frankfurt: the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt)
tldr: In Frankfurt, residence registration (Anmeldung) is handled by a network of district citizens' offices (Bürgerämter) managed by the Central Citizens' Office (Zentrales Bürgeramt). Since 2024 it can be done fully online via wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de — without an appointment (Termin). The service is free and the deadline is 14 days under §17 BMG. To book an in-person visit, use frankfurt.de.

steps.title: Frankfurt's system of district citizens' offices (Bürgerämter)

content.text: In Frankfurt you can do your residence registration (Anmeldung) at any of the ~10 district citizens' offices (Bürgerämter) spread across the districts. They are managed by the Central Citizens' Office (Zentrales Bürgeramt). Since 2024 online registration has been available via the federal portal wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de — but only with a document that has an activated eID chip (a German national identity card (Personalausweis), an EU eID card, or a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) with the eID function) and a BundID account. Anyone who has just arrived and doesn't yet have such a document does their first registration in person.

items: Main portal: frankfurt.de/leistungen/Umzug-8958631/Abmeldungen-Ummeldungen-Anmeldungen-8958634/Anmeldung-einer-Wohnung
Registration is free
Deadline: 14 days from move-in (§17 BMG)
Online registration: wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de — no appointment, instant
In-person visit: book via frankfurt.de

steps.title: Online registration (if you have BundID and eID)

content.text: As of January 1, 2024, a federal law has obliged all states to offer online residence registration (Anmeldung) via wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de. Frankfurt is one of the first cities where the service works reliably. Advantages: no appointment (Termin), available 24/7, instant result.

items: A German national identity card (Personalausweis) OR a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) with an eID chip
An activated eID function (enabled at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) with a PIN)
A BundID account (id.bund.de)
A card reader OR a smartphone with NFC and the 'AusweisApp'
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) as a PDF for upload

content.text: Go to wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de → log in via BundID → select the state of Hessen and the city of Frankfurt → enter your data and upload the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) → confirm with your eID. The registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung) arrives in your BundID account and by mail within 3–5 days.

Go to frankfurt.de → 'Leistungen' → 'Anmeldung einer Wohnung' → 'Termin vereinbaren'. Choose any district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) — you can register at any of them, not just the one for your district. Slots are usually 3–6 weeks out.

items: Frankfurt registration form (Anmeldeformular) — PDF from frankfurt.de
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from your landlord (Vermieter) — §19 BMG
Passport of everyone moving in
Marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) / birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) — original + certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung)
Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — if you already have one
Appointment confirmation

items.title: 3. Visit to the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt)

content.text: The visit lasts 10–15 minutes. The registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung) is issued on the spot. If you wish, you can order a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) — 10€ when applying in writing or in person in Frankfurt, free online — which you'll need for the bank, your employer and insurance.

A rental contract (Mietvertrag) does NOT replace the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) — the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) in Frankfurt states this directly on its website: 'Bestätigung des Wohnungsgebers (Mietvertrag reicht nicht)'.
The online service wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de does NOT work for a first residence registration (Anmeldung) in Germany without a German ID. If you've just arrived from abroad — in-person visit only.

Frankfurt has a second-home tax (Zweitwohnsteuer) — under the local statute (Satzung) this is about 10% of the annual rent excluding utilities (Nettokaltmiete) for second addresses (the city sets the rate). If you're already registered in another city and are registering a second residence (Zweitwohnsitz) in Frankfurt, work out whether a main residence (Hauptwohnsitz) wouldn't be better.

If you're more than 14 days late — §54 Abs. 2 BMG, a fine of up to 1000€. The district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) in Frankfurt is relatively lenient: for a first delay of up to 2 months it's usually just a warning (Verwarnung); for a delay of 3–6 months — a fine of 30–100€.

costs.note: Free according to the official Stadt Frankfurt fee schedule

costs.note: Written certificate 10€; electronic (online via BundID) — free.

costs.note: Written 10€; online free (einfache and erweiterte at the same price).

title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) in Hamburg: the citizens' service centre (Kundenzentrum)
tldr: In Hamburg, residence registration (Anmeldung) is handled not by a district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) but by a citizens' service centre (Kundenzentrum) — a district centre that is part of the district authority (Bezirksamt). You book an appointment (Termin) online via the hamburg.de portal or by phone at 115. By law (§17 BMG) you must register within 14 days of moving in; if you're late you face an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG). The registration itself is free; a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) costs roughly 10–16 €. You'll need to bring your passport and the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from the property owner.

steps.title: Where to register your address in Hamburg

content.text: Unlike Berlin with its district citizens' offices (Bürgerämter), in Hamburg you register your address at a citizens' service centre (Kundenzentrum, KZ) — these are district citizens' service centres. The city is divided into seven districts (Bezirke): Hamburg-Mitte, Altona, Eimsbüttel, Hamburg-Nord, Wandsbek, Bergedorf and Harburg, and each district has several citizens' service centres.

Important: you are NOT required to go to the citizens' service centre (Kundenzentrum) for your new place of residence. Hamburg lets you choose freely — you can book at any citizens' service centre in the city where an appointment opens up sooner. This is a lifesaver, because slots are taken very quickly.

items: The authority is called the citizens' service centre (Kundenzentrum), not the Bürgeramt or the residents' registration office (Einwohnermeldeamt)
There are more than 20 citizens' service centres (Kundenzentren) across the city in seven districts
You can book at ANY citizens' service centre, without being tied to your address
Single booking and information point — the hamburg.de portal and phone 115
The residence registration (Anmeldung) service is free on site

content.text: An appointment (Termin) is booked online at hamburg.de in the citizens' service (Bürgerservice) online-services section → 'Termin vereinbaren'. Select the service 'Wohnsitz anmelden' (or 'An-, Ab- und Ummeldung von Wohnungen'), then a convenient citizens' service centre (Kundenzentrum) and an available date. Without an appointment it's almost impossible to get seen in Hamburg — the system works strictly by appointment.

items: Open hamburg.de → Online-Dienste → Termin vereinbaren
Select the service 'Wohnsitz anmelden / Ummeldung'
Browse several citizens' service centres (Kundenzentren) — the dates vary a lot
Slots often open in the morning; check the site at 7:00–8:00
Note the booking number and keep the confirmation (sent by email)

items.title: 2. If there are no slots online — phone 115

items: Call the single authorities' number 115 (Mon–Fri, business hours)
The operator may offer slots that aren't available online
Ask about the more remote citizens' service centres (Bergedorf, Harburg) — the queue there is shorter
Ask whether there are any leftover slots (Restplätze) for the morning

content.text: Don't wait for the perfect appointment close to home. It's better to take any early date in a far-off district and travel there than to miss the 14-day deadline. Under §17 BMG the count runs from the move-in date (Einzugsdatum), not from the date you found an available appointment — the authority counts the delay from your actual move-in.

The set of documents in Hamburg is standard for all of Germany. The main thing is not to forget the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung); without it they won't register you, even if you really do live at the address.

items: Passport or ID card for each person being registered (including children)
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) — confirmation from the owner/landlord of the housing (§19 BMG)
Completed registration form (Meldeschein) — download it at hamburg.de or pick it up on site
Marriage/birth certificates — advisable for a family (not always required)
Rental contract (Mietvertrag) — as proof, sometimes requested in addition

content.text: After the residence registration (Anmeldung) the official enters you in the residents' register (Melderegister) and issues a confirmation. If you need an official registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung), order it separately — there's a fee.

The landlord must issue the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) within 14 days of move-in (§19 BMG). If they drag their feet, remind them in writing — without this document registration is impossible, and the delay falls on you.

The registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) is an official document confirming that you are registered at a specific address. In Hamburg it's more expensive than in many other cities: a simple certificate costs roughly 10–16 € depending on the form (simple einfache or extended erweiterte Meldebescheinigung).

items: Simple registration certificate (einfache Meldebescheinigung) — basic certificate with name and address
Extended registration certificate (erweiterte Meldebescheinigung) — extended (with additional data, for certain authorities)
You can order it during the residence registration (Anmeldung) itself or later online at hamburg.de
The cost in Hamburg is noticeably above the national average (~10–16 €)
The certificate is needed for the bank, employer, registry office, driving licence, etc.

content.text: The registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung), which you get for free when you register, and the paid registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) are different documents. Many authorities accept the free confirmation, so don't pay for the certificate in advance until you know for sure that they specifically require a Meldebescheinigung.

costs.note: More expensive than average in Hamburg; depends on the simple/extended form.

costs.note: Under §54 BMG for breaching the 14-day deadline; in practice often a token fine or a warning.

title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) in Leipzig: booking and documents
tldr: In Leipzig, residence registration (Anmeldung) is handled by district citizens' offices (Bürgerämter) — there are several across the city's districts. You book an appointment (Termin) online via the leipzig.de portal or by phone at 0341 123-0; there is also limited walk-in service during peak hours. Under §17 BMG you must register within 14 days of moving in, otherwise you face an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG). The registration itself is free; a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) costs about 5–10 €. The main document people often forget is the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from the landlord (§19 BMG).

steps.title: Where to register your address in Leipzig

content.text: In Leipzig, residence registration (Anmeldung) is done at district citizens' offices (Bürgerämter) — the city's citizens' service centres. There are several: the central citizens' office in the Mitte district (Otto-Schill-Straße / Burgplatz) plus district offices — for example in Gohlis, Grünau, Plagwitz and Südvorstadt. The city is part of the federal state of Saxony (Sachsen), but the registration rules are the same across all of Germany (BMG).

The central office is in the Mitte district, plus several district citizens' offices (Bürgerämter)

Select the service 'Wohnsitz anmelden / Ummeldung', then a convenient district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) and an available date. If the available slot falls later, be sure to save the booking confirmation: it proves you tried to book on time and helps you avoid or reduce an administrative fine (Bußgeld).

title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) in Munich: the appointment at the KVR
tldr: In Munich, address registration is run by the KVR (Kreisverwaltungsreferat, the city's district administration department), and specifically by the district citizens' office (Bürgerbüro) within it. You book an appointment (Termin) online via stadt.muenchen.de (the Bürgerbüro / Terminvereinbarung section). Munich is notorious for the longest queues in Germany: you can wait weeks for an available appointment. Under §17 BMG you must register within 14 days of moving in, and if the appointment falls later — keep the confirmation to prove you tried. Registration is free; a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) costs about 5–12 €.

steps.title: KVR and the district citizens' office (Bürgerbüro): where to go

content.text: In Munich, resident registration is handled by the KVR (Kreisverwaltungsreferat) — a large city authority of the district administration. Within it, services for citizens (including residence registration, Anmeldung) are handled by the district citizens' office (Bürgerbüro). There are several Bürgerbüro branches in the city: the main one at Ruppertstraße 19, plus Pasing, Orleansplatz (Ostbahnhof) and others.

items: Authority: the KVR (Kreisverwaltungsreferat), the Bürgerbüro department
Main office: Ruppertstraße 19
Branches: Pasing, Orleansplatz, Leonrodstraße and others
You can book at any branch — choose whichever has the earlier appointment
The residence registration (Anmeldung) is free on site

steps.title: How to land an appointment (Termin) at the KVR

content.text: Getting an appointment (Termin) in Munich is the main headache. Booking goes through stadt.muenchen.de → Bürgerbüro → Terminvereinbarung. Slots appear in batches and are taken within minutes. You need to check the site regularly and at the right time.

items: Open stadt.muenchen.de → Bürgerservice → Terminvereinbarung Bürgerbüro
Select 'An-/Ummeldung Wohnsitz'
Check all the branches — the queue in Pasing is usually shorter than in the centre
New slots are often posted early in the morning and at the start of the week
Book as soon as you see a date — don't hesitate
Call 115 — the single authorities' number
Ask about an emergency appointment when the 14-day deadline is running out
Operators sometimes give slots that aren't available online
Ask which branches process new residents faster

content.text: Munich holds the record for waiting time: an actual appointment is often 4–8 weeks out. That's far more than the legal 14 days (§17 BMG). The solution: book as early as you can and save the appointment confirmation (Terminbestätigung) showing the booking date — it proves you met your obligation on time, and the blame for the delay lies with the authority's workload.

steps.title: Documents for residence registration (Anmeldung) in Munich

items: Passport/ID for each person being registered
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from the landlord (§19 BMG) — mandatory
Completed registration form (Meldeschein) — download it at stadt.muenchen.de
Marriage certificate / children's birth certificates — for families
Rental contract — sometimes requested as proof

content.text: All adult family members moving in together can be registered on one form, but personal presence is usually required, or a power of attorney (Vollmacht) for whoever comes to the appointment.

Without the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) the appointment is wasted — you won't be registered and you'll have to look for a slot again, losing weeks. Get this document from the property owner in advance: under §19 BMG they must issue it within 14 days.

steps.title: After registration and the registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)

content.text: After the residence registration (Anmeldung) you'll be given a free registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung). If you need an official registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung), order it — in Munich it's about 5–12 €. A few weeks later you'll also get a letter by mail with your tax identification number (steuerliche Identifikationsnummer), if you didn't already have one.

items: Registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung) — free, issued on the spot
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) — ~5–12 €, on request
The tax identification number (Steuer-ID) arrives by mail automatically (if you're a new resident of Germany)

title: Registering a newborn: birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) + registration (Anmeldung)
tldr: Under §17 BMG, a child born in Germany is automatically considered registered at the mother's address if both parents are registered there — in that case you don't need a separate residence registration (Anmeldung). But first you have to obtain the birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) from the registry office (Standesamt) responsible for the place of birth. If the parents are registered at different addresses or the family is moving, the newborn's registration is done separately, and the 14-day deadline of §17 BMG applies here too. The birth certificate and the basic registration are free.

steps.title: First — the birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) from the registry office (Standesamt)

content.text: Before you think about registration, you need to obtain the birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde). It's issued by the registry office (Standesamt) of the district where the maternity hospital is located. The maternity hospital sends a birth notification to the registry office, but you still have to submit the parents' documents: passports, the marriage certificate (if you have one) or the acknowledgement of paternity (Vaterschaftsanerkennung), and for unmarried parents sometimes additional papers.

items: The registry office (Standesamt) is tied to the place of birth, not to your place of residence
It's best to submit the documents within a week of the birth
You'll need the parents' passports and the marriage certificate or the acknowledgement of paternity
Foreign documents may require translation and legalisation or an apostille
The birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) is issued in several copies — order 3–5 straight away

steps.title: When a separate registration (Anmeldung) isn't needed

content.text: The good news: if both parents (or a single mother) are already registered at the same address, then under §17 BMG the newborn is considered registered at that same address automatically from the moment of birth. The registry office (Standesamt) passes the data to the residents' registration authority (Meldebehörde), and in most cases there's no need to register the child separately at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt).

items: Both parents registered at the same address → the child is registered there automatically
A landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) for the child isn't needed separately if the address is the same
The registry office passes the birth data to the residents' register itself
You can then request confirmation of the child's registration from the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt)

content.text: 'Automatic' registration only works if the child's address matches the parents' already registered address. If you're registered at different addresses, or the child will live separately (which is rare), you'll need an ordinary residence registration (Anmeldung), and here the 14-day deadline of §17 BMG applies again.

steps.title: If the registration does have to be done separately

content.text: A separate residence registration (Anmeldung) for a newborn is needed, for example, when the parents are registered at different addresses and the child's main address has to be determined, or when the family moves shortly after the birth. In that case you book an appointment at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) and bring the birth certificate plus the standard documents.

items: The child's birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) (original)
Passports/IDs of both parents
A landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) for the new address if the family is moving (§19 BMG)
If the parents have different addresses — an agreement on the main place of registration
The completed registration form (Anmeldung) for the child

content.text: Registering the child isn't an end in itself but the trigger for everything else: child benefit (Kindergeld), the child's health insurance (family insurance, Familienversicherung), the child's tax number (the Steuer-ID arrives automatically), and enrolment at a daycare centre (Kita). Without a birth certificate and a confirmed address these applications won't be accepted.

costs.label: Birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde), first copy
costs.note: The first original; additional copies are usually 5–7 € each.

costs.label: Registration (Anmeldung) of a newborn
costs.note: Registration is free; in most cases it happens automatically.

costs.label: Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) for the child (if needed)
costs.note: A paid certificate, only if a specific authority requires it.

sources.title: Familienportal des Bundes — after the birth of a child

title: Second residence (Zweitwohnsitz): second registration and the second-home tax (Zweitwohnungsteuer)
tldr: If you have two homes in Germany (for example one for work and one for family), you're obliged to register both: one as your main residence (Hauptwohnung) and the other as a secondary residence (Nebenwohnung), also known as a second residence (Zweitwohnsitz). This is required under §21–22 BMG, and the 14-day deadline of §17 BMG applies to the second registration too. For the second residence many cities levy a second-home tax (Zweitwohnungsteuer) — a local tax (often 5–20 % of the annual net rent). The registration (Anmeldung) itself is free; to register the second home you also need a landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung; §19 BMG).

steps.title: Main (Hauptwohnung) and secondary (Nebenwohnung) residence: what's the difference

content.text: Under §21 BMG, if a person has several homes in Germany, one of them must be designated as the main residence (Hauptwohnung) and the rest as secondary (Nebenwohnung). The main residence is the home you use predominantly. For people with a family it's usually the family home; for single people it's wherever you spend more of your time.

items: Main residence (Hauptwohnung) — the predominantly used home (§21 BMG)
Secondary residence (Nebenwohnung), also known as a second residence (Zweitwohnsitz) — any additional home
For people with a family the main residence is usually the family address
The main/secondary status affects taxes and official correspondence
Both homes must be registered within 14 days (§17 BMG)

steps.title: How to register a second residence (Zweitwohnsitz)

content.text: You register the second home at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) of the city where the secondary residence (Nebenwohnung) is located. The procedure is the same as for the main registration: book an appointment, fill in the registration form (Anmeldung), and bring your passport and a landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from the landlord of the second home (§19 BMG). On the form you state that this is a secondary residence and give the address of your main residence (Hauptwohnung).

items: Passport or ID
A landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) for the second home (§19 BMG)
The address of your main residence (Hauptwohnung) — to enter on the form
The registration form (Anmeldung) marked as a secondary residence (Nebenwohnung)
14 days from moving into the second home (§17 BMG)
For missing it — an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG)
A change of main↔secondary status is also registered (re-registration, Ummeldung)

content.text: Many people forget: registering a second home is an obligation, not an option. Even a room you rent in another city for work and sleep in a few nights a week is legally a home (Wohnung) and must be registered as a secondary residence (Nebenwohnung) under §17 and §21 BMG.

Many cities and municipalities (Berlin, Hamburg, München, Köln and hundreds of others) levy a second-home tax (Zweitwohnungsteuer) — a local tax on an additional home. It's a separate municipal tax, and its rate depends on the city: usually 5–20 % of the annual rent excluding utilities (Nettokaltmiete). The tax is tied specifically to the secondary residence (Nebenwohnung) status, so registering the second home automatically puts you on the radar of the city's tax office.

items: The rate depends on the city (often 5–20 % of the annual Nettokaltmiete)
It's paid by the owners/tenants of the secondary residence (Nebenwohnung)
The city learns about the second home from the residence registration (Anmeldung) data
There are exceptions: students, and married people forced into a second home by work — check with the local tax office (Steueramt)
The tax is independent of the administrative fine (Bußgeld) — these are separate payments

content.text: Sometimes it pays to think carefully about which home is your main residence (Hauptwohnung). If your main activity is in a city with no second-home tax (Zweitwohnungsteuer), it makes sense to make that one your main residence. But the status can't be chosen arbitrarily — it has to reflect where you actually live predominantly (§21 BMG), otherwise it's a violation.

costs.label: Registration (Anmeldung) of a second home (Nebenwohnung)
costs.note: The registration itself is free.

costs.label: Second-home tax (Zweitwohnungsteuer)
costs.note: Depends on the city: usually 5–20 % of the annual Nettokaltmiete; in some places there's no tax at all.

costs.label: Administrative fine (Bußgeld) for a late Anmeldung
costs.note: Under §54 BMG for breaching the 14-day registration deadline.

title: Cities where residence registration (Anmeldung) is possible without an appointment (walk-in)
tldr: In some German cities, getting your residence registration (Anmeldung) done without an appointment (Termin) — that is, as a walk-in — is far more realistic than in Berlin or Munich. Many mid-sized cities (Leipzig, Dresden, Bremen, Hannover, Nuremberg and others) keep either morning walk-in hours or a short online queue. This is a lifesaver when the 14-day deadline of §17 BMG is closing in and the next available appointment is a month away. The registration itself is free everywhere; you must bring your passport and the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) (§19 BMG). Missing the deadline can mean an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG).

content.text: The main problem with residence registration (Anmeldung) in big cities is not the paperwork but getting an appointment (Termin). In Berlin and Munich you can wait weeks for a free slot, while the 14-day deadline of §17 BMG runs from the day you arrive. A walk-in (Spontankunden / Offene Sprechstunde / Restplätze) lets you simply show up and join a live queue without a booking — a fallback for when everything online is taken.

items: Walk-in = registration without a prior booking
Often only during certain morning hours, and only until the slots run out
A lifesaver when the 14-day deadline (§17 BMG) is looming
Same documents: passport + landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) (§19 BMG)
The service on-site is free

steps.title: Which cities are more realistic for a walk-in

content.text: Walk-in availability changes constantly, so don't rely on a fixed list — go by the type of city instead. In mid-sized cities, and in the district citizen offices (Bürgerämter) of large cities, queues are noticeably shorter. Before you go, check the city portal: the format (online queue, morning Restplätze, live queue) is listed there.

items: Leipzig (leipzig.de) — often has a morning walk-in for Spontankunden
Dresden (dresden.de) — district citizen offices (Bürgerbüros), shorter queue
Bremen (bremen.de) — BürgerServiceCenter, same-day slots possible
Hannover (hannover.de) — district citizen offices (Bürgerämter) with a live morning queue
Nuremberg (nuernberg.de) — district citizen offices (Bürgerämter), often Restplätze
In large cities, look for the OUTLYING district offices — they're less busy

content.text: Don't treat a walk-in as a guarantee. Live-queue slots run out fast, and a session can be cancelled if the office is overloaded. Always keep an online appointment booked in parallel, and check the city's website for the current format: the "walk-in" status at German authorities changes without notice.

steps.title: How to do a walk-in properly

content.text: To improve your chances with a walk-in, arrive right at opening time. Live-queue places and morning Restplätze are gone within the first few minutes. Bring the complete set of documents — if anything is missing, you'll be sent home and your attempt is wasted.

items: Arrive 20–40 minutes before the office opens
Bring your passport/ID and the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) (§19 BMG)
Fill in the registration form (Anmeldung / Meldeschein) in advance
Choose outlying district offices rather than the central one
If there's no online appointment and no walk-in, save evidence of your attempts

content.text: If there's neither an appointment nor a walk-in available and the 14 days are running out, that's not your fault under §17 BMG — but prove your attempts: screenshots of the empty calendar, a booking confirmation for a late date. When it comes to an administrative fine (Bußgeld) under §54 BMG, authorities usually take an objective lack of slots into account.

costs.label: Anmeldung (with or without an appointment)
costs.note: Registration is free in any city and with any appointment format.

costs.label: Meldebescheinigung (registration certificate)
costs.note: A paid official certificate; depends on the city.

costs.label: Bußgeld for a late Anmeldung
costs.note: Under §54 BMG; usually reduced where a proven lack of appointments is shown.

sources.title: Stadt Hannover — Anmeldung einer Wohnung (Zuzug nach Hannover)

title: What residence registration (Anmeldung) is and why you need it
tldr: Residence registration (Anmeldung) is mandatory under §17 BMG for anyone who moves into new housing in Germany. You must do it within 14 days at your local citizens' office (Bürgeramt) or residents' registration office (Einwohnermeldeamt). Without it almost nothing works: opening a bank account, getting a tax identification number (Steuer-ID), obtaining a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel), signing an internet contract, enrolling a child in school. Registration is free, but it requires a landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from the landlord (§19 BMG). Missing the deadline can mean an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG).

content.text: Residence registration (Anmeldung) is the official recording of your home address. Germany has no residence stamp in the passport like some countries do, but it does keep a residents' register (Melderegister), and everyone who moves into housing must enter their address there. The legal basis is §17 of the Federal Registration Act (Bundesmeldegesetz, BMG).

items: Registration = entering your address into the residents' register (Melderegister)
An obligation under §17 BMG for everyone who moves into housing
Done at the local citizens' office (Bürgeramt) / residents' registration office (Einwohnermeldeamt) / Kundenzentrum
Deadline — 14 days from the date of move-in
The service itself is free

content.text: Residence registration is the "key" to all of German bureaucracy. Without a confirmation of registration (Anmeldebestätigung) you will hit a wall almost everywhere, because many processes only start once you appear in the residents' register.

items: Tax identification number (Steuer-ID) — arrives automatically after registration
Bank account — most banks require a registered address
Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) requires registration
Contracts: internet, mobile service, insurance
Enrolling children in daycare (Kita) and school, health insurance, driver's license

content.text: Residence registration is not permission to live in Germany and not a residence permit. It is simply a record of your address. But without it you can get almost nothing else, so it is the first step after moving — before the bank and the SIM card.

steps.title: How to do it and what to bring

content.text: To register, you need to book an appointment at the local citizens' office (Bürgeramt) (or go to a city that offers walk-ins), fill out the registration form (Anmeldung / Meldeschein) and bring a basic set of documents. The most important of these is the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) under §19 BMG.

items: Passport or ID card for each person being registered
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from the landlord (§19 BMG)
Completed registration form (Anmeldung / Meldeschein)
For families — marriage/birth certificates (not always required)
Sometimes — the rental contract as additional proof

content.text: The most common beginner mistakes: missing the 14-day deadline of §17 BMG, and turning up without the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung). Without the landlord's confirmation they will not register you, and missing the deadline can mean an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG). So ask your landlord for this document the moment you move in.

costs.label: Anmeldung (residence registration)
costs.note: The registration itself is free throughout Germany.

costs.label: Meldebescheinigung (registration certificate)
costs.note: A paid official certificate, if an authority requires it; depends on the city.

costs.label: Bußgeld for a late Anmeldung
costs.note: Under §54 BMG for missing the 14-day deadline.

title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) as a family: children, spouse
tldr: If the whole family is moving, you can register all of them (Anmeldung) at once in a single appointment (Termin) — which saves time. Under §17 BMG the 14-day deadline applies to each family member. Minor children are registered by their parents (legal guardians), and each one needs a document (passport/birth certificate). A single landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) (§19 BMG) covers everyone moving into the same flat. Registration is free; registration certificates (Meldebescheinigung) cost money. Missing the deadline can mean an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG).

steps.title: One appointment (Termin) for the whole family

content.text: Good news: a family can usually be registered in a single appointment (Termin). When you book at the district citizen office (Bürgeramt), state the number of people (the system often has a "how many persons" field). The official then completes the residence registration (Anmeldung) for everyone moving into the same flat at one address in one go.

items: When booking the appointment, state the number of people being registered
All family members at one address = one procedure
A single landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) per flat is enough (§19 BMG)
The 14-day deadline under §17 BMG applies to each person
Registration is free for everyone

steps.title: Children: who registers them and how

content.text: Minor children are registered by their parents as legal guardians (gesetzliche Vertreter). The child doesn't have to be there in person, but each one needs an identity document: a passport or a birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde). For foreign children, the birth certificate may need a translation.

items: Children under 16 are registered by their parents (legal guardians)
For each child — a passport or a birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde)
With different surnames or custody arrangements — documents proving the right to register the child
Children born in Germany are often already registered automatically (§17 BMG)
Foreign certificates sometimes need to be translated

content.text: If the parents register at different addresses, you need to decide where the child's primary residence (Hauptwohnung) will be. This affects child benefit (Kindergeld), the choice of daycare (Kita) or school, and tax classes. Decide in advance, so the official enters the correct primary address for the child.

The set of documents is standard, but separate for each person. A single landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) covers the whole flat, but identity documents are needed for every family member.

items: Passport/ID for each adult
A passport or birth certificate for each child
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) for the flat (§19 BMG) — one for everyone
Marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) — for spouses
A completed registration form (Anmeldung) (often one form can cover the whole family)

content.text: The main traps for families: missing the 14 days (§17 BMG) amid the chaos of moving, and turning up without translations of the children's documents. Ask the landlord for the confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) the moment you move in, and translate foreign certificates in advance — otherwise the appointment will have to be rescheduled.

costs.label: Anmeldung for the whole family
costs.note: Registration is free regardless of the number of family members.

costs.label: Meldebescheinigung (per person if needed)
costs.note: A paid certificate; price is per document and depends on the city.

costs.label: Bußgeld for a late Anmeldung
costs.note: Under §54 BMG; the 14-day deadline counts for each family member.

title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) without a lease (Untermiete)
tldr: You can register your residence (Anmeldung) even without a lease in your own name — for example, with a sublet (Untermiete), or when living with friends or relatives. Under §19 BMG the key document is not the lease but the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) — a confirmation from whoever provides you with the housing (the housing provider, Wohnungsgeber). This can be either the owner or the main tenant (Hauptmieter) in a lawful sublet. The 14-day deadline of §17 BMG applies here too. A bogus registration (Scheinanmeldung) carries severe fines under §54 BMG.

steps.title: A lease is not a requirement

content.text: A common myth says you need a lease in your own name to register. That's not the case. Under §19 BMG, residence registration (Anmeldung) requires not a lease (Mietvertrag) but a landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) — a written confirmation from the person who actually provides you with the housing (the housing provider, Wohnungsgeber). This can be the owner, the main tenant in a sublet, or the family member you live with.

items: The key document is the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) (§19 BMG), not the lease (Mietvertrag)
The housing provider (Wohnungsgeber) is whoever provides the housing (the owner or the main tenant, Hauptmieter)
Registration is possible when living with friends, relatives, or in a sublet
The 14-day deadline of §17 BMG applies the same way
Registration remains free

steps.title: Sublet (Untermiete): subletting and the landlord's consent

content.text: In a sublet (Untermiete), the main tenant (Hauptmieter) rents you a room or flat. For your residence registration, they act as the housing provider (Wohnungsgeber) and sign the confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung). One important point: for a lawful sublet, the main tenant generally needs the consent of their own landlord (Vermieter) — otherwise it breaches their lease, even though the authority usually doesn't check for this consent at registration.

items: In a sublet — the main tenant (Hauptmieter)
With relatives or friends — whoever officially lives there or owns the place
The form lists the housing provider's (Wohnungsgeber) details and the address
The housing provider's signature is mandatory (§19 BMG)
The main tenant (Hauptmieter) usually needs the consent of their own landlord (Vermieter) to sublet
Without consent, the main tenant risks their lease
For registration, the authority checks the confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung), not the landlord's consent
It's better to have the consent in writing — in case of disputes

content.text: The housing provider (Wohnungsgeber) is required to confirm your actual move-in under §19 BMG. You absolutely must not arrange a bogus registration (Scheinanmeldung) at an address where you don't live. That breaches §54 BMG: an ordinary late registration is punishable by a fine of up to 1000 €, but providing an address for a bogus registration (a breach of §19 Abs. 6 BMG) carries a fine of up to 50 000 € — for both the resident and whoever issued the false confirmation.

steps.title: Documents when registering without your own lease

content.text: The set differs only slightly from the usual one: instead of a lease in your own name, the key document becomes the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from whoever takes you in. Sometimes the authority also asks for a copy of the main tenant's (Hauptmieter) main lease or the owner's consent — but not everywhere.

items: Passport or ID
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) from the housing provider (§19 BMG)
A completed registration form (Anmeldung)
In a sublet, sometimes — a copy of the main tenant's (Hauptmieter) lease or the owner's consent
For a family — documents for each member

content.text: If the person you live with refuses to sign the confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung), registration is impossible, and the 14-day deadline of §17 BMG keeps running against you. Sort out the confirmation BEFORE you move in — issuing it is a legal obligation of the housing provider (Wohnungsgeber), not a favour.

costs.label: Anmeldung in a sublet / without your own lease
costs.note: Registration is free; you only need the Wohnungsgeberbestätigung.

costs.label: Meldebescheinigung (registration certificate)
costs.note: A paid official certificate, if the authority requires it.

costs.label: Bußgeld for a late registration or Scheinanmeldung
costs.note: Under §54 BMG: up to 1000 € for a late Anmeldung, and up to 50 000 € for a bogus registration (§19 Abs. 6 BMG), including for whoever takes you in.

title: Extended registration certificate (erweiterte Meldebescheinigung): when you need it
tldr: A registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) comes in two types: simple (einfache — name and address) and extended (erweiterte — with additional data: nationality, marital status, previous addresses, details of spouse/children). The extended certificate is required, for example, by the registry office (Standesamt) for marriage, by some courts, and sometimes by consulates and foreign authorities. You can order it at the district citizen office (Bürgeramt) or online via the city portal; it usually costs 5–15 €. The free registration confirmation (Anmeldung), issued when you register (§17 BMG), is a different document.

steps.title: Two types of certificate: simple (einfache) and extended (erweiterte)

content.text: The registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) is an official document confirming that you are registered at your place of residence. The simple one (einfache) contains the minimum: your name, date of birth and current address. The extended one (erweiterte) includes far more: nationality, marital status, previous addresses, sometimes details of your spouse and children, and your date of arrival. Which form you choose depends on what the authority requires.

items: Simple registration certificate (einfache Meldebescheinigung) — name, date of birth, current address
Extended registration certificate (erweiterte Meldebescheinigung) — plus nationality, marital status, previous addresses
The extended one may include details of your spouse and children
Don't confuse it with the free registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung)
Both forms are ordered at the district citizen office (Bürgeramt) or online

steps.title: When you specifically need the extended one

content.text: The extended certificate is required wherever extra details about you matter. Most often that means the registry office (Standesamt) when getting married, where you have to prove your marital status and addresses, as well as some courts, notaries, consulates and foreign authorities.

items: Registry office (Standesamt) for getting married (proof of marital status)
Courts and notarial procedures
Consulates and foreign authorities (often with an apostille)
Sometimes — pension and social-security authorities
If the authority explicitly says "erweiterte Meldebescheinigung" — get that one

content.text: Don't order the extended certificate "just in case". Many authorities are fine with the simple form, or even the free registration confirmation (Anmeldung). Check exactly which document is required first, so you don't pay extra or disclose more data than necessary.

steps.title: How to order it and how much it costs

content.text: You can order the registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) during the residence registration (Anmeldung) itself, later in person at the district citizen office (Bürgeramt), or online via the city portal (in many cities with electronic identification). The cost is usually 5–15 € depending on the city and the form; the extended one is sometimes slightly more expensive than the simple one.

items: Options: at registration, later in person, or online via the city portal
Online often requires an eID (electronic ID) and the AusweisApp
The cost is usually 5–15 €
There's no strict expiry, but authorities prefer a "fresh" one (under 3–6 months old)
For use abroad you may need an apostille

content.text: Remember the difference: you get the registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung) for free when you register under §17 BMG, whereas the registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung; especially the extended one) is a separate, paid document. Many authorities inside Germany accept the free confirmation, so don't pay in advance until you're sure of the requirement.

costs.label: einfache Meldebescheinigung
costs.note: A simple certificate; price depends on the city.

costs.label: erweiterte Meldebescheinigung
costs.note: An extended certificate with additional data; sometimes more expensive than the simple one.

costs.label: Anmeldebestätigung at registration
costs.note: The free Anmeldung confirmation is issued right away under §17 BMG.

title: Re-registering at a new address (Ummeldung) when moving within the city
tldr: When you move to a new address within Germany, you must re-register (Ummeldung) within 14 days (§17 BMG). In practice, re-registration is the same as a residence registration (Anmeldung) at the new address: you book an appointment at the district citizen office (Bürgeramt) / Kundenzentrum / KVR and bring your passport and the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung). Important: the new registration automatically cancels the old domestic registration — a separate deregistration (Abmeldung) at the previous address is NOT needed. Deregistration is only required when you move abroad. The service is usually free; missing the deadline can mean an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG).

content.text: Re-registering at a new address (Ummeldung) means changing your registered address when you move within Germany — within the same city or to another one. Legally it's the same registration obligation under §17 BMG: you declare your new home to the authority at your new place of residence within 14 days of moving in.

items: Re-registration = registering at the new address when moving within the country
Deadline — 14 days after moving in (§17 BMG)
Done at the district citizen office (Bürgeramt) / Kundenzentrum / KVR at the NEW address
You need your passport and the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) for the new home
The service is usually free

steps.title: Deregistration (Abmeldung) within the country is not needed

content.text: A key point that trips many people up: when moving within Germany, you do NOT need to separately deregister (Abmeldung) from your old address. When you register the new address, the authority automatically closes the previous registration in the central register.

items: Moving within Germany — only registration (Anmeldung) at the new address
The old registration is cancelled automatically by the register system
A separate visit to the old authority is not required
This works both between cities and between states
Within the same city it's called re-registration (Ummeldung)

content.text: Deregistration (Abmeldung) is needed ONLY when moving abroad — when you leave Germany and keep no home here (§17 Abs. 2 BMG). In that case you must deregister explicitly, otherwise you stay in the register and continue to count as a resident.

When you re-register, the address on your national ID card (Personalausweis) and residence permit is updated (a sticker with the new address — free). But many other documents and services you have to update yourself.

items: The address on your national ID card (Personalausweis)/residence permit is updated at the appointment (the sticker is free)
Report the new address to your bank, your insurer, and your health insurance fund (Krankenkasse)
Update your vehicle registration (Kfz-Zulassung) when moving to a different district
Mail forwarding — a forwarding order (Nachsendeauftrag) with Deutsche Post (paid)
Inform your employer and the tax office (Finanzamt; via the ELSTER portal) if necessary

content.text: Don't put off your re-registration (Ummeldung): the 14-day deadline of §17 BMG applies to moving within the country too, and being late risks an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG). Book an appointment right after moving, especially in large cities with long queues.

costs.note: Re-registration within the country is usually free.

costs.label: New-address sticker on the Personalausweis
costs.note: Updating the address on the ID at the Ummeldung is free.

costs.label: Bußgeld for being late
costs.note: Under §54 BMG for breaching the 14-day deadline.
