title: Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung): what it is
tldr: The landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung; also Wohnungsgeberbescheinigung) is a mandatory document for residence registration (Anmeldung), introduced by the 2015 reform of the registration law (§19 BMG). It's a written confirmation from the property owner or landlord (the housing provider, Wohnungsgeber) that you have actually moved in at that address. The document must contain the landlord's name and address, the address of the home, the date of move-in (Einzugsdatum) and the names of everyone who moved in. The landlord is required to issue it within 14 days of move-in. Without this paper, registration won't be done. A landlord's refusal or delay is a breach of §54 BMG (fine of up to 1000 €), and issuing the confirmation for a bogus registration (§19 Abs. 6 BMG) — up to 50 000 €.

content.text: The landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) is a confirmation from the person who provided you with the housing (the housing provider, Wohnungsgeber: owner or landlord) that you have actually moved in at the stated address. Since the 2015 reform (§19 BMG), this document has been mandatory for any residence registration (Anmeldung) — without it the authority won't register your residence.

The reform was introduced to combat bogus registration (Scheinanmeldung) — registering at addresses where the person doesn't live. Previously the applicant's word was enough; now the signature of whoever provided the housing is required.

items: Legal basis — §19 BMG (Mitwirkung des Wohnungsgebers)
Mandatory for registration (Anmeldung) since 1 November 2015
The housing provider (Wohnungsgeber) is the property owner or landlord
In a sublet, the main tenant gives the confirmation (with the owner's consent)
Without the document, registration won't be done

content.text: The contents of the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) are defined by law. If even one of the mandatory items is missing, the authority may refuse to accept the document.

items: The landlord's name and address (housing provider, Wohnungsgeber)
The address of the home you're moving into
Date of move-in (Einzugsdatum)
The names of everyone who moved in (including family members)
An indication of whether it's a move-in (Einzug) or a move-out (Auszug)
The landlord's signature

content.text: Ready-made confirmation forms (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) are available on every city's website (service.berlin.de, hamburg.de, stadt.muenchen.de, stuttgart.de). Download it, have the landlord fill it in and sign it, and bring the original to the registration appointment (Anmeldung).

The landlord is required to issue the confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) within 14 days of move-in (§19 BMG). This is their legal obligation — they can neither refuse it nor charge for it.

items: Deadline to issue — 14 days after move-in (§19 BMG)
The landlord may not demand payment for the document
Refusal or delay is a breach of §54 BMG (a fine of up to 1000 € for the landlord)
You can get the document in advance, by the move-in date
A scan/PDF will do if the authority allows it, but usually the original is needed

content.text: If the landlord stalls on the document, remind them in writing, citing §19 BMG and the 14-day deadline. Without the confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) you won't be able to register (Anmeldung) on time, and being late under §17/§54 BMG formally falls on you — so document your attempts to get the paper.
The landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) is a legal document. Forging it, or confirming residence where a person doesn't actually live, is a punishable offence.

items: You must not sign a confirmation of fictitious residence (bogus registration, Scheinanmeldung)
You must not forge the landlord's signature
Buying a "registration at an address" without actually living there is an offence
Issuing a false confirmation for a bogus registration is a breach of §54 BMG (a fine of up to 50 000 €)

content.text: For a false confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) and for providing an address for a bogus registration, §54 BMG (a breach of §19 Abs. 6 BMG) provides for a fine of up to 50 000 € — for both the landlord and the resident; organisers of mass bogus registrations face criminal consequences. Only register where you actually live.

costs.label: Wohnungsgeberbestätigung
costs.note: The landlord is required to issue it for free (§19 BMG); charging for the document is not allowed.

costs.label: Anmeldung with this document
costs.note: The registration itself is free in most cities.

costs.label: Bußgeld for a violation
costs.note: Under §54 BMG: refusal or delay with the document — up to 1000 €; a false confirmation for a bogus registration (§19 Abs. 6 BMG) — up to 50 000 €.

title: Booking an appointment (Termin) at the foreigners' authority (ABH): how to catch a slot
tldr: The foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) is the main bottleneck for all residence permits (Aufenthaltstitel). In Berlin, the immigration office (Landesamt für Einwanderung, LEA) genuinely makes you wait 3–6 months, sometimes up to a year. This guide covers where to click, how to catch slots, and what to do if your visa expires before the appointment (temporary confirmation of legal status, Fiktionsbescheinigung).

steps.title: What the foreigners' authority (ABH) is and why there are no appointments

content.text: The foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH; in Berlin, the immigration office LEA, Landesamt für Einwanderung) is a regional body: each city or state runs its own. There is no single federal portal. As a result, the rules, queues and booking systems differ: Berlin — via otv.verwalt-berlin.de and the LEA contact form; Munich — via muenchen.de; Hamburg — via hamburg.de.

items: The foreigners' authority (ABH) issues and renews the residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) (§§ 4, 4a AufenthG)
Berlin (LEA) in 2026 is the main problem spot: waves of online-slot lockouts
From 2024–2026, many LEA functions have moved to a contact form: you send a request, and an official assigns the appointment for you
Average wait for an appointment at the LEA: 3–6 months; at peaks — up to 9–12
A renewal application is usually submitted 6–8 weeks before expiry; many authorities also accept it 3 months ahead — check with your own office

steps.title: A step-by-step strategy for hunting an appointment

content.text: The approach depends on the city. First check the official portal, then work several fronts in parallel.

items: Berlin: otv.verwalt-berlin.de/ams/TerminBuchen — try in the morning at 7:00 and after 18:00; if there are no slots, switch to the contact form (Kontaktformular) on service.berlin.de
München: muenchen.de/auslaenderbehoerde — booking via the Bürgerservice
Hamburg: hamburg.de — Einwohner-Zentralamt, online booking
Köln/Frankfurt/Stuttgart — each has its own portal; google 'Stadt + Ausländerbehörde Termin'
Slots often appear at 7:00–9:00 (the morning release) and around midnight
Monday and Thursday are the most "productive" days
Try the out-of-town branches (Außenstelle) — in Berlin these include, for example, Friedrich-Krause-Ufer and Keplerstraße
Clear your browser cookies or use incognito mode

items.title: 3. If there are no online slots — write

content.text: Using the contact form (Kontaktformular) on the LEA/ABH website, describe your situation: the type of residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel), the expiry date of your current permit, and the reason for urgency (work, travel). LEA Berlin officially confirms that appointments are assigned via the contact form.

items.title: 4. Temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) — if your visa expires

content.text: §81 (4) AufenthG (Fortgeltungsfiktion): if you applied for renewal before your current residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) expired, your previous status is deemed to remain valid until the foreigners' authority (ABH) decides, and you are issued a temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) — a temporary confirmation of lawful stay (§81 (5) AufenthG). The fee is 13€. With it you can work if your previous status allowed it, but travel outside the Schengen area may be restricted — check with the authority before you leave.

Services like termin-reservieren.de, Telegram bots and browser extensions track slots automatically. Using them isn't illegal as such, but in 2024–2025 LEA Berlin blocked such services and temporarily shut down online booking because of abuse. Use them at your own risk.

steps.title: What to bring to the appointment

items: A valid passport + a copy of the photo page
Your current residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) / visa (if any)
Registration confirmation (Anmeldebescheinigung) for your address — no older than 6 months
A biometric photo, 35×45 mm, to the BMI standard
Evidence of the basis of your stay: employment contract, salary statement, lease, insurance
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) — a certificate from GKV/PKV
Money: 100€ for first issuance, 96€ for renewal (card / German debit card Girocard, as cash isn't accepted everywhere)

content.text: If you didn't apply before your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) expired, you lose your right to a temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung). What follows is unlawful stay (§95 AufenthG), up to criminal liability, and a risk of refusal when you later apply for status. If there are no online slots, SEND A REQUEST VIA THE CONTACT FORM before the expiry date — this counts as a timely application.

A temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) is not the same as a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel): with it you can't travel visa-free to third countries outside the Schengen area, and some employers are reluctant to accept it as proof of a work permit (Arbeitserlaubnis).
Since 2024, Berlin's LEA periodically disables online booking. Don't fixate on a single route: write via the contact form (Kontaktformular) and try the branches (Außenstellen) in parallel.

costs.note: Standard fee under §45 AufenthV in 2026.

costs.note: For most categories

title: Filing an asylum application (Asylantrag) through BAMF
tldr: An asylum application (Asylantrag) is filed in person at a branch (Außenstelle) of the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) at an initial reception centre (Erstaufnahmeeinrichtung). The stages: registration → arrival certificate (Ankunftsnachweis) → formal application → interview (Anhörung) → decision. The procedure is free. The basic regulation is the asylum act (AsylG, Asylgesetz).

content.text: An asylum application (Asylantrag) is a request for one of the forms of international protection: refugee status (Flüchtlingsschutz §3 AsylG), the right of asylum (Asylberechtigung Art. 16a GG), subsidiary protection (subsidiärer Schutz §4 AsylG) or a deportation ban (Abschiebungsverbot §60 AufenthG). The decision is made by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge, BAMF).

items: The application is filed in person — you cannot do it by post or online
The procedure is entirely free
Decision time — BAMF's formal target is 6 months; in practice anything from several months to 1–2 years
During the procedure you hold a permission to stay for the duration of the asylum review (Aufenthaltsgestattung) (§55 AsylG) — a temporary right of stay

The reform of the Common European Asylum System (GEAS / Pakt zur Migration und Asyl) comes into force in stages in 2026: faster procedures, new Dublin rules and border procedures — track the current timelines via official BAMF/EUAA sources

content.text: The intention to seek asylum (Asylgesuch) can be declared to any authority — the police, a border officer, or BAMF. From there you are directed to an initial reception centre (Erstaufnahmeeinrichtung, EAE).

At the reception centre (EAE) you go through registration: fingerprinting, photo, identification (PIK-System). You receive an arrival certificate (Ankunftsnachweis, AKN) — proof of registration as an asylum seeker. With it you are entitled to accommodation, food and medical care under §4 AsylbLG.

The federal EASY system distributes you across the states according to the "Königsteiner Schlüssel" (quotas). You are then directed to the relevant reception centre (EAE) of the state whose BAMF branch (Außenstelle) is responsible for you.

items: Takes place at a BAMF branch (Außenstelle), usually in the same reception centre (EAE)
You fill in the application form (Asylantrag) (a native-language interpreter is provided)
You receive a permission to stay for the duration of the asylum review (Aufenthaltsgestattung) — it replaces the arrival certificate (Ankunftsnachweis)
An interview date (Anhörungstermin) is set (often several weeks later)

content.text: BAMF checks whether another EU country is responsible for the case (fingerprints in EURODAC). If so, you can be transferred to that country within 6 months. You can challenge this with a claim to the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) (deadline 1 week).
A personal interview with a BAMF case officer (Entscheider) — the key moment of the procedure. For details, see the separate guide 'Asyl-Anhörung: how to prepare'.

The written decision (Bescheid) arrives by post or at the reception centre (EAE). Possible outcomes: recognition (one of the 4 forms of protection), rejection, or "offensichtlich unbegründet" (manifestly unfounded — an appeal deadline of 1 week instead of 2).

items: A free interpreter at all official interviews (§17 AsylG)
The right to a lawyer — at your own expense; with a permission to stay (Aufenthaltsgestattung) you can apply for legal advice aid (Beratungshilfe) / legal costs aid (Prozesskostenhilfe)
Medical care (medizinische Versorgung) under §4, §6 AsylbLG: acute cases, pregnancy, vaccinations
Accommodation, food, pocket money (Taschengeld ~204€/month for adults in 2026)
After 3 months, usually — the right to asylum procedure counselling (Asylverfahrensberatung) (free counselling at BAMF)
Right of appeal: 2 weeks at the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) (1 week for "offensichtlich unbegründet")

content.text: Do NOT leave the state you are assigned to without a permission to leave (Verlassenserlaubnis) — that breaches the obligation to reside in the assigned area (Residenzpflicht) (§56 AsylG) during the first 3 months.
The deadline to appeal a negative decision is VERY short: 2 weeks (or 1 week for "offensichtlich unbegründet"). It runs from the service of the decision (Bescheid). Miss it and you face deportation.
Concealing important facts at the interview (Anhörung) is later treated as undermining the credibility of your account — a leading reason for rejections. Every contradiction is recorded in the file.

Asylum and Dublin Regulation (Dublin) cases depend heavily on individual circumstances and strict deadlines. Individual legal advice is recommended (a specialist migration-law lawyer, Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht, or free asylum procedure counselling, Asylverfahrensberatung / Beratungsstelle: Caritas, Diakonie, AWO, ProAsyl).

costs.label: Asylantrag
costs.note: The asylum procedure is not subject to any state fee

costs.label: Lawyer (optional)
costs.note: 0€ with a Beratungshilfeschein from the Amtsgericht; otherwise 200–800€

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung of documents
costs.note: From 25€ per page with a vereidigter Übersetzer

title: Asylum interview (Asyl-Anhörung): how to prepare
tldr: The interview (Anhörung) (§25 AsylG) — a personal interview with a case officer (Entscheider) at the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) — is the key stage of the procedure. The decision rests almost entirely on it. Preparation is essential: a timeline, evidence, and consistency with family members' statements. It lasts 2–5 hours, sometimes longer.

steps.title: What the interview (Anhörung) is and why it decides everything

content.text: The interview (Anhörung) is a personal interview with a case officer (Entscheider — a dedicated BAMF officer), governed by §25 AsylG. Your task is to set out the grounds of persecution (Verfolgungsgründe): what happened to you in your country of origin, who is persecuting you, and why the state failed to protect you. The decision on your case is made on the basis of your account + country information (Herkunftsländerleitsätze) + evidence.

items: Conducted through an interpreter (free)
The written record in German is read back to you through the interpreter — be sure to correct any errors
In some cases a video link is possible — rare, and at BAMF's discretion
Typically lasts 2–5 hours; complex cases — a whole day
Currently usually held 4–12 weeks after the application (Asylantrag) is filed

steps.title: Preparation: what to do in advance

content.text: Go to asylum procedure counselling (Asylverfahrensberatung; free counselling, organised by BAMF + welfare associations, Wohlfahrtsverbände: Caritas, Diakonie, AWO, ProAsyl). If you can, hire a specialist migration-law lawyer (Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht), who may attend the interview (Anhörung) with you.

items: All key events with dates (month/year at minimum)
Who, what, where, why
The exit route: dates, countries, transit, means of transport
Say this timeline out loud 3–5 times — it should sound natural
Any documents: summonses, court rulings, medical reports, photos of scars, social-media screenshots
Third-party testimony (relatives, journalists, human-rights defenders)
Evidence of belonging to a group (LGBTQ+, religion, opposition): photos of demonstrations, membership cards, publications
If you have a psychiatric or trauma diagnosis — a doctor's report on PTSD (PTBS)

content.text: BAMF holds a separate interview (Anhörung) for each adult family member. Contradictions between statements are a common reason for rejections. Agree on the facts IN ADVANCE, but tell it in YOUR OWN words.

items.title: 4. On the day of the interview (Anhörung)

items: Bring your passport, the arrival certificate (AKN)/permission to stay (Aufenthaltsgestattung), and all original documents + copies
Check the interpreter: make sure you understand their dialect; if not — ask for a replacement BEFORE the start
Breaks are your right: ask for one if you're tired, need the toilet, or are emotionally overwhelmed
At the end, listen CAREFULLY to the read-back of the record and enter ALL corrections
A free interpreter (§17 AsylG) — in your native language or a language you understand
A lawyer may be present (at your own expense)
A person of trust (Vertrauensperson) — a friend, family member or NGO representative — may attend with BAMF's consent
Special needs: a female officer (Entscheider) and a female interpreter for victims of sexual violence, and a special regime for minors and vulnerable applicants
Breaks on request
The right not to answer questions that are traumatising — but you must explain why

content.text: "I don't remember the exact date" is fine. But answering "I don't remember" every time about key events comes across as unreliability. Better: "around the end of March 2023, about 2 weeks after Newroz".
Don't sign the record without reading it. Always ask for a read-back. If what's written isn't what you said — insist on a correction. After you sign, your account is almost impossible to change.

Holding things back (for example, hiding your orientation or religion out of shame) is later perceived as "Steigerung des Vortrags" — an escalation of the account. This is a leading reason for rejections. Better to say everything up front — if necessary, through an interpreter and an officer (Entscheider) of the same sex.

Asylum and Dublin Regulation (Dublin) cases depend heavily on individual circumstances and strict deadlines. Individual legal advice is recommended (a specialist migration-law lawyer, Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht, or free asylum procedure counselling, Asylverfahrensberatung / Beratungsstelle: Caritas, Diakonie, AWO, ProAsyl).

costs.label: Anhörung itself
costs.note: Free, including the interpreter

costs.label: Lawyer at the Anhörung
costs.note: Fee of a Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht

costs.label: Psycho-trauma report (for §60 AufenthG)
costs.note: When arranged through a specialist centre (Behandlungszentren für Folteropfer) — often free

title: Residence card (Aufenthaltskarte) for family members of EU citizens
tldr: If you are not an EU citizen but the spouse, child or parent of an EU citizen who exercises freedom of movement in Germany, your status is governed by FreizügG/EU (not AufenthG). The residence card (Aufenthaltskarte) under §5 FreizügG/EU is issued for up to 5 years and processed by the foreigners' authority (ABH) within 6 months. The fee is low: under §47 AufenthV it equals the charge for a national ID card (Personalausweis) — 46 € / 22,80 € for people under 24.

steps.title: What it is and who it's for

content.text: The residence card (Aufenthaltskarte; Residence Card for Family Members) is a document confirming that you, as a family member of an EU/EEA citizen, exercise freedom of movement under Directive 2004/38/EG (implemented in Germany through the Freizügigkeitsgesetz/EU). The card is declaratory: the right arises by law, and the card merely confirms it.

items: Governing act: §5 FreizügG/EU, plus §3 and §4 (right to family life)

IMPORTANT: it applies to the family of a citizen of ANOTHER EU country (not Germany), or to the family of a German who returned after living for a long time in another EU country (the Surinder Singh effect)
For family members of a GERMAN citizen who did not exercise freedom of movement, §28 AufenthG applies, not FreizügG/EU
Lower fee than usual: under §47 AufenthV it is the same as for a national ID card (Personalausweis, see below), not 100 €
Validity: up to 5 years
After 5 years of lawful residence — a permanent residence card (Daueraufenthaltskarte) under §5 (5) FreizügG/EU

steps.title: Who counts as a family member

content.text: §3 FreizügG/EU defines the group of privileged family members:

items: Spouse or registered partner
Children and grandchildren under 21, or older if dependent on the EU citizen or their spouse
Parents and grandparents, if dependent on the EU citizen or their spouse
Extended group (§3a FreizügG/EU): a partner in a durable relationship, or other dependent relatives — granted at the authority's discretion

content.text: First, both the EU citizen and the third-country family member register their address at the local citizens' office (Bürgeramt) and receive a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung).

items.title: 2. File the application with the foreigners' authority (ABH)

items: File the application with the foreigners' authority (ABH/LEA) for your place of residence (by booking an appointment; see the relevant guide)
The processing time for the card is up to 6 months (§5 (2) FreizügG/EU); in the meantime you receive a certificate confirming the application was filed (Bescheinigung über die Antragstellung)
The card is valid for up to 5 years
Passport
Biometric photo
Registration confirmation (Anmeldebescheinigung)
Proof of the family relationship: a marriage or birth certificate with an apostille (Apostille) and a certified translation
Proof that the EU citizen is exercising freedom of movement: an employment contract, registration as self-employed, or proof of studies plus insurance and sufficient funds
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) for the whole family

steps.title: What the residence card (Aufenthaltskarte) gives you

items: The right to work without a separate permit (§2 FreizügG/EU)
Access to social benefits on equal terms with EU citizens (with limitations for the first 3 months)
Visa-free travel within the Schengen area
After 5 years — a permanent residence card (Daueraufenthaltskarte)
Retention of the right after divorce under certain conditions (§3 (4–5) FreizügG/EU): the marriage lasted ≥3 years, of which ≥1 year in Germany, or there are children with custody/access rights

content.text: The foreigners' authority (ABH) often confuses FreizügG/EU with AufenthG and hands you the 100€ fee form. The residence card (Aufenthaltskarte) under §5 FreizügG/EU is NOT free, but it is cheaper than the standard fee: §47 AufenthV caps the charge at the fee for a national ID card (Personalausweis) — roughly 37,00 € for people aged 24 and over and 22,80 € under 24; check the current rate. Cite §47 AufenthV if you are charged 100 €.

If the EU citizen does NOT work, study, or have sufficient funds and insurance, they are not 'freizügigkeitsberechtigt' (not entitled to freedom of movement), and the family member's right lapses. The foreigners' authority (ABH) is then entitled to revoke the residence card (Aufenthaltskarte).

Marriage and birth certificates from non-EU countries often require an apostille (Apostille; Hague Convention) or consular legalization at the embassy, plus a translation by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer). This takes 2–8 weeks.

costs.label: Residence card (Aufenthaltskarte), initial issue
costs.note: Fee under §47 AufenthV — the same as for a national ID card (Personalausweis): roughly 37,00 € from age 24, 22,80 € under 24, rather than the 100 € for a standard residence permit (AT). Check the current rate.

costs.label: Apostille (Apostille) on the certificate
costs.note: In the country where the document originates

costs.label: Certified translation (Beglaubigte Übersetzung)
costs.note: Per page from a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer)

title: All types of residence title (Aufenthaltstitel): §16–§38 in brief
tldr: The Residence Act (Aufenthaltsgesetz, AufenthG) divides residence titles into chapters and sections: studies (§§16–17), work (§§18–21), humanitarian grounds (§§22–25b), family (§§27–36) and special cases (§§37–38). This cheat sheet helps you work out which section fits your situation.

content.text: AufenthG distinguishes 5 types of residence title (Aufenthaltstitel) under §4:

items: Visa (Visum) under §6 — national or Schengen
Temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) under §7 — a fixed-term permit to stay
EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) under §18g — for the highly qualified
Permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §9 — permanent residence
EU long-term residence permit (Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt-EU) under §9a — EU permanent residence
§16a — vocational training (Berufsausbildung)
§16b — university studies (Studium)
§16c — Erasmus and short programs
§16d — recognition of a foreign qualification (Anerkennung) plus supplementary training
§16e — university applicant (Studienbewerber): applying to study
§16f — school and language courses
§17 — searching for a training or study place (Suche eines Ausbildungs-/Studienplatzes): up to 9 months
§18 — general provisions on employment (Beschäftigung)
§18a — skilled worker (Fachkraft) with recognized vocational training (Berufsausbildung)
§18b — skilled worker (Fachkraft) with an academic degree

§18c — permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) for skilled workers (Fachkräfte): under §18c (1) after 36 months; under §18c (2) for EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) holders after 21/27 months
§18d — research (Forschung; researchers, see EU Directive 2016/801)
§18g — EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU; since 2023 it replaced the former §18b)
§19 — permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) for the highly qualified (Hochqualifizierte; top executives, researchers)
§19c — special cases of employment (Beschäftigung) under the Employment Ordinance (Beschäftigungsverordnung)
§19d — temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) for qualified persons with a deportation deferral (qualifizierte Geduldete)
§19e — special types of employment (e.g. au pair, voluntary service)

content.text: The category of your residence title (Aufenthaltstitel) determines your rights: whether you can work, bring your family, receive BAföG, or move to a permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis). A change of the purpose of residence (Zweckwechsel) often requires a SEPARATE application, and sometimes a fresh entry on a visa.

Moving from a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) under §16b (studies) to §18a/18b is usually straightforward, but moving from §25 (5) or a deportation deferral (Duldung) under §60a to §18a is much harder — you have to meet all the requirements of a skilled worker (Fachkraft).

title: EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU): salary thresholds 2026
tldr: The EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) under §18g AufenthG is a status for the highly qualified. 2026 thresholds: 50 700€ gross/year for standard professions (Regelberuf), and 45 934,20€ for a shortage profession (Engpassberuf) or recent graduates (≤3 years). It is calculated as 50% (or 45,3%) of the income ceiling for social-contribution assessment (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) of 101 400€. The fee is 100€.

steps.title: What the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) is

content.text: The EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) is a residence title (Aufenthaltstitel) for foreigners with an academic degree who do qualified work in Germany at a salary above the set threshold. It is governed by §18g AufenthG (since 2023; previously §18b) and implements EU Directive 2021/1883.

items: For whom: non-EU citizens with a higher education degree (bachelor's or higher, recognized in Germany)
IMPORTANT: for IT specialists without a degree there is a separate path under §18g (2), requiring 3+ years of experience in the last 7 years
Validity: up to 4 years (or the contract term plus 3 months, if shorter)
Freedom to change jobs after 12 months of work on the Blue Card (previously this required the foreigners' authority's permission, ABH)
Permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) after 27 months (or 21 months with B1) — §18c (2) AufenthG
EU mobility: after 12 months you can apply for a Blue Card in another EU country under simplified rules

content.text: New amounts apply from 1 January 2026. They are tied to the income ceiling for social-contribution assessment (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze, BBG) for pension insurance, which in 2026 is 101 400€/year, and they are revised annually — check the current threshold before applying.

items: Standard professions (Regelberuf): 50 700€ gross/year = 4 225€/month (50% of BBG)
Shortage professions (Engpassberuf): 45 934,20€ gross/year = 3 827,85€/month (45,3% of BBG)
Career starters (Berufseinsteiger; degree obtained ≤ 3 years ago): 45 934,20€ gross/year
IT specialist without a degree (§18g (2)): 45 934,20€ plus 3+ years of relevant experience in the last 7 years
What counts toward salary: ONLY the guaranteed fixed gross salary. NOT counted: bonuses, options, sign-on, housing or transport. IMPORTANT.

content.text: Use the degree-recognition database anabin.kmk.org to check whether your university and field of study are recognized (status H+ means 'recognized'). If not, you'll need a separate recognition of the qualification (Anerkennung) through the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB; Zentralstelle für ausländisches Bildungswesen).

items: The employment contract must be for a qualified position matching your field of study
A salary above the threshold (50 700€ / 45 934,20€)
A contract for at least 6 months

items.title: 3. Apply for a D visa at the embassy

content.text: If you are outside the EU, you need a national visa (Nationales Visum) for §18g AufenthG. Since 2024, an accelerated procedure for skilled workers (beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren) has applied to many professions — the employer handles the case at the foreigners' authority (ABH) in Germany.

items.title: 4. Residence registration (Anmeldung) plus an appointment (Termin) at the foreigners' authority (ABH)

content.text: After arrival: residence registration (Anmeldung) at your address → an appointment (Termin) at the foreigners' authority (ABH/LEA) → collection of the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) plastic card. The fee is 100€. The card arrives by post in 4–6 weeks.

items: Passport
Biometric photo
Recognized degree (or its equivalent via the Central Office for Foreign Education, ZAB)
Employment contract / declaration of the employment relationship (Erklärung zum Beschäftigungsverhältnis; the foreigners' authority's form, ABH)
Registration confirmation (Anmeldebescheinigung)
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung): statutory (GKV) or proof of private cover (PKV-Bestätigung)
For a shortage profession (Engpassberuf) — a job description linked to the ISCO classification

content.text: Bonuses in the offer do NOT count toward the threshold. If you are offered '50 000€ base + 5 000€ bonus', that's 50 000€ < 50 700€, and a Blue Card in a standard profession (Regelberuf) is off the table. Ask them to raise the base to the threshold.

A shortage profession (Engpassberuf) is defined by an ISCO-08 CODE (132, 133, 134, 21, 221, 222, 225, 226, 23, 25 — IT, engineers, doctors, pharmacists, maths/physics teachers, etc.) in § 18g (1) Nr. 2 AufenthG. The foreigners' authority (ABH) checks against the list; if your position doesn't fall under it, the threshold goes back to 50 700€.

Changing employer in the first 12 months requires NOTIFYING the foreigners' authority (ABH) under §18g (4) — otherwise you can lose the Blue Card. Since 2024 this is a notification, not a permission, but don't drag it out.

title: Blue Card (Blaue Karte): family reunification without A1
tldr: The family of an EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) holder enjoys privileges under §29 (5) AufenthG: the spouse does NOT have to prove housing or A1 German. The D visa for reunification is processed at the embassy, and work is permitted immediately. Validity is synchronized with the principal's Blue Card.

steps.title: What the privileges are and who they're for

content.text: Standard family reunification (Familiennachzug) under §30 AufenthG requires the spouse to be aged 18+, to have basic German at the A1 level (Goethe-Zertifikat A1 or equivalent), and to have sufficient living space available. For the families of the highly qualified, §29 (5) AufenthG WAIVES these requirements.

items: Applies to the family of a holder of: an EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) under §18g, an ICT card (ICT-Karte) under §19, a Mobile ICT card (Mobile ICT-Karte) under §19b, a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) for researchers under §18d, self-employed persons (Selbstständige) under §21, and a number of other qualified statuses (the exact list is in §29 (5) and §30 (1) AufenthG)
No need to pass A1 German BEFORE entry
No need to prove sufficient living space (ausreichender Wohnraum)
Work permitted immediately (§27 (5))
The spouse's temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) is synchronized with the principal's Blue Card
Spouse or registered partner (including same-sex partnerships; the marriage must have been performed in a country where it is legal)
Minor unmarried children (§32)
Children who have not turned 18 at the time the application is filed at the embassy — even if the procedure drags on
Parents of the Blue Card holder — only in exceptional cases (a hardship case, Härtefall, §36 (2))
A marriage entered into AFTER the principal moved to Germany (a so-called Nachholeehe) also qualifies; the §29 (5) privileges are retained

items.title: 1. The principal obtains the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU)

content.text: See the separate guide 'EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU): salary thresholds 2026'. Without an active Blue Card, the §29 (5) privileges do not apply.

items.title: 2. Filing documents at the German embassy

items: Visa appointment (Visumstermin; category D — family reunification with an EU Blue Card holder, Familiennachzug zu Inhaber einer Blauen Karte EU)
Marriage certificate with an apostille (Apostille) plus a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung)
Children's birth certificates with an apostille (Apostille) plus a translation
Passports of everyone coming
A copy of the principal's Blue Card plus a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
The principal's employment contract and salary statements
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) for everyone (at least for the 90 days of entry)

content.text: The standard processing time is 6–12 weeks. If the principal arrived with a Blue Card from another EU country and the family had already been living together there, §29 (5) provides an additional simplification (no check of sufficient means of subsistence, ausreichender Lebensunterhalt). On arrival: residence registration (Anmeldung) and an appointment (Termin) at the foreigners' authority (ABH) for the plastic card.

items: The spouse can work immediately — NO separate permit is needed, and there's NO need to wait 12 months as with ordinary family reunification (Familiennachzug)
Children attend daycare (Kita) or school
After 5 years of lawful residence — a permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) for the spouse (§9, if the general conditions are met, including B1 and pension contributions)
On dissolution of the marriage — an independent right of residence under §31 AufenthG (provided the marriage lasted ≥3 years in Germany, or there is a hardship case, Härtefall)

content.text: The 'without A1' privilege in §29 (5) AufenthG applies ONLY to reunification with a Blue Card holder, highly qualified specialist (Hochqualifizierter), researcher (Forscher) and the like. For ordinary §30 (spouse reunification, Ehegattennachzug), A1 is still mandatory (with exceptions for citizens of the USA, Canada, Japan, etc.).

Marriage certificates from countries outside the Hague Convention (e.g. many African countries, Iran) require not an apostille (Apostille) but consular legalization at the German embassy in the country of origin — this can take 3–6 months.

If the principal's Blue Card (Blaue Karte) ends (job loss, change of status), the spouse's right under §29 (5) is also at risk. The foreigners' authority (ABH) may require the family to be moved to §30 — and then A1 will be needed.

title: Shortage professions (Engpassberufe) for the Blue Card (Blaue Karte): the list
tldr: Shortage professions (Engpassberufe) carry a reduced salary threshold for the Blue Card in 2026: 45 934,20€ instead of 50 700€. The list is fixed in §18g (1) Nr. 2 AufenthG via ISCO-08 codes: IT, engineers, doctors, pharmacists, STEM teachers, veterinarians, and others.

content.text: A shortage profession (Engpassberuf) is a profession with a recognized labour shortage. For the purposes of the Blue Card, §18g (1) Nr. 2 AufenthG fixes the list via the codes of the international classification of occupations ISCO-08 (International Standard Classification of Occupations). This does NOT coincide with the ordinary list of shortage professions (Mangelberufe) of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) used for other purposes.

items: Advantage: a reduced threshold of 45 934,20€ instead of 50 700€ in 2026
Advantage: no consent of the Federal Employment Agency is required (Zustimmung der Bundesagentur für Arbeit; under §18g (1) both categories proceed without the BA's consent)
The list is closed and cannot be expanded at the foreigners' authority's discretion (ABH)
Since the Skilled Immigration Act 2023 reform, the list has been significantly expanded

steps.title: Full list of professions (ISCO-08 codes under §18g)

content.text: §18g (1) Nr. 2 letters a–c AufenthG lists the following groups:

items: ISCO 132 — managers in manufacturing, mining, construction and logistics
ISCO 133 — managers in IT and communication services
ISCO 134 — managers in professional services (including healthcare, education and finance)
ISCO 21 — science and engineering professionals (physicists, chemists, mathematicians, statisticians, engineers of all specialties, architects, landscape designers)
ISCO 221 — doctors (Ärzte; including general practitioners, Allgemeinmediziner, and medical specialists, Fachärzte)
ISCO 222 — higher-level nursing staff (nursing, Krankenpflege, and midwives — university level)
ISCO 225 — veterinarians
ISCO 226 — other health professionals with a higher education degree (dentists, pharmacists, dietitians, audiologists, optometrists, physiotherapists — university level)
ISCO 23 — teaching professionals (university lecturers, secondary and special education, including special-needs teachers, Sonderschulpädagogen)
ISCO 25 — ICT professionals (software developers, systems analysts, network and database specialists, cybersecurity)

content.text: There is a special path for IT (ISCO 133 — IT managers, or 25 — IT specialists) and related professions in the same category for people who do NOT have a higher education degree but do have experience:

items: A position in ISCO 133 or 25
At least 3 years of professional experience in the last 7 years at a comparable level
Salary at the shortage-profession (Engpass) threshold: 45 934,20€ in 2026
All other §18g requirements apply

steps.title: How to prove your position is an Engpassberuf

content.text: In the employment contract or a separate declaration of the employment relationship (Erklärung zum Beschäftigungsverhältnis; the foreigners' authority's form, ABH), the employer must describe the position so that it can be assigned unambiguously to an ISCO code. For example, not 'manager' but 'IT Operations Manager (ISCO 133)'.

The degree must be in the same or an adjacent field. For example, a physics degree for a data scientist position is fine; a philology degree for a developer is questionable, in which case you need the §18g (2) path via experience.
Use the degree-recognition database anabin.kmk.org to make sure your university has the H+ status and your field of study matches. This is the basis for §18g (1) Nr. 1.

The §18g (1) Nr. 2 list does not coincide with the 'Top Mangelberufe' (top list of shortage professions) from the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) or with other shortage-profession lists under the BeschV. Don't confuse them: the shortage-profession (Mangelberuf) status for the Western Balkans regulation (Westbalkan-Regelung) under §26 (2) BeschV is an entirely different legal construct.

Managerial positions (ISCO 132/133/134) are often contested by the foreigners' authority (ABH): 'you're a lead developer, not an IT manager.' Make your case — the share of time spent managing the team, budgets and hiring. Without that, it may be assigned to ISCO 25 (also a shortage profession, Engpass, but the threshold is the same).
The 45 934,20€ salary is the GROSS fixed base. Bonuses and the variable part do not count (see the separate guide 'EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU): thresholds').

title: Blue Card (Blaue Karte) → permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) in 21/27 months
tldr: §18c(2) AufenthG is the fast track to permanent residence (the permanent settlement permit, Niederlassungserlaubnis, NE) for EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) holders. With German at the B1 level, the NE is issued after just 21 months of work on the Blue Card; with A1, after 27 months. The key condition is that pension contributions (Rentenversicherung) are paid throughout the entire qualifying period of 21 or 27 months. You also need a valid Blue Card, secured housing, a clean criminal record, and a basic knowledge of the legal order. The fee for the NE is 113 €. This is the fastest route of all residence permits to permanent status in Germany.

steps.title: Why a Blue Card (Blaue Karte) holder gets an accelerated NE

content.text: The EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) is a temporary residence permit for skilled workers with a higher education degree and a salary above the set threshold. But its main bonus is accelerated access to permanent residence (the permanent settlement permit, Niederlassungserlaubnis, NE). Under §18c(2) AufenthG the usual 5-year period for the NE is shortened to 21 or 27 months depending on your level of German.

items: 21 months — with a confirmed German level of B1 (a language certificate, Sprachzertifikat)
27 months — without B1 (basic German at the A1 level is enough)
Mandatory contributions to the pension insurance (Rentenversicherung) throughout the entire qualifying period: 21 months with B1, otherwise 27
A valid EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) at the time of applying for the NE
The fee for the NE — 113 € (the standard amount for all permanent residence permits)

content.text: The 21/27-month period counts only the time spent holding the Blue Card and paying pension contributions. Months on other residence permits (student §16b, a spouse's permit) do NOT count toward this accelerated clock — they follow the ordinary rules of §9 AufenthG (5 years). First get the Blue Card, and only then does the count begin.

Two key parameters determine the period: your level of German and your accumulated contributions to the pension system. Your language level is confirmed by a certificate from a recognized exam (the telc examination system, the Goethe-Institut, the Austrian ÖSD certificate, or the university-entrance exam TestDaF). Pension contributions are shown in a statement from the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) — the Versicherungsverlauf.

items: B1 → a 21-month period: a telc B1 certificate / Goethe-Zertifikat B1 / the integration-course test DTZ
without B1 (A1 is enough) → a 27-month period: a basic A1 certificate from a recognized provider
The certificate must be from an accredited institution, not a self-assessment
Without a confirmed language level, the NE on the accelerated track will not be granted
The pension contribution rate is 18,6% of the gross salary (split with the employer)
§18c (2) requires contributions for 21 months (with B1) or 27 months (with A1) — mandatory (Pflicht-) or voluntary (freiwillige) Beiträge
Order a contribution-history statement (Versicherungsverlauf) at deutsche-rentenversicherung.de
Voluntary contributions (freiwillige Beiträge) may be used to top up the months

content.text: If you worked partial months, were on unpaid leave, or changed jobs with gaps, check your contribution-history statement (Versicherungsverlauf) in advance — gaps in pension contributions can push back the date you become entitled to the NE. The foreigners' authority (ABH) looks specifically at the months of actual contributions, not at the calendar period of holding the card.

steps.title: Filing the NE application at the ABH

content.text: You apply for the permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) at the local foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) for your place of residence. Book an appointment well in advance — in large cities (Berlin, Munich, Frankfurt) the queue can stretch to 2–3 months. If your Blue Card is about to expire before the NE is issued, ask for a temporary confirmation of lawful status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) to keep your legal status.

items: Passport plus a valid EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU)
A German certificate at B1 or A1
Contribution-history statement (Versicherungsverlauf) from the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung)
Proof of employment and salary (employment contract, Arbeitsvertrag; payslips, Gehaltsabrechnungen)
A rental contract or proof of secured housing
Biometric photo 35×45 mm
Certificate of no criminal record, if requested by the foreigners' authority (ABH)

content.text: The permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) gives an unlimited right to live and work in Germany and opens the path to citizenship. But the NE can be lost if you leave Germany for more than 6 months without special permission from the foreigners' authority (ABH) under §51 AufenthG. For long absences, obtain written consent to retain your status.

title: Opportunity card (Chancenkarte): points under the new rules
tldr: The opportunity card (Chancenkarte) under §20a AufenthG is a points-based job-seeker visa, in force since 1 June 2024. It lets you live in Germany legally for a year and look for work; you may do side jobs of up to 20 hrs/week and test yourself out on a contract for up to 2 weeks (trial employment, Probebeschäftigung). You need at least 6 points (see the table in §20b AufenthG): German above A1 (A2=1, B1=2, B2=3), English C1=1; age (under 35 = 2, 35–39 = 1); work experience (5 years = 3, 2 years = 2); partial recognition of a qualification (a decision on identified gaps, Defizitbescheid) = 4; a shortage profession (Engpassberuf) = 1; previous lawful residence ≥6 months = 1; a spouse who also qualifies for the opportunity card = 1. Basic condition: a profession with ≥2 years of training or a university degree, plus a check via the anabin/ZAB databases and German A1 or English B2. Finances: ~13 092 € in a blocked account (Sperrkonto) for the year, or an official permit to do side work. Fee: 75 € for the visa plus 100 € for the residence permit at the foreigners' authority (ABH).

steps.title: What the opportunity card (Chancenkarte) is and who it's for

content.text: The opportunity card (Chancenkarte) is a new type of national visa and residence permit for job-seeking, introduced by §20a AufenthG as part of the Skilled Immigration Act (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz) and in force since 1 June 2024. The logic is simple: if you haven't yet found an employer to sponsor you under §18a/§18b/§19c, but you generally fit the German market, the state gives you a year to come and look for work on the ground.

Unlike the old §20 'job-seeker visa' (Visum zur Arbeitsplatzsuche), the opportunity card (Chancenkarte) lets you, during this year, work part-time up to 20 hours a week in any occupation — as a cashier, a courier, in a Späti — and take trial contracts (trial employment, Probebeschäftigung) of up to two weeks with any employer. This covers rent and food while you look for a full offer (Job-Angebot).

items: For whom: skilled workers from outside the EU (including citizens of Russia, Belarus and Ukraine)
Basic threshold: a profession with ≥2 years of training or a recognized university degree
At least 6 points on the §20a Abs. 2 scale
Financial guarantees: a blocked account (Sperrkonto) or a permit to do side work
At least German A1 or English B2
Validity: 12 months, non-renewable (you'll need to switch to §18a/§18b/§19c)
Once hired for qualified work — transition to a §18 residence permit without leaving the country

content.text: The points scale is set out in §20a Abs. 2 AufenthG. Points add up across several categories. The minimum for the opportunity card (Chancenkarte) is 6 points, plus meeting the basic conditions (qualification + language + finances).

items: Partial recognition of a qualification (a decision on identified gaps, Defizitbescheid, on partial equivalence) — 4 points. IMPORTANT: with FULL recognition you are already a skilled worker (Fachkraft) and apply under §18a/§18b directly, without the opportunity card
German (above A1): A2 — 1, B1 — 2, B2 — 3 points (the table is in the annex, Anlage, to AufenthG; A1 gives no points)
English C1: 1 point (points for German and English add up)
Relevant work experience: 2 years in the last 5 — 2 points; 5 years in the last 7 — 3 points
Age at the time of filing: under 35 (up to and including 34) — 2 points; 35–39 — 1 point
Ties to Germany: lawful and continuous residence of ≥6 months in the last 5 years — 1 point
A spouse comes along and also qualifies for the Chancenkarte — 1 point
A university degree in a shortage profession (Engpassberuf: IT, engineers, medical staff) — 1 point

content.text: Example: a 32-year-old programmer, 6 years of IT experience, German A2, English C1, a decision on identified gaps received (Defizitbescheid; partial recognition). Let's count: age (2) + 5+ years of experience (3) + German A2 (1) + English C1 (1) + partial recognition (4) = 11 points — with room to spare. A reminder: with FULL recognition of the degree you are already a skilled worker (Fachkraft) and apply under §18a/§18b directly, so the opportunity card is not needed.

Without a degree check via the anabin database, the opportunity card (Chancenkarte) won't be granted. The check is free: https://anabin.kmk.org → Hochschulabschlüsse. If your university is marked H+, the degree is recognized automatically. If it's H- or ?/unknown, you'll need an official degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) through the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB): 200 €, 3 months.

For the year of residence you need to prove that your subsistence is secured (Lebensunterhaltssicherung) — that you have funds to live without social benefits. The amount is tied to the BAföG requirement (BAföG-Bedarf, §13 BAföG) and for 2026 is ~1091 €/month × 12 = 13 092 € (expect a small indexation for 2026). Ways to prove it: a blocked account (Sperrkonto), an official permit to do side work, or a declaration of commitment (Verpflichtungserklärung) from a sponsor in Germany.

items: Blocked account (Sperrkonto): Fintiba (5 €/month), Expatrio (5-9 €/month), Coracle, Deutsche Bank (limited access)
You deposit the full amount, and a limit of ~1091 € is released to you each month
Opening — online with a Russian passport, video verification + a SWIFT money transfer
Declaration of commitment (Verpflichtungserklärung) — a sponsor in Germany signs an undertaking at the foreigners' authority (ABH) to support you (an income of 2500+ €/month is required)
An employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag) for side work at a salary of ≥1091 €/month is also accepted
A scholarship from a recognized foundation (DAAD, Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung) also works

content.text: Since 2022, SWIFT transfers from Russia to Germany for private individuals are only possible through Raiffeisenbank, Uralsib, OTP or Gazprombank (not from sanctioned banks). It's better to transfer via a third country: open an account in Armenia, Kazakhstan or Georgia and send the money from there to the blocked account (Sperrkonto). Check Fintiba's country FAQ — the list changes.

You apply via videx.diplo.de and an appointment at a German embassy or consulate. For Russians and Belarusians, direct appointments in Moscow/Bonn have been difficult since 2022 but are possible; the alternative is third countries — Ankara, Yerevan, Tbilisi, Almaty. Processing time: 2-6 months.

items: Step 1: check your degree on anabin.kmk.org (H+, or an official degree assessment, Zeugnisbewertung, from the Central Office for Foreign Education, ZAB)
Step 2: obtain a language certificate (Goethe A2/B1, telc, TestDaF, IELTS B2)
Step 3: complete the online form on videx.diplo.de — select 'Chancenkarte zur Arbeitsplatzsuche' (opportunity card for job-seeking)
Step 4: open a blocked account (Sperrkonto) and fund it with 13 092 €
Step 5: book an appointment at the embassy (Terminvergabe) and pay the 75 € fee
Step 6: document package + biometrics + interview
Step 7: wait 8-16 weeks for the visa
Step 8: entry + residence registration (Anmeldung) within 14 days
Step 9: appointment at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) to be issued the plastic opportunity card (Chancenkarte)

content.text: Document package: passport + copy, 2 biometric photos, the completed VIDEX form, degree + translation + anabin/ZAB, language certificate, CV (Lebenslauf), motivation letter, documents for the points (employment records, contracts), confirmation of the blocked account (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung), travel health insurance (e.g. MAWISTA from 30 €/month), and an apostille (Apostille) on the degree (for Russia — 2500 RUB via the Ministry of Education and Science).

The visa in your passport is valid for entry for 3-6 months. After arrival you have 14 days to do the residence registration (Anmeldung) at the local citizens' office (Bürgeramt), then 2-3 months to obtain the plastic opportunity card (Chancenkarte) at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde).

items: Residence registration (Anmeldung) — registering at your rental address (the landlord's confirmation of move-in, Wohnungsgeberbestätigung)
Opening a German account (N26, DKB, Commerzbank) and releasing the limit from the blocked account (Sperrkonto)
The tax identification number (Steuer-ID) arrives by post in 2-3 weeks
An appointment (Termin) at the foreigners' authority (ABH) — sometimes a 1-3 month wait, so book it right away
Job-seeking: LinkedIn, StepStone, Indeed, the Make-it-in-Germany Jobbörse, the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit)

With an offer of ≥50 700 € (Blue Card 2026, standard profession, Regelberuf; shortage profession, Engpass, 45 934,20 €) or a recognized qualification — transition to §18b/§19c without leaving the country
A job application (Bewerbung) by German rules: a CV in Europass format, a photo, a cover letter (Anschreiben), and educational documents (Zeugnisse)

content.text: The opportunity card (Chancenkarte) is non-renewable. If you haven't found work within 12 months, you have to leave or apply for a new visa. You can, however, switch to §16d (qualification courses for recognition) or §17 (vocational training), if there are grounds.

title: Change of the purpose of residence (Zweckwechsel)
tldr: A change of the purpose of residence (Zweckwechsel) is a change of the residence purpose (Aufenthaltszweck) without leaving the country — for example, from studies §16b to work §18a/§18b or a Blue Card (Blaue Karte), or from family reunification to independent work. Legally this is the issue of a new residence permit under a different §, and approval rests with the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH). Some changes are directly restricted by law: on the §20 job-seeker visa, for instance, you cannot stay without switching to a work permit, and some humanitarian statuses do not allow a free switch to work. For §16b students, switching to work after graduation is permitted by law. The fee for the new permit is 100 €. The main thing is to apply before your current title expires.

steps.title: What a change of the purpose of residence (Zweckwechsel) is and when it's allowed

content.text: Every German residence title (Aufenthaltstitel) is issued for a specific purpose: studies, work, family, job-seeking, and so on. If your life situation changes — you finish your studies and find a job, or move from a dependent spouse's status to your own work — you need a change of the purpose of residence (Zweckwechsel): the foreigners' authority (ABH) issues a new residence permit under a different section of AufenthG. This is not an automatic extension but a new decision that the authority can approve or reject.

items: Student §16b → work §18a/§18b or an EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) under §18g after graduation — permitted by law
Job-seeker visa §20 → a work permit once you have an offer — the typical scenario
A spouse's permit → your own work permit once you have a job
§16d (degree recognition) → §18a after successful adaptation (Anpassung)
You must apply before your current permit expires

content.text: Not every change of purpose is allowed. Some humanitarian and temporary statuses (e.g. §16f school education or certain §25 cases) restrict a free switch to work purposes. Also, on a national D visa issued strictly for one purpose, you cannot switch 'on the spot' to another without prior coordination. Always check with your foreigners' authority (ABH) whether the specific change (Wechsel) is permissible.

The change-of-purpose procedure (Zweckwechsel) is the same as applying for a new residence permit under the target section. You book an appointment (Termin) at the foreigners' authority (ABH), bring the grounds for the new purpose (employment contract, degree, proof of work), and pay the fee. While the decision is pending and the old title has expired, the ABH issues a temporary confirmation of lawful status (Fiktionsbescheinigung).

items.title: 1. Gather documents for the new purpose

items: Passport + current residence permit
For work: an employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag), a job description, a degree + recognition
Completed application for the issue of a residence title (Antrag auf Erteilung eines Aufenthaltstitels)
Proof of health insurance and secured housing
Biometric photo 35×45 mm

items.title: 2. File with the foreigners' authority (ABH) before the title expires

items: Book an appointment (Termin) in advance (online portal or email)
If no appointment is available before expiry, file the application in writing on time
If the review is not complete, you receive a temporary confirmation of lawful status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) under §81
Sometimes the Federal Employment Agency's consent (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) is required for the work purpose

content.text: The main risk of a change of purpose (Zweckwechsel) is applying too late or with an incomplete package and ending up without legal status. The 2023 reform (the Skilled Immigration Act, Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz) expanded the options for skilled workers to switch to work permits, but the basic rule remains: the new ground must exist at the time of filing.

If you are moving from studies §16b to work, don't wait until your student permit is about to expire. As soon as you get the offer, apply for the change of purpose (Zweckwechsel) or, if you don't yet have your degree in hand, for §20 (job-seeking). An interruption of lawful residence resets the months accumulated toward future permanent residence and can complicate the extension.

title: Dublin III: which country is responsible for your application
tldr: The Dublin III Regulation (Regulation 604/2013) determines which EU country is obliged to examine an asylum application. The basic rule: the first EU country you officially entered or where you filed your application is responsible. Fingerprints are uploaded to the Eurodac database, which shows where you first registered. If you filed your application in Germany but Eurodac shows entry through another EU country, Germany can request a transfer (Überstellung/Dublin-Transfer) back to the responsible country. The transfer deadline is usually 6 months. There are exceptions: family reunification, unaccompanied minors and humanitarian grounds. The application under the Dublin procedure is free.

steps.title: What Dublin III is and how it works

content.text: Dublin III is EU Regulation No 604/2013, which does not grant asylum in itself but merely distributes responsibility among EU countries (plus Norway, Iceland, Switzerland and Liechtenstein). The main principle: a protection application is examined by only one country, and the applicant cannot be shuttled around the whole EU. The aim is to avoid both 'asylum shopping' and the situation where no one takes responsibility.

items: Legal basis — Regulation (EU) No 604/2013 (Dublin III)
As a rule, the responsible country is the first EU country of entry or registration
Fingerprints are entered into Eurodac on the first application
The application is examined by only one EU member state
Applies in the EU plus Norway, Iceland, Switzerland and Liechtenstein

content.text: Dublin III determines only the responsible country, not the outcome of the asylum case. A transfer to another EU country (Dublin-Transfer) does not mean deportation to your home country — you are transferred to the EU country obliged to examine the application. These are different procedures, with different rights and appeal deadlines.

steps.title: Criteria for determining the responsible country

content.text: Dublin III sets a strict hierarchy of criteria. First, family ties and the interests of minors are checked, and only then the country of first entry. In practice, for most adult applicants the decisive factor is Eurodac: the database that stores the fingerprints of everyone who has filed an application or been apprehended while crossing an EU border illegally.

items: Unaccompanied minors — the country where a family member is located
Reunification with a spouse or children who already have protection in an EU country
These criteria take precedence over the 'first country of entry' rule

items.title: 2. The first country of entry per Eurodac

items: If your fingerprints are already in Eurodac from another EU country, that country is responsible
Visas and residence permits issued by another country are taken into account
Germany requests that country's consent to take the applicant (Take Charge/Take Back)

content.text: If Germany recognizes another country as responsible, the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) issues a decision of inadmissibility (Unzulässigkeitsentscheidung) and transfer (Dublin-Transfer). You have a short window to appeal to the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht): §34a AsylG gives you 1 week to file a motion to suspend the transfer. If the transfer has not taken place within 6 months of the receiving country's consent (or the court's confirmation), responsibility passes to Germany.

items: The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) issues a transfer decision (Dublin-Transfer) when another country is responsible
The deadline is very short: a motion to suspend the transfer (Antrag nach §80 Abs. 5 VwGO) is filed within 1 week of being served with the decision (§34a AsylG)
The standard transfer deadline is 6 months
In the event of absconding (Untertauchen) the deadline is extended to 18 months
Once 6 months have passed, the case is examined by Germany

content.text: Appeal deadlines in Dublin cases are extremely tight. If you have received a decision from the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) on a transfer to another EU country, contact free legal advice immediately (asylum-procedure counseling, Asylverfahrensberatung; Caritas, Diakonie, Pro Asyl). Missing the appeal deadline makes the transfer final.

Asylum cases and Dublin cases depend heavily on individual circumstances and tight deadlines. Individual legal advice is recommended (a specialist lawyer for migration law, Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht, or free asylum-procedure counseling, Asylverfahrensberatung / a counseling center: Caritas, Diakonie, AWO, ProAsyl).

costs.note: The asylum procedure and determining the responsible country are free.

costs.label: Lawyer for appealing a Dublin decision
costs.note: Refugees with low income can receive a subsidy for legal advice (Beratungshilfe) / a subsidy for court costs (Prozesskostenhilfe).

title: Extension (Verlängerung) of a residence permit at the foreigners' authority (ABH)
tldr: An extension (Verlängerung) is the renewal of a temporary residence title (Aufenthaltstitel) at the local foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH). The main rule: apply BEFORE your current card expires, ideally 6-8 weeks ahead. If the grounds still hold (the same job, the same studies, the same marriage), the extension usually goes through without problems. The documents depend on the type of permit: an employment contract and payslips for work, university enrollment (Immatrikulation) for studies. If the foreigners' authority (ABH) doesn't manage to decide before the card expires, it issues a temporary confirmation of lawful status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) under §81(4), which keeps your status lawful. The fee for an extension is 96 € (for most titles; less for minors).

steps.title: When and where to apply for an extension

content.text: A residence permit in Germany is almost always temporary — the Blue Card, the §18 work permit, the §16b student permit, and so on are issued for 1-4 years. Before it expires, you need to extend it (verlängern) at the same foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) that issued it. Don't confuse an extension with a new permit: in an extension (Verlängerung) the purpose of residence stays the same.

items: Apply 6-8 weeks before the card expires
An appointment (Termin) at the foreigners' authority (ABH) — book it in advance, as queues run up to 2-3 months
The grounds (work/studies/marriage) must still hold
The fee for an extension — 96 € for most titles
If the decision drags on — a temporary confirmation of lawful status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) preserves your status

content.text: It is critically important to file the application BEFORE the end date of your current permit. If you applied on time, your stay is deemed lawful even after the card expires (the continued-validity fiction, Fortgeltungsfiktion, §81(4) AufenthG). But if you missed the date, your stay becomes unlawful, and the extension turns into a new procedure with a risk of refusal.

The base package is the same for everyone, but to it are added the documents confirming that the purpose of residence still holds. The foreigners' authority (ABH) checks that the conditions of the original issue are still met.

items: Passport + current residence permit card (electronic residence permit card, eAT)
Completed extension application (Antrag auf Verlängerung)
Biometric photo 35×45 mm
Proof of health insurance
Residence registration (Anmeldung)
Work: an employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag) + recent payslips (Gehaltsabrechnungen)
Studies §16b: an enrollment certificate (Immatrikulationsbescheinigung) and a transcript of grades
Marriage: a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) of joint residence, and the spouse's income
Blue Card (Blaue Karte): proof of a salary above the threshold

steps.title: Temporary confirmation of lawful status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) as a bridge

content.text: If the foreigners' authority (ABH) doesn't manage to issue the new card before the old one expires, it issues a temporary confirmation of lawful status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) under §81(4) AufenthG — a paper confirmation that your previous permit remains in force until a decision is made. This lets you stay in the country lawfully, work (if you worked under the previous title), and, if necessary, leave and re-enter.

With a temporary confirmation of lawful status (Fiktionsbescheinigung), travel outside the EU can be problematic — not all consulates and border services recognize it as a full residence permit for re-entry. Before travelling, check with the foreigners' authority (ABH) whether you can return on a Fiktionsbescheinigung plus the old card, or whether it's better to wait for the new electronic card (eAT).

costs.note: Standard fee for extending a residence title (Aufenthaltstitel) for adults.

costs.note: For children the fee is reduced; in some cases there is an exemption.

title: Temporary confirmation of status (Fiktionsbescheinigung): while your application is being decided
tldr: A temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) under §81(3) and §81(4) AufenthG is a paper document that the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) issues while it processes your application for a residence permit or its extension. The fee is 13 €. It is important to distinguish two cases: §81(3) is for people who were staying legally without a permit (for example, after visa-free entry) and are applying for the first time; §81(4) is for people whose residence permit expired after they had filed their extension application on time (continued validity of the previous permit, Fortgeltungsfiktion). The right to work depends on your previous status: under §81(4) it is usually retained, while under §81(3) it is noted separately. This is not a full residence permit, and travelling outside the EU with it is risky.

steps.title: What it is and why you need it

content.text: When you apply for a residence permit or its extension, the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) often cannot decide right away — especially in large cities with long backlogs. So that you don't end up in a legal vacuum, a temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) is issued under §81 AufenthG. It is an A5/A6 document that "fictitiously" (hence the name) preserves your status until your application is decided.

items: Fee — 13 € (§47 Abs. 1 Nr. 7 AufenthV)
§81(3) — you are applying for the first time while staying legally without a permit
§81(4) — extension: the previous residence permit continues to be valid (Fortgeltungsfiktion)
Validity is usually a few months and can be extended
The document explicitly states whether work is allowed (the Erwerbstätigkeit field)

content.text: A temporary confirmation (Fiktionsbescheinigung) is not a residence permit — it only confirms that your status is "frozen" until a decision is made. If the foreigners' authority ultimately refuses, the legality of your stay ends. Do not treat this confirmation as a guarantee of approval. In difficult cases, individual legal advice is recommended.

The most common question is whether you can work on this confirmation. The answer depends on which note is entered in the document and what your previous status was. Read the Erwerbstätigkeit (right to gainful employment) field on the document itself carefully.

items: §81(4) with a previous work-based residence permit — the right to work is usually retained
If the document says "Erwerbstätigkeit gestattet/erlaubt" — you may work
If it says "Erwerbstätigkeit nicht gestattet" — you may not work
If in doubt, request a written clarification from the foreigners' authority
Within Germany the confirmation is fully valid
Travel outside the EU is risky: returning may be difficult
Before travelling, clarify with the foreigners' authority whether you will be able to return
Carry both the temporary confirmation and your previous residence permit card

content.text: A temporary confirmation of legal status is often needed by employers, banks, and when signing contracts. Keep it together with your passport and don't let it expire: if the validity is running out and there is still no decision, request an extension from the foreigners' authority in good time.

If you filed your extension application on time but the foreigners' authority did not issue a confirmation because of backlogs, your stay is still considered legal under §81(4): continued validity of the previous permit (Fortgeltungsfiktion) takes effect by operation of law. But without the paper this is hard to prove to an employer, so insist on receiving the document or at least written confirmation that the application was filed.

costs.note: Fixed fee under §47 Abs. 1 Nr. 7 AufenthV.

costs.note: If the decision on the application drags on beyond the document's validity.

title: Freelance visa (Freiberufler-Visum) in Berlin: the specifics
tldr: The freelance visa (Freiberufler-Visum) under §21(5) AufenthG is a residence permit for the liberal professions (artists, IT consultants, journalists, translators, teachers, etc.). Berlin is the most popular city for this visa, and the local immigration authority (Landesamt für Einwanderung, LEA) sets its own requirements. You need to prove that your activity is genuinely a liberal profession (Freiberuf) rather than a commercial trade (Gewerbe), that you have clients or commissions in Germany (letters of intent, Absichtserklärungen), financial means, private or voluntary statutory health insurance, and tax registration with the tax office (Finanzamt) including a tax number (Steuernummer). The residence permit is usually issued for up to 3 years (in practice often 1–3 years). The issuance fee is 100 €. Berlin's immigration authority is known for long waits — book your appointment well in advance.

steps.title: Liberal profession or commercial trade — this matters

content.text: §21 AufenthG divides self-employment into two types: §21(1) — commercial activity (Gewerbe, business) and §21(5) — liberal profession (Freiberuf). For §21(5) your activity must fall within the so-called catalogue professions (Katalogberufe) from §18 EStG: artists, writers, journalists, teachers, translators, IT consultants, engineers, doctors, lawyers, and similar "intellectual" professions.

items: §21(5) — liberal profession (Freiberuf): no trade licence (Gewerbeschein) needed
§21(1) — commercial activity (Gewerbe): trade, crafts, business — a different set of requirements
Members of the liberal professions register directly with the tax office (Finanzamt), not with the trade office (Gewerbeamt)
Berlin actively issues §21(5) to freelancers in creative and IT fields
The Skilled Immigration Act reform (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz, 2023–2024) simplified a number of routes

content.text: Misclassification is a common reason for refusal. If the immigration authority deems your activity commercial (for example, reselling goods, e-commerce), you won't get a §21(5) visa — you'd need §21(1) with a business plan and proof of economic interest. The line between a liberal profession and a commercial trade is often disputed, so determine your type of activity under §18 EStG in advance; in ambiguous cases, individual legal advice is recommended.

Berlin's immigration authority (Landesamt für Einwanderung, LEA) requires a detailed package proving that you'll be able to live off freelancing. The key elements are letters of intent (Absichtserklärungen) from prospective German clients and a financing plan.

items: As a rule, at least two letters of intent (Absichtserklärungen) from German clients
A portfolio of work and a CV confirming your qualifications
A financing plan (Finanzierungsplan) with a revenue forecast
For regulated professions — a licence or recognition (for example, a licence to practise medicine, Approbation)

items.title: 2. Finances, insurance, and the tax office

items: Proof of financial means (savings or income)
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) — private or voluntary statutory
Tax number (Steuernummer) / tax registration (steuerliche Erfassung) with the tax office
Residence registration (Anmeldung) at a Berlin address + a rental contract

content.text: Citizens of a number of countries (USA, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Israel, and others) can enter Germany without a visa and apply for §21(5) once in Berlin. Citizens of most third countries (including Russia, Belarus, Ukraine) first obtain a national D visa at a German mission, then obtain the residence permit at the immigration authority. Berlin's immigration authority is known for long waits to get an appointment (Termin).

Getting an appointment at Berlin's immigration authority can take weeks or months. If your visa-free 90-day period or your D visa expires before the appointment, file your application in writing in good time and request a temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) so that you don't lose your legal status. Don't count on a slot opening up at the last minute.

costs.note: Fee at Berlin's immigration authority for issuing the residence permit card (§45 AufenthV).

costs.label: National D visa (for visa-required countries)
costs.note: Paid at the embassy/consulate before entry.

costs.label: Private health insurance for a freelancer
costs.note: Per month; depends on age, plan, and coverage.

costs.note: Help with registering at the tax office (Finanzamt) and obtaining a tax number (Steuernummer) (optional).
