title: Permanent residence for children: §35 AufenthG
tldr: Children of foreigners who have grown up in Germany have a simplified path to a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §35 AufenthG. Two options: at 16 (§35 Abs.1 Satz 1) — 5 years on a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis); for adults 18+ (§35 Abs.1 Satz 2) — 5 years on a temporary residence permit (AE) + sufficient German + self-support or continued study. It's a lifelong status for the integrated children of migrants. For minors it's free (§52 AufenthV).

steps.title: What it is and who it's for

content.text: §35 AufenthG is a special provision for the children of migrants who have grown up in Germany. If a child came to Germany young (or was born here to foreign parents without German citizenship) and has lived for at least 5 years on a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) under §32 (family reunification with a child, Familiennachzug zum Kind), they get a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) either at 16 (§35 Abs.1 Satz 1, in simplified form) or as an adult 18+ (§35 Abs.1 Satz 2, with conditions). It's recognition of integration through school and socialisation in German society.

items: Applies to minors holding a permit under §32 AufenthG (family reunification, Familiennachzug)
And to children born in Germany to foreign parents
Two options: §35 Abs.1 Satz 1 (from age 16) and §35 Abs.1 Satz 2 (adults 18+)
For children under 18 it's free (§52 AufenthV)
The status is personal — it remains even if the parents move away

content.text: The simplest path is issuance of the permanent residence permit (NE) on reaching 16, provided the conditions are met.

items: Age: 16 reached
5 years on a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) under §32 AufenthG (family reunification with a child, Familiennachzug zum Kind)
Time spent in Germany before 16 on another residence permit (for example, as part of a refugee family) may also count
Sufficient knowledge of German (usually confirmed by the school)
Securing means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) is not required at this age — the child is not obliged to work

content.text: The application is submitted through the parents. Sometimes the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) sends a reminder a month before the 16th birthday, but you shouldn't count on it. Once issued, you get an electronic residence permit card (eAT) with the entry "Niederlassungserlaubnis — §35 AufenthG".

steps.title: Option 2: NE for adults 18+ (§35 Abs.1 Satz 2)

content.text: If for some reason the child did not obtain the permanent residence permit (NE) at 16 (for example, because they had not yet completed 5 years on a temporary permit, AE), a second path opens up after they reach adulthood (18+). §35 Abs.1 Satz 2 does not explicitly set a strict upper age limit.

You can apply after turning 18. §35 Abs.1 Satz 2 does not explicitly set an upper limit (21), but you shouldn't delay: if you apply late, the foreigners' authority (ABH) may insist on the general conditions of §9 — that's a matter of its discretion.
At least 5 years on any temporary residence permit (AE; including §32, §25, sometimes §28). The permission to stay during an asylum procedure (Aufenthaltsgestattung) does not count.
5 years of schooling in Germany, or a completed school-leaving certificate (Schulabschluss), or current vocational training (Ausbildung). This demonstrates integration.

Either self-support through work or remuneration from vocational training (Ausbildung), or continued study (school, university, vocational education). For students, note: the foreigners' authority (ABH) may require a declaration of support from the parents (Verpflichtungserklärung).
Sufficient knowledge of German — usually B1–B2 level. A certificate isn't always mandatory — school grades or a school-leaving certificate (Schulabschluss) are accepted.
No convictions beyond the set limits (§9 Abs.2 Satz 1 Nr.4). Offences committed as a minor are often assessed more leniently under the juvenile justice law (Jugendgerichtsgesetz).
Under 18 — the parents as legal representatives (gesetzliche Vertreter). From 18 — the child themselves. The application is submitted to the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH).

items: Antrag auf Niederlassungserlaubnis (§35)
The child's passport and current residence permit
Birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde)
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
School enrolment certificate (Schulbescheinigung) or report cards (Zeugnisse)
B1 certificate (if you have one; not mandatory at 16)
Vocational training contract (Ausbildungsvertrag; for adults)
Parents' passports and residence permits
The child's health insurance (Krankenversicherung)

content.text: 2–3 months before the 16th birthday (option 1) or from age 18 (option 2). If the 5-year period ends after the 16th birthday, apply as soon as it's complete.
Processing takes 4–10 weeks. The fee is 0€ for minors, 113€ for 18+. You get an electronic residence permit card (eAT) with the entry "Niederlassungserlaubnis — §35 AufenthG".

steps.title: The benefits of §35 for the child

items: Permanent status — independent of the parents
If the parents are deported, a child with an NE stays in Germany
The right to work without restrictions from age 18
A basis for future naturalisation (Einbürgerung; for those who grew up in Germany, the conditions are simplified under §10 StAG)
Retained for absences of up to 6 months without losing the status

content.text: Strategy: §35 → then naturalisation under §10 StAG. For children who grew up in Germany, the citizenship conditions are simplified: 5 years of residence + B1 + the citizenship test. From age 16 a child can apply with parental consent, and from 18 on their own.

§35 is not an automatic process. The foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) often doesn't send a reminder. The parents have to submit the application themselves at the right time (1–2 months before the 16th birthday).
If the parents lose their residence permit (for example, a refused renewal) before the child has obtained §35, problems can arise. Apply for §35 in good time to protect the child's status.
Time on a national visa (category D on entry) does not count. The 5-year clock starts from the first temporary residence permit card (Aufenthaltserlaubnis).
If the child has left Germany to go abroad before obtaining §35, the status won't be preserved. The family must stay in Germany until the application is filed.

Compulsory schooling (Schulpflicht): if the child skips school or fails to move up from grade to grade, the foreigners' authority (ABH) can refuse §35 on grounds of insufficient integration (§35 Abs.3 Satz 1 Nr.1).

title: State fee for permanent residence: €113 + charges
tldr: A permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis, §9 AufenthG) is a permit for permanent residence in Germany. The standard state fee for issuing it is 113€ (for most categories). For certain cases the rates differ: for highly qualified specialists under §18c Abs.3 it's 147€, and for the self-employed under §21 it's 124€. On top of the fee itself, budget for the related costs: a language certificate, the Leben in Deutschland test, a pension-contributions statement, photos and translations. This guide breaks down what makes up the final total.

content.text: The permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) is governed by §9 AufenthG, and the amount of the fee by §44 AufenthV (the residence ordinance, Aufenthaltsverordnung). The standard issuing charge for most applicants is 113€. This is the charge for processing the permit at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde); it does not depend on which route you took to permanent residence or how long it took.

items: Legal basis for permanent residence — §9 AufenthG (permanent residence permit, Niederlassungserlaubnis)
Standard issuing fee — 113€
The amount of the charge is set by §44 AufenthV
Paid at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) when the card is issued
Separate from the fees for your previous (temporary) residence permit

content.text: For certain categories, §44 AufenthV provides for different rates. For highly qualified specialists under §18c Abs.3 AufenthG (Hochqualifizierte — for example, scientists, senior executives) the charge is 147€; for a permanent residence permit (NE) for the self-employed under §21 AufenthG it's 124€. Some statuses qualify for reductions or fee exemptions. The authority will tell you the exact rate for your category — check before you apply.

items: Standard — 113€ ("in all other cases", §44 AufenthV)
Highly qualified specialists (§18c Abs.3) — 147€
Self-employed (§21) — 124€
EU long-term residence (Daueraufenthalt-EU, §9a) — 109€
For minor children under §35 — free (§52 AufenthV)
The final rate is confirmed by the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde)

content.text: Don't confuse the permanent-residence fee with the cost of renewing an ordinary residence permit or of obtaining an EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte). These are different items in the §44 AufenthV schedule, and the amounts differ.

Besides the 113€, preparing for permanent residence usually requires additional outlay: a language certificate (typically B1 level), the Leben in Deutschland test, a pension-contributions statement, biometric photos, and sometimes document translations. These costs aren't part of the state fee, but without them you can't file the application.

items: A German certificate (usually B1) — the exam is paid
The "Leben in Deutschland" test (~25€)
An integration course — if needed
Certificates are attached to the application
A statement from the pension fund (pension insurance, Rentenversicherung) about contributions
Biometric photos for the document
Proof of income and housing
Document translations if needed

costs.note: Base rate for the permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §9 AufenthG / §44 AufenthV.

costs.note: For highly qualified specialists (Hochqualifizierte) under §44 AufenthV; confirm with the authority.

costs.note: For a permanent residence permit (NE) under §21 AufenthG; §44 AufenthV.

costs.note: Charge for the test on knowledge of life in Germany.

costs.note: Depends on the exam provider; biometric photos are separate.

title: B1 for permanent residence: what level you need
tldr: For a standard permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §9 AufenthG you need sufficient knowledge of German (ausreichende Kenntnisse der deutschen Sprache) — in practice this is B1 on the CEFR scale (§9 Abs. 2 Nr. 7). It is proven with a telc Deutsch B1 certificate, a Goethe-Zertifikat B1, an ÖSD B1, a DTZ result at B1 level, or a certificate (Bescheinigung) of successful completion of an integration course (Integrationskurs). For certain categories (a permanent residence permit, NE, under §18c for skilled workers, §21 for the self-employed) B1 is formally enough too, but the specific legal basis is worth checking against your foreigners' authority's (Ausländerbehörde) leaflet. Under §9 Abs. 2 Satz 3-6 the requirement can be lowered or waived for the elderly, the ill and people with disabilities (a hardship case, Härtefall). Without a proven B1 the application for a permanent residence permit (NE) usually won't be accepted — it's one of the most common blockers.

content.text: §9 Abs. 2 Nr. 7 AufenthG requires sufficient knowledge of German (ausreichende Kenntnisse der deutschen Sprache). Under §2 Abs. 11 AufenthG, "sufficient" (ausreichend) means B1 level on the Common European Framework (GER/CEFR). So for a standard permanent residence permit you need exactly B1, not A2: A2 is simple knowledge (einfache Kenntnisse), which is not enough for a permanent residence permit (NE).

For special grounds for a permanent residence permit (NE) — for example §18c AufenthG (skilled workers) or §21 Abs. 4 (the self-employed) — the law also relies on B1, but the specific basis is worth checking against your foreigners' authority's (Ausländerbehörde) leaflet. For the EU Blue Card (Blue Card) under §18c Abs. 2 the logic is reversed: a permanent residence permit after 21 months requires B1, while after 27 months simple knowledge (einfache Kenntnisse, A1) is enough — the shorter timeframe is the reward for a higher language level.

items: Standard permanent residence permit (NE) under §9 → you need B1 (written and spoken)
A2 doesn't count for §9 — only for certain reduced-requirement paths
The level has to be proven with a document, not "by word of mouth"
The certificate is permanent: language exams don't have an expiry date
Under §9 Abs. 2 Nr. 8 you additionally need basic knowledge of the legal and social order (Grundkenntnisse der Rechts- und Gesellschaftsordnung; see the separate guide on Leben in Deutschland)

content.text: The foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) accepts several types of proof. The most universal is a B1-level language exam certificate from an accredited provider.

items: telc Deutsch B1 — the most common and inexpensive option
Goethe-Zertifikat B1
ÖSD Zertifikat B1
Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer (DTZ) with a B1 result
A certificate (Bescheinigung) of successful completion of an integration course (Integrationskurs; includes the DTZ)
A German school-leaving certificate or a German university degree — usually accepted as proof of language
A B2 or C1 certificate also works: it covers B1

content.text: A B1 certificate in a single skill (for example, only listening, Hören, or reading, Lesen) is not the same as a full B1. For a permanent residence permit (NE) you need an overall B1 result across all four skills. Check that the certificate shows an overall level of B1, not "teilweise B1" (partial).

§9 Abs. 2 Satz 3-6 AufenthG provide for relaxations. This isn't a loophole but a genuine legal basis for people who objectively find it hard to pass B1. The decision remains at the authority's discretion (Ermessen).

If a person cannot meet the language requirement because of a physical, mental or psychological illness or disability (körperliche, geistige oder seelische Krankheit oder Behinderung), it can be lowered or waived. You need a medical certificate (ärztliches Attest) confirming this inability.

items.title: 2. If there was no entitlement to or chance of an Integrationskurs

content.text: For certain groups the law allows that simple spoken knowledge (einfache mündliche Kenntnisse, around A1) is enough, if the person had no opportunity to take part in an integration course (Integrationskurs). This is a rare and individual case, decided by the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) at its discretion.

For minors and a number of special grounds (for example, a permanent residence permit (NE) for family members of German citizens or for refugees under §26 Abs. 3), the language requirements are governed separately and can be more lenient than the standard §9.

A reduction of the requirement on hardship grounds (Härtefall) doesn't happen automatically. You have to submit a justification and proof (a medical report, documents showing you had no access to a course). The foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) won't accept a bare "learning the language is hard for me".
The most reliable path is to pass telc or Goethe B1 in advance, before you even book your permanent residence permit (NE) appointment, so that the certificate is already in your document package.

items: Register for telc Deutsch B1 or Goethe B1 (registration is often 4-8 weeks ahead)
If you attended an integration course (Integrationskurs) — keep the course certificate (Zertifikat Integrationskurs) and the DTZ result
Order a duplicate certificate in advance if the original is lost
Check whether your foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) recognises the specific provider (telc, Goethe and ÖSD are recognised everywhere)
If you're also planning naturalisation (Einbürgerung) — note that citizenship under §10 StAG also requires B1; the accelerated 3-year path with C1 was abolished on 30.10.2025

content.text: Don't confuse B1 for a permanent residence permit (NE) with the language requirements for family reunification (often A1) and for naturalisation (Einbürgerung; B1 under §10 StAG). Each process has its own threshold, and an A1 certificate is no good for a permanent residence permit. The former accelerated 3-year path to citizenship with C1 level was abolished on 30.10.2025.

costs.label: telc Deutsch B1 exam
costs.note: The price depends on the examination centre (Prüfungszentrum) and city; within an integration course (Integrationskurs) the DTZ is often free.

costs.label: Goethe-Zertifikat B1
costs.note: More expensive than telc; can be taken in separate modules.

costs.label: Duplicate certificate
costs.note: If the original is lost; requested from the exam provider.

costs.label: State fee for the NE
costs.note: Standard fee for the permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §9 AufenthG (§44 AufenthV).

title: Citizenship by descent: §5 StAG
tldr: Acquisition of citizenship by declaration (Erklärungserwerb) for descendants of Germans. IMPORTANT: for descendants of victims of Nazi-era denaturalization (redress of historical injustice, Wiedergutmachung) §15 StAG applies; §5 StAG is for children of Germans excluded by earlier versions of the law on grounds of sex/family status (children of German mothers before 1.1.1975 and children born out of wedlock to German fathers before 1.7.1993), made permanent by the 2021 reform. B1, the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) and income are not required; the fee is nominal. Check that the rules are current at gesetze-im-internet.de/stag.

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: Acquisition of citizenship by declaration (Erklärungserwerb) means obtaining citizenship through a declaration (Erklärung) rather than classic naturalization (§10 StAG). Pay attention to the paragraph numbering: §15 StAG covers the redress of historical injustice (Wiedergutmachung) for persons who were deprived of, or lost, German citizenship as a result of Nazi persecution between 1933 and 1945 (on political, racial or religious grounds, Art.116 Abs.2 GG) AND THEIR DESCENDANTS. §5 StAG is a separate provision for children of Germans excluded by earlier versions of the law on grounds of sex or family status; the right to declare under §5 was made permanent by the law of 20 August 2021 (4. StAÄndG).

items: You can apply from abroad, with no requirement to live in Germany (under both §5 and §15 StAG)
You do not have to give up your current citizenship — multiple citizenship (Mehrstaatigkeit) is allowed
No B1, no naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest), no income proof — this is not §10 StAG
Applications from abroad can be filed with the Federal Office of Administration (Bundesverwaltungsamt, BVA) directly or through a German consulate

content.text: §5 StAG covers several groups. The key is to prove a line of descent from a German (Deutscher) or from a victim of denaturalization under §§ 6 ff. der 11. Verordnung zum Reichsbürgergesetz vom 25. November 1941.

items.title: 1. Descendants of victims of Nazi-era denaturalization

content.text: If an ancestor was deprived of or lost German citizenship between 30.01.1933 and 08.05.1945 on political, racial or religious grounds, the applicant and their descendants are entitled to naturalization under §15 StAG (redress of historical injustice, Wiedergutmachung). This is NOT §5 StAG.

Before the 1974 reform, a child acquired citizenship only through the father, and only within marriage. Children born in wedlock to a German mother and a foreign father before 1.1.1975 can now declare for citizenship.

items.title: 3. Children born out of wedlock to German fathers before 1.7.1993

content.text: Before 1993, a child born out of wedlock to a German father did not acquire citizenship automatically. Now they can — under §5 StAG.

items.title: 4. Descendants of the persons listed above

content.text: Children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren of the persons in groups 1-3 — provided the line of descent was not broken.
The evidence base is the main challenge. You need to gather archival documents covering the entire line of descent.

items: Birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) of the applicant + of all ancestors in the line up to the German (Deutscher)
Marriage certificates of ancestors (Heiratsurkunde)
Old German documents of the ancestor: passport (Reisepass), certificate of community membership (Heimatschein), naturalization certificate (Einbürgerungsurkunde)
For Nazi victims: proof of denaturalization (Federal Archive, Bundesarchiv; Reichsanzeiger list)
Applicant's passport (Reisepass)
Certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) of all non-European documents, with apostille (Apostille)

content.text: Holocaust-related documents are often traced through the Federal Archive in Berlin (Bundesarchiv Berlin) or the Arolsen Archives (formerly ITS) — free of charge, but the process takes 6-18 months.

The application is filed with the Federal Office of Administration (Bundesverwaltungsamt, BVA) in Cologne — directly or through the nearest German consulate (embassy/consulate, Botschaft/Konsulat). The application form under §5 StAG (Antrag nach §5 StAG) is available at bva.bund.de.

The application is filed with the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) for your place of residence (district office Landratsamt, district administration Kreisverwaltung or municipal citizens' office städtisches Bürgeramt — depending on the federal state, Land).
Processing times at the Federal Office of Administration (BVA) are currently (2026) 18-36 months due to the surge in applications after the 2021 reform.

Do not confuse the provisions: §15 StAG is the redress of historical injustice (Wiedergutmachung) for victims of Nazi persecution and their descendants; §5 StAG removes earlier discrimination on grounds of sex/family status; §14 StAG is discretionary naturalization abroad (Einbürgerung im Ausland) at the authority's discretion (Ermessen). Choose the basis that fits your situation.

The right to acquire citizenship by declaration (Erklärungserwerb) under §5 StAG extends to descendants of the affected persons, but the scope and conditions depend on your specific line of descent and year of birth; check the exact coverage in your case with the Federal Office of Administration (BVA). Individual legal advice is recommended.

If the entitlement was broken (for example, an ancestor previously gave up German citizenship voluntarily), the §5 basis may not apply. The Federal Office of Administration (BVA) assesses each line individually — check that this is current.

costs.note: Free in most cases (Gebührenbefreiung) for Wiedergutmachung cases

costs.label: Einbürgerungsbehörde fee (if from Germany)
costs.note: Depends on the category and the federal state

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung of documents
costs.note: Per page, by a vereidigter Übersetzer

costs.label: Apostille on foreign documents
costs.note: In the country that issued the document

title: Marriage to a German citizen: §9 StAG (3 years in the country + 2 years of marriage)
tldr: The spouse of a German citizen can naturalize under §9 StAG after 3 years of legal residence in Germany and at least 2 years of marriage (after the reform of 27.06.2024 it is 3+2 instead of the previous 4+3, under §9 Abs.1 Nr.3). You need B1, the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) and self-sufficiency. Dual citizenship has been allowed for everyone since 2024.

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: §9 StAG (naturalization of spouses of Germans, Einbürgerung von Ehegatten Deutscher) is a fast track to citizenship for spouses of Germans. After the citizenship modernization reform (Staatsangehörigkeitsmodernisierungsgesetz), which took effect on 27 June 2024, the requirements are: 3 years of legal residence in Germany and at least 2 years of a valid marriage. The provision is used by thousands of foreign spouses every year — it is the second most popular route after §10 StAG.

items: Period of residence in Germany: 3 years (§9 Abs.1 StAG)
Length of marriage: at least 2 years, and the marriage must still exist at the time of naturalization
The spouse must be a German citizen at the time of the decision
Dual citizenship is now allowed for everyone (multiple citizenship, Mehrstaatigkeit)

content.text: All requirements are set out in §9 i.V.m. §10 StAG — this means that some of the §10 conditions (language, test, loyalty) apply to §9 as well.

items: The residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) must be "zur dauerhaften Ausübung gewählt" — §28 AufenthG (reunification with a German spouse) or a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis)
Money: self-sufficiency without basic income support (Bürgergeld, formerly Hartz IV)/SGB II/SGB XII (exceptions: §10 Abs.6 — incapacity, education)
Language: B1 (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, Gemeinsamer Europäischer Referenzrahmen) — telc, the Goethe-Institut (Goethe), ÖSD
Naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) of the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF): at least 17 of 33 correct answers
Loyalty: a commitment to the free democratic basic order (Bekenntnis zur freiheitlichen demokratischen Grundordnung) — a loyalty declaration to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung)
No convictions: §12a StAG — thresholds for penalties
Identity verification (Identitätsklärung): clear confirmation of identity and citizenship
Naturalization application (Antrag auf Einbürgerung; the form depends on the federal state)
Passport (Reisepass) + residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel)
Marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) + birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) of the spouse + naturalization/birth certificate (Einbürgerungs-/Geburts-Urkunde) of the German partner
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung; covering the last 3+ years)
Proof of income: pay slips (Lohnabrechnungen), tax assessments (Steuerbescheide) or self-employment (Selbständigkeit)
B1 certificate (B1-Zertifikat; telc/Goethe/ÖSD)
Naturalization test certificate (Einbürgerungstest-Zertifikat)
The certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis) is requested by the authority (Behörde) itself
CV (Lebenslauf)

content.text: The application is filed with the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) for your place of residence — either the district office (Landratsamt, in rural districts) or the city administration/citizens' office (Stadtverwaltung/Bürgeramt, in cities). In Berlin it is the State Office for Immigration (Landesamt für Einwanderung, LEA). Many federal states (NRW, BW, BY, HE) now accept online applications.
Processing time is 6-24 months depending on the federal state and the workload of the authority (Behörde). In Berlin the realistic time is 18-30 months (as of 2026).

After approval there is a formal ceremony, the signing of the loyalty declaration to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung) and the issuance of the naturalization certificate (Einbürgerungsurkunde). Only then are you a German (Deutsche/Deutscher).

Before the reform of 27.06.2024, §10 Abs.1 Nr.4 StAG required giving up your previous citizenship. The reform abolished this requirement for everyone: §10 Abs.1 Nr.4 weggefallen, and §12 StAG (the former exceptions) was fully repealed — multiple citizenship (Mehrstaatigkeit) is now accepted for everyone. You should still check the laws of your own country, however: some strip citizenship automatically when another is acquired (for example, Ukraine under Art.19 of the Law of Ukraine "On Citizenship", although in practice it does not enforce this).
Russia and Belarus require mandatory notification of the authorities (MVD/FSB) about the acquisition of a foreign citizenship; see the separate country guides.

The marriage must genuinely exist at the time of the authority's (Behörde) decision. If you divorce while the case is pending, it is refused. A registered civil partnership (eingetragene Lebenspartnerschaft; equivalent to marriage since 2017) does count.
A sham marriage is grounds for withdrawal of naturalization (Rücknahme der Einbürgerung) under §35 StAG (within 10 years in the case of deliberately false information).
If the German spouse acquired citizenship recently themselves (by naturalization, Einbürgerung), you need to confirm that they are German at the time you file.

title: Citizenship refusal: how to appeal
tldr: A refusal (rejection notice, Ablehnungsbescheid) under §10 or §9 StAG is challenged by an objection (Widerspruch) within 1 month (if the federal state has kept the pre-court objection procedure, Widerspruchsverfahren) or directly by a lawsuit (Klage) before the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht). The key is to analyze the reasoning (Begründung) of the decision and identify where the authority (Behörde) made an error in its legal assessment. Lawyer's fee — roughly 1000–3000€; the chances depend on the specific legal errors and evidence and vary greatly from case to case. The deadline for the lawsuit must not be missed. Individual legal advice is recommended.

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: If the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) issues a rejection notice (Ablehnungsbescheid), you have a formal route of appeal through the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht). Under §10 StAG, naturalization is a right (Anspruch, not a favor), so the courts review whether the refusal was justified. The key is to read the instructions on legal remedies (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung) at the end of the decision: they state the deadline and the competent body.

items: Deadline for the objection (Widerspruch; if applicable) — 1 month from service
Deadline for the lawsuit (Klage) — 1 month (for most cases, §74 VwGO)
The lawsuit is filed with the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) at the seat of the authority (Behörde)
You can file through a lawyer or in person (no mandatory representation, Anwaltszwang, at first instance)

content.text: Analyzing the reason for the refusal is half the battle in court. The authority (Behörde) often errs in its assessment.

§10 Abs.1 Nr.3 StAG. The authority (Behörde) may consider the income insufficient. But §10 Abs.1 Nr.3 has exceptions for people who are not at fault for their unemployment/receipt of basic income support (Bürgergeld, formerly Hartz IV).

§12a StAG — thresholds: a fine (Geldstrafe) of up to 90 daily rates (Tagessätze) — or a custodial sentence (Freiheitsstrafe) of up to 3 months suspended, the enforcement of which was deferred and which was subsequently expunged — is disregarded (außer Betracht). Above the threshold, the assessment is individual (at the authority's discretion, Ermessen). Individual legal advice is recommended.
§10 Abs.1 Nr.1 StAG. If there is a record with the Office for the Protection of the Constitution (Verfassungsschutz), the application is refused. Here a lawsuit (Klage) is almost the only route.
Refusals are common when the certificate is not on the list in §3 IntV. The fix: obtain a recognized certificate and re-apply (a new application, Antrag).

If a passport from the country of origin is unavailable (Syria, Iran, LNR/DNR), the authority (Behörde) may doubt your identity. Identity verification is a requirement of the opening sentence of §10 Abs.1 StAG; for stateless persons and refugees a "tiered model" applies (Stufenmodell; where a passport is impossible, other official documents are accepted) under the application guidance of the Federal Ministry of the Interior (Anwendungshinweise BMI). There is no separate §10a in the StAG — check that this is current.

items.title: 1. Read the Bescheid and the Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung

content.text: The end of the decision states where to appeal (administrative court, Verwaltungsgericht) and the deadline (usually "1 Monat"). If the federal state has kept the pre-court objection procedure (Widerspruchsverfahren; for example, NRW, RLP), you first file an objection (Widerspruch) with the same authority (Behörde), then the lawsuit (Klage).

An initial consultation (Erstberatung) — up to 226€ (under §34 RVG). The lawyer will assess your chances and strategy. You can often apply for legal aid for court costs (Prozesskostenhilfe; a free procedure for those on a low income).

items.title: 3. File the Klage with the Verwaltungsgericht

content.text: The lawsuit (Klage) is filed on paper or through the special electronic citizen's mailbox (besonderes elektronisches Bürgerpostfach, beBP) or the lawyer's mailbox (Anwaltspostfach). It should set out: the claimant, the defendant (the federal state/authority, Land/Behörde), the relief sought (an action to compel, Verpflichtungsklage, the issuance of the naturalization certificate, Einbürgerungsurkunde), and the facts and the law (§ StAG).

Proceedings before the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) take 12-30 months. An oral hearing (mündliche Verhandlung) is possible. The decision is a judgment (Urteil), which can be appealed to the Higher Administrative Court (Oberverwaltungsgericht) by way of appeal (Berufung).

Sometimes it is faster not to litigate but to fix the defect (obtain a B1 certificate, build up income, wait for a conviction to lapse) and file a new application (Antrag). Especially if the reason is curable. But then you pay the 255€ again.
The deadline for the lawsuit (Klage) must not be missed — after one month the decision (Bescheid) becomes final (bestandskräftig) and can no longer be challenged.

Filing the lawsuit (Klage) does not exempt you from paying the court costs (Gerichtskosten) — the court requires an advance (Vorschuss). Calculation: 3 fees (Gebühren) based on the value in dispute (Streitwert) under the GKG (for naturalization the value in dispute is usually 10.000€, with a court fee in the region of 700€). Confirm the exact amount with the court/lawyer.

If the decision (Bescheid) states "sofort vollziehbar", that makes no sense for a naturalization (Einbürgerung) refusal — immediate enforceability only applies when an already granted citizenship is being withdrawn. Do not confuse the two.

Always correspond with the authority (Behörde) in writing and with proof of delivery (a registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, Einschreiben mit Rückschein, or the electronic lawyer's mailbox, beA, through a lawyer).

costs.label: Court fee at the Verwaltungsgericht
costs.note: At a Streitwert of 10.000€ — Vorschuss ≈723€, refunded if you win

costs.label: Lawyer's fee (Fachanwalt)
costs.note: Under the RVG; a Streitwert of 10.000€ gives a base fee of 1093€ + Auslagen

costs.label: Erstberatung
costs.note: Maximum under §34 RVG for private individuals

costs.label: Prozesskostenhilfe
costs.note: If income is below the Freibeträge — the court pays (application under §114 ZPO)

title: Russian citizens: obtaining German citizenship in 2026
tldr: After the reform of 27.06.2024, Germany allows dual citizenship for everyone, including Russians. Under Art. 6 of Federal Law FZ-62, Russia does not automatically strip citizenship for acquiring a foreign one, but there is an obligation to notify the Russian MVD within 60 days (for those living in Russia, failure carries a fine/criminal liability under Art.330.2 of the Criminal Code). Renouncing Russian citizenship has been effectively impossible since 2022, but it is no longer required anyway.

content.text: UPDATE (2026): the fast-track naturalization after 3 years was abolished as of 30.10.2025 (the Sixth Act amending the StAG, Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG). For Russian citizens, as for everyone, the standard 5-year period under §10 StAG applies. Dual citizenship is allowed on the German side; separately, check your obligations under Russian law (notification). Check that this is current.

Before 27.06.2024, Russians acquiring German citizenship were generally required, under §10 Abs.1 Nr.4 StAG in its former version, to give up their Russian citizenship. This created a problem: since 2022 Russia has effectively stopped accepting applications to renounce citizenship (Presidential Decree No.1325/2002 is formally still in force, but consulates have suspended the procedures). After the StAG reform, renunciation is no longer required: §10 Abs.1 Nr.4 weggefallen, and §12 StAG (the former exceptions on multiple citizenship, Mehrstaatigkeit) was repealed — multiple citizenship is now permitted for everyone. This has substantially simplified the route to naturalization (Einbürgerung) for Russians in Germany. Individual legal advice is recommended.

items: Renouncing Russian citizenship is no longer required (§10 Abs.1 Nr.4 weggefallen, §12 StAG repealed)
Standard period — 5 years of residence (§10 StAG)
Marriage to a German citizen — 3 years of residence + 2 years of marriage (§9 StAG)
The 3-year fast track (former §10 Abs.3 StAG) was ABOLISHED as of 30.10.2025 — it is now 5 years for everyone

steps.title: What you need on the German side

content.text: The requirements are standard for everyone — Russian nationality grants neither advantages nor restrictions under the StAG (there is no sanctions-based exclusion).

items: 5 years of legal residence (the 3-year fast track was abolished as of 30.10.2025)

Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel): a permanent residence permit (NE, settlement permit), EU long-term residence (Daueraufenthalt-EU) or a suitable temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis; §28, §18g, etc.)
B1 (telc/Goethe/ÖSD) — mandatory
Naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) of the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) — 17/33
Self-sufficiency: without basic income support (Bürgergeld, formerly Hartz IV)
Loyalty declaration to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung) to the free democratic basic order
Identity verification (Identitätsklärung) — usually via a valid Russian passport

content.text: If your Russian passport has expired and the consulate will not issue a new one, identity verification (Identitätsklärung) becomes more difficult. A Russian birth certificate + old passports + a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) can serve as evidence. Identity verification is governed by the opening sentence of §10 Abs.1 StAG; where requiring a passport is unreasonable (Unzumutbarkeit), the "tiered model" (Stufenmodell) applies under the application guidance of the Federal Ministry of the Interior (Anwendungshinweise BMI; other official documents). There is no separate §10a in the StAG.

steps.title: What you need on the Russian side

content.text: Under FZ-62 "On Citizenship of the Russian Federation" (the new 2023 version, which replaced the 2002 law), acquiring a foreign citizenship does not automatically lead to the loss of the Russian one. But there is an obligation to notify — Art.6 of FZ-62.

items.title: If you live permanently in Russia

content.text: You are required to submit a notification to the territorial GUVM of the MVD within 60 days of acquiring the foreign citizenship/residence permit (previously, of the passport). Failure to do so falls under Art.330.2 of the Russian Criminal Code (a fine of 200.000₽ or 400 hours of community work); for those who simply miss the deadline, a fine of 500-1000₽ under the Code of Administrative Offenses.

items.title: If you live permanently outside Russia

content.text: There is NO obligation to notify if you reside permanently abroad (Art.6 part 5.1 of FZ-62). Proof is a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) + de-registration (Abmeldung) from Russia or the absence of registration in Russia. If you come to Russia temporarily, the obligation arises only if you take up permanent residence there.

items.title: If you want to renounce Russian citizenship

content.text: It is theoretically possible — an application to the Russian Embassy or GUVM. In practice, since 2022 processing times stretch over years, and many consulates effectively do not accept the documents. The decision is made by the President of Russia. For the purposes of naturalization (Einbürgerung), renunciation is not required after the StAG reform, so there is usually no point in it. Confirm the current procedure and timelines with the consulate; individual legal advice is recommended.
A few typical problems that Russians in Germany run into.

items: Russian passport: renewed only at the Embassy (Berlin, Bonn, Munich, Hamburg, Leipzig) or at Consulates-General; the wait for an appointment (Termin) is 2-6 months
Apostille (Apostille) on Russian documents (birth and marriage certificates): only in Russia, or through a proxy — see the website of the Russian Ministry of Justice
Certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung): only by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) in Germany; a Russian notary does not count

Identity verification (Identitätsklärung) for those who left Russia without a valid passport: under §10 Abs.1 StAG you must justify that requiring a passport is unreasonable (Unzumutbarkeit) and use other official documents (the tiered model, Stufenmodell)

content.text: Notifying the Russian MVD from Germany: this is done only in person, through the territorial GUVM office upon entry into Russia. There is NO electronic form. If you do not enter Russia, there is no obligation (permanent residence abroad).

Russian citizens from Crimea/LNR/DNR: for the authority (Behörde), such passports may raise questions on the identity-verification side (Identitätsklärung); a Ukrainian passport or a Ukrainian SSR birth certificate is useful.

Men liable for military service: acquiring German citizenship does not release them from Russian military obligations from Russia's point of view. From Germany's point of view — §6 ZDG (compulsory military service, Wehrpflicht, has been suspended in Germany since 2011).
Sanctioned persons (SDN US OFAC, EU Annex I): in theory not an obstacle for §10 StAG, but the authority (Behörde) may raise the question of loyalty (§10 Abs.1 Nr.1).
After obtaining a German passport, enter Russia on your Russian one — this is a requirement of FZ-62 and of Russian border guards. In the EU/Germany — on the German one.

title: 3 years (ABOLISHED as of 30.10.2025): special integration achievements
tldr: ABOLISHED: the 3-year naturalization route under §10 Abs.3 StAG (C1 + special integration achievements, besondere Integrationsleistungen), introduced by the reform of 27.06.2024, was repealed by the Sixth Act amending the StAG (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG; in force from 30.10.2025). §10 Abs.3 is now weggefallen. From 30.10.2025 the minimum period for naturalization as of right (Anspruchseinbürgerung) is 5 years for everyone (§10 StAG). The material below is a historical note on the rules in force from 27.06.2024 to 29.10.2025. For the current route, see the "5 years" guide.

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: NOTE (2026 update): the fast-track naturalization after 3 years (§10 Abs.3 StAG, C1 + special integration achievements, besondere Integrationsleistungen) has been ABOLISHED. The Sixth Act amending the citizenship law (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des Staatsangehörigkeitsgesetzes; passed by the Bundestag on 08.10.2025, in force from 30.10.2025) repealed this route — §10 Abs.3 is now weggefallen. The minimum period of residence for naturalization as of right (Anspruchseinbürgerung) under §10 StAG is 5 years for everyone. The section below is kept as a historical note (the route was in force from 27.06.2024 to 29.10.2025). Check that this is current at gesetze-im-internet.de/stag and bmi.bund.de.

The reform — the citizenship modernization act (Staatsangehörigkeitsmodernisierungsgesetz; BGBl. I 2024 Nr.104), which took effect on 27 June 2024 — introduced a new fast track: §10 Abs.3 StAG. This shortened the period of residence to 3 years (previously a similar §10 Abs.3 with 6 years existed, which has now been repealed). The idea: to reward those who have integrated above average. The criteria were left to the discretion of the authority (Behörde), but the Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI) issued application guidance (Anwendungshinweise).

items: Period of residence: 3 years (instead of 5)
Language: C1 (Gemeinsamer Europäischer Referenzrahmen)
Special integration achievements — must be proven
All other §10 StAG requirements (naturalization test, Einbürgerungstest; loyalty, income, no criminal record)

content.text: The law does not give an exhaustive list (an open-ended provision, offene Tatbestand), but §10 Abs.3 S.2 gives examples. According to the application guidance of the Federal Ministry of the Interior (Anwendungshinweise BMI; August 2024):

A C1 certificate (the Goethe-Institut, Goethe; telc, TestDaF). This is a standalone basis — even without other achievements it may be enough (according to the practice of the Federal Ministry of the Interior, BMI).

A school-leaving certificate (Abitur) with a good average (grade average, Notendurchschnitt, better than 2,5), a higher-education degree (Studienabschluss), vocational training (Berufsausbildung) completed with distinction. Proven by a certificate (Zeugnis).
Stable employment, income above the industry average, professional advancement. Useful: an employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag), pay slips (Lohnabrechnungen), a letter of recommendation.

Voluntary work (ehrenamtliche Tätigkeit) — for example, the fire service (Feuerwehr), the Federal Agency for Technical Relief (THW), the German Red Cross (DRK), a sports club, a church, a political party. Proven by a certificate (Bescheinigung) from the organization.
For example, sporting achievements, a cultural contribution, scientific publications. The authority (Behörde) assesses this individually.

The application is standard, at the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) for your place of residence, but the application (Antrag) must explicitly cite §10 Abs.3 StAG and include supporting documents.

items: The standard §10 StAG package (passport, residence permit Aufenthaltstitel, registration certificate Meldebescheinigung for 3+ years, income, certificate of good conduct Führungszeugnis)
C1 certificate (C1-Zertifikat; telc/Goethe/TestDaF)
Naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) of the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF; 17/33)
Documents on your achievements: diplomas, references, certificates (Bescheinigungen)
CV (Lebenslauf) emphasizing integration

content.text: A hearing (Anhörung) — an interview — is often scheduled. The case worker assesses your motivation and the reality of your integration. This is not the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest), but a personal interview.

Processing times are the same as for §10 StAG — 6-24 months depending on the federal state (Land). The real statistics after the 2024 reform: §10 Abs.3 was approved less often because of the high evidentiary bar.
Based on the early practice of the authorities (Behörden; Berlin LEA, München KVR, Hamburg Einwohner-Zentralamt), typical approved cases were:

items: An IT specialist with an EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) + C1 + 3 years in the volunteer fire service (Feuerwehr Freiwillig)
A top student + C1 + tutoring (Tutoring) at a community organization
A doctor with recognized qualifications + C1 + work at a hospital (Klinikum)
A teacher of Russian/Ukrainian + C1 + a church parish + long-term voluntary work (Ehrenamt)

content.text: Simply holding a C1 with no other achievements is formally sufficient under the wording of §10 Abs.3 S.2 StAG, but in practice some authorities (Behörde) required a combination.
If refused under §10 Abs.3, you can switch to the standard §10 Abs.1 (5 years) without filing a new application (Antrag) — the authority (Behörde) can consider both scenarios.
Voluntary work (Ehrenamt) must be documented by the organization, stating the period and the nature of the activity. "I helped friends" does not count.
"Above-average" income is a relative category; a benchmark: gross income above the median (Median; roughly 50.000€/year in Germany in 2026).
The C1 certificate (C1-Zertifikat) must be on the list of recognized ones (telc C1, Goethe C1, TestDaF 4-5, ÖSD C1, DSH-2/3).

title: 5 years — the standard naturalization period
tldr: §10 StAG in the version of 27.06.2024: the standard period of residence was reduced from 8 to 5 years. Requirements: B1, the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest), self-sufficiency, loyalty to the Basic Law (Grundgesetz), no serious criminal record. Dual citizenship is now allowed for everyone. This is the main naturalization route in Germany.

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: §10 StAG — naturalization as of right (Anspruchseinbürgerung) — is the main naturalization route in Germany. It is not a "favor" (discretion, Ermessen) of the authority (Behörde) but a legal entitlement (a right, Anspruch): if all conditions are met, citizenship MUST be granted. The reform — the citizenship modernization act (Staatsangehörigkeitsmodernisierungsgesetz), in force since 27.06.2024 — cut the basic period of residence from 8 to 5 years (§10 Abs.1 Nr.1), the biggest change to German citizenship law in 25 years.

items: Standard period: 5 years of legal and continuous residence in Germany
Dual citizenship: allowed for everyone (§10 Abs.1 Nr.4 weggefallen, §12 StAG repealed)
The language, test and income requirements remain
The 3-year route for special achievements (§10 Abs.3) was ABOLISHED as of 30.10.2025 — it is now 5 years for everyone

content.text: The full list is in §10 Abs.1 StAG. The conditions of §10 Abs.1 must all be met at the same time (numbering: opening sentence — 5 years + established identity; then Nr.1, 1a, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7; Nr.4 weggefallen).

items.title: Nr.1 + Nr.1a — Loyalty and historical responsibility

content.text: A written loyalty declaration to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung; §10 Abs.1 Nr.1) + acknowledgment of historical responsibility (Nr.1a). Antisemitism, racism, extremism are an obstacle.

items.title: Opening sentence of Abs.1 — 5 years of legal residence + established identity

content.text: The residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) must be "zur dauerhaften Ausübung gewählt". A permanent residence permit (NE, settlement permit), EU long-term residence (Daueraufenthalt-EU), the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU), §28 (family), §18g (skilled worker, Fachkraft) all qualify. §16/§17 (study) do NOT count. Interruptions of more than 6 months reset the period.

items.title: Nr.2 — Aufenthaltstitel at the time of the decision

content.text: The residence permit must be valid at the time of naturalization (Einbürgerung) — otherwise it is refused.

Income covers the means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) of the family without basic income support (Bürgergeld, formerly Hartz IV)/SGB II/SGB XII. Exceptions: §10 Abs.6 (illness/disability/age) and special groups. Note: §10 Abs.6 expressly exempts only from Nr.6/Nr.7 (language/test); relief on means of subsistence is assessed individually — check that this is current with the authority (Behörde).
telc Deutsch B1, Goethe-Zertifikat B1, ÖSD B1, DTZ B1, or a German school/university qualification (Abschluss deutscher Schule/Hochschule). Speak+Listen+Read+Write.
33 questions, 17 correct needed. Exempt: holders of a German university (deutsche Hochschule) degree in political science/law/social sciences. The cost is 25€, prepare at bpb.de.

§12a StAG: a fine (Geldstrafe) of up to 90 daily rates (Tagessätze) — or a custodial sentence (Freiheitsstrafe) of up to 3 months suspended and subsequently expunged — is disregarded. Above the threshold, an individual assessment (discretion, Ermessen). Antisemitic, racist, xenophobic or other acts contrary to human dignity, as well as terrorist offenses, are an obstacle; check your specific situation with the authority (Behörde) and a lawyer.
Clear confirmation of identity and current citizenship — a requirement of the opening sentence of §10 Abs.1 StAG (there is no separate §10a in the StAG).

A year before the 5-year mark: get B1, pass the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest), gather 3 years of pay slips (Lohnabrechnungen), and check that your certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis) is clean.

Location: the district office (Landratsamt) in rural districts, the city citizens' office (Stadt-Bürgeramt) in cities, the State Office for Immigration (LEA) in Berlin. Application: on paper or online (NRW, BW, BY, HE, HH already accept it electronically).
255€ in advance or after a positive decision — depending on the federal state (Land).
6-24 months. In Berlin — realistically 18-30 months. The authority (Behörde) may request additional documents — respond on time.

After the decision — an invitation to a formal ceremony: the loyalty declaration to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung) + the naturalization certificate (Einbürgerungsurkunde). From that moment you are a German (Deutsche/Deutscher). Then — a passport (Reisepass) at the citizens' office (Bürgeramt).
The citizenship modernization act (Staatsangehörigkeitsmodernisierungsgesetz; BGBl. I 2024 Nr.104, in force 27.06.2024) — the key changes:

items: Standard period: 8 → 5 years (§10 Abs.1)
Special achievements: the 3-year route (§10 Abs.3) was introduced on 27.06.2024 but ABOLISHED as of 30.10.2025 — it is now 5 years for everyone
Dual citizenship for everyone (§12 StAG)
Children of foreigners by birthright (ius soli): 8 → 5 years of a parent's residence (§4 Abs.3)
Marriage §9 StAG: 3 years of residence + 2 years of marriage
Tougher loyalty requirements: antisemitism is an outright refusal
§12 StAG (the former exceptions on multiple citizenship, Mehrstaatigkeit) fully repealed (weggefallen)

content.text: §16/§17 AufenthG (study) does NOT count toward the 5 years (check with the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) how study time is credited — verify that this is current).
Long interruptions of residence may reset the period — confirm the specific thresholds with the authority (Behörde; verify that this is current).
Basic income support (Bürgergeld), even partial, is an obstacle unless you fall under §10 Abs.6. Do not give up work before you file.
Your name after naturalization (Einbürgerung): it can be adapted to German norms (the name change act, Namensänderungsgesetz) — a separate procedure.

title: Where to apply: the Einbürgerungsbehörde for your district
tldr: An application for naturalisation (Einbürgerung) is submitted to the naturalisation authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) for your place of residence (Wohnsitz, per the registration certificate, Meldebescheinigung). In urban districts this is the city administration / citizens' office (Stadtverwaltung/Bürgeramt), in rural ones the district office / district administration (Landratsamt/Kreisverwaltung), in Berlin the Immigration Office (LEA), and in Hamburg the Central Residents' Registration Office (Einwohner-Zentralamt). Since 2024 many federal states have launched online submission.

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: Naturalisation (Einbürgerung) is a matter for the federal states (Ländersache). Although the StAG is a federal law, applying it is the job of the 16 states, and within each state it is handled at district or city level. That is why the forms, timelines and online systems differ. The general principle is the same: you apply to the authority (Behörde) for your official place of residence (main residence, Hauptwohnsitz, under the registration law, Meldegesetz).

items: Submit only to the naturalisation authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) for your main residence (Hauptwohnsitz)
The address is determined by your latest registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
If you have two places of residence (Wohnsitz) — submit at the main one (Hauptwohnsitz)
If you move (Umzug) during the procedure — the case is transferred to the new authority (Behörde)

steps.title: Where to apply in each federal state

content.text: The Immigration Office (Landesamt für Einwanderung, LEA). Previously it was the district offices (Bezirksämter). Since 2024 intake has been centralised at the LEA. Apply online via the Service-Portal Berlin.
The Central Residents' Registration Office (Einwohner-Zentralamt, EZA), naturalisation department (Abt. Einbürgerung). Address: Amsinckstraße 28. Online-Portal Hamburg.de.

In Munich — the district administration office (Kreisverwaltungsreferat, KVR), München. In other cities — the district offices (Landratsämter) or independent cities (kreisfreie Städte). Bayern-Portal.
District offices (Landratsämter) in rural districts, city administrations (Stadtverwaltungen) in the cities (Stuttgart, Karlsruhe, Mannheim and others). Service-bw.de — the central portal.

The most populous federal state (Land). In each of its 30+ districts there's a citizens' office / foreigners' authority (Bürgeramt/Ausländerbehörde) with a naturalisation department (Einbürgerung). Köln, Düsseldorf, Essen and others — city authorities (Ämter). NRW's online services are expanding rapidly.

District or city offices (Landrats- oder Stadtbüros). Frankfurt am Main — the Office for Multicultural Affairs (Amt für Multikulturelle Angelegenheiten) + the naturalisation authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde).

Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt, Thüringen, Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-V., Schleswig-Holstein, Niedersachsen, Bremen, Saarland, Rheinland-Pfalz — district offices (Landratsämter) or independent cities (kreisfreie Städte). Contacts on the state (Land) website + bund.de.
After the 2024 reform, several federal states rolled out online services under the Online Access Act (Onlinezugangsgesetz, OZG):

items: Berlin: service.berlin.de — appointment booking (Termin) + digital application (Antrag)
Hamburg: hamburg.de/einbuergerung — fully online since 2024
Bayern: bayernportal.de — partly online (depends on the district)
Baden-Württemberg: service-bw.de — application (Antrag) by PDF, appointment booking online
NRW: einbuergerung.nrw — a 2024/2025 pilot project
Hessen: civento.hessen.de — application (Antrag) digitally
Sachsen, Thüringen and others: still mostly paper

content.text: Even with an online application (Antrag), original documents (passport, marriage certificate Heiratsurkunde) are presented in person — without this the authority (Behörde) won't make a final decision.

Search "Einbürgerungsbehörde + your city/district" or via 115 (the single authorities' number, Behördennummer). On bund.de there's a general search in the directory of authorities (Behördenverzeichnis).
At many authorities (Behörden) a consultation appointment (Beratungstermin) before submission is mandatory. Here a staff member checks that you meet the §10 requirements. This appointment is free.
The application with the full document package. The form depends on the federal state. Most authorities (Behörden) accept the application (Antrag) by post, in person or online.

items.title: 4. How many meetings with the Behörde

content.text: Depending on complexity — 1-3 appointments: the main hearing (Anhörung), document check, ceremony.

If you change your place of residence (Wohnsitz), you need to notify both the old and the new authority (Behörde). The case is transferred (case handover, Aktenabgabe), and the processing period usually starts over — the new authority reviews the application from the beginning.
Moving to another federal state (Bundesland) in the middle of the process is a guaranteed delay of 3 to 12 months (the case is transferred).
If you live in one city but work in another — submit the application (Antrag) only at your main residence (Hauptwohnsitz), not at your place of work.
In large cities the wait for an information consultation (info-Beratung) is 3-9 months. Book in advance, before your 5-year period ends.
An online application (Online-Antrag) doesn't mean "faster" — it just simplifies submission. The review process itself takes the same 6-24 months.

title: Belarusian citizenship and naturalisation (Einbürgerung)
tldr: After the 2024 StAG reform, Germany allows dual citizenship, so Belarusians can obtain German citizenship without renouncing their Belarusian one. Under the Law of the Republic of Belarus "On Citizenship" (of 1.08.2002 No. 136-Z, as amended in 2023), acquiring a foreign citizenship does NOT automatically lead to loss of Belarusian citizenship. But there is a risk of citizenship being revoked by Presidential Decree, and complications with consulates.

content.text: The reform — the citizenship modernisation act (Staatsangehörigkeitsmodernisierungsgesetz; 27.06.2024) — abolished the ban on dual citizenship in Germany. Belarusian law is formally similar: Art. 20 of the Law of the Republic of Belarus "On Citizenship" (of 01.08.2002 No. 136-Z) says that acquiring a foreign citizenship does not entail automatic loss of Belarusian citizenship. In practice, there are risks (especially after 2020-2024).

items: Germany: dual citizenship allowed for everyone since 27.06.2024
Belarus: no automatic loss is provided for
A Belarusian obligation to report another citizenship — NONE (unlike Russia)
Risk: the President of Belarus has the power to revoke citizenship (2023 Law)

content.text: The base law is No. 136-Z "On Citizenship of the Republic of Belarus" of 01.08.2002 (as amended in 2006, 2017, 2023). Key articles:

"A person who is a citizen of the Republic of Belarus is not recognised as belonging to the citizenship of a foreign state, unless otherwise provided by international treaties of the Republic of Belarus." — The wording means: Belarus does not recognise a second citizenship as a fact, but it does not annul its own. To Belarus, you are Belarusian only.
Renunciation is only possible by petition, reviewed by the President. The timeframe is from 1 to 4+ years. Since 2022 many applications have been suspended.

Citizenship is lost: on entering the military/police service of a foreign state without the consent of Belarusian state bodies; on voluntarily acquiring a foreign citizenship with simultaneous renunciation of Belarusian citizenship. Merely acquiring a foreign citizenship is NOT a loss.
Since 2023, Presidential Decree No. 1 has expanded the grounds for loss — for "discrediting Belarus" from abroad. This created a risk for émigrés who openly criticise the regime.

steps.title: What you need on the German side

content.text: The standard requirements of §10 StAG — Belarusian nationality gives neither advantages nor restrictions (there are no sanctions-related exceptions against Belarusian citizens).

items: 5 years of legal residence (the accelerated 3-year path was abolished on 30.10.2025)

A residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel): permanent residence permit (NE), EU long-term residence (Daueraufenthalt-EU) or a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis; §28, §18g, §24 — mass influx from Ukraine, Massenzustrom, and others)
B1 + the naturalisation test (Einbürgerungstest)
Self-support, without basic benefits (Bürgergeld, formerly Hartz IV; exceptions under §10 Abs.6)
A declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung) to the Basic Law (Grundgesetz)
Establishing identity (Identitätsklärung) — usually via a Belarusian passport

content.text: Belarusians granted protection in Germany (§25 Abs.1/2 AufenthG): for them, establishing identity under §10 Abs.1 StAG allows other official documents (a graduated model, Stufenmodell, per the application notes of the Federal Ministry of the Interior, Anwendungshinweise BMI), if obtaining a Belarusian passport is impossible or unreasonable (unzumutbar).
The main difficulty is dealing with Belarusian consulates to renew a passport or get an apostille (Apostille).

items: A Belarusian passport has been renewable ONLY on the territory of Belarus since 2023 — Decree No. 278 (issuance abroad is suspended)
This rule creates a problem for émigrés: travelling to Belarus for a new passport is risky (political persecution)
An apostille (Apostille) on Belarusian documents (birth, marriage certificates) — only through the Belarusian Ministry of Justice, and almost impossible remotely
A certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) — by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) in Germany from old documents

An alternative if you have no valid passport — arguing that the requirement is unreasonable (Unzumutbarkeit) under §10 Abs.1 StAG (the graduated model, Stufenmodell; there is no separate §10a in the StAG)

content.text: Decree No. 278 has effectively created a "passport trap" — for many Belarusian émigrés the passport has expired or is expiring with no way to renew it.

items: Application for naturalisation (Antrag auf Einbürgerung; the authority's form, Behörde)
Belarusian passport (or an explanation of why the requirement is unreasonable, Unzumutbarkeit)
Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) + registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) covering 5+ years
Belarusian birth certificate with an apostille (Apostille) + certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung)
B1 certificate (B1-Zertifikat) + naturalisation test certificate (Einbürgerungstest-Bescheinigung)
Payslips (Lohnabrechnungen) / tax assessment (Steuerbescheid)
Criminal record certificate (Führungszeugnis; requested by the authority, Behörde)

content.text: To the naturalisation authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) for your place of residence. Many Belarusians successfully complete §10 StAG in Berlin, München and Frankfurt after the 2024 reform.

No notification to Belarus is required. To enter Belarus you still use your Belarusian passport; within the EU/Germany you use the German one. For travel to third countries, choose whichever passport gives you the easier visa requirements.
When entering Belarus after naturalisation (Einbürgerung) — you must use the Belarusian passport, otherwise border guards may refuse you entry or refer the case to the KGB.

Information about obtaining German citizenship may become known to Belarusian authorities (via leaks, banks, social media). For people with "extremist" status this creates a risk of Belarusian citizenship being revoked under Decree No. 1.

Belarusian men liable for military service: obtaining a German passport does not exempt you from Belarusian military obligations from the Belarusian point of view. From the German point of view — no obligations.
If you're planning to renounce Belarusian citizenship — it's a very long road (1-4+ years, via the President of Belarus), and after the StAG reform it isn't required.

title: Applying for citizenship in Berlin
tldr: In Berlin, applications for naturalisation (Einbürgerung) have, since late 2023, been processed centrally by the Immigration Office (Landesamt für Einwanderung, LEA) rather than the district offices (Bezirksämter). Submission is online via the portals service.berlin.de and einbuergerung.berlin.de: you fill in a digital form, upload scanned documents and wait for an invitation. Berlin's main difficulty is the large backlog: before the reform the wait for a decision reached 2–3 years, and although the LEA has launched a digital pipeline and hired staff, the queues remain long. Under the current version of §10 StAG the standard residence period is 5 years for everyone; accelerated naturalisation after 3 years (the former §10 Abs.3, C1 + special integration achievements) was ABOLISHED on 30.10.2025 (the Sixth Act amending the StAG, Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG) and is unavailable. The base language level is B1; dual citizenship is allowed for everyone. The state fee is 255 € (adult) under §38 StAG. Apply online as early as possible: the date a complete application is filed fixes the law that applies. Individual legal advice is recommended.

steps.title: Who processes the application in Berlin

content.text: Since late 2023 Berlin has centralised naturalisation: instead of 12 district offices (Bezirksämter), applications are received and processed by the Immigration Office (Landesamt für Einwanderung, LEA) — the same authority responsible for residence permits. This was done to relieve the districts and speed up the process through a single digital pipeline on the einbuergerung.berlin.de portal.

Submission is fully online: you register on the portal, fill in the form (application for naturalisation, Antrag auf Einbürgerung), upload scans and send it. Berlin has effectively wound down paper submission through the citizens' office (Bürgeramt) for new cases. After review, the LEA invites you to an in-person appointment to check the originals and hand over the naturalisation certificate (Einbürgerungsurkunde).

items: Authority: the Immigration Office (Landesamt für Einwanderung, LEA), Berlin
Submission portal: einbuergerung.berlin.de and service.berlin.de
Format: online form + uploaded scans, no queue at the citizens' office (Bürgeramt)
Originals are checked at the final appointment
Legal basis: §10 StAG — the standard of 5 years for everyone (the accelerated 3-year path under §10 Abs.3 was abolished on 30.10.2025)

content.text: Berlin applies the federal conditions of §10 StAG. The reform of 27.06.2024 reduced the base residence period from 8 to 5 years. The accelerated 3-year path (the former §10 Abs.3, C1 + special integration achievements, besondere Integrationsleistungen), introduced by the same reform, was abolished by the Sixth Act amending the StAG (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG) on 30.10.2025: §10 Abs.3 is now weggefallen. Now, for naturalisation as of right (Anspruchseinbürgerung), a single period applies — 5 years for everyone.

items: Residence: 5 years (the accelerated 3-year path was abolished on 30.10.2025)
Language: B1 under §10 Abs.1 Nr.6 StAG
The naturalisation test (Einbürgerungstest) passed (33 questions, at least 17 correct needed)
Means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt): supporting yourself and your family without basic benefits (Bürgergeld, formerly Hartz IV; §10 Abs.1 Nr.3 StAG)
A declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung) to the free democratic order (§10 Abs.1 Nr.1 StAG)
Dual citizenship allowed for everyone — renouncing the previous one is not required (§10 Abs.1 Nr.4 weggefallen, §12 StAG abolished)

content.text: Gather your scans in advance: the LEA portal doesn't keep the form indefinitely, and collecting documents from abroad (birth, marriage certificates) takes a long time. Documents in foreign languages need a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung).

items: A valid passport + residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel; electronic residence permit card, eAT)
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) and proof of 5 years of residence
B1 certificate (telc, Goethe, ÖSD) or a DTZ from an integration course
Naturalisation test certificate (Einbürgerungstest; LeitBest)
Proof of income: payslips (Lohnabrechnungen), employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag), tax assessment (Steuerbescheid)
Birth/marriage certificates with a certified translation
A completed declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung)

steps.title: The reality of the queues and how to speed things up

content.text: Berlin is known for its large naturalisation backlog. Before the reform the wait for a decision reached 2–3 years, and longer in some districts. Centralisation at the LEA and digitalisation are meant to speed up the process, but the surge in applications after the 2024 reform (dual citizenship, the 5-year period) has increased the queues again. Realistically count on 12–24 months or more from submission to the certificate (Urkunde). Check the specific timeframes with the LEA — verify they're current.

What helps: apply online as early as possible — the date a complete application is received fixes the applicable law and your status. Upload ALL documents at once and without errors: incomplete applications get pushed to the back of the queue pending follow-up requests. Respond to the LEA's requests on time. If the delay becomes excessive, an action for failure to act (Untätigkeitsklage) at the Berlin administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht Berlin) is possible, usually through a lawyer.
Minor children can be included in your application jointly (joint naturalisation, Miteinbürgerung; §10 Abs. 2 StAG) — this is cheaper than separate cases.

title: C1 in 3 years (ABOLISHED as of 30.10.2025)
tldr: ABOLISHED: accelerated naturalisation after 3 years (§10 Abs.3 StAG: C1 + special integration achievements, besondere Integrationsleistungen) was repealed by the Sixth Act amending the StAG (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG) on 30.10.2025. Now everyone follows the standard path — 5 years with B1 (§10 StAG). C1 no longer shortens the naturalisation period. The section below is kept as a historical reference; check the current state at gesetze-im-internet.de/stag and bmi.bund.de.

content.text: ATTENTION (2026 update): accelerated naturalisation after 3 years (§10 Abs.3 StAG, C1 + special integration achievements, besondere Integrationsleistungen) has been ABOLISHED. The Sixth Act amending the citizenship law (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des Staatsangehörigkeitsgesetzes; passed by the Bundestag on 08.10.2025, in force since 30.10.2025) repealed this path — §10 Abs.3 is now weggefallen. The minimum residence period for naturalisation as of right (Anspruchseinbürgerung) under §10 StAG is 5 years for everyone. The section below is kept as a historical reference (the path was in effect 27.06.2024–29.10.2025). Check the current state at gesetze-im-internet.de/stag and bmi.bund.de.

Before the reform, accelerated naturalisation after 6 years (and previously 7) was possible for special integration achievements. The reform of 27 June 2024 rewrote §10 Abs. 3 StAG: the period was now reduced to 3 years, but the bar was raised — a language level of C1 is required, not B1, plus special integration achievements (besondere Integrationsleistungen).

It's important to understand: this is NOT an automatic right at C1. C1 is only one of the two mandatory components. Without special integration achievements, even a C1 speaker follows the standard 5-year path. And conversely: volunteering without C1 doesn't open the fast track.

items: Residence period: 3 years instead of 5 (§10 Abs. 3 StAG)
Language: C1 on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (GER; certified in writing), not B1
Additionally: special integration achievements (besondere Integrationsleistungen; mandatory)
All other conditions of §10 Abs. 1 StAG remain

content.text: C1 level is proven with a certificate from a recognised provider: telc Deutsch C1, Goethe-Zertifikat C1, ÖSD Zertifikat C1, TestDaF (with the corresponding scores) or DSH-2/3 for those who studied at a German university. A German university degree in German is often accepted as proof of level.

items: telc Deutsch C1 / telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule
Goethe-Zertifikat C1
ÖSD Zertifikat C1
TestDaF (TDN 4–5) or DSH-2/DSH-3
A degree from a German-language university (at the authority's discretion, Behörde)

content.text: The certificate must cover all four skills (reading, listening, writing, speaking). Check with your naturalisation authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) which documents exactly it accepts as proof of C1 — the practice varies slightly across federal states.
The law doesn't give a closed list, leaving the assessment to the authority (Behörde). In practice, achievements like these count:
Good results at work: stable employment with progression, high qualifications, outstanding professional performance. In study — excellent grades, scholarships, academic awards.

Long-term voluntary involvement: work in an association (Verein), the volunteer fire brigade (Freiwillige Feuerwehr), the Federal Agency for Technical Relief (THW), a church or social organisation, a sports club as a coach, helping refugees. Confirmed by letters from the organisations.

The authority (Behörde) may recognise a combination: for example, full-time employment + active volunteering + participation in community life. The more convincing the portfolio of evidence, the higher the chance.

items: Letters (Bescheinigungen) from organisations about volunteering
A reference from work (Arbeitszeugnis) assessing your performance
Diplomas, certificates, scholarship confirmations
Letters of recommendation

steps.title: Who the fast track really suited

content.text: CURRENT AS OF 2026: there is no longer an accelerated path after 3 years — §10 Abs.3 is weggefallen as of 30.10.2025. Now the standard path applies to everyone — 5 years with B1 (§10 StAG). The text below describes the procedure in effect 27.06.2024–29.10.2025.

While the fast track was in effect, it was beneficial above all to highly qualified specialists with C1, active volunteers and top students. Today C1 and special achievements don't shorten the naturalisation period: count on the standard 5 years. All the conditions of §10 Abs.1 StAG remain mandatory: income without basic benefits (Bürgergeld), a declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung), the naturalisation test (Einbürgerungstest). Individual legal advice is recommended.
