title: Children on the application: joint naturalization
tldr: Minor children can acquire citizenship TOGETHER with a parent through joint naturalization (Miteinbürgerung) under §10 Abs. 2 StAG. This is not a separate case: the children are added to the naturalizing parent's application, and relaxed requirements apply to them (for example, the residence and language requirements for young children are heavily eased or waived altogether), while the fee under §38 StAG is reduced to €51 per child instead of €255. If a child applies on their own without a parent, the full fee applies. After the 2024 reform, dual citizenship is allowed for everyone, so children keep their previous citizenship too. Apply for your children at the same time as yourself — it is cheaper, faster, and simpler in terms of paperwork.

content.text: §10 Abs. 2 StAG allows minor children (minderjährige Kinder) to be included in the naturalizing parent's application. They are naturalized "jointly" (Miteinbürgerung) even if the children themselves do not yet formally meet all the conditions required of an adult — primarily the residence period and, for young children, the language level.

The logic is simple: the family acquires citizenship as a single unit. This avoids a situation where the parents are German but the child remains a foreigner with their own residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel).

items: Legal basis: §10 Abs. 2 StAG (joint naturalization of children)
Children are added to the parent's application; they do not apply separately
Relaxed residence and language requirements for children
Fee reduced to €51 instead of €255 (§38 StAG)

content.text: For jointly naturalized children the conditions are milder than for an adult and depend on age. Young children are generally exempt from the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) and from formal B1; for school-age children, school attendance and actual integration are taken into account.

items: The child is a minor (under 18) at the time of the decision
Lives in Germany together with the parent (the residence requirement for children is shorter)
The naturalization test and B1 are generally not required for younger children
Children aged 16 and over may have to make their own declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung)

content.text: If the child is 16–17 years old, the authority (Behörde) often requires them to make their own declaration of loyalty to the free democratic order and may assess their integration more strictly. Check with your naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde).

The key financial benefit: under §38 StAG the fee for a jointly naturalized minor is €51 instead of the full €255. This benefit applies only when the child is naturalized TOGETHER with a parent. If the child applies independently, with their own application (eigener Antrag), the full fee of €255 applies.

items: The child's birth certificate with a certified translation
The child's passport and residence permit
The child's registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Custody documents / consent of the other parent if you live apart
School certificates (Schulbescheinigung) as proof of integration

content.text: If you live apart or share custody, written consent from the other parent for the child's naturalization is usually required. Without it, the case can stall.

After the StAG reform of 27.06.2024, dual citizenship is allowed for everyone under §12 StAG — children do not need to give up their previous citizenship. They acquire German citizenship and keep their original one, which is especially convenient for families who plan to maintain ties with their home country.

Tip: apply for your children at the same time as yourself. It is cheaper (€51 vs €255) and faster (one case, one set of cross-referenced documents), and it avoids the mismatch where the parent is already a citizen while the child is still in the queue. The backlog in large cities (Berlin, Hamburg, Munich) slows down adults' and children's cases alike.

title: Citizenship fee: €255 adult, €51 child
tldr: The state fee for naturalization is set in §38 StAG: €255 for an adult and €51 for a minor child naturalized TOGETHER with a parent (Miteinbürgerung). If the child applies independently, the full fee of €255 applies. The StAG reform of 27.06.2024 did not change these fees. The fee under §38 StAG covers only the state charge for the decision; on top of it you pay for related items: the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest, €25), a B1/C1 language certificate (€99–180), and certified translations of documents (€30–80 per page). The fee is usually paid upon a positive decision, before the citizenship certificate (Einbürgerungsurkunde) is handed over. A reduction or installment plan is possible for low-income applicants — but receiving the basic Bürgergeld benefit is a separate matter that blocks naturalization under §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StAG.

steps.title: How much the decision costs: §38 StAG

content.text: The amount of the state fee for naturalization is laid down directly in the law — §38 StAG. For an adult it is €255. For a minor child naturalized jointly with a parent (Miteinbürgerung), the fee is reduced to €51. The reform of 27.06.2024 did not touch these figures.

items: Adult: €255 (§38 Abs. 2 StAG)
Child jointly with a parent: €51
Child independently (without a parent): €255
This is the state fee ONLY for the decision; other costs are separate

content.text: €255 is only the tip of the iceberg. On the way to the certificate (Urkunde) you will incur additional expenses, so budget for them in advance:

items: Naturalization test: €25 (taken at a recognized center, e.g. the adult education center VHS)
B1 language certificate: €99–150 (telc, Goethe, ÖSD examiners)
B1 is sufficient for naturalization — a separate C1 certificate is no longer required (the 3-year fast track was abolished as of 30.10.2025)
Certified translation of documents: €30–80 per page
Requesting certificates from abroad: variable
An apostille or legalization of foreign documents may be required

content.text: The DTZ (Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer, the German test for the integration course) at level B1 can replace a separate language exam — this saves money if you have already completed the course.

The fee under §38 StAG is generally paid NOT when you apply, but upon a positive decision — before the citizenship certificate is handed over. The authority (Behörde) sends a fee notice (Gebührenbescheid) with payment details; payment is usually by bank transfer (Überweisung). Without payment the certificate is not issued, and it is precisely the handover of the certificate that makes you a citizen.

items: Wait for the fee notice (Gebührenbescheid) from the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde)
Payment is usually by bank transfer to the details provided
Payment is a condition for handing over the citizenship certificate
Keep your proof of payment

steps.title: Fee reduction and an important caveat

content.text: §38 StAG allows a reduction or waiver of the fee (Ermäßigung/Befreiung) or an installment plan on grounds of public interest or in view of your financial circumstances — especially where it concerns the naturalization of several children. Ask the authority about an installment plan (Ratenzahlung) or a fee reduction if your budget is limited.

A paradox: you cannot invoke low income to reduce the fee and at the same time receive a basic benefit without consequences — receiving the basic benefit or social assistance (Sozialhilfe) under §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StAG BLOCKS the naturalization itself (the rule was tightened by the 2024 reform). In other words, a fee reduction and the right to citizenship are different matters, and the latter weighs more.

title: Dual citizenship since 2024: the rules
tldr: The key change of the StAG reform of 27.06.2024: multiple citizenship (Mehrstaatigkeit) is now allowed for everyone. The previous requirement to give up your original citizenship (Aufgabe der bisherigen Staatsangehörigkeit) has been abolished — the old version of §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 4 StAG and the narrow exceptions of §12 StAG no longer apply. This means that when you naturalize as a German, you generally keep your previous citizenship — without having to renounce it and without the former restrictions (EU, Switzerland, impossibility of renunciation, etc.). The mirror image: Germans who voluntarily acquire a foreign citizenship no longer automatically lose their German one as they did under the former §25 StAG. Important: Germany's permission does not override the rules of YOUR country — some states strip you of citizenship themselves or do not recognize dual citizenship. Check the laws of your country of origin separately; in disputed cases, individual legal advice is recommended.

content.text: Before 27 June 2024, Germany as a general rule required renunciation of the previous citizenship upon naturalization (Vermeidung von Mehrstaatigkeit — avoiding multiple citizenship). There were exceptions — for EU and Swiss citizens, as well as for cases where renunciation is impossible or involves excessive hardship — but the basic requirement remained renunciation.

The reform (Gesetz zur Modernisierung des Staatsangehörigkeitsrechts) changed the approach: multiple citizenship (Mehrstaatigkeit) is now accepted as a general rule. §12 StAG (the provision on the former exceptions) has been repealed (weggefallen), and the condition in §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 4 StAG (Aufgabe der bisherigen Staatsangehörigkeit) has been abolished — renunciation of the previous citizenship is no longer required.

items: Renunciation of the previous citizenship is no longer required
The rule applies to all countries, not only the EU and Switzerland
Legal basis: the reform of 27.06.2024 — §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 4 weggefallen, §12 StAG repealed
You become German while keeping your original citizenship

steps.title: For Germans acquiring a foreign citizenship

content.text: The reform works both ways. Previously, a German who voluntarily acquired a foreign citizenship would generally lose their German one automatically under the former version of §25 StAG (unless they had obtained permission to retain it in advance, Beibehaltungsgenehmigung). After the reform, automatic loss in the former form no longer applies: you can acquire the citizenship of another country and keep your German one.

If you naturalized in a third country BEFORE 27.06.2024 without such permission, you may have lost your German citizenship under the former version of §25 StAG. The new version does not automatically restore that status retroactively — check your situation with the Federal Office of Administration (Bundesverwaltungsamt); individual legal advice is recommended.

steps.title: Check the laws of your own country

content.text: Germany allows dual citizenship — but that does not oblige your country of origin to do the same. Some states automatically strip you of citizenship when you voluntarily acquire another; others do not recognize dual citizenship or require notification or permission. Germany's permission does not protect you from sanctions under the laws of your home country.

Before naturalizing, check with the consulate or a lawyer of your country of origin: whether it strips citizenship when you acquire German citizenship, whether you must file a notification, and whether your rights are preserved (inheritance, real estate, entry). For some countries, dual citizenship creates complications with military service or taxation.

Dual citizenship gives you the right to two passports, the freedom to live and work in both countries, and easier entry. But it also brings obligations: possible double taxation (depending on tax treaties), military service, and the need to enter and leave each country on its own passport.

items: Right to a German passport while keeping your original citizenship
Freedom of movement and work in the EU
Check the tax consequences (DBA — double taxation agreements)
Clarify military service in both countries
Entry into each country is on its own passport

title: Applying in Hamburg: Bezirksämter
tldr: In Hamburg the naturalization application is submitted to the district office — the Bezirksamt (Einbürgerungsabteilung) for your place of residence; there are seven in total (Hamburg-Mitte, Altona, Eimsbüttel, Hamburg-Nord, Wandsbek, Bergedorf, Harburg). Information and forms are on the hamburg.de portal. Hamburg offers an online pre-application (Online-Antrag / Self-Service) with a later document upload, but the final check is done at the Bezirksamt. The federal conditions of §10 StAG apply: the standard residence period is 5 years, language B1, dual citizenship is allowed for everyone, and you need the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) and means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) without the basic Bürgergeld benefit. Note: fast-track naturalization in 3 years (the former §10 Abs. 3 StAG) was abolished as of 30.10.2025 and is no longer available. The fee is €255 (adult) / €51 (child) under §38 StAG. As in Berlin and Munich, Hamburg has a significant backlog — submit a complete set of documents as early as possible.

content.text: Unlike Berlin with its centralized authority, Hamburg has kept naturalization at the district level: the application is handled by the naturalization department (Einbürgerungsabteilung) of the district office (Bezirksamt) for your place of registration (Wohnsitz). There are seven district offices: Hamburg-Mitte, Altona, Eimsbüttel, Hamburg-Nord, Wandsbek, Bergedorf, Harburg.

The starting point is the hamburg.de portal: there you will find the application form, document checklists and the online pre-application (Self-Service). The usual path: fill in the online questionnaire, upload or send your documents, then attend an appointment at the district office to verify the originals and — upon a positive decision — for the ceremonial handover of the citizenship certificate (Einbürgerungsurkunde).

items: Authority: the naturalization department of your district office
Seven districts: Mitte, Altona, Eimsbüttel, Nord, Wandsbek, Bergedorf, Harburg
Portal: hamburg.de (forms, checklists, online pre-application)
The deciding factor is the district where you are registered

content.text: Hamburg applies the federal conditions of §10 StAG — they are uniform across the country. The reform of 27.06.2024 reduced the residence period from 8 to 5 years. The 3-year fast track, in force since 27.06.2024, was abolished as of 30.10.2025 (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG): the general 5-year period now applies to everyone.

items: Residence: 5 years (standard); the 3-year track abolished as of 30.10.2025
Language: at least B1 (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 6 StAG)
Naturalization test passed (33 questions, at least 17 correct)
Means of subsistence without the basic benefit (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StAG)
Declaration of loyalty to the constitution, Loyalitätserklärung (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG)
Dual citizenship allowed for everyone (§12 StAG repealed)

content.text: Gather the full set before applying: an incomplete application gets stuck in the queue for follow-up requests. Foreign documents require a certified translation.

items: Passport + residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel, eAT)
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) from Hamburg + residence history
B1 certificate (or higher) or DTZ (the German test for the integration course) with a B1 result
Naturalization test certificate
Proof of income: payslips (Lohnabrechnungen), employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag), tax assessment (Steuerbescheid)
Birth and marriage certificates with a certified translation
Completed declaration of loyalty to the constitution

content.text: Hamburg, like other large cities, has seen a wave of applications after the 2024 reform (5 years + dual citizenship). The queues at the district offices are significant, and processing often drags on for many months, sometimes more than a year. The city is expanding online processing, but the queues persist. Timelines vary by district — check the exact figures on hamburg.de.

What helps: use the online pre-application and upload the full set at once; track the status and respond to the district office's requests on time. Include minor children jointly in your application (§10 Abs. 2 StAG) — that's €51 per child instead of €255. If the delay becomes excessive, you can file a complaint about the authority's inaction (Untätigkeitsklage) with the Hamburg administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht Hamburg); in that case individual legal advice is recommended.

title: Means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt): without social benefits
tldr: §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StAG requires that you be able to support yourself and your dependents without resorting to the basic Bürgergeld benefit (SGB II) or social assistance, Sozialhilfe (SGB XII). The StAG reform of 27.06.2024 tightened this rule significantly: the former broad clause that exempted people who received benefits "through no fault of their own" (nicht zu vertreten) has been narrowed. As a general rule, even a partial top-up (aufstockendes Bürgergeld) while in full-time employment now bars naturalization — except in narrow cases: the guest-worker generation (Gastarbeiter, who arrived before 1974) and former GDR contract workers, those in full-time employment who cannot support their family because of childcare, and cases of particular hardship (Härtefälle). Housing benefit (Wohngeld), child benefit (Kindergeld), parental allowance (Elterngeld), BAföG and unemployment benefit ALG I generally do not bar naturalization. Income is proven with payslips (Lohnabrechnungen), a tax assessment (Steuerbescheid) and an employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag). Individual authorities vary in practice — in disputed cases, individual legal advice is recommended.

content.text: One of the conditions for standard naturalization: you must be able to support yourself and the family members who are your dependents (unterhaltsberechtigte Familienangehörige) without resorting to payments under SGB II (Bürgergeld) or SGB XII (Sozialhilfe). This is §10 Abs. 1 Satz 1 Nr. 3 StAG. The authority assesses not only the present moment but also the outlook for the stability of your income.

items: Barring: basic Bürgergeld benefit (SGB II), social assistance / basic income support, Grundsicherung (SGB XII)
Generally not barring: child benefit, parental allowance, housing benefit, BAföG, short-time work allowance (Kurzarbeitergeld), unemployment benefit ALG I
Counted as income: salary, self-employment, pension, spouse's income, alimony
Benefit community (Bedarfsgemeinschaft): a benefit received by one family member usually blocks the whole application
The income outlook must be positive and stable

steps.title: Why the 2024 reform made the rule stricter

content.text: The paradox of the reform: it cut the period from 8 to 5 years and allowed dual citizenship, yet the income requirement became stricter. Before 27.06.2024, the former version exempted those who received benefits through no fault of their own (nicht zu vertreten). The reform narrowed this general clause, leaving only a few specifically listed groups.

This is especially sensitive for those who work full-time but, because of a low salary and a large family, receive a top-up to the basic benefit (aufstockendes Bürgergeld) from the job center (Jobcenter). Previously such people often qualified under the "through no fault of their own" clause. After 27.06.2024 such a top-up generally bars naturalization — except for the narrow exceptions below. The specific assessment is made by your authority; individual legal advice is recommended.
The law kept exceptions only for strictly defined cases. They are narrow — do not count on them without a clear basis:

items.title: The guest-worker generation and GDR contract workers

content.text: Former guest workers (Gastarbeiter) who arrived under recruitment agreements before recruitment ended in 1974, and former GDR contract workers (Vertragsarbeiter): for them the income requirement is eased in recognition of their contribution.
Those who work full-time (or whose spouse works full-time) but cannot fully support the family because they care for minor children or relatives. This is a narrow exception and requires proof.
Individual cases of particular hardship (Härte). The authority assesses them case by case; you cannot count on this as a rule.
The authority wants to see stable, predictable income. Gather proof for the recent months and confirmation of the outlook (a permanent employment contract strengthens the forecast).

items: Payslips for 3–12 months
Employment contract (a permanent one strengthens the forecast)
The latest tax assessment (for the self-employed — a BWA management report and a certificate from a tax advisor, Steuerberater)
Proof of pension or annuity, if applicable
Spouse's income within the benefit community
A certificate from the job center confirming you do not receive the basic benefit

content.text: If even one member of your benefit community receives the basic benefit, this usually blocks the whole application, even if you personally earn an income. Before applying, make sure the family has fully exited SGB II, and check the current practice of your naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde).

title: B1 for citizenship: telc, Goethe, ÖSD
tldr: For standard naturalization, §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 6 StAG requires sufficient command of German at level B1 on the GER/CEFR scale (ausreichende Deutschkenntnisse). You can prove B1 with a certificate from a recognized provider — telc Deutsch B1, Goethe-Zertifikat B1, ÖSD Zertifikat B1 — or with a DTZ certificate (Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer, the test for the integration course) showing a B1 result, or with a German school or university diploma. §10 Abs. 6 StAG provides for an exemption from the language requirement in case of illness, disability or age that makes taking the exam impossible. A B1 certificate costs €99–180. Note: fast-track naturalization in 3 years at level C1 (the former §10 Abs. 3 StAG) was abolished as of 30.10.2025 — C1 no longer shortens the period. For standard naturalization, B1 remains the basic requirement.

content.text: Standard naturalization requires sufficient command of German (ausreichende Kenntnisse der deutschen Sprache), defined as level B1 on the Common European scale (GER/CEFR). This is §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 6 StAG. Level C1 previously gave access to the 3-year fast track, but that rule (the former §10 Abs. 3 StAG) was abolished as of 30.10.2025, so C1 is no longer required for naturalization.

items: Standard naturalization (5 years): B1 on the GER
The level covers comprehension, speaking, reading and writing
The 3-year fast track at C1 abolished as of 30.10.2025
B1 remains the basic requirement for all applicants

content.text: Several types of proof are accepted. The most common path is a language certificate from a recognized provider or a DTZ from the integration course:
telc Deutsch B1, Goethe-Zertifikat B1, ÖSD Zertifikat B1, telc Deutsch B1+Beruf and similar certificates from recognized institutes. The certificate must confirm exactly B1.

The DTZ test (Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer) is taken at the end of the integration course (Integrationskurs). A "B1" result in the DTZ is accepted as proof of language command for naturalization — a separate exam is then not needed.

A German school leaving certificate (generally not below a certain grade level), a diploma from a German-language school or a degree from a German university are usually counted as proof of level. Check recognition with your naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde).

items: telc Deutsch B1
Goethe-Zertifikat B1
ÖSD Zertifikat B1
DTZ (integration course) with a B1 result
German diploma or degree

content.text: §10 Abs. 6 StAG exempts you from the language requirement (and from the naturalization test, Einbürgerungstest) if you cannot meet it for objective reasons: because of a physical, mental or intellectual illness or a disability (Krankheit, Behinderung) or because of age (altersbedingt).

items: Illness or disability that prevents taking the exam
Age that makes taking the exam impossible
Confirmed by a medical certificate or an opinion from the authority's doctor (amtsärztliches Attest)

content.text: An exemption under §10 Abs. 6 StAG is not granted on request alone: you need objective proof (for example, an opinion from the authority's doctor — amtsärztliches Gutachten). Advanced age by itself does not automatically grant an exemption — the authority assesses each case individually.

If you have completed the integration course, check your DTZ result — at B1 a separate exam is not needed and you save money. If you do not have a certificate, sign up for telc, Goethe or ÖSD in advance: places are limited, and the result goes into your document set. Check which certificates your naturalization authority accepts — the practice varies slightly between states.

Do not confuse the levels: for citizenship you need B1, not the A1/A2 from other procedures (family reunification, for example, requires A1). The certificate must clearly state B1 and cover all skills.

costs.note: B1 exam at a recognized provider; the price depends on the city.

costs.label: Integration course + DTZ
costs.note: Often subsidized by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF); the DTZ can replace a separate exam.

costs.note: State fee under §38 Abs. 2 StAG.

title: Declaration of loyalty (Loyalitätserklärung): on the free order
tldr: Under §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG, naturalization requires a written declaration of commitment to the free democratic order (Bekenntnis zur freiheitlichen demokratischen Grundordnung des Grundgesetzes) — the so-called declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung). The StAG reform of 27.06.2024 strengthened this requirement: the declaration now explicitly affirms that you recognize Germany's special historical responsibility for the National Socialist regime and its consequences, in particular for the protection of Jewish life, and that the peaceful coexistence of peoples and the prohibition of a war of aggression are part of this order. Antisemitic, racist and other inhumane (menschenverachtende) acts are incompatible with naturalization — §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 and §11 StAG exclude anyone who has committed them. The declaration is signed in person; a knowingly false affirmation can be grounds for revoking the naturalization.

content.text: §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG requires the person being naturalized to make a written declaration of commitment to the free democratic basic order of the constitution (Bekenntnis zur freiheitlichen demokratischen Grundordnung des Grundgesetzes für die Bundesrepublik Deutschland) and to declare that they neither pursue nor have supported aspirations directed against it.

This is not a formality: your signature on the declaration is a substantive condition. The authority is entitled to check whether your actions or views contradict it, including through inquiries to the security agencies.

items: Written declaration of commitment to the free democratic order (freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung)
Declaration renouncing anti-constitutional aspirations
Signed in person, usually on application or at the appointment
Legal basis: §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG

content.text: The reform of 27.06.2024 expanded the content of the declaration. It now explicitly includes: recognition of Germany's special historical responsibility for National Socialist violence (NS-Unrechtsherrschaft) and its consequences, in particular for the protection of Jewish life (Schutz jüdischen Lebens), as well as an affirmation that the prohibition of waging a war of aggression and the peaceful coexistence of peoples are part of the constitutional order.

items: Recognition of historical responsibility for the NS regime
Commitment to protecting Jewish life in Germany
Recognition of the prohibition of a war of aggression
Commitment to the equality of people and to human dignity (Menschenwürde, Art. 1 GG)

content.text: Antisemitic, racist, xenophobic and other inhumane (menschenverachtende) acts are incompatible with commitment to the free democratic order. Under §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 and §11 StAG, anyone who has committed such acts cannot be naturalized. This covers statements, participation in relevant organizations and hate crimes.

items: Antisemitic acts or statements exclude naturalization
Racist and other inhumane acts exclude naturalization
Support for anti-constitutional or extremist aspirations — §11 StAG
Polygamy and acts against gender equality are also problematic

content.text: §11 StAG separately excludes naturalization where there are grounds to believe that the person supports or has supported extremist or anti-constitutional aspirations, as well as where there is a threat to security.

You sign the declaration in person — the form is usually provided by the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) on application or at the appointment before the certificate (Urkunde) is handed over. The content matches the text of §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG in its current version. Sign it knowingly: the declaration is a legally significant statement.

A knowingly false declaration of commitment (when your actual views or actions contradict it) can become grounds for revoking the naturalization (Rücknahme) under §35 StAG, if the decision was obtained by deception. Do not sign as a formality something you do not actually follow; in disputed situations, individual legal advice is recommended.

title: Applying in Munich: KVR
tldr: In Munich the naturalization application is submitted to the Kreisverwaltungsreferat (KVR) — the city authority responsible, among other things, for naturalization (Einbürgerung). Information and forms are on the muenchen.de portal. The KVR offers online forms and an appointment or pre-application system, after which your documents are checked and you attend an appointment. The federal conditions of §10 StAG apply: the standard residence period is 5 years and language B1; you need the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest), income without the basic Bürgergeld benefit (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StAG), and a declaration of loyalty to the constitution — Loyalitätserklärung (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG); dual citizenship is allowed for everyone (§12 StAG repealed). Note: fast-track naturalization in 3 years (the former §10 Abs. 3 StAG) was abolished as of 30.10.2025 and is no longer available. The fee is €255 (adult) / €51 (child) under §38 StAG. Munich, like Berlin and Hamburg, is known for long waiting times — submit a complete set of documents in advance.

content.text: In Munich, naturalization is handled by the Kreisverwaltungsreferat (KVR) — a large city authority responsible for foreigners' matters, registration and citizenship. The starting point is the muenchen.de portal, which posts the forms, document checklists and the application or booking procedure.

The typical path: fill in the online form or pre-application, send or upload your documents, and wait for the KVR's check and an invitation to an appointment to verify the originals; upon a positive decision comes the handover of the citizenship certificate (Einbürgerungsurkunde).

items: Authority: Kreisverwaltungsreferat (KVR), München
Portal: muenchen.de (forms, checklists, booking)
Format: online pre-application, check, in-person appointment
Legal basis: §10 StAG (5 years)

content.text: Munich (Bavaria) applies the federal conditions of §10 StAG. The reform of 27.06.2024 reduced the residence period from 8 to 5 years. The 3-year fast track, in force since 27.06.2024, was abolished as of 30.10.2025 (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG): the general 5-year period now applies to everyone.

items: Residence: 5 years (standard); the 3-year track abolished as of 30.10.2025
Language: at least B1 (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 6 StAG)
Naturalization test passed (33 questions, at least 17 correct)
Means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) without the basic benefit (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StAG)
Declaration of loyalty to the constitution (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG)
Dual citizenship allowed for everyone (§12 StAG repealed)

content.text: Gather a complete set before applying — incomplete applications go into the queue for follow-up requests, and that means months. Foreign documents require a certified translation.

items: Passport + residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel, eAT)
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) from Munich + residence history
B1 certificate (or higher) or DTZ (the German test for the integration course) with a B1 result
Naturalization test certificate
Proof of income: payslips (Lohnabrechnungen), employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag), tax assessment (Steuerbescheid)
Birth and marriage certificates with a certified translation
Completed declaration of loyalty to the constitution

content.text: Munich is known for long naturalization waiting times. After the 2024 reform (5 years + dual citizenship) the number of applications rose sharply, and the queues at the KVR are significant — processing often drags on for many months, sometimes more than a year. The KVR is expanding online processing, but the queues persist; check current timelines on muenchen.de.

What helps: submit the online pre-application and the full set at once; track the status and respond to the KVR's requests on time. Include minor children jointly (§10 Abs. 2 StAG) — €51 per child instead of €255. If the delay becomes excessive, you can file a complaint about the authority's inaction (Untätigkeitsklage) with the Munich administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht München); in that case individual legal advice is recommended.

title: A1 for a family visa: where to take it in Russia/CIS
tldr: For family reunification (Familiennachzug, §30 AufenthG) the spouse of a third-country national is, as a rule, required to prove German at A1 level even BEFORE entry. A1-level certificates from the Goethe-Institut ('Start Deutsch 1'), as well as telc and ÖSD, are accepted. In Russia in 2026, Goethe A1 costs roughly 95-115€ and telc 70-95€; centres operate in Moscow, St Petersburg, Novosibirsk, Almaty, Tashkent and Minsk.

steps.title: Why you need A1 before entry

content.text: Under §30 Abs. 1 Satz 1 Nr. 2 AufenthG, a spouse joining a resident of Germany through family reunification (Ehegattennachzug) is, as a rule, required to prove basic German ('einfache Deutschkenntnisse') at A1 level on the CEFR (GER) before a national D visa is issued. That means understanding simple phrases, introducing yourself and answering everyday questions. The requirement is meant to ease integration and counter forced marriages. You present the certificate at the German consulate together with the visa application.

items: The requirement applies to spouses from non-EU countries (Drittstaatsangehörige)
As a rule, the certificate must have been issued no more than a year before the visa application
A1-level certificates are accepted: Goethe-Zertifikat A1 / Start Deutsch 1, telc Deutsch A1, ÖSD KID A1 / A1
Internal tests by an adult education centre (Volkshochschule), Berlitz and online certificates are, as a rule, NOT accepted — check with the consulate
A1 level is roughly 80-100 hours of study for a complete beginner

content.text: Under §30 Abs. 1 Satz 3 AufenthG, a number of categories are exempt from the pre-entry A1 requirement. If you fall under an exception, you do not need to take A1 — but an integration course in Germany may still be required if there is an obligation under §44a AufenthG.

items: The spouse of an EU/EEA or Swiss citizen (Freizügigkeit)
The spouse of an EU Blue Card (Blue Card EU) holder (§30 Abs. 1 Satz 3 Nr. 6 AufenthG)
The spouse of an ICT-Karte holder, §18c (permanent residence permit for the highly qualified, Niederlassungserlaubnis für Hochqualifizierte), §19c Abs. 1 (researchers)
Citizens of Australia, Israel, Japan, Canada, the Republic of Korea, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, the USA (privileged countries under §41 AufenthV)
Hardship: serious illness, disability, an objective inability to learn the language (a medical report is needed)
An evidently low need for integration ('Integrationsbedarf') — for example, the spouse's higher education combined with command of the language of their country of residence

steps.title: Where and how to take A1 in Russia and the CIS

content.text: Despite the closure of the main Goethe-Institut in Moscow in 2022, exams are administered by official exam partners (Prüfungspartner). It is worth registering 4-6 weeks before your preferred date. Goethe and telc usually hold the exam in a single day: the written part (Hören, Lesen, Schreiben) and the oral part (Sprechen) — around 65 minutes in total.

items: Russia — Goethe-Institut Moskau (online registration via goethe.de/ins/ru), partners in St Petersburg, Novosibirsk, Yekaterinburg
Kazakhstan — Goethe-Institut Almaty (goethe.de/ins/kz)
Uzbekistan — Goethe-Institut Tashkent (goethe.de/ins/uz)
Belarus — Goethe-Institut Minsk (goethe.de/ins/by)
Ukraine — Goethe-Institut Kyiv (goethe.de/ins/ua), telc partners in Lviv
Georgia / Armenia — Goethe in Tbilisi, Yerevan
telc partners in Russia — see the list at telc.net (Prüfungszentren section)

content.text: Free materials: the Goethe.de 'Üben' section, Deutsche Welle (Nicos Weg A1), the DW Audiotrainer. The recommended course is 60-80 hours with a teacher plus 40 hours of self-study. Textbooks: Schritte plus Neu A1, Menschen A1, Netzwerk neu A1.

Registration is online via the centre's website. Payment is by card or bank transfer. Slots fill up fast, especially at Goethe Moskau: sometimes you have to check for new slots every few days. External candidates (Externe), who are not enrolled in the centre's course, usually pay more.

Results are issued in 2-4 weeks. The certificate itself does not expire, but for §30 AufenthG it is usually only recognised for one year. Make 2-3 certified copies (for the consulate and your own archive). For submission to the German consulate you need the original plus a copy.

A certificate older than a year is, as a rule, not accepted by the consulate (the period is counted from the day you submit the visa documents). If you obtain the certificate but apply for the visa 14 months later, you will have to retake it.

The online format 'Goethe-Test PRO Deutsch' is a separate product for assessing your level in a business context. It is not accepted for §30 AufenthG: you need an in-person Goethe-Zertifikat A1 / Start Deutsch 1.

The pass mark is 60 out of 100 points. If you score lower, many centres let you retake only the failed part within a year through the same centre (Modulwiederholung) — check the conditions in advance.
If your spouse is getting an EU Blue Card or a permit under §18c, do not register for A1 'just in case'. Claim the exemption under §30 Abs. 1 Satz 3 Nr. 6 AufenthG right away at the consulate.

costs.note: Cheaper than Goethe, recognised by the same consulates

costs.note: The Austrian equivalent, also accepted by German consulates

costs.label: Preparation course (60-80 hours)
costs.note: Heavily dependent on the city and format (group vs individual)

title: B2/C1 for the job market: the real ROI
tldr: B1 is the minimum for everyday communication and for citizenship, but for office jobs outside IT/engineering you usually need B2 (most positions for skilled professionals, Fachkraft), and for medicine, law and the civil service C1. In Germany in 2026, Goethe B2 costs 289€ and C1 349€; telc B2/C1 are roughly 229/249€. Moving from B1 to B2 in commercial roles adds an estimated 15-25% to your salary, and B2 to C1 another 10-15% (these are estimates; the exact figures vary widely).

steps.title: Which level you need for which job

content.text: Under the CEFR (Gemeinsamer Europäischer Referenzrahmen) the levels A1-C2 describe competencies, but the job market looks at specific certificates and your actual ability to work. B1 is an 'independent user' who understands work conversations on familiar topics. B2 is 'advanced': you take part in discussions and write business letters. C1 is 'proficient': you speak up in meetings and write reports unaided. C2 is 'native-level'.

items: IT, engineering, science — B1-B2 is often enough (international teams working in English)
Sales, marketing, HR, accounting — B2 at minimum, realistically C1
Medicine (doctors) — you need B2 plus a professional-language medical exam (Fachsprachprüfung) at C1 level through the medical chamber (Ärztekammer)
Law — C1 plus specialised legal German (Rechtsdeutsch)
Civil service (Beamte) — usually C1-C2, often a separate exam
Care work (Pflege) — as a rule B2 to be admitted to the recognition exam
Teaching (Lehrer) — a high level, often C2 depending on the state's requirements

content.text: For employment the accepted exams are the Goethe-Zertifikat, telc Deutsch, ÖSD, TestDaF (B2-C1 only) and DSH (for universities). Employers are most familiar with Goethe and telc. For the recognition of professional qualifications (Anerkennung), the list of accepted certificates is set by the specific recognition authority (Anerkennungsstelle) — check in advance.

The most widely recognised certificate among employers and regulators. More expensive, with waiting lists in big cities. B2 has 4 modules (Lesen, Hören, Schreiben, Sprechen), and you can take them one at a time (Modulprüfung). Official 2026 prices in Germany (adults): B2 €289, C1 €349; abroad they differ.

Recognised by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF), the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) and the medical chambers (Ärztekammern). Usually cheaper than Goethe. There are specialised versions: telc Deutsch B2-C1 Medizin, telc Deutsch B2-C1 Pflege, telc Deutsch B1-B2 Beruf. Approximate 2026 prices: B2 ~229€, C1 ~249€ (depends on the centre); specialised medical modules cost more.
Accepted by German employers and BAMF. Useful if you live in Austria or sit the exam in Eastern Europe, where the network of ÖSD partners is denser. Prices are comparable to telc.
Level B2-C1, aimed at universities. It is rarely used for the job market, but if you already have a TestDaF with TDN 4-5 across all sections, list it on your CV as a reference point comparable to C1.

Indirect data (the StepStone Gehaltsreport, IAB studies) shows that German at B2+ level noticeably raises a skilled professional's median salary compared with B1, and C1 adds a further boost in commercial roles; roughly, B1→B2 is +15-25% and B2→C1 another +10-15%. In IT the gain is usually lower (5-10%), but it opens up local positions with better conditions. Preparation time from B1 to B2 is roughly 200-300 study hours, and from B2 to C1 another 300-400.

items: Budget for B2: roughly 1500-3000€ (course, textbooks, exam)
Budget for C1: another 2000-4000€
Timeline: B1→B2 intensively in 4-6 months, or 9-12 months in the background
Professional language courses (Berufssprachkurse) from BAMF (§45a AufenthG, DeuFöV) — B2/C1 courses, free if you meet BAMF's conditions
Education voucher (Bildungsgutschein) from the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) — can cover C1 for the unemployed
Tax deduction: work-related language costs can be claimed as work-related expenses (Werbungskosten) on your tax return (Steuererklärung)

content.text: Many IT specialists stay at B1 for years and miss out on growth opportunities. Senior/Lead positions almost always require B2+ because of the intense communication with the business side.

A B2/C1 certificate without real speaking practice will not convince an employer — it shows quickly in an interview. Alongside exam prep, attend conversation meetups (Stammtisch), find a language partner (Tandem) and network in German.

The Goethe C1 comes in two formats: the 'Goethe-Zertifikat C1' and (formerly) the 'Zentrale Mittelstufenprüfung' — both are valid, but employers sometimes confuse them. State the full name and the year you obtained it.

BAMF's professional language courses come with a reimbursement clause: if you drop out without a valid reason, you may be asked to repay the costs. Check the conditions with the provider organisation (Träger).

title: Dialects: Bairisch, Schwäbisch, Plattdeutsch and others
tldr: Standard German (Hochdeutsch) is what you learn in courses and at school, and it is understood everywhere. But in Bavaria, Baden-Württemberg, Saxony, the north and in Cologne, you may run into a dialect at the shop, in a taxi or at the doctor that sounds almost like a different language. You don't have to understand dialect — locals usually switch to Hochdeutsch if you ask — but recognising the basics makes daily life noticeably easier.

steps.title: What dialects are and where they are spoken

content.text: German dialects (Mundarten / Dialekte) are not 'bad German' but historical forms of the language that existed before standard German (Hochdeutsch) was unified between the 16th and 19th centuries on the basis of Luther's Bible translation. In formal settings (government offices, TV news, school, university) Hochdeutsch is always used. In everyday life in the southern and northern states, dialects are very much alive.

items: Bairisch (Bayrisch) — Bavaria, except Franconia; ~10 million speakers
Schwäbisch — Baden-Württemberg (Stuttgart, Tübingen, Ulm); ~8 million
Fränkisch — northern Bavaria (Nuremberg, Würzburg, Bamberg)
Plattdeutsch (Niederdeutsch) — Schleswig-Holstein, Lower Saxony, Mecklenburg
Sächsisch — Saxony (Dresden, Leipzig, Chemnitz)
Kölsch / Rheinisch — Cologne, Düsseldorf, the Rhineland
Berlinerisch — Berlin (fading fast, ~30% of speakers left)
Hessisch — Hesse (Frankfurt, Kassel)

content.text: In Munich a taxi driver might say 'Servus, wo gehts hi?' instead of 'Guten Tag, wohin möchten Sie?'. In a Stuttgart bakery you'll hear 'Grüß Gott, was darfs sei?' ('Was darf es sein?'). In Hamburg a pensioner will say 'Moin' instead of 'Guten Morgen' even at 17:00. In Leipzig 'Nu' means 'Ja'. This is not disrespect — it is just normal local speech.

items: Servus = Hallo / Tschüss
Pfiat di = Tschüss (Behüt dich Gott)
Brezn = Brezel, Semmel = Brötchen
Schmankerl = a delicacy, Wiesn = Oktoberfest
I mog di = Ich mag dich
Dahoam = zu Hause, woaß i ned = weiß ich nicht
Grüß Gott = Hallo (formal)
Spätzle = classic dish, Maultaschen
Schaffe = arbeiten, Häusle = a little house
Ade = Tschüss, Mol guggâ = mal schauen
I hab koi Zeit ned = ich habe keine Zeit (double negative)
Moin / Moin Moin = universal greeting
Wat? = Was? (as in Dutch)
Dat geiht = das geht
Recognised as a separate language under the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages
In the north there are schools that teach Plattdeutsch

items.title: Sächsisch — the most recognisable by intonation

content.text: A drawn-out 'oi'; 'ei' sounds like 'ee', 'au' like 'oo'. 'Nu freilich' = 'na klar'. Surveys regularly rank it first as 'Germany's least-liked dialect' — but it is part of the local identity, and locals appreciate it when you at least try to understand.

steps.title: What a newcomer should do about it

content.text: There is no point learning a dialect for an exam — all official tests (Goethe, telc, DTZ, TestDaF) are in Hochdeutsch. But in daily life in the southern states it helps to recognise 10-20 key words and not freeze when a shop assistant answers 'Passt scho' (= 'alles gut'). If you really don't understand, ask politely: 'Entschuldigung, könnten Sie das bitte auf Hochdeutsch sagen?' Nobody will take offence.

items: At work and in official institutions — always Hochdeutsch
With local friends — you can gently ask them to 'translate'
YouTube: the channels 'Easy German' and 'Deutsch mit Marija', the BR Heimat series (Bairisch), NDR Plattdeutsch
TV series: 'Hubert ohne Staller' (Bairisch), 'Großstadtrevier' (light Hamburgisch), 'Tatort Münster' (Münsterland)
Don't try to speak dialect yourself — below B2 it sounds like a parody
In Austria and Switzerland it's even harder: Schweizerdeutsch is effectively a separate language

content.text: In a job interview at a Bavarian company, do NOT switch to Bairisch, even if the interviewer uses dialect — stick with Hochdeutsch. It's a sign of respect and professionalism.
At the doctor (Arzt) and at a public office (Behörde), speak Hochdeutsch and ask for the same. In practice staff switch to standard German when asked — that's normal and appropriate.

Don't confuse dialect (Dialekt) with accent (Akzent / Aussprache). A Berliner can speak clean Hochdeutsch with a light accent, while a Bavarian farmer speaks a Bairisch you won't understand at all. These are different things.
In your first months in the southern states it's normal to feel lost — even native Germans from Hamburg often don't understand rural Bairisch. It's not a problem with your language skills.

costs.label: Bairisch / Schwäbisch phrasebook for tourists
costs.note: Not essential, more of a fun read

costs.label: Plattdeutsch course at the VHS
costs.note: Only in the north (Hamburg, Bremen, Kiel); a semester of 10-12 sessions

costs.label: Subscription to local podcasts/YouTube
costs.note: BR Heimat, NDR, MDR — free via the ARD-Mediathek

title: DSH: the alternative to TestDaF for university
tldr: DSH (Deutsche Sprachprüfung für den Hochschulzugang) is the German-language exam run by German universities for foreign applicants. The level ranges from B2 to C2; most programmes require a DSH-2 result. You usually take it at the university itself, it normally costs 100-200€ and it is offered twice a year. If you are applying, choose between DSH and TestDaF: DSH is often more convenient and is accepted by your own university, but check in advance whether other universities will recognise it.

steps.title: What DSH is and who needs it

content.text: DSH (Deutsche Sprachprüfung für den Hochschulzugang ausländischer Studienbewerber) is a language exam developed by the German universities themselves under the framework rules of the German Rectors' Conference (Hochschulrektorenkonferenz, HRK) and the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education (Kultusministerkonferenz, KMK). You need it to enrol in German-taught Bachelor's or Master's programmes at public universities if you don't hold a German school-leaving certificate or an equivalent qualification.

items: Purpose — to prove you can study in German: follow lectures and seminars and write papers
Recognised by German universities under the common DSH framework regulation (DSH-Rahmenordnung, RO-DT)
Alternatives: TestDaF (TDN 4 in all parts ≈ DSH-2), Goethe C2, telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule, ÖSD C1, the entrance qualification exam of the preparatory college (Feststellungsprüfung Studienkolleg)
Not used for work visas — it's an academic certificate
Exempt are holders of a German school-leaving certificate (Abitur), graduates of a deutsche Auslandsschule, and DSD II Stufe holders

content.text: DSH is graded at three result levels (not three separate exams). A score from 57% gives DSH-1, from 67% DSH-2, and from 82% DSH-3. Most Bachelor's programmes accept DSH-2; medicine and law often require DSH-3.
The minimum level. Accepted on some technical and natural-science programmes (mathematics, physics) and on some ERASMUS exchange programmes. Not enough for most subjects.
The standard for the vast majority of Bachelor's and Master's programmes in Germany. Equivalent to TestDaF TDN 4 in all 4 modules. Sufficient for the social sciences, economics, engineering and IT.
The highest level. Required for medical faculties (Humanmedizin, Zahnmedizin) at most universities, as well as for law (Staatsexamen Jura), German studies, Slavic studies and translation programmes.

DSH is run by the universities' language centres (Sprachenzentren) and preparatory colleges (Studienkollegs) twice a year — usually in February/March (for the summer semester) and in August/September (for the winter semester). You apply online on the Sprachenzentrum's website, separately from your application to the study programme itself.

items.title: 1. Choose a university and check recognition

content.text: First check on the programme's website (Studienbüro / Akademisches Auslandsamt) which DSH level is accepted. You can sit DSH at another university, but there's little point — your own university usually gives priority to its own candidates.

items: The deadline is usually 6-8 weeks before the exam
Sometimes you need confirmation of admission to the programme or a preliminary invitation
Payment online or by bank transfer (Überweisung); €100-200 depending on the university
External candidates (not enrolled) pay more — €150-250

content.text: 3-4 hours: Leseverstehen (understanding an academic text of ~600-1000 words), Hörverstehen (a 10-15 minute lecture with questions), wissenschaftssprachliche Strukturen (the grammar of academic language), Textproduktion (a structured text of ~250 words: describing a graph or table, building an argument). The exact structure and timing depend on the university.

Held if you reach at least the passing threshold in the written part (often around 57%). 15-20 minutes: a short presentation based on a text or graph plus a conversation with the panel. It is graded separately, and your final DSH level is the lower of the written and oral results.

Results are issued within 2-4 weeks. The certificate is formally valid indefinitely, but many universities want a 'recent' one (1-2 years). The retake conditions and the limit on attempts depend on the university — check first.

steps.title: DSH vs TestDaF: which to choose

content.text: TestDaF (in Germany in 2026 roughly 210€ in the digital format) is taken at accredited centres worldwide, including Tbilisi and Almaty, and is recognised by all German universities. DSH is usually taken in Germany — so it makes sense if you are already here (for example after a Studienkolleg preparatory college) or arrived on a student visa (§16b AufenthG) specifically to prepare.

A DSH taken at another university is formally recognised under the DSH-Rahmenordnung, but in practice individual universities (especially medical faculties) may require a retake. Check before applying.
Digital TestDaF (TestDaF digital) and paper TestDaF carry the same weight. The digital one is faster (results in 3 weeks) but requires confident typing on a German keyboard with ä/ö/ü/ß.
Don't take DSH 'for practice' six months before your real attempt — some universities have a permanent limit of 2 attempts, and a failed DSH-1 will lock you out.
Don't take DSH 'for practice' shortly before your real attempt: some universities cap the number of attempts, and a poor result can lock you out. Check the retake rules first.

title: The integration course's final test (DTZ)
tldr: The Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer (DTZ) is the mandatory final exam of the integration course (Integrationskurs); it tests German at the A2-B1 level. You take it through telc or G.A.S.T.; for course participants the BAMF covers the cost. On your own it costs roughly 120-160€. A B1 result is needed to get 50% of the course fee back, for citizenship (§10 StAG, minimum 5 years of residence) and for a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §9 AufenthG. If you don't reach B1, one free retake through the BAMF is possible if you meet the conditions.

content.text: The Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer (DTZ) is a scalable A2/B1 test, developed on behalf of the BAMF as the final exam of the integration course (Sprachprüfung des Integrationskurses). 'Scalable' means the same set of tasks is graded against two scales: some tasks count as A2, others as B1. As a result you get separate grades for the 4 skills, and each can be A2 or B1.

items: Consists of 4 modules: Hörverstehen, Leseverstehen, Schreiben, Sprechen
Duration: ~140 minutes for the written part + 16 minutes oral
Result: each skill is awarded an A2 or B1 level separately
Certificate: 'unter A2', 'A2', 'B1', broken down by each skill
Accepted by the BAMF, the foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde), the registry office (Standesamt) and employers as proof of B1

steps.title: Why reaching B1 matters so much

content.text: Your DTZ result affects your rights and obligations after the course. If even one module falls into A2, you have formally not reached B1 on the DTZ. That closes off or slows down a number of processes.

items: Refund of 50% of the course fee (§9 IntV) — if you reach B1 within 2 years of the date your authorisation (Berechtigung) was issued

Citizenship (§10 StAG) — minimum 5 years of residence; B1 is needed as proof of linguistic integration. The accelerated naturalisation after 3 years (introduced in 2024) was abolished as of 30.10.2025
Permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §9 AufenthG (usually after 5 years) — B1 required (spoken and written)
The obligation under §44a AufenthG is fulfilled by completing the course and passing the final exams
For highly qualified workers and EU Blue Card holders, the shorter path to permanent residence requires language proof (A1 or B1 depending on the category)

content.text: If you are officially enrolled in an integration course (Integrationskurs) through the BAMF, the course provider (Träger) automatically registers you for the DTZ at the end of the course. The cost is covered by the BAMF. The exam date is usually in the last week of the course. The Träger tells you the address and time.

If you didn't take the course or didn't manage to sit it with your group, register at any telc-Prüfungszentrum or with G.A.S.T. The cost for self-payers is roughly 120-160€ (depending on the centre). Find a centre at telc.net (in the Prüfungszentren-Suche section).

items: Hörverstehen (~25 min) — dialogues, announcements, news, topics from daily life and work
Leseverstehen (~45 min) — short texts, notices, instructions, articles
Schreiben (~30 min) — a formal letter or email (complaint, request, report)
Sprechen (~16 min, in pairs) — introducing yourself, discussing a picture, planning something (e.g. organising a party)

content.text: If you don't reach B1 and you meet the BAMF conditions, you are entitled to one free retake — usually after an additional 'Wiederholerkurs' (up to 300 teaching hours). This is a significant bonus — don't miss it.

A common mistake is underestimating the oral part. Sprechen is done in a pair with another candidate, and if your partner stays silent or panics, it's harder for you to produce enough speech to be graded at B1. Practise the dialogue while you're still on the course.

In Schreiben, keep a clear structure: Anrede ('Sehr geehrte Frau X'), Bezug ('Bezugnehmend auf …'), the main text, and a Grußformel ('Mit freundlichen Grüßen'). Without a formal structure your score can be dropped to A2 even when the content is correct.

If you are obliged to attend under §44a and don't even pass the DTZ at A2, the foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde) may take that into account when renewing your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) under §8 Abs. 3 AufenthG. Take the exam seriously.

For the 50% refund (Kostenerstattung), the deadline is 2 years from the date the authorisation (Berechtigung) was issued by the BAMF, not from the DTZ date. Submit your application right after passing.

The standalone DTZ certificate does not replace the 'Zertifikat Integrationskurs': the latter is issued only if you pass both the DTZ (B1) and the 'Leben in Deutschland' test. For §10 StAG (citizenship) you need both results.

costs.note: Free for those who don't pass the DTZ at B1 on the first attempt

costs.note: If you self-paid €1540 and passed B1 within 2 years — €770 is refunded under §9 IntV

title: Goethe-Zertifikat A1-C2: where to take it and how much it costs
tldr: The Goethe-Zertifikat is the most widely recognised German certificate in the world. Six levels (A1-C2), all accepted by the BAMF, embassies, universities and employers. 2026 prices in Germany for adults (external candidates): A1 155€, A2 175€, B1 259€, B2 289€, C1 349€, C2 359€; participants in Goethe courses usually get around a 20% discount. Prices abroad differ. You can take it in modules (Modulprüfung) — handy when you only need to retake one part.

content.text: The Goethe-Zertifikat is a range of official exams from the Goethe-Institut, the state institution for promoting the German language and culture abroad. The six levels match the CEFR (GER): from A1 'Start Deutsch 1' to C2 GDS 'Großes Deutsches Sprachdiplom'. All certificates are valid indefinitely (formally unbefristet), but many institutions want a 'recent' one (up to 2 years).

items: A1 Start Deutsch 1 — simple phrases; for the family visa (§30 AufenthG)
A2 — everyday situations
B1 — independent user; the minimum for citizenship (§10 StAG) and permanent residence (Niederlassung) under §9 AufenthG
B2 — working German; for most skilled-worker (Fachkraft) jobs
C1 — academic German; accepted by universities as an alternative to DSH/TestDaF
C2 GDS — effectively native level; for DaF teachers and translators

content.text: Since 2019 the Goethe-Institut has moved B1, B2 and C1 to a modular system: the four parts (Lesen, Hören, Schreiben, Sprechen) can be taken together or separately. In Germany in 2026 a single module costs roughly ~104€ (B1) and ~114€ (B2/C1). This is convenient: if you only failed Schreiben, you retake just that part, not the whole exam. The final certificate is issued once all four modules are passed.
All 4 modules in one day. The total price is lower. Suitable for confident candidates and for those who need a result quickly (scholarship, visa).

A single module is ~€104-114 (B1-C1, Germany 2026). The total for all modules comes out higher than a Gesamtprüfung, but it lowers the risk. There's no limit on the gap between modules — you can spread them over a year. The certificate is issued once all 4 are passed (≥60% in each).

items: BAMF — for the Integrationskurs and Berufssprachkurse
The foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde) — for AufenthG §9, §28, §30
The registry office (Standesamt) — for §10 StAG (citizenship), B1 minimum
Universities — C1/C2 as an alternative to DSH/TestDaF
Medical chambers (Ärztekammern) — for recognition of a doctor's diploma (often B2/C1 Medizin)
Employers — especially B2/C1 for office positions

steps.title: Where to take it in Germany and abroad

content.text: In Germany — Goethe-Institute in the major cities (Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, Frankfurt, Dresden, Düsseldorf) and a network of Prüfungspartner at VHS adult-education centres and language schools. In Russia and the CIS — the Goethe-Institut and accredited centres.

items: Russia — Goethe Moscow (online registration via goethe.de/ins/ru), partners in St Petersburg (the Goethe-Institut via cooperation), Novosibirsk, Kaliningrad
Kazakhstan — Goethe-Institut Almaty
Uzbekistan — Goethe-Institut Tashkent
Belarus — Goethe-Institut Minsk
Ukraine — Goethe-Institut Kyiv (+ partners in Lviv, Odesa)
Georgia — Goethe-Institut Tbilisi
Armenia — Goethe-Zentrum Yerevan
Registration: on goethe.de you choose a centre and an available date; pay by card or bank transfer (Überweisung)

content.text: Goethe-Test PRO Deutsch is a separate online product for assessing your level in a business context (roughly ~100€). Don't confuse it with the Goethe-Zertifikat: PRO is recognised by employers as an assessment, but it does not replace the official Goethe-Zertifikat for the BAMF or for visas.

The Goethe-Zertifikat C2 GDS consists of four separate modules, and you can take them over several years. But it's best to check with the Goethe-Institut how 'old' and 'new' modules can be combined — the format is updated from time to time.
Slots for A1/A2 in Russia sell out within days. Goethe Moscow usually opens registration about 2-3 months before the exam. Subscribe to the notifications.
When registering, enter your name in Latin letters EXACTLY as it appears in your passport. Even a one-letter discrepancy makes the certificate invalid for the consulate.
A course at the Goethe-Institut does NOT automatically register you for the exam — you have to register separately. The price for 'in-house' students is 10-15% lower.

title: Finding an integration course (Integrationskurs) via BAMF-NAvI
tldr: BAMF-NAvI (bamf-navi.bamf.de) is the official search tool for integration courses across Germany. Enter a postcode or city and it shows provider organisations (Träger) with filters: general course, women's, parents', youth, literacy (Alphabetisierungskurs), intensive (Intensivkurs). Compare the options on schedule (morning/evening), childcare, distance and start date. You need to enrol BEFORE submitting your Berechtigungsschein to the BAMF.

content.text: BAMF-NAvI (Navigator für Migrationsangebote, formerly WebGIS BAMF) is the official portal of the Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge, listing all provider organisations (Träger) of integration courses and Berufssprachkurse. It is available at bamf-navi.bamf.de. The search is free and requires no registration.

items: Covers Träger (provider organisations) across Germany: VHS, Caritas, AWO, private schools
Filters: course type, language, schedule, availability of childcare (Kinderbetreuung), Träger status
Shows contacts, the nearest start dates, and the 'places available / Warteliste' status
Does not show: prices (for §44 — €0, for self-payers — €2.29/hour in 2026) or participant reviews

content.text: Under §11 IntV there are several course formats depending on the target group. The basic one is the Allgemeiner Integrationskurs: 700 teaching hours (600 language + 100 orientation course, Orientierungskurs). Special courses are usually 300 hours longer (up to 900-1000) and adapted to the group's needs.

The standard: 600 hours of language (6 modules of 100 hours each) + 100 hours of the orientation course (Orientierungskurs). The most common one, available everywhere. Morning, evening and weekend groups.
Accelerated: 400 hours of language + 30 hours of orientation. For those who learn at a fast pace. Less often available in smaller towns.

900 hours of language + 100 hours of orientation. For those who cannot read and write (primary literacy). Don't confuse it with the Zweitschriftlernerkurs (below): Russian speakers with no foundation in German are usually better suited to the latter, since they are already literate in Cyrillic.

900 + 100 hours. For those who read in a non-Latin script (Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese, Greek). The pace is slower than the general course. Suitable for most Russian speakers with no foundation in German.
900 + 100 hours. Gender and age groups with adapted topics. The Frauenkurs often comes with childcare (Kinderbetreuung), which is critical for mothers.

items.title: 1. Get your Berechtigungsschein from the BAMF

content.text: Under §44 AufenthG you have the right (Anspruch); under §44a you are obliged (Verpflichtung). The application goes to your local BAMF via a form or through the foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde). You don't need to name a specific Träger in the application — the Berechtigungsschein is issued 'for any provider'.

items: Enter the PLZ (postcode) or city
Choose a radius (usually 5-25 km)
Filter: 'Integrationskurs Allgemein' / Intensiv / Alphabetisierung
Filter: Kinderbetreuung — if you need childcare
Sort by start date (Kursbeginn)

content.text: Call or email 2-3 Träger. Ask about: the next start date, the format (morning/evening), whether there's a placement test (Einstufungstest), Kinderbetreuung, the teaching method (lecture-style vs interactive), and the textbook (Lehrwerk). Reserve a place in advance — slots go fast.

The Träger runs a placement test to work out whether you need module 1 (the full course) or can go straight into module 3-4. The test is short and free. If you already speak the language at B1, the Träger will send you to the DTZ without a course.

items.title: 5. Register and turn up on the first day

content.text: Bring your passport, the Berechtigungsschein and your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel), if you have one. Sign the contract with the Träger. If you have a right or obligation under §44/§44a — the fee is €0; if you pay yourself — €2.29/hour (2026), i.e. ~€1603 for 700 hours.
Don't choose a Träger on proximity alone. Teaching quality varies a lot — look for real reviews of the specific Träger, for example in your own community's online groups.
With repeated absences the Träger has the right to expel you, and the Berechtigungsschein may 'expire'. A transfer to another group is usually only possible for a valid reason (illness, work).
When you move to another city, re-register the Kurs through the new BAMF and a new Träger. Don't stay in the old course, or you'll lose all the hours you've accumulated when the Lehrwerk changes.
BAMF-NAvI may show 'Plätze frei', but the slots can actually be taken within a day. Call, don't wait.
Watch the Träger status: 'zugelassen' = active, 'aufgehoben' = removed from the BAMF system. Don't enrol with an 'aufgehoben' provider.
