title: Free integration course (Integrationskurs): §44 AufenthG
tldr: The Integrationskurs is free if you have a right (Anspruch, §44 AufenthG) or an obligation (Verpflichtung, §44a AufenthG). The right usually applies to newcomers with a long-term residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel), to EU citizens with an integration need (Integrationsbedarf), and to late repatriates (Spätaussiedler). The obligation applies, for example, to Bürgergeld recipients without sufficient German and in cases of family reunification. Students under §16a/§16b usually have no right, but §22-25 (humanitarian) and §28 (family of a German citizen) do. 700 hours plus the DTZ for €0.

content.text: There are two legal routes to a free integration course (Integrationskurs). Under §44 AufenthG it's a right (Anspruch): you may attend, but you don't have to. Under §44a it's an obligation (Verpflichtung): you must attend, under threat of sanctions. In both cases the course is FREE for the participant (€0).

items: Anspruch (§44) — voluntary, but free

Verpflichtung (§44a) — mandatory; otherwise sanctions: a cut in Bürgergeld (under SGB II — by 30%), complications when renewing the residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) and with settlement (Niederlassung)
In both cases the BAMF pays for the course and the DTZ; it may also cover childcare (Kinderbetreuung) and travel (Fahrtkosten)
Validity of the Berechtigungsschein — usually 2 years from the date of issue

content.text: The right to a free course belongs to newcomers who obtain a long-term residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) for the first time. The right is granted within 2 years of receiving the permit. After that — only under special conditions.

items: §7 AufenthG (general residence permit)
§18b (Fachkraft), §18g (Chancenkarte), §18c (Niederlassung Hochqualifizierte)
§19c (researcher), §21 (self-employment) — yes, they have the right
§28 (family member of a German citizen), §29 (family member of a foreigner), §30 (Ehegatte)
§25 (humanitäre Gründe), §25a (jugendliche Geduldete), §25b (lang Geduldete)
§38a (langfristig Aufenthaltsberechtigte from another EU country)
EU Blue Card (§18g Abs. 1) — yes

content.text: Under §9 BVFG (Bundesvertriebenengesetz), late repatriates (Spätaussiedler) are automatically German citizens but still have the right to an integration course under §44 Abs. 1 Satz 1 Nr. 3 AufenthG. The same applies to family members (§7 BVFG).

Under §44 Abs. 4, EU citizens can be granted the right (admission, Zulassung) if there is an 'Integrationsbedarf'. The BAMF decides on a case-by-case basis. In practice it is granted if your German is at a low level and you plan to live in Germany long-term.
Under §44 Abs. 4 Satz 2, even German citizens with a migration background can be granted admission (Zulassung) if they speak German poorly. A rare but real route.
An obligation means you must turn up to the course. The BAMF, foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde) or job centre (Jobcenter) issues a formal Verpflichtung — refusal carries sanctions.

items: Those with a right under §44 but insufficient German — obligation under §44a Abs. 1
Bürgergeld recipients (SGB II) below B1 — by referral from the Jobcenter (§44a Abs. 1)
Participants in Ehegattennachzug who haven't reached the required language level
Individual cases at the discretion of the Ausländerbehörde
Sanctions for non-attendance: a 30% cut in Bürgergeld under SGB II; complications when renewing the residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel); the possibility of recovering the estimated Kostenbeitrag

steps.title: Who does NOT have the right (exceptions)

content.text: Not every residence-permit (Aufenthaltstitel) category grants the right to a free course. The exceptions often come as an unpleasant surprise.

items: §16a AufenthG (Berufsausbildung) — usually no right to the Integrationskurs (but job-related courses may be possible)
§16b AufenthG (Studium) — no right; students learn the language at the university's Sprachenzentrum
§16d (recognition of qualifications) — usually no right
§17 (looking for a training place) — usually no right
§19 (ICT-Karte) — no right to a BAMF course; the employer often pays for an in-house course
§24 (vorübergehender Schutz, including Ukrainians) — yes, the right exists (since 2022)
Tourists (Schengen visa) and short-term posted workers — no

content.text: When you first receive your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel), the foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde) often issues a Berechtigungsschein from the BAMF straight away (especially for §28, §30). If they don't — ask for it.

items.title: 2. Submit an application to the BAMF

items: The form 'Antrag auf Zulassung zum Integrationskurs' from the BAMF website
A copy of the Aufenthaltstitel or temporary proof of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung)
A copy of your passport
A free-form statement of the reason (for EU citizens)
Submit by post to the Regionalstelle BAMF (address by PLZ) or in person

content.text: Takes 2-6 weeks. The Berechtigung is sent by post. It's valid for 2 years: you must start the course within that period. With it, the BAMF pays the Träger directly.
Through bamf-navi.bamf.de you choose a provider organisation (Träger), present your Berechtigungsschein and start learning. See the separate guide 'Finding a course via BAMF Navi'.

A common mistake is to look for a Träger first and get the Berechtigungsschein 'later'. The correct order is the reverse: get the Berechtigungsschein first, then enrol. Otherwise the Träger will bill you at €2.29/hour.
Students under §16b do NOT have the right to a BAMF course — but many universities offer free German courses through their Sprachenzentrum. Use that resource.
If you leave Germany before finishing the course for more than 6 months, the Berechtigungsschein 'expires'. Re-apply when you return.
When your status changes (§16b → §18b etc.), check whether you've gained the right. People often miss the 2-year window after a change.
A Verpflichtung under §44a from the Jobcenter obliges you not only to attend but to PASS. If you don't pass the DTZ at A2 minimum, the obligation may be extended by another year.

The 50% refund of the course fee (roughly ~€802 with full self-payment) is available only to those who paid themselves AND reached B1 within 2 years. For §44/§44a participants the refund doesn't apply — they didn't pay for the course.

costs.label: Integrationskurs under §44 / §44a
costs.note: The BAMF pays the Träger directly

costs.label: Kinderbetreuung during the course
costs.note: For §44/§44a participants the BAMF pays, if the Träger arranges it

costs.label: Fahrtkostenzuschuss (travel reimbursement)
costs.note: On application to the BAMF, if the journey is longer than 30 min one way or the Träger is far

costs.label: DTZ final exam
costs.note: For course participants the BAMF pays; on your own €120

costs.label: Refund on passing B1 (Selbstzahler only)
costs.note: 50% of €1603 ≈ €802; apply through the BAMF within 2 years of the date the Berechtigung was issued

sources.title: AufenthG §44 — Berechtigung zur Teilnahme am Integrationskurs
AufenthG §44a — Verpflichtung zur Teilnahme am Integrationskurs
BAMF — Merkblatt zum Antrag auf Zulassung zum Integrationskurs (630.009r)

title: The integration course (Integrationskurs): what it is and who qualifies
tldr: The Integrationskurs is the state integration course run by the BAMF: ~600–700 hours of language (up to level B1) plus an orientation course (Orientierungskurs, ~100 hours on Germany's law, history and society). It is based on §43–44 AufenthG. Whether you have a right or an obligation to attend depends on your status: many people have the right (Teilnahmeberechtigung), some are obliged (Teilnahmeverpflichtung under §44a AufenthG). If you pay yourself, an hour costs 2.29 € (~1603 € for the course), but on a low income an exemption is possible, and if you pass B1 within 2 years you can get 50 % of the fee back.

content.text: The Integrationskurs is a state integration programme organised by the BAMF (Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge) on the basis of §43 AufenthG. The course has two parts: a language course (Sprachkurs) usually lasting 600 hours, taking you up to level B1, and an orientation course (Orientierungskurs, ~100 hours) on Germany's legal system, history and culture. There are also special courses: for women, parents and young people, and with literacy training.

items: Language course: ~600 hours, aiming for level B1 (GER)
Orientierungskurs: ~100 hours on Germany's law, history and society
Final exams: the DTZ (Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer) and the 'Leben in Deutschland' test
Special courses (Frauen-, Eltern-, Jugend-, Alphabetisierungskurs) with more hours
Organised and funded by the BAMF (§43 AufenthG)

content.text: Access depends on your status. Many foreigners with a residence permit have the right to attend (Teilnahmeberechtigung, §44 AufenthG). Some people are obliged to take the course (Teilnahmeverpflichtung, §44a AufenthG) — for example if their German is insufficient and the foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde) or job centre (Jobcenter) decides so. EU citizens and some other categories can attend if places are available.

items: Teilnahmeberechtigung (right) — §44 AufenthG, for many residence-permit holders
Teilnahmeverpflichtung (obligation) — §44a AufenthG, by decision of the authority
The obligation often applies when German is weak and you receive benefits
EU citizens — if places are available
Admission is arranged through the BAMF / Ausländerbehörde / Jobcenter

content.text: If you are obliged to attend (Verpflichtung under §44a AufenthG), attendance is not voluntary. Absences and refusal can lead to sanctions: a reduction in social benefits and complications when renewing your residence permit. Take the Verpflichtung seriously and keep all referrals.

If you pay yourself, the fee (Kostenbeitrag) is 2.29€ per teaching hour. For the standard 700 hours (600 language + 100 orientation) that's about 1603€. But many people pay less or nothing at all: benefit recipients (Bürgergeld) and people on a low income can get a full exemption (Kostenbefreiung). On top of that, if you reach B1 within 2 years you can get back half of the fee you paid.

items: Self-payment: 2.29 € per hour (~1603 € for a 700 h course)
Kostenbefreiung — exemption for those on benefits or a low income
Refund of 50 % of the fee on passing B1 (DTZ) within 2 years
Travel reimbursement is possible for a long journey
Apply for the exemption or refund — through the BAMF

content.text: The 50 % refund does not happen automatically: you must pass the DTZ at level B1 within 2 years of your authorisation (Berechtigung) and submit an application to the BAMF. Don't delay the exam or enrolment — the two-year period counts from the date of authorisation, not from the start of classes.

costs.label: Integrationskurs (self-payment)
costs.note: 2.29 €/hour; ~1603 € for 700 h. On benefits/low income — exemption (0 €).

costs.label: Refund on passing B1 within 2 years
costs.note: 50 % of the fee paid is refunded through the BAMF on passing the DTZ at B1 in time.

costs.label: DTZ / 'Leben in Deutschland' test
costs.note: For course participants the final exams are part of the programme; a retake may be chargeable.

title: BAMF course vs private schools
tldr: You can learn German through a state integration course (Integrationskurs) from the BAMF (§43 AufenthG) or at a private language school. The BAMF course is cheap (2,29 €/hour, ~1603 € for the whole course, often free) and gives you access to the official DTZ/B1 exams, but the pace is steady and the groups are large. Private schools (the Goethe-Institut, telc partners and others) are faster, more flexible on schedule and go up to C1/C2, but more expensive (often several times over). The choice depends on your status, budget, speed and goal — integration or, say, a visa or job that needs C1.

content.text: The integration course (Integrationskurs) from the BAMF (§43 AufenthG) is a system with a clear goal: bring you up to B1 and teach you about society. Its strengths are the price and the way it's built into the bureaucracy: the course leads to the official DTZ exam, and the result counts towards permanent residence and citizenship. Its weaknesses are the pace and flexibility: groups are large, the schedule is fixed, and the ceiling is usually B1.

items: Cheap: 2,29 €/hour, often free if you receive benefits or have a low income
Access to the DTZ and the 'Leben in Deutschland' test
The result counts towards permanent residence and citizenship
Downside: a steady pace, large groups, a B1 ceiling
Downside: enrolment and admission go through the BAMF/Ausländerbehörde (bureaucracy)

content.text: Private language schools — the Goethe-Institut, telc partner schools, local courses — offer flexibility: intensive courses, evening groups, one-on-one lessons and levels all the way to C1/C2. They get you to a result faster if you need a high level for work or a visa. The main downside is cost: an intensive module can run to several hundred euros, and the full path to C1 is noticeably more expensive than a BAMF course.

items: Flexibility: intensive, evening, online and one-on-one lessons
Levels up to C1/C2 — for work, study or a visa
Small groups, faster results
Downside: expensive (often several times more than the BAMF course)
They prepare you for the Goethe-Zertifikat and telc exams

content.text: A school certificate and a passed exam are not the same thing. For official purposes (residence permit, permanent residence, citizenship, diploma recognition) the authorities accept only standardised certificates (telc, Goethe, ÖSD, TestDaF), not a 'course attendance note'. Check EXACTLY which exam the school prepares you for.

steps.title: How to choose for your situation

content.text: The decision comes down to three things: your status (whether you have a right or an obligation to take an integration course), your budget and the level you need. For many people it makes sense to start with a BAMF course up to B1 (cheap, and it counts towards your status) and then top up to C1 at a private school or on a professional language course (Berufssprachkurs) under §45a AufenthG if needed.

items: You have the right/obligation and B1 is enough → BAMF Integrationskurs
You need C1 for work/study quickly → a private school or intensive course
You need professional German → Berufssprachkurs §45a (often free)
Budget is tight → BAMF + self-study
Goal is an official certificate → pick the course for the exam you need (telc/Goethe)

content.text: Don't pay for an expensive private intensive course if your status entitles you to a free or nearly free integration course. First check your entitlement to a BAMF course (§44 AufenthG) and the option of a Berufssprachkurs (§45a AufenthG) — it can save you more than a thousand euros.

costs.label: BAMF Integrationskurs
costs.note: 2,29 €/hour; ~1603 € for 700 h, often free with an exemption.

costs.label: Private school (intensive module)
costs.note: Per module/level; the full path to C1 is noticeably more expensive.

costs.label: telc / Goethe-Zertifikat exam
costs.note: The price depends on the level (A1–C2) and the centre.

title: Fachsprachprüfung for doctors
tldr: To obtain a licence to practise medicine (Approbation; the authorisation to work as a doctor) in Germany, a foreign doctor must prove not only general German at B2 but also professional medical language — through the Fachsprachprüfung (FSP), a specialised exam at C1 level. It is administered by the state medical chambers (Ärztekammer). The exam simulates a real consultation: a conversation with a 'patient', documentation (Arztbrief) and a conversation with a 'colleague'. It usually costs 350–700 € depending on the state. This is a separate stage on top of qualification recognition.

content.text: The Fachsprachprüfung (FSP) is an exam in professional medical German, mandatory for foreigners to obtain a licence to practise medicine (Approbation; the full authorisation to work as a doctor). It tests not general language (that's proven with a B2 certificate) but the ability to work in German in a clinic: to understand the patient, keep records and communicate with colleagues at C1 level. The exam is administered by the state medical chambers (Ärztekammer).

items: The FSP is an exam in medical German (C1 level)
Mandatory for the Approbation of foreign doctors
Administered by the state medical chambers (Landesärztekammer)
General B2 is proven with a separate certificate (telc/Goethe)
The FSP is about language in the clinic, not medical knowledge as such

content.text: The exam simulates a doctor's working day and consists of three parts of about 20 minutes each. It's not a tick-box test but a set of role-play situations, with examiners playing the patient and the colleague.

items: Taking a 'patient's' history in everyday German
You need to understand complaints phrased in plain words
Being able to explain things without Latin terms
Writing down the history and the plan
Using correct medical terminology
A structured medical document
Presenting the case to a 'colleague' in specialist vocabulary
Translating everyday complaints into professional terms
Discussing the diagnosis and treatment plan

content.text: A common mistake candidates make is overestimating their general German. You can have everyday C1 and still fail the FSP because you can't switch between the 'patient's language' and the 'colleagues' language'. Prepare specifically for the two registers: plain language for the conversation with the patient, and professional language for the documentation and the case report.

steps.title: Registration, cost, link to the Approbation

content.text: You register for the FSP at the medical chamber (Ärztekammer) of the federal state where you will apply for the Approbation. The cost and details vary by state — roughly 350-700€. The FSP is just one of the stages: the Approbation also requires recognition of your qualification (Anerkennung der Ausbildung), a general German certificate (usually B2) and, for graduates from outside the EU, often a medical-knowledge exam (Kenntnisprüfung).

items: Registration — at the Landesärztekammer of the relevant state
The cost is usually 350–700 € (depends on the state)
Besides the FSP you need: general B2, qualification recognition, sometimes a Kenntnisprüfung
If you fail the FSP you can retake it (often after a break)
Special 'Deutsch für Mediziner' courses and the Berufssprachkurs Pflege/Medizin help you prepare

content.text: Don't confuse the FSP (language) with the medical-knowledge exam (Kenntnisprüfung) — these are different exams on the way to the Approbation. And note: to prepare for medical German there are specialised professional language courses (Berufssprachkurse) under §45a AufenthG (Medizin/Pflege modules) that are free if you meet the conditions.

costs.label: Fachsprachprüfung (FSP)
costs.note: Depends on the federal state and Ärztekammer (2026: from €350 in Nordrhein to €700 in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern).

costs.label: General German B2 certificate (telc/Goethe)
costs.note: A separate exam, required for the Approbation in addition to the FSP (telc B2 ~€229, Goethe B2 €289, 2026).

costs.label: Deutsch für Mediziner preparatory course
costs.note: Private intensive courses are paid; Berufssprachkurs §45a modules can be free.

sources.title: Marburger Bund — Kosten der Fachsprachenprüfung (C1) nach Bundesländern
Anerkennung in Deutschland — Approbation als Arzt/Ärztin
telc — Deutsch B2·C1 Medizin (Fachsprachprüfung für Mediziner)

title: ÖSD: the Austrian certificate accepted in Germany
tldr: ÖSD (Österreichisches Sprachdiplom Deutsch) is an Austrian system of German exams that is also recognised in Germany on a par with telc and Goethe. ÖSD certificates at levels A1–C2 are accepted by German authorities for a residence permit, family reunification, permanent residence and citizenship (wherever proof of German is required — for example §9 AufenthG for permanent residence and §10 StAG for naturalisation). The exams are taken at accredited centres worldwide, which is handy if you're still abroad. They usually cost 80–200 € depending on the level and the country.

content.text: ÖSD (Österreichisches Sprachdiplom Deutsch) is the official Austrian system of German-language exams, covering levels from A1 to C2 on the common European scale (GER). It is a full-fledged international German certificate, alongside the Goethe-Zertifikat and telc. ÖSD exams are taken at certified exam centres in Austria, Germany and dozens of other countries.

items: ÖSD is an Austrian German diploma (A1–C2)
Maps to the GER levels, like telc and Goethe
Taken at accredited centres worldwide
There are integration variants (e.g. the ÖSD Integrationsprüfung)
Recognised outside Austria, including in Germany

content.text: Yes. German authorities generally recognise ÖSD certificates on a par with telc and Goethe, because all of them are tied to the single GER scale and the ALTE association's standards. ÖSD works wherever German law requires proof of a language level: for example A1 for spousal reunification (§30 AufenthG), B1 for permanent residence (Niederlassungserlaubnis, §9 AufenthG) and for citizenship (§10 StAG).

items: A1 — often for family reunification (Ehegattennachzug)
B1 — for permanent residence (Niederlassungserlaubnis, §9 AufenthG) and citizenship (§10 StAG)
B2/C1 — for work, study and qualification recognition
ÖSD is recognised on a par with telc/Goethe on the GER scale
If the authority requires a specific certificate — check in advance

content.text: Sometimes a specific authority or university requires one particular certificate (for example only telc or only Goethe for a certain procedure). ÖSD is widely accepted, but before you pay for the exam check with the target authority that it accepts ÖSD at the level you need — this saves you from having to retake it.

steps.title: How to take it and what it costs

content.text: Find an accredited ÖSD exam centre (Prüfungszentrum) on the official ÖSD website — there are some in Germany and abroad. Register for the level you need and pay the fee. The exam has four parts: reading, listening, writing and speaking. The convenience of ÖSD is that its centres are spread around the world, so you can get the certificate even before you move.

items: Find an ÖSD Prüfungszentrum at osd.at
Register for the level you need (A1–C2)
The cost is usually 80–200 € (depends on the level and the country)
Structure: reading, listening, writing, speaking
The certificate has no expiry date (but authorities like 'fresh' results)

content.text: An ÖSD certificate is valid indefinitely, but in practice some procedures (for example qualification recognition or extending a status) want a result no older than 1–2 years. If you took the exam a long time ago, check whether it will be accepted before you file your documents.

costs.label: ÖSD exam (A1–B1)
costs.note: Lower levels; depends on the centre and the country where you take it.

costs.label: ÖSD exam (B2–C2)
costs.note: Higher levels are usually more expensive.

costs.label: Retaking individual modules
costs.note: At many centres you can retake individual parts; the price is lower than for the full exam.

sources.title: §44 AufenthG — Berechtigung zur Teilnahme (context of language requirements)

title: Top 10 apps and websites for self-study
tldr: Free and paid resources help you learn German on your own. The free flagship is DW (Deutsche Welle) Learn German: complete A1–C1 courses, the "Nicos Weg" series, grammar and podcasts. The Goethe-Institut offers exercises and practice tests, and the VHS-Lernportal (run by the association of adult education centres) prepares you for the DTZ for free. Apps like Duolingo, Babbel and Anki are good for vocabulary and for building a daily habit. Self-study is a great complement to the integration course (Integrationskurs), but for official purposes you still need a certificate (telc/Goethe/ÖSD).

content.text: Start with the free, high-quality official platforms. Their strength is that the material is structured by CEFR level (A1–C1) and is often tailored specifically to life in Germany and to the DTZ exam (the German test that you sit at the end of the integration course).

items: DW Learn German (dw.com/learngerman) — A1–C1 courses, the "Nicos Weg" series, podcasts — free
VHS-Lernportal — free preparation for the DTZ and the Integrationskurs
Goethe-Institut — free exercises, grammar, practice tests
DLF "Nachrichten leicht" (Deutschlandfunk) — the news in simple German
ARD/ZDF Mediathek with subtitles — listening practice with real language

steps.title: Apps for vocabulary and building a habit

content.text: Mobile apps work best not as your only source, but as a way to study 10–15 minutes every day and build up your vocabulary. They are great for filling the gaps between course lessons.

items: Duolingo — gamification, a daily habit (free with ads)
Babbel — dialogues and grammar, designed for adults (subscription)
Anki — flashcards with spaced repetition, free (powerful for vocabulary)
Memrise / Quizlet — word sets, including for exams
Seedlang / Tandem — practice with native speakers and live conversation

content.text: Don't make Duolingo your only method. Gamified apps are good at training word recognition, but weak at developing writing and spontaneous speech. For B1 and above, combine them with a course, conversation practice (Tandem) and DW/VHS materials.

steps.title: How to combine them, and where self-study reaches its limit

content.text: The ideal is to combine three things: a structured course (DW Learn German or the integration course) for grammar, apps (Anki/Duolingo) for daily vocabulary, and live practice (Tandem, conversation clubs) for speaking. But remember: no app issues a certificate that the authorities recognise.

items: Structure: DW Learn German or the integration course as your foundation
Vocabulary every day: Anki/Duolingo/Memrise
Speaking: Tandem, conversation clubs, language meetups
Listening: DW podcasts, the news in simple German
For official purposes — a telc/Goethe/ÖSD certificate, not "progress in an app"

content.text: Progress in an app is not the same as a certificate. For a residence permit, permanent residence (§9 AufenthG), family reunification and citizenship, the authorities require an official level certificate (telc, Goethe, ÖSD) or a DTZ result. Self-study prepares you for the exam, but you still have to sit the exam itself.

costs.label: DW Learn German / VHS-Lernportal
costs.note: Completely free official platforms (A1–C1, DTZ preparation).

costs.label: Paid apps (Babbel etc.)
costs.note: Approximate monthly subscription; Duolingo and Anki have free versions.

costs.label: Official certificate (telc/Goethe/ÖSD)
costs.note: Needed for official purposes; depends on the level and the centre.

title: AOK: regional ties
tldr: The AOK is not a single fund but 11 independent regional health insurance funds (Krankenkassen: AOK Bayern, AOK Nordost, etc.). You can only join the AOK whose region covers your place of residence or work. In 2026 the additional contributions vary from one AOK to another: from roughly 2.5% to 3.7%.

steps.title: What the AOK is and why it is "regional"

content.text: The AOK (Allgemeine Ortskrankenkasse) is the largest public health insurance system (GKV) in Germany: around 27 million members in total. Legally it is made up of 11 independent health insurance funds (Krankenkassen), each with its own statutes, budget, additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) and bonus programme. The logo and name are shared, but each fund keeps its own balance sheet.

items: 11 regional AOKs cover all 16 federal states
Each AOK sets its own additional contribution (the 2026 GKV average is 2.9%)
The base rate is the same: 14.6% of gross, split 50/50 with the employer
Bonus programmes and extras (PZR, osteopathy, vaccinations) differ

content.text: Which fund you join is determined by your place of residence (Wohnort) or, in some cases, your place of work (Beschäftigungsort). You can't simply live in NRW and stay with AOK Bayern — the law, §173 SGB V, allows only justified exceptions (for example, keeping your fund for a transitional period after a move).

items: AOK Baden-Württemberg — Baden-Württemberg
AOK Bayern — Bavaria
AOK Bremen/Bremerhaven — Bremen
AOK Hessen — Hesse
AOK Niedersachsen — Lower Saxony
AOK Nordost — Berlin, Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
AOK NordWest — Schleswig-Holstein and Westphalia-Lippe
AOK PLUS — Saxony and Thuringia
AOK Rheinland/Hamburg — Rhineland and Hamburg
AOK Rheinland-Pfalz/Saarland — Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland
AOK Sachsen-Anhalt — Saxony-Anhalt

content.text: Joining is completely free. If you are already with another health insurance fund, your new AOK cancels the old contract (Kündigung) for you — you don't have to write to anyone separately. The minimum membership period with your current fund is 12 months, and the notice period is 2 months to the end of the month. Exceptions: changing jobs, and the special right of termination (Sonderkündigungsrecht) when the additional contribution goes up.
Go to aok.de — the site will work out your region from your postcode and suggest your local AOK.

items: Application online on the AOK website
Passport / residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) details
Tax identification number (Steuer-ID), if you already have one
A certificate (Bescheinigung) from your employer, or proof of self-employment (Selbständigkeit) or student status

content.text: The AOK issues a proof of membership within 1–3 working days — your employer needs it to calculate your contributions. The plastic electronic health card (Gesundheitskarte, eGK) arrives by post within 1–3 weeks.

The additional contribution varies from one AOK to another by 0.5–1 percentage point. For example, AOK Bayern and AOK PLUS are traditionally cheaper than the nationwide funds, while AOK Nordost is above average. Before joining, check the current rate on the fund's website.
If you move to another state, you can keep your fund, but it is usually more convenient to switch to the local AOK: service branches (Geschäftsstelle) nearby, direct contracts with local clinics.
Each AOK has its own bonus programme (Bonusprogramm): AOK PLUS gives up to 600€/year, AOK Bayern up to 250€. Don't mix them up when comparing.

costs.label: Base GKV contribution
costs.note: % of gross salary, split 50/50 with the employer

costs.label: Average Zusatzbeitrag 2026
costs.note: % — between the different AOKs from ~2.5% to ~3.7%; split 50/50

costs.label: Joining and switching
costs.note: Free; the new fund cancels the old one itself

title: 116117 — a doctor at home after hours
tldr: 116117 is the single nationwide number for the medical on-call service (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst): unscheduled care when doctors' offices are closed but it is not a life-threatening emergency. Free, around the clock. There is an official "116117.app" from the KBV.

steps.title: What it is and when to call

content.text: 116117 is the medical on-call service (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst) run by the National Association of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians (Kassenärztliche Bundesvereinigung, KBV). Use it when your condition needs a doctor but is not life-threatening and your family doctor's office (Hausarzt) is already closed: in the evening, at night, at weekends and on public holidays. The call is free and works across the whole of Germany.

items: 116117 is NOT an ambulance. For a life-threatening emergency (heart attack, stroke, road accident, severe bleeding) call 112 only
Works 24/7 across all of Germany
Free from mobile and landline phones
No area code, no prefix

content.text: The operator works through a checklist of questions, assesses how urgent your case is and offers one of several types of help. A medical professional makes the decision, not you.
If the case is not acute — a telephone consultation, advice on taking medication or on waiting until your family doctor's office opens.
An on-call practice (often at a hospital) — they will give you the nearest address and its opening hours.
If you are hard to transport (the elderly, children with a high fever, people with reduced mobility) — they will send a doctor to your home.
If the operator judges the situation to be life-threatening — they will transfer you to the emergency ambulance service.

The official "116117.app" (developed by KBV/kv.digital) is available in the App Store and on Google Play. Through it you can book appointments (Termine) with general practitioners, gynaecologists, eye doctors, paediatricians and psychotherapists, search for on-call practices, and filter by accessibility (Barrierefreiheit) and by the languages a doctor speaks.

items: Search for online appointments with statutory-insurance doctors (Kassenärzte), using the public insurance card (GKV)
Map of on-call practices with directions
Filter by the doctor's language (Russian, English, etc.)
Direct 112 call from the home screen

content.text: At peak times (Friday evening, weekends) the wait for an operator can be 10–20 minutes. Have the essentials ready in advance: your address, your symptoms, your insurance number (on your electronic health card, eGK).

An on-call practice is not the same as a hospital emergency department (Notaufnahme). If you go to the emergency department without a life-threatening condition, you may be sent to the on-call practice across the way.
Privately insured people (under private health insurance, PKV) can also call 116117 — the service is for everyone; billing is handled separately.

costs.label: 116117 call
costs.note: Free from mobile and landline across all of Germany

costs.label: 116117.app
costs.note: Free, iOS and Android

costs.note: Covered by public insurance; for private insurance — billed according to the tariff

title: Barmer: signing up and services
tldr: Barmer is the second-largest health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) in Germany (~8.7 million members), operating nationwide (bundesweit). You can join online in 5 minutes, with no paperwork. Bonus of up to 200€/year, Geld-zurück-Tarife of up to 1350€ over 3 years, Teledoktor 24/7.

content.text: Barmer is one of the largest substitute funds (Ersatzkassen), operating across all of Germany, and you can join no matter which state you live in. In 2026 the base rate of public health insurance (GKV) is 14.6% plus the Barmer additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) (check it on the website; the 2026 GKV average is 2.9%). Split 50/50 with the employer.

items: Bundesweit — no regional ties, unlike the AOK
Around 8.7 million members
Full GKV package: doctors, hospital, medication, prevention, rehabilitation
Free family coverage (Familienversicherung) for a spouse/children when their income is below the limit

steps.title: How to submit the Mitgliedsantrag online

content.text: The online form at barmer.de/mitglied-werden takes 5–10 minutes. You don't need to upload any documents — verification is done via your tax identification number (Steuer-ID) and address. If you are already with another health insurance fund, Barmer cancels the old contract for you — no letters required from you.

items: Full name, date of birth, address
Tax identification number (11 digits)
Employer details or status (student / self-employed / unemployed)
IBAN for possible refunds

content.text: On the barmer.de website — the Online-Aufnahmeantrag. You can sign it electronically, with no paper post.

The electronic proof of membership (Mitgliedsbescheinigung) arrives by email within 1–2 days. You give it to your employer. The electronic health card (Gesundheitskarte, eGK) comes by post within 1–3 weeks.
Barmer actively promotes "Meine Barmer" — an app and web portal for sick notes, appointments, the bonus programme and messaging with the fund. Extra perks on top of the basic GKV package:

items: Barmer Bonus — up to 200€/year for check-ups, sport, vaccinations
Geld-zurück-Tarife — up to 1 350€ back over 3 years for healthy behaviour
Reiseimpfungen Plus — 100% coverage of recommended travel vaccinations
Teledoktor 24/7 — telephone consultation with German doctors
Zuschuss of up to 200€/year for certified courses (yoga, nutrition, quitting smoking)

content.text: Barmer is traditionally a little more expensive than the cheapest regional company health insurance funds (BKK). If saving 0.3–0.5% of gross matters to you — compare first at gkv-zusatzbeitrag.de.
Professional teeth cleaning (PZR) is only partially covered by Barmer, via the bonus programme. Check the current amount before your visit.
The minimum membership period is 12 months. Special right of termination (Sonderkündigungsrecht): if Barmer raises the additional contribution, you can leave without the 2-month notice period.

title: BKK: company health insurance funds
tldr: BKK (Betriebskrankenkassen) are company health insurance funds, around 70 of them, originally set up at large employers (Siemens, VW, Bosch). Today most are open to everyone. They often have the lowest additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) in the public health insurance system (GKV) — from around 2.18%.

steps.title: What a BKK is and who it suits

content.text: A BKK (Betriebskrankenkasse) is a company health insurance fund, historically open only to the employees of a single employer. Since 1996 BKKs have been allowed to open up to the general public (open, geöffnete BKK). Today most are open to everyone, either nationwide (bundesweit) or in several states. There are around 70 BKKs in the system and about 8.8 million members, coordinated by the umbrella association BKK Dachverband.

items: Around 70 BKKs in the system, ~8.8 million members
Most are open (geöffnet) — anyone can join, not only an employee
Some BKKs remain closed (geschlossen) — only for the company's employees
The same range of public-insurance services as AOK/TK/Barmer

content.text: The best-known nationwide open BKKs, which are easy to join online:

items: BKK VBU — bundesweit, among the leaders on price
BKK Mobil Oil — bundesweit, active digital services
BKK firmus — bundesweit, known for its low additional contribution
BKK ProVita — bundesweit, a focus on prevention
Siemens BKK (SBK) — bundesweit, one of the largest BKKs
BKK24 — bundesweit, a strong online service branch (Online-Geschäftsstelle)
Audi BKK — almost all states, historically part of the Volkswagen group

content.text: The main thing to compare is the additional contribution (in 2026 the GKV average is 2.9%, with the BKK spread running from 2.18% to 4.39%). After that, look at bonuses, the limits on professional teeth cleaning (PZR), osteopathy and homeopathy, and the optional plans (Wahltarife).
At gkv-zusatzbeitrag.de or test.de — a table of all health insurance funds with their current rates.
On the BKK's website or at bkk-dachverband.de, check whether the fund is open in your region.

items: Name, address, date of birth
Tax identification number (Steuer-ID)
Employer or status
Signature (often electronic)

content.text: Proof of membership (Mitgliedsbescheinigung) — within 1–3 days by email. The electronic health card (Gesundheitskarte) — by post within 1–3 weeks.
Closed BKKs (geschlossen) are not for everyone. If your employer is not on the list of participants, your application will be refused.
Small BKKs sometimes merge with one another or with larger funds. This costs you nothing, but services may be reorganised (the app, bonus programmes).
A cheap rate doesn't always mean a saving. If the fund doesn't cover professional teeth cleaning, osteopathy or alternative methods, the real saving shrinks.

title: Bonusheft: a discount on crowns
tldr: The bonus booklet (Bonusheft) is a paper or electronic booklet recording your regular dental visits. Under §55 SGB V, regular check-ups raise the base fixed subsidy (Festzuschuss) for dental prosthetics (Zahnersatz): 5 years without gaps — by 20% (70% of the standard in total), 10 years — by 30% (75% in total). Without a bonus booklet, in 2026 the fund pays the basic 60%. From 1 January 2027 the rates are due to fall: the GKV-Beitragssatzstabilisierungsgesetz was approved by the Cabinet on 29.04.2026, but is still going through the Bundestag/Bundesrat — the final text may change, so check that it is up to date.

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: The bonus booklet is a personal record of your regular preventive dental visits. It is governed by §65a SGB V and §55 SGB V. The fund uses it to work out the share of coverage for dental prosthetics (crowns, bridges, dentures). The longer you have attended check-ups without gaps, the higher the fixed subsidy — the payment from public health insurance (GKV) towards the standard base model of treatment.

items: The bonus booklet is free, issued by any dentist (Zahnarzt)
1 visit a year for adults, 2 a year for children and teenagers
The dentist adds a stamp at each check-up
You can keep it on paper, or some funds offer an electronic bonus booklet (E-Bonusheft) in the app (the MIO standard from the National Association of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians, KBV)

content.text: Public insurance covers not "a percentage of your bill" but a fixed subsidy — a fixed amount tied to the standard treatment option (Regelversorgung). The dentist's actual bill depends on the model you choose: a standard resin crown, metal-bonded ceramic, or all-ceramic. The fixed subsidy stays the same — the difference is at your own expense.

items: Without a bonus booklet — the basic 60% of the fixed subsidy for the standard cost (current 2026)
5 years of regular visits — a bonus of +20%, 70% in total
10 years of regular visits — a bonus of +30%, 75% in total
Hardship rule (Härtefallregelung): on a low income the fund covers 100% of the standard treatment
From 1 January 2027 the rates are due to fall to 50% / 60% / 65% (GKV-Beitragssatzstabilisierungsgesetz, approved by the Cabinet on 29.04.2026, at the Bundestag/Bundesrat stage)

steps.title: How to keep it and present it correctly

content.text: The rules are simple, but the details matter: the dentist enters the date, not you. A gap of even a couple of months resets the 5-year or 10-year counter.
Just ask your dentist at your first visit: "Bitte ein Bonusheft" — it is issued free of charge.

items.title: 2. Have at least 1 check-up a year

content.text: Once per calendar year: 1 visit for each year. It's best to book it for around the same date so you don't miss it.

items.title: 3. Before prosthetic treatment — a treatment and cost plan (Heil- und Kostenplan, HKP)

content.text: The dentist draws up a treatment and cost plan, and you send it to your health insurance fund with a copy of the bonus booklet attached. The fund then approves the fixed subsidy and the amount you have to pay.
When the pages run out, you are issued a new one — don't throw the old one away, you'll need it to prove the 10-year bonus.
One missed year resets the 5/10-year counter. It counts by calendar year, not "12 months from your last visit".
Professional teeth cleaning (PZR) does NOT count as a check-up (Kontrolltermin). The stamp in the bonus booklet is given specifically for a check-up (Kontrolle), not for a cleaning.
When you change dentists, always bring your bonus booklet with you — the new dentist doesn't have your old stamps in their system.

If the 2027 reform comes into force, having a bonus booklet will still be more advantageous than not having one — but the absolute amount of the fixed subsidy will fall (60% → 50%, 70% → 60%, 75% → 65%). The hardship rule for low-income people is retained. Expensive prosthetics with a medical indication are worth planning before the changes.

costs.note: Free, issued by any dentist

costs.label: Check-up (Kontrolltermin)
costs.note: Covered by GKV with no co-payment

costs.label: Standard crown (standard treatment, Regelversorgung)
costs.note: Of which public insurance covers 60–75% via the fixed subsidy

costs.label: Surcharge for a ceramic crown
costs.note: On top of the fixed subsidy, at your own expense

title: DAK-Gesundheit: app and services
tldr: DAK-Gesundheit is the third-largest substitute fund (Ersatzkasse) in the public health insurance system (GKV). The "DAK App" replaces visits to the service branch (Geschäftsstelle): you can upload bills, order certificates, use video consultations and the AktivBonus bonus programme.

content.text: DAK-Gesundheit is a nationwide health insurance fund (bundesweit-Krankenkasse) with around 5.4 million members. It offers the full public-insurance (GKV) package; check the additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) at dak.de (the 2026 GKV average is 2.9%). DAK's strength is its digital services and its video link with doctors through the DAK App.

items: Bundesweit, anyone can join
DAK App: iOS / Android, free
Video consultation with a doctor (DAK Online-Videosprechstunde)
AktivBonus — up to 250€/year for a healthy lifestyle
A separate DAK ePA-App — the electronic patient record (ePA)

steps.title: What the DAK App can do

content.text: Secure login via the digital health ID (GesundheitsID), face or fingerprint. Once registered, you can do almost everything that used to require a visit to the service branch.

items: Upload bills and receipts straight from your camera — refunded to your account
Order a temporary proof of insurance (Ersatzbescheinigung) if your electronic health card (eGK) is lost
Report a change of address / surname / IBAN
Apply for a new electronic health card (Gesundheitskarte)
Manage the AktivBonus bonus programme
Use the online video appointment (Online-Videosprechstunde) — a video link with a doctor
Handle matters relating to children under family coverage (Familienversicherung)
Get personalised reminders for preventive check-ups (Vorsorgeuntersuchungen)

steps.title: How to register in the DAK App

content.text: Registration takes 5–15 minutes. The fastest route is via the online ID (Online-Ausweis) or the digital health ID (GesundheitsID). The alternative is video identification (Video-Ident) or identification at the post office (PostIdent).
App Store (id1333473784) or Google Play (de.dak.dak_app). Free.

items: Digital health ID (GesundheitsID) — recommended
Online ID (Online-Ausweis) — the eID function of your national ID card (Personalausweis) with a PIN
Video identification with a DAK staff member
Identification at the post office (PostIdent) at a Deutsche Post branch

content.text: For the online ID you need a national ID card with an activated eID and a 6-digit PIN. For the digital health ID — an electronic health card with a PIN from the fund.
From then on — Face ID/Touch ID for quick, password-free login.
The DAK App and the DAK ePA-App are two different apps. The electronic patient record (ePA, elektronische Patientenakte) is a separate app, for your medical data and for sharing it with doctors.
You have to order the PIN for the electronic health card from DAK separately (via the website or the App). It isn't issued by default.
The online video appointment works only during the service's opening hours, not 24/7. At night — call 116117.

title: The dentist: what public insurance (GKV) covers and what it doesn't
tldr: Public health insurance (GKV) covers basic dentistry in full: check-ups, treating cavities (amalgam/resin in the back teeth), extractions, emergencies. Professional teeth cleaning (PZR), white fillings in the back teeth, implants and ceramics — at your own expense. Inpatient stay: 10€/day, maximum 280€/year.

content.text: Basic dentistry (zahnärztliche Grundversorgung) is paid in full by the fund — with no patient co-payment (Zuzahlung), once you have shown your electronic health card (eGK). It is governed by §28 SGB V and the framework agreement with dentists (Bundesmantelvertrag-Zahnärzte).

items: 1 check-up a year for adults (for the entry in the bonus booklet, Bonusheft)
2 check-ups a year for children and teenagers under 18
Cavity treatment: amalgam in the back teeth, white composites in the front teeth
Tooth extractions and surgical procedures
Root canal treatment (Wurzelkanalbehandlung), provided the tooth can be saved
Periodontitis treatment (Parodontitis-Therapie, PAR-Behandlung) — expanded since 2021
Prevention for children (Individualprophylaxe, IP1–IP5)
Local anaesthesia for covered procedures

content.text: Anything above the "standard" (the standard treatment, Regelversorgung) is at your own expense. This applies to materials, aesthetic options and most preventive services beyond the necessary minimum.

items: Professional teeth cleaning (PZR, professionelle Zahnreinigung): 80–150€ per session, recommended 1–2 times a year
White fillings in the back teeth: a surcharge of 30–80€ per tooth
Ceramic crowns: 300–800€ surcharge on top of the fixed subsidy (Festzuschuss)
All-ceramic bridges: 500–1500€ surcharge per unit
Implants: 1500–3000€ per tooth — public insurance only pays the fixed subsidy for the crown on top of the implant
Whitening (Bleaching): 300–800€, entirely at your own expense
Bruxism splints: partially; non-standard ones — a surcharge
Orthodontics for adults: only at KIG 3+ (severe cases), otherwise at your own expense

content.text: Patient co-payments are governed by §61 SGB V. Importantly, for most outpatient dental services there is no co-payment at all. It only comes up for an inpatient stay and for certain types of prosthetics.

items.title: Inpatient stay at an oral and maxillofacial clinic (Kieferklinik)

content.text: 10€/day, maximum 28 days a year = 280€/year. Counted across all hospitals combined.

10% of the price, minimum 5€, maximum 10€ per pack (current in 2026). From 2027 the threshold is due to rise to 7,50€ / 15€ — the GKV-Beitragssatzstabilisierungsgesetz was approved by the Cabinet on 29.04.2026 and is going through the Bundestag/Bundesrat; watch for the final version.
Not a "patient co-payment", but the difference between the actual bill and the fixed subsidy (see the guide on the bonus booklet).

The fund is obliged to exempt you from co-payments above the cap: 2% of your annual gross income (1% for the chronically ill). On a low income, submit an application for exemption (Antrag auf Befreiung) to your health insurance fund, attaching your receipts — you will receive an exemption notice (Befreiungsbescheid) for the rest of the year.

items: General cap: 2% of annual gross
Chronically ill (chronisch krank under §62 SGB V): 1% of annual gross
Children under 18: no co-payment is charged at all
Hardship rule (Härtefallregelung) for dental prosthetics: if income is below the threshold — 100% of the standard treatment

content.text: Before expensive treatment (dental prosthetics, an implant), always request a treatment and cost plan (Heil- und Kostenplan, HKP) and send it to the fund BEFORE you start. Otherwise there is a risk that the fixed subsidy won't be approved. If the fund refuses or approves less than expected, you can file an objection (Widerspruch) to its decision within a month.

Professional teeth cleaning is not covered by public insurance as a mandatory service (Pflichtleistung) — but around 90% of funds give a voluntary contribution (Zuschuss) of 40–120€/year. Check specifically with your own: on its website or via the App.

Remember: a "private service" (Privatleistung) on a dental bill means out of your own pocket. You sign a separate document — an additional-cost agreement (Mehrkostenvereinbarung) — before treatment begins.
Without a bonus booklet, you lose 10–15% of the subsidy on a crown. Keep it from your very first visit.

title: E-Rezept: the electronic prescription
tldr: Since 1 January 2024, all prescriptions charged to the fund (Kassenrezepte) for prescription medicines have been issued electronically. You can collect them at any pharmacy: with your electronic health card (eGK) via NFC, through the "Das E-Rezept" app from the gematik agency, or with a printed paper code. This guide shows how to set up the App and pick up prescriptions in one tap.

content.text: The E-Rezept is the official standard for the electronic prescription in the public health insurance system (GKV). It was developed by the gematik agency (the national digital health agency). Since 01.01.2024 doctors have been required to use it for all prescriptions charged to the fund. The validity period is the same 28 days when charged to the fund, and up to 3 months as a self-pay prescription (Selbstzahler-Rezept).

items: Mandatory for all statutory-insurance doctors (Kassenärzte) since 1 January 2024
Covers prescription-only (pharmacy-only, apothekenpflichtig) medicines
Does not abolish paper prescriptions in specific cases (narcotic BtM, T-Rezept, private)
Validity: 28 days charged to the fund, then up to 3 months at your own expense
Can be collected at any pharmacy in Germany, including online pharmacies

steps.title: Three ways to get your medicine

content.text: You decide on the spot, whichever is more convenient. All three options are equally valid.

items.title: 1. With the electronic health card (Gesundheitskarte, eGK)

content.text: The simplest way: go to the pharmacy and place your electronic health card on the reader. The pharmacist sees your prescriptions and dispenses the medicine. No app and no PIN needed.

You download the App from gematik (iOS 16+ or Android), log in with your electronic health card + PIN, and see your prescriptions. You can send a prescription to a pharmacy online and simply come in to pick it up, or order delivery.

items.title: 3. With a printout of the token code (Token): QR/PIN code

content.text: If you don't have the App and don't want to hand over your electronic health card — the doctor prints out a token (Token): a QR code + a 12-digit code. You take this slip to the pharmacy like an ordinary prescription.

steps.title: How to set up the E-Rezept App

content.text: The most convenient method is the App, but it requires a one-time setup. To log in you need an electronic health card with NFC, a PIN from your fund and an NFC-compatible smartphone (most iPhones and Android phones made after 2016).

items.title: 1. Order a PIN from your fund

content.text: The PIN doesn't come with the electronic health card by default. Order it in your fund's online portal (Meine TK, Meine AOK, Meine Barmer, etc.) or at a service branch (Geschäftsstelle). It arrives by post within 1–2 weeks.
"Das E-Rezept" from gematik — free in the App Store and on Google Play. Minimum iOS 16.

items: Enter the 6-digit access number (Zugangsnummer) on the front of the electronic health card
Enter the PIN (6–8 digits)
Hold the electronic health card against the back of your smartphone (NFC) — keep it there for 10–15 sec
Confirm the link

content.text: Go to the Rezepte (Prescriptions) section → select a prescription → "Einlösen" (Redeem) → choose a pharmacy (on the map) → pick it up or get it by courier.
You can't log in to the App without a PIN. The most common problem for newcomers is trying to log in with just the electronic health card and no PIN. Order the PIN in advance.
Prescriptions for narcotic painkillers (BtM prescriptions), the T-Rezept (thalidomide, etc.) and private prescriptions (Privatrezepte) are still on paper for now. The E-Rezept does not abolish them.
The patient co-payment (Zuzahlung) still applies: 10% of the price, min 5€, max 10€ per pack (2026). You pay it at the pharmacy regardless of how you present the prescription.

For privately insured people (under private health insurance, PKV), the E-Rezept is still optional, and many private insurers are not yet connected to the gematik network. You will more often get a paper private prescription (Privatrezept).

costs.note: Free from gematik, iOS and Android

costs.label: PIN for the eGK
costs.note: Free from your fund — order it separately
