title: eGK — the electronic health card
tldr: The eGK (elektronische Gesundheitskarte) is the plastic card from your health insurer that you show at every doctor's visit. It carries your photo, name, insurance number and a chip; newer cards support NFC and are protected by a PIN for access to the electronic patient record (ePA). The card arrives by post from your health insurer (Krankenkasse) free of charge once your insurance is set up. Without an eGK a doctor may ask you to pay for the visit in cash as a private patient, so get it straight away. The card has replaced the old paper insurance slip and has to be read once in every quarter.

steps.title: What the eGK is and why you need it

content.text: The electronic health card (elektronische Gesundheitskarte, eGK) is the mandatory ID for anyone insured under the statutory health insurance system (GKV). Under §291 SGB V every member of a health insurer receives such a card. On the front are your photo, name, date of birth and insurance number; inside, the chip stores the insured person's administrative data (Versichertenstammdaten): who you are, which insurer you're with and whether your insurance is active. The card is issued by the health insurer itself once you have set up your membership.

items: The electronic health card is needed at EVERY doctor's visit — it's scanned once per quarter (Quartal)
The card has replaced the old paper slip (Krankenschein) — paper ones are no longer used
Modern cards with NFC let you log into the electronic patient record (ePA) and your insurer's apps
The card carries a photo (except for children under 15 and people who can't come in person)
The card is personal — it's tied to you and not transferable

content.text: Without a valid electronic health card the doctor is formally entitled to treat you as a private patient and issue a private bill (Privatrechnung). The practice usually gives you a deadline to bring in the card or an Ersatzbescheinigung (a temporary certificate from the insurer) — typically up to 10 days, but no later than the end of the current quarter; the bill is then cancelled. Check the exact deadline with the practice itself. So always carry the card with you, and request a replacement straight away if you lose it.

steps.title: How to get and activate the card

items.title: 1. Set up membership with a health insurer

items: Choose a health insurer (TK, AOK, Barmer, DAK, hkk, IKK etc.) and apply
If you're employed, your employer reports your details to the insurer to register you
You'll need: your residence registration (Anmeldung), your passport and, if you have one, your social security number (Sozialversicherungsnummer)
The insurer opens your membership and asks you for a photo for the card
You can upload the photo via the insurer's app/portal or send it by post
The requirements are the same as for a biometric passport photo (front-facing, neutral background)
No photo is required for children under 15
Without a photo the insurer can't issue a full card
The card arrives by post free of charge within 1–3 weeks
For the NFC functions (ePA, online services) the insurer sends a PIN in a separate letter
Check that the name and insurance number on the card are correct
Activate online access through the insurer's app if you plan to use the ePA

content.text: Since 2025 an electronic patient record (ePA, elektronische Patientenakte) is created automatically for everyone insured under the statutory system, unless you have opted out (Opt-out). The electronic health card, with its NFC chip and PIN, serves as the access key: by holding the card to your phone you log into the ePA via your insurer's app and see diagnoses, prescriptions and scans. The technical standard for the cards and the ePA is set by the state organisation gematik.

items: The ePA stores electronic prescriptions (E-Rezept), doctors' letters and test results
You decide which documents a particular doctor can see
You can opt out of the ePA (objection, Widerspruch) through your insurer at any time
To access the ePA you need the electronic health card with NFC, the PIN and your insurer's app or a verified account
Keep the PIN separate from the card — it protects access to your medical data

content.text: If you lose the card, notify your insurer immediately — it will block the old one and issue a new one. Don't share your ePA PIN with anyone: with the PIN and the card, someone could access your medical data. Calls or letters asking you to "confirm your card PIN" are almost always a scam.

costs.label: Issuing the eGK
costs.note: The card is issued free of charge by the health insurer when you set up your membership.

costs.label: Replacement if lost
costs.note: Most insurers issue a replacement free of charge; some charge a token fee of 5–10 € for a reissued card — check with your insurer.

title: Notaufnahme: when to go to the hospital
tldr: The hospital emergency department (Notaufnahme) is only for genuine emergencies: stroke, heart attack, severe injuries, heavy bleeding, breathing problems. In a life-threatening situation call 112. If the problem is urgent but not life-threatening (high fever at night, severe pain when practices are closed), call 116117, the on-call medical service (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst). The emergency department uses a triage system: the most serious cases are seen first, and with minor complaints you may wait many hours. Treatment is covered by your health insurance fund; there is no separate entrance fee.

steps.title: When it really is a Notaufnahme case

content.text: The hospital emergency department (Notaufnahme; also Rettungsstelle or Zentrale Notaufnahme, ZNA) is the hospital unit for acute, potentially life-threatening conditions. It is not a substitute for a doctor's appointment and not a way to "jump the queue" for a specialist. If a condition is life-threatening, do not drive yourself — call an ambulance on 112.

items: Call 112 for: chest pain, signs of a stroke (drooping face, slurred speech), loss of consciousness, heavy bleeding, difficulty breathing, severe injury
Go to the emergency department for acute but non-life-threatening conditions that need immediate care (fracture, deep wound, acute abdomen)
Signs of a stroke — the FAST test: Face, Arms, Speech, Time (call 112 immediately)
Bring your electronic health insurance card (eGK), a list of your medications and your documents; but in a life-threatening situation you will be treated even without them

content.text: 112 is the single free emergency number in Germany and the EU; it works from any phone even with no credit on your account. If in doubt whether to call, it is better to call. The dispatcher will decide whether an ambulance is needed.

steps.title: What to do if it is NOT an emergency

content.text: Most problems — fever, sore throat, a minor injury, a flare-up of a chronic condition — do not require the emergency department. If your practice is closed (evening, weekends, holidays), there is the on-call medical service (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst) on 116117. The call is free and available around the clock; you will be directed to an on-call doctor, an on-call practice (Bereitschaftspraxis) or, if necessary, to the hospital.

items: 116117 — for urgent but non-life-threatening cases outside normal practice hours
Many large hospitals have an on-call practice (Bereitschaftspraxis) right next to the emergency department — less serious patients are referred there
Find pharmacies with night duty (Notdienst) on aponet.de or from the notice on the door of any pharmacy
During opening hours, see your family doctor (Hausarzt) for an ordinary complaint, not the hospital

content.text: If you come to the emergency department with a minor complaint that does not belong there, you will be seen last under the triage system — you can realistically wait 4–8 hours or more. This is not a violation of your rights; it is medical triage by severity.

steps.title: Triage, the queue and the cost

items: At the entrance a nurse or doctor assesses severity (often using the Manchester Triage System scale)
The queue runs NOT by arrival time but by the severity of the condition
Acute cases (red/orange level) are seen immediately
Minor cases (green/blue) wait the longest — sometimes many hours
Registration with your electronic health insurance card (eGK), then triage and waiting
Tests, an ECG or scans may follow — with more waiting in between
In the end: treatment and discharge, a referral to a specialist, or admission
Bring water, a charger and patience — the process is long
For people insured under statutory health insurance (GKV), treatment in the emergency department is covered by the fund; there is no separate entrance fee
The practice fee (Praxisgebühr; a 10 € co-payment per visit) was abolished in Germany in 2013
If admitted, adults pay a co-payment (Zuzahlung) of 10 €/day (maximum 28 days per year)
Calling an ambulance on 112 when medically necessary is also covered

costs.label: Treatment in the Notaufnahme (GKV)
costs.note: Covered by your health insurance fund; there is no separate entrance fee.

costs.label: Inpatient co-payment (Krankenhaus-Zuzahlung)
costs.note: 10 € per day of hospital stay, maximum 28 days per calendar year; 0 € for children and for those exempt.

costs.label: Call to 112 / 116117
costs.note: Both numbers are free and available around the clock.

title: English-speaking doctors by city
tldr: In large cities (Berlin, Munich, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Cologne) finding an English-speaking doctor is realistic; in small towns it is harder. The most convenient filter is Doctolib (you can filter by the consultation language), plus doctor lists on embassy websites (US/UK Embassy), the doctor search (Arztsuche) of your regional physicians' association (KV) and expat groups on Facebook/Reddit. Many practices state the language in their profile. If no English-speaking doctor is available, bring someone to the appointment or use a translation app; for serious diagnoses a professional medical interpreter is better.

steps.title: Where to look for English-speaking doctors

content.text: German doctors are not required to consult in English, but in large cities many practices cater to international patients and state their consultation languages outright. The bigger the city, the better the chances. Start with online directories that let you filter by language, then add embassy lists and expat communities.

items: Doctolib (doctolib.de) — filter by specialty, insurance (statutory GKV / private PKV health insurance) and often by the consultation language
The doctor search (Arztsuche) of your physicians' association (Kassenärztliche Vereinigung, KV) — the official register of practices with the languages listed
Doctor lists on embassy websites: the U.S. Embassy, the British Embassy and others publish medical provider lists
Expat communities: Facebook groups ("Expats in Berlin/Munich"), the r/germany subreddit, the Toytown forum
Jameda and Google reviews — the comments sometimes mention the consultation language

content.text: Embassy lists are reference information, not a recommendation of a specific doctor. The embassy is not responsible for the quality of treatment. Always check whether the practice accepts your insurance (statutory GKV or private PKV health insurance) — for people insured under GKV you need a doctor marked "alle Kassen".

items: Berlin, Munich, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Cologne, Düsseldorf — many practices with consultations in English
In Frankfurt and Munich the choice is especially wide thanks to the large international business community
University hospitals (Uniklinik) often have international departments
In large cities it is also easier to find English-speaking specialist doctors (Fachärzte) and psychotherapists
The choice of English-speaking doctors is limited — plan more time for the search
Widen your search radius to the nearest large city
Younger doctors are more likely to speak English than older ones
Confirm the consultation language by phone in advance: "Do you speak English?" / "Sprechen Sie Englisch?"
Confirm the consultation language — the online profile is not always up to date
Ask whether the practice is taking new patients ("Nehmen Sie neue Patienten auf?")
Clarify whether they accept statutory health insurance (GKV) or only private patients (Privatpatienten)
Note down the address and time; bring your electronic health insurance card (eGK) to the appointment

steps.title: If there is no English-speaking doctor

content.text: It is not always possible to find a doctor who speaks English, especially in a narrow specialty or outside the big cities. In that case, prepare for the language barrier in advance — this matters most with serious diagnoses, where accuracy is essential.

items: Bring a friend or acquaintance who speaks German to the appointment
Use translation apps for basic communication
Write out your symptoms and questions in German in advance
For a serious diagnosis, ask for a professional medical interpreter (Dolmetscher)
Hospitals sometimes have an interpreter service — ask at reception

content.text: Automatic translation can distort medical information (dosages, diagnoses, contraindications). For important decisions — surgery, serious treatment — insist on a human interpreter and ask for a written medical report (Arztbrief) to double-check.

costs.label: Finding a doctor (Doctolib, Arztsuche, embassy lists)
costs.note: All the main directories and lists are free.

costs.label: Appointment with an English-speaking doctor under GKV
costs.note: Covered by the fund if the doctor accepts GKV; make sure it is not a purely private practice (Privatpraxis).

costs.label: Medical interpreter (optional)
costs.note: Roughly 50–90 € per hour; usually not covered by GKV except in specific cases — check with your fund.

sources.title: U.S. Embassy Germany — Medical Assistance / Provider Lists
TK — Finding a doctor in Germany (English)

title: Family insurance (Familienversicherung): spouse and children for free
tldr: Family insurance for dependents (Familienversicherung, §10 SGB V) is a huge advantage of the statutory health insurance system (GKV): a non-working spouse and children are insured FOR FREE, with no separate contributions. The condition is that their own regular income does not exceed the limit: in 2026 this is 565 €/month as a rule, or 603 €/month with a mini-job. Private health insurance (PKV) does not allow this — there you pay a separate contribution for each family member. For families with one working and one non-working partner, this is often the decisive argument in favour of GKV. You set it up by applying to your health insurance fund.

steps.title: Who can be insured for free

content.text: Under §10 SGB V, a member of statutory health insurance (GKV) can insure family members for free if they have no insurance of their own and their income is within the limit. This applies to spouses and registered partners, as well as to children. No additional contributions are due for them — they are covered under the main insured person.

items: A spouse or registered partner (eingetragene Lebenspartnerschaft)
Biological children, adopted children, stepchildren, and in some cases grandchildren
The family member must live in Germany (or the EU/EEA under certain conditions)
The family member must not have their own statutory or private insurance
Everyone insured under the family model must be with the same fund as the main insured person

content.text: Family insurance is possible ONLY in statutory health insurance (GKV). If the main insured person is in private health insurance (PKV), there is no free family insurance — a separate full contribution is paid for the spouse and each child. This is a key downside of PKV for families.

The main condition is that the family member's regular own income (Gesamteinkommen, total income) must not exceed the limit. The limit is tied to the monthly reference figure (Bezugsgröße; 1/7 of it). The confirmed figures for 2026 are given below.

items: General income limit 2026: 565 €/month (1/7 of the monthly Bezugsgröße)
For a mini-job (geringfügige Beschäftigung) the limit is higher: 603 €/month in 2026
Total income (Gesamteinkommen) is the sum of income under tax law (salary, rental income, capital income, etc.)
Children have the same income limit; if it is exceeded, the child is insured separately
The fund checks income regularly and may request evidence

content.text: If a family member's income exceeds the limit even slightly and on a regular basis, the family insurance ends — and they have to be insured separately (for example, voluntarily (freiwillig) in GKV). Report income changes to the fund in good time, otherwise a retroactive recalculation is possible.

items: Children are insured for free up to age 18
Up to age 23 — if they are not working (without their own income above the limit)
Up to age 25 — if they are in education or vocational training (Ausbildung/Studium)
With no age limit — for children with a severe disability who cannot support themselves

If one parent is in private health insurance (PKV) and their income is above a certain threshold and higher than the income of the GKV parent, the child may NOT be entitled to free family insurance — check §10 Abs. 3 SGB V

steps.title: How to set up family insurance

items.title: 1. Request and fill in the application

items: Get the family insurance questionnaire (Fragebogen zur Familienversicherung) from your fund (online or by post)
Enter the details of your spouse/children and their income
Attach marriage/birth certificates if required

items.title: 2. Submit to the fund and receive the cards

items: Send the application to the fund of the main insured person
The fund will check eligibility and issue an electronic health insurance card (eGK) for each family member
Children get their own eGK in their name
Report any change of job, income or family status to the fund
Once a year the fund may send a request to confirm the details
If the income limit is exceeded, arrange separate insurance in good time

If the fund has refused family insurance and you believe the refusal is unjustified, file an objection (Widerspruch, a pre-court appeal) within one month; for disputed cases consult the fund or the consumer protection association (Verbraucherzentrale)

costs.label: Family insurance (Familienversicherung)
costs.note: Completely free — no separate contributions are paid for the spouse and children in GKV.

costs.label: A family in PKV (for comparison)
costs.note: In the private system there is a separate contribution for each family member — roughly from ~200 €/month per person; the children's tariff is cheaper than an adult's.

title: Family doctor (Hausarzt): how to find one
tldr: A family doctor (Hausarzt, a general practitioner) is your entry point into German healthcare. They treat ordinary illnesses, issue referrals (Überweisung) to specialists, prescriptions and sick notes (Krankschreibung). You can find a family doctor through the doctor search (Arztsuche) of the German KBV, Doctolib, jameda or the 116117.de website. The main problem is that doctors are often overloaded and not taking new patients (Aufnahmestopp), so call several practices. Once you have chosen one, you register as a regular patient (Stammpatient).

content.text: In Germany the family doctor (Hausarzt; specialty Allgemeinmedizin or Innere Medizin) is the primary level of care. For most specialists (except a gynaecologist, ophthalmologist and paediatrician) you are expected to come with a referral from your family doctor rather than go directly. They also keep your medical history, issue repeat prescriptions and provide your sick note.

items: Treats colds, infections and chronic illnesses, and runs basic tests
Issues a referral (Überweisung) to a specialist (cardiologist, orthopaedist, etc.)
Provides the sick note for your employer (Krankschreibung, AU-Bescheinigung)
Writes prescriptions, including electronic ones (E-Rezept)
Carries out preventive check-ups (Check-up 35, vaccinations)
Coordinates treatment if several specialists are looking after you

content.text: There are several reliable ways to find a family doctor nearby who accepts people insured under statutory health insurance (gesetzlich Versicherte) and is taking new patients.

items: The doctor search (Arztsuche) of the KBV (arztsuche.116117.de) — the official search for doctors with a statutory health insurance (GKV) contract
116117.de — the portal of the Kassenärztliche Bundesvereinigung, search by specialty and district
Doctolib — online booking, with available slots visible in real time
jameda — doctor reviews and ratings, with booking
Your fund's website — many have their own doctor navigator (Arztnavigator)
Word of mouth: ask colleagues and neighbours who they recommend

content.text: Filter by languages: many practices state that the doctor speaks English or Russian. This matters for describing symptoms accurately. Also check that the doctor has a GKV contract (Kassenarzt) rather than being a private doctor (Privatarzt), otherwise you will have to pay yourself.

steps.title: Booking and registering as a Stammpatient

content.text: Once you have chosen a doctor, you need to book a first appointment and register as a regular patient. Many practices limit the intake of new patients (Aufnahmestopp), so be ready to call 5–10 practices.

items: Ask: "Nehmen Sie neue Patienten auf?" (Are you taking new patients?)
Clarify whether they accept people insured under statutory health insurance (gesetzlich Versicherte)
On Doctolib the available slots are visible without a call
If everyone has a closed intake, call 116 117 — the appointment service (Terminservicestelle) of the physicians' association (Kassenärztliche Vereinigung, §75 SGB V) will help you find a slot
Note down the date, time and address of the practice
Bring your electronic health insurance card (Gesundheitskarte) — it is scanned at reception
Fill in the health questionnaire (Anamnesebogen; about chronic illnesses)
Mention your allergies and the medications you take
Ask to be entered as a regular patient (Stammpatient)
Clarify the opening hours and how to order repeat prescriptions

content.text: Do not wait for an acute illness to look for a family doctor — find one in advance, while you are healthy. During flu season and in large cities the search can take weeks. If you are already ill and do not yet have a regular doctor, contact the on-call service (Bereitschaftsdienst, phone 116 117), and in a serious situation the hospital emergency department (Notaufnahme).

costs.label: Appointment with a Hausarzt (statutorily insured)
costs.note: Fully covered by GKV; the Praxisgebühr was abolished in 2013.

costs.label: Co-payment (Zuzahlung) for a prescription medicine
costs.note: Standard GKV co-payment; children under 18 are exempt.

costs.label: Services outside the GKV catalogue (IGeL)
costs.note: Individual paid services; not compulsory, paid separately.

title: Insurance for freelancers: statutory (GKV) or private (PKV)
tldr: A freelancer/self-employed person in Germany is not automatically subject to compulsory statutory health insurance (GKV) and chooses between voluntary statutory insurance (freiwillige GKV) and private insurance (PKV). In voluntary GKV the contribution is calculated on income (~14.6% + the additional contribution Zusatzbeitrag ~2.9%), but no lower than a minimum base — in 2026 this is 1 318,33 €/month, i.e. a minimum of ~260–280 €/month. PKV is cheaper for the young and healthy without children, but it is a "one-way street": returning to GKV after age 55 is almost impossible. Artists and journalists may qualify for the KSK (Künstlersozialkasse) and pay like employees. The choice is strategic — decide years ahead.

steps.title: Two paths: voluntary GKV or PKV

content.text: The self-employed and freelancers (apart from certain groups) are not required to be in statutory health insurance (GKV) — but health insurance itself is compulsory by law for everyone. The choice is essentially between two options: stay in or join the statutory system voluntarily (freiwillige gesetzliche Krankenversicherung), or move to private health insurance (PKV). The decision affects your costs — and your family — for decades.

items: Voluntary GKV (freiwillige GKV) — the contribution depends on income, there is free family insurance, and the rules are the same for everyone
Private PKV — the contribution depends on age, health and the chosen package, not on income; each family member is paid for separately
In voluntary GKV ALL income counts (including rent and capital), not only from self-employment
Moving GKV → PKV is possible, but the way back is almost closed after age 55

steps.title: How freiwillige GKV is calculated in 2026

content.text: In voluntary GKV the contribution is calculated on your income at the general rate: 14.6% (the general contribution rate, allgemeiner Beitragssatz) plus your fund's additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag; the 2026 average is around 2.9%), giving ~17.5% in total. On top comes the long-term care insurance contribution (Pflegeversicherung). But there is a minimum base (Mindestbemessungsgrundlage): even on a low income the contribution is calculated on at least that amount.

items: Minimum base (Mindestbemessungsgrundlage) 2026: 1 318,33 €/month — the contribution does not fall below this (one third of the monthly reference figure Bezugsgröße)
Minimum contribution for health insurance alone 2026: roughly ~230 €/month (14.6% + the additional contribution Zusatzbeitrag on the minimum base)
Including long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung), the minimum is roughly ~260–280 €/month
The upper cap is the income ceiling for social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) 2026: 5 812,50 €/month (income above this does not count)
The fund calculates the contribution provisionally and, on the basis of the tax assessment (Einkommensteuerbescheid), recalculates it retroactively
Free family insurance for dependents (Familienversicherung) is available for a non-working spouse and children

content.text: In voluntary GKV the fund counts ALL of your income, not only from freelancing: rental income, investments and other activities also go into the base. After you file your annual tax return, a large retroactive recalculation of contributions is possible — keep a reserve.

steps.title: When PKV is cheaper and where the trap is

content.text: Private health insurance (PKV) can be significantly cheaper for a young, healthy freelancer without children: the contribution does not depend on income and, with good health, starts lower than a percentage of a high income in GKV. But the contribution rises with age and with worsening health, and there is no free family insurance.

items: PKV is roughly 200–800 €/month depending on age, health and the package
The PKV contribution rises over the years; in old age it can become very high
For a spouse and each child in PKV there is a separate contribution (in GKV they are free)
On entry to PKV there is a medical assessment (Gesundheitsprüfung) — chronic illnesses make it more expensive or block entry

content.text: PKV is a one-way street (Einbahnstraße). Returning to GKV becomes almost impossible after age 55 (§6 Abs. 3a SGB V). If the PKV contribution becomes unaffordable in old age, there will be no way back into cheap GKV. Plan for decades, not for the coming year.

If your self-employment is creative or journalistic (artist, musician, designer, writer, journalist), you may qualify for the social insurance fund for creative workers (Künstlersozialkasse, KSK). Through the KSK you pay contributions like an employee: the KSK covers roughly half of the contribution (the state + a levy on clients), rather than you paying it all. This is a serious saving compared with ordinary voluntary GKV.

items: The KSK suits creative/journalistic professions with regular income from that activity
You pay roughly half of the contributions for health, care and pension — the KSK covers the rest
An application and proof of the nature of the activity and the income are required
If approved, you stay in GKV on terms close to those of employees
Details and the application are on the Künstlersozialkasse website

costs.label: freiwillige GKV (minimum 2026)
costs.note: Roughly 260–280 €/month including Pflegeversicherung; calculated on the minimum base of 1 318,33 €/month even on a low income.

costs.label: PKV (range)
costs.note: Roughly 200–800 €/month depending on age, health and package; rises with age.

costs.label: KSK (for creative professions)
costs.note: The contribution itself depends on income, but the KSK covers roughly half — your personal burden is half that of ordinary freiwillige GKV.

sources.title: SGB V §6 / §240 — freiwillige Versicherung und Beitragsbemessung
Künstlersozialkasse (KSK) — Versicherung für Künstler und Publizisten

title: Calculating statutory health insurance (GKV) contributions: 14.6% + additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag)
tldr: The statutory health insurance GKV contribution consists of the general rate of 14.6% (§241 SGB V) plus your fund's individual additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag; the 2026 average is around 2.9%), giving ~17.5% of gross income in total. For employees the contribution is split 50/50 with the employer — so roughly half is deducted from your salary. The contribution is calculated only up to the income ceiling for social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze, BBG): in 2026 this is 5 812,50 €/month (69 750 €/year); income above the ceiling is not subject to the contribution. On top there is the long-term care insurance contribution (Pflegeversicherung).

steps.title: What the contribution is made up of

content.text: The statutory health insurance (GKV) contribution has two parts. The first is the general contribution rate (allgemeiner Beitragssatz), fixed by law at 14.6% (§241 SGB V). The second is the additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag), which each fund sets itself (§242 SGB V); the 2026 average is around 2.9%. Together this gives roughly 17.5% of the assessable income. The long-term care insurance contribution (Pflegeversicherung) is charged separately.

items: General contribution rate (allgemeiner Beitragssatz): 14.6% — the same for all funds (§241 SGB V)
Additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag): individual to each fund; the 2026 average is ~2.9% (§242 SGB V)
Total for health: ~17.5% of the assessable income
Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) — separate, on top (depends on whether you have children)
Check your fund's exact additional contribution rate on its website

content.text: Do not confuse 14.6% and 17.5%. The law fixes only the general rate of 14.6%; the fund's additional contribution is added on top and differs between funds. So for the same income the contribution at a cheap and an expensive fund can differ by tens of euros per month.

For employees the contribution is split equally between the worker and the employer. This applies both to the general rate of 14.6% and to the additional contribution — since 2019 the Zusatzbeitrag is also split 50/50 (parity financing, paritätische Finanzierung). That is, roughly half of the total contribution is deducted from your salary, and the employer pays the other half.

items: The worker pays ~half: roughly 8.75% of gross (7.3% + half of the additional contribution)
The employer pays the other half — you do not see it as a deduction on your payslip
The deduction happens automatically from your salary (payslip, Lohnabrechnung)
The self-employed in voluntary GKV (freiwillige GKV) have no employer — they pay the whole contribution themselves

content.text: The contribution is calculated not on all income but up to a ceiling — the income ceiling for social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze, BBG). Income above the ceiling is not subject to the health contribution. In 2026 the BBG in GKV is 5 812,50 €/month (69 750 €/year). This means the maximum contribution is capped — no matter how much you earn above the ceiling, the contribution does not rise.

items: BBG GKV 2026: 5 812,50 €/month = 69 750 €/year
Income above the BBG is not counted when calculating the health contribution
Maximum health contribution 2026: ~17.5% of 5 812,50 € ≈ ~1 017 €/month (before the split with the employer)
Do not confuse the BBG with the threshold for moving to private health insurance (Versicherungspflichtgrenze, JAEG) — these are different thresholds
The BBG is indexed annually — check the current figures

content.text: The BBG (contribution ceiling, 2026: 5 812,50 €/month) and the compulsory insurance threshold (Versicherungspflichtgrenze/JAEG; the threshold for moving to PKV, 2026: 6 450 €/month) are two DIFFERENT numbers. The first caps the size of the contribution, the second determines whether you can move to PKV at all. They are often confused.

items: Income below the BBG — fully assessable
Total health contribution: ~17.5% × 3 000 € = ~525 €/month
Worker's share (50%): ~262 €/month deducted from salary
On top — the long-term care insurance contribution (Pflegeversicherung)
Income above the BBG — the contribution is calculated only up to 5 812,50 €
Total health contribution: ~17.5% × 5 812,50 € ≈ ~1 017 €/month
Worker's share (50%): ~508 €/month
Income above 5 812,50 € is not subject to the health contribution

costs.label: General GKV rate (allgemeiner Beitragssatz)
costs.note: 14.6% of the assessable income (§241 SGB V); for employees split 50/50 with the employer.

costs.label: Zusatzbeitrag (average 2026)
costs.note: Around 2.9% on top, individual to each fund (§242 SGB V); also split 50/50.

costs.label: Maximum health contribution 2026
costs.note: ~17.5% of the BBG of 5 812,50 €/month ≈ ~1 017 €/month total (before the split with the employer); the worker's share is ~half.

title: The income threshold for private health insurance (PKV) in 2026
tldr: The compulsory insurance threshold (Versicherungspflichtgrenze, also called the Jahresarbeitsentgeltgrenze, JAEG) is the annual income threshold above which an employee is no longer required to be in statutory health insurance GKV and may choose private insurance PKV. In 2026 the JAEG is 77 400 €/year (6 450 €/month). To move to PKV, your regular annual gross income must exceed this threshold. It is important not to confuse the JAEG with the income ceiling for social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze, 2026: 69 750 €/year). Moving to PKV is a strategic decision — getting back out after age 55 is almost impossible.

content.text: Under §6 SGB V, employees are required to be in statutory health insurance (GKV) as long as their income does not exceed a certain threshold — the compulsory insurance threshold (Versicherungspflichtgrenze), called in the law the annual earnings threshold (Jahresarbeitsentgeltgrenze, JAEG). Only once a worker crosses this threshold are they released from compulsory GKV membership (versicherungsfrei) and gain the right to choose private health insurance (PKV). The purpose of the threshold is to keep most workers in the solidarity-based statutory system.

items: JAEG 2026: 77 400 €/year = 6 450 €/month
It is the regular annual gross income that counts (excluding one-off, irregular payments)
The threshold applies to employees; for the self-employed the rules for moving to PKV are different
The threshold is indexed annually — an increase is expected for 2027
Exceeding it must be regular and sustained, not a one-off

content.text: The JAEG (the threshold for moving to PKV, 2026: 77 400 €/year) and the income ceiling for social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze, 2026: 69 750 €/year) are DIFFERENT numbers. The JAEG answers the question "can I move to PKV", the BBG answers "from what income amount is the contribution calculated". They must not be confused.

steps.title: How exactly the threshold is reached

items: Regular payments count: base salary, guaranteed bonuses, a 13th salary
One-off, unpredictable bonuses usually do NOT count
Income must sustainably exceed 77 400 €/year
For part-time work, project it onto a full year
Release from compulsory GKV usually takes effect at the end of the calendar year in which the threshold is exceeded, provided it will also be exceeded in the following year
The fund/employer checks that the condition is met
A drop in income below the threshold restores the obligation to be in GKV
You can stay in GKV voluntarily (freiwillig) — this is allowed and often sensible
Or move to PKV — but weigh the long-term consequences
Consider your family: in GKV the spouse and children are free, in PKV there is a separate contribution for each

content.text: Exceeding the threshold does not mean you have to rush into private health insurance (PKV). Many highly paid employees deliberately stay in voluntary GKV for the free family insurance and the predictability. The decision depends on your age, health, whether you have children, and your plans.

PKV is a one-way street. After age 55 it is practically impossible to return from PKV to GKV (§6 Abs. 3a SGB V). If your income later falls or the PKV contribution rises in old age, there will be no way back into cheap GKV. Do not make the decision purely for a short-term saving.

costs.label: Versicherungspflichtgrenze (JAEG) 2026
costs.note: 77 400 €/year (6 450 €/month) — the annual income threshold for the right to choose PKV.

costs.label: Beitragsbemessungsgrenze GKV 2026 (for comparison)
costs.note: 69 750 €/year (5 812,50 €/month) — the income ceiling for calculating the contribution; not to be confused with the JAEG.

title: Statutory (GKV) vs private (PKV) health insurance: which to choose in 2026
tldr: Statutory health insurance GKV and private PKV are two different systems. GKV: the contribution depends on income (~17.5%), free family insurance, the same rules for everyone. PKV: the contribution depends on age and health, can be cheaper for a young, healthy single person with a high income, but rises over the years, and each family member is paid for separately. The main factors in the choice are income, age, family and health. The key warning: PKV is a one-way street; returning to GKV after age 55 is almost impossible (§6 Abs. 3a SGB V). In most cases GKV is more advantageous for people with families.

steps.title: The fundamental difference between the systems

content.text: Statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung, GKV) is a solidarity-based system: the contribution depends on income, not on your state of health, and a non-working family is insured for free. Private health insurance (private Krankenversicherung, PKV) is an individual contract: the contribution depends on your age at entry, your state of health and the chosen package of services, but not on income. These are two fundamentally different systems, not simply a matter of "cheaper" versus "more expensive".

items: GKV: ~17.5% of income up to the ceiling; the family (spouse + children) is free
PKV: a fixed contribution by age/health; each family member separately
GKV: the same range of services by law; PKV: services per the chosen tariff (which may be broader or narrower)
PKV is available to employees only with income above the compulsory insurance threshold (JAEG; 2026: 77 400 €/year), and to the self-employed and civil servants almost always
High income + single → PKV may be cheaper (the contribution does not rise with income)
Middle income → GKV is usually cheaper and simpler
In GKV the contribution is capped by the income ceiling for social contributions (BBG; 2026: 5 812,50 €/month)
A non-working spouse and children → a huge plus for GKV (free under §10 SGB V)
In PKV each family member is a separate contribution (which easily outweighs the saving)
Planning children → a serious argument for GKV
Young and healthy → entry to PKV is cheaper and without surcharges
Chronic illnesses → PKV is more expensive or refuses (medical assessment, Gesundheitsprüfung)
The PKV contribution rises with age; in old age it can become a heavy burden

steps.title: The PKV trap: a one-way street

content.text: The most important thing when choosing PKV is that it is almost impossible to undo at an older age. The law severely limits the return to GKV: after age 55 the return is practically closed (§6 Abs. 3a SGB V). This means that choosing PKV at 30 is a decision for life, retirement included — when your income falls but the PKV contribution, if anything, climbs.

PKV is a one-way street (Einbahnstraße). Returning to GKV after age 55 is almost impossible. If the PKV contribution becomes unaffordable in old age, cheap GKV will no longer be open to you. PKV that looks cheap when you are young often turns into expensive contributions in old age.

items: Calculate the contribution in both systems over a 20–40 year horizon, not just for now
Factor in your plans for family and children — this often decides in favour of GKV
Assess your state of health and the possible surcharges in PKV
Remember the age-55 return cap — plan for old age
If in doubt, stay in GKV (including voluntarily, freiwillig) — this is reversible, unlike PKV
Consult an independent insurance adviser (Versicherungsberater), not just an insurance agent

costs.label: GKV (employee)
costs.note: ~17.5% of income up to the ceiling of 5 812,50 €/month (2026), split 50/50 with the employer; the family is free.

costs.label: PKV (range)
costs.note: Roughly 200–800 €/month per person depending on age, health and tariff; rises with age.

sources.title: SGB V §6 — Versicherungsfreiheit und Rückkehr in die GKV (Abs. 3a)
vdek — GKV und PKV im Vergleich
TK — Wechsel zwischen GKV und PKV

title: TK, AOK, Barmer, DAK — which to choose
tldr: The basic services at every statutory insurer (GKV) are the same by law, so you choose on three things: the size of the additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag), the extra services (Zusatzleistungen — bonuses, prevention, osteopathy and so on) and the quality of the service/app. TK is tech-savvy, with a handy app, and popular with expats. AOK is regional, with a strong office network. Barmer and DAK are large federal insurers with a wide range of programmes. You can switch insurer after 12 months of membership with a 2-month notice period; if the Zusatzbeitrag rises, you can switch early (a special right to terminate, Sonderkündigungsrecht).

steps.title: What's the same and what differs

content.text: All statutory insurers are required by law (SGB V) to provide the same catalogue of basic medical services (mandatory services, Pflichtleistungen): doctor's visits, hospital, medicines, prevention. So you don't need to worry about the basics — they're identical everywhere. The differences are in the price (additional contribution, Zusatzbeitrag), the voluntary bonuses and the quality of service.

items: The same: the general rate of 14.6% and the mandatory catalogue of services
Differs: the insurer's additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag)
Differs: extra services (Zusatzleistungen) — bonus programmes, prevention, extra vaccinations, osteopathy, travel services
Differs: service, app, English-language support, office network
This is the only part of the contribution that differs between insurers
The 2026 average is around 2.9%, but specific insurers are higher or lower
A difference of 0.5–1% on a good salary is tens of euros a month
Check the current rate on the insurer's website and in the comparison on krankenkassen.de
Bonus programmes (Bonusprogramm) for prevention and sport
Subsidies for professional teeth cleaning, travel vaccinations, osteopathy
Programmes for the chronically ill (DMP) and support during pregnancy
Compare what you actually need
The quality of the app and online account (important for the electronic patient record ePA, certificates, prescriptions)
English-language support — crucial for expats
Offices nearby, if face-to-face contact matters to you
How quickly they answer queries and process documents

steps.title: A quick look at the largest insurers

items: TK (Techniker Krankenkasse) — tech-savvy, a strong app, English-language support, popular with expats and IT
AOK — regional (AOK Bayern, AOK Nordost etc.), a large office network, strong on personal service
Barmer — a large federal insurer, broad prevention and support programmes
DAK-Gesundheit — a large federal insurer, well-developed programmes for families and the chronically ill
hkk and IKK — separate insurers (see the respective guides) with a competitive additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag)

content.text: Don't choose an insurer purely on the lowest additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag). The insurer can change the rate at any time. Take into account the service, the app and the extra services you actually need — paying a couple of euros more can pay off in convenience and English-language support.

items: The minimum membership period is 12 months, after which you can switch with a 2-month notice period
Just apply to the new insurer — it will notify the old one itself (electronic termination)
If the additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) rises, you have a special right to switch early (Sonderkündigungsrecht)
You don't lose the basic services when you switch — the catalogue is the same everywhere
It's easy to compare rates and services on krankenkassen.de or comparison portals

costs.label: Zusatzbeitrag (2026 average)
costs.note: Around 2.9% on top of the 14.6% rate; the exact figure depends on the insurer and is split 50/50 with the employer.

costs.label: Switching insurer
costs.note: Free; minimum membership 12 months, 2 months' notice (early if the Zusatzbeitrag rises).

title: hkk: one of the cheapest statutory insurers (GKV)
tldr: hkk (Handelskrankenkasse) is a statutory health insurer with one of the lowest additional contributions (Zusatzbeitrag) in Germany. The basic services are the same as at every statutory health insurer GKV (the same catalogue by law), but thanks to the low additional contribution the final percentage taken from your salary is lower than at most large insurers — on a good income that's tens of euros saved a month. hkk is available across Germany (bundesweit), and almost anyone insured under the GKV can join. A good choice for those who optimise their spending and don't need a dense network of offices.

steps.title: Why hkk is attractive on price

content.text: The basic range of services at every statutory insurer is the same by law (SGB V), so the real difference in price comes down to the additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag), which each insurer sets itself (§242 SGB V). hkk has traditionally kept one of the lowest additional contributions on the market, which makes it attractive for anyone who wants to pay less for the same basic services.

items: Basic medical services — the same as at any statutory health insurer (GKV; doctor's visits, hospital, medicines, prevention)
hkk's additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) is one of the lowest in Germany
On a high income the difference in the additional contribution makes a noticeable saving each month
Available across the country (bundesweit), not tied to a region
Check the exact current additional-contribution rate on hkk.de

content.text: The lowest additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) today is not guaranteed forever — the insurer may raise it. If it rises, you get a special right to switch insurer early (Sonderkündigungsrecht). Don't choose an insurer on price alone — take into account the service and the extra services you need.

items: Those who optimise their spending and want the lowest additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag)
Those comfortable sorting things out online/by phone without frequent office visits
Employees on a high salary, where even a fraction of a percent makes a noticeable saving
The self-employed on voluntary statutory insurance (freiwillige GKV), who pay the contribution in full and for whom every percent matters
Families — free family insurance for relatives (Familienversicherung) works at hkk just as at other GKV insurers
Look up the current additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) on hkk.de
Compare it with your current insurer and work out the saving
Check the extra services that matter to you
Fill in the online application to join on the hkk website
hkk will notify your previous insurer itself (electronic termination)
Observe the minimum 12-month membership period at your previous insurer (or use the special right to switch early, Sonderkündigungsrecht, if the contribution rises)
hkk will issue a new electronic health insurance card (eGK) in your name
From the date you join, you show doctors the hkk card
Set up the hkk app/online account if needed

costs.label: hkk basic services
costs.note: Covered as at any GKV; the catalogue of services is the same by law.

costs.label: Zusatzbeitrag hkk
costs.note: One of the lowest in Germany; for employees it's split 50/50 with the employer. Check the current rate on hkk.de.

costs.label: Joining and switching insurer
costs.note: Free; minimum membership 12 months, 2 months' notice.

title: IKK for tradespeople
tldr: IKK (Innungskrankenkasse) funds are public health insurers (Krankenkasse) that historically grew out of the skilled trades and the guild workforce (the trades Handwerk, guild associations Innungen). Today the largest of them — IKK classic and IKK gesund plus — are open to almost anyone insured under the statutory health insurance system (GKV), not just tradespeople. The core benefits are the same as with any statutory insurer (GKV); the differences lie in the supplementary contribution (Zusatzbeitrag), the extra programmes and the service. IKK keeps a focus on supporting skilled-trade professions and small businesses, but employees, the self-employed and family members can all join.

steps.title: What IKK is and who it is for

content.text: An Innungskrankenkasse (IKK) is a historic type of health fund (Krankenkasse) that grew out of the skilled-trade guilds (Innungen). Originally they served workers at trade businesses first and foremost. Today most IKK funds are open to everyone insured under the statutory health insurance system (GKV): the restriction by profession was lifted long ago. Like all statutory funds, an IKK is required to provide the single catalogue of benefits set by law.

items: IKK classic — the largest one, available to almost everyone across Germany
IKK gesund plus — a regional IKK, also open to a broad range of people
Core benefits — the same as with any statutory insurer GKV (doctor visits, hospital, medication, prevention)
It keeps a focus on supporting the trades (Handwerk) and small business (programmes, advice)
Employees, the self-employed and family members can join — not only tradespeople

content.text: Not every IKK operates nationwide — some are regional. Before joining, check on the fund's website whether the IKK you have chosen is available in your region and what its current supplementary contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) is.

items: A competitive supplementary contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) — compare it with other funds
Programmes and advice geared towards tradespeople and small business
Prevention and bonus programmes (Bonusprogramm), as with other statutory insurers GKV
Free family insurance (Familienversicherung) for a non-working spouse and children
Personal service and a network of offices in the regions where the fund operates
Find out which IKK is available in your region (IKK classic — almost everywhere)
Check the current supplementary contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) and the extra services you need
Compare with other funds (TK, AOK, hkk, etc.)
Fill in the online application on the website of the IKK you have chosen
The IKK will notify your previous fund itself (electronic termination)
Mind the 12-month membership period at your previous fund, or use the special right to terminate early (Sonderkündigungsrecht) if its contribution goes up
The IKK will issue a new electronic health card (eGK) in your name
From the start date of your membership you show doctors your IKK card
Set up the app or online portal if you need it

costs.label: IKK core benefits
costs.note: Covered just as with any statutory insurer (GKV); the catalogue of benefits is uniform by law.

costs.label: IKK supplementary contribution (Zusatzbeitrag)
costs.note: Depends on the specific IKK; for employees it is split 50/50 with the employer. Check the current rate on the fund's website.

costs.label: Joining and switching funds
costs.note: Free; minimum membership period of 12 months, two months' notice.

title: Psychotherapy: how to get it on statutory insurance (GKV)
tldr: Psychotherapy (Psychotherapie) is fully covered by statutory insurance under SGB V §27 and the psychotherapy directive (Psychotherapie-Richtlinie) issued by the Federal Joint Committee (G-BA). The path usually runs like this: first an introductory appointment (Psychotherapeutische Sprechstunde), then, if needed, short-term therapy (Kurzzeittherapie, 12–24 sessions) or long-term therapy (Langzeittherapie, 60+ sessions). The main problem is the long waiting times for therapists who hold a contract with the funds. If you cannot find a fund-covered slot (Kassenplatz) within a reasonable time, you can use cost reimbursement (Kostenerstattung) — the fund then has to pay for a private therapist. The easiest way to find a specialist is through the therapist search (Therapeutensuche) of your statutory health physicians' association (KV) and the 116117 service.

content.text: Psychotherapy is a medical service, and for anyone insured under statutory health insurance (GKV) it is free. The entitlement to treatment is set out in §27 SGB V (treatment of illness, Krankenbehandlung), and the procedure and scope are defined by the psychotherapy directive (Psychotherapie-Richtlinie) of the Federal Joint Committee (Gemeinsamer Bundesausschuss, G-BA). The fund pays for the recognised methods: behavioural therapy (Verhaltenstherapie), depth-psychology-based therapy (tiefenpsychologisch fundierte Psychotherapie), psychoanalytic therapy (analytische) and systemic therapy (systemische).

items: Fully covered by statutory insurance GKV — no co-payment per session

Recognised methods under the directive (Richtlinienverfahren): behavioural (Verhaltenstherapie), depth-psychology-based (tiefenpsychologisch fundierte), psychoanalytic (analytische) and systemic (systemische) therapy
The therapist must be approved to work with the funds (Kassenzulassung; a contract with a fund) — otherwise you pay for the sessions yourself
A referral from your family doctor (Hausarzt) is NOT required to see a psychotherapist — you can go directly
For minors there are child and adolescent therapists (Kinder- und Jugendlichenpsychotherapeuten)

steps.title: The path to therapy: Sprechstunde → Kurzzeit → Langzeit

items: This is the mandatory first step — an introductory consultation (up to 6 times, 25 minutes each)
The therapist assesses whether therapy is needed and which method is suitable
At the end you receive a document (individual patient information, Individuelle Patienteninformation, PTV 11) with a recommendation
You can book directly at a practice or via 116117 / eterminservice.de

items.title: 2. Acute treatment (Akutbehandlung) in case of urgent need

items: If your condition is acute, acute treatment (Akutbehandlung) is possible before full therapy begins
Up to ~24 units of 25 minutes for stabilisation, without lengthy formal approval from the fund
It helps you avoid waiting months when you simply cannot wait
Short-term therapy (Kurzzeittherapie): 12 sessions, extendable by another 12 (up to 24 in total)
Long-term therapy (Langzeittherapie): from 60 sessions and more where justified; the maximum scope depends on the method
The therapist submits an application (Antrag) to the fund; as a rule it is approved
Sessions are usually once a week for about 50 minutes

steps.title: Waiting times and the Kostenerstattung route

content.text: The real problem is not the entitlement to therapy but the waiting times. There are not enough therapists with a fund contract, and the wait for a slot (Kassenplatz) can stretch out over months. But there is a lawful workaround: if you can document that you cannot find a free slot within a reasonable time, the fund is obliged to pay for treatment with a private therapist who does not hold approval to work with the funds (Kassenzulassung), under the cost-reimbursement procedure (Kostenerstattung; SGB V §13 Abs. 3).

items: Use the therapist search (Therapeutensuche) of your statutory health physicians' association (Kassenärztliche Vereinigung) to find practices
Call several practices and record the refusals: date, name, the waiting time offered
Contact the 116117 service to arrange an introductory appointment (Psychotherapeutische Sprechstunde)
If you could not find a slot with a fund-covered therapist (Kassenplatz) within a reasonable time, gather evidence of the refusals
Submit an application for cost reimbursement (Kostenerstattung) to the fund, with the report from the introductory appointment (Sprechstunde, PTV 11) and the list of refusals
Once it is approved, the fund pays for therapy with a private (Privat-) therapist

content.text: The fund may refuse cost reimbursement (Kostenerstattung) at first — this is common practice. Do not give up: file a written objection (Widerspruch) within one month, attaching the documented refusals from practices and the report from the introductory appointment (Sprechstunde). In a crisis, call the psychological helpline Telefonseelsorge on 0800 111 0 111 (free, 24/7), and in a life-threatening situation — 112.

costs.label: Psychotherapy under GKV
costs.note: Fully covered by the fund — the introductory appointment (Sprechstunde), short-term (Kurzzeittherapie) and long-term therapy (Langzeittherapie) with no co-payment.

costs.label: Therapy via cost reimbursement (Kostenerstattung)
costs.note: Once approved, the fund reimburses the cost of a private therapist; the patient pays nothing out of pocket.

costs.label: Therapy with a private therapist without approval
costs.note: Roughly per session if you pay privately without cost reimbursement (Kostenerstattung); not reimbursed without the procedure.

title: Mietbewerbungsmappe: what to put in it
tldr: Every flat in Berlin, Munich or Hamburg draws 50-200 applications. A rental application folder (Mietbewerbungsmappe) is your CV for the flat. The minimum: a cover letter (Anschreiben), a credit report from the credit bureau (Schufa-BonitätsAuskunft, 39,95€), a certificate of no rent arrears (Mietschuldenfreiheitsbescheinigung), your last 3 payslips (Lohnzettel), and a copy of your national ID card (Personalausweis) or residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel). Without a complete folder (Mappe) you will not even be invited to view the flat (Besichtigung).

steps.title: What a Mietbewerbungsmappe is and why it matters

content.text: A rental application folder (Mietbewerbungsmappe; also Bewerbermappe, Selbstauskunftsmappe) is the set of documents that a landlord (Vermieter) or agent (Makler) expects from every applicant. On Germany's tight market (especially Berlin, München, Frankfurt, Hamburg) a landlord can receive 50-200 responses a day. Anyone who sends in an incomplete or carelessly assembled folder is filtered out automatically — they will not even be invited to a viewing.

The purpose of the folder is to convince the landlord within 30 seconds that you are a solvent, reliable and trouble-free tenant. This is the format Germans are used to: everything in one PDF, clear, in German, and matter-of-fact.

items: Prepare the folder in advance — while you are still searching, not once you have found a place
A single PDF file with a cover page and table of contents looks professional
Print 3-5 paper copies for the viewing
Update your payslips (Lohnzettel) and the Schufa credit report every 3 months — old ones are not accepted

content.text: The minimum set most landlords expect in 2026:

Half a page in German: who you are, what you do, your household composition (with or without children, pets), why you want this particular flat, and how long you plan to stay. The tone is formal but human. The address and subject line should match the exact title of the listing.

This is a report on your credit history in Germany. Order it at meineschufa.de — it costs 39,95€ and arrives by post in 3-5 days. IMPORTANT: you need the credit report specifically (BonitätsAuskunft; the version for the landlord, 2 pages), not the free data copy under the right of access (Datenkopie nach Art. 15 DSGVO; this one is free, but it is not suitable for a rental application — it contains too much personal data, and many landlords will not accept it).

A certificate from your previous landlord confirming that you have no rent arrears. It is usually issued free of charge on request. If you have just arrived in Germany, you can replace it with a note in your cover letter ("Erstwohnsitz in Deutschland" — first place of residence in Germany) or a letter from your previous landlord abroad, with a translation.

items: Your last 3 payslips (Lohnzettel) from your employer
Or your employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag) plus your first payslip — if you have been working <3 months
For the self-employed (Selbständige): a business performance report (BWA, Betriebswirtschaftliche Auswertung) plus your latest tax assessment (Steuerbescheid)
For students: the student grant decision (BAföG-Bescheid) or proof of parental income (Einkommensnachweis) plus a guarantee (Bürgschaft)
A copy of your national ID card (Personalausweis) or passport (Reisepass; both sides)
A copy of your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — if you are not an EU citizen
A registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) for your current address

content.text: A standard tenant questionnaire (Mieter-Selbstauskunft) with the usual questions: marital status, income, profession, and whether you have any convictions in rental matters. A template is available from the tenants' association Mieterbund (mieterbund.de) or at immoscout24.de. Fill it in honestly — the landlord can check.

steps.title: What to add to stand out

content.text: On an overcrowded market the basics are not enough. What boosts your chances:

items: A photo of you or your family — debatable, but in Germany it often helps (a warm photo, not a passport one)
A guarantee (Bürgschaft) from your parents or employer — if your income is shaky
A deposit guarantee (Mietkautionsbürgschaft) via Kautionsfrei.de or Plus Wohnen — an alternative to a cash deposit
A reference letter (Referenzschreiben) from a previous landlord
A short CV or a link to your LinkedIn — if you work for a prestigious firm
A statement of intent: "mindestens 3 Jahre Mietzeit geplant" (planning to rent for at least 3 years) — landlords dislike frequent tenant turnover

steps.title: How to format it so it gets read

content.text: Format and presentation matter almost as much as content.

items: One PDF, not 10 separate files
File size up to 10 MB — otherwise many email services will reject it
File name: 'Bewerbung_Ivanov_Maxim_Berlin_Mustermannstr12.pdf'
All documents in German — translated by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) if needed
The Schufa report and payslips — no older than 3 months
A handwritten signature on the cover letter and the self-disclosure form (Selbstauskunft; scan it in)

content.text: Do not send the whole folder with your very first response. Under data protection principles (the EU regulation DSGVO, data minimisation Datenminimierung) the landlord may request the Schufa report and proof of income only after inviting you to a viewing. For first contact, a cover letter and a brief self-disclosure (Selbstauskunft) are enough. This is both legally sound and psychologically smart: too much data at once looks suspicious.

Do NOT hand over original documents. Copies only. The landlord has no right to keep the original of your national ID card (Personalausweis) or passport (Reisepass) — that is a direct breach of the data protection regulation (DSGVO). If they demand it, that is a red flag (possibly a scammer).

The credit report (Schufa BonitätsAuskunft) is NOT the same as the free data copy (Datenkopie). The free one (for checking your own data under DSGVO) will not be accepted: it contains ALL your data, including "soft facts", and many landlords know its format is not meant for rentals. Pay the 39,95€ and order the right one.

Remember the rental deposit (Mietkaution): under §551 BGB it may not exceed 3 cold rents (Kaltmieten — rent without utilities). If a landlord demands 4-6 months, that is unlawful. You may pay it in 3 monthly instalments (§551 Abs. 2 BGB).

costs.label: Schufa-BonitätsAuskunft
costs.note: Order at meineschufa.de, delivered in 3-5 days by post. Valid for 3 months.

costs.label: Initial consultation with the tenants' association (Mieterbund-Erstberatung)
costs.note: Annual membership in the tenants' association Mieterbund (mieterbund.de) for legal support with application and contract problems

costs.label: Certified translation (Beglaubigte Übersetzung) of documents
costs.note: Per page with a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) — if you need translations of diplomas or certificates

costs.label: Rental deposit (Mietkaution)
costs.note: A maximum of 3 cold rents (Kaltmieten) under §551 BGB; can be paid in 3 instalments. Alternative: a deposit guarantee (Mietkautionsbürgschaft) at ~5% of the sum per year

sources.title: BGB §551 — Begrenzung und Anlage von Mietsicherheiten

title: Besichtigung: how to impress the landlord
tldr: A flat viewing (Besichtigung) is an interview where the landlord (Vermieter) picks 1-2 people out of 30 applicants. A ready, printed-out rental application folder (Mietbewerbungsmappe), clear questions about utility costs (Nebenkosten) and heating (Heizung), a tidy appearance and punctuality decide the outcome. A group viewing (Massenbesichtigung) is the norm; an individual one is rare.

steps.title: What a Besichtigung is and the types you will encounter

content.text: A viewing (Besichtigung) is an in-person inspection of the flat, after which the landlord (Vermieter) decides who to offer the contract to. On the German market there are two main formats:

items: Group viewing (Massenbesichtigung) — typical in Berlin and München: 20-50 people turn up in one time slot
Individual viewing (Einzelbesichtigung) — rarer, usually for expensive rentals or with private landlords
A series of back-to-back appointments (Sammeltermin) — several 10-15 minute slots in a row, with small groups

content.text: Your task is to show within 10-15 minutes that you are a serious, solvent and pleasant person. The landlord makes the decision in the first 30 seconds; the rest is confirmation.

steps.title: What to do before the visit

content.text: The day before the viewing, send a short confirmation by email: "Sehr geehrte/r ..., hiermit bestätige ich den Besichtigungstermin am ... um ... Uhr." This reduces the risk of the landlord cancelling or forgetting.

3-5 copies of the complete folder, in a binder or stapled, with a cover page, table of contents and a family photo. Landlords value readiness — and those who bring the full package are considered first.

items.title: 3. Research the area and the property

items: The official rent index for the area (Mietspiegel) — so you can tell whether the price is at market level
Utility costs (Nebenkosten) in the listing (cold rent + utilities = gross/warm rent Warmmiete)
Year of construction (Baujahr) and type of heating (Heizung)
Schools (Schulen), nurseries (Kitas), transport links (Verkehrsanbindung) — if you have children

items.title: 4. Draw up a list of questions

content.text: 7-10 specific questions written down on paper. This shows you are serious.
The questions fall into two groups: about the flat (showing you know your stuff) and about the landlord's plans (showing you intend to stay a long time).

items: Wie hoch sind die Nebenkosten und die Heizkosten im Schnitt? (what are the utility and heating costs on average?) — ask for the real figure for the past year
Welche Heizungsart (Gasetagenheizung, Fernwärme, Wärmepumpe)? (what type of heating: gas per-flat, district, heat pump?) — it affects the bills
Wann wurden Fenster/Bad/Küche zuletzt renoviert?
Gibt es einen Hausmeister? Wer ist Ansprechpartner bei Problemen?
Ist die Wohnung im Mietspiegel? Wie wurde die Miete kalkuliert? (is the flat in the rent index, and how was the rent calculated?) — a nod to the rent cap (Mietpreisbremse)
Wie viele Bewerber gibt es bereits? (how many applicants are there already?) — to gauge your chances
Wann ist Einzugstermin möglich? (when is move-in possible?) — flexibility on the date
Wer war der Vormieter, warum zog er aus? (who was the previous tenant, and why did they move out?) — a sign of how long tenancies in the building last
Gibt es Hausordnung-Besonderheiten (Lärm, Haustiere, Grillen)?
Wer übernimmt Schönheitsreparaturen?

content.text: German rental culture is formal but human. The landlord (a private one especially) is looking for a "netten Mieter" — a pleasant tenant who will not cause problems.

items: Arrive 5 minutes early — never be late
Dress smart casual: a shirt or blouse, nothing sporty
Greet everyone with a handshake (if it is not a group viewing)
Do not criticise the flat out loud in front of the landlord — even if there is visible mould
Take your shoes off if there are slippers at the door or others have done so
Take photos only with permission
Do not bring children under 5 — it is distracting and spoils the impression
Do not turn up in a large group — two people at most
At the end, hand over the printed folder with the words: "Hier ist meine vollständige Bewerbung" (here is my complete application)
Send a thank-you email the same evening confirming your interest

content.text: Too good to be true = a scam. If an 80 m² flat in central Berlin is going for 700€ warm rent (Warmmiete) and the landlord is "currently in the UK and will send the keys by post after a prepayment", that is rental fraud (Mietbetrug), 100%. Never pay anything before signing the contract and inspecting the place in person.

Do not sign the rental contract (Mietvertrag) right at the viewing. Take it home, read it over in the evening, and check the rent cap (Mietpreisbremse) for the area and any unlawful clauses (cosmetic repairs Schönheitsreparaturen with fixed deadlines — void under BGH rulings). If you are pressured with "sign now or it's gone", that is manipulation.

The handover protocol (Übergabeprotokoll) at move-in is a sacred document. Before signing it, walk through the ENTIRE flat and photograph every stain, scratch and crack. Note the meter readings (water Wasser, electricity Strom, gas Gas). Sign both copies and keep one. Without this, when you move out the landlord will pin the previous tenants' defects on you.

The agent's commission (Maklerprovision) for rentals is governed by the orderer principle (Bestellerprinzip; since 2015): whoever hired the agent pays. If the landlord placed the listing, the landlord pays the commission, not you. Demanding money from the tenant for a rental that the landlord ordered is unlawful (§2 Abs. 1a WoVermRG). The maximum permitted commission is 2 net cold rents (Nettokaltmieten) plus 19% VAT (USt).

costs.label: Besichtigung — the visit itself
costs.note: Free; any request for money to view = a scam

costs.label: Travel in large cities
costs.note: A day ticket for public transport (Tageskarte ÖPNV) — if you are rushing to 3-5 viewings in a day

costs.label: Agent's commission (Maklerprovision) — if you hired the agent
costs.note: A maximum of 2 net cold rents (Nettokaltmieten) + 19% VAT (USt) under §3 WoVermRG

costs.label: Mieterbund-Mitgliedschaft
costs.note: Legal advice on the rental contract and handover protocol, annual membership
