title: bonify: monitoring your Schufa (the largest credit bureau)
tldr: bonify (bonify.de) is a free service for monitoring your Schufa score. Since 2023 it has belonged to Schufa Holding and shows your real score with no delay, plus alerts about changes. It's more convenient than the paid BonitätsAuskunft (29.95€ per request) if you only need to view and keep track of your score. Important: on 17 March 2026 SCHUFA switched to a new score scale of 100–999 (instead of the former Basisscore of 0–100%) and made the online account with your data and score free for everyone — so a separate monitoring service is now needed less often.

content.text: Schufa is Germany's main credit bureau. Its score (since 17 March 2026 — a new scale of 100–999, the higher the better; previously it was a Basisscore of 0–100%) is checked by landlords, mobile operators, banks and car-leasing companies. In the past, to view it you had to pay for the BonitätsAuskunft (29.95€ per request) or request a free data copy (Datenkopie) once a year under Art. 15 DSGVO (it used to arrive by paper letter in 2–4 weeks; now the data is also available online).

Bonify started out as a startup offering free access to your score. In 2023 it was acquired by Schufa Holding, and it now operates as SCHUFA's official app for private individuals: free, in real time, with alerts about changes to your score and entries.

items: Your real SCHUFA score updates automatically
Alerts when new entries appear
The option to download a BonitätsAuskunft at a discount or for free (depending on the plan)
Read-only — it does not affect the score itself
Available via app and web

content.text: Registration takes 5–10 minutes and requires identity verification (to rule out fraud under someone else's name).

items.title: 1. Download the app or go to bonify.de

items: Name, date of birth, address (as in your residence registration, Anmeldung)
Email and password
Consent to query your data at Schufa

content.text: Video-Ident with your passport/residence permit, or confirmation via a bank account (linking your IBAN with a micro-transaction). Without verification your score won't be shown.

The score is shown on the new 100–999 scale (since 17 March 2026; previously it was a percentage, 0–100). The entries cover all current accounts (Girokonto), credit cards, instalment plans and phone contracts. If you see an entry that isn't yours or an error — use the 'Korrektur anfordern' button (request a correction). SCHUFA is required to review the request within one month (Art. 15/16 DSGVO, § 34 BDSG).

Bonify shows the basic score, but for a rental contract (Mietvertrag) a landlord often needs the paper BonitätsAuskunft specifically (with a stamp, as of a given date). You'll still have to order it separately for 29.95€ — but through bonify it's often cheaper or included in the premium plan.

Don't confuse the free data copy (Datenkopie, § 34 BDSG / Art. 15 DSGVO) with the BonitätsAuskunft. The Datenkopie is the legally required disclosure of your data, without a stamp, free once a year. The BonitätsAuskunft is a commercial certificate to present to third parties.

Viewing your own score through bonify does NOT lower your Schufa (it's a 'Selbstauskunft'). But every query from a bank/landlord (a 'Kreditanfrage') slightly lowers your score for a few months. So don't apply to 10 banks in a row.

title: Credit cards in Germany: Mastercard, Visa, AmEx
tldr: In Germany a real 'credit card' (a Kreditkarte with a monthly statement) is less common than a Mastercard/Visa debit card. Visa and Mastercard are accepted almost everywhere; American Express — in large chains and online, but not at the bakery (Bäckerei) or the snack bar (Imbiss). AmEx Blue is free, Gold starts at 144€/year (the new metal version — 240€/year), Platinum 720€/year. To build a credit history at Schufa (the largest credit bureau), getting a real credit card usually requires about 6 months of residency.

steps.title: Three types of card in Germany

content.text: In Germany you need to distinguish: (1) Debitkarte (instant debit from your account — N26, DKB, ING, comdirect issue exactly this under the Visa/Mastercard brand); (2) Charge-Karte (the balance builds up over the month and is debited as a single sum — the classic AmEx Gold/Platinum); (3) Kreditkarte with a real credit line and the option to pay in instalments (revolving credit — rare in Germany; typical examples are Barclaycard, the DKB Visa Kreditkarte).

items: Visa and Mastercard — the widest acceptance
AmEx — large chains, hotels, online; not at bakeries
A real Kreditkarte = +Schufa history
Visa/MC Debit ≠ a credit card for renting a car abroad (some rental companies don't accept Debit)
Cashback and bonuses — mainly on premium AmEx and DKB tiers

content.text: The strategy depends on your needs: everyday spending, business trips, or building up your Schufa.

items: DKB Visa Debit — included with the Cash-Konto
ING Visa Debit — included with the Girokonto
Barclays Visa — a real credit card, 0€/year, revolving credit
AmEx Blue Card — 0€/year, no minimum income
Hanseatic Genialcard — 0€/year, no foreign fee

content.text: 144€/year on the previous version; since March 2025 new customers can only get the metal Gold for 240€/year. The Membership Rewards welcome bonus depends on the current promotion (check on americanexpress.com/de). Access to some Lounges via Priority Pass with a guest. Travel insurance.
720€/year. Full Priority Pass, Centurion Lounges, 200€ travel credit, Marriott Gold + Hilton Gold + Sixt Platinum status. Worth it if you spend >3000€/month on travel.

For your Schufa score to grow, you need at least one real Kreditkarte with a monthly limit (not a Debit) that you use and pay off on time. The DKB Visa Kreditkarte or Barclaycard are the most accessible after 6 months of residence registration (Anmeldung).
AmEx is NOT accepted everywhere in Germany. ALDI, Lidl, small supermarkets, most bakeries, snack bars and taxis (not Uber) do NOT accept AmEx. Always have a Visa or Mastercard as a backup.

Visa Debit ≠ Visa Credit when renting a car, especially in the USA/Canada/UK. Sixt in Germany accepts Debit; Hertz and Avis abroad often don't. If you plan to rent cars often, get at least a basic Barclays Visa Kreditkarte.

AmEx revolving (minimum payment 5–10%) charges 18–22% per year on overdue balances — which gets expensive. AmEx is a charge card; by the rules it must be paid in full every month. Don't confuse it with European credit cards.
When you get any real Kreditkarte, Schufa makes a 'harte Anfrage' — your score temporarily dips for 6–12 months. Don't apply to several banks at once.

content.text: Girocard is Germany's national payment system, run by Deutsche Kreditwirtschaft. Until 2007 it was called 'EC-Karte' (Electronic Cash), and many Germans still call it that out of habit ('Zahlen Sie mit EC?'). Technologically it works differently from Visa/Mastercard and doesn't work outside Germany without a co-badge.

Many older terminals in small shops accept Girocard only by PIN, without contactless. Remember your PIN; don't rely on Apple Pay alone (though Apple Pay with Girocard has worked since 2020 at Sparkasse and Volksbank).

A big trap for those who arrive with only an N26: you walk up to a bakery (Bäckerei), order an 8€ breakfast, and at the till — 'Nur Girocard oder Bar' (only Girocard or cash). The N26 Mastercard Debit won't be accepted. Always keep 20–50€ in cash in your wallet.

Withdrawing cash with a Girocard AT ANOTHER bank's ATM (not your own network) costs 4–8€ per withdrawal. Use: a Sparkasse card at a Sparkasse ATM, Volksbank at Volksbank, or the Cash Group / Cashpool networks for your banks.

title: Freistellungsauftrag: exempting €1000
tldr: A Freistellungsauftrag is an instruction to your bank NOT to withhold tax on your capital income (interest, dividends, gains from sales) up to the tax-free allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag): 1000 € for a single person and 2000 € for spouses/partners with a joint instruction. Without it, the bank immediately withholds the withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25 % (+ the solidarity surcharge Soli + church tax). The legal basis is §44a EStG and §20 Abs. 9 EStG. The instruction is filed with the bank free of charge online; you need your tax identification number (Steuer-ID) for it. You can split the allowance across several banks, but the total must not exceed 1000/2000 €.

content.text: Capital income (Kapitalerträge) — interest on deposits, dividends, gains from selling stocks/ETFs — is taxed via the withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) at a rate of 25 % plus the solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) and, where applicable, church tax. The bank withholds this tax automatically. But everyone is entitled to a tax-free allowance, the Sparerpauschbetrag: 1000 € per year (2000 € for spouses with a joint instruction). A Freistellungsauftrag tells the bank not to withhold tax up to this amount.

Without a Freistellungsauftrag the bank will withhold tax even on the first euro of interest. The money isn't lost — you can reclaim it through your annual tax return (the Anlage KAP attachment to the return). But that's extra paperwork, and the money only comes back a year later. It's far easier to file the instruction once and receive income up to the limit tax-free right away.

The Sparerpauschbetrag is 1000 € for a single person and 2000 € for spouses/registered partners who have filed a joint instruction (Gemeinsamer Freistellungsauftrag). If you have accounts at several banks, you can split the allowance between them — but the TOTAL of all instructions must not exceed 1000/2000 € (§20 Abs. 9 EStG).

items: 1000 € per year per person, 2000 € for spouses (jointly)
Can be split across several banks
The sum of all Freistellungsaufträge ≤ the limit — otherwise it's a violation
Applies to interest, dividends and gains from selling securities

content.text: A Freistellungsauftrag is filed free of charge with each bank/broker where you have capital income. Usually it's a couple of clicks in your online banking. You absolutely need your tax identification number (Steuer-Identifikationsnummer, Steuer-ID) — without it the bank cannot apply the exemption.

items: Log in to your online banking → the Freistellungsauftrag / Steuern section
Enter the exemption amount and your Steuer-ID
For spouses, choose the joint instruction (Gemeinsamer FSA)
Confirm — the instruction usually takes effect from 1 January of the current year
Split the 1000/2000 € across banks by their share of the income
For example, 600 € at bank A and 400 € at bank B
Make sure the total doesn't exceed the limit
Adjust the distribution if you change your deposits

steps.title: What else is important to know

content.text: The instruction stays in effect until you change or revoke it, and it covers the entire calendar year. The limit has been indexed: until 2023 it was 801/1602 €, now it's 1000/2000 €. Banks automatically recalculated old instructions proportionally, but check the amounts yourself.

If your total capital income exceeds the limit, the bank will withhold 25 % tax on the excess — that's normal. But if your overall income is low, the 25 % rate may be higher than your personal rate — in that case, through your tax return (the more-favourable-option check, Günstigerprüfung; the Anlage KAP attachment) you can reclaim part of it. For church tax, the bank automatically queries your religious-affiliation flag at the Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt); to keep the bank from seeing it, you can file a blocking notice (Sperrvermerk) at the BZSt. In complex cases (several income sources, foreign accounts) it makes sense to consult a tax advisor (Steuerberater).

costs.label: Filing a Freistellungsauftrag
costs.note: Free at any bank/broker.

costs.label: Sparerpauschbetrag — limit per person
costs.note: 2000 € for spouses with a joint instruction (§20 Abs. 9 EStG).

costs.label: Abgeltungsteuer without an instruction
costs.note: 25 % + Soli (+ church tax) is withheld on all capital income without an FSA.

title: Current account (Girokonto) vs instant-access savings (Tagesgeld) vs fixed-term deposit (Festgeld)
tldr: Three basic types of account in Germany solve different tasks. The current account (Girokonto) is for everyday payments: salary, rent, card, SEPA transfers (the single European payments area); the interest is close to zero. The instant-access account (Tagesgeld) is for an 'emergency cushion': the money is available at any moment, the rate floats, and the interest is higher than on a Giro. A fixed-term deposit (Festgeld) 'locks' the money for a term (3 months to several years) at a fixed rate, usually higher than Tagesgeld, but you can't withdraw early. In all cases deposits are protected by the deposit guarantee scheme (Einlagensicherung) up to 100 000 € (EU banks). Interest is subject to the withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) — file an exemption instruction (Freistellungsauftrag).

content.text: The current account (Girokonto) is the main account you can't do without in Germany: your salary comes in to it, and rent, insurance and subscriptions are debited from it via direct debit (Lastschrift); a debit card is linked to it. Interest on the balance is usually zero or symbolic — it's not a savings tool but a 'wallet'.

items: For salary, rent, cards and SEPA transfers
Supports direct debit (Lastschrift; auto-debits) and recurring payments (Dauerauftrag; standing orders)
Interest ~0 % — not for savings
Often free with regular incoming funds (online banks)

content.text: A Tagesgeldkonto is an account for an 'emergency cushion'. The money is available at any moment (no lock-up period), the rate floats and the bank may change it. The interest is noticeably higher than on a Giro. You can't pay by card directly from a Tagesgeld — the money is transferred back to your Girokonto.

items: Money available any day (no term)
Floating rate, the bank may change it
Good for a reserve fund (3–6 salaries)
Paying by card isn't possible — only a transfer to the Giro

steps.title: Festgeld — a fixed term and rate

content.text: A fixed-term deposit (Festgeld) — you put the money in for a fixed term (for example, 6, 12, 24 months) at a rate known in advance. It's usually higher than Tagesgeld and doesn't change during the term. The downside: until the end of the term the money is generally unavailable without losing the interest.

items: You have a sum you definitely won't need for N months
You want to lock in a rate in a falling market
You're ready not to touch the money until the end of the term
The term and the rate (effektiver Jahreszins)
What happens at the end of the term (auto-renewal? — turn it off if needed)
The bank's country and its deposit protection scheme

content.text: Deposits at EU banks are protected by the deposit guarantee scheme (Einlagensicherung) — by law up to 100 000 € per customer per bank. So it's better to spread a large sum across different banks/countries, staying under the limit at each. Interest on Tagesgeld and Festgeld is capital income (Kapitalerträge), taxed via the withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25 %.

To avoid paying tax on interest up to 1000 € (2000 € for spouses), file an exemption instruction (Freistellungsauftrag) with the bank — otherwise the bank will immediately withhold the 25 % withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer). Also be careful with high 'welcome' rates: they're often a promotion lasting 3–6 months, after which the rate drops. Focus on the rate for existing customers (Bestandskunden), not just the promo period.

costs.label: Girokonto — maintenance
costs.note: Often free at online banks with regular incoming funds; branch banks may charge a monthly fee.

costs.label: Tagesgeld / Festgeld — opening and maintenance
costs.note: Usually free; you earn on the interest.

costs.label: Deposit protection (Einlagensicherung)
costs.note: Statutory protection up to 100 000 € per customer per bank (EU).

title: German IBAN: DE + 20 digits
tldr: A German IBAN is always 22 characters long: country code DE + 2 check digits (Prüfziffer) + 8 digits of the bank code (Bankleitzahl, BLZ) + 10 digits of the account number (Kontonummer). Format example: DE00 0000 0000 0000 0000 00. Under SEPA rules, a single IBAN is enough for a transfer within the euro zone — a BIC is usually NOT needed. Under IBAN-Only, a company may not legally refuse a direct debit (Lastschrift) or your salary because of a 'foreign' IBAN from another SEPA country (IBAN discrimination (IBAN-Diskriminierung) is prohibited by EU Regulation 260/2012). A SEPA transfer within the EU is free or nearly free and usually arrives within 1 business day (Instant — within seconds).

steps.title: What a German IBAN is made of

content.text: An IBAN (International Bank Account Number) in Germany always consists of 22 characters. Structure: DE (country code) + 2 check digits (Prüfziffer, for error detection) + 8-digit bank code (Bankleitzahl, BLZ) + 10-digit account number (Kontonummer, padded with leading zeros where needed).

items: Always 22 characters for Germany
DE — country code
2 digits — check number (Prüfziffer, checksum)
8 digits — bank code (Bankleitzahl)
10 digits — account number (Kontonummer)

content.text: For transfers within the SEPA zone (EU/EEA countries in euros), the IBAN-Only rule means a single IBAN is enough — you do NOT need to enter a BIC; the bank works it out automatically. A BIC may be required only for transfers outside SEPA (for example, to non-EU countries) or in a foreign currency.

items: SEPA transfer (in euros within the EU/EEA): only the IBAN is needed
A BIC is required for payments outside SEPA or in another currency
Just give the recipient your IBAN and name

content.text: Under EU Regulation 260/2012 (SEPA-Verordnung), so-called IBAN discrimination is prohibited: an employer, landlord, insurer or utility company may NOT demand a specifically German IBAN and may not refuse to pay your salary or to set up a direct debit just because you have an IBAN from another SEPA country (many fintechs issue an IBAN from another SEPA country — for example, N26 historically gave German DE-IBANs, while a number of services issue Lithuanian LT- or Irish IE-IBANs).

If a company says 'we only accept IBANs starting with DE', that is a breach of SEPA rules. You can point to the ban on IBAN discrimination and, if necessary, complain to BaFin. In practice almost all German parties accept an IBAN from another SEPA country without any problem, but it pays to know your rights.

steps.title: How to make a transfer and check the IBAN

content.text: For a SEPA transfer in your online banking, enter the recipient's IBAN, name and the amount. A regular transfer arrives within 1 business day; an instant SEPA transfer (SEPA-Echtzeitüberweisung, Instant Payment) arrives within seconds (often free). Check the IBAN before sending: the check digits guard against typos, but verify the recipient's name yourself.

items: Enter the IBAN, the recipient's name and the amount
Payment reference (Verwendungszweck) — for example, an account or contract number
Choose a regular or instant (Echtzeit, Instant) transfer
The length is strictly 22 characters for DE
Compare each block of digits against the original
Unsure about the recipient? Send a small amount first

costs.label: SEPA transfer in euros (within the EU)
costs.note: Usually free at banks for private customers.

costs.label: SEPA-Echtzeitüberweisung (Instant)
costs.note: Often free; some banks charge a small fee.

costs.label: Transfer outside SEPA / in a currency
costs.note: Depends on the bank and country; a BIC is needed here.

title: ING: the online-banking classic
tldr: ING (formerly ING-DiBa) is one of Germany's largest online banks. The current account (Girokonto) is free with a monthly incoming payment (benchmark from around 700 €), otherwise a monthly fee applies. It comes with a free Girocard debit card and a Visa Debit, and cash withdrawals with the Visa are free above a certain amount at many ATMs. You open it online with VideoIdent/PostIdent; you need a German address and a tax identification number (Steuer-ID). It supports Apple Pay and Google Pay. Deposits are covered by deposit insurance (Einlagensicherung) up to 100,000 €. ING is also popular for an instant-access savings account (Tagesgeld, Extra-Konto) and brokerage (Depot) — handy for keeping everything at one bank.

steps.title: What ING is and who it suits

content.text: ING (formerly ING-DiBa) is a large German online bank with no branches and a long-standing reputation. Its core product is a free current account (Girokonto) with a Girocard and a Visa Debit. It is convenient because you can keep a current account, an instant-access savings account (Tagesgeld, Extra-Konto) and a brokerage account (Depot) all at one bank. A good choice for newcomers who value stability and support in German.

items: Fully online — app and web banking
Current account + Girocard + Visa Debit
All in one place: current account, instant-access savings account (Tagesgeld, Extra-Konto), brokerage account (Depot)
Supports Apple Pay and Google Pay

steps.title: What you need to open one

content.text: You will need a German address (once you have your residence registration, Anmeldung), a valid ID document and a tax identification number (Steuer-ID). Identification is done online via VideoIdent or in person via PostIdent at the post office. The interface and support are in German; basic information is sometimes also available in English.

items: Residence registration in Germany (an address after the Anmeldung)
Passport or EU ID card
Tax identification number (Steuer-Identifikationsnummer, Steuer-ID)
A smartphone for VideoIdent and the app

content.text: You apply at ing.de: fill in the form, complete identification, and once you are approved the cards and PIN arrive by post, in separate letters. Then you set up the app and, if you like, add Apple Pay or Google Pay.

items: ing.de → Girokonto eröffnen
Fill in your details and provide your Steuer-ID
Complete VideoIdent (have your ID ready) or PostIdent
Wait for the cards and PIN (in separate letters)
Install the ING app and confirm your login
Add Apple Pay / Google Pay if you want
Set up a regular incoming payment to keep the account free

content.text: Deposits at ING are protected by the German deposit insurance scheme (Einlagensicherung) up to 100,000 € per customer. Cash withdrawals with the Visa card are free at many ATMs above a certain minimum amount. The instant-access savings account (Tagesgeld, Extra-Konto) is free to open and conveniently linked to your current account for moving reserves around.

The ING current account is free with a monthly incoming payment (benchmark from around 700 €) OR for customers under 28. Without meeting that condition, the bank charges a monthly fee. Terms change from time to time — check the current requirements and pricing at ing.de before opening.

costs.label: Girokonto — maintenance (with incoming payment)
costs.note: Free with a monthly incoming payment from roughly around 700 € or for customers under 28.

costs.label: Girokonto — without incoming payment
costs.note: A monthly fee may apply; depends on the current pricing.

costs.label: Extra-Konto (Tagesgeld)
costs.note: Free to open and maintain; the return is interest.

title: Schufa score: how to improve it
tldr: SCHUFA is Germany's largest credit bureau, and almost every contract that involves deferred payment (renting a flat, a phone plan, a loan, instalments, a credit card) comes with a SCHUFA check. Your Schufa-Score credit rating (since 17 March 2026, a single 100–999 scale based on 12 disclosed criteria; the former base score (Basisscore) in percent 0–100% and the separate industry scores have been abolished, so every requester now sees one value) shows banks and landlords how likely you are to pay. It does not improve quickly, but it does improve steadily: pay your bills on time, do not open unnecessary accounts and cards, do not max out your credit lines, avoid switching banks (Kontowechsel) frequently, and be sure to correct any errors in your data. Once a year you are entitled to a free copy of your data (Datenkopie under Art. 15 DSGVO). Incorrect negative entries are a common cause of a low score, and you can and should dispute them.

steps.title: What the Schufa score is and what it affects

content.text: SCHUFA (Schutzgemeinschaft für allgemeine Kreditsicherung) collects data about your contracts: accounts, cards, loans, instalment plans and mobile contracts. Based on that data it calculates a credit rating (Score) — an estimate of how likely you are to meet your obligations. Banks, landlords, telecom operators and online shops request it before signing a contract.

items: The rating is a single 100–999 scale (since 17 March 2026; the higher, the better). It used to be a base score (Basisscore) in percent 0–100%
With the reform of 17 March 2026, the six industry scores (Branchenscores) were replaced by a single score, so every company sees the same value
What it affects: loan approval, instalment terms, renting a flat, a mobile contract
What it does NOT affect: your salary and nationality are not directly part of the score
A conditions enquiry 'Konditionsanfrage' does not hurt the rating, unlike a credit enquiry 'Kreditanfrage'

content.text: There is no magic way to raise the rating in a day — it reflects your behaviour over time. But there is a set of habits that steadily improve it, and a few typical mistakes that drag it down.

items: Pay all bills and direct-debit payments (Lastschrift) on time — late payments and payment reminders (Mahnungen) hit the rating hardest
Do not open lots of accounts and credit cards 'just in case' — having too many worsens the score
Do not use your credit lines and overdraft (Dispo) in full — keep your debt low
Avoid switching banks (Kontowechsel) frequently over a short period
When buying on credit or instalments, ask for a conditions enquiry 'Konditionsanfrage' rather than a credit enquiry 'Kreditanfrage'
Close unnecessary old cards and unused contracts

content.text: Too many credit enquiries in a short period (for example, when you apply to five banks in a row) are read by SCHUFA as a risk signal. Compare offers via a conditions enquiry (Konditionsanfrage) instead — this type of enquiry is visible only to you and does not lower the rating. And keep in mind: closing a very old account can unexpectedly wipe out a 'positive history', so sometimes it is better to keep the old account active.

About a third of people's SCHUFA records contain inaccuracies: debts that were paid off but never closed, other people's entries due to matching names, or outdated address data. Every incorrect negative entry pulls the rating down, so the first step to improving it is to check and clean up your data.

items: Request a free copy of your data, the Datenkopie (Art. 15 DSGVO), at meineschufa.de
Check every entry: is it current, is it yours, has it been paid?
If you find an error, file a written objection with SCHUFA, with supporting evidence
SCHUFA is obliged to check and delete or correct incorrect data
Settled debts must be marked as 'erledigt' (settled); keep an eye on the deletion deadlines (Löschfristen)

content.text: Do not pay dubious 'Schufa improvement companies' that promise to 'erase' entries for money — correct negative entries cannot be deleted, and you can fix errors yourself for free. Be careful: some of them harvest your data or charge you for nothing. The official and free route is via meineschufa.de and a written objection.

costs.label: Datenkopie (Art. 15 DSGVO)
costs.note: Free once a year (Art. 15 DSGVO); since the 2026 reform the score and data are also available in the free online SCHUFA account

costs.label: Correcting an incorrect entry
costs.note: Filing an objection and correcting incorrect data with SCHUFA is free.

costs.label: Paid monitoring / BonitätsAuskunft
costs.note: Monitoring subscriptions (~3.95 €/month) or a one-off BonitätsAuskunft (29.95 €) — not required to improve your score.

sources.title: Verbraucherzentrale — Scoring mit Kundendaten: Auskunft bei Schufa & Co. verlangen

title: Anlage N: the return for employees
tldr: Anlage N is the main attachment to the income tax return (Einkommensteuererklärung) for everyone who earns a salary (Arbeitslohn) as an employee. In it you report the salary from your wage and tax statement (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung), your work-related expenses (Werbungskosten), and the wage tax (Lohnsteuer), solidarity surcharge (Soli) and church tax (Kirchensteuer) that were withheld. The deadline for a voluntary return is 4 years (until 31.12.2030 for 2026); for a mandatory return it is usually 31.07.2027 for 2026 (or 28.02.2028 if you use a tax adviser, Steuerberater).

steps.title: What Anlage N is and why you need it

content.text: Anlage N (Anlage Nichtselbständige Arbeit) is an attachment to the main form (Mantelbogen) ESt 1 A, in which an employee (Arbeitnehmer) declares income from employment (Einkünfte aus nichtselbständiger Arbeit, §19 EStG). The data from the wage and tax statement (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung), which your employer sends by the end of February of the following year, is carried over here. Anlage N also lets you claim work-related expenses (Werbungskosten) and get back overpaid wage tax (Lohnsteuer).

If the standard deduction for employees (Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag, 1,230 € per year since 2023) is higher than your actual work-related expenses, the tax office applies it automatically. It is worth filing a return if your expenses exceed this amount.

items: Filed together with the Mantelbogen ESt 1 A
The standard deduction for employees (Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag) of 1,230 € is applied automatically
The average refund via Anlage N in Germany is around 1,000–1,100 €
Code name in ELSTER: ESt 1 A + Anlage N

steps.title: What to enter: the key fields of Anlage N

content.text: Anlage N has two pages. The first holds the data from the wage and tax statement (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung); the second holds your work-related expenses (Werbungskosten).

items.title: 1. Income from the wage and tax statement (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung)

items: Gross salary (Bruttoarbeitslohn, line 3 of the statement) → line 6 of Anlage N
Withheld wage tax (Einbehaltene Lohnsteuer) → line 19
Solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) → line 20
Church tax (Kirchensteuer) → line 21
The employer's eTIN or Steuer-ID
If you had several employers, file a separate Anlage N for each
Commuting allowance (Entfernungspauschale): a flat 0.38 €/km from the 1st kilometre — from 2026 (Steueränderungsgesetz 2025); the former tiered 0.30/0.38 € scheme no longer applies
Work equipment (Arbeitsmittel): laptop, phone, literature, protective clothing
Professional development (Fortbildung): German courses, IT certificates, conferences
Home office study (Häusliches Arbeitszimmer) or the working-from-home flat rate (Homeoffice-Pauschale, 6 €/day, up to 1,260 €/year for 2026)
Job-application costs (Bewerbungskosten): printouts, photos, travel to interviews
Maintaining two households (Doppelte Haushaltsführung, a second flat for work)
Contributions to professional associations (Berufsverbände) and a trade union (Gewerkschaft)

content.text: Fill it in via Mein ELSTER (mein.elster.de) — the 'Einkommensteuererklärung' form with the Anlage N attachment. Once you have logged in with a certificate file (Zertifikatsdatei) or via ELSTERSecure, the form is partly pre-filled (Belegabruf — retrieval of statements): your salary, wage tax, and health and pension insurance contributions (Kranken-/Rentenversicherung) are already loaded automatically.

An employee in tax class (Steuerklasse) I, with a gross annual salary (Bruttojahreslohn) of 55,000 €, commutes 30 km one way over 220 working days. Wage tax (Lohnsteuer) of 9,800 € was withheld. The calculation uses the 2026 rate.

items: Commuting allowance (Entfernungspauschale): 30 km × 0.38 € = 11.40 €/day × 220 = 2,508 €
Homeoffice (50 days): 50 × 6 € = 300 €
Arbeitsmittel (laptop, partial): 400 €
Total work-related expenses: 3,208 € (instead of the standard deduction Pauschbetrag of 1,230 €)
Additional deduction: 1,978 €
Tax saving at a ~30% rate: ~593 € refund

content.text: The commuting allowance (Entfernungspauschale) counts only for days you actually went to work, not calendar days. If you worked from home for 100 days, the trips for those days do not count (but instead you can claim the working-from-home flat rate, Homeoffice-Pauschale).
Do not double up: for any single day you can claim either the commuting allowance or the working-from-home flat rate, not both.

Retrieval of statements (Belegabruf) in ELSTER does not always show all the data. Check it against the paper wage and tax statement (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung) — even a single-digit difference will trigger a follow-up query (Rückfrage) from the tax office (Finanzamt).

If you received short-time work allowance (Kurzarbeitergeld), parental allowance (Elterngeld), or unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld) I of more than 410 €, a return is mandatory (progression proviso, Progressionsvorbehalt, §32b EStG).

costs.label: ELSTER
costs.note: Free for everyone

costs.label: WISO Steuer / Smartsteuer
costs.note: Paid software with prompts; pays for itself if you are unsure about Werbungskosten

costs.label: Lohnsteuerhilfeverein (membership)
costs.note: Annual fee; suitable for employees with up to 13,000 €/26,000 € (single/family) of passive income

costs.label: Steuerberater
costs.note: Per StBVV; for complex cases

title: Außergewöhnliche Belastungen: deductions for medical costs
tldr: Extraordinary expenses (Außergewöhnliche Belastungen, §33 EStG) are unavoidable large expenses — above all medical ones — that exceed reasonable limits. They are reimbursed through your tax return for the portion that exceeds the reasonable burden (zumutbare Belastung, 1–7% of income). This covers treatment, glasses, dental work, rehabilitation and care for relatives. Receipts and a doctor's prescription (Verordnung) are mandatory.

content.text: Extraordinary expenses (außergewöhnliche Belastungen allgemeiner Art, §33 EStG) are expenses that exceed the usual spending of other taxpayers with the same income and family situation. The tax office (Finanzamt) deducts from your taxable income only the portion that exceeds the reasonable burden (zumutbare Belastung), calculated under §33(3) EStG.

The reasonable burden depends on three factors: your level of income (Gesamtbetrag der Einkünfte), your marital status (single/married) and the number of children. The rate ranges from 1% to 7% of income and is applied in tiers (gestaffelt).

items: Governed by §33 EStG (general) and §33a/§33b EStG (special cases: alimony, the care flat rate (Pflege-Pauschbetrag), the disability flat rate (Behinderten-Pauschbetrag))
Entered in the main form (Mantelbogen) ESt 1 A on pages 3–4

Keep all receipts and invoices at least until the tax assessment (Steuerbescheid) becomes final (bestandskräftig) — in practice at least 8 years; for private individuals there is no fixed retention obligation under §147 AO (that applies to businesses; the period for accounting documents (Buchungsbelege) was reduced from 10 to 8 years from 2025)

content.text: First and foremost, health costs not covered by the health insurance fund (Krankenkasse). Important: you must have a doctor's prescription (Verordnung) BEFORE the purchase, otherwise the tax office will refuse it.

items: Patient co-payments (Zuzahlungen) at the pharmacy and for inpatient stays (10 €/day, max 28 days)
Braces, implants, dentures (the part not covered by the health insurance fund)
Glasses and contact lenses (an optician's prescription is needed)
Hearing aids
Naturopath (Heilpraktiker, if the method is generally recognised)
Physiotherapy by prescription (Rezept)
Psychotherapy (if not covered by the fund)
Rehabilitation (Reha) and spa treatment (Kuren) — with a certificate from a public health officer (amtsärztliches Attest) obtained BEFORE the treatment begins
Care flat rate (Pflege-Pauschbetrag): 600 € (care level Pflegegrad 2) up to 1,800 € (Pflegegrad 4/5) — §33b(6) EStG
Disability flat rate (Behinderten-Pauschbetrag): 384 €–2,840 € depending on the GdB (degree of disability), §33b(3)
With GdB 100% or the marks H/Bl/TBl in the disability ID card (Merkzeichen) — 7,400 €
Care-home costs (minus the household saving Haushaltsersparnis ~10,992 €/year)
Beerdigungskosten (funeral costs) — if the inheritance does not cover them
Recovery after a natural disaster (flood, fire)
Termination of pregnancy (Schwangerschaftsabbruch), artificial insemination (künstliche Befruchtung)
Divorce costs — NOT accepted since 2013 (BFH ruling)

steps.title: How to calculate the reasonable burden (zumutbare Belastung)

content.text: The calculation is tiered. Example: single, no children, income 50,000 €.

items: Reasonable burden = 767 + 2,080 = 2,847 €
If your medical costs were 4,500 €, you can deduct 4,500 − 2,847 = 1,653 €
At a 30% tax rate — a saving of about 496 €

content.text: For married couples and those with children the rates are lower (1–4%). Since 2017 a tiered calculation has applied (ruling of the Federal Fiscal Court, BFH-Urteil VI R 75/14), which is more favourable than the old method.

Without a public health officer's expert opinion (amtsärztliches Gutachten) obtained BEFORE the treatment begins, the tax office will reject the costs of: spa treatment (Kur), a special school in the case of dyslexia, psychotherapy with a non-fund psychotherapist, or a special diet for an illness.
Costs reimbursed by the health insurance fund, an insurance company (Versicherung) or your employer do not count. Enter only the net amount you paid yourself.
Cosmetic procedures, dietary supplements without a prescription, and gym memberships are NOT accepted, even with a doctor's recommendation.
Costs of treatment abroad are accepted, but the invoice must state the specific diagnosis and the procedures performed. The receipt must be in German or English, or come with a certified translation.

costs.note: Filing the return is free

costs.label: Amtsärztliches Attest
costs.note: Cost of the Gesundheitsamt opinion

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung of a medical invoice
costs.note: Per page, if you were treated abroad

title: Capital gains: 25% Abgeltungsteuer
tldr: Capital income (dividends, interest, profit from selling shares/ETFs) in Germany is subject to the withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% + 5.5% solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag, 26.375% in total) + church tax where applicable. The tax-free allowance for capital income (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) is 1,000 € for singles and 2,000 € for spouses. At German brokers the tax is withheld automatically at source (Quellensteuer); at foreign ones you have to declare it via the Anlage KAP attachment. Different rules apply to crypto (§23 EStG: hold for 1 year to qualify for exemption).

steps.title: What the withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) is

content.text: The withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer, §32d EStG) is a flat 25% tax on capital income (Einkünfte aus Kapitalvermögen, §20 EStG): dividends, interest on deposits, and realised profit from selling shares, ETFs, funds and bonds. On top of the 25% comes a solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) of 5.5% (26.375% in total) and, if you are registered with a church (Kirche), church tax (Kirchensteuer) of 8% or 9% of that tax (depending on the state).

The 'Abgeltung' (finality) principle means the tax is considered final — the taxed income is not added to your salary and does not affect progression (unless the more-favourable-option check (Günstigerprüfung) applies — see below).

items: Base rate: 25% + 5.5% Soli + 8/9% church tax (Kirchensteuer, if applicable)
Tax-free allowance for capital income (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) 2026: 1,000 € single / 2,000 € spouses
At a German broker the tax is automatically withheld as withholding tax (Quellensteuer)
Foreign brokers (IBKR, Trading 212, Trade Republic) — self-declaration via the Anlage KAP attachment

content.text: The main thing to do is set up an exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) with your German broker or bank. This is an instruction to exempt amounts within the tax-free allowance from tax.

items: Set it up in the broker's or bank's online account
You can split the 1,000 € across several banks (but no more than that in total)
Without this order the bank withholds tax even on the first euro
For spouses — a joint order (gemeinsamer Freistellungsauftrag, a joint return is required)

items.title: 2. Advance lump-sum tax (Vorabpauschale, the pre-tax on ETFs)

items: Introduced by the InvStG 2018 reform — for accumulating ETFs
Calculated annually as the Bundesbank base rate (Basiszins) × 70% × the fund's value
In 2024 many investors paid noticeable amounts for the first time due to the rise in the Basiszins (2.29% for 2023)
Reduces the base on a future sale (Anrechnung)

items.title: 3. Foreign broker — the Anlage KAP attachment

items: Obtain an annual tax statement (Jahressteuerbescheinigung) or its equivalent (for IBKR — a report for the calendar year)
Enter all dividends and realised trades in Anlage KAP
Claim the tax withheld at source (Quellensteuer) in other countries (US W-8BEN — 15%) in lines 41–44 of Anlage KAP
Under the double taxation agreement, the foreign withholding tax is credited

content.text: If your personal tax rate is below 25% (for example, because of low total income), you can ask for the ordinary rate to be applied — tick 'Günstigerprüfung' (the more-favourable-option check) in line 4 of Anlage KAP. The Finanzamt automatically picks the more favourable option.

Crypto assets are NOT subject to the withholding tax. Under the Ministry of Finance letter (BMF-Schreiben) of May 2022 and the 2023 update, they are classified as 'andere Wirtschaftsgüter' (other economic assets) and fall under private sale transactions (Privatveräußerungsgeschäfte, §23 EStG).

items: Speculation period (Spekulationsfrist): 1 year — if you held the asset for ≥ 1 year, the profit is tax-free
If you sold within a year: tax at your personal rate (up to 45% + Soli)
Tax-free threshold (Freigrenze): 1,000 € per year (from 2024, was 600 €) — not a tax-free allowance (Freibetrag) but a threshold (Freigrenze), meaning that at 1,001 € the whole amount is taxed
Staking, lending — special rules; Ministry of Finance letter (BMF-Schreiben) 06.03.2025 extends the speculation period to 10 years where assets are used to generate income
Report it in the Anlage SO attachment (Sonstige Einkünfte — other income)

content.text: Losses (Verluste) on shares (Aktien) can only be offset against profits (Gewinne) on shares — there is a separate loss-offset pot (Verlustverrechnungstopf) for 'Aktien'. Since 2020, losses on futures transactions (Termingeschäfte — options, futures) have been capped at 20,000 €/year — a contested rule, with the Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) yet to rule on it.

When you move to Germany, shares bought BEFORE the move do NOT get a new acquisition value (Anschaffungswert) as of the entry date (Zuzug) — the historical purchase price is used — so if the gain accrued while you were still abroad, the tax in DE will be on the entire profit. Document the acquisition cost (Anschaffungskosten) before moving.

Exit tax (Wegzugsteuer, §6 AStG): if you hold a stake of ≥ 1% in a corporation (Kapitalgesellschaft) and move away from Germany, this counts as a deemed sale, taxed on the entire profit. From 2025 the rules are tighter; deferral is possible only on a move to the EU/EEA, with a 7-year instalment plan.
The tax-free allowance for capital income (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) does not carry over between years. If you did not use it in 2025, it is lost.

title: Change your tax class (Steuerklasse): online via ELSTER
tldr: You can change your tax class online in your Mein ELSTER account (the tax authority's online portal) using the form 'Antrag auf Steuerklassenwechsel bei Ehegatten' (application to change the tax class for spouses) or 'Antrag auf Steuerklassenwahl'. You can change class several times a year (the restriction was lifted in 2020). The change takes effect from the month following submission. For single parents — tax class II with the single-parent relief (Entlastungsbetrag, since 2023: 4,260 € + 240 € for each additional child).

steps.title: What a tax class is and why change it

content.text: Your tax class (Steuerklasse, §38b EStG) determines how much wage tax (Lohnsteuer) your employer withholds from your salary each month. This is NOT the annual tax amount — that is recalculated in your tax return. The tax class only affects your cash flow during the year and the size of benefits tied to net salary (Nettolohn): Eltern-, Arbeitslosen-, Kranken-, Mutterschaftsgeld (parental, unemployment, sickness and maternity benefits).

items: I — single, divorced, widowed (after the first year)
II — single parents (Alleinerziehende) entitled to the relief (Entlastungsbetrag, 4,260 € + 240 €/child from the 2nd)
III — married, partner with lower or no income
IV — both spouses work with similar income (the default after marriage)
IV with a factor (IV mit Faktor) — a precise adjustment to avoid a back payment
V — married, partner with higher income
VI — for a second and any further jobs (without a tax-class card, Lohnsteuerklasse)

steps.title: Which combination is more advantageous, and when

content.text: For spouses the optimal combination depends on the ratio of incomes. III/V gives more net pay to the spouse in III and less to the one in V; but over the year the total is the same as with IV/IV. The only difference lies in how it is distributed and in the basis used for wage-replacement benefits (Lohnersatzleistungen): parental allowance (Elterngeld) and sickness benefit (Krankengeld).

items: One spouse earns substantially more (>60% of total income)
A child is expected in the family — the future recipient of parental allowance must be in class III for 7 months before the birth (which raises the basis for the allowance)
One of the spouses does not work or works in a mini-job (Minijob)
Note: with III/V a return is mandatory (§46(2) Nr. 3a EStG)
Similar incomes for both (difference <20%)
You do not want to file a return (if there are no other §46 triggers)
Simplicity — each pays tax as a single person, but the spousal splitting benefit (Splittingvorteil) is applied via the return (if you file)
The best option for most couples with different incomes
Wage tax is withheld more precisely — close to the annual tax amount (Steuerschuld)
Less chance of facing a back payment (Nachzahlung)
Introduced by §39f EStG; requested specifically via ELSTER

items.title: 4. Tax class II for single parents

items: Condition: you live alone with a child who is registered in your household (Haushalt)
You receive child benefit (Kindergeld) or the child tax allowance (Kinderfreibetrag)
Application via 'Versicherung zum Entlastungsbetrag für Alleinerziehende'
If a new partner moves in, you must return to class I, otherwise you face a penalty (Strafe)

steps.title: How to change it via ELSTER

content.text: Since 2020 (the Bürokratieentlastungsgesetz, the act to reduce bureaucracy) you can change your tax class as many times a year as you like — previously the limit was once a year. There is a separate form for spouses and a different one for single people.
mein.elster.de → log in with a certificate file (Zertifikatsdatei) or the ELSTERSecure app.

items: For spouses: 'Antrag auf Steuerklassenwechsel bei Ehegatten/Lebenspartnern'
For class IV with a factor: the same form, plus the 'Faktorverfahren' (factor method) checkbox
For single parents: 'Versicherung zum Entlastungsbetrag' (an Anlage attachment in the return) and a request to the tax office (Finanzamt)
Provide the tax identification numbers (Steuer-ID) of both spouses
Your current and desired tax classes
Estimated annual incomes (for the factor, Faktor)
Signature via the ELSTER certificate (ELSTER-Zertifikat) — both spouses must confirm, or one submits and the other formally signs

content.text: The change applies from the 1st of the month following submission. Submit on 15 June and it takes effect on 1 July. The employer sees the new class automatically via the ELStAM system (Elektronische Lohnsteuerabzugsmerkmale — electronic wage-tax deduction features).

The III/V → IV/IV-with-a-factor reform: the German government planned an automatic switch in 2030, but the reform has been postponed and the exact timing for 2026 is not confirmed. Keep an eye on the latest information from the Ministry of Finance (BMF) — for now all classes apply as before.
If you chose III/V, filing a return is MANDATORY (§46(2) Nr. 3a EStG). Miss it and you face a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag, 0.25%/month of the tax, min. 25 €/month).

Switching to class III before maternity leave is advantageous, but the family benefits office (Familienkasse) requires the class to have been in place for at least 7 months before the start of maternity protection (Mutterschutz). Plan ahead.
Class VI on a second job is standard. Do not be alarmed by the high withholding — the overpayment comes back via your return.

After a divorce: from the month of separation (Trennung) you can still stay in III/V until the end of the calendar year. From 1 January of the following year, both spouses move to class I (or II for the one the children live with).

title: DBA with Russia: status of the treaty in 2026
tldr: Important: the double taxation agreement (DBA) between Germany and Russia from 1996 formally remains in force, but Russia has unilaterally SUSPENDED key provisions (Articles 5–22 and 24) — Decree of the President of the Russian Federation No. 585 of 8 August 2023. In response, Germany (the Ministry of Finance letter BMF-Schreiben 'Stand der DBA', 20.01.2025) confirms that the DBA is legally retained, but that German taxation rights are no longer limited by it from 01.01.2024, because the Russian Federation has been placed on the list of non-cooperative jurisdictions (the act on countering tax havens, Steueroasen-Abwehrgesetz, StAbwG). In practice this means that reduced withholding-tax (Quellensteuer) rates and many crediting methods no longer apply, and income may be taxed in full in both countries. Any decision on a specific case should be made only through a tax adviser (Steuerberater).

steps.title: Status of the Russia-Germany DBA in 2026

content.text: The DBA between the FRG and the Russian Federation was signed in Moscow on 29 May 1996 and updated by a 2007 protocol. Formally, the agreement has not been denounced by either side. However, in 2023–2026 substantial changes took place that in practice strip it of effect for most articles.

Timeline: on 8 August 2023, by a verbal note, Russia unilaterally suspended Articles 5–22 and 24 of the DBA, as well as points 2–7 of the Protocol to the agreement (the basis being Decree of the President of the Russian Federation No. 585 of 08.08.2023). This affects, in particular, the reduced withholding-tax (Quellensteuer) rates on dividends, interest and royalties, and the non-discrimination provision (Art. 24). The German side, in the Ministry of Finance letter (BMF-Schreiben) 'Stand der Doppelbesteuerungsabkommen' of 20 January 2025, records that the agreement formally remains in force, but that German taxation rights are no longer limited by it from 01.01.2024, because the Russian Federation has been placed on the list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions (Steueroasen-Abwehrgesetz, StAbwG). From 2026, §11 StAbwG additionally applies (a restriction of benefits on dividend payments and the sale of shares). Status as of 2026: the DBA is technically in force, but effectively 'frozen'.

items: Formal status: the DBA has not been denounced and remains in the Federal Law Gazette (Bundesgesetzblatt)
Practical status: key provisions are mutually suspended
The Ministry of Finance letter (BMF-Schreiben) 'Stand der DBA zum 01.01.2025' of 20.01.2025 — the main source; see also Stand der DBA zum 01.01.2026
Each case must be handled individually, through a tax adviser (Steuerberater) and a Federal Central Tax Office statement (BZSt-Auskunft)

content.text: The situation is changing fast. Before taking any action (transferring money, selling property in Russia, receiving dividends from Russia), be sure to check against the latest publication of the Ministry of Finance (BMF) and the BZSt — the status here is given as of 2026-05-29.

If you are a German tax resident and receive income from Russia — or vice versa — protection (Schutz) against double taxation may not apply automatically. However, §34c EStG (Anrechnung ausländischer Steuern — crediting of foreign taxes) applies regardless of the DBA and can partly reduce the burden.

items.title: 1. Income from Russia for a German resident

items: Renting out a flat in Russia: taxed at 30% personal income tax (non-resident of Russia) or 13/15% (resident of Russia) — and then again in Germany
Dividends from Russian companies: the reduced 5%/15% rate under the DBA is no longer guaranteed — the full 15% may be withheld
Interest on a Russian deposit: personal income tax, then taxed again in DE
§34c(1) EStG lets you credit the Russian tax against the German one, but no more than the German tax on that income (the maximum creditable amount, Anrechnungshöchstbetrag)
Claimed via the Anlage AUS attachment to the return
Official confirmation of the Russian tax paid is required (a certified 2-NDFL certificate)
The document must be translated into German by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer)
An apostille (Apostille) is often required (Russia is a party to the Hague Convention)
A Russian pension (state or employment-based) for a German resident is taxed in DE
The Russian side does not withhold tax on the pensions of Russian residents, but if the recipient is a German resident, the situation is more complex
Reported in the Anlage R-AUS attachment (for foreign pensions)

steps.title: Residency: where you are a taxpayer

content.text: Section 1 EStG: you are subject to unlimited taxation (unbeschränkt steuerpflichtig) in Germany if you have a place of residence here (Wohnsitz, a flat) or your habitual abode (gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt, a continuous stay of more than 6 months). This means your worldwide income (Welteinkommen) is taxed. On the Russian side, under the Russian Tax Code, a resident is someone who spends more than 183 days a year in Russia.

Where a DBA exists, a tie-breaker applies under Article 4 of the DBA (permanent home → centre of vital interests → habitual abode → nationality). With this mechanism suspended, both countries may assert your residency — a technical 'dual residence'. This is the most problematic situation.

items: Germany: §1 EStG — place of residence or habitual abode
Russia: Art. 207 of the Russian Tax Code — 183+ days within 12 months
With dual residence and no DBA tie-breaker, both countries may claim you
Document every day of presence, plus tickets, rent and bills
Keep all certificates of tax withheld in Russia
Have translations certified
Get an apostille on key documents (ownership certificates, bank statements)
Keep the paper originals — electronic ones may be rejected
Look for an adviser experienced with the DBA with Russia (DBA-Russland) — there are not many
An income-tax help association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein) is NOT allowed to advise on foreign income — only a tax adviser can
For large amounts, request a binding ruling (verbindliche Auskunft) from the tax office (Finanzamt) — it is paid for, but legally binding

content.text: The Anlage AUS attachment is filled in separately for each type of income and each country. You enter the gross amount, the foreign tax, and the elimination method (Anrechnung — crediting — under §34c(1), or a deduction as work-related expenses, Werbungskosten, under §34c(3)).
Do not rely on old DBA calculators and materials from 2022 or earlier — after August 2023 many provisions no longer apply. Check only against the latest Ministry of Finance letters (BMF-Schreiben).

Transferring money between Germany and Russia: besides tax matters, there is sanctions legislation (EU-Verordnung 833/2014 and its extensions). For amounts above 100,000 € per year, pay special attention — a permit (Genehmigung) from the German Federal Bank (Deutsche Bundesbank) or BAFA may be required.

Russian assets (Russisches Vermögen — real estate, accounts): for the German tax office, everything must be declared in the return (the worldwide-income principle, Welteinkommensprinzip). Concealment is tax evasion (Steuerhinterziehung, §370 AO), a criminal offence.

Duty to cooperate (Mit-Wirkungspflicht) under §90 AO: for foreign income, the taxpayer is obliged to provide ADDITIONAL information (an extended duty to cooperate, erweiterte Mitwirkungspflicht). The tax office can reject expenses and credits if the documentation is insufficient.

title: DBA with Ukraine: rules and application
tldr: The double taxation agreement between Germany and Ukraine from 1981 (with a 1996/2003 protocol) is in force and fully applied. Dividends — 5%/10%, interest — 0%/2%/5%, royalties — 0%/5%. The method of elimination is crediting (Anrechnung, §34c EStG). For Ukrainians with temporary protection (§24 AufenthG), the special residency rules matter. The Finanzamt confirms application of the DBA via a certificate of tax residency (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung) from the Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt).

content.text: The agreement currently in force between the FRG and Ukraine was signed on 3 July 1995 (building on the earlier Soviet-German one from 1981) and entered into force in 1996. It was amended by a 2012 protocol. The agreement remains fully in force in 2026 — neither side has suspended its provisions.

items: The DBA is in force and applied by both sides
Published in the Federal Law Gazette (Bundesgesetzblatt) II 1996 S. 252
Method of elimination: crediting (§34c EStG)
Status confirmed in the current DBA-Liste of the Ministry of Finance (BMF) 2026

content.text: The DBA sets the maximum withholding-tax rates that the source state of the income may levy. If the rate under domestic law is higher, the DBA rate applies.

items: 5% — if the recipient holds at least 20% of the payer's capital
10% — in all other cases
Applies both to German companies with stakes in Ukrainian ones and vice versa
0% — if the recipient is a state or a state bank
2% — on bank interest in specifically stipulated cases
5% — the standard maximum rate
0% — for the use of copyright in literature, science and art
5% — patents, trademarks, know-how
Taxed in the country where the real estate is located
Germany applies crediting to eliminate double taxation
Declared in the Anlage V and Anlage AUS attachments

content.text: For Ukrainian citizens who received protection under §24 AufenthG (the mass-influx directive, Massenzustrom-Richtlinie, from March 2022), special advisory rules of the Ministry of Finance (BMF) apply.

items: If you have registered your residence in Germany (Anmeldung) and work here, you are subject to unlimited taxation (unbeschränkt steuerpflichtig, §1 EStG)
Keeping a home and family in Ukraine does NOT automatically make you a Ukrainian resident for German tax purposes — the tie-breaker under Art. 4 of the DBA applies
The Ministry of Finance letter (BMF-Schreiben) of May 2022 (Ukraine-Sondermaßnahmen — special measures for Ukraine): simplified rules for refugees
Income from remote work for a Ukrainian employer while in Germany is subject to German tax, but under the DBA Ukraine has a right to tax the source income
Income from Ukraine (rent, dividends) goes in the Anlage AUS attachment, with confirmation of the Ukrainian tax

content.text: The Ministry of Finance has issued special guidance since 2022 to ease the tax position of Ukrainian refugees. For example, where someone is staying in Germany and continues to work for a Ukrainian employer, equitable solutions (billigkeitsmäßige Lösungen) are provided for. Check with the tax office (Finanzamt) and the latest Ministry of Finance letters (BMF-Schreiben).

steps.title: Certificate of tax residency (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung) — the key document

content.text: If you are a German resident and want to obtain the reduced withholding-tax rate in Ukraine (or a refund of excess tax withheld), you need a certificate of tax residency (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung).

items: Apply to your local tax office (Finanzamt) using the form 'Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung'
State the country, purpose and period
Issued free of charge, usually within 2–4 weeks
For Ukraine — on a bilingual form or with a certified translation
Submit it to your Ukrainian counterparty or broker
On the basis of the certificate, they apply the DBA rate
If the tax has already been withheld — file a refund application via the Ukrainian tax service
A Ukrainian resident with income from Germany needs a certificate from the Ukrainian tax service
Submit it to the Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt, Bundeszentralamt für Steuern) for the refund procedure (Erstattungsverfahren)
Refund of excess capital gains tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) under §50c EStG

content.text: Dual residence: if you have a place of residence (Wohnsitz) in both countries, the Art. 4 DBA tie-breaker applies (in sequence: permanent home (ständige Wohnstätte) → centre of vital interests (Mittelpunkt der Lebensinteressen) → habitual abode (gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt) → nationality (Staatsangehörigkeit)). This is a subjective assessment — the tax office may reach a different decision than you expect.

Remote work from Germany for a Ukrainian employer: taxed in Germany (salary is taxed at the place of work — Lohn am Arbeitsort, §19 EStG + Art. 15 DBA). The Ukrainian employer does not withhold German wage tax (Lohnsteuer) — you pay it yourself via your return (advance payments, Vorauszahlungen, then the final assessment, Veranlagung). A social-insurance obligation (Sozialversicherungspflicht) may also arise — check this separately via DVKA/BZSt.

Do not declare the Ukrainian tax as work-related expenses (Werbungskosten) without justification — where a DBA exists, the tax office expects crediting (Anrechnung) under §34c(1). Only where there is no DBA, or the maximum creditable amount (Höchstbetrag) is exceeded, can you deduct it as a cost under §34c(3).

Documents from Ukraine must be translated into German by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer). An apostille (Apostille) is not needed between Ukraine and Germany (Ukraine has been a party to the Hague Convention since 2003, and between EU countries and Ukraine a simplified regime applies in most cases).

title: DBA with the USA: FATCA and dual filing
tldr: The US-Germany DBA (1989, protocol 2006/2008) is in force and applied. Dividends — 5%/15%, interest — 0%, royalties — 0%. US citizens (including Green Card holders) remain obliged to file a tax return with the IRS even as German residents — Citizenship-Based Taxation. Additional obligations: FATCA Form 8938 and FBAR (FinCEN 114). German tax is credited in the US via Form 1116 (Foreign Tax Credit) or FEIE (Form 2555).

content.text: The DBA between the USA and the FRG was signed on 29 August 1989 and entered into force in 1990. It was substantially updated by the protocol of 1 June 2006 (which entered into force on 28 December 2007). It is one of the most detailed of Germany's DBAs and is fully in force in 2026.

items: The DBA with the USA + the protocol (Protokoll) 2006 — both in force
Method of elimination: predominantly crediting (Anrechnung, §34c EStG); for some income — exemption (Freistellung)
Saving Clause (Art. 1(4)): the USA retains the right to tax its citizens as non-residents
Published in the Federal Law Gazette (Bundesgesetzblatt) II 2006 S. 1184

steps.title: US citizens and Green Card holders in Germany

content.text: The USA is one of only two countries in the world (along with Eritrea) that applies Citizenship-Based Taxation: tax obligations are tied to citizenship, not only to residency. So a US citizen or Green Card holder living in Germany must file a tax return BOTH in Germany (as a resident) AND in the USA (as a citizen).

items: Form 1040 — the ordinary tax return
Deadline: 15 April; for US persons abroad — an automatic extension to 15 June; with Form 4868 — to 15 October
Worldwide income is declared (the same as in Germany)
The filing obligation arises when income exceeds the annual threshold (for 2023 — $13,850 for a single person; indexed annually)
You can exclude earned income up to the annual FEIE limit (for 2024 — $126,500; for 2025 — $130,000; indexed annually — check against the current IRS form)
Requirement: Bona Fide Residence (a full tax year in Germany) or Physical Presence (330+ days in 12 months)
Earned Income only — salary, not dividends/interest
Plus: Foreign Housing Exclusion for rent
Crediting of German wage tax (Lohnsteuer)/income tax (Einkommensteuer) against US tax
Calculated separately by income category (passive, general)
Often more advantageous than FEIE, especially with low US income and high wage tax in DE
You can combine them: FEIE on salary + FTC on dividends

content.text: Besides the tax return, US persons are obliged to report foreign financial accounts. These are two separate systems — FATCA (via the IRS) and FBAR (via FinCEN).

items: Filed if the combined total across all foreign accounts EXCEEDED $10,000 on even a single day in the year
Counted: current accounts, deposits, brokerage accounts, and sometimes savings-type insurance
Deadline: 15 April (automatic extension to 15 October)
Filed electronically via the BSA E-Filing System
Penalty for non-filing: $10,000 per unfiled account (non-willful), up to 50% of the balance (willful)
Filed together with Form 1040
Thresholds for a US person abroad: $200,000 at year-end or $300,000 at any point (single); double for married couples
Broader than FBAR — includes foreign shares, fund holdings and insurance
Penalty for non-filing: $10,000+
Under the IGA between Germany and the USA, German banks identify US persons
They pass the data to the Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt) → the IRS automatically
So it is impossible to hide an account at a savings bank (Sparkasse) from the IRS
Some brokers (Trade Republic, Scalable Capital) refuse to open accounts for US persons because of the FATCA burden

steps.title: Non-US citizens with income from the USA

content.text: If you are a German resident who is not a US citizen but receives dividends/interest from American shares, ETFs (NYSE), or income from renting out US real estate, the ordinary DBA applies.

items: Dividends from US shares: by default, US withholding tax (US-Quellensteuer) of 30%; under the DBA — 15%
Getting the benefit: submit Form W-8BEN to your broker (standard for all foreign investors)
Brokers in Germany (DKB, Comdirect, Trade Republic) submit W-8BEN automatically — 15% withholding
These 15% are creditable (anrechenbar) in the Anlage KAP attachment (§32d(5) EStG) — they reduce the withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) in Germany
Income from US real estate: taxed in the USA (Form 1040-NR) + the Anlage AUS attachment in Germany
To recover an over-withheld amount (if 30% was withheld but it should have been 15%) — Form 1042-S from the broker and a 1040-NR filing

content.text: 'Accidental Americans' — people born in the USA who never lived there — often have no idea they are obliged to file a US return. After FATCA began (2014), the problem surfaced on a massive scale. The IRS Streamlined Filing Procedures let you become compliant without penalties if the non-filing was non-willful.

PFIC (Passive Foreign Investment Company): almost all European ETFs (UCITS) are PFICs for US tax purposes. The rules are draconian: taxation under mark-to-market or throwback rules, plus the complex Form 8621. US persons in Germany are often forced to invest only in US-domiciled ETFs, which are unavailable through German brokers under MiFID II.

German pension products Riester/Rürup/bAV (Altersvorsorge — retirement savings): the IRS does not recognise their tax relief. Contributions may be subject to US tax, and the pensions are only partly exempt under Art. 18 of the DBA.
The Saving Clause (Art. 1(4) DBA) lets the USA tax its citizens as if the DBA did not exist. As a result, many DBA benefits do not apply to US persons — you have to rely on the FTC via Form 1116.

Renouncing US citizenship: the 'Exit Tax' (IRC §877A) — if you are a covered expatriate (income >$201,000/year over the last 5 years or net worth >$2 million), there is a deemed sale of all assets with Capital Gains Tax due.

title: Who is required to file a tax return
tldr: Most employees in Germany are NOT required to file a tax return (Einkommensteuererklärung) — for them, the wage tax withheld from their salary (Lohnsteuerabzug) counts as final. But §46 EStG contains a long list of exceptions: side income >410€, tax classes (Steuerklasse) III/V or IV with a factor (IV-Faktor), wage-replacement benefits (Lohnersatzleistungen — parental allowance, short-time work allowance) >410€, two employers, and more. Deadline: 31 July of the following year, or, through a tax advisor (Steuerberater), until the end of February of the year after that. Filing late means a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag) of at least 25€/month.

steps.title: Mandatory filing (Pflichtveranlagung) vs. filing on request (Antragsveranlagung)

content.text: In Germany there are two types of tax assessment: mandatory (Pflichtveranlagung) and on request (Antragsveranlagung). Most employees with a single employer, tax class (Steuerklasse) I/IV and no side income are NOT required to file a return. For them, the wage tax (Lohnsteuer) counts as final (§46(2) EStG).

But this is often a missed opportunity: when you file a voluntary return, the average refund is around 1.000€. The deadline for voluntary filing is 4 years (until 31.12 of the fourth year), so for 2026 it runs until 31.12.2030.

items: Mandatory filing: filing is compulsory, deadline 31.07 of the following year
Filing on request: voluntary, deadline 4 years
Through a tax advisor or income-tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein), the mandatory filing deadline runs until the end of February of the year after that
The self-employed — business owners (Gewerbe) and members of the freelance professions (Freiberufler) — are always required to file

steps.title: Who is REQUIRED to file a return

content.text: The full list is in §46(2) EStG. Below are the most common cases. If even one of these applies to you, you are subject to mandatory filing.

items: Income other than salary: rent, freelancing, interest above the saver's tax-free allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag), sale of crypto
Threshold: 410€/year — hardship relief (Härteausgleich; §46(2) Nr. 1 EStG)
Between 410€ and 820€ — partial relief (Härteausgleich, second tier)
Unemployment benefit I (Arbeitslosengeld I)
Sickness benefit (Krankengeld; beyond the continued-pay period, Lohnfortzahlung, of 6 weeks)
Parental allowance (Elterngeld)
Maternity benefit (Mutterschaftsgeld)
Short-time work allowance (Kurzarbeitergeld)
Insolvency benefit (Insolvenzgeld)
These benefits are tax-free but are factored into the progression clause (Progressionsvorbehalt; §32b EStG) — they raise the rate on your other income
Working for two or more employers at the same time (tax class VI on the second one)
Except for mini-jobs (Minijob) with a flat tax (Pauschalsteuer) of 2%
§46(2) Nr. 2 EStG
Spouses in III/V — always required (§46(2) Nr. 3a EStG)
Spouses in IV/IV with a factor (mit Faktor) — required (§46(2) Nr. 3a EStG)
Pure IV/IV without a factor — NOT automatically required
Class VI — almost always triggers mandatory filing
You received a severance payment (Abfindung) under the one-fifth rule (Fünftelregelung; §34 EStG)
A marriage was dissolved during the year and both spouses remarried
Special allowances (pension-provision payments, Versorgungsbezüge, from several sources)
A tax-free allowance (Freibetrag) in your wage tax (e.g. for work-related expenses, Werbungskosten) > 1.230€ together with income above a certain threshold
You received salary from a foreign employer without wage tax withholding (§38 EStG)
You want to claim losses from prior years (loss carryforward, Verlustvortrag)
Capital income without withholding tax at source (Quellensteuerabzug; foreign broker)

steps.title: Deadlines and consequences of filing late

content.text: Deadlines are governed by §149 AO (the Fiscal Code, Abgabenordnung).

items: Mandatory filing without a tax advisor: 31 July of the following year (for 2026 → 31.07.2027)
Mandatory filing through a tax advisor or income-tax assistance association: the last day of February of the year after that (for 2026 → 28.02.2028)
Filing on request (voluntary): 4 years (for 2026 → 31.12.2030)
Late-filing surcharge (§152 AO): 0,25% of the tax owed for each month of delay, minimum 25€/month, maximum 25.000€
For very long delays — an estimate (Schätzung) of the tax base by the tax office, usually to your disadvantage

content.text: Since 2019 the late-filing surcharge is in most cases imposed automatically (a mandatory rule, Soll-Vorschrift, §152(2) AO) — with no discretion for the tax-office official. That is why filing on time is critically important.

items.title: 1. On your own through the ELSTER tax portal

items: mein.elster.de — registration and a certificate file (Zertifikatsdatei)
The tax-return form ESt 1 A + the relevant annexes (Anlagen)
The automatic data retrieval (Belegabruf) pulls in details from your employer and insurers
Free
WISO Steuer, Smartsteuer, Taxfix, Buhl Tax — 25-50€
More convenient than the ELSTER portal for non-German speakers (Taxfix — a mobile app with a question-based flow)
They all export to ELSTER
Only for employees and pensioners (§4 Nr. 11 StBerG)
Passive-income limit: 13.000€/26.000€ (single/family)
Cost: 70-150€/year membership fee (based on income)
For the self-employed and complex cases (double-taxation treaty DBA, real estate, inheritance)
Fees set by the StBVV (Tax Advisors' Remuneration Regulation, Steuerberatervergütungsverordnung)
200-800€ for a simple case, substantially more for a complex one

content.text: Don't confuse a tax-free threshold (Freigrenze) with a tax-free allowance (Freibetrag). The 410€ hardship relief is a threshold: at 411€ the whole amount is taxed, not just the excess. This applies to side income (Nebeneinkünfte) and wage-replacement benefits.

Many people think parental allowance (Elterngeld) doesn't raise their tax — but it does. Under the progression clause (Progressionsvorbehalt), the rate on your remaining income is calculated as if the allowance had been taxed. Often, after receiving the allowance, you get a back-tax bill (Nachzahlung) of 1-3 thousand euros.

If you moved to Germany or away from Germany during the year, you are partly required to file (with limited tax liability, beschränkt steuerpflichtig, for the foreign portion). A return is almost always needed. Take the progression clause into account for foreign income earned before the move, too.

The most commonly missed trigger: you received short-time work allowance in 2020-2024 and didn't file a return. The tax office identifies such cases through data from the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) and sends a reminder (Erinnerung) plus a late-filing surcharge.

The tax identification number (Steuer-Identifikationsnummer; 11 digits) is your permanent number for life. The tax number (Steuernummer, from the tax office, Finanzamt) changes when you move. Don't mix them up on your return.
