title: ELSTER Mobile: file from your phone
tldr: MeinELSTER+ is the official, free app from the German tax authorities for iPhone and Android. With it you can photograph supporting documents (Belege — receipts, certificates), submit a simple return (the simplified tax return for pensioners, vereinfachte Steuererklärung für Rentner, or straightforward employee cases) and view your finished tax assessment (Steuerbescheid) right on your phone. To log in to the app, you first need an ELSTER certificate (ELSTER-Zertifikat): the easiest way is to transfer it into the app via a QR code from the web portal. For complex cases (self-employment, rental income, foreign income) you're better off using the ELSTER web portal or paid software, but for a typical employee MeinELSTER+ handles the whole return.

steps.title: What MeinELSTER+ can do and who it's for

content.text: MeinELSTER+ is the official app of the ELSTER tax portal (Elektronische Steuererklärung — electronic tax return), run by the German fiscal administration. It's free, with no ads and no hidden fees: you pay 0€, unlike WISO or Taxfix. Download it from the App Store or Google Play under the name MeinELSTER+.

items: Scan supporting documents (Belege): photograph receipts, certificates and invoices, and the app stores them in the ELSTER cloud and inserts them into your return
Simple return: for employees with a standard situation and for pensioners (the simplified tax return, vereinfachte Steuererklärung)
View your tax assessment (Steuerbescheid): the finished decision from the tax office (Finanzamt) arrives and can be read right in the app
Notifications about the processing status of your return
Manage your profile and certificate

content.text: The app is designed for straightforward cases. If you have self-employment income (the Anlage S/G annexes), rental income (the Anlage V annex), a large amount of foreign income, or the progression clause (Progressionsvorbehalt), the ELSTER web portal or paid software is more convenient — not all of the return's annexes (Anlagen) are available in the mobile app.

steps.title: Logging in: transferring your ELSTER-Zertifikat into the app

content.text: To file a return through the app, you need an ELSTER certificate (ELSTER-Zertifikat) — your digital key. If you don't have one yet, first register at elster.de (this takes about 2 weeks because of the activation code, Aktivierungs-PIN, sent by post — see the separate registration guide).

items.title: 1. Generate a QR code in the ELSTER web portal

content.text: Log in to elster.de from a computer, open the "Mein ELSTER" section → the area for the mobile app, and generate a QR code to transfer your certificate to your phone. This is a secure way to link the app to your account without registering again.

items.title: 2. Scan the QR code in MeinELSTER+

content.text: Open the app, choose login via QR code and point the camera at the code on your computer screen. The certificate is transferred into the app, after which you set a password / Face ID for logging in.

items: The app shows your details and your tax identification number (Steuer-ID)
The section for scanning supporting documents (Belege) is available
You can see the list of your returns and official decisions (Bescheide)

content.text: Without a valid ELSTER certificate you cannot file a return from the app. Registration by post takes about 2 weeks, so start early, especially if the filing deadline is approaching.

steps.title: Filing the return and receiving the official decision (Bescheid)

content.text: In the app, fill in the available fields: the data from your wage tax statement (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung) — which the app can partly pull in from the pre-fill (automatic data retrieval, Belegabruf) — work-related expenses (Werbungskosten), and other expenses. The scanned supporting documents are attached to the relevant items. After checking everything, you submit the return with a single tap, and it goes straight to your tax office.

items: Check that the pre-fill data (Belegabruf) came through: salary, insurance contributions, pension data
Add work-related expenses (Werbungskosten) if they exceed the tax-free flat allowance (Pauschbetrag)
Attach the scanned certificates and receipts
Submit and save the electronic acknowledgement of receipt
The official decision will arrive in the app within a few weeks — it also shows the refund or back-payment amount

costs.note: The official free app of the German tax administration; no ads or paid features.

costs.note: Filing itself is free; you only pay for commercial software or an advisor if you use them instead of ELSTER.

title: Registering with ELSTER: the ELSTER-Zertifikat certificate
tldr: The ELSTER tax portal is the free official service of the German tax authorities for filing your return online. To log in you need an ELSTER certificate (ELSTER-Zertifikat) — a digital key. Registration is free, but it runs in several steps with postal verification: you enter your tax identification number (Steuer-ID) and email, then the tax office (Finanzamt) sends an activation ID (Aktivierungs-ID) by email and an activation code (Aktivierungs-Code, PIN) by ordinary letter — which takes about 2 weeks. After activation you download the certificate file (.pfx) and keep it like a password. Start the process early: because of the postal letter, you can't do it at the last minute.

content.text: The most common registration method is a certificate file (Zertifikatsdatei). It's free and works on any device. There are alternatives (the electronic ID card eID, ELSTERSecure), but the file is the simplest option for most people.

items: Tax identification number (Steuer-Identifikationsnummer, Steuer-ID) — 11 digits, sent by letter after your first residence registration (Anmeldung) or shown on your wage tax statement (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung)
A valid email address you have permanent access to
A postal address in Germany — the letter with the activation code (Aktivierungs-Code) will be sent there
Date of birth
About 2 weeks of lead time before your deadline — the letter goes by ordinary post

content.text: The tax identification number (Identifikationsnummer) is NOT the same as the tax number (Steuernummer). For ELSTER registration you need specifically the 11-digit tax identification number. If you don't have it, request a duplicate from the Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern, BZSt).

At elster.de, choose "Create a user account" (Benutzerkonto erstellen) → login method "certificate file" (Zertifikatsdatei). Indicate that you are registering as a private individual using your tax identification number. Enter your tax identification number, date of birth and email.

items.title: 2. Confirm your email and receive the activation ID (Aktivierungs-ID)

content.text: Almost immediately you'll get an email with a confirmation link and an activation ID (Aktivierungs-ID). Click the link. The tax office then triggers the dispatch of the second part — the activation code (Aktivierungs-Code, PIN) — by ordinary letter to your address.

items.title: 3. Wait for the letter with the activation code (~2 weeks)

content.text: The activation code is sent by post for security (two-channel protection: one code by email, the other by post). It usually takes up to 2 weeks. The code has an expiry date, so don't put off activation once the letter arrives.

Go back to elster.de and enter the activation ID (from the email) and the activation code (from the letter). The system generates a .pfx certificate file — download it and set a password for it. You'll need this file and password every time you log in.

steps.title: How to store and use the certificate

content.text: The .pfx file is your key to your tax data. Keep it like a password: in a secure place, with a backup. If you lose the file or forget the password, there's no recovery — you'll have to register all over again (with the postal letter again).

items: Make a backup of the .pfx file (e.g. in encrypted cloud storage or on a USB stick)
Memorize or securely save the certificate password
The certificate is valid for about 3 years; ELSTER will remind you in advance to renew it
One certificate can be used both in the ELSTER web portal and in the MeinELSTER+ app (via QR transfer)

content.text: Don't lose the file or the password: if lost, the certificate cannot be recovered, and re-registration will again require the ~2-week wait for the postal letter.

costs.label: Registration and the ELSTER-Zertifikat
costs.note: Registration on the official ELSTER portal is completely free.

title: ELSTER vs WISO vs SteuerGo vs Taxfix
tldr: The ELSTER tax portal is the free official service: it can submit any return, but with no prompts and no check for the maximum refund — the form is "dry". Paid software does the same thing, but with interview-style logic, deduction tips and a comparison with the previous year. WISO Steuer is the most complete (~36€), good for complex cases. SteuerGo (~25-35€) is an inexpensive web service with an interface in many languages. Taxfix (~40€) is a question-and-answer app, handy for beginners and employees with a simple situation. All the paid options submit the return through the ELSTER interface, and none of them gets your refund any faster — only the convenience differs.

content.text: The ELSTER tax portal is the official service of the German tax authorities, completely free (0€). Through it you can submit absolutely any return, including the most complex annexes (Anlage S, V, KAP, AUS, etc.). The downside: the interface shows the bare tax forms, doesn't explain which deductions you're entitled to, and doesn't suggest how to increase your refund.

items: Cost: 0€
Suitable if you understand the structure of the return or your case is standard
Has a pre-fill feature (automatic data retrieval, Belegabruf) — pulls in your salary and insurance data
No interview logic and no automatic deduction finder
No "what would have been more favorable" comparison

steps.title: Paid software: what you're paying for

content.text: Paid programs are a layer on top of the same process: they ask questions in plain language, sort your answers into the right lines for you, look for deductions, and finally submit the return through the same ELSTER interface. The speed of the refund from the tax office (Finanzamt) is identical — only the ease of filling it in differs.

The most complete and popular package. It covers complex cases: self-employment, rental income, capital, foreign income. Import of last year's data, a maximum-refund check, detailed prompts. The best choice if your situation is complicated.

A web service that runs in the browser with no installation. Appealing for its price and its multilingual interface (clear even if you don't speak German). Good for employees with a medium level of complexity.

A mobile app in a question-and-answer format. It doesn't show the tax forms at all — it just asks questions. Handy for beginners and people with a simple situation (one employer, standard deductions). For complex cases it offers fewer options.

Paid software usually lets you calculate your estimated refund for free and only charges you when you submit. Prices can change from year to year and with promotions — check the current cost before you buy.

steps.title: How to choose for your situation

items: Simple situation (one employer, standard deductions) and you want it for 0€ — ELSTER or the MeinELSTER+ app
A beginner, you don't like forms, you want an interview — Taxfix
You want an inexpensive, easy-to-understand interface, including a non-German one — SteuerGo
A complex case (self-employment, rental income, capital, foreign income) — WISO
Not sure you can do it yourself, and you only have employment income — consider an income-tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein); there's a separate guide on this

content.text: The key point: no paid service speeds up the payout or has a privileged channel to the tax office. You're paying purely for convenience and help finding deductions. If you're confident in your abilities, the ELSTER portal gives the same result for free.

title: Which tax office (Finanzamt) is yours by postcode
tldr: Your tax office (Finanzamt) is determined by your residential address (the residence tax office, Wohnsitzfinanzamt), not by where you work. The easiest way to find yours is through the official tax-office search (Finanzamtsuche) on the website of the Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern, BZSt): you enter a postcode (PLZ) or city and get the address, phone number and opening hours of your tax office. It's free. If you move, your tax office changes automatically based on your new registered address; you usually don't need to notify the tax authorities separately — the data is passed on through your residence registration (Anmeldung), but the new tax office will be the one shown on your return from then on.

steps.title: The principle: the tax office at your place of residence

content.text: For private individuals, the competent (zuständig) office is the tax office (Finanzamt) for your main place of residence — the residence tax office (Wohnsitzfinanzamt). Not the one for your employer, and not the one where your company is registered. If you're registered as living in a particular district, your tax office is tied to that address.

items: Depends on your registered address (main residence, Hauptwohnsitz), not on your work
In large cities, a single city can be split among several tax offices (Finanzämter) by district or street
For the self-employed and companies, a separate jurisdiction may apply (the business tax office, Betriebsfinanzamt)

steps.title: How to find it through the tax-office search (Finanzamtsuche, BZSt)

content.text: Go to the official tax-office search (Finanzamtsuche) of the Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern, BZSt). It's a free official service — don't use third-party paid sites.
Enter the postcode (Postleitzahl) or the name of the city. The service will show the competent tax office with its address, phone, fax and often its consultation hours.

items: The name and address of the tax office (for letters and returns)
Phone number and opening hours (Servicezeiten)
The office number (Finanzamtsnummer) — sometimes needed on forms

steps.title: What to do when you move

content.text: When you move, you do the usual residence registration (Anmeldung) at your new address at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt). After that, the tax office for your new address becomes the competent one. You usually don't need to write to the tax authorities separately — but on your next return, give the new tax office, and correspondence and the official decision (Bescheid) will come from there.

Your tax identification number (Steuer-ID; 11 digits) doesn't change when you move — it's tied to you for life. The tax number (Steuernummer, assigned by the tax office), however, may change when the office changes. Take your current tax number from your most recent official decision (Bescheid).

costs.note: The official service is free.

title: Extending the filing deadline (Fristverlängerung)
tldr: If you're required to file a return (mandatory filing, Pflichtveranlagung), the standard deadline is 31 July of the following year. Can't make it? Send the tax office (Finanzamt) an informal request for a deadline extension (Antrag auf Fristverlängerung under §109 AO) — by letter or through the ELSTER tax portal, with a reason. The extension is at the tax office's discretion, but they usually grant a couple of months. The most reliable way to buy time is to hand your return to a tax advisor (Steuerberater) or an income-tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein): for their clients, the deadline is automatically extended to roughly the end of February of the following year (about 7 months longer). Filing late without an extension risks a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag).

content.text: If you're required to file a return (for example, you have a tax-free allowance, Freibetrag, in your withholding data ELStAM, side income, the progression clause, Progressionsvorbehalt, a joint return with class III/V, and so on), the basic deadline is 31 July of the year following the tax year. If the return is voluntary (filing on request, Antragsveranlagung), you essentially have up to 4 years, and this topic doesn't apply to you.

items: Mandatory filing (Pflichtveranlagung): deadline 31 July of the following year
With a tax advisor or income-tax assistance association: automatically until roughly the end of February of the following year (about 7 months longer)
Filing on request (voluntary): up to 4 years, no extension needed

content.text: The legal basis for an extension is §109 Abgabenordnung (the Fiscal Code, AO). The request is submitted in free form: by letter or via a message through the ELSTER portal to your tax office. State your tax number (Steuernummer), the tax year, the new deadline you want, and the reason (illness, missing documents, a business trip, etc.). The decision is at the tax office's discretion (Ermessen), but with a reasonable justification they usually accommodate you and grant a couple of months.

items.title: 1. Submit it BEFORE the deadline expires

content.text: The request must go out before 31 July. An extension request filed after the deadline is treated less favorably and does not cancel a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag) that has already arisen.

items.title: 2. What to state in the request

items: Name, address, tax number (and, if you have it, the tax identification number, Steuer-ID)
The tax year you're extending
A specific new date you're requesting the deadline until
A brief justification for the delay

content.text: The tax office will either confirm the new deadline or (often) tacitly accept it. Keep a copy of the request and the proof of submission via the ELSTER portal.

An extension under §109 AO is not guaranteed — it's a discretionary right of the tax office. Don't consider the deadline extended until you've received approval, or until the requested date has passed without objection.

steps.title: Automatic extension through a tax advisor or income-tax assistance association

content.text: The most reliable way to buy a lot of time is to hand your return to a tax advisor (Steuerberater) or, for employees, to an income-tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein). For their clients, the law grants an extended general deadline: the return can be filed until roughly the end of February of the year following the usual deadline — that is, about 7 months longer. No separate request is needed for this.

If you miss the deadline without an extension, the tax office may impose a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag), and for a long delay, enforcement measures too. If you're at risk of filing late, it's better to submit a request under §109 in advance or arrange help from an advisor or income-tax assistance association.

costs.label: Deadline-extension request (§109 AO)
costs.note: Submitting an informal request to the Finanzamt is free.

costs.label: Help from a Steuerberater / Lohnsteuerhilfeverein
costs.note: Lohnsteuerhilfeverein — membership fee ~50-200€/year; a Steuerberater is more expensive and depends on the case. In return, the deadline is automatically extended to ~the end of February.

title: Household services (haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen): deduction for services
tldr: Under §35a EStG, part of what you spend on household services and home repairs is deducted directly from your tax (not from your income — it's a tax reduction, Steuerermäßigung). Household services (haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen — cleaning, gardener, care) — 20% of the cost, up to 4000€ per year. Tradesman services (Handwerkerleistungen — installation, maintenance) — 20%, up to 1200€ per year, but only for the work itself (labor costs, travel, equipment), NOT for materials. A strict condition: you need an invoice (Rechnung) and payment by bank transfer (Überweisung) — cash is not accepted. The costs are claimed on your tax return; for tenants, part of the annual service-charge statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) also qualifies.

content.text: §35a EStG gives a tax reduction (Steuerermäßigung) — a cut in the tax itself, not in your taxable income. This is more favorable than ordinary deductions: 20% of the eligible costs is subtracted one-to-one from your tax. There are two separate caps.

items: Household services (haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen): cleaning, window washing, gardener, personal care, in-home services — 20%, up to 4000€ of tax savings per year
Tradesman services (Handwerkerleistungen): repair, installation, maintenance (Wartung), finishing work in your home — 20%, up to 1200€ per year
Household employment (haushaltsnahe Beschäftigungsverhältnisse — a mini-job, Minijob, in the home): 20%, a separate cap of up to 510€
It counts for a home you use yourself (apartment, house), including as a tenant

content.text: For tradesman services, only the labor is deductible: labor cost (Arbeitslohn), travel costs (Fahrtkosten), equipment costs (Maschinenkosten). The cost of materials (Material) does NOT count. So ask the tradesman to itemize labor and materials separately on the invoice — otherwise the deduction from that invoice is lost.

steps.title: Strict conditions: an invoice (Rechnung) + bank transfer (Überweisung)

content.text: The law requires two things at once: you must have an invoice (Rechnung) from the provider, and payment must go by cashless transfer to their account (bank transfer, Überweisung; cashless payment, unbare Zahlung). Paying in cash forfeits the deduction entirely — this is the most common mistake.

items: An invoice (Rechnung) breaking down labor and materials
Payment by transfer only — keep the account statement (Kontoauszug) as proof
Cash payment (Barzahlung) = no deduction, even if you have an invoice
Keep the documents; you usually don't need to attach them to your return, but the tax office (Finanzamt) may ask for them

steps.title: How to claim it on your return

items.title: 1. Gather the invoices and proof of payment

content.text: Collect all the year's invoices (Rechnungen) for home and repair work, together with bank confirmations of payment. For tenants: the annual service-charge statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) often lists household services and tradesman work as a separate line — that amount can be claimed too.

items.title: 2. Enter it on your return (the household-expenses annex, Anlage Haushaltsnahe Aufwendungen)

content.text: On your return (via the ELSTER portal or software), enter the amounts for household services and tradesman work separately — only the labor portion. The program will apply the 20% and the 4000€/1200€ caps itself.

items: Household services: savings of no more than 4000€/year (i.e. costs up to 20000€ give the full effect)
Tradesman services: savings of no more than 1200€/year (labor costs up to 6000€)
The caps are annual and don't carry over to the next year

content.text: A deduction under §35a is only possible if the costs aren't attributable to work-related expenses (Werbungskosten), business expenses (Betriebsausgaben) or special expenses (Sonderausgaben) — you can't count the same costs twice. A home office for work, for example, follows different rules.

costs.label: Tax-savings cap — Handwerkerleistungen
costs.note: 20% of labor costs, up to 1200€ per year; materials don't count.

costs.label: Tax-savings cap — haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen
costs.note: 20% of the cost, up to 4000€ per year.

sources.title: §35a EStG — Steuerermäßigung bei haushaltsnahen Beschäftigungen, Dienstleistungen und Handwerkerleistungen

title: Working from home (Homeoffice): 6€/day, up to 1260€/year
tldr: The home-office flat rate (Homeoffice-Pauschale; §4 Abs. 5 Nr. 6c / §9 Abs. 5 EStG) is a simplified flat-rate deduction for working from home: 6 € for each day you mainly worked at home, up to 210 days a year, i.e. up to 1 260 € per year. Its main advantage over the old "home study" (häusliches Arbeitszimmer) is that you do NOT need a separate study — you can work at the kitchen table. It's a work-related expense (Werbungskosten, for employees) or a business expense (Betriebsausgaben, for the self-employed) that reduces your income. One important restriction: for a single day you can't take both the home-office flat rate and the commuting flat rate (Pendlerpauschale) — if you went to the office that day, it counts as a commuting day, not a home day. As with the commuting flat rate, you only see a real benefit once your work-related expenses exceed the employee flat-rate allowance (Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag) of 1 230 €.

steps.title: What the home-office flat rate (Homeoffice-Pauschale) is

content.text: The home-office flat rate was introduced in §4 Abs. 5 Satz 1 Nr. 6c EStG (for business owners) and extended to employees via §9 Abs. 5 EStG. Since 2023 it has become permanent and more generous than the "Covid" version. It's a flat amount per day worked at home, with no need to prove specific costs.

items: Rate: 6 € for each day worked mainly at home
Maximum: 210 days per year
Maximum deduction: 210 × 6 € = 1 260 € per year
Type: work-related expense (Werbungskosten, employees) / business expense (Betriebsausgaben, self-employed)
No separate study required — working at any desk at home qualifies

content.text: The condition "mainly at home" means that the bulk of your work that day was done from home. It doesn't have to be the whole day — but if you worked at home in the morning and then went to the office, the day usually counts as a commuting day instead (the commuting flat rate, Pendlerpauschale), see below.

steps.title: The flat rate vs. a home study (Arbeitszimmer)

content.text: There are two ways to account for working at home, and they're mutually exclusive for a given period. The flat rate suits most people — it's simpler and doesn't require a separate room.

items: Home-office flat rate: 6 €/day, up to 1 260 €/year, WITHOUT a separate study and with no receipts
Home study (häusliches Arbeitszimmer): a deduction of the actual costs of a separate room, BUT only if it's used almost exclusively for work AND is the center of all your activity
If home is your sole place of work (e.g. a freelancer with no office): you can take either the annual flat rate (Jahrespauschale) of 1 260 € or the actual study costs
For most remote workers who have an employer's office, only the flat rate is actually available

content.text: A full deduction for a home study (actual rent/utilities in proportion to floor area) has been strictly limited since 2023: it's available only to those for whom the home study is the center of ALL their professional activity. An ordinary employee who occasionally works from home can use the home-office flat rate.

The calculation is straightforward: number of home days × 6 €, but no more than 210 days (1 260 €). Keep a simple record of the days (a calendar or spreadsheet) in case the tax office (Finanzamt) asks.

items: 210+ home days: capped at 1 260 € (you won't get more)
Claimed in the employee annex (Anlage N) — in the home-office flat-rate field; the self-employed claim it in the Anlage EÜR/G annex
Keep a list of the dates you worked at home as proof

content.text: The key rule of §9 EStG: for ONE and the same day you can't take both the home-office flat rate and the commuting flat rate (Pendlerpauschale). If you went to the office that day, it counts as a commuting day (Pendlertag), not a home day. So plan ahead: pure home days → 6 €, days with a commute → the distance-based commuting flat rate (Entfernungspauschale). You can't combine the two for a single day.

As with the commuting flat rate, remember the employee flat-rate allowance (Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag) of 1 230 €: it's granted automatically. If your total work-related expenses (home office + commute + other) are below 1 230 €, the flat rate gives no separate benefit — it's already "built into" the flat-rate allowance. The benefit appears once your total crosses 1 230 €.

costs.label: Maximum annual deduction (deduction from income)
costs.note: 210 days × 6 €. This is Werbungskosten, not a cash refund.

costs.label: Typical deduction for partial remote work
costs.note: 60-180 home days × 6 €.

costs.label: Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag (granted automatically)
costs.note: Werbungskosten below this amount provide no additional benefit.

title: Church tax (Kirchensteuer): 8-9% and how to avoid it
tldr: Church tax (Kirchensteuer) is paid only by official members of a recognized church (mainly Catholic or Protestant). It's a surcharge on income/wage tax: 8% of the wage tax (Lohnsteuer) in the states of Bayern and Baden-Württemberg, 9% in all other states. It's calculated on the amount of TAX, not on your salary, so the actual share of your income is small but still noticeable. Your employer withholds it automatically based on your withholding data (ELStAM; your denomination is recorded there). If you're not a church member, there's no tax. The only legal way to stop paying while remaining formally religious is to leave the church (Kirchenaustritt) at the registry office (Standesamt) or the local court (Amtsgericht).

content.text: Church tax (Kirchensteuer) is paid only by officially registered members of a church that collects the tax (above all the Roman Catholic and Protestant churches). If you've never joined such a church in Germany, or have left it, there's no tax. Your denomination is recorded in your withholding data (ELStAM); it usually gets entered there when you register your residence (Anmeldung), if you state your religion.

items: The states of Bayern and Baden-Württemberg: 8% of the wage tax (Lohnsteuer) / income tax (Einkommensteuer)
All other federal states: 9%
The base is the amount of income tax, NOT your gross salary
Not a church member = no church tax is charged

content.text: The 8-9% is calculated on the tax you pay, not on your income. Example: with wage tax of 6000€ a year, the church tax comes to roughly 480-540€. The amount is noticeable, but it's a small share of your salary, not 9% of gross.

For employees, the employer withholds the church tax together with the wage tax (Lohnsteuer) and forwards it to the church via the tax office (Finanzamt). The rate is taken automatically from your withholding data (ELStAM), based on your state of residence and your denomination. Church tax is also withheld on capital income (the withholding tax on capital income, Abgeltungsteuer) — the bank does this automatically if it knows your denomination through data from the Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt).

items: On salary — withheld by the employer based on your withholding data (ELStAM)
On capital income — withheld by the bank together with the withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)
On your annual return, church tax counts as a special expense (Sonderausgabe; it partly reduces your taxable income)

content.text: There's one legal way to reduce or avoid church tax: officially leave the church — a church exit (Kirchenaustritt). This is done at the registry office or the local court (depending on the state), costs around 30€, and the tax stops from the following month. Once you've left, your data is updated for the employer and the bank, and the withholding stops. The details are in a separate guide on leaving the church.

Simply stopping going to church, or not stating your religion to your employer, isn't enough: as long as you're officially listed as a member, the church is entitled to the tax. You can only end it through a formal church exit (Kirchenaustritt).

costs.label: Kirchensteuer rate
costs.note: 8% of the tax in Bayern/Baden-Württemberg, 9% in other states; the specific amount depends on your tax.

costs.label: Kirchenaustritt (leaving the church)
costs.note: A one-time fee of around 30€ at the Standesamt/Amtsgericht ends the tax from the following month.

title: Leaving the church (Kirchenaustritt): the official exit procedure
tldr: A church exit (Kirchenaustritt) is the official act of leaving the church, which ends church tax (Kirchensteuer; 8-9% of your tax). You submit the declaration in person at the registry office (Standesamt) or the local court (Amtsgericht) — exactly which body depends on the federal state. The fee is usually around 30€ (free in some states, higher in others). Bring a valid national ID card (Personalausweis) or passport (plus a marriage certificate if you have one). Once you've left, you receive an exit certificate (Austrittsbescheinigung); church tax then stops, as a rule, from the following month. It's a purely civil procedure handled by a secular body — you don't need to speak to the church itself.

content.text: Leaving the church is the only legal way to end church tax while remaining a tax resident of Germany. The procedure is a civil one: it's handled by a secular body, not the church itself. Depending on the state, that's the registry office (Standesamt) or the local court (Amtsgericht). Check your city's website to see which body processes a church exit.

items: Body: the registry office (Standesamt) or the local court (Amtsgericht) — depends on the federal state
Fee: usually ~30€ (lower or free in some places, a bit higher in others)
An appointment (Termin) is often required in advance
No need to arrange anything with the church — it all goes through the state body
A valid national ID card (Personalausweis) or passport (for foreigners — passport plus a registration certificate, Meldebescheinigung, if needed)
Marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) — requested in some states
Cash or card to pay the fee (~30€)
Knowing which denomination you belong to (Catholic/Protestant, etc.)

content.text: The exit declaration is submitted in person — in most states it can't be done by post or online, since you have to identify yourself with a document. Minors and matters concerning children are handled separately.

You receive an exit certificate (Austrittsbescheinigung). Keep it: it proves that your membership has ended. The body notifies the tax office (Finanzamt) and updates your withholding data (ELStAM), and church tax stops being charged, as a rule, from the calendar month following your exit. Your employer will see the change of denomination in the ELStAM data and stop withholding automatically.
The certificate is your proof of exit. You'll need it if the tax keeps being withheld by mistake, or for the bank (for church tax on capital income).

items.title: 2. Check the withholding on your next paycheck

content.text: After 1-2 months, check your payslip (Gehaltsabrechnung): the church-tax line should disappear. If it doesn't, show the exit certificate to HR or the tax office.
Leaving ends the tax only from the moment it's processed (usually from the following month). Church tax already withheld for earlier months of the current year is not refunded.

costs.label: Fee for the Kirchenaustritt
costs.note: Roughly ~30€; lower or free in some states, a bit higher in others.

title: Lohnsteuerermäßigung: wage tax reduction
tldr: Normally, expenses (work-related expenses — Werbungskosten; commuting costs, insurance, maintenance payments) only reduce your tax after the fact — once you file your annual return, as a refund. The wage tax reduction (Lohnsteuer-Ermäßigung, §39a EStG) lets you enter a tax-free allowance (Freibetrag) into your electronic wage tax deduction records (ELStAM) in advance, so your employer withholds less wage tax (Lohnsteuer) from your salary every month — the money stays with you right away instead of sitting at the tax office (Finanzamt) for a year. The application (Antrag auf Lohnsteuer-Ermäßigung) is submitted to the tax office via the tax authority's ELSTER portal. The downside: if you have an allowance entered, you are generally obliged to file an annual return (mandatory assessment — Pflichtveranlagung), where the amount is reconciled.

steps.title: The idea: money now, not a refund a year later

content.text: If you consistently have high tax-reducing expenses (a long commute, large work-related expenses — Werbungskosten; insurance contributions, maintenance, disability), you don't have to wait for the annual return and refund. Under §39a EStG you can register a tax-free allowance (Freibetrag) — a non-taxable amount — in advance in your electronic wage tax deduction records (ELStAM). Your employer will then withhold less wage tax (Lohnsteuer) from your salary each month.

items: commuter allowance (Pendlerpauschale) for a long commute (Entfernungspauschale)
work-related expenses (Werbungskosten) above the standard flat amount (Pauschbetrag)
special deductible expenses (Sonderausgaben) and extraordinary expenses (außergewöhnliche Belastungen)
flat-rate allowance for people with disabilities (Pauschbetrag für Menschen mit Behinderung)
maintenance payments (Unterhalt) and more

content.text: The effect is a higher net salary throughout the year instead of one large refund after filing. In essence, you stop giving the state an interest-free loan a year in advance and keep your own money right away.

steps.title: How to file the Antrag auf Lohnsteuer-Ermäßigung

items.title: 1. Fill out the application via ELSTER

content.text: The application is called Antrag auf Lohnsteuer-Ermäßigung. The most convenient way to file it is through the tax authority's ELSTER portal (you need an ELSTER-Zertifikat) or on paper at the tax office. You state your expected expenses for the year; the tax office calculates the tax-free allowance.

Once approved, the tax office enters the tax-free allowance into your electronic wage tax deduction records (ELStAM, Elektronische LohnSteuerAbzugsMerkmale). Your employer reads them automatically and reduces the monthly wage tax — you don't need to bring anything to them separately.

The tax-free allowance is usually valid for up to 2 calendar years, after which it must be renewed with a new application. If your circumstances have changed (for example, your commute has changed), submit a new application.

For most tax-free allowances (Freibeträge) there is a threshold: the application only makes sense if the total amount of expenses exceeds the application threshold (Antragsgrenze; under §39a Abs. 2 EStG — generally 600€ on top of the corresponding flat amounts — Pauschbeträge). The tax office does not enter smaller amounts into ELStAM.

steps.title: An important consequence: the obligation to file a return

content.text: If a tax-free allowance has been entered in your ELStAM, you are generally obliged to file an annual tax return (mandatory assessment — Pflichtveranlagung). The logic is simple: the state reduced your monthly tax in advance based on expected expenses, and the year-end return checks whether the expenses matched reality.

items: Allowance entered → usually obliged to file a return
The deadline for such a return is the standard one (31 July of the following year), as with a mandatory assessment (Pflichtveranlagung)
If the expenses turned out to be lower than declared, you may have to pay extra at year-end
If they were higher, the difference is refunded

content.text: Don't overstate your expected expenses in the application: if you don't actually incur them, the tax-free allowance turns out to be excessive, and you'll have to pay back tax based on the annual return.

costs.label: Filing the Lohnsteuer-Ermäßigung application
costs.note: The application to the Finanzamt via ELSTER is free.

title: Lohnsteuerhilfeverein: a cheap alternative
tldr: An income tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein) is a non-profit association that prepares tax returns for employees and pensioners for a fixed annual membership fee (roughly 50-200€ depending on income), rather than for a percentage of the refund. It's cheaper than a tax advisor (Steuerberater) and gives you live advice, unlike software. The key limitation under §4 StBerG: they can only help with employee/pensioner income types (salary, pension, rental within small limits, etc.). If you have income from self-employment or business (the Anlage S/G attachments), the association is NOT allowed to help you — then you need a tax advisor. As a member, you get an extended filing deadline (until roughly the end of February).

steps.title: What it is and what it costs

content.text: An income tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein, often abbreviated LStHV) is a mutual-aid association entitled to provide tax assistance within the scope of §4 Nr. 11 StBerG. You join a local branch and pay an annual membership fee, the amount of which depends on your annual income (a fee scale — Beitragsstaffel). In return, they handle your tax return in full and advise you.

items: Cost: the membership fee is usually ~50-200€ per year, based on income level
A fixed fee, not a percentage of the refund
Live advice from a specialist, not just software
Suitable for employees and pensioners
Major associations: VLH, BVL (formerly BDL/NVL) and others (across Germany)

content.text: This is the main thing to understand. By law (§4 Nr. 11 StBerG), an income tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein) is only allowed to handle returns for certain types of income — mainly salary, pension, state benefits, capital income and rental within set limits. If you have income from self-employment, freelancing or business activity (income from self-employed work — Einkünfte aus selbständiger Arbeit; a trade — Gewerbe; the Anlage S or G attachments), they are NOT allowed to help you.

Even a small amount of income from self-employment or freelancing (the Anlage S/G attachments) takes you outside the authority of an income tax assistance association. In that case the return must be handled by a tax advisor (Steuerberater). Don't try to hide such income — the association is obliged to refuse.

items: Allowed: salary (the Anlage N attachment), pension, parental allowance (Elterngeld)/unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld), capital income (the Anlage KAP attachment), rental within the limit
Not allowed: income from self-employment/freelancing (the Anlage S attachment), business activity (the Anlage G attachment), agriculture
With mixed income that includes self-employment — only a tax advisor (Steuerberater)

steps.title: How to join and what it gives you

content.text: Find a local branch (advice center — Beratungsstelle) of a major association — for example, VLH (vlh.de) or the BVL associations (bvl-verband.de). They have a tool for finding the nearest advisor by postal code.

items: Membership application and payment of the annual fee
Wage tax certificate (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung) from your employer
Receipts for expenses (work-related expenses — Werbungskosten; insurance, commute)
Tax identification number (Steuer-ID) and bank details for the refund

content.text: As a member of an income tax assistance association, you get the same extended deadline as with a tax advisor (Steuerberater): you can file the return until roughly the end of February of the year following the usual 31 July deadline. No separate extension request is needed.

costs.label: Lohnsteuerhilfeverein membership fee
costs.note: The annual fee depends on income level; it's fixed, not a percentage of the refund.

sources.title: §4 StBerG — Befugnis zu beschränkter Hilfeleistung in Steuersachen (Lohnsteuerhilfevereine)

title: Pendlerpauschale: 0,38 €/km (from 2026)
tldr: The commuter allowance (Pendlerpauschale; commuting allowance — Entfernungspauschale, §9 Abs. 1 Nr. 4 EStG) is a work-related expense (Werbungskosten) for the commute to work: you deduct a fixed amount from your taxable income for each kilometer between your home and your first place of work. IMPORTANT: from 1 January 2026 the rate is uniform — 0,38 € for EVERY kilometer, starting from the first (tax amendment act — Steueränderungsgesetz 2025). The previous two-tier scheme (0,30 € for the first 20 km, 0,38 € from the 21st) only applied until 31.12.2025. Only ONE leg counts (not the round trip!), per working day, regardless of how you travel — car, train, bicycle or on foot. The typical annual deduction is 700-1 800 €. This is a work-related expense: it reduces your income, not your tax directly, and only helps if it exceeds the employee flat amount (Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag, 1 230 €) in total. The distance is measured along the shortest reasonable route.

content.text: The commuting allowance (Entfernungspauschale; colloquially the commuter allowance — Pendlerpauschale) is set out in §9 Abs. 1 Nr. 4 EStG. It is a type of work-related expense (Werbungskosten) — a cost incurred in earning income that is deducted from your taxable earnings. The state acknowledges that the commute to work costs money and grants a fixed rate per kilometer for it.

items: Type: work-related expense (Werbungskosten) — reduces income, not tax directly
What for: the journey from your home (Wohnung) to your first place of work (erste Tätigkeitsstätte)
Regardless of transport: car, train, bus, bicycle, on foot, carpool
Only ONE leg per day counts (the trip there — Hinweg; OR the trip back — Rückweg, not both)
Per actual working day (vacation and sick days don't count)

content.text: The most common mistake is counting the commute "there and back". §9 EStG explicitly refers to the one-way distance (einfache Entfernung) — one way only. If it's 30 km to work, you count 30 km per day, not 60.

From the 2026 tax year the rate is uniform: 0,38 € for each kilometer of the shortest route between home and the first place of work, starting from the 1st kilometer. This was enshrined permanently by the tax amendment act (Steueränderungsgesetz 2025, passed 19.12.2025). Until 31.12.2025 a two-tier scheme applied: 0,30 € for the first 20 km and 0,38 € from the 21st km.

items: 2026: 0,38 € for each km from the 1st (uniform rate, permanent)
2021-2025 (for older returns): 0,30 € for 1-20 km, 0,38 € from the 21st km
Counted per working day, one way
Distance — the shortest reasonable route by road (a route that is more favorable given traffic — verkehrsgünstigere Strecke — is allowed if it is genuinely faster)
When traveling by public transport: if your actual tickets cost more than the flat amount (Pauschale), you can claim the actual costs

content.text: The old "ceiling" of 4 500 €/year only applies to people who do NOT use their own car (bicycle, on foot, carpool). If you drive to work in your own car or a company vehicle, there is no upper ceiling.
The formula from 2026 onward: km × 0,38 € × the number of working days in the year (usually ~220-230 days are assumed for a five-day week). The two-tier calculation is no longer needed.

Worked example for 35 km (2026): 35 × 0,38 = 13,30 € per working day, which over 230 days comes to 3 059 €. This amount is deducted from your taxable income; at a tax rate of ~30% the real saving is about 918 €. For returns for 2025 and earlier, apply the old two-tier scheme (0,30 €/0,38 €).

steps.title: How to claim it and the catch with the Pauschbetrag

content.text: The commuter allowance is claimed in the Anlage N attachment (income from employment) of the income tax return (Einkommensteuer). But there's an important catch: every employee is automatically given an employee flat amount (Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag; flat amount for work-related expenses — Werbungskostenpauschale) of 1 230 € per year, without any receipts.

items: Claimed in the Anlage N attachment: home address, work address, number of km, number of working days
Only work-related expenses ABOVE 1 230 € provide a real benefit (the flat amount is granted anyway)
If your commuter allowance is below 1 230 €, it is "absorbed" by the flat amount and gives no separate benefit
If the commuter allowance = 3 059 €, the excess over 1 230 € genuinely lowers your tax
You can add other work-related expenses to the commuter allowance (Werbungskosten: work clothing, training, tools, home office)
Proof of distance is usually not required, but in case of doubt the tax office (Finanzamt) checks it against a map

content.text: For one and the same day you cannot claim both the commuter allowance (Pendlerpauschale; commuting to work) and the home office flat amount (Homeoffice-Pauschale; working from home). If on a given day you both went to the office and finished work at home, choose whichever is more advantageous for that day — combining them is not allowed.

costs.label: Typical annual Pendlerpauschale (deduction from income)
costs.note: For a commute of 10-25 km and ~220-230 working days (rate 0,38 €/km from 2026). This is a deduction from income, not a cash refund.

costs.label: Pendlerpauschale for a long commute (35-50 km)
costs.note: Uniform rate of 0,38 €/km from 2026 (previously the higher part started from the 21st km).

costs.label: Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag (granted automatically)
costs.note: Werbungskosten below this amount provide no additional benefit.

sources.title: ELSTER — Anlage N (Einkünfte aus nichtselbständiger Arbeit)

title: Progressionsvorbehalt: foreign income
tldr: The progression proviso (Progressionsvorbehalt, §32b EStG) is the rule that makes "tax-free" income affect your tax anyway. The income itself (parental allowance — Elterngeld; unemployment benefit — Arbeitslosengeld; sickness benefit — Krankengeld; short-time work allowance — Kurzarbeitergeld; as well as foreign income exempt from German tax under a double taxation agreement — DBA) is not taxed. BUT it raises the tax RATE applied to the rest of your ordinary income. In other words, the tax on your salary is calculated as if those payments had been income, and that higher rate is then applied only to the portion that is actually taxable. Because of this, a year with parental allowance or foreign income often ends in an additional payment, and in such cases you usually become obliged to file a return.

steps.title: What it is and which income is affected

content.text: The progression proviso (Progressionsvorbehalt) under §32b EStG is a mechanism whereby certain tax-exempt income is not itself taxed but is taken into account when calculating your tax rate. Because Germany has a progressive scale (the higher the income, the higher the rate), such payments "push" the rate up, so all the rest of your taxable income is taxed at a higher rate.

items: Wage-replacement payments (Lohnersatzleistungen): parental allowance (Elterngeld), unemployment benefit Arbeitslosengeld I, sickness benefit (Krankengeld), short-time work allowance (Kurzarbeitergeld), maternity benefit (Mutterschaftsgeld)
Foreign income exempt from German tax under a double taxation agreement (DBA, Doppelbesteuerungsabkommen) that carries a progression proviso (Progressionsvorbehalt)
Certain other exempt payments under §32b EStG

content.text: Don't confuse the two: the parental allowance (Elterngeld) or the foreign income itself is NOT taxed. Only your ordinary taxable income (your salary, for example) is taxed at the increased rate. This is not double taxation of the exempt income.

The mechanics work in three steps. Step 1: the tax office (Finanzamt) takes your taxable income and adds the exempt payments to it, producing a fictitious, increased income. Step 2: for this increased income, an average tax rate is determined on the progressive scale. Step 3: this higher rate is applied only to your actually taxable income — without the exempt payments.

A hypothetical example: an annual salary (taxable) of 30 000€, plus parental allowance (Elterngeld) of 10 000€. Without the progression proviso, the rate would be calculated for 30 000€ — say ~15%. With the progression proviso, the rate is determined for 40 000€ — say ~18%. That 18% is then applied to the 30 000€ of salary, not to 40 000€. The result is a higher tax than you would pay without the payments, even though the 10 000€ benefit itself was not taxed. The figures are illustrative and depend on the year and the scale.

items: Step 1: taxable income + exempt payments = fictitious base
Step 2: an increased average rate is derived from the fictitious base
Step 3: the increased rate is applied only to the actually taxable income

steps.title: Consequences: additional payment and the obligation to file a return

content.text: Because your employer withheld wage tax (Lohnsteuer) during the year without accounting for these later payments, a year with parental allowance (Elterngeld), unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld) or foreign income often ends in an additional payment (Nachzahlung) once everything is recalculated. This is normal, and it simply means the progression proviso raised your effective rate.

items: If your wage-replacement payments (Lohnersatzleistungen) for the year exceed 410€, you are generally obliged to file a return (mandatory assessment — Pflichtveranlagung)
Foreign income that is exempt under a double taxation agreement (DBA) also usually triggers an obligation to declare
The amounts come from your statements: for parental allowance, from the decision of the parental allowance office (Elterngeldstelle); for other benefits, from the relevant authorities
On the return, these amounts go in the Anlage N attachment (income affecting progression — Progressionseinkünfte) on the relevant lines, and foreign income goes in the Anlage AUS attachment

content.text: Set money aside in advance for a possible additional payment, especially if you received a large parental allowance (Elterngeld) or foreign income during the year. It helps to estimate the likely result in tax software before filing, so the additional payment doesn't come as a surprise.

costs.note: Filing itself is free; only software or an advisor may cost money.

costs.note: The amount depends on the size of the exempt payments and your income; Progressionsvorbehalt raises the rate, not the tax on the payment itself.

title: 13th salary, Weihnachtsgeld, Urlaubsgeld
tldr: In Germany, the 13th salary (Christmas bonus — Weihnachtsgeld) and holiday pay (Urlaubsgeld) are NOT mandatory by law — you are entitled to them only if they are written into your employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag) or a collective (tariff) agreement (Tarifvertrag). Around 53% of employees receive them. The amount ranges from 25% to 100% of a month's salary.

steps.title: What it is and who is entitled

content.text: In Germany there are three terms that often get confused. The Christmas bonus (Weihnachtsgeld) is a bonus usually paid in November together with your salary. Holiday pay (Urlaubsgeld) is a supplement to your salary when you go on vacation (not to be confused with vacation remuneration — Urlaubsentgelt — which is your ordinary salary for vacation days; everyone is entitled to that by law). The thirteenth salary (13. Monatsgehalt) is literally a "13th salary", usually paid in December.

Important: none of these payments is mandatory under federal law. You only have a right to them if they are written into your employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag), a collective (tariff) agreement (Tarifvertrag) or a works agreement with the works council (Betriebsvereinbarung).

items: The Christmas bonus is received by ~53% of employees in Germany (WSI/Hans-Böckler-Stiftung statistics)
In sectors covered by a collective (tariff) agreement (Tarifvertrag), the share reaches 77%
Amount: from 25% to 100% of a month's gross salary, 50-80% on average
Vacation remuneration under the tariff (Urlaubsentgelt) is MANDATORY under §11 BUrlG — not to be confused with holiday pay (Urlaubsgeld)

steps.title: How to check whether you're entitled to a payment

content.text: Open your employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag) and look for the key terms. If none of them appears, the employer is formally not obliged to pay — but there may still be an established company practice (betriebliche Übung).

items: The "Pay" section (Vergütung / Gehalt) — a clause on special payments (Sonderzahlungen)
Wordings such as "13. Gehalt", "Weihnachtsgeld in Höhe von ... %", "Jahressonderzahlung" (annual special payment)
A voluntariness clause, "Freiwilligkeitsvorbehalt" — the employer reserves the right not to pay

content.text: If your employer is bound by a collective (tariff) agreement (Tarifvertrag; IG Metall, ver.di and others), the bonuses are set out there. Ask HR which agreement applies, or check the union's website.

If the employer has paid the Christmas bonus 3 years in a row without a "freiwillig" (voluntary) clause, you acquire a right to the payment by custom (established company practice — betriebliche Übung); rulings of the Federal Labor Court (BAG, Bundesarbeitsgericht) confirm this.

The Christmas bonus (Weihnachtsgeld) and holiday pay (Urlaubsgeld) count as other payments (sonstige Bezüge) under §39b EStG. They are subject to the same taxes as salary (wage tax — Lohnsteuer; the solidarity surcharge — Soli, if applicable; church tax), plus full social security contributions. Because of tax progression, proportionally more is withheld from a single large amount — this is normal, and you get part of it back with your annual return.

items: Subject to wage tax (Lohnsteuer) by class, and to the solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) if income is above the threshold

From 2026: social security (health insurance — KV; pension — RV; unemployment insurance — AV; long-term care insurance — PV) is withheld in full up to the income ceiling for social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze)
Part of the tax can be reclaimed through your tax return (Steuererklärung), especially under tax class Steuerklasse VI

content.text: Cut-off date clause (Stichtagsklausel): the contract may require you to still be with the company on 1 December in order to receive the Christmas bonus. If you leave earlier, you lose the entitlement. Check the wording.

Repayment clause (Rückzahlungsklausel): some contracts require you to repay the Christmas bonus if you leave before a certain date the following year. The Federal Labor Court (BAG) applies a graduated approach: for a payment of up to 100€, a repayment clause is not permissible; for an amount up to roughly one month's salary, a tie-in is allowed at most until 31 March; for a larger amount, a longer tie-in is possible. The exact period depends on the wording — in a dispute, have it checked by an employment lawyer.

Voluntariness clause (Freiwilligkeitsvorbehalt): the wording "freiwillig, ohne Anspruch auf Rechtsanspruch für die Zukunft" means the payment can be canceled at any time. The Federal Labor Court (BAG) held it lawful (10 AZR 281/08).

title: Abfindung: severance pay
tldr: Severance pay (Abfindung) in Germany is NOT mandatory by default. The formula "0.5 months' gross × years of service" applies under §1a KSchG (dismissal for operational reasons + waiver of a lawsuit) and is often used as a benchmark in a settlement (Vergleich). Actual amounts range from 0.25 to 1.5 months' salary per year of service. It is subject to wage tax (Lohnsteuer; under the one-fifth rule — Fünftelregelung), but NOT to social security contributions.

steps.title: What it is and when you're entitled to it

content.text: Severance pay (Abfindung) is a one-off cash payment from the employer when the employment relationship ends. The big myth: "if you're dismissed, you're entitled to severance pay". In practice, the law grants a right to it only in rare cases.
The main situations in which severance pay arises:

items: §1a KSchG: the employer offers severance pay in the dismissal letter itself in exchange for waiving an unfair-dismissal lawsuit (Kündigungsschutzklage) — the standard is 0.5 months' gross per year of service
Social plan (Sozialplan) under §112 BetrVG: in the case of mass layoffs at companies with a works council (Betriebsrat)
Settlement (Vergleich) at the labor court (Arbeitsgericht) after filing a lawsuit — the most common route, and negotiable
Termination agreement (Aufhebungsvertrag) — the parties agree on an amount
§9 KSchG: the court dissolves the contract and awards severance pay if returning to work is unreasonable

content.text: The standard benchmark formula (Faustformel; rule of thumb) used by the German courts:
Severance pay = 0.5 × (monthly gross salary — Bruttomonatsgehalt) × (years of service with the company — Jahre der Betriebszugehörigkeit)

Example: gross 4 500€/month, 6 years of service → 0.5 × 4 500 × 6 = 13 500€. In negotiations the range runs from 0.25 (weak position for the employee) to 1.5 months' salary (strong position: long service, an obviously unlawful dismissal, protected categories).

items: Long service (>10 years)
Age 50+ (worse chances of finding a job)
Severe disability (Schwerbehinderung) — the consent of the disability integration office (Integrationsamt) is required
Pregnancy or parental leave — special protection
Works council membership (Betriebsrat) — special protection under §15 KSchG
Obviously unlawful grounds for dismissal
Probation period (Probezeit) — you'll get almost nothing
Service <2 years (the KSchG does not apply in small companies of <10 people)
Dismissal for conduct (verhaltensbedingte Kündigung) with evidence
Proximity to retirement age

content.text: Severance pay (Abfindung) is taxable (steuerpflichtig), but since 2006 it has NOT been subject to social security contributions (Sozialversicherungsbeiträge — health KV / pension RV / long-term care PV / unemployment AV). This is a major advantage.

items: Wage tax (Lohnsteuer): the one-fifth rule (Fünftelregelung) under §34 EStG applies — the tax is calculated as if the amount were spread over 5 years (softening the progression)
From 2025, the one-fifth rule is applied only with the annual return (tax return — Steuererklärung), not automatically by the employer
Solidarity surcharge and church tax — yes, if applicable
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung), pension insurance (Rentenversicherung) — NO contributions on severance pay

content.text: Example of the one-fifth rule: severance pay of 30 000€ on an annual income of 50 000€. Without the "fifth", the tax would be calculated on the whole amount at once. With the "fifth", the tax on (50 000 + 6 000) is calculated, then the difference × 5 = the final tax (Steuer) on the severance pay. The saving is often 1 000-5 000€.

A termination agreement (Aufhebungsvertrag) = a blocking period (Sperrzeit) of 12 weeks under §159 SGB III. The Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) treats this as voluntarily giving up your job and blocks unemployment benefit Arbeitslosengeld I for 12 weeks. The exception: a valid reason ("wichtiger Grund"; for example, the threat of dismissal plus severance pay within the §1a formula).

Suspension period (Ruhenszeitraum) under §158 SGB III: if the severance agreement effectively "bought you out" of the notice period, unemployment benefit (ALG I) is suspended for that period. Example: instead of 3 months' notice you receive a lump sum — and for those 3 months ALG I is not paid.

Do NOT sign a termination agreement (Aufhebungsvertrag) on the spot. The law gives no right of withdrawal (a "cooling-off period" — Widerruf), but you can always take 24-48 hours to consult a specialist employment lawyer (Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht). Every day of delay is potentially +1000€ in severance pay.

After a dismissal (Kündigung) you have 3 weeks (under §4 KSchG) to file a lawsuit at the labor court (Arbeitsgericht). This is your main leverage — without the threat of a lawsuit, the employer won't raise the severance pay.
Under §1a KSchG the severance offer is tied to waiving the lawsuit. If you want more, decline the standard formula and file a lawsuit.

At the first-instance labor court (Arbeitsgericht) each side bears its own legal costs (§12a ArbGG), even the winner. But the chances of getting +50-100% on the severance pay through a settlement (Vergleich) usually outweigh those costs.

title: Anschreiben: formulas and templates
tldr: The cover letter (Anschreiben) for a job application (Bewerbung) in Germany is usually 1 A4 page. The structure is strict: header, date, subject line, salutation, 3-4 paragraphs, sign-off, signature. The format is DIN 5008. For classic applications (a corporation — Konzern; the public sector) it is mandatory; for startups and tech it is often replaced by a short message.

content.text: A cover letter (Anschreiben) in Germany follows the DIN 5008 standard. This isn't a mere formality — a recruiter reads the structure in seconds. Length: strictly 1 A4 page; font Arial/Calibri 11 or Times New Roman 12; margins of ~2.5 cm.

items: Header: your name, address, phone, email (at the top, on the right or left)
Addressee: company, department, name of the HR manager (Frau/Herrn ...)
Date: on the right, in the format "Berlin, 28. Mai 2026"
Subject line (Betreff): in bold, for example "Bewerbung als Softwareentwickler — Referenz 12345"
Salutation (Anrede): "Sehr geehrte Frau Müller," or "Sehr geehrter Herr Schmidt,"
Body: 3-4 paragraphs
Sign-off: "Mit freundlichen Grüßen"
Handwritten signature (scanned) + your printed name
Attachments (Anlagen): a list of the enclosed documents

content.text: The classic "AIDA" structure (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action) in its German version:
Do NOT open with "hiermit bewerbe ich mich" — it's a cliché. Start with something specific: why this particular company, what drew you to it.

Template: "Ihre Stellenausschreibung als [Position] auf [Plattform/Website] hat mich sofort angesprochen, da [a specific reason — product, mission, technology]. Mit [N] Jahren Erfahrung in [Bereich] möchte ich mich gern bei Ihnen vorstellen."
Specific achievements, figures, tools — but do NOT duplicate your CV (Lebenslauf).

Template: "In meiner aktuellen Position bei [Firma] verantworte ich [specific tasks]. Dabei konnte ich [a specific result — reduced X by 30%, launched Y]. Mit [skill A, B, C] bringe ich genau die Kompetenzen mit, die Sie suchen."
Why this particular company. Show that you've done your research.
Template: "Besonders begeistert mich [a specific project/value of the company]. Ich sehe in [Firma] die Möglichkeit, [how you plan to contribute]."
Salary, availability, and a call for an interview.

Template: "Meine Gehaltsvorstellung liegt bei [N] € brutto jährlich. Verfügbar bin ich ab [date] / nach Absprache mit einer Kündigungsfrist von [N] Wochen. Über die Einladung zu einem persönlichen Gespräch freue ich mich sehr."

If the posting asks you to state your salary expectations ("Gehaltsvorstellung"), do NOT ignore it, or your CV will land in the bin. State the annual gross salary (Bruttojahresgehalt), not a net monthly figure.

items: An exact figure: "55 000 € brutto jährlich" — the clearest option
A range: "zwischen 50.000 und 58.000 € brutto jährlich" — leaves room for negotiation
Only if asked: otherwise discuss it at the interview
Use the StepStone Gehaltsreport, kununu or Glassdoor for your sector and region as a guide

content.text: An anonymous salutation (Anrede), "Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren", is acceptable but lowers your chances. Find the HR contact's name in the site's legal notice (Impressum), on LinkedIn, or by calling the company.

The AGG (Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz — General Equal Treatment Act) has prohibited discrimination since 2006. Do NOT mention your marital status, religion, origin, or the age of your children in the cover letter — unless it is genuinely relevant (for example, a native language for a language position).
A typo in the HR contact's name or the company name means an instant rejection. Double-check it three times, especially when copying text between applications.

Length: an A4 page is the norm. Two pages — only if you're a senior with 15+ years of experience in a rare field. Never put the cover letter (Anschreiben) inside the CV (Lebenslauf) — they are separate PDF files.

title: Registering with the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit)
tldr: You need to register with the Federal Employment Agency (BA) in two different ways. Registration as a job seeker (Arbeitsuchend-Meldung): 3 months before your contract ends (or within 3 days of a sudden dismissal), otherwise you face a blocking period (Sperrzeit) of 1 week. Registration as unemployed (Arbeitslos-Meldung): in person on the first day of unemployment, otherwise unemployment benefit (ALG I) is delayed. Registration is free. You can do it online via arbeitsagentur.de.

steps.title: Two different registrations — don't confuse them

content.text: This is the most common mistake foreigners make with the Federal Employment Agency (BA). There are TWO different statuses, with different deadlines and different consequences.

items: Job seeker (Arbeitsuchend): register as soon as you learn of an upcoming dismissal — at least 3 months before the contract ends, under §38 SGB III
Unemployed (Arbeitslos): register on the first day of actual unemployment under §141 SGB III — the moment from which unemployment benefit (ALG I) is counted

content.text: Being late with the job seeker registration (Arbeitsuchend-Meldung) = a blocking period (Sperrzeit) of 1 week (§159 Abs. 1 Nr. 7 SGB III) and the loss of a week's unemployment benefit (ALG I). Being late with the unemployed registration (Arbeitslos-Meldung) = ALG I is paid only from the day you register, not from the dismissal.

This is the step for everyone who has learned that a fixed-term contract (befristeter Vertrag) is ending or has received a notice of dismissal (Kündigung). The goal is to give the Federal Employment Agency (BA) time to find you a job.

items: 3 months before the contract ends (if you know in advance)
Within 3 days of receiving the notice of dismissal (Kündigung), if it came later (a sudden dismissal)
For a fixed-term contract (befristeter Vertrag) — 3 months before the term ends
Online: arbeitsagentur.de → "Arbeitsuchend melden" (register as a job seeker; an account is required)
By phone: 0800 4 555500 (free)
In person at your local employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit)
CV (Lebenslauf)
Diplomas and certificates
Your current employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag) or notice of dismissal (Kündigung)
Contact details and your desired profession

steps.title: Arbeitslos registration and the ALG I application

content.text: On the first day after your job ends, you must register as unemployed (Arbeitslos), in person or online. The application for unemployment benefit (ALG I, Arbeitslosengeld 1) can be submitted earlier — up to 3 months in advance.

In person at the employment agency (Arbeitsagentur) for your place of residence (by appointment), OR online through your personal account on arbeitsagentur.de using the eID (the online ID function of your ID card) or a certificate from the tax authority's Elster portal.

items: Online application (Online-Antrag) at arbeitsagentur.de (digital identification required)
Employment certificate (Arbeitsbescheinigung) from your employer (they submit it themselves via BA-Online)
Steuer-ID
Health insurance card (Krankenversichertenkarte)
IBAN for the payment

content.text: The official decision (Bescheid) arrives within 2-4 weeks. The first payment covers the following month and is backdated. Until then, you can apply for an advance (Vorschuss) if you're in financial difficulty.
Registration is not "set it and forget it". You have duties to cooperate (Mitwirkungspflichten), and breaching them = a blocking period (Sperrzeit) or other sanctions.

items: Own job-search efforts (Eigenbemühungen): submit job applications and keep a record — usually 4-6 per month

Reachability (Erreichbarkeit): collect mail from the Federal Employment Agency (BA) daily at your registered address and respond to summonses the same day (the reachability order — Erreichbarkeitsanordnung)
Appointments (Termine): attend every invitation from your placement advisor (Vermittler)
Report changes (Veränderungen melden): new earnings, illness, or any absence of >3 weeks
Absence from your place of residence (Ortsabwesenheit; vacation — Urlaub): no more than 3 weeks per year, and only with permission from the Federal Employment Agency (BA)

content.text: A termination agreement (Aufhebungsvertrag) almost always = a blocking period (Sperrzeit) of 12 weeks. If your employer offers one, first consult a specialist lawyer (Fachanwalt) — the loss of unemployment benefit (ALG I) may outweigh the severance pay (Abfindung).

Without a valid residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) or permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis), unemployment benefit (ALG I) is not paid. With an EU Blue Card (Blue Card) or a residence permit for employment (Aufenthaltstitel zur Erwerbstätigkeit), payment is possible, but your status will be checked. Unemployment of more than 3 months can affect the renewal of your residence permit.
A trip (Reise) outside Germany without permission = deregistration and loss of benefits. Arrange any absence from your place of residence (Ortsabwesenheit) at least a week in advance.
