title: Unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld I): 60% / 67% of gross
tldr: Unemployment benefit (ALG I) under SGB III: 60% of the calculated net (Leistungsentgelt) without children, 67% with at least one child. The requirement: at least 12 months of mandatory contributions (Pflichtbeitrag) within the last 30 months. The payment period runs from 6 to 24 months depending on length of service and age. The income ceiling for calculating social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) for unemployment insurance (ALV) in 2026 is 8 450 €/month, uniform across the country (the West/East split has been abolished).

content.text: Entitlement to unemployment benefit (ALG I) under §137 SGB III requires three conditions to be met at the same time.

items: Unemployed (Arbeitslos): no job, or work of fewer than 15 hours per week
Unemployment registration (Arbeitslosmeldung): you have registered in person at the employment agency (Arbeitsagentur)

Minimum qualifying period (Anwartschaftszeit): you have accumulated at least 12 months of mandatory contributions (Pflichtbeiträge) to unemployment insurance (Arbeitslosenversicherung) within the last 30 months (the framework period — Rahmenfrist)

content.text: The following count toward the mandatory contributions (Pflichtbeiträge): regular employment with social contributions paid (subject to social insurance — sozialversicherungspflichtig), part of parental leave (Elternzeit, up to 3 years), care leave (Pflegezeit), military or civilian service, and time spent receiving sickness benefit (Krankengeld). A mini-job (Minijob, up to 603€/month) does NOT count — no unemployment insurance (AV) contributions are paid on it.
The amount of unemployment benefit (ALG I) is calculated under §149-152 SGB III via the assessment base (Bemessungsentgelt; average gross) → the calculated net (Leistungsentgelt) → a percentage.
The average daily gross earnings over the last 12 assessment months. The assessment base (Bemessungsentgelt) = (gross over 12 months) / 365 days.

From the assessment base (Bemessungsentgelt), the Federal Employment Agency (BA) deducts a flat 21% for social contributions, wage tax (Lohnsteuer) according to your tax class (Steuerklasse), and the solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) where applicable. The result is the calculated net (Leistungsentgelt).

60% of the calculated net (Leistungsentgelt) without children; 67% if at least 1 child (a child allowance — Kinderfreibetrag) is registered in your wage tax deduction features (Lohnsteuermerkmale). Half a child allowance is enough.

Example: gross 4 000€/month, tax class Steuerklasse I, no children. The assessment base (Bemessungsentgelt) is ~131,50€/day. After deducting 21% and wage tax (Lohnsteuer), the calculated net (Leistungsentgelt) is ~80€/day. Unemployment benefit (ALG I) = 80 × 0,60 ≈ 48€/day ≈ 1 440€/month. With a child: 80 × 0,67 ≈ 53,60€/day ≈ 1 608€/month.

The amount is capped by the income ceiling for calculating social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze, BBG) for unemployment insurance (Arbeitslosenversicherung): in 2026 it is uniform across Germany at 8 450 €/month (with no West/East split, which was abolished from 2025). Because of this, the maximum unemployment benefit (ALG I) in 2026 is roughly 2 810 €/month for class I without children and about 3 621 €/month for class III with a child.
The payment period for unemployment benefit (ALG I) under §147 SGB III depends on the length of mandatory insurance (Pflichtversicherung) and your age when the entitlement arises.
Under 50 (standard):

items: 12 months of service → 6 months of ALG I
16 months → 8 months
20 months → 10 months
24 months → 12 months (maximum for under-50s)

content.text: Older workers:

items: 50+: up to 15 months (with 30 months of service)
55+: up to 18 months (with 36 months of service)
58+: up to 24 months (with 48 months of service) — the maximum

content.text: A blocking period (Sperrzeit) under §159 SGB III is a period in which you hold the entitlement but receive no money. It substantially shortens the total payment period.

items: Blocking period for giving up work (Sperrzeit bei Arbeitsaufgabe): 12 weeks if you quit yourself without a valid reason ("wichtiger Grund") or signed a termination agreement (Aufhebungsvertrag)
Blocking period for refusing offered work (Sperrzeit bei Arbeitsablehnung): 3-12 weeks for turning down a suitable offer
Blocking period for late job-seeker registration (Sperrzeit bei verspäteter Arbeitsuchendmeldung): 1 week for registering late
Blocking period for non-attendance (Sperrzeit bei Meldeversäumnis): 1 week for missing an appointment (Termin) without a valid excuse (Entschuldigung)

content.text: A blocking period (Sperrzeit) of 12 weeks means a loss of ~25% of the entire unemployment benefit (ALG I) period if that period is 24 weeks. A decision by the Federal Employment Agency (BA) can be appealed at the social court (Sozialgericht) within 1 month — a lawsuit (Klage) is free under §183 SGG.

items: Own job-search efforts (Eigenbemühungen): submit applications and keep a record of them (usually 4-6/month)
Appointments (Termine): attend meetings with your placement adviser (Vermittler)
Availability (Verfügbarkeit): respond to letters from the Federal Employment Agency (BA) within 3 days
Application process (Bewerbungsverfahren): attend interviews (Vorstellungsgespräche)
Report changes (Veränderungen melden): a side job, illness, or an absence
Illness (Krankheit): a doctor's note from the first day while you are unemployed

content.text: A side job while receiving unemployment benefit (ALG I): up to 165€/month is not deducted; anything above that is deducted from the benefit (minus necessary expenses). Above 15 hours per week, you lose your unemployed (Arbeitslos) status and ALG I payment stops.

costs.label: Application for ALG I
costs.note: Free; via arbeitsagentur.de or in person

costs.label: Beratungshilfe (legal aid)
costs.note: On a low income — almost free for advice on a Bescheid

costs.label: Anwalt für Sozialrecht for an appeal
costs.note: At the Sozialgericht first instance — no court costs under §183 SGG

title: Employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag): key clauses
tldr: Since 1 August 2022 (the reform of the law on proof of working conditions — NachwG), the employer must provide a written employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag) with a mandatory set of clauses within 7 days of starting work. Pay attention to: the probation period (Probezeit, up to 6 months), the notice period for dismissal (Kündigungsfrist, §622 BGB), the fixed term of the contract (Befristung), the notice period during probation (Probezeit-Kündigungsfrist), overtime clauses (Überstunden-Klauseln), and the transfer clause (Versetzungsklausel). A verbal contract is also valid but creates problems.

steps.title: What the contract must contain under NachwG

content.text: The reform of the law on proof of working conditions (NachwG, Nachweisgesetz) of 1 August 2022 (which implements an EU directive — EU-Richtlinie 2019/1152) requires the key conditions to be set out in writing as a mandatory matter. The deadline is 7 days from the start of work for the main clauses and 1 month for the rest. Non-compliance carries a fine of up to 2000€ per case (§4 NachwG).
Mandatory clauses under §2 NachwG:

items: the names and addresses of the parties
the start date of work (Arbeitsbeginn)
for a fixed-term contract (befristet) — the end date or the foreseeable duration
the place of work (Arbeitsort) — or a note on the possibility of working at different locations
the position and a description of the tasks (Tätigkeit)
the amount and composition of pay (Vergütung) — salary, supplements, method of payment
the agreed working time (vereinbarte Arbeitszeit) and the rules on breaks
the length of the probation period (Probezeit), if any
the length of vacation (Urlaub)
the conditions for overtime (Überstunden)
the notice period for dismissal (Kündigungsfrist) plus the procedure and form (written form — Schriftform!)
any applicable collective (tariff) agreements (Tarifverträge) and works agreements (Betriebsvereinbarungen)
the obligation to undergo further training (Pflicht zur Fortbildung), if any
an employer-funded company pension (betriebliche Altersversorgung) — the provider's details

content.text: The probation period (Probezeit) under §622 Abs. 3 BGB is a maximum of 6 months. The notice period for a dismissal (Kündigung) is 2 weeks (instead of the usual 4 weeks).

items: a maximum of 6 months — it cannot be extended (the only exceptions are illness — Krankheit; and maternity leave — Mutterschutz)
the notice period (Kündigungsfrist) during probation: 2 weeks (§622 Abs. 3 BGB)
the KSchG does not apply during probation — dismissal is possible without justification
maternity protection (Mutterschutz) and protection for severely disabled people (Schwerbehindertenschutz) still apply

content.text: After the NachwG reform (the law on proof of working conditions) of 2022: if the contract sets a probation period (Probezeit) for a fixed-term contract (befristeter Vertrag), it must be proportionate to the overall length of the contract (§15 Abs. 3 TzBfG). For example, for a 6-month contract the probation period is a maximum of 2-3 months.

The notice period under §622 BGB is one of the most common mistakes in contracts. The periods depend on length of service and apply TO the employer; for the employee, by default, it is 4 weeks before the 15th or the end of the month.
The employer's notice period for dismissal (Kündigungsfrist) under §622 Abs. 2 BGB:

items: up to 2 years of service — 4 weeks before the 15th or the end of the month
from 2 years — 1 month to the end of the month
from 5 years — 2 months
from 8 years — 3 months
from 10 years — 4 months
from 12 years — 5 months
from 15 years — 6 months
from 20 years — 7 months

content.text: The contract may set longer periods for both sides, or set the same period for the employee as for the employer. But the period for the employee cannot be longer than the one for the employer (§622 Abs. 6 BGB) — otherwise the clause is void.

steps.title: Dangerous clauses — what to look out for

content.text: The wording "Mit dem Gehalt sind alle Überstunden abgegolten" is considered invalid under rulings of the Federal Labor Court (BAG, 5 AZR 765/10) if it is too vague. Specifics are needed, e.g. "bis zu 10 Überstunden monatlich".

"Der Arbeitgeber behält sich vor, den Arbeitnehmer an einen anderen Ort zu versetzen" — permissible within §106 GewO (the employer's right to give instructions — Direktionsrecht), but it must not substantially worsen your conditions. For a relocation of more than 50 km, consent is usually required.

A ban on working for competitors after you leave is valid only if compensation is paid for the duration of the ban (Karenzentschädigung) of at least 50% of your last salary (§74 HGB). Without compensation, the clause is void.

The contract may require you to repay the cost of further training (Fortbildung) if you leave before a set term. Under a ruling of the Federal Labor Court (BAG, 3 AZR 192/05): a maximum tie-in of 5 years for expensive training, and proportionally less for short courses.
"Alle Ansprüche verfallen nach 3 Monaten" — valid with a minimum of 3 months for both sides. These clauses often make people forget about unpaid overtime.

items: Take 24-72 hours to review it — do NOT sign under pressure
Check the salary against brutto-netto-rechner.info (taking your tax class — Steuerklasse — into account)
Check the sector's collective (tariff) agreement (Tarifvertrag) — the terms are often better than in the contract
Look up the company on kununu.com — ratings and warnings
For contracts above 60k gross or with a non-compete (Wettbewerbsverbot), a consultation with a specialist employment lawyer (Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht) at 80-150€ often pays off
Keep a copy of the signed original — the employer is obliged to provide it

costs.label: Contract review by a Fachanwalt
costs.note: An hourly consultation before signing; invests in the chance to improve the terms

costs.label: Translation of the contract into Russian (vereidigter Übersetzer)
costs.note: For long contracts; the employer is usually not obliged to translate

costs.label: Beratung via DGB-Rechtsschutz
costs.note: Free for union members; includes a review of the contract

title: Betriebsrat: the works council
tldr: A works council (Betriebsrat) can be set up in any company with at least 5 employees (§1 BetrVG). It has broad rights: consent on dismissals (§102 BetrVG), participation in working-time matters (Arbeitszeit), and a social plan (Sozialplan) in case of layoffs. Council members are protected: dismissal is banned under §15 KSchG. The employer bears the costs.

steps.title: What it is and who can set it up

content.text: A works council (Betriebsrat) is an elected body that represents employees under the Works Constitution Act (Betriebsverfassungsgesetz, BetrVG). It is NOT a trade union — it operates only within a single establishment (Betrieb; a production unit). A single company may have several works councils (Betriebsräte; one per site) plus a central council (Gesamtbetriebsrat).

items: At least 5 employees entitled to vote (wahlberechtigte), of whom at least 3 are eligible to be elected (wählbare) — §1 BetrVG
Right to vote (wahlberechtigt): 16+, at least 6 months with the company
Not created automatically — employees have to take the initiative
The size of the council grows with the workforce: 5-20 employees = 1 member; 21-50 = 3; 51-100 = 5; and so on under §9 BetrVG up to 35 members
Term of office — 4 years, with regular elections

content.text: Rights fall into three levels: full participation (Mitbestimmung; nothing can be done without consent), consultative participation (Mitwirkung), and information (Information; the right to be informed).

items: Start and end of working hours (Beginn und Ende der Arbeitszeit)
Overtime and reduction of working hours
Arrangement of breaks (Pausen)
How pay and bonuses are calculated
Internal company rules (Hausordnung)
Social facilities (canteen Kantine, parking)
Video surveillance and performance-monitoring tools
Occupational health and safety (Arbeitsschutz)
Consent to hiring, transfer, promotion/demotion in companies with more than 20 employees
A hearing (Anhörung) before ANY dismissal — without consulting the council a dismissal (Kündigung) is void (§102 Abs. 1 BetrVG)
An objection (Widerspruch) by the council gives the employee the right to keep working until the court rules (§102 Abs. 5 BetrVG)

items.title: On changes to the establishment (Betriebsänderungen, §§111-112 BetrVG)

items: Closure, downsizing, relocation — a reconciliation of interests (Interessenausgleich) must be negotiated
Social plan (Sozialplan) — compensation/severance pay (Abfindung) in case of layoffs
No council — no right to a social plan (a major gap in protection)

steps.title: How to set up a Betriebsrat

content.text: Setting up a council is a common trigger for pressure from the employer. Under §119 BetrVG this is a criminal offence (under criminal law, Strafrecht), but in practice harassment (Mobbing), denied promotions, and attempts to dismiss the organizers are common. Protection: bring in a trade union early (ver.di, IG Metall) — they have lawyers.

In companies without a council, a staff meeting (Betriebsversammlung) elects 3 employees to the electoral board (Wahlvorstand). Alternatively, the labour court (Arbeitsgericht) appoints it upon request.
For companies with 5-100 employees there is a simplified procedure (§14a BetrVG): elections within 2-3 weeks.

From the moment the invitation to the staff meeting (Betriebsversammlung) goes out, everyone who issues the invitation is covered by special protection against dismissal (Kündigungsschutz) under §15 KSchG. The protection lasts up to 6 months.
The employer bears all costs of the council's work under §40 BetrVG: premises, office equipment, legal advice, training, and time off for council duties.

items: Release from work (Freistellung): in companies with 200 or more employees at least 1 council member is fully released; the scale is set by §38 BetrVG
Training (Schulungen): new members are entitled to training on the BetrVG (usually 1 week, paid)
Bringing in experts (Hinzuziehung von Sachverständigen): where needed, the council may call in experts at the employer's expense
Meetings (Sitzungen) — during working hours

content.text: Without a council, the employer is NOT obliged to draw up a social plan (Sozialplan) in case of layoffs. That's why, in a crisis, companies often try to make the council redundant "along with the establishment" — but §15 KSchG protects the council for up to 1 year after the mandate ends.

Works council (Betriebsrat) members do NOT receive extra pay for the council work as such: §37 BetrVG only guarantees that their previous pay level is maintained (the honorary-office principle, Ehrenamtsprinzip — an honorary, unpaid position). Inflated payments to council members are risky for the employer: in the well-known Volkswagen case the BAG (ruling of 21.02.2024) clarified the criteria, and excessive payments can be treated as breach of trust (Untreue, §266 StGB).
The council does not replace a trade union. Collective bargaining (Tarifverhandlungen) is conducted only by the trade union (Gewerkschaft) — the council has no right to strike (Streik).

costs.label: Betriebsrat costs
costs.note: The employer bears all costs under §40 BetrVG

costs.label: Schulungen for works council members
costs.note: Paid by the employer; typically 1 800-2 500€ per course

costs.label: Juristische Beratung via ver.di / IG Metall
costs.note: Free for union members

title: Bewerbungsfoto: do you need a photo
tldr: Since 2006 (the AGG anti-discrimination act) a photo in a job application (Bewerbung) is NOT mandatory, and many large companies explicitly ask you NOT to attach one. But in traditional sectors (banks, the public sector, small businesses, retail) a photo is still expected. A professional shot costs 50-150€ at a studio. A modern application won't suffer without one.

content.text: The AGG (Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz) of 14 August 2006 prohibits discrimination in hiring on the grounds of race/ethnic origin, sex, religion/belief, disability, age, and sexual orientation (§1 AGG).

A photo makes all of these characteristics visible, so many companies deliberately drop the photo (Foto) to reduce the risk of a compensation claim (Entschädigungsklage) under §15 AGG (potentially 3 months' salary).

items: The law does NOT ban photos — it bans discrimination based on them
The law does NOT require you to attach a photo — the employer cannot demand one
In Bayern and some other federal states a photo may be mandatory when applying to the police (Polizei-Bewerbung) (an ID form)

steps.title: When to attach one (and when not)

items: Small and medium-sized businesses (Mittelstand), especially in the provinces
Banks, insurance, law firms — traditional sectors
Retail, hospitality, the hotel business (front office)
The public sector and civil servants (Beamte; if explicitly requested)
Performers, models, and other public-facing roles
Large tech companies (SAP, Siemens, and BMW often write "keine Foto")
Startups and remote work
If the listing explicitly says "anonyme Bewerbung" (anonymous application)
Any platform that asks only for a PDF with no photo field
English-language applications to international companies (a photo = red flag)

content.text: If in doubt, do NOT attach one. Modern practice is shifting in that direction.

steps.title: What the photo should look like

content.text: An application photo (Bewerbungsfoto) is NOT a passport photo and NOT a selfie. It's a business portrait, usually in colour, taken professionally.

items: Format: square or 3:4, at least 600×800 px
Size on the page: 4×5 or 4×6 cm in the top-right corner of the CV (Lebenslauf)
Background: a single colour (grey, white, blue) or softly blurred
Clothing: appropriate to the sector — shirt/blouse/jacket for office positions
Face: 60-70% of the frame, a slight smile, looking straight ahead
Lighting: studio, with no shadows on the face

content.text: Do NOT use holiday photos, selfies, or cropped group shots. They come across as unprofessional.

steps.title: Where to get it and how much it costs

items: Professional studio photographer: 60-150€ — the best option
Photo booth (Foto-Box; DM, Rossmann) for a passport photo (Passfoto) plus retouching: 10-15€ — acceptable, but it shows
A photographer who comes to you or works in startup coworking spaces: 80-200€
A shot for your portfolio (LinkedIn + Lebenslauf): usually included in the package

content.text: A good photo can be used for 2-3 years. If you work in one sector long-term, it pays off. The Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur) also covers an application photo through the job-placement budget (Vermittlungsbudget, §44 SGB III) for registered jobseekers — ask your placement adviser (Vermittler).

costs.label: Professional Bewerbungsfoto at a studio
costs.note: With retouching and digital copies

costs.label: Foto-Box (DM/Rossmann/Photo-Me)
costs.note: A basic solution; lower quality than a studio

costs.label: Vermittlungsbudget BA
costs.note: Free for registered jobseekers under §44 SGB III

sources.title: Antidiskriminierungsstelle des Bundes — Bewerbung ohne Foto

title: Kündigungsschutz: protection against dismissal
tldr: The Protection Against Dismissal Act (KSchG) applies if the establishment has more than 10 employees and you have worked there for more than 6 months. The dismissal must then be "sozial gerechtfertigt" — justified on one of three grounds: betriebsbedingt (operational), personenbedingt (personal, e.g. illness), or verhaltensbedingt (conduct). The key risk: you have just 3 weeks from receipt to challenge any written Kündigung (§4 KSchG). Miss it, and the dismissal is deemed lawful even if it was unjustified.

content.text: The Protection Against Dismissal Act (Kündigungsschutzgesetz, KSchG) is the "general" protection against dismissal. It does not apply automatically to everyone: two conditions under §1 and §23 KSchG must be met at the same time.

items: Size of the establishment: more than 10 employees (counted on a pro-rata basis, with part-timers weighted by a factor); for contracts predating 2003 the threshold is more than 5
Length of service: you have worked continuously at this establishment for more than 6 months (the waiting period, Wartezeit)
Both conditions must be met at the same time at the moment you receive the notice of dismissal (Kündigung)

content.text: If the establishment is small (a small business, Kleinbetrieb — up to 10 employees) or your length of service is under 6 months, the general KSchG does not apply. Even then, a baseline protection still applies: a ban on arbitrariness (good faith, Treu und Glauben, §242 BGB), a ban on discrimination (AGG), and special protection for pregnant women, people on parental leave (Elternzeit), severely disabled people, and works council (Betriebsrat) members.
When the KSchG applies, an ordinary (ordentliche) dismissal is permissible only if it is socially justified under §1 KSchG. The law recognizes exactly three categories of grounds.

The job disappears: downsizing, restructuring, or closure of a department. The employer must carry out a social selection (Sozialauswahl) — choosing the least "socially protected" among comparable employees for dismissal, based on length of service, age, number of dependants, and disability. Mistakes in the social selection are a frequent ground for overturning a dismissal.

For objective reasons the employee cannot do the job: long-term or frequent illness, or loss of a required licence. Most often this is a dismissal on health grounds (krankheitsbedingte Kündigung), and it requires a negative health prognosis and proof of a real burden on the establishment.

Breach of duties: absenteeism, refusal to carry out tasks, disciplinary violations. As a rule, a prior written warning from the employer (Abmahnung) on the same matter is required — without it, such a dismissal is often overturned.

steps.title: The key deadline: 3 weeks to file a claim

content.text: This is the most important point on the topic. Under §4 KSchG you have only 3 weeks from receipt of the written notice of dismissal (Kündigung) to file a protection-against-dismissal claim (Kündigungsschutzklage) at the labour court (Arbeitsgericht). Miss the deadline and, under §7 KSchG, the dismissal is deemed valid from the very start, even if it was completely unjustified. Reinstating the deadline (§5 KSchG) is possible only in very narrow, exceptional cases.

items: The 3-week deadline starts on the date you receive the notice of dismissal, not the date of the dismissal itself
The deadline is the same for all types of dismissal, including without notice / extraordinary (fristlose/außerordentliche)
The claim is filed at the labour court for your place of work; there is no filing fee
Do not wait for the notice period (Kündigungsfrist) to run out — the three weeks run in parallel
The works council (Betriebsrat; if there is one) must be consulted before the dismissal under §102 BetrVG; a breach is a separate ground for overturning it

steps.title: What to do if you receive a Kündigung

items: Record the date you received the letter

Do not sign a termination agreement (Aufhebungsvertrag) or a settlement agreement (Abwicklungsvertrag) under pressure — this can cost you unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld) through a blocking period (Sperrzeit)
Within the same window, register your status: you must report that you are jobseeking (arbeitssuchend) to the employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit) immediately, otherwise your benefit may be reduced

items.title: 2. Urgently see a lawyer or your trade union

content.text: Contact a specialist employment lawyer (Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht) or, if you are a member, your trade union — they offer free legal protection (Rechtsschutz). Many protection-against-dismissal claims end with severance pay (Abfindung), often around a benchmark of ~0.5 month's salary for each year of service, but this is a matter for negotiation, not an automatic right.

costs.label: Filing a Kündigungsschutzklage at the Arbeitsgericht
costs.note: There is no fee to file the claim; in the first instance each party bears its own costs regardless of the outcome.

costs.label: Lawyer for a Kündigungsschutzklage
costs.note: Depends on the Streitwert (usually ~3 months' salary); covered if you have Rechtsschutzversicherung or trade union membership.

title: Probationary period (Probezeit)
tldr: A probationary period (Probezeit) in Germany lasts at most 6 months. During this time the notice period is shortened to 2 weeks for both sides under §622 (3) BGB, with no tie to the 15th of the month or the end of the month, and you don't need to give a reason for the dismissal. The general protection under the Protection Against Dismissal Act (KSchG) still only kicks in after 6 months of service, so the "easy to dismiss" window largely coincides with the probationary period. But baseline protection (pregnancy, severe disability, discrimination) applies even during the probationary period.

steps.title: What a Probezeit is and how long it lasts

content.text: A probationary period (Probezeit) is an initial phase during which employer and employee size each other up. The law limits it to a maximum of 6 months (§622 (3) BGB). A probationary period is not mandatory: it is set in the employment contract, and it can be shorter or absent altogether.

items: Maximum duration — 6 months
Set by the contract; shorter or none at all is allowed
Salary, holiday, and sick pay during the Probezeit are the same as for regular employees
For fixed-term (befristete) contracts the probationary period must be proportionate to the term of the contract

steps.title: Notice period during the Probezeit: 2 weeks

content.text: Under §622 (3) BGB, during an agreed probationary period the notice period is shortened to 2 weeks — for both sides. These 2 weeks are not tied to the 15th of the month or the end of the month: you count exactly 14 days from the date you receive the written notice of dismissal (Kündigung).

items: The 2-week period applies for as long as the probationary period lasts
The notice of dismissal must be in writing and signed — §623 BGB
The contract or a collective (tariff) agreement (Tarifvertrag) may set a different period (but not one worse for the employee than for the employer)
If the notice of dismissal is sent at the end of the probationary period, the 2-week period may end after it — that's allowed

content.text: An important nuance: the general protection under the Protection Against Dismissal Act (KSchG; socially justified grounds for dismissal are required) only begins after 6 months of service — the waiting period (Wartezeit) under §1 KSchG. This window largely coincides with the maximum probationary period. That's why, in the first 6 months, the employer can dismiss without proving an operational, personal, or conduct-based (betriebs-, personen- oder verhaltensbedingt) reason.

"No KSchG" does not mean "no protection at all". Even during the probationary period the following still apply: a ban on discrimination (AGG), and special protection for pregnant women (§17 MuSchG requires authority approval), people on parental leave (Elternzeit), severely disabled people, and works council (Betriebsrat) members. And the deadline to file a claim is the same: 3 weeks from receipt of the notice of dismissal (Kündigung) under §4 KSchG. If the grounds are questionable, react immediately.

items: Check your contract for whether there is a probationary period and how long it is
During the probationary period the same rights to holiday and sick pay apply
The notice of dismissal counts as 14 days from receipt, with no rounding to the end of the month
For a questionable or discriminatory dismissal — 3 weeks to file a court claim (Klage), even during the probationary period
Free initial advice — your trade union if you are a member, or the labour court's claims-intake office (Arbeitsgericht-Rechtsantragstelle)

costs.label: Probezeit — no separate costs
costs.note: The probationary period requires no fees; it is part of the normal employment contract.

costs.label: Lawyer's advice for a questionable dismissal
costs.note: Erstberatung Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht; through a trade union if you are a member — free.

title: Bilanz vs EÜR: when is it mandatory
tldr: Simplified income-and-expense accounting (EÜR, Einnahmenüberschussrechnung, §4 Abs. 3 EStG) is a simplified cash-basis method for the liberal professions (Freiberufler) and small traders (Gewerbetreibende). A balance sheet (Bilanz; double-entry bookkeeping under HGB §238 ff) is mandatory if turnover exceeds 800.000€ or profit exceeds 80.000€ per year (thresholds in §141 AO, raised in 2024). Members of the liberal professions under §18 EStG use simplified accounting regardless of turnover.

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: In Germany there are two ways to account for profit: simplified income-and-expense accounting (Einnahmenüberschussrechnung, EÜR, §4 Abs. 3 EStG) — a simple cash-basis 'income minus expenses' method, and a balance sheet (Bilanz) — full double-entry bookkeeping (doppelte Buchführung) with a balance sheet and a profit-and-loss statement (Gewinn- und Verlustrechnung) under HGB §238 ff. Which method is mandatory determines the complexity of your annual reporting and the cost of a tax adviser (Steuerberater).

The key provision is §141 of the Fiscal Code (Abgabenordnung, AO): traders (Gewerbetreibende) become obliged to keep books (buchführungspflichtig) if in a calendar year they exceed at least one threshold: turnover (Umsatz) over 800.000€ or profit (Gewinn) over 80.000€. Until 2024 the figures were 600.000€ and 60.000€ — the thresholds were raised by the 'Wachstumschancengesetz' and apply to financial years from 2024 onward. As of 2026, exactly these figures are in force.

items: Simplified accounting (EÜR) — cash basis: the payment date counts, not the invoice date
Balance sheet (Bilanz) — accrual basis: the date the obligation arises counts
Members of the liberal professions (Freiberufler) under §18 EStG can always use simplified accounting regardless of turnover
Corporations (Kapitalgesellschaften; GmbH, UG, AG) always keep a balance sheet under HGB
Thresholds under §141 AO from 2024: turnover (Umsatz) 800.000€ / profit (Gewinn) 80.000€

steps.title: Who is required to keep a Bilanz

content.text: The obligation to keep a balance sheet (Bilanzierungspflicht) arises on two grounds: either you are registered as a merchant (Kaufmann) under the HGB (e.g. a registered merchant eingetragener Kaufmann e.K., OHG, KG, GmbH), or you are a trader (Gewerbetreibender) who has exceeded the thresholds of §141 AO.

items: GmbH, UG (haftungsbeschränkt), AG — always a balance sheet (HGB §242)
OHG, KG — always a balance sheet
e.K. (eingetragener Kaufmann) — always a balance sheet, except for the exemption under §241a HGB

content.text: §241a HGB exempts an e.K. from a balance sheet if turnover is ≤ 800.000€ and profit ≤ 80.000€ in the two most recent consecutive financial years. You may then use simplified accounting despite the entry in the commercial register (Handelsregister).

items.title: 3. Traders (Gewerbetreibende) without an entry in the commercial register

content.text: Exceed even one threshold of §141 AO and the tax office (Finanzamt) sends a notice that the bookkeeping obligation has begun (Mitteilung über den Beginn der Buchführungspflicht). The balance sheet is then mandatory from the following calendar year. The thresholds are checked annually using the data from the tax return (Steuererklärung).

Members of the liberal professions (§18 EStG) — doctors, lawyers, engineers, IT consultants by analogy, artists, journalists — can always use simplified accounting. Even a member of a liberal profession with a turnover of 2.000.000€ a year is not required to prepare a balance sheet.

Simplified accounting is simpler, cheaper, and requires no stocktaking. A balance sheet gives a more accurate picture, but it requires a tax adviser (costs of 1.500-5.000€/year instead of 500-1.500€ for simplified accounting) and is more complex to maintain.

items: Simplified accounting: the Anlage EÜR form on the ELSTER tax portal, free; cash-basis accounting; no stocktaking
Balance sheet: an electronic balance sheet (E-Bilanz) via ELSTER (§5b EStG); a stocktake (Inventur) is required on 31.12; invoices are recognized by the date they are issued
Simplified accounting is advantageous if you have many outstanding invoices at year-end (it defers tax)
A balance sheet is advantageous for long-term projects with provisions (Rückstellungen)
Switching from simplified accounting to a balance sheet — a one-off transition calculation (Überleitungsrechnung); switching back is only possible after 3 years

content.text: If the tax office has sent a request to keep a balance sheet (Aufforderung zur Bilanzierung) — you cannot ignore it. Being late to switch risks a fine and an estimate of your profit by the tax office at its own discretion (Schätzung).

One year with a turnover of 850.000€ — and the following year you are obliged to keep a balance sheet, even if turnover drops again. The exemption requires two consecutive years below the threshold (for an e.K. — §241a HGB).

IT consultants often assume they are members of a liberal profession by analogy with an engineer (Ingenieur). If the tax office reclassifies the activity as a trade (Gewerbe; e.g. reselling software rather than consulting), the thresholds of §141 AO apply.
A balance sheet is filed electronically via an electronic balance sheet (E-Bilanz, §5b EStG). The tax office has not accepted a paper balance sheet since 2013.

title: EÜR: simplified accounting
tldr: Einnahmenüberschussrechnung (EÜR, §4 Abs. 3 EStG) is a cash-basis accounting method: income minus expenses by the payment date. It is filed via ELSTER as the 'Anlage EÜR' together with the Einkommensteuererklärung. For Freiberufler and Kleingewerbe with turnover up to 800.000€ / profit up to 80.000€ (§141 AO) it is the only mandatory reporting format.

content.text: Simplified income-and-expense accounting (EÜR) is the Einnahmenüberschussrechnung under §4 Abs. 3 EStG: a simplified way of calculating profit as the difference between business income (Betriebseinnahmen) and business expenses (Betriebsausgaben), recognized on the cash-flow principle (Zufluss-Abfluss-Prinzip, §11 EStG) — that is, by the date money actually arrives in or leaves the account, not by the date the invoice is issued.

Simplified accounting is submitted via the Anlage EÜR form on the ELSTER tax portal every year as part of the income tax return (Einkommensteuererklärung). Since 2017 the paper form is no longer accepted — electronic filing only. The deadline is the general income-tax return deadline (ESt-Erklärung; usually 31.07 of the following year, or, through a tax adviser (Steuerberater), until the end of February the year after).

items: Cash basis: the payment date counts, not the invoice (Rechnung) date
Submitted as the Anlage EÜR form on the ELSTER tax portal
Available to members of the liberal professions (Freiberufler) always, and to commercial activity (Gewerbe) up to the thresholds of §141 AO
A simple Excel sheet or Lexoffice / sevDesk is enough
Requires no stocktaking, balance sheet, or provisions (Rückstellungen)

content.text: In simplified accounting you record two flows: business income (Betriebseinnahmen) and business expenses (Betriebsausgaben). Every business expense must be evidenced (belegt) — by an invoice, a receipt, or a bank statement. The retention period for accounting records (Buchungsbelege) and invoices (Rechnungen) was shortened to 8 years as of 1 January 2025 (§147 Abs. 3 AO and §14b Abs. 1 UStG as amended by the Bürokratieentlastungsgesetz IV). The new rule applies to records whose retention period had not yet expired by 31.12.2024.

items: All fees (Honorare) and invoices (Rechnungen; gross, unless you are a small business Kleinunternehmer)
Advance payments received (Anzahlungen)
Sale of fixed assets (Verkauf von Anlagevermögen; selling equipment)
Withdrawals of assets for personal use (Privatentnahmen aus Sachwerten)
VAT refunds (Erstattung von USt) from the tax office (Finanzamt)
Office costs (Bürokosten): office rent, internet, telephone
Work equipment (Arbeitsmittel): a laptop up to 1.000€ net — a low-value asset (GWG), written off immediately (§6 Abs. 2 EStG)
Over 1.000€ net — depreciation (Abschreibung, AfA) per the BMF tables
Professional development (Fortbildung): courses, conferences, specialist literature
Travel costs (Reisekosten): 0,30€/km by car; hotel in full; meal allowances (Verpflegungspauschalen; 28€/day in Germany when away for a full 24h)
Contributions to the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) / Chamber of Skilled Crafts (HWK) / a professional association (Berufsverband)
Tax adviser (Steuerberater) and software (Lexoffice, sevDesk)
Pro-rata costs of a home office (anteilige Kosten Arbeitszimmer; if it meets §4 Abs. 5 Nr. 6b EStG)

content.text: If you are not a small business (Kleinunternehmer; §19 UStG, turnover up to 25.000€ last year as of 2025), an advance VAT return (Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung) is filed monthly or quarterly. Simplified accounting is then kept using either the gross or the net method, your choice — the key is to be consistent.

The Anlage EÜR is a separate form in your personal account on the Mein ELSTER portal. It is filled in mostly by hand: the program asks you to enter the amounts for each line item. You can also import directly from Lexoffice / sevDesk through a certified API.

items: Log in to mein.elster.de with your certificate file (Zertifikatsdatei)
Select 'Einkommensteuererklärung' → 'Anlage EÜR'
Enter business income (Betriebseinnahmen; fields 11-22)
Enter business expenses (Betriebsausgaben; fields 23-66): separately for staff (Personal), premises costs (Raumkosten), depreciation (AfA), and travel (Reisekosten)
Set the profit-calculation method (Gewinnermittlungsart) to 'Einnahmenüberschussrechnung'
Sign and submit together with the main form (Mantelbogen) ESt 1 A and the Anlage S (for members of the liberal professions) or Anlage G (for commercial activity)

content.text: The cash-flow principle (Zufluss-Abfluss) does NOT apply to regularly recurring payments (regelmäßig wiederkehrende Zahlungen) within 10 days before or after the end of the year (§11 Abs. 1 S. 2 EStG). January's rent paid on 28.12 counts as a December expense.

Buying a laptop for 1.200€ net is not a business expense (Betriebsausgabe) in full but depreciation (AfA): for computer equipment, since 2021 the BMF has allowed immediate write-off (Sofortabschreibung) over 1 year, but you have to choose this explicitly in the return.

Business-entertainment expenses (Bewirtungskosten; restaurants with clients) — only 70% are deductible; the remaining 30% and the tip (Trinkgeld) are non-deductible. An entertainment receipt (Bewirtungsbeleg) stating the names of those present and the occasion is mandatory.

Withdrawals for personal use (Privatentnahmen) and personal contributions (Privateinlagen) are a common mistake. Transferring money from the business account to a personal one is not a business expense but a withdrawal (Entnahme); it does not reduce profit.

The retention period for receipts and invoices (Rechnungen) is 8 years as of 2025 (§147 Abs. 3 AO, the BEG IV reform); annual financial statements (Jahresabschlüsse) and inventory lists (Inventare) are still kept for 10 years. During a tax audit (Betriebsprüfung) the tax office (Finanzamt) can request records for the entire period.

title: Coworking: Mindspace, WeWork, betahaus
tldr: Coworking is a flexible alternative to renting an office for Freiberufler and startups: prices are 100-400€/month for a hot desk, 250-700€/month for a fixed desk, and 600-1.500€/month for a private office. The costs are fully deductible as Betriebsausgaben. In Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, and Cologne the choice is wide — Mindspace, WeWork, betahaus, Impact Hub, Spaces, Factory.

content.text: A coworking space (Coworking Space) is a shared office: a workspace by subscription with no long-term lease. For members of the liberal professions (Freiberufler) and freelancers in Germany it solves three problems: separating work from home (important for the home-office rules, Häusliches Arbeitszimmer, §4 Abs. 5 Nr. 6b EStG), getting a business address (Geschäftsadresse) for the legal notice (Impressum) and invoices (Rechnungen), and getting into a community of other startup people.

items: Hot desk: any free spot, 100-250€/month
Fixed desk: your own desk, 250-700€/month
Private office: a closed room for 1-10 people, 600-2.500€/month
Most include: WiFi, meeting rooms (a set number of hours per month), coffee, a printer, and mail handling
Day pass: 20-40€ a day, no subscription
betahaus Kreuzberg — a classic of the startup scene, hot desk from 199€
Mindspace Krausenstraße / Skalitzer Straße — premium segment, from 350€
Factory Berlin Mitte / Görlitzer Park — an investor community, from 300€
WeWork Sony Center / Atrium Tower — corporate style, from 350€
St. Oberholz Rosenthaler Platz — café-coworking, day pass 25€
WeWork Oskar-von-Miller-Ring, Neuturmstraße — from 400€
Mindspace Salvatorplatz — from 380€
Impact Hub Munich — focus on social impact, from 250€
Combinat 56 — an independent coworking space, from 240€
betahaus Hamburg Schanze — from 199€
Mindspace Hamburg Rödingsmarkt — from 350€
Design Offices Köln Mediapark — from 350€
STARTPLATZ Köln (Mediapark) — incubator + coworking, from 199€

content.text: Spaces (IWG) — a large network with locations in Frankfurt, Düsseldorf, Stuttgart, and Hannover. Regus — the cheapest private offices across Germany. In smaller towns, look for local coworking spaces via the site coworkinggermany.de.

Coworking costs are a 100% business expense (Betriebsausgabe) under §4 Abs. 4 EStG, with no annual cap of 1.260€ such as the one that limits the deduction for working from home (the annual or daily flat rate, Jahres- bzw. Tagespauschale, §4 Abs. 5 Nr. 6b/6c EStG). If you are a small business (Kleinunternehmer; §19 UStG), the gross amount is recognized in full. If you are a trader on the standard regime (Regelunternehmer), the VAT (USt; 19%) goes into the input VAT deduction (Vorsteuerabzug).

items: A coworking subscription — rental costs (Mietkosten), the field 'Raumkosten und Nebenkosten' in the Anlage EÜR
Input VAT (Vorsteuer) of 19% is reclaimed through the advance VAT return (USt-Voranmeldung)
A day pass while working in another city — travel costs (Reisekosten; the field 'Übrige beschränkt abziehbare Betriebsausgaben')
A business address (Geschäftsadresse) via coworking — can be used in the legal notice (Impressum; §5 TMG) and on invoices (Rechnungen)

content.text: A virtual office (just an address with no workspace) is not always accepted for a VAT identification number (USt-Identifikationsnummer). The Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern, BZSt) may refuse to issue a USt-IdNr if the address is a PO box.

If the coworking space is your only 'office', then at residence registration (Wohnsitzanmeldung; Anmeldung) and trade registration (Gewerbe) the activity address does not match the residence address. The tax authority assigns the case by place of residence (Wohnsitz), but the trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) goes by the office address. This is normal, but it's important not to mix them up.
Most coworking spaces require a credit-bureau report (SCHUFA-Auskunft) or an advance payment (Vorauszahlung) when you sign a contract for a private office. For a hot desk a card is usually enough.
A day pass via Coworker.com or another platform is a café service, not a rental. The input VAT (Vorsteuer) is still reclaimable, but check the invoice (Rechnung) for a VAT statement (USt-Ausweis).

title: Business plan for the §21 visa
tldr: §21 AufenthG (Aufenthaltserlaubnis zur selbständigen Tätigkeit) requires a Businessplan + Finanzplan, which are assessed by the IHK or HWK (for the skilled crafts). Criteria: wirtschaftliches Interesse or regionales Bedürfnis, secured financing, a positive effect on the economy. The visa is issued for 3 years, then comes a Niederlassungserlaubnis. For Freiberufler the requirements are more lenient.

content.text: §21 of the Residence Act (Aufenthaltsgesetz) is a residence permit for self-employment (a temporary residence permit for pursuing a self-employed activity, Aufenthaltserlaubnis zur Ausübung einer selbständigen Tätigkeit). It splits into two subtypes: §21 Abs. 1 — for traders (Gewerbetreibende); §21 Abs. 5 — for members of the liberal professions (Freiberufler). Citizens of the EU/EEA/Switzerland need no visa — freedom of movement (Freizügigkeit) applies.

Under §21 Abs. 1 the applicant must show that the business meets an economic interest (wirtschaftliches Interesse) or a regional need (regionales Bedürfnis), has a positive effect on the economy, and has secured financing. The decision is made by the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) on the basis of an opinion from the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) or the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (HWK).

items: §21 Abs. 1 — for founders / entrepreneurs (Gründer / Unternehmer; a trade Gewerbe)
§21 Abs. 5 — for the liberal professions (freie Berufe; more lenient criteria)
Visa term — up to 3 years, then an extension or a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis)
A permanent residence permit under §21 Abs. 4 — after 3 years, on successful execution of the plan and secured means
Visa fee — 100€, extension — 96€, Niederlassungserlaubnis — 113-147€

content.text: A business plan (Businessplan) for the §21 visa must be in German, usually 20-40 pages plus financial appendices. There is a template in the BMWK Existenzgründer-Portal (existenzgruender.de). The main thing is that the Chambers of Industry/Commerce and Skilled Crafts (IHK/HWK) assess how realistic it is, not its literary qualities.

items: The business idea (Geschäftsidee) in 5 sentences
Target audience (Zielgruppe) and market niche (Marktnische)
Founder (Gründer): qualifications and experience
Capital requirement (Kapitalbedarf) and financing (Finanzierung)
Turnover and profit (Gewinn) forecast for 3 years

content.text: CV, education with translations of diplomas (and, if needed, qualification recognition Anerkennung via Anabin/ZAB), professional experience, the reason for moving to Germany, and language certificates (B2 is recommended for commercial activity).

items: Size and development of the market (Größe und Entwicklung des Marktes; sources: Statista, IfM Bonn, IHK statistics)
Analysis of competitors in the region
Target audience (Zielgruppe): B2B, B2C, a customer profile
Pricing strategy (Pricing-Strategie) with justification
Marketing-Plan: Online (SEO, Social), Offline (Events, Networking)
Capital-requirement plan (Kapitalbedarfsplan): what you need to buy and what to invest in
Financing plan (Finanzierungsplan): own funds (eigene Mittel) + bank loan (Bankkredit) + subsidies (Förderung)
Profitability planning (Rentabilitätsplanung) for 3 years: turnover, expenses, and profit month by month
Liquidity plan (Liquiditätsplan): incoming and outgoing cash flows
The founder's living costs (Lebenshaltungskosten; a minimum of 1.500-2.000€/month for a family is usually required)
Proof of secured means of subsistence (Sicherung des Lebensunterhalts; §5 AufenthG): an account with a buffer of at least 12-24 months

steps.title: The process via the IHK / Ausländerbehörde

content.text: The visa application is filed at the German embassy (Botschaft) abroad (if you are not in the country) or at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) at your place of residence (if you are already in Germany with a different status — for example, as a student). The foreigners' authority sends the business plan to the Chamber of Industry and Commerce or the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (IHK or HWK) for an opinion (Stellungnahme).

items: 1. Prepare the business plan in German + translations of diplomas
2. File the application at the embassy (Botschaft; a national visa D-Visum) or the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde; a temporary residence permit Aufenthaltserlaubnis)
3. The authority forwards the plan to the Cologne Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK Köln; or your local IHK) / the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (HWK)
4. The chamber issues an opinion (Stellungnahme) within 4-8 weeks (positive or negative)
5. The foreigners' authority makes a decision (usually following the chamber's assessment)
6. On a positive decision — a visa/temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) for 3 years

content.text: §21 Abs. 5 AufenthG for the liberal professions (freie Berufe; §18 EStG) — doctors, artists, IT consultants by analogy — is simplified: no proof of an economic interest is required; secured subsistence and the actual ability to practise the profession are enough.

items: No approval from the Chamber of Industry and Commerce is needed (but for the medical professions, Heilberufe, the Chamber of Skilled Crafts — yes)
You need diplomas / licences (a licence to practise medicine Approbation for doctors, an admission Zulassung for lawyers)
A simple concept (Konzept) of the activity is enough (not a full business plan)
You must have clients (Auftraggeber) or preliminary contracts (Vorverträge) worth enough to cover your living costs
Language requirements depend on the profession: for doctors — C1 (a professional-language exam, Fachsprachenprüfung), for IT — usually B1-B2

content.text: The chamber often refuses if the financial plan (Finanzplan) is unrealistic (for example, promising a turnover of 200.000€ in the first year without written contracts). It's better to show a conservative forecast with reserves.

§21 is a visa for active business. Simply 'investing' in a German business without operational management does not qualify — §21 Abs. 1 covers that in rare cases, but a real operational role is usually needed.

If you are over 45, the foreigners' authority may require proof of pension provision (Altersvorsorge): voluntary contributions to the German pension fund (DRV), a private pension, or proof of assets of 200.000€+. This is a formal requirement of §21 Abs. 3.

A permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) after 3 years is not automatic. You have to show: the business is running, the profit covers your living costs, there are no debts to the tax office (Finanzamt), German at B1, and 60 months of contributions to the pension system (the German pension fund DRV or a private one).

A business plan in English only is often the reason the chamber refuses. A translation into German is mandatory (the BMWK explicitly requires German as the language of business, Geschäftssprache Deutsch).

title: Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung
tldr: The Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung is a mandatory electronic questionnaire via ELSTER for all new Freiberufler and Gewerbetreibende in Germany. Since 2021 the paper form has been abolished. Based on the answers, the Finanzamt assigns a Steuernummer, estimates Vorauszahlungen, and decides on the Kleinunternehmer-Regelung (§19 UStG). It is filed within 1 month of starting the activity (§138 AO).

content.text: The Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung (tax-registration questionnaire) is the initial questionnaire about a new activity (under §138 of the Fiscal Code, Abgabenordnung) that every member of a liberal profession (Freiberufler) or trader (Gewerbetreibender) fills in when starting work in Germany. Since 1 January 2021 it must be submitted EXCLUSIVELY electronically via the ELSTER tax portal — the tax office (Finanzamt) no longer accepts paper forms.

Based on the answers, the tax office: 1) assigns a tax number (Steuernummer; for invoices with VAT, USt-Rechnungen); 2) determines whether you are liable for VAT (USt) or fall under the small-business special regime (Kleinunternehmer-Regelung) §19 UStG; 3) estimates advance income-tax payments (Einkommensteuer-Vorauszahlungen) for the current year; 4) for commercial activity (Gewerbe), opens a trade-tax (Gewerbesteuer) file.

items: Mandatory via the ELSTER tax portal (mein.elster.de)
Deadline: within 1 month of starting the activity (§138 Abs. 1 AO)
For members of the liberal professions — it replaces the trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung)
For commercial activity — filed AFTER the trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung); the details are forwarded automatically (via the single point of contact, 'Einheitlicher Ansprechpartner')
Free

content.text: The questionnaire runs to 8 pages on the ELSTER tax portal. Filling it in takes 30-60 minutes if your answers are thought through in advance. Mistakes can be corrected later via a correction ('Korrektur') or through a tax adviser (Steuerberater).

items: Name, address, date of birth, tax identification number (Steuer-ID, Identifikationsnummer)
Marital status, denomination (Konfession; for church tax Kirchensteuer)
Bank details (Bankverbindung) for refunds and debits

items.title: 2. Details of the activity (Angaben zur Tätigkeit)

items: An exact description of the activity ('Software-Entwicklung als IT-Berater')
Start date of the activity (Aufnahme der Tätigkeit)
Activity address (may match the place of residence, Wohnsitz)
Liberal profession or trade (freiberuflich oder gewerblich) — a critically important item; it affects the trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) and bookkeeping
If it is a trade — the number from the trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung)
Expected revenue (turnover, Umsatz) in the year of founding and the next year
Expected profit (Gewinn)
On this basis the tax office sets advance income-tax payments (Vorauszahlungen Einkommensteuer; quarterly)
A realistic but not inflated forecast: overstate it and you'll be paying income tax (ESt) on credit
Small business (Kleinunternehmer; §19 UStG): turnover ≤ 25.000€ last year and ≤ 100.000€ in the current year — the threshold updated as of 2025
Waiving the small-business special regime (Verzicht auf Kleinunternehmer-Regelung) obliges you to pay VAT (USt) for at least 5 years, but gives you the input VAT deduction (Vorsteuerabzug)
Taxation on receipt or on invoice (Ist- oder Soll-Versteuerung): on receipt (Ist; turnover ≤ 800.000€) — VAT by the date of receipt; on invoice (Soll) — by the date of the invoice
A request for a VAT identification number (USt-Identifikationsnummer, USt-IdNr) for working with the EU — a separate checkbox
Profit-calculation method (Gewinnermittlungsart): simplified accounting (EÜR; §4 Abs. 3 EStG) or a balance sheet (Bilanz; §4 Abs. 1 / §5 EStG)
Financial year (Wirtschaftsjahr) = calendar year
Indicate whether you have a tax adviser (Steuerberater; if so, attach a power of attorney Vollmacht)

content.text: The tax office processes the questionnaire in 2-6 weeks. Afterwards a letter arrives with the tax number (Steuernummer; 12-13 digits) and the decision on the VAT regime (USt-Regelung). The tax number must be stated on every invoice (§14 Abs. 4 UStG). In parallel comes a decision on advance payments (Bescheid über Vorauszahlungen) for income tax (ESt) and, for commercial activity, trade tax (GewSt).

items: The tax number arrives by post in 2-6 weeks
You can only start issuing invoices (Rechnungen) after receiving the tax number (or state 'Steuernummer beantragt' — tax number applied for)
The VAT identification number (USt-IdNr; DE...) arrives separately from the Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern, BZSt)
Advance income-tax payments (ESt) — 4 times a year: 10.03, 10.06, 10.09, 10.12
Advance trade-tax payments (GewSt) — 15.02, 15.05, 15.08, 15.11

content.text: If you are an IT consultant and tick 'Gewerbebetrieb' (commercial business) out of ignorance, the tax office will open a trade-tax file (Gewerbesteuer-Akte) and send you advance payments for it (Vorauszahlungen GewSt). A correction is possible, but painful. First check whether you fall under §18 EStG (a member of a liberal profession, Freiberufler).

The turnover (Umsatz) forecast needs to be realistic. Overstate it, and the tax office will set huge advance payments (Vorauszahlungen), with the money leaving your account before the real income comes in. Understate it, and after the first tax return (Steuererklärung) a large back payment (Nachzahlung) arrives.

The small-business special regime (Kleinunternehmer-Regelung; §19 UStG) is advantageous for a B2C business (private-individual clients), but NOT for B2B (clients that are other companies), because without VAT (USt) you cannot reclaim the input VAT (Vorsteuer) on equipment and services. As of 2025 the threshold is 25.000€ for the previous year and 100.000€ for the current one.
Waiving small-business status (Verzicht auf Kleinunternehmerschaft; waiving §19) binds you for 5 years. You cannot change your mind in the 2nd year.

If the activity started more than 30 days ago without a tax-registration questionnaire (Fragebogen), that is a breach of §138 AO. The fine is up to 25.000€ (in theory). In practice the tax office usually requires a back payment from the date of the actual start.

title: Liberal profession (Freiberufler) vs trade (Gewerbe): the difference
tldr: Freiberufler (§18 EStG) — members of the 'liberal professions' (Katalogberufe and similar): doctors, lawyers, engineers, IT consultants, artists. They don't pay Gewerbesteuer, don't need a Gewerbeanmeldung, and can always keep an EÜR. Gewerbe (§15 EStG) — everything else: trade, manufacturing, the skilled crafts. They pay Gewerbesteuer on profit above 24.500€ (Freibetrag §11 GewStG) and need a Gewerbeanmeldung for 20-65€.

content.text: The German tax code splits self-employment into two types: income from self-employed work (Einkünfte aus selbständiger Arbeit; §18 EStG, members of the liberal professions 'Freiberufler') and income from a trade (Einkünfte aus Gewerbebetrieb; §15 EStG, traders 'Gewerbetreibende'). This determines whether you need to register at the trade office (Gewerbeamt), whether trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) is paid, whether membership in the Chamber of Industry and Commerce or the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (IHK/HWK) is mandatory, and which bookkeeping format applies.

items: Member of a liberal profession: §18 EStG, no trade tax, no trade registration
Trade: §15 EStG, trade tax on profit above the 24.500€ tax-free allowance (Freibetrag), mandatory trade registration
A member of a liberal profession does not automatically join the Chamber of Industry and Commerce, whereas a trader (Gewerbetreibender) is required to
The obligation to keep a balance sheet (Bilanz-Pflicht) never arises for members of the liberal professions (always simplified accounting EÜR)
The status is decided by the tax office (Finanzamt) based on the tax-registration questionnaire (Fragebogen) and the nature of the activity

steps.title: Who is a Freiberufler under §18 EStG

content.text: §18 EStG distinguishes three groups: catalogue professions (Katalogberufe; listed in the law), similar professions ('ähnliche Berufe'; close in substance), and scientific, artistic, literary, teaching, and educational ('wissenschaftliche, künstlerische, schriftstellerische, unterrichtende, erzieherische') activity.

items.title: 1. Catalogue professions (Katalogberufe; explicitly listed in §18 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 EStG)

items: Medical professions (Heilberufe): doctors (Ärzte), dentists (Zahnärzte), vets (Tierärzte), alternative practitioners (Heilpraktiker), physiotherapists (Krankengymnasten), midwives (Hebammen)
Legal advice (Rechtsberatung): lawyers (Rechtsanwälte), notaries (Notare), patent attorneys (Patentanwälte)
Economic advice (Wirtschaftsberatung): tax advisers (Steuerberater), auditors (Wirtschaftsprüfer), sworn auditors (vereidigte Buchprüfer)
Technical professions (technische Berufe): architects (Architekten), engineers (Ingenieure), surveying engineers (Vermessungsingenieure), pilots (Lotsen)
Auxiliary medical professions (Heilhilfsberufe): nurses (Krankenpfleger), masseurs (Masseure)
Language intermediaries (Sprachmittler): interpreters (Dolmetscher), translators (Übersetzer; sworn)
Consulting economists (beratende Volks- und Betriebswirte)
Maler, Bildhauer, Musiker, Schauspieler, Sänger
Journalisten, Schriftsteller, Lektoren, Verleger
Wissenschaftler, Lehrer, Erzieher, Coaches (if there is a substantive teaching process)
Photographers (Fotografen) — only if the work is creative (not reportage or catalogue)

items.title: 3. Similar professions (Ähnliche Berufe; per case law)

items: IT consultants — often recognized as similar to an engineer (Ingenieur-ähnlich) if there is relevant higher education (a university degree in computer science, FH-Studium Informatik) or equivalent self-study
Web developers (Web-Entwickler) — a contested category; the Federal Fiscal Court (Bundesfinanzhof, BFH) requires proof of deep engineering knowledge (ingenieurmäßige Kenntnisse)
Data scientists and ML engineers — usually Freiberufler if they hold a relevant degree
UX designers without an artistic education — usually a trade (Gewerbe)

steps.title: Who is a Gewerbe under §15 EStG

content.text: A trade (Gewerbe) is anything that is NOT a liberal profession and NOT agriculture or forestry (Land- und Forstwirtschaft; §13 EStG). The hallmarks of a commercial business (Gewerbebetrieb) under §15 Abs. 2 EStG: independence, sustainability (Nachhaltigkeit), participation in general economic activity, and a profit-seeking intent.

items: Retail and wholesale trade (Einzelhandel and Großhandel; shops, online trade)
The skilled crafts (Handwerk; requires entry in the register of craftsmen, Eintragung in die Handwerksrolle, plus a master craftsman's certificate Meisterbrief for regulated professions)
Hospitality (Gastronomie; restaurants, cafés)
Online services: marketplaces, SaaS resale
Webshops via Shopify, eBay, Amazon
Affiliate marketing, dropshipping
Beauty, fitness, coaching (Beauty, Fitness, Coaching; without a therapeutic education)
Brokerage (Vermittlung; brokers Makler, agents Agenten)

content.text: The main financial difference is the trade tax (Gewerbesteuer, GewSt). For a trade it amounts to 7-17% of profit (the municipal rate Hebesatz depends on the municipality Gemeinde: Berlin 410%, Munich 490%, Frankfurt 460%). The tax-free allowance (Freibetrag) for a sole trader (Einzelunternehmer) is 24.500€/year (§11 Abs. 1 GewStG).

items: Trade tax = (profit - 24.500€) × 3,5% × Hebesatz/100
Example: profit 60.000€, Berlin (410%): (60.000-24.500) × 3,5% × 4,1 = 5.094€ of trade tax (GewSt)
Trade tax is partially credited against income tax (Einkommensteuer; §35 EStG): up to 4× the base tax amount (Steuermessbetrag)
At a municipal rate (Hebesatz) ≤ 380% the trade tax is fully neutralized; at higher rates — only partially
Member of a liberal profession: 0€ of trade tax always
Additional costs of a trade: the Chamber of Industry and Commerce contribution (IHK-Beitrag; ~50-300€/year) and the trade registration (Gewerbeanmeldung; 20-65€ one-off)

content.text: Mixed activity (gemischte Tätigkeit; for example, an IT consultant who also resells licences) — the tax office may apply the 'tainting' theory (Abfärbetheorie; §15 Abs. 3 Nr. 1 EStG): if the trade (Gewerbe) share is > 3% and > 24.500€, your ENTIRE activity becomes a trade. The fix: split it via two civil-law partnerships (GbR) or a separate sole proprietorship (Einzelunternehmen) for the trading part.

An IT consultant without a degree in computer science (Informatik) — the tax office often reclassifies this as a trade (Gewerbe). The defence: a self-documented case for the engineering nature of the activity (ingenieurmäßige Tätigkeit; projects, training, certificates). In a dispute — a court claim (Klage) at the fiscal court (Finanzgericht); the average duration is 1-2 years.

Switching from a liberal profession to a trade (Freiberufler → Gewerbe) retroactively is a nightmare: the tax office recalculates trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) 4 years back with interest of 6% per year. It's better to clarify your status when filing the tax-registration questionnaire (Fragebogen).

Medical professions (Heilberufe) without a licence to practise medicine (Approbation) or an alternative-practitioner permit Heilpraktiker-Erlaubnis (for example, a pure wellness masseur or a nutritionist) — a trade (Gewerbe), not a liberal profession. A massage-school certificate is not enough.

Artists (Künstler) — members of a liberal profession only if the activity is original ('eigenschöpferische'). A wedding photographer working from templates is a trade (Gewerbe); a photographic artist with an original style is a member of a liberal profession. The line is fine.

title: List of the liberal professions (freie Berufe, §18 EStG)
tldr: The liberal professions (freie Berufe) under §18 EStG fall into three groups: catalogue professions (Katalogberufe — an explicit list: doctors, lawyers, engineers, architects, tax advisers (Steuerberater)), artistic and academic professions (künstlerisch/wissenschaftliche Berufe — artists, journalists, academics) and similar professions (ähnliche Berufe — IT consultants with a relevant degree). Your status is determined by the tax office (Finanzamt) when you submit the questionnaire (Fragebogen); disputed cases are decided by the tax court (Finanzgericht).

steps.title: What the liberal professions (freie Berufe) are

content.text: The liberal professions (freie Berufe) are a category of activity under §18 EStG (income from self-employed work, Einkünfte aus selbständiger Arbeit). They get tax benefits: exemption from trade tax (Gewerbesteuer), no business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung), and the simplified cash-basis accounting (EÜR) is always available regardless of turnover. The law splits them into three sub-categories, listed in §18 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 EStG.

items: Catalogue professions (Katalogberufe) — explicitly listed in the EStG
Activity-based professions (Tätigkeitsberufe) — academic, artistic, literary, teaching, educational
Similar professions (ähnliche Berufe) — by analogy with the catalogue ones (case law matters here)
Specialised education or a recognised qualification is usually required
If the activity fits none of these categories, it is a trade (Gewerbe, §15 EStG)

content.text: Under §18 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 EStG, the following count as catalogue professions. The list is closed — case law does not extend it (but the similar professions, ähnliche Berufe, sit right alongside it).

items: Doctors (Ärzte; a licence, Approbation, is required)
Dentists (Zahnärzte; Approbation)
Veterinarians (Tierärzte; Approbation)
Naturopaths (Heilpraktiker; a Heilpraktiker-Erlaubnis permit under HeilprG)

Dental practitioners (Dentisten), remedial gymnasts/physiotherapists (Krankengymnasten/Physiotherapeuten), midwives (Hebammen), medical masseurs (Heilmasseure), qualified psychologists (Diplom-Psychologen)
Medical professions require relevant training plus admission to the profession (Berufszulassung)

items.title: 2. Legal and economic advisory (Rechts- und Wirtschaftsberatung)

items: Lawyers (Rechtsanwälte; a fully qualified lawyer, Volljurist, plus admission by the bar association, Rechtsanwaltskammer)
Notaries (Notare; appointment, Bestellung, by the state government, Landesregierung)
Patent attorneys (Patentanwälte)
Auditors (Wirtschaftsprüfer; the WP-Examen exam)
Tax advisers (Steuerberater; the StB-Examen exam)
Sworn auditors (Vereidigte Buchprüfer)
Consulting economists (Beratende Volks- und Betriebswirte; with a VWL/BWL degree plus at least 3 years of practice)
Engineers (Ingenieure; an FH/Uni degree in engineering)
Architects (Architekten; entry in the chamber of architects, Architektenkammer)
Surveying engineers (Vermessungsingenieure)
Pilots/maritime pilots (Lotsen)
Commercial chemists (Handelschemiker)

items.title: 4. Language and academic professions (Sprach- und Wissenschaftsberufe)

items: Sworn interpreters and translators (vereidigte Dolmetscher und Übersetzer; or those with a relevant degree)
Academics (Wissenschaftler; research activity with publications)
Teachers (Lehrer) and educators (Erzieher; with a teaching qualification)
Journalists (Journalisten), photojournalists (Bildberichterstatter), writers (Schriftsteller)

steps.title: Similar professions (ähnliche Berufe) — the grey zones

content.text: The Federal Fiscal Court (Bundesfinanzhof, BFH) expanded §18 EStG through the concept of a 'similar profession' (ähnlicher Beruf) — a profession similar to a catalogue one in the nature of the activity, the education and the responsibility involved. The main grey zone is IT and digital.

items: IT consultant / software architect: recognised as engineer-like (Ingenieur-ähnlich) with an FH/Uni degree in computer science, or with a 'self-taught level' (autodidaktisches Niveau) equal to a degree (which you must prove!)
Software developer (Software-Entwickler): with a computer-science degree — a member of a liberal profession (Freiberufler); without one — usually a trade (Gewerbe)
Data scientist, ML engineer: with a degree in computer science / mathematics / statistics — a liberal profession
DevOps / SRE / cloud engineer: the position is disputed, but the BFH leans towards a liberal profession where the architectural work is complex
Web designer / frontend developer: more often a trade, except in purely creative cases

A nurse (Krankenpfleger) in an outpatient care service (ambulanter Pflegedienst) may be a liberal profession (per BFH case law); a salaried carer (Pfleger) in a care home (Heim) is an employee (Arbeitnehmer)
Coaches without therapeutic training — usually a trade
A psychotherapy naturopath (Heilpraktiker für Psychotherapie) — a liberal profession (only a special permit, Erlaubnis, is needed)

content.text: As long as the tax office (Finanzamt) doesn't challenge it, your status stands. If in doubt, it will request evidence — especially from IT consultants without a formal degree.

items: An FH / Uni degree — the strongest evidence
Relevant certifications: AWS Solutions Architect, Microsoft Certified, Cisco, SAP — they support your case but don't replace a degree
Project descriptions emphasising engineering work (ingenieurmäßige Tätigkeit; analysis, design, not just coding)
Records of hours worked (Stundennachweise) broken down into analysis, design and implementation

In a dispute — an application for a binding ruling from the tax office (Antrag auf verbindliche Auskunft; costs ~250-500€ at the Finanzamt) or an expert opinion (Gutachten) from a specialist (Sachverständiger)
A lawsuit (Klage) at the tax court (Finanzgericht): 1-2 years, with a court fee based on the amount in dispute

content.text: Certifications instead of a degree don't always work. Under settled BFH case law (see Urteile vom 22.09.2009, VIII R 79/06 and VIII R 63/06) a self-taught person (Autodidakt) can be recognised as engineer-like only if they prove 'theoretische Kenntnisse in Breite und Tiefe, die der eines Diplom-Informatikers entsprechen' — that is, depth, not just breadth. You have to prove this, and disputed cases are best discussed with a tax adviser (Steuerberater).

If the Finanzamt already recognised you as a member of a liberal profession in the first year and then changes its mind, that is a new decision (Bescheidung) — you can file an objection (Einspruch; 1 month) and a lawsuit (Klage).

For a writer (Schriftsteller) or journalist (Journalist), status does not depend on print runs or fees. A blogger with a single subscriber and good writing is a member of a liberal profession. But the content must be literary (schriftstellerisch), not just reposting / aggregating.

Artistic professions (Künstler) can get the benefits of the Artists' Social Insurance Fund (Künstlersozialkasse, KSK): additional social insurance on favourable terms. The KSK is a separate procedure — don't confuse it with recognition of liberal-professional status.

Degrees from the CIS, Turkey or India need recognition of the qualification (Anerkennung) via the anabin database on the recognition of foreign degrees (ZAB — the Central Office for Foreign Education). Without it the Finanzamt won't count your education as 'gleichwertig'.
