title: GbR: the simple civil-law partnership
tldr: The GbR (civil-law partnership, Gesellschaft bürgerlichen Rechts, §705 ff BGB) is the simplest form for joint activity by 2+ people, with no minimum capital. The partners are fully liable with their personal assets. Since 2024, the MoPeG reform (modernisation of partnership law) introduced the 'eGbR' — a voluntary entry in the partnership register (Gesellschaftsregister; ~120-300€). Taxes: each partner is taxed individually on their share of the profit.

content.text: The GbR (civil-law partnership, Gesellschaft bürgerlichen Rechts) is the simplest form of joint business in Germany: §705-740 BGB. It arises automatically as soon as two or more people agree on a joint activity with a common purpose (including a business). You don't need: minimum capital, a notarised contract, an entry in the commercial register (Handelsregister), or a company seal.

Since 1 January 2024 the MoPeG (the act modernising partnership law, Gesetz zur Modernisierung des Personengesellschaftsrechts) has been in force — the biggest reform of partnership law in 100 years. It introduced the 'registered GbR' (eingetragene GbR, eGbR) — a voluntary entry in the new partnership register (Gesellschaftsregister) that gives legal capacity for transactions involving real estate, GmbH shares and the like.

items: At least 2 partners (Gesellschafter): individuals or legal entities
No minimum capital — in theory even 0€
A verbal or written agreement — written is recommended
Full personal liability (joint and several, gesamtschuldnerisch, §721 BGB)
Since 2024: the eGbR — an optional entry in the partnership register
Good for a shared office, a project, or a trial-run startup

steps.title: How to set up a GbR

content.text: Setting up a GbR involves minimal formalities. However, the tax and registration paperwork depends on the type of activity (liberal profession, Freiberufler, vs trade, Gewerbe).

items: The purpose of the partnership (Gesellschaftszweck) — describe it precisely
The shares (Beteiligungsverhältnis) — e.g. 50:50
Distribution of profits and losses (Gewinnverteilung)
Management (Geschäftsführung) — who makes decisions
Exit terms (Kündigung) and inheritance
No notary needed — a simple written form is enough
Templates on existenzgruender.de or from the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK)

If all partners are members of a liberal profession: a questionnaire (Fragebogen) on the tax portal ELSTER for the GbR itself, plus a tax-registration form (Anlage zur steuerlichen Erfassung) from each partner
If it's a trade (Gewerbe): a business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) for EACH partner at the trade office (Gewerbeamt; 20-65€ × N people)
A tax number (Steuernummer) for the GbR from the tax office (Finanzamt) — a separate number
A VAT identification number (USt-IdNr) — applied for through the Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt) for the GbR itself
Entry in the partnership register (Gesellschaftsregister) via a notary
Cost: ~120-300€ for the entry plus notary fees
Mandatory for GbRs that own real estate or GmbH shares (per practice since 2024)
After registration the name carries the suffix 'eGbR'
If the eGbR exceeds the turnover/size thresholds, it automatically becomes a general partnership (OHG)

content.text: A GbR without a register entry is awkward for many banks. Ones that open accounts: Postbank, Sparkasse (with a partnership agreement, Gesellschaftsvertrag), Holvi, Qonto, Penta for the startup segment. With an extract from the partnership register (Gesellschaftsregister), banks accept an eGbR like an ordinary legal entity.

steps.title: The tax treatment of a GbR

content.text: A GbR is a co-entrepreneurship (Mitunternehmerschaft, §15 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 EStG): the GbR itself pays no income tax (Einkommensteuer). The profit is split by shares and taxed at each partner as their personal income. This is 'transparent taxation' — the main reason to choose a GbR over a GmbH.

items: The GbR files a declaration for the separate and uniform determination of income (Erklärung zur gesonderten und einheitlichen Feststellung; via ELSTER)
Each partner carries their share of the profit into their personal income-tax return (ESt-Erklärung; the Anlage S or Anlage G appendix)
VAT (Umsatzsteuer) — the GbR pays it as a single entity (unless it is a small business, Kleinunternehmer §19 UStG, threshold 25.000€ since 2025)
Trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) — only if the GbR runs a trade; the tax-free allowance (Freibetrag) is 24.500€ per GbR (not per partner!)
If even one partner runs a trade, the whole GbR becomes a trade (the 'contagion' theory, Abfärbetheorie, §15 Abs. 3 EStG)

content.text: The main drawback of a GbR is the unlimited personal liability of all partners. Under §721 BGB (the new version since 2024) the partners are jointly and severally liable (gesamtschuldnerisch) — each with their personal assets for the entire debt of the GbR.

items: A creditor can demand the full amount from any partner
The internal settlement between partners is a separate matter
An incoming partner is also liable for the GbR's old debts — §721a BGB (n.F. since 2024)
Leaving doesn't release you from debts that arose BEFORE you left: residual liability (Nachhaftung) for up to 5 years (§728b BGB n.F.)
Protection: business liability insurance (Betriebshaftpflichtversicherung; 200-1.000€/year for a small GbR), professional indemnity insurance (Vermögensschadenhaftpflicht) for consultants

content.text: The 'contagion' theory (Abfärbetheorie, §15 Abs. 3 Nr. 1 EStG): if in a GbR of 3 doctors even one starts selling food supplements (a trade, Gewerbe), the whole GbR becomes a trade and pays trade tax (Gewerbesteuer). The solution is separation (Trennung) via two GbRs.

Without a written partnership agreement (Gesellschaftsvertrag), the default rules of the BGB apply: after the MoPeG reform, profits and losses are distributed by participation shares, and where there is no agreement on the value of contributions — equally, per head (§709 Abs. 3 BGB n.F.); decisions are taken unanimously. In a dispute this is a source of conflict — always put the terms in writing.

Since 2024, for GbRs that own real estate, an entry in the partnership register (eGbR) is effectively mandatory — without it the land registry (Grundbuchamt) won't register transactions. If your GbR owns property, switching to an eGbR is compulsory.
A GbR cannot issue shares or attract VC investment in the classic sense. For serious scaling — a UG/GmbH. The GbR is for getting started and for freelance teams.

Bogus self-employment (Scheinselbständigkeit): if a 2-person GbR serves one client 80%+ of the time, the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, DRV) may treat it as disguised employment, with social contributions (Sozialabgaben) back-charged for 4 years. Diversify your clients.

title: Registering a business (Gewerbeanmeldung)
tldr: Any commercial activity (a trade, Gewerbe) in Germany must be registered at the trade office (Gewerbeamt; often part of the public-order office, Ordnungsamt) BEFORE you start work. You submit the GewA1 form, pay 20–65 € and receive your trade licence (Gewerbeschein). Bring your national ID card (Personalausweis) or passport and a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) that ALLOWS self-employment (Selbständigkeit) — this is critical for non-EU citizens. Registration automatically triggers three things: notification of the tax office (Finanzamt; a tax-registration questionnaire, Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung, will arrive), compulsory membership in the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) or the Chamber of Crafts (HWK), and — if you hire staff — a company number (Betriebsnummer). Note: the liberal professions (freie Berufe — doctors, lawyers, IT freelancers, journalists, translators) do NOT register a trade; they go straight to the Finanzamt.

steps.title: Trade (Gewerbe) or liberal profession — do you need a Gewerbeanmeldung

content.text: Before you go and register, work out the type of activity. A trade (Gewerbe) is a commercial activity: retail, crafts, catering, an online shop, brokering, any service run 'as a business'. That is exactly what is subject to business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) under §14 GewO. The liberal professions (freie Berufe) under §18 EStG do NOT go through trade registration — they report the start of their activity directly to the tax office (Finanzamt).

items: Trade (registration required): retail, e-commerce, a restaurant, repairs, a broker, an agency, dropshipping
Liberal professions (NO trade registration): doctor, lawyer, tax adviser, architect, journalist, translator
Grey zone: IT and development — often a liberal profession, but the Finanzamt decides case by case
When in doubt? Your status is determined by the Finanzamt, not by you — better to clarify in advance
A classification error = back-payments of trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) or a fine for an unregistered trade

content.text: Don't try to 'declare' yourself a freelancer to avoid trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) and IHK membership. The final say belongs to the Finanzamt: if it reclassifies your activity as a trade retroactively, you'll have to pay back the trade tax for all the past years. The line between a liberal profession (freiberuflich) and a commercial activity (gewerblich), especially in IT and consulting, is a frequent subject of dispute.

steps.title: The key point for non-EU citizens: does your residence permit allow self-employment (Selbständigkeit)

content.text: This is the crucial and most underestimated point. EU/EEA citizens register a trade freely. But for third-country nationals, the residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) must explicitly allow self-employed activity. Without the right endorsement, the trade office (Gewerbeamt) won't register you, or the registration will be invalid.

items: Check the text on your residence permit: 'Selbständige Tätigkeit gestattet' (self-employed activity permitted) or 'Erwerbstätigkeit gestattet' (gainful activity permitted)
If it says 'Selbständige Tätigkeit nicht gestattet' (self-employed activity not permitted) — first go to the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde)
A settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis, permanent residence) and the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) usually allow self-employment
Student permits §16b and many work permits §18 do NOT allow a trade without separate consent
Changing the purpose of stay to self-employment goes through §21 AufenthG

content.text: Starting a trade without the permission on your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) is a serious breach of immigration law that can cost you the extension of your permit. First obtain permission from the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde), if necessary by changing the purpose under §21 AufenthG, and only then go to the Gewerbeamt.

steps.title: Submitting the GewA1 form: the process and documents

content.text: Registration is done at the trade office (Gewerbeamt) for the place where your business operates. In many cities this is online via a service portal, or in person with an appointment (Termin). You fill in the GewA1 (Gewerbe-Anmeldung), pay the fee and immediately receive your trade licence (Gewerbeschein) — confirmation of registration.

items: A national ID card (Personalausweis; for EU citizens) or a passport
A residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) with permission for self-employment (Selbständigkeit; for third countries)
The completed GewA1 form
For regulated crafts — a craft card (Handwerkskarte) / entry in the register of craftsmen (Handwerksrolle)
For certain activities (catering, security, brokering) — special permits (Erlaubnis)
Describe the activity (Tätigkeit) precisely — the classification depends on it
State the start date (Beginn der Tätigkeit) — not backdated
Main or secondary business (Haupt- / Nebenerwerb)
The business address (Betriebsstätte)
Signature — and pay the fee on the spot by card/cash

content.text: The trade licence (Gewerbeschein) is issued on the spot. It's not yet a 'licence for everything' — regulated sectors (restaurants, transport, financial brokering §34c/§34f GewO) require additional permits that you must obtain BEFORE you start.
The trade office (Gewerbeamt) itself forwards the data to several authorities. You don't file separate applications — but you should be ready for incoming letters and obligations.

items: The tax office (Finanzamt) will send a 'tax-registration questionnaire' (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung; now submitted via the tax portal ELSTER)
From the questionnaire you'll get a tax number (Steuernummer) and settle the §19 UStG question (small business, Kleinunternehmer)
Automatic membership in the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK; trade/services) or the Chamber of Crafts (HWK; crafts), with an annual fee
If you hire staff — a company number (Betriebsnummer) from the employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit)
The statutory accident-insurance association (Berufsgenossenschaft) — a separate registration

content.text: IHK/HWK membership is compulsory and paid — this surprises newcomers. For low turnover there are discounts and exemption from the basic fee in the first years, but you'll get the registration and the fee letter regardless. You can't ignore IHK letters: the fee is charged whether or not you reply.

title: GmbH: setting up a limited company
tldr: The GmbH (limited liability company, Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung) is the German equivalent of an LLC. Its main advantage is set out in §13 Abs. 2 GmbHG: only the company's assets are liable for its debts, while the founders' personal assets are protected. The minimum share capital (Stammkapital) is 25 000 € (§5 GmbHG), but at formation it's enough to actually pay in half — 12 500 € (§7 Abs. 2 GmbHG). Formation must go through a notary (§2 GmbHG) and an entry in the commercial register (Handelsregister), section B (Abteilung B). Budget for formation: notary, registration and publication — roughly 600–1000 € on top of the capital itself, and with a standard articles via the model protocol (Musterprotokoll) it's cheaper. After formation the GmbH must keep double-entry bookkeeping (a balance sheet, Bilanz), file accounts and publish them in the federal gazette (Bundesanzeiger). Note for non-EU citizens: you can set up a GmbH, but obtaining the status of managing director (Geschäftsführer) with a salary is a separate question of the residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) and §21 AufenthG.

steps.title: What a GmbH is and who it suits

content.text: A GmbH is an independent legal entity (juristische Person) governed by the GmbHG. The main reason it's set up is to limit liability: under §13 Abs. 2 GmbHG, only the GmbH's own assets are available to creditors for the company's obligations — not the founders' personal accounts and flats. This makes the GmbH the standard for businesses with real risks, employees, investors and large contracts.

items: A GmbH suits: a business with liability risks, hiring, attracting investors, serious B2B contracts
Minimum share capital (Stammkapital) is 25 000 € (§5 GmbHG); pay in at least 12 500 € at formation (§7 GmbHG)
No 12 500 €? Consider the mini-LLC (UG, haftungsbeschränkt) — the 'mini-GmbH' from 1 € under §5a GmbHG
A GmbH looks more solid to banks and partners than a sole proprietorship (Einzelunternehmen) or a civil-law partnership (GbR)
Downside: double-entry bookkeeping, mandatory publication of accounts, higher running costs

content.text: Limited liability does NOT protect the managing director (Geschäftsführer) from personal liability in case of breaches: unpaid taxes and social contributions, delay in filing for insolvency (Insolvenzverschleppung), gross negligence. 'I set up a GmbH, so now I risk nothing' is a dangerous misconception.

steps.title: Share capital and the articles of association

content.text: Share capital (Stammkapital) is not 'frozen' money: once paid into the business account (Geschäftskonto), it can be used for the needs of the business (rent, equipment, salaries). It's working capital, not a deposit. The articles of association (Gesellschaftsvertrag / statute, Satzung) define the name, purpose, partners' shares and the management arrangements.

items: The model protocol (Musterprotokoll) — a simplified template from the annex to the GmbHG: cheaper at the notary
Suitable for simple cases: up to 3 partners, one managing director (Geschäftsführer)
Individual articles are needed for a complex share structure, special rights, vesting
In doubt — take individual articles; redoing them later is more expensive
Open a business account (Geschäftskonto) for the GmbH i.G. (in Gründung — in formation)
Pay in at least 12 500 € (with a single founder, the full amount or proof of it is often required)
Keep the statement — the notary and the commercial register (Handelsregister) will ask for proof of the deposit
A contribution in kind (Sacheinlage) is possible, but it complicates and increases the cost of formation

content.text: Forming a GmbH without a notary is impossible (§2 GmbHG): the notary certifies the articles and the application to the commercial register (Handelsregister). Once the capital is paid in, the notary files the application with the Handelsregister, section B (Abteilung B — for corporations). The GmbH is only considered legally to exist from the moment of the register entry.

items: The notary certifies the articles of association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) and the list of partners (Gesellschafterliste)
After confirmation that the capital is paid in, the notary files the application with the Handelsregister B
The entry in the Handelsregister = the legal birth of the GmbH
Next — a business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) at the trade office (Gewerbeamt) and the tax-registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung) via the tax portal ELSTER
Finally — IHK/HWK membership and, where needed, publication in the federal gazette (Bundesanzeiger)

content.text: During the GmbH i.G. phase (between signing the articles and the register entry) the founders bear extended personal liability (Vorbelastungshaftung). Don't start major transactions or take on obligations until the entry in the Handelsregister is complete.
A GmbH is not 'set it up and forget it'. Ongoing obligations arise that cannot be ignored without consequences for the managing director (Geschäftsführer) personally.

items: Double-entry bookkeeping (doppelte Buchführung) and an annual balance sheet (Bilanz)
Corporation tax (Körperschaftsteuer) ~15% + the solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag), plus trade tax (Gewerbesteuer)
Mandatory publication of the annual accounts (Jahresabschluss) in the federal gazette (Bundesanzeiger; in abbreviated form for small GmbHs)
Timely filing of returns via ELSTER and payment of prepayments
Any changes (address, director, shares) — again through a notary at the Handelsregister

content.text: The tax burden of a GmbH is calculated at two levels: first the profit is taxed at company level (corporation tax Körperschaftsteuer + trade tax Gewerbesteuer), then on payout of dividends — at the founder level. For low turnover this can work out more expensive than a sole proprietorship (Einzelunternehmen). Run the numbers with a tax adviser (Steuerberater) before formation.

costs.label: Share capital (Stammkapital), to pay in at formation
costs.note: At least 12 500 € under §7 GmbHG; working capital, not 'frozen'.

costs.label: Notary + Handelsregister + publication
costs.note: Cheaper via the Musterprotokoll; individual articles are more expensive.

costs.label: Steuerberater (bookkeeping, initial support)
costs.note: Monthly; double-entry bookkeeping and a Bilanz are mandatory.

title: EXIST: a grant for academic startups
tldr: EXIST is a federal support programme for knowledge-intensive startups from the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Klimaschutz, BMWK). The main strand for founders is the start-up grant (EXIST-Gründungsstipendium): up to 12 months of funding for a team from a university or research institute developing an innovative, technology- or knowledge-intensive product. The grant covers a living allowance (for a graduate/specialist roughly ~3000 €/month, less for technical staff and students), plus material costs (up to ~10 000 € per team) and coaching. The application is submitted NOT by the founder directly, but by the university/research institution as the applicant — so the first step is always to find your university's start-up advisory service (Gründungsberatung) / entrepreneurship centre. For more mature projects there's EXIST-Forschungstransfer. Important: the grant is not a salary; it is not taxed as business income, but it comes with strict conditions on employment and timing.

steps.title: What EXIST is and which strands exist

content.text: EXIST is funded by the BMWK and (in part) the European Social Fund. The programme targets precisely the knowledge-intensive and technological startups linked to universities and research institutes — it is not a general grant 'for any business'. If your idea is to open a café or an online shop, EXIST won't fit.

items: EXIST-Gründungsstipendium: a start-up grant for up to 12 months for a team of founders from a university
EXIST-Forschungstransfer: for projects requiring serious R&D refinement (two phases)
EXIST-Potentiale / Startup-Factories: funding for the universities themselves, not founders directly
Suitable: deep tech, software, biotech, engineering, knowledge-intensive services
NOT suitable: classic retail, gastronomy, crafts without an innovative component

steps.title: The start-up grant (Gründungsstipendium): what it covers and how much

content.text: The EXIST-Gründungsstipendium gives the team time and money to turn an idea into a business plan and a prototype without being distracted by earning a living. The grant is paid per person and depends on the qualification.

items: A PhD holder/graduate with experience: roughly ~3000 €/month (a net grant, not a salary)
A university graduate: ~2500 €/month; a technical staff member: ~2000 €/month; a student: ~1000 €/month
A child supplement — on top of the grant
Material costs (Sachausgaben): up to ~10 000 € per team (less for solo founders)
A coaching budget: up to ~5000 € for consulting and mentoring
Duration — up to 12 months; the team is usually 1 to 3 founders

content.text: The EXIST grant is not a salary and not income from a trade (Gewerbe). While you receive it, you generally must not work full-time as an employee in parallel or carry on commercial activity related to the project. Combining it with other income sources is strictly limited by the programme's conditions — check with the start-up advisory service (Gründungsberatung) before you apply.

steps.title: How to apply: through the university, not directly

content.text: The key feature of EXIST: the formal applicant (Antragsteller) is the university or research institution, not the team of founders. So the path to the grant always begins with your university's entrepreneurship centre.

items.title: 1. Find your university's start-up advisory service (Gründungsberatung)

items: Look for the entrepreneurship centre (Entrepreneurship-Center) / start-up advisory service (Gründungsberatung) / transfer office (Transferstelle) of your university
A link to the university is mandatory — you usually need an academic mentor (Mentor)
The centre will help prepare the application and act as the official applicant
For foreigners: a link to a German university/research institute is critical — without it EXIST is unavailable

items.title: 2. Prepare the idea and the team

items: A clear description of the innovation and its scientific/technological novelty
A balanced team (technical + business) improves your chances
A draft of the business idea and a development plan for the grant year
A link between the idea and your research/study results at the university

content.text: EXIST is competitive: applications go through expert review. Apply well in advance — preparation with the entrepreneurship centre takes weeks and months. Submitting 'at the last minute on your own, bypassing the university' won't work: without a university applicant, the application is not accepted.

costs.label: Cost of submitting the application
costs.note: Submission is free; the university/research institute files it as the applicant.

costs.label: Founder's grant (paid to YOU)
costs.note: Per month, depends on qualification; not a salary but a grant.

costs.label: Material costs + coaching (per team)
costs.note: Sachausgaben up to ~10 000 € and coaching up to ~5000 €.

title: The commercial register (Handelsregister): registering a company
tldr: The Handelsregister is the commercial register (public, kept by the local courts, Amtsgericht) where merchants and companies are registered. For corporations (GmbH, UG, AG) the entry is mandatory and constitutive: §11 GmbHG — a GmbH comes into existence as a legal entity only from the moment of the entry. The register is split into section A (Abteilung A — sole merchants, Einzelkaufleute, OHG, KG) and section B (Abteilung B — GmbH, UG, AG). Sole proprietors (Einzelunternehmer) and the civil-law partnership (GbR) are not in the register if turnover is small; a large merchant (a Kaufmann under §1 HGB running an 'in kaufmännischer Weise eingerichteter Gewerbebetrieb') must register as an e.K. in section A. The application is filed ONLY through a notary in electronic form (§12 HGB). Entries are public and freely available online at handelsregister.de. The cost of the entry (notary + court fee) for a simple GmbH is roughly 150–400 € in court fees plus the notary.

steps.title: Who must register and who doesn't

content.text: The commercial register (Handelsregister) is not for everyone. The obligation depends on the legal form and the scale of the activity. Corporations always register; for sole proprietors it all depends on whether they count as a merchant (Kaufmann) under the HGB.

items: Must register: GmbH, UG (haftungsbeschränkt), AG — the entry is constitutive (§11 GmbHG)
Must register: OHG, KG, and a sole merchant (Einzelkaufmann, e.K.) with large turnover under §1 HGB
Need NOT register: a small sole proprietor (Einzelunternehmer; small trade, Kleingewerbe) and a civil-law partnership (GbR) without the features of a merchant
Section A (Abteilung A): e.K., OHG, KG; section B (Abteilung B): GmbH, UG, AG
Voluntary registration of an e.K. is possible — it gives a company name and an air of solidity

content.text: Don't confuse business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) with the entry in the commercial register (Handelsregister): these are DIFFERENT procedures. The Gewerbeanmeldung at the trade office (Gewerbeamt) is needed by almost all merchants, whereas the Handelsregister entry is only for certain forms/scales. A GmbH goes through BOTH procedures.

steps.title: How the entry is made: only through a notary

content.text: The application to the commercial register (Handelsregister) is filed solely in electronic form through a notary (§12 HGB) — you can't just 'go to the court and register yourself'. The notary certifies the signatures and forwards the documents to the local court (Amtsgericht), acting as the registry court (Registergericht).

items.title: 1. Documents and data for the entry

items: For a GmbH/UG: the articles, the list of partners, the managing director's (Geschäftsführer) details, proof of capital
The company name (Firma) — check its uniqueness with the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) in advance
The object of the business and the company address
For an e.K.: the entrepreneur's details and an application for a voluntary/mandatory entry
The notary files the electronic application with the registry court (Registergericht)
The court checks the formalities and the company name (often requesting the IHK's opinion)
After the entry, an HRB number (for section B) or an HRA number (for section A) is assigned
The entry is published and becomes available at handelsregister.de

steps.title: The register's publicity and legal effects

content.text: The commercial register (Handelsregister) is public: anyone can look up a company's data for free at handelsregister.de. It's a trust instrument in commerce — partners check who has signing authority and what the company's status is. Important legal effects are attached to the entry under §15 HGB (the public reliability of the register).

items: Entries are public and freely available online (handelsregister.de)
§15 HGB: third parties may rely on the content of the register
Any changes (director, address, capital) must be registered promptly
Failure to register changes promptly = a risk of liability and fines (a coercive fine, Zwangsgeld)

content.text: Data published in the commercial register (Handelsregister) (directors' names, the address, the amount of capital) becomes public — this cannot be 'hidden'. Also, don't ignore letters from the registry court (Registergericht) about missing data: the court can impose a coercive fine (Zwangsgeld) for failure to comply with the registration obligation.

costs.label: Registergericht court fee (GmbH)
costs.note: Depends on the form and complexity; a UG/e.K. is cheaper.

costs.label: Notary (certification and filing)
costs.note: Depends on the capital and the articles; the Musterprotokoll is cheaper.

costs.label: Looking up data at handelsregister.de
costs.note: Basic access to the register is free.

title: HWK: the Chamber of Crafts
tldr: The Chamber of Crafts (Handwerkskammer, HWK) is compulsory for anyone carrying on a craft activity (a craft, Handwerk). If your profession is listed in annex A (Anlage A) to the Crafts Code (Handwerksordnung, HwO) it is a craft requiring authorisation (zulassungspflichtiges Handwerk): to open a business and get into the register of craftsmen (Handwerksrolle), you need a master craftsman's certificate (Meisterbrief), or an exception under §7/§7a/§8 HwO. Professions in annexes B1/B2 (Anlage B1/B2) — no mandatory master. Membership in the HWK is compulsory and paid (as is membership in the Chamber of Industry and Commerce IHK for trade/services): the annual fee consists of a basic part (Grundbeitrag) and a part based on profit. For foreign master craftsmen, the HWK recognises a foreign qualification through an equivalence procedure (Gleichwertigkeit). Note: a business registration (Gewerbe) for a craft is impossible without a prior entry in the chamber's register of craftsmen (Handwerksrolle).

steps.title: Is it a craft or not: annexes A, B1, B2 (Anlage A, B1, B2)

content.text: The first question is whether your activity counts as a craft (Handwerk) under the Crafts Code (Handwerksordnung). This determines whether you need the Chamber of Crafts (HWK) and a master craftsman's certificate (Meisterbrief). The lists of professions are given in the annexes to the HwO.

items: Annex A (Anlage A) — crafts requiring authorisation (zulassungspflichtige Handwerke): a master craftsman's certificate (Meisterbrief) is required, e.g. electrician, plumber, hairdresser, baker
Annex B1 (Anlage B1) — crafts not requiring authorisation (zulassungsfreie Handwerke): no mandatory master
Annex B2 (Anlage B2) — trades similar to crafts (handwerksähnliche Gewerbe): related activities
For all three — membership in the HWK, not the IHK
Not a craft (trade, services, IT) — that's the IHK, not the HWK

content.text: Starting a craft requiring authorisation (annex A, Anlage A) without an entry in the register of craftsmen (Handwerksrolle) is a breach that risks a fine and a ban on the activity (a risk of illegal work, Schwarzarbeit). First the entry in the Handwerksrolle via the HWK, and only then the business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung).

steps.title: The master requirement (Meisterpflicht) and exceptions for foreigners

content.text: For professions in annex A (Anlage A) a master craftsman's certificate (Meisterbrief) is required as a general rule. But the HwO provides for exceptions, including ones that matter for foreign specialists with a foreign qualification.

items: An exceptional authorisation (Ausnahmebewilligung) under §8 HwO — an individual permit where there is sufficient experience
The rule for experienced journeymen (Altgesellenregelung) under §7b HwO — for journeymen with many years of leadership experience
EU/EEA citizens: simplified access under §7/§9 HwO (freedom to provide services, Dienstleistungsfreiheit)
Recognition of a foreign qualification as equivalent to a master (equivalence, Gleichwertigkeit)

items.title: 2. Recognition of a foreign master craftsman's certificate

items: You apply for an equivalence determination (Gleichwertigkeitsfeststellung) at the competent HWK
The HWK compares your qualification with the German master (Meister) level
Partial equivalence with further training (an adaptation, Anpassung) is possible
Advice — via the portal anerkennung-in-deutschland.de

content.text: Membership in the HWK is compulsory and paid, just like in the IHK for trade. The fee consists of a basic part and a part dependent on profit (trade income, Gewerbeertrag). There are reliefs for small startups.

items: The basic fee (Grundbeitrag) — a fixed annual part
The apportionment / additional fee (Umlage / Zusatzbeitrag) — a percentage of profit (Gewerbeertrag)
For newcomers with low turnover — a partial exemption in the first years
The HWK also keeps the register of apprentices (Lehrlingsrolle) and runs examinations
The fee letter will arrive automatically after the entry in the register of craftsmen (Handwerksrolle)

content.text: You can't ignore HWK letters: the fee is charged whether or not you reply, and non-payment is followed by a reminder and enforcement. If your turnover is low — apply for relief/exemption from the basic fee (Grundbeitrag); it isn't granted automatically.

costs.label: Entry in the Handwerksrolle
costs.note: A one-off fee for the entry in the register of craftsmen.

costs.label: Annual HWK fee (Grundbeitrag)
costs.note: The basic part; plus a part based on profit. Reliefs for newcomers.

costs.label: Recognition of a qualification (Gleichwertigkeit)
costs.note: Depends on the profession and the scope of the HWK's review.

title: IHK: membership and fees
tldr: The Chamber of Industry and Commerce (Industrie- und Handelskammer, IHK). For most types of trade (Gewerbe — trade, services, industry, anything that is NOT a craft and NOT a liberal profession), membership in the IHK is compulsory by law (the IHKG — Gesetz zur vorläufigen Regelung des Rechts der Industrie- und Handelskammern). You become a member automatically after the business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) — no application needed; the fee letter comes by itself. The fee consists of a basic part (Grundbeitrag) and an apportionment (Umlage — a percentage of trade income, Gewerbeertrag). The key relief: under IHK rules, small entrepreneurs not registered in the commercial register (Handelsregister), with profit below a certain threshold (often trade income/profit up to ~5200 €/year), are EXEMPT from the basic fee, and in the first 2 years after founding there are additional reliefs. The liberal professions (freie Berufe) and craftsmen (in the HWK) are NOT in the IHK.

steps.title: Who automatically becomes an IHK member

content.text: IHK membership is not voluntary: under the IHKG, everyone who runs a trade (Gewerbe) and is subject to trade tax (Gewerbesteuer), apart from crafts and the liberal professions, automatically becomes a member of the chamber for their place of business. You don't file a separate application — the trade office (Gewerbeamt) passes on your data and the IHK sends the letter itself.

items: IHK members: trade, e-commerce, services, industry, agencies, IT firms (as a trade)
NOT IHK members: craftsmen (they're in the Chamber of Crafts HWK) and the liberal professions (freie Berufe)
Membership arises automatically after the business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung)
The membership and fee letter will arrive without any application from you
GmbH/UG — always IHK members (as corporations they run a trade)

content.text: The annual IHK fee (Beitrag) consists of two parts. Each chamber sets the specific rates itself in its fee regulations (Beitragsordnung), so the amounts differ by region.

items: The basic fee (Grundbeitrag) — a fixed basic part (depends on the form and turnover)
The apportionment (Umlage) — a percentage of trade income (Gewerbeertrag, profit) after the tax-free allowance
The IHK takes the base for the apportionment from the tax office's (Finanzamt) trade-tax (Gewerbesteuer) data
The rate amounts are in the fee regulations (Beitragsordnung) of the specific chamber (they differ by city)

steps.title: Reliefs for small and new entrepreneurs

content.text: This is the most important and most underestimated thing: many newcomers fear 'expensive IHK fees', although with low profit they may be exempt from the basic part. The reliefs are based on federal-level decisions under the IHKG.

items: Not registered in the commercial register (Handelsregister) and trade income (Gewerbeertrag) below the threshold (often ~5200 €) — exemption from the basic fee (Grundbeitrag) and the apportionment (Umlage)
Those founding a business (Existenzgründer) with trade income up to 25 000 €: in the founding year — full exemption from fees
2nd-3rd founding year: only half the basic fee (Grundbeitrag); 4th year — the full Grundbeitrag without the apportionment
These reliefs are for individuals and partnerships (Personengesellschaften), not for a GmbH/AG
The exact thresholds and timeframes are in your IHK's fee regulations (Beitragsordnung)

content.text: You can't simply ignore IHK letters in the hope of 'not paying'. The fee is charged automatically, and non-payment is followed by a payment reminder (Mahnung) and enforcement. If your profit is low or you've only just started — report your income to the IHK and cite the exemption for small/new entrepreneurs; then the fee is legally zeroed out.

costs.label: Grundbeitrag IHK (basic annual fee)
costs.note: Depends on the chamber and the form; exemption for small ones.

costs.label: Umlage (percentage of profit)
costs.note: A percentage of Gewerbeertrag above the tax-free allowance; rate per the Beitragsordnung.

costs.label: Membership for small/new (with exemption)
costs.note: With profit below the threshold and in the first founding year — 0 €.

sources.title: IHKG — Gesetz über die Industrie- und Handelskammern

title: Small business (Kleinunternehmer) §19 UStG: €22 000
tldr: The small-business scheme (Kleinunternehmerregelung, §19 UStG) lets a small business NOT charge VAT (Umsatzsteuer) and skip the complex VAT reporting. NOTE: from 1 January 2025 a reform changed the thresholds — it is NO LONGER the old 22 000 €. The new limits: turnover in the PREVIOUS year up to 25 000 € (net) AND in the CURRENT year up to 100 000 €. If you exceed 100 000 € in the current year, the small-business (Kleinunternehmer) status is lost immediately from that transaction. Pros: invoices without VAT (advantageous for private clients), less bureaucracy, no monthly advance VAT return (Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung). Cons: you can't reclaim input VAT (Vorsteuer) on your purchases, which is a disadvantage with large investments. You choose the status in the tax-registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung) via the tax portal ELSTER. Since 2025, small businesses are formally exempt but are obliged to accept an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) from B2B counterparties.

steps.title: The new thresholds from 2025: not 22 000, but 25 000 / 100 000

content.text: This is the main change that confuses many: until 2024 the small-business (Kleinunternehmer) threshold was 22 000 € (previous year) and 50 000 € (current-year forecast). From 1 January 2025 the §19 UStG reform introduced new limits, and they work differently.

items: Previous year: turnover did not exceed 25 000 € (it used to be 22 000 €)
Current year: turnover does not exceed 100 000 € (the forecast used to be 50 000 €)
Exceeding 100 000 € in the current year = immediate loss of status from that transaction
These are net turnovers (total turnover, Gesamtumsatz), counted on actual receipts
The old 22 000 € threshold is NOT current from 2025 — don't go by it

content.text: The logic of the thresholds has changed: previously, exceeding the forecast didn't hit you retroactively within the same year; now, if you exceed 100 000 € in the current year, you lose the status IMMEDIATELY, and the VAT obligation starts from that transaction. Track your turnover in real time, especially as the business grows.

steps.title: Pros and cons of small-business (Kleinunternehmer) status

content.text: Small-business (Kleinunternehmer) status is not always the best choice. It's advantageous if your clients are private individuals (who can't reclaim VAT) and you have few purchases. And it's disadvantageous if you invest a lot or work mainly with businesses.

items: Clients are private individuals: a price without VAT makes you 19% more competitive
Minimal bureaucracy: no advance VAT return (Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung)
Simple invoices without VAT shown
Low own purchases — losing input VAT (Vorsteuer) is no great loss
Large investments (machinery, equipment) — you can't reclaim input VAT (Vorsteuer)
Clients are mainly B2B — VAT doesn't bother them, they reclaim it
You plan rapid growth above the thresholds — the switch is unavoidable anyway
Purchases abroad / reverse charge complicate the picture

steps.title: How to choose the status and about the electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) 2025

content.text: Small-business (Kleinunternehmer) status is chosen in the tax-registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung) when registering the activity via the tax portal ELSTER. You can also waive it voluntarily (opting for standard taxation, Option zur Regelbesteuerung), but then you're bound by that choice for several years.

items: The status is chosen in the tax-registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung; ELSTER)
A voluntary waiver (Verzicht) binds you for 5 years — think it through
On invoices, state the basis: 'Steuerbefreiung als Kleinunternehmer nach §19 UStG'
Since 2025: even small businesses are obliged to ACCEPT an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) from B2B counterparties
Issuing an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) yourself will become mandatory later: from 2027 (turnover >800 000 €), from 2028 — for everyone in B2B

content.text: A common small-business (Kleinunternehmer) mistake is showing VAT on an invoice 'out of habit'. If, as a Kleinunternehmer, you show a VAT amount on an invoice, you'll be OBLIGED to pay it to the tax authorities under §14c UStG, even though you don't have the status for it. Never show VAT on invoices while you're a small business.

costs.label: Registering the status via ELSTER
costs.note: The Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung is submitted free of charge.

costs.label: Accounting software (Lexoffice/sevDesk etc.)
costs.note: Per month; for a Kleinunternehmer the basic plans are enough.

costs.label: Steuerberater (optional, consultation)
costs.note: One-off; many Kleinunternehmer keep their own books (EÜR).

title: KSK: the social fund for creative professions
tldr: The Artists' Social Insurance Fund (Künstlersozialkasse, KSK) is a mechanism unique to Germany: self-employed artists, musicians, writers, journalists, designers and photographers pay only HALF the contributions for pension (pension insurance, Rentenversicherung), health (health insurance, Krankenversicherung) and care (long-term care insurance, Pflegeversicherung), like employees. The other half is topped up by clients via the artists' social contribution (Künstlersozialabgabe) and the federal budget (the Artists' Social Insurance Act, Künstlersozialversicherungsgesetz — KSVG). Membership conditions: you are a self-employed creative worker, the activity is carried on professionally and not temporarily, and the expected annual income is above 3900 € (the minimum threshold, Mindestgrenze; in the first 3 years it can be lower for beginners). Contributions are calculated on the annual profit you project yourself. It's a huge saving compared with full private or voluntary insurance. The application goes directly to the KSK; the decision on admission is made by the fund itself.

steps.title: What the KSK provides and why it's advantageous

content.text: An ordinary self-employed person pays the social contributions entirely themselves. Through the KSK, a creative freelancer is effectively put on a par with an employee: half of the contributions for pension, health and care are topped up for them by clients and the state. That's a saving of about 50% on social insurance — the main reason it's worth joining.

items: The KSK covers: pension insurance (Rentenversicherung), health insurance (Krankenversicherung), long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung)
You pay ~half the contributions, the other half — the artists' social contribution (Künstlersozialabgabe) from clients + a state subsidy
The basis is the Artists' Social Insurance Act (Künstlersozialversicherungsgesetz, KSVG)
The KSK is not a separate insurer but an intermediary: it transfers the contributions to the health funds (Krankenkassen) you choose
A huge saving compared with full private/voluntary insurance

steps.title: Who can join: the membership conditions

content.text: The KSK is not for all self-employed people, only for artistic and journalistic professions carried on professionally (as a source of income, erwerbsmäßig) and not as a temporary hobby. The fund assesses each application individually.

items: Visual art (Bildende Kunst): artists, illustrators, photographers, graphic/web designers
Music (Musik): musicians, composers, music teachers
Performing arts (Darstellende Kunst): actors, directors, dancers
Word/journalism (Wort/Publizistik): writers, journalists, (literary) translators, copywriters
A lecturer/teacher in these fields — often eligible too

items.title: 2. Conditions on income and the nature of the work

items: The activity is self-employed (selbständig), not employed
Professional and not temporary (not a one-off hobby)
Expected annual income above the minimum threshold (Mindestgrenze) of 3900 €
In the first 3 years (a beginner, Berufsanfänger) you can temporarily be below the minimum
No more than 1 employee (apart from assistants/apprentices) — otherwise it's disputable

steps.title: Submitting the application and calculating contributions

content.text: The application is submitted directly to the KSK (a questionnaire on their website). The fund checks your activity and income, and where necessary requests a portfolio, contracts and invoices. Contributions are calculated on your forecast of annual profit, which you report yourself.

items: Fill in the registration questionnaire (Fragebogen / Erhebungsbogen) at kuenstlersozialkasse.de
Attach evidence of creative activity: contracts, invoices, a portfolio
Report your annual income forecast (Jahresarbeitseinkommen) — the contributions are calculated from it
The KSK calculates your monthly contribution and transfers it to the funds you've chosen
Once a year you report the forecast for the next year; large discrepancies are checked

content.text: Don't understate your income forecast to lower your contributions: the KSK cross-checks the data, and systematic understatement can lead to back-payments and penalties. Conversely — if your actual income drops below the minimum for a long time (outside the first 3 years), membership may be terminated. Report realistic figures and update them when things change.

costs.label: Submitting the application to the KSK
costs.note: Submitting and reviewing the application is free.

costs.label: Your contribution (the member's share)
costs.note: Per month; depends on the income forecast — it's ~half the full social contributions.

costs.label: Saving compared with full insurance
costs.note: The other half is topped up by clients (Künstlersozialabgabe) and the state.

title: Master craftsman requirement (Meisterpflicht): trades that require a master
tldr: The master craftsman requirement (Meisterpflicht) is the rule that you must hold a master craftsman's certificate (Meisterbrief) to run your own business in certain trades. The affected occupations are listed in Annex A (Anlage A) to the Trade and Crafts Code (Handwerksordnung, HwO) — these are the trades that require a licence (zulassungspflichtige Handwerke). In 2020 the list was expanded again: the master requirement was reinstated for 12 occupations (tilers, parquet layers, sign makers and others). You cannot open such a business without a master's certificate — you must either pass the master's examination (Meisterprüfung) or obtain an exemption: §7b HwO (rule for experienced journeymen, Altgesellenregelung), §8 HwO (individual permit, Ausnahmebewilligung), §7a (partial rights), or have a foreign qualification recognised as equivalent to a master. EU citizens have simplified access (freedom to provide services, Dienstleistungsfreiheit, §9 HwO). You may work as an employee in these trades WITHOUT a master's certificate — the requirement applies only to the head of an independent business.

steps.title: Which occupations require a master (Annex A, Anlage A)

content.text: The master requirement applies only to the occupations listed in Annex A (Anlage A) to the HwO — the trades that require a licence (zulassungspflichtige Handwerke). There are about a hundred such specialities, where the quality of the work affects people's safety (heightened risk of harm, Gefahrgeneigtheit) or the preservation of cultural heritage. In 2020 the list was expanded once more.

items: Examples from Annex A (Anlage A): electrician, plumber/heating engineer (SHK), hairdresser, baker, butcher, carpenter, car mechanic
In 2020 the master requirement was reinstated for 12 occupations: tilers, parquet layers, concrete workers, sign makers and others
Annexes B1 (trades without a licence requirement, zulassungsfrei) and B2 (crafts-like activities, handwerksähnlich) — NO mandatory master
Not sure which annex (Anlage) your occupation falls under — ask the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (Handwerkskammer, HWK)
The master requirement applies to the head of the business, not to its employees

content.text: Opening a trade that requires a licence (zulassungspflichtiges Handwerk) without a master or a lawful exemption is illegal work (Schwarzarbeit): it risks fines, a ban on the activity, and problems with clients (contracts may be declared void). You cannot "start now and sort it out later".

steps.title: Routes without sitting the German master's examination (Meister)

content.text: Passing the master's examination (Meisterprüfung) is not the only route. The Trade and Crafts Code (HwO) provides several lawful exemptions, which are especially useful for experienced specialists and for foreigners with a foreign qualification.

items: §7b HwO (rule for experienced journeymen, Altgesellenregelung): a journeyman with many years of experience, including managerial duties
§8 HwO (individual permit, Ausnahmebewilligung): with proven knowledge and experience
§7a HwO: the right to carry out part of a trade (partial activity, Teiltätigkeit) without a full master
§9 HwO + EU/EEA: simplified access for EU citizens (freedom to provide services)
Apply for a determination of equivalence (Gleichwertigkeitsfeststellung) at the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (Handwerkskammer)
The Chamber of Skilled Crafts (HWK) compares your qualification with the level of a German master
Partial equivalence with a top-up training course is possible
Information and advice — anerkennung-in-deutschland.de

content.text: It is important to understand where the line falls: the master requirement applies to running a craft business independently (as the technical manager, Betriebsleiter), not to working as an employee. If you are a skilled specialist without a master's certificate, you can legally work in a firm as long as a master heads the business.

items: You may work as an employed master/specialist in someone else's firm WITHOUT a master's certificate
You cannot open your own Annex A (Anlage A) business without a master or an exemption
Alternative: hire a technical manager (Betriebsleiter) with a master qualification for your business
A master's certificate is not required for employment, but it raises your pay and career prospects
A master craftsman's certificate (Meisterbrief) also grants the right to train apprentices (the right to provide vocational training, Ausbildungsberechtigung)

content.text: Hiring a master as technical manager (Betriebsleiter) is lawful, but the master must genuinely run the technical side and not just be a name on paper. A sham technical manager is a violation that the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (HWK) checks for. The master must actually work in the business and oversee its quality.

costs.label: Meisterprüfung (preparation + examination)
costs.note: Meistervorbereitung courses are expensive; partly covered by Aufstiegs-BAföG.

costs.label: Ausnahmebewilligung / Altgesellenregelung
costs.note: Processing fee at the Handwerkskammer.

costs.label: Recognition of a foreign qualification
costs.note: Gleichwertigkeitsfeststellung via the HWK.

title: Invoice (Rechnung): mandatory details
tldr: An invoice (Rechnung) in Germany must contain a strictly defined set of details under §14 and §14a UStG — otherwise a business client cannot reclaim input VAT (Vorsteuer) and you risk claims from the tax office (Finanzamt). Mandatory fields: the full name and address of the supplier and the recipient, your tax number (Steuernummer) OR your VAT identification number (USt-IdNr.), the date of issue, a sequential invoice number (fortlaufende Rechnungsnummer), the quantity and description of the goods/services, the date of delivery, the net amount, the VAT rate and VAT amount (or a reference to §19 UStG for a small business, Kleinunternehmer). For invoices up to 250 € simplified rules apply (small-amount invoice, Kleinbetragsrechnung, §33 UStDV). KEY CHANGE FOR 2025: from 1 January 2025, in domestic B2B transactions within Germany it is mandatory to be ABLE TO RECEIVE an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) — a structured electronic invoice compliant with EN 16931, e.g. XRechnung/ZUGFeRD; the obligation to ISSUE them is being phased in over 2027-2028. From 2025 a plain PDF no longer formally counts as an electronic invoice.

content.text: An invoice without the mandatory details is a problem not only for you but also for your client: a business recipient will not be able to reclaim input VAT (Vorsteuer). That is why §14 Abs. 4 UStG sets out clearly what every invoice must contain.

items: Full name and address of the supplier (you) and the recipient
Your tax number (Steuernummer) OR your VAT identification number (USt-IdNr.)
The date the invoice is issued (Ausstellungsdatum)
A sequential, unique invoice number (fortlaufende Rechnungsnummer)
The quantity and exact description of the goods/services (Menge und Art)
The date or period of delivery or of the service provided (Lieferdatum / Leistungszeitpunkt)
The net amount, the VAT rate (7% or 19%) and the VAT amount shown separately
Small business (Kleinunternehmer): instead of VAT — a reference to the exemption under §19 UStG

content.text: The invoice number must be unique and continuous — you cannot reuse numbers or assign them arbitrarily. And never break out VAT if you are a small business (Kleinunternehmer): under §14c UStG any VAT shown on an invoice must be paid to the tax authorities, even without VAT-payer status.

steps.title: Simplified invoices up to 250 € (small-amount invoice, Kleinbetragsrechnung)

content.text: The law makes a concession for small invoices. A small-amount invoice (Kleinbetragsrechnung) under §33 UStDV is an invoice whose total amount (gross) does not exceed 250 €. It requires fewer details.

items: Enough: the supplier's name and address, the date, a description, the gross amount and the VAT rate
NOT required: the recipient's details, the invoice number, the VAT amount shown separately
Threshold — 250 € gross (including VAT)
Convenient for retail, cafés and small sales
Above 250 € — you need the full set of details under §14 UStG

steps.title: Electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) 2025: what changed for B2B

content.text: This is the most important change. From 1 January 2025, in transactions between businesses within Germany (B2B, domestic, inländisch) the definition of an invoice changed: a "real" electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) is one in a structured format compliant with the European standard EN 16931 (for example XRechnung or ZUGFeRD), while a plain PDF now counts as an "other" invoice rather than an electronic one.

items.title: 1. Receiving an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) — mandatory already from 2025

items: From 01.01.2025 all B2B recipients must be ABLE to accept an electronic invoice
Having an e-mail address to receive a structured invoice is enough
This applies to small businesses (Kleinunternehmer) too — they must also be able to accept an electronic invoice
Format: XRechnung (XML) or the hybrid ZUGFeRD (PDF+XML compliant with EN 16931)

items.title: 2. Issuing an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) — phased in from 2027

items: Until the end of 2026 — a transition period; you may send paper or PDF with the recipient's consent
From 2027 — the obligation to issue an electronic invoice if last year's turnover exceeded 800 000 €
From 2028 — the obligation applies to everyone in B2B
B2C (private clients) and foreign invoices are not affected by the electronic invoice obligation

content.text: Do not ignore the obligation to ACCEPT an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung): it already applies from 2025. If a counterparty sends you an XRechnung/ZUGFeRD, you are obliged to accept and process it. Use accounting software (Lexoffice, sevDesk, etc.) that can create and read EN 16931 formats so you keep pace with the phased transition.

costs.label: Accounting/invoicing software (Lexoffice, sevDesk)
costs.note: Per month; supports XRechnung/ZUGFeRD for E-Rechnung.

costs.label: Creating an invoice template
costs.note: Free within the software; a manual invoice — only if the §14 details are met.

costs.label: Steuerberater (review, optional)
costs.note: One-off; useful for complex reverse charge/EU cases.

title: Bogus self-employment (Scheinselbständigkeit): the risks
tldr: Bogus self-employment (Scheinselbständigkeit) is one of the most dangerous traps for freelancers in Germany. Under §7 SGB IV, if a "self-employed" person actually works like an employee — embedded in the structure of a single client, following instructions, with no employees of their own and earning most of their income from one client — the activity is reclassified as an employment relationship. The consequences are severe: the client is charged social security contributions (health, pension, unemployment) retroactively, sometimes for years. You can check your status in advance through the status determination procedure (Statusfeststellungsverfahren) at the clearing office (Clearingstelle) of the German pension insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, DRV). The main red flag — one client provides more than 5/6 of your income. This affects both the contractor and especially the client, who risks large back payments.

content.text: Bogus self-employment (Scheinselbständigkeit) is a situation where a person is formally registered as self-employed (issues invoices, runs a business, Gewerbe, or works as a freelancer) but in fact works like an ordinary employee. §7 SGB IV defines employment (Beschäftigung) by reference to dependent work, integration into an organisation and subordination to instructions. If these features are present, the law sees an employment relationship, whatever you call it.

items: What decides the matter is the substance of the relationship, not the formal contract (contract for work/contract for services, Werkvertrag/Dienstvertrag)
The key law — §7 SGB IV (the concept of employment, Beschäftigung)
Signs of dependent work: instructions on the time, place and manner of work
Integration into the client's structure (workplace, access rights, time sheet)
No genuine entrepreneurial risk of your own and no clients of your own

steps.title: Red flags: signs of bogus self-employment

content.text: The pension insurance (DRV) and the tax office (Finanzamt) look at the overall picture. The more it matches a typical employment relationship, the higher the risk of reclassification.

items: One client provides more than 5/6 (about 83%) of your income
No employees of your own and no other clients
The client dictates when, where and exactly how you work
You are integrated into the team: internal email, badge, workplace, schedules
No genuine entrepreneurial risk of your own (fixed, regular pay)
You used to be a permanent employee of this same client in the same role

content.text: The one-client rule is the freelancer's main trap. If 5/6 or more of your income comes from a single client, that is a strong indicator of bogus self-employment (and also of a risky proximity to the status of an employee-like person, arbeitnehmerähnliche Person, in pension insurance). Diversify your clients from the very start — it is not just good business hygiene but legal protection.

steps.title: Consequences: retroactive back payment of social contributions

content.text: If the activity is found to be employment, the consequences fall primarily on the CLIENT as the de facto employer. All social security contributions for the past period are charged retroactively — sometimes going back several years.

items: Back charge of social contributions: health (KV), long-term care (PV), pension (RV) and unemployment insurance
The client pays both the employer's share and (within limits) the employee's share
Back payments can cover up to 4 years, and longer in cases of intent
Late-payment penalties are possible and, in serious cases, criminal liability (§266a StGB — non-payment of contributions)
The contractor risks losing input VAT deductions (Vorsteuer) and having invoices reclassified

content.text: In cases of deliberate evasion, the non-payment of social contributions under §266a StGB is a criminal offence for the responsible persons at the client. That is why serious companies are wary of single-client freelancers and often demand proof of genuine self-employment (other clients, your own equipment, your own risk). Do not take a client's refusal as nit-picking — it protects both them and you.

steps.title: How to protect yourself: the status determination procedure (Statusfeststellungsverfahren)

content.text: Rather than guessing, you can have your status determined officially in advance. The status determination procedure (Statusfeststellungsverfahren) is carried out by the clearing office (Clearingstelle) of the German pension insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung, DRV). It gives legal certainty to both sides.

items.title: 1. Filing the application with the clearing office (Clearingstelle)

items: The application is filed with the pension insurance's clearing office (Clearingstelle DRV) — the Statusfeststellung form
Either the contractor or the client can request it
Attach the contract, a description of the work and details of other clients
Better to file at the start of the engagement, not after the fact
The pension insurance (DRV) issues a decision: self-employment or employment
The decision gives legal protection to both sides
If employment is found — set up an employment contract and pay contributions on time
You can appeal (objection, Widerspruch), but it is better to structure the work as genuinely self-employed

content.text: Practical tip: from the very start, build up the features of genuine self-employment — several clients, your own equipment, freedom in how you organise your work, your own risks and the ability to turn down a job. This both reduces the risk of bogus self-employment and makes the status determination procedure (Statusfeststellung) easier to pass.

costs.label: Statusfeststellungsverfahren at the DRV
costs.note: The status determination procedure at the Clearingstelle DRV is free.

costs.label: Back charge of social contributions on reclassification
costs.note: Can reach tens of thousands of euros for past years; falls mainly on the client.

costs.label: Legal advice (optional)
costs.note: An Anwalt for labour/social law to assess the contract and the risks.

title: Anabin: the database of foreign universities
tldr: Anabin (anabin.kmk.org) is a free official database on the recognition of foreign degrees, maintained by the Central Office for Foreign Education (Zentralstelle für ausländisches Bildungswesen, ZAB) at the KMK. It contains assessments of foreign universities and degrees: H+ — equivalent to a German one, H+/- — partially, H- — not recognised. It is the first stop for anyone who wants to work in their profession in Germany. A search takes 10 minutes and costs nothing.

steps.title: What Anabin is and why you need it

content.text: Anabin is the KMK's public information system (the Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs of the Länder, Kultusministerkonferenz) on foreign educational institutions and qualifications. It is maintained by the Central Office for Foreign Education (Zentralstelle für ausländisches Bildungswesen, ZAB) — the central body at the KMK that is officially responsible for assessing foreign degrees in Germany.

The database has two main sections: universities (Hochschulen) and university degrees (Hochschulabschlüsse). For each university a status of H+, H+/- or H- is given. For each degree, it shows the German level it corresponds to (Bachelor/Master/Diplom) and an assessment of its equivalence.

items: H+ = the university/degree is recognised as equivalent to a German one
H+/- = partially recognised (often regional or non-state universities)
H- = not recognised as higher education in the sense of German law
H+/H- = the status is in question, assessed individually
Access is free, no registration is needed, and the interface language is German

content.text: The logic of the check: first look at the university, then at the degree itself. For a positive result you need both statuses to be H+.

items: Open anabin.kmk.org → the institutions section (Institutionen) → search (Suchen)
Choose the country (for example, Russische Föderation, Republik Belarus, Ukraine)
Enter the university name in German or transliteration (sometimes several variants at once)
Look at the status column (Status): H+ / H+/- / H-
Save the exact German name of the university — you will need it on any application form (Antragsformular)
Go to the university degrees section (Hochschulabschlüsse) → search (Suchen)
Choose the country and the type of degree (Bakkalaureat, Spezialist, Magister, etc.)
Find the exact wording as it appears on your degree (for example, "Спеціаліст з правознавства")
Look at the correspondence (Entsprechung): which German level it matches (Bachelor, Master, Diplom (Univ.))
Look at the equivalence class (Äquivalenzklasse): gleichwertig / entspricht / nicht gleichwertig

content.text: If the university or degree is not found, you can submit an individual application (Antrag) to the ZAB for an official assessment of your foreign degree (Zeugnisbewertung) — see the separate guide. It costs 208€ and takes about 3 months. Free advice is also available at the IQ-Netzwerk; individual advice (IQ-Beratungsstelle / Fachstelle) is recommended.
Anabin is not the act of recognition itself. It is a reference database. But it is exactly what is used by:

items: Employers — to quickly assess your degree (especially in IT and engineering)
The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) / the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) — when applying for the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU, §18g AufenthG) to confirm an H+ university
The IHK FOSA / the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (HWK) — at the start of the qualification recognition procedure (Anerkennung)
Universities (Hochschule) — when applying for a master's or doctoral programme
The Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) — when assessing vacancies for foreigners

content.text: For non-regulated professions (industrial engineer, programmer, economist) an H+ in Anabin is often enough — formal recognition of the qualification (Anerkennung) is not mandatory under §2 BQFG. For regulated professions (reglementierte Berufe — doctor, lawyer, teacher, architect) Anabin is only the first step; after it you need a full application (Antrag).

The status in Anabin can change. If 5 years ago your university was H+ and now it is H+/-, the current status is the one that applies when you file. Save a screenshot showing the date as at the time you submit your documents.

Many commercial/non-state universities in Russia, Belarus and Ukraine have a status of H+/- or H-. This applies to universities founded after 1991 with a licence for paid tuition only. Check in advance, before you move.

If your degree is a Specialist (5 years) of the Soviet/post-Soviet type, it is usually equated to a Master, not a Bachelor. This matters for the Blue Card (Blaue Karte): you need an academic higher education degree (akademischer Hochschulabschluss).

An H+ status in Anabin does NOT in itself grant the right to work as a doctor, lawyer or teacher. For these professions you need a licence to practise (Approbation) or an entry in the register (Eintragung) — Anabin only confirms that the degree is recognised as higher education.

costs.label: Search in Anabin
costs.note: Free, no registration

costs.label: Zeugnisbewertung from the ZAB (if the university is not in the database)
costs.note: Standard fee (since June 2024); processing time about 3 months

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung of the degree
costs.note: Per page from a vereidigter Übersetzer; translations are needed for the Antrag

title: Qualification recognition (Anerkennung) of a degree: where to start
tldr: Qualification recognition (Anerkennung) is the official procedure for recognising a foreign qualification in Germany under the BQFG (Berufsqualifikationsfeststellungsgesetz). For regulated professions (reglementierte Berufe — doctor, lawyer, teacher, architect) it is mandatory; for non-regulated ones (industrial engineer, IT, economist) it is voluntary. A decision under §6 BQFG is issued within 3 months of the complete submission of documents; the cost is 100-600€. The recognition partnership (Anerkennungspartnerschaft, §16d Abs. 3 AufenthG, since 1 March 2024) lets you start work BEFORE recognition is completed.

steps.title: What qualification recognition (Anerkennung) is and who needs it

content.text: Qualification recognition (Anerkennung; full name — Anerkennung ausländischer Berufsqualifikationen) is the legal confirmation that your foreign qualification is equivalent to a German profession. The main law is the BQFG (Berufsqualifikationsfeststellungsgesetz) of 2012, plus sector-specific laws (Bundesärzteordnung, the architects' acts of the Länder, etc.).

The key distinction is between regulated professions (reglementierte Berufe) and non-regulated ones (nicht-reglementierte). For the former, you CANNOT work in the profession without recognition. For the latter it is not formally required, but employers often want to see an official decision (Bescheid).

items: Regulated (reglementiert): doctor, nurse, pharmacist, lawyer, teacher, architect, engineer (in some Länder), psychotherapist, tax adviser
Non-regulated (nicht-reglementiert): programmer, economist, marketer, journalist, designer, industrial engineer
Skilled trades with vocational training (Ausbildungsberufe) — Bäcker, Kfz-Mechatroniker and others — via the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (HWK) or IHK FOSA
Under §6 BQFG a decision is issued within 3 months of the complete submission of documents
Since 1 March 2024 the recognition partnership (Anerkennungspartnerschaft, §16d AufenthG) applies — you can work BEFORE the procedure is completed

content.text: The logic: identify your profession → find the competent authority (zuständige Stelle) → gather the documents → submit the application (Antrag).

Open anerkennung-in-deutschland.de → the recognition finder section (Anerkennungs-Finder). Choose your profession, the country where you obtained your degree and the Land where you intend to live. The system will show which authority is responsible, which documents are needed and what the cost is.

items: netzwerk-iq.de → on-site advice (Beratung vor Ort)
There are branches in every Land; advice in German, English, Russian and Ukrainian
They will help you put together the document package and the cover letter
Free, takes 1-2 meetings
Degree + supplement/transcript of grades (certified copy, beglaubigte Kopie)
Certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) into German (sworn translator, vereidigter Übersetzer)
Apostille (Apostille) on the original degree (from the issuing country)
A detailed CV (Lebenslauf, CV) in German — with dates and hours
References from employers (Arbeitszeugnisse) / employment record book, work certificates + translations
Passport + registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
A declaration on previous applications (Erklärung über frühere Anträge — that you have not applied before)

content.text: You submit it to the competent authority (zuständige Stelle): for doctors — the Landesärztekammer/Bezirksregierung; for engineers — the Land's Ingenieurkammer; for skilled trades — IHK FOSA (industry) or the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (HWK, crafts); for non-regulated academic qualifications — a degree assessment at the ZAB (Zeugnisbewertung). After submission the 3-month period under §6 BQFG starts to run.
Under §10 BQFG there are three possible results:

items: Full equivalence of the qualification (volle Gleichwertigkeit) — full recognition, you can work without restrictions

Partial equivalence (teilweise Gleichwertigkeit) — partial recognition; you need to complete an adaptation course (Anpassungslehrgang), an adaptation placement (Anpassungspraktikum) or an examination assessing your professional knowledge (Kenntnisprüfung)

No equivalence (keine Gleichwertigkeit) — refusal; there is usually a right to object (Widerspruch) within a month (the deadline and procedure depend on the notice of available remedies, Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung, in the decision, Bescheid)

content.text: With partial equivalence (teilweise Gleichwertigkeit), the decision (Bescheid) states exactly which knowledge or hours are missing. For non-regulated professions, closing the gap is voluntary; for regulated ones, the shortfall is made up through an adaptation course (Anpassungslehrgang), an adaptation placement (Anpassungspraktikum) or a knowledge/aptitude examination (Kenntnis-/Eignungsprüfung). The right to choose between the course and the examination is set out in §15 BQFG, but special sector-specific rules apply to certain regulated professions.

Since 1 March 2024 the main part of the Skilled Immigration Act 2.0 reform has been in force. Under §16d Abs. 3 AufenthG a recognition partnership (Anerkennungspartnerschaft) has been introduced: you can enter Germany and start work BEFORE the recognition procedure is completed.

items: Required: a foreign university degree OR vocational training of at least 2 years + an employment contract + a recognition partnership (Anerkennungspartnerschaft) with the employer
German level: at least A2 at the time of application
Employer and employee jointly sign a commitment to start recognition within 6 months
A temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) is issued, as a rule, for 1 year with the possibility of extension (total period up to 3 years)
If recognition is successful — switch to §18a/§18g AufenthG (skilled worker, Fachkraft / EU Blue Card, Blaue Karte EU)

content.text: This is an alternative to the visa for the recognition of a professional qualification (Visum zur Anerkennung der Berufsqualifikation, §16d Abs. 1) — with that route you first have to complete recognition and only then obtain a full work permit. The recognition partnership is faster, but it commits the employer.

Do not submit documents to the ZAB as a substitute for recognition (Anerkennung) for a regulated profession. A degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) from the ZAB is just that — a degree assessment; it does not grant the right to work as a doctor or lawyer. You need an application (Antrag) to the Land authority (Landesbehörde).

Submit your application (Antrag) in the Land where you intend to work. In many cases recognition is valid across the whole country, but for a number of regulated professions (teachers, and partly architects) each Land decides for itself. Individual advice (IQ-Beratungsstelle / Fachstelle) is recommended.
Translations must be done by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) in Germany or an equivalent. Translations from an ordinary agency in Russia/Belarus/Ukraine are often not accepted.
Keep your originals! Many chambers return certified copies (beglaubigte Kopien) but keep the originals for a while. Make duplicates in the issuing country in advance.
