title: Recognition grant (Anerkennungszuschuss)
tldr: The recognition grant (Anerkennungszuschuss) covers the costs of the recognition procedure (Anerkennung): fees, translations, expert assessments (procedure costs, Verfahrenskosten, up to 600€), as well as a qualification analysis (Qualifikationsanalyse) of up to 1 200€ and adaptation training (Anpassungsqualifizierung) of up to 3 000€. From 1 January 2025 the income threshold has been raised to 32 000€/year for single people and 50 000€ for those jointly assessed (gemeinsam veranlagt). From 2025 the programme is funded by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (Bundesministerium für Arbeit und Soziales, BMAS) and the EU via ESF Plus; applications are processed by f-bb; you submit the application via anerkennung-in-deutschland.de BEFORE paying any invoices.

steps.title: What it is and who is eligible

content.text: The recognition grant (Anerkennungszuschuss) is a one-off grant from a federal programme that covers the costs of the procedure to recognise a foreign professional qualification. The programme has run since 2016; from 1 January 2025 it continues on new terms and is funded by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (Bundesministerium für Arbeit und Soziales, BMAS) together with the EU via ESF Plus. The central body that processes applications is f-bb (Forschungsinstitut Betriebliche Bildung).

The grant is not a loan; you do not have to repay it. The procedure costs themselves (Verfahrenskosten) are covered up to a maximum of 600€; the qualification analysis (Qualifikationsanalyse) — up to 1 200€; adaptation training (Anpassungsqualifizierung) — up to 3 000€. What you can spend it on: chamber fees, certified translations (beglaubigte Übersetzungen), notarised copies, travel to examinations, study literature, and the apostille (Apostille).

items: Procedure costs (Verfahrenskosten) — up to 600€; qualification analysis (Qualifikationsanalyse) — up to 1 200€; adaptation training (Anpassungsqualifizierung) — up to 3 000€ per person
Taxable income (zu versteuerndes Einkommen) from 2025 — no more than 32 000€/year for a single person and 50 000€ for those jointly assessed (gemeinsam veranlagt)
Age and nationality do not matter
You must have a right of residence (Aufenthaltsrecht) in Germany (any residence permit, Aufenthaltstitel) OR an application filed from abroad with a concrete plan to move
The same person can receive the grant again for adaptation training (Anpassungsqualifizierung) after the first decision (Bescheid)

content.text: Apply BEFORE paying any invoices! The recognition grant (Anerkennungszuschuss) is NOT reimbursed retroactively — grants are awarded only for costs not yet paid. This is the most common mistake.

items: Application form (Antragsformular) — download it from anerkennung-in-deutschland.de
Financial plan: a list of costs with amounts (fee, translation, travel)
Proof of income: a tax assessment (Steuerbescheid) for the last year OR an income statement + a wage tax certificate (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung)
Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — a copy
A letter from the competent authority (zuständige Stelle): confirmation that the recognition procedure (Anerkennung) has started or is about to start

content.text: Apply via the portal anerkennung-in-deutschland.de or directly to f-bb (Forschungsinstitut Betriebliche Bildung) — the central body that processes applications. You can also go through the free advice service of the IQ-Netzwerk — they will help you fill it in and gather the documents.
The decision comes within 4-6 weeks. The approval notice (Bewilligungsbescheid) states the specific amount and the deadline by which you must spend the money (usually 12 months).

items: You pay the costs from your own account
You collect the original invoices and proofs of payment (Zahlungsnachweise)
You send them to f-bb
The money is transferred to your bank account within 4-8 weeks

content.text: If your income does not qualify or you need a larger amount:

items: An education voucher (Bildungsgutschein) from the employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit) — for the unemployed or recipients of unemployment benefit (ALG); it covers adaptation courses (Anpassungskurse)
AFBG (upgrade grant, Aufstiegs-BAföG) — for the master/specialist track (Meister/Fachwirt), up to 15 000€
A scholarship from the Deutschlandstipendium programme — for students
Land level: some Länder (NRW, BW, Hessen) have their own grants, of up to 1000-1500€
The job centre (Jobcenter) — payment for language courses (Sprachkurse) and further training (Fortbildung) if you receive basic income support (Bürgergeld)

content.text: With joint taxation (gemeinsam veranlagt), the spouses' combined taxable income (zu versteuerndes Einkommen) is taken into account. If your spouse earns well, the grant may be refused even if you yourself are out of work.

The grant does not cover language courses (Sprachkurse) or preparation for the professional language examination (Fachsprachprüfung). Those costs go through an education voucher (Bildungsgutschein) or the job centre (Job-Center).

The grant covers the costs of fees and translations regardless of the outcome of the procedure. But the costs of an appeal (objection, Widerspruch) or of resubmitting after a refusal are, as a rule, not covered.

From 1 January 2025 the programme continues on new terms. Applications to take part are accepted until 30 June 2027, and payment claims until 30 September 2028. The terms and thresholds change from time to time — check the current status before applying. Individual advice (IQ-Beratungsstelle / Fachstelle) is recommended.

costs.label: Anerkennungszuschuss grant
costs.note: Verfahrenskosten up to 600€; Qualifikationsanalyse up to 1 200€; Anpassungsqualifizierung up to 3 000€

costs.label: Your own share at the maximum amount
costs.note: If costs are ≤ 600€ — the grant covers everything

costs.label: Bildungsgutschein (for the unemployed)
costs.note: Covers Anpassungskurse and part of the retraining; no 600€ cap

title: Architect: the Chamber of Architects (Architektenkammer)
tldr: To call yourself an "Architekt" in Germany and to sign a building application (Bauantrag), you need an entry in the architects' register (Eintragung in the Architektenliste) of the Land where you work (a protected professional title, geschützte Berufsbezeichnung). Architectural law is different in each Land (BauKaG NRW, BayBauKaG, etc.). Required: an architecture degree (at least 4 years) + 2 years of practice. The cost is 100-500€ + annual fees of 300-700€. The procedure takes about 3-6 months. Conditions vary by Land — individual advice at the Chamber of Architects (Architektenkammer) is recommended.

content.text: In Germany, architect (Architekt) is a protected professional title (geschützte Berufsbezeichnung). To officially call yourself an architect, to sign a building application (Bauantrag — an application for a building permit) or to lead projects, you need an entry in the architects' register (Eintragung in the Architektenliste) of the Land where you work.

Regulation is at the Land level: BayArchG (Bavaria), BauKaG NRW (North Rhine-Westphalia), HArchG (Hesse), etc. The Federal Chamber of Architects (Bundes-Architektenkammer, BAK) coordinates, but the decisions are made by the Land chambers (LAK).

items: Without an entry in the register (Eintragung) you cannot work as an architect (Architekt) or sign a building application (Bauantrag)
You can work as a civil engineer (Bauingenieur), a designer (Entwurfsverfasser) or an employee (Mitarbeiter) of an architecture firm — without an entry in the register
An entry in the register (Eintragung) grants the right to submit building designs (bauvorlageberechtigung)
The profession is recognised under the EU directive on the recognition of professional qualifications (EU-Berufsanerkennungs-Richtlinie) 2005/36/EG; for non-EU nationals — an individual route
An entry in the register (Eintragung) is a prerequisite for being subject to the HOAI (the fee scale for design work)

steps.title: Requirements for an entry in the register (Eintragung)

content.text: The conditions are broadly the same across all Länder, but the details differ.

items: A higher education degree (Studienabschluss) in architecture — with a standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit) of at least 4 years
A bachelor of architecture (3 years) is often not enough — usually at least 4 years of study are required (Bachelor + Master or Diplom)
It must be in the field of "architecture" (Architektur), not civil engineering (Bauingenieurwesen) or interior design (Innenarchitektur) — those have separate chambers
The university must be H+ in Anabin (see the separate guide)
At least 2 years of practice under the supervision of an architect entered in the register (eingetragene Architektin/Architekt)
In Germany or in an EU/third country — but the experience must be documented
Areas: design planning (Entwurfsplanung), site management (Bauleitung), planning for approval (Genehmigungsplanung)
Proof — activity certificates (Tätigkeitsnachweise) / references from employers (Arbeitszeugnisse) describing the tasks and hours
Some Länder (Bayern) accept practice logged online via the Architects' Council of Europe

content.text: From the moment you are entered in the register (Eintragung) you are required to undertake annual continuing professional development (Fortbildung, 8-16 hours/year). Courses are run by the Land chamber (LAK) or external institutes. This is a condition for keeping your membership.

You apply to the Chamber of Architects (Architektenkammer) of the Land where your main place of work (Hauptsitz) or place of residence (Wohnsitz) is located. If you work in NRW but live in RLP, you usually apply at the place of work. An entry in the register (Eintragung) in one Land is, as a rule, recognised in the others, but when you move you need a re-registration (Umtragung) with the relevant Land chamber (LAK).

items: Application for entry in the architects' register (Antrag auf Eintragung in die Architektenliste)
Certified copy (beglaubigte Kopie) of the degree + transcript
Certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) into German
An extract from Anabin (Anabin-Auszug, printout) or a university assessment from the ZAB (ZAB-Bewertung)
Activity certificates (Tätigkeitsnachweise) for 2 years of practice
CV (Lebenslauf) in German
Police clearance certificate (Führungszeugnis)
Passport copy + registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Proof that you have taken out professional liability insurance (Anmeldung der Berufshaftpflichtversicherung)

content.text: For degrees from third countries, if substantial differences (wesentliche Unterschiede) are found, the registration committee (Eintragungsausschuss) may impose an adaptation course (Anpassungslehrgang) OR an aptitude examination (Eignungsprüfung) — an examination on German building law, the HOAI, and the contract for work under the BGB (BGB-Werkvertrag). Under §15 BQFG the right to choose between the course and the examination usually lies with the applicant, but the details depend on the Land's architects' act (Architektengesetz) and the chamber's decision.

After a positive decision you are entered in the architects' register (Architektenliste). You receive a membership card (Mitgliedsausweis) and the right to use the title Architekt/Architektin. You pay a registration fee (Eintragungsgebühr, 100-500€) + the first annual contribution.
The entry in the register (Eintragung) is a one-off payment. The membership contribution (Mitgliedsbeitrag) is annual and usually depends on income.

items: ByAK (Bavaria): registration about 250€, annual contribution 290-790€ by income
AKNW (NRW): registration about 350€, annual contribution 350-690€
Chamber of Architects of Berlin (Architektenkammer Berlin): registration about 200€, annual contribution 300-580€
Professional pension fund (Versorgungswerk — the architects' pension fund): a separate contribution of ~18.6% of income (as with the pension insurance, DRV, for most people)
Professional liability insurance (Berufshaftpflichtversicherung): 300-1000€/year (depends on turnover)

content.text: If your degree is "Architecture" with 4 years of study under the Soviet/post-Soviet system, it usually passes. But "Design of the architectural environment" or "Urban planning" may not be recognised as architecture (Architektur) — they fall under urban planners (Stadtplaner) or interior designers (Innenarchitekt).

An entry in the register (Eintragung) is tied to the Land. If you move, you formally need to file a re-registration (Umtragung) with another Land chamber (LAK); the fee is usually small, but the procedure exists.

Without an entry in the register (Eintragung) you cannot sign a building application (Bauantrag), but you can work at a private firm as an "Architekt im Praktikum" or "Mitarbeiter" — at a salary 20-30% lower.

Professional liability insurance (Berufshaftpflicht) starts from the moment of entry in the register (Eintragung). If you are an employee, the firm insures you. If you are a freelancer, you must take it out yourself; without it you will not be entered in the register, or your entry will be suspended.

title: Belarusian degree: the specifics
tldr: Almost all Belarusian state universities (BSU, BNTU, BSUIR, etc.) have an H+ status in Anabin. Specialist degrees (5 years) are equated to a Master, a bachelor (4 years) — to a Bachelor. The main difficulty is the apostille (Apostille) in Belarus (issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ~1 base unit, an in-person visit or a power of attorney) and translations by a sworn translator in Germany. Since 2022 some consular services for Belarusian citizens abroad have been restricted — plan to obtain your documents in advance.

steps.title: What you need to know about Belarusian degrees

content.text: Belarus signed the Hague Apostille Convention in 1992, so a Belarusian degree is legalised through an apostille (Apostille) rather than a consular chain. Most state universities in Belarus are listed in Anabin with an H+ status. This means the degree is recognised as full higher education in Germany.
The Belarusian education system: bachelor (4 years) ≈ Bachelor, specialist (5 years, mostly until 2013) ≈ Diplom (Univ.) / Master, master (1-2 years after the bachelor) ≈ Master.

items: BSU, BNTU, BSUIR, BSEU, BSPU — all H+ in Anabin
State regional universities (Skaryna GSU, BrSU, GrSU) — usually H+
Non-state/commercial ones (MIU, IPD, BIP) — often H+/- or H-
Degrees from before 1991 (BSSR) are rated against the Soviet table, usually H+
Degrees after 2013 — the Bologna system, easier to map to Bachelor/Master

content.text: Obtaining documents and an apostille (Apostille) remotely from Belarus is possible but difficult. Since 2022 some services require personal presence. Plan a trip or a notarised power of attorney.

items.title: 1. Get a duplicate of the degree and the supplement

items: If the originals are lost or left at home, the university issues a duplicate; the timeframe is 1-3 months
A duplicate marked "Duplicate" is suitable for qualification recognition (Anerkennung)
The cost of a duplicate — 1-3 base units (~15-50€)
It can be done by power of attorney through a relative or acquaintance

items.title: 2. Apostille (Apostille) at the Belarusian Ministry of Foreign Affairs

items: Main Consular Directorate of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minsk, 19 Lenina St.
On Belarusian-format degrees the apostille (Apostille) is issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, not the Ministry of Education
Cost: 1 base unit (~18€ in 2026, check this)
Timeframe: 2-5 working days
Filed in person or by a representative with a power of attorney
If the degree is of the Soviet type — sometimes prior certification by the Ministry of Education is needed

content.text: Translations from Belarus (even notarised ones) are often not accepted in Germany. Have the translation done by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) in Germany: 30-80€/page. You can find a list on bdue.de or justiz.de.

items: The Belarusian "certificate of no criminal record" — required for a licence to practise medicine (Approbation), the Chamber of Architects (Architektenkammer) and lawyers
Issued by the Information Centre of the Belarusian Ministry of Internal Affairs, timeframe 5-15 days
Since 2022 — with personal presence or via a Belarusian consulate in the country of residence
In Germany, also request the German police clearance certificate (Führungszeugnis) through the Federal Office of Justice (Bundesamt für Justiz)
An apostille (Apostille) is needed on the certificate too

content.text: The process itself is no different from other countries and is described in the guide "Anerkennung of a degree: where to start". The Belarusian specifics:

items: The ZAB is well acquainted with Belarusian degrees; an official degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) costs 208€, with processing taking on average about 3 months

For regulated professions (doctor, engineer) — the decision (Bescheid) is often "teilweise gleichwertig" (partially equivalent) with a requirement to complete an adaptation course (Anpassungslehrgang)
For IT and industrial engineering — an H+ in Anabin is often enough, and recognition (Anerkennung) is not needed

A specialist degree (5 years) is usually equated to a Master, which opens the way to the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU, §18g AufenthG) if the salary is above the threshold: in 2026 ≈ 50 700€/year for ordinary professions and ≈ 45 934€ for shortage occupations (Engpassberufe)
An IELTS/TOEFL/DSH certificate is not tied to the degree — it is a separate item for the employer

content.text: If your degree is in Belarusian and Russian, a translator in Germany may ask you to specify which language they are translating from. Not all sworn translators (vereidigter Übersetzer) work with Belarusian. Look for a translator for Russian + Belarusian, or have the Russian part translated.

Do not confuse an apostille (Apostille, Hague) with consular legalisation. Some documents (for example, those issued by the Belarusian Armed Forces or the church) cannot be apostilled. Check with the Belarusian Ministry of Foreign Affairs before filing.

Degrees from new private universities in Belarus (opened after 2010) may have an H+/- status in Anabin or be absent altogether. Request an official degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) from the ZAB BEFORE you move, so you do not get a refusal from an employer.

If you changed your surname after obtaining the degree (marriage, divorce), you need to add a marriage/divorce certificate with an apostille (Apostille) and translation. Otherwise the documents may be returned.

title: Professional driving licence (truck, LKW; bus, Bus)
tldr: To work as a truck (LKW) or bus driver in Germany, you need a German driving licence (Führerschein) of class C/CE (trucks) or D/DE (buses) plus the professional driver basic qualification (Berufskraftfahrer-Grundqualifikation) under the BKrFQG. Foreign truck and bus licences are NOT converted automatically — you will have to complete training and examinations at a driving school (Fahrschule). Age: class C from 21 (with the basic qualification, Grundqualifikation, from 18), class D from 24 (with the basic qualification from 21). Total costs — 3000-8000€.

steps.title: What you need to work as a truck/bus driver (LKW/Bus)

content.text: In Germany a professional driving licence is two separate documents. First: a driving licence (Führerschein) of the right class (C for trucks of 7.5+ tonnes, CE for truck+trailer, D for buses, DE with a trailer). Second: the professional driver basic qualification (Berufskraftfahrer-Grundqualifikation) under the Professional Drivers' Qualification Act (Berufskraftfahrer-Qualifikationsgesetz, BKrFQG) — separate vocational training of 140-280 hours.

Regulation: the BKrFQG, the regulation on driving authorisation (Fahrerlaubnis-Verordnung, FeV), and the Passenger Transport Act (Personenbeförderungsgesetz, PBefG) for buses. Oversight and registration — the Federal Office for Logistics and Mobility (Bundesamt für Logistik und Mobilität, BALM, formerly the BAG) and the Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA, Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt).

items: Class C/CE — trucks over 7.5 t
Class D/DE — buses with more than 9 seats
Minimum age (Mindestalter): C — 21 (with the basic qualification, Grundqualifikation, 18), D — 24 (with the basic qualification 21)
The basic qualification (Grundqualifikation) is mandatory for all truck and bus drivers in commercial transport
Continuing training (Weiterbildung) every 5 years — 35 hours, to keep the key code (Schlüsselzahl) 95

content.text: The main point: a passenger-car licence (class B) from a third country can be exchanged for a German one within the first 6 months of your stay (usually with an examination). A truck or bus licence will almost always have to be obtained from scratch.

Class C, CE, D and DE licences from the EU are recognised in full. They are exchanged for a German driving licence (Führerschein) without examinations. But the professional driver basic qualification (Berufskraftfahrer-Grundqualifikation) must be confirmed — if the issuing country has an equivalent key code (Schlüsselzahl) 95, it is recognised.

items: A passenger-car class B licence can be converted (also with an examination — theory + practice)
C/CE/D/DE licences from third countries are NOT converted automatically
You need to obtain a German C/CE/D/DE through a driving school (Fahrschule) — theory + practice
Your foreign experience will be credited as prior licence holding (Vorbesitz) — this lowers the required training hours
Most driving schools (Fahrschulen) offer an "Aufbaukurs" (top-up course) of 30-50 hours instead of the full 90-hour course

content.text: This is a separate programme. There are two options under §4 BKrFQG: the accelerated basic qualification (beschleunigte Grundqualifikation, 140 h of theory + practice) or the full basic qualification (vollständige Grundqualifikation, 350 h + an examination). Timeframe: 2-3 months. Cost: 2500-4000€. A foreign vocational-school diploma (if it covers 280+ hours) is recognised and removes half of the requirements.

items: Medical examination (ärztliche Untersuchung) under §11 FeV — general, with a family doctor (Hausarzt) or a company doctor (Betriebsarzt)
Ophthalmological examination (augenärztliche Untersuchung) under §12 FeV — with an ophthalmologist (Augenarzt)
For class C/D additionally: a test of physical resilience (Untersuchung der Belastbarkeit, a stress test)
Cost: 150-300€ in total
Validity of the certificates — 1 year before submission to the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle)

content.text: A 9-hour first-aid course, mandatory for all licence classes. Cost: 30-50€. Valid indefinitely.

items: Enrol at a driving school (Fahrschule) that specialises in LKW/Bus (not every school does)
Theory: 6-18 double lessons (with a discount for prior licence holding, Vorbesitz, B)
Practice: 5-10 special drives (Sonderfahrten) + general hours (depends on prior licence holding, Vorbesitz)
TÜV/DEKRA — the theory and practical examinations

content.text: In parallel with or after the driving licence (Führerschein) — the basic qualification (Grundqualifikation) at the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) or a certified training centre. After the examination at the IHK you receive a certificate (Bescheinigung); the key code (Schlüsselzahl) 95 is printed on the driving licence.

items.title: 5. Submitting the application (Antrag) to the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle)

content.text: Application + all certificates + the first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe) + a biometric photo + a copy of your passport + a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung). You submit it to the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle, at the district citizens' office, Bürgeramt). Within 4-6 weeks you receive your driving licence (Führerschein).

Under §5 BKrFQG all professional drivers must undergo 35 hours of continuing training every 5 years, otherwise the key code (Schlüsselzahl) 95 will expire and you will not be allowed to work as a driver.

items: 35 h / 5 modules of 7 hours each
Topics: safety, fuel economy, legislation, the transport of dangerous goods
Can be spread over 5 years or compressed into a single week
Cost: 400-800€ for the package
Afterwards — updating the key code (Schlüsselzahl) 95 at the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle)

content.text: Many people think a professional driver (Berufskraftfahrer) = a driving licence (Führerschein). That is not so. Without the basic qualification (Grundqualifikation, key code Schlüsselzahl 95) you cannot work as a driver in commercial transport, even with a C/CE/D/DE licence.

A Russian/Belarusian/Ukrainian diploma from a transport technical college or vocational school (140+ hours of transport theory) can be credited towards part of the basic qualification (Grundqualifikation) — it saves 2000-3000€. Submit an application to the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) for recognition of the prior qualification (Anerkennung der Vorqualifikation).

Age matters. Without the basic qualification (Grundqualifikation) you cannot get behind the wheel of a truck (LKW) before 21, or a bus before 24. With the basic qualification — 18 and 21 respectively. There are no workarounds.

If you are being hired as a driver, the employer may pay for the driving licence (Führerschein) and the basic qualification (Grundqualifikation). This is common in logistics and public transport — ask about it when you are hired.

costs.label: Führerschein C/CE (with Vorbesitz B)
costs.note: Fahrschule + TÜV examinations

costs.label: Führerschein D/DE
costs.note: More expensive due to the additional requirements

costs.label: Berufskraftfahrer-Grundqualifikation
costs.note: 140-350 hours; with a discount for a foreign diploma

costs.label: Medical examination + Augenarzt
costs.note: Under §§11-12 FeV; valid for 1 year

costs.label: Erste-Hilfe-Kurs
costs.note: 9 hours, indefinitely

costs.label: Weiterbildung every 5 years
costs.note: 35 hours, mandatory

title: Engineer: entry in the Chamber of Engineers (Ingenieurkammer)
tldr: In most German Länder the title "Ingenieur" is protected by the Länder's engineering acts (Ingenieurgesetze). You can work in industry (Daimler, Bosch, Siemens) without an entry in the register (Eintragung) — the position is called skilled worker (Fachkraft), development engineer (Entwicklungsingenieur), etc. But for an engineer with the right to submit building designs (bauvorlageberechtigter Ingenieur), or for a freelancer — a consulting engineer (Beratender Ingenieur) — you need an entry in the register of the Land's Chamber of Engineers (Ingenieurkammer). The cost is 50-200€ + an annual contribution of 100-400€. You need an engineering degree (at least 4 years) with an H+ status in Anabin.

steps.title: Is the title of engineer (Ingenieur) protected

content.text: Almost every Land has its own engineering act (Ingenieurgesetz). Under it, "Ingenieur" is a protected professional title (geschützte Berufsbezeichnung): using the title without a legal basis is prohibited and punishable (as an administrative offence, Ordnungswidrigkeit, under Land law; assuming protected titles may also fall under §132a StGB). The basis for the title is an engineering degree, and in a number of Länder additionally an entry in the register (Eintragung) with the chamber.

In industry (corporations, mechanical engineering, IT, chemistry) you can work with a foreign degree without an entry in the register (Eintragung), via an H+ in Anabin. This profession is non-regulated (nicht-reglementiert) in the sense of the BQFG. The employer assesses the degree itself.
An entry in the register (Eintragung) with the Chamber of Engineers (Ingenieurkammer) is mandatory for:

items: An engineer with the right to submit building designs (bauvorlageberechtigter Ingenieur) — the right to sign off building designs (structural calculations, Statik; site management, Bauleitung)
A consulting engineer (Beratender Ingenieur) — a status for freelancers, analogous to an architect (Architekt)
An expert engineer (Sachverständige Ingenieur) — court expert assessments, a certified expert (geprüfter Sachverständiger)
A structural inspection engineer (Prüfingenieur für Standsicherheit) and so on
A tunnel designer (Tunnelplaner), a structural designer (Tragwerksplaner) — separate additional entries in the register (Eintragungen)

content.text: It depends on your goal. The key distinction:

items: An engineering degree + H+ in Anabin = enough
Qualification recognition (Anerkennung) is formally NOT needed
The employer looks at your CV, degree and experience, and checks the H+ in Anabin
For the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU, §18g AufenthG) only an H+ is needed
You can be employed as an "Ingenieur" under your employment contract, but not as a consulting engineer (Beratender Ingenieur)

items.title: Option B: Entry in the register (Eintragung) with the chamber (Kammer)

items: A 4+ year degree in an engineering field (civil engineering, Bauingenieurwesen; mechanical engineering, Maschinenbau; electrical engineering, Elektrotechnik; etc.)
H+ in Anabin or an individual degree assessment from the ZAB (Zeugnisbewertung)
Submission to the Chamber of Engineers (Ingenieurkammer) of the relevant Land
For the right to submit building designs (bauvorlageberechtigter) — additionally 2 years of practice under the supervision of an engineer entered in the register (eingetragener Ingenieur)
Cost of the entry in the register (Eintragung): 50-200€; annual contribution 100-400€

items.title: Option C: A degree assessment from the ZAB (Zeugnisbewertung, without working)

content.text: If you want an official document confirming your degree (for example, for the Blue Card, Blaue Karte, or for an employer who is not familiar with Anabin), order an official degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) from the ZAB. It costs 208€, takes 3 months, and you receive a certificate (Bescheinigung) in German.

steps.title: Entry in the register (Eintragung) with the Chamber of Engineers (Ingenieurkammer)

content.text: Each Land has a Chamber of Civil Engineers (Ingenieurkammer-Bau — for civil engineers), and often chambers for other disciplines too. They are coordinated by the Federal Chamber of Engineers (Bundesingenieurkammer, BIngK). You apply in the Land where your main place of business (Hauptsitz) or place of residence (Wohnsitz) is located.

items: Application for entry in the register (Antrag auf Eintragung)
Certified copy (beglaubigte Kopie) of the degree + transcript
Certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) into German
An extract from Anabin (Anabin-Auszug) or an assessment from the ZAB (ZAB-Bewertung)
CV (Lebenslauf) in German
Activity certificates (Tätigkeitsnachweise) for 2 years of practice (for the right to submit building designs, bauvorlageberechtigter)
Police clearance certificate (Führungszeugnis)
Passport + registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)

content.text: The timeframe is about 2-4 months. There are three possible outcomes: entry in the register (Eintragung) without conditions; entry with a requirement to close substantial differences (wesentliche Unterschiede) through an adaptation course (Anpassungslehrgang) or an aptitude examination (Eignungsprüfung); or a refusal with the right to object (Widerspruch). The specific decision is at the chamber's discretion — individual advice (IQ-Beratungsstelle / Fachstelle) is recommended.

items: Registration fee (Eintragungsgebühr): 50-200€ (depends on the Land)
Annual membership contribution (Mitgliedsbeitrag): 100-400€ (depends on income and the chamber)
Professional pension fund (Versorgungswerk): in some Länder there is a separate pension fund for engineers (contributions of around 18,6% of income)
Professional liability insurance (Berufshaftpflichtversicherung, for freelancers): 300-800€/year
Continuing professional development (Fortbildung): 8-16 hours/year, through the chamber (Kammer) or external institutes

content.text: Do not confuse "Diplom-Ingenieur (FH)" and "Bachelor of Engineering": in German documents the wording of the title is stated precisely. A post-Soviet specialist degree (5 years) is usually mapped to Diplom (Univ.), and a bachelor's degree (4 years) to the Bachelor level; the exact correspondence is determined by Anabin or an official degree assessment from the ZAB (Zeugnisbewertung).

If your university is NOT in Anabin, or has an H- status, do not give up right away — some employers in IT accept a portfolio + experience without formal recognition (Anerkennung). But for the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU, §18g) and for an entry in the register (Eintragung) with the chamber, an H+ is mandatory.

The professions of "technologist" or "mechanic" (without an engineering degree) are not an engineer (Ingenieur) but a skilled worker (Facharbeiter). They go through IHK FOSA / the Chamber of Skilled Crafts (HWK), not through the Chamber of Engineers (Ingenieurkammer).

Expert status (Sachverständige) is a separate certification obtained after the entry in the register (Eintragung). Without it you cannot act as a sworn court expert (gerichtlich beeidigter Sachverständiger). It requires a course + examination at the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK), ~2000-4000€.

title: Fachsprachprüfung: medical German
tldr: Fachsprachprüfung (FSP) is the mandatory medical-German exam required to obtain a medical licence (Approbation). On top of general German at level B2, it tests specialised medical vocabulary at level C1. Structure: a patient interview, writing an Arztbrief, and presenting a case to a colleague (about 60 minutes in total). The fee charged by the state medical association (Landesärztekammer) is 350-450€. No FSP means no Approbation, and without Approbation you cannot work as a doctor. Preparation usually takes 3-6 months.

content.text: The Fachsprachprüfung Medizin (FSP) is the profession-specific German-language exam for doctors, run by the state medical associations (Landesärztekammern). It is NOT TestDaF and NOT a Goethe-Zertifikat. Its structure and content are standardised by the Bundesärztekammer's "Eckpunktepapier" of 2014/2017, but it is administered by the states (BLÄK, ÄKWL, ÄKNo and others).

The goal is to check whether a doctor can safely communicate with patients and colleagues in German. Without proof of your language skills there is no Approbation under §3 Bundesärzteordnung (BÄO); as a rule you need general German at level B2 plus medical Fachsprache (specialised language) at level C1. Without an Approbation you cannot work as a doctor at all, except in a limited way under supervision and on the basis of a temporary permit to practise (Berufserlaubnis).

items: Level: general German B2 + medical Fachsprache at level C1
Duration: 60 minutes (3 parts of 20 minutes each)
Taken at the state medical association (Landesärztekammer) of the state where you will apply for the licence (Approbation)
Cost: 350-450€ (depends on the state)
Validity: indefinite once you pass
Alternative in some states: telc Deutsch Medizin B2-C1 (telc.net)

content.text: The exam has three parts separated by short breaks. It simulates a real working day.

items: Conversation with a "patient" (an actor or examiner)
Gather complaints, medical history, allergies, medication, social history
Use plain language — NO medical terms with the patient
Take notes
Finish with a polite summary and an explanation of the next steps
Write a structured letter to a colleague based on the results of the Anamnese
Structure: Anamnese → Diagnose (presumed) → Therapie/Prozedere
Use medical terminology CORRECTLY (in Latin/German)
By hand, on paper, without a dictionary
Grammar and spelling are graded
Present the case to a senior colleague (the examiner)
Dialogue: your diagnosis, the reasoning, the plan for examination and treatment
Expect questions — you must be able to defend your plan
Full medical terminology is used
Logic and medical knowledge are assessed, not just language

content.text: Without a solid C1 (Goethe-Zertifikat C1 or telc Deutsch C1) it makes no sense to sit the FSP. Do Goethe/telc first, then the medical part. The most successful candidates tend to be those who have lived in Germany for at least 6-12 months.

items: telc Deutsch B2-C1 Medizin — a structured course/textbook
Inlingua, Goethe-Institut — they offer dedicated FSP courses (1000-3000€)
Charité International Academy (Berlin), Asklepios — clinical courses for doctors
Online: DocCheck, AMBOSS (German medical knowledge platform), Mediscript
Books: "Deutsch für Ärztinnen und Ärzte" (Springer), "Mündliche Prüfung Medizin" (Thieme)
A clinical placement in a hospital (Hospitation/Praktikum) — observing ward rounds (Visite) and talking to patients
Stammtisch for migrant doctors (available in larger cities)
Paid FSP simulations with native-speaker doctors (200-400€ for 4-5 sessions)
YouTube: the "Deutsch für Ärzte" channels, FSP-Vorbereitung

content.text: You book at the Landesärztekammer of the region where you intend to apply for the Approbation. The queue in the larger states (Bayern, BW, NRW) is 3-6 months. Submit your application as soon as your C1 is ready.

Grading: bestanden / nicht bestanden. If you fail (nicht bestanden), you can retake it, usually after 3-6 months, paying again. The number of retakes is not limited (unlike the knowledge exam, the Kenntnisprüfung, which allows only 3 attempts).

items: Results are usually given right after the exam
You receive a certificate (Bescheinigung) — valid indefinitely
The certificate is submitted to the state authority (Landesbehörde) together with the licence application (Approbations-Antrag)
Some states accept telc Deutsch C1 Medizin or a Goethe-Zertifikat + an additional test
A certificate from private providers (Charité, telc) is not accepted in every state — check first

content.text: The main reason for failure is underestimating the medical vocabulary. General C1 alone is not the same as the FSP. Anatomie, Symptome, Erkrankungen, Medikamente, lab values — all in German. Prepare specifically.
The second reason is failing to switch register: plain language with the patient, technical terminology with the colleague. Practise both registers.

Don't confuse the FSP and the Kenntnisprüfung: the FSP tests language, the Kenntnisprüfung tests medical knowledge at the level of the German Staatsexamen. Doctors from third countries usually need both exams, unless their education is recognised as fully equivalent.

The state matters. An FSP passed in one state is recognised in the others, but the Landesbehörde may ask for an additional document. Sit it in the state where you will apply for the Approbation to save yourself the bureaucracy.

A certificate (Bescheinigung) of German level from a language school (not from the medical association, Ärztekammer) does NOT replace the FSP. Only an official certificate from the association or telc Medizin (where accepted) counts.

title: IT professionals: recognition not needed
tldr: The main piece of good news for IT specialists: the profession of programmer, developer or administrator is NOT regulated in Germany (kein reglementierter Beruf). This means that formal recognition of qualifications (Anerkennung) under the BQFG is NOT required in order to work in IT — the employer decides for itself whether you are a good fit, and you can work with no relevant degree at all, on experience alone. This is critically important for migration: under §19c Abs. 2 AufenthG combined with §6 BeschV, IT specialists with proven experience (at least 2 years within the last 5) can obtain a residence permit even WITHOUT a degree and without a mandatory German-language proof. Recognition is only useful in two cases: (1) for the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) you usually need a recognised/comparable degree OR proven IT experience; (2) to help the employer assess your foreign degree, an official evaluation of the foreign degree (Zeugnisbewertung) from the ZAB (Central Office for Foreign Education) can help — this is NOT mandatory recognition but a statement of comparability.

steps.title: Why IT is an unregulated profession

content.text: In Germany professions are split into regulated (reglementiert — doctor, lawyer, teacher, nurse) and unregulated. For regulated ones you need official recognition of your qualification (Anerkennung) just to be allowed to work at all. IT (Softwareentwickler, DevOps, Data Scientist, Sysadmin, QA etc.) is NOT among the regulated ones.

items: IT professions are not regulated — there is no mandatory degree recognition under the BQFG
The employer assesses the candidate's qualifications and experience itself
You can work without a relevant degree — on the basis of experience and skills
No "licence to practise the profession" (Berufszulassung) is required for IT
This drastically simplifies entering the job market compared with doctors/nurses

content.text: Don't confuse recognition of the profession with recognition of the degree for migration. The IT work itself requires no recognition, but for some types of residence permit (see below) you still need either a recognised/comparable degree or proven experience. These are different things.

steps.title: What you need for a residence permit: the Blue Card and experience

content.text: Although the work itself requires no recognition, migration law (AufenthG) sets its own requirements. The good news: the reform of the Skilled Immigration Act (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz) greatly simplified the path specifically for IT.

items: Usually requires a recognised or comparable university degree + a salary above the threshold
For IT specialists WITHOUT a degree, a Blue Card is possible with proven experience
Experience requirement in IT: at least 2 years, gained within the last 5 (§6 BeschV)

For shortage occupations and certain categories the Blue Card salary threshold is lower than the general one; the general mandatory German-language requirement for the §19c Abs. 2 + §6 BeschV route has been abolished (language proof is required only in justified individual cases)
§19c Abs. 2 + §6 BeschV: a residence permit for IT specialists with practical experience (2 years within the last 5) without a degree
the opportunity card (Chancenkarte) — a points-based visa for finding work
For degree holders — the standard route for a skilled worker with an academic qualification (Fachkraft mit akademischer Ausbildung)
An employer + a sufficient salary matter more than formal recognition

steps.title: When a Zeugnisbewertung (ZAB) is useful after all

content.text: Although there is no mandatory recognition, it is sometimes worth "translating your foreign degree into German terms". For that there is the Zeugnisbewertung from the ZAB (Zentralstelle für ausländisches Bildungswesen) — not recognition, but an official statement of what your degree corresponds to in the German system.

items: First check your university/degree in anabin (anabin.kmk.org), the database for the recognition of foreign degrees — it's free
If your university is in anabin with status H+, the degree is usually recognised as comparable
A Zeugnisbewertung from the ZAB is a paid statement of comparability (helps with the Blue Card and with the employer)
This is NOT mandatory recognition (BQFG) — not needed for the IT work itself
Useful for salary negotiations and for making your CV more convincing

content.text: Don't waste time or money on full "degree recognition" for IT work — as a mandatory procedure for this profession, it simply does not exist. Focus on checking your university in anabin and, if needed, on a Zeugnisbewertung for migration purposes.

title: The knowledge exam (Kenntnisprüfung) for doctors
tldr: The Kenntnisprüfung (KP) is a state knowledge exam taken by doctors from third countries when their foreign medical education is recognised as NOT fully equivalent to the German one (no full equivalence of qualification, Gleichwertigkeit). It is the route to a full medical licence (Approbation). The exam tests the level of a graduate of a German medical faculty (Stand des deutschen Staatsexamens): internal medicine, surgery and related subjects plus German medical law; it is held in an oral-practical format (mündlich-praktisch) that includes an examination with a patient. Before the KP you need: proof of German (as a rule B2 general + C1 medical / Fachsprachprüfung), often a temporary permit to practise the profession (Berufserlaubnis) during preparation, and documents submitted to the state's Approbationsbehörde. The number of attempts is limited (as a rule, no more than three). An alternative to the exam is an adaptation course (Anpassungslehrgang), but for non-EU doctors the KP is usually the main route.

content.text: The Approbationsbehörde first compares your education with the German one. If it is recognised as fully equivalent, no KP is needed and you go straight to the Approbation. If substantial differences (wesentliche Unterschiede) are found, they can be closed either through the knowledge exam (Kenntnisprüfung) or through an adaptation period. For doctors from third countries the KP is the most common route.

items: Full equivalence (Gleichwertigkeit) — no KP needed, straight to the licence (Approbation)
Substantial differences (wesentliche Unterschiede) — a choice between the exam (Kenntnisprüfung) and an adaptation course (Anpassungslehrgang)
For non-EU doctors the KP is the more common requirement
The KP tests the level of the German Staatsexamen (a medical-faculty graduate)
Passing the KP leads to a full licence (Approbation), not to a temporary permit (Berufserlaubnis)

steps.title: What you need BEFORE the exam: language and documents

content.text: You will not be admitted to the Kenntnisprüfung without meeting the prerequisites. The main ones are language and an application with documents submitted to the state's Approbationsbehörde. Often a temporary permit to practise (Berufserlaubnis) is issued for the preparation period — the right to work as a doctor under supervision.

items: General German at level B2 (in most states)
Medical Fachsprache at level C1 — the Fachsprachprüfung at the Ärztekammer
The Fachsprachprüfung is taken BEFORE, or in parallel with, admission to the KP
Without proof of language you will get neither an Approbation nor a Berufserlaubnis
Diploma and the transcript with grades (certified translations by a sworn translator)
Proof of medical activity / curriculum
Certificate of good standing and a health certificate
Application to the Approbationsbehörde of the exact state where you will work
Often — a temporary permit to practise (Berufserlaubnis) for the duration of KP preparation

steps.title: Content and format of the Kenntnisprüfung

content.text: The KP is an oral-practical exam (mündlich-praktisch), close to a real clinical situation. The board checks whether you are ready to work independently and safely as a doctor in Germany at the level of a German medical-faculty graduate.

items: Main blocks: Innere Medizin and Chirurgie (internal medicine and surgery)
Additionally — related subjects at the state's discretion
Mandatory: German medical law, pharmacology, radiation protection, emergency care
The patient part: taking the history, examination, making a diagnosis, treatment plan
Duration: usually several hours, before a board of several doctors

content.text: The number of attempts is limited: as a rule the KP can be retaken twice (3 attempts in total). Once these are used up, obtaining an Approbation in Germany becomes extremely difficult. Prepare seriously — there are dedicated preparation courses (KP-Vorbereitungskurse). Don't confuse the KP with the Fachsprachprüfung: these are two DIFFERENT exams. Individual counselling (IQ-Beratungsstelle / Fachstelle) is recommended.

costs.label: Kenntnisprüfung (exam fee)
costs.note: Depends on the state; retakes are paid for again.

costs.label: Fachsprachprüfung (medical German)
costs.note: Ärztekammer fee; separate from the KP.

costs.label: KP preparation courses (optional)
costs.note: KP-Vorbereitungskurse; greatly improve your chances of passing.

title: Lawyers: can you work in the field
tldr: Becoming a German lawyer (Rechtsanwalt) with a foreign degree is almost impossible without a German legal education: full admission (Anwaltszulassung) requires two Staatsexamen and a Referendariat. But you can work in the legal field. Lawyers from the EU/EEA register as a niedergelassener europäischer Rechtsanwalt and, after 3 years of practising German law, can obtain full status. Everyone else can advise on the law of their home country and on international law, work in in-house legal departments, compliance and legal tech. Practising German law proper is only possible via the Staatsexamen.

content.text: The profession of Rechtsanwalt is strictly regulated in Germany. The classic path is long: law faculty, the Erstes Staatsexamen, then the Referendariat (a two-year practical traineeship in courts, the prosecution service, law firms and the administration) and the Zweites Staatsexamen. Only after that is a person considered a Volljurist and can obtain the Anwaltszulassung — admission by the bar association (Rechtsanwaltskammer).

A foreign law degree by itself does not give the right to work as a German lawyer and is not equated with the Staatsexamen. You cannot "recognise" a foreign law degree as a German one the way it is done for doctors: the system is built on German state exams.

items: A lawyer (Rechtsanwalt) is a regulated profession with admission (Zulassung)
You need two Staatsexamen and a Referendariat (Volljurist status)
A foreign degree is not directly equated with the Staatsexamen
Admission is granted by the Rechtsanwaltskammer of the relevant district
This is about German legal practice; you can work "in law" in other ways

steps.title: Lawyers from the EU: niedergelassener europäischer Rechtsanwalt

content.text: For lawyers from EU/EEA countries there is a special, easier path under the EuRAG. If you already hold lawyer status in your EU country, you can register in Germany as a niedergelassener europäischer Rechtsanwalt and practise under your home professional title.

items: Available to lawyers from EU/EEA countries under the EuRAG
Registration with a German Rechtsanwaltskammer under your home title
You can advise on German law and represent clients
After ~3 years of effective and regular practice of German law — full status
Alternatively — pass the aptitude exam (Eignungsprüfung) for admission

content.text: After at least three years of effective and regular activity in the field of German law, a European lawyer can be admitted as a German Rechtsanwalt without the Staatsexamen. For those who want full status sooner, the EuRAG offers the Eignungsprüfung — an exam on professional aptitude in German law. The decision on admission is made by the association on the basis of its own assessment, so check the exact requirements for proof of practice with your Rechtsanwaltskammer in advance.

steps.title: Lawyers from outside the EU: where to work

content.text: If you are not from the EU, the only path into German legal practice runs through a German legal education and the Staatsexamen. But the legal market is broad, and most roles do not require Rechtsanwalt status.

You can register and advise on the law of your country of origin and on public international law (the Rechtsanwaltskammer keeps a register of such activity in foreign law). This is in demand at international firms that serve clients from your region.

Company legal departments, compliance, contract management, data protection (GDPR), legal operations and legal-tech startups are happy to hire lawyers with a foreign education: formal lawyer admission is not needed there, and knowledge and languages are valued.

A German LL.M. helps strengthen your position: a master's in German or European law gives you knowledge of the system, the language and a network, although it does not by itself replace the Staatsexamen or grant admission.

items: Lawyer from the EU → register under the EuRAG as a europäischer Rechtsanwalt
Want full status from the EU quickly → sit the Eignungsprüfung
Lawyer from outside the EU → advising on foreign law + in-house/compliance
Full German legal practice from third countries → only via the Staatsexamen
Strengthening your profile → an LL.M. in German law and strong German

content.text: German at C1–C2 level is critical almost everywhere: legal work is all about language. For unregulated legal roles (compliance, legal tech) you can, if you wish, get an official evaluation of your degree (Zeugnisbewertung) from the ZAB (Central Office for Foreign Education; about 208 €) so that your education is clearer to the employer, although formally this is not required. If you are unsure which route to take, the IQ-Beratungsstelle and the Rechtsanwaltskammer itself offer free advice.

title: Medical licence (Approbation)
tldr: The medical licence (Approbation) is a full and indefinite state licence granting the right to work as a doctor in Germany independently and without restriction (the basis is §3 Bundesärzteordnung, BÄO). Without it, a doctor can only work under a temporary permit to practise (Berufserlaubnis) that is limited in time and place and requires supervision. The path to the Approbation for a doctor from a third country: (1) submit an application to the state's Approbationsbehörde, which compares the education (Gleichwertigkeitsprüfung); (2) prove your language — general B2 plus medical C1 (Fachsprachprüfung); (3) in case of incomplete equivalence, sit the knowledge exam (Kenntnisprüfung) or complete an adaptation course (Anpassungslehrgang); (4) prove good standing and health. For EU/EEA citizens, education is more often recognised automatically under Directive 2005/36/EG. The Approbation is issued by a specific state, but it is valid throughout Germany.

content.text: The key thing to understand from the very start: the Approbation is a full and indefinite licence, while the temporary permit (Berufserlaubnis) is limited in time. Many foreign doctors start on a Berufserlaubnis while they work towards recognition, but the ultimate goal is the Approbation.

items: Approbation: indefinite, without restriction, throughout Germany (§3 BÄO)
Berufserlaubnis: limited in time and place, work under supervision (§10 BÄO)
A Berufserlaubnis is convenient while preparing for the Kenntnisprüfung
Only the licence (Approbation) gives the right to your own practice (Niederlassung) and full independence
The Approbation is issued by a state, but it is valid throughout the country

steps.title: The path to the Approbation: steps

content.text: The procedure depends on the country of the diploma. For the EU/EEA — simplified automatic recognition under Directive 2005/36/EG. For third countries — an individual equivalence check and, if necessary, an exam.

items: Education from the EU is usually recognised automatically (Directive 2005/36/EG)
You need language, and certificates of good standing and health
A Kenntnisprüfung is, as a rule, not required
Submission to the state's Approbationsbehörde
Gleichwertigkeitsprüfung: comparison of the education with the German one
In case of substantial differences (wesentliche Unterschiede) — Kenntnisprüfung or Anpassungslehrgang
Language: general B2 plus medical C1 (Fachsprachprüfung)
You can start with a Berufserlaubnis during preparation

content.text: Whatever your country of origin, you must submit a complete set of documents to the Approbationsbehörde. Language and personal suitability (persönliche Eignung) are mandatory conditions, without which the Approbation will not be granted.

items: Diploma and the transcript with grades — certified translations by a sworn translator
Proof of medical practice and work experience
Language certificates: general B2 plus medical C1 (Fachsprachprüfung)
a certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis) and a medical health certificate (ärztliches Gesundheitszeugnis)
For third-country nationals — a valid residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) allowing work as a doctor

content.text: The procedure depends on the state (Bundesland): timelines, language requirements and the details of the Kenntnisprüfung differ. Apply to the Approbationsbehörde of the exact state where you plan to work, and allow many months for the whole process. The IQ-Beratungsstelle and the "Gut vorbereitet" programme — which lets you start preparing for recognition in advance, while still abroad — offer free guidance.

costs.label: Application for the Approbation (fee)
costs.note: Depends on the state; excluding a possible Kenntnisprüfung.

costs.label: Fachsprachprüfung (medical German)
costs.note: Ärztekammer fee.

costs.label: Translations and certification of documents
costs.note: Sworn translation of the diploma and transcripts.

title: Recognition as a nurse/Pflegefachfrau
tldr: The profession of nurse in Germany is regulated (Pflegeberufegesetz, PflBG), so you cannot work as a Pflegefachfrau/Pflegefachmann without recognition. The procedure is handled by the competent authority of the state (often the Regierungspräsidium or Landesamt). The authority compares your education with the German Pflegefachfrau/-mann; in case of substantial differences (wesentliche Unterschiede) you choose between an adaptation course with practical training (Anpassungslehrgang) and a knowledge exam (Kenntnisprüfung). Language: usually B2 (in some states B1 covers part of the duties, but the standard is B2). Until you have full recognition you can work as a Pflegehelfer/Pflegeassistenz (nursing assistant). An important advantage for nurses: the "gut vorbereitet" programme and accelerated recognition (beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren, §81a AufenthG) let you start the process while still abroad and arrive quickly under §18a AufenthG (Fachkraft mit Berufsausbildung). Once recognised, your salary and status are noticeably higher than an assistant's.

steps.title: A regulated profession: recognition is mandatory

content.text: Unlike IT, nursing (Pflege) is a strictly regulated profession. To bear the protected title Pflegefachfrau/Pflegefachmann and work in a full nursing position, you need official recognition of your foreign qualification. Without it, you will only be hired as an assistant (Pflegehelfer/Pflegeassistenz) — on a lower salary and with less responsibility.

items: The basis is the Pflegeberufegesetz (PflBG); the title is protected by law
Without recognition — only the position of Pflegehelfer/Pflegeassistenz
The procedure is handled by the competent authority of the state (Regierungspräsidium / Landesamt)
Recognition opens up the full position of Pflegefachkraft and higher pay
Information and finding the authority — anerkennung-in-deutschland.de and the Anerkennungs-Finder

content.text: The state authority compares your education and experience with the German ones. If the differences are not substantial, recognition is full. If there are substantial differences (wesentliche Unterschiede), you will be offered a choice of one of two ways to compensate for them.

items: Application to the competent authority of the state where you will work
Diploma, training programme, experience — with certified translations
The authority issues an official decision (Bescheid): full recognition or a list of differences
A language certificate (as a rule B2) — mandatory

items.title: 2. Compensating for differences: Lehrgang or Prüfung

items: Anpassungslehrgang: an adaptation course with practical training in a clinic (several months)
Kenntnisprüfung: an exam at the level of the German Pflegefachfrau/-mann
The choice between them is yours (the applicant's right under the BQFG/PflBG)
After completing it successfully — full recognition and the title Pflegefachfrau/-mann

steps.title: Accelerated recognition and arrival from abroad

content.text: Nurses are a shortage occupation, so there are convenient fast-track routes for them. You can begin the recognition process while still at home and arrive with an employer already in place, under a special skilled-worker visa.

items: Beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren (§81a AufenthG) — an accelerated procedure via the employer
The "gut vorbereitet" programme helps you gather documents and prepare in advance
Entry under §18a AufenthG (Fachkraft mit Berufsausbildung) after or during recognition
Entry is possible to complete an Anpassungslehrgang (§16d AufenthG) before full recognition
The employer often helps with documents, housing and the adaptation course

content.text: Don't settle for working as a Pflegehelfer for years without a clear recognition plan: an assistant's pay and rights are noticeably lower than those of a Pflegefachkraft. Start the recognition procedure right away (where possible via §81a and the "gut vorbereitet" programme) and agree a timeline with the employer for reaching the full qualification.

costs.label: Application for recognition (state authority fee)
costs.note: Depends on the state and the scope of the review.

costs.label: Anpassungslehrgang or Kenntnisprüfung
costs.note: The course is often paid for or subsidised by the employer; the exam is a separate fee.

costs.label: Document translations + language course/exam
costs.note: Sworn translations and a German B2 certificate.

title: The university entrance qualification (Abitur)
tldr: The Abitur (Allgemeine Hochschulreife) is Germany's highest school-leaving qualification, granting the right to apply to any Universität for any subject. You earn it after the Gymnasium (12 or 13 years depending on the state — most states had returned to G9 by 2025/2026). Without the Abitur, the path to university runs through the Fachabitur, vocational training (Berufsausbildung) with an aptitude exam (Eignungsprüfung), or recognition of a foreign qualification via anabin.kmk.org.

steps.title: What the Abitur is and the three levels of Hochschulreife

content.text: The Abitur is both the final exam of the Gymnasium and the qualification itself, granting the Allgemeine Hochschulreife (general right to enter university). It is regulated at state level (Schulrecht is a Länder competence), but a common standard has been developed through the KMK (Kultusministerkonferenz): the Bildungsstandards für die Allgemeine Hochschulreife. That is why the Abitur of Bavaria and that of Hamburg are legally equivalent, even though average grades differ across states.

items: Allgemeine Hochschulreife (Abitur) — any university, any subject
Fachgebundene Hochschulreife — a Universität, but a limited range of subjects
Fachhochschulreife (Fachabitur) — only a Fachhochschule / Hochschule für angewandte Wissenschaften
Grading scale: from 1,0 (best) to 4,0 (passing); below 4,0 — Nicht bestanden

steps.title: G8 vs G9: how many years of school

content.text: In the 2000s many states shortened the Gymnasium to 12 years (G8 — the "turbo-Abitur"). After widespread complaints from parents and teachers, almost all states reverted to G9 (13 years) by 2025/2026. G8 as the main model now remains mainly in Sachsen and Thüringen; a number of states (Bayern, Hessen, NRW, Baden-Württemberg, Niedersachsen) have officially returned to G9 in stages. Check the website of your state's Kultusministerium.

items: G8 = Gymnasium grades 5–12, Abitur at 17–18
G9 = Gymnasium grades 5–13, Abitur at 18–19
Berlin/Brandenburg — primary school (Grundschule) up to grade 6, Gymnasium from grade 7 to 12/13
The Schuljahr starts in August/September depending on the state

content.text: The Abitur is not a single exam but a combined grade: ~2/3 comes from grades in the Qualifikationsphase (the last 2 years of the Oberstufe), ~1/3 from the actual Abiturprüfungen. Usually 4–5 exams: 3–4 written + 1 oral/presentation. Core subjects (Leistungskurse / erhöhtes Niveau) are taken at an advanced level, the rest at the basic level (Grundkurse). As a minimum: one exam in German, maths or a foreign language, plus one in a natural science or social-studies subject.
The last 4 semesters of the Oberstufe. Course grades (Kurshalbjahresnoten) count towards the final Abitur score — up to 600 out of 900 points.
Written exams in the spring of the final year, the oral one later. Some states use the Zentralabitur (uniform exam papers), others use papers set by the schools themselves.

items: Minimum 300 out of 900 points
Converted to the 1,0–4,0 scale (1,0 = ~823 points)
the entry threshold (Numerus Clausus) for popular subjects: medicine is usually 1,0–1,2

content.text: The certificate is issued by the Gymnasium. It is valid for life, in all German states, and — under KMK agreements — for admission in most EU countries too.

steps.title: For newly arrived pupils and foreign qualifications

content.text: If a child arrives in Germany during secondary/upper school, they are first placed in a Willkommensklasse / DaZ-Klasse (Deutsch als Zweitsprache) for 1–2 years of language preparation, then moved into a regular Gymnasium class or a comprehensive school (Gesamtschule). Foreign qualifications are recognised through the anabin.kmk.org database (the "Schulabschlüsse" section). Some qualifications give direct access to university; others require a preparatory college (Studienkolleg; 1 year of preparation plus an entrance aptitude exam, the Feststellungsprüfung).

items: anabin.kmk.org — the official KMK database for the recognition of foreign school qualifications
Russian / Ukrainian / Kazakh certificates: a preparatory college (Studienkolleg) + 1–2 semesters at a home-country university is often required
The preparatory college is free when you enrol at a state university
TestAS / DSH / TestDaF — language tests for admission to a German university

content.text: The Numerus Clausus (NC) for popular subjects (medicine, psychology, law) is very tough — 1,0–1,4. Alongside the grade quota there are Wartesemester (waiting semesters) and quotas under the Auswahlverfahren der Hochschulen — read up on the procedure at hochschulstart.de.

An Abitur from one state is formally recognised everywhere, but the curricula differ. Moving from one state to another in the middle of the Oberstufe can leave gaps (for example in a second foreign language).
A private boarding Gymnasium (Internat-Gymnasium) costs 20 000–40 000€/year. A state Gymnasium is free — you only pay for Schulbedarf (books, materials, excursions).
Fachabitur ≠ Abitur. With the Fachhochschulreife you cannot enrol at a Universität for medicine, law or the classic humanities — only at a Hochschule für angewandte Wissenschaften.

costs.note: Free; Schulbedarf 100–300€/year for books, materials, excursions

costs.label: Private Gymnasium / Internat
costs.note: Per year; depends on the school and accommodation (Internat = boarding)

costs.note: Free at a state-university Studienkolleg; there are paid private ones

title: BAföG: financial aid for students
tldr: BAföG (Bundesausbildungsförderungsgesetz) is state financial aid for pupils and students from low-income families. After the 2024 reform, the maximum rate is 992€/month and the age limit has been raised to 45. Half the amount is a Zuschuss (non-repayable), half is an interest-free loan with a repayment cap of 10 010€. You apply via bafoeg-digital.de.

steps.title: What BAföG is and who is eligible

content.text: BAföG (Bundesausbildungsförderungsgesetz) is a 1971 federal law on financial support for education. It covers pupils at a Berufsfachschule, Gymnasium students from low-income families, and students at a Hochschule (university). For non-EU foreigners it is available with a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis), a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) for studying + 5 years of legal residence in Germany, or refugee status (Geflüchtete) with recognised status. EU citizens qualify on the same terms as Germans if their main place of residence is in Germany.

items: Age limit: 45 at the start of studies (raised from 30 after the 2024 reform)
Studies must be full-time and at a recognised educational institution
Family income must not exceed the set Freibeträge
For non-German citizens: status under §8 BAföG

steps.title: How much is paid: a maximum of 992€/month

content.text: The maximum BAföG rate from the 2024/2025 winter semester is 992€/month for students living away from their parents (following the Bundesrat increase in summer 2024). The amount includes the Grundbedarf (base rate ~475€), the Wohnzuschlag (housing supplement, up to 380€), and the KV/PV-Zuschlag (Kranken-/Pflegeversicherung contribution, ~137€). The exact amount depends on the income of the parents, the spouse and the student themselves, and is calculated individually.
The basic needs allowance for living and food. For university students ~475€/month after the 2024 reform.
Up to 380€/month for students not living with their parents. It does not depend on the actual rent — it is a fixed flat amount (Pauschale).
A supplement for Kranken- und Pflegeversicherung (health and long-term-care insurance) — for students under 30 it runs through the student rate of statutory health insurance (GKV).

items: Tax-free amounts (Freibeträge) for parents: ~2540€/month for a married couple

Tax-free amount (Freibetrag) for a student's side job: ~556€/month (6 672€/year) from 1 January 2026 — this is below the mini-job (Minijob) threshold of 603€/month, so a side job of 603€ all year slightly exceeds the limit and BAföG is reduced proportionally
Student's assets: a limit of 15 000€ up to age 30, 45 000€ above that

content.text: The key feature of BAföG for university students: 50% is a Zuschuss (a state subsidy, not repayable), 50% is a staatliches Darlehen (a state interest-free loan). Repayment of the loan begins 5 years after the end of the maximum study period for the subject. The overall repayment cap is 10 010€ (Schuldenkappung after the 2024 reform), even if you received more. The minimum payment is 130€/month, with instalments over up to 20 years.

items: 50% Zuschuss — not repayable
50% Darlehen — 0% interest, repayment after 5 years
Max. repayment — 10 010€ (anything above is written off)
Discount for early repayment: 8–25% off
Full write-off in cases of social hardship (§18a BAföG)

content.text: First you need to find the competent office (Amt) — the Amt für Ausbildungsförderung — which for students is the university's Studierendenwerk and for pupils the Amt at the Landratsamt for their place of residence. You can find it via das-neue-bafoeg.de or bafoeg-digital.de. It is best to apply online via bafoeg-digital.de (the national electronic platform). Processing takes 8–12 weeks, with payment backdated to the month of application (even an incomplete application — Formblatt 1 stating the "university and subject").

Identification via BundID (a single account for public services) + ELSTER (the tax authority's online portal) or the Online-Ausweisfunktion. You can't do without a BundID — set one up in advance at id.bund.de.

items: Formblatt 1 — the student's application
Formblatt 2 — the university's enrolment certificate
Formblatt 3 — details of the parents' income (for the year before last)
Formblatt 5 — after the 4th semester: proof of academic progress
Formblatt 8 — for foreigners: status
Immatrikulationsbescheinigung
the rental contract (Mietvertrag) for the Wohnzuschlag
the parents' tax assessment (Steuerbescheid) / income certificate (EkSt-Bescheinigung)
the residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) for foreigners

content.text: The BAföG-Amt will send a notice of award (Bewilligungsbescheid) with the amount and the period (usually for 2 semesters). The money arrives in your bank account monthly, by the start of the month.
Apply before the start of the semester — even incompletely (just Formblatt 1). Payment is only backdated to the month of application. If you are late, you lose the money for the missed months.

After the 4th semester a Leistungsnachweis (Formblatt 5) is mandatory — proof that you are making progress. Without it, BAföG will not be extended. Most universities issue it automatically at the student services office.

Changing your subject after the 1st or 2nd semester is allowed if you have a "wichtigem Grund" (good reason); later than that, you lose your entitlement to BAföG for the new course. Study §7 Abs. 3 BAföG.

Income above the BAföG-Freibetrag (~556€/month, 6 672€/year from 1 January 2026) reduces the payment. Note: this is not the same as the Minijob threshold of 603€/month — annual earnings of exactly 603€ a month already slightly exceed the limit. The Deutschlandstipendium scholarship (up to 300€/month) does not affect BAföG, unlike most other scholarships.

For non-EU citizens, status is critical. An Aufenthaltserlaubnis under §16b AufenthG (studies) does NOT by itself grant BAföG. You need 5 years of legal residence + the parents' employment, or §8 Abs. 2 BAföG.

costs.note: Free via bafoeg-digital.de

costs.label: Maximum payment 2026
costs.note: Per month for students living away from home, with all supplements

costs.label: Darlehen repayment — maximum
costs.note: Schuldenkappung; anything above is written off

title: Bilingual schools: lists by city
tldr: Germany has three types of bilingual school: state bilinguale Züge (for example SESB in Berlin — 9 languages, free), international schools (English/French — private, 15 000–25 000€/year) and private community schools by diaspora (Russian, Ukrainian and Polish Saturday schools). The right choice depends on the language, your budget and your long-term goals (Abitur vs IB Diploma).

content.text: In Germany a "bilingual school" (bilinguale Schule) is a broad concept. Legally there are three categories: 1) state schools with a bilingualer Zug — a normal German education, but part of the subjects are taught in a second language (English/French/Russian/Polish); 2) Internationale Schulen / Privatschulen — they usually lead to the International Baccalaureate (IB) or Cambridge IGCSE rather than the Abitur; 3) Ergänzungsschulen — private Saturday schools and language courses run by diaspora communities.

items: A state bilinguale Schule = free, leads to the German Abitur
An Internationale Schule = 10 000–30 000€/year, the IB Diploma is recognised via the KMK
A Diaspora-Schule = supplementary, usually once a week, native language + culture
Recognition of the IB Diploma: KMK-Beschluss from 2018, valid in all states

content.text: Berlin leads in the number of bilingual schools thanks to the Staatliche Europa-Schule Berlin (SESB) — a state system running since 1992. SESB schools operate with 9 language partners: English, French, Spanish, Italian, Greek, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish. These are fully free state schools with bilingual teaching from grade 1 to the Abitur. Enrolment is through the district Schulamt, with places split between "native speakers" of the partner language (50%) and "non-native speakers" (50%).

items: SESB Deutsch-Russisch: Grundschule Lew-Tolstoi (Lichtenberg) + Sophie-Scholl-Schule (Schöneberg)
SESB Deutsch-Englisch: Charles-Dickens-Grundschule + Quentin-Blake-Grundschule
SESB Deutsch-Französisch: Judith-Kerr-Grundschule + Romain-Rolland-Gymnasium
Fee-paying: JFK School (German-English state-private, website jfksberlin.org)
Berlin Cosmopolitan, Berlin International School — private, IB/Cambridge

content.text: Bavaria and Hesse rely more on private international schools — historically linked to diplomatic and corporate circles (the banks in Frankfurt, BMW/Siemens in Munich). There are fewer state bilinguale Züge, but they do exist — usually offering English in the Gymnasium from grade 7.

items: Bavarian International School (BIS) — English, IB
Lycée Jean Renoir — French, state-run
Munich International School (MIS) — English, IB
Phorms München — bilingualer Zug, English, private primary school (Grundschule) and Gymnasium
The European School — for the children of EPA staff
Frankfurt International School (FIS) — IB, Oberursel
International School of Frankfurt-Rhein-Main (ISF) — IB
Phorms Frankfurt — bilingualer Zug
Lycée Français Victor Hugo
ERS Frankfurt — the European School Rhein-Main
International School of Hamburg (ISH) — IB
Phorms Hamburg
Heinrich-Hertz-Schule — bilingualer Zug, English, state-run
International School of Düsseldorf (ISD)
St. George's School (English) — Köln
Lycée Français de Düsseldorf

content.text: For families who want to keep up Russian: besides the SESB Russisch in Berlin, there is a network of Ergänzungsschulen — usually running on Saturdays or as a Sprachschule after regular school. Some are subsidised through the Russisches Haus (Berlin) or cultural associations. Most are run as Vereine (associations), with paid tuition (50–150€/month).

items: Berlin: Mitra (Bildungsverein), Russisches Haus educational programmes
München: the "Raduga" school, private Saturday groups
Hamburg: the "Svetlyachok" school, Russian-speaking children's centres
Frankfurt: the "Russian School Frankfurt" (Verein)
NRW: the network of Ukrainian- and Russian-speaking schools grew after 2022

content.text: SESB and similar state schools are highly competitive. Enrolment in the upper grades of primary school (Grundschule) is practically closed; you need to apply a year before grade 1. Non-native speakers are admitted by lottery.
IB Diploma vs Abitur: both give access to university via hochschulstart.de, but for admission to German medical and law faculties the Abitur is often preferred. Check on the university's website.
Private international schools require an Aufnahmeprüfung and an interview in English/German. The school year starts in August, so applications go in 6–12 months ahead.
Schulgeld at private schools is not fully tax-deductible — only 30% (max. 5000€/year) under §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 9 EStG.
When moving from a non-EU country, it is better to enrol your child in a bilinguale Schule from the first grade; in secondary school entry is heavily restricted.
