title: Parental allowance (Elterngeld): Basis vs Plus
tldr: Parental allowance (Elterngeld) has three modes: Basis (12 months for one parent + 2 "Partnermonate" = 14 between them, at the full amount), ElterngeldPlus (double the duration for half the amount — letting you combine it with Teilzeit) and the Partnerschaftsbonus (+4 months each if both work 24–32 h/week in parallel). They can be combined. Regulated by §§4–6 BEEG.

steps.title: The three Elterngeld modes in one picture

content.text: The BEEG (Bundeselterngeld- und Elternzeitgesetz) distinguishes three forms: Basiselterngeld (§4 BEEG), ElterngeldPlus (§4a BEEG) and the Partnerschaftsbonus (§4b BEEG). They can be combined for one child — for example, start with 6 months of Basis, then switch to 8 months of Plus, and add 4 months of Partnerschaftsbonus. The main rules: the child must live in the same household as the parent, the parent must not work more than 32 hours/week, and there is an income limit (for children born from 1 April 2025 — a single limit of 175 000€/year zu versteuerndes Einkommen for both couples and single parents).

items: Basiselterngeld: 12 months for one + 2 "Partnermonate" = 14 between them (14 automatically for a single parent)
ElterngeldPlus: each Basis month = 2 Plus months at half the amount
Partnerschaftsbonus: +4 Plus months each if both work 24–32 h/week in parallel
The months can be combined flexibly

content.text: Basiselterngeld is paid for up to 12 months to one parent + 2 "Partnermonate" on condition that the second parent also takes at least 2 months off work. That makes 14 months between the two. The amount is 65% of your net salary over the 12 months before the birth (for children born from 1 September 2021 — 65%; on a lower salary — 67%; maximum 1800€/month, minimum 300€). It suits a parent who leaves work entirely during this time.

items: 65–67% of net salary (the 12 months before maternity leave, Mutterschutz)
Max 1800€/month, min 300€/month (even if you did not work before the birth)
You can work up to 32 h/week, but the Elterngeld is recalculated
Mehrkindzuschlag +10% (min. 75€) if there are older children under 3

content.text: ElterngeldPlus was introduced in 2015 specifically for those who want to combine childcare with part-time work. The idea: each "Basis month" turns into 2 "Plus months" with a payment of ~50% of the Basis amount (max 900€/month). So 12 Basis months become 24 Plus months. If you work 20–30 hours a week, Plus can give you MORE money overall than Basis, because half of the "Plus payment" is not offset against your income from work (there is a detailed formula in §2 Abs. 4 BEEG).

items: 2 Plus months = 1 Basis month
Plus amount = max Basis / 2 (= max 900€/month)
Ideal when working 20–32 h/week
Can be combined with Basis in any order

content.text: The Partnerschaftsbonus is 4 extra Plus months for each parent if both work 24–32 hours a week in parallel during those 4 months. So a couple can get up to 8 bonus months in total. The aim is to encourage shared involvement in childcare. The checks are strict: work less than 24 or more than 32 h/week and you will have to pay it back.
Both parents live with the child, both work 24–32 h/week in parallel for at least 4 months. Even the self-employed (Selbständige) can do this, but their working hours have to be documented.
Each gets 4 Plus months at the ElterngeldPlus rate (~50% of Basis, max 900€/month). That makes up to 4×900×2 = 7200€ in total.
The Elterngeldstelle requires an Arbeitszeitnachweis from the employer, or a Stundenzettel for the self-employed (Selbständige). The check usually happens after the fact.

Income cap: for children born from 1 April 2025 a single limit of 175 000€/year applies (zu versteuerndes Einkommen) — the same for couples and for single parents. Go over it and you get NOTHING. This was lowered in stages: 300 000€ (couples) / 250 000€ (singles) until April 2024, then 200 000€ / 150 000€, now a single 175 000€. Check the current figure at familienportal.de.

Mutterschutzgeld and the employer's supplement for the first 8 weeks after the birth are counted against the allowance (Elterngeld) — in practice the mother's first 2 months of Basis Elterngeld come out at zero (but the months are used up).

Working more than 32 h/week during parental leave (Elternzeit) means a complete loss of the allowance (Elterngeld) for that month. The check is via the employer, or via Stundennachweise for the self-employed (Selbständige).
Partnerschaftsbonus + Basis in parallel are not possible: the bonus only exists in Plus mode. Plan the order of the months in advance.
The application goes to the Elterngeldstelle (at state/municipal level) within 3 months of the birth; it can be backdated by only 3 months.

costs.label: Basiselterngeld — maximum
costs.note: Per month; 65–67% of net over the 12 months before the birth

costs.label: Basiselterngeld — minimum
costs.note: Per month; guaranteed even without income before the birth

costs.label: ElterngeldPlus — maximum
costs.note: Per month; exactly half of Basis

costs.label: Partnerschaftsbonus — max. duration
costs.note: 4 Plus months each; up to 8 months per family

costs.label: Application
costs.note: Free via the Elterngeldstelle / online at elterngeld-digital.de

title: Calculating parental allowance (Elterngeld): 65-67% of net income
tldr: Parental allowance (Elterngeld) is calculated as 65% (for net income >1240€) or 67% (for net income <1240€) of your average net income over the 12 months before maternity leave (Mutterschutz) begins. The cap is 1800€/month and the minimum is 300€. For the self-employed, the calendar year before the birth is used. Your spouse's income does not affect the calculation, but as of 1 April 2025 a single income limit (Einkommensgrenze) of 175 000€ applies (to couples and single parents alike).

content.text: The net income used for parental allowance is not the same as the net figure on your payslip. It is calculated using a special formula in §2 BEEG: from your gross income (Bruttoeinkommen), flat-rate deductions are subtracted — taxes (Steuern) based on your tax class (Steuerklasse), social contributions (around 21% flat) and a flat-rate allowance for work-related expenses (Werbungskostenpauschale). In other words, the parental allowance office (Elterngeldstelle) does not look at your actual tax assessment (Steuerbescheid) but "reconstructs" your net income using a simplified formula. Sometimes this works out better than the real calculation, sometimes worse.

items: Assessment period (Bemessungszeitraum): the 12 months before maternity leave (Mutterschutz) begins for the mother
For the father: the 12 months before the birth of the child
Your tax class (Steuerklasse) during the assessment period is critical (see optimization)
Flat-rate allowance for work-related expenses (Werbungskostenpauschale) 1230€/year (2026 figure; check it)

content.text: The rate depends on your net income before the birth: the lower the income, the higher the percentage that is replaced. This is "progressive replacement".
67% + bonus: for every 2€ below 1000€ the rate rises by 0.1% (up to 100% in theory); in practice the ceiling is ~100%.
Exactly 67% — this is the "sweet spot".
The rate declines linearly from 67% to 65%: for every 2€ above 1200€ it drops by 0.1%, reaching 65% at a net income of 1240€ (§2 Abs. 2 BEEG).
65% of net income, but a maximum of 1800€/month (=> at a net income of ~2770€ the basic allowance (Basis) hits the cap).

steps.title: The self-employed (Selbständige): calculation based on annual profit

content.text: For the self-employed and freelancers, the basis is not the 12 months before the birth but the last completed calendar year before the birth. The reference document is the tax assessment (Steuerbescheid) for that year. This rule smooths out seasonal fluctuations, but it can also penalize those who have just started a business. Tip: if 2025 was a "weak" year, you can — with the parental allowance office's (Elterngeldstelle) approval — shift the assessment period (Bemessungszeitraum) to 2024 (provided there was self-employed activity in both years — §2b BEEG).

items: Basis: profit from self-employment (Gewinn aus Selbständigkeit) for the calendar year
Divided by 12 → average monthly net income
Employment income (Anstellung) in the same year is calculated separately, then added
Mixed income (Mischeinkommen — employment + self-employment) — both sources are treated under their own rules

content.text: For married couples: if the mother switches tax class (Steuerklasse) from V to III at least 7 months BEFORE the assessment period begins (i.e. 19 months before the birth) — taking class III means less tax is withheld and net income is higher — parental allowance will be calculated on a higher net income. This is a classic legal optimization. The partner (class V) pays more tax each month, but it all evens out in the annual tax return (Steuererklärung).

items: Changing tax class (Steuerklasse) — at the tax office (Finanzamt), free of charge, form "Antrag auf Steuerklassenwechsel"
Submit at least 7 months before the assessment period begins (or before maternity leave)
Effect: up to +400€/month of allowance at high incomes
The partner can be on tax class V short-term — the annual tax return will even it out

content.text: 65% × 2000 = 1300€/month of basic allowance (Basiselterngeld). ElterngeldPlus = 650€/month × 24 months.
65% × 3500 = 2275€, but the cap is 1800€/month — so you get 1800€. Plus = 900€/month.

items.title: Example 4: not working before the birth

content.text: Minimum 300€/month. Students, the unemployed and migrants without employment all receive the base rate (Sockelbetrag).

The single income limit (Einkommensgrenze) of 175 000€/year (for children born on or after 1 April 2025 — for couples and single parents alike) applies to taxable income (zu versteuerndes Einkommen) for the calendar year BEFORE the birth. If both spouses earn well, plan in advance who takes parental allowance and when.

Maternity benefit (Mutterschutzgeld — from the health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) plus the employer) for the 8 weeks after the birth is offset against parental allowance → the mother's first 2 months of basic allowance often come to 0€, yet those months are still used up.

If you work in parallel during parental leave (Elternzeit), your current income is compared with your pre-birth net income, and the allowance is reduced by the difference. The Plus mode leaves you half the basic Plus rate (Plus-Sockel) in any case.

Sickness benefit (Krankengeld), including for pregnancy complications, lowers the calculated net income within the assessment period. Such months can be excluded from the period under the grounds for shifting it (Verschiebetatbestände, §2b BEEG).
Bonuses and one-off payments (Sonderzahlungen: 13th/14th salary, Weihnachtsgeld) are only included if paid regularly. A one-off bonus is NOT counted.

costs.note: % of net; 67% at net 1000–1200€; more below <1000€

costs.label: Basis maximum
costs.note: Per month at net >~2770€

costs.label: Minimum (Sockel)
costs.note: Per month; with no income or low income

costs.label: Einkommensgrenze (children born on or after 1 April 2025)
costs.note: Single threshold for zu versteuerndes Einkommen per year — the same for couples and single parents.

costs.label: Former threshold for single parents (children born before 1 April 2025)
costs.note: Applied to single parents before the April 2025 reform; couples — 200 000€.

title: Parental leave (Elternzeit): job protection
tldr: Parental leave (Elternzeit, §§15–16 BEEG) is leave of up to 3 years per child with a guaranteed right to return to your job. You apply to your employer in writing at least 7 weeks before it starts, and it can be split into up to 3 parts. Protection against dismissal applies from the moment you apply (but no earlier than 8 weeks before the start). You may work up to 32 hours/week, including for another employer with your first employer's consent.

content.text: Parental leave (Elternzeit) is an employee's legal right to unpaid leave to care for a child up to 3 years old, with the right to return to the job. It is governed by §15 BEEG. The employer CANNOT refuse. The right does not depend on length of service, type of contract (including fixed-term (befristet) and part-time (Teilzeit)) or gender. The key requirements are an employment contract and a shared household with the child. Parental leave is not the same as parental allowance (Elterngeld): the first is about labour law, the second is about money. You can take parental leave without the allowance and vice versa.

items: Up to 3 years per child (part of it can be taken up to the child's 8th birthday via a transfer)
Both parents have the right independently of each other
Up to 24 months can be transferred to between the child's 3rd and 8th birthdays (without the employer's consent for children born after 01.07.2015)
Can be split into up to 3 parts (without the employer's consent)

content.text: An application for parental leave is submitted to your employer IN WRITING (a paper letter with a handwritten signature — email/fax are NOT accepted under §16 BEEG!). The deadline is no later than 7 weeks before the desired start of leave (for a period up to the child's 3rd birthday). For a period after the child's 3rd birthday — 13 weeks. In the application you must state the EXACT periods for the first two years of leave (this is binding). For the third year onwards you are free to decide later — no commitment is needed now.

items: Full name, personnel number
Child's date of birth (or expected date)
Exact start and end dates of each period of parental leave
Handwritten signature

content.text: In person against a receipt, or by registered mail with acknowledgement of receipt (Einschreiben mit Rückschein). The date the employer receives it is key for calculating protection against dismissal (Kündigungsschutz).
The employer is OBLIGED to confirm the parental leave in writing (§16 Abs. 1 BEEG). This is your record.

From the moment you submit your application (but no earlier than 8 weeks before the start of the first period) until the end of parental leave, the employer CANNOT dismiss you, except in exceptional cases — company insolvency, or gross misconduct with the approval of the occupational health and safety authority (Gewerbeaufsicht/Arbeitsschutzbehörde, §18 BEEG). This is stronger than ordinary protection against dismissal (Kündigungsschutz): even start-ups and small businesses (Kleinbetriebe, <10 employees), where the ordinary KSchG does not apply, must comply.

items: Applies from 8 weeks before parental leave begins
Covers any grounds for dismissal (Kündigungsgründe) except the exceptions under §18 BEEG
Applies even in a small business (Kleinbetrieb)
A termination agreement (Aufhebungsvertrag) is still possible (with the employee's consent)

steps.title: Working during parental leave: up to 32 hours/week

content.text: You may work during parental leave — but no more than 32 hours per week on average over the month (since September 2021). You may work: for your current employer (this takes priority, §15 Abs. 4 BEEG); for another employer, with the written consent of the first; or as a self-employed person, also with consent. The employer can only refuse for "compelling operational reasons" (zwingende betriebliche Gründe) — which in practice is not easy.

items.title: 1. Right to part-time work (Teilzeit, §15 Abs. 7 BEEG)

content.text: If the company has >15 employees, your tenure is >6 months and the company has been operating for >6 months, you have a LEGAL right to demand part-time work (Teilzeit, 15–32 hrs/week) for at least 2 months.
At least 7 weeks before part-time work begins (or 13 weeks after the child's 3rd birthday). State the hours and how they are to be distributed.
The employer must refuse in writing, with reasons, within 4 weeks. Otherwise your request is deemed accepted.
After parental leave you return to the same or an equivalent position at your previous salary.

The application MUST be in writing with a handwritten signature. An email application has NO legal effect — the Federal Labour Court (Bundesarbeitsgericht) confirmed this in 2016. That means protection against dismissal does not apply, and the employer can dismiss you.

The dates you commit to for the first 2 years are binding. They can only be changed with the employer's consent or due to significant changes (the birth of another child, serious illness). Plan ahead.

Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) during parental leave: free family insurance (Familienversicherung) in the statutory health insurance (GKV) through your spouse. If your spouse is in private health insurance (PKV), you have to pay voluntarily (freiwillig, ~150–200€/month minimum).
The employer is entitled to reduce your holiday entitlement (Urlaubsanspruch) proportionally for the months of full parental leave (§17 Abs. 1 BEEG). For months worked part-time, holiday is not cut.
Transferring 24 months to between the child's 3rd and 8th birthdays: for children born BEFORE 01.07.2015 the employer's written consent is needed; AFTER that date, only written notification.
Fixed-term contracts (befristete Verträge): parental leave does NOT extend the contract term. If the contract ends during leave, it simply ends.

costs.note: Unpaid leave; Elterngeld is paid separately

costs.label: Application
costs.note: Free; Einschreiben recommended (~5€)

costs.label: GKV during Elternzeit
costs.note: Through the spouse's Familienversicherung or the Elterngeld period

costs.label: PKV during Elternzeit
costs.note: Per month; cannot be fully suspended, but you can switch to a cheap Anwartschaftstarif

title: Primary school (Grundschule): enrolling in 1st grade
tldr: School in Germany is compulsory from age 6 (compulsory schooling, Schulpflicht). Enrolment in 1st grade happens a year before school starts — usually in the autumn of the previous year. There is a catchment-area requirement (Einzugsgebiet, the district of residence), but there are alternatives: a bilingual school (bilinguale Schule), a private school (Privatschule) or a free school (Freie Schule). A school-entry medical examination (Schuleingangsuntersuchung) by the health authority (Gesundheitsamt) and school registration (Schulanmeldung) at the school administration office (Schulamt) are both mandatory.

content.text: In Germany, compulsory schooling (Schulpflicht) is a constitutional duty, not just a right. It is governed by the state school laws (Schulgesetze der Länder). Unlike in the US or UK, homeschooling (Homeschooling) is prohibited in Germany — the Constitutional Court (Verfassungsgericht) and the Federal Court of Justice (BGH) have confirmed this repeatedly. Compulsory schooling begins at age 6 (the cut-off date (Stichtag) is usually 30 June or 30 September, depending on the state). Children aged 5–6 can be enrolled earlier (early enrolment, Vorzeitige Einschulung) with the school's approval; for 6–7-year-olds with developmental delays, enrolment can be deferred (Zurückstellung) by 1 year.

items: Compulsory schooling begins at age 6 (the cut-off date (Stichtag) varies)
Lasts 9 or 10 years depending on the state
Homeschooling is prohibited by law
Primary school (Grundschule) = grades 1–4 (Berlin/Brandenburg: 1–6)

content.text: State primary schools operate on the catchment-area principle (Einzugsgebiet, Schulbezirk) — each school is assigned a geographical district, and a child is automatically directed to the school in their district. You can look up your catchment area on the website of your city's school administration office (Schulamt/Schulverwaltungsamt). In some states (Hamburg, parts of Berlin) there is free choice among the nearest schools, but with priority for local children when places are oversubscribed.

items: Find your catchment area (Einzugsgebiet): schulamt.de or the municipality's website
Berlin: free choice since the 2010s, but 50% of places reserved for the catchment area
Hamburg: 2 "preferred schools" when applying, with priority for the 1st
When moving to a new school — application + waiting period (Wartezeit)

content.text: School registration (Schulanmeldung) is the mandatory registration of a child for 1st grade; it takes place in the autumn of the year before school starts (for school in August 2026 → registration in October–November 2025). The school administration office (Schulamt) automatically sends an invitation by post, based on the residents' register (Melderegister). If no letter has arrived 6 months before registration, request one yourself from the school administration office. Don't be late: missing registration is an administrative offence (Ordnungswidrigkeit), with a fine of 500–1000€.

items.title: 1. Receive the invitation (Einladung) from the school administration office (Schulamt)

content.text: It arrives by post, usually in September–October the year before school starts. If it hasn't arrived, call the school administration office.

A mandatory medical examination at the children's and youth health service (Kinder- und Jugendgesundheitsdienst) of the health authority (Gesundheitsamt). They check hearing, vision, speech development, motor skills and vaccinations. Free of charge. The results go to the school.

items: Child's birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde)
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) for the family
Vaccination certificate (Impfausweis; the measles vaccination (Masern-Pflicht) is mandatory for 1st grade)
Parent's national ID card or residence permit (Personalausweis/Aufenthaltstitel)
Registration form (Anmeldebogen) from the school
Custody certificate (Sorgerechtsbescheinigung; if the parents are not married)

content.text: The school sends confirmation before the summer holidays (Sommerferien) ahead of 1st grade. From that moment the child is OFFICIALLY a pupil at that school.
Besides the "ordinary" catchment-area primary school, there are other options — all of which require a separate application and often a competitive process or lottery:

items: Bilingual state school (bilinguale staatliche Schule — SESB in Berlin and equivalents) — free, competitive
Free/private primary school (Freie/Private Grundschule — Waldorf, Montessori, denominational) — tuition fee (Schulgeld) 100–800€/month
International school (Internationale Schule, IB-oriented) — 10 000–20 000€/year
Inclusive school (Inklusionsschule, for children with special needs) — free
All-day school (Ganztagsschule, supervision until 16:00) — usually free or a small fee (Beitrag)

steps.title: Starting school (Einschulung): the first day of school

content.text: The first day of school (Einschulungstag) is a big event in Germany. It usually takes place on a Saturday in the first week of the new school year. The main tradition is the school cone (Schultüte, or Zuckertüte in the eastern states) — a large cardboard cone filled with gifts and sweets that the child carries to school. The school holds a ceremony (Festakt) with speeches, and parents take photos. Basic costs for 1st grade: a school satchel (Schulranzen, 150–300€), a school cone (10–50€ if homemade, 30–80€ ready-made), and textbooks and supplies (~100€).

items: School satchel (Schulranzen) 150–300€ (ergonomic, to DIN 58124)
School cone (Schultüte) 30–80€
School supplies (Schulbedarf — notebooks, pens, markers): 50–100€
Sports kit bag (Sportbeutel) + sports clothes: 30–60€
Walking or cycling to school is the norm; parents don't drive children

content.text: Mandatory measles vaccination (Masern-Impfpflicht): since 2020 the measles vaccination has been mandatory for all children in primary school (Grundschule) and daycare (Kita). Without proof, the child will not be admitted. Accepted proof is a vaccination certificate (Impfausweis) OR a certificate (Bescheinigung) from the paediatrician (Kinderarzt) confirming a past measles infection.

Moving to a different catchment area (Einzugsgebiet) a couple of months before 1st grade may mean the school changes. If you want to stay, file an application for an exception (Antrag auf Ausnahme) with the school administration office (Schulamt), with reasons.
If the child speaks little German, a preparatory class (Vorschulklasse) or preparatory course (Vorlaufkurs, 1 year of language preparation) may be recommended. In some states this is mandatory.

Enrolling in a bilingual or private school is a separate process WITHIN the ordinary school registration (Schulanmeldung). First complete registration at your address, then apply to the alternative school.
Don't bring too large a school cone (Schultüte): the first-grader has to carry it themselves (40–60 cm is usually enough).

costs.note: Free through the Gesundheitsamt

title: Grammar school (Gymnasium) vs comprehensive school (Gesamtschule): which to choose
tldr: After 4th grade (or 6th in Berlin/Brandenburg), the family chooses a type of school (Schulform) for their child: a grammar school (Gymnasium, leading directly to the Abitur), a comprehensive school (Gesamtschule — integrated, all abilities, leading to any school-leaving certificate), an intermediate school (Realschule, the Mittlere Reife certificate) or a lower secondary school (Hauptschule). In half the states the teacher gives a binding school recommendation (Schulempfehlung); in the other half it is non-binding. After any type of school you can still reach the Abitur via the upper level of a comprehensive school (Oberstufe Gesamtschule) or a vocational grammar school (Berufliches Gymnasium).

content.text: The German school system after primary school (Grundschule) is traditionally "three-tier" (grammar school (Gymnasium) / intermediate school (Realschule) / lower secondary school (Hauptschule)), but in reality most states now run a two-tier system (grammar school + integrated school). The specific set of school types is the responsibility of each state (the school law, Schulgesetz).

items: Grammar school (Gymnasium): grades 5–12 (G8) or 5–13 (G9). Direct route to the Abitur. Academic track.

Comprehensive school (Gesamtschule — integrated secondary school (Integrierte Sekundarschule), district school (Stadtteilschule)): all abilities together, with differentiation within. Any certificate from the Hauptschule level up to the Abitur.
Intermediate school (Realschule): grades 5–10, leaving certificate — the intermediate school-leaving certificate (Mittlere Reife, Realschulabschluss).
Lower secondary school (Hauptschule): grades 5–9 (or 10), leaving certificate — the lower secondary certificate (Hauptschulabschluss), followed by vocational training (Ausbildung).
Special-needs school (Förderschule): for children with special needs.

steps.title: The school recommendation (Schulempfehlung): binding or not

content.text: At the end of 4th grade (or 6th in Berlin/Brandenburg), the class teacher (Klassenlehrer) issues a school recommendation (Schulempfehlung). The legal weight of the recommendation varies greatly between states:

items: Bayern, Sachsen, Thüringen: the recommendation is effectively binding; parents can override it only by passing a trial lesson (Probeunterricht, a 3-day exam)
Baden-Württemberg: partly binding again since 2024 (new school law, Schulgesetz)
NRW, Hessen, Berlin, Hamburg, Brandenburg, etc.: the parents' wishes (Elternwille) have the final say, and the recommendation is advisory
In states with a binding recommendation you need a 2,33 — 2,66 average in the core subjects for the Gymnasium

content.text: The grammar school (Gymnasium) is an academically oriented school. The pace of learning is fast, a second foreign language is mandatory from grade 6–7, and Latin is often offered as an option. The goal is the Abitur in grade 12 or 13. It suits children who find learning easy and are motivated. Among the downsides: a competitive environment, a heavy workload, and the risk of moving "down" to another school (Schulwechsel) if grades slip.

items: Plus: a direct route to university (Universität), in any field
Plus: a broad academic base (2 foreign languages, natural sciences)
Minus: heavy workload, little time for hobbies
Minus: with low grades there may be a school change (Schulwechsel) to an intermediate or comprehensive school
Repeating a year (Sitzenbleiben) is possible from grade 5–6 onwards

content.text: The comprehensive school (Gesamtschule; in Hamburg — district school (Stadtteilschule), in Berlin — integrated secondary school (Integrierte Sekundarschule, ISS)) is "together for everyone". Children of different levels learn in the same class, with differentiation handled within subjects (ability-level courses (Fachleistungskurse): the E-Kurs for stronger pupils, the G-Kurs for the basic level). The goal is social integration and a late choice of track. Many comprehensive schools have a grammar-school upper level (Gymnasiale Oberstufe, grades 11–13) leading to the Abitur.

items: Plus: mixed classes, less social pressure
Plus: you can reach the Abitur even after starting at the basic level
Plus: a wider choice of clubs and project work (AGs)
Minus: the pace is geared to the average level — strong pupils may be bored
Minus: the Abitur takes 1 year longer than at a G8 grammar school

steps.title: Routes to the Abitur "the roundabout way"

content.text: One of the main myths is "no Gymnasium = no Abitur". In fact, Germany has many legal routes to the Abitur after an intermediate or comprehensive school:

items.title: 1. Via the grammar-school upper level of a comprehensive school (Gymnasiale Oberstufe Gesamtschule)

content.text: After 10th grade at a comprehensive school (with an intermediate education certificate (Mittlerer Bildungsabschluss) + entitlement (Berechtigung)), you move into the upper level (Oberstufe, grades 11–13) and sit the Abitur.

A specialized grammar school (Wirtschaft, Technik, Gesundheit, Sozialwesen) — grades 11–13 after the intermediate school-leaving certificate (Mittlere Reife). You earn the general university entrance qualification (Allgemeine Hochschulreife) plus a subject-specific base.
For adults: earning the Abitur in the evening or full-time. Free. Takes 3 years.

items.title: 4. University of applied sciences entrance qualification (Fachhochschulreife) via vocational training (Berufsausbildung)

content.text: Vocational training (Ausbildung) plus a vocational upper secondary school (Berufsoberschule, BOS) leads to the university of applied sciences entrance qualification (Fachhochschulreife) or the general university entrance qualification (Allgemeine Hochschulreife).

In states with a binding recommendation (Empfehlung — Bayern, Sachsen), parents often try to "push" their child into the Gymnasium via a trial lesson (Probeunterricht) — but if the child can't cope, they will be moved out by the end of 5th grade anyway. It's better to start at an intermediate or comprehensive school and move up via the upper level (Oberstufe).

A school change (Schulwechsel) "downwards" (Gymnasium → comprehensive school) after grade 6–7 is a common, non-alarming scenario — statistically ~10–15% of Gymnasium pupils make it. Don't treat it as a tragedy.
G8 vs G9 is an important factor in the choice. At a G9 Gymnasium the child has an extra year to "mature"; G8 is intense. If the child is a "late starter", G9 may be better.

International applications (Internationale Bewerbung): when applying to a foreign university, what counts is the Abitur and the average grade, not the specific type of school (Schulform). So the route via a vocational grammar school (Berufliches Gymnasium) is not "worse".

For migrant families: at the transition from 4th grade there is often not enough German for the Gymnasium — it's better to spend 1–2 years at a comprehensive school with language support, then transfer. This is completely normal.

costs.label: State Gymnasium/Gesamtschule
costs.note: Free; Schulbedarf 200–500€/year

costs.label: Internat-Gymnasium (private boarding)
costs.note: Per year; the most expensive — Salem, Schloss Neubeuern

costs.label: Private Gesamtschule (Waldorf, Phorms)
costs.note: Per month; depends on the Schulgeld model

costs.label: Probeunterricht (Bayern)
costs.note: Free; a 3-day exam in case of a negative Empfehlung

costs.label: Textbooks and materials
costs.note: Per year; in some states Lernmittelfreiheit (free)

title: After-school care (Hort): after school
tldr: After-school care (Hort) is an extended-day group for primary-school children (Grundschule, grades 1–4). After lessons the child stays under supervision: lunch, help with homework (Hausaufgabenbetreuung), games and a holiday programme. After-school care can be attached to the school or be a separate municipal facility; a place is requested through the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) or directly at the school. The fee depends on the family's income (0–200 €/month), with meals charged separately. From 2026, a legal right (Rechtsanspruch) to all-day after-school care (all-day supervision, Ganztagsbetreuung) for primary-school children is being phased in under the All-Day Support Act (Ganztagsförderungsgesetz).

steps.title: What after-school care (Hort) is and who needs it

content.text: After-school care (Hort, in full: school after-school care (Schulhort) or children's after-school care (Kinderhort)) is a form of childcare for primary-school-age children outside lesson hours. In many states the German primary school (Grundschule) finishes early — around 11:30–13:00 — so working parents need supervision for their child until the end of the working day. After-school care covers exactly this window: children go there after lessons and stay until 16:00–17:00, and all day during the holidays.

The legal basis for childcare is Book Eight of the Social Code (Achtes Buch Sozialgesetzbuch, SGB VIII), the book on child and youth services. After-school care is classed among the daycare facilities (Kindertageseinrichtungen) for schoolchildren and is funded by the municipality (Kommune) through the youth welfare office (Jugendamt). It goes by different names in different states: Hort, schoolchild care (Schulkindbetreuung), open all-day school (OGS, Offene Ganztagsschule), or primary school with supervision (Betreuende Grundschule).

items: After-school care (Hort) — for children aged 6–10 (grades 1–4 of primary school)
Purpose — supervision + lunch + help with homework + activities
Can be at the school (in der Schule) or in a separate building nearby
Holiday care (Ferienbetreuung) — an extra plus for working parents
The fee depends on the family's income and is set by the municipality

steps.title: Forms of after-school care: Hort, OGS, all-day school (Ganztagsschule)

content.text: In practice you will come across several models, and it's important to understand the difference — it determines where you apply and how much you pay.

items: A separate facility; the child goes there after school
Application usually through the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) or directly at the after-school care centre
Flexible hours, a well-developed holiday programme
After-school care is organized right in the school building
Enrolment through the school when the child is admitted
Participation is voluntary, but once you enrol it usually applies for the whole school year
The full day is mandatory for all pupils at this school
Lessons and activities alternate until 15:00–16:00
A separate care fee is usually not charged (only meals are paid for)

content.text: The procedure depends on the model and the state, but the general logic is the same: a place in after-school care is requested in advance, often at the same time as the child's enrolment in 1st grade (Einschulung). Don't delay — in big cities, places are limited.

items: Find out from the school which model applies (Hort, OGS, all-day)
If it's after-school care through the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) — fill in the application for after-school care (Antrag auf Hortbetreuung)
If it's OGS — submit the application when registering for 1st grade
Attach income certificates (Einkommensnachweis) for calculating the fee
State the days and times you need (often you can choose 3 or 5 days a week)
Apply by the spring of the year in which the child starts school

content.text: The right to an after-school care place (legal right, Rechtsanspruch) for primary-school children is being phased in from the 2026/2027 school year and will extend to all primary-school grades (Grundschule) by 2029/2030 (the All-Day Support Act, Ganztagsförderungsgesetz). But even after the rule takes effect, waiting lists and a shortage of places in big cities will remain — apply as early as possible and look into a childminder (Tagesmutter) in parallel.

After-school care (Hort) is a paid service, but the fee is socially graded: the contribution (after-school care fee, Hortbeitrag) is calculated by the municipality based on the family's income, the number of children and the number of hours booked. Low-income families can get care free or at a large discount, and benefit recipients (basic income support (Bürgergeld), housing benefit (Wohngeld), child supplement (Kinderzuschlag)) get a fee exemption and meals paid through the education and participation package (Bildung und Teilhabe, BuT).

items: Care fee: from 0 to about 200 €/month depending on income
Lunch (Mittagessen) is paid separately — usually 3–4 € a day
Large families often get a discount for the second and subsequent children
On basic income support (Bürgergeld) / housing benefit (Wohngeld) — an exemption, and the education and participation package (BuT) covers lunches and excursions
An application for a fee reduction (Beitragsermäßigung) is submitted to the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) with an income certificate

costs.label: Hort fee (per month)
costs.note: Depends on the family's income; low-income — free or discounted.

costs.label: After-school care lunch (per day)
costs.note: Paid separately; with Bürgergeld covered through BuT.

costs.label: Holiday programme (Ferienbetreuung)
costs.note: Usually included in the monthly fee; in some models there is an extra charge for it.

title: Child benefit (Kindergeld): application and 2026 rates
tldr: Child benefit (Kindergeld) is a benefit the state pays for EACH child, regardless of the parents' income. In 2026 the rate is 259 € per month per child. It is paid by the family benefits office (Familienkasse) at the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit). Everyone who lives in Germany and pays taxes here is entitled to it (including foreigners with a suitable residence permit). You apply in writing or online, and the child needs a tax identification number (Steuer-ID). For high-income families, the tax office (Finanzamt) automatically compares child benefit with the child tax allowance (Kinderfreibetrag) through a favourability check (Günstigerprüfung) and applies whichever is more beneficial.

steps.title: What child benefit (Kindergeld) is and the 2026 rate

content.text: Child benefit (Kindergeld) is the basic child benefit in Germany. It is paid not as assistance for the needy, but as support for families with children in general: a millionaire, a student and a recipient of basic income support (Bürgergeld) all receive it. The money is transferred to the parent's account every month.

In 2026, child benefit is 259 € per month per child — the same for the first, second, third and every further child. The rate was raised on 1 January 2026 from 255 € to 259 € (in 2025 it was 255 €, and 250 € before that). The amount is reviewed every year and may go up, so always check the current figure on the website of the family benefits office (Familienkasse).

items: 2026 rate: 259 € per month per child
Paid by the family benefits office (Familienkasse) at the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit)
Paid monthly into a bank account in Germany (IBAN)
Entitlement does not depend on income — it is not a social benefit
Paid until age 18, and during studies/vocational training (Ausbildung) until age 25

content.text: Do not confuse child benefit (Kindergeld — a monthly payment) with the child tax allowance (Kinderfreibetrag). These are two alternatives that serve the same purpose, and you cannot receive both at once: when it processes your annual tax return, the tax office (Finanzamt) carries out a favourability check (Günstigerprüfung) and applies whichever option is more beneficial for your family. For most families, child benefit is the more beneficial one.

Child benefit (Kindergeld) is available to anyone who has their residence or habitual abode in Germany (Wohnsitz / gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt). Citizens of the EU/EEA/Switzerland receive it on the same basis as everyone else. Third-country nationals qualify if they hold a suitable residence permit that allows work or confirms integration.

items: German citizens and citizens of the EU/EEA/Switzerland — yes
Permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis, permanent residence) — yes
EU Blue Card (Blue Card) or a work residence permit with the right to work — yes
Recognised refugees and holders of subsidiary protection — yes
A purely study or tourist status without the right to work — usually no
The child may live abroad in an EU country — entitlement is often retained (EU coordination)

content.text: If both parents work in different EU countries, a priority rule (Vorrangregel) applies: the country of employment pays first, and the second tops up the difference if its rate is higher. This is coordinated under EU Regulation 883/2004 — the family benefits office (Familienkasse) sorts it out itself, but do state the second parent's employment abroad in the application.

steps.title: Documents and the child's tax identification number (Steuer-ID)

content.text: The key document is the tax identification number (steuerliche Identifikationsnummer, Steuer-ID) of both the child and the applicant. For a child born in Germany, the tax identification number arrives automatically by post a few weeks after the birth is registered. For a child who has come from abroad, the number is assigned after residence registration (Anmeldung).

items: Tax identification number (Steuer-ID) of the child and the applicant (mandatory)
Child's birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde)
Proof of residence (registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) / registration (Anmeldung))
For children over 18 — proof of studies/vocational training (a school, university or vocational-training certificate (Schul-, Studien- oder Ausbildungsbescheinigung))
Residence permit (for third-country nationals)
Account IBAN for crediting the payment

content.text: Apply on time: child benefit (Kindergeld) is paid retroactively for a maximum of 6 months before the month of application. If you delay, the money for the earlier period is simply lost.
You submit the application to the family benefits office (Familienkasse) for the region where you live. There are three ways to do it.

items: Through the online service of the family benefits office (Familienkasse) at arbeitsagentur.de
You need the child benefit application form (Antrag auf Kindergeld) plus the child annex (Anlage Kind)
Some applications can be submitted with an electronic signature or by uploading scans
Download the forms from the family benefits office (Familienkasse) website, then print and fill them in
Attach copies of your documents and the tax identification number (Steuer-ID)
Send them by post to your family benefits office
The family benefits office (Familienkasse) sends a child benefit decision (Kindergeldbescheid) with a number (child benefit number, Kindergeldnummer)
The first payment arrives in the IBAN you provided
Keep the child benefit number (Kindergeldnummer) — you will need it for all future enquiries

steps.title: Children over 18 and the end of payments

content.text: After age 18, child benefit (Kindergeld) does not stop automatically, but conditions start to apply. The benefit continues until age 25 if the child is in school, university or vocational training (Ausbildung), or is in a transition period of up to 4 months between two stages of education.

items: Up to age 18 — no conditions
Ages 18–25 — while in school, university, vocational training (Ausbildung) or voluntary service (Freiwilligendienst)
Transition period between two stages of education (up to 4 months) — yes
After the first qualification, a second job of more than 20 hrs/week may end the entitlement
Notify the family benefits office (Familienkasse) when studies end, or about a move or a change of status

content.text: Be sure to notify the family benefits office (Familienkasse) of any changes (the child dropped out of studies, moved abroad, or started working full-time). The office will demand repayment of any overpayment, sometimes with interest.

costs.label: Kindergeld 2026 (per month per child)
costs.note: The same for each child; paid by the state, with no contribution from the parent.

costs.label: Application
costs.note: Free through the Familienkasse.

costs.label: Child's Steuer-ID
costs.note: Assigned automatically, free of charge.

title: Child supplement (Kinderzuschlag): for low-income families
tldr: The child supplement (Kinderzuschlag, KiZ) is a top-up to child benefit (Kindergeld) for working families on a low income whose earnings are enough for themselves but not for their children. In 2026 the maximum rate is up to 297 € per month for each child, on top of the usual 259 € of child benefit. It is paid by the family benefits office (Familienkasse) at the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit). The conditions: you receive child benefit, your income is above the minimum threshold (Mindesteinkommensgrenze) but below the upper one, and with the supplement your family does not need basic income support (Bürgergeld). Recipients of the supplement automatically get access to the education and participation package (Bildung und Teilhabe) and an exemption from daycare (Kita) / after-school care (Hort) fees.

content.text: The child supplement (Kinderzuschlag, KiZ for short) is designed for families who work and earn enough for themselves but not enough to also cover the cost of their children. Without the supplement, such families would fall into basic income support (Bürgergeld). The aim of the supplement is to keep work more worthwhile than social benefits and to stop families becoming fully dependent on the state.

The supplement (KiZ) is paid in addition to child benefit (Kindergeld) and also goes through the family benefits office (Familienkasse). The legal basis is § 6a of the Federal Child Benefit Act (Bundeskindergeldgesetz, BKGG). In 2026 the maximum amount is up to 297 € per month for each child; the actual payment may be lower and is calculated individually based on income.

items: 2026 maximum: up to 297 €/month for each child
Paid ON TOP of child benefit (259 €), not instead of it
Paid by the family benefits office (Familienkasse); a separate application from child benefit
For working families on a low income, not for the unemployed on basic income support (Bürgergeld)
Legal basis — § 6a BKGG

content.text: You are entitled to the child supplement (KiZ) if all the conditions are met at the same time. The key one is that the family's income falls within the right range: enough for the parents, but with children added the family would be below the needs threshold.

items: You receive child benefit (Kindergeld) for the child
The child is no older than 25, unmarried and lives with you
The parents' income is above the minimum threshold (minimum income limit, Mindesteinkommensgrenze): 900 € gross for couples, 600 € for single parents
Income and assets are below the upper limit (upper income limit, Höchsteinkommensgrenze)
Taking the supplement + housing benefit (Wohngeld) into account, the family does not need basic income support (Bürgergeld)

content.text: Earnings, housing benefit (Wohngeld) and self-employment income are all counted. Many families wrongly assume they won't qualify — but the threshold is fairly generous, and even families with a middle income and several children are often entitled to the supplement.

steps.title: How much is paid and how it is calculated

content.text: The amount of the supplement (KiZ) is not fixed: it starts at the maximum of 297 € per child and decreases as the family's income rises. The parents' income above the minimum threshold reduces the supplement, and the child's own income (for example, maintenance (Unterhalt)) reduces it even more sharply.

items: Starting maximum — 297 € per child
Parents' income above the threshold reduces the payment gradually
Maintenance and the child's income reduce the supplement by 45 % of the amount
It is easiest to check the exact calculation via the online calculator KiZ-Lotse on the family benefits office (Familienkasse) website
With several children, the amounts add up

content.text: The family benefits office (Familienkasse) website has an online calculator, KiZ-Lotse: in a couple of minutes it shows whether you are entitled and the approximate amount. This is the best first step before applying.

The application is submitted to the family benefits office (Familienkasse) — separately from child benefit (Kindergeld), even if you already receive child benefit. The supplement is granted for 6 months (the granting period, Bewilligungszeitraum), after which it has to be renewed.

items: Run the online calculator KiZ-Lotse at arbeitsagentur.de
Prepare income certificates for the last few months
Find out the amount of your housing benefit (Wohngeld), if you receive it
Online via the family benefits office (Familienkasse) service or on paper
Attach income certificates (Einkommensnachweise), the rental contract and the child benefit number (Kindergeldnummer)
List all children and the income of both parents
The supplement (KiZ) is granted for 6 months at a fixed amount
Towards the end of the period, submit a renewal application (Weiterbewilligungsantrag)
Apply early so there is no gap in payments

steps.title: What the supplement gives you on top

content.text: Receiving the supplement (KiZ) is not just about money. Families with the child supplement (Kinderzuschlag) automatically get access to the education and participation package (Bildung und Teilhabe, BuT) and are exempted from daycare and after-school care fees.

items: Education and participation (Bildung und Teilhabe): school supplies, lunches, excursions, clubs
Fee exemption (Beitragsbefreiung) for daycare (Kita) and after-school care (Hort)
An extra 15 € per month for the child's participation in sport/culture
Coverage of school lunches at daycare/school

content.text: The supplement (KiZ) and basic income support (Bürgergeld) are mutually exclusive. If your income is so low that, even with the supplement and housing benefit (Wohngeld), the family is still in need, the family benefits office (Familienkasse) will refuse the supplement and direct you to basic income support at the job centre (Jobcenter). This is normal — basic income support is the better option in that case.

costs.label: Kinderzuschlag 2026 (maximum per month per child)
costs.note: On top of Kindergeld; the actual amount depends on income.

costs.label: Application
costs.note: Free through the Familienkasse.

costs.label: Top-up for participation in sport/culture (BuT)
costs.note: Per month per child while receiving KiZ.

title: A daycare place (Kita-Platz): search and the legal right (Rechtsanspruch)
tldr: Daycare (Kita, Kindertagesstätte) is for children from roughly age 1 until school. The key thing to know: from the moment a child turns 1, every child has a LEGAL right to a place at a daycare centre or with a childminder (Tagesmutter) — this is the legal right (Rechtsanspruch) under § 24 SGB VIII. But the right on paper does not equal a place in practice: in big cities the waiting lists are huge. You need to apply well in advance, to several centres at once. If the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) has not provided a place in time, you have the right to demand one and even to file a lawsuit (Klage), recovering the cost of a paid childminder.

steps.title: The legal right to a place (§ 24 SGB VIII)

content.text: A key fact about the German childcare system: from the day a child turns 1, they have a right enshrined in law (the legal right, Rechtsanspruch) to a place at a daycare facility or in family-based childcare (Kindertagespflege) — with a childminder (Tagesmutter). The basis is § 24 of Book Eight of the Social Code (Achtes Buch Sozialgesetzbuch, SGB VIII). For children under 1, a place is provided only in special circumstances (the parents' work, study or job search).

items: From age 1 — an unconditional right to a place at a daycare centre (Kita) or with a childminder (§ 24 Abs. 2 SGB VIII)
Under age 1 — only with the parents' work/study/job search
From age 3 until school — an extended right to a full place (§ 24 Abs. 3 SGB VIII)
The local youth welfare office (Jugendamt) / youth welfare provider (Träger der Jugendhilfe) is obliged to provide a place
The number of hours (half-day/full-day) depends on the family's needs

content.text: Important: the right guarantees a place, but not a specific centre near your home. The youth welfare office (Jugendamt) may offer a place in another district or with a childminder (Tagesmutter), and formally that counts as fulfilling its obligation, as long as the journey is reasonable.

In big cities (Berlin, München, Hamburg, Frankfurt, Köln) demand for places far exceeds supply. So start the search long before you actually need the place — ideally right after the child is born, or even during pregnancy.

items: Start 9–18 months before the desired start date
Apply to several centres at once (5–10), not just one
Find out your city's system: a central portal, a daycare voucher (Kita-Gutschein) or direct applications
Attend open days (Tag der offenen Tür)
Keep a list: where you applied, the date, the status and the contact person
Don't withdraw from other centres' waiting lists until a contract is signed

content.text: Many cities have centralized online portals (for example, Kita-Navigator in NRW, or Kita-Portal in various states) through which a single application goes to several centres. In other cities you have to contact each centre directly and get the voucher from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt).

items: The child's registration (Anmeldung) at the place of residence (registration certificate, Meldebescheinigung)
Birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde)
Proof of the parents' employment/study (for priority and hours)
Proof of vaccination or consultation (proof of measles protection (Masernschutznachweis) is mandatory)
In states with a voucher — a daycare voucher (Kita-Gutschein) from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt)
Income certificate — if the fee depends on income

content.text: Since 2020, admission to daycare (Kita) requires proof of measles protection (Masernschutznachweis) under the Measles Protection Act (Masernschutzgesetz): either vaccination or a medical exemption. Without it, the centre is not allowed to admit the child.

steps.title: What to do if there is no place

content.text: If your child has already turned 1 and the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) has been unable to provide a place within a reasonable time (as a rule, you need to submit a request at least 6 months in advance), your legal right has been breached — and the law is on your side. Act step by step.

items: Submit a written notice of need (Bedarfsanzeige/Antrag) to the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) at least 6 months in advance
Keep the submission date — it proves the notice period
Record all refusals and the absence of any offers in writing
Write to the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) demanding a place by a specific date
Cite § 24 SGB VIII and the legal right (Rechtsanspruch)
Give notice that otherwise you will go to court and claim compensation
If they do nothing — an urgent application (Eilantrag) / lawsuit (Klage) at the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht)
You can demand that a place be provided at the earliest opportunity
You can recover from the city the cost of a paid childminder/private centre (damages, Schadensersatz)
Many families win such cases — the court sides with the parents

content.text: Don't give up after a verbal refusal from a youth welfare office (Jugendamt) employee. The right to a place is a duty of the state, not a favour. If negotiations don't help, consult a lawyer specializing in social or administrative law, or a local parents' advice centre.

costs.note: Depends on the state and income; free in Berlin, income-based in other states.

costs.label: Meals (Verpflegung)
costs.note: Paid separately; in Berlin a fixed contribution of ~23 €/month.

costs.label: Application and place
costs.note: Joining the waiting list and being provided a place are free.

title: ACV, AvD: alternatives to the ADAC auto club
tldr: ADAC is Germany's largest auto club, but not the only one. ACV (Auto Club Verkehr) from ~55€/year (the Junge Leute tariff) and AvD (Automobilclub von Deutschland) from ~80€/year offer a similar set of services — breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe), towing (Abschleppen), legal protection — often with more flexible tariffs. If ADAC doesn't suit you on price or because of its reputation (the "Gelber Engel" award scandal in 2014), you have a choice.

steps.title: Why you need an auto club in Germany

content.text: An auto club (Automobilclub) is a membership organization that, when your car breaks down, sends a roadside mechanic (Pannenhelfer) to the scene, tows the car to the nearest garage (towing, Abschleppen), helps with legal disputes (traffic-law legal protection, Verkehrsrechtsschutz) and often provides cover abroad (Auslandsschutz). Without membership, calling a tow truck on the Autobahn costs 200-500€, and a repair on the spot starts at 150€. The annual fee for any club pays for itself with the very first breakdown.

items: ADAC — 22 million members, the largest in Europe, but the busiest
ACV (Auto Club Verkehr — the No. 2 auto club by size) — ~400 thousand members
AvD (Automobilclub von Deutschland — the oldest auto club, since 1899) — a premium image
ACE (Auto Club Europa — the No. 3 auto club) — geared to union members and commuters
BAVC — a motorcycle club

steps.title: Comparison of ACV and AvD tariffs for 2026

content.text: Prices are current as of June 2026. The tariffs depend on the region and on partner offers (for example, a discount through the Austrian auto club ÖAMTC via cross-membership).

items: ~70€/year for one driver
Breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe) and towing (Abschleppen) across Germany and Europe
Traffic-law legal protection (Verkehrsrechtsschutz) through partners (option +30€)
Cover abroad (Auslandsschutzbrief) included
An additional family member +25€/year
AvD Komfort: ~84€/year — breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe), towing (Abschleppen), a rental car (Mietwagen) for 3 days
AvD Premium: ~145€/year — adds legal protection, medical repatriation (Krankenrücktransport) and a hotel for up to 4 nights
Cover abroad (Auslandsschutz) is included in all tariffs
Help comes through a network of partner garages

content.text: Register online at acv.de or avd.de by applying for membership (Mitgliedschaft beantragen). Pay by direct debit (SEPA-Lastschrift) or bank transfer (Überweisung). The membership card arrives by post in 5-10 days. Breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe) is active from the first day after payment — unlike insurance, which has a waiting period (Wartezeit).

The arrival time of the roadside mechanic (Pannenhelfer) at ACV and AvD is longer than at ADAC: on average 60-90 minutes versus 30-45 minutes. In Berlin or on the A2 Autobahn at rush hour you can wait as long as 2 hours. If speed matters, ADAC is still the best choice.

Traffic-law legal protection (Verkehrsrechtsschutz) is often sold as an add-on rather than included in the base tariff — read the service description (Leistungsbeschreibung). At AvD, legal protection is included only in the Premium tariff.
With most clubs, membership can only be cancelled by 30 September (the notice period (Kündigungsfrist) is 3 months before the end of the year); otherwise it automatically renews for another year.

items: I drive a lot around Germany and want a fast response — ADAC
An old car, frequent breakdowns, on a budget — ACV
Premium service, holiday trips, I want a rental car (Mietwagen) — AvD Premium
A union member or daily commuter — ACE
Motorcycle only — BVDM or BAVC

title: ADAC: membership and towing
tldr: ADAC (Allgemeiner Deutscher Automobil-Club) is Europe's largest auto club (22 million members). As of May 2026, basic membership costs 54€/year, ADAC Plus 94€/year (with cover abroad, Auslandsschutz), and ADAC Premium 139€/year (the full package with a rental car (Mietwagen) and medical repatriation (Krankenrücktransport)). By decision of the members' meeting (Mitgliederversammlung) of 23.05.2026, from 1 January 2027 the fees rise to 64€ / 114€ / 174€ respectively (the first increase in 6+ years) — check that this is current. Breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe) arrives in 30 minutes on average, and towing (Abschleppen) up to 100 km is free. It pays for itself with one breakdown.

steps.title: What ADAC is and what membership includes

content.text: ADAC is an association of motorists, founded in 1903. Its main service is breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe): the "yellow angels" (Gelbe Engel) arrive in a special roadside assistance vehicle (Pannenhilfefahrzeug), fix the car on the spot in about 80% of cases, and if necessary tow it to a garage. ADAC also gives legal advice, publishes test reviews of cars and tyres, and provides discounts on hotels and rental cars (Mietwagen).

items: Breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe) in Germany — in all tariffs, 24/7
Towing (Abschleppen) to the nearest garage — in all tariffs
Cover abroad (Auslandsschutzbrief) — only Plus and Premium
A rental car (Mietwagen) and hotel — only Premium
Medical repatriation by plane (Krankenrücktransport) — only Premium

steps.title: ADAC 2026 tariffs and how to choose

content.text: Prices are current as of June 2026 (54€ / 94€ / 139€). From 1 January 2027 the fees rise to 64€ / 114€ / 174€ — the first increase in more than 6 years, approved at the members' meeting (Mitgliederversammlung) on 23.05.2026. Partner membership (Partnermitgliedschaft) for a spouse costs roughly half the basic fee.

items: Breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe) across Germany 24/7
Towing (Abschleppen) up to 100 km / to the nearest garage
Legal advice by phone
Discounts on ADAC tests, hotels and rental cars (Mietwagen)
Membership card (ADAC Mitgliedsausweis)
Everything in basic, plus:
Cover abroad (Auslandsschutzbrief) — breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe) and towing (Abschleppen) in Europe and Turkey
Medical repatriation (Krankenrücktransport) in case of illness/accident abroad
Emergency callback service while travelling (Reiserückrufservice)
A rental car (Mietwagen) for 3 days for a breakdown >50 km from home
Everything in Plus, plus:
A rental car (Mietwagen) for up to 7 days (instead of 3)
A hotel for up to 4 nights while waiting for a repair
Travel cancellation insurance up to 10 000€
Extended medical repatriation (Krankenrücktransport), including an outpatient ambulance (ambulanter Krankenwagen)

content.text: Apply at adac.de/mitgliedschaft, through the "ADAC App" or at any ADAC office (ADAC-Geschäftsstelle; there's one in every major city). Breakdown assistance (Pannenhilfe) works from the first day after payment. The card arrives in 5-7 days; until then you can use the digital card in the app.

steps.title: How to call ADAC when you break down

content.text: If the car breaks down, pull over onto the hard shoulder, switch on the hazard lights (Warnblinker), put on a high-visibility vest (Warnweste, mandatory under §53a StVZO), and place the warning triangle (Warndreieck) 50-100 m back (100-200 m on the Autobahn).

items: +49 89 22 22 22 — the main breakdown assistance number (Pannenhilfe, 24/7)
0180 2 22 22 22 — the short German number (6 cents/min)
Via the ADAC app — the "Pannenhilfe" button automatically sends your GPS coordinates
On the Autobahn: an emergency call column (Notrufsäule; orange posts every 2 km) — the little arrow points to the nearest one
Member number (Mitgliedsnummer)
Exact location (Autobahn, km, direction; address in town)
Make and model of the car + the licence plate (Kennzeichen)
What happened (engine problems (Motorprobleme), a flat tyre (Reifenpanne), a dead battery (Batterie leer))
How many people are in the car, and whether there are children/animals

content.text: Basic membership does NOT include cover abroad (Auslandsschutzbrief). If you're driving on holiday to Italy or Croatia, get Plus — otherwise, for a breakdown abroad you'll have to pay for towing out of your own pocket (1000-3000€).

ADAC does not cover scheduled maintenance (the TÜV inspection, an oil change). If you run out of fuel, they'll help you get to the nearest petrol station, but this is a one-off service, no more than a couple of times a year; if abused, they may refuse.

Cancellation — only by 30 September for the end of the year (the notice period (Kündigungsfrist) is 3 months). If you forget, it renews automatically. Cancel in writing by email or post, with confirmation.

The 2014 scandal over the "Gelber Engel" award: ADAC had falsified the voting for "favourite car of the year". After a reform, trust was largely restored, but if reputation matters to you on principle, take a look at ACV or AvD.

title: AU: emissions test
tldr: Abgasuntersuchung (AU) is the car's exhaust-emissions test. Since 2018 it is carried out only together with the Hauptuntersuchung (HU) — every 2 years at TÜV, DEKRA, GTÜ or KÜS. On its own the AU costs ~30-50€, bundled with the HU it is 90-150€. Without the AU you won't get the HU sticker (Plakette), and without that you may not drive — a 75€ fine + 1 Punkt (if you are more than 8 months overdue).

steps.title: What the AU is and who needs it

content.text: The emissions test (Abgasuntersuchung) checks that your exhaust meets environmental limits. The former §47a StVZO, which governed a separate AU, has been repealed (weggefallen); today the AU is part of the mandatory technical inspection (Hauptuntersuchung) and is carried out under §29 StVZO in conjunction with Anlage VIIIa. AU and HU used to be done separately, but since 1 January 2018 the AU is integrated into the HU and is carried out only at inspection points (Prüfstellen) authorised for the full HU (TÜV, DEKRA, GTÜ, KÜS). Ordinary garages (Werkstätten) no longer carry out the AU on their own.

items: Mandatory for all petrol and diesel cars
NOT required for electric cars (no exhaust)
Required for hybrids (they have a combustion engine)
Frequency: every 24 months together with the HU
New cars: first AU/HU after 36 months

content.text: Technically the AU takes 10-20 minutes. The inspector (Prüfer) connects diagnostic equipment to the OBD-2 port, reads the error codes (Fehlercodes) and the emissions data. For diesels there is an additional opacity measurement (Trübungsmessung). Petrol engines with a catalytic converter are checked for CO, HC and NOx.

items: Warm the engine up to operating temperature (~80°C)
Check the engine warning light (Motorkontrollleuchte, check engine) — it must be off
Top up AdBlue (for diesels with SCR)
Bring the registration certificate, part I (Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil I, Fahrzeugschein) and the inspection service book (Prüfbuch)
TÜV station — with or without an appointment (Termin), price 90-120€ (HU+AU)
DEKRA branch (DEKRA-Filiale) — usually cheaper, 85-110€
GTÜ inspection point (GTÜ Prüfstelle) — available at many garages
KÜS — the fourth large organisation
Through your own garage — the car goes to the inspector (Prüfer), price +20€

content.text: If the car passes, the inspector (Prüfer) sticks the inspection sticker (HU-Plakette) onto the rear plate (the colour changes every year: in 2026 it is blue (blau), in 2027 yellow (gelb)). The inspection report (Prüfbericht) shows the result "ohne Mängel". With minor defects (geringe Mängel) the HU still passes, but the defects must be fixed. With significant defects (erhebliche Mängel) you have to fix them and come back for a re-inspection (Nachprüfung) within a month — that is +30-40€.

Since 2023 the mandatory particle-number measurement (Partikelanzahl-Messung) is back for diesels — on older Euro 5 diesels this is a common reason for failure. Before the AU, check the condition of the diesel particulate filter (Dieselpartikelfilter, DPF).

If the HU/AU is more than 2 months overdue, the inspector (Prüfer) carries out an extended inspection (erweiterte HU) at a higher fee; being overdue can also incur a fine (Verwarnungsgeld). More than 8 months overdue means a 75€ fine + 1 point (Punkt) in the KBA register in Flensburg.

Tampering with the AdBlue system ("AdBlue-Killer", "NOx-Emulator") is punishable and can qualify as a criminal offence (Straftat). The inspector (Prüfer) sees such interventions — the car gets no sticker (Plakette), plus you face criminal liability.

title: Autobahn: rules and limits
tldr: The German Autobahn is not "driving without rules". The recommended speed (Richtgeschwindigkeit) is 130 km/h, and roughly 30% of stretches have specific limits. Mandatory: stay right by default (Rechtsfahrgebot), an emergency corridor in a jam (Rettungsgasse), no overtaking on the right. Violations are expensive: 100€ for the wrong lane, hundreds of euros and a driving ban for dangerous driving ("Rasen").

content.text: The Autobahn is governed by the road-traffic rules StVO (Straßenverkehrs-Ordnung) and StVZO. Unrestricted stretches make up only about 70% of the network; on the other 30% there are specific speed limits (Tempolimits), often variable, usually 80-120 km/h. On free stretches the recommended speed (Richtgeschwindigkeit) is 130 km/h: exceeding it is not fined, but in a crash at a speed above 130 km/h the insurer can cut the payout because of contributory fault (Mitverschulden).

items: Keep to the right (Rechtsfahrgebot, §2 StVO) — stay in the rightmost free lane
Overtake only on the left (§5 StVO) — overtaking on the right is forbidden, except in a jam
Emergency corridor (Rettungsgasse, §11 Abs. 2 StVO) — mandatory in a jam (Stau)
Minimum speed 60 km/h (if your car is slower, you may not use the Autobahn)
No pedestrians, bicycles, or mopeds <50 cc

content.text: The emergency corridor (Rettungsgasse) is the gap between the leftmost lane and the one next to it on the right, which drivers form in a jam (Stau) or when slowing down. Under §11 Abs. 2 StVO it is mandatory from the moment traffic moves at walking pace (Schrittgeschwindigkeit) or stops. You don't need to wait for sirens — form the corridor as soon as traffic slows.
The left lane moves as far left as possible (you may not pull onto the hard shoulder (Standstreifen)!), the right one as far right as possible. The corridor forms between them.
The leftmost lane goes left. The middle and right lanes go right. The corridor forms between the left and middle lanes (and NOT between the middle and right, as people often wrongly assume).
The leftmost goes left. The rest go right. The corridor runs between the leftmost and the second-from-left lane.

items: Failing to form an emergency corridor (Rettungsgasse): 200€ + 2 points (Punkte) + 1-month driving ban (Fahrverbot)
Obstructing emergency vehicles: up to 320€ + 2 Punkte
Driving along the Rettungsgasse ("I'll skip the queue"): 240-320€ + 1-month Fahrverbot

content.text: Under the updated fines catalogue (Bußgeldkatalog) 2026, the fines for speeding outside built-up areas (including the Autobahn):

items: Up to 10 km/h: 20€
26-30 km/h: 150€ + 1 Punkt (in the Probezeit — Aufbauseminar)
31-40 km/h: 200€ + 1 Punkt + optionally 1-month Fahrverbot
41-50 km/h: 320€ + 2 Punkte + 1-month Fahrverbot
51-60 km/h: 480€ + 2 Punkte + 2-month Fahrverbot
61-70 km/h: 600€ + 2 Punkte + 3-month Fahrverbot
>70 km/h: 700€ + 2 Punkte + 3-month Fahrverbot

content.text: Blocking the left lane (Linke Spur blockieren) — driving in the left lane without overtaking costs 80€ + 1 Punkt. This is one of the most common violations among foreigners. The left lane is for overtaking only; once you finish the manoeuvre, move back to the right immediately.

Overtaking on the right (Rechts überholen) is forbidden when traffic flows faster than 60 km/h. The exception is a jam (Stau), where you may pass on the right with a speed difference of up to 20 km/h. Otherwise 100€ + 1 Punkt.
The hard shoulder (Standstreifen) is not for resting or a toilet stop, only for emergencies. Misusing the hard shoulder is 75€ + 1 Punkt.
Phone in hand while driving (Telefonieren am Steuer) — 100€ + 1 Punkt; in a crash or with another traffic violation — 200€ + 2 Punkte + 1-month Fahrverbot. Hands-free is allowed.

Probationary period (Probezeit, the first 2 years after getting your licence): any serious category-A violation (A-Verstoß), e.g. exceeding the limit by 21 km/h or more, extends the probationary period by 2 years (up to 4 years total) and triggers a mandatory follow-up seminar (Aufbauseminar, 250-450€).

title: Buying a used car: mobile.de, autoscout24
tldr: Mobile.de and AutoScout24 are the two main platforms for buying a used car in Germany (about 90% of the market). A car 5-10 years old costs 8,000-15,000€ on average. Always check: the HU-Bescheinigung, the service book (Service-Heft), the number of previous owners (Vorbesitzer) in the Fahrzeugbrief, the no-claims class (Schadensfreiheitsklasse) with the insurer, and the VIN. Before the deal it is worth ordering a DEKRA check for 100-300€.

steps.title: Where to look for a car

content.text: Germany's used-car market is more transparent than in most countries. Deals happen through three channels: online platforms, dealerships (Autohaus) and private ads. Haggling here is far less aggressive than in Russia or Turkey — you can usually knock at most 5-10% off the asking price.

items: mobile.de — the #1 platform, ~1.5 million listings, filters for everything
AutoScout24 (autoscout24.de) — #2, similar functionality
Kleinanzeigen (free classifieds board, formerly eBay-Kleinanzeigen) — private sellers, cheaper but riskier
Dealership offline (Autohaus) — 1-2K€ more expensive, but a statutory warranty (Gewährleistung) of 12 months is mandatory
Auctions (Auktionen: Copart, BCA) — for the experienced, often post-accident cars

content.text: The standard path: filters on the platform → 3-5 candidates → viewing (Besichtigung) → test drive (Probefahrt) → purchase contract (Kaufvertrag) → re-registration at the vehicle registration office (Zulassungsstelle). The whole thing takes 2-4 weeks.

items: Make/model (Marke/Modell), mileage (Kilometerstand), year (Baujahr), price (Preis) — the main filters
The "HU bis" filter — go for at least 12 months of remaining HU
The "Anzahl Vorbesitzer" filter (number of previous owners) — ≤2 is ideal, ≥4 is risky
Sorting by price ascending (Preis aufsteigend, cheapest first) often reveals hidden problems
The "Suchen mit Bildern" feature (search with photos) — cars without photos are usually problematic
Registration certificate, part I (Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil I, Fahrzeugschein) — the car's "passport"
Registration certificate, part II (Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil II, Fahrzeugbrief) — the main proof of ownership
Latest inspection report (letzter HU-Bericht, Prüfbericht) — all defects from the last inspection
Service book (Service-Heft, Scheckheft) — all services with garage stamps
Invoices (Rechnungen) for major repairs
For an accident car (Unfallwagen) — proof of the repair
Check that the VIN on the vehicle title (Fahrzeugbrief) matches the one on the body and engine
Paint-thickness gauge (Lackdickenmessgerät; magnetic) — reveals filler
Check the service book (Service-Heft) — missed services = a red flag
OBD-2 scanner (10€ Bluetooth adapter + app) — error codes (Fehlercodes)
Test drive (Probefahrt) of 30+ min, including the Autobahn
A DEKRA check for 100-300€ if the car costs more than 10,000€
ADAC model purchase contract (ADAC Musterkaufvertrag, free download) — the standard template
Between private individuals: the clause "gekauft wie gesehen" (bought as seen) excludes liability for defects (Sachmängelhaftung) — but not for deliberately concealed defects
At a dealer (Autohaus): a minimum statutory warranty (Gewährleistung) of 12 months is mandatory under §476 BGB
Pay only once you have the vehicle title (Fahrzeugbrief) in hand!
Cashless: by bank transfer (Überweisung) via GeldKarte or Sofort-Überweisung
Cash >10,000€ — the bank will require proof of the funds' origin (Herkunftsnachweis)

content.text: After the purchase you have 30 days to re-register (Ummeldung) at the vehicle registration office (Kfz-Zulassungsstelle) of your district (Landkreis). You need: the vehicle title (Fahrzeugbrief), national ID card or passport (Personalausweis/Pass), the insurance confirmation number (eVB-Nummer) from your insurer (you get it online in 5 min), a direct-debit mandate (SEPA-Mandat) for the vehicle tax (KFZ-Steuer), and the inspection certificate (HU-Bescheinigung). Cost 35-70€ + new plates 25-40€.

Mileage tampering (Tachomanipulation). Check via CARFAX-style services: CARFAX Europe, FAHRZEUGAKTE, or autoDNA. Compare the mileage (Kilometerstand) with the entries in the service book (Service-Heft) and the inspection report (HU-Bericht).

A concealed accident car (Unfallwagen). The "wie gesehen" clause does not protect the seller if they deliberately hid an accident: under §444 BGB the exclusion of liability cannot be invoked in cases of wilful deception (arglistige Täuschung). The deal can be challenged (Anfechtung) even years later — but you have to prove the deception.

Pseudo-private sale (Schein-Privatverkauf): dealers pose as private sellers to dodge the mandatory statutory warranty (Gewährleistung). Signs: the seller has several cars on the platform, won't show a national ID card (Personalausweis) and rushes you to pay.
Fake ads (Fake-Inserate) on Kleinanzeigen asking you to transfer a deposit: the car doesn't exist. Never pay in advance — only after viewing it in person.

Don't forget car insurance (KFZ-Versicherung) before you submit the documents: without the insurance confirmation number (eVB-Nummer) they won't register the car. Compare on check24.de, verivox.de — the difference can be 2x.
