title: DEKRA check when buying
tldr: The DEKRA Gebrauchtwagen-Check is an independent technical inspection of a car before you buy it. The basic Check is 100-200€, the Check+ with diagnostics is 200-300€. The buyer orders and pays for the inspection. They check 75-150 points: body, engine, chassis, electrics, documents. It is worth doing for cars over 7,000€ — it pays for itself with a single problem uncovered.

content.text: This is a technical inspection of a car by an independent expert (Sachverständiger) before you buy it. Unlike the HU/AU, which only check road safety (Verkehrssicherheit), the used-car inspection (Gebrauchtwagen-Check) uncovers hidden defects: traces of accidents, rolled-back mileage, corrosion, wear, and unrecorded repairs. The main providers are DEKRA, TÜV (NORD/SÜD/Rheinland), GTÜ and KÜS.

items: An independent assessment of the condition — the seller has no influence
A written inspection report (Prüfbericht) to argue the price
Legal value in later disputes
Not to be confused with the HU — this goes deeper and wider
Pays off on cars from 7,000€

steps.title: Types of inspection and the process

content.text: DEKRA offers three levels of inspection. You can come to a DEKRA station (DEKRA-Station) or have an expert (Sachverständiger) come to the seller — the latter is handier for long trips.

items: Basic check: body, engine (from the outside), tyres, brakes, lights
~50 points
Time: 30-45 min
Written report (Bericht) with photos
Suitable for cars up to 7,000€
Full inspection + OBD-2 diagnostics
Test drive (Probefahrt) with the inspector (Prüfer)
Paint-thickness measurement (Lackdickenmessung; to find filler/respraying)
Check of the vehicle title (Fahrzeugbrief), service book (Service-Heft), VIN
~100 points
Suitable for cars 7,000-15,000€
Everything from the standard one + a lift
Check of the underbody, exhaust and chassis from below
Endoscopy (Endoskopie) with a camera if anything is suspected
Check via CARFAX-style services
A full expert valuation (Wertgutachten)
For cars 15,000€+ and premium makes (BMW, Mercedes, Audi)

content.text: Book via dekra.de/de/gebrauchtwagencheck or by phone. If the seller is far away, pick a DEKRA station (DEKRA-Station) near them so they bring the car themselves. The inspection takes 1-2 hours, and the report (Bericht) arrives by email within a day.

If the seller refuses a Check, that is a warning sign. A trustworthy seller understands that the buyer pays for the inspection for their own peace of mind. A refusal often means there is something to hide.

A Check does not uncover 100% of hidden defects: internal faults in a DSG gearbox or minor electrical glitches may only show up months later. The expert's (Sachverständiger) liability is limited — read the terms (AGB).
Don't order a Check at a garage (Werkstatt) recommended by the seller — that's a conflict of interest. Use an independent provider only.
An alternative is private experts (Sachverständige), e.g. Carexpert: cheaper (60-150€), but their report carries less weight in disputes than one from DEKRA or TÜV.

title: Dekra: an alternative to TÜV
tldr: DEKRA, GTÜ and KÜS are officially recognised alternatives to TÜV for the Hauptuntersuchung (HU) and Abgasuntersuchung (AU) under §29 StVZO. Their authority and the Plakette are identical. DEKRA is usually 5-15€ cheaper than TÜV, and GTÜ and KÜS are cheaper still. The inspection quality is identical: all organisations work to the same federal standards under state supervision.

steps.title: Who besides TÜV carries out the HU

content.text: In Germany, the right to carry out the HU/AU belongs to organisations accredited as a technical inspection body (Technische Prüfstelle, TP) or a supervisory organisation (Überwachungsorganisation, ÜO) under §29 StVZO. In practice that means four large networks plus regional ones. The inspection sticker (Plakette) is the same everywhere (its colour depends on the year, blue in 2026), and it is valid for 24 months.

items: TÜV (NORD, SÜD, Rheinland, HESSEN, THÜRINGEN, Saarland) — ~50% of the market
DEKRA — ~25% of the market, uniform across Germany
GTÜ (Gesellschaft für Technische Überwachung) — ~15%
KÜS (Kraftfahrzeug-Überwachungsorganisation freiberuflicher Kfz-Sachverständiger) — ~10%
All of them = identical authority and Plakette

steps.title: Where it's cheaper and more convenient

content.text: The price of the HU+AU varies by state because of the different fee schedule (Gebührenordnung). For example, the HU is more expensive in Bayern and cheaper in NRW. Within a single city the difference between TÜV and DEKRA is usually 10-20€.

items: TÜV SÜD: 95-135€
TÜV NORD: 90-125€
TÜV Rheinland: 95-130€
TÜV — its own inspection points (Prüfstellen) in larger cities
DEKRA — its own branches (Filialen) + many garages (garage inspection, Werkstattprüfung)
GTÜ and KÜS — almost only at garages (partner garages, Vertragspartner-Werkstätten)
Find the nearest one: dekra.de/standortsuche, tuev-sued.de/standorte

content.text: TÜV stations are often walk-in, but with 30-60 min queues. DEKRA, GTÜ and KÜS usually go through your garage and need an appointment (Termin) in advance. If you do the HU at your own garage (Werkstatt), it usually books the inspector (Prüfer) itself, who comes by 1-2 times a week.

TÜV is not a car brand or a "quality mark", but the name of one of the inspection organisations. When a seller says "the car passed TÜV", ask exactly who inspected it: a sticker (Plakette) from DEKRA is just as legitimate.

Garage inspection (Werkstattprüfung, the HU right at your garage): by law the inspector (Prüfer) is independent of the garage, but there can still be subtle pressure. If in doubt, it's better to go to a separate TÜV or DEKRA station.
GTÜ and KÜS are rarer in Eastern Germany — DEKRA dominates there. In the West it's TÜV Rheinland in NRW and TÜV SÜD in Bayern/BW.

The sticker (Plakette) and being overdue: after the HU you get a sticker whose colour and numbers indicate the month and year of the next inspection. Being more than 2 months overdue means a higher fee, and more than 8 months means a 75€ fine + 1 point (Punkt).

title: Bußgeldkatalog: fines
tldr: The Bußgeldkatalog (BKat) is the official catalogue of fines for traffic violations. The current version has applied since 2021 (with up-to-date 2026 rates). Penalties are split into Verwarnungsgeld (up to 55€, no Punkte) and Bußgeld (from 60€, usually with Punkte and/or a Fahrverbot). 8 Punkte in Flensburg means your licence is revoked. Foreigners are sent fines to their registered address (Anmeldung).

content.text: The German penalty system has three levels. A warning fine (Verwarnungsgeld, up to 55€) is for a minor violation and is paid without admitting guilt. An administrative fine (Bußgeld, from 60€) is for a serious violation and is issued via a fine notice (Bußgeldbescheid) with a right of appeal. A criminal offence (Straftat) — e.g. driving without a licence (Fahren ohne Fahrerlaubnis) or 1.1‰ blood alcohol and above — means court, a fine and/or imprisonment.

items: Verwarnungsgeld up to 55€ — no points (Punkte), no entry in KBA Flensburg
Bußgeld from 60€ — often +1-2 Punkte, sometimes a driving ban (Fahrverbot)
Punkte are held in the driving-fitness register (Fahreignungsregister, FAER) in Flensburg
8 Punkte = automatic revocation of the driving licence (Führerschein)
Punkte expire after 2.5/5/10 years depending on severity

Mit Gefährdung: 320€ + 2 Punkte + 1-month Fahrverbot
Mit Sachbeschädigung: 360€ + 2 Punkte + 1-month Fahrverbot

content.text: After the 2014 reform the system was simplified: points (Punkte) are issued by the Federal Motor Transport Authority (Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt, KBA) in Flensburg, and the register is called the driving-fitness register (Fahreignungsregister, FAER). You can check your own Punkte for free online at kba.de using your national ID card (Personalausweis) and the activated online ID function (Online-Ausweisfunktion).

items: 1 Punkt — a minor violation (held for 2.5 years)
2 Punkte — a serious violation (held for 5 years)
3 Punkte — a Straftat (held for 10 years)
1-3 Punkte: nothing
4-5 Punkte: a warning (Ermahnung)
6-7 Punkte: a stern warning (Verwarnung) + the offer of a driving-fitness seminar (Fahreignungsseminar, FAS) for 400-500€
8 Punkte: revocation of the driving entitlement (Entzug der Fahrerlaubnis) for at least 6 months + the MPU "Idiotentest"

content.text: A questionnaire (Anhörungsbogen) arrives 6-8 weeks before the fine notice (Bußgeldbescheid). You have the right not to incriminate yourself — you are not obliged to say who was driving. Sometimes a case is dropped because the limitation period has run out (Verjährungsfrist — 3 months for administrative offences, Ordnungswidrigkeiten).

Probationary period (Probezeit, the first 2 years after getting your licence): any serious category-A violation (A-Verstoß) — exceeding the limit by 21 km/h or more, phone in hand, running a red light — extends the probationary period by 2 years (up to 4 years) and triggers a mandatory follow-up seminar (Aufbauseminar) for 250-450€. For repeat offences the licence is revoked.

Foreign drivers: within the EU, fines are enforced across borders from 70€. Holders of Russian, Ukrainian or Belarusian licences are fined under German rules, but get no Punkte — their licence is not in the German register.

An appeal (Einspruch) is filed within 2 weeks of the Bußgeldbescheid. If the fine is >250€ or there's a Fahrverbot, it's worth contacting a traffic-law lawyer (Verkehrsrechtsanwalt, often covered by legal-protection insurance, Rechtsschutzversicherung). The chance of a reduction is 30-50%.
An environmental zone (Umweltzone) exists in most large cities: you need a green environmental sticker (grüne Umweltplakette) on the windscreen. Entering without one is 100€.

title: Punkte in Flensburg: 8 = losing your licence
tldr: In Germany all traffic violations are recorded in a single driving-fitness register (Fahreignungsregister, FAER) at the KBA in Flensburg. A points system applies (Fahreignungs-Bewertungssystem): each violation earns 1 to 3 points (Punkte). Once you reach 8 points, the driver loses their licence (Fahrerlaubnis); you can only get it back after a block of at least 6 months and, as a rule, a medical-psychological assessment (MPU). The system is governed by §4 StVG. Important: the points are separate from the monetary fine (Bußgeld) and the driving ban (Fahrverbot).

content.text: The driving-fitness points system (Fahreignungs-Bewertungssystem) is based on §4 StVG. For violations that endanger road safety, points (Punkte) are added to the driving-fitness register (FAER), kept by the Federal Motor Transport Authority (Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt, KBA) in Flensburg. The more serious the violation, the more points.

items: 1 point — an ordinary serious violation (Ordnungswidrigkeit), e.g. major speeding
2 points — a violation with a driving ban (Fahrverbot) or a criminal offence (Straftat) without revocation of the licence
3 points — a criminal offence with revocation of the licence, e.g. drink-driving
Points are added regardless of the monetary fine
The register is kept by the KBA in Flensburg — hence the phrase "points in Flensburg"

content.text: The §4 StVG system is tiered. First you get a warning, then a paid stern warning, and only at 8 points is the licence revoked. At each step there is a chance to change course.

items: The points are simply on record in the register; you don't lose your licence
You can voluntarily take a driving-fitness seminar (Fahreignungsseminar) and remove 1 point (only at 1–5 points, once every 5 years)
A written warning from the authority
They recommend taking a driving-fitness seminar (Fahreignungsseminar) — you can still remove 1 point
A paid written warning
At this stage the seminar no longer removes points
The driving entitlement (Fahrerlaubnis) is revoked
The minimum block (Sperrfrist) is 6 months
To get the licence back, a medical-psychological assessment (MPU) is usually required

steps.title: How long points stay on record

content.text: Points don't last forever — each has its own deletion period (Tilgungsfrist) under §29 StVG. The period depends on the severity of the violation and counts from the date the decision takes effect, not the date of the violation.

items: 1 point (ordinary Ordnungswidrigkeit) — deleted after 2.5 years
2 points (violation with a Fahrverbot or a Straftat without revocation) — after 5 years
3 points (Straftat with revocation of the licence) — after 10 years
Important: a new fine does NOT extend old points — each is deleted on its own timer (since 2014)

content.text: You can check your own Flensburg balance for free online via the KBA using the electronic ID function (eID) or by a written request. Don't rely on memory — only the official KBA register gives exact figures.

costs.label: Requesting your own points balance from the KBA
costs.note: Online via eID and a postal request are free.

costs.label: Fahreignungsseminar (seminar to remove a point)
costs.note: Consists of a traffic-education and a psychological part; removes 1 point only at 1–5 points.

costs.note: The cost of the assessment itself; preparation and courses may cost extra.

title: Belarusian licence: exchange
tldr: Belarus is not in the EU/EEA and is not listed in Anlage 11 FeV, so there is no simplified-exchange agreement with Germany. That means you cannot swap a Belarusian licence "one for one": a foreign licence is valid only for the first 6 months after your permanent residence is established (§29 FeV), after which you need a German licence, for which you have to re-sit the theory and practical tests. During those 6 months you may drive on the Belarusian licence with a certified translation or an international driving permit. The exchange itself is processed at the Führerscheinstelle of your registered address under §31 FeV.

steps.title: The status of a Belarusian licence in Germany

content.text: Belarus is one of the so-called "third countries" (Drittstaaten) and is not on the Anlage 11 FeV list. Germany has no exam-free recognition agreement with such countries. This means that after moving you cannot simply swap a Belarusian licence for a German one — you will have to sit exams.

items: Belarus — not EU/EEA and not in Anlage 11 FeV
For the first 6 months after residence registration (Anmeldung) you may drive on the Belarusian licence (§29 FeV)
You need a certified translation of the licence or an international driving permit (IDP)
After 6 months a German driving licence (Führerschein) is required

content.text: Under §29 FeV a foreign licence is valid in Germany for 6 months from the moment you have a normal place of residence (ordentlicher Wohnsitz) — in practice from your residence registration (Anmeldung). After that period you may not drive on the Belarusian licence: this counts as driving without a licence (Fahren ohne Fahrerlaubnis, §21 StVG) and is a criminal offence.

The 6 months count from the start of permanent residence, not from the date you passed your test. Start booking a driving school and the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) right after registering, so you make it before the grace period ends.

steps.title: What you need for the exchange

content.text: Since there is no simplified exchange, the §31 FeV procedure includes exams. The upside is that with a valid Belarusian licence you usually do not need to complete the mandatory minimum of lessons at a driving school — passing the theory and practical tests is enough. That is noticeably cheaper than a full course.

items: Application to the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) of your registered address
Belarusian licence + a certified translation (a sworn translator, vereidigter Übersetzer, or ADAC)
Biometric photo, passport, registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Eye test (Sehtest) and a first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe-Kurs)
Theory test (available in Russian) and a practical test
Verifying the licence's authenticity via the embassy can take weeks

content.text: The theory test (through TÜV or DEKRA) is available in several languages, including Russian — confirm the language when booking. After the German licence is issued, the Belarusian one is usually confiscated and returned to the issuing authority.

costs.label: Certified translation of the licence
costs.note: From a sworn translator or via ADAC.

costs.label: Führerscheinstelle fees + exams
costs.note: Application, issuing the licence, TÜV/DEKRA fees for theory and practical.

costs.label: A few practice/training drives with an instructor
costs.note: There are usually no mandatory hours, but practice before the test is advised; depends on the driving school.

title: 6 months to exchange — the countdown
tldr: A foreign licence (from outside the EU/EEA) is valid in Germany for just 6 months from the moment a normal place of residence (ordentlicher Wohnsitz) is established — §29 FeV. The big confusion: the countdown starts NOT from entry and NOT from the date the licence was issued, but from the date you became a permanent resident (usually the Anmeldung). After 6 months, driving on a foreign licence is Fahren ohne Fahrerlaubnis (§21 StVG), a criminal offence. Exception: those who prove in advance that they came for at most 12 months get the period extended to 12 months.

content.text: The key concept is the normal place of residence (ordentlicher Wohnsitz) under §7 FeV. It is the place where you live at least 185 days a year because of personal and professional ties. In practice such residence arises at the moment of registration (Anmeldung), and it is from that date that §29 FeV counts the 6 months.

items: The countdown is NOT from the date of entry into the country
The countdown is NOT from the date the foreign licence was issued
The countdown is from when a normal place of residence (ordentlicher Wohnsitz) arises — usually from registration (Anmeldung)
The period is exactly 6 months
It concerns licences from countries outside the EU/EEA

content.text: Once the 6 months are up, a foreign licence is no longer valid in Germany. If you keep driving, it qualifies as driving without a licence (Fahren ohne Fahrerlaubnis) — §21 StVG. This is not a minor violation but a criminal offence (Straftat): you risk a fine or imprisonment of up to 1 year, and in a crash the insurer can refuse to pay out.

There is no automatic "grace period". If you haven't obtained a German licence or started the exchange procedure within 6 months, you may not get behind the wheel. In a check, the police go by your registration date (Anmeldung).

§29 FeV provides for an exception: if you prove in advance to the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) that you are staying in Germany for no longer than 12 months (a posting, studies, a student exchange), the validity of the foreign licence is extended to 12 months. You must submit the evidence BEFORE the basic 6 months expire.

items: Submit an application to the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) in advance
Attach proof of a temporary stay (a contract, a letter from the university/employer)
The extension lasts at most until 12 months from the start of residence
For those staying long-term, the only route is the exchange or sitting the exams

costs.label: Applying for an extension to 12 months
costs.note: The fee depends on the Führerscheinstelle; often nominal.

costs.label: Fine/sentence for driving without a licence (§21 StVG)
costs.note: This is a criminal offence: a monetary fine (Geldstrafe) in daily rates or imprisonment of up to 1 year — the amounts are set by the court individually.

title: Full training at a Fahrschule: cost
tldr: If you have no licence at all (or it can't be exchanged), you'll have to take a full course at a driving school (Fahrschule) for category B. According to the ADAC, the total cost averages 2,500–3,500 €, and in large cities it reaches 4,000 € and above. The cost is made up of the driving school's base fee, the mandatory theory and practical lessons, special drives (Sonderfahrten: Autobahn, night, rural — at least 12 under FahrschAusbO) and the TÜV/DEKRA exam fees. The Erste-Hilfe-Kurs and Sehtest are mandatory. The law does not fix an exact number of driving lessons — it depends on the learner.

content.text: The final price for a category-B licence (passenger car) varies a lot by region and depends on how many driving lessons you'll need. The law (FahrschAusbO) strictly fixes only the minimum of special drives and the amount of theory; the number of ordinary driving lessons is set by your instructor based on your readiness.

items: The driving school's base fee (Grundbetrag) — one-off
Theory classes (at least 14 double lessons of 90 min: 12 basic + 2 for category B)
Ordinary driving lessons (Übungsstunden) — the number is individual
Special drives (Sonderfahrten) — a mandatory minimum of 12: 5 rural, 4 Autobahn, 3 night
Admission to the exam (Vorstellung zur Prüfung) — the driving school's fee for admitting you to the exam
TÜV/DEKRA fees for the theory and practical exams

content.text: Besides the driving school itself, you won't be admitted to the exam without two things: a first-aid course and an eye test. They are usually done at the very start, before applying to the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle).

items: 9 teaching units (one day)
Run by DRK, Johanniter, Malteser, ASB and others
Costs about 35–50 €
The certificate never expires
Done at an optician (Optiker) or eye doctor
Costs about 6–12 €
Valid for 2 years for the application
You need a biometric photo for the application

content.text: The biggest expense is driving lessons, and the per-hour price in large cities (Munich, Hamburg) is noticeably higher than in small towns. So it's worth comparing driving schools and preparing for the theory yourself via apps, to avoid paying for extra lessons.

Be wary of driving schools that advertise a suspiciously low base fee (Grundbetrag): they often make up for it with a high price per driving lesson (45–80 € per 45 min) and charge separately for admission to each exam. Ask for the full price list (Preisliste) in writing.

items: Compare the price lists of several driving schools (Fahrschulen)
Prepare for the theory with the official app (Führerschein-App) so you pass first time
Re-sitting an exam = a new TÜV/DEKRA fee, so save money by preparing
The theory can be taken in Russian — confirm when booking

costs.note: The average price across Germany; more expensive in large cities, depends on the number of driving lessons.

costs.note: One day, the certificate never expires.

costs.note: At an optician; valid for 2 years for the application.

title: Russian driving licence: exchanging it in Germany
tldr: Russia is a third country (Drittstaat) and is NOT on the Anlage 11 FeV list. That is exactly why the exchange is not one-to-one: to swap a Russian category B licence for a German one you generally have to pass both the theory and the practical exam (as for any country not listed in Anlage 11). Full driving-school training is not mandatory, though — passing both exams is enough. The 6-month rule applies (§29 FeV): after that you may no longer drive on your Russian licence. Apply at the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) for the place where you are registered (§31 FeV); you will need a certified translation.

content.text: Russia is NOT included in Anlage 11 FeV — the list of non-EU/EEA countries for which an exchange without exams, or with only one exam, is available. Because Russia is not on this list, exchanging a category B licence requires passing both the theory and the practical exam. There is no full recognition without a knowledge check (unlike for EU countries).

items: Russia is NOT in Anlage 11 FeV; an exchange is only possible by taking exams
Both the theory AND the practical exam are required (for category B)
Mandatory driving-school lessons are NOT required
A 6-month grace period applies under §29 FeV
Categories are matched using the FeV correspondence table

content.text: The exchange is handled under §31 FeV at the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) for the place where you are registered. Prepare the full set of documents in advance — without a certified translation of your licence the application will not be accepted. The authority may also verify the document's authenticity separately, which takes time.

items: Application for the exchange (Antrag auf Umschreibung) at the driving licence authority
Russian licence + certified translation (sworn translator, vereidigter Übersetzer, or ADAC)
Passport and registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Biometric photo
Eye test (Sehtest) and first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe-Kurs)
Booking for the theory and practical exams via TÜV or DEKRA

content.text: The theory exam can be taken in Russian — it is an officially supported language. The practical exam is taken in German with an examiner, but basic commands are enough. Once your German licence is issued, the Russian one is usually confiscated.

Don't put it off: under §29 FeV a Russian licence is valid in Germany for only 6 months from the start of permanent residence (usually from your registration, Anmeldung). Within that time you must submit the application and pass both exams. Booking the exams and verifying the licence's authenticity can drag on for weeks.

If the 6 months have expired and you still don't have a German licence, you may not get behind the wheel (that is driving without a licence, Fahren ohne Fahrerlaubnis, §21 StVG, a criminal offence). Start the procedure right after you register.

costs.note: With a sworn translator or via ADAC.

costs.note: Application, licence issuance, TÜV/DEKRA fee for theory and practical.

costs.note: First aid and eye test — mandatory.

costs.note: None are mandatory, but a few lessons with an instructor are usually advised.

title: UK driving licence: post-Brexit
tldr: After Brexit the United Kingdom is no longer in the EU/EEA, so a British licence is now exchanged in Germany under the third-country rules. The good news: the UK is included in Anlage 11 FeV with an exam-free exchange for category B — a British licence is swapped one-to-one on the basis of §30 FeV. The 6-month rule (§29 FeV) applies from the start of permanent residence. Apply at the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle). Licences issued in the EU format before Brexit are now exchanged under the new procedure too.

content.text: Before the UK left the EU, a British licence was valid in Germany just like any EU licence — in effect, no exchange was needed until it expired. After Brexit the United Kingdom became a third country (Drittstaat). But the EU and Germany added the UK to Anlage 11 FeV on favourable terms, so the exchange stayed simple.

items: The UK is now a third country, not EU/EEA
The UK is in Anlage 11 FeV with an exam-free exchange for category B
A British licence is swapped one-to-one for a German one (§30 FeV)
A 6-month grace period applies under §29 FeV

content.text: Since no exams are required for category B, the procedure comes down to submitting documents to the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) for the place where you are registered, under §30 FeV. The British photocard licence is usually accepted by the authority even without a translation, but some authorities do ask for one — check in advance.

items: Application at the driving licence authority for the place where you are registered
British driving licence (photocard)
Passport and registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Biometric photo
Eye test (Sehtest)
Sometimes a certified translation (depends on the authority)

content.text: For higher categories (trucks C, buses D) the conditions in Anlage 11 may differ and may require exams. This guide covers category B (passenger cars). On exchange, the British licence is confiscated and returned to the DVLA.

Despite the simple exchange, the §29 FeV rule applies to British licences too: they are recognised in Germany for 6 months from the start of permanent residence. Even though the exchange is exam-free, it is better to submit the application within this period so that no questions arise during checks.

items: The 6-month countdown starts when you establish your ordinary residence (ordentlicher Wohnsitz), in practice from your registration (Anmeldung)
A first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe-Kurs) for category B in a plain exchange is usually NOT required
Check the list of documents with your driving licence authority — practice varies slightly
Book an appointment in advance: queues can be long

title: Ukrainian driving licence: exchanging it
tldr: Ukraine is a third country and is not yet on the Anlage 11 FeV list: in a standard exchange of a Ukrainian category B licence you have to pass the theory and practical exams (§31 FeV). Adding Ukraine to Anlage 11 (for an exam-free exchange) is so far only in a draft law and, as of May 2026, has not yet entered into force — check whether this is current. For refugees from Ukraine with temporary protection (§24 AufenthG) there is special relief: their foreign licence is recognised for longer than the usual 6 months (this is set out in separate regulations whose validity is regularly extended). Apply at the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) for the place where you are registered; you will need a certified translation. Higher categories (C/D) may require exams.

content.text: Ukraine is not yet listed in Anlage 11 FeV, so in a standard exchange for category B the theory and practical exams are required. A direct one-to-one exchange without exams is planned (a draft law to add Ukraine to Anlage 11), but as of May 2026 it is not yet in force — check whether this is current.

items: Ukraine is NOT yet in Anlage 11 FeV (inclusion is planned)
Category B in a standard exchange — with the theory and practical exams (until Ukraine is added to Anlage 11)
Full driving-school training is not required
For higher categories (C — trucks, D — buses) exams may apply
Apply at the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) for the place where you are registered

content.text: For people who fled Ukraine and received temporary protection (§24 AufenthG) there is special relief: a Ukrainian licence is recognised in Germany without an exchange for the entire duration of the protection status (this is set out in a separate provision that has been extended several times). The usual 6-month limit of §29 FeV does not apply to them while the protection status is in effect. The specific deadlines are set by a separate regulation that is periodically extended — check the current date.

The exact cut-off for recognising refugees' licences shifts as the regulations are extended. Before driving, check the current deadline on the ADAC website or with your driving licence authority — don't rely on outdated information. Once the relief ends, you must either exchange the licence or stop driving.

The exchange itself is handled under §30/§31 FeV. Gather the documents in advance: the authority may verify the licence's authenticity through Ukrainian agencies, which takes time. A certified translation is mandatory.

Passport/refugee document and registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) or temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung)
Biometric photo
Eye test (Sehtest)
No exams are needed for category B; for C/D check the requirements

title: What came before the Deutschlandticket: the story of the 9€-Ticket and the 49€-Ticket
tldr: The Deutschlandticket (originally the 49€-Ticket) is a pass for all public transport in Germany. It launched in May 2023 as a replacement for the summer 9€-Ticket (June–August 2022). In January 2025 the price rose to 63€/month, and in 2026 it has stayed at 63€/month. It covers all öPNV (S-Bahn, U-Bahn, trams, buses, regional trains RE/RB) across the country, but NOT ICE/IC/EC.

steps.title: What it is and why the history matters

content.text: In 2022 the German government introduced a temporary 9€-Ticket for June, July and August — a measure to help the public cope with rising fuel prices after the war began. For 9€ you could travel on all local public transport (öffentlicher Personennahverkehr, öPNV) across the country. The experiment revealed huge demand: more than 52 million tickets were sold. As a replacement, the permanent Deutschlandticket launched on 1 May 2023 at 49€/month (hence the popular name 49€-Ticket).

items: 9€-Ticket: June–August 2022, a one-off measure
49€-Ticket / Deutschlandticket: from 1 May 2023, permanent
The 49€/month price held until the end of 2024
From 1 January 2025 the price rose to 63€/month
In 2026 the price has stayed at 63€/month
Subscription only (Abo) with a monthly charge; to cancel from the end of the month, do it before the 10th

steps.title: What it covers and what it doesn't

content.text: The main source of confusion for newcomers is what counts as local transport (öPNV) versus long-distance (Fernverkehr).

items: S-Bahn (S1, S7, S9, etc.) in every city
U-Bahn (metro) in Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, Frankfurt, Nuremberg
Tram (Straßenbahn) and buses (Bus) in every Verkehrsverbund
DB regional trains: RE (Regional-Express), RB (Regionalbahn)
Other operators' trains running in Nahverkehr mode: ODEG, NWB, metronom, etc.
FEX (Flughafen-Express) Berlin → BER
ICE (InterCity Express) — high-speed
IC / EC (InterCity / EuroCity)
Flixtrain — a private operator
ÖBB NightJet night trains
Long-distance buses: Flixbus, BlaBlaCar Bus

content.text: You can buy the Deutschlandticket through dozens of apps: DB Navigator, BVG (Berlin), MVGO (Munich), hvv switch (Hamburg), KVB (Cologne), as well as on the website deutschlandticket.de. The ticket exists only in digital form (as a Handy-Ticket or Chipkarte) — it is not issued on paper.

items: Subscription only (Abo); most apps won't let you buy it for a single month without a subscription
Cancel before the 10th of the current month — you won't be charged for the next one
You can buy it a month in advance (handy for holidays)
During a check the inspector scans the QR code in the app
You need a photo ID (passport/Personalausweis) — the ticket is personal

content.text: Boarding an ICE with a Deutschlandticket counts as fare-dodging (Schwarzfahren). The fine is 60€ + the full ticket price. ICE inspectors check every ticket, and a Deutschlandticket does not show up as valid in their system.

In some regions (for example, the Inselbahn on Wangerooge or the Brockenbahn in the Harz) the Deutschlandticket does NOT apply — these are tourist narrow-gauge railways. Always check in DB Navigator before travelling.
The 63€ price is fixed for 2026, but it may rise in future: the funding is split between the federal government and the states and is reviewed every year. Follow the news on deutschlandticket.de.

title: BER Berlin-Brandenburg: how to get to the city centre
tldr: BER airport (Berlin Brandenburg Willy Brandt) is in fare zone C of the VBB. The fastest way to central Berlin (Hauptbahnhof) is the FEX (Flughafen-Express) in 30 min or the S9 in 45 min. ABC ticket: single 5,00€, day pass (24-Stunden-Karte) 12,90€, or use the Deutschlandticket (63€/month, valid everywhere). A taxi from the centre is 50-70€.

content.text: BER (IATA code: BER) opened in October 2020 after 9 years of delays. It is in Schönefeld, around 25 km southeast of central Berlin, technically in the state of Brandenburg. That is why it falls in fare zone C of the VBB system (Verkehrsverbund Berlin-Brandenburg) — you need an ABC ticket, not AB.

The underground station is right beneath T1, with a lift from the arrivals hall

RE7/RE8 run to Hauptbahnhof via Ostbahnhof. Faster than the S-Bahn, and they leave from the same underground platform.

VBB tickets are sold at the machines at BER station (with English and Russian options) and in the BVG, VBB Bus & Bahn and DB Navigator apps. Buy the ticket BEFORE you go onto the platform — a check can happen right after boarding.

content.text: The most common mistake is buying an AB ticket instead of ABC. The airport is in zone C! With an AB ticket you'll be fined 60€ (the increased fare for travelling without a valid ticket, erhöhtes Beförderungsentgelt). Inspectors on the FEX and S9 check constantly.
The FEX and RE leave from the underground platform alongside the S-Bahn — easy to mix up. Check the Bahnsteig 1-6 display: the S-Bahn is usually on 3-4, the RE/FEX on 5-6.
At night the S9 runs hourly, and the FEX does not run from ~23:00 to ~04:00. The alternatives are the night buses N7/N60 to Rudow + the U7 into the centre, or a taxi (60-80€ at night).

title: Frankfurt Airport (FRA): how to get there and catch an ICE
tldr: FRA is Germany's largest airport and the main ICE interchange hub. Right beneath Terminal 1 are two stations: the Regionalbahnhof (S-Bahn S8/S9 to Hbf in 12 min, ticket ~5,80€) and the Fernbahnhof (ICE/IC direct to Munich, Cologne, Hamburg, Berlin, without stopping at Frankfurt Hbf). An S-Bahn ticket is also valid on the tram/bus in the centre. The Deutschlandticket (63€/month) covers the S-Bahn but NOT the ICE.

From the Terminal 1 arrivals hall, follow the German signs 'Regionalbahnhof' and the S-Bahn pictogram (a green circle with a white S), then take the escalators down. From Terminal 2, take the free SkyLine People Mover to T1 and walk.

The signs for the Fernbahnhof and the Regionalbahnhof are different. For the Fernbahnhof there's a footbridge over the car terminal, about a 5-7 minute walk from Terminal 1. Allow enough time.
An ICE Sparpreis is tied to a specific train (Zugbindung). If you miss your ICE, the ticket is not valid on the next one. Only the Flexpreis lets you travel on any ICE during the day.
When buying an S-Bahn ticket at the machine, make sure Tarifgebiet 5090 (Frankfurt) is selected — that's the base one. Many people accidentally pick Wiesbaden and pay twice as much.

title: BVG Berlin: zones A/B/C, fares and travel passes
tldr: Berlin's transport runs on the VBB system with three zones: A (the centre inside the S-Bahn Ring), B (outer Berlin up to the city boundary) and C (Brandenburg, including BER and Potsdam). For most residents the AB ticket is the right one. A single AB is 4,00€, a day pass (24-Stunden-Karte) is 11,20€, a monthly Monatskarte AB is ~96€. But the Deutschlandticket (63€/month) is cheaper and works across all of Germany — almost always the better deal.

steps.title: How the zones and operators work

content.text: BVG (Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe) is the city operator of the U-Bahn, trams and buses in Berlin. The S-Bahn is run by DB, and regional trains by VBB. But there is a single ticket — the VBB-Tarif — valid on all of them together. The zones break down as follows:
Inside the S-Bahn Ring (S41/S42). Includes Mitte, Kreuzberg, Friedrichshain, Prenzlauer Berg, Charlottenburg, Schöneberg, Wedding and Moabit.

From the Ring to the city boundary. Includes Lichtenberg, Marzahn, Spandau, Tempelhof-Schöneberg (part), Reinickendorf, Treptow-Köpenick, Steglitz-Zehlendorf, Pankow (part) and TXL (the former airport).

Beyond Berlin: BER Airport (Schönefeld), Potsdam, Oranienburg, Bernau, Königs Wusterhausen, Falkensee. For these you need an ABC ticket. From 1 January 2026 the separate BC level was dropped from the Berlin fare — only AB and ABC remain (plus an Anschlussfahrausweis into zone C as an add-on to AB).

Prices are for 2026 (on 1 January they rose by ~6% on average). All tickets must be validated (entwerten) before boarding — at the machine on the platform, or at the validator on the tram/bus. For the S-Bahn and U-Bahn, validate on the platform. No validation = fare-dodging (Schwarzfahren).

items: Kurzstrecke (3 stops on the U/S-Bahn or 6 by bus/tram): 2,80€
Einzelfahrschein AB: 4,00€ (valid 2 hours / 120 min, transfers allowed)
Einzelfahrschein ABC: 5,00€
4-Fahrten-Karte AB: 12,40€ (4 trips, 3,10€ each)
24-Stunden-Karte (Tageskarte) AB: 11,20€ (24 hours from validation)

24-Stunden-Karte Kleingruppe AB (up to 5 people): ~32€
For regular trips an Abo or Monatskarte is better value than single tickets

Deutschlandticket: 63€/month — valid everywhere, better value than almost anything else

content.text: There are three places to buy: machines at the stations, apps and kiosks.

DB-Automat (red) — S-Bahn, regional
Both sell VBB tickets, but the interface differs
They accept cards and cash (not everywhere notes over 20€)

Jelbi — multimodal (BVG + scooters + bikes)
VBB Bus & Bahn — for regional travel and Brandenburg
DB Navigator — for the S-Bahn and regional, payment by card
All apps accept Apple Pay / Google Pay

content.text: BVG inspectors are usually in plain clothes and show a badge (Dienstausweis). If you have no ticket, the increased fare for travelling without a valid ticket (erhöhtes Beförderungsentgelt) is 60€. You can pay online at bvg.de/efb or by postal transfer. For repeat offences the matter may be referred to the public prosecutor: fare-dodging is still a criminal offence under §265a StGB (Erschleichen von Leistungen) — the Bundestag rejected decriminalisation on 16 April 2026.
BER is in zone C! Don't buy an AB ticket if you're going to the airport. This is the most common tourist mistake — a 60€ fine.
Buses and trams do NOT sell the Tageskarte — only the Einzelfahrschein. Buy a day pass in advance at a machine or in the app.
You must validate the ticket BEFORE boarding the S-Bahn/U-Bahn (the validators are on the platform). On a tram/bus, validate once inside. An unvalidated ticket = fare-dodging, even if you bought it.
The Deutschlandticket (63€) is usually better value than a regular Monatskarte AB (~96€) and covers the whole country. A regular Monatskarte only makes sense if you rarely travel within AB.

title: Call a Bike and Nextbike: bike rental in German cities
tldr: Germany has two major bike-sharing services with apps: Call a Bike from DB (in Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Cologne) and Nextbike (dominant in Leipzig, Dresden, Karlsruhe, Nuremberg, plus many other cities). Prices are similar: 1-1.50€ for 15-30 minutes, 9-12€ per day. A BahnCard 25/50 gives a discount on Call a Bike. You can leave the bike almost anywhere (Free-Floating) or at a station, depending on the city.

content.text: There are several services, but in each city there is usually one de facto monopolist. Check before your trip: sometimes they compete, sometimes they don't.

Get Call a Bike or nextbike from the App Store / Google Play. To register: email + a payment method (credit card or Apple Pay / Google Pay).

content.text: Don't leave the bike just anywhere — there are No-Parking-Zones in the centre. If you leave it there, you'll be charged an extra 20-30€ fine. Check the map before ending the trip.
Bikes may not be taken across the city boundary (Geofence). If you ride a bike out of Berlin into Potsdam, the app will start charging penalties or demand that you return it.

In Germany a helmet is NOT required by law, but cycling drunk is punished: at 1.6 per mille there is absolute unfitness to drive (Fahruntüchtigkeit) — already a criminal offence (a fine and possible loss of your driving licence, even though you were on a bike).
Cycle paths (Radweg) along the pavement are mandatory where there's a sign. Riding on the roadway instead = a 15-25€ fine. A bike at night without a lamp — 20€.

title: KVB Cologne: transport, fares and the KölnPass
tldr: KVB (Kölner Verkehrs-Betriebe) is the operator of the Stadtbahn (U-Bahn + tram), buses and the Rheinseilbahn cable car in Cologne. From 1 June 2026 the region switched to the new Rheinlandtarif: instead of seven fare levels there are now three. Trips within the city are Preisstufe 1b: a single EinzelTicket is 4,00€, a TagesTicket 24h is 9,60€, a MonatsTicket is ~120€. The Deutschlandticket (63€/month) is almost always better value. Low-income residents can get the KölnPass — KVB travel at a reduced price.

content.text: KVB is the city operator. But tickets are uniform across the whole Cologne-Bonn region — this is the VRS fare (Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Sieg). A single ticket is valid on the KVB tram, the DB S-Bahn, and the bus to Bonn (as long as you're in the right zone).

items: Stadtbahn — a hybrid of U-Bahn (underground in the centre) and tram (above ground on the outskirts)
Lines 1-18, marked with a 'U' where they run underground
The S-Bahn (S6, S11, S12, S13, S19) is run by DB, on the same VRS ticket
Buses: Stadtbus in the city, RegioBus to the suburbs
The Rheinseilbahn cable car — a separate fare (5€ one way); VRS does NOT apply

content.text: The fare is split into levels (Preisstufen) by trip distance. From 1 June 2026 the new Rheinlandtarif applies: instead of the former seven levels there are now three. Trips within Cologne are still in Preisstufe 1b. Check the current levels and prices on kvb.koeln or vrs.de.
The whole city of Cologne (Lindenthal, Ehrenfeld, Nippes, Mülheim, Deutz, etc.). EinzelTicket 4,00€, TagesTicket 24h 9,60€ (Rheinlandtarif, 2026). Suitable for most residents and tourists.
Under the new Rheinlandtarif the cities of Bonn and Aachen are also Preisstufe 1b, with their own city prices, just like Cologne. A trip between two different cities is charged at a higher level.
The nearest suburbs beyond the city (Hürth, Frechen, etc.). The EinzelTicket costs more than the city one (check the exact price on vrs.de). For regular trips the Deutschlandticket is better value.
More distant suburbs and regions. After the switch to the Rheinlandtarif there are fewer long-distance levels. For such trips the Deutschlandticket is almost always simpler and cheaper.

With it, KVB travel is much cheaper.

title: BahnCard 25/50/100: how to choose one and work out the saving
tldr: The BahnCard is a Deutsche Bahn discount card for long-distance ICE/IC/EC trains and Sparpreis tickets. The BC 25 (62,90€/year) gives a 25% discount and pays off after ~3-4 Sparpreis trips. The BC 50 (244€/year) — 50% on Flexpreis, 25% on Sparpreis, pays off if you travel for more than 100€/month. The BC 100 (4899€/year) — unlimited ICE/IC/EC across all of Germany plus city öPNV. Auto-Verlängerung — the card renews automatically; you must give notice 6 weeks in advance (for cards bought or renewed before 9 July 2024) or 4 weeks (for newer ones — the deadline was shortened after a Verbraucherzentrale lawsuit)!

steps.title: The types of BahnCard and who needs one

content.text: The BahnCard is an annual subscription from DB that gives a discount on long-distance train tickets (ICE, IC, EC). Do NOT confuse it with the Deutschlandticket — they are different things. The BahnCard does not work on local public transport (öPNV; city transport), and the Deutschlandticket does not work on the ICE.

content.text: Take a typical route, Berlin → München by ICE.

Makes sense for those who work in two cities

steps.title: Where and how to buy, and a word on auto-renewal

content.text: The BahnCard is bought at bahn.de/bahncard, in DB Navigator, or at a DB Reisezentrum at the station.

items: The digital BahnCard appears in DB Navigator immediately after payment
The plastic card arrives by post in 1-2 weeks
Valid for exactly 12 months from the start date
IMPORTANT: auto-renewal (Verlängerung) is on by default
You must cancel in advance (for new cards from 9 July 2024 — 4 weeks before expiry; for older ones — 6 weeks), or you'll be charged for another year
Cancellation: bahn.de/bahncard → 'Vertrag verwalten', or by post/email

content.text: The BC 50 gives 50% ONLY on Flexpreis. On Sparpreis the discount is the same as the BC 25 (25%). Many people overpay for the BC 50 thinking they'll get 50% on cheap tickets.

AUTO-RENEWAL is the main trap. The card renews automatically for a year with no reminders. Cancel via bahn.de in advance (4 weeks for new cards, 6 weeks for those bought before 9 July 2024). Set a calendar reminder the moment you buy it.
The Sparpreis is tied to a specific train (Zugbindung). If you miss it, the ticket is not valid. Only the Flexpreis lets you travel on any ICE during the day.

If your train is delayed (Verspätung) you have passenger rights (Fahrgastrechte; EU Regulation 2021/782): a delay of 60 min or more on arrival — 25% of the ticket price refunded; 120 min or more — 50%. The form is at bahn.de/fahrgastrechte. Under the regulation the deadline to claim is 3 months, but in practice DB accepts claims for up to 12 months. The refund comes as a bank transfer or a voucher (Gutschein).

If a delay or cancellation makes you miss the last train of the day and you can't reach your destination before midnight, DB must pay for a taxi (up to 120€) or reasonable hotel costs for the night (in practice around 80€/night). They don't advertise this at the station, but you are entitled to it under the passenger-rights rules (Fahrgastrechte; EU Regulation 2021/782). Keep all your receipts.

title: DB Navigator: the essential app for trains in Germany
tldr: DB Navigator is the official, free app of the German railways (Deutsche Bahn) for finding trains, buying tickets (ICE, IC, RE, S-Bahn) and the all-in-one Deutschlandticket, plus a mobile boarding pass and real-time delay tracking. It works nationwide, and you can also buy tickets from city operators BVG, MVV, RMV, HVV and the regional transport associations (Verbund) here. It works offline (cached timetables) and supports Apple Pay / Google Pay.

content.text: DB Navigator is the No. 1 transport app in Germany. Download it free from the App Store / Google Play. You don't need to register to search and browse, but you do to buy tickets and join the BahnBonus loyalty programme.

items: Journey search (Verbindungssuche) across Germany and Europe
Buying ICE/IC/EC tickets, Sparpreis and Super-Sparpreis fares
Buying the Deutschlandticket (as a subscription, Abo)
Buying tickets for city transport associations (Verbünde): BVG, MVV, RMV, HVV, KVB and others
Digital boarding pass — a QR code for the conductor on the train
Real-time delays and platform changes (Gleisänderung)
Komfort Check-in to confirm you've boarded — important for passenger rights (Fahrgastrechte)
BahnBonus — a loyalty programme that earns points for your trips
Carriage sequence on the platform (Wagen-Reihung) for a specific ICE
Open the app → 'Verbindungen' (Connections)
Enter Von / Nach (from / to)
Date and departure time
Optional: BahnCard discount card, 1st/2nd class (Klasse), children
Pick a train → 'Angebote anzeigen' (Show offers) → Sparpreis / Flexpreis
Payment: credit card (Kreditkarte), PayPal, SEPA, Apple Pay, Google Pay
The ticket appears in the 'Tickets' section, available offline

content.text: On the day of travel, open the ticket in the app and tap 'Komfort Check-in' (confirm boarding). If the conductor walks past and doesn't check your ticket, your boarding is already on record. This matters when filing a passenger rights claim (Fahrgastrechte) after a delay: otherwise DB can refuse compensation by claiming you never boarded.
Menu → 'Tickets' → 'Deutschlandticket'. It's set up as a subscription (Abo) and charged monthly. Cancel it in the same section before the 10th of the month.

items: Search for a train → tap a specific one → 'Live-Auskunft' (real-time info)
Shows the delay in minutes and the current location
A platform change (Gleisänderung) is highlighted in red
Push notifications for saved trips

content.text: DB Navigator covers almost everything, but every city has its own app with its own strengths:

items: BVG-App (Berlin) — works better with BVG trams and buses
MVGO (Munich) — integrated with MVG-Rad bike hire
hvv switch (Hamburg) — multimodal, including StadtRAD bike hire and car sharing
RMVgo (Frankfurt/Hesse) — shows RMV regional services more accurately
KVB-App (Cologne) — KölnPass, local VRS fares
Trainline — a private competitor, sometimes cheaper for Europe
Omio — for flight + train + bus tickets

content.text: Komfort Check-in — don't tap it if you've missed your train! It would count as confirming you boarded a cancelled/delayed train, and you then wouldn't be able to file a passenger rights claim (Fahrgastrechte) for another train.

Check the fare carefully before buying. A Super Sparpreis cannot be exchanged or refunded at all (exception: free cancellation within 3 hours of purchase, as long as it's before the first day of travel). A regular Sparpreis can be rebooked or cancelled before departure for a 10€ fee. Only the Flexpreis can be cancelled free of charge.
The ticket in the app shows a QR code — but the conductor sometimes asks for the national ID card (Personalausweis) or passport the ticket was booked under. Carry your ID.
Push notifications about delays work poorly when roaming without internet. Download the ticket to 'Offline-Tickets' in advance (in the app settings).

title: Deutschlandticket: 63 €/month — what it is and what's included
tldr: The Deutschlandticket (D-Ticket) is a single subscription covering all regional and local public transport across Germany. From 2025 the price rose from 49 € to 63 € per month. With it you can ride any regional trains (RE, RB), the S-Bahn, U-Bahn, trams and buses anywhere in the country, but NOT long-distance trains (ICE, IC, EC) and NOT FlixBus coaches. The ticket is always personal, digital (in an app or as a chip card) and set up as a cancellable monthly subscription (Abo). Through your employer (corporate travel pass, Jobticket) you can get an extra discount.

content.text: The Deutschlandticket is valid on all local public transport (Nahverkehr, ÖPNV) across Germany, with no tie to a specific region or transport association (Verkehrsverbund). That's its main advantage: one ticket works in Berlin, in Munich and in any small town.

items: Regional trains: RE (Regional-Express), RB (Regionalbahn)
Local transport: S-Bahn, U-Bahn, trams (Straßenbahn), city buses
Valid all over Germany, not just in your region
NOT valid on long-distance trains: ICE, IC, EC
NOT valid with private long-distance operators (FlixBus, FlixTrain)

content.text: From 2025 the D-Ticket costs 63 € per month (it used to be 49 €, hence the old name '49-Euro-Ticket'). It's always a subscription (Abonnement) charged monthly. The ticket is personal and digital — you can't pass it on to someone else.

items: Price — 63 € per month (since 2025)
Only as a subscription (Abo) with monthly billing
Digital: in an app (DB Navigator, your transport association's app) or a chip card
The ticket is personal — you can't lend or transfer it
When checked, you show the ticket on your phone plus an ID document

content.text: If your employer sets up the Deutschlandticket as a corporate travel pass (Jobticket) and pays at least 25% of the price, an extra 5% discount is added on top, so the ticket costs 59,85 € instead of 63 €. The employer covers at least a quarter of that amount, so the employee ends up paying around 45 € or less (down to nothing if the company covers it all). Ask the HR department (Personalabteilung) whether such a programme exists.

For socially vulnerable groups, many cities and regions offer discounted versions (a social tariff Sozialticket / a D-Ticket for university students, school pupils, or recipients of the basic income benefit Bürgergeld) cheaper than 63 €. Check local fares with your transport association (Verkehrsverbund).

costs.note: Per month, by subscription; price as of 2025.

costs.label: Deutschlandticket as a Jobticket
costs.note: With the +5% the base price is 59,85 €; the employer pays ≥25%, so the employee pays roughly 45 € or less (depends on the company).

costs.label: Discounted versions (social / student tariff)
costs.note: Depends on the region and category; in some states it's cheaper or nearly free for students/Bürgergeld recipients.

title: Buying and cancelling the Deutschlandticket
tldr: The Deutschlandticket is sold only as a monthly subscription (Abo) — there's no single-trip version. You can set it up through the DB Navigator app, the bahn.de website, your regional transport association's app (VRR, RMV, BVG and others) or a transport company. The ticket is valid for a calendar month (from the 1st to the last day), not for 30 days from purchase. To cancel, do so by the 10th of the current month and the subscription then ends at the end of that same month. Cancel in the same app/portal where you signed up.

content.text: The D-Ticket is sold by many providers, but always as a subscription (Abo). Pick whichever operator is convenient — the conditions and price are the same, only the app/portal differs. Many people prefer their regional association's app because cancelling there is simpler.

items: The DB Navigator app or the bahn.de website (Deutsche Bahn, the German railways)
The app/portal of your regional transport association: VRR, RMV, BVG, MVG and others
Your local transport company (Verkehrsbetrieb)
You'll need: payment details (SEPA/card) and an e-mail address
The ticket is personal — registered to a specific person

steps.title: When it starts and how long it lasts

content.text: An important detail: the Deutschlandticket is valid for a calendar month — from the 1st to the last day, NOT for 30 days from the day of purchase. If you buy the ticket mid-month, it usually activates from the start of the next month (or covers the rest of the current one — this depends on the provider). The subscription renews automatically every month until you cancel it.

Don't buy the ticket in the last days of the month 'just for a single day' — you'll pay for a whole month. If you need a trip right now, work out whether a single ticket is cheaper and set up the D-Ticket from the start of the next month.

Since it's a subscription, you have to actively cancel it or the charges continue. The standard deadline is the 10th of the current month: the subscription then ends at the end of that same month and there are no charges from the next one. Cancel later and you'll pay for one more month.

items: In the same app/portal where you set up the subscription
The 'Mein Abo' (My subscription) section → Kündigen (Cancel)
Save the cancellation confirmation (by e-mail)
Standard — by the 10th of the current month
Then the last paid month is the current one
Confirm the exact deadline with your provider — for some it's slightly different

content.text: The subscription can be paused and resumed month by month — handy if you're away for a month. But each time, watch the cancellation deadline of the 10th, or you'll be charged for the next month.

costs.label: Deutschlandticket (monthly subscription)
costs.note: Charged every month until cancelled; price as of 2025.

costs.label: Cancelling the subscription (Kündigung)
costs.note: Free; just make sure to do it before the deadline (usually the 10th of the month).

title: E-Roller: TIER, Voi, Lime
tldr: Electric scooters (E-Scooter / E-Roller) in Germany are governed by a dedicated regulation, the eKFV. The essentials: top speed — 20 km/h, minimum age — 14, no licence needed. Insurance is mandatory: an annual insurance sticker (Versicherungsplakette, also called the Versicherungskennzeichen) goes on the scooter — about 30 € a year. You may ride on bike lanes and the road, but not on the pavement. Alcohol limits are the same as for cars (0,5 ‰, 0 ‰ for novice drivers). Rental scooters from TIER, Voi and Lime are already insured — they carry the sticker.

content.text: Electric scooters are officially called Elektrokleinstfahrzeuge (very small electric vehicles) and are governed by the eKFV regulation (Elektrokleinstfahrzeuge-Verordnung). It sets out the speed, the age, the insurance and where you may ride. These rules apply both to your own scooter and to rental ones (TIER, Voi, Lime, Bolt).

items: Maximum design speed — 20 km/h (eKFV)
Minimum age — 14
No driving licence needed
A helmet isn't required, but is recommended
The scooter must have general operating approval (Allgemeine Betriebserlaubnis, ABE)

content.text: This is the most common mistake private scooter owners make: under the eKFV an e-scooter may only be used on the road with an insurance sticker (Versicherungsplakette, also called the Versicherungskennzeichen). It's a small sticker on the back that's renewed every insurance year (which runs from 1 March to the end of February). The sticker colour for the 2026/27 insurance year is black (it has changed in previous years). You can't ride without a valid sticker — it's the same offence as riding a moped without insurance.

items: Third-party liability insurance (Haftpflicht) — mandatory under the eKFV
The Versicherungsplakette insurance sticker goes on the back of the scooter
Costs about 30 € a year (cheaper for young people / online)
The insurance year starts on 1 March — a new sticker in its own colour
Rental TIER/Voi/Lime scooters are already insured — you don't need a separate sticker

content.text: Riding your own e-scooter without a valid insurance sticker counts as riding without insurance cover (Fahren ohne Versicherungsschutz), a criminal offence under §6 PflVG; on top of that, in a crash you pay for the damage out of your own pocket. Don't skimp on the sticker.

steps.title: Where you may ride, and alcohol

content.text: Under the eKFV, the choice of lane for e-scooters is the same as for bicycles, but with some important prohibitions. The pavement (Gehweg) and pedestrian zones are off limits — unless there's a special sign permitting them.

items: Ride on bike paths (Radweg), bike lanes; where there are none — on the road
On the pavement and in pedestrian zones — FORBIDDEN
Only one person per scooter — you may not carry passengers
Alcohol: limit 0,5 ‰, same as for cars; for drivers in their probationary period (Probezeit) and under 21 — 0 ‰
For drink-riding — penalty points in Flensburg and a risk to your car driving licence

content.text: Drink-riding an e-scooter is punished just as harshly as drink-driving a car: at 1,1 ‰ it's a criminal offence, with a fine, penalty points and possible withdrawal of your CAR driving licence. The scooter is not a 'safe' alternative after the bar.

costs.note: Approximately; mandatory for a private e-scooter, renewed every insurance year (from 1 March).

costs.note: Starting fee for a ride; insurance is already included by the operator.

title: Taking your bike on the train: the rules
tldr: In Germany you can take a bike on most regional trains (RE, RB, S-Bahn), but you need a separate bike ticket (Fahrradkarte) — it's NOT included in the Deutschlandticket. On long-distance trains (ICE, IC) a bike requires a pre-booked space (Stellplatz) — spaces are limited, so book ahead. During rush hour there are time restrictions (Sperrzeiten) on the S-Bahn/U-Bahn. A folding bike (Faltrad) usually travels free as luggage. The rules differ between transport associations (VRR, RMV and others) — check the local ones.

steps.title: On regional trains and the S-Bahn

content.text: On regional trains (RE, RB) and the urban S-Bahn, bikes are carried in special areas marked with a bicycle pictogram. Almost everywhere you need a separate bike ticket (Fahrradkarte / Fahrradtageskarte) for this. The price and rules depend on your region's transport association (Verkehrsverbund).

items: You need a separate bike ticket (Fahrradkarte) — often as a day ticket
The bike goes in the area with the bicycle pictogram (Fahrrad)
Spaces are limited — prams and wheelchairs have priority
During rush hour there may be time-based bans on carrying bikes (Sperrzeiten)
Rules and prices differ by association: VRR, RMV, VBB and others

content.text: On the German railways' (Deutsche Bahn) long-distance trains, carrying a bike is harder: you not only have to buy a bike ticket but also RESERVE a specific bike space in advance (Fahrradstellplatz). There are only a few such spaces per carriage, and in season they sell out fast. Not every ICE even has bike spaces.

items: A space reservation (Stellplatzreservierung) for the bike is mandatory
Bought together with the ticket on bahn.de / in DB Navigator
Spaces are scarce — book ahead, especially in summer
Some high-speed ICE trains have no bike spaces at all
A folding bike (Faltrad), folded up, travels free as luggage

content.text: Without a space reservation, a bike won't be allowed on the ICE/IC even if the carriage is half empty. When buying your ticket, check that the specific train has a free bike space (Fahrradstellplatz).

A common mistake is thinking the Deutschlandticket covers a bike too. It doesn't: the D-Ticket only covers your own travel, while a bike needs a separate ticket at the local association's fare. In some regions there are exceptions at certain times — check the local rules.

items: The Deutschlandticket does NOT include carrying a bike
A bike needs its own ticket (Fahrradkarte) at the local fare
In some associations there's free/discounted carriage on weekends or in the evening
A folding bike usually travels free as hand luggage
Check the current rules on your transport association's (Verkehrsverbund) website

costs.note: Day ticket for a bike; the price depends on the Verkehrsverbund.

title: Hamburg HVV: getting around
tldr: HVV (Hamburger Verkehrsverbund, Hamburg's transport association) is Hamburg's transport network: U-Bahn, S-Bahn, buses and ferries on the Elbe, combined into a zone-based system. You buy tickets in the HVV app, at machines or via DB Navigator. For regular travel the Deutschlandticket at 63€/month is almost always better value than an ordinary monthly HVV pass. Checks are random, and you need a valid ticket from the moment you board.

steps.title: What's part of the HVV network

content.text: HVV brings together all public transport in Hamburg and the surrounding area under a single fare. One ticket is valid on every mode of transport within the zones you've paid for.

items: U-Bahn (metro, lines U1–U4)
S-Bahn (urban rail)
Buses, including night buses (Nachtbus) and the MetroBus
Ferries on the Elbe (HADAG) — included in the standard fare
Regional trains (R/RB/RE) within the HVV zones

content.text: Hamburg is divided into fare zones (Ringe/Zonen): the city centre is ring A, then B, C, D and so on. The price of a single ticket depends on how many zones you cross. For the centre, zone A is usually enough.

items: Single ticket for one one-way trip (Einzelkarte)
Day ticket valid after 9:00 (9-Uhr-Tageskarte), cheaper than the full one
All-day ticket (Tageskarte)
Buy via: the HVV app, machines at stations, DB Navigator

content.text: In Hamburg you must have a valid ticket before you board. There are no turnstiles on the metro or S-Bahn, but inspectors (in plain clothes) check at random. No ticket means an increased fare for the trip (erhöhtes Beförderungsentgelt) of 60€.

steps.title: Which is better value: an HVV subscription (Abo) or the Deutschlandticket

content.text: If you travel daily, work it out per month. The Deutschlandticket at 63€ covers all of HVV and is valid across all of Germany — it's almost always better value than an ordinary monthly HVV pass, or at least on a par with it, since that pass often costs more even for a single zone.

items: Travelling around the city every day → Deutschlandticket 63€
A couple of trips a month → single tickets in the HVV app
One or two days of sightseeing → a day ticket (Tageskarte)
In Hamburg the D-Ticket is set up right in the HVV app

costs.note: Kurzstrecke (short trip) ~2,10€, full Hamburg AB — about 4,10€ (2026); in the app/online roughly 7% cheaper.

costs.label: Tageskarte (day ticket)
costs.note: Ganztageskarte Hamburg AB — about 8,20€ (2026); the 9-Uhr version after 9:00 is cheaper; online roughly 7% cheaper.

title: AusweisApp: setting up the eID for online government services
tldr: AusweisApp (until 2023 — AusweisApp2) is the official app for using the eID function of the German national ID card (Personalausweis) via NFC. It's free, for iPhone/Android/Desktop. With it you log in to the single government services account BundID and the tax authority portal ELSTER, and submit applications online without travelling to the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt). The key requirement: the eID must be activated (Online-Ausweisfunktion eingeschaltet) and you must have a 6-digit PIN.

steps.title: What AusweisApp is and why you need it

content.text: AusweisApp is the official app of the Federal Ministry of the Interior (Bundesministerium des Innern, BMI), developed by Governikus GmbH & Co. KG. It lets you use the chip in your national ID card (Personalausweis) and the electronic residence permit card (eAT, elektronischer Aufenthaltstitel) for online identification. In essence it's an NFC reader with a secure channel to the service. In November 2023 the app was renamed from AusweisApp2 back to AusweisApp — the functionality stayed the same.

items: Free and official — third-party equivalents aren't needed and aren't safe

System requirements keep rising: for 2026 this is roughly iOS 17.0+ / Android 9.0+ with NFC, and on desktop — Windows/macOS/Linux plus an external card reader or a smartphone acting as the reader (check the current version at ausweisapp.bund.de)
You need an activated eID function and your own 6-digit PIN (not the 5-digit transport PIN!)
Used to log in to BundID, the ELSTER tax portal, the pension fund Rentenversicherung, Kfz-Online, and online residence registration (Anmeldung) in some states
Supports the Smart-eID — an eID stored directly in the smartphone's secure element (Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer, no physical card)

content.text: Download the app only from the official App Store / Google Play stores or from ausweisapp.bund.de. Beware of fakes: the genuine developer is Governikus GmbH & Co. KG.

items.title: 1. Check whether the eID is activated

content.text: Since July 2017, the eID function has been activated by default when a new national ID card (Personalausweis) is issued. If your card is old (issued before 2017) or the function was switched off, the eID is activated at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) free of charge.

items.title: 2. Change the transport PIN to a 6-digit one

content.text: When the card is issued, you receive an envelope with a transport PIN (Transport-PIN, 5 digits) and a PUK. Before using AusweisApp for the first time, you need to replace it with your own 6-digit PIN. You do this right in the app: 'PIN ändern' (Change PIN) → enter the 5-digit one → set a new 6-digit one. If the transport PIN is lost, it's reset free of charge at the Bürgeramt.

items.title: 3. Open AusweisApp and run the Selbstauskunft

content.text: In the app, choose 'Meine Daten einsehen' (View my data) — this is a free test: hold your national ID card (Personalausweis) against the back of your iPhone (the NFC antenna is at the top of the body) and enter your PIN. If the data is read, everything works.

items.title: 4. Use it to log in to services

items: BundID (id.bund.de) — choose 'Mit Online-Ausweis anmelden' (log in with the electronic ID)
The ELSTER tax portal — an alternative to the certificate file (Zertifikatsdatei)
Bundesportal verwaltung.bund.de — applications for parental allowance, BAföG and so on
The service opens AusweisApp via a deep link; you hold your card to the phone and confirm with your PIN

content.text: On compatible Samsung Galaxy smartphones (S20 and newer, Android only) the eID can be moved into the device's secure element. Then you don't need to carry the physical card — the phone is enough. On the iPhone the Smart-eID is still unavailable as of 2026; see the list of supported models at personalausweisportal.de.

steps.title: Where the iPhone's NFC is and how to hold the card correctly

content.text: On the iPhone, the NFC antenna is in the upper part of the back cover (next to the camera). Take off your case if it's thick or has a metal plate. Lay your national ID card (Personalausweis) on a table, turn the iPhone face down and rest its top on the card. Don't move it until the operation finishes (5-15 seconds).

items: Remove a MagSafe leather case — it can interfere
Don't hold the card in your hand; place it on a flat surface
The reading takes 5-15 seconds, don't move it
On a 'Verbindung abgebrochen' (connection lost) error — try again and change the position

content.text: The transport PIN (5 digits) ≠ the working PIN (6 digits). You can't log in to an online service with the 5-digit one. If you've forgotten it, you'll have to go to the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) for a PIN reset letter (PIN-Rücksetzbrief) — free, but 1-2 weeks by post.

After 3 wrong PIN entries the card is blocked. You can only unblock it with the 10-digit PUK from the envelope. If the PUK is lost, you'll need to visit the Bürgeramt and pay for a reset (about 6-30€ depending on the state).
A national ID card (Personalausweis) with an eID only works while the document itself is valid (10 years for adults). After the card is replaced — a new PIN and setting it up again.
Don't install 'AusweisApp2' or clones from third-party developers — that's phishing. The genuine developer is Governikus; search by the exact name 'AusweisApp Bund'.

costs.note: The app is free and official
