costs.note: If the card was issued with the eID switched off — activation is free

costs.label: PIN-Rücksetzbrief
costs.note: Free on request at the Bürgeramt; sent by post in 1-2 weeks

costs.label: Block/unblock fee if the PUK is lost
costs.note: Depends on the state and city

costs.label: New Personalausweis
costs.note: Standard for those 24+ (from 07.02.2026, was 37€); under 24 — 27,60€

title: BundID: a single account for all government services
tldr: BundID (id.bund.de) is the central account for online government services in Germany: BAföG, parental allowances, tax services, applications to the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt). One login at the federal level and (gradually) the state level. Registration is free; the trust level depends on how you log in — the eID (national ID card, Personalausweis) gives the highest level, the ELSTER tax portal a high level, and a username + password (Benutzername+Passwort) the basic level.

steps.title: What BundID is and why you need it

content.text: BundID is a single account for government services (Nutzerkonto Bund) based on the Online Access Act (Onlinezugangsgesetz, OZG). The idea is simple: instead of a separate login on every portal, one account for federal online services and gradually for the states (Länder). It launched in 2019; by 2026 hundreds of services are available through it, including Elterngeld Digital, BAföG Digital, applications for the housing benefit (Wohngeld) and i-Kfz (in some states).

items: Free, no subscriptions
Three trust levels (Vertrauensniveau): low (niedrig, password), substantial (substanziell, ELSTER), high (hoch, eID)
Many services require 'substanziell' or 'hoch' — a simple password login won't do
A permanent mailbox (Postfach) — correspondence with authorities in one place
Replaces (but doesn't abolish) the individual states' service accounts (Servicekonten) — Bayern ID, BayernPortal, ServiceBW and others

content.text: Go to id.bund.de and click 'Konto erstellen' (Create an account). Choose your identification method — it determines your level and which services you'll be able to apply for.

Click 'Mit Online-Ausweis registrieren' (Register with the electronic ID). AusweisApp opens, you hold your national ID card (Personalausweis) to your iPhone (NFC) and enter your 6-digit PIN. Your name, address and date of birth load automatically. Level: hoch (high) — all services are open.

If you already have an account on the ELSTER tax portal with a certificate, click 'Mit ELSTER registrieren' (Register via ELSTER), upload the .pfx file and enter the password. Level: substanziell (substantial) — most services are open, except a few that require the eID.

items.title: Option C: EU login via eIDAS

content.text: If you have an eID from another EU country (Italia CIE, Estonia e-ID, Spain DNIe), you can register via the eIDAS-Node. The level is usually substanziell or hoch depending on the country.
The simplest, but the level is niedrig (low). Only suitable for a very limited range of services (information services). Most authorities won't accept this login.

steps.title: Which services are available through BundID

items: Elterngeld Digital — parental allowance (via ELSTER + BundID)
BAföG Digital — student grants (bafoeg-digital.de)
Wohngeld online — housing benefit (coverage growing)
i-Kfz — registering and re-registering a car online
Online residence registration (Anmeldung) — in Hamburg, Bremen, Köln and others (depends on the city)
Applications to the child benefit office (Familienkasse), the pension fund (Rentenversicherung), the employment office (Arbeitsamt)
Application for naturalisation (Antrag auf Einbürgerung) — in some states

content.text: BundID and Bayern ID / ServiceBW / Mein Servicekonto NRW are DIFFERENT systems. The states are gradually integrating BundID, but not everywhere. For a state-level service, the portal may require a separate state account.

If you registered with a password (level niedrig), you can raise the trust level by linking the eID or the ELSTER tax portal to the same account. So if your eID function is active, choose it right away — that way you avoid the extra steps.

The BundID mailbox (Postfach) doesn't replace an official postal address: an authority may send its reply there, but legally significant notices (an official decision, Bescheid) often go by post in parallel.
Don't confuse BundID with De-Mail (that system is being wound down and will be fully shut off by the end of 2026) or with the ELSTER tax portal (that's a separate tax service).

costs.label: BundID registration
costs.note: Free, no subscriptions

costs.label: Using the services
costs.note: BundID itself is free; the government fees for specific applications (i-Kfz, Wohnsitzanmeldung) are paid separately at the authority's rates

title: DSGVO: your rights and how to use them
tldr: The DSGVO (the EU's data protection regulation, known internationally as the GDPR) gives you the right to find out free of charge what data a company holds about you (Art. 15), to demand its deletion (Art. 17) or its transfer (Art. 20). The deadline for a reply is 30 days. For a breach, complain to your state's data protection commissioner (LfDI). In Germany the DSGVO applies alongside the federal data protection act (Bundesdatenschutzgesetz, BDSG). Below is a template for a data request (Auskunftsersuchen) and where to complain.

steps.title: What the DSGVO is and what rights you have

content.text: The DSGVO (Datenschutz-Grundverordnung, known internationally as the GDPR — Verordnung (EU) 2016/679) has applied since 25 May 2018. In Germany it's supplemented by the federal data protection act (Bundesdatenschutzgesetz, BDSG). The regulation covers any company or authority that processes the data of people located in the EU — regardless of where the company itself is registered.

items: Art. 15 — the right to information (Auskunftsrecht): the right to learn what data is held about you, to whom it was passed and on what grounds
Art. 16 — correction (Berichtigung) of inaccurate data
Art. 17 — the right to be forgotten (Recht auf Vergessenwerden): deletion of data (with caveats)
Art. 18 — restriction of processing (Einschränkung)
Art. 20 — data portability (Datenübertragbarkeit): getting your data in machine-readable form and moving it to another service
Art. 21 — objection (Widerspruch) to processing (including marketing)
Art. 22 — protection from automated decisions (including profiling)

steps.title: How to submit a data request (Auskunftsersuchen) under Art. 15

content.text: You can send the request by email to the company's data protection officer (Datenschutzbeauftragter, DPO) — usually datenschutz@firma.de — or by ordinary letter. The form is free; the main thing is to identify yourself unambiguously and cite Art. 15 DSGVO. The basic deadline for a reply is one month; for complex or numerous requests it can be extended by another two months, provided you're notified (Art. 12 Abs. 3).

items.title: 1. Find the data protection officer's contact (Datenschutzbeauftragter)

content.text: The site's privacy policy (Datenschutzerklärung, usually in the footer) lists the data protection officer's (DPO) email. If there isn't one, write to the general contact marked 'z.Hd. Datenschutzbeauftragter / for the attention of the DPO'.

The company is entitled to ask for reasonable proof of identity — but NOT to require a copy of your national ID card (Personalausweis). Usually an email address from their database or a customer number is enough. If they demand a scan of your ID, black out everything except your name and photo.

items.title: 4. If they don't reply — complain to the data protection commissioner (LfDI)

content.text: After 1 month with no reply, complain to your state's data protection commissioner (Landesbeauftragte für Datenschutz, LfDI) — BlnBDI in Berlin, LfDI BW in Baden-Württemberg and so on. The complaint is free, with an online form on the supervisory authority's site. Fines for breaching the DSGVO go up to 20 million € or 4% of turnover (Art. 83).

items: The consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) — templates for a request (Auskunft), deletion (Löschung), objection (Widerspruch): verbraucherzentrale.de
datarequests.org — a generator for DSGVO letters in German/English
datenanfragen.de — the same in German, with a database of data protection officer (DPO) contacts for most companies
BfDI (the federal data protection commissioner, Bundesbeauftragte für Datenschutz) — bfdi.bund.de; handles federal bodies and telecoms
Your state's data protection commissioner (LfDI) — for complaints against private companies operating in your state

content.text: The right to deletion (Art. 17) isn't absolute. If there's a legal obligation to retain the data (for example, tax law — 10 years under §147 AO), the company is entitled to refuse. But even then it must restrict the processing (Art. 18).
A company isn't entitled to require a copy of your national ID card (Personalausweis) for identification if your identity can be confirmed another way. That conflicts with Art. 5 (data minimisation).
A data request (Auskunft) under Art. 15 is free once. For repeated 'manifestly unfounded' requests they may charge a reasonable fee or refuse (Art. 12 Abs. 5).

A site outside the EU (for example, in the USA) but aimed at German users (German language, prices in €) still falls under the DSGVO (Art. 3 Abs. 2). You can complain to your data protection commissioner (LfDI).

costs.label: Auskunft request under Art. 15
costs.note: Free once; repeated 'manifestly unfounded' ones — for a fee at the company's discretion

costs.label: Complaint to the LfDI / BfDI
costs.note: Free; a complaint to the Verwaltungsgericht — court costs at the usual rates

costs.label: Data protection lawyer (Erstberatung)
costs.note: If you want professional support — under the RVG

title: De-Mail in 2026: what's left and what to replace it with
tldr: De-Mail is an official secure email system, launched in 2012 for legally significant correspondence with authorities. By 2026 it has effectively been wound down: most providers (T-Online, GMX/web.de) have already closed the service, and the state De-Mail is being switched off by 31 December 2026 as part of cutting red tape (Bürokratierückbau). If you had a De-Mail account, export your correspondence archive. The replacements: the mailbox of the single BundID account (Postfach) with eID login, the special electronic mailbox for lawyers BeA, and ordinary email with a qualified electronic signature (QES) for everyone else.

steps.title: What De-Mail was and why it never took off

content.text: De-Mail was launched in 2012 under the De-Mail Act (De-Mail-Gesetz): the idea was a mailbox with verified identity, transport encryption and proof of delivery. Sending cost about 0,39€ per message. The providers included T-Online (Telekom), GMX/web.de (1&1) and Mentana-Claimsoft (Francotyp-Postalia). The system never caught on: authorities weren't obliged to accept it, the encryption only protected the transmission channel and not the messages themselves (not end-to-end), and the charge for sending put users off. Telekom (T-Online) closed the service in 2022, and 1&1/GMX/web.de in 2024–2025. The Bundestag decided to end the state De-Mail as part of the act to reduce red tape (Bürokratierückbau) within the Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI); a full shutdown is planned by 31 December 2026.

items: Don't use De-Mail for new tasks — the system is being wound down
Old De-Mail addresses of the form user@t-online.de-mail.de no longer work
The mailbox archive (Postfach-Backup) needs to be exported through the provider's interface before the closure date
The legal effects of messages delivered earlier remain valid

steps.title: What to do with an existing De-Mail account

content.text: If you still have an active De-Mail account (for example, with Mentana-Claimsoft), you need to save your correspondence and pick a replacement. The steps:

Log in to the De-Mail web interface and download the archive (PDF/EML/MBOX). Mentana-Claimsoft has a 'Postfach exportieren' (export mailbox) function. Keep it on reliable storage for at least 10 years — in case of tax or court disputes.

items.title: 2. Tell your contacts about the new channel

content.text: Send a notice to all authorities and partners that your De-Mail address is no longer valid. Give an alternative: the BundID mailbox (Postfach) for authorities, ordinary email plus a qualified electronic signature (QES) for private parties, or post.

After exporting, close it via 'Konto schließen' (Close account). If the provider has already announced the end of the service, follow its instructions — don't ignore them: otherwise you could miss a notice about a court or tax procedure.

steps.title: What to use instead of De-Mail in 2026

items: The BundID mailbox (Postfach) — for correspondence with authorities; login via the eID or the ELSTER tax portal
Mein ELSTER — for all tax correspondence with the tax office (Finanzamt)
BeA (the special electronic mailbox for lawyers) — a mandatory channel for lawyers since 2018, still working in 2026
Professional electronic mailboxes (beN, eBO, beBPo) — for notaries and authorities
A qualified electronic signature (QES) + ordinary email — for private and B2B deals: a signed PDF is equivalent to a signed letter
Registered letter with proof of delivery (Einschreiben mit Rückschein) — the good old Deutsche Post (German post), still legally watertight

content.text: Don't send important documents to authorities' De-Mail addresses in 2026 — there's a high risk they're no longer being read. Use the BundID mailbox (Postfach) or physical post.
Contracts (for example, for a 'De-Mail-Postfach' service) may have been terminated automatically — check that you're not still being charged.
A De-Mail archive only has legal force if it was exported with the provider's digital signature. A plain screenshot doesn't count as evidence.

The De-Mail Act (De-Mail-Gesetz) is being repealed as part of cutting red tape (Bürokratierückbau), but individual references to De-Mail still appear for a while in a number of sections of the VwVfG and BMG. Before taking any legally significant action, check the current version of the rules at gesetze-im-internet.de.

costs.label: De-Mail-Sendung (historical)
costs.note: Per message; no longer relevant in 2026

costs.label: BundID + eID
costs.note: A free replacement for communicating with authorities

costs.label: QES (electronic signature) — annual licence
costs.note: From D-Trust, Sign-Me, DocuSign — replaces the De-Mail signature

costs.label: Einschreiben mit Rückschein
costs.note: Deutsche Post — always works

title: Passport and ID card (Personalausweis) online
tldr: Since 2024 (PAuswV reform), some federal states and cities accept applications for a new national ID card (Personalausweis) and passport (Reisepass) online: you submit your data and pay in advance via BundID (the single login for government services), while biometrics and fingerprints are taken in person at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt; a 5-minute visit instead of 30). The document itself is produced by Bundesdruckerei, with delivery in 3-5 weeks. A standard passport (Reisepass) costs 70€, a national ID card (Personalausweis) 46€ (from 07.02.2026).

steps.title: What 'online application' means and where it works

content.text: Since the 2024 reform of the Passverordnung / Personalausweisverordnung, the issuing process can be split into an online part (submitting the form, biometric photo, payment) and an offline part (taking fingerprints, signature, identity verification). You cannot get a passport entirely online — by law, biometrics require your physical presence. But an online pre-application cuts the appointment (Termin) at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) down to 5-10 minutes.

items: Available via BundID + eID (or the tax office portal ELSTER) on your state's/city's portal
Berlin, Hamburg, Bavaria, North Rhine-Westphalia lead on coverage
In smaller towns the online form may be basic (appointment booking and payment only)
Passport (Reisepass) = travel document for abroad; national ID card (Personalausweis) = ID card (within the EU this is enough)
Validity: passport (Reisepass) — 10 years (adults), 6 years (under 24); national ID card (Personalausweis) — 10 years (6 years for those under 24)

content.text: Since 1 May 2025, a digital biometric photo is required for passports and the national ID card (Personalausweis). Until 31 July 2025 paper photos were still allowed as an exception, but by 2026 they are no longer accepted. The photo must arrive via a secure chain: either a certified photographer takes it and transmits it through an encrypted cloud (you get a printout with a Data-Matrix code), or it is taken right at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) on a PointID terminal (about 6€).

On your city's portal (e.g. service.berlin.de, hamburg.de/online-dienste, muenchen.de/dienstleistungen), choose 'Reisepass beantragen' or 'Personalausweis beantragen'. Log in via BundID (eID or ELSTER), fill in the form, enter the photo's Data-Matrix code from the photographer and pay by card.

After the online submission, the system offers free slots at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt). In big cities expect a 2-6 week wait. If it's urgent, there's an express application (Express-Antrag) for an extra fee.

items.title: 4. Visit the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt; 5-10 min)

items: Fingerprints taken (mandatory since 2021 for the national ID card (Personalausweis) under EU-Verordnung 2019/1157)
Signature check
Check of the previous ID/passport (returned to you)
Confirm the PIN or activate the eID function

content.text: Bundesdruckerei (the state producer) makes the document in roughly 3-4 weeks. You can collect it in person at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) once notified or, since 1 May 2025, have it delivered to your home address (Direktversand, extra fee around 15€).

items: Express passport (Express-Reisepass) — 4-5 working days, 32€ surcharge on top of the fee
Temporary passport (Vorläufiger Reisepass) — issued at the district citizens' office on the spot, valid 1 year, 26€, no chip (for urgent trips)
Express national ID card (Express-Personalausweis) — usually 3-4 days, 32€ surcharge
Temporary national ID card (Vorläufiger Personalausweis) — issued the same day, valid 3 months, 10€

content.text: Since 2025 the biometric photo must be digital and from a certified source only. A selfie or a shot from an ordinary camera will not be accepted. Don't submit the online application without the photo's Data-Matrix code from a photographer or without a photo from the terminal at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt).

Not every district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) handles online applications. Before submitting, make sure the branch you choose supports the online application (Online-Antrag) — otherwise you'll still have to fill in the paperwork on site.

You must hand in your old national ID card (Personalausweis) or passport (Reisepass) when collecting the new one, if it is still valid. The old document is invalidated (a hole is punched in it) and returned only on separate request — for example, if it contains valid visas.

If your passport or national ID card (Personalausweis) is lost, you must report it to the police (a report, Anzeige) — the confirmation is needed to apply for a new one. Without it, the fee may be increased.

costs.note: From 07.02.2026 (was 37€), 10 years

costs.label: Personalausweis (<24)
costs.note: From 07.02.2026 (was 22,80€); valid 6 years

costs.label: Reisepass (24+)
costs.note: 10 years, 32 pages

costs.label: Reisepass mit 48 Seiten
costs.note: For frequent travellers

costs.label: Express-Zuschlag
costs.note: Express issuance in 3-5 working days

costs.note: Issued on the spot, no chip, 1 year

costs.note: Digital, with a Data-Matrix code; a photo on the PointID terminal at the Bürgeramt is around 6€

title: QES: the qualified electronic signature
tldr: A qualified electronic signature (Qualifizierte elektronische Signatur, QES) under the eIDAS-Verordnung (EU) 910/2014, Art. 25 has the same legal force as a handwritten signature and satisfies the electronic form under §126a BGB. You need it for contracts that require written form, for filing documents in BeA and the electronic case file (E-Akte), and for signed applications. Providers in Germany: D-Trust (Bundesdruckerei) with its Sign-Me service, DocuSign, Certifaction and others. A single signature costs from a few euros, an annual licence from around 30€.

steps.title: What QES is and where you need it

content.text: The eIDAS regulation (Verordnung (EU) Nr. 910/2014; updated by the eIDAS 2.0 regulation — Verordnung (EU) 2024/1183, in force since May 2024) distinguishes three types of electronic signature: simple (einfache, EES), advanced (fortgeschrittene, FES) and qualified (qualifizierte, QES). Only the qualified signature (QES) under Art. 25 Abs. 2 eIDAS is treated as equivalent to a handwritten signature and satisfies the electronic form (elektronische Form) under §126a BGB, which replaces the statutory written form (gesetzliche Schriftform).

items: A qualified signature (QES) is required for: an employment contract subject to written form, terminating a tenancy, suretyship contracts, notarial declarations, filing via BeA by lawyers
It is created through a qualified trust service provider (qualifizierter Vertrauensdiensteanbieter, QTSP); the list is kept by the Bundesnetzagentur
It is tied to your identity via identification (Video-Ident, eID or an in-person visit)
It is valid across all EU countries — cross-border recognition under eIDAS

Under eIDAS 2.0, EU countries must provide an EUDI-Wallet (European Digital Identity Wallet) by the end of 2026; authorities must accept it from 2027, and the qualified signature (QES) will become part of it
D-Trust GmbH (Bundesdruckerei) — d-trust.net; sign-me.de for cloud signing
Bundesdruckerei Sign-Me — cloud-based qualified signature (QES) without a smartcard, identification via eID or Video-Ident
DocuSign Germany — integrated with DocuSign eSignature, QES add-on
Certifaction — a Swiss provider operating in Germany
Atos / Eviden — enterprise solutions
Nect / IDnow — Video-Ident and signature-as-a-service
DGN Service (for healthcare) — eHBA for doctors

steps.title: How to get a QES (using D-Trust's Sign-Me as an example)

content.text: Go to sign-me.de, pick a plan (from 'Single' at ~5€ per signature to an annual subscription for 30-50€). Create an account.

items: eID via AusweisApp — free, instant
Video-Ident via WebID/IDnow — free, ~10 minutes
Identification at a post office (Personal-Ident, Postident) — free, 1-2 days

content.text: Upload a PDF document to Sign-Me, choose where the signature goes, confirm with a 6-digit TAN from the D-Trust App. The qualified signature (QES) is embedded into the PDF — you can open and verify it with Adobe Acrobat or validator.bund.de.

The recipient opens the PDF and sees the blue 'Signaturen gültig' badge. For long-term validity (LTV), enable archiving — otherwise the certificate expires in 2-3 years and the signature formally becomes 'unverified' (though its legal force at the time of signing is preserved).

items: Filing documents in BeA by lawyers (mandatory)
Documents for the electronic case file (E-Akte; courts' electronic files) — §130a ZPO
Filing special documents with the tax office (Finanzamt) (most ELSTER submissions are already QES-like)
Tenancy agreements, terminations, guarantee documents
B2B contracts with international counterparties in the EU
Filing with the commercial register (Handelsregister; for GmbH resolutions) — usually via a notary, but also possible with a qualified signature (QES)

content.text: Don't confuse the qualified signature (QES) with the advanced one (FES, fortgeschrittene). DocuSign 'standard' is an advanced signature (FES), not a qualified one. For §126a BGB you need precisely the qualified one — a separate DocuSign QES product or Sign-Me.

A qualified signature (QES) from a provider in another EU country is valid in Germany (eIDAS Art. 25 Abs. 3); you can check a trust service provider's (QTSP) status in the EU Trusted List (EU Trusted List, eIDAS-Vertrauensliste) via the EU Trusted List Browser.

A qualified signature (QES) certificate is usually valid for 2-3 years. After it expires you can no longer sign new documents; documents already signed remain valid (but get a timestamp (Zeitstempel) for LTV).

To file documents in BeA, a lawyer either signs with a qualified signature (QES) using their beA-Karte (a chip card with a certificate), or sends the document with a simple signature but personally from their own beA mailbox over a secure channel (§130a Abs. 3 ZPO). An arbitrary cloud QES doesn't work here.
The free 'electronic signatures' from Adobe / Microsoft are simple (EES) or advanced (FES) signatures, not qualified ones (QES). They do NOT replace the legal force of a handwritten signature.

costs.note: Per signature; ideal for one-off tasks

costs.label: Sign-Me Jahreslizenz
costs.note: Unlimited for a single user

costs.label: D-Trust QES-Smartcard
costs.note: + card reader 30-60€; for intensive use

costs.label: DocuSign QES Add-on
costs.note: Per envelope, on top of the regular subscription

costs.label: Video-Ident
costs.note: Free, included in the price of the signature

title: City apps: Berlin Service, Köln, München
tldr: Germany's big cities offer mobile apps for booking an appointment (Termin) at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt), paying for parking, filing requests with municipal services and receiving city notifications. They are free, on the App Store/Google Play. The most advanced: Berlin Service (formerly BENN), Köln App, München App, Hamburg Service, Frankfurt-Tipps. Some features require login via BundID (the single login for government services).

content.text: In 2022–2024, German cities have been launching mobile apps for their Service-Portal en masse. The idea is to give residents a single point for everyday services: book an appointment (Termin) at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt), pay a parking fine, report a pothole, learn about road closures, read local news. As a rule, such apps are free, ad-free and support login via eID/BundID.

items: Berlin: 'Berlin Service' (iOS/Android) — the official app of the Senate Chancellery (Senatskanzlei)
Köln: 'KÖLNbox' and 'Köln Service' — for booking at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) and parking
München: 'München Servicekonto' and 'München App' (tourist + civic part)
Hamburg: 'Hamburg Service' — Bürgeramt, parking, waste
Frankfurt: 'Mainova App' (utilities) + 'Frankfurt App' (general)
Stuttgart: 'Stuttgart Service'
State level: BayernPortal-App, Mein Servicekonto NRW

content.text: On the App Store, search by city name + 'Service' / 'App'. IMPORTANT: the developer must be listed as the city/state (Stadt/Land; for example, 'Stadt Köln' or 'Land Berlin'), not a third-party developer. Dubious fake apps have already appeared.
To submit applications you need a login. In Berlin and Hamburg — via BundID. In Bavaria — Bayern ID. In NRW — Mein Servicekonto NRW. In most cases setup takes 2-3 minutes via eID.

City notifications are things like a reminder of an upcoming appointment (Termin), the status of an application, information about road closures near your home. Enable only the categories you need so you don't drown in messages.

items: Book an appointment (Termin buchen) — residence registration (Anmeldung), passport (Pass), driving licence (Führerschein)
Defect reporting service (Mängelmelder) — report a pothole or a broken traffic light
Waste collection dates (Mülltermine) — the waste pickup schedule
Parking (Parken) — paying for a parking ticket (often a separate EasyPark/PaybyPhone integration)
Public transport (ÖPNV) — tram and bus timetables
Berlin Service — service.berlin.de (district citizens' office (Bürgeramt), BAB, vehicle registration (KFZ-Anmeldung))
BVG-App — Berlin transport + ticketing
BSR (Berliner Stadtreinigung; Berlin's cleaning service) — waste and booking bulky-waste collection (Sperrmüll)
Köln Service — koeln.de, district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) + defect reporting service (Mängelmelder)
KVB — Köln transport
München-App + Münchner-Müll-App
MVV (Verkehrsverbund) — München transport
Hamburg Service + HVV switch (multimodal transport)
Frankfurt-Tipps + FES-App (waste)
RMV (Verkehrsverbund) — Frankfurt
Stuttgart Service + VVS
BayernPortal — at the level of the state of Bavaria

content.text: City apps don't cover federal services (passport, tax returns, BAföG). For those you need BundID and the corresponding portals.
Don't trust 'fine payment' in apps not developed by the municipality. Berlin/Köln/München accept fines via the payment portal (Bezahl-Portal) of the city website, not via third-party services.
An appointment (Termin) is the scarcest resource. In Berlin new slots usually appear around 07:00 in the morning. App notifications help you catch freed-up slots in time.
Submissions via the defect reporting service (Mängelmelder) are public (visible to other residents). Don't put personal data in the description.

title: Courts' E-Akte: electronic filing of documents
tldr: Since 1 January 2022, lawyers, notaries and authorities are OBLIGED to file documents with the courts electronically only (§130d ZPO, §65a SGG, §55a VwGO). Citizens may — but are not obliged to. Filing channels: BeA (lawyers), beN (notaries), beBPo (authorities), eBO (organisations and private individuals), Mein Justizpostfach (a free channel for citizens), EGVP. For a private individual the simplest and cheapest is the free Mein Justizpostfach via BundID (the single login for government services).

steps.title: What the E-Akte is and who must use it

content.text: The electronic case file (E-Akte) is the electronic handling of court cases in Germany. It was rolled out in stages: from 2018 as an option, from 1 January 2022 mandatory for 'professional electronic participants' — lawyers (Rechtsanwälte), notaries (Notare), authorities (Behörden; BRAO §31a, BNotO §78n). At the statutory level, the framework is set by §130a-d ZPO (civil procedure), §55a-d VwGO (administrative), §65a SGG (social), §41a StPO (criminal).

items: Lawyers are obliged to use BeA (besonderes elektronisches Anwaltspostfach; special electronic lawyer mailbox) — bea-brak.de
Notaries — beN (besonderes elektronisches Notarpostfach; special electronic notary mailbox)
Authorities — beBPo (besonderes elektronisches Behördenpostfach; special electronic authority mailbox)
Citizens and organisations voluntarily — eBO (besonderes elektronisches Bürger- und Organisationenpostfach; special electronic mailbox for citizens and organisations)
For private individuals there is also a simpler, free channel — Mein Justizpostfach (MJP) at mjp.justiz.de, login via BundID
The old system: EGVP (Elektronisches Gerichts- und Verwaltungspostfach; electronic court and administration mailbox) — partly replaced, but still working

content.text: eBO (launched in 2022) is a secure channel for filing documents with a court from a private individual or organisation. Your identity is confirmed at registration, most conveniently via the eID function of the national ID card (Personalausweis). Note: dedicated eBO software for citizens is usually paid. For simple correspondence with a court, a private individual is better off with the free Mein Justizpostfach (login via BundID). After registration you receive a SAFE-ID, to which the court can send replies.

For eBO, install certified eBO software (e.g. Governikus Communicator; for citizens it is usually paid) and register via the SAFE portal with identity verification by eID. If you don't need paid software, choose the free Mein Justizpostfach at mjp.justiz.de with login via BundID. In both cases you get a SAFE-ID for your mailbox.

The document must be PDF/A. Signature: either a qualified electronic signature (QES), or 'einfache Signatur + sicherer Übermittlungsweg' (simple signature + secure transmission path) — i.e. just your name in the PDF, if it is filed through a certified eBO channel with a verified identity.

In the eBO client select 'Empfänger' (recipient) → search for the court (local court (Amtsgericht) / regional court (Landgericht)) by SAFE-ID. Attach the PDF and press send. You get a receipt of arrival (Eingangsbestätigung) — this is your proof of timely filing (important for deadlines).

items: BeA is mandatory infrastructure, accessed via the beA-Karte (a special chip card with a certificate)
Signature: either a qualified electronic signature (QES), or a simple signature sent from within the beA mailbox — 'einfache Signatur + Versand aus dem beA' (under §130a Abs. 3 ZPO)
Messages are stored on BRAK servers (Bundesrechtsanwaltskammer; Federal Bar Association)
Since 2024 there is beA-mobile — an app for iOS/Android
Cost: the annual BRAK fee for running beA (~63€/year per lawyer) + beA-Karte Basis ~35€/year

content.text: Since 1 January 2022 the court does NOT ACCEPT paper documents from lawyers, notaries and authorities. Filing by fax or post = invalid filing = a missed deadline. This doesn't apply to citizens — they may file however they like.
The receipt of arrival (Eingangsbestätigung) from eBO/BeA is legally critical proof of the filing time (§130a Abs. 5 ZPO). Always keep the PDF receipt.
Documents must be in PDF/A format (archival). An ordinary PDF may be rejected if it contains fonts not embedded in the file.
For documents with a qualified electronic signature (QES), check the certificate's validity before sending. An expired QES = an unsigned document = an invalid filing.
Message size in BeA/eBO is limited (100 MB per message, 200 files). Split large attachments into parts.

costs.label: Mein Justizpostfach (citizens)
costs.note: A free channel for private individuals; login via BundID + eID

costs.label: BeA-Pflichtbeitrag (lawyers)
costs.note: The annual BRAK fee for running beA (~63€/year per lawyer), included in membership dues

costs.label: beA-Karte Basis
costs.note: ~35,81€/year (beA-Karte Basis, brutto); check the current figure with your Rechtsanwaltskammer

costs.label: QES for a one-off filing
costs.note: Sign-Me Pay-per-Use

costs.label: QES — annual subscription
costs.note: If you file documents regularly

costs.label: eBO software (e.g. Governikus Communicator)
costs.note: Client for eBO; for citizens/organisations usually paid — check with the provider

title: Electronic invoice (E-Rechnung): ZUGFeRD, XRechnung
tldr: Since 2025, Germany has a phased obligation for electronic invoices (electronic invoice, E-Rechnung) in B2B transactions. An electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) is a structured electronic invoice in a defined format (under the European standard EN 16931), not just a PDF. Two key formats: XRechnung (pure XML, the standard for public procurement) and ZUGFeRD (a hybrid — PDF/A-3 with embedded XML). From 1 January 2025 all B2B companies in Germany must at least be able to receive an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung); the obligation to issue them is being phased in through 2028. This guide explains the formats, the deadlines and what an entrepreneur needs to do.

content.text: An electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) is an invoice in a structured electronic format that can be read and processed automatically. Under the German definition (and the European standard EN 16931), an ordinary PDF or a scan of a paper invoice does NOT count as an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) — a machine-readable structured format is required. The goal is to automate accounting and combat tax errors.

items: An electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) is a structured format, not a PDF/scan
It complies with the European standard EN 16931
It is machine-readable: the data is processed automatically
It concerns above all B2B transactions within Germany
The legal basis is changes to the UStG (the VAT law)

content.text: The two main formats in Germany comply with EN 16931. XRechnung is a pure XML format, the standard for transactions with public authorities (B2G). ZUGFeRD is a hybrid format: visually it is a PDF/A-3, but inside it is embedded XML with the same data, so the invoice is convenient for both humans and machines.

items: Pure XML without a visual layer
The standard for invoices to public authorities (B2G)
Strictly compliant with EN 16931
Processed by systems automatically
PDF/A-3 with embedded XML
Convenient for a human (seen as a PDF) and for a machine
From version 2.x compatible with EN 16931 (the EN 16931/XRechnung profile)
Often used in B2B

steps.title: Deadlines and what an entrepreneur should do

content.text: From 1 January 2025, every B2B business in Germany must be able to RECEIVE an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung). The obligation to ISSUE electronic invoices is being phased in: in 2025–2027 transitional rules apply (depending on turnover), and from 1 January 2028 an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) in B2B becomes mandatory for practically everyone. Paper and plain PDF invoices in B2B are gradually being phased out.

items: From 01.01.2025 — obligation to receive an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung; B2B)
2025–2027 — transitional rules for issuing (by turnover)
From 01.01.2028 — issuing an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) mandatory for almost everyone
Prepare a system to receive XRechnung/ZUGFeRD
Choose accounting software with EN 16931 support

content.text: Even if your obligation to issue invoices kicks in later, you must be able to receive an electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) already from 2025. A counterparty is entitled to send you a structured invoice, and you must be able to receive and process it.

costs.label: Receiving an E-Rechnung
costs.note: You can receive a structured invoice for free (e.g. via software or a validator).

costs.label: Accounting software with E-Rechnung support
costs.note: Per month; there are free tools and paid services (DATEV, Lexware and others).

costs.label: Integration/setup for a business
costs.note: Heavily depends on company size and the systems used.

title: eSIM: where to buy and how to activate
tldr: eSIM (embedded SIM) is supported by all major German carriers — Telekom, Vodafone, O2, 1&1 — as well as Aldi Talk and congstar. It is activated in a few minutes via a QR code or the carrier's app; it works on the iPhone XS and newer and on modern Android flagships. Handy for tourists and as a second line (Dual-SIM).

steps.title: What an eSIM is and why you need it

content.text: An eSIM (embedded SIM) is a chip built into the phone that replaces the physical SIM card. The carrier profile is loaded 'over the air' — via a QR code or through an app. In Germany, eSIM is supported by Telekom, Vodafone, O2 Telefónica and 1&1, and among the discounters by congstar (Telekom network) and Aldi Talk (Telefónica/O2 network). One phone can store several eSIM profiles and run in Dual-SIM mode.

items: Supported on the iPhone XS / XR and newer; on iPhone 14 and newer models for the US market — eSIM only
Supported on the Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer, Pixel 3 and newer, many modern Android phones
On an iPhone you can store up to 8 eSIM profiles, with 2 active at once
Works with any German plan — contract (Vertrag) or prepaid (Prepaid)
Ideal for a second number (work + personal) or for travel

content.text: The process is the same with every carrier: you order a plan, get a QR code and scan it in your phone's settings.

For a permanent contract — Telekom (MagentaMobil), Vodafone (GigaMobil), O2 (O2 Mobile), 1&1. For prepaid (Prepaid) — Aldi Talk Combi-Paket, congstar Prepaid, Vodafone CallYa, Telekom MagentaMobil Prepaid. When ordering on the website, choose 'eSIM' instead of a physical SIM.

After identification (PostIdent or Video-Ident for a contract; for prepaid (Prepaid) — the mandatory identification under § 172 TKG 2021) the QR code will arrive by email or appear in the carrier's app (MeinMagenta, MeinVodafone, Mein O2, Aldi Talk App).
Settings → Cellular → Add eSIM → Use QR Code. Scan the code — the phone loads the profile in 1–2 minutes. Name the plan ('Work', 'Personal') and choose it as the default for data and calls.
Settings → Network & internet → SIMs → Download a SIM instead → Next → scan the QR code. On Samsung the path is: Settings → Connections → SIM manager → Add mobile plan.

items.title: 5. Transferring an eSIM when changing phones

content.text: iPhone to iPhone — the eSIM Quick Transfer feature via Bluetooth (iOS 16 and newer). Otherwise order a new QR code from the carrier (Telekom — free in the app; Vodafone — 0–10€; O2 — free via Mein O2).
A QR code can be scanned only ONCE. If you deleted the profile or switched phones without Quick Transfer, the old QR code won't work — you'll need a new one from the carrier.

A prepaid (Prepaid) eSIM in Germany requires identification (usually Video-Ident; § 172 TKG 2021): passport and your face on camera. There is no anonymous activation. Identification usually takes a few minutes.
Older models — iPhones before the XS, many Android phones before 2019 — don't support eSIM. Check your device before buying: dial *#06# (an EID number should appear) or look in Settings → About.

costs.label: eSIM activation on order
costs.note: Free with most carriers when taking a new contract/plan

costs.label: Re-issuing a QR code
costs.note: Telekom/O2 — usually 0€ via the app; Vodafone — up to 9.99€

costs.label: Aldi Talk eSIM Prepaid
costs.note: Combi-Paket S 7.99€/4 weeks; Combi-Paket M 12.99€/4 weeks

costs.label: congstar Prepaid eSIM
costs.note: Allnet Flat 5 GB ~10€/4 weeks on the Telekom network

title: Free TV channels: ARD, ZDF
tldr: Germany's public broadcasting (ARD, ZDF, Deutschlandradio, regional channels) is funded by the mandatory broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) — 18.36€/month per household (Wohnung), regardless of whether you own a TV or not. The content is available for free over the air (DVB-T2), on cable, by satellite and via streaming through the ARD Mediathek and ZDF Mediathek.

content.text: Public-service broadcasting (Öffentlich-rechtlicher Rundfunk) is a system separate from the state. ARD is an association of nine regional companies (BR, NDR, WDR, MDR, HR, RBB, SR, SWR, Radio Bremen) that together produce the 'Das Erste' channel, and each runs its own regional programme (Drittes Programm). ZDF (Zweites Deutsches Fernsehen) is a separate nationwide network headquartered in Mainz. There are also joint channels (3sat, arte, KiKA, Phoenix) and Deutschlandradio (three radio stations). All of this is funded through the broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag).

items: Das Erste (ARD) — the main channel, the Tagesschau news at 20:00
ZDF — the main competitor, the heute news at 19:00
arte — a Franco-German cultural channel
3sat — a German-Austrian-Swiss cultural channel
Phoenix — news and parliamentary broadcasts
KiKA — the children's channel of ARD/ZDF
Tagesschau24, ZDFinfo, ARD-alpha — niche channels

content.text: Since you pay the broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) by virtue of being registered anyway, you may as well make use of it.

ARD Mediathek (ardmediathek.de) and ZDF Mediathek (zdf.de/mediathek) are apps for iOS, Android, Smart TV, Fire TV and Apple TV. No registration needed, everything is free and ad-free. Live streams (Livestream) and an archive ranging from 7 to 365 days are available — including Tagesschau, Tatort, documentaries and sport (Bundesliga highlights, Olympia).

You'll need an antenna and a DVB-T2 HD receiver (or a new TV with such a tuner). The public channels (ARD, ZDF and others) are free on DVB-T2. The private channels (RTL, ProSieben, Sat.1) run via the freenet TV platform — 8.99€/month. DVB-T2 coverage mainly spans big cities and metropolitan areas.

Since July 2024 cable TV (Kabel-TV) is no longer automatically part of the utility and operating costs (Nebenkosten) (the abolition of the Nebenkostenprivileg). Tenants now sign a contract themselves: Vodafone GigaTV Kabel — from ~13€/month. The public channels are free there too, but you pay separately for the cable signal itself.
You'll need a dish and a DVB-S2 receiver. The public channels in HD are free and unencrypted. Private HD channels — via HD+ (about 6€/month).
Telekom MagentaTV (~10€/month on top of internet), Vodafone GigaTV, Waipu.tv (from 6.99€). Convenient if you already have fast internet; the public channels are available there too.

The broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) is payable IN ANY CASE — even if you have no TV, no radio and no internet. It is a charge for the mere possibility of reception, tied to the household (Wohnung). A full exemption is possible only in strictly defined cases (§ 4 RBStV — for example, when receiving certain social benefits). Non-payment leads to back charges and enforced collection through a bailiff (Gerichtsvollzieher).

In the Mediathek many films and series are available for a limited time (the availability period, Verweildauer) — usually from 7 to 90 days, sometimes up to a year. Watch in time: once removed, the content is gone. The availability period is regulated by the interstate media treaty (Medienstaatsvertrag) and serves, among other things, to protect the interests of private broadcasters.

Because of geographic licensing, some content (especially sport and foreign films) is unavailable outside Germany. A VPN with a German IP technically solves the problem, but it violates the service's terms of use.

costs.label: Rundfunkbeitrag
costs.note: Per month per Wohnung; for 2026 the rate of 18.36€ applies (unchanged since 2021). The earlier proposal to raise it to 18.94€ was blocked by the states; the new KEF recommendation (February 2026) is 18.64€ from 2027. A Bundesverfassungsgericht decision is pending (hearing on 23.06.2026), so the increase has not yet taken effect. Check the current rate at rundfunkbeitrag.de.

costs.label: ARD/ZDF Mediathek
costs.note: Completely free, ad-free and without registration

costs.label: freenet TV (private DVB-T2 HD)
costs.note: Per month; the public DVB-T2 channels are free

costs.label: HD+ (private satellite HD)
costs.note: Per month; the public channels in HD on Astra are free

costs.label: Vodafone Kabel-TV
costs.note: Since July 2024 — a separate contract, not part of Nebenkosten

title: Internet: DSL vs cable vs Glasfaser
tldr: Germany has three main technologies: DSL (copper, up to 250 Mbit) — available almost everywhere, but slow; cable (Kabel; Vodafone, up to 1000 Mbit) — in the cities; fibre (Glasfaser; optics, up to 10 Gbit) — wherever it has been laid (around 40% of households in 2026). Before ordering, check availability (Verfügbarkeit) by address — even on the same street speeds can differ tenfold.

content.text: The internet available in Germany depends not on the plan but on the infrastructure at your specific address. If your neighbour has 1 Gbit, that doesn't mean you'll get more than 16 Mbit. Before ordering, always check availability (Verfügbarkeit) on the carrier's website — by the exact address with the house number.

items: DSL/VDSL — copper telephone lines, up to 100/250 Mbit (with Super-Vectoring); the main carrier is Telekom, resold by 1&1, O2, Vodafone
Cable (Kabel) — coaxial, DOCSIS 3.1 technology, up to 1000 Mbit; provider Vodafone (formerly Kabel Deutschland)
Fibre (Glasfaser; FTTH/FTTB) — fibre straight into the flat or basement, 100–10000 Mbit; Telekom, Deutsche Glasfaser, municipal city networks
5G/LTE Hybrid — a backup option if nothing else is available; Vodafone GigaCube, Telekom Speedbox

content.text: The sequence is: first an availability check, then a comparison of plans, then the order.

Go to telekom.de, vodafone.de, 1und1.de, o2online.de and enter the address — the site will show the maximum speed for each technology. In parallel, the broadband atlas (Breitbandatlas) of the Bundesnetzagentur (gigabitgrundbuch.bund.de) shows which technologies exist on the street, independently of the carrier.

Aggregators — Check24, Verivox, Finanztip. Look at the effective price over 24 months including promotions (new-customer bonus (Neukunden-Bonus) 50–200€) and the real speed, not 'up to'. Under § 57 TKG the carrier must state the minimum, normally available and maximum speed.

MagentaZuhause S (16 Mbit) — from ~30€, M (100 Mbit) — ~40€, L (250 Mbit) — ~50€. After 6–24 months the price usually rises by 10–15€. The minimum term is 24 months, after which the contract can be cancelled at any time with 1 month's notice (TKG 2021).

Plans of 50/250/500/1000 Mbit. The 1 Gbit plan — ~50–60€/month after the promotion. No technician needed if there's already a cable socket (Multimedia-Dose). The downside is a shared channel: at peak times the speed can drop.

items.title: 5. Glasfaser — Telekom MagentaZuhause Glasfaser / Deutsche Glasfaser

content.text: If the building is connected to FTTH — take it. Symmetric speeds of 100/300/1000 Mbit, low ping (5–10 ms), a stable connection. 250 Mbit — ~50–65€/month. To connect the flat you need an ONT (Optical Network Terminal) — the carrier usually installs it for free.

The real speed is regulated by § 57 TKG and the implementing ordinance TK-Transparenzverordnung. If measurements show that the actual speed deviates significantly and persistently from what's stated in the contract, you may have the right to a price reduction (Minderung) or early termination. The official measurement tool is breitbandmessung.de (Bundesnetzagentur); it also produces a report that documents the deviation. Check the exact thresholds and procedure in the current version of the ordinance.

At the end of the 24-month term the contract renews automatically, but under TKG 2021 it can now be cancelled monthly with 1 month's notice. Don't miss the end of the promotion — the price usually rises by 10–20€/month.

'Up to 1000 Mbit' on cable is marketing. In the evenings, on Vodafone Kabel the speed often drops by a factor of 2–3 because the channel is shared between tenants. On fibre (Glasfaser) this doesn't happen.

costs.label: DSL 100 Mbit (Telekom/1&1/O2)
costs.note: Per month after promotions; in the first 6 months there's often a discount of up to 50%

costs.label: Kabel 1 Gbit (Vodafone)
costs.note: Per month; in reality the peak-time speed can be 2–3 times lower

costs.label: Glasfaser 250 Mbit
costs.note: Per month; the symmetric upload is a big advantage

costs.label: Glasfaser connection
costs.note: Often free when ordering during the construction phase (Vorvermarktung), later — up to 750€

costs.label: Router (Fritz!Box 7590, purchase)
costs.note: Renting from the carrier 0–5€/month or buying your own under § 41b TKG (Routerfreiheit)

title: Cancelling a mobile contract
tldr: Under the TKG reform in force since December 2021, the maximum initial term of a mobile contract is 24 months, after which it can be cancelled AT ANY TIME with 1 month's notice. Cancel in writing or in text form (email, a form on the website). On a price increase the carrier must notify you in advance and grant the right to a free exit (special right of termination, Sonderkündigungsrecht).

content.text: On 1 December 2021 the reform of the telecommunications act (Telekommunikationsgesetz, TKG) came into force. The key changes for the consumer: (a) the initial term is a maximum of 24 months; (b) automatic renewal is possible, but with a right to monthly cancellation; (c) text form (Textform; no signature or original needed) is enough to cancel; (d) on a material change of terms a special right of termination (Sonderkündigungsrecht) applies; (e) after cancellation the provider must arrange the porting of your number to the new carrier, as a rule within one working day.

items: Notice period: 1 month to the end of any month (after the initial 24)
Form: text form (Textform) — email, a form on the website, the provider's chatbot
Proof of receipt matters more than the date of sending
Special right of termination (Sonderkündigungsrecht) — on a price increase, a change of plan terms, a move to an area without coverage
Number porting — as a rule within 1 working day, free

content.text: If you simply want to leave the carrier — follow the standard procedure. If you have a special right of termination (Sonderkündigungsrecht) — state it explicitly in your notice.

items.title: 1. Find the end date of the initial term

content.text: In the carrier's app (MeinMagenta, MeinVodafone, Mein O2, Control Center 1&1) open the 'Vertrag' (contract) section. It shows the Vertragsbeginn (contract start) and Mindestlaufzeit (minimum term). Under the new rules the minimum term cannot exceed 24 months (old contracts concluded before December 2021 may be for 24 months with auto-renewal for 12).

Subject: Kündigung Mobilfunkvertrag. Text: «Hiermit kündige ich meinen Mobilfunkvertrag, Kundennummer [number], Rufnummer [number], zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt. Bitte bestätigen Sie die Kündigung sowie das Beendigungsdatum schriftlich.» If you want to port your number, add: «Ich möchte meine Rufnummer mitnehmen.»

The best channel is the dedicated form on the carrier's website ('Kündigung online', online cancellation). If the contract was concluded online, by law the carrier must have a simple cancellation button (Kündigungsbutton, § 312k BGB): cancelling online must be no harder than concluding the contract. To cancel by email, check the current address on the specific carrier's website (Telekom, Vodafone, O2, 1&1) in the 'Kündigung' (cancellation) section or in the help — the addresses change periodically. Keep the screenshot of the form or the confirmation email for at least 6 months.

Within a few days the carrier must send a cancellation confirmation (Kündigungsbestätigung) with the exact end date of the contract. If no confirmation arrives — write again and warn of a possible complaint to the Bundesnetzagentur (the consumer service, Verbraucherservice).

A right to early termination arises on a unilateral change of terms, including a price increase (§ 57 TKG 'Vertragsänderung, Minderung und außerordentliche Kündigung'), on a reduction of the promised speed or features, and on a move to an area without that carrier's coverage. The period to exercise this right is stated in the carrier's own notice — check it in each case. The result is an early exit without penalty.

A carrier's promise over the phone to lower the price if you stay does not by itself extend the minimum term (Mindestlaufzeit). But carriers often dress up such an offer as a new contract. Always insist on written confirmation of all changes — otherwise you can find yourself tied in for another 24 months.

Don't confuse cancellation (Kündigung) and withdrawal (Widerruf). Withdrawal (Widerruf) is possible within 14 days after concluding the contract online (§ 312g BGB, a distance contract). After that period — only cancellation (Kündigung) under the TKG rules.

When porting a number, do NOT cancel the contract before submitting the porting request. Since December 2021 this happens automatically: you order a new plan with a competitor, tick 'Rufnummernmitnahme' (number porting) in the order, and the new carrier itself initiates the cancellation and porting (as a rule within 1 working day). The old account is closed as of the porting date.

costs.label: Cancellation
costs.note: Free — the law does not allow charging for cancellation

costs.label: Number porting (Portierung)
costs.note: Since December 2021 — free under § 59 TKG (previously — up to 30€)

costs.label: Early exit via Sonderkündigung
costs.note: No penalty on a price increase or a move out of the coverage area

costs.label: Legal advice (Verbraucherzentrale)
costs.note: If the carrier doesn't respond: a consultation 20–30€, help with a complaint — up to 90€

costs.label: Complaint to the Bundesnetzagentur
costs.note: Free via verbraucherservice@bnetza.de

title: Mobile carriers: Telekom, Vodafone, O2, 1&1
tldr: Germany has four network operators (MNO): Telekom (the best coverage, the most expensive), Vodafone (good coverage, mid-range price), O2 Telefónica (average coverage, cheaper), 1&1 (the newest, the 4th network, partly via roaming on O2). For remote areas — Telekom; in the city, O2 and 1&1 save 30–40%. Everyone has 5G, but Telekom covers more widely.

steps.title: The four networks and their characteristics

content.text: Germany currently has four mobile network operators (Mobilfunknetzbetreiber, MNO) — operators with their own physical infrastructure. All the other brands (congstar, Aldi Talk, Lidl Connect, Freenet, Mobilcom-Debitel, Klarmobil and dozens of others) are MVNOs/resellers that buy access to one of these four networks.

items: Telekom (Deutsche Telekom / T-Mobile) — the leader in coverage, especially outside cities; 5G claimed for roughly 98% of the population
Vodafone — wide 4G, good 5G in cities; Telekom's main competitor
O2 (Telefónica Germany) — has caught up in cities, weaker in rural areas; the cheapest 4G among the MNOs
1&1 — launched as the 4th network operator (MNO) in 2023; its own network is being built, the rest via national roaming (National Roaming) on the O2/Telefónica network

steps.title: How to choose for your profile

content.text: The main rule: check the coverage exactly where you actually live and travel.

The mobile network monitoring (Mobilfunk-Monitoring) of the Bundesnetzagentur (gigabitgrundbuch.bund.de/MN) shows real 4G/5G coverage maps for all carriers. There are also the carriers' own maps: telekom.de/netzausbau, vodafone.de/netzabdeckung, o2online.de/netzabdeckung. Enter a postcode (Postleitzahl) or address.

items.title: 2. Telekom — for those often out of town

content.text: Plans MagentaMobil S (10 GB) — ~30€, M (40 GB) — ~45€, L (unlimited) — ~75€. 5G included. The best coverage, especially in rural areas, on the train, in the mountains. The downside is the price.

GigaMobil S (15 GB) — ~30€, M (50 GB) — ~40€, XL (unlimited) — ~60€. Coverage in cities is almost as good as Telekom's, a bit worse in rural areas. The advantage is RED+ Allnet for the family (a shared data pool).

items.title: 4. O2 — a balance of price and quality

content.text: O2 Mobile S (15 GB) — ~25€, M (40 GB) — ~35€, Unlimited Smart — ~30€ (but the speed is capped at 25 Mbit). 5G included. In Berlin, Munich and Hamburg the coverage is excellent. In rural Bavaria or in eastern Germany there are gaps.

items.title: 5. 1&1 — the youngest network, proceed with caution

content.text: Allnet-Flat 20 GB — ~20€, Unlimited — ~35€. 1&1 has been building its own 5G network since 2023, but it's still small. The rest of the coverage is via national roaming (National Roaming) on the O2 network (from 2025 partly on Vodafone). If stability matters, check the coverage at your exact address.

'Unlimited' means different speeds with different carriers. Telekom MagentaMobil L — no limit. O2 Unlimited Smart — 25 Mbit, Basic — 10 Mbit. Vodafone GigaMobil XL — full speed. Read the fine print before ordering.

'There's a signal' and '5G works at 100 Mbit' are different things. By the carriers' maps, 4G coverage is almost everywhere, but 5G beyond the metropolitan areas still has gaps. If 5G is critical — Telekom is ahead.

Resellers (congstar, Aldi Talk, Freenet) often give the same network 30–50% cheaper, but without priority: at peak times your traffic is served after the main carrier's customers. For most users the difference is unnoticeable.

title: Portierung: keeping your number
tldr: Porting your number (Rufnummernmitnahme) to a new provider has been free since December 2021 under § 59 TKG and is usually completed within one business day. You order it directly when signing up for a new plan: tick "Rufnummer mitnehmen" and enter your old provider and number. The old contract is automatically terminated on the porting date.

content.text: Porting a number (Rufnummernportierung) means transferring your mobile or landline number from your old provider to a new one. Since the TKG reform of December 2021 the process has been free (the old provider used to charge up to 30€) and usually takes no more than one business day (Werktag). If the technical port does not happen by the next business day, under § 59 TKG you are entitled to claim 10€ in compensation from the provider responsible for the delay, for each day of delay.

items: The old and new contracts can be with different providers of any type (MNO, MVNO, Prepaid)
Timeframe — usually up to 1 business day for active contracts
A number from a contract that has already ended can be ported within about 30 days after it expires
You can port a number even in the middle of a contract term
The old contract is automatically terminated on the porting date

content.text: The process is simple: the new provider does almost everything for you.

items.title: 1. Sign up for a new plan

content.text: In the cart, or after choosing a plan on the new provider's website or in their store, tick "Ich möchte meine Rufnummer mitnehmen". Enter your old number, your old provider (for mobile, the brand name: Telekom, O2, congstar, etc.) and the desired porting date.

The porting authorization (Portierungserklärung) is either part of the online sign-up or a separate signature in the store. In essence it is the power of attorney that lets the new provider request your number from the old one.

On the scheduled day the old SIM stops working and the new SIM/eSIM starts receiving calls on your number. The downtime is usually from half an hour to a few hours during that day. It is best to choose a business day in the morning.
Call yourself from another number, receive an SMS code and check the internet. If something is wrong, call the new provider's hotline.

Do NOT terminate the old contract BEFORE ordering the port. Once it is closed, the number goes back into the provider's pool and after a while may be assigned to another customer. The window for porting a number from a finished contract is about 30 days.

WhatsApp, Telegram, banking apps and 2FA services are tied to your number. After porting, everything keeps working (it is the same number), but apps like Signal or Telegram may require re-verification by SMS on a new device. Don't block the old SIM until you have received all the codes you need.

If the provider drags out the port beyond one business day, under § 59 TKG, in the event of a service interruption you are entitled to claim 10€ or 20% of the monthly plan fee for each additional business day — whichever is higher. Claim it in writing. A complaint to the Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur, verbraucherservice@bnetza.de) speeds up the process.

costs.label: Porting the number (Portierung)
costs.note: Free under § 59 TKG since December 2021 (before that — up to 30€)

costs.label: Compensation for porting delay
costs.note: For each business day of delay beyond the deadline — 10€; in case of a service interruption — 10€ or 20% of the monthly fee, whichever is higher (§ 59 TKG)

title: Prepaid: Aldi Talk, congstar
tldr: The best prepaid deals in Germany: Aldi Talk (Telefónica/O2 network, flexible, 7.99€/4 weeks for Combi-Paket S with 4 GB) and congstar Prepaid (Telekom network, slightly more expensive but better coverage). No long-term commitments, you can pause the plan, number porting is free. Activation requires identification (usually Video-Ident: passport + face on camera).

content.text: Prepaid is a "SIM without a contract": you pay in advance and can change or pause the plan at any time. It is handy for newcomers (you need neither a residence registration (Anmeldung) nor a credit history at the Schufa bureau), for short stays, a second number, kids or guests from abroad. All prepaid SIMs in Germany require identification at activation (usually Video-Ident; § 172 TKG 2021), but it is a formality that takes a few minutes.

items: No 24-month tie-in — you pay in advance by the week or month
Coverage matches the underlying provider's network (Aldi Talk — O2; congstar — Telekom)
You can keep the SIM inactive — the number is retained as long as the balance is positive or there is activity (usually within a few months)
Porting your number between prepaid SIMs is free
5G is available on current Aldi Talk and congstar plans

content.text: For most needs Aldi Talk is enough; for rural areas, congstar; for tourists, a travel eSIM (see below).

Telefónica/O2 network, 5G on current plans. Combi-Paket S (4 GB + Allnet-Flat) — 7.99€/4 weeks; M (8 GB) — 12.99€; L (18 GB) — 17.99€; XL (30 GB) — 22.99€. Sold in any Aldi store and online (alditalk.de). Activation and Video-Ident are done through the Aldi Talk app.
Telekom network (the best coverage in Germany), 5G. Allnet Flat 5 GB — ~10€/4 weeks, 15 GB — ~20€/4 weeks. Ideal for those who are often out of town or on the train. Order at congstar.de.
Also the Telefónica/O2 network (the same as Aldi Talk), with comparable prices. Smart 1500: 5 GB + Allnet for 7.99€/4 weeks. Convenient if there is a Lidl nearby.

Branded prepaid directly from the MNOs. More expensive (15–25€/month), but with no intermediaries and direct support. Vodafone CallYa Digital — 24.99€/4 weeks: unlimited Allnet and unlimited data on 5G.
Saily, Airalo, Holafly — eSIMs for 1–30 days without German Video-Ident (they operate under European licenses). Suitable for tourists and short visits. Not cost-effective for long-term residence.

Identification at activation is mandatory — passport or residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) and your face on camera (usually Video-Ident). Under § 172 TKG 2021 there are no anonymous prepaid SIMs in Germany.

The Aldi Talk Combi-Paket renews automatically every 4 weeks if there is enough money in the balance. If you don't want it to renew, turn off auto-renewal (Verlängerung) in the app, otherwise your balance will be deducted without your noticing.

With Aldi Talk and other MVNOs, speed during peak hours may be throttled because their traffic has lower priority on the underlying network. This may not be enough for 4K streaming at peak times, but it is more than enough for everyday tasks and navigation.

title: EU roaming: the rules
tldr: Since 2017 the EU/EEA has applied the "Roam like at home" principle: your German plan works in the 27 EU countries, plus Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, at domestic prices. Regulation EU 2022/612 extended this rule until June 2032. Unlimited data plans are subject to a fair use limit. Switzerland, the UK and Turkey are not in the EU, so roaming there is usually paid.

steps.title: What Roam Like At Home means

content.text: RLAH (Roam Like At Home) is the EU-wide rule that has been in force since 15 June 2017 and was extended by Regulation EU 2022/612 until 30 June 2032. In short: when you travel across the EU/EEA, your German mobile plan (Vertrag or Prepaid) works at the same prices as at home. Minutes, SMS and gigabytes are drawn from your main package. There is no need to buy separate "roaming packages".

items: 27 EU countries plus Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein — 30 EU/EEA countries in total
Minutes and SMS — no separate limits within your plan
Data may have a fair use limit on unlimited plans
Calls within the country you're visiting and back to Germany — at your domestic rate
Calls from Germany to the EU are not covered by RLAH and count as international (3–19 cents/min)

steps.title: In practice and the fine print

content.text: In most cases you don't need to set anything up — your phone picks up the network in Italy or Spain on its own and your plan just works.
Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Data Roaming = ON. Without this, SMS and calls work but the internet does not. On iPhone and Android, data roaming is often off by default.

items.title: 2. Understand fair use for unlimited plans

content.text: Under EU regulation, a provider may apply a fair use limit to unlimited plans while roaming. The rough formula: data limit = (average monthly plan price excluding VAT ÷ wholesale roaming rate per GB) × 2. As of 2026 the wholesale rate is 1.10€/GB (from 1 January 2027 it drops to 1.00€/GB and stays there until 30 June 2032). On a plan of around 30€ net, this works out to roughly a few dozen GB. Check the specific fair use limits for your plan (for example, Telekom MagentaMobil, O2, Vodafone GigaMobil) with your provider — they change.

items.title: 3. What is NOT covered by RLAH

content.text: Not covered: Switzerland, the UK (after Brexit), Turkey, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino, the Vatican and the Balkan countries. The conditions depend on the provider: for example, with some Telekom plans Switzerland is included in the EU-Roaming option, with certain Vodafone GigaMobil plans the UK is included in the unlimited bundle, while with O2 Switzerland is usually charged extra. Check before you travel.

items.title: 4. Permanent roaming — not for living abroad

content.text: RLAH is designed for trips, not for permanent use of a German SIM abroad. The provider may check "predominant use": if over an observation period (about 4 months) you have spent more time abroad than in Germany, it may impose a surcharge. In practice this is rarely applied.

items.title: 5. Outside the EU — separate packages or eSIM

content.text: In the US, Thailand, Turkey or Russia, RLAH does not apply. A provider's standard rates in distant roaming zones are very expensive (often 10€ or more per MB). Use packages like Telekom Travel & Surf (from 4.95€/day), eSIM apps (Airalo, Saily) or a local SIM.
When you enter a country, your provider must send an SMS with the roaming conditions — it states the fair use limit and the call rates. Save that message or check the conditions in the app.

Exceeding the fair use data limit does not cut you off but adds a surcharge at the regulated wholesale rate (as of 2026 — 1.10€/GB excluding VAT). On an unlimited plan they won't cut you off in Italy beyond your fair use limit, but your bill may grow.

On cruise ships, planes and in border areas your phone may pick up a "ship" or satellite network (for example, MCP, OnAir) — roaming there is at very high rates and RLAH does not apply. In the settings you can manually select only terrestrial networks.

title: Pharmacies: what you can buy without a prescription
tldr: In Germany the pharmacy (Apotheke) is the only place you can buy medicines. Over-the-counter (rezeptfrei, but apothekenpflichtig): paracetamol, ibuprofen, ASS (aspirin), nasal sprays, cold and stomach remedies. Antibiotics and strong painkillers — only with a doctor's prescription (Rezept). OTC prices: 2–10 €. At night and on weekends an emergency pharmacy (Notdienst) is open — find its address on aponet.de or on the sign on the door of the nearest closed pharmacy.

steps.title: Why everything is sold only at the pharmacy

content.text: Germany has a strict pharmacy monopoly on the sale of medicines — Apothekenpflicht. Unlike in the US or Portugal, in a supermarket or drugstore (Drogerie; dm, Rossmann) you won't even find paracetamol. They only sell dietary supplements (Nahrungsergänzungsmittel), cosmetics, hygiene products and vitamins.

Pharmacies are recognizable by the red Gothic letter A on a white background. Opening hours are usually Mo–Fr 8:30–18:30, Sa until 13:00–14:00. On Sundays and holidays only the on-call ones are open (Notdienst-Apotheke) — they take turns by district.

items: Apothekenpflichtig — sold only at the pharmacy, but without a prescription
Verschreibungspflichtig (Rx) — a doctor's prescription is required
Freiverkäuflich — can be bought in a Drogerie/supermarket (rarely: medicinal teas, simple ointments)
Prescriptions: the pink paper one or the electronic E-Rezept via your insurer's app
Under statutory insurance (gesetzlich) the patient makes a co-payment (Zuzahlung) of 5–10 € for a prescription medicine

steps.title: What to buy without a prescription

content.text: A basic home medicine cabinet in Germany — any Apotheke will sell you all of these without questions, though the pharmacist may ask about your symptoms and suggest an alternative.

items: Paracetamol (Paracetamol) — for pain and fever, 500 mg, up to 10 tablets without a prescription, 2–4 €
Ibuprofen (Ibuprofen) — 400 mg, up to 20 tablets without a prescription, 3–6 €
ASS (Acetylsalicylsäure / Aspirin) — 500 mg, for headache, 4–7 €
Nasal sprays (Nasenspray) — Otriven, Nasic, 4–7 €
For colds — GeloMyrtol, ACC (Acetylcystein), Wick MediNait, 8–15 €
For the stomach — Iberogast, Omeprazol 20 mg (up to 14 tablets without a prescription), Imodium
Antihistamines — Cetirizin, Loratadin, 5–10 €
Topical — Hansaplast plasters, Voltaren/Diclofenac ointments, Bepanthen

content.text: Antibiotics (Amoxicillin, Azithromycin, etc.) in Germany are sold STRICTLY by prescription. No pharmacy will sell them without a Rezept, even for cash. If your cold won't go away, see your family doctor (Hausarzt) or go to the emergency department (Notaufnahme).

In Germany pharmacies take turns being on duty 24/7. You can find the on-call pharmacy (Notdienst-Apotheke) in your district at aponet.de (enter your postal code, Postleitzahl), by calling 22 8 33 (a paid number) or simply on the door of the nearest closed pharmacy — there is always a notice with the address of the nearest open one.

items: For using the Notdienst the pharmacy charges a surcharge of 2,50 € per visit (Notdienstgebühr)
Notdienst applies Mo–Fr from 18:30 to 8:30, Sa from 14:00, all day Sunday and on holidays
The 116 117 number is the after-hours doctors' service, not to be confused with 112 (ambulance)
For serious cases — the Notaufnahme at a hospital or 112
The electronic prescription E-Rezept is valid at any pharmacy in Germany via the insurer's app or the health insurance card (GesundheitsKarte)

content.text: Don't order prescription medicines through Russian or Turkish online pharmacies — that counts as illegal import, the parcel will be held at customs, plus a fine. Legal online pharmacies in Germany: DocMorris, Shop-Apotheke, Aponeo — but Rx medicines require you to upload a prescription.

costs.note: Prices are roughly the same at all pharmacies; cheaper are the generics ratiopharm, Hexal.

costs.label: Nasal spray or cough syrup
costs.note: Otriven, GeloMyrtol, Wick — a typical cold kit.

costs.note: Standard co-payment under statutory insurance (gesetzlich); children under 18 are exempt.

title: Bäckerei: real German bread
tldr: German bread culture means 300+ officially registered types of bread and 1200 types of rolls. In 2014 UNESCO added it to the list of intangible cultural heritage. A bakery (Bäckerei) opens at 6:00–7:00, and the best rolls are snapped up before 9:00. On Sundays it's one of the few places allowed to open (under §12 Ladenschlussgesetz / the state-level Ladenöffnungsgesetze, usually for ~3 hours). A roll (Brötchen) costs 0,40–0,80 €, a loaf of Vollkornbrot — 3–5 €. Tell a real bakery apart from a Backshop chain (where the bread is only thawed).

steps.title: Why Germans are obsessed with bread

content.text: Germany has more than 3200 officially registered types of bread and rolls in the Brotregister of the German Bread Institute (Deutsches Brotinstitut). That is a record for a single country. In 2014 UNESCO added "Deutsche Brotkultur" to the list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity.

The main difference from French or Italian bread is the use of rye (Roggen) and sourdough (Sauerteig). Such bread keeps for a long time, has a dense structure and a sour taste. A typical German breakfast is Brötchen with butter, cheese and cold cuts; lunch is a cold sandwich (Stulle, Pausenbrot); and dinner is literally called Abendbrot — "evening bread".

items: Vollkornbrot — wholegrain rye, the most "German" one, 3–5 €/loaf
Roggenbrot — rye made with sourdough
Mischbrot / Graubrot — mixed wheat-and-rye, the basic loaf
Pumpernickel — dark and slightly sweet, steamed for a long time (Westfalen)
Bauernbrot — "farmhouse", large and round
Dinkelbrot — made from spelt, considered "healthy"
Brötchen / Semmel / Schrippe / Wecken — regional names for rolls
Laugenbrezel, Laugenstange — pretzel and stick in a lye glaze

steps.title: A real Bäckerei vs a Backshop

content.text: Not every place with a "Bäckerei" sign bakes bread on site. The big chains (Kamps, BackWerk, and partly Lidl/Aldi) are bake-off stations (Aufbackstationen), where frozen dough is merely finished off. A real craft bakery (Handwerksbäckerei) works with its own sourdough and local flour, and is usually family-run, with a bakehouse attached to the shop.

items: A sign of a real bakery — membership in the bakers' guild (Innungsmitglied, Bäckerinnung), shown by the guild plaque on the door
A warm smell from early morning, with the bakehouse visible through the glass
Prices a bit higher: Brötchen 0,50–0,80 € versus 0,30 € in a Backshop
Bread that is not of perfectly uniform shape, with a cracked crust
Closed for an hour at lunch in many small towns
Holds a Brotregister certificate — a guarantee of the type classification

content.text: In Berlin, Sironi, Albatross and Domberger Brot-Werk are well known; in Munich — Hofpfisterei, Wimmer; in Hamburg — Effenberger, Springer. Find a local bakery by searching "Bäckerei Innung [city]".

steps.title: When it's open: Sundays and holidays

content.text: Germany has the federal Ladenschlussgesetz and regional Ladenöffnungsgesetze — on Sundays and holidays shops are closed. But bakeries have a special exemption: §12 Ladenschlussgesetz (and the corresponding state laws) allows the sale of baked goods on Sundays for a limited time — usually up to ~3 hours in the morning (each state sets the exact hours, for example 7:00–10:00 or 8:00–11:00). Check what's current.

items: Weekdays: the bakery opens at 6:00–7:00, closes at 18:00–19:00
Saturday: 6:30–14:00, often open until 16:00
Sunday: 3 hours in the morning, exact time — on the door (Sonntagsöffnung)
Holidays (gesetzliche Feiertage): closed, or the same 3 hours in the morning
Train stations and airports (Bahnhof, Flughafen) — bakeries open all week on a special schedule
Petrol station (Tankstelle) — sells rolls 24/7, but it's not a real bakery
A café attached to a bakery may stay open longer as a Bistro/Café

content.text: Don't show up at a bakery after 11:00 on a Sunday — even if the shop is technically open, there's almost no choice left. The morning rolls are gone by 9:30. On weekdays it's the same: by 14:00 in small bakeries only Vollkornbrot and the unpopular types are left.
