title: Organic stores: Alnatura, Denn's
tldr: Germany has the most developed organic market in Europe. The main organic supermarket chains are Alnatura (~150 stores), Denn's BioMarkt (~340), Basic, BioCompany (Berlin) and VollCorner (Munich). Prices are 25–40% higher than regular supermarkets, but the range is unique: gluten-free, vegan, Demeter products, regional farmers. Organic labelling is regulated by the EU: the green EU leaf is mandatory, plus the German Bio-Siegel and stricter private labels — Bioland, Demeter, Naturland.

content.text: The word "Bio" in Germany is legally protected — it can only be used for products certified under the EU-Öko-Verordnung (Regulation (EU) 2018/848). The packaging must carry the green EU leaf and the code of the control body (for example, DE-ÖKO-006). In addition, there may be the German state Bio-Siegel (a hexagon).

Germany is the largest organic market in Europe: turnover in 2024 was ~16 billion €, and organic's share of food was ~7%. Even Aldi, Lidl and Rewe stock certified products on their regular "Bio" shelves — but specialized organic markets have a wider range and often stricter standards.

items: EU-Bio-Logo (the green leaf) — the EU minimum standard, mandatory
Bio-Siegel (the German hexagon) — the same as EU, but a national mark
Bioland — a private association, stricter than EU (a ban on air-freighting products, higher animal welfare standards)
Demeter — biodynamics, the strictest standard
Naturland — a private association, also above EU
Fairtrade — a social label, which may or may not come with organic certification

content.text: In big cities several national and regional organic chains operate. They all sell fresh vegetables, meat, dairy, groceries, cosmetics and dietary supplements under their own private labels.

items: Alnatura — the most recognizable brand, ~150 stores; the flagship is the Alnatura Super Natur Markt, plus products in Rewe, dm
Denn's BioMarkt — the largest chain, ~340 stores across Germany and Austria
BioCompany — a regional chain in Berlin/Brandenburg, ~70 stores
Basic Bio — Bavaria, Baden-Württemberg, NRW
VollCorner — Munich and the surrounding area
Erdkorn — northern Germany, Hamburg
Locally — small farm shops (Hofladen, Bio-Hofladen)

content.text: If you want the lowest price — organic versions exist at Aldi (Gut Bio), Lidl (Bio Organic), Rewe (Rewe Bio) and Edeka (Bio+). On average they are 20–30% cheaper than at Alnatura, but the range is narrower and the standard is usually the EU minimum rather than Bioland/Demeter.

steps.title: What to buy at an organic store

content.text: An organic market makes sense for categories where the difference between a conventional and an organic product is especially noticeable — in taste, safety or ethics.

items: Eggs — definitely Bio (code 0 on the shell), free-range hens
Dairy — Demeter milk from a returnable glass bottle (Pfand), sugar-free yogurts
Meat and cold cuts — the welfare standards are considerably stricter
Vegetables and fruit — regional, seasonal; prices are not much higher than at the supermarket
Bread — real Vollkorn-Sauerteig, often Demeter grain
Dry grains and flour — especially wholegrain, spelt (Dinkel)
Gluten-free products — a bigger selection than at Rewe
Vegan substitutes — tofu, tempeh, oat drinks
Cosmetics and cleaning products — Sonett, Sodasan, Weleda

content.text: Not all "eco" products are actually organic. The words "Natur", "aus der Natur" and "vom Bauernhof" have NO legal meaning and may appear on conventional products. Trust only certified logos with the control body's code (DE-ÖKO-XXX).

costs.label: A litre of organic milk
costs.note: At Aldi/Lidl Bio — from 1,30 €; Demeter in glass — up to 2,20 €.

costs.label: A dozen organic eggs
costs.note: Demeter and Bioland are more expensive than basic Bio.

costs.label: Organic bread (Vollkorn 1 kg)
costs.note: At a Bäckerei with Demeter grain it comes out more expensive.

costs.label: A week's basket of groceries (1 person)
costs.note: The same basket at Rewe — 45–70 €. Organic markup 25–40%.

title: Cash vs card: where it's accepted
tldr: Germany is the most "cash-loving" country in the EU after Austria. According to the Bundesbank, ~50% of retail payments are still made in cash. All the big chains (Aldi, Lidl, Rewe, Edeka, Kaufland, dm, Rossmann) accept the German debit card (Girocard), Visa, Mastercard, Apple/Google Pay. But the Bäckerei, the kebab shop, the Biergarten, a small café, taxis, the doctor, the nail technician, the hairdresser and many Wochenmarkt stalls are still Nur Bargeld. Always carry 30–50 € in cash. The deposit on containers (Pfand) is returned at a reverse vending machine (Rücknahmeautomat) and credited to your receipt.

content.text: "Bargeld ist gedruckte Freiheit" — "cash is printed freedom", a common German mantra. According to a Bundesbank study, about half of retail transactions are paid in cash. The reasons: a deep attachment to privacy, distrust of big banks, the historical experience of the inflation crises of the 20th century, and simply habit.

Legally a seller has the right to refuse to accept a card: "Kein Kartenzahlung" is a lawful sign. Although euro banknotes are legal tender, the individual sales contract allows the method of payment to be restricted.

items: Carry 30–50 € in small notes and coins for everyday use
Coins in your wallet are useful for the deposit bag (Pfand-Tasche), lockers at the pool (Schwimmbad) and supermarket trolleys
It's cheapest to withdraw cash at your own bank or at partners of CashGroup, Cash Pool
Sparkasse and Volksbank-Raiffeisen — their own ATM networks
At REWE, Penny, Aldi, Lidl, dm you can withdraw cash with a card on purchases from 5–10 € (Cashback)

content.text: Most big chains accept both the Girocard (the German debit card, with blue/red V-Pay/Maestro marks), international Visa/Mastercard, and contactless via Apple Pay, Google Pay, Garmin Pay.

items: Accept all card types: Aldi, Lidl, Rewe, Edeka, Kaufland, Netto, Penny
Drogerie: dm, Rossmann, Müller — cards work
All online shops (Amazon, Otto, Zalando) — card or PayPal
Petrol stations, parking, IKEA, MediaMarkt — cards
Deutsche Bahn (counter, machine, app) — cards
Museums, cinemas — usually cards
Chain restaurants (Vapiano, L'Osteria, Hans im Glück, McDonald's) — cards

content.text: The Girocard is Germany's own system; it works almost everywhere in Germany but is poorly accepted abroad. Visa/Mastercard are more universal, but small shops sometimes dislike them because of the high fees.
There is a whole "cash segment" of German life where cards are still not accepted, or accepted reluctantly. This applies especially to small trades, food service and the service sector.

items: Small Bäckerei — often Nur Bargeld, or card only from 10 €
Imbiss, Dönerbude, Currywurst stand — usually cash only
Biergarten, Kiosk, Spätkauf — predominantly cash
Farmers' market (Wochenmarkt) — almost everywhere cash
Taxis (outside chain apps) — ask Kartenzahlung möglich? before getting in
Hairdresser, nail salon, massage (Friseur, Nagelstudio, Massage) — often cash plus a tip (Trinkgeld) separately
Family doctor, dentist (Hausarzt, Zahnarzt) for private payment — cash or bank transfer (Überweisung)
Tradesperson (Handwerker; plumber, electrician) — usually an invoice for bank transfer, sometimes cash in hand at a discount

content.text: A tip (Trinkgeld) in Germany is 5–10%, and it's customary to leave it in cash even if the main bill is paid by card. Just round up and tell the waiter the total before paying by card ("Macht 27 Euro"), or leave coins on the table.

steps.title: Pfand: how to get your deposit back

content.text: Under §31 VerpackG (Verpackungsgesetz), Germany has a mandatory deposit on single-use and reusable beverage containers. It is not a price — it is a deposit you get back when you return the container.

items: Einweg (single-use PET/cans): 0,25 € — marked with the DPG logo
Mehrweg glass (beer, lemonade): 0,08–0,15 €
Mehrweg PET (mineral water): 0,15 € + 1,50 € per crate
Beer glass bottles 0,5 l: often 0,08 €, crate 1,50–3,30 €
Return at a Rücknahmeautomat: available at Lidl, Aldi, Kaufland, Rewe, Edeka, Penny
You get a Pfandbon (receipt), which you can either cash out at the till or deduct from your next purchase
Einweg-Pfand is only accepted by shops that sell a similar type of container

content.text: A Pfand-bon is only valid in the chain (and often the specific store) where it was issued. Hand in a Lidl receipt at Lidl, a Rewe one at Rewe. The validity period is usually 1–3 years, with the exact date on the receipt.

costs.note: Standard Einweg-Pfand with the DPG logo.

costs.note: Beer 0,08 €, water/lemonade 0,15 €.

costs.note: The drink itself is sold on top.

costs.note: Depends on the bank and network; at Sparkasse/Volksbank within your own network — 0 €.

title: Cleaning: Helpling, BookATiger
tldr: Regular apartment cleaning through the Helpling and BookATiger platforms costs 20–35 €/hour; a cleaner for 2 hours a week works out to ~250 €/month. Under §35a EStG you can get back 20% of the cost (max. 4000 €/year) in your annual tax return, if you pay legally and via an account. The services handle the paperwork themselves, insure the cleaner and provide a replacement in case of illness. Paying cash "through a friend" gives no tax deduction and leaves you without insurance if there's damage.

content.text: In Germany there are three workable ways to hire a cleaner: an online platform (Helpling, BookATiger), a classic cleaning company (Putzfirma), and a mini-job (Minijob) — hiring a private individual directly, with registration at the Minijob-Zentrale.

items: Helpling (helpling.de) — the largest platform, ~20–28 €/hour, operates in most big cities
BookATiger (bookatiger.com) — the premium segment, 25–35 €/hour, focused on regular clients
Batmaid — a Swiss player, active in the southern states
Helpster, ZipJet (cleaning + laundry) — niche options
Putzfirma — a traditional company, a direct contract, 25–40 €/hour
Minijob via the Minijob-Zentrale — the cheapest, but all the paperwork is on you

content.text: Upsides of platforms: you book via the website/app in under a minute, pay by card, get an automatic receipt for the tax office, insurance against damage, and a replacement cleaner in case of illness. Downsides: more expensive than going direct, and the cleaner's actual wage is only part of the cost.

steps.title: How to book for the first time

content.text: The basic scenario is weekly cleaning of 2–3 hours. The platforms first offer a trial slot, then a regular slot with the same person.

items: Apartment size in m² — determines the recommended duration
Frequency: one-off, every 2 weeks, weekly
Extras: windows, oven, fridge, ironing
Your own cleaning supplies — state this, otherwise the cleaner brings their own for a surcharge
The platform offers a specific person or several profiles
On the profile — rating, reviews, experience, languages (important: many speak only German/Polish/Russian)
Confirm the date of the first visit
Get a receipt and an order ID
Show the apartment and your priorities (what matters more: kitchen, windows, floor)
Point out where the supplies, bucket and vacuum cleaner are
Give a spare key or stay home
Give feedback afterwards: the platform will save your preferences
Trinkgeld — 2–5 € if you like (not required, but customary)

steps.title: §35a EStG: claim back 20% on your taxes

content.text: Under §35a Einkommensteuergesetz (EStG) you can get back 20% of the cost of household services in your own home (haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen). The maximum deduction is 4000 € per year — that is, up to 20 000 € of expenses a year.

items: This is not a deduction from income but a tax credit (Steuerermäßigung) — a direct reduction of the tax due
Covers: cleaning, ironing, dog walking, a gardener, minor repairs
The service must be provided in your household in Germany
Payment by transfer (Überweisung) or card — cash is NOT accepted for the deduction
You need an invoice from the provider showing the split between labour and materials
The Helpling/BookATiger platforms issue a "§35a-Bescheinigung" in the client area
It's entered in the supplementary form of the return (Anlage Haushaltsnahe Aufwendungen) in the annual tax return (Steuererklärung)

content.text: If you pay the cleaner in cash outside the platform (Schwarzarbeit), you save 5–10 €/hour today, but you lose the right to the 20% tax deduction and the insurance. The fine for illegal work (Schwarzarbeit) is up to 30 000 € for the employer, and for the cleaner it means the loss of rights to sick pay, holiday and pension. A platform or an official Minijob closes these risks.

If you need a cleaner regularly and on a limited budget, you can take the route of hiring a household helper (Haushaltshilfe als Minijob): register a private individual as a Minijobber at the Minijob-Zentrale (earnings up to 603 €/month in 2026). You don't need a platform, but you take on the employer's obligations.

items: Registration via the simplified Haushaltsscheck-Verfahren procedure at minijob-zentrale.de
Flat-rate contributions of ~14,5–15% of the wage (health insurance, pension, tax, U1/U2/UV contributions) — paid by the employer
Also §35a EStG, but at a special rate for Minijob: 20% of expenses, maximum 510 €/year (not 4000 €, as for services via a company/platform)
Wage limit 603 €/month (Geringfügigkeitsgrenze 2026)
The cleaner is entitled to paid holiday, sick leave and maternity leave (Mutterschutz)
The contractual setup: an employment contract, a timesheet, regular transfers

costs.note: Net spend; after the §35a refund, effectively 160–240 €.

title: Hundeführerschein in Berlin
tldr: Berlin is governed by the Berliner Hundegesetz (BlnHundG, in force since 22 July 2016). Contrary to a widespread myth, the "dog licence" (Hundeführerschein) in Berlin is NOT mandatory for all owners — it is voluntary and is only needed to walk a dog off the leash outside designated exercise areas (Hundeauslaufgebiete). It consists of theory (Sachkundenachweis) and practice. Mandatory for everyone: registration in the central dog register (Hunderegister; within 6 months) and the dog tax (Hundesteuer); for dangerous breeds (Listenhunde) additionally a Sachkundenachweis and a temperament test (Wesenstest). Prices for the voluntary Hundeführerschein: course + theory 80–150 €, practice 70–150 €. Hundesteuer Berlin 2026: 120 €/year for the first dog. Check what's current at berlin.de.

steps.title: Berliner Hundegesetz: what the law requires

content.text: The Berliner Hundegesetz (BlnHundG) came into force on 22 July 2016 (the latest amendments — 2024). Its aim is to increase owners' responsibility and reduce the number of bites. The widespread myth that since 2022 the Hundeführerschein has been mandatory for all new owners does not match the law in force: a general obligation to take the "dog licence" in Berlin has NOT been introduced — it was only a discussed political plan. Check what's current.

items: Sachkundenachweis (theory) — voluntary for ordinary dogs; mandatory for Listenhunde / dangerous breeds
The "dog licence" (theory + practice) — voluntary; needed only to exempt the dog from the general leash obligation (Leinenpflicht)
Dogs acquired earlier (Bestandshunde; before 22 July 2016) are exempt from the general leash obligation as long as they stay with the same owner
Without a Hundeführerschein the dog must be on a leash everywhere except the Hundeauslaufgebiete
With a Hundeführerschein — off the leash is allowed, but not in parks, the forest, public transport or crowds (a leash is always mandatory there)
Kampfhunde / dangerous breeds — separate, stricter rules

content.text: These rules apply only to the state of Berlin. Other states (Niedersachsen since 2013, Schleswig-Holstein, etc.) have their own similar requirements. In most states the Hundeführerschein is not yet mandatory, but it is recommended.

The theory exam tests basic knowledge: dog behaviour, body language, feeding, veterinary care, and Berlin's laws (the leash, the muzzle requirement on public transport — Maulkorbpflicht, the protocols after bites — Beißzwischenfall).

items: Courses are offered by certified dog schools (Hundeschulen) and vets (Tierärzte)
Course length: 4–8 hours (1–2 evenings) or online
A list of approved schools is on the website of the Senate Department for Justice and Consumer Protection (Senatsverwaltung für Justiz und Verbraucherschutz)
The course is not mandatory, you can prepare on your own, but it is recommended
30–40 multiple-choice questions
Administered by licensed vets or organizations (Berliner Tierärztekammer)
Cost 30–50 €
The certificate has no expiry and transfers when you move to another state
Taken in German; a translation on site is usually not provided

content.text: For an ordinary dog the Sachkundenachweis in Berlin is voluntary — people do it to earn the right to walk the dog off the leash. For Listenhunde / dangerous breeds it is mandatory: within 8 weeks of registration the owner must present a Sachkundenachweis, a temperament test and a certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis), otherwise they risk a fine. Check the current requirements at berlin.de.
After living with the dog for about 12 months, you take the practical exam. It tests obedience, the dog's behaviour in the city, and its reaction to other dogs, people, bicycles and noise.

items: 10–20 sessions at a Hundeschule, usually 1–2 times a week
Basic commands: Sitz, Platz, Bleib, Hier, Aus, Fuß
Behaviour on and off the leash
Reaction to other dogs, children, cyclists, runners
Behaviour in a shop, a café and on public transport
Package cost 200–400 €
Administered by a certified vet or a dog behaviour expert
Length 30–60 minutes on the streets of Berlin with various situations
Exam cost 70–150 €
If you fail — a retake in 2–4 weeks
The certificate is registered with the district office (Bezirksamt)

content.text: Besides the Hundeführerschein, every dog in Berlin must be registered and is subject to the Hundesteuer dog tax.

items: Dog tax: register at the tax office or district office (Finanzamt/Bezirksamt) within 1 month; plus the central dog register — within 6 months (online ~17,50 €)
Dog tax in Berlin 2026: 120 €/year for the first dog, 180 € for each additional one
For Listenhunde in Berlin the tax is the same (120/180 €) — there is NO higher rate for "dangerous" breeds in Berlin (unlike in many other cities)
A microchip + registration with TASSO or FINDEFIX is recommended
Dog owner liability insurance (Hundehaftpflichtversicherung) is mandatory in Berlin
Leinenpflicht: on the leash everywhere except the permitted Hundeauslaufgebiete
A muzzle is mandatory: on public transport and at large events
In Berlin's forests (Grunewald, etc.) — separate rules, with seasonal restrictions in spring

content.text: Owner liability insurance for all dogs is mandatory in six states: Berlin, Hamburg, Niedersachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt, Schleswig-Holstein and Thüringen (in the rest — usually only for Listenhunde). Without a policy you risk a fine (in Berlin — up to 10 000 €). The cost is about 50–120 €/year. Take a policy with cover from 5 million € and no deductible (Selbstbeteiligung 0). Check what's current for your state.

costs.label: Theory course (Sachkundekurs)
costs.note: Not mandatory, but recommended.

costs.label: Theory exam (Sachkundenachweis)
costs.note: At a certified Tierarzt.

costs.label: Preparatory sessions (Hundeschule)
costs.note: A package of 10–20 sessions.

costs.label: Practical exam (Hundeführerschein)
costs.note: Depends on the examiner and the district.

costs.label: Total to obtain the licence
costs.note: Not counting the preparatory sessions at the school.

costs.label: Hundesteuer Berlin (1st dog, per year)
costs.note: The same tariff 120/180 € for all breeds; there is no higher rate for Listenhunde in Berlin.

costs.label: Hundehaftpflichtversicherung (per year)
costs.note: Cover 5–10 million €.

title: Drogerie: dm, Rossmann, Müller
tldr: Drugstores (Drogerie) are German shops for cosmetics, hygiene, household chemicals, dietary supplements and photo services. The leader is dm-drogerie markt (~2000 stores), then Rossmann (~2300), Müller (~600, with electronics and toys). They are not pharmacies: there are NO medicines, but a huge selection of creams, shampoos, baby food and private labels (Balea, alverde at dm, isana at Rossmann). Closed on Sundays. The dm programme: PAYBACK + 5% when paying via the app. Online pharmacy chains — Shop-Apotheke, DocMorris.

steps.title: What a Drogerie is and what it is not

content.text: Drogerie is the historical German name for a "chemist's and hygiene shop". Unlike a pharmacy (Apotheke), a drugstore does not sell medicines, but it has a huge range of cosmetics, perfumery, cleaning products, baby products, dietary supplements, sports nutrition, photo printing and, in some chains, toys and electronics.

items: Drogerie ≠ Apotheke: no paracetamol or any other medicines
You can buy: shampoos, creams, toothpastes, razors, sanitary pads, nappies, pet food
Dietary supplements (Nahrungsergänzungsmittel): magnesium, vitamin D, omega, calcium — cheaper than at the pharmacy
Cleaning products: detergents, dishwashing liquid, surface cleaners — the same range as in the supermarket
Photo printing: dm and Rossmann print photos and photo books from an online order
Müller additionally sells toys, stationery and consumer electronics

content.text: The three main players in the Drogerie market occupy different niches. Prices are roughly the same; the differences are in the private labels, the loyalty programme and the atmosphere.

items: dm-drogerie markt: ~2000 stores in DE, the leader by turnover; private labels Balea (cosmetics), alverde (natural cosmetics), dmBio (food), Babylove (baby), Sundance (sun protection)
Rossmann: ~2300 stores, second by turnover; private labels isana, alterra (natural cosmetics, Naturkosmetik), Babydream, Domol (cleaning products), Winston (supplements)
Müller: ~600 stores, a premium format, often in shopping centres; a wider range: perfumery, toys, stationery, USB gadgets; private labels Aveo, Today, a Tedi competitor
Budni: a regional player in the north (Hamburg, Schleswig-Holstein)
Schlecker — went bankrupt in 2012, no longer exists

content.text: If you're deciding "where to drop in" — dm and Rossmann are practically interchangeable. dm is a bit stronger in natural cosmetics (alverde, Balea Sensitiv). Rossmann is on average slightly cheaper for cleaning products (Domol). Müller — if you need toys or stationery in one place.

items: PAYBACK: works at dm; for every 2 € — 1 point, 200 points = 2 € off
dm app: 5% "Glücksrabatt" when paying via the app (not every day, but often)
Rossmann app: coupons, 10% on a category every day of the week
Müller-card: a classic stamp-collecting one (1% cashback)
Final markdown (Letzte Reduzierung) — stickers on items before they're written off, up to -50%
Range change (Sortimentswechsel): twice a year, big clearances of collections
Online order (Online-Bestellung) with in-store pickup — no delivery, a wider range
The cheapest prices on baby nappies and formula — at Rossmann (Babydream)

content.text: Drogerie are closed on Sundays and official holidays. At train stations (Bahnhof) and airports, branches operate on a special schedule until late evening. On weekdays the stores are mostly open Mo–Sa 8:00–20:00, and in city centres until 22:00.

If you need medicines, supplements and hygiene products delivered, there are two big legal online pharmacies — Shop-Apotheke (Dutch, but with a German warehouse) and DocMorris. They differ from a Drogerie in that they can also sell Rx medicines via E-Rezept.

items: shop-apotheke.com — the largest online pharmacy in Germany
DocMorris — the oldest, supports E-Rezept via the app
OTC prices are usually lower than at a physical Apotheke
Free delivery from 19 € (typically)
Standard delivery 2–3 days across Germany
For Rx you need an E-Rezept (the insurer's app) or to upload a scan of the prescription
amazon.de and dm.de also sell part of the Drogerie range

costs.note: The same product at the pharmacy — 8–15 €.

costs.note: Significantly cheaper than Pampers of the same size.

title: Public holidays 2026: by federal state
tldr: Germany has 9 nationwide public holidays (Neujahr — New Year, Karfreitag — Good Friday, April 3, Ostermontag April 6, Tag der Arbeit May 1, Christi Himmelfahrt May 14, Pfingstmontag May 25, Tag der Deutschen Einheit October 3, 1./2. Weihnachtstag) and up to 4 regional ones. Under §193 BGB and the Ladenschlussgesetz, these days are treated like Sundays: shops are closed, public transport runs on the Sunday schedule, with exceptions only for bakeries (Bäckerei; sales under §12 Ladenschlussgesetz / state law, usually until ~3 hours in the morning), train stations (Bahnhof), petrol stations (Tankstelle) and pharmacies (Apotheke) on emergency duty (Notdienst). Bavaria has the most holidays (13); Berlin and Hamburg the fewest (10).

content.text: These are nationwide statutory public holidays (bundesweite gesetzliche Feiertage), days off in all 16 German states. Shops are closed, schools and offices do not operate, and public transport runs on the Sunday schedule.

items: January 1 (Thu) — New Year (Neujahr)
April 3 (Fri) — Good Friday (Karfreitag)
April 6 (Mon) — Easter Monday (Ostermontag)
May 1 (Fri) — Labour Day (Tag der Arbeit)
May 14 (Thu) — Ascension Day (Christi Himmelfahrt), the 39th day after Easter
May 25 (Mon) — Whit Monday (Pfingstmontag)
October 3 (Sat) — German Unity Day (Tag der Deutschen Einheit)
December 25 (Fri) — Christmas Day (1. Weihnachtstag)
December 26 (Sat) — Boxing Day (2. Weihnachtstag, Stephanstag)

content.text: In 2026 Tag der Deutschen Einheit, 1. Weihnachtstag and 2. Weihnachtstag fall on weekends — these are "lost" holidays: Germany does not give a substitute day off (unlike the UK or Portugal). Many companies do, however, grant a "bridge" (Brückentag) — a working day between a holiday and the weekend — for example, between May 14 (Thu) and May 15 (Fri).

German states add 1 to 4 regional holidays on top of the 9 federal ones. This is critical if you work remotely for a company in another state or are planning a trip — shops may be closed in one state and open in the neighbouring one.

items: January 6 (Tue) — Epiphany (Heilige Drei Könige): Baden-Württemberg, Bayern, Sachsen-Anhalt
March 8 (Sun) — International Women's Day (Internationaler Frauentag): only Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern (falls on a Sunday in 2026)
April 4 (Sat) — Holy Saturday (Karsamstag) — not a federal public holiday
June 4 (Thu) — Corpus Christi (Fronleichnam): BW, BY, HE, NRW, RP, SL, and in Catholic districts of Sachsen and Thüringen
August 15 (Sat) — Assumption of Mary (Mariä Himmelfahrt): all of Saarland + Catholic districts of Bayern
September 20 (Sun) — World Children's Day (Weltkindertag): Thüringen (a Sunday in 2026)
October 31 (Sat) — Reformation Day (Reformationstag): BB, MV, SN, ST, TH (eastern states) + HB, HH, NI, SH (since 2018)
November 1 (Sun) — All Saints' Day (Allerheiligen): BW, BY, NRW, RP, SL (a Sunday in 2026)
November 18 (Wed) — Day of Repentance and Prayer (Buß- und Bettag): only Sachsen (the Wednesday before the last Sunday of the church year)

content.text: Bavaria leads in number of holidays: 13 in 2026 (9 federal + Epiphany + Corpus Christi + Assumption of Mary in Catholic regions + All Saints' Day). Berlin and Hamburg each have 10 in 2026 (9 + International Women's Day or Reformation Day).

steps.title: What's closed on a public holiday

content.text: Under §193 BGB and the regional Sunday and public holiday laws (Sonn- und Feiertagsgesetze), a public holiday is treated like a Sunday. A general ban on work, trade and noisy activities applies.

items: Closed: supermarkets, drugstores (Drogerie), shopping centres, banks, the post office, government offices (Behörde)
Closed: hairdressers, car repair shops, most restaurants
Open: bakeries (Bäckerei; sale of baked goods under §12 Ladenschlussgesetz / state law, usually ~3 hours in the morning), cafés, restaurants
Open: train stations (Bahnhof) and airports (Flughafen) — shops and pharmacies until 22:00
Open: petrol stations (Tankstelle) — 24/7
Pharmacies (Apotheke): emergency duty only (Notdienst), search on aponet.de
Museums and cinemas — usually open
Public transport: on the Sunday/holiday schedule (Sonn- und Feiertagsfahrplan, less frequent)

content.text: On "quiet" holidays (stille Feiertage) — Good Friday (Karfreitag), the National Day of Mourning (Volkstrauertag), the Sunday of the Dead (Totensonntag), Holy Saturday (Karsamstag, in some states) — a dancing ban (Tanzverbot) applies. Clubs are closed and noisy events are prohibited. In Bayern the dancing ban is the strictest — until 24:00 on Good Friday.
A "bridge" (Brückentag) is a working day between a holiday and the weekend. By taking a single day of leave you get 4 days off. In Germany this is a sport: "holiday optimisers" plan a year ahead.

items: Ascension Day 14.05 (Thu) + 15.05 (Fri) bridge = 4 days off
Labour Day 01.05 (Fri) is a long weekend on its own
Good Friday 03.04 + Easter Monday 06.04 = 4 days (no leave needed)
Whit Monday 25.05 (Mon) — a long weekend
October 3, 2026 (Sat) and Christmas (Weihnachten, Fri+Sat) — no bonus
Especially worthwhile in 2026: May 4–8 (1 day of leave = 5 days free)
In Bayern: around Corpus Christi June 4 (Thu) + June 5 (Fri) bridge = 4 days off

content.text: The statutory minimum leave under German law (§3 BUrlG) is 24 working days for a 6-day week, i.e. 20 for a five-day week. In practice a typical employment contract gives 25–30 days, plus federal and regional public holidays on top.

costs.label: Statutory minimum leave under BUrlG (per year)
costs.note: 20 working days for a 5-day week; a typical contract is 25–30 days.

costs.label: Premium for working on Sundays and public holidays (Sonn- und Feiertag)
costs.note: Under collective (tariff) agreements (Tarifvertrag): Sunday +50%, public holiday +100–150% on top of the base rate.

costs.label: Pharmacy emergency-duty surcharge (Notdienstgebühr Apotheke) on a public holiday
costs.note: Standard surcharge for service on emergency duty (Notdienst).

title: IKEA vs Höffner vs XXXLutz
tldr: There are several ways to furnish a flat in Germany. IKEA — self-service, affordable prices, self-pickup and assemble-it-yourself. Höffner and XXXLutz (as well as Möbel Boss, Roller, Poco) are large furniture stores with delivery and assembly, promotions and instalment plans. To save money, second-hand platforms work well: the classifieds board eBay Kleinanzeigen and the charity shop Sozialkaufhaus. This guide helps you choose the right format for your budget and timeline: fast and cheap by yourself, or more expensive but with turnkey delivery and assembly.

content.text: IKEA is the most popular choice for newcomers. Low prices, a consistent style, everything in stock on the day of purchase. The downside: you transport and assemble the furniture yourself. Delivery costs money and depends on volume; assembly can be ordered separately through partners (e.g. TaskRabbit). Every major city has a store, and small items are ordered online.

items: Low prices, consistent style, in stock on the day of purchase
Self-pickup or paid delivery by volume
Assemble it yourself or pay extra for a service
Convenient for a first, quick furnishing

content.text: Höffner and XXXLutz are large furniture houses with a wide range, frequent promotions and delivery and assembly services. The cheaper segment is Möbel Boss, Roller and Poco: there you can buy basic furniture inexpensively, often with delivery. These stores often offer instalment plans (Finanzierung) and free delivery on purchases above a certain amount.

items: Höffner / XXXLutz — wide selection, delivery and assembly
Möbel Boss / Roller / Poco — budget segment
Frequent promotions (Rabatt) and seasonal sales
Delivery and assembly for an extra fee, sometimes free above a threshold
Instalment plans (Finanzierung) for large purchases

content.text: Before taking an instalment plan, check the effective annual interest rate (effektiver Jahreszins): "0%" is only available under certain conditions. Factor in the cost of delivery and assembly — at large stores it can add a fair amount to the bill.

The cheapest route is the second-hand market. On the classifieds board eBay Kleinanzeigen and in Facebook groups people often give furniture away for free (zu verschenken), especially when moving. Charity shops (Sozialkaufhaus) sell used furniture very cheaply. Pick up large items yourself — renting a van (Transporter) for a couple of hours costs less than new delivery.

items: Classifieds board eBay Kleinanzeigen — second-hand and free (zu verschenken)
Charity shop (Sozialkaufhaus) — inexpensive used furniture
Check the condition and dimensions before buying
Rent a Transporter to pick up large items yourself

title: Aldi, Lidl, Rewe, Edeka
tldr: Grocery chains in Germany split into discounters and supermarkets. Aldi and Lidl are discounters: a limited range, low prices, a focus on own brands. Rewe and Edeka are full-service supermarkets: more brands, fresh-food sections, higher prices. The picture is rounded out by Penny, Netto and Kaufland (cheaper), while the Bio chains Alnatura and Denn's are organic. Important things to know: a deposit on containers (Pfand; 0,08–0,25 €), card payment accepted almost everywhere, and shops closed on Sundays. This guide helps you decide where to shop on a budget.

content.text: Aldi (Aldi Süd in the south, Aldi Nord in the north) and Lidl are discounters with the lowest prices. The range is narrower than in a supermarket, with a focus on own brands (Eigenmarken), but the quality of the basics is good. Penny and Netto work similarly. This is where it pays to buy the staples of your diet: grains, dairy, vegetables, frozen food.

items: Aldi and Lidl — the lowest prices, a narrow range
Focus on own brands (Eigenmarken)
Penny and Netto — also discounters
Good value for basic groceries and frozen food

content.text: Rewe and Edeka are classic supermarkets with a wide choice of brands, good fresh-food sections, a bakery and often international products. Prices are higher than at the discounters. Kaufland is a hypermarket with a large range and often competitive prices. For organic products there are the specialist chains Alnatura and Denn's Biomarkt.

items: Rewe / Edeka — wide choice of brands and fresh food
Kaufland — hypermarket, large range
Alnatura / Denn's — organic (Bio)
Prices higher than discounters, but more choice
Rewe and others offer online delivery in major cities

content.text: Most bottles and cans carry a deposit on the container (Pfand): single-use PET bottles and cans — 0,25 €, many glass ones — 0,08–0,15 €. You return empty containers at a reverse-vending machine (Pfandautomat) in the shop and get a voucher for a discount. Payment by German debit card (Girocard) and credit cards is accepted almost everywhere; cash is also in use. Important: on Sundays and public holidays grocery shops are closed — stock up in advance (shops at train stations and petrol stations help out).

items: Deposit on containers (Pfand): cans/PET — 0,25 €, reusable glass — 0,08–0,15 €
Return containers at the reverse-vending machine (Pfandautomat), get a discount voucher
Cards accepted almost everywhere; keep a little cash on hand
Sundays and public holidays — shops closed, stock up in advance
Open on Sundays: shops at train stations (Bahnhof) and petrol stations (Tankstelle)

content.text: Don't throw deposit containers in the regular bin — that's losing money. The voucher from the reverse-vending machine has to be handed to the cashier or used when paying for your shopping, otherwise the discount is lost.

costs.label: Deposit on containers (Pfand) for single-use containers
costs.note: PET bottles and cans; refunded on return.

costs.note: Reusable bottles (Mehrwegflaschen); refunded on return.

title: House rules (Hausordnung)
tldr: The house rules (Hausordnung) are the internal rules of conduct that are often part of the tenancy agreement and binding. They govern quiet hours (Ruhezeiten — usually 22:00–06:00 and often all of Sunday), use of the stairwell and basement, taking out and sorting rubbish, the tenants' cleaning rota (Kehrwoche), bicycle storage, balcony grilling and noise. A breach can lead to a formal warning (Abmahnung) from the landlord, and a systematic one to termination. Knowing the house rules helps you avoid conflict with the neighbours and penalty letters.

content.text: The main rule in German buildings is quiet during certain hours. Night-time quiet (Nachtruhe) is usually 22:00 to 06:00, often with an added midday quiet (Mittagsruhe, e.g. 13:00–15:00) and completely quiet Sundays and public holidays. During these times you may not play loud music, drill, run a noisy wash cycle or play instruments above a reasonable level. Check the exact hours in your house rules (Hausordnung) — they can vary.

items: Night-time quiet usually 22:00–06:00
Often a midday quiet (e.g. 13:00–15:00)
Sundays and public holidays — a day of quiet, no noisy work
Drilling, loud music, washing machine — only during permitted hours
The exact hours are in your house rules (Hausordnung)

content.text: Total silence is not required by law — ordinary domestic noise is permitted. But if quiet hours (Ruhezeiten) are breached, a neighbour may complain and the landlord may issue a formal warning (Abmahnung). Repeated serious breaches can become grounds for terminating the contract.

The house rules govern the use of common areas: the stairwell, the basement (Keller), the courtyard, the bicycle parking. A Kehrwoche often applies — a rota of tenants for cleaning the stairwell and pavement, especially in southern Germany. Rubbish must be sorted and put out according to the collection schedule. Blocking escape routes (e.g. leaving prams and shoes in the stairwell) is usually prohibited under fire regulations.

items: Follow the cleaning rota (Kehrwoche) for the stairwell/pavement
Sort rubbish and put it out according to the collection schedule
Don't block the stairwell or escape routes
Bicycles and prams — only in the designated places
Use the basement and courtyard according to the house rules

steps.title: What is binding and what isn't

content.text: The house rules are binding if they are part of the tenancy agreement or the landlord is entitled to set rules of use. But they cannot override your statutory rights: for example, they cannot completely ban visitors, showering at night or small pets. Rules that contradict the law or are excessively restrictive are invalid. If you're unsure whether a requirement is lawful, check with a tenants' association (Mieterverein).

items: Binding if included in the tenancy agreement
Cannot override the tenant's statutory rights
Cannot ban visitors, night-time showers or small pets
Excessive and unlawful clauses are invalid
In doubt — check with a tenants' association (Mieterverein)

costs.label: Complying with the house rules (Hausordnung)
costs.note: Free; a breach can cost you a warning or a dispute.

costs.label: Possible penalty/consequences
costs.note: A formal warning (Abmahnung) from the landlord; on repeat breaches — risk of termination of the contract.

title: Launderettes: Waschsalon
tldr: If your flat has no washing machine of its own, self-service launderettes (Waschsalon, or Waschcenter) come to the rescue in Germany. You pay for a wash cycle (~3–5 €) and separately for drying (~1–4 €), bring your own detergent or buy it on site. Payment is by coins, card or app. Many launderettes are open late, but remember quiet hours and Sundays in residential buildings with a shared laundry room (Waschküche). This guide explains how to use the machines, how much it costs and how not to ruin your clothes.

steps.title: Where to do laundry without your own machine

content.text: There are two options. The first — a public self-service launderette (Waschsalon/Waschcenter): easy to find on a map (search "Waschsalon" nearby). The second — a shared building laundry room (Waschküche) in your basement, where the machines are paid for with tokens or a card and used on a schedule or in turns. Student halls of residence usually have their own machines paid for with a campus card or an app.

items: Self-service launderette (Waschsalon / Waschcenter) — find one nearby on a map
Shared building laundry room (Waschküche) in the basement — machines by token/card
In halls of residence — payment by campus card or app
Check the opening hours and whether you need coins

steps.title: How to use it and how much it costs

content.text: Load the laundry, choose the programme and temperature, add detergent (your own or from a vending machine). Payment is by coins, by notes via a change machine, by card or via an app. A wash cycle is usually 3–5 €, drying in a tumble dryer (Trockner) is separate, ~1–4 € for the time. Don't overload the drum and sort the laundry by colour and temperature.

items: Load the laundry without overloading the drum
Choose the programme and temperature for the fabric
Add your own detergent or buy it from a vending machine
Pay by coins, card or app
Drying (Trockner) is paid for separately

content.text: Check the maximum temperature on clothing labels: a hot wash and drying can shrink and ruin items. Don't leave laundry unattended for long — in launderettes other users may take it out.

If you use a shared building laundry room (Waschküche), observe quiet hours (Ruhezeiten): doing laundry at night or on a Sunday may breach the house rules (Hausordnung). There is often a booking schedule on a board or in a list. After use, wipe down the machine and clean the dryer filter. Commercial self-service launderettes (Waschsalon) run on their own schedule, many until late evening.

items: In a shared building laundry room (Waschküche) observe quiet hours (Ruhezeiten) and the schedule
Don't do laundry late at night or on Sundays in a residential building
Clean the dryer filter and wipe down the machine after yourself
A commercial self-service launderette (Waschsalon) — on its own hours, often until late

costs.label: One wash cycle
costs.note: Depends on the launderette, programme and temperature.

costs.label: Drying (Trockner)
costs.note: Usually paid for by the time, separately.

costs.label: Detergent from the vending machine
costs.note: If you don't bring your own.

title: Waste separation (Mülltrennung): 5 bins
tldr: Sorting waste in Germany is mandatory and tightly organised. At its core there are five streams: the yellow bin/bag (Gelbe Tonne/Sack) for packaging with plastic and metal, the blue bin for paper (Papier) and cardboard, the brown/green bin for organic waste (Bio) — food and garden waste, the grey/black bin for the rest (Restmüll), plus glass into glass containers (Altglas) by colour. Separately — deposit containers (Pfand; returned in the shop) and hazardous waste. Incorrect sorting can lead to warnings and extra collection charges. This guide explains what goes in which bin.

content.text: Remember the five basic categories. The yellow bin or yellow bag (Gelbe Tonne/Gelber Sack) — for packaging: plastic, metal, composite cartons (Tetra Pak). The blue bin for paper (Papier/Blaue Tonne) — paper and cardboard. The brown or green bin for organic waste (Biotonne) — food leftovers, peelings, garden waste. The grey/black bin for the rest (Restmülltonne) — everything that can't be sorted. Glass is thrown into public glass containers (Altglas), separated by colour.

items: Yellow bin/bag (Gelbe Tonne/Sack) — packaging: plastic, metal, Tetra Pak
Blue bin for paper (Blaue Tonne, Papier) — paper and cardboard
Bin for organic waste (Biotonne) — food and garden waste
Bin for the rest (Restmülltonne) — everything else that can't be sorted
Glass containers (Altglas) — glass by colour (white/green/brown)

content.text: Glass is sorted by colour into street glass containers (Altglas): clear (Weißglas), green (Grünglas) and brown (Braunglas); blue and other colours usually go in with the green. Bottles and cans with a deposit on the container (Pfand) are not thrown away — you return them in the shop and get the money back. Hazardous waste (batteries, paints, medicines, electronics) is disposed of separately: batteries — in shops, electronics and chemicals — at a recycling centre (Wertstoffhof/Recyclinghof).

items: Glass — by colour: clear (Weißglas), green (Grünglas), brown (Braunglas)
Don't throw away deposit containers (Pfand) — return them in the shop
Batteries — at collection points in shops
Electronics, paints, medicines — at a recycling centre (Wertstoffhof)
Bulky waste — request a bulky-waste collection (Sperrmüll, often free)

content.text: You cannot put glass into the glass containers (Altglas) during quiet hours and on Sundays because of the noise — this breaches the local quiet rules. Dispose of glass during the day on weekdays.

The exact rules, bin colours and collection schedule are set by your city's local waste management service (Abfallwirtschaft/Entsorgungsbetrieb) — their website has a waste-collection calendar (Abfallkalender). The details differ between states (in some places paper is brown, organic green). For poor sorting, the collection service may refuse to empty the bin, leave a warning or charge an extra fee. Compliance is part of the obligations under the building's house rules (Hausordnung).

items: Check the waste-collection calendar (Abfallkalender) on your city's website
Colours and the collection schedule depend on the state and district
Poor sorting — refusal of collection, a warning or an extra charge
Sorting is often written into the house rules (Hausordnung)
Bulky/construction waste — separately at a recycling centre (Wertstoffhof)

costs.label: Basic sorting
costs.note: Sorting itself is free; collection is included in the utility charges (Nebenkosten).

costs.label: Bulky-waste collection (Sperrmüll)
costs.note: Free on request in many cities; in some — a small fee.

costs.label: Surcharge for incorrect sorting
costs.note: Possible if bins are contaminated; charged by the municipal service.

title: AsylbLG: asylum-seeker benefits
tldr: The Asylum Seeker Benefits Act (Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz, AsylbLG) is a benefits system separate from SGB II for asylum seekers, people with a deportation deferral (Duldung; Geduldete) and holders of a permission to stay pending the asylum decision (Aufenthaltsgestattung). The rates are lower than the basic benefit (Bürgergeld; in 2026 — 455€/month for a single person: 253€ necessary needs, notwendiger Bedarf + 202€ personal needs, persönlicher Bedarf, versus 563€ of the basic benefit), with part paid in kind. After 36 months of residence (§2 AsylbLG, analogue payments, Analogleistung) the rates are brought up to the level of the basic benefit.

content.text: The Asylum Seeker Benefits Act (Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz, AsylbLG) has been in force since 1993 — a special benefits law for people without a recognised protection status. The rates are deliberately lower than the general SGB II (basic benefit, Bürgergeld). The Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) already found the previous rates to violate the constitutionally guaranteed subsistence minimum (Existenzminimum) in 2012 (1 BvL 10/10), after which they were raised. In 2026 the court again reviewed the level of the rates (decision of 15.04.2026, 1 BvL 5/21): some of the previous amounts were said to have been calculated on outdated data, so the legal assessment of the AsylbLG remains contested.

items: Applies to: asylum seekers (Asylbewerber; with a permission to stay pending the asylum decision, Aufenthaltsgestattung), people with a deportation deferral (Geduldete; §60a AufenthG), some people obliged to leave the country (Ausreisepflichtige)

Does not apply to: recognised beneficiaries of asylum (Asylberechtigte), refugees under the Geneva Convention (GFK-Flüchtlinge), beneficiaries of subsidiary protection (subsidiär Schutzberechtigte) — they receive the basic benefit (Bürgergeld; SGB II) or social assistance (Sozialhilfe; SGB XII)
Administered by the social welfare office (Sozialamt) at the place of mandatory residence (Wohnsitzauflage), not by the job centre (Jobcenter)
Part of the benefits in kind (Sachleistungen): food, hygiene, clothing — especially in the initial reception centre (Erstaufnahmeeinrichtung)

content.text: The rates are split into necessary needs (notwendiger Bedarf; food, housing, medical care — §3a Abs.1) and necessary personal needs (notwendiger persönlicher Bedarf; pocket money — §3a Abs.2). The amounts are recalculated annually and published in the Federal Law Gazette (Bundesgesetzblatt). The figures for 2026 (official announcement, Bekanntmachung of 27.10.2025, BGBl. 2025 I Nr. 251, in force from 1.1.2026):

items: Single adult (needs level, Bedarfsstufe, 1): 253€ necessary needs + 202€ personal needs = 455€/month
In the initial reception centre (Erstaufnahmeeinrichtung): the larger part is in kind (Sachleistungen); only the pocket money (Taschengeld; personal needs) is paid out — about 202€/month
Partners in a shared household (needs level 2): 227€ + 182€ = 409€/person
After 36 months of residence — §2 AsylbLG: the rates are brought up to the basic benefit (Bürgergeld; in 2026 — 563€ for a single person)

content.text: Important: since February 2024 the waiting period for analogue payments (Analogleistung) has been extended from 18 to 36 months (Act on Improving Returns, Gesetz zur Verbesserung der Rückführung, in force from 27.02.2024). This means 3 years of reduced AsylbLG rates instead of the previous year and a half.

The application is submitted to the social welfare office (Sozialamt) at the assigned place of residence (Wohnsitzauflage). In the initial reception centre (Erstaufnahmeeinrichtung) — automatically through the reception centre administration.

items: Permission to stay pending the asylum decision (Aufenthaltsgestattung) or deportation deferral (Duldung)
BAMF certificate (BAMF-Bescheinigung) confirming the asylum application (Asylantrag)
Proof of residence (allocation decision, Zuweisungsbescheid)
Bank details (if paid to an account, not possible everywhere)

items.title: 2. Submission to the social welfare office (Sozialamt)

content.text: The form "application for benefits under the AsylbLG" (Antrag auf Leistungen nach AsylbLG). Most states have an online form; otherwise — an in-person visit. Caritas, Diakonie and Pro Asyl provide help.
A decision within 2-4 weeks. Payment monthly via a payment card (Bezahlkarte; since 2024 in most states — a card instead of cash, with a cash-withdrawal limit of 50€/month).

steps.title: Medical care and work under AsylbLG

content.text: Under §4 AsylbLG medical care is limited: only acute illnesses (akute Erkrankungen) and pain conditions (Schmerzzustände), pregnancy, vaccinations. Full statutory health insurance (GKV) comes after 36 months (§2 AsylbLG, analogue payments) or on obtaining a status. Some states (Berlin, Brandenburg, NRW, Bremen, Hamburg, Schleswig-Holstein, Thüringen) have introduced the electronic health card (elektronische Gesundheitskarte, eGK) for recipients of AsylbLG benefits.

Work: banned for the first 3 months (§61 AsylG). After that — you need an employment permit (Beschäftigungserlaubnis) from the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde; often with the consent of the Federal Employment Agency, Bundesagentur für Arbeit). Income reduces the benefit under §7 AsylbLG (income offset, Anrechnung).

The payment card (Bezahlkarte; since 2024) is very restrictive: no transfers abroad, no online purchases in non-listed shops. This is lawful — the Federal Constitutional Court (BVerfG) has not yet ruled, but the social courts (Sozialgerichte) have already lifted restrictions in individual cases.

Restriction of the benefit entitlement (Anspruchseinschränkung) under §1a AsylbLG: if you refuse to cooperate (Mitwirkung; e.g. you have not applied for a passport, Pass) the benefit is cut to the bare minimum of "bed, bread, soap" (Bett+Brot+Seife). The law is contested but applied.

If asylum is refused (Ablehnung) and a deportation deferral (Duldung) follows, benefits are often recalculated — turn to a lawyer for migration law (Anwalt für Migrationsrecht). Help covering court costs (Verfahrenshilfe; Prozesskostenhilfe, PKH) for the social court (Sozialgericht) is free on a low income.

costs.label: Cost of submitting the application (Antrag)
costs.note: Free through the social welfare office (Sozialamt)

costs.label: Consultation with a lawyer for migration law (Anwalt für Migrationsrecht)
costs.note: With a legal advice voucher (Beratungshilfeschein; under the Beratungshilfegesetz) — 15€ or free

costs.label: Lawsuit (Klage) at the social court (Sozialgericht)
costs.note: Proceedings at the social court (Sozialgerichtsverfahren) are not subject to court fees (§183 SGG)

title: Bildungspaket: help for school
tldr: The "education and participation" package (Bildung und Teilhabe, BuT; §28 SGB II / §34 SGB XII / §6b BKGG) is a package of support for school and leisure for children from families on the basic benefit (Bürgergeld), social assistance (Sozialhilfe), housing benefit (Wohngeld), the child supplement (Kinderzuschlag) or AsylbLG benefits. In 2026: 195€/school year for school supplies (from Aug.+Feb.), free lunches, payment for clubs of 15€/month, school trips, a tutor (learning support, Lernförderung).

content.text: The "education and participation" package (Bildung und Teilhabe, BuT), colloquially the education package (Bildungspaket), came about in 2011 after a decision of the Federal Constitutional Court (BVerfG; 1 BvL 1/09): the standard benefit rate (Regelsatz) does not cover children's specific costs for school, sport and culture. These are separate payments on top of the basic benefit (Bürgergeld) and housing benefit (Wohngeld).

items: School supplies (Schulbedarf): about 130€ on 1 August + 65€ on 1 February = ~195€/year (the rate is indexed annually; check the current amount)
Lunches (Mittagessen): free lunches at school or daycare (Kita)
Learning support (Lernförderung): payment for a tutor
Class trips (Klassenfahrten) and excursions (Ausflüge): the full cost of school trips
Participation in social and cultural life (Teilhabe; leisure): 15€/month for clubs — sport, music, culture
School transport (Schülerbeförderung): travel to school if the distance is more than 2–3 km

content.text: Entitlement to BuT does not depend only on the basic benefit (Bürgergeld) — there are several entry channels:
Families with children up to 25 (if in education) are automatically entitled; the application goes through the job centre (Jobcenter).
Pensioners and people unable to work (Erwerbsunfähige) with children (rare, but it happens) — through the social welfare office (Sozialamt).

Working people on a low income who receive housing benefit (Wohngeld) and/or the child supplement (Kinderzuschlag; §6a BKGG) — the application goes through the family benefits office (Familienkasse) or the housing benefit office (Wohngeldstelle).
Asylum seekers are also entitled (§3 Abs.4 AsylbLG refers to §28 SGB II) — through the social welfare office (Sozialamt).

The application is submitted separately from the basic benefit (Bürgergeld) at the office that pays the main benefit. School supplies (Schulbedarf) are usually paid out automatically with the basic benefit; everything else — on application (Antrag).
On the website of the job centre (Jobcenter) or the city (Stadt) — "Antrag Bildung und Teilhabe". Often a separate form for each child.

items: School certificate (Schulbescheinigung)
Confirmation of lunches at school/daycare (Bestätigung Mittagessen Schule/Kita)
Contract with a sports club/music school (Vertrag Verein/Musikschule; for the leisure participation, Teilhabe, 15€)
Cost estimate for the class trip (Kostenübersicht für Klassenfahrt)

content.text: A decision in 2-6 weeks. Many states use a BuT card (BuT-Karte; an electronic card) — Hamburg, Berlin, NRW; otherwise direct payment (Direktzahlung) to the service provider.

items: Learning support (Lernförderung) is available not only when there's a risk of "being held back a year" — since 2019 a general need is enough (Drittes Gesetz zur Änderung des SGB II)
The leisure participation (Teilhabe) 15€ can be saved up over six months and spent all at once — for example, on a summer camp
Class trips (Klassenfahrten) — the full cost, including multi-day trips abroad
School lunches are completely free (the 1€ parental contribution is gone since 2019)
It also works for daycare (Kita): catering (Verpflegung), excursions (Ausflüge), leisure participation (Teilhabe)

content.text: Tip: if a child has just joined a club — apply (Antrag) for the leisure participation (Teilhabe) straight away; the application is usually valid for 12 months.

The school-supplies rate (Schulbedarf; about 195€/year) is often confused with the old amount of 116€ — since 2021 it has been indexed annually. For 2026, check the current amount in §34 SGB XII / §28 Abs.3 SGB II.
If a parent works (a recipient of a low-income top-up, Aufstocker — basic benefit, Bürgergeld, + salary), the entitlement to BuT is not lost. Many job centres (Jobcenter) forget this — insist on it.

Housing benefit recipients (Wohngeld-Empfänger) often don't know about BuT. The application goes to the housing benefit office (Wohngeldstelle) or the family benefits office (Familienkasse) — not the job centre (Jobcenter)! This is the biggest mistake working families make.

costs.label: Submitting the BuT application (Antrag)
costs.note: Free at all offices

costs.label: School-supplies rate (Schulbedarf) 2026
costs.note: 130€ August + 65€ February (§28 Abs.3 SGB II, after indexation, Indexierung, 2026)

costs.label: Leisure participation (Teilhabe; sports club/music)
costs.note: Per month per child up to 18 years

costs.label: Lunches at school/daycare (Mittagessen Schule/Kita)
costs.note: Completely free (full cost covered, Übernahme der vollen Kosten)

title: Bürgergeld for foreigners: the rules
tldr: The basic benefit (Bürgergeld; SGB II) is available to foreigners with a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) and permitted gainful activity (erlaubte Erwerbstätigkeit), but §7 Abs.1 SGB II excludes the first 3 months of residence (waiting period, Karenzfrist) and those who came only to look for work. EU citizens — special rules (§7 Abs.1 S.2 Nr.2). Receiving the basic benefit can affect the extension of a residence permit (§5 Abs.1 Nr.1 AufenthG) — but not in every case.

content.text: The basic rule (§7 Abs.1 SGB II): the recipient must be able to work (erwerbsfähig; 15-67 years, fit for work) and in need (hilfebedürftig; without sufficient means). Foreigners additionally — habitual residence (gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt) in Germany + the right to work.

items: Recognised beneficiaries of asylum (Asylberechtigte) / refugees under the Geneva Convention (GFK-Flüchtlinge) / beneficiaries of subsidiary protection (subsidiär Schutzberechtigte) — yes
Permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) or EU long-term residence (Daueraufenthalt-EU) — yes
Temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) with permission to work — yes
EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) — yes
§24 AufenthG (Ukrainians) — yes (treated as Bürgergeld since 1.6.2022)
Student under §16b — NO (excluded under §7 Abs.5 SGB II)
Job-seeking (Arbeitsuche) — NO (§7 Abs.1 S.2 Nr.2)
First 3 months of residence without a status — NO (waiting-period rule, Karenzregel)

content.text: EU freedom of movement does not equal an automatic right to social benefits (Sozialleistungen). The Court of Justice of the EU (EuGH; the Dano judgment, Dano-Urteil C-333/13, Alimanovic C-67/14) allowed Germany to exclude EU citizens without a right of residence.

If there is an employment relationship (Arbeitsverhältnis) of at least 1 hour/week with a wage — the status of an employee (Arbeitnehmer), with entitlement to the basic benefit (Bürgergeld) as a low-income top-up recipient (Aufstocker).
Only after 1 year of work and involuntary loss — the employee status (Arbeitnehmerstatus) is retained for a further 6 months, after which it is lost. Without work — no basic benefit (Bürgergeld).
After 5 years of legal residence (right of permanent residence, Daueraufenthaltsrecht; §4a FreizügG/EU) there is full entitlement to the basic benefit (Bürgergeld).

This is the most important and most misunderstood part. §5 Abs.1 Nr.1 AufenthG requires that your livelihood is secured (Sicherung des Lebensunterhalts) — receiving the basic benefit (Bürgergeld) can become an obstacle to an extension.

items: No obstacle: humanitarian residence permits (humanitäre Titel; §§22-26 AufenthG, including refugees, Flüchtlinge, §24 Ukraine), family reunification (Familiennachzug) with a German citizen (§28 AufenthG), permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis; already issued)
An obstacle: extension of a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) for work (§§18a-18c), student residence permit (§16b), the self-employed (Selbständige; §21)

Contested: family reunification (Familiennachzug) with a foreigner (§30) — a secured livelihood (Lebensunterhalt) is required; the Blue Card (Blaue Karte; §18b) — with substantial side earnings usually ok
The permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §9 — requires 5 years without social benefits (Sozialleistungen; exception for refugees, Flüchtlinge, §26 Abs.3)

content.text: Advice from the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde): before applying for the basic benefit (Bürgergeld), consult a migration advice service (Migrationsberatung; MBE, JMD) — for some residence permits it is better to take housing benefit (Wohngeld) + the child supplement (Kinderzuschlag), which do not count as a social benefit (Sozialleistung) within the meaning of §5 AufenthG.
At your place of registration (Anmeldung). Book an appointment via arbeitsagentur.de or by phone on 0800 4 5555 00.

items: HA — main application (Hauptantrag; the main form)
Annex WEP (Anlage WEP) — person able to work (Erwerbsfähige Person)
Annex KdU (Anlage KdU) — housing costs
Annex VM (Anlage VM) — assets (Vermögen)
Annex EK (Anlage EK) — income
Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) + work permit (Arbeitserlaubnis)
Tenancy agreement (Mietvertrag), heating bill (Heizkostenabrechnung)
Bank statements (Kontoauszüge) for 3 months

content.text: A decision usually within 4 weeks; in urgent cases — an advance (Vorschuss). Payment monthly at the start of the month to your account (Konto).

Ukrainians (§24 AufenthG): since 1.6.2022 treated as on the basic benefit (Bürgergeld). Since 2024 there have been draft laws discussed about returning newly arriving people to the AsylbLG system — keep an eye on the changes (BMI / BMAS).

Family reunification (Familiennachzug): if a spouse came to join a working partner and that partner lost their job — the basic benefit (Bürgergeld) for the family may mean the spouse's residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) cannot be extended. The solution — housing benefit (Wohngeld) + the child supplement (Kinderzuschlag) or a quick return to work.

The waiting period (Karenzzeit; the first year of the basic benefit, Bürgergeld) has been sharply cut by reform since 2025: rent costs (Mietkosten) are checked immediately, the appropriateness requirement (Angemessenheit) is strict. The figures depend on the city (the official rent index, Mietspiegel).

The protected-assets threshold (Vermögensfreigrenze; protected assets, Schonvermögen): in the first year of receipt (waiting period, Karenzzeit) — 40.000€ for the head of the household of need (Bedarfsgemeinschaft) plus 15.000€ for each further member, thereafter 15.000€ per person. From 1 July 2026, under the reform "new basic security" (neue Grundsicherung; Gesetz zur Umgestaltung der Grundsicherung für Arbeitsuchende), the rules on the waiting period (Karenzzeit) and protected assets (Schonvermögen) change — check the version of the SGB II in force.

costs.note: Free at the job centre (Jobcenter)

title: Bürgergeld: rates 2026
tldr: The basic benefit (Bürgergeld; SGB II) replaced Hartz IV on 1.1.2023. The standard need (Regelbedarf) in 2026 is 563€/month for a single person (level, Stufe, 1); the rate was not raised compared with 2025 (a zero round, Nullrunde). Children 0–5 years: 357€; 6–13: 390€; 14–17: 471€. On top — housing costs (KdU, Kosten der Unterkunft): rent (Miete) and heating costs (Heizkosten) within the limits of appropriateness (Angemessenheit). From 1 July 2026 the basic benefit is renamed "new basic security" (neue Grundsicherung), but the standard rate (Regelsatz) itself stays at 563€.

content.text: The basic benefit (Bürgergeld) is the social minimum provision for people able to work (erwerbsfähige Personen; 15-67 years) and their family members. Introduced by the reform of 1.1.2023 (the basic-benefit act, Bürgergeld-Gesetz, of 16.12.2022) in place of Hartz IV / Arbeitslosengeld II. Since 2025 some of the reform's easings have been rolled back (the growth initiative, Wachstumsinitiative): tougher sanctions, a lower protected-assets threshold (Vermögensfreigrenze).

items: Funded by the state through the job centre (Jobcenter; jointly the Federal Employment Agency, BA, + the municipality, Kommune)
Consists of: standard need (Regelbedarf) + additional needs (Mehrbedarfe) + housing costs (KdU) + social insurance (Sozialversicherung)
Income is offset (income offset, Anrechnung) — there are tax-free amounts (Freibeträge) for those who work
Protected-assets threshold (Vermögensfreigrenze): 15.000€ per person (40.000€ in the first year of the waiting period, Karenzzeit)

content.text: The decision on the rates for 2026 (the regulation indexing the standard-need levels, Regelbedarfsstufen-Fortschreibungsverordnung, October 2025): the rates are frozen at the 2025 level — the so-called zero round (Nullrunde). The formal index calculation (§28a SGB XII) would have given around 557€, i.e. less than the previous rate, and it cannot be lowered (protection of the level reached, Besitzschutz), so for a single person it remained 563€.

items: Level (Stufe) 1 — single people/single parents (Alleinstehende/Alleinerziehende): 563€/month
Level (Stufe) 2 — partners in a household of need (Partner in Bedarfsgemeinschaft; each): 506€/month
Level (Stufe) 3 — adults in a shared household without partnership (e.g. a 25-year-old living with parents): 451€/month
Level (Stufe) 4 — teenagers 14-17 years: 471€/month
Level (Stufe) 5 — children 6-13 years: 390€/month
Level (Stufe) 6 — children 0-5 years: 357€/month

content.text: Important: 2026 is a freeze (protection of the level reached, Besitzschutz, under §28a Abs.5 SGB XII: the calculated amount is 557€, but the rate cannot be lowered, so it stayed at 563€). In addition, from 1 July 2026 the basic benefit (Bürgergeld) is renamed "new basic security" (neue Grundsicherung; Gesetz zur Umgestaltung der Grundsicherung für Arbeitsuchende): the standard rate (Regelsatz) itself stays at 563€, but the rules on the waiting period (Karenzzeit), the treatment of assets (Vermögen) and sanctions change — check the version of the SGB II in force.

On top of the standard rate (Regelsatz), the job centre (Jobcenter) pays the housing costs (Kosten der Unterkunft, KdU; §22 SGB II) — cold rent (Kaltmiete) + utility costs (Nebenkosten) + heating costs (Heizkosten) — in an "appropriate" (angemessener) amount. What counts as appropriate (angemessen) is determined by each municipality (Kommune; a housing-cost directive, KdU-Richtlinie, or the official rent index, Mietspiegel).
Previously: in the first year any rent (Miete) is paid. Since 2025 this has been abolished for new recipients in most cases — an appropriateness check (Angemessenheit) straight away.

items.title: After the waiting period (Karenzzeit) — cost-reduction procedure (Kostensenkungsverfahren)

content.text: If the flat is "inappropriate" (unangemessen) — the job centre (Jobcenter) gives 6 months to reduce the costs: moving, subletting a room, negotiating with the landlord (Vermieter). After that — they pay only the appropriateness limit (Angemessenheits-Grenze).

items: Berlin (1 person): ~520€ cold rent (Kaltmiete) + heating costs (Heizkosten)
München: up to 880€ (a special market)
Köln: ~480€
Small towns: ~340-420€
Single parents (Alleinerziehende; §21 Abs.3 SGB II): +36% (1 child under 7) or +12% for each child
Pregnancy (Schwangerschaft) from the 13th week: +17% of the standard rate (Regelsatz)
Disability (Behinderung) with integration assistance (Eingliederungshilfe): +35%
Costly diet (Kostspielige Ernährung; on medical grounds, proven by a certificate): individual
Hot water (Warmwasser; if it does not run through the heating, Heizung): 2,3% of the standard rate (Regelsatz; ~13€)
School textbooks/education (Schulbücher/Bildung) — through the education package (Bildungspaket) §28 SGB II

content.text: Since 28.3.2024 (the Bundestag decision, Bundestag-Beschluss, "Totalverweigerer-Sanktionen") sanctions have been tightened — the Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) in 2019 (1 BvL 7/16) allowed reductions of up to 30%, with the new regulation up to 100% for a total refusal to cooperate (Totalverweigerung).

items: Duty to apply for jobs (Bewerbungspflicht) — job search, reports to the job centre (Jobcenter)
Cooperation plan (Kooperationsplan; §15 SGB II) — replaced the integration agreement (Eingliederungsvereinbarung)
Duty to appear (Meldepflicht): attendance when summoned by the job centre (Jobcenter)
Sanctions of 10% / 20% / 30% for breaches (§31a)
On a total refusal to cooperate (Totalverweigerung) — up to 100% of the standard rate (Regelsatz) for 2 months (housing costs, KdU, remain)

content.text: Presumed household of need (Vermutete Bedarfsgemeinschaft): if you live with a partner for >12 months or with a shared child — the job centre (Jobcenter) treats you as a household of need (Bedarfsgemeinschaft; §7 Abs.3 SGB II). The partner's income is taken into account.
Duties to cooperate (Mitwirkungspflichten; §§60-67 SGB I): if you don't provide documents — they can refuse entirely. Keep all receipts confirming the submission of documents (Eingangsbestätigungen).
An objection (Widerspruch) is filed within 1 month. A lawsuit (Klage) at the social court (Sozialgericht) is free (§183 SGG). Legal aid for court costs (Prozesskostenhilfe) is available.

Undeclared work (Schwarzarbeit) + the basic benefit (Bürgergeld) = social benefit fraud (Sozialleistungsbetrug; §263 StGB) — up to 5 years in prison. Declare any side job; there are tax-free amounts (Freibeträge).
For foreigners, the basic benefit (Bürgergeld) can affect the extension of a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — see the separate guide "Bürgergeld for foreigners: the rules".

costs.note: Free through the job centre (Jobcenter; online or in person)

costs.note: Per month, frozen at the 2025 level.

costs.note: Free

title: Divorce: Trennungsjahr and the Familiengericht
tldr: Divorce in Germany is only possible through the family court (Familiengericht, §1564 BGB) after a mandatory year of living apart (Trennungsjahr, §1565 BGB). At least one lawyer (Anwalt) is required (mandatory legal representation, Anwaltszwang, §114 FamFG). The cost depends on the value of the proceedings (Verfahrenswert: 3 × the family's net income + assets, Vermögen): usually 1.500-4.000€ in total (court fees + 1 lawyer). On a low income, there is a subsidy for family court costs (Verfahrenskostenhilfe, VKH).

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: Divorce (Scheidung) in Germany is governed by §§1564-1568 BGB and §§111-150 FamFG. The principle of irretrievable breakdown of the marriage (Zerrüttungsprinzip): a marriage is dissolved if it is "unheilbar zerrüttet" (irretrievably broken down) — the court does not investigate fault, only the fact of the breakdown. The key condition is the year of living apart (Trennungsjahr).

items: 1 year of living apart (Trennungsjahr) — mandatory in 99% of cases
divorce on grounds of hardship (Härtefallscheidung, §1565 Abs.2 BGB) before the year is up — only in cases of violence, crime, etc.
After 3 years of living apart — irrebuttable presumption (unwiderlegliche Vermutung) of breakdown (§1566 Abs.2)
a lawyer (Anwalt) is mandatory for at least one party (mandatory legal representation, Anwaltszwang)
Decided by the family court (Familiengericht) — a division of the local court (Amtsgericht) where one of the spouses lives

content.text: The year of living apart (Trennungsjahr, §1567 BGB) is a year of living "von Tisch und Bett getrennt" (separated from table and bed). Separate households: separate beds, no cooking together, no shared budget. You can live in the same apartment (living apart within the apartment, "Trennung innerhalb der Wohnung") if you use separate infrastructure.
You need to document the date — a letter to your partner, an email, ideally with proof of delivery. This will serve as proof (nachgewiesen) in the lawyer's pleading (Anwaltsschriftsatz).

items: Vacationing together
Sexual relations
Cleaning/laundry/cooking for each other
A joint account without a clear division

content.text: Brief attempts at reconciliation (Versöhnungsversuche, up to 3 months) do not interrupt the year of living apart (§1567 Abs.2).

Through the anwaltauskunft.de portal, the Federal Bar Association (BRAK), or local family law lawyers (Familienrechtsanwälte). The fee for an initial consultation (Erstberatung) for a consumer is capped under §34 RVG — no more than 190€ net (including expenses and VAT, in practice up to ~226€).

items: marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) + family record book (Stammbuch der Familie)
birth certificates (Geburtsurkunden) of the children
proof of the start date of living apart (Trennungsdatum)
the income of both spouses over the last 12 months (payslips, Lohnabrechnungen; tax assessment, Steuerbescheid)
rental contract (Mietvertrag), insurance policies (Versicherungen)
information on the pension rights adjustment (Versorgungsausgleich)

content.text: The lawyer files it with the local court (Amtsgericht) — the family court for the place where the family lives (or where one of the spouses lives with the children).

The pension rights adjustment is carried out automatically — pension rights accrued during the marriage are split in half (§1 VersAusglG). You can waive it before a notary at the court if the marriage was <3 years.
3-9 months after filing — an oral hearing (mündliche Verhandlung). The spouses confirm that they want to divorce. The court's decision (Beschluss) is handed down the same day.

1 month after the court decision (if no immediate appeal, Beschwerde, was filed) — the divorce becomes final. The lawyer will receive a certificate of legal effect (Rechtskraftvermerk) for the registry office (Standesamt).

A divorce by mutual consent (einvernehmliche Scheidung) is the fastest and cheapest. A contested divorce (streitige Scheidung) with disagreements over support (Unterhalt), parental rights (Sorgerecht), or the division of assets (Vermögensaufteilung) can drag on for years and cost tens of thousands of euros.

items: By consent (einvernehmlich): only 1 lawyer (for one of the spouses), the other agrees. Cost ~1.500-3.000€
Contested (streitig): 2 lawyers + additional related matters (Folgesachen): equalization of accrued gains (Zugewinnausgleich), support (Unterhalt), household goods (Hausrat)
Mediation (Mediation) — an alternative through family mediation (Familienmediation, 300-2.000€), does not replace the court
Related matters can be settled in a separate separation agreement (Trennungsvereinbarung) before a notary

content.text: If your income is low, the court pays for the lawyer and the court costs (Gerichtskosten) — §§76 ff. FamFG together with §§114 ff. ZPO. This is the equivalent of the legal aid subsidy (Prozesskostenhilfe) for family matters (Familiensachen).

items: Income after deductions <~600€/month — fully free of charge
Up to ~1.500€/month — Ratenzahlung (payment in installments)
protected amount of assets (Vermögensfreigrenze): ~10.000€ (excluding your primary home)
the VKH application form (VKH-Antrag) — from your lawyer or at amtsgericht.de
the lawyer is appointed from those who take VKH cases

content.text: Don't try to divorce "amicably at a notary" — a notarized agreement to dissolve a marriage has no legal effect in Germany. Only the family court can dissolve a marriage.

There is no single lawyer for both of you! A lawyer always represents the interests of one client. The second spouse signs a consent (Zustimmung) without their own lawyer — but risks not understanding the consequences.
You can't claim the year of living apart was "a long time ago, we just forgot to count it." The date is fixed in writing — otherwise the court will demand proof.

The residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) of a foreign spouse: after a divorce, the right to stay is retained only if the marriage lasted >3 years (§31 AufenthG) or in a case of hardship (Härtefall). Otherwise — the permit is revoked.
