title: Divorce with children: custody
tldr: In a divorce with children, parental rights (custody, Sorgerecht) usually remain joint (gemeinsam, §1626 BGB) — even after the divorce, unless the court decides otherwise. The right to contact (Umgangsrecht, §1684 BGB) is guaranteed to both parents and to the child. Child support (Kindesunterhalt) is paid by the parent who lives apart, based on the Düsseldorf Table (Düsseldorfer Tabelle) 2026. Complex cases go through the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) and the family court (Familiengericht).

content.text: §1626 BGB: parental custody (elterliche Sorge) includes care for the child (Personensorge) and management of the child's assets (Vermögenssorge). After a divorce, custody remains joint (gemeinsam) — this is the default; you have to specifically request sole custody (alleiniges Sorgerecht).

items: joint custody (gemeinsames Sorgerecht) — the standard, requires cooperation between the ex-spouses
sole custody (alleiniges Sorgerecht) — you must apply to the family court and prove it is in the child's best interests (welfare of the child, Kindeswohl)
individual areas (Teilbereiche) can be assigned to one parent (for example, choice of school, Schulwahl; medical decisions) under §1671 Abs.1 S.2 BGB
the right to determine the child's place of residence (Aufenthaltsbestimmungsrecht) — often assigned to one parent
the court rules on the principle of the child's welfare (Kindeswohl), not on "fairness between the parents"

content.text: §1684 BGB: each parent has the right and the duty to have contact with the child, and the child has the right to contact with both. This cannot be revoked even where the other parent has sole custody (Alleinsorge) — except in rare cases of a threat to the child's welfare (Kindeswohlgefährdung).
Under the residence model (Residenzmodell) the child lives with one parent; the other has the child every other weekend + half of the school holidays. The most common model in Germany.

Under the alternating model (Wechselmodell) the child lives alternately — week on/week off or 2/2 with each parent. A 2017 ruling of the Federal Court of Justice (BGH) (XII ZB 601/15) allows the alternating model even against the will of one parent, for the child's welfare. Growing in popularity.
The nest model (Nestmodell) is a rare option: the child stays in the home and the parents take turns moving in. An expensive model.

items.title: Umgang without the right to Sorge

content.text: Even a parent without custody (or a father, Vater, after acknowledging paternity without custody, Anerkennung ohne Sorge) has the right to contact.

The Düsseldorf Table (Düsseldorfer Tabelle, edition valid from 1.1.2026) is the generally accepted reference for calculating child support in Germany. It is not a law, but every court uses it. It is paid by the parent the child does not permanently live with (the parent liable for cash maintenance, Barunterhaltspflichtiger).

items: Age groups: 0–5 / 6–11 / 12–17 / adults (18+)
15 income brackets based on the payer's net earnings (from 2.100€ to 11.200€)
Bracket 1 (net up to 2.100€), 2026 — minimum support (Mindestunterhalt): 0–5 years — 486€/month, 6–11 — 558€, 12–17 — 653€, 18+ — 693€
Half of the child benefit is deducted from the amount (Kindergeld; in 2026 Kindergeld = 259€, i.e. ~130€ for minors)
the payer's necessary minimum for their own support (notwendiger Selbstbehalt): 1.450€/month if employed, 1.200€ if not employed (unchanged in 2026)

content.text: If the payer evades payment — you can receive an advance on child support (Unterhaltsvorschuss) under the child support advance act (Unterhaltsvorschussgesetz, UhVorschG): the state pays an advance until the child comes of age (since 2017 with no upper age limit), and then recovers the money from the debtor.
Besides child support, there is spousal support (Ehegattenunterhalt).

Support during the period of living apart (Trennungsunterhalt) — from the moment of separation until the divorce, for the spouse with the lower income. Calculation: 3/7 of the income difference (if both work) or 45% (if one is not working).

Post-divorce support (nachehelicher Unterhalt) — after a divorce, only for specific reasons: support for caring for a child (Betreuungsunterhalt), illness (Krankheit), age (Alter), support during education or further training (Aus- oder Fortbildungsunterhalt), a top-up to one's own income (Aufstockungsunterhalt). The duration is limited under §1578b BGB.
Since 2008, the principle of personal responsibility (Eigenverantwortung): everyone provides for themselves after a divorce. Support for an ex-spouse is the exception.
The youth welfare office (Jugendamt, §§50-52a SGB VIII) is a mandatory participant in all family court proceedings involving children. It is both support and oversight.

items: assistance with maintenance (Beistandschaft, §§1712-1717 BGB): free representation of the child in establishing support
consultation (Beratung) on separation/divorce — free of charge (§17 SGB VIII)
supervised contact (begleiteter Umgang) — supervision of visits in cases of conflict
a statement (Stellungnahme) to the family court — the youth welfare office writes its opinion on custody/contact
in the event of a threat to the child's welfare — taking the child into care (Inobhutnahme; removal of the child, §42 SGB VIII)

content.text: Many foreigners are afraid of the youth welfare office because of its reputation. In reality it is first and foremost an offer of help (Hilfsangebot); removals are rare and only for serious reasons. Bring in your own lawyer (Anwalt) if you are unsure.
Don't sign a "voluntary consent to sole custody (Alleinsorge)" for the other parent without a lawyer (Anwalt). It changes everything for years to come.

Moving abroad with the child after a divorce (mit Kind ins Ausland nach Scheidung): with joint custody (gemeinsames Sorgerecht), moving to another country requires the consent of the other parent or a court decision (§1671 BGB + the Hague Convention on Child Abduction, Haager Kindesentführungsabkommen). Abduction is a criminal offence.

Refusing to hand over the child for contact (Umgangsverweigerung) is punishable by an administrative fine for non-compliance (Ordnungsgeld) of up to 25.000€ + enforcement (Vollstreckung, §89 FamFG). Likewise — the child refusing contact does not release the parent from their obligation.

You can't cancel or reduce support on your own — you have to file a petition for modification with the court (Abänderungsklage). Simply stopping payment = debt + seizure of assets/account (Pfändung) + possible criminal prosecution (Strafverfahren, §170 StGB).

title: Hilfetelefon: 08000 116 016
tldr: The helpline (Hilfetelefon) "Gewalt gegen Frauen" (violence against women) is a free, anonymous, round-the-clock hotline at 08000 116 016, operating in 18 languages including Russian. Help for victims of all forms of violence (physical, psychological, sexual, digital, economic). A men's helpline ("Männer-Hilfetelefon") 0800 123 9900 runs in parallel. In acute danger — call 110 (police).

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: The helpline "Gewalt gegen Frauen" is a government service under the Federal Office for Family Affairs and Civil Society Tasks (BAFzA, Bundesamt für Familie und zivilgesellschaftliche Aufgaben); it has operated since 2013 on the basis of the helpline act (Hilfetelefongesetz). The goal is low-threshold access to help: you call anonymously and get advice and contacts for local support.

items: Number: 08000 116 016 (free from any German phone)
Available 24/7, 365 days a year
Services: phone, chat, email, video call with sign-language interpretation
18 languages, including Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, English, Turkish, Arabic, Farsi
does not appear on your itemized call list (Einzelverbindungsnachweis)
Fully anonymous — no name, address, or status needed

steps.title: What kind of violence is a reason to call

content.text: You can call about any form of violence — there is no situation "too minor" to reach out. The advisors will help you assess how serious it is.

items: physical violence (körperliche Gewalt) — beatings, shoving, choking
psychological violence (psychische Gewalt) — threats, humiliation, control, isolation
sexualized violence (sexualisierte Gewalt) — rape (including within marriage), coercion
digital violence (digitale Gewalt) — tracking via apps, blackmail with intimate photos, cyberstalking
economic violence (ökonomische Gewalt) — denying access to money, documents, work
stalking (Stalking, §238 StGB)
domestic violence (häusliche Gewalt) — violence within the family
forced marriage (Zwangsheirat), genital mutilation (Genitalverstümmelung), human trafficking (Menschenhandel)

content.text: An advisor (Beraterin — all women, professional psychologists / social workers) will listen and help you understand the situation. They won't tell you what to do unless you ask.

They will tell you about your rights and options: a women's shelter (Frauenhaus), the violence protection act (Gewaltschutzgesetz: removing the spouse from the home, Wegweisung; a no-approach order, Annäherungsverbot), filing a police report (Anzeige), legal aid.
They will give you contacts for the nearest women's shelter, a counseling center (Beratungsstelle), a lawyer (Anwältin). They will help with an interpreter if you need one.
You can call again — there is no limit. Each time it's a new advisor; your history is not stored (anonymity).

items: Notruf 110 — police (in acute danger)
Notruf 112 — medical emergency
Männer-Hilfetelefon: 0800 123 9900 (for male victims)
Hilfetelefon Sexueller Missbrauch: 0800 22 55 530
Frauenhaus-Koordinierung: frauenhauskoordinierung.de — a list of all shelters
Weisser Ring: 116 006 (victims of crime in general)
Nummer gegen Kummer für Kinder: 116 111

content.text: Online: hilfetelefon.de — chat, email consultation, information in 18 languages. For the deaf/hard of hearing — video call with sign-language interpretation.

The violence protection act (Gewaltschutzgesetz, GewSchG, 2002) is the basis of legal protection. It lets you obtain a court order barring approach, contact, or appearing near your home — without a divorce and without a criminal case.

items: assignment of the home to the victim (Wohnungszuweisung, §2 GewSchG): the perpetrator must leave the home for up to 6 months
a contact ban (Kontaktverbot), a no-approach order (Annäherungsverbot) — the court sets an exclusion zone
filed with the family court (Familiengericht), without mandatory legal representation (Anwaltszwang) — you can do it without a lawyer
violating the order = a criminal offence (Straftat, §4 GewSchG), up to 1 year in prison
a subsidy for court costs (Verfahrenskostenhilfe) is available for those on low incomes
in an acute case — removal from the home (Wegweisung) by the police for 10-14 days (without a court)

content.text: If your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) depends on your partner — there is a hardship clause (Härteklausel) §31 Abs.2 AufenthG: in cases of violence, the right to stay is retained without the 3-year marriage. Turn to a migration counseling service (Migrationsberatung).

title: Certificate of capacity to marry (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis)
tldr: A certificate of capacity to marry (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis, §1309 BGB) is a certificate from your country of citizenship stating that there are no impediments to the marriage. Most foreigners need it to marry in Germany. Russians obtain it through the Russian consulate; the USA, Australia and the UK do not issue one — you need an exemption from the requirement (Befreiung) through the president of a higher regional court (OLG, Oberlandesgericht). Valid for 6 months. Cost: 20-50€ at a consulate; an exemption through the OLG — 75-200€.

steps.title: What it is and why it matters

content.text: The certificate of capacity to marry (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis, "certificate of marital capacity") is a document from your country of citizenship confirming that, under local law, you are not already married and have no other impediments (age, kinship, etc.) to entering into a marriage. §1309 BGB requires the registry office (Standesamt) to obtain this certificate from foreigners.

items: required for most foreigners (not for Germans, and not for most EU citizens who have alternatives)
Valid for 6 months from the date of issue
must carry an apostille (Apostille; the Hague Convention, Haager Übereinkommen) or consular legalization (Legalisation)
a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) into German is mandatory (if the document is not in German or English)
if the country does not issue one — an exemption from the requirement (Befreiung) through the president of a higher regional court (OLG)

content.text: Russia issues the certificate of capacity to marry through Russian consulates in Germany (Berlin, Hamburg, Bonn, Munich, Leipzig).

items: International passport + internal Russian passport (copies of all pages)
Birth certificate
if divorced — divorce certificate with an apostille (Apostille)
If widowed — death certificate of the spouse
Completed consular application form
cost ~30-50€ + certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) 30-70€
Processing time: 2-6 weeks

content.text: Since 2022, some Russians have faced delays because of the political situation. The alternative is an exemption from the requirement (Befreiung) through a higher regional court (OLG) if the consulate is, for objective reasons, unavailable (for example, if it refuses to issue one). Many higher regional courts have been accepting such applications in 2024-2025.

Issued through the Belarusian consulate (Berlin, Munich). The process is similar to Russia. Delays are possible due to politics; an exemption through a higher regional court (OLG-Befreiung) is a workable fallback.

Ukrainian citizens with §24 AufenthG (protection under the directive, Schutz nach RL 2001/55/EG) or another status: the certificate is issued through a Ukrainian registry office or consulate. Since 2022 some higher regional courts grant the exemption from the requirement (Befreiung) without a long wait for the certificate — upon confirmation of refugee status.

items.title: Ukrainian men of military service age

content.text: They cannot return to obtain documents — this counts as an objective impediment. The registry office (Standesamt) and the higher regional court usually accommodate this.

steps.title: USA, UK, Australia, Canada: countries without an Ehefähigkeitszeugnis

content.text: Common-law countries have no concept of a "certificate of capacity to marry." The solution is an exemption from the obligation to produce the document (Befreiung von der Beibringungspflicht) through the president of the competent higher regional court (§1309 Abs.2 BGB).

items: an affidavit / declaration of marital status (Affidavit / Single Status Declaration) before a notary or consul
an apostille (Apostille; the Hague Convention, Haager Übereinkommen) on the affidavit
a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) into German
birth certificate (Birth certificate) + apostille + translation
if divorced — divorce decree (Divorce decree) + apostille + translation
International passport
application for an exemption (Antrag auf Befreiung) — through the registry office, which forwards it to the higher regional court

content.text: Processing time at the higher regional court: 6-12 weeks. The decision applies only to a specific marriage with a specific person and is limited to 6 months.

items.title: 1. Book an appointment at the Standesamt

content.text: The registry office for the place where one of the partners is registered (residence registration). The notice of intended marriage (Anmeldung der Eheschließung, formerly the banns, "Aufgebot"). Often a long wait for an appointment — 4-8 weeks.
Each registry office issues an exact list tailored to the couple (it depends on citizenships and marital status). Don't start gathering documents before your appointment at the registry office.

items: international passport + residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel)
birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) with an apostille (Apostille) + translation
certificate of capacity to marry (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis) or an exemption from the requirement (Befreiung)
registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung; residence registration, Anmeldung)
if divorced — divorce judgment (Scheidungsurteil) with a certificate of legal effect (Rechtskraftvermerk) + apostille

content.text: Filed through the registry office; decided by the president of the higher regional court (OLG-Präsident) of the competent OLG (by federal state). Court fee 75-200€.
2-6 months after the notice of intended marriage — a wedding date is set. No mandatory witnesses (Trauzeugen) — but you can have 2 witnesses if you wish.

The 6-month validity: if the certificate of capacity to marry expires before the wedding date — you request it again. Plan ahead: obtaining the certificate + translation + processing at the registry office + waiting for the wedding ≈ 4-6 months.

The apostille (Apostille) must be on the document, not on the translation. First the apostille in the country of issue — then a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) in Germany by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer).

Name spellings (Mehrname): if your name is transliterated differently across your foreign documents, you will need a certificate of name spelling (Namensbescheinigung) or a single ruling from the registry office. Otherwise the documents may not be accepted.

Marrying to obtain a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — a sham marriage (Scheinehe) — is a crime (§95 Abs.2 AufenthG). The registry office and the foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde) coordinate when there are suspicions.

Marrying abroad (Eheschließung im Ausland): you can marry abroad (for example, in Denmark) — there is no requirement for a certificate of capacity to marry there. The marriage is then recognized in Germany (recognition, Anerkennung, as long as it does not violate public policy, ordre public). A popular alternative for couples from countries with problematic consulates.

title: Eingetragene Lebenspartnerschaft
tldr: A registered partnership (eingetragene Lebenspartnerschaft) is governed by the registered partnership act (Lebenspartnerschaftsgesetz, LPartG). IMPORTANT: since 1 October 2017 (the marriage opening act, Eheöffnungsgesetz, "marriage for all") new partnerships are NO LONGER concluded — same-sex couples now register an ordinary marriage (Ehe) at the registry office (Standesamt) under §1353 BGB. Existing partnerships remain valid and can be converted into a marriage (conversion, Umwandlung) at the registry office. This guide explains what to do if you registered a partnership before 2017, and why new couples need to go for an ordinary marriage.

steps.title: What a Lebenspartnerschaft is and what changed

content.text: A registered partnership (eingetragene Lebenspartnerschaft) is an institution introduced in 2001 under the registered partnership act (LPartG) specifically for same-sex couples, at a time when an ordinary marriage was not available to them. It granted almost all of the rights of spouses: living together, a mutual duty of support, inheritance rights, and a joint tax class. After the marriage opening act (Eheöffnungsgesetz, "Ehe für alle" — marriage for all) was passed, same-sex couples gained the right to a full marriage (Ehe) under §1353 BGB as of 1 October 2017.

Since 1 October 2017, NEW registered partnerships are no longer concluded in Germany (§1 LPartG in its current version). If you are a couple (of any gender) who wants to formalize your relationship now — you need an ordinary marriage at the registry office (Standesamt), not a partnership (Lebenspartnerschaft). The partnership procedure is closed to new couples.

If your partnership was registered before 1 October 2017 (in Germany, or a recognized foreign one), it remains fully in force. All rights and obligations under the registered partnership act are retained: a shared surname, the duty of support (§5 LPartG), the right to inherit, custody of shared children.

items: A partnership registered before 01.10.2017 is valid indefinitely
Converting it into a marriage is NOT required — it is a right, not an obligation
all certificates (partnership certificate, Lebenspartnerschaftsurkunde) are issued by the registry office (Standesamt) where you registered
a foreign partnership is recognized if it is comparable to the German one (the registry office checks this)

steps.title: Converting a partnership into a marriage (Umwandlung)

content.text: An existing partnership can be converted into a marriage. This is done at any registry office (Standesamt): both partners appear in person, declare that they wish to marry each other, and confirm that they are in a registered partnership. The date of the marriage is then usually counted "retroactively" for pension and tax purposes from the time the partnership was entered into.

items: Valid ID cards / passports of both partners
partnership certificate (Lebenspartnerschaftsurkunde)
a current registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung; proof of registered residence)
For a foreign partnership — a certified translation and an apostille
book an appointment (Termin) at the registry office (Standesamt) — online or by phone at the town hall
Both partners come in person — representation is not possible
after the declaration the registry office issues a new marriage certificate (Eheurkunde)
Notify your insurer, your employer, and the tax office about the change of status

content.text: Both a partnership and a marriage give the same key advantages: joint taxation of spouses (Ehegattensplitting; an equivalent regime for partners), favorable inheritance tax (tax class I, Steuerklasse I; a high tax-free allowance of 500 000 €), the right to free family co-insurance (Familienversicherung), and a survivor's pension (Hinterbliebenenrente).

For inheritance without a will, a partner/spouse receives a statutory share under §1931 BGB. But if you want to deviate from the standard shares (for example, to exclude other heirs), you need a will or an inheritance contract (Erbvertrag) before a notary. Don't rely on "everything passing automatically to the partner" — if there are children or parents, the share is split.

costs.label: Umwandlung Lebenspartnerschaft → Ehe
costs.note: Standesamt fees vary by federal state/city; conversion is usually cheaper than a new wedding.

costs.label: Eheurkunde / Lebenspartnerschaftsurkunde (certificate)
costs.note: Per copy; the international form costs more.

costs.label: Consultation with a notary (Erbvertrag, optional)
costs.note: Depends on the value of the assets (Geschäftswert); only if you draw up a will/contract.

title: Free family counseling
tldr: Germany has an extensive network of FREE family counseling services (family counseling, Familienberatung; parenting counseling, Erziehungsberatung). Under §28 SGB VIII parents have the right to free parenting counseling (a parenting counseling center, Erziehungsberatungsstelle), and under §17–18 SGB VIII to help with divorce, custody disputes, and problems with children. Counseling is provided by major charitable organizations (Caritas, Diakonie, AWO, pro familia, Deutscher Kinderschutzbund) and the youth welfare office (Jugendamt). Support is anonymous, independent of your residence status and income, and often available in several languages. Many services also work by phone/online.

content.text: Free counseling is provided by municipal services — the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) — and independent charitable organizations (non-statutory providers, freie Träger). All of them are funded by the state under SGB VIII, so for the family the service is free and does not depend on income, citizenship, or residence status.

items: a parenting counseling center (Erziehungsberatungsstelle) — questions of upbringing, children's behavior, school (§28 SGB VIII)
Caritas, Diakonie, AWO, Paritätischer — general family and crisis help
pro familia — relationships, pregnancy, sexual health
Deutscher Kinderschutzbund — protection of children's rights, helpline
the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) — custody, divorce, threat to the child's welfare (§8a SGB VIII)

content.text: Family counseling helps with practically any everyday and emotional family problem: conflicts with teenage children, difficulties at school, divorce and the division of custody, violence within the family, parental burnout, and helping a migrant child settle in. Under §17 SGB VIII parents have the right to support during a separation, and under §18 SGB VIII to counseling on questions of custody and the right to contact with the child (Umgangsrecht).

items: Problems with a child's upbringing and behavior
Divorce, the division of custody (Sorgerecht) and the arrangement of contact (Umgang)
Conflicts between parents and teenagers
Psychological strain, stress, parental burnout
Suspicion of violence — the service is obliged to help confidentially

steps.title: How to find a service and make an appointment

content.text: The fastest route is to call your local youth welfare office (Jugendamt) or open the bke.de portal (the Federal Conference for Parenting Counseling, Bundeskonferenz für Erziehungsberatung), which has online counseling and a directory of services. For urgent anonymous support there are free helplines. Appointments are usually made by phone or email; emergency cases are seen without a wait.

items: search on bke.de or your city's website (family counseling, Familienberatung, + the city name)
call the youth welfare office — they will refer you to the right service
Ask whether there is a counselor who speaks Russian/Ukrainian/English
bke online counseling (bke-Onlineberatung) — anonymous messaging with psychologists, free
Nummer gegen Kummer (line for children): 116 111, for parents: 0800 111 0 550
the helpline (Hilfetelefon) "Gewalt gegen Frauen" (violence against women): 116 016 (24/7, multilingual)

content.text: Counselors are bound by professional confidentiality (the duty of confidentiality, Schweigepflicht). They do NOT pass information to the foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde) and do not depend on your residence permit. Any parent or child can reach out, even without German — they often arrange an interpreter.

There is one exception to confidentiality: if there is a concrete threat to the child's welfare (threat to the child's welfare, Kindeswohlgefährdung, under §8a SGB VIII), the service is obliged to act in the child's interests. This is protection for the child, not a sanction against the family — but be aware that in such cases the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) gets involved.

costs.note: Completely free under SGB VIII regardless of income and status.

costs.label: Helplines (Nummer gegen Kummer, Hilfetelefon)
costs.note: Free call, anonymous, including from a mobile phone.

costs.label: bke online counseling
costs.note: Free after registering under a pseudonym.

title: Frauenhaus: a women's shelter
tldr: A women's shelter (Frauenhaus) is a protected refuge where women (with children) who have suffered domestic violence can live anonymously and safely. The address is kept secret. Admission is round-the-clock and does not depend on citizenship, residence status, or knowledge of German. In parallel, under the violence protection act (Gewaltschutzgesetz, GewSchG), the court can issue a protective order against the abuser (Schutzanordnung; a no-approach order) and assign the shared home to the victim (§1, §2 GewSchG). The main emergency contact is the helpline (Hilfetelefon) "Gewalt gegen Frauen" (violence against women) 116 016, free, anonymous, 24/7, in 17+ languages. In danger — call 110 (police) right away.

steps.title: If you are in danger right now

content.text: If you or your children are in immediate danger — call 110 (police); it's free from any phone, even without a SIM or credit. The police can immediately remove the abuser from the apartment (removal from the home, Wohnungsverweisung) and impose a ban on returning for up to 10–14 days. Don't wait "until it gets worse."

After the police intervene, you'll have time to calmly turn to the court for longer-term protection and/or move to a women's shelter (Frauenhaus). The police also pass your details (with your consent) to a local support service (Interventionsstelle), which will then contact you directly.

The main round-the-clock contact is the federal helpline (Hilfetelefon) "Gewalt gegen Frauen" (violence against women): 116 016. The call is free and anonymous, available in 17+ languages via an interpreter, 24/7. The advisors will help you find an available place at the nearest women's shelter (Frauenhaus), explain the steps, and, if you wish, connect you with a local service.

items: 116 016 — the helpline (Hilfetelefon) Gewalt gegen Frauen, violence against women (24/7, free, multilingual)
Online chat and email consultation at hilfetelefon.de
frauenhaus-suche.de — a map of shelters with available places
The call does not appear on your itemized bill

steps.title: What to bring and how a Frauenhaus works

content.text: You can come to a women's shelter (Frauenhaus) with your children. The shelter's address is secret and the entrance is monitored. Housing, meals, and support from social workers are provided; the women help one another. Staff accompany you to government offices, to a lawyer, to the job and social welfare center (Jobcenter). If you left your documents at home, that's not a problem — they can be sorted out later.

items.title: 1. What to bring if you can

items: Your and your children's passports/IDs, residence permit
Health insurance cards, bank card, a little cash
Medications, glasses, important keys
The children's favorite things — a toy, clothes
Safety matters more than belongings — leave without documents if you have to
The police can escort you home for your things later
Lost documents can be reissued through government offices

content.text: Under the violence protection act (Gewaltschutzgesetz, GewSchG) the family court (Familiengericht) can issue a protective order (Schutzanordnung): barring the abuser from approaching you, calling you, or entering the apartment (§1 GewSchG), as well as temporarily assigning the shared home to the victim (§2 GewSchG). You can file the application yourself, without a lawyer; in urgent cases the court decides within days (an interim order, einstweilige Anordnung).

The cost of staying in a women's shelter is often covered by the state. If you have no income, the cost is borne by the job and social welfare center (Jobcenter)/social services; if you have asylum-related status, by the relevant authority. The financial question should NOT stop you from reaching out — the social workers will help arrange the payments on the spot.

costs.label: Hilfetelefon 116 016 and online consultation
costs.note: Completely free, anonymous, 24/7, multilingual.

costs.label: Staying in a Frauenhaus
costs.note: Usually covered by the Jobcenter/social services; with no income — free for the woman.

costs.label: Schutzanordnung through the Familiengericht
costs.note: Court fees; for low income — Verfahrenskostenhilfe (exemption from costs).

title: Bestattung: funerals in Germany
tldr: Funerals (Bestattung) in Germany are strictly regulated. There is a duty to bury (Bestattungspflicht) and, almost everywhere, mandatory burial in a cemetery (Friedhofszwang) — an urn or body cannot be kept at home, and ashes are buried in a cemetery. First a doctor issues a confirmation of death (Totenschein), then the registry office (Standesamt) issues the death certificate (Sterbeurkunde). The funeral is usually handled by a funeral home (Bestattungsinstitut). The costs are borne by the heirs under §1968 BGB (funeral costs, Beerdigungskosten). Funeral law itself is the responsibility of the federal states (state law, Landesrecht), so the details of the burial act (Bestattungsgesetz) vary. A budget cremation costs roughly from 1000–1500 €, a traditional funeral several thousand euros.

content.text: First the death must be confirmed: a doctor is called (for a death at home — the family doctor, Hausarzt, or an ambulance via 116 117 / 112), who issues a confirmation of death (Totenschein). Without this document, no further processing is possible. If the person died in a hospital or nursing home, the confirmation of death is issued there.

items: at home: call a doctor to confirm the death and issue the Totenschein
In a hospital/hospice: the institution issues the document
If the circumstances are unclear, the police are called (110)
The body must be handed over within the period set by the federal state (usually 36 hours)

content.text: Within a few days the death is registered at the registry office (Standesamt) for the place of death, which issues the death certificate (Sterbeurkunde). This document is needed for insurance, the bank, the pension, and the inheritance. Order several copies right away — they'll be needed by different authorities.

items: confirmation of death (Totenschein) from the doctor
ID of the deceased
Birth and/or marriage certificate of the deceased
order 5–10 copies of the death certificate (Sterbeurkunde)
usually the funeral home (Bestattungsinstitut) handles the registration
you can do it yourself at the registry office for the place of death
the first copy of the death certificate is often free, the rest cost a fee

content.text: Germany has mandatory burial in a cemetery (Friedhofszwang): the body or the urn with the ashes must be buried at an official cemetery (Friedhof). Keeping ashes at home or scattering them is generally prohibited (the details depend on the federal state). The main types: earth burial (Erdbestattung), cremation (Feuerbestattung) with burial of the urn, woodland burial (Ruheforst/Friedwald), anonymous burial, and burial at sea (Seebestattung) — the last only through specialized services.

The duty to bury (Bestattungspflicht) means that the next of kin are OBLIGED to arrange the burial within the set period (in most federal states the body must be buried/cremated within a few days). A failure to do so can result in an administrative fine (Bußgeld). If relatives do not act, the public order office (Ordnungsamt) takes over the costs and the arrangements — but then recovers them from those responsible.

Under §1968 BGB the costs of a dignified burial are borne by the heirs (Erben). If the heirs cannot pay and the deceased had no means, you can apply for coverage of the funeral costs (Bestattungskostenübernahme; a welfare funeral, Sozialbestattung) at the social welfare office (Sozialamt) under §74 SGB XII — it covers the "necessary" costs of a modest funeral.

Compare funeral home quotes carefully — prices vary a lot. The cheapest is an anonymous or woodland cremation (from ~1000–1500 €); a traditional funeral with a coffin, headstone, and ceremony easily exceeds 4000–7000 €. Ask for a written quote (Kostenvoranschlag) and don't sign up for extra services under pressure.

costs.note: Per copy; the first one for welfare purposes is often free.

costs.label: Cremation (Feuerbestattung), basic option
costs.note: Includes the cremation and a simple urn burial; prices depend on the federal state and cemetery.

costs.label: Traditional funeral (Erdbestattung)
costs.note: Coffin, plot, headstone, ceremony, funeral home services.

costs.label: Sozialbestattung (Sozialamt assistance, §74 SGB XII)
costs.note: Coverage of the necessary costs if neither the deceased nor the persons obliged have means.

title: Basic income support in old age (Grundsicherung im Alter): for pensioners
tldr: Basic income support in old age and in case of reduced earning capacity (Grundsicherung im Alter und bei Erwerbsminderung, §41 ff. SGB XII) is a basic social benefit for the elderly (who have reached pension age) and people with permanent full incapacity to work, whose income and pension are not enough to live on. This is NOT the Bürgergeld basic benefit (that one is for those able to work). The application is filed at the social welfare office (Sozialamt). It covers the subsistence minimum (the standard need, Regelbedarf), housing costs (rent, Miete, + heating within reasonable limits), and a top-up to insurance. Important: with basic income support in old age, recourse against children for maintenance (Unterhaltsrückgriff) usually does NOT apply if their annual income is below 100 000 € (§94 SGB XII). You can apply even with a minimal pension.

content.text: Basic income support in old age and in case of reduced earning capacity is available to people who are ordinarily resident in Germany and who have either reached pension age (the standard age limit, Regelaltersgrenze, gradually rising toward 67) or are over 18 and permanently fully incapable of working (full incapacity to work, volle Erwerbsminderung, indefinitely), and who cannot cover the subsistence minimum with their own income and assets (§41 SGB XII).

items: Pension age reached (for those born from 1964 — 67 years) OR permanent full incapacity to work
Ordinary residence in Germany
Income (including pension) and assets are not enough for the subsistence minimum
This benefit does NOT reduce your future pension and does not have to be repaid

content.text: Basic income support covers: the standard need (Regelbedarf — a fixed amount to live on, indexed annually), the actual costs of housing and heating within reasonable limits (reasonable housing costs, angemessene Kosten der Unterkunft), and contributions to health and long-term care insurance. For special needs, top-ups for an increased need (Mehrbedarfe) are possible — for example, with a disability carrying the mark G (Merkzeichen G).

items: the standard need (Regelbedarf) — a base amount for food, clothing, daily life
the costs of an apartment (rent, Miete) and heating within reasonable limits
contributions to health insurance (Krankenversicherung) and long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung)
a top-up for an increased need (Mehrbedarf) — for disability, a special diet, or pregnancy

content.text: The application is filed at the social welfare office (Sozialamt; the social assistance provider, Träger der Sozialhilfe) for your place of residence. Often you can also file it through the pension fund (the German Pension Insurance, Deutsche Rentenversicherung), which forwards it to the social welfare office. You'll need documents on income, pension, rent, and assets.

items: ID and a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Pension notice (Rentenbescheid), proof of income
rental contract (Mietvertrag) and the heating bill (utility costs, Nebenkosten)
Account statements and information on assets
in case of incapacity — an assessment of reduced earning capacity (Erwerbsminderung)
the social welfare office (Sozialamt) for your place of residence — the main address
you can go through the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) — they will forward it
Forms are available online on your city's/district's website

content.text: The key difference from ordinary social assistance (Sozialhilfe): with basic income support in old age, the recipient's children and parents are generally NOT called upon to provide maintenance (support, Unterhalt) unless their annual gross income exceeds 100 000 € (the threshold under §94 SGB XII / the relatives' relief act, Angehörigen-Entlastungsgesetz). For this reason many elderly people needlessly fail to apply, afraid of burdening their children.

Assets are taken into account, but there is protected property (Schonvermögen) — small savings, a reasonably sized apartment/house in regular use, and household items are not taken. Don't refuse to apply out of fear that "they'll take everything": have your eligibility assessed through the social welfare office (Sozialamt) or a consultation with VdK/Caritas. The application itself is free.

costs.note: Free; handled at the Sozialamt.

costs.note: Indexed annually; housing and heating are paid separately on top.

costs.label: Children's income threshold for Unterhaltsrückgriff
costs.note: If a child's annual income is below 100 000 €, they are not called upon to provide maintenance (§94 SGB XII).

title: Erbschaft: inheritance
tldr: Inheritance in Germany is governed by inheritance law (Erbrecht) in the BGB (§1922 ff.). If there is no will, the statutory order of succession (gesetzliche Erbfolge) applies: the spouse/partner (§1931 BGB) and the children inherit first. An inheritance is accepted "automatically" — but together with the debts, which is why, for an inheritance with debts, you have only 6 weeks to renounce the inheritance (Ausschlagung, §1944 BGB) at the probate court (Nachlassgericht). Inheritance tax (Erbschaftsteuer) depends on the family relationship: a spouse has a tax-free allowance of 500 000 €, children 400 000 €. To dispose of the estate's assets you often need a certificate of inheritance (Erbschein).

content.text: If the deceased left no will (Testament) or inheritance contract (Erbvertrag), the statutory order of succession applies (gesetzliche Erbfolge, §1924–1931 BGB). The first order is the children and their descendants; the spouse/registered partner inherits alongside them under §1931 BGB. If there are no children, the parents, siblings, and then the further orders inherit.

items: 1st order: the deceased's children, grandchildren
2nd order: parents, siblings (if there are no descendants)
The spouse/partner inherits alongside these orders (§1931 BGB)
Living together without marriage does NOT confer a statutory right to inherit

steps.title: Acceptance and renunciation — watch the deadline!

content.text: In Germany an inheritance is deemed accepted "automatically" unless you renounce it. Along with the assets, the deceased's debts pass to you. If you suspect that the debts exceed the assets, you have only 6 weeks from the moment you learned of the inheritance to declare a renunciation of the inheritance (Ausschlagung) at the probate court (Nachlassgericht) or before a notary (§1944 BGB). The 6-month period applies only if the deceased lived abroad.

Miss the 6-week deadline and you automatically accept the inheritance TOGETHER WITH THE DEBTS, becoming liable for them with your own assets. If the composition of the estate is unclear, don't delay: either renounce it or limit your liability (estate insolvency, Nachlassinsolvenz; the plea of insufficiency of the estate, Dürftigkeitseinrede). If you renounce, the inheritance passes to the next in line — warn your relatives, or the debts will pass down to them instead.

To dispose of accounts and real estate and to transfer ownership, you often need a certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) — an official document issued by the probate court (Nachlassgericht; a division of the local court, Amtsgericht). Sometimes a bank accepts a notarized will instead of a certificate of inheritance. For real estate you have to make changes in the land register (Grundbuch).

items: an application to the probate court (Nachlassgericht) for the deceased's last place of residence
death certificate (Sterbeurkunde), documents proving the relationship (birth/marriage certificates)
The will, if there is one
The fee depends on the value of the estate (Geschäftswert)
Bank, insurance companies, employer/pension fund
the land registry office (Grundbuchamt) — transfer of real estate
the tax office (Finanzamt) — an inheritance tax return (Erbschaftsteuer) if the allowance is exceeded
Cancel the deceased's subscriptions and contracts

content.text: Inheritance tax (Erbschaftsteuer) depends on the degree of relationship (tax class) and the amount above the tax-free allowance (Freibetrag): spouse/partner — 500 000 €, children — 400 000 € per child, grandchildren — 200 000 €, others — 20 000 €. The family home (Familienheim) inherited by a spouse can be fully exempt under certain residence conditions.

You must report the inheritance to the tax office (Finanzamt) within 3 months (the duty to notify, Anzeigepflicht), even if you think there will be no tax. The tax office will ask you for a return itself if one is needed. Most "ordinary" inheritances within a family fall within the tax-free allowance (Freibetrag) and no tax arises, but don't ignore the notification.

costs.note: Depends on the value of the estate; there is a fixed scale (GNotKG).

costs.label: Erbschaftsteuer — spouse's Freibetrag
costs.note: Tax-free; for children — 400 000 € per child.

costs.label: Ausschlagung (renunciation of inheritance)

title: Marriage for foreigners: documents
tldr: In Germany a marriage is concluded only at the registry office (Standesamt) under §1310 BGB; a religious or other ceremony has no legal force. For foreigners the main hurdle is paperwork. You will almost always need a certificate of no impediment to marriage (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis) from your country of citizenship; if your country does not issue one, you need an exemption from the requirement (Befreiung) granted by the president of the Higher Regional Court (Oberlandesgericht). All foreign documents must come with a certified translation and usually an apostille/legalisation. You first file the notice of intended marriage (Anmeldung der Eheschließung). Note: a sham marriage (Scheinehe) for a residence permit is a criminal offence and is actively checked.

steps.title: Where and how a marriage is concluded

content.text: In Germany only a civil marriage at the registry office (Standesamt, §1310 BGB) is legally valid. A religious ceremony is possible but does not replace registration at the registry office. The process starts with the notice of intended marriage (Anmeldung der Eheschließung) — this is the submission of documents and the declaration of intent to marry, after which the registry office checks your capacity to marry.

items: Only the registry office (Standesamt) performs a legally valid marriage
First comes the notice of intended marriage (Anmeldung der Eheschließung): application and documents
The registry office checks capacity to marry, then sets the ceremony date
At least one partner usually must be registered as resident in that registry office's area

content.text: Which documents are required depends on your citizenship and family history, but the basic set for each partner is roughly the same. Foreign documents must come with a certified translation into German and, as a rule, with an apostille or consular legalisation.

items: Valid passport / ID card
Birth certificate (with translation and apostille)
Current registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Certificate of no impediment to marriage (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis)
If divorced/widowed — documents on the end of the previous marriage

steps.title: The certificate of no impediment and its absence

content.text: The certificate of no impediment to marriage (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis) confirms that under the law of your country there are no obstacles to the marriage. This certificate is issued by an authority of your country of citizenship (often the consulate). The problem is that many countries do not issue it (for example Russia, Ukraine and several others).

items.title: 1. If your country does not issue the certificate

items: You file an application for exemption from the requirement (Befreiung) to the president of the Higher Regional Court (Oberlandesgericht)
The registry office prepares the application and forwards it to the OLG
The OLG checks capacity to marry under foreign law instead of the certificate
Processing often takes several weeks or months
Translation only by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer)
Apostille (for Hague Convention countries) or consular legalisation
Check the list with the registry office BEFORE ordering documents from abroad

content.text: Documents from abroad take a long time to obtain and legalise, so start several months ahead. The registry office may request additional papers depending on your situation. Once approved, the marriage must be concluded within six months of the capacity check.

A sham marriage (Scheinehe) for the sake of a residence permit is an offence. The registry office (Standesamt) and the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) are entitled to interview the couple separately and to refuse registration if they suspect one. This applies to genuine couples too: be ready to answer everyday questions calmly. A genuine marriage with honest documents causes no problems.

costs.note: The base fee is higher if at least one partner is a foreigner.

costs.note: Depends on the federal state and income; calculated individually.

costs.label: Sworn translation of documents (per document)
costs.note: Depends on length; apostille/legalisation are paid separately.

costs.label: Eheurkunde (marriage certificate)
costs.note: Per copy; the international form is more expensive.

title: BU: occupational disability insurance
tldr: Occupational disability insurance (Berufsunfähigkeitsversicherung, BU) is a private insurance that pays a monthly pension if illness or injury means you can no longer carry out your occupation, by at least 50%, for at least 6 months. The state reduced-earning-capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente) under §43 SGB VI covers only a small part and does not consider your occupation. BU is recommended early: it makes sense to insure 60–80% of your net income, and premiums for a healthy 30-year-old are usually 50–200€/month. Underwriting is strict: it is important to answer the medical questions (Gesundheitsfragen) for the last 5–10 years honestly. If BU is not possible, alternatives are basic-ability insurance (Grundfähigkeitsversicherung), critical-illness insurance (Dread Disease) and loss-of-earning-capacity insurance (Erwerbsunfähigkeitsversicherung).

steps.title: Why you need BU and what the state covers

content.text: Occupational disability insurance (Berufsunfähigkeitsversicherung) protects your income for the case when you can no longer work in your specific occupation. This is the key difference from the state reduced-earning-capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente, §43 SGB VI), which looks at any job on the labour market rather than the one you trained for.

The state reduced-earning-capacity pension averages around 950–1100€ gross (a rough figure; check current numbers with the German Pension Insurance, DRV) and is paid only if your remaining capacity to work is less than 6 hours a day in ANY job (full reduced earning capacity, volle EM: <3h/day; partial reduced earning capacity, teilweise EM: 3–6h/day). This is often too little to keep paying rent and loans.

items: BU pays if you cannot work in your occupation, by 50%+, for 6+ months
The state reduced-earning-capacity pension (EM-Rente) requires a qualifying period (Wartezeit) of 60 months (§43 Abs. 1 SGB VI)
Without BU, young people without 5 years of contributions are often not entitled to EM-Rente at all
The self-employed and members of the liberal professions (Freiberufler) are mostly not covered by the state system
Mental illness causes ~30% of BU cases; cancer, musculoskeletal and cardiovascular conditions account for the rest
The BU pension comes in addition to the EM-Rente, not instead of it

content.text: If you work in Germany and have no BU, then with a serious illness your income — once sick pay runs out (Krankengeld; 78 weeks) — can drop to 30–40% of your former net. This is the main argument in favour of BU.

steps.title: Key terms of a BU contract

content.text: When choosing BU, focus not on the price but on the wording in the insurance conditions (Versicherungsbedingungen). A cheap tariff often contains an abstract referral to other work (abstrakte Verweisung) — the insurer can refer you to any other suitable job — or limits the disability prognosis to 3 years instead of an open-ended term.

items: Waiver of abstract referral (Verzicht auf abstrakte Verweisung) — essential; the insurer cannot tell you to "work as a cashier, you've still got hands"
Concrete referral (Konkrete Verweisung) — may apply if you have actually found comparable work
Six-month prognosis period (Prognosezeitraum 6 Monate) — standard under §172 VVG; better to choose tariffs with this period
BU pension (BU-Rente): the amount of the monthly payment; target 60–80% of your net
Insurance term (Versicherungsdauer): up to age 65–67 (matching the standard retirement age, Regelaltersgrenze)
Top-up guarantee (Nachversicherungsgarantie): the option to increase the pension without new medical questions (Gesundheitsfragen) at key events (marriage, child, mortgage, pay rise)
Premium and benefit dynamics (Beitragsdynamik and Leistungsdynamik): growth of premium and payout with inflation
Deferral and waiting-period clause (Stundungs- und Karenzklausel): a pause in payments during temporary financial difficulty

content.text: Read the exclusions (Ausschlüsse) carefully: pre-existing conditions, extreme sports, certain occupations. Check whether there is worldwide cover (Weltweiter Schutz) — important if you plan to live outside Germany.

steps.title: Underwriting: medical questions and risk classes

content.text: BU is a product with strict underwriting. The insurer asks detailed medical questions (Gesundheitsfragen) covering 5–10 years. An incorrect answer is a breach of the duty of disclosure (Anzeigepflicht, vorvertragliche Anzeigepflicht) under §19 VVG: the insurer may refuse payment or cancel the contract retroactively.

Before the official application, use an independent broker to make an anonymous preliminary risk enquiry (anonyme Risikovoranfrage) with several insurers. This lets you assess your risk class and conditions without an entry in the insurers' information system (Hinweis- und Informationssystem, HIS) — the insurers' internal database.

items: Your patient file (Patientenakte) at your family doctor (Hausarzt) for the last 5 years
All findings (Befunde) from specialists (Facharzt): orthopaedist, psychotherapist, ENT, cardiologist, etc.
A list of all sick notes (Krankschreibungen) with diagnoses (ICD-10 codes)
Hospital stays, operations, regular medication
Psychotherapy — even one-off sessions are important to state

items.title: 3. Submit the application and go through the Risikoprüfung

content.text: The insurer may offer: a normal tariff, a surcharge (Zuschlag), exclusion of certain diagnoses (Ausschluss), deferral (Zurückstellung) or rejection (Ablehnung). If rejected or excluded, consider alternatives: basic-ability insurance (Grundfähigkeitsversicherung), loss-of-earning-capacity insurance (EU-Versicherung), critical-illness insurance (Dread Disease).

Never submit a "normal" application before you have a positive answer to the anonymous preliminary enquiry (anonyme Voranfrage). Any rejection (Ablehnung) goes into HIS and makes approval with other insurers harder.

When occupational disability occurs you must file a benefit application (Leistungsantrag). The insurer will ask for detailed medical documents, a description of your occupation and actual activities, income before and after, and doctors' reports. The process often takes 3–9 months.

items: A description of your occupation before the illness: tasks, workload, % of time on different activities
All medical findings confirming that for 6+ months you cannot perform 50%+ of your tasks
Confirmation from your employer or clients
Submission of the benefit application (Leistungsantrag) in writing
If in doubt — turn to the insurance ombudsman (Versicherungsombudsmann; free) or to a specialist lawyer for insurance law (Versicherungsrecht)
The insurer's response time is usually up to 6 months
After approval — a re-check (Nachprüfung) every 1–3 years: whether the BU status still applies

content.text: Do not sign a settlement (Vergleich) or a waiver without consulting an independent expert. About 30% of rejected BU cases are won after a challenge.

steps.title: Alternatives when BU is not possible

content.text: If BU is too expensive or you have been rejected on health grounds, there are alternatives with less strict underwriting and narrower cover.

items: Basic-ability insurance (Grundfähigkeitsversicherung): pays on the loss of basic abilities (sight, walking, use of hands, working at a PC); the health check (Gesundheitsprüfung) is usually simpler
Loss-of-earning-capacity insurance (Erwerbsunfähigkeitsversicherung, EU): pays when you cannot work in ANY job — close to the state reduced-earning-capacity pension (EM-Rente), cheaper than BU
Critical-illness insurance (Dread Disease / Schwere Krankheiten): a lump sum for heart attack, stroke, cancer, etc.
Accident insurance (Unfallversicherung): accidents only, not illnesses — only 1–2% of BU cases
Multi-risk tariffs (Multi-Risk-Tarife): a combination of basic abilities + EU + Dread Disease
Long-term-care insurance (Pflegeversicherung; private top-up for care, Pflege-Zusatz): for the case where care is needed

content.text: Many of these products cover no more than 20–30% of BU scenarios. Use them as a supplement or as "better than nothing", but not as a full replacement.

costs.label: BU premium for a healthy 30-year-old office worker
costs.note: Per month with a BU-Rente of 1500€. Depends on occupation (Risikoklasse), health, term and options.

costs.label: BU premium for manual occupations or age over 40
costs.note: Per month with a BU-Rente of 1500€. A craftsman, nurse or builder falls into higher risk classes.

costs.label: Anonyme Voranfrage via an independent broker
costs.note: Free — the broker receives a Courtage from the insurer. Check independence.

costs.label: Verbraucherzentrale consultation
costs.note: For individual advice on choosing BU without selling a specific product.

title: bAV: company pension from the employer
tldr: The company pension from the employer (betriebliche Altersvorsorge, bAV) is the second pillar of the German pension system under §1 BetrAVG. An employee is entitled to divert part of their salary (Entgeltumwandlung): part of the gross salary goes into the bAV free of tax and social contributions (up to 4% of the contribution ceiling BBG free of social contributions = ~338€/month in 2026, up to 8% of BBG free of tax = ~676€/month; the BBG is a single 101 400€/year). Since 2022 the employer must add a top-up (Zuschuss) of at least 15%. There are 5 ways of organising it (Durchführungswege): direct insurance (Direktversicherung), pension fund (Pensionskasse), pension fund (Pensionsfonds), support fund (Unterstützungskasse), direct commitment (Direktzusage). Payouts in old age are fully subject to income tax and to health-insurance contributions (Krankenkassenbeitrag). The bAV is worthwhile with a long horizon, a high marginal tax rate and a generous employer top-up.

steps.title: What the bAV is and the three pension pillars

content.text: The German pension system has three pillars: state pension insurance (gesetzliche Rentenversicherung; under SGB VI), the company pension from the employer (betriebliche Altersvorsorge; under BetrAVG) and the private pension (private Altersvorsorge; Riester, Rürup, ETF). The bAV is the second pillar and is governed by the company pensions act (Betriebsrentengesetz, BetrAVG).

Under §1a BetrAVG every employee subject to compulsory pension insurance has the right to require their employer to divert part of their salary (Entgeltumwandlung): part of the gross salary is directed into the bAV. Since 2022 the employer is obliged to add a top-up (Zuschuss) of at least 15% (for new contracts this applied from 2019; for all contracts, from 2022).

items: The bAV is the second pillar (Säule) in the three-pillar system
The right to divert part of the salary (Entgeltumwandlung) under §1a BetrAVG: up to 4% of the contribution ceiling (BBG; single RV, in 2026 ≈ 338€/month)
A further 4% of the BBG is free of tax but subject to social contributions
The employer is obliged to a 15% top-up (Zuschuss) since 2022 (§1a Abs. 1a BetrAVG)
The savings stay with the employee when changing jobs (portability, Portabilität)
Vesting of rights (Unverfallbarkeit) from 3 years of service and reaching age 21
The pension protection association (Pensions-Sicherungs-Verein, PSV) protects against the employer's insolvency

steps.title: 5 ways of organising it (Durchführungswege) under §1b BetrAVG

content.text: BetrAVG provides for 5 ways of organising (Durchführungswege) a bAV. They differ in tax treatment, guarantees, investment options and who pays — the employee or the employer.

items: Direct insurance (Direktversicherung) — life insurance (Lebensversicherung) in the employee's name; the most common route; guarantee + profit participation
Pension fund (Pensionskasse) — a specialised insurer for the sector; similar to direct insurance, sometimes with better conditions for large employers
Pension fund (Pensionsfonds) — more freedom in investments (shares, ETFs), higher potential return and risk
Support fund (Unterstützungskasse) — an external fund, without the §3 Nr. 63 EStG limit; popular for top managers
Direct commitment (Direktzusage, Pensionszusage) — the employer's promise to pay a pension from its own funds; typical in large companies

The tax and social-insurance treatment varies: §3 Nr. 63 EStG (direct insurance, pension fund, pension fund) gives exemption from tax up to 8% of the BBG and from social contributions up to 4% of the BBG (the RV BBG is single West/East from 2025)

content.text: When changing employers, check portability (Portabilität): whether the contract can be transferred. For direct insurance (Direktversicherung) this is possible under §4 BetrAVG; for a direct commitment (Direktzusage) it is usually harder.

The main argument for the bAV is the saving on tax and social contributions on the way in. In 2026 you can direct up to 8% of the contribution ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze; single RV, 101 400€/year → 8% ≈ 8 112€/year ≈ 676€/month) free of income tax, and up to 4% (≈ 338€/month) free of social contributions.

items: On the way in: a tax break under §3 Nr. 63 EStG — up to 8% of the BBG (single RV) per year
Social contributions: the break only up to 4% of the BBG (health, care, pension, unemployment)
In retirement: deferred taxation (nachgelagerte Besteuerung) — payouts are fully subject to income tax (as other income, sonstige Einkünfte)
Health insurance of pensioners (Krankenversicherung der Rentner, KVdR): the full contribution to the health fund on bAV payouts (~16–17%)
Tax-free allowance (Freibetrag) in the KVdR in 2026: 197,75€/month (1/20 of the monthly reference figure, monatliche Bezugsgröße = 3 955€/20)
Riester subsidy (Riester-Förderung) on a bAV is possible via direct insurance (Direktversicherung) with the allowance model (Zulagen-Modell)
Survivors' pension (Hinterbliebenenrente): possible for a spouse and children with a contract that includes protection

content.text: Whether it is "worthwhile or not" is an individual calculation. At an average income and without an employer top-up the bAV often loses to a simple ETF savings plan (ETF-Sparplan) because of full taxation and health-fund contributions in the payout phase. Compare the scenarios before signing.

steps.title: How to set up a bAV

content.text: The specific process depends on the employer: a large company often has a framework contract (Rahmenvertrag) with an insurer and a fixed top-up (Zuschuss), while a small one may offer only the basic minimum. The right to divert part of the salary (Entgeltumwandlung) belongs to all employees under §1a BetrAVG.

items.title: 1. Ask HR about the company's terms

items: Which way of organising it (Durchführungsweg) is offered (usually direct insurance, Direktversicherung)
The size of the employer's top-up (Zuschuss) — at least 15%, often 20–50%, sometimes 100%
From what amount participation starts
The provider — Allianz, R+V, Versorgungswerk, etc.
The terms of the pension scheme (Versorgungsordnung) and the collective agreement (Tarifvertrag)

content.text: Compare three scenarios: bAV with an employer top-up vs a net investment in ETFs vs Riester/Rürup. Take into account your marginal tax rate now and the expected one in retirement, health-fund contributions, guarantees and employer risk.

The contract (the agreement to divert part of the salary, Entgeltumwandlungsvereinbarung) is signed between the employee and the employer. The employer notifies the insurer of the new contribution amount. When changing employers, discuss a transfer (Übertragung) under §4 BetrAVG.

items: Calculating without the health-fund contributions in retirement — the bAV often looks better than it is
Loss of accrued rights (Anwartschaft) if you leave before 3 years (the vesting periods, Unverfallbarkeitsfristen)
High acquisition and administration costs (Abschlusskosten and Verwaltungskosten) with direct insurance (Direktversicherung) — they can eat up half the return
A contract with the minimum 15% top-up and a "weak" insurer — work out the net IRR
Ignoring the option to suspend contributions (Beitragsfreistellung) during financial difficulty
Moving to a country outside the EU — bAV payouts may become less favourable for tax
Transferring accrued rights (Anwartschaft) without calculating the surrender costs (Storno-Kosten)
Combining a bAV with Riester is possible but not always worthwhile

content.text: When you leave, do not rush to cash out in full (a severance payment, Abfindung): under §3 BetrAVG this is only possible for small amounts. Keeping the accrued rights (Anwartschaft) until age 67 is often more worthwhile.

costs.label: Entgeltumwandlung bAV
costs.note: Monthly, the usual range. The maximum under §3 Nr. 63 EStG in 2026: ≈ 676€/month (8% of the BBG, single RV).

costs.label: Pflicht-Zuschuss from the employer
costs.note: At least 15% of the employee's contribution under §1a Abs. 1a BetrAVG (if the employer saves Sozialabgaben).

costs.label: Abschlusskosten Direktversicherung
costs.note: Usually 2.5–4% of the Beitragssumme in the first 5 years; check the Effektivkosten in the product information.

costs.label: KV contribution on the bAV pension in retirement
costs.note: About 16–17% of the payout above the Freibetrag (197,75€/month in 2026).

title: Reduced-earning-capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente)
tldr: The reduced-earning-capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente, EM-Rente) under §43 SGB VI is a state pension for those who, because of illness or injury, can no longer work a full day. The full pension (volle EM-Rente) applies when remaining work capacity is under 3 hours a day in any job; the partial one (teilweise EM) at 3–6 hours. Requirements: a 60-month qualifying period (Wartezeit) and 36 months of compulsory contributions (Pflichtbeiträge) in the last 5 years before the disability began. The amount is calculated via pension points (Entgeltpunkte) with an attribution period (Zurechnungszeit) up to the standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze); the average full EM-Rente in 2026 is ≈ 950–1150€ gross. Since 2019 new pensioners benefit from an attribution period that, for a pension starting in 2026, runs to age 66 years 3 months. Apply through the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung), usually with support from a lawyer (Rechtsanwalt) or a social association (Sozialverband; VdK, SoVD).

steps.title: What the EM-Rente is and who is entitled

content.text: The reduced-earning-capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente) is a state pension under §§43, 240 SGB VI for people who, because of illness or injury, have lost their capacity to work before reaching the standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze; 67 for those born in 1964 and later).

Two degrees are distinguished: full reduced earning capacity (volle Erwerbsminderung; remaining work capacity <3 hours a day in ANY job) and partial reduced earning capacity (teilweise Erwerbsminderung; 3–6 hours a day). Your occupation is not considered — only your general capacity to work on the labour market.

items: Full pension (volle EM-Rente): <3 h/day in any job → full payment
Partial pension (teilweise EM-Rente): 3–6 h/day → half of the full EM-Rente
Occupational protection (Berufsschutz) exists only for those born before 02.01.1961 (the former occupational-disability pension, alte Berufsunfähigkeitsrente)
If there is partial reduced earning capacity but the labour market (Arbeitsmarkt) offers no suitable positions: full EM via the labour-market pension (Arbeitsmarktrente)
The condition must last at least 6 months (§43 Abs. 2 SGB VI)
The DRV decides on the basis of a medical report (medizinisches Gutachten)
On rejection — an objection (Widerspruch) within 1 month

content.text: Two things matter for entitlement to the EM-Rente: total insurance time and recent contributions. Under §43 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 SGB VI you need a 60-month qualifying period (Wartezeit) and 36 months of compulsory contributions (Pflichtbeiträge) in the last 5 years before the reduced earning capacity (Erwerbsminderung) began.

items: 60 months of total insurance time (qualifying period of 5 years, Wartezeit von 5 Jahren)
36 months of compulsory contributions (Pflichtbeiträge) in the last 5 years before the insured event (Versicherungsfall)
Counted: employment, self-employment with compulsory insurance, sick pay (Krankengeld), ALG I, child-raising periods (Erziehungszeiten; up to 3 years per child)
Not counted: a mini-job (Minijob) without opt-in, years without contributions, long-term ALG II before 2011
Early fulfilment of the qualifying period (Vorzeitige Wartezeiterfüllung) — for accidents at work, under §53 SGB VI
Young people with under 5 years of contributions are usually not entitled to EM-Rente at all — this is the main argument for a private BU

content.text: If you have periods without contributions, check your insurance record (Versicherungsverlauf) with the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung). An account clarification (Kontenklärung) will help recover missed periods of school, training and child-raising (Schul-, Studien- und Erziehungszeiten).

steps.title: How the amount of the EM-Rente is calculated

content.text: The EM-Rente formula is the same as for the regular pension: pension points (Entgeltpunkte) × access factor (Zugangsfaktor) × pension-type factor (Rentenartfaktor) × current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert). The current pension value is 40,79€ per pension point (until 30.06.2026) and rises to 42,52€ from 01.07.2026 (pension adjustment, Rentenanpassung +4,24%).

The main difference is the attribution period (Zurechnungszeit) under §59 SGB VI: it is counted as if you had continued earning an average income up to the standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze). For new EM-Rente recipients whose pension starts in 2026, the attribution period runs to age 66 years 3 months (the threshold rises in stages to 67).

items: Pension-type factor (Rentenartfaktor): 1.0 for full EM, 0.5 for partial EM
Access factor (Zugangsfaktor): 0.892–1.0 (a deduction of 0.3% for each month before age 65, maximum 10.8%)
The attribution period (Zurechnungszeit) counts future years as average pension points
Current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert): 40,79€ per pension point until 30.06.2026, from 01.07.2026 — 42,52€ (+4,24%)
The average full EM-Rente for new cases — a rough figure ≈ 950–1100€ gross (check current numbers with the DRV)
Tax: deferred taxation (nachgelagerte Besteuerung) under §22 EStG (taxable share 83% for 2026 cases)
Health and long-term-care contributions (KV+PV) ≈ 11% of the EM-Rente

content.text: The EM-Rente is not indexed like a salary. If you receive the EM-Rente early, it stays low until it converts into the old-age pension (Regelaltersrente). Check your entitlement to housing benefit (Wohngeld) and basic income support (Grundsicherung; §41 SGB XII) if your income is low.

The application is filed with the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) — in person, by post or online. In parallel the DRV arranges a medical report (medizinisches Gutachten). The process often takes 6–12 months, longer in complex cases.

items: R0100 — the application for an insured person's pension (Antrag auf Versichertenrente)
All medical findings, hospital discharge reports (Krankenhausentlassungsberichte), doctors' letters (Arztbriefe)
A list of current medication
Your current insurance record (Versicherungsverlauf)
Rehabilitation reports (Reha-Berichte), if there were any
Sick notes (Krankschreibungen) for the last 2 years
Details of your employer and last salary

content.text: Via the online service at deutsche-rentenversicherung.de (with eID or Elster), by post, in person at an advice point (Auskunfts- und Beratungsstelle), or through an authorised representative (Versichertenältester). You can bring in a social association (Sozialverband) VdK or SoVD — they help either free of charge or for a membership fee.

The DRV arranges a socio-medical report (Sozialmedizinisches Gutachten) with a consultant doctor. This is the decisive stage: come with all your documents and describe the specific limitations by hours and types of activity. Under §61 SGB I cooperation is mandatory, otherwise a rejection is possible.

The principle "rehabilitation before pension" (Reha vor Rente, §9 SGB IX): the DRV may first refer you to rehabilitation (Reha). Only if it does not restore your capacity to work is the EM-Rente considered.

About 40–50% of first applications are rejected. The objection period (Widerspruch) is 1 month from receipt of the decision (Bescheid). After a rejection of the objection you can file a lawsuit (Klage) at the social court (Sozialgericht; free, no mandatory lawyer). Your chances are better with support from a social association (Sozialverband) or a specialist lawyer.

items: Objection period (Widerspruchsfrist): 1 month under §84 SGG
Lawsuit (Klage) at the social court (Sozialgericht): 1 month after the decision on the objection (Widerspruchsbescheid)
Advice aid (Beratungshilfe) and legal-costs aid (Prozesskostenhilfe) are available on a low income
Side income (Hinzuverdienst) with partial EM: a minimum threshold of 41 527,50€ a year (2026); the individual one may be higher — the DRV publishes it annually
Full EM: up to 20 763,75€ a year (≈1 730€/month) without reduction (2026)
Time-limited vs open-ended EM-Rente (Befristete vs unbefristete EM-Rente): the first is usually for 3 years and requires an extension application (Verlängerungsantrag)
Social associations (Sozialverbände) VdK and SoVD: membership of 6–9€/month gives support with the objection and the lawsuit

content.text: While receiving the EM-Rente it is important to comply with the duty to inform the DRV about changes in your health, income and rehabilitation. Non-compliance can lead to a demand to repay what was paid out (Rückforderung).

costs.label: Filing the Antrag with the DRV
costs.note: Free. All Deutsche Rentenversicherung services for filing require no fee.

costs.label: Membership of the Sozialverband VdK
costs.note: Per month. Provides support with filing, Widerspruch and Klage.

costs.label: Lawyer for Sozialrecht
costs.note: With Beratungshilfe / Prozesskostenhilfe — free or with a minimal contribution. Otherwise — under the RVG.

costs.label: Average volle EM-Rente 2026
costs.note: Gross per month for new cases. Depends on Entgeltpunkte and Zurechnungszeit.
