title: Hausratversicherung: contents insurance
tldr: Household contents insurance (Hausratversicherung) covers movable property in a rented flat or your own home against fire, lightning strike, explosion, water (leaks from pipes), storm, hail, burglary and vandalism. It is based on the VVG and the property-insurance conditions (Versicherungsbedingungen VHB); it is not required by law but is strongly recommended. The cost is 30–150€/year for a typical flat; the sum insured (Versicherungssumme) is calculated as 650€ × m² of living space (rule of thumb). What matters: the waiver of the underinsurance check (Unterversicherungsverzicht), options for bicycles, laptops and valuables, and natural-hazard damage (Elementarschaden; floods, earthquake). Glass breakage (Glasbruch) is a separate option or a separate policy.

content.text: Household contents insurance (Hausratversicherung) is property insurance for movable property (Hausrat) inside the home. The standard risks are defined by the insurance conditions (Versicherungsbedingungen; VHB 2022/2024), which meet the requirements of the VVG.

items: Fire (Feuer): fire, lightning strike, explosion, implosion, aircraft crash
Water from pipes (Leitungswasser): leaks from water pipes, heating, washing/dishwashing machine
Storm/hail (Sturm/Hagel): wind of force 8 on the Beaufort scale (≈62 km/h), hail
Burglary (Einbruchdiebstahl): burglary, robbery (Raub)
Vandalism (Vandalismus) after a break-in

Optional: bicycle theft (Fahrraddiebstahl; external cover, Außenversicherung); natural-hazard damage (Elementarschaden; flood, earthquake, landslide); glass breakage (Glasbruch); overvoltage damage (Überspannungsschaden)
Does not cover: simple theft without a break-in (on the street, in a café), damage to the building (that is buildings insurance, Wohngebäudeversicherung)

content.text: The sum insured (Versicherungssumme) must match the full replacement value of the property (the new value, Neuwert). If it is set too low, the insurer can apply underinsurance (Unterversicherung) under §75 VVG and reduce the payout proportionally.

items: Rule of thumb: 650€ × m² of living space (for an average household)
Example: 70 m² → sum insured ≈ 45,500€
An alternative is an exact calculation based on a room-by-room inventory
Always insist on the waiver of the underinsurance check (Unterversicherungsverzicht) — the insurer waives the check for under-valuation
Sub-limits: valuables (Wertsachen) are often covered only up to 20% of the sum insured; cash and documents have separate limits
Valuables (Wertsachen) in a safe (Tresor): a higher limit
External cover (Aussenversicherung): usually 10–25% of the sum insured and up to 3–6 months

content.text: When buying expensive equipment (cameras, laptops, bicycles worth more than 1000€) check the sub-limits. You often need separate tariff extensions or a specialised policy (for example bicycle insurance, Fahrradversicherung).

Since 2024 there has been active debate in Germany about making natural-hazard insurance (Elementarschadenversicherung) compulsory because of more frequent floods (the Ahr valley, Ahrtal 2021). As of 2026 this is still an optional extension.

items: Natural-hazard damage (Elementarschaden) covers: flooding (Überschwemmung), backflow in pipes (Rückstau), earthquake, landslide, avalanche, snow pressure, volcanic eruption
Flood-risk zoning (ZÜRS-Geo): 4 flood-risk zones — the premium depends on the zone of your address
Glass-breakage insurance (Glasbruchversicherung): damage to window panes, glass-ceramic hobs, sometimes shower cubicles
Bicycle theft (Fahrraddiebstahl): important in cities; usually with a limit of 1–5% of the sum insured
Overvoltage damage (Überspannungsschaden): damage to equipment from a thunderstorm — usually included in newer tariffs
Loss of keys (Schlüsselverlust) for the flat or shared building keys
Gross negligence (Grobe Fahrlässigkeit): check whether the insurer waives the reduction of the payout (Kürzung) in case of gross negligence (a window left open when away)

steps.title: What to do in a claim

content.text: Under §82 VVG the policyholder must comply with their obligations (Obliegenheiten): report the event without delay, minimise the damage, leave the scene unchanged until it is recorded, and provide evidence.

In case of a break-in, robbery or vandalism — call 110 at once and obtain a police report (Strafanzeige) with a reference number. For fire, a water leak or damage caused by neighbours — document it too.

items: Photos and video of all damaged items and places
A list of stolen/damaged items with an approximate value
Receipts, warranties, photos from before the incident (it helps to keep an inventory list, Inventarliste)
Witnesses' contact details
Do not throw away remnants before agreeing with the insurer

content.text: Via the online form, by phone or by post within 7 days (the exact deadline is in the insurance conditions, Versicherungsbedingungen). State the claim number (Schadensnummer), a description, the amount, and attach the documents. The insurer may send a claims adjuster (Schadensregulierer) to assess it.
Do not sign full settlement of the claim before checking the full amount. In a dispute — the insurance ombudsman (Versicherungsombudsmann; free) or a lawyer for insurance law (Versicherungsrecht).

costs.label: Hausratversicherung — annual premium
costs.note: For a typical flat of 60–100 m². Depends on the region (Tarifzone under ZÜRS), Selbstbeteiligung and options.

costs.label: Elementarschaden extension
costs.note: Extra per year. Depends heavily on the ZÜRS zone: minimal in Zone 1, noticeably higher in Zone 4.

costs.label: Fahrraddiebstahl-Erweiterung
costs.note: Per year. For a bicycle worth more than 1000€ a separate Fahrradversicherung is often more worthwhile.

costs.label: Selbstbeteiligung per claim
costs.note: Optional. Premium reduction if you accept an SB of 150–500€.

title: Requesting a Rentenauskunft
tldr: The pension statement (Rentenauskunft) is an official statement from the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) about your pension entitlements: current pension points (Entgeltpunkte), a pension forecast if your income stays the same, and your insurance record (Versicherungsverlauf). From age 55 it is sent automatically every 3 years (§109 SGB VI); before that, from age 27, a shorter pension information (Renteninformation) arrives annually. You can request the pension statement early through the online service at deutsche-rentenversicherung.de (with eID, Elster or a DRV login) or by post. It is free. In parallel it is useful to carry out an account clarification (Kontenklärung; V0100): to check and confirm all periods (studies, children, unemployment, work abroad).

content.text: Many people confuse two DRV documents: the pension information (Renteninformation; from age 27, annual, brief) and the pension statement (Rentenauskunft; from age 55 automatically every 3 years, detailed). Both are based on §109 SGB VI.

items: Pension information (Renteninformation): from age 27, ≥5 years of insurance time, a brief forecast; annual
Pension statement (Rentenauskunft): from age 55 automatically, or on request earlier; the full insurance record (Versicherungsverlauf)
Both documents show: current pension points (Entgeltpunkte), a forecast of the full old-age pension (volle Altersrente) at 67
The forecast is given in 2 variants: taking today's contributions into account and with inflation
Does not include: bAV, Riester, private pensions, inheritance
The insurance record (Versicherungsverlauf) is a separate document listing all contribution periods
Requesting the pension statement (Rentenauskunft) before age 55 is recommended at least once for the account clarification (Kontenklärung)

steps.title: Requesting it via the online service

content.text: Since 2020 the DRV has offered a full online service (Online-Service) at deutsche-rentenversicherung.de. Authentication is via your ID card (Personalausweis) with the eID function, an Elster certificate (Elster-Zertifikat) or a DRV login (DRV-Login; an activation letter by post).

items: Go to deutsche-rentenversicherung.de → online services (Online-Dienste) → registration (Registrierung)
Choose a method: eID, Elster, or a DRV activation letter (DRV-Aktivierungsbrief) by post
Enter your insurance number (Versicherungsnummer; from a payslip or an old DRV letter)
Confirm your identity and activate the account
The activation code by post arrives within 5–10 working days

content.text: After logging into the online service: "Renten- und Auskunftsservice" → "Rentenauskunft beantragen". Choose the format (Vollständig, with or without the insurance record), state a reason (often a required field, Pflichtfeld) and send the request.

The document usually arrives by post within 4–8 weeks. In your account, the insurance record (Versicherungsverlauf) is available online at any time. Save the PDF — you will need it for the account clarification (Kontenklärung) and when applying for your pension.
There is no "DRV app" with full functionality — be wary of third-party apps. The official service is only at deutsche-rentenversicherung.de.

An account clarification (Kontenklärung) is a full audit of your insurance account. The DRV offers it to all insured people from age 27 (application V0100). The aim is to make sure that all periods (work, studies, military service, children, unemployment, work abroad) are recorded.

items: V0100 — the application for an account clarification (Antrag auf Kontenklärung); can be filed online or by post
Attach: employment records/work documents (Arbeitspapiere), school and university certificates, children's birth certificates, your military service book, documents on work abroad
Creditable periods (Anrechnungszeiten): school after age 17, university up to 8 semesters (3 years credited)
Consideration period (Berücksichtigungszeit) per child: up to 10 years (studies, unemployment)
Child-raising periods (Kindererziehungszeiten): 3 years of pension points per child born from 1992
Work abroad: V0800 to confirm foreign insurance time (EU, treaty countries)
After the account clarification the insurance record becomes binding (Versicherungsverlauf 'verbindlich'): it can only be challenged with new documents

content.text: The earlier the account clarification, the easier it is to recover documents. With time, schools close, employers disappear and foreign systems are restructured. Ideally do it before age 35.

The document contains many numbers, some of which are misleading. The key fields are the current pension points (Entgeltpunkte), the forecasts with/without inflation, and the insurance record (Versicherungsverlauf).

items: Current pension points (Aktuelle Entgeltpunkte): how many 'pension points' you have already accrued

Qualifying period (Wartezeit): whether you have reached 5 years (for any pension), 35 years (for the old-age pension for long-term insured persons, Altersrente für langjährig Versicherte), 45 years (especially long-term insured, besonders langjährig, without a deduction from age 63–65)
Forecast without growth (Prognose ohne Steigerung): the pension if you stop working now
Forecast with 1%/2% growth (Prognose mit Steigerung 1%/2%): the pension assuming growth in the pension value (Rentenwert)
Accrued entitlement (Erworbene Anwartschaft): your current entitlement in euros (pension points × current pension value)
Gaps (Lücken) in the insurance record (Versicherungsverlauf): periods without contributions — potentially closable
Gross vs net: the document shows gross; deduct tax + health and long-term-care contributions (KV/PV) ≈ 11–15%

content.text: The forecast is given in nominal euros without purchasing power. Your real pension in 30 years will be lower — be sure to top it up with a bAV and/or a private pension.

costs.label: Requesting a Rentenauskunft
costs.note: Free for all insured people. Can be requested repeatedly.

costs.label: Kontenklärung V0100
costs.note: Free. Support is provided by the DRV Auskunfts- und Beratungsstellen (also free).

costs.label: eID function of the Personalausweis
costs.note: Already included in new cards since 2010. PIN activation at the Bürgeramt is free; a PIN change costs 6€.

costs.label: Consultation with an independent Rentenberater
costs.note: Per hour. Not to be confused with the DRV Beratungsstellen (free).

title: Entgeltpunkte: how the pension is calculated
tldr: The state pension in Germany is calculated by the formula: pension points (Entgeltpunkte) × access factor (Zugangsfaktor) × pension-type factor (Rentenartfaktor) × current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert; §64 SGB VI). For a year of work with an average salary (the average annual earnings, Durchschnittsentgelt 50 493€ in 2025, 51 944€ in 2026) you earn 1.0 pension point; half the average → 0.5 points. The current pension value is 40,79€ per point until 30.06.2026, and from 01.07.2026 — 42,52€. The contribution ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) for 2026 (single, West/East) is 101 400€/year (8 450€/month) — above this amount no contributions are made. The standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze) is 67 for those born from 1964; an early pension comes with a deduction (Abschlag) of 0.3%/month. Extra points are credited for children (child-raising period, Kindererziehungszeit), caring for relatives and military service (Wehrdienst).

steps.title: The pension formula under §64 SGB VI

content.text: The monthly pension is calculated by a clear formula set out in §64 SGB VI: monthly pension = pension points (Entgeltpunkte) × access factor (Zugangsfaktor) × pension-type factor (Rentenartfaktor) × current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert). Each multiplier reflects a particular aspect of your pension history.

items: Pension points (Entgeltpunkte, EP) — how many 'pension points' you have accrued over your whole life
Access factor (Zugangsfaktor) — adjusts for early/deferred retirement (1.0 at the standard retirement age; −0.3% for each month early; +0.5% for each month later)

Pension-type factor (Rentenartfaktor) — the type of pension (§67 SGB VI): 1.0 old-age pension, 0.25 small widow's pension (kleine Witwenrente), 0.55 large widow's pension (große Witwenrente), 0.1 half-orphan's pension (Halbwaisenrente), 0.2 full-orphan's pension (Vollwaisenrente)
Current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert, aRW) — the price of 1 point in euros; 40,79€ until 30.06.2026, from 01.07.2026 — 42,52€
Example: 45 EP × 1.0 × 1.0 × 42,52€ = 1 913€ gross monthly pension (at the value from 01.07.2026)
Tax: deferred taxation (nachgelagerte Besteuerung; for 2026 cases — 83% is taxable)
Social contributions: ~11% in health and long-term-care contributions (KV+PV) is deducted

content.text: The main source of pension points (Entgeltpunkte) is paid work with compulsory contributions (Pflichtbeiträge). For a calendar year you earn points by the formula: your gross / the average annual earnings (Durchschnittsentgelt).

items: Average annual earnings (Durchschnittsentgelt): 50 493€/year (2025, provisional), 51 944€/year (2026); under §69 SGB VI
1 year on the average salary = 1.0 EP
A salary below 50% of the average → max 1.5 × your EP thanks to the basic pension (Grundrente; pension based on minimum income, Rente nach Mindesteinkommen, §262 SGB VI)
Limit: the contribution ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) for 2026 (single) 101 400€/year → max ≈ 1.95 EP/year
Compulsory contribution rate (Pflichtbeitragssatz) 2026: 18.6% of gross (9.3% employee + 9.3% employer)
The self-employed: voluntary or compulsory contributions (the artists' social insurance fund KSK, craftsmen), with possible maximum and minimum contributions (Höchst- und Mindestbeiträge)
A mini-job (Minijob): 3.6% from the employee or a possible exemption (Befreiung); yields small EP

content.text: Besides paid work there are a number of sources of pension points (EP) that are important for women, parents and those who care for relatives.

items: Child-raising period (Kindererziehungszeit, §56 SGB VI): 3 years per child born from 1992 (= 3 EP); 2.5 years for those born before 1992 ('mothers' pension II', Mütterrente II). Mothers' pension III (Mütterrente III) raises them to 3 years from 01.01.2027 (payouts from 2028)
During the child-raising period it is counted as if the parent had earned an average salary
Consideration period (Berücksichtigungszeit): up to 10 years of extra protection against gaps (Lücken)
Caring for relatives (Pflege von Angehörigen): when caring for at least 10 h/week — EP depending on the care recipient's care level (Pflegegrad)
Creditable period (Anrechnungszeit) for studies: 3 years maximum (it used to count as a source of EP; since 2009 — only as a qualifying period, Wartezeit)
Military service (Wehrdienst), alternative service (Zivildienst), federal voluntary service (Bundesfreiwilligendienst): EP are credited by the state
Sick pay (Krankengeld), ALG I, illness: counted with EP roughly matching the previous income
ALG II / basic income support (Bürgergeld): since 2011 no EP are credited, only a creditable period (Anrechnungszeit)

content.text: If you had these periods — be sure to file V0100 (account clarification, Kontenklärung). Without confirmation by documents the DRV may not count them automatically.

The standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze, §35 SGB VI) rises from 65 for those born before 1947 to 67 for those born from 1964. Early retirement is possible via the old-age pension for long-term insured persons (Altersrente für langjährig Versicherte; 35 years of service, from age 63) or for especially long-term insured persons (besonders langjährig Versicherte; 45 years, without a deduction, Abschlag).

items: Old-age pension (Regelaltersrente): age 67, 1.0 access factor, 5 years qualifying period
Old-age pension for long-term insured persons (Altersrente für langjährig Versicherte): from 63, requires 35 years; a deduction (Abschlag) of 0.3%/month up to the standard retirement age (max 14.4%)

Old-age pension for especially long-term insured persons (Altersrente für besonders langjährig Versicherte): 45 years of service, without a deduction from 64 (for those born in 1964); the threshold changes
Old-age pension for people with a severe disability (Altersrente für schwerbehinderte Menschen, §37 SGB VI): from 62, with a degree of disability (GdB) ≥50, max deduction 10.8%
Deferring the pension (Hinausschieben): +0.5%/month = +6%/year (a 1.06 supplement for 1 year)
Flexible pension (Flexirente) since 2017 — you can draw part of the pension and keep working
Side income (Hinzuverdienst) since 2023 — the limit has been removed for the old-age pension and full pensions (Vollrenten)

content.text: Let's take typical scenarios and do the maths. All figures are gross per month, based on a current pension value (aRW) of 42,52€ per point (the value from 01.07.2026).

items: Scenario A: 40 years of work on the average salary → 40 EP × 42,52€ = 1 701€/month gross
Scenario B: 45 years on the average + 1 child (3 EP) → 48 EP × 42,52€ = 2 041€/month
Scenario C: 30 years at 0.7 of the average + 3 years of raising × 2 children → (30 × 0.7 + 6) × 42,52€ = 27 × 42,52 = 1 148€/month
Scenario D: 40 years at the contribution ceiling (BBG) → 40 × 1.95 × 42,52€ = 3 317€/month gross (close to the maximum pension, Höchstrente)
Scenario E: early at 63 (with 35 years) → −14.4% deduction → 40 EP × 0.856 × 42,52€ = 1 456€
Scenario F: defer until 70 → +18% supplement → 40 EP × 1.18 × 42,52€ = 2 007€
From the gross figure deduct ~11% in health and long-term-care contributions (KV+PV) and income tax (often 0–10% for pensioners)

content.text: As of 2026 the average full old-age pension (volle Altersrente) is around 1,500–1,600€ gross. This is often below the basic-income-support threshold (Grundsicherungsschwelle). That is why a bAV, an ETF savings plan (ETF-Sparplan) and savings are strongly recommended as a supplement.

costs.label: Pflichtbeitrag Rentenversicherung
costs.note: 18.6% gross in 2026, a 50/50 split with the employer. Not above the single Beitragsbemessungsgrenze of 101 400€/year (8 450€/month); West/East unified from 2025.

costs.label: Freiwillige Beiträge for the self-employed
costs.note: Per month. Minimum 112,16€/month (Mindestbeitrag 2026), maximum 1 571,70€/month (Höchstbeitrag under the BBG).

costs.label: Ausgleichszahlung for an early pension
costs.note: Possible under §187a SGB VI — to offset the Abschlag with a one-off payment. The amount depends on the Abschlag and your age.

title: Russian pension while living in Germany
tldr: A Russian pension can be paid to people residing in Germany, on the basis of the 1973 agreement between the USSR and the FRG (as amended) and the provisions of Federal Law 400 'On insurance pensions' and Federal Law 166 'On state pension provision'. Since 2015 most categories must annually confirm that they are still alive, through the Russian consulate or a notary. A pension in Germany does not cancel the Russian one — Russia and Germany have no agreement on totalising contribution periods (important: the 1973 agreement covered limited categories). Taxation: the Russian pension is taxed in Germany under §22 EStG; in Russia it is exempt under Art. 217 of the Tax Code. You need a Russian settlement account or an account at a foreign bank (after notifying the Federal Tax Service). Apply to the SFR via Gosuslugi, in person or by post.

content.text: In 1973 the USSR and the FRG signed an agreement on social security (it entered into force in 1975). It covered a limited category — ethnic Germans and certain others. After the collapse of the USSR Russia continued as the successor state, but its position has shifted over time.

Since 2015, under Federal Law 400 'On insurance pensions' (in force from 01.01.2015), the pension is paid to all categories of recipients regardless of country of residence, provided they annually confirm that they are alive. This applies to insurance pensions earned in Russia.

items: Old-age insurance pension — paid abroad under Federal Law 400
Disability pension — paid abroad
Survivor's pension — paid abroad
Social pension (Federal Law 166) — NOT paid abroad
State long-service pension (military, civil servants) — paid; check the regime
Funded pension — paid; a lump sum or a fixed-term one under Federal Law 360
The 1973 USSR-FRG agreement applies to limited categories and is now largely outdated

content.text: After 2022 the practical side of payments abroad has become more difficult because of sanctions: SWIFT restrictions, problems with transfers. Check the current procedure with the SFR before applying.

steps.title: No agreement on totalising contribution periods

content.text: Unlike the agreements between Russia and Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Belarus, Russia and Germany have NO bilateral agreement in force on the mutual recognition of contribution periods for pension purposes. This means that Russian and German contribution periods are counted separately.

items: Russian contribution periods are not counted towards the German pension (Rente)
German contribution periods are not counted towards the Russian pension
Each country awards its own pension under its own rules
The 1973 USSR-FRG agreement covered specific categories (late resettlers, Aussiedler) and has largely lost its relevance

Late resettlers (Aussiedler) under the foreign pensions act (Fremdrentengesetz, FRG) could receive a German pension for Russian contribution periods until the 1990s — this is no longer available to today's newcomers
For the German pension it is important to earn at least 5 years in Germany (qualifying period, Wartezeit under §50 SGB VI)
Russian contribution periods are needed to receive the Russian insurance pension (min. 15 years of insurance time in 2026)

content.text: Do not trust intermediaries who promise to 'transfer' your Russian contribution period to the German system. For most categories this is impossible.
Applying for a Russian pension from Germany is possible in several ways. Since 2022 some online services have been unavailable to users in the EU, so it is useful to have several options.

If you have an active Gosuslugi account with a verified profile and access from Germany (via VPN or other lawful means), you can apply online. The service: 'Establishing a pension' → choose the type of pension → upload documents.

items.title: 2. Via the Russian consulate in Germany

items: Consulates: Berlin, Bonn, Hamburg, Munich, Leipzig, Frankfurt
Book an appointment via rusconsulboncn.org / rusconsulberlin.org or similar sites
Documents: application, Russian passport, SNILS, employment record book/personal account statement, salary certificates
The consulate forwards it to the SFR according to jurisdiction
Processing time — up to 3 months after the SFR receives it

items.title: 3. Via an authorised person in Russia

content.text: Have a notarised power of attorney drawn up (in Germany — via the consulate or with an apostille). The authorised person files the application with the SFR at the place of your former registration / last place of work in Russia.
By registered letter with a list of contents to the Department for the Pension Provision of Persons Residing Abroad (SFR, Moscow). Confirm the address at sfr.gov.ru.

To continue receiving the pension abroad you must annually confirm that the recipient is alive. This is a requirement of Russian Government Decree No. 1386 of 17.12.2014 and the provisions of Federal Law 400.

items: Deadline: annually, no later than 31 December of the year following the year of the previous confirmation
Where: the Russian consulate, a German notary (with translation and apostille), a Russian diplomatic mission
Document: an act of personal appearance (a form approved by the SFR)
Alternative: appearing in person at a territorial body of the SFR in Russia
The document is forwarded to the SFR; payments are suspended if the deadline is missed
Resumption: after a renewed confirmation, with a back-payment for the suspended period

content.text: If you miss the confirmation, payments are suspended from 1 January of the following year. Resumption is possible but with a delay of 2–4 months. Set a reminder in your calendar.
The pension is paid in roubles. The ways to receive it depend on the current sanctions situation; check before applying.

items: To a Russian bank account (Sberbank, VTB, etc.) — the most stable
To a foreign account — theoretically possible, in practice complicated by sanctions
When credited to a foreign account — mandatory notice to the Russian Federal Tax Service about opening it
Withdrawing funds: with a Mir bank card (where accepted), by transfers to relatives, via Russian intermediaries
In Germany: the Russian pension is taxable income under §22 EStG (other income, sonstige Einkünfte, foreign pensions, ausländische Renten)

Under the 1996 Russia-FRG double taxation agreement (DBA) the pension was, as a rule, taxed in the country of residence (Germany); however, from 08.08.2023 Russia suspended the relevant articles of the DBA — check the current status
In Russia the pension is exempt from personal income tax under Art. 217 of the Tax Code
Declaring in Germany: Anlage R-AUS in the annual tax return (Steuererklärung)

content.text: Note: by a note of 08.08.2023 Russia suspended the operation of Art. 5–22 and 24 of the 1996 Russia-FRG double taxation agreement (DBA); from 01.01.2024 German taxation rights are governed by national law (the act against tax havens, Steueroasen-Abwehrgesetz) rather than the DBA. Because of this the exemption 'taxed only in the country of residence' is no longer guaranteed — be sure to check the current status with a tax adviser (Steuerberater) for international taxation.

costs.label: Filing the application with the SFR
costs.note: Free. All SFR services for awarding a pension are without a fee.

costs.label: Consular fee for certifying the act of personal appearance
costs.note: Depends on the consulate. Alternative — a German notary with translation and apostille (50–150€).

costs.label: Notarisation and apostille in Germany
costs.note: Notary + Apostille + sworn translation. Needed for documents in Russia.

costs.label: Steuerberater for declaring a foreign pension
costs.note: Per year, if included in the Steuererklärung. Optional, you can file yourself via Elster.

sources.title: SFR: How to receive a Russian pension while living abroad
Russian Government Decree No. 1386 of 17.12.2014 — procedure for payments to persons abroad
Agreement between the USSR and the FRG on social security of 24.05.1973
§22 EStG — Besteuerung sonstiger Einkünfte, ausländische Renten

title: Privathaftpflicht: personal liability
tldr: Personal liability insurance (Privathaftpflichtversicherung) is the most important voluntary insurance in Germany, covering damage to third parties caused by your fault (§823 BGB). It protects against claims of millions of euros for injuries, property damage and financial losses. The cost is 50–100€/year for a family; cover should be at least 5 million, and 10–50 million euros is recommended. It covers a spouse and children on a single policy (family tariff, Familientarif). It does not cover: damage at work (professional liability insurance, Berufshaftpflicht), driving a car (motor liability, Kfz-Haftpflicht), deliberate acts. Important options: cover for unrecoverable claims (Forderungsausfalldeckung), loss of keys (Schlüsselverlust), internet liability (Internet-Haftpflicht), children incapable of tort (deliktunfähige Kinder).

content.text: Under §823 BGB anyone who intentionally or negligently infringes another person's right (life, health, property, freedom) is obliged to make good the damage. This liability is unlimited — a claim can run to tens of millions if you cause serious harm to health.

Unlike health insurance (Krankenversicherung) or motor liability (Kfz-Haftpflicht), personal liability insurance (Privathaftpflicht) is not required by law, but it is strongly recommended by all consumer advice centres (Verbraucherzentralen). About 85% of households in Germany have this policy.

items: Covers harm to health (Personenschaden), property damage (Sachschaden), financial loss (Vermögensschaden)
Classic examples: you knock down a pedestrian on your bike → disability → a claim of 2 million euros
You flood the neighbour → flat repairs → 30 thousand euros
Your child breaks a friend's TV → 1500 euros
Without insurance — liability from your personal assets for life
Seizure of wages (Pfändung) within the protected-income limits (Pfändungsfreigrenzen) — deductions can continue right up to retirement
A premium of 50–100€/year against a potential claim of millions of euros

steps.title: What it covers and what it does not

content.text: The standard insurance conditions (Versicherungsbedingungen, PHB) define cover and exclusions. Read them carefully — cheap tariffs often save on key options.

items: Covers: damage to third parties (not to your family members on the same policy)
Covers: guests in your flat, friends, passers-by
Covers: damage in a rented flat (damage to rented property, Mietsachschäden) — optional, important to check
Covers: sport (football, skiing, tennis, riding), if not professional
Covers: an everyday bicycle (but not an e-bike >25 km/h)
Does NOT cover: driving a car, motorcycle, moped (that is motor liability, Kfz-Haftpflicht)
Does NOT cover: professional activity (that is professional liability insurance, Berufshaftpflicht)
Does NOT cover: deliberately causing harm (intent, Vorsatz)
Does NOT cover: damage caused to your family members within the same policy
Does NOT cover: animals other than small pets (for dogs — separate dog liability insurance, Hundehaftpflicht, compulsory in some federal states)

content.text: The difference between a basic and a good tariff lies not in the premium (often 20–40€/year) but in the options. These extensions often decide whether the insurer pays out in a specific situation.

items: Sum insured (Versicherungssumme) of at least 5 million €; 10–50 million is recommended (the premium barely rises)

Cover for unrecoverable claims (Forderungsausfalldeckung): if someone causes harm to YOU and cannot pay — your insurance pays out (important in an accident with an uninsured driver or a penniless troublemaker)

Children incapable of tort (Deliktunfähige Kinder): children under 7 (10 on the road) are not liable under §828 BGB; parents too are often not at fault if they met their duty of supervision (Aufsichtspflicht) — but the insurer pays out as a goodwill gesture
Loss of keys (Schlüsselverlust): damage from losing flat/work keys (replacing locks, master keys) — cover up to 50,000€
Internet and cyber damage (Internet- und Cyberschäden): damage from a hacked account, mistaken transfers, copyright infringements
Damage to rented property (Mietsachschäden): damage to the furniture and building of a rented flat/hotel; standard 100,000+€
Damage during a favour (Gefälligkeitsschäden): damage while helping for free (you helped a friend move and broke a vase)
Gradual damage (Allmählichkeitsschäden): gradual damage from a leak, mould, etc.
Excess (Selbstbeteiligung) of 150€ — reduces the premium by ~10–20%, sensible for most people

content.text: Do not buy a policy with cover of 1–3 million €. Serious injury to a pedestrian with lifelong disability easily reaches 5–10 million. The difference in premium is minimal.

steps.title: Family tariff and filing a claim

content.text: A single family tariff (Familientarif) covers spouses in a marriage/registered partnership and children. Children who are studying (school, vocational training, first degree) are covered until they finish their first education or until age 25–30. Unmarried partnerships are covered if living together (a marriage-like cohabitation, eheähnliche Lebensgemeinschaft).

items: Family tariff (Familientarif): 1 policy → spouses + minor children + students in their first education
A surcharge of ~20% on the single tariff (Single-Tarif)
On divorce — separate policies for each
Children after their first degree / vocational training need their own policy
Au-pairs, domestic workers — separate rules
Filing a claim: notify the insurer no later than 7 days
Do NOT pay and do NOT admit fault to the injured party without the insurer's consent
Keep witnesses' contact details, photos, evidence
In a dispute with the insurer — the insurance ombudsman (Versicherungsombudsmann) or a lawyer for insurance law (Versicherungsrecht)
The limitation period (Verjährung) for claims under §195 BGB — usually 3 years

content.text: If you receive a claim from the injured party, IMMEDIATELY pass it to your insurer and sign NOTHING yourself. The insurer negotiates in your interests and pays for a lawyer if necessary.

costs.label: Privathaftpflicht — Single-Tarif
costs.note: Per year for a single policy with cover of 10+ million €.

costs.label: Privathaftpflicht — Familientarif
costs.note: Per year. Covers spouses and children until they finish their first education.

costs.label: Hundehaftpflicht (separate)
costs.note: Per year for a dog. Compulsory in Berlin, Hamburg, Thuringia, Saxony, Lower Saxony, Schleswig-Holstein and others.

costs.label: Selbstbeteiligung
costs.note: Optional. An SB of 150€ reduces the premium by 10–20%.

sources.title: Verbraucherzentrale: Private Haftpflichtversicherung — ein absolutes Muss für alle!

title: Rechtsschutzversicherung: legal expenses insurance
tldr: Legal expenses insurance (Rechtsschutzversicherung) covers the costs of a lawyer, court, experts and part of the opponent's costs if you lose. It is modular: private (Privat-), traffic (Verkehrs-), employment (Berufs-/Arbeits-) and tenancy (Miet-Rechtsschutz). It costs roughly 150-400 €/year depending on the modules and the excess (Selbstbeteiligung). The key catch is the waiting period (Wartezeit, usually ~3 months): disputes that arose before the end of this period, or that were already brewing when the contract was signed, are not covered. Take it out in advance, before a conflict.

steps.title: What it covers and which modules there are

content.text: Legal expenses insurance (Rechtsschutzversicherung) takes on the financial risk of a legal dispute: your lawyer's fee, court fees, the cost of experts and witnesses, and — if you lose — the opposing party's costs. This does not mean you will win the case, but you will not be ruined by the costs. The insurance is built from modules, and you only pay for the ones you need.

items: Private insurance (Privat-Rechtsschutz) — private disputes (purchases, contracts, neighbours)
Traffic insurance (Verkehrs-Rechtsschutz) — accidents, fines, car disputes
Employment insurance (Berufs-/Arbeits-Rechtsschutz) — employment conflicts, dismissals
Tenancy insurance (Miet-/Wohnungs-Rechtsschutz) — disputes with a landlord/tenant
Covered: lawyer's fee, court costs (Gerichtskosten), experts, the opponent's costs if you lose
Free telephone legal advice is often included

content.text: The most common reason for refusing payment is the waiting period (Wartezeit) and the clause on when the dispute arose. For most modules a waiting period of about 3 months applies: the insured event must occur AFTER it ends. Disputes that were already running or clearly brewing when the contract was signed are not covered — otherwise people would take out a policy right when a conflict had already started.

The main takeaway: take out legal expenses insurance (Rechtsschutz) in advance, in calm times. If you have already received a rent increase, a notice of dismissal or a fine — for THAT dispute the insurance most likely will not work. The ~3-month waiting period is typical for tenancy, employment and general disputes; for accidents and a number of cases it is often absent. The exact periods are in the conditions (Versicherungsbedingungen).

items: Waiting period (Wartezeit) ~3 months — typical for tenancy, employment and private insurance
Traffic insurance (Verkehrs-Rechtsschutz) and some cases — often without a waiting period
NOT covered: prior/brewing disputes (pre-contractual nature, Vorvertraglichkeit)
Usually excluded: family/inheritance law (often only advice), intent, business disputes of the self-employed without a separate module
An excess (Selbstbeteiligung) of ~150-300 € per case reduces the premium

steps.title: How to choose and what it costs

content.text: The price depends on the set of modules, the size of the excess and the family composition. A rough figure is 150-400 € a year. A higher excess (Selbstbeteiligung) lowers the annual premium but increases your costs in each case. Compare not only the price but also the conditions: the size of the cover (Deckungssumme), free choice of lawyer and the scope of employment disputes.

items: Identify your risks: do you have a car, a tenancy, salaried work
A family tariff often covers a spouse and children
Choose the excess (Selbstbeteiligung) deliberately (0 € is more expensive, 300 € is cheaper)
Check the free choice of lawyer (freie Anwaltswahl)
Compare independent tests (Stiftung Warentest) before buying
Remember: membership of a tenants' association (Mieterverein) often already includes tenancy insurance (Miet-Rechtsschutz)

costs.label: Rechtsschutzversicherung (per year)
costs.note: Depends on the number of modules, the family and the size of the excess.

costs.label: Selbstbeteiligung per case
costs.note: Optional; the higher it is, the cheaper the annual premium.

title: Riester private pension (Riester-Rente): is it worth it
tldr: Riester-Rente is a private pension with a government subsidy: a basic allowance (Zulage) of 175€/year + 300€ per child born from 2008 onwards (185€ for children born before 2008). It is open to people who are mandatorily insured in the state pension scheme (gesetzliche Rentenversicherung; RV-pflichtig), to civil servants (Beamte) and to certain others. To get the full allowance you must contribute 4% of last year's gross income (minus the allowances, with a minimum own contribution of 60€/year, Sockelbeitrag). The downsides: high fees — for signing the contract and for administration (Abschluss- und Verwaltungskosten), often weak returns, inflexibility, and payouts that are fully taxed (deferred taxation, nachgelagerte Besteuerung). There is also a Wohn-Riester variant for housing. The honest take: for many people with one child and a low income the allowances make the maths work, but for childless people on a good income Riester often loses out to a simple ETF portfolio. Run the numbers in a calculator and read the contract costs (Vertragskosten).

steps.title: What Riester is and who is entitled to it

content.text: Riester-Rente is a state-subsidised form of private retirement saving (§§10a, 79 ff. EStG). The state adds a direct allowance (Zulage) to your contributions and/or grants a tax deduction — the tax office (Finanzamt) automatically works out which of the two is more favourable through a comparison test (Günstigerprüfung).

items: Basic allowance (Grundzulage): 175€/year per insured person
Child allowance (Kinderzulage): 300€/year for each child born from 2008 onwards, and 185€ for a child born before 2008
For the full allowance you must contribute 4% of last year's gross income (including the allowances), up to a maximum of 2 100€/year taken into account
Minimum own contribution (Sockelbeitrag): 60€/year
Career-starter bonus (Berufseinsteiger-Bonus): a one-off 200€ for those who sign a contract before the age of 25

content.text: Riester is open to people with a direct entitlement to the allowance (unmittelbar zulageberechtigt): employees and salaried staff who are mandatorily insured in the state pension scheme (gesetzliche Rentenversicherung), recipients of unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld), civil servants (Beamte), military personnel, and parents during a child-raising period (Erziehungszeit; the child's first 3 years). The self-employed and members of the liberal professions (Freiberufler) who do not pay into the pension scheme are usually NOT entitled to Riester — for them there is Rürup (see the separate guide).

Indirect entitlement to the allowance (mittelbar zulageberechtigt): the spouse of someone entitled to Riester can receive their own allowance (Zulage) by signing a separate contract and contributing at least 60€/year. But on divorce, or if the main partner loses their entitlement, the allowance can disappear.

steps.title: Pros, cons and who really benefits from Riester

content.text: Riester has been criticised for decades over its high costs and weak returns. But with the right profile the allowances can outweigh the drawbacks. The main factors are the number of children and the income level.

items: Worth it: families with children — the child allowance (Kinderzulage) of 300€/child sharply raises the share of state support (Förderquote)
Worth it: people on a low gross income — a relatively high share of subsidy for a small own contribution
Worth it: high income + entitlement to a large special-expenses deduction (Sonderausgabenabzug) under §10a EStG (up to 2 100€)
Questionable/not worth it: childless people on a good income — an ETF savings plan (ETF-Sparplan) often delivers more after fees
Downside: the costs for signing the contract and for administration (Abschluss- und Verwaltungskosten) eat into the return, especially with classic pension insurance (klassische Rentenversicherung)
Downside: inflexibility — the money is locked up until retirement; an early exit means paying back all allowances (Zulagen) and tax breaks (Steuervorteile)
Downside: payouts in old age are fully taxed (deferred taxation, nachgelagerte Besteuerung)

content.text: The 100% guarantee on contributions paid in (Beitragsgarantie) sounds safe, but in an era of low interest rates it forces providers to keep the money in low-yield bonds. The real (after-inflation) return on many Riester contracts is close to zero or negative.

A classic Riester policy (Riester-Versicherung) gives a guaranteed annuity but a low return and high costs. The fund-linked version (fondsgebundene; Fonds-Riester) invests in funds/ETFs — more potential, but the contribution guarantee (Beitragsgarantie) caps the equity share.
In terms of fees the cheapest option is a bank savings plan. The downside: these have almost stopped being offered because of low interest rates, and the return is modest too.

Wohn-Riester (§§92a, 92b EStG) lets you use the accumulated capital and allowances to buy or pay off the loan on your own home. The state support (Förderung) is effectively invested in your square metres. The downside: in old age a notional housing-support account (Wohnförderkonto) is taken into account for tax, and you have to pay tax on it.

With Wohn-Riester the home must remain your main residence. Selling it or renting it out without reinvesting in a new home triggers an additional tax assessment from the housing-support account (Wohnförderkonto). Work this out before you buy.

steps.title: How to decide and sign up

items: Calculate the share of state support (Förderquote): the sum of allowances (Zulagen) + the tax break (Steuervorteil), divided by your own contribution
Compare it with the alternative: the same monthly contribution into a broad ETF (MSCI World) with no state subsidy
Ask the provider for the product information sheet (Produktinformationsblatt) with all costs (Kosten; effective costs, Effektivkosten) clearly stated
Check that you contribute exactly 4% of gross income (max 2 100€) for the full allowance — no more, no less
File an application for a permanent allowance (Dauerzulagenantrag) — an automatic yearly claim for the allowance (Zulage), so you don't have to apply by hand each time
Whenever you change employer or income, update your details with the provider so the allowance isn't cut

content.text: If you're unsure, get independent advice at a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale; paid, but without selling you a product) rather than only from an insurance agent (Versicherungsvertreter), who has an interest in the commission for signing the contract (Abschlussprovision).

Don't sign up for Riester just for the "tax saving". If you terminate the contract early (a termination that forfeits the subsidy, förderschädliche Kündigung), you'll have to pay back all allowances (Zulagen) and tax breaks — and the outcome can end up worse than an ordinary savings account.

costs.label: Minimum own contribution for the full Zulage
costs.note: Per year. Sockelbeitrag 60€; for the full allowance — 4% of last year's gross income minus Zulagen, with a maximum of 2 100€ taken into account.

costs.label: Grundzulage
costs.note: Per year per insured person, provided the 4% contribution condition is met.

costs.label: Kinderzulage per child (born from 2008)
costs.note: Per year for each child entitled to Kindergeld; 185€ for children born before 2008.

costs.label: Verbraucherzentrale advice on Riester
costs.note: For an independent assessment of the contract without selling a specific product.

sources.title: Verbraucherzentrale: Riester-Rente — das müssen Sie über die private Altersvorsorge wissen

title: Zahnzusatzversicherung: supplementary dental cover
tldr: Zahnzusatzversicherung is private top-up cover added to statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) for dental treatment. Statutory insurance (GKV) covers only the minimum: fixed allowances (Festzuschüsse) for dentures (Zahnersatz; roughly 60% of the standard option with a bonus booklet) and basic prevention. The top-up cover pays for dentures, implants, high-quality fillings, and sometimes professional teeth cleaning (PZR) and orthodontics. It costs ~10–40€/month depending on the scope and your age. Important: almost all tariffs have a waiting period (Wartezeit; often 8 months) and a tiered limit (Staffelung) — a cap on payouts in the first years. The golden rule: sign up WHILE your teeth are healthy — treatment that has already started or is already known about is not covered (§19 VVG, pre-contractual duty of disclosure, vorvertragliche Anzeigepflicht).

steps.title: What the GKV covers and why you need top-up cover

content.text: Statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung, GKV) pays for teeth on a fixed-allowance system (Festzuschüsse): the allowance is tied to the standard care (Regelversorgung) — the simplest medically adequate option. If you want ceramic, implants or higher-quality dentures (Zahnersatz), you pay the difference yourself, and it can run into several thousand euros.

items: The fixed GKV allowance (GKV-Festzuschuss) covers ~60% of the standard care (Regelversorgung), rising to ~75% with a complete bonus booklet (Bonusheft; 10 years of regular check-ups)
Statutory insurance usually does NOT fund implants (only a fixed allowance, as for classic dentures)
High-quality fillings (composite/inlay, Kunststoff/Inlay, in the back teeth) — partly at your own expense
Professional teeth cleaning (PZR) is almost always not included in statutory insurance
Supplementary dental cover (Zahnzusatz) closes the gap between the fixed allowance and the real cost

content.text: A good supplementary dental tariff reimburses 70–90% (sometimes up to 100% including the fixed allowance) of the cost of dentures and implants — turning a 4 000€ implant bill into a co-payment of a few hundred euros.

steps.title: What the cover pays for and what to look at

items: Dentures (Zahnersatz): crowns, bridges, dentures — the core point of the cover
Implants (Implantate): check the limit on the number and the reimbursement percentage
Tooth preservation (Zahnerhalt): high-quality fillings, root canal treatment (Wurzelbehandlung), gum-disease treatment (Parodontose)
Prevention / professional cleaning (Prophylaxe / PZR): reimbursement of professional cleaning (e.g. 2×/year up to a limit)
Orthodontics (Kieferorthopädie): rare for adults, with separate children's tariffs for kids
Reimbursement percentage: look for tariffs at 80–90%+ including the fixed allowance

content.text: Compare the ratio of reimbursement to limits, not the price. A cheap tariff with 50% reimbursement can end up costing more in a real case than one that's a couple of euros more with 85%.

Pay attention to the maximum limits (Höchstgrenzen; annual/overall reimbursement caps) and to whether the fixed GKV allowance (GKV-Festzuschuss) is counted inside the percentage or on top of it. The wording "90% inklusive Vorleistung GKV" is worse than "90% des Rechnungsbetrags".

Most tariffs have a waiting period (Wartezeit; often up to 8 months) during which there is no payout for planned treatment. The exception is treatment after an accident. Some tariffs advertise "ohne Wartezeit" but offset this with a tough tiered limit (Staffelung).

In the first years there is a cap on total payouts — for example, no more than 1 000€ in year 1, 2 000€ over the first 2 years, and so on. Full coverage usually kicks in from year 4–5. That's why the cover is valuable as protection against future problems, not immediate ones.

items.title: 3. Health questions (Gesundheitsfragen; duty of disclosure, Anzeigepflicht)

content.text: When you sign up you'll be asked about the current state of your teeth: missing teeth, treatment that has started or been recommended, current crowns/dentures. Under §19 VVG you must answer honestly — the insurer won't pay for treatment that is already known about or has started, and it can contest the contract.

The golden rule: take out supplementary dental cover (Zahnzusatz) WHILE your teeth are healthy. Once the dentist has documented the need for dentures (Zahnersatz; a diagnosis of "in need of treatment", behandlungsbedürftig, or an already-issued treatment and cost plan, Heil- und Kostenplan), it's too late — that treatment won't be covered.

costs.label: Monthly Zahnzusatzversicherung premium
costs.note: Depends on age, scope of cover and reimbursement percentage. For older people and tariffs with PZR — closer to the top end.

costs.label: Implant with crown without insurance
costs.note: Per tooth; the GKV-Festzuschuss covers only a small part, the main argument in favour of top-up cover.

costs.label: Professional cleaning (PZR) without insurance
costs.note: Per session; recommended 1–2 times a year.

sources.title: Verbraucherzentrale: Zahnzusatzversicherungen — lohnt sich ein Abschluss?

title: Rettungsdienst: the ambulance service
tldr: Germany has a single emergency number — 112 (free, works across the whole EU, including with no SIM and no credit on your account). Use it to call the fire brigade (Feuerwehr), the ambulance service (Rettungsdienst) and mountain/water rescue. 110 is for the police only. In a city the arrival time of an ambulance (Rettungswagen) is usually 8-15 minutes, and the services and transport are covered 100% by your health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) in a confirmed emergency.

steps.title: What 112 is and how the Rettungsdienst works

content.text: 112 is the single Europe-wide emergency number (Europaweite Notrufnummer), shared by all EU countries. In Germany the call goes to the integrated control centre (Integrierte Leitstelle, ILS) of the federal state or district, and the dispatcher decides who to send: an emergency doctor (Notarzt), an ambulance (Rettungswagen, RTW), a patient transport vehicle (Krankentransport) or the fire brigade. In the big cities (Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, Frankfurt) dispatchers usually speak English; Russian is not guaranteed, but they bring in an interpreter if needed.

items: 112 — free from any mobile, even without a SIM and with no credit
110 — police (Polizei) only; you can also ask them to send an ambulance
The ambulance service (Rettungsdienst) is governed by state laws (the rescue-services law, Rettungsdienstgesetz, of each federal state, Land)
The target arrival time (Hilfsfrist) is usually 8-12 minutes in a city, up to 15 min in rural areas
Transport to hospital is included and is also covered by statutory insurance (GKV)

steps.title: How to call correctly: the 5 W-Fragen

content.text: German dispatchers are trained to work through five "W" questions (5 W-Fragen). Don't hang up first — the dispatcher will end the call once they have all the information. If you don't speak German, say "English please" or "I need a translator" straight away.
The exact address: street, house number, floor, town. If you're in a car on the motorway — the direction and the kilometre marker (Kilometertafel).
Briefly: heart attack (Herzinfarkt), road accident (Verkehrsunfall), fall (Sturz), fire (Brand). Don't go into detail — the dispatcher will ask follow-up questions.

items.title: 3. Wie viele? — How many are injured

content.text: This matters for deciding how many vehicles to send. In a mass road accident a mass-casualty protocol (MANV) is triggered.

Consciousness (conscious? ansprechbar?), breathing (breathing? atmet?), bleeding, chest pain. If the person isn't breathing, the dispatcher will start telephone-guided resuscitation instructions (Telefon-Reanimation).

items.title: 5. Warten auf Rückfragen — Wait for questions

content.text: Stay on the line. In parallel the dispatcher is already sending a crew — while you're talking, the vehicle is on its way.

steps.title: What to do until the ambulance arrives

content.text: Open the building entrance, switch on the lights, and send someone out to the street to meet the crew. At a road accident — put out the warning triangle (Warndreieck) 100 m back, switch on the hazard lights, and wear a high-vis vest (Warnweste). If the casualty isn't breathing, the dispatcher on 112 will dictate the compression rate in real time (100-120/min). Germany runs a bystander-resuscitation campaign (Laienreanimation): even without training, pressing on the breastbone is better than nothing.

Don't confuse 112 and 116 117. 116 117 is the on-call medical service (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst; outpatient care in the evenings and at weekends) for urgent but non-life-threatening cases: high fever, back pain. If life is at risk — call 112.

If you call an ambulance "for nothing" (for example, asking to be taken to hospital for a routine appointment), you may be billed 200-500€ for an unjustified call-out. But when in doubt it's better to call — the penalties for failing to help are far higher.

§323c StGB — failure to render assistance (unterlassene Hilfeleistung). Failing to help (for example, walking past someone lying unconscious) is a criminal offence: a fine or up to 1 year in prison. The minimum is to call 112.

costs.label: Calling 112
costs.note: Free from any phone, in any EU country.

costs.label: Rettungswagen + transport
costs.note: In a confirmed emergency — 100% covered by GKV/PKV.

costs.label: Krankentransport (planned transport)
costs.note: With a Verordnung (referral) — Zuzahlung of 10% (min. 5€, max. 10€) per trip.

costs.label: Unjustified call-out
costs.note: Only in clear abuse; in a good-faith mistake — free.

sources.title: 112 — the single European emergency number (Europäische Kommission)

title: Finding a lawyer: anwaltsregister
tldr: In Germany only lawyers (Rechtsanwälte) admitted by a bar association (Rechtsanwaltskammer) have the right to represent you in court. You can find a vetted lawyer through the official register of the Federal Bar (BRAK; the nationwide official lawyer directory, bundesweites amtliches Anwaltsverzeichnis) or through the German Bar Association (DAV) service anwaltauskunft.de, filtering by the specialisation of a specialist lawyer (Fachanwalt). The cost of an initial consultation (Erstberatung) is capped by law at 190€ + USt (§34 RVG) for private individuals.

steps.title: Who a Rechtsanwalt is and how a Fachanwalt differs

content.text: A lawyer (Rechtsanwalt, RA) is a licensed jurist with the right to represent clients in court. Admission is granted by a regional bar association (Rechtsanwaltskammer, RAK) under the rules of the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO, Bundesrechtsanwaltsordnung). Beyond the basic status, a lawyer can earn the qualification of a specialist lawyer (Fachanwalt) — a specialist in a particular field (for example, in employment law, Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht; in migration law, Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht; in family law, Fachanwalt für Familienrecht). To do so they must prove experience of ≥100 cases in the specialisation and complete a theoretical course of 120+ hours.

items: There are ~24 recognised specialist-lawyer specialisations in total (FAO §1)
Germany has ~167 500 practising lawyers (01.01.2026, BRAK statistics)
For migration matters — a specialist lawyer for migration law (Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht; ~600 people nationwide)
A notary (Notar) is a separate profession, not to be confused with a lawyer (a notary certifies, but does not represent)
A legal adviser (Rechtsbeistand) or a "lawyer" without admission under the BRAO has no right to go to court

content.text: Don't rely on a random Google search and don't trust "Russian-speaking lawyers" from adverts without checking. Before you get in touch, look the person up in the official register — it takes 30 seconds and protects you from charlatans.

rechtsanwaltsregister.org — the official register of all 28 bar associations (RAK). Enter a name/town and you'll see the status (active/inactive, aktiv/inaktiv), the admission, and the date practice began. If they're not in the register, they're not a lawyer.

items.title: 2. DAV anwaltauskunft.de — a service with filters

content.text: A free service of the German Bar Association (Deutscher Anwaltverein). Filters: specialist lawyer (Fachanwalt), consultation language (Russian, English, Ukrainian), region, area of law. Handy for finding a specialist.

items.title: 3. The website of your regional RAK

content.text: Each state bar association (the Berlin bar, RAK Berlin; the Munich bar, RAK München; and so on) keeps its own member register (Mitgliederverzeichnis). This is especially useful for complaints about a lawyer — you have to take them to that lawyer's bar association (RAK).
Arrange an initial consultation (Erstberatung). Ask explicitly: "Ist das eine Erstberatung nach §34 RVG?" and "Welche Gebühr fällt an?" — the price must be agreed in writing BEFORE the consultation.

steps.title: What a lawyer costs: RVG and Vergütungsvereinbarung

content.text: Lawyers' fees are governed by the Lawyers' Remuneration Act (RVG, Rechtsanwaltsvergütungsgesetz). For an initial consultation (Erstberatung; advice without a mandate) §34 RVG sets a cap of 190€ + USt = 226,10€ gross for private individuals. After that it's by the RVG scale (depending on the value in dispute, Streitwert) or by an individual remuneration agreement (Vergütungsvereinbarung; hourly, usually 200-450€/hour net).

items: Initial consultation (Erstberatung): up to 190€ + USt (§34 RVG)
A simple order-for-payment procedure (Mahnverfahren) for a 1000€ debt: ~80-150€ under the RVG
A full civil case with a value in dispute (Streitwert) of 5000€: first instance ~1000-1500€
Hourly: typically 200-350€/hour net in the regions, 350-600€/hour in the big cities
A fixed fee (Pauschalhonorar) — must be agreed in writing (a remuneration agreement, Vergütungsvereinbarung)

content.text: Never pay cash "in hand" and without a receipt. A lawyer is obliged to issue an invoice (Rechnung) under the rules of §10 RVG. Otherwise the payment won't count towards either the legal-advice subsidy (Beratungshilfe) or legal-expenses insurance (Rechtsschutzversicherung).

Don't confuse legal-expenses insurance (Rechtsschutzversicherung; the insurer covers the fee) with a litigation-costs subsidy (Prozesskostenhilfe; state aid for those on a low income). Many insurance policies exclude family law and employment disputes — read the terms (Bedingungen).

A lawyer isn't obliged to take on your case in the event of a conflict of interest or non-payment. But if they decline, they must warn you in advance so you have time to find another before any deadlines (Fristen) expire.

costs.label: Erstberatung (private individuals)
costs.note: Cap of 190€ + 19% USt under §34 RVG; lawyers often charge 80-150€.

costs.label: Beratungshilfe-Schein (low income)
costs.note: Eigenanteil of 15€; the rest is paid by the Amtsgericht.

costs.label: Hourly rate
costs.note: Net; fixed in a Vergütungsvereinbarung; rates are higher at large law firms.

costs.label: Civil case, first instance (Streitwert 5000€)
costs.note: Under the RVG; the loser reimburses the winner.

title: Arbeitsgericht: the labour court
tldr: The labour court (Arbeitsgericht) is the specialised court for employment disputes (dismissals, pay, references). You can file a claim in person without a lawyer, there's no court fee on filing, and in the first instance each side bears only its own lawyer's costs (§12a ArbGG). The key deadline: 3 weeks to challenge a dismissal (a claim for protection against dismissal, Kündigungsschutzklage, §4 KSchG) — miss it and the dismissal becomes effective.

steps.title: What the Arbeitsgericht is and which disputes it handles

content.text: The labour court (Arbeitsgericht, ArbG) is the first instance in employment disputes between an employee (Arbeitnehmer) and an employer (Arbeitgeber). It is governed by the Labour Courts Act (ArbGG, Arbeitsgerichtsgesetz). Above it sit the state labour court (Landesarbeitsgericht, LAG) and the Federal Labour Court (Bundesarbeitsgericht, BAG). Germany has ~110 local labour courts (Arbeitsgerichte) — you can find yours by postcode through justiz-online.de.

items: Dismissal disputes (a claim for protection against dismissal, Kündigungsschutzklage)
Unpaid wages, bonuses, holiday pay (a wage claim, Lohnklage)
Your job reference (Arbeitszeugnis) — content and ratings
Overtime (Überstunden) and compensation for untaken leave (Urlaubsabgeltung)
Mobbing, discrimination (via the AGG)
Not covered: the social court (Sozialgericht) — for unemployment (the job centre, Jobcenter; the employment agency, Agentur für Arbeit)

content.text: German employment law has hard cut-off deadlines (Ausschlussfristen), after which a claim is automatically dismissed. Missing the deadline for a claim for protection against dismissal (Kündigungsschutzklage) is the most common mistake foreigners make: the 3 weeks run from the moment the dismissal is DELIVERED (Kündigung; receipt, Zugang), not from the date stated in the letter.

items.title: Claim for protection against dismissal (Kündigungsschutzklage): 3 weeks (§4 KSchG)

content.text: 21 calendar days from the date the letter is received. If the deadline falls on a weekend, it moves to the next working day. Miss it and the dismissal (Kündigung) is treated as effective, with almost no way to challenge it.

items.title: Wage claim (Lohnklage): collective agreement / employment contract (Tarifvertrag / Arbeitsvertrag)

content.text: Often a cut-off deadline (Ausschlussfrist) of 3 months from the moment the payment falls due (Fälligkeit; when the wage should have been paid). Sometimes it's two-stage (first a written claim, then the lawsuit). Check §15-16 of your contract.

The right to demand a reference has a general limitation period of 3 years from the end of the year of dismissal, but in practice courts reject claims after ~1 year as forfeited through inaction (verwirkt; effectively time-barred).

items.title: Fixed-term contract (Befristung) — claim to have it declared permanent (Entfristungsklage): 3 weeks

content.text: If you're challenging a fixed-term contract — the same 3 weeks from the end of the term (§17 TzBfG).

You can do it in person without a lawyer: at the legal-applications office (Rechtsantragstelle) of your labour court (Arbeitsgericht) a clerk will draw up the claim from your dictation (a claim recorded for the record, Klage zur Niederschrift). Free of charge. You can also file in writing — templates are on the court's website. There's no court fee on filing, only court fees (Gerichtsgebühren) if you lose (and even those are modest in the first instance).

items: Arbeitsvertrag
The dismissal (Kündigung; with the envelope — proof of receipt, Zugang)
Payslips (Lohnabrechnungen) for the last 3 months
Correspondence with the employer (email, WhatsApp)

content.text: By place of work or the employer's registered address. Through justiz-online.de or by googling "Arbeitsgericht + town".

Either in writing (fax/email with a qualified electronic signature, qualifizierte Signatur), or in person at the legal-applications office (Rechtsantragstelle). Under §46c ArbGG — also via the beA portal (beA-Portal) with an electronic signature.

After ~2-6 weeks comes the first, conciliation hearing (Güte). The judge tries to reconcile the parties. ~50% of cases end in a settlement (Vergleich) with a severance payment (Abfindung; compensation). Typically 0.5 of a month's salary × years of service.

items.title: 5. Chamber hearing (Kammertermin; if there's no settlement)

content.text: If you didn't settle, the main hearing comes in 3-6 months. By this point it's advisable to have a lawyer. The decision is either given orally in the room or in writing within 3 weeks.

§12a ArbGG: in the first instance each side pays its own lawyer regardless of the outcome. That means even if you win, the 1500€ for the lawyer still comes out of your own pocket (unless you have legal-expenses insurance, Rechtsschutzversicherung).

You can't "come to an arrangement" with the employer without putting it in writing. Verbal promises along the lines of "we won't fire you, drop the claim" carry no weight at the labour court (Arbeitsgericht) — withdrawing the claim without a settlement (Vergleich) = you've lost.

If you're receiving unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld) after a dismissal, signing a settlement (Vergleich) with a severance payment (Abfindung) can trigger a benefit suspension (Sperrzeit) of 12 weeks from the employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit) if there's a "Verzicht auf Kündigungsschutzklage" or a termination agreement (Aufhebungsvertrag). Get advice before signing.

costs.label: Filing a claim (Klage)
costs.note: No court fee on filing; fees are charged only when a decision is made.

costs.label: Your own lawyer, first instance
costs.note: Under the RVG, depending on salary (Streitwert = 3 months' salary in a Kündigung case).

costs.label: Gerichtsgebühr on a Urteil
costs.note: Paid by the loser; with a Vergleich often 0 or half.

costs.label: Beratungshilfe for preparation
costs.note: If your income is low — a 15€ Eigenanteil for an initial consultation.

title: If you're arrested: your rights
tldr: If you're arrested (Festnahme or provisional arrest, vorläufige Festnahme), the StPO gives you ironclad rights: to stay silent and answer no questions at all (§136 StPO), to call a lawyer, to demand an interpreter (free of charge), and to inform relatives. The police must read you these rights before any questioning begins (the caution, Belehrung). No signatures and no statements without a lawyer — that's rule no. 1 for foreigners.

steps.title: Types of arrest and the time limits

content.text: In Germany the police (Polizei) can detain you on several grounds: provisional arrest (vorläufige Festnahme; §127 StPO) — an on-the-spot arrest on suspicion; police custody (Ingewahrsamnahme) — administrative detention under the state police law (PolG) (to avert a danger, for example at a demonstration); pre-trial detention (Untersuchungshaft, U-Haft) — arrest on a judge's order (§112 StPO). Without a court order they can hold you at most until the end of the next day (Art. 104 GG).

items: Art. 104 II GG: by the end of the next day — a judge must decide
§127 StPO: provisional arrest (vorläufige Festnahme) — arrest by the police
§128 StPO: brought before a judge "without delay" (unverzüglich) (a hearing, Vorführung)
§136 StPO: a mandatory caution (Belehrung) before questioning
§137 StPO: the right to a lawyer at any stage

steps.title: Your rights under §136 StPO — learn them by heart

content.text: Before any questioning (Vernehmung) the police are OBLIGED to read you your rights. If they don't, the statement can't be used in court (a ban on using the evidence, Verwertungsverbot). Memorise 4 phrases in German — they open and close any situation.

"Ich möchte von meinem Schweigerecht Gebrauch machen" — "I am exercising my right to remain silent." You don't have to answer any question about the case. Silence cannot be taken as an admission of guilt. Personal details (name, address, date of birth, nationality) — these you are obliged to give.

items.title: 2. The right to a lawyer (§137 StPO)

content.text: "Ich möchte mit einem Anwalt sprechen" — "I want to speak to a lawyer." You have this right at any time of day. If you don't have your own, the police are obliged to give you a list of on-call lawyers (Notdienst; an emergency criminal-defence service, Strafverteidiger-Notdienst, available round the clock in many cities).

items.title: 3. The right to an interpreter (§185 GVG)

content.text: "Ich brauche einen Dolmetscher" — "I need an interpreter." Free of charge and mandatory. Don't sign anything until you've understood every word. If the interpreter is translating badly, demand another one.

"Ich möchte einen Angehörigen benachrichtigen" — the right to inform someone close to you of your arrest. Foreigners also have the right to contact their consulate (the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, Wiener Konsularrechtsübereinkommen, Art. 36).

steps.title: What to do, step by step

content.text: The most common mistake is trying to "explain it all to the officers, person to person". That almost always hurts you: statements are recorded and used against you. The right strategy is to stay silent and wait for a lawyer.
Resistance = a fresh charge (§113 StGB, resistance, Widerstand, up to 3 years). Even if the arrest is unlawful, that's for a court to decide later, not for you to settle on the street.

items.title: 2. Give your name, address, date of birth, nationality

content.text: This is mandatory under §111 OWiG. You also have to show ID. After that — stop. No "where were you", "why were you going there", "what's in your bag".

Clearly: "Schweigerecht. Anwalt. Dolmetscher." (right to silence, lawyer, interpreter). You can repeat it like a mantra. After that they are obliged to stop the questioning until a lawyer arrives or calls.

items.title: 4. Don't sign anything without a lawyer

content.text: Especially the interrogation record (Vernehmungsprotokoll) and a confession (Geständnis). A signature = confirmation. If you're asked to sign "that you've been informed of your rights", that's different (the caution record, Belehrungsprotokoll), and that's OK.

items.title: 5. Ask for the emergency criminal-defence service (Strafverteidiger-Notdienst)

content.text: In Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, Cologne and Frankfurt there are 24/7 criminal-defence lawyer hotlines. The police know the numbers and are obliged to connect you. Via the state portal of the emergency lawyer service (Anwaltsnotdienst) or the German Bar Association (DAV) anwaltsnotruf.de.

"If you confess, we'll let you go" is manipulation. The police in Germany have no power to promise deals. Deals (an agreement in the proceedings, Verständigung; §257c StPO) are concluded only by a court.

The right to silence does NOT apply to your identity. Refusing to give your name is §111 OWiG (a fine of up to 1000€) and possible police custody (Ingewahrsamnahme) until your identity is established. Name, address, date of birth, nationality — give these.

For foreigners, your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel): a criminal charge can affect your status. At the very least, a notification (Mitteilung) goes to the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde). That's why it's especially important to have a criminal-defence lawyer (Strafverteidiger) with a specialisation in migration law (Migrationsrecht).

If you're the victim or a witness rather than a suspect, you have different rights. A witness, too, can refuse to answer if the answer would incriminate themselves (§55 StPO) or a close relative (§52 StPO).

costs.label: Pflichtverteidiger (appointed)
costs.note: Free in serious cases (§140 StPO); on acquittal, the state pays.

costs.label: Wahlverteidiger (chosen yourself)
costs.note: Depends on the case; under the RVG or a Vergütungsvereinbarung.

costs.label: Strafverteidiger-Notdienst first piece of advice
costs.note: Often free brief advice by phone; full defence is paid.

costs.label: Interpreter at the police/court
costs.note: Free under §185 GVG.

title: Free legal advice (Beratungshilfe)
tldr: The legal-advice subsidy (Beratungshilfe) is a state programme for people on a low income: you get an advice voucher (Berechtigungsschein) from the local court (Amtsgericht) and take it to any lawyer (Rechtsanwalt). It costs you a 15€ own contribution (Eigenanteil), and the court pays the rest. It's suitable for out-of-court matters: complaints about the job centre (Jobcenter), consumer disputes, migration law, tenancy. Under the Legal Advice Act (BerHG, Beratungshilfegesetz) this is the constitutional minimum of access to justice.

steps.title: What Beratungshilfe is and who is entitled to it

content.text: The legal-advice subsidy (Beratungshilfe) is governed by the Legal Advice Act (BerHG, Beratungshilfegesetz) and gives you the right to free legal advice (for a symbolic 15€ contribution) and out-of-court representation from any lawyer (Rechtsanwalt). This is OUT-of-court help — for the court case itself there is a different programme, the litigation-costs subsidy (Prozesskostenhilfe, PKH).

items: Own contribution (Eigenanteil) — 15€ once per matter (not per hour!)
Covers advice and correspondence (for example, an objection, Widerspruch, to a job-centre decision, Jobcenter-Bescheid)
Does NOT cover conducting the case in court itself — for that there's the litigation-costs subsidy (PKH)
Applies only to private individuals, not to businesses
Applies throughout Germany, except in Hamburg and Bremen (there it's public legal information, öffentliche Rechtsauskunft)

content.text: You're entitled to the legal-advice subsidy (Beratungshilfe) if your income means you couldn't afford a lawyer. The calculation follows §115 ZPO — the same as for the litigation-costs subsidy (PKH). In practice the threshold is: after deducting housing, insurance, maintenance payments and tax-free allowances (Freibeträge), you should have less than ~20€/month of "surplus" left.

items: Recipients of basic income support (Bürgergeld; SGB II) — as a rule, qualify by income
Recipients of basic social security (Grundsicherung; SGB XII), social assistance (Sozialhilfe), or housing benefit (Wohngeld) + a low income
Students on BAföG — usually qualify
People working with a net income <1500€ and a family — often qualify (after deductions)
Asset threshold: protected assets (Schonvermögen) of ~10 000€ + 500€ per child

content.text: There are two routes: go to the local court (Amtsgericht) for the voucher first and then to a lawyer — or go straight to a lawyer, who then files the application retrospectively. The second option is more convenient if the lawyer is experienced, but not all of them will do it.

items: Payslips (Lohnabrechnungen) / the basic-income-support decision (Bürgergeld-Bescheid) for the last 3 months
The tenancy agreement (Mietvertrag) and utility costs (Nebenkosten)
Insurance contracts (liability, Haftpflicht; home contents, Hausrat; etc.)
Proof of maintenance payments, if any
Bank statements (Kontoauszüge) for 3 months

items.title: 2. Fill in the application for the subsidy (Antrag auf Beratungshilfe)

content.text: Download it from justiz.de or pick it up at any local court (Amtsgericht). State the subject matter (Angelegenheit) specifically, for example "Widerspruch Bürgergeld-Sanktion". Sign the declaration (Erklärung) about your financial circumstances.

items.title: 3. Submit it to the local court (Amtsgericht) where you live

content.text: File the application at the legal-applications office (Rechtsantragstelle) / legal-advice-subsidy office (Beratungshilfestelle). The voucher (Berechtigungsschein) is usually issued the same day or within a week. It's valid for one matter (Angelegenheit).

Not all of them take the legal-advice subsidy (Beratungshilfe; because the court's payment is low). To search: anwaltauskunft.de — the filter "Beratungshilfe ja". Or call local tenants' associations (Mietervereine), Caritas or AWO — they keep lists.

Hand over the voucher (Schein) and 15€. The lawyer will advise you and write, for example, an objection (Widerspruch) or a payment reminder (Mahnung). If you then have to go to court, you apply separately for the litigation-costs subsidy (PKH).

The legal-advice subsidy (Beratungshilfe) is NOT for criminal cases (there it's an appointed defence lawyer, Pflichtverteidiger, under §140 StPO) and NOT for divorce (there it's the litigation-costs subsidy, PKH, straight away). The exact list is in §2 BerHG.

One voucher (Schein) — one matter (Angelegenheit). If you have both a tenancy problem and one with the job centre (Jobcenter), you need two vouchers, two times 15€. Don't try to "tack on" an extra question — the lawyer won't be able to account for it to the court afterwards.
If your financial situation changes within 4 years (you receive an inheritance, you win in court), you're obliged to tell the local court (Amtsgericht). Otherwise the aid can be reclaimed (§9 BerHG).

costs.label: Client's Eigenanteil
costs.note: Paid to the lawyer at the appointment; once per matter.

costs.label: The advice and correspondence itself
costs.note: Paid by the Amtsgericht at the reduced RVG-Anlage rates.

costs.label: If the lawyer obtains an Erstattungsanspruch
