costs.note: If you win against the other party and they reimburse the costs, the Beratungshilfe is returned to the state.

costs.label: Refusal — appeal
costs.note: Against a refusal you file an Erinnerung under §7 BerHG (no fixed deadline); a judge of the Amtsgericht decides on it.

title: Blackout: getting prepared
tldr: The Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (Bundesamt für Bevölkerungsschutz und Katastrophenhilfe, BBK) recommends that every household keep a 10-day emergency supply: 20 litres of water per person (2 l/day × 10 days), food of ~2200 kcal/day per person (tinned food, grains), batteries, a battery-powered radio, a first-aid kit, and cash. A full basket costs 200-500€ as a one-off, after which you only top it up. This isn't panic but self-protection (Selbstschutz) under §5 ZSKG (the Civil Defence Act, Zivilschutzgesetz).

steps.title: Why the BBK advises being prepared

content.text: Germany is a high-tech country with vulnerable infrastructure. The Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (Bundesamt für Bevölkerungsschutz und Katastrophenhilfe, BBK) has published a guide to emergency preparedness (Ratgeber für Notfallvorsorge) — an official preparedness guide. This isn't theory: in 2021 the flood (Hochwasser) in the Ahr valley (Ahrtal) left thousands of people without water and electricity for 7+ days. In the winter of 2022/23 there was talk of a gas crisis. Most power cuts (Stromausfall) last 1-3 hours, but a large-scale blackout (Blackout) can last a full day.

items: 10 days — the official BBK recommendation (it used to be 14)
ZSKG §5 — citizens have a duty to engage in self-protection (Selbstschutz)
Public warnings (Bevölkerungswarnungen) come through the NINA app (BBK) and Cell Broadcast
The siren test day (Sirenenwarntag) every September — a drill of the warning system
The BBK provides checklists (Checklisten) free of charge as PDFs at bbk.bund.de

content.text: Stock up on what you actually eat. A "shelf of tins plus rotation" is the best strategy: on your normal shopping trips you buy 1-2 tins extra, eat the old ones and put the new ones into the supply. That way nothing goes off and you don't need one-off "survivalist" purchases.

items: 1.5 litres of drinking water per person per day (BBK recommendation)
Another ~0.5 l/person/day for cooking (so ~2 l/person/day per the BBK)
Total 10-day supply: ~20 l per person (40 l for two)
Storage: 1.5 l bottles, a cool place, rotate once a year
As a last resort — water-purification tablets (Wasserentkeimungstabletten; Micropur and the like)
Tinned food: fish, meat, vegetables, pulses
Dry staples: rice, pasta, oats
UHT milk, vegetable oil
Nuts, dried fruit, chocolate
Anything that doesn't need a fridge and cooks without a stove
Battery or wind-up torches
Candles and matches/a lighter
A camping stove for cooking + 2 gas canisters (store outside the flat/on the balcony)
Warm blankets, a sleeping bag
A thermos for boiled water
A battery-powered radio (FM, UKW; + DAB+ if available)
A power bank ≥ 20 000 mAh (fully charged)
Spare batteries in various sizes
The NINA app installed and notifications (push) enabled
Key phone numbers written down on paper
A DIN 13164 first-aid kit (Verbandskasten; like the one in your car)
A 14-day supply of your regular medication
Copies of your passport, residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) and insurance card (Versichertenkarte) in a waterproof bag
200-500€ in cash in small notes (ATMs and cards may not work)
Key contracts (insurance, tenancy) as copies

steps.title: What to do during a Blackout

content.text: The main rule: don't panic and conserve resources. The vast majority of blackouts (Blackout) are over within a few hours. Listen to the radio (instructions are broadcast via a regional radio station), don't open the fridge unless you have to (food keeps for 4-6 hours), and never use a generator or a camping stove indoors — carbon monoxide kills within minutes.

items: Unplug sensitive electronics from the mains (to avoid a surge when power returns)
One light in one room, the rest dark — to save batteries
Don't call 112 unless there's a real threat — the lines are overloaded
Check on neighbours, especially the elderly
If the flat is getting cold — gather in one room with blankets

content.text: Never use a barbecue (Grill), charcoal or gas, indoors. Carbon monoxide (CO) is odourless. 100+ deaths a year in Germany.

An emergency generator (Notstromgenerator): outdoors only, at least 3 m from windows. Earthing is mandatory. And you need an isolating transformer (Trenntrafo) so you don't kill the grid repair crews.

Don't overpay for ready-made "survival kits" (Prepper-Pakete) online at 800€ — a kit to the BBK standard can be put together in an ordinary supermarket for 200-300€. What matters is actually having a supply, not showing it off.
The NINA app is free, in German and basic English. Alternatives: KATWARN, MoWaS. Cell Broadcast (DE-Alert) has worked on any modern phone without any apps since 2023.

costs.label: Basic Notvorrat for 2 people
costs.note: A one-off purchase; rotate as you use it.

costs.label: A good DIN 13164 first-aid kit
costs.note: At DM, Rossmann or Amazon.

costs.label: A battery or wind-up radio
costs.note: Models with a wind-up dynamo + USB charging are better value.

costs.label: A camping stove + 2 gas canisters
costs.note: A camping stove is enough for 10 days of cooking if you're sparing.

costs.label: The NINA app + Cell Broadcast
costs.note: Free, both services are run by the state.

title: Verbraucherzentrale: consumer protection
tldr: The consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale, VZ) is a network of 16 state consumer organisations + a federal umbrella body (Bundesverband, vzbv). It helps with contracts forced on you, online-shop fraud, and problems with energy suppliers, telecoms, banks and insurers. Advice costs 15-90€ per question (depending on the state and the topic), with a lot of information and template letters free online. Under §8 UWG the consumer advice centre has the right to bring class actions (a model declaratory action, Musterfeststellungsklage).

content.text: The consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) is a set of non-profit organisations (a registered association, e.V.), funded by the state and by membership fees. Each federal state has its own consumer advice centre (for example, Verbraucherzentrale NRW, Verbraucherzentrale Bayern), plus the umbrella Federation of German Consumer Organisations (Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverband, vzbv) in Berlin. They have operated since 1957 and form part of Germany's consumer-protection system (Verbraucherschutz).

items: 16 state consumer advice centres (VZ) + a federal umbrella body (Bundesverband)
~200 local advice points (Beratungsstellen) across Germany
Topics: contracts, energy, digital law, food, insurance, finance, tenancy
Languages: German, partly English, and in the big cities — Arabic, Ukrainian, Russian
They also work online — verbraucherzentrale.de + advice by email or in chat

steps.title: When to turn to them: typical cases

content.text: The consumer advice centre (VZ) covers almost all everyday consumer disputes with companies. If your dispute is with a private individual (for example, a private seller on eBay), that's an ordinary civil dispute and the consumer advice centre won't help with it. If it's against a company — there's almost always a department of the centre for it.

You signed up in the street or over the phone and want to back out. There's a right of withdrawal (Widerrufsrecht) of 14 days under §355 BGB — the consumer advice centre will help with a withdrawal template (Widerruf).
Sharp tariff increases, incorrect annual bills (Jahresrechnung), a basic-supply provider (Grundversorger) refusing to take you back. The consumer advice centre will check whether it's lawful.
Hidden charges, poor internet speed (you can claim a discount under §57 TKG), or an inability to terminate early (Sonderkündigung) when you move home.

Reclaiming loan fees (a processing fee, Bearbeitungsgebühr — the Federal Court of Justice, Bundesgerichtshof, ruled these void), disputes over Riester, problems with private health insurance (PKV) increases. The consumer advice centre runs several model actions (Musterklagen).
Non-refunds, fake shops, the subscription trap (Abo-Falle). Under §312j BGB the button must clearly say "zahlungspflichtig bestellen" — otherwise the contract is void.

The fastest way is online via verbraucherzentrale.de — select your state and the topic. Many questions are solved with template letters (Musterbriefe) at no charge. For more complex matters — book a personal consultation.
Search by topic on verbraucherzentrale.de — there's usually an article with step-by-step instructions and a template letter (Musterbrief). In 80% of cases that's enough.

In person, online (an online appointment, Online-Termin) or by phone — 15-30€ for a short standard consultation (15-30 min) and 60-90€ for a detailed one (for example, going over a private health insurance, PKV, contract). The exact prices are on the website of your state consumer advice centre (VZ).

items: The disputed contract / bill itself
Correspondence with the company
Proof of payment
A timeline of events on one page

items.title: 4. If there's a model declaratory action (Musterfeststellungsklage)

content.text: Consumer advice centres run class actions (since 2018, §606 ZPO). Registering in the claims register of the Federal Office of Justice (Klageregister Bundesamt für Justiz) is free. For example, against VW Diesel, Mercedes, or health-insurance-fund (Krankenkassen) increases. A win in a model action (Musterklage) = you automatically win too.

The consumer advice centre (VZ) is NOT a lawyer. They don't represent you in court. For a lawsuit you need a lawyer (Rechtsanwalt). But the centre often gives you a referral and writes the first formal complaint.

When you register in the claims register (Klageregister) for a model declaratory action (Musterfeststellungsklage) you are legally bound — you can't run your own case in parallel. If the consumer advice centre loses, you lose too. Think it over before registering.
In Berlin, Hamburg and Bremen there is free public legal information (öffentliche Rechtsauskunft) at the courts — an alternative to the consumer advice centre (VZ) for people on a low income.
Beware of copycat sites: the real ones are only verbraucherzentrale.de and vzbv.de. Everything else (verbraucherschutz24.com and the like) is private and commercial.

costs.label: Information and Musterbriefe online
costs.note: Free at verbraucherzentrale.de and vzbv.de.

costs.label: Short consultation (15-30 min)
costs.note: Depends on the state and the topic.

costs.label: Detailed consultation (Verbraucherrecht)
costs.note: For example, a review of a Bausparen or PKV contract.

costs.label: Registration in a Musterfeststellungsklage
costs.note: Free via the Klageregister Bundesamt für Justiz.

costs.label: Schlichtungsstellen (e.g. SÖP for transport)
costs.note: Many sectors have free arbitration bodies — the VZ will refer you.

title: Schuldnerberatung: help for debtors
tldr: Debt counselling (Schuldnerberatung) is free help for people with debts they can't service. It offers: negotiations with creditors, a repayment plan (an out-of-court attempt at agreement, außergerichtlicher Einigungsversuch) and preparation for consumer insolvency (Verbraucherinsolvenz) with a subsequent discharge of residual debt (Restschuldbefreiung; the writing-off of debts) after 3 years under the revised §287 InsO. Caritas, Diakonie, AWO and Volkssolidarität are the main providers, and their services are free for clients. The Federal Working Group on Debt Counselling (Bundesarbeitsgemeinschaft Schuldnerberatung; bag-sb.de) is the national directory.

steps.title: What Schuldnerberatung is and who it suits

content.text: Debt counselling (Schuldnerberatung) is a social service that helps people who've ended up in a debt spiral: unpaid loans, rent, fines, debt collectors (Inkasso). This is NOT a lawyer or a financial adviser — it's a social worker + a jurist specialising in dealing with creditors. Free debt counselling (a recognised body, anerkannte Stelle) has a special status: only it can issue the certificate (Bescheinigung) needed to start consumer insolvency (Verbraucherinsolvenz) under §305 InsO.

items: Free — at Caritas, Diakonie, AWO, Volkssolidarität, and municipal services
Paid (commercial, gewerbliche) — usually lawyers or firms; not valid for the certificate (Bescheinigung)
The right to free help — for any debtor, not only recipients of basic income support (Bürgergeld)
In Germany around 5-6 million people are considered over-indebted (überschuldet; according to recent SchuldnerAtlas data)
The average debt of a debt-counselling client is around 30 000€

content.text: The earlier you go, the better your chances of getting out without insolvency. Don't wait until the bailiff (Gerichtsvollzieher) turns up or your account (Konto) is frozen. The first warning signs: being 1+ month late on several bills, using one loan to pay off another, being afraid to open the post box.

items: There's already an order for payment (Mahnbescheid) or an enforcement order (Vollstreckungsbescheid)
A threat of a power cut-off (Stromsperre) or a tenancy termination (Mietkündigung)
The account (Konto) is under attachment (Pfändung) — you need to open an attachment-protected account (P-Konto) immediately
Several debt-collection firms (Inkasso) are writing at the same time
You don't understand who you owe and how much

content.text: The process is staged and usually takes 6-18 months for the out-of-court phase, plus 3 years for the discharge-of-residual-debt period (Restschuldbefreiung) if it goes to insolvency (Insolvenz). At each stage there are points of no return — you can exit if your situation has improved.

Find your nearest service (Stelle) on meine-schulden.de or bag-sb.de. The waiting list is often 2-6 weeks (up to 3 months in the big cities). If it's urgent (for example, a power cut-off, Stromsperre), say so when you book — they usually give you an emergency appointment.

items: Gathering ALL the creditors
Contracts, bills, payment reminders (Mahnungen)
A record of income and expenditure
An attachment-protected account (P-Konto), if not yet opened
Stabilisation: stopping any new debt

content.text: The counsellor (Berater) sends all creditors a proposed plan: either monthly payments (an instalment, Rate) or a one-off payment (Einmalzahlung) at a discount. If the creditors who account for most of the debt agree, you can sign a settlement (Vergleich) and avoid insolvency (Insolvenz).

The counsellor (Berater) issues a certificate of an unsuccessful attempt at agreement (Bescheinigung über erfolglosen Einigungsversuch) — a mandatory document for filing with the insolvency court (Insolvenzgericht). The court fee can be deferred (a deferral, Stundung).

Since 01.10.2020 it's 3 years (it used to be 6). You're obliged to work or look for work and to hand over everything above the attachment-exempt threshold (Pfändungsfreigrenze; for a single person in 2026, around 1.555€ net per month). After 3 years comes the discharge of residual debt (Restschuldbefreiung), and the remaining debts are written off.

An attachment-protection account (Pfändungsschutzkonto, P-Konto) is an ordinary account with a special status: setting it up is governed by §850k ZPO, and the protected amount by §899 ZPO. The attachment-protection account automatically shields the basic tax-free amount (Grundfreibetrag) from being seized by creditors: until 30.06.2026 that's around 1.555€/month (rounded up to 1.560€ on the account), and from 01.07.2026 — around 1.587€ (the threshold is updated each year on 1 July). Any ordinary current account (Girokonto) can be converted into an attachment-protection account free of charge — the bank is obliged to do this within 4 working days. Open such an account IMMEDIATELY at the first signs of debt problems, before the creditors (Gläubiger) apply for attachment (Pfändung): it's harder afterwards.

Do NOT pay firms like "Schulden weg in 24 Stunden" — these are often fraudsters. They take an advance of 500-3000€, do the same as free debt counselling (Schuldnerberatung), and often do it worse. The check: a recognised body (anerkannte Stelle) is listed on the website of the state social-affairs ministry (Sozialministerium).

During the good-conduct phase (Wohlverhaltensphase) you have to hand over half of any inheritance you receive to the insolvency administrator (Insolvenzverwalter; §295 InsO). You also can't "gift away" assets before insolvency: such transactions are voidable (a challenge, Anfechtung) — under §134 InsO a gift can be reversed for a period of up to 4 years.
The discharge of residual debt (Restschuldbefreiung) does NOT cover: maintenance payments, fines, tax debts from evasion, debts arising from crimes. These remain even after insolvency (Insolvenz).

After the discharge of residual debt (Restschuldbefreiung), the entry at the SCHUFA credit bureau is kept for another 6 months (under the rules in force since March 2023; it used to be 3 years). During that period it's almost impossible to get credit.

costs.label: Schuldnerberatung at an anerkannte Stelle
costs.note: Free for the client; funded by the state and by church/social associations.

costs.label: Opening a P-Konto
costs.note: The conversion is free (§850k ZPO); the Girokonto itself may carry the bank's normal fee.

costs.label: Verbraucherinsolvenz — Gerichtskosten
costs.note: Can be deferred through Stundung and then written off.

costs.label: Paid Schuldnerberatung (lawyer)
costs.note: Only if specifically recommended and the benefit is clear; usually not needed.

costs.label: Insolvenzverwalter Vergütung
costs.note: Paid out of the asset pool; the debtor doesn't pay directly.

title: Deportation (Abschiebung): procedure and protection
tldr: Deportation (Abschiebung, §58 AufenthG) is the forcible enforcement of the obligation to leave Germany (Ausreisepflicht) once voluntary departure has not happened. Beforehand you are usually given a demand to leave (Ausreiseaufforderung) with a deadline and a deportation warning (Abschiebungsandrohung). The deportation date is NOT announced in advance (§59 Abs. 1 S. 8). There are protections: a ban on deportation (Abschiebungsverbot) §60 (threat to life, torture, serious illness), suspension via a deportation deferral (Duldung) §60a, an appeal to the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) and an urgent application (Eilantrag), help from the hardship commission (Härtefallkommission) and a lawyer. Detention pending deportation (Abschiebungshaft, §62) is allowed only by court order.

content.text: Deportation (Abschiebung) under §58 AufenthG is the forcible enforcement of the obligation to leave, which arises after a residence permit is refused, asylum is rejected, or a permit expires. First the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) or the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) issues a written demand to leave (deportation warning, Abschiebungsandrohung under §59) stating a period for voluntary departure — usually 7-30 days. Only if you have not left and there are no legal obstacles may the ABH carry out a forced removal.

items: Obligation to leave the country (Ausreisepflicht) — vollziehbar = enforceable
Deportation warning (Abschiebungsandrohung) §59 — written warning with a period for voluntary departure
Under §59 Abs. 1 S. 8 the exact deportation date is NOT announced in advance (after the first failure to leave)
Deportation (Abschiebung) §58 — the forced removal itself by the police/ABH
Entry and residence ban (Einreise- und Aufenthaltsverbot) §11 — after a deportation an entry ban of several years is usually imposed

content.text: Never ignore letters from the foreigners' authority (ABH) or the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF). Their deadlines are short and often decide the outcome of the case. On the same day you receive a deportation warning (Abschiebungsandrohung) or a refusal, contact a specialist immigration lawyer (Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht) or an advice centre (Beratungsstelle) — a missed appeal deadline closes off almost every avenue of defence.

steps.title: When deportation is prohibited: §60 and Duldung

content.text: The law recognises obstacles to removal. A ban on deportation (Abschiebungsverbot) under §60 AufenthG protects you if you face persecution, torture, or inhuman treatment in the destination country (§60 Abs. 5 — via the ECHR), or a concrete serious danger to life and health, including a severe illness that cannot be treated there (§60 Abs. 7). If departure is temporarily impossible for factual or legal reasons, you are issued a deportation deferral (Duldung) under §60a — this is not a residence permit, only a suspension of the deportation.

items.title: Grounds for a ban on deportation §60 (Abschiebungsverbot)

items: §60 Abs. 1 — threat of persecution under the Geneva Convention
§60 Abs. 5 — violation of the ECHR (inhuman treatment)
§60 Abs. 7 — concrete danger to life/health, severe illness with no treatment in the country of return
Medical obstacles are confirmed by a qualified medical certificate (qualifizierte ärztliche Bescheinigung, §60a Abs. 2c)

content.text: If there is a factual obstacle (for example no passport, not fit to fly due to illness, an unfinished course of training) or a legal one, the foreigners' authority (ABH) must issue a deportation deferral (Duldung) under §60a. This is a document titled "Suspension of removal" (Aussetzung der Abschiebung) that does not legalise your stay but protects you from immediate removal. The deportation deferral is covered in more detail in a separate guide.

A medical obstacle is recognised only with a qualified medical certificate (qualifizierte ärztliche Bescheinigung under §60a Abs. 2c AufenthG: diagnosis, examination method, severity, consequences of removal). An ordinary certificate is not enough — ask your doctor for a document in exactly this format.

Against a refusal of a permit and a deportation warning (Abschiebungsandrohung) you file an appeal with the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht). Often the lawsuit (Klage) by itself does not suspend the removal, so at the same time you file an urgent application (Eilantrag — Antrag auf Anordnung der aufschiebenden Wirkung under §80 Abs. 5 VwGO or einstweilige Anordnung §123 VwGO). The deadline is extremely short — usually one or two weeks, and in some cases counted in days.

items: Lawsuit (Klage) — the main action before the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) against the refusal/threat of removal
Urgent application (Eilantrag) — to suspend the deportation until the court decides
The deadline is stated in the instructions on legal remedies (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung) at the end of the decision — follow it to the letter
Legal advice aid (Beratungshilfe) and legal costs aid (Prozesskostenhilfe, PKH) cover the costs on a low income
A specialist immigration lawyer sharply improves your chances — do not go it alone

content.text: In addition, each federal state has a hardship commission (Härtefallkommission) (§23a AufenthG) — the commission can recommend a residence permit in exceptional humanitarian cases, even where the courts have refused. The application is not made by the person directly but through a commission member (churches, charities, members of parliament). This is not a right but an act of grace, yet in a hopeless situation it is worth trying via the state refugee council (Flüchtlingsrat).

Detention pending removal (Abschiebungshaft, §62 AufenthG) is permissible ONLY by court order (judicial reservation, Richtervorbehalt) and only where there is a concrete risk of absconding. If detained, immediately demand a lawyer and a review of the lawfulness of the arrest — an unlawful detention can be challenged, and the judge must hear you in person. IMPORTANT (from 1 June 2026): the former court-appointed lawyer assigned automatically (appointed lawyer, Pflichtanwalt; §62d AufenthG no longer exists) has been abolished — you now have to organise a lawyer yourself, so demand contact with a lawyer/advice centre (Beratungsstelle) as soon as you are detained.

costs.label: Lawyer's consultation (Erstberatung)
costs.note: With a Beratungshilfeschein from the Amtsgericht — free, or a token 15 € for the client.

costs.label: Court fee at the Verwaltungsgericht
costs.note: With Prozesskostenhilfe the state covers the costs; otherwise it depends on the Streitwert.

costs.label: Härtefallantrag
costs.note: Submitted through a commission member or the Flüchtlingsrat — no state fee.

sources.title: BGBl. 2025 I Nr. 364 — law on safe countries of origin (repeal of §62d, in force from 01.06.2026)

title: Discrimination complaints (AGG)
tldr: The General Equal Treatment Act (Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz, AGG) protects against discrimination on six grounds (§1): race/ethnic origin, sex, religion/belief, disability, age, sexual identity. The ban applies at work and in access to goods and services, including renting housing. Key deadline: you must assert a claim against your employer in writing within 2 months (§15 Abs. 4 AGG). The Federal Anti-Discrimination Agency (Antidiskriminierungsstelle des Bundes) advises free of charge. You can claim compensation (Entschädigung/Schadensersatz §15) and file a lawsuit.

content.text: The General Equal Treatment Act (AGG) prohibits discrimination on the six grounds listed in §1: race and ethnic origin, sex, religion or belief, disability, age, sexual identity. The ban applies to employment (§§6-18: hiring, pay, dismissal, promotion) and to mass-market civil-law transactions (§§19-21), which include renting housing, insurance, restaurants and shops.

items: §1 — six protected grounds: race/ethnic origin (Rasse/ethnische Herkunft), sex (Geschlecht), religion/belief (Religion/Weltanschauung), disability (Behinderung), age (Alter), sexual identity (sexuelle Identität)
§3 — forms: direct (unmittelbare) and indirect (mittelbare) discrimination, harassment (Belästigung), sexual harassment
Employment §§6-18 and access to goods/services §§19-21
Renting housing is covered (except minor everyday transactions and sharing a home with the owner)
Not covered: nationality as such, beyond the ethnic-origin ground; tax and family law

content.text: It is important to distinguish a grievance from legal discrimination: the Equal Treatment Act (AGG) only applies if the unequal treatment is linked to one of the six grounds in §1. A rude boss or a rejection unconnected to a protected ground does not, in itself, fall under the AGG.

steps.title: The 2-month deadline and the claim (§15 Abs. 4)

content.text: The most important thing in employment cases is the deadline. Under §15 Abs. 4 AGG you must assert a claim for compensation (Entschädigung) or damages (Schadensersatz) against your employer IN WRITING within 2 months. The period runs from the moment you learned of the discrimination (for a rejected application — from receiving the rejection). Missing this deadline almost always means losing the right to compensation.

items: Submit it in writing (letter/email with confirmation) within 2 months
Describe what happened, which §1 ground is affected and what evidence you have
State your demand: compensation (Entschädigung) and/or damages (Schadensersatz) under §15 AGG
Keep a copy and proof of dispatch (registered letter Einschreiben, screenshot)
After asserting the claim you have a further 3 months to file a lawsuit with the labour court (Arbeitsgericht, §61b ArbGG)

items.title: Easing of the burden of proof (§22)

content.text: §22 AGG eases the position of the injured party: it is enough to present circumstantial evidence (indicia) suggesting discrimination, after which the burden of proving the contrary shifts to the respondent. So document everything: the wording of job adverts and rejections, correspondence and witnesses.

Two months for the claim (§15 Abs. 4) and then three months for the lawsuit (§61b ArbGG) are hard deadlines. Do not wait weeks for advice: submit a written claim to your employer as soon as possible, even if the details are still being clarified.

steps.title: Where to complain and who helps

content.text: The Federal Anti-Discrimination Agency (Antidiskriminierungsstelle des Bundes, ADS) advises free of charge on all forms of discrimination, helps assess your case and put you in touch with the parties. At work you have the right to file a complaint (Beschwerde) with your employer's internal body under §13 AGG. Beyond that, trade unions, the federal states' anti-discrimination centres and specialist employment lawyers can help.

items: Federal Anti-Discrimination Agency (Antidiskriminierungsstelle des Bundes) — free advice (antidiskriminierungsstelle.de)
§13 AGG — right to complain (Beschwerde) to the employer's internal body
Trade union (Gewerkschaft) and works council (Betriebsrat) — support and representation at work
Regional anti-discrimination centres (Antidiskriminierungsverbände)
Labour court (Arbeitsgericht) — lawsuit for compensation; no lawyer required at first instance

content.text: In housing and consumer cases (§§19-21) the claim is directed at the landlord/service provider, and the dispute is decided by the ordinary civil court (Zivilgericht / local court, Amtsgericht). Here the general limitation period applies rather than the 2-month rule of §15, but recording evidence and reacting quickly is still critical.

costs.label: Advice from the Antidiskriminierungsstelle
costs.note: Free for everyone.

costs.label: Written claim under §15 Abs. 4
costs.note: Filing it yourself is free; the cost of an Einschreiben is a few euros.

costs.label: Lawsuit at the Arbeitsgericht
costs.note: At first instance each side bears its own costs; on a low income Prozesskostenhilfe is available.

title: Deportation deferral (Duldung): tolerated stay
tldr: A deportation deferral (Duldung, §60a AufenthG) is NOT a residence permit, only a temporary suspension of deportation (Aussetzung der Abschiebung). The obligation to leave remains, but removal is temporarily not carried out (no passport, illness, training, etc.). There are special types: a deferral for the duration of training (Ausbildungsduldung, §60c, the 3+2 model) and a deferral for the employed (Beschäftigungsduldung, §60d). Since 2022 those living here long-term with no prospect of leaving can apply for the opportunity right of residence (Chancen-Aufenthaltsrecht, §104c) — for 18 months to move on to a genuine permit. The deferral must be renewed regularly at the foreigners' authority (ABH).

steps.title: What a Duldung is and what it is not

content.text: A deportation deferral (Duldung) under §60a AufenthG is an official confirmation that your deportation is temporarily suspended (Aussetzung der Abschiebung). This is crucial to understand: a deportation deferral is NOT a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel). The obligation to leave the country (Ausreisepflicht) formally remains; its enforcement is merely postponed while an obstacle exists — a missing passport, illness, unfinished training, protection of family life, and so on.

items: Deportation deferral (Duldung) = suspension of deportation, NOT legalisation of your stay
Issued when departure is temporarily impossible for factual or legal reasons (§60a Abs. 2)
The document is called the "Certificate on the suspension of removal" (Bescheinigung über die Aussetzung der Abschiebung)
The term is short (often 1-6 months) and must be renewed regularly at the foreigners' authority (ABH)
You may change your place of residence with restrictions (residence rule Wohnsitzauflage, residence obligation Residenzpflicht in some cases)

content.text: Do not confuse a deportation deferral (Duldung) with the permission to stay while an asylum claim is being processed (Aufenthaltsgestattung) or with a residence permit. A deferral does not give the rights a permit has, and time spent on a deferral counts only partly towards later periods. The main goal is to use this breathing space to move on to a genuine permit.

The law created special types of deportation deferral (Duldung) to offer a way forward for those who work or study. The deferral for the duration of training (Ausbildungsduldung) under §60c AufenthG (known as the 3+2 model) is granted for the duration of recognised vocational training and, if successful, leads to a residence permit to work in the trained occupation. The deferral for the employed (Beschäftigungsduldung) under §60d is for the long-term employed who meet certain length-of-service requirements and are independent of state benefits.

items.title: Deferral for the duration of training §60c (Ausbildungsduldung, 3+2)

items: Granted for the duration of qualified vocational training (qualifizierte Berufsausbildung, usually 2-3 years)
After successful completion — a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) to work in the occupation (usually for a further 2 years)
Your identity must be established (Identitätsklärung) by a certain deadline
Does not apply where there is a near, concrete deportation date or serious criminal convictions
For securely employed people on a deferral (Geduldete) with sufficient length of service
Requires securing your livelihood without state benefits
Established identity and no serious obstacles
Also a bridge to a subsequent residence permit

content.text: Establishing identity (Identitätsklärung) is the bottleneck for almost every path out of a deportation deferral (Duldung). Actively gather documents from your country of origin and record your efforts: the foreigners' authority (ABH) must see that you are cooperating in good faith (Mitwirkung), otherwise it will refuse the deferral for the duration of training (Ausbildungsduldung) and other paths.

The opportunity right of residence (Chancen-Aufenthaltsrecht) under §104c AufenthG (from 31 December 2022) is a trial right of residence for those who have lived in Germany for a long time on a deportation deferral (Duldung). It is granted once, for 18 months, to use that time to meet the conditions for the ordinary residence permit for long-term residents (§25a/§25b): support yourself, learn the language, clarify your identity. At the end of the 18 months you must move on to a genuine permit — this is not a renewable status.

items: Condition — long-term residence in the country as of a set cut-off date (Stichtag) on a deferral/permission to stay (Duldung/Gestattung)
No serious criminal convictions and a commitment to the democratic order
Granted once for 18 months — this is a chance, not a permanent status
The goal is to meet the requirements of §25a (young people) or §25b (long-term residents) within that period
Apply at the foreigners' authority (ABH); it is worth going with advice from the refugee council (Flüchtlingsrat)/a lawyer

content.text: Free help with all types of deportation deferral (Duldung) and the move to a permit is provided by migration advice services (Migrationsberatung, MBE/JMD), the federal states' refugee councils (Flüchtlingsräte) and Caritas/Diakonie. They will help assess which path is realistic in your case and prepare the documents for the foreigners' authority (ABH).

Every renewal of the deportation deferral (Duldung) is a deadline: do not miss your appointment date at the foreigners' authority (ABH) and do not let the deferral "expire". A gap puts you back under threat of immediate deportation. Book the renewal in advance and keep your documents ready.

costs.label: Issuing/renewing the Duldung
costs.note: The Bescheinigung itself usually carries no significant fee; check with your ABH.

costs.label: Migrationsberatung (MBE/JMD)
costs.note: Advice is free (Caritas, Diakonie, AWO, trade-union centres).

costs.label: Immigration lawyer
costs.note: On a low income, a Beratungshilfeschein from the Amtsgericht is available.

title: 110 and 112: police and medics
tldr: In Germany 110 is the police (Polizei) and 112 is the fire and ambulance service (fire brigade Feuerwehr + emergency medical service Rettungsdienst). 112 is the single European number (112.eu): it works in every EU country, free, around the clock, even with no credit on your account and with a locked SIM card. Call 112 when life is in danger (heart attack, stroke, severe injury, fire) and 110 for a crime or danger from people. In large cities the operators often bring in an interpreter; a few basic German phrases speed up help. When in doubt, call 112.

content.text: The main rule is simple: 110 is the police, 112 is the fire and ambulance service. Both numbers are free, work across Germany 24/7 and are reachable even with no credit on your account, in some cases without a SIM card, and from any network. 112 is the single emergency number across the whole European Union (112.eu), so it will help you on trips around Europe too.

items: 112 — fire, stopped breathing, heart attack, stroke, severe injury, loss of consciousness, heavy bleeding
110 — crime, assault, theft, danger from people, a road accident with a hazardous situation
Both are free and work around the clock across the country
112 works in every EU country (112.eu)
Unsure which service — call 112 and the operator will redirect you

content.text: Do not waste time hunting for the "right" number when life is in danger. Signs of a stroke (the FAST test — drooping face, weakness in an arm, slurred speech), chest pain, choking — call 112 straight away. Better to overestimate the severity than underestimate it.

The operator will guide you through the questions — there is no formula to memorise, but it helps to keep the "5 W" scheme in mind. Most important: state the location clearly and do not hang up first — the operator will end the call once they have gathered everything needed and, if necessary, given you instructions (for example, how to perform CPR).

items: Where? (Wo?) — street, house number, town, landmarks
What happened? (Was?) — fire, road accident, person unconscious
How many are injured? (Wie viele?)
What injuries? (Welche Verletzungen?) — or symptoms
Wait (Warten) — wait for the questions, do not hang up first
Ich brauche einen Krankenwagen — I need an ambulance
Es brennt — there is a fire
Eine Person ist bewusstlos — a person is unconscious
Sprechen Sie Englisch? — do you speak English?
Ich spreche kein Deutsch — I do not speak German

content.text: Many control rooms in large cities can bring in an interpreter, and operators often understand English. However, this is not guaranteed in every rural district, so basic German words and a clear statement of the location noticeably speed up help. Give the address slowly and spell it out if the operator asks you to repeat it.

items: Deaf and hard of hearing: the pan-European emergency-call app "nora" (the official emergency-call app in Germany)
Many federal states support an emergency call via an app with geolocation
112 works even with the phone's keypad locked (emergency call)
State your location as precisely as possible — it saves minutes

content.text: A false alarm (a deliberately invented one) is punishable (§145 StGB). But a genuine mistake in judging the severity of a situation does NOT count as a false alarm — do not be afraid to call if you are truly worried for someone's life and health.

costs.label: Call to 110 / 112
costs.note: Free, including with no credit on your account; 112 works across the whole EU.

costs.label: nora app (Notruf-App)
costs.note: The official free emergency-call app in Germany.

sources.title: 112 — the single European emergency number (Europäische Kommission)
nora — die offizielle Notruf-App der Bundesländer

title: Fire service (Feuerwehr): fire
tldr: You call the fire service on 112 (free, 24/7, across the whole EU). In a fire the rule is: get people out, close the door of the burning room behind you, leave the building by the stairs (NEVER the lift), call 112. Smoke detectors (Rauchmelder) are mandatory in all 16 federal states. 112 calls out both the fire brigade and the ambulance (emergency doctor Notarzt) — one number for both. Do not open a door that feels hot, move through smoke crouched down, and if your way out is cut off, stay in the flat and signal from the window.

steps.title: What to do in a fire

content.text: You call the fire service (Feuerwehr) on 112 — free and around the clock. In a fire the priority is lives, not property. Remember the order: warn and get people out, close the door of the burning room behind you (this holds back the fire and smoke), leave the building by the stairs and call 112. Never open a door if it feels hot — there may be a fully developed fire behind it.

items: Loudly warn the neighbours and lead everyone to the exit
Close the door of the burning room behind you, but do not lock it
Go down the stairs — NEVER use the lift
If the corridor is full of smoke, move crouched down — the air is cleaner near the floor
If your way out is cut off, stay in the flat, close the door, seal the gaps with wet cloth and signal from the window
Give the exact address: street, building, floor, town
Say what is burning and whether people are in danger (Personen in Gefahr)
Report whether the exits are blocked and whether there are any injured
Do not hang up until the operator has finished
Meet the firefighters at the entrance if it is safe to do so

content.text: The main danger in a fire is not the flames but the smoke (poisoning from the combustion fumes). A few breaths of thick smoke can incapacitate you. So if your way out is heavily smoke-filled, do NOT run out through the smoke: shut yourself in a room, seal the gaps and attract attention from the window.

Smoke detectors (Rauchmelder) are mandatory in all 16 federal states — at least in bedrooms, children's rooms and the corridors leading to the exit. As a rule the owner pays for installation, while keeping them operational (Betriebsbereitschaft) is the tenant's responsibility in many states; in some states maintenance is the owner's too. A single detector costs 10-30 €.

items: Mandatory in all 16 states (the rules are in each state's building code Bauordnung)
Minimum: bedrooms, children's rooms, escape routes (corridors)
Installation — usually the owner; checking they work is often the tenant's job
Test the alarm regularly and change the battery (or fit 10-year models)
Look for the DIN EN 14604 marking when buying

steps.title: Feuerwehr versus Notarzt and first aid

content.text: Many people are confused by the split between services, but in practice it is simple: 112 is the single number for both the fire brigade and the ambulance/emergency crew (emergency medical service Rettungsdienst/emergency doctor Notarzt). You do not need to look for a separate number for medics at a fire with casualties — the 112 operator will dispatch both a fire engine and a doctor at the same time.

items: 112 = fire brigade (Feuerwehr) + emergency medical service (Rettungsdienst, ambulance) at the same time
Tell the operator if there are injured or anyone suffering smoke inhalation — an emergency doctor (Notarzt) will come
Before they arrive: get people out of the smoke into fresh air, and if breathing has stopped start CPR following the operator's prompts
Use a fire extinguisher (Feuerlöscher) only on a small source of fire and when you have a safe way out
Do NOT put out burning oil on the stove with water — cover it with a lid or a fire blanket (Löschdecke)

content.text: Never put out burning fat or live electrical appliances with water: water will cause a flare-up (a grease explosion, Fettexplosion) or an electric shock. In the kitchen keep a lid or a fire blanket (Löschdecke) on hand. If the fire spreads — do not play the hero, get out and call 112.

costs.label: Call to 112
costs.note: Free, 24/7; calls out the fire brigade and the ambulance.

costs.label: Smoke detector (Rauchmelder)
costs.note: Around 10-30 € each; in rented housing the owner usually arranges installation.

costs.label: Fire blanket (Löschdecke)
costs.note: Cheap protection for the kitchen against a grease fire.

sources.title: 112 — the single European emergency number (Europäische Kommission)
Feuerwehrverband — Notruf 112 und Verhalten im Brandfall
BBK — Feuer: Verhalten im Brandfall und Notruf 112

title: Personal insolvency (Verbraucherinsolvenz)
tldr: Consumer insolvency (Verbraucherinsolvenz, InsO §§304-314) lets a private individual clear their debts. Since the 2020 reform the good-conduct phase (Wohlverhaltensphase) has been cut to 3 years, after which the court grants discharge of residual debt (Restschuldbefreiung, InsO §287). First a pre-court stage is MANDATORY: an attempt at out-of-court settlement through debt counselling (Schuldnerberatung; free at Caritas/Diakonie/AWO) — without its certificate the court will not accept your application. Protect your income and account with a seizure-protection account (P-Konto).

content.text: Before thinking about insolvency, turn to a recognised debt counselling service (anerkannte Schuldnerberatungsstelle). This is not only sensible but legally required: the consumer insolvency (Verbraucherinsolvenz) procedure begins with an attempt at an out-of-court settlement with creditors. If it fails, the counselling service issues a certificate of failure (Bescheinigung über das Scheitern), without which the court will NOT accept your application.

items: Free debt counselling (Schuldnerberatung): Caritas, Diakonie, AWO, municipal (kommunale) centres
They will check whether insolvency is realistic or whether restructuring/a settlement (Vergleich) is enough
They will prepare the mandatory attempt at an out-of-court settlement with creditors
They will issue the certificate (Bescheinigung) of a failed settlement — your ticket to court
Immediately convert your account into a seizure-protection account (P-Konto, Pfändungsschutzkonto) to protect it from seizure

content.text: A seizure-protection account (P-Konto, Pfändungsschutzkonto) protects a basic amount of your income from seizure by creditors. Any ordinary account can be converted into a P-Konto free of charge on request to the bank — do this as early as possible, otherwise your whole salary may go towards paying off debts. Beware of paid commercial providers: state and charitable debt counselling (Schuldnerberatung) is free.

Consumer insolvency (Verbraucherinsolvenz) is governed by §§304-314 InsO. After the out-of-court settlement fails, you file an application with the insolvency court (Insolvenzgericht; this is a division of the local court, Amtsgericht) on the prescribed forms. The court attempts a court settlement plan, and if that fails it opens the proceedings themselves (opened insolvency proceedings, eröffnetes Insolvenzverfahren), appoints a trustee (Treuhänder) and the good-conduct phase (Wohlverhaltensphase) begins.

Through debt counselling (Schuldnerberatung) you propose a repayment plan to your creditors. If even one refuses and the plan collapses, a certificate (Bescheinigung) of failure is issued (a mandatory condition under §305 InsO).

items: An official set of forms is completed (insolvency application, Insolvenzantrag)
An inventory of assets, a list of creditors and debts and the certificate of failure are attached
At the same time you file the application for discharge of residual debt (Restschuldbefreiung, §287 InsO)
The court may attempt a court debt-settlement plan (gerichtlicher Schuldenbereinigungsplan)

items.title: 3. Opening of proceedings and the Treuhänder

content.text: The court opens the proceedings, appoints a trustee (Treuhänder) and realises any available assets for the creditors. The protected minimum income (the seizure-exempt threshold, Pfändungsfreigrenze) remains yours.

After the proceedings open, the good-conduct phase (Wohlverhaltensphase) begins. Since the 2020 reform (for applications from 1 October 2020) it has been cut to 3 years (previously 6 years). During this time you must meet certain obligations (Obliegenheiten): try to work, report any change of job/address, and hand over the seizable part of your income and any inheritance towards repayment. After 3 years the court grants discharge of residual debt (Restschuldbefreiung, §287 InsO) — release from the remaining debts.

items: Good-conduct phase (Wohlverhaltensphase) = 3 years since the 2020 reform (previously 6 years)
Obligations (Obliegenheiten): work/seek work in good faith, report changes, do not conceal income
Discharge of residual debt (Restschuldbefreiung) §287 — after a successful phase
NOT discharged: maintenance withheld intentionally, fines, debts from intentional tort, tax debts from evasion
In a repeat procedure the income-assignment period (Abtretungsfrist) is 5 years (if discharge of residual debt has already been granted before)

content.text: Concealing assets or income, refusing to cooperate, or running up new intentional debts during the good-conduct phase (Wohlverhaltensphase) leads to the discharge being refused (refusal, Versagung). Then the whole procedure is wasted and the debts remain. Be completely transparent with the court and the trustee (Treuhänder).

costs.label: Schuldnerberatung
costs.note: Free at Caritas, Diakonie, AWO and municipal centres.

costs.label: Court costs (Verfahrenskosten)
costs.note: If you lack the means, a Stundung (deferral) of the court costs is possible — pay later or not at all.

costs.label: P-Konto
costs.note: Converting an ordinary account into a P-Konto is free by law.

sources.title: Bundesministerium der Justiz — Verbraucherinsolvenz und Restschuldbefreiung

title: Lost documents: where to go
tldr: If you lose or have stolen a German ID document (national identity card Personalausweis/passport Reisepass) or other papers: first file a loss report (Verlustanzeige) with the police — most conveniently through your state's online police station (Online-Wache). Then book an appointment to order a replacement at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt). A stolen card with an eID/online-identification function must be blocked through the single blocking hotline (Sperr-Notruf) 116 116. Theft — always report it to the police to protect against misuse; a simple loss — also advisable. Replacing a passport/ID document costs money and production takes weeks.

content.text: The first step when documents are lost or stolen is to file a loss report (Verlustanzeige; report of loss/theft) with the police. For theft this is mandatory; for a simple loss it is strongly recommended, because a police report protects you if the document is used by fraudsters. The easiest way is to file the report online through your federal state's online police station (Online-Wache), without leaving home.

items: Your state's online police station (Online-Wache) — online report of loss/theft (polizei.de leads to the state portals)
Or in person at any police station (Polizeidienststelle)
Keep the confirmation (file number Tagebuchnummer/certificate) — you need it at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) and as protection against misuse
For theft always file a criminal complaint (Strafanzeige), not only a loss report (Verlustanzeige)
Note down exactly which documents are missing (ID card Ausweis, passport, driving licence, insurance cards)

content.text: If you have lost documents with an online-identification function (eID on the national identity card Personalausweis or on the electronic residence-permit card eAT), immediately block the eID function through the free blocking hotline (Sperr-Notruf) 116 116 so that third parties cannot use it. There is a separate guide for the foreign residence permit (eAT) — the procedure there is stricter.

steps.title: Order a replacement at the Bürgeramt

content.text: Replacements for German documents are issued at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt/Bürgerbüro; for the identity card and the passport) by prior appointment (Termin). Take a biometric photo, the police confirmation and any surviving documents that prove your identity. Producing a new card usually takes 3-4 weeks; for urgent cases there are express-issue options (Express) for an extra fee.

items: A biometric photo (in the required format)
The police certificate/confirmation of the loss report (Verlustanzeige)
A birth certificate or another document proving your identity
Proof of registration (Anmeldebestätigung), if requested
Money/a card for the fee

items.title: If you need a document urgently

content.text: While the new one is being produced you can get a temporary document: a provisional national identity card (vorläufiger Personalausweis) or a provisional passport (vorläufiger Reisepass) — these are issued faster but cost more each and have a limited validity. Ask about express issue (Express) at your district citizens' office (Bürgeramt).

Besides the ID card and passport, when a bag or wallet is stolen a whole set of items usually goes missing with it. Work through the list: block your bank cards, replace your driving licence (Führerschein) at the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle), and re-order your health-insurance card from your statutory health-insurance fund (Krankenkasse). A foreign passport is replaced through your country's consulate, and the electronic residence-permit card (eAT) through the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde; there are separate guides on this).

items: Bank cards — blocked through your bank or the single blocking hotline (Sperr-Notruf) 116 116
Driving licence (Führerschein) — replaced at the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle/Fahrerlaubnisbehörde)
Health-insurance card (Gesundheitskarte) — a new one from your statutory health-insurance fund (Krankenkasse), usually free or for a small fee
Foreign passport — through your country's consulate (see the guide on losing a passport)
Electronic residence-permit card (eAT) — immediately to the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde; see the separate guide)

content.text: Do not put off blocking your cards and eID: between the loss and the block, fraudulent transactions are possible. The single free blocking hotline (Sperr-Notruf) 116 116 works around the clock for bank and SIM cards and for the eID function of ID documents.

costs.label: Verlustanzeige with the police
costs.note: Reporting a loss/theft is free (online or in person).

costs.label: Replacing the Personalausweis
costs.note: Around 46 € (for people aged 24 and over, the rate from 07.02.2026); for under-24s about 27,60 €.

costs.label: Replacing the Reisepass (passport)
costs.note: Around 70 € and up; the Express option costs more.

costs.label: Sperr-Notruf 116 116
costs.note: Blocking cards and eID is free, 24/7.

title: Lost passport: the consulate
tldr: A foreign passport is replaced NOT by the German authorities but by your country's consulate/embassy. The procedure: 1) file a loss report (Verlustanzeige) with the German police (online police station Online-Wache) and get a certificate; 2) go to your country's consulate for a new passport or an emergency travel document; 3) inform the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) if the passport is needed to renew your residence permit. Without a valid passport you may run into problems with travel and renewing your permit — act quickly. The consular fee depends on the country.

steps.title: Report the loss to the German police

content.text: The first step is a loss report (Verlustanzeige; report of loss or theft) with the German police. For theft this is mandatory; a police certificate is almost always required by the consulate and protects you if the passport is used by fraudsters. It is convenient to file online through your federal state's online police station (Online-Wache). Keep the confirmation (file number Tagebuchnummer) — you will need it at the consulate.

items: Your state's online police station (Online-Wache) or in person at a police station (Polizeidienststelle)
For theft — a criminal complaint (Strafanzeige) is mandatory, not only a loss report
Keep the police certificate/file number (Tagebuchnummer) for the consulate
Note down the number of your old passport if you remember it (it speeds up the consulate's work)
Make copies of all the identity documents you have

content.text: The German district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) does NOT issue replacements for a foreign passport — it is responsible only for German documents. For a new passport of another country's citizen you go solely to that country's consulate/embassy. Do not waste time at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt).

A new passport or an emergency travel document is issued by your country's consulate (Konsulat) or embassy (Botschaft) in Germany. Each country has its own rules, timelines and fees, so find your consulate's contact details and the list of required documents in advance. They often require the police certificate, photos, an application form and proof of identity (a copy of the old passport, an identity card, a birth certificate).

The standard route is to order a new passport. Production can take weeks or months, as the passport is often printed in the country of citizenship. Apply as early as possible, especially if a residence-permit renewal is coming up.

items: If you need to travel home urgently — ask about an emergency travel document
It usually allows a single trip to the country of citizenship
It is issued faster than an ordinary passport
For staying in Germany it usually does not replace a full passport — check with the foreigners' authority (ABH)

steps.title: Inform the Ausländerbehörde and the link to your permit

content.text: If your residence permit is in the passport, or the passport is needed to renew your permit, report the loss to the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH). A valid passport is a condition of most residence permits (passport obligation, Passpflicht under §3 AufenthG), so not having a passport can delay your renewal. The ABH will advise what to do while the new passport is being produced.

items: Inform the foreigners' authority (ABH) if the passport is linked to your residence permit
Passport obligation (Passpflicht) §3 AufenthG — a valid passport is usually mandatory for a permit
If the electronic residence-permit card (eAT) is a separate card, it is not lost together with the passport, but check both documents
If it was lost together with the eAT, see the separate guide on losing the residence permit
Keep all certificates — they prove you are restoring your documents in good faith

content.text: A long period without a valid passport complicates travel and renewing your residence permit. Start the consular process right after the police, and record every contact — this proves to the foreigners' authority (ABH) that the delay is not your fault.

costs.label: Verlustanzeige with the police
costs.note: Free (online or in person).

costs.label: New passport at the consulate
costs.note: The consular fee depends on your country of citizenship — check with your consulate.

costs.label: Emergency travel document
costs.note: The fee depends on the country; usually cheaper and faster than a full passport.

sources.title: Auswärtiges Amt — Auslandsvertretungen (find consulates in Germany)

title: Lost electronic residence-permit card (eAT): replacement
tldr: If your electronic residence-permit card (eAT — elektronischer Aufenthaltstitel) is lost or stolen, act immediately: 1) file a loss report (Verlustanzeige) with the police; 2) block the eID/PIN through the single blocking hotline (Sperr-Notruf) 116 116 or the eAT blocking hotline; 3) inform the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) as soon as possible and apply for a replacement. A replacement costs roughly 60-100 €. While the new eAT is being produced, the authority issues a temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung). The eAT is the residence permit itself, so losing it is more serious than losing an ordinary card.

steps.title: Immediately: police and blocking the eID

content.text: The electronic residence-permit card (eAT, elektronischer Aufenthaltstitel) is a chip card that AT THE SAME TIME confirms your residence permit and contains an online identification function (eID) with a PIN. So if it is lost or stolen, act without delay on two fronts: file a loss report (Verlustanzeige) with the police and block the eID/PIN so that the card cannot be used for online services in your name.

items: Loss report (Verlustanzeige) to the police — online through the online police station (Online-Wache) or in person (keep the certificate)
Block the eID function through the blocking hotline (Sperr-Notruf) 116 116 (free, 24/7)
For theft — a criminal complaint (Strafanzeige) is mandatory
Note down the card/permit number if you remember it
Immediately schedule a visit to the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde)

content.text: Block the eID/PIN immediately — a lost electronic residence-permit card (eAT) with a known PIN lets third parties use the online identification. The free blocking hotline (Sperr-Notruf) 116 116 works around the clock; keep this number on hand.

steps.title: Inform the Ausländerbehörde and order a replacement

content.text: Since the electronic residence-permit card (eAT) is the residence permit itself, you must report the loss to the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) as soon as possible and apply for a replacement (Ersatz). The ABH will issue a new eAT; production, as with the first issue, takes several weeks (the card is printed by the Federal Printing Office Bundesdruckerei). Take your passport, a biometric photo and the police certificate of the loss.

items: A valid passport
A biometric photo
The police certificate of the loss report (Verlustanzeige)/theft
The application for a replacement eAT (the foreigners' authority's form)
Proof of registration (Meldebescheinigung), if required

content.text: Replacing the electronic residence-permit card (eAT) costs money — usually around 60-100 € depending on the situation and the validity period. This is an administrative fee for producing the new card; check the exact amount with your foreigners' authority (ABH).

steps.title: Fiktionsbescheinigung while the card is being produced

content.text: While the new electronic residence-permit card (eAT) is being printed, your status is confirmed by a temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) — a temporary paper certificate issued by the foreigners' authority (ABH). It records that your residence permit remains valid and, as a rule, lets you stay in the country and work to the same extent as before. Carry it together with your passport until you receive the new card.

items: Temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung) — temporary confirmation that your status is valid
Issued by the foreigners' authority (ABH) for the period while the new eAT is being produced
Carry it together with your passport (for example, for travel and for your employer)
For trips abroad, check with the ABH in advance — a temporary confirmation (Fiktionsbescheinigung) is not always recognised by other countries
Once you receive the new eAT, reactivate the eID and set a new PIN if you wish

content.text: Do not put off the visit to the foreigners' authority (ABH): the electronic residence-permit card (eAT) is your residence permit. Without a confirming document (eAT or the temporary confirmation of legal status Fiktionsbescheinigung) it is hard to prove your stay is legal and that you have the right to work. Remember: a deportation deferral (Duldung) and a temporary confirmation (Fiktionsbescheinigung) are not the same thing; the temporary confirmation confirms a valid permit, not a suspension of deportation.

costs.label: Verlustanzeige with the police
costs.note: Free (online or in person).

title: Order for payment (Mahnverfahren)
tldr: The court order-for-payment procedure (gerichtliches Mahnverfahren, ZPO §688 onwards) is a simplified court process for collecting monetary claims. The creditor files an application, and the order-for-payment court (Mahngericht) sends the debtor a court order for payment (Mahnbescheid). KEY deadline: from the moment the order is served you have 14 days to file an objection (Widerspruch). If you stay silent, the creditor obtains an enforcement order (Vollstreckungsbescheid), which allows seizure of your account and wages. The objection is free and filed on the attached form. NEVER ignore a court order for payment (Mahnbescheid)!

content.text: The court order-for-payment procedure (gerichtliches Mahnverfahren, ZPO §688 onwards) is a simplified, cheap court procedure for collecting monetary debts without a full trial. The creditor files an application with a specialised order-for-payment court (Mahngericht) without proving, at this stage, that the claim is well founded. The court merely checks the application formally and sends you an official court order for payment (Mahnbescheid) in a yellow envelope with a certificate of service (Zustellungsurkunde).

items: Governed by ZPO §§688 onwards (the court order-for-payment procedure, gerichtliches Mahnverfahren)
The order for payment (Mahnbescheid) is issued by a COURT (the order-for-payment court, Mahngericht), not an ordinary reminder letter from a company
At this stage the court does NOT check whether you actually owe the money
The date of service is recorded (certificate of service, Zustellungsurkunde) — the deadline runs from it
The creditor files online through mahngerichte.de

content.text: Do not confuse a court order for payment (Mahnbescheid; an official court order in a yellow envelope) with an ordinary payment reminder (Mahnung) — a pre-court reminder from a company or debt collector. A court order for payment (Mahnbescheid) is already a court matter and has a strict deadline to respond.

The most important thing: from the moment the court order for payment (Mahnbescheid) is served you have 14 days to file an objection (Widerspruch). A ready-made form is attached to the order (objection form, Widerspruchsformular) — you just mark that you object to the claim in whole or in part, sign it and send it to the stated court. The objection is free and does NOT require any reasons at this stage: it simply moves the case into ordinary litigation, where the creditor will then have to prove the claim.

items: Use the objection form (Widerspruchsformular) attached to the court order for payment (Mahnbescheid)
Mark your objection (in whole or in part) and sign it
Send it to the stated order-for-payment court (Mahngericht) within 14 days of service
No reasons are required at this stage — they will be needed later in the litigation
Keep a copy and proof of dispatch (preferably a registered letter Einschreiben/a fax with a report)

content.text: After the objection (Widerspruch) the case may move into ordinary litigation (contested proceedings, streitiges Verfahren), where the court examines the claim on the merits. The creditor then has to prove the debt, and you set out your arguments. At this stage it is worth involving a lawyer or debt counselling.

14 days from the moment of SERVICE is the decisive deadline. Count it from the date on the yellow envelope/the certificate of service (Zustellungsurkunde), not from the date of the letter. Missing the deadline sharply worsens your position: the court moves to the next stage and the creditor can obtain an enforcement order.

If you do not file an objection (Widerspruch) in time, the creditor can ask the court to issue an enforcement order (Vollstreckungsbescheid). This is now an enforcement instrument (enforcement title, Vollstreckungstitel): on its basis your bank account can be seized (account seizure, Kontopfändung), part of your wages withheld (wage garnishment, Lohnpfändung), and a bailiff (Gerichtsvollzieher) sent. There is also a short deadline to challenge the enforcement order — an appeal (Einspruch, usually 14 days) — but the conditions are now stricter.

items: Without an objection (Widerspruch) → an enforcement order (Vollstreckungsbescheid)
This is an enforcement title (Vollstreckungstitel): account seizure, wage garnishment and a bailiff's visit are possible
Against the enforcement order (Vollstreckungsbescheid) there is an appeal (Einspruch) — also usually 14 days from service
The title is valid for many years, so you must react at once
Protect your income with a seizure-protection account (P-Konto, Pfändungsschutzkonto) if there is a risk of account seizure

content.text: If the claim is genuinely well founded but you cannot pay all at once, do not stay silent: contact the creditor about instalments (Ratenzahlung) and turn to free debt counselling (Schuldnerberatung; Caritas, Diakonie, AWO). But if you consider the debt unjustified, be sure to file an objection (Widerspruch) in time, or you will lose the chance to contest it.

NEVER ignore a court order for payment (Mahnbescheid) or an enforcement order (Vollstreckungsbescheid) in the hope that it will "sort itself out". Silence is treated as an admission of the debt and leads to an enforcement order with seizure of your account and wages. Even if you are abroad or ill — respond in writing within the deadline.

title: Help with court costs (Prozesskostenhilfe)
tldr: Legal aid for court costs (Prozesskostenhilfe, PKH, §114 ZPO) is state assistance that covers court fees and your lawyer's fee in civil cases if you have a low income and the case has a reasonable chance of success. For pre-trial legal advice and out-of-court help there is separate legal-advice aid (Beratungshilfe), obtained through the local court (Amtsgericht) for a token fee of ~15€. The aid is income-dependent (means-test): the court checks your income, assets and expenses. PKH may be granted entirely free of charge or with payment in instalments.

content.text: If you cannot afford a lawyer and the court fees, the state can cover these costs — so that access to justice does not depend on your wallet. There are two different instruments: legal-advice aid (Beratungshilfe) — for advice and help BEFORE or OUTSIDE court; legal aid for court costs (Prozesskostenhilfe, PKH) — for the court proceedings themselves in civil cases. The legal basis for PKH is §114 ZPO (Zivilprozessordnung).

items: Beratungshilfe — pre-trial advice/help from a lawyer, applied for at the local court (Amtsgericht)
Beratungshilfe: you pay the lawyer only a token ~15€ (your own contribution, Eigenanteil)
Prozesskostenhilfe (§114 ZPO) — covers court fees (Gerichtskosten) and the lawyer's fee in the proceedings
PKH applies to civil cases (rent, family, debts, employment disputes)
In criminal cases, instead of PKH you have a court-appointed defence lawyer (Pflichtverteidiger) / victim's lawyer (Opferanwalt)
PKH can be full (free of charge) or with payment in instalments (Ratenzahlung) depending on income

steps.title: Conditions: income and chances of the case

content.text: PKH is granted when two conditions under §114 ZPO are met at the same time. The first is financial: given your personal and economic circumstances, you cannot pay for the proceedings, or can pay only part of the cost (a means-test on income, assets and mandatory expenses). The second is substantive: the claim or defence has a sufficient chance of success (hinreichende Erfolgsaussicht) and is not clearly hopeless or malicious (mutwillig).

items: Income is assessed after deducting housing, maintenance costs, taxes and contributions
Assets are taken into account (savings above the protected amount may count against you)
The case must have a reasonable chance — the court assesses it on the merits
If your income changes within 4 years, the court can demand a repayment
Supporting documents: income statements, rent, account statements, debts

content.text: PKH covers YOUR costs (your lawyer + court fees), but if you lose a civil case you are, as a rule, still obliged to reimburse the winning side's costs — PKH does not cover that. So weigh the risks with a lawyer in advance. And remember the possible repayment: if your financial situation improves, the court can demand back what was paid out within 4 years.

items: Go to the local court (Amtsgericht) for your area to request an entitlement voucher (Berechtigungsschein)
Fill in the form and attach proof of income and expenses
Take the voucher to a lawyer — you pay only the ~15€ own contribution (Eigenanteil)
Suitable for letters, advice, negotiations outside court
Fill in the form 'Erklärung über die persönlichen und wirtschaftlichen Verhältnisse'
Submit it together with the claim to the competent court (often through a lawyer)
Attach proof of income, assets and expenses
The court decides on PKH (in full or with instalments) before or during the proceedings
You can find the form on justiz.de and at the court itself

costs.label: Beratungshilfe — Eigenanteil to the lawyer
costs.note: Token contribution; the state covers the rest.

costs.label: Prozesskostenhilfe (court proceedings)
costs.note: Covers Gerichtskosten and your lawyer's fee for those eligible by income; instalments possible.

costs.label: Winning side's costs if you lose
costs.note: NOT covered by PKH in civil proceedings — borne by the loser.

title: Armenian citizens: visas and work in Germany
tldr: Armenian citizens must obtain a Schengen visa (Schengen-Visum) to enter Germany (an Armenian passport is not part of the visa-free regime). For work and long-term stay, the main options are the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte, since June 2024), the EU Blue Card (Blue Card) §18b AufenthG, the skilled-worker visa §18a/§18b and the language-course visa (Sprachkurs) §16f. The fee for a national type-D visa is 75€, and for a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) in Germany it is 100€.

content.text: Armenia is NOT part of the EU visa-free regime (unlike Georgia and Moldova). To enter Germany, Armenian citizens need a visa. Visa types: the Schengen visa (Schengen-Visum, type C) for a short trip of up to 90 days, and the national visa (Nationales Visum, type D) for long-term stay and relocation. The national visa is issued at the German embassy in Yerevan (Botschaft der Bundesrepublik Deutschland in Eriwan) and is then converted in Germany into a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel).

items: Armenian passport = a Schengen visa is mandatory
Type C — up to 90 days (tourism, business, visits)
Type D — more than 90 days (work, study, family reunification)
Submission at the German Embassy in Yerevan (Marshal Baghramyan ave. 29)
National-visa applications are made through VFS Global or directly at the embassy

content.text: Since 1 June 2024 the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte, §§20a, 20b AufenthG) has been in force — a points-based system for finding work. Armenians are eligible on the general terms. The card grants the right to stay in Germany for up to 1 year to look for work (including part-time work of up to 20 hours a week and trial employment (Probebeschäftigung) of up to 2 weeks).

items: A recognized education/degree OR 2 years of professional experience in your field
German at level A1 OR English at B2
Proof of means of subsistence (at least ~1027€/month or a blocked account, Sperrkonto)
A valid passport

content.text: Points for: age under 35 (2 points), German B2 (3), B1 (2), A2 (1), English C1 (1), work experience 3+ years (2) / 5+ years (3), previous study/work in Germany (1), a spouse/partner also eligible (1), and others.

items.title: 3. Apply at the German Embassy in Yerevan

items: Application form for a national visa (Nationales Visum, Chancenkarte)
Proof of points (diplomas, certificates, experience)
Financial proof (a blocked account, Sperrkonto, or a formal sponsorship undertaking, Verpflichtungserklärung)
Biometric photos, insurance, fee 75€

steps.title: Blue Card and the skilled-worker visa

content.text: The EU Blue Card (Blue Card EU, §18b AufenthG) is for specialists with a higher education degree and a contract with a salary from 50 700€/year (2026), while for shortage professions (Mangelberufe: IT, engineers, medical staff) and recent graduates it is from 45 934€/year. The card is usually valid for up to 4 years. An Armenian degree must be listed with an H+ rating in the degree-recognition database Anabin (anabin.kmk.org), or assessed as equivalent through the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB). The exact thresholds are adjusted annually — check them on make-it-in-germany.com.

items: Degree recognition: anabin.kmk.org → check for H+/H-
If the degree is not in Anabin: request an official degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) from ZAB (~200€)
A contract with a German employer stating the salary
For IT without a degree — §19c Abs. 2 AufenthG (5 years of experience)
Permanent residence (permanent settlement permit, Niederlassungserlaubnis) — after 27 months (B1) or 21 months (B2)

content.text: Armenia joined the 1961 Hague Convention in 1994 — the apostille is affixed by the Armenian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia). All Armenian documents (degree, transcript of grades, birth/marriage certificate) must have an apostille and a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) by a sworn translator in Germany.

items: Apostille on the degree and its supplement — the Armenian MFA in Yerevan
Certified translation into German (beglaubigte Übersetzung) — a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer, 30-80€/page)
Birth certificate — apostille mandatory
Police clearance certificate (for long-term visas) — the Armenian Ministry of the Interior + apostille
Marriage certificate (Trauungsurkunde) with apostille — for family reunification

content.text: An Armenian degree cannot simply be translated — it must be recognized. Without an H+ entry in the Anabin database, you will not be granted a Blue Card. Before applying, always check your university on anabin.kmk.org.
At VFS Global in Yerevan, the wait for a national-visa appointment is 2-4 months. Book well in advance. Do not use intermediaries promising expedited processing — that is illegal.
Financial proof on a blocked account (Sperrkonto) must be at least 12,324€ for 2026 (1027€×12 months). Less than that — rejection.
An Armenian internal passport is not valid for entry — you need an international (travel) passport valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned date of departure from the Schengen area.

costs.note: Long-term D visa, including Chancenkarte, Blue Card
