title: Belarusians in Germany: grounds for asylum
tldr: Belarusian citizens can claim asylum in Germany on the basis of §3 AsylG (refugee protection, Flüchtlingsschutz) or §4 AsylG (subsidiary protection, subsidiärer Schutz). The main grounds are participation in the 2020 protests, journalistic activity, political activism, LGBT persecution, and military conscription. The application is filed through BAMF and is free of charge. The stakes are high: a rejection can lead to deportation, so you need a lawyer from the very start.

steps.title: Legal basis of asylum in Germany

content.text: Germany has three levels of protection: 1) the right to asylum (Asylberechtigung) under Art. 16a Grundgesetz (political asylum for people persecuted by the state); 2) refugee protection (Flüchtlingsschutz) under §3 AsylG (refugee status under the Geneva Convention); 3) subsidiary protection (Subsidiärer Schutz) under §4 AsylG (if there is a threat of the death penalty, torture, inhuman treatment, or serious harm in an armed conflict). In addition, §60 Abs. 5/7 AufenthG — a ban on deportation (Abschiebungsverbot) on humanitarian or medical grounds.

items: Art. 16a GG — the right to asylum (Asylberechtigung; narrow, only persecution by the state)
§3 AsylG — refugee protection (Flüchtlingsschutz; persecution for race, religion, nationality, social group, politics)
§4 AsylG — subsidiary protection (Subsidiärer Schutz; risk of the death penalty, torture, harm in conflict)
§60 Abs. 5 AufenthG — ban on deportation under the EMRK (European Convention on Human Rights)
§60 Abs. 7 AufenthG — ban on deportation on medical/humanitarian grounds

content.text: BAMF (Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge) reviews each case individually, but since 2020 a practice has developed of recognizing the following grounds for Belarusian citizens. The share of positive decisions (Schutzquote) for Belarus, according to BAMF data for 2023-2024, is one of the highest among CIS countries (relatively high; the specific figures change by year and category — check the exact numbers in current BAMF statistics). Assess your chances with a lawyer specializing in migration law (Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht), and assess the risks in your country of origin with a lawyer specializing in Belarusian law.

items: Participation in the 2020 protests (photos, videos, detentions, fines)
Political activity in the opposition (CR, the Coordination Council, the BNR, Svezhy Veter)
Journalists of independent media (TUT.by, Naša Niva, Belsat, Zerkalo)
Activists of women's marches and solidarity
Evading conscription into the Belarusian army (especially given the country's support for Russia's war)
LGBT+ persecution (Belarus has no legal protection, homophobia is growing)
Trade-union activity and strikes at enterprises
Lawyers who defended political prisoners
Family members of political prisoners who receive threats
Being linked to a designated "extremist" group or material (Telegram chats, symbols)

steps.title: How to file an asylum application

content.text: The application is filed in person at one of the BAMF branches (Außenstelle). The procedure has several stages. After filing, you receive a temporary residence authorization for the duration of the asylum review (Aufenthaltsgestattung) — a certificate of admission to the asylum procedure. Distribution across the federal states is handled through the EASY system / Königsteiner Schlüssel — you cannot choose your state, except in cases of family reunification.

On entry — tell a federal police officer (Bundespolizei) "Ich beantrage Asyl". If you are already in the country — at any police station, the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) or directly at a BAMF branch (Außenstelle). They record your details and issue a certificate of registration as an asylum seeker (Bescheinigung über die Meldung als Asylsuchender, Ankunftsnachweis).

You are sent to an initial reception centre (Erstaufnahmeeinrichtung). You stay there until you are allocated to a state (from a few days to 6 months). Free of charge: housing, food, medical care, pocket money of 174€/month (as of 2026).

items: Filling in the form in your native language (Russian and Belarusian are available)
Fingerprinting (dactyloscopy) — for EURODAC and the Dublin check
Submission of documents: passport, evidence of persecution
A date for the personal hearing (Anhörung) is set

content.text: This is a multi-hour personal interview (Anhörung) with a BAMF officer, recorded in a transcript. You tell the story of your persecution. An interpreter and (highly recommended!) a lawyer are present. This is the most important event in the whole process — the decision is made on the basis of the hearing.

The decision comes as an official notice (Bescheid) — it can be recognition (Anerkennung), rejection (Ablehnung) or "manifestly unfounded" (offensichtlich unbegründet). The deadline to appeal (a court action, Klage) to the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) is 1-2 weeks, depending on the wording of the decision. Do NOT appeal without a lawyer.

The personal hearing (Anhörung) is not a court, but this is exactly where your fate is decided. Preparation is critically important. BAMF asks detailed questions: dates, places, the sequence of events, names, addresses. Contradictions in your account = grounds for rejection.

items: Prepare a written timeline: dates of detentions, charges, fines
Gather evidence: photos from protests, screenshots of posts, summonses
Translate documents from Belarus — translators work from Belarusian and Russian
Find a specialist lawyer in migration law (Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht)
Free consultations: Caritas, AWO, Diakonisches Werk, Pro Asyl
Request medical certificates if you have PTSD or injuries from detentions (important for §60 Abs. 7)
Prepare country information: reports from Viasna, BHC, HRW, Amnesty
Do not lie or embellish — lies, once exposed, mean rejection + an entry ban

content.text: The Dublin Regulation: if you have a Schengen visa (Schengen-Visum) from another country or you entered through it, BAMF can transfer your case there (Poland, Lithuania). This is especially relevant for Belarusians, who often enter through Poland. The transfer deadline is 6 months; if it is missed, Germany reviews the case.
Travelling to Belarus during the procedure = revocation of protection. Do not return even for a funeral — it will be read as the absence of a genuine fear of persecution.
Do not use old/other people's Belarusian documents. Forged documents are a criminal offence under §267 StGB, leading to denial of protection and deportation.

Evading conscription is not in itself a ground for protection — you need to show that you are being conscripted into a unit waging a war of aggression or being forced to take part in war crimes (a reference to the rulings of the BVerwG and the EuGH in the Ukrainian-Russian cases).
With a manifestly-unfounded rejection (offensichtlich unbegründet), the appeal deadline is 1 week. Without a lawyer you will miss it. Get to a lawyer (Rechtsanwalt) urgently!

costs.note: The asylum procedure in Germany is entirely free of charge (§29 AsylG)

costs.note: Erstberatung; worth investing in at the start of the process

costs.label: Lawyer — handling the case
costs.note: Through all instances; for low income — Beratungshilfe and Prozesskostenhilfe

title: The Belarusian consulate in Berlin: what you can (and cannot) do
tldr: After Lukashenko's Decree No. 278 (4 September 2023), Belarusian consulates abroad effectively stopped issuing and renewing passports for Belarusian citizens — a passport can now be processed only on the territory of Belarus. The consulate in Berlin (Am Treptower Park 32) continues to handle notarial acts, apostilles and basic certificates, but Belarusian émigrés usually avoid visiting it. The alternative is to approach the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) for a travel document (Reisedokument).

steps.title: Status of the Belarusian consulate in Germany

content.text: The Embassy of the Republic of Belarus in Germany (Botschaft der Republik Belarus in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland) is in Berlin at Am Treptower Park 32, 12435 Berlin. The consular section operates by appointment. Website: germany.mfa.gov.by. After Decree of the President of the Republic of Belarus No. 278 of 4 September 2023 "On documenting citizens of the Republic of Belarus", the consulate's services for Belarusians abroad are substantially limited.

items: Address: Am Treptower Park 32, 12435 Berlin
Website: germany.mfa.gov.by
Consular section: by prior appointment only
Immediately after Decree No. 278: passport services for Belarusian citizens were sharply cut back
Still available: notarial acts not requiring appearance in Belarus, legalization, civil-registry extracts

content.text: Decree of the President of the Republic of Belarus No. 278 of 4 September 2023 "On the procedure for issuing documents and performing acts" effectively stopped the issuing/exchange of Belarusian citizens' passports through diplomatic missions abroad. The rule is framed as a requirement to be personally present in Belarus to apply for a new passport. The effect for émigrés: an expired passport cannot be renewed without returning to Belarus.

items: Issuing a new passport — only at Belarusian Interior Ministry offices on the territory of Belarus
Exchange on expiry — only in Belarus
Replacement after loss — only in Belarus
A return certificate (SNV) — issued for a one-off trip to Belarus
Registration of a child's birth — theoretically possible, but with restrictions

content.text: The consulate still performs a number of functions, but many émigrés, especially the politically active, avoid any contact with it. For those not at risk, the following services are formally available. Prices are in euros, according to the Belarusian MFA tariff.

Powers of attorney and declarations for use on the territory of Belarus (for example, a power of attorney to sell real estate, or consent for a child to travel). Prices ~30-100€ depending on the type of document.

Belarus is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention. The apostille for documents issued in Belarus is affixed in Belarus (by the civil-registry offices for civil-status acts, and by the Ministry of Justice for the rest). The consulate in Berlin helps with the legalization of German documents for Belarus.

items: Requests for police clearance certificates from Belarus — through the consulate
Civil-registry extracts — certificates of marriage, birth, divorce
Help with restoring civil-status documents

content.text: If your passport is lost and there is no way to obtain a new one abroad, an SNV is issued for a one-off trip to Belarus. The cost is about 30€. IMPORTANT: once you have entered Belarus, you can leave again only with a new passport, which will take time to process.

If you have protection status in Germany (a person entitled to asylum, Asylberechtigter; a refugee, Flüchtling; a person with subsidiary protection, subsidiär Schutzberechtigter) — you should NOT approach the consulate of your country of origin (this contradicts the very nature of protection and can lead to its revocation under §72 AsylG). Use German documents.

items: Travel document for refugees (Reiseausweis für Flüchtlinge, blue passport) — for recognized refugees
Travel document for persons with subsidiary protection (Reiseausweis für subsidiär Schutzberechtigte) — for §4 AsylG
Travel document for foreigners (Reiseausweis für Ausländer, grey passport) — for persons without a valid passport (§5 AufenthV)
Apply at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde); fee ~50-100€
For notarial matters — a German notary (Notar) or translator (Übersetzer) for Belarusian documents

content.text: If you have protection status in Germany and you approach the Belarusian consulate, BAMF can interpret this as re-establishing contact with the persecuting state. Revocation of protection (Widerruf der Schutzgewährung) under §73 AsylG is possible. Consult a lawyer before approaching it.

An SNV is a one-way ticket. Once you enter Belarus, you fall under the country's normal legal system, where detention, interrogation and confiscation of property are possible. It is especially dangerous for participants in the 2020 protests, journalists, and activists.

Decree No. 278 did not announce a "complete abolition" of passport services — the wording leaves room for individual cases. But in practice the consulates refuse en masse. Do not count on an exception.

An expired Belarusian passport in Germany is NOT an automatic breach of German law as long as you hold a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) and a passport-substitute document (Passersatzpapier, Reiseausweis). Do not panic — go to the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde).

title: A Belarusian in Germany: I can't go back — what to do
tldr: If your Belarusian passport has expired and returning to Belarus is dangerous because of political persecution, there are legal routes in Germany: an asylum application (Asylantrag, §3/§4 AsylG), a humanitarian residence permit (§22, §23, §25 AufenthG), a travel document for foreigners (Reiseausweis für Ausländer, §5 AufenthV) for persons without a passport. Do nothing and you risk a deportation deferral (Duldung) and the loss of the right to work. Get to a lawyer and the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) urgently.

steps.title: The situation: your Belarusian passport is expiring, return is dangerous

content.text: After Decree No. 278 of 4 September 2023, many Belarusians in Germany found themselves in a position where their passport is expiring and a new one can only be obtained in Belarus. For those who took part in the 2020 protests, worked in independent media, or supported political prisoners, return means a real risk of arrest, imprisonment and confiscation of property. German law has several solutions for such cases.

items: An asylum application (Asylantrag) under §3 AsylG (refugee protection, Flüchtlingsschutz) — the main route
§22, §23 AufenthG — a humanitarian residence permit (through the state or the Interior Ministry)
§25 Abs. 3 AufenthG — a residence permit when departure is impossible
§25 Abs. 5 AufenthG — a residence permit when departure is legally/factually impossible
Travel document for foreigners (Reiseausweis für Ausländer, §5 AufenthV) — the grey passport

content.text: If there are specific grounds for persecution (participation in protests, opposition activity, journalism, LGBT, evading the army, etc.), the best route is an asylum application (Asylantrag). It is filed at BAMF, free of charge. Details are in the guide "Belarusians: grounds for asylum". This route grants the right to work, a legal status, and a travel document (travel document for refugees, Reiseausweis für Flüchtlinge).

items: Upon recognition (bei Anerkennung) as a refugee (Flüchtling) — a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) for 3 years + a travel document
Subsidiary protection (Subsidiärer Schutz) — 1 year with extension + a travel document
The right to work from the moment of recognition (and even before that — after 3 months in Germany)
Access to language courses (the integration course, Integrationskurs)
Family reunification is possible (§29 AufenthG)

content.text: If asylum is not a fit (no personal persecution, missed deadlines, risk of rejection), there are the humanitarian provisions of the Residence Act (Aufenthaltsgesetz). They grant a residence permit without refugee status.

Admission from abroad (Aufnahme aus dem Ausland) — usually under a federal admission programme (Bundesaufnahmeprogramm). For those already in Germany it is applied more rarely, but it is possible by a decision of the Federal Interior Ministry (BMI) in individual cases.

items.title: §23 AufenthG — admission by a state's decision

content.text: §23 Abs. 1 AufenthG — mass programmes (for example, states such as Berlin and Bremen may run a special procedure for Belarusians). §23 Abs. 2 — an individual case through the state's Interior Ministry (Innenministerium). §23a AufenthG — the state's hardship commission (Härtefallkommission; for individual hardship cases).

items: If BAMF has established a ban on deportation (Abschiebungsverbot) under §60 Abs. 5 or Abs. 7 AufenthG
A temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) for 1 year with extension
The right to work is permitted
Does not require recognition of refugee status

content.text: If departure is impossible in fact (no valid passport, the country does not issue documents) or in law (risk of persecution), and this situation persists, a residence permit is issued. This is the key provision for Belarusians with an expired passport! It runs for 1 year and is renewable; after 18 months you automatically gain the right to work.

This is Germany's "grey passport" for foreigners who cannot obtain a passport from their country of origin for valid reasons. It is governed by §5 AufenthV (Aufenthaltsverordnung). The application is filed at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde).

items: Condition: the foreigner cannot reasonably be expected to obtain a passport from their country
Condition: the stay in Germany is lawful (you hold a residence permit, Aufenthaltstitel; a deportation deferral, Duldung, does not count)
Submission at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) for your area
Documents: proof of attempts to renew the Belarusian passport + the text of Decree No. 278
Issuing time — 1-3 months, sometimes longer
Cost: ~76€ for an adult (valid for 6 years)
With the travel document (Reiseausweis) you can travel to most Schengen countries (BUT NOT to Belarus!)

content.text: A deportation deferral (Duldung, §60a AufenthG) — a "toleration of deportation" — is NOT a residence permit. It is merely a suspension of deportation. You receive it when there is an obligation to leave (Ausreisepflicht) but deportation is in fact impossible. For Belarusians it is often issued when the passport has expired and they cannot leave. Duldung is a poor position: a limited right to work (a separate permit is needed), no integration courses, no right to family reunification.

items: Duldung ≠ a residence permit. It is a status of suspended deportation.
The right to work — only on request to the foreigners' authority (an employment permit, Beschäftigungserlaubnis)
After 18 months of Duldung — a transition to §25b AufenthG is possible (the well integrated)
After 30 months — §25a AufenthG for young people under 27
The goal is not to get stuck on a Duldung, but to move on to a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel)

content.text: Delay = slipping into a deportation deferral (Duldung). If your passport has already expired, go to the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) and/or file an asylum application (Asylantrag) IMMEDIATELY — do not wait. Every month without a status worsens your position.

Approaching the Belarusian consulate to renew your passport "for the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde)" can be interpreted by BAMF as voluntarily re-establishing contact with the persecuting state. Consult a lawyer first!

Decree No. 278 does not say "Belarusians may not renew their passport" — it says "only on the territory of Belarus". This may sound formally neutral, but in practice it makes renewal impossible for émigrés. Make sure your lawyer understands that this affects all Belarusians, not just the politically persecuted.

Do not go to the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) without a lawyer experienced in Belarusian cases. Every word on the record matters. Contacts: Pro Asyl, Beratungsstelle für politisch Verfolgte aus Belarus (Berlin).

title: Belarusian passport: renewal in Germany (Decree No. 278)
tldr: After Lukashenko's Decree No. 278 of 4 September 2023, the renewal and replacement of a Belarusian passport at the embassy in Berlin has stopped — it can now be done only on the territory of Belarus. For those who cannot return, the only legal route is the German travel document for foreigners (Reiseausweis für Ausländer, §5 AufenthV) and/or a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) under §25 Abs. 5 AufenthG. Start the procedure urgently, 6-12 months before the passport expires.

content.text: Decree of the President of the Republic of Belarus No. 278 of 4 September 2023 "On documenting citizens of the Republic of Belarus" introduced a requirement that a citizen be personally present in Belarus to process or exchange a passport. This effectively closed off the option of renewing a passport through the consulate in Berlin for anyone who cannot or does not want to return to Belarus. The law is published on pravo.by.

items: Date of entry into force: 4 September 2023
Issuing authority: only Interior Ministry offices in Belarus
Exchange on expiry — only in Belarus
Replacement after loss — only in Belarus
Replacement upon a change of name — only in Belarus
Initial issue to an adult — only in Belarus

steps.title: What a Belarusian in Germany should do

content.text: If you hold a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel; any residence permit) and your Belarusian passport is about to expire, you need to act IN ADVANCE — 6-12 months ahead. There are three options: 1) Actually return to Belarus (for those with no political risks); 2) A travel document for foreigners (Reiseausweis für Ausländer; the grey passport of Germany); 3) For persons with protection status — a travel document for refugees / persons with subsidiary protection (Reiseausweis für Flüchtlinge / subsidiär Schutzberechtigte; the blue passport).

items: Only for those who did NOT take part in protests, sign petitions or make donations
Check yourself against the "extremist" lists on pravo.by and in open databases
Processing a passport in Belarus — up to 1 month (standard) or 3-15 days (express, for a surcharge)
Cost in Belarus — a few base units (about 50-80 BYN ~15-25€)
Do not return to Belarus if you have the slightest doubt!

items.title: Option B: Reiseausweis für Ausländer (§5 AufenthV)

content.text: The main route for most Belarusians in Germany without protection status. It is a German travel document — the grey passport. It is issued when a foreigner cannot reasonably be expected to obtain a passport from their country of citizenship. Valid for 6 years. The application is filed at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde).

items.title: Option C: Reiseausweis for persons with a status

items: Persons entitled to asylum / refugees (Asylberechtigte / Flüchtlinge) under §3 AsylG → the blue passport (Geneva Convention, Genfer Konvention)
Persons with subsidiary protection (Subsidiär Schutzberechtigte) → a separate travel document §1 Abs. 3 AufenthV
These documents grant freedom of movement in Schengen and most countries
Submission at BAMF/the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde), free of charge or ~50€

steps.title: How to obtain a Reiseausweis für Ausländer

content.text: The travel document for foreigners (Reiseausweis für Ausländer; RfA, the grey passport) is issued under §5 AufenthV. The main condition is "Unzumutbarkeit der Passbeschaffung" (the unreasonableness of obtaining a passport). For Belarusians, after Decree No. 278, this is argued as a factual impossibility.

items: The text of Decree No. 278 (in Russian + a translation into German)
The Belarusian consulate's reply refusing to renew the passport (if any)
A letter/email with an attempt to book an appointment at the consulate
Documents on political activity (if any) — for the impossibility of return
If you have protection status — the official BAMF decision (Bescheid)

items.title: 2. Book an appointment at the Ausländerbehörde

content.text: Book an appointment (Termin) for the service "Ausstellung Reiseausweis für Ausländer". In Berlin, use the appointment portal (service.berlin.de); in other cities, the local portals. The wait ranges from several weeks to months.

items: Application (Antrag auf Ausstellung eines Reiseausweises)
Valid or expired Belarusian passport
Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel)
Biometric photos
Documents on the impossibility of obtaining a Belarusian passport
Fee ~76€

content.text: The decision is made by the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde), sometimes with the involvement of the BMI. Issuing takes 1-6 months, depending on the state. If it is refused, you file an objection (Widerspruch), and then go to court.
Additional documents that may be needed during the procedure. The more evidence you provide, the better your chance of a quick positive decision.

items: Residence registration (Anmeldung, Meldebescheinigung) — the registration confirmation
Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — a valid residence permit
Expired/valid Belarusian passport
The supplement from the passport (Anlage Reisepass)
Birth certificate (with apostille) + translation
Marriage certificate (if any) + translation
Biometric photos 35×45 mm
The text of Decree No. 278 with a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung)
Any media publications about consular practice after the Decree
Letters about the attempt to approach the consulate

content.text: A travel document (Reiseausweis) for persons without protection status does NOT permit entry into Belarus — it is a substitute for the country-of-origin passport. You will not be let into Belarus with it (there is no Belarusian visa for the country's own citizens).

Do not wait for your passport to expire! The application takes months. If the passport has expired and the travel document (Reiseausweis) has not yet arrived, you formally have no valid ID — problems may arise with your bank, your employer and at a police check.

When extending a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) on an expired Belarusian passport, questions may arise. Bring all proof of your renewal attempts + the text of Decree No. 278 + (if you have it) the decision on the travel document (Reiseausweis).

Some foreigners' authorities (Ausländerbehörden) are not well versed in the Belarusian situation and may demand a formal refusal from the consulate. The argument to make: the consulate does not issue a formal refusal, but Decree No. 278 says "only in Belarus" — and that is a de facto refusal.
With a travel document (Reiseausweis), the range of countries you can travel to is limited — some states do not recognize it without a visa. Check before you travel.

title: Chinese citizens: visas, students and work in Germany
tldr: Chinese (PRC) citizens must obtain a visa to enter Germany. The most common route is the student visa §16b AufenthG (TU München, RWTH Aachen, FU/HU Berlin, TU Berlin). For specialists, there is the EU Blue Card (Blue Card) §18b and the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte). Documents go through the APS verification procedure (Akademische Prüfstelle, the academic verification office at the embassy in Beijing). Fees: type C — 90€, type D — 75€, residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — 100€.

content.text: PRC citizens must obtain a visa to enter Germany. The German embassy in Beijing (Deutsche Botschaft Peking) and the consulates-general in Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu and Shenyang each serve different provinces. Website: china.diplo.de. First comes document verification through APS (Akademische Prüfstelle, the academic verification office), then the visa is processed through VFS Global or directly at the mission.

items: Type C (Schengen) — up to 90 days, for tourism, business
Type D (national visa) — for study, work, family over 90 days
The embassy in Beijing + 4 consulates-general
APS — mandatory for study and academic work
Submission through the China Visa Application Service Centre (VFS)

content.text: APS (Akademische Prüfstelle, the academic verification office) is a mandatory check of academic documents for Chinese citizens who want to study or do academic work in Germany. It was set up as a safeguard against forged documents. It operates at the embassy in Beijing and has branch offices. The aim is to confirm the authenticity of degrees and a sufficient level of knowledge.

items.title: 1. Which documents are needed for the APS

items: School leaving certificate (高中毕业证书) + Gaokao (高考)
Bachelor's certificate (学士学位证书) + diploma (Diplom, 毕业证书)
Transcript of grades (成绩单)
All documents — originals + certified copies + translations
Language certificate (TestDaF, DSH for German; IELTS/TOEFL for English-language programmes)

content.text: Register at aps.org.cn. Submit the documents in person or by post. Bachelor's holders and students sit an interview (APS Interview) in German or English. The aim is to verify that the applicant really studied in their field.

After successful verification, you receive the APS certificate (APS-Zertifikat, 10 copies). Without it, German universities do not accept documents from Chinese applicants. The procedure takes 2-4 months and costs about 250€.

The most common route to Germany for Chinese citizens. According to BAMF and DAAD data, Chinese students are the largest group of foreign students from non-European countries. Top fields: engineering (TU München, RWTH Aachen, KIT), business (Mannheim, Frankfurt School), music/art (UdK Berlin).

items: Admission by a university (Zulassungsbescheid)
The APS certificate (APS-Zertifikat)
Financial proof: a blocked account (Sperrkonto) of 12,324€ (1027€×12) for 2026
Health insurance
Language: German DSH-2/TestDaF 4 or English B2-C1 (depending on the programme)
Apply for the visa at the embassy or consulate-general responsible for your place of registration in China
Issuing time — 8-12 weeks, fee 75€

steps.title: Blue Card and Chancenkarte for Chinese specialists

content.text: Chinese specialists with a higher education degree have the same routes available as citizens of other third countries. The EU Blue Card (Blue Card EU, §18b AufenthG) requires a contract with a salary from 50 700€/year (standard 2026) or from 45 934€/year (shortage professions Mangelberufe: IT, doctors, engineers). The Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte, §§20a, 20b AufenthG), in force since June 2024, is for finding work. The exact thresholds are adjusted annually.

items: Degree recognition: anabin.kmk.org → Chinese 985/211 universities usually hold H+ status
If the university is not in Anabin: an official degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) from ZAB (~200€)
Marriage certificate (Trauungsurkunde), birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) — with a PRC apostille and translation
Police clearance certificate from the PRC (无犯罪记录证明) — apostille, translation
D visa at the embassy in Beijing, ~3 months processing
A transition from §16b (student) to §18b (Blue Card) after graduation, without leaving the country, is possible

content.text: The PRC joined the Hague Apostille Convention (Apostille Convention) in November 2023 — since then the apostille has applied. Before that, full consular legalization was required. The apostille is now affixed by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or by the authorized provincial Foreign Affairs Offices (FAO).

items: Apostille — the PRC MFA or a provincial FAO (after 7 November 2023)
Certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) from Chinese into German — by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) in Germany
Names: pinyin vs. characters — use a single, consistent transliteration across all documents
Birth and marriage certificates — apostille + translation
Degrees — through APS, then ZAB if necessary
Police clearance certificate — usually valid for 6 months

content.text: Without the APS certificate (APS-Zertifikat), universities in Germany will not accept an application from a PRC citizen, even with a perfect degree. APS is not a formality but a genuine check, complete with an interview.
The blocked account (Sperrkonto) must be opened at a German bank or with a licensed provider (Expatrio, Fintiba, Coracle). Chinese banks and accounts in the PRC are not accepted.

The name on the visa must match the passport exactly (pinyin). Any discrepancy on the residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel), the degree or at the bank causes problems. Always check the Latin-script spelling.
Family reunification for the parents of Chinese students or workers is almost impossible (§36 AufenthG requires a hardship case, Härtefall). A tourist visit by invitation is possible.
A police clearance certificate from the PRC is valid for 6 months. Order it only when you need it, not in advance.

When applying for a Blue Card, the employer must obtain prior approval (Vorabzustimmung) from the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit, BA) for most professions — this is not the visa itself but the BA's consent. Without it, the application is rejected.

title: Georgian citizens: visa-free entry 90/180 days
tldr: Since 28 March 2017, Georgian citizens with a biometric passport can enter the Schengen countries (including Germany) without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180 days. This is a tourist regime — you may NOT work. For work/study/relocation you need a national visa (Nationales Visum, D) or a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel). Visa-free travel gives you a good head start on a job search via the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) and the EU Blue Card (Blue Card).

content.text: Under EU Regulation 2017/372 of 1 March 2017 (which amended Regulation 539/2001), Georgian citizens with biometric passports were granted visa-free entry into the Schengen area. The visa-free regime has been in force since 28 March 2017. The limit is 90 days in any 180-day period, for tourism, visiting relatives or business meetings. You may NOT work without a national visa (Nationales Visum) D.

items: Start date: 28 March 2017
Basis: Regulation (EU) 2017/372 (an amendment to the Regulation on visa requirements)
Term: 90 days in every 180 days
Condition: a biometric Georgian passport
Allowed: tourism, business visits, visiting family, study of up to 90 days
Not allowed: work, long-term study, a residence permit

content.text: The 90/180 rule is often misunderstood. It is NOT "90 days per half-year" but a sliding window: on any given day, you look back over the previous 180 days, and in total you must have spent no more than 90 days in Schengen during that period. So you can stay 90 days in a row, then spend 90 days outside Schengen, then stay another 90.

items: Calculator: ec.europa.eu/assets/home/visa-calculator/calculator.htm
Every day of entry and exit counts (even a partial day = 1 day)
All Schengen countries are counted together (Germany + France + Italy...)
NOT counted toward the 90/180: the UK, Ireland and Cyprus (outside Schengen). Croatia has been in Schengen since 1 January 2023, so it counts.
ETIAS: as of mid-2026 the system has not yet launched; it is expected at the end of 2026, with a transition period — the visa-free regime remains in place in the meantime

content.text: Visa-free travel is for tourism. To stay longer you must either leave Schengen and wait, or obtain a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel). Georgians often use the visa-free regime to scout out the country, look for work and file residence-permit applications.

items: Since June 2024 — a points-based card for finding work
Requirements: education/experience, language (German A1 or English B2), funding
You can apply at the embassy in Tbilisi BEFORE entry
Validity — up to 1 year
You can work up to 20 h/week + trial employment (Probebeschäftigung) of up to 2 weeks

content.text: §18b AufenthG. A contract with a salary from 50 700€/year (or from 45 934€/year for shortage professions Mangelberufe) for 2026. A Georgian degree must be in Anabin with an H+ rating or recognized through ZAB.
§18a/§18b AufenthG. For specialists with relevant education or training and a contract. The salary is below the Blue Card level; Anabin/ZAB recognition or recognition of the profession is required.

Admission to a German university → a D visa at the embassy in Tbilisi → a transition to a student residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel). A blocked account (Sperrkonto) for students — 11 904€ (992€×12) for 2026.
If your spouse is a German citizen or holds a German residence permit. Through the embassy in Tbilisi.

Important: since 23 December 2023, Georgia has been included in the list of safe countries of origin (sichere Herkunftsstaaten) under Anlage II AsylG. This means that asylum applications from Georgian citizens are reviewed under an accelerated procedure, with a presumption that they are unfounded. Positive decisions are possible only with proof of specific individual persecution.

items: Georgia — on the Anlage II AsylG list since 2023
Applications are reviewed under §29a AsylG as "offensichtlich unbegründet"
The deadline to appeal a rejection is 1 week
A work ban during the procedure
After a rejection, a fresh application is possible only with substantially new circumstances
In most cases, not recommended for Georgian citizens

content.text: Georgia joined the 1961 Hague Convention in 2007 — the apostille is affixed by the Georgian Ministry of Justice (the House of Justice). All documents for Germany (degrees, certificates, statements) require an apostille + a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung).

items: Apostille on the degree — the Georgian Ministry of Justice (sda.gov.ge)
Certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) Georgian → German — a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) in Germany
Civil-registry certificates — apostille mandatory
Police clearance certificate — the Georgian Ministry of Justice + apostille
A Georgian biometric passport — mandatory for visa-free travel
Old passports without biometrics — the visa-free regime does NOT apply

content.text: Visa-free travel does NOT grant the right to work. Working in Germany without a D visa breaches §95 AufenthG, punishable by a fine of up to 5000€ or up to 1 year in prison, plus deportation and an entry ban (Einreisesperre). This also applies to remote work under a German contract.
Exceeding 90 days is an overstay (Überstand). The consequences: an entry ban (Einreisesperre) of 1-5 years and a flag in the Schengen SIS II system. Count the days carefully!
Applying for asylum as a Georgian citizen means an almost certain rejection plus an entry ban (Einreisesperre). Use the Chancenkarte, the Blue Card or a student visa, not asylum.

ETIAS is not a visa but a mandatory prior authorization for visa-free visitors to Schengen. As of mid-2026 the system has not yet launched; it is expected at the end of 2026, followed by a transition period. After launch the fee is 20€ (raised from the previous 7€; those under 18 and over 70 are exempt), and the authorization is valid for 3 years. You are meant to apply for it in advance, before travelling. Check the timing and conditions on the official portal travel-europe.europa.eu.
On entry, the federal police (Bundespolizei) may ask about your purpose, your means and your return ticket. Be ready to show an accommodation booking, a return ticket and ~50€/day on a card.

title: Indian citizens: the Blue Card as the main route
tldr: India is the largest source of EU Blue Cards (Blue Card) in Germany: according to BAMF, Indian citizens are the largest group of Blue Card recipients (a significant share of the cards in 2023–2024; for exact shares, see current BAMF statistics). The main routes: the EU Blue Card (Blue Card) §18b AufenthG (IT, engineers, doctors), the Opportunity Card Chancenkarte §20a AufenthG (since June 2024), the student visa §16b. Fees: D visa — 75€, residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — 100€. The biggest barrier is the long wait for an appointment at the embassy in New Delhi.

content.text: India is one of the largest sources of qualified migrants for Germany. According to BAMF, Indian citizens are the largest group of EU Blue Card (Blue Card EU) recipients (for the exact shares by year, see BAMF statistics). This reflects the high proportion of IT specialists, engineers and researchers among them. The German embassy in New Delhi and the consulates-general in Mumbai, Bangalore, Kolkata and Chennai handle visa applications. Website: india.diplo.de.

items: India's share of Germany's Blue Cards: the No. 1 country of origin
Main sectors: IT (Software Engineer), mechanical engineering, medicine
The embassy in New Delhi + 4 consulates-general
Submission of applications through VFS Global India
Long waits for an appointment — 3-6 months

steps.title: Blue Card EU — the main route

content.text: The EU Blue Card (Blue Card EU) is governed by §18b AufenthG (after the 2023 reform). Since 18 November 2023, the rules have been eased under Directive (EU) 2021/1883. This is the fastest route for Indian specialists with a higher education degree and a contract in Germany.

items: A higher education degree (Bachelor, minimum 3 years) OR, for IT, 3 years of experience (§19c Abs. 2 for IT without a degree)
The degree is recognized in Anabin (H+) or assessed as equivalent through ZAB
A contract with a German employer (at least 6 months)
Salary: 50,700€/year general standard, 45,934€/year for Mangelberufe (as of 2026)
Mangelberufe: IT, engineers, doctors, mathematicians, natural sciences

items.title: 2. Submission in New Delhi / a consulate-general

items: Appointment through VFS Global India (vfsglobal.com/de-in)
Application for a national visa (Nationales Visum)
Contract + job offer (Beschäftigungsangebot)
Degree + official degree assessment Anabin/ZAB (Zeugnisbewertung)
Biometric photos, travel insurance
Proof of accommodation (an Airbnb booking / Wohnungsbescheinigung)
Fee 75€

content.text: For most Blue Cards the employer obtains prior approval (Vorabzustimmung) from the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit, BA) — this takes 2-4 weeks. It is not mandatory for all Mangelberufe, but it is recommended to speed things up.

items.title: 4. Timelines and the Blue Card term

items: Visa processing at the embassy — 8-12 weeks
The Blue Card is issued for the contract term + 3 months (max 4 years)
Permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) — after 27 months (German B1) or 21 months (German B2)
The right to change employer — after 1 year, without the consent of the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde)
Family — enters under a simplified scheme (§30 AufenthG), without a German-language requirement

content.text: Since 1 June 2024 — the points-based Opportunity Card Chancenkarte (§§20a, 20b AufenthG). For Indians, this is an alternative if you do not yet have a contract in hand. You can look for work in Germany for up to 1 year.

items: Basic requirements: education (3 years) or experience (2 years) + language + finances
At least 6 points in the points system
Finances: a blocked account (Sperrkonto) of 12,324€ OR a formal sponsorship undertaking (Verpflichtungserklärung) from a sponsor
The Chancenkarte is valid for 1 year, extension possible if you have an offer
Part-time work during the search: 20 h/week + trial employment (Probebeschäftigung) of 2 weeks
On receiving an offer — a transition to §18a/§18b at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde), without leaving the country

content.text: Indian students are a large group at German technical universities (TU München, RWTH Aachen, KIT, TU Berlin). The §16b AufenthG visa. For PhDs and postdocs, there is §18d AufenthG (researcher, Forscher), with a simplified scheme through a Hosting Agreement.

items: Students: admission (Zulassung) + a blocked account (Sperrkonto) of 12,324€ + insurance + APS (not required for Indians, unlike the PRC)
Finances: you can prove a scholarship (Stipendium) from DAAD/Erasmus
Issuing time for a student visa — 6-12 weeks
The right to work: 140 full days or 280 half-days per year
After graduation — a temporary residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) for 18 months to look for work (§20 AufenthG)
Researcher (Forscher) §18d — a hosting agreement (Aufnahmevereinbarung) with a recognized institute is needed
Researchers (Forscher) can bring their family without German-language knowledge

content.text: A special case. India joined the Hague Apostille Convention (in 2005), BUT Germany raised an objection to India's accession at the time, so the Convention does NOT apply between Germany and India — an Indian apostille has no force for Germany. German missions in India stopped consular legalization back in 2000. Instead, a document-verification procedure (Verifikationsverfahren) applies: the authenticity of Indian documents is checked by a German authority/court through authorized providers — the applicant cannot initiate it themselves. In practice this means: check in advance with the receiving authority (the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde), the civil-registry office, the university) and on the website of the German embassy in Delhi which document-confirmation procedure applies in your case. Confirm the exact procedure with a specialist lawyer.

items: An Indian apostille (MEA) does NOT work for Germany — the Convention does not apply between Germany and India
Legalization at German missions in India was stopped in 2000
A verification procedure (Verifikationsverfahren) applies: the check is initiated by a German authority or court, not by the applicant
Check the document-confirmation procedure with the receiving authority and on india.diplo.de
Certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) English/Hindi → German — by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) in Germany
Anabin: many Indian universities are in the H+ category
Marriage Certificate, Birth Certificate — obtain official state registration (MRO/SDM)
PCC (Police Clearance Certificate) — for long-term visas, not older than 6 months

content.text: VFS Global India waiting times are the main pain point. In New Delhi and Bangalore, Blue Card appointments are 3-6 months out. Book as soon as you have a contract. Do not use "agents" — they often resell the same appointment with a 200-500€ markup.

An Indian apostille does not work for Germany: although India has been a party to the Hague Convention since 2005, Germany objected to its accession, so the Convention does not apply between the two countries. German missions in India stopped legalization in 2000; instead, a verification procedure (Verifikationsverfahren; the check is requested by a German authority) applies. Do not rely on the "MEA apostille" — check the requirements on india.diplo.de and with the receiving authority.

Recognition of marriage: an Indian marriage performed only by religious rites, without state registration, may NOT be recognized in Germany. Obtain a Marriage Certificate from the local MRO/SDM and have it legalized.
IT without a degree (§19c Abs. 2 AufenthG) is formally possible, but in practice the foreigners' authority often demands a degree. Be ready for lengthy explanations and 5+ years of experience.

A salary below the shortage-profession threshold (Mangelberufe; 45,934€ as of 2026) = a Blue Card rejection. If the offer is lower, consider §18b as an ordinary skilled worker, with different thresholds, rather than a Blue Card.
English in India is no substitute for German. The sooner you start learning German (A1-B1), the easier integration, extensions and permanent residence become — in 21 months instead of 27.

title: Iranian citizens: sanctions restrictions
tldr: Iranian citizens can enter and live in Germany on the usual grounds: §16b (study), §18a/§18b and §18g (EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU), qualified work), §16f (job search), and they can apply for asylum (Asyl) in cases of political persecution. But because of EU and US sanctions, Iranians face serious restrictions in banking: transfers between Germany and Iran through banks are practically impossible (most Iranian banks are cut off from SWIFT, OFAC restrictions apply, and dollar transactions are especially risky). There is no separate APS structure for Iran — documents are submitted through uni-assist/the university; for sensitive technical and natural-science fields the embassy may carry out an additional security check (Sicherheitsüberprüfung). This guide is about the realities: which grounds for stay are available, how to work around the banking dead end through legal channels, and where sanctions actually interfere with everyday life.

steps.title: Grounds for stay for Iranian citizens

content.text: From the standpoint of migration law, Germany imposes no general entry ban on Iranians — the sanctions target the regime and specific individuals and organizations, not citizens as such. So the usual titles under the Residence Act (Aufenthaltsgesetz) are available: study (§16b AufenthG — one of the most popular grounds), the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) and qualified employment (§18b, §18g AufenthG), the job-search visa §16f, and family reunification. Separately, there is the right to asylum and protection under the Asylum Act (Asylgesetz) and §60 AufenthG for persons facing a well-founded risk of political, religious or gender-based persecution.

items: Study — §16b AufenthG: enrolment at a university + proof of funding (a blocked account, Sperrkonto, ~11 904 €/year, verify the figure)
Qualified work — §18b / the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) §18g if you have a degree and the threshold salary
Job/study search — §16f / §20 AufenthG for specialists and graduates
Asylum — an asylum application (Asylantrag) at BAMF in cases of persecution; protection under §60 AufenthG

content.text: For sensitive technical and natural-science fields (nuclear physics, rocketry, certain areas of chemistry/biotechnology) the embassy may carry out an extended security check (Sicherheitsüberprüfung). This is lawful and delays the visa review by weeks or months. Do not submit forged documents — if discovered, they lead to rejection and a block on future applications.

Important: for Iranian citizens there is NO separate APS structure (Akademische Prüfstelle, the academic verification office), as there is for the PRC, India and Vietnam. Iranian applicants submit their educational documents directly through uni-assist or to a preparatory college or university (Studienkolleg), which checks their authenticity and level. So no formal "APS certificate" is required for Iran. Separately from the academic check, the embassy may carry out a security check for sensitive fields (see the previous section). Check the specific document requirements on the website of the German embassy in Tehran and with your chosen university.

items: Check your university/degree in advance in the database anabin.kmk.org (the H+ category — recognized)
Submit your educational documents through uni-assist or directly to the university or preparatory college (Studienkolleg)
Gather originals of your leaving certificate, degree, transcripts of grades + certified translations
Bear in mind that for sensitive fields an extended visa check is possible (see the section on grounds for stay)

steps.title: Banks and transfers: the main problem

content.text: This is the key practical difficulty. Most Iranian banks are cut off from SWIFT and are under EU and US (OFAC) sanctions. Direct Iran↔Germany transfers through the banking system effectively do not work. German banks are extremely reluctant to carry out any transaction connected with Iran, for fear of US secondary sanctions — especially dollar payments. This creates a vicious circle: opening a blocked account (Sperrkonto) and proving funding for study with money from Iran is almost impossible.

Money for a blocked account (Sperrkonto) is more often routed through third countries or through relatives and sponsors outside Iran. Blocked-account providers (specialized services, for example) accept payments from outside Iran. The realistic route is a sponsor abroad, a transfer from a country outside the sanctions perimeter, or funds that have been legally exported and declared.

items.title: 2. An everyday bank account in Germany

content.text: An Iranian with a lawful residence permit can open a current account (Girokonto) in Germany — it is a right (a basic account, Basiskonto, under the Payment Accounts Act, Zahlungskontengesetz). But the bank carries out enhanced due diligence (KYC) and may refuse transfers connected with Iran. For salary, rent and daily life the account works normally; the problem is specifically cross-border transactions with Iran.

items.title: 3. Do not try to circumvent sanctions

content.text: Using "hawala", front accounts or other means to circumvent sanctions is a criminal offence under the Foreign Trade Act (Außenwirtschaftsgesetz, AWG). Frozen funds and a blocked account are a real risk. Discuss any transaction connected with Iran with your bank and, if necessary, with a lawyer specializing in export control and sanctions (Exportkontrolle).

For some Iranians the basis for stay is protection. An asylum application (Asylantrag) is filed at the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge, BAMF). Relevant grounds include persecution on political or religious grounds (including conversion from Islam, or atheism), participation in protests, persecution of LGBT people, and risk to women activists. If recognized, refugee status (§3 AsylG) or subsidiary protection (§4 AsylG) is granted, or a ban on deportation under §60 AufenthG.

items: An asylum application is filed in person, as early as possible after entry
Prepare evidence of persecution (documents, screenshots, testimonies)
If rejected — get to a lawyer urgently: the appeal deadlines at the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) are very short
Refugees under §3 AsylG are entitled to a bank account (a basic account, Basiskonto) by law

title: Kazakhstan citizens: visas and Spätaussiedler
tldr: Kazakhstan is a visa-required country for the EU: to enter you need a Schengen C visa (tourism/visit) or a national D visa (work, study, family reunion). But Kazakhstan has a unique channel: the world's largest diaspora of ethnic Germans. Under §4 BVFG you can obtain Spätaussiedler status — effectively a direct path to German citizenship via an admission decision (Aufnahmebescheid) from the Bundesverwaltungsamt, without a D visa and without giving up your Kazakh passport. Skilled professionals can use the usual work routes: EU Blue Card (§18b AufenthG), §18a/§18b for qualified workers, and the Chancenkarte (points-based job-search card, §20a AufenthG). The apostille on Kazakh documents is issued by the Kazakh Ministry of Justice; diplomas are checked via anabin/ZAB.

content.text: Kazakhstan is on the Annex I list of EU Regulation 2018/1806 — a visa is required for any entry into the Schengen area. For short stays (up to 90 days within a 180-day period) you apply for a Schengen visa of category C; for a long-term stay, a national visa of category D, issued by the German embassy (Botschaft) in Astana or the consulate general (Generalkonsulat) in Almaty.

items: C visa (Schengen): tourism, visiting family, business trip — up to 90/180 days
D visa (national): work, study, family reunion, Chancenkarte — more than 90 days
Visa appointment — via the German embassy in Astana / consulate general in Almaty, often with a wait of several weeks
Late repatriates (Spätaussiedler) enter NOT on a visa but on an admission decision (Aufnahmebescheid) + Übernahmebescheid (see below)
Diplomas and qualifications are checked via the anabin database (the database for recognising foreign diplomas) and ZAB (the Central Office for Foreign Education) before applying for a work visa
Kazakh documents are legalised with an apostille (Kazakhstan is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

steps.title: Spätaussiedler under §4 BVFG — the main channel

content.text: Kazakhstan is home to one of the largest communities of Russian (Volga) Germans, deported in 1941. The Federal Expellees Act (Bundesvertriebenengesetz, BVFG) grants their descendants the status of late repatriate (Spätaussiedler). Under §4 Abs. 1 BVFG, a late repatriate is a person of German ethnicity (deutscher Volkszugehöriger) from the republics of the former USSR who left them after 31.12.1992 within the admission procedure (Aufnahmeverfahren) and settled in the Federal Republic. After registration under §15 BVFG the person automatically acquires German citizenship under §7 StAG — without a separate naturalisation (Einbürgerung) and without giving up the Kazakh passport.

items: The admission application (Aufnahmeantrag) is filed FROM ABROAD with the Federal Office of Administration (Bundesverwaltungsamt, BVA), Cologne

You must prove German ethnicity (deutsche Volkszugehörigkeit) under §6 BVFG: a German nationality entry in your documents (birth certificate, old passport with the nationality entry) and a German upbringing
language test: §6 Abs. 2 Nr. 3 BVFG — you need a confirmed minimum of German at A1 (a language assessment test, Sprachstandstest, or a Goethe-Zertifikat A1)
The BVA issues an admission decision (Aufnahmebescheid) to the applicant and an inclusion decision (Einbeziehungsbescheid) to family members (§7 Abs. 2, §8 BVFG)
After the move — registration (Registrierung) at the Friedland border transit camp (Grenzdurchgangslager Friedland) and issuance of a certificate (Bescheinigung) under §15 BVFG
German citizenship — by operation of law (kraft Gesetzes) under §7 StAG; the Kazakh one is retained (dual)
Family members (Familienangehörige) without German ethnicity enter under §7/§8 with a right of residence

content.text: Since 2013 the language requirement has been eased: A1 is enough, and family members are allowed to take the test in Germany. But "basic knowledge of German" (einfache Deutschkenntnisse) is genuinely tested — failing the test at the embassy (Sprachstandstest) blocks the admission decision. Be ready for an interview in German.

steps.title: Routes for skilled workers and the Chancenkarte

content.text: If you have no German roots, the general routes under the Skilled Immigration Act (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz) apply. The Make it in Germany portal is the official entry point. In 2024 the opportunity card (Chancenkarte, §§20a, 20b AufenthG) was added — a points-based visa for searching for a job on the spot.

items: EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU, §18g AufenthG): degree + contract with a salary from 50 700€/year (2026), or from 45 934€/year for shortage occupations (Mangelberufe)
§18a/§18b AufenthG: recognised qualification (Anerkennung) + employment contract
Opportunity card (Chancenkarte, §20a AufenthG): points system — degree/vocational training + language + age + experience; up to 1 year to search for a job
§16d AufenthG: for recognition of a foreign qualification, with the right to work part-time
Kazakh diplomas are checked via anabin (the ZAB database) — you need an H+ rating or partial recognition
A mandatory requirement (Voraussetzung) for all routes: German at A1–B1, or English for a Blue Card in IT

content.text: For IT specialists without a formal degree, a Blue Card is possible with 3 years of relevant experience within the last 7 years (§18g AufenthG). This is especially relevant for Kazakh developers.

title: Kazakh driving licence: exchange
tldr: Kazakhstan is NOT on the Anlage 11 FeV list (the annex listing the states whose licences are exchanged without an exam or with a partial exam). This means: holders of a Kazakh licence can drive in Germany for the first 6 months after moving (provided they have a translation/international permit), but for permanent driving you must fully convert the licence (Umschreibung), passing both the theory AND the practical exam. A medical/eye test and a first-aid course are also mandatory. This guide shows the real procedure: the 6-month window, the documents you need, the exams and the costs.

steps.title: Status of the Kazakh licence in Germany

content.text: Germany divides countries into categories under Anlage 11 FeV. EU/EEA states exchange 1:1. Some third countries are in Anlage 11 (full exchange without an exam, or with only a practical/theory exam). Kazakhstan is NOT listed in this annex (check the current text of Anlage 11 — the list changes). The general rule of §31 FeV therefore applies to a Kazakh licence: if the country is not on the list, you must pass both the theory and the practical exam.

Do not confuse Kazakhstan with "special agreements". There is no simplified exchange (Umschreibung) for a Kazakh licence in Anlage 11 — count on full exams. Always check against the current version of Anlage 11 FeV on gesetze-im-internet.de, as the list is periodically expanded.

Once you have established permanent residence in Germany (usually from the moment of residence registration, Anmeldung), the Kazakh licence is valid for driving for a further 6 months (§29 FeV). During this period it makes sense to start the conversion immediately, because preparing for the exams, booking and lessons all take time. After the 6 months expire you may no longer drive on the Kazakh licence — that counts as driving without a licence (Fahren ohne Fahrerlaubnis, §21 StVG), a criminal offence.

items: Get an official translation of the Kazakh licence (from a sworn translator, vereidigter Übersetzer, or the ADAC — Germany's largest automobile club)
Start the licence exchange (Umschreibung) right after registration — don't wait until the end of the 6 months
Take an eye test (Sehtest) and a first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe-Kurs)
Enrol at a driving school (Fahrschule) to prepare for the exams

content.text: The application to exchange the licence is filed at the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle). Because Kazakhstan is not in Anlage 11, the authority will schedule both a theory (Theorieprüfung) and a practical (praktische Prüfung) exam. The theory is taken on a computer (available in several languages — check whether Russian is offered). The practical is with a TÜV (technical inspection and certification service) / DEKRA examiner. The German licence is only issued after you pass.

items.title: 1. Documents for the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle)

items: Valid passport (Reisepass) + residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel)
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Original Kazakh licence + certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung)
Biometric photo, eye test and first-aid course certificate

content.text: Both theory and practical are mandatory. Category B (passenger car) is the most common case. It's easier to prepare at a driving school, which will help with booking and provide study material. After you pass, the licence is exchanged; the Kazakh original is usually withheld and sent back to the issuing authority.

title: Russian accounts and sanctions
tldr: Because of EU sanctions, transfers between Russia and Germany are heavily restricted. The largest Russian banks (Sberbank, VTB, Sovcombank, Otkritie and others) are cut off from SWIFT and under EU sanctions, which blocks direct transfers. In addition, there is a general EU ban on accepting deposits over 100 000 € from Russian citizens/residents at a bank in any single EU country. What still works: transfers via NON-sanctioned banks (for example Raiffeisenbank Russia, Gazprombank — the status changes, check current lists), but with delays, intensified checks and often refusals by German banks on compliance grounds. This guide is about what actually works, what is blocked and how to avoid having your funds frozen.

content.text: Through successive sanctions packages (Regulation (EU) 833/2014 as amended), the EU has cut a number of Russian banks off from SWIFT and frozen their assets in the EU. This means: direct SWIFT transfers between these banks and Germany are impossible. The sanctioned ones traditionally include Sberbank, VTB, Sovcombank, Otkritie Bank, Promsvyazbank, Novikombank and others — the list keeps expanding, so always check against the current consolidated EU list.

items: SWIFT cut-off of sanctioned banks → direct transfers are impossible
EU ban on deposits from Russian residents over 100 000 € at a single bank in an EU country
Asset freeze for persons/entities named on the sanctions lists
Intensified compliance by German banks on any transactions involving Russia

content.text: Having your funds frozen is a real risk if your counterparty or bank ends up on a sanctions list. Do not split large sums across different banks to get around the 100 000 € limit — that counts as circumventing sanctions and is punishable under the Foreign Trade and Payments Act (Außenwirtschaftsgesetz).

Transfers Russia↔EU are not entirely banned in principle — what is banned are transactions with sanctioned banks and certain persons/purposes. Transferring an individual's personal funds via a NON-sanctioned bank is formally possible, but complicated in practice: German banks require proof of the origin of the funds (Herkunftsnachweis) and the purpose of the transfer, and may refuse on internal-policy grounds (de-risking). A bank's "non-sanctioned" status can change — check before every transaction.

Some Russian banks are, at the time of checking, not under sectoral EU SWIFT sanctions. Transfers can theoretically go through them, but with delays and fees. Before a transaction, always check the bank against the consolidated EU sanctions list and ask the receiving German bank whether it will process such an incoming transfer.

items.title: 2. Proof of the origin of the funds

items: Prepare proof of the origin of the funds (Herkunftsnachweis): sale contract, income statement, account statements
State a clear payment purpose (personal funds, not commerce under sanctions)
Be ready for compliance queries and a temporary freeze for review

content.text: The EU ban concerns the acceptance of deposits over 100 000 € from Russian citizens/residents at a bank in any single EU country. There are exceptions (for example for citizens of an EU/EEA country or holders of a residence permit of an EU country). If you hold a German residence permit, the exception may apply — confirm this with the bank in writing.

steps.title: A German account and everyday life

content.text: A Russian citizen with a legal residence permit has the right to a basic account (Basiskonto) under the Payment Accounts Act (Zahlungskontengesetz) in Germany — the bank cannot refuse purely because of nationality. For salary, rent and everyday life the account works normally. The problem is specifically cross-border transactions with Russia. For life in Germany it makes sense to keep your money in a German account and not depend on transfers from Russia.

If your Russian bank is under sanctions, your funds there are inaccessible for transfer within the EU. Visa/Mastercard cards issued in Russia do not work in Germany. Plan your finances on the assumption that the direct Russia→Germany channel can close at any moment.

title: Russian citizens: applying for a visa in 2026
tldr: Since 12 September 2022 the EU–Russia Visa Facilitation Agreement has been FULLY suspended (Council Decision (EU) 2022/1500). For Russian citizens this means: the visa fee has risen from 35 € to 80 € (the standard Visa Code fee), more supporting documents are required, processing times are significantly longer, and the rules for issuing multiple-entry visas are stricter. In 2026, applying for a German Schengen/national visa runs through a limited number of locations: the embassy in Moscow and a few representations (intake is heavily reduced). This guide covers the current procedure, the fee, the documents and the realities of getting an appointment.

content.text: By Council Decision (EU) 2022/1500 of 9 September 2022 (in force from 12.09.2022), the EU–Russia Visa Facilitation Agreement was fully suspended. It replaced the earlier partial suspension (Decision 2022/333). From that moment, Russians are assessed strictly under the Visa Code (Regulation (EC) 810/2009), like citizens of any third country with no facilitation.

items: Visa fee: 80 € (instead of the former 35 € under the facilitation agreement)
More supporting documents (purpose, finances, ties, insurance)
Significantly longer processing times than before
Stricter rules for multiple-entry visas

content.text: Tourist Schengen visas are currently issued to Russians on a very limited basis; many EU countries have in effect suspended tourist flows. Germany assesses applications on the merits, but the priority is humanitarian, family, work and study grounds. Do not count on an easy tourist visa.

Intake of German visa applications from Russians in 2026 is heavily restricted. The embassy (Botschaft) in Moscow and a few representations are operating; visa centres (intake runs through the VisaMetric service) have partly cut back their services. The specific intake point and appointment availability depend on the visa type (Schengen type C or national type D) and your region. Always check the current information on the official website of the German diplomatic mission.

Short stays up to 90 days. Fee 80 €. Appointments and intake are heavily restricted; processing times are longer than usual. Grounds that are looked on more favourably: visiting close relatives, medical reasons, business/official purposes with an invitation.

For a long-term stay: study (§16b AufenthG), work / EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte, §18b/§18g), family reunion. This is the main legal route for relocating. The national visa fee is usually 75 €. Appointments for national visas are often more available than for Schengen.

items: Valid passport (validity and blank pages per the requirements)
Completed application form, photo to standard, medical insurance with Schengen coverage
Proof of purpose (invitation, university admission, employment contract)
Proof of finances and ties; for a type D visa, the documents for the relevant AufenthG residence ground

content.text: Because facilitation has been fully suspended, prepare an extended package: the more convincing your purpose and ties, the higher your chances. Forged invitations/bookings are grounds for refusal and for being entered in the database. Apply well in advance, allowing for the longer processing times.

From 1 January 2026 a German visa can no longer be placed in a non-biometric Russian passport: non-biometric (5-year) passports are not accepted for application (intake stopped on 15 December 2025). You need a valid biometric passport. Check the requirements on the diplomatic mission's website and at the service centre (VisaMetric).

title: The Russian consulate in Berlin
tldr: The consular section of the Russian Embassy in Berlin and the Russian Consulate General in Bonn (after 2022 these are the only two operating Russian consular points in Germany; the consulates general in Hamburg, Frankfurt, Leipzig and Munich have been closed since late 2023 – early 2024) provide consular services to Russian citizens: issuing and renewing a passport, notarial acts (powers of attorney, certifications), civil-status records, certificates, consular registration, a proof-of-life act for pension purposes. The main reality of 2026 is long queues and long waits for an appointment (often months) and reduced staff. Booking is done through an electronic system (kdmid.ru / the representation's website germany.mid.ru). This guide covers the services, booking and how to minimise the wait.

content.text: The consular section of the Russian Embassy in Berlin and the Russian Consulate General in Bonn provide the standard consular services for Russian citizens — this is the main channel for documents valid in Russia. IMPORTANT: after 2022 the network shrank sharply. According to the German Federal Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt) and the Russian representations, as of 2026 only two points operate in Germany — Berlin (the embassy's consular section) and Bonn (the consulate general); the consulates general in Hamburg, Frankfurt am Main, Leipzig and Munich have been closed since late 2023 – early 2024 following the mutual expulsion of diplomats. This creates long queues and long waits for an appointment.

items: Passport: issuance and renewal (including biometric)
Notarial services: powers of attorney, consents, certification of copies and signatures
Civil-status records, certificates, requesting documents from Russia
Consular registration, a proof-of-life act to continue pension payments

content.text: Appointments are booked electronically through the unified system of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (kdmid.ru) and the representation's website germany.mid.ru. The 2026 reality is high demand and long waits: slots are snapped up quickly, and the wait for an appointment can stretch to months, especially for passport services. Plan ahead.

items: Register in the kdmid.ru pre-booking system
Choose the right representation for your German region
Check regularly for new slots — they are snapped up quickly
Prepare your complete set of documents in advance so you don't lose the slot

content.text: Consular districts divide German territory between the embassy in Berlin and the consulates general. You must apply to the institution to whose district your federal state of residence belongs. The list of districts is on germany.mid.ru.

Because of reduced staff and restrictions, timelines are unstable. Don't leave a passport renewal to the last month of the old one's validity. For urgent needs (for example a proof-of-life act for a pension), ask about alternatives — the fact of being alive can sometimes be confirmed by a German notary or authority instead.

steps.title: How to cut the wait and prepare

content.text: Since slots are limited, the key to success is precise preparation for a single visit. Check the list of documents for your service on germany.mid.ru in advance, pay the fee by the required method and check the validity of all your papers. Many refusals and repeat visits are due to an incomplete package or the wrong application form.

items: Download and complete the application using the exact form for your service
Check the requirements for photos, copies and translations in advance
Confirm the method of paying the consular fee (cash/transfer)
Bring the originals and copies of all documents to the appointment

content.text: Don't rely on "I'll sort it out on the spot" — re-booking can take weeks. If your matter can be settled without the consulate (for example confirmation for a pension via a German authority), consider that route so as not to use up a scarce slot.

title: Russian driving licence: 2026 changes
tldr: Russia is NOT on the Anlage 11 FeV list (the annex of countries whose licences are exchanged without a full exam). This means: after moving to Germany you may drive on a Russian licence only for the first 6 months (§29 FeV), and for permanent driving you need a full Umschreibung, passing both the theory and the practical exam. There are no longer any simplifications. An eye test (Sehtest) and a first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe) are also mandatory. This guide covers the current 2026 procedure, the 6-month window, the exams and the costs.

content.text: Russia is absent from Anlage 11 FeV — the annex listing the states with a simplified licence exchange (Umschreibung) — either fully without an exam or with only a partial one. Since Russia is not on the list, the general rule applies: conversion requires passing both the theory and the practical exam (§31 FeV). This is not a "change specifically for Russians" but a consequence of the country's absence from Anlage 11 — check the current version of the list.

There is no simplified exchange of a Russian licence for a German one without exams. Adverts for a "fast exchange without an exam" are a scam. Any exchange of a licence issued outside an Anlage 11 country requires exams.

From the moment you establish permanent residence in Germany (usually residence registration, Anmeldung), the Russian licence is valid for driving for a further 6 months (§29 FeV). After that, driving on it counts as driving without a licence (Fahren ohne Fahrerlaubnis, §21 StVG), a criminal offence. You should therefore start the licence exchange (Umschreibung) straight away, without waiting for the period to run out.

items: Get a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung) of the Russian licence (from a sworn translator, vereidigter Übersetzer, or the ADAC — Germany's largest automobile club)
Enrol at a driving school (Fahrschule) to prepare for the theory and practical
Take an eye test (Sehtest) and a first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe)
File the licence-exchange application at the driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) right after registration

content.text: The application is filed at the local driving licence authority (Führerscheinstelle). A theory exam (on a computer, Russian is often available — check) and a practical exam (with a TÜV — technical inspection and certification service — / DEKRA examiner) are scheduled. For category B this is the most common scenario. After you pass, the German licence is issued; the Russian original is usually withheld.

items: Passport (Reisepass) + residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel)
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Russian licence + certified translation
Biometric photo, eye test and first-aid course certificate

content.text: It's convenient to prepare at a driving school, which will book your exams and provide the materials. After you successfully pass the theory and practical, the German licence is issued.
