title: Russian passport in Germany
tldr: A Russian foreign-travel passport is issued and renewed through Russia's consular institutions in Germany. After the network was cut back in 2022–2023, only two points operate in Germany: the consular section of the Russian Embassy in Berlin and the Russian Consulate General in Bonn (the consulates general in Hamburg, Frankfurt, Leipzig and Munich are closed). Two options are available: the new-generation biometric passport (valid 10 years, issued at the consulate with fingerprinting) and the old-style passport (valid 5 years). The main reality of 2026 is long queues and long waits for an appointment and for production (the biometric passport often takes months, since the data is processed in Russia). This guide covers the difference between the passports, the documents, booking via kdmid.ru and the timelines.

content.text: At the consulate you can apply for a new-generation passport (biometric, valid 10 years) or an old-style one (5 years). The biometric one requires you to appear in person to give fingerprints and be photographed; its data is processed in Russia, so production takes longer. The old-style passport is simpler and faster, but valid for less time and harder to obtain for children, who have separate requirements.

items: Biometric (10 years): fingerprinting + photo at the consulate, longer production
Old-style (5 years): no fingerprints, usually faster
For children it is issued separately, with parents' consent/documents
Decide in advance which type you need — it affects booking and timelines

content.text: Appointments are booked through the kdmid.ru system and the representation's website germany.mid.ru, at the institution for your consular district. Demand is high, passport slots are snapped up quickly, and the wait for an appointment can run to months. After you apply, the biometric passport takes a further considerable time to produce.

items: Russian internal passport and/or a valid foreign-travel passport
Completed application on the proper form (via the system/portal)
Proof of legal residence in Germany (residence permit / residence registration, Anmeldung) — check the requirements
Receipt for payment of the consular fee, photo to requirements

content.text: Don't put off the renewal until the last months of the passport's validity: the appointment + production of a biometric passport can easily add up to six months or more. If you need the passport urgently (for example to renew a residence permit at the foreigners' authority, Ausländerbehörde), start the process early and check the timelines with the consulate.

steps.title: The passport and renewing your residence permit in Germany

content.text: A valid passport is needed not only for travel but also to renew your German residence permit: the foreigners' authority records your residence data, and the electronic residence card (eAT) is tied to a valid passport. If your passport is expiring, synchronise the timelines — otherwise the residence permit may be issued for a shortened period (up to the passport's expiry date).

items: Make sure the passport is valid at the time of renewing the residence permit
Factor the long production times into planning the renewal of your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel)
If the passport's remaining validity is short, the residence permit may only be issued up to its expiry date
Keep the old passport if it contains valid visas/stamps (on request)

content.text: An expired passport complicates any dealings at the foreigners' authority and any travel. Start the renewal well in advance, allowing a margin for consular queues and production.

title: Receiving a Russian pension in Germany
tldr: You can receive a Russian pension while living in Germany, but with mandatory annual confirmation. The procedure for paying pensions to those who have moved abroad is governed by Russian Government Decree No. 1386 of 17.12.2014. Once a year you must confirm "the fact of being alive" — by drawing up a proof-of-life act at a Russian consulate (free of charge; the details are transmitted electronically to the SFR) or by confirming your status with a competent German authority. The Russia–Germany Double Taxation Agreement also applies (check the DBA status — it has changed). The main difficulty of 2026 is the sanctions restrictions on bank transfers from Russia. This guide covers confirmation, the payment routes and taxes.

content.text: For persons who have moved to permanent residence outside Russia, the payment of an insurance pension is governed by the Regulation approved by Russian Government Decree No. 1386 of 17.12.2014. The key requirement is to confirm, once a year, the fact that the person is alive, otherwise the payment is suspended. The confirmation is issued free of charge.

items: Method 1: a proof-of-life act at a Russian consulate in Germany (free of charge)
Method 2: confirmation of the fact of being alive by a competent German authority/official
The details of the act are transmitted electronically to the SFR on the day it is drawn up
You do not need to send the paper act to Russia yourself

content.text: The confirmation must be done annually and on time. Missing it leads to the payment being suspended until you submit the confirming document. Check the deadline by which you must submit the confirmation to the SFR or the consulate.

By law the pension is paid into an account in Russia or by another prescribed method. The main practical problem of 2026 is EU sanctions: if the receiving bank in Russia is under sanctions/cut off from SWIFT, transferring the funds to Germany is difficult or impossible. Many pensioners receive the pension into a Russian account and manage it by other available means, since a direct Russia→Germany transfer is often blocked.

Check with the SFR which account the payment is made to, and in what manner, for those who have moved abroad. A direct transfer to a German account via a sanctioned bank is generally impossible. The real routes are limited and depend on the bank.

Do not try to circumvent sanctions through schemes and intermediaries — that risks a freeze and a breach of the Foreign Trade and Payments Act (Außenwirtschaftsgesetz). Plan your budget in Germany without relying on a stable direct channel from Russia.

A German resident generally pays tax on their worldwide income, including foreign pensions. The Double Taxation Agreement between Russia and Germany (DBA) determines which country taxes the pension, but its application has changed (Russia has unilaterally suspended a number of articles), so you MUST check the current status and consult a tax adviser (Steuerberater). A foreign pension usually needs to be declared to the German tax office (Finanzamt).

items: A German resident declares worldwide income, including a pension from Russia
Check whether the Russia–Germany DBA still applies (the status has changed)
Keep records of the amounts and any tax withheld in Russia
If it gets complicated — consult a tax adviser on foreign pensions

title: Powers of attorney for Russia from Germany
tldr: A power of attorney for actions in Russia (selling a flat, court representation, dealing with property) can be drawn up from Germany in two ways. Route 1: a consular power of attorney at a Russian consulate — it is valid in Russia immediately, without an apostille or translation, but requires an appointment and a wait (fee ~20–50 €). Route 2: at a German notary (Notar) — after which you need an apostille (Apostille) on the German document and a notarised translation into Russian for use in Russia. This guide covers choosing the route, the requirements for the content of the power of attorney and the costs.

steps.title: Route 1: a consular power of attorney

content.text: The most direct route is to draw up the power of attorney at a Russian consulate in Germany. The consul performs a notarial act under Russian law, and such a power of attorney is valid in Russia immediately, without an apostille and without a separate translation (it is drawn up in Russian). The downside is the need to book via kdmid.ru/germany.mid.ru and a possible wait.

items: Book a notarial act at the Russian consulate
Bring your passport and the exact details of the principal and the attorney
Formulate the powers in advance (exactly what you authorise and for what term)
The finished power of attorney is valid in Russia without an apostille or translation

steps.title: Route 2: a German Notar + apostille + translation

content.text: If a consular appointment is unavailable or inconvenient, the power of attorney can be certified by a German notary (Notar). But the German document must be "legalised" for use in Russia: an apostille (Apostille) must be obtained from the competent German authority (for notarial acts, usually the president of the regional court, Landgericht), and then a notarised translation into Russian must be made.

The notary certifies your signature or the document itself. Formulate the powers as specifically as possible (the property's address, cadastral details, the list of actions) so that the Russian side accepts the power of attorney without questions.

Russia and Germany are parties to the 1961 Hague Convention, so an apostille is sufficient rather than full consular legalisation (Legalisation). The apostille is placed on the notarial document by the authorised German authority of the federal state.

For Russia, a notarised translation of the document (together with the apostille) into Russian is usually required. Check with the receiving side in Russia (notary, Rosreestr, court) whether the apostille itself must also be translated. Errors in the translation/powers lead to the power of attorney being rejected.

steps.title: Which route to choose and the term of validity

content.text: If a consular appointment is available, that is the most reliable route: the power of attorney is in Russian straight away and needs no apostille/translation. The route via a German notary is chosen when a consular appointment is unavailable or you need a document under German law. Clearly define the scope of the powers and the term of the power of attorney — without a stated term, in Russia it is generally valid for one year.

items: A consular appointment is available → a consular power of attorney (simpler for Russia)
An appointment is unavailable / you need the German format → notary + apostille + translation
State the term of validity (without one — usually 1 year under the Russian Civil Code)
For real-estate transactions, specify the property and the concrete actions

content.text: Agree the format of the power of attorney in advance with whoever will accept it in Russia (notary, Rosreestr, bank, court). Different bodies impose different requirements on the wording — better to check before drawing it up than to redo it.

title: Russian school certificate: recognition for university
tldr: A Russian certificate of general secondary education (11 grades) on its own usually does NOT give a direct right to enrol at a German university (Hochschulzugangsberechtigung, HZB). The level of recognition is checked via the anabin.kmk.org database and/or a recognition authority (zeugnisanerkennung / uni-assist). Most often you need either a year of study at a Russian university + a Studienkolleg, or a Studienkolleg straight away with the Feststellungsprüfung exam, after which an HZB arises. The exact conditions depend on the region and the university. This guide covers checking in anabin, the role of the Studienkolleg and the path to the right of admission.

content.text: The first step is to check the level of your certificate in the anabin.kmk.org database — the database for recognising foreign diplomas (the Schulabschlüsse mit Hochschulzugang section). The database shows whether your Russian certificate gives direct access to university, access only to a preparatory college attached to a university (Studienkolleg), or requires additional conditions. For most Russian certificates there is no direct access — you need a preparatory college or a year of university in Russia.

items: Find Russia in anabin → Schulabschlüsse and look at the status of the certificate
Check what your certificate qualifies you for: direct access, access to a preparatory college, or nothing
Take your study profile into account (a technical vs. humanities course needs different preparatory-college tracks)
Save a printout of the anabin result for your application

content.text: A preparatory college (Studienkolleg) is a preparatory year at a German university for foreigners whose school certificate does not give direct access. There are different courses by study profile (T — technical, M — medicine/biology, W — economics, G/S — humanities/languages). The year ends with an entrance qualifying exam (Feststellungsprüfung, FSP); passing it gives the right of admission to university (Hochschulzugangsberechtigung) for the corresponding group of subjects.

items.title: 1. The route via a year of university in Russia

content.text: An alternative to the preparatory college: a year (sometimes two) of successful study at a recognised Russian university can give access to a German university directly or reduce the requirements. Check the conditions in anabin and with the target university/uni-assist — they differ by federal state.

items.title: 2. Language and admission to the Studienkolleg

items: For a preparatory college you usually need German at B1–B2 level (an entrance test, Aufnahmetest)
The application often goes via uni-assist or directly to the preparatory college
Certified translations of the certificate and the transcript of grades
After the FSP you receive the right of admission (HZB) and apply for a subject-specific programme

content.text: The right of admission to university (HZB) is the formal right to enrol at a German university. It arises after the preparatory college + FSP or via another recognised route (a year of university in Russia + conditions). Only with an HZB can you apply for admission to a bachelor's programme. For a master's, a different logic applies — there the Russian bachelor's/specialist diploma is recognised (also via anabin and the university).

Don't apply for a bachelor's without an HZB — the application will be rejected. First complete the recognition of your certificate (anabin / preparatory college), then apply via uni-assist. The conditions differ by federal state and university — always check with the specific university.

title: Proving your residence permit for Russia
tldr: Sometimes Russian authorities need proof that you live legally in Germany: for military registration, tax matters, registering/deregistering, or banking procedures in Russia. The proof comes from German documents — a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) and your residence permit card (Aufenthaltstitel) — which, for use in Russia, usually need to be translated into Russian and, if required, have an apostille (Apostille) attached. This guide covers which documents confirm your status, how to legalise them for Russia, and the typical situations (military registration, tax residency).

content.text: Germany has no single "residence-permit certificate" in the Russian sense. Your status is confirmed by: your residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — an electronic card (eAT) carrying a national visa/residence permit/settlement permit, a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) from the local citizens' office (Bürgeramt), and, if needed, a certificate of residence (Aufenthaltsbescheinigung). These are the documents used to prove residence to Russian authorities.

items: Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel, eAT) — the residence/settlement permit card
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) — for your place of residence
Extended registration certificate (Erweiterte Meldebescheinigung) — on request
For long-term residence — confirmation from the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde)

content.text: For a German certificate to be valid in Russia, it is usually translated into Russian and, where required, has an apostille attached. Russia and Germany are both parties to the Hague Convention, so an apostille (Apostille) is enough — full consular legalisation is not needed. The apostille on a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) is issued by the authorised German state body; you then have a notarised translation made.

Check whether the receiving Russian authority actually requires an apostille. For certificates from the local citizens' office (Bürgeramt), the apostille is issued by the competent state authority. Sometimes a certified translation alone is enough — it depends on who in Russia accepts the document.

The translation into Russian is done by a sworn translator; for Russia, notarisation of the translation is often required. You can have the translation done through the Russian consulate, or notarise it with a Russian notary on arrival — agree the format with the receiving party in advance.

Proof of residence in Germany is most often needed for: military registration (men of conscription age), tax residency (confirming you are a tax resident of Germany, not Russia), and banking/property procedures in Russia. The logic is the same everywhere — provide a German certificate with a translation (and an apostille if required).

Russian military-registration and tax-residency questions have legal consequences — do not act on guesswork. For military registration and disputed tax situations, consult a Russian lawyer; for the German side, an official registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) is enough.

costs.note: Fee for the registration certificate; depends on the municipality.

costs.note: Per document at the authorised state authority.

title: Turkish citizens: visas, family reunion
tldr: Turkey is a visa country for the EU: you need a Schengen C visa or a national D visa. But Turkish citizens have a unique protection — EU–Turkey Association law (Assoziationsrecht), above all Decision 1/80 of the Association Council. It grants workers and their family members privileged labour-market access and protection against any worsening of their status (Stillhalteklausel / standstill). Germany has the largest Turkish diaspora, so family reunion (§§28–30 AufenthG) is a mass scenario: spouses, children, and parents of German citizens and residence-permit holders. Spouses generally need basic German at A1 level before entry (§30 Abs. 1 AufenthG), although Association law softens this in some cases. After the 2024 StAG reform, Turks can naturalise after 5 years while keeping their Turkish passport (dual citizenship is now allowed). Fast-track naturalisation after 3 years for special achievement has been abolished as of 30 October 2025 — the single minimum period is 5 years.

content.text: Turkey is in Annex I of EU Regulation 2018/1806 — a visa is required for entry. Short-term: a Schengen C visa (up to 90/180 days); long-term: a national D visa. German visas are issued by the consulates general in Istanbul, Izmir and Antalya, and by the embassy in Ankara.

items: C visa: tourism, visit, business — up to 90 days in 180
D visa: work, study, family reunion, Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) — more than 90 days
Diplomas are checked against the anabin database / Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB) before a work visa
Turkish documents are legalised with an apostille (Apostille; Turkey is a party to the Hague Convention)
For the qualified — EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU, §18g), §18a/§18b, Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte, §20a)

content.text: The EEC–Turkey Association Agreement (1963) and its Additional Protocol (1970), together with Decision 1/80 of the Association Council, create a special legal regime. It has direct effect: EU and German courts apply it over and above the ordinary residence law (AufenthG).

items: Art. 6 Beschluss 1/80: after 1 year of legal work for one employer, a Turkish worker strengthens their right to work; after 4 years — free access to any employment
Art. 7 Beschluss 1/80: family members of a Turkish worker gain labour-market access after 3 and 5 years
Standstill clause (Stillhalteklausel, Art. 13 Beschluss 1/80, Art. 41 of the Additional Protocol): bars the introduction of NEW restrictions worse than those in force when the rules took effect
Consequence of the standstill clause: some requirements (e.g. certain fees and language conditions) do not apply to Turks as strictly as to other third countries
Enhanced protection from expulsion for long-resident Turkish citizens (case law of the Court of Justice, EuGH)
Direct effect — you can invoke it in court against the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde)

content.text: Association law is complex and case-specific: the actual benefits depend on length of employment, family-member status and residence history. In a dispute with the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde), consult an immigration lawyer specialising in Association law (Assoziationsrecht).
Family reunion is the main channel for the Turkish community. The rules: §28 (joining a German citizen), §29 (general conditions), §30 (spouses), §32 (children).

items: §28 AufenthG: reunion with a German citizen — spouse, minor children, the parent of a minor citizen
§30 AufenthG: spouse of a foreigner holding a residence permit — usually requires A1 German BEFORE entry + both spouses being at least 18
§32 AufenthG: children under 18; under 16 without language, 16–18 — with sufficient German or a positive integration prognosis
§29 conditions: sufficient living space and means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) without social assistance
The D visa for family reunion is applied for from Turkey at the German consulate
Association law may soften the A1 language requirement for family members of Turkish workers — check case by case

content.text: The 2024 reform of the citizenship law (StAG) changed a lot for the Turkish community: previously Turks generally lost their Turkish passport when naturalising, but now dual citizenship is allowed on the German side. As of 30 October 2025, fast-track naturalisation after 3 years for special achievement has been abolished — a single minimum period of 5 years applies.

items: From 27.06.2024: naturalisation after 5 years (previously 8); the fast track after 3 years was abolished on 30.10.2025
Dual citizenship is now allowed — giving up your Turkish passport is NOT required
Core conditions of §10 StAG: B1 language, naturalisation test (Einbürgerungstest), self-support, no criminal record, declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung)
Children born in Germany may acquire citizenship by right of soil — ius soli (§4 Abs. 3 StAG) without the obligation to choose a citizenship (Optionspflicht)
Turkey generally permits dual citizenship — but check Turkish rules (including military-service obligations) with a specialist in Turkish law

title: British nationals after Brexit
tldr: After Brexit, British nationals fall into two groups. Group 1 — those who were legally resident in Germany before 31.12.2020: they are protected by the Withdrawal Agreement (Austrittsabkommen) and keep rights close to freedom of movement. They are issued a residence document, the Aufenthaltsdokument-GB (under §16 FreizügG/EU — transitional provisions). Group 2 — those who arrived from 01.01.2021: they count as third-country nationals and must obtain an ordinary residence permit under the residence law (Aufenthaltsgesetz): work §18, EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte) §18g, study §16b, etc., although there are simplifications for British nationals under §41 AufenthV (visa-free entry to then obtain a residence permit). This guide covers both groups, the documents needed, and the differences.

content.text: British nationals legally resident in Germany before the end of the transition period (31.12.2020) are protected by the Withdrawal Agreement. Their rights to reside and work are preserved on terms close to the former freedom of movement. The confirming document is the Aufenthaltsdokument-GB, issued by the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde). This is not an ordinary third-country residence permit but a document reflecting the protected status under the Withdrawal Agreement (WA).

items: Condition: legal residence in Germany before 31.12.2020 (end of the transition period)
Document: Aufenthaltsdokument-GB from the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde)
Rights close to the former freedom of movement (work, residence)
Family members can also be covered by WA protection

content.text: If you lived in Germany before 2021 but did not obtain the Aufenthaltsdokument-GB, contact the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) as soon as possible and prove your residence (registration, employment contracts, bank statements). Without the document your status is harder to demonstrate, although protection under the Withdrawal Agreement (WA) arises from the fact of residence rather than from the card itself.

British nationals who moved after 01.01.2021 are third-country nationals. They need an ordinary permit under the residence law (Aufenthaltsgesetz): work (§18a/§18b), EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU, §18g), study (§16b), self-employment (§21), family reunion. The advantage: under §41 AufenthV, British citizens (like those of the USA, Canada, Australia and others) may enter Germany without a national visa and apply for a residence permit while already in Germany, within the permitted period.

British nationals can enter without a visa and, during their stay, apply for the residence permit they need at the local immigration office (Ausländerbehörde). This is more convenient than arranging a national visa in advance. But you may only work once you have the corresponding permit.

items: Qualified work — §18b AufenthG (degree + contract)
EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) — §18g (degree + salary threshold)
Study — §16b; self-employment/freelance — §21
Book an appointment at the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) early — waiting times can be long

content.text: Brexit changed status but did not close the door. Group 1 should keep their Aufenthaltsdokument-GB and not lose the protected status (a long absence can weaken it). Group 2 should plan their residence permit like any qualified third-country professional. Separately: UK driving licences are exchanged in Germany without a test (see the separate guide), which makes everyday life easier.

Don't confuse the two groups: 31.12.2020 is the dividing line. You cannot obtain Withdrawal Agreement status retroactively if you moved in 2021 or later. Clarify your case with the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) and, if in doubt, with an immigration lawyer.

costs.note: Issuance of the WA document; the fee depends on the case (often symbolic/reduced).

costs.label: Residence permit under the Aufenthaltsgesetz (group 2)
costs.note: Fee for issuing the Aufenthaltstitel; Blaue Karte/work falls in this range.

costs.label: Immigration lawyer (for difficult cases)
costs.note: Advice on WA status or on choosing a third-country permit.

title: UK driving licences in Germany
tldr: Good news for British nationals: despite Brexit, UK / Northern Ireland licences are exchanged in Germany WITHOUT a test. The United Kingdom is listed in Anlage 11 FeV (with the entry "alle" — all categories, no theory or practical test) thanks to a bilateral mutual-recognition agreement that is still in force in 2026. This sets British nationals apart from citizens of Russia/Kazakhstan, whose licences require full tests. The same 6-month window applies (§29 FeV): you may drive on your UK licence for six months, after which you need a licence exchange (Umschreibung; no test, but with an application, a translation and an eyesight check — Sehtest). This guide covers the no-test exchange, the 6-month window and the documents.

steps.title: UK in Anlage 11: exchange without a test

content.text: The United Kingdom is listed in Anlage 11 FeV — the list of countries whose licences are exchanged for German ones without a test. The entry for the UK states "alle" (all categories) and "nein/nein" for the theory and practical tests. The basis is the bilateral agreement between Germany and the UK on mutual recognition of driving licences, in force since 2022 and still valid in 2026. In other words, Brexit did not worsen the status of UK licences.

items: UK in Anlage 11 FeV: all categories, no theory or practical test
Brexit did NOT abolish the exchange — a bilateral agreement applies
This differs from Russia/Kazakhstan (their licences are not in Anlage 11 → full tests)
Only an eyesight check (Sehtest) may be required

content.text: Despite the no-test exchange, since 01.01.2021 UK licences are NO longer EU licences. The 6-month rule therefore applies: after six months of residence you must convert your licence to a German one. You cannot simply keep driving on a UK licence indefinitely.

From the moment you establish a permanent place of residence (usually the residence registration — Anmeldung), your UK licence remains valid for driving for another 6 months (§29 FeV). Within that period you must apply for a licence exchange (Umschreibung) at the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle). Since no tests are required, the procedure is simple — it is mainly a document check and the issuing of the German licence.

items: Valid UK/NI driving licence
Passport + residence status/document (WA document or residence permit)
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) — for your registration (Anmeldung)
Biometric photo, eyesight check (Sehtest); translation of the licence (often required)

content.text: After checking the documents, the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle) issues the German licence without a test. The UK original is usually withdrawn and returned to the DVLA. Check with your authority whether a certified translation is needed and for which categories.

The no-test exchange under Anlage 11 covers ordinary car categories (B and others). But for "heavy" categories (C/D — lorries, buses) additional requirements may apply: a medical examination, a psycho-physical assessment (especially for D), a time limit. Check your categories in advance — some of them may require more documents.

items: Category B is usually exchanged without a test and without extra requirements
For C/D, a medical examination and additional assessments are possible
Check how your UK categories map to the German classes
If your UK licence is about to expire — exchange it before it runs out

content.text: The advantage over citizens of Russia and Kazakhstan is clear: their licences are not in Anlage 11 and require full tests, whereas UK licences are exchanged without theory or practical. Don't miss the 6-month window — after it, driving on a UK licence is illegal.

costs.note: Administrative fee of the Führerscheinstelle for the no-test exchange.

costs.label: Sehtest and photo
costs.note: Eyesight check and biometric photo.

costs.label: Translation of the licence (if required)
costs.note: Certified translation/breakdown of categories (ADAC or a sworn translator).

title: Ukrainians: §24 temporary protection until 2027
tldr: Ukrainian citizens receive temporary protection in Germany under §24 AufenthG — the national implementation of the EU Temporary Protection Directive (2001/55/EG), activated by the Council of the EU in March 2022 by an implementing decision (Durchführungsbeschluss 2022/382). Protection has been extended by a Council of the EU decision until 4 March 2027 (approved in June–July 2025). The §24 status grants the right to reside, to work (without a separate permit), access to the basic benefit Bürgergeld (SGB II) and medical care, as well as integration courses. The application runs without an asylum procedure: registration with the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) and issuance of a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) under §24. From this status you can switch to another residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel): work §18, EU Blue Card §18b, study §16b, family reunion. Issuing the residence-permit card (AT) costs around 100€, but for Ukrainians it is often reduced/waived.

content.text: After Russia's full-scale invasion, on 4 March 2022 the Council of the EU activated the Temporary Protection Directive (2001/55/EG) for the first time in history, by an implementing decision (Durchführungsbeschluss (EU) 2022/382). In Germany it is implemented through §24 AufenthG — a residence permit for persons granted temporary protection.

items: EU Directive 2001/55/EG — Temporary Protection Directive, activated 04.03.2022
German §24 AufenthG — the national implementation
Extension: the Council of the EU unanimously approved it in June 2025, formally confirmed until 4 March 2027
Status WITHOUT an asylum procedure — no need to go through the asylum procedure (Asylverfahren)
Covers Ukrainian citizens and certain categories of people who were resident in Ukraine on 24.02.2022
The EU is discussing transitional mechanisms for the period AFTER March 2027

content.text: §24 is a temporary status. Those who plan to stay long-term should switch to a stable residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) in good time — work, study, family reunion — rather than waiting for the regime to end in 2027.
The scope of rights under §24 is noticeably broader than for ordinary asylum seekers — a deliberate decision by the EU and Germany to enable rapid integration.

items: Right to reside on the residence-permit card (Aufenthaltstitel) §24 AufenthG
Right to work — without a separate work permit (Arbeitserlaubnis); employment is allowed immediately
Access to the basic benefit Bürgergeld (SGB II) through the job centre (Jobcenter) — unlike asylum seekers (AsylbLG)
Medical care through the ordinary insurance system — statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung)
Right to integration and language courses (Integrationskurs)
Children's access to school and kindergarten
Freedom of movement within Schengen as part of your status

steps.title: How to apply and how to change status

content.text: Obtaining §24 goes through the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) without an asylum procedure. After registration, a residence permit is issued. Important: if needed, you can switch to another residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel).

items: Residence registration (Anmeldung) and contact with the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde)
Proof of Ukrainian citizenship (passport) or of residence status in Ukraine on 24.02.2022
Biometrics and issuance of the residence-permit card (Aufenthaltstitel) §24
Registration with the job centre (Jobcenter) for the basic benefit Bürgergeld and with a health insurer (Krankenkasse)
Switch to §18a/§18b (work), §18b Blue Card, §16b (study), §28/§30 (family) — if the conditions are met
Time spent on §24 counts toward the period for naturalisation from the moment the status is granted
Switching to a work residence permit is often better long-term: it does not depend on the temporary-protection regime being extended

content.text: Follow the official decisions of the EU and the Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI) on the fate of the regime after March 2027. Transitional rules are currently under discussion, but the final mechanism may change — plan your move to a stable permit well in advance.

costs.label: Aufenthaltstitel §24 (card issuance)
costs.note: Standard fee for the AT card ~100€; for Ukrainians often reduced/waived under the temporary-protection regime.

costs.label: Anmeldung (residence registration)
costs.note: Registration at the Bürgeramt is free.

costs.label: Integrationskurs
costs.note: For §24 recipients the course is usually free/subsidised by BAMF.

title: D visa in Russia: appointment and dossier
tldr: For 2026, applying for a national D visa from Russia is possible at the German missions in Moscow, Kaliningrad, Yekaterinburg and Novosibirsk; St Petersburg does not accept national visas. Appointments are booked via the German embassy's website (germania.diplo.de), and the queue is usually several months. Documents must be in German, with an apostille (Apostille): the Ministry of Education and Science for diplomas, the registry office (ZAGS) for civil-status records, and with a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung). The fee is 75 €, paid in roubles at the embassy's exchange rate. Biometrics are taken at the mission. After approval the visa is usually issued within a few weeks; entry must fall within the window stated in the visa.

content.text: Since 2022, Germany has significantly cut its consular presence in Russia. For 2026, national D visas (for work, study, family reunion, Chancenkarte) are accepted at four missions: Moscow (embassy), Kaliningrad, Yekaterinburg and Novosibirsk (consulates general). The consulate general in St Petersburg is closed for D visas and accepts only Schengen visas for a limited list of grounds.

items: Moscow (Embassy, ul. Mosfilmovskaya, 56) — all D categories, the main flow
Kaliningrad (Consulate General) — for residents of the region and the North-West
Yekaterinburg — the Urals, the Volga region, Siberia
Novosibirsk — Siberia and the Far East
St Petersburg — closed for D visas
Alternative: applying in a third country (Ankara, Yerevan, Tbilisi, Almaty) — a separate guide

content.text: You should apply at the consular district of your registration, but in practice Moscow accepts Russian citizens from various regions. If you are registered, say, in Krasnodar, you can usually still book in Moscow, but you must justify the reason in the form. Check the current district allocation on the missions' websites: it changes.

Booking is done via the website germania.diplo.de → the "Visa" section → "Nationales Visum". In 2024–2026 the German embassy in Moscow uses a scheme where you first fill in the application in the online form VIDEX (videx.diplo.de), get an application number, and then register for an appointment (Termin).

items: Step 1: create an application at videx.diplo.de
Step 2: print the form, get the QR code and the VIDEX number
Step 3: at germania.diplo.de, select the D-visa type and request an appointment (Termin)
Step 4: join the virtual queue (Warteliste) — the wait is usually several months
Step 5: a few weeks before the date you receive a letter confirming the appointment (Termin)
Step 6: print the letter and appear in person
Moscow handles the main flow of D applications, with the longest queue
In Kaliningrad and Yekaterinburg the queue is usually shorter

content.text: In urgent cases (for example, family reunion — Familienzusammenführung — with a German citizen, or humanitarian grounds) the mission may grant a priority appointment (Termin). Check the conditions and the contact address on the website of the specific mission, as they change from time to time.

The basic package is the same for all D visas, but specific documents are added depending on the type. Russian certificates are translated into German with a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung); in Russia this is usually a notarised translation plus an apostille (on the original or on the notary's endorsement).

items: Passport + copies of the photo pages (valid for at least 1 year)
Internal passport + copy
2 biometric photos 35×45 mm (German standard, light background, no smile)
Printed VIDEX form with signature + QR code
Termin confirmation (printout of the letter)
Fee 75 € — in roubles at the embassy's exchange rate
Travel health insurance (Reisekrankenversicherung) with coverage of at least 30 000 €
Documents for the grounds: employment contract / university admission (Zulassung) / blocked account (Sperrkonto) / family member's invitation (Familienangehöriger)
Proof of accommodation: rental contract, registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung) or declaration of commitment to cover costs (Verpflichtungserklärung)

content.text: The Russian internal passport is not used in Germany, but the mission will ask for it to check your registration. If you are registered outside the consulate's service area, an explanation may be required. Check the exact list of documents against the leaflet (Merkblatt) on the mission's website for your visa category.

Official Russian documents (diplomas, school certificates, birth, marriage and divorce certificates, police clearance certificates) are usually needed with an apostille for the German authorities. Russia is a party to the Hague Convention, and the apostille is affixed in Russia to originals or notarised copies.

items: Apostille on a diploma — Rosobrnadzor/Ministry of Education and Science of Russia, state fee ~2500 RUB, up to 45 days
Apostille on ZAGS (registry office) certificates — the regional ZAGS office, ~2500 RUB
Apostille on a police clearance certificate — the Interior Ministry of the issuing region, ~2500 RUB
Apostille on a police clearance certificate — the Interior Ministry of the issuing region, ~2500 RUB
Translation into German — by a sworn translator or a notarised translation + apostille on the endorsement
Translation in Germany — at the JVEG rate, roughly 30–80 €/page
Document freshness: a police clearance certificate is usually no older than 6 months, register extracts no older than 3 months

content.text: Alternative for diplomas: you can first obtain an official assessment of your foreign diploma (Zeugnisbewertung) from the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB) in Germany (around 200 €) — it partly replaces the apostille and translation, since the office itself verifies the diploma's authenticity. This is convenient for the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) and §18b.

On the appointed day, arrive early. Inside there is a security check (you leave your phone in a locker), then document submission, biometrics (fingerprints, photo) and an interview in German, English or Russian. The 75 € fee is paid in cash in roubles at the embassy's exchange rate.

items: Appointment (Termin) duration: roughly 30–60 minutes
Biometrics: digital photo and fingerprints (from age 12)
Interview: purpose of travel, language skills, finances, work/study plans
A serious discrepancy between the application and your spoken answers can lead to refusal
After submission, the documents are sent to Germany (the ABH/BVA of the receiving region)
Processing time: up to 3 months by law, but usually a few weeks in practice
Family reunion (Familienzusammenführung) — longer, due to coordination with the ABH
When ready, you receive a notification — the passport is collected in person or via a courier service

content.text: Do not provide false information in the VIDEX form and do not conceal past Schengen refusals: the mission has access to the EU Visa Information System (VIS). Discrepancies can lead to refusal and an entry ban.

costs.label: Consular fee for the D visa
costs.note: Paid in roubles at the embassy's exchange rate. Children under 18 — 37,50 €.

costs.label: VIDEX and Terminvergabe
costs.note: Registration is free, but booking an appointment can take a long time.

costs.label: Certified translation of documents (Russia)
costs.note: Roughly 30–50 €/page at a notary in Russia; in Germany — 30–80 €/page by a sworn translator.

costs.label: Apostille (Ministry of Education/Justice/ZAGS)
costs.note: State fee ~2500 RUB per document, taking from a few days to 45 days.

costs.label: Travel health insurance
costs.note: MAWISTA, Care Concept, ERGO etc. — for the entry period, coverage of at least 30 000 €.

costs.label: Courier return of the passport
costs.note: If not collected in person — passport delivery by courier service within Russia (where available).

title: D visa via Ankara: for Russians
tldr: Because of queues and closures in Russia, many Russians apply for a D visa at the German missions in Turkey — Ankara (embassy), Istanbul and Izmir (consulates general). The conditions: legal residence in Turkey (Ikamet/Kimlik, a work visa or a valid visa-free stamp) and a justification for why you are applying here rather than in Russia. Applying without a Kimlik is possible, but the chances are lower; the mission checks for stable ties to Turkey: a lease, an employment contract, a bank account. Timing: the appointment and processing can take several months. The fee is 75 €, paid in TRY. Russian documents need an apostille and translation; Turkish documents need notarisation (Tasdik) and a sworn translation (Yeminli Tercüme).

steps.title: Why Turkey as the country of application

content.text: Since 2022, the flow of Russians applying for a German D visa has largely shifted to third countries. Turkey is one of the popular options: relatively easy entry for Russians, the possibility of obtaining a Turkish residence permit — Ikamet (Kimlik) — and three German missions.

items: Ankara — the German embassy, accepts D categories
Istanbul — consulate general, also accepts D visas
Izmir — consulate general, a narrower list
Key condition: at the time of application you must be legally present in Turkey
Ideally you should have a valid Kimlik (Ikamet) or a work visa
Applying without a Kimlik during the visa-free period is possible, but the chances are lower
The mission will check your ties to Turkey: a lease, an employment contract, a bank account

content.text: In recent years Turkey has tightened the issuance of tourist Ikamet, and refusals have become more frequent in the big cities. Conditions and statistics change quickly, so check the current situation before moving and don't build your plan on a single scenario.

German missions in Turkey accept third-country nationals (including Russia, Belarus, Ukraine) if two conditions are met: legal residence in Turkey and a convincing justification for why the application is being made here rather than in the home country.

items: Condition 1: a valid Kimlik (Ikamet), a work permit Çalışma izni, or a valid visa-free stamp
Condition 2: a document of long-term ties to Turkey: a lease (Kira sözleşmesi), an employment contract, a bank account, a tax number (vergi numarası)
Condition 3: an explanation of why you are not applying in Russia (closure of missions, queues, relocation)
Applications by Russian citizens via Turkey are permitted if the conditions are met
A past refusal from Moscow is visible in the EU visa system (VIS)

content.text: Booking is done via the website ankara.diplo.de or istanbul.diplo.de. The principle is the same as in Moscow: first the online VIDEX form, then selecting the D-visa type and joining the virtual queue (Warteliste).

items: ankara.diplo.de → "Termin" → "Nationales Visum"
The queue in Ankara and Istanbul is usually several months
Izmir — narrow categories, but sometimes a shorter queue
Urgent categories (family reunion — Familienzusammenführung — with a German citizen, medical) are processed with priority
The letter confirming the appointment (Termin) arrives by email in advance

content.text: Free slots appear irregularly, in part because of cancellations of previously booked appointments. Check the mission's website regularly; be cautious with third-party automatic-booking services — they don't guarantee results and may violate the mission's rules.

The basic package is the same as in Russia, but a block of Turkish documents is added. Russian documents must carry an apostille and a translation; Turkish documents must be notarised (Tasdik) and translated by a sworn translator (Yeminli Tercüman).

items: Russian passport + copies of the pages (valid for at least 1 year)
Turkish Kimlik (Ikamet) + copy — the key proof of legality
VIDEX form with QR code
2 biometric photos to the German standard
Documents for the visa grounds (contract, diploma, blocked account — Sperrkonto, family documents)
Russian documents — with an apostille and a translation into German
Turkish documents (lease, bank account) — Tasdik + Yeminli Tercüme into German
Travel health insurance for entry into Germany (not for the stay in Turkey)
Cover letter: why you are applying in Turkey rather than in Russia

content.text: Russian documents cannot be apostilled in Turkey — this is done only in Russia. If the apostille is not arranged in advance, the documents will have to be sent to Russia and back, which takes weeks or months. So prepare the apostille before leaving Russia.

The 75 € fee is paid in Turkish lira (TRY) at the embassy's exchange rate on the day of the appointment. Because of lira exchange-rate swings, the rouble and lira equivalent vary noticeably, so check the amount before your visit. Payment is usually in cash, and a receipt is issued on the spot.

items: Fee 75 € — in TRY at the embassy's current exchange rate
Children under 18 — 37,50 €
Processing time for a D visa in Turkey: usually a few weeks
Family reunion (Familienzusammenführung) — longer, due to coordination with the ABH
You will be notified when it's ready by SMS/email; collection in person or via courier
After approval, the visa is glued into the passport within a few days

content.text: One detail to note: the passport is usually returned only in Turkey, and shipping to Russia is generally not available. If you leave Turkey before the visa is ready, you will need to return or arrange collection through a trusted person in Turkey.

costs.note: Paid in TRY at the embassy's exchange rate on the day of the appointment.

costs.label: Turkish Ikamet (Kimlik)
costs.note: State fee + Kart Bedeli + health insurance; the total depends on the period and the lira rate.

costs.label: Yeminli Tercüme (sworn translation) into German
costs.note: In Istanbul and Ankara, Turkish translations are usually cheaper than Russian ones.

costs.label: Tasdik (notarised certification of copies) in Turkey
costs.note: At a notary (Noter).

costs.label: Lease + bank account for ties to Turkey
costs.note: Monthly rent plus deposit (usually 1–2 months' rent).

title: D-visa categories: §16, §18, §21, §22
tldr: A national D visa is the entry ticket for a specific type of residence permit. The main categories: §16 (education — §16a for vocational training (Ausbildung), §16b for university study, §16d for qualification recognition, §16f for language courses and school), §17 (search for a study/training place), §18 (work — §18a/§18b for skilled workers, §18g for the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU), §19c for others), §20 (job search), §20a (Opportunity Card — Chancenkarte), §21 (entrepreneurship and the liberal professions — Freiberufler), §22-§26 (humanitarian grounds, protection), §28-§32 (family reunion). The category determines the duration, fees, and rights to work and to bring family. A basic D visa costs 75 €, is issued for 3–6 months for entry, and is then exchanged for an electronic residence-permit card (eAT) at the ABH.

steps.title: Why the system of paragraphs exists

content.text: The residence law (Aufenthaltsgesetz, AufenthG) is the main law on the residence of foreigners in Germany. It is divided into paragraphs, each regulating its own ground for a residence permit. When you apply for a D visa, the VIDEX form requires a specific §, which determines your subsequent status, rights and obligations.

Knowing the right paragraph matters: when you change jobs or your life situation, the ABH may propose switching to a different §, and that changes the scope of your rights. For example, the EU Blue Card (§18g) gives a fast track to settlement, whereas the student §16b does not.

items: §16 — education and qualification recognition (§16a, §16b, §16d, §16f)
§17 — search for a study/training place (Ausbildung itself — §16a, study — §16b)
§18-§19 — employment
§20 — job search; §20a — Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte)
§21 — self-employment and freelance
§22-§26 — humanitarian grounds, protection
§28-§32 — family reunion

content.text: §16 is a group of paragraphs for those coming to Germany to study: §16a (vocational training — Berufsausbildung), §16b (university study — Studium, including the preparatory stage: a university preparatory college — Studienkolleg, a preparatory language course — studienvorbereitender Sprachkurs), §16d (measures for recognising a foreign qualification), §16f (language courses and schooling).

items: §16b — university student; you need admission (Zulassung) + a blocked account (Sperrkonto) ~11 904 €/year (for study)
§16b (Abs. 1) — preparatory stage: university preparatory college (Studienkolleg), preparatory language course (studienvorbereitender Sprachkurs)
§16a — vocational training (Berufsausbildung): dual or school-based
§16d — measures for recognising a foreign profession (nurses, doctors and others)
§16f — language courses and schooling
Student work rights under §16b: 140 full or 280 half days per year
After university — §20 (job search up to 18 months), then §18a/§18b

content.text: This is the central group of paragraphs for employment. §18a — for skilled workers with vocational training (after Ausbildung), §18b — for skilled workers with a university degree. §18g — the EU Blue Card: the minimum salary in 2026 is 50 700 € gross per year for ordinary professions (Regelberuf) and 45 934,20 € for shortage occupations and recent graduates (Engpassberufe) — IT, engineers, doctors and others.

items: §18a — skilled worker with vocational training (Fachkraft mit Berufsausbildung)
§18b — skilled worker with a university degree (Hochschulabschluss)
§18g — EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) — by salary threshold, a path to settlement in 21/27 months
§18c — permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) for skilled workers; usually ~3 years, for the Blue Card — 21/27 months
§19c — other employment purposes, including IT specialists with experience but no formal recognition, and au pairs
§19 — intra-corporate transfer (ICT-Karte); §19e — European Voluntary Service (Freiwilligendienst)
Residence-permit duration: usually up to 4 years or for the contract term
Work rights: at the start often tied to a specific employer

content.text: §21 regulates two types of self-employed activity: business activity (Gewerbe — §21 Abs. 1) and the liberal professions (Freiberuf — §21 Abs. 5). The latter is usually simpler: the liberal professions (Freiberufler) include IT developers (without an agency), journalists, artists, translators, and doctors in private practice. Berlin is known for its liberal approach to §21(5) — which is why it is called the "city of freelancers".

items: §21 Abs. 1 — business activity (Gewerbe): business plan, financing, economic interest for the region
§21 Abs. 5 — liberal profession (Freiberufler): contracts with clients (Auftragsbestätigungen) + qualification
Means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) + KSK (the social-insurance fund for creative workers) or private health insurance
Initial residence permit — usually 1–3 years, extended on proof of income
After ~3 years of successful activity, a permanent residence permit is possible (Niederlassungserlaubnis, §21 Abs. 4)
Berlin is more lenient toward freelancers in IT and design
Munich and Hamburg are usually stricter about the document package

content.text: A §21 residence permit is granted for self-employed activity, not for employment (Angestelltenverhältnis). If office employment appears alongside it, you must coordinate your status with the ABH (a switch to §18 or a combined permit is possible). In ambiguous cases, individual legal advice is recommended.

§22-§26 — humanitarian grounds and protection: §22 (admission for special reasons and government programmes), §23 (federal-state programmes and admission by federal decision), §24 (temporary protection, including for refugees from Ukraine), §25 (asylum and subsidiary protection), §26 (duration and extension). Paragraphs §28-§32 relate to family reunion — there are separate guides for them.

items: §22 — humanitarian admission for special reasons (usually not applied for on your own)
§23 — federal-state and federal programmes, including Jewish immigration (quota refugees — Kontingentflüchtling)
§24 — temporary protection for Ukrainians (extended until 4 March 2027)
§25 — recognised refugees and the subsidiarily protected
§28 — reunion with a German citizen (spouse, child, parents)
§29-§30 — reunion with a foreign spouse holding a residence permit
§32 — minor children joining a parent with a residence permit
§33 — children born in Germany

title: §19c: for skilled workers
tldr: §19c AufenthG is the "umbrella" paragraph for qualified employment. §19c Abs. 1 permits employment under a special clearance of the employment ordinance (Beschäftigungsverordnung) with the consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit, BA). §19c Abs. 2 is the key category for specialists with pronounced practical experience (including IT) WITHOUT diploma recognition: 2 years of relevant experience in the last 5 years are enough, plus an offer from an employer and a salary of at least 45% of the pension-insurance ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) = ~45 630 € gross/year in 2026 (for applicants aged 45+ — ~55 770 €). For IT specialists (§6 Abs. 3 BeschV), proof of language has not been required since 2024. The residence permit is usually up to 4 years or for the contract term. A permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §18c Abs. 1: normally after 60 months (for specialists with experience — after 36 months with B1, §18c Abs. 1). Fees: D visa 75 € + AT 100 €. Since the requirements and categories are interpreted case by case, individual legal advice is recommended.

content.text: §19c AufenthG applies in the version following the reform — the Skilled Immigration Act (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz, 2023–2024). It is the "umbrella" paragraph for qualified employment in cases that do not fit the classic §18a (after vocational training — Ausbildung) or §18b (after university). Its subsections provide different grounds for entry.

items: §19c Abs. 1 — employment under the special rules of the employment ordinance (Beschäftigungsverordnung) with the consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit, BA)
§19c Abs. 2 — specialists with pronounced practical experience (§6 BeschV), including IT, WITHOUT diploma recognition (the main category for IT applicants from Russia/Belarus/Ukraine)
§19c Abs. 3 — specific groups by decision of the responsible authority (Federal Ministry of the Interior, BMI)
Intra-corporate transfer is regulated separately — the intra-corporate transfer card (ICT-Karte, §19 AufenthG)
The most popular path is Abs. 2 for experienced specialists and IT

steps.title: §19c Abs. 2 — experience instead of a diploma

content.text: §19c Abs. 2 in combination with §6 BeschV lets you move on a full residence permit without diploma recognition, provided you have an employer, an offer with a salary above the threshold, and proven practical experience. From 1 March 2024 the experience requirement was lowered to 2 years in the last 5 (previously 3 years in 7), and for IT specialists (§6 Abs. 3 BeschV) proof of language is no longer required.

items: Documented relevant experience: at least 2 years in the last 5
A concrete offer from a German employer for a matching position
Salary at least 45% of the pension-insurance ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze, §6 BeschV): ~45 630 € gross/year in 2026 (applicants 45+ — ~55 770 € or proven pension provision)
Diploma recognition (anabin database, Central Office for Foreign Education — ZAB, apostille on the diploma) is not required
For IT specialists (§6 Abs. 3 BeschV) proof of language is not required; for other §6 professions basic language may be requested
Suitable: Software Engineer, DevOps, SRE, Data Engineer, ML Engineer, QA and related IT roles
For non-IT roles (e.g. design, product management) §18b or the Blue Card by salary is more practical — individual legal advice is recommended

content.text: Proving experience is the hardest part. Accepted: employment record books with stamps and a translation, contracts with a translation, reference letters from former employers on letterhead with a stamp and signature. Letters without a stamp or notarisation are often not accepted. The Federal Employment Agency (BA) checks that the working conditions are no worse than for comparable local workers.
The basic D-visa package plus the specifics of §19c. The key is your employment history and the offer.

items: Passport and copies
VIDEX form with the category §19c Abs. 2
Employer's offer on letterhead (employment contract — Arbeitsvertrag — or confirmation of hiring — Einstellungszusage)
Declaration on the employment relationship (Erklärung zum Beschäftigungsverhältnis, BA form) — filled in by the employer
Position description (Stellenbeschreibung) detailing the tasks
Reference letters, CV, link to LinkedIn
Employment record books with an apostille and translation (or employers' confirmations — Bestätigungen)
Confirmation of the salary in the offer (gross/year)
Attaching a diploma is not mandatory, but desirable if you have one
Health insurance for the first months

content.text: §19c Abs. 2 requires a salary of at least 45% of the annual pension-insurance ceiling (45% Beitragsbemessungsgrenze, §6 BeschV).

items: The income ceiling for social contributions in the general pension insurance (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze, general RV) in 2026: 101 400 € gross/year
Threshold for §19c Abs. 2 (§6 BeschV, 45% BBG): ~45 630 € gross/year (≈3 802,50 €/month) in 2026
For applicants over 45: ~55 770 € gross/year or proof of adequate pension provision
A full-time rate is assumed; part-time employment is usually not counted
Included: base salary, guaranteed payments (13th salary, fixed bonus)
Not included: stock options, RSUs, variable bonuses
If the salary is below the threshold — refusal or an offer to switch to the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte, §20a)
Taxes and contributions on ~45 630 € — roughly 25–30% (check with a current calculator)

content.text: The §19c Abs. 2 threshold (~45 630 €) is close to, but not equal to, the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) thresholds: shortage occupations (Engpassberufe) 45 934 € / standard professions 50 700 € in 2026. If you have a recognised diploma, it is often more advantageous to apply for the Blue Card: it gives a faster path to settlement — a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) after 27 months without B1 or 21 months with B1, §18c Abs. 2. The details depend on the profession and salary — individual legal advice is recommended.

steps.title: What §19c grants and where to move on

content.text: A §19c residence permit is usually issued for up to 4 years or for the term of the employment contract (whichever is shorter). At the start, the right to work is tied to the employer in the offer; a change of employer should be coordinated with the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) in good time.

items: Right to work — with the employer in the offer; when changing employer, notify the ABH (check the procedure and deadlines with your ABH)
Family: §30 for the spouse and §32 for children (language and income requirements depend on the situation)
The spouse can usually work without restrictions

Permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §18c Abs. 1 — normally after 60 months; for specialists with recognised education/experience — after 36 months with B1 (exact periods depend on the category and the ABH's decision)
Citizenship — normally after 5 years (after the StAG reform of 30.10.2025; fast-track 3-year naturalisation abolished)
Right to leave Germany and return — without restrictions while the residence permit is valid

content.text: The periods until a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) and the applicability of particular benefits depend on the §19c subcategory, the language level and the ABH's decision (discretion — Ermessen). Before planning a move to settlement, individual legal advice is recommended.

title: Reunion with children: §32
tldr: §32 AufenthG covers the reunion of minor children with a parent who holds a residence permit or German citizenship. Under 16 — a simplified process, with no language requirement; for children aged 16–17, §32 Abs. 2 requires German at C1 level or a positive integration prognosis (there are exceptions, including for children of EU Blue Card (Blue Card) holders and §19). Conditions: the other parent's consent to the child leaving (notarised), secured income of the receiving parent and sufficient housing, and health insurance. The child receives a residence permit tied to the parent's status. Fees: D visa 37,50 € + AT 50 €. Settlement for children is possible under §35. Individual legal advice is recommended — income and language requirements are assessed case by case.

steps.title: Who qualifies and on what conditions

content.text: §32 AufenthG allows minor children to join one or both parents who hold a residence permit or German citizenship. The key threshold is 18 years; what matters is the date the application is filed at the mission abroad, not the date the visa is issued.

items: Child under 16 — a simplified procedure with no language requirements
Child aged 16–17 — §32 Abs. 2 requires German at C1 or a positive integration prognosis (see exceptions below)
At least one parent must hold a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel, AT) or German citizenship
The other parent's consent to the child leaving (if they are not coming) — notarised, with an apostille and translation
If there is only one parent on the documents — a death certificate or a court ruling on sole custody
If the child is about to turn 16 — it makes sense to file the application before their 16th birthday
The child's residence permit is valid within the parent's status, with the option to extend

content.text: For children aged 16–17, §32 Abs. 2 requires German at C1 level or a well-founded prognosis of successful integration taking into account education and living conditions. The bar is high, but the law provides exceptions and alternatives.

items: The C1 language requirement does not apply if the receiving parent holds an EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU, §18g), has §19 status, or is recognised as a refugee / has subsidiary protection
Alternative: moving at the same time as the parents (§32 Abs. 1)
Alternative: prior education in German in the country of origin
Alternative: a positive integration prognosis — then the C1 requirement may be relaxed
§32 Abs. 4 allows a residence permit to avoid particular hardship (Härtefall) at the discretion (Ermessen) of the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde)
Filing the application before the 16th birthday lets you avoid the language barrier

content.text: Cases where the child is 17 with only a few months until 18 often end in refusal without C1 if no exception applies. Possible paths: wait until 18 and apply for §16b (study) or another category, or first obtain German citizenship for the parent (then §28 applies without a language barrier for the child). Individual legal advice is recommended.

The package is split into two parts: the parent's documents in Germany and the child's documents from the country of origin. The child's documents are apostilled and translated at their place of issue.

items: Child's birth certificate (apostille and translation)
The other parent's consent to the child leaving (notarised, with an apostille and translation)
Child's passport (valid for at least 1 year)
2 biometric photos
Travel health insurance
VIDEX form (filled in by the parent for minors)
Copy of the parent's AT or German passport
Confirmation of residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung)
Proof of income: the latest payslips (Lohnabrechnungen) or tax assessment (Steuerbescheid)
Rental contract stating the number and size of rooms (the space norm is set by the state)
Confirmation from the landlord of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung)
Parents' marriage certificate or a custody document

content.text: The receiving parent must prove they will support the child without help from the job centre (Jobcenter). The calculation is based on need (Bedarf): the subsistence minimum for the child by age, plus the parent's own support, plus rent. Check the specific rates for the current year.

items: For the parent: the subsistence minimum — means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) — plus rent and insurance
For the child: the basic need (Regelbedarf) by age (a benchmark from the minimum maintenance — Mindestunterhalt — 2026: 482/554/649 € — check the current rates)
Housing: a benchmark of about 12 m² of living space per person (excluding kitchen and bathroom); the exact norm depends on the state
One child under 6 can usually share a room with the parents
Income is proven for several months (payslips — Lohnabrechnungen)
For the self-employed — tax assessment (Steuerbescheid), business analysis (BWA), list of clients
Child benefit (Kindergeld) does not count as income (Einkommen) for §32 purposes

content.text: If you receive the basic benefit Bürgergeld (formerly Hartz IV), reunion under §32 is generally not possible. The exception is reunion with a German citizen (then §28 is assessed, where the economic check is gentler). Since income is assessed case by case, individual legal advice is recommended.

The child enters on a D visa and, in Germany, receives a plastic residence-permit card (Aufenthaltstitel, AT) at the immigration office (Ausländerbehörde). The residence-permit duration is tied to the parent's status.

items: Residence registration (Anmeldung) at the local citizens' office (Bürgeramt) within the set deadline (usually within 14 days)
Enrolment in kindergarten (Kita) or school via the school authority (Schulamt) for your place of residence
Schooling is compulsory (generally from age 6)
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) — usually as a family member (family insurance — Familienversicherung)
Apply for child benefit (Kindergeld) at the child-benefit office (Familienkasse) — 259 €/month per child (2026)
The tax identification number (Steuer-ID) and social-insurance number (Sozialversicherungsnummer) arrive by post
Book an appointment (Termin) at the immigration office to issue the residence-permit card
From age 14, the child attends the Termin in person

content.text: On reaching the age of majority, the §32 residence permit loses its basis: the young person needs to switch to §16b (study), §16a (vocational training — Ausbildung) or a work status. Settlement for children is possible under §35 — a special permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) for children if the conditions are met: length of residence and language level. Check the exact conditions and periods with the immigration office (ABH).

costs.note: Half the adult fee, paid at the mission abroad.

costs.note: Half the adult fee, paid after arrival.

costs.note: Birth certificate and the other parent's consent — usually 3–5 pages.

costs.note: In Russia — about 2500 RUB per document via the ZAGS or the Ministry of Justice.

title: Spouse reunification: §28–§30
tldr: Spouse reunification is governed by §28 (to a German citizen), §29 (the general reunification rule for joining a foreign resident) and §30 (joining a foreign resident as a spouse, Ehegattennachzug). The basic requirement for most foreign spouses is German A1 (Goethe, telc, ÖSD) and a marriage recognised in Germany. An A1 exemption applies to spouses of EU Blue Card (Blue Card EU) holders, §18d (research), certain §18a/§18b categories and a number of other cases. Proof of financial support is required under §29–§30; under §28 it is not formally required, but in practice the foreigners' authority (ABH) asks for evidence. A spouse's first residence permit is usually for 1–3 years, with an unrestricted right to work. Naturalisation of a German citizen's spouse is possible under §9 StAG (3 years of residence + 2 years of marriage). Individual legal advice is recommended.

content.text: The choice of paragraph depends on the status of the person the spouse is joining. This is critical: it determines the fees and the income and language requirements.

items: §28 — spouse of a German citizen (DE passport)
§29 — general conditions for reunification with a foreigner who holds a residence permit AT (including study, protection, EU Blue Card)
§30 — spouse reunification (Ehegattennachzug) with a foreign resident (with the A1 language requirement)
§36 — other family members (for example, the parents of a minor German citizen)
FreizügG/EU — spouse of an EU citizen; not governed by AufenthG

content.text: If your partner is an EU citizen (not German), you move under FreizügG/EU rather than AufenthG: usually without A1 and without an income check. The residence card for family members of EU citizens (Aufenthaltskarte) and its fees are governed separately. Check the exact fee with your own foreigners' authority (ABH), since the rates are revised from time to time.

steps.title: The A1 requirement: who needs it and who does not

content.text: Under §30 Abs. 1 (and §28 Abs. 1 for the spouse of a German citizen), when applying for the visa the foreign spouse normally has to prove basic German at A1 — with a Goethe "Start Deutsch 1" certificate, telc A1 or ÖSD A1.

items: Where to take it: Goethe-Institut, telc, ÖSD
Cost in Russia is around 100–130 €, in Turkey 80–120 €
Exemption if the spouse in Germany holds an EU Blue Card (§18g)
...or has researcher status (§18d)
...or falls into certain §18a/§18b categories (check with the consulate)
...or has an evidently low need for integration support / a clear inability to learn the language
...or is a national of a visa-exempt country (for example the USA, Canada, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Israel)
The list of §30 Abs. 1 exemptions is interpreted case by case — individual legal advice is recommended

content.text: The German mission verifies A1 certificates directly with the Goethe-Institut. Using a forgery leads to a refusal and a lengthy entry ban.

steps.title: Recognition of the marriage in Germany

content.text: Not every foreign marriage is automatically recognised in Germany. A marriage concluded in Russia through the civil registry office with both parties present in person is recognised. Marriages by proxy (Ferntrauung), religious marriages without state registration and online marriages in third countries may not be recognised.

items: Marriage certificate with apostille and a translation into German
A marriage registered with the Russian civil registry office is recognised; the apostille is affixed by the competent authority of the federal subject
A religious marriage without state registration is not recognised
Polygamous marriages: for reunification purposes one marriage is recognised
Same-sex marriages are recognised if concluded where this is lawful
Marriages involving a minor are scrutinised especially strictly and may not be recognised

content.text: If there is doubt, the marriage can be registered in Germany after entering on a visa for the purpose of marriage (§6 Abs. 3 in conjunction with §28). The registry office (Standesamt) usually requires apostilled birth certificates, a certificate of capacity to marry (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis) or an exemption from it, and documents on the dissolution of any previous marriages. Because the requirements depend on the country and the registry office, individual legal advice is recommended.

Under §29–§30 the host spouse has to prove sufficient income. Under §28 (joining a German citizen) there is no formal check, but in practice the ABH often asks for the same documents — especially where there is doubt.

items: Needs-based calculation (Bedarf): the subsistence minimum for each person plus rent (roughly 2500–3500 €/month net; verify for the current year)
Payslips (Lohnabrechnungen) for several months or a tax assessment (Steuerbescheid; for the self-employed)
If income falls short, a third party can give a formal declaration of commitment to cover costs (Verpflichtungserklärung)
Housing: a guideline of about 12 m² of living space per person; a rental contract in your name
Confirmation that the spouse is registered at your address (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung)
Under §28 the economic criterion is not formally mandatory, but a check is possible
If you receive basic benefits (Bürgergeld), reunification under §29 is generally not possible
Some easing is possible (serious illness, disability, young children) — assessed case by case

content.text: The applicant spouse's package plus the package of the host spouse in Germany. The application is filed at the German mission in the applicant's place of residence.

items: Passport of the applicant spouse and copies
Online visa form VIDEX (category "Ehegattennachzug")
2 biometric photos
Marriage certificate with apostille and translation
German A1 certificate (if required)
Police clearance certificate with apostille and translation
Certificates of dissolution of any previous marriages (if applicable) with apostille
Health insurance valid on entry
Copy of the host spouse's passport or AT
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) — no older than 6 months
Rental contract and the landlord's confirmation of move-in
Payslips for several months and the employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag)
Evidence of a genuine marriage (joint photos, correspondence, tickets) — at the ABH's request

content.text: After entry: residence registration (Anmeldung), an appointment at the ABH and collection of the plastic AT card. The first residence permit is usually for 1–3 years, renewable as long as the marriage continues.

items: Unrestricted right to work from day one
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) — family insurance for family members (Familienversicherung) through the spouse or own cover (mandatory)

An integration course (Integrationskurs) is mandatory if the language level is below what is required; the course is subsidised by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF); a participant co-payment, or free of charge on a low income
A permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §28 Abs. 2 — usually after 3 years if the marriage continues and the conditions are met
An independent residence permit after divorce — §31 (as a rule, where the marriage lasted at least 3 years in Germany)
Naturalisation of a German citizen's spouse — §9 StAG: 3 years of lawful residence and at least 2 years of marriage (subject to the other conditions)

content.text: If a divorce occurs in the first years of the marriage, the spouse may lose the derived right under §29–§30 and must switch to an independent basis (work, study) or to an independent residence permit under §31. Victims of domestic violence are protected: §31 Abs. 2 allows the AT to be extended even without a minimum duration of marriage. Situations vary — individual legal advice is recommended.
