title: Temporary confirmation of status (Fiktionsbescheinigung): what it gives you
tldr: A temporary confirmation of legal status (Fiktionsbescheinigung, §81 Abs. 3–5 AufenthG) is an official certificate from the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde, ABH) confirming that, while a new application is being processed, a "fiction" of your previous status applies. It is issued if the application to extend or for a new residence permit was filed in time. It lets you live and work in Germany; travel within the Schengen area is usually possible, but travel to third countries is risky. The fee is 13 €. It is normally valid for 3–6 months and can be extended. Important: the saving continuation fiction (Fortgeltungsfiktion, §81 Abs. 4) applies only if the application is filed BEFORE the previous residence permit (AT) expires. If you miss the deadline, the right of residence is not preserved. Individual legal advice is recommended, especially when planning travel.

content.text: A Fiktionsbescheinigung is a document issued by the foreigners' authority to a foreigner whose residence permit is expiring or has expired but who has already applied for a new one. Under §81 AufenthG, while the application is being processed, the previous status legally ("fictionally") continues to apply.

items: It is not a standalone residence permit but a continuation of the previous status
Usually issued for 3–6 months, renewable
Fee — 13 € (under the AufenthV)
The certificate states which paragraph of §81 applies: Abs. 3, 4 or 5
The right to work matches what the previous AT allowed

content.text: §81 AufenthG contains three different "fictions", each with its own set of rights.

items: §81 Abs. 3 (permission fiction, Erlaubnisfiktion) — for those staying lawfully without an AT (for example visa-free) who have applied for their FIRST AT; it grants a right of residence while the application is processed, usually without the right to work
§81 Abs. 4 (Fortgeltungsfiktion) — the main one: for extending an AT when filed BEFORE expiry; it preserves the rights of the previous AT, including work
§81 Abs. 5 — for cases of a status change under specific provisions; the scope of rights is set by the relevant rule

content.text: Check the expiry date of your AT urgently. File the extension application well in advance. If the foreigners' authority (ABH) cannot give you an appointment (Termin) in time, submit the application (Antrag) by post or through the city's online portal — the application counts as filed from the date it reaches the ABH. Keep the confirmation of receipt (Eingangsbestätigung).
Under §81 Abs. 4, the rights of the previous AT are preserved: residence, work to the previous extent, insurance, banking, renting. It is in effect a continuation of the status until the ABH decides.

items: Right to live in Germany — yes
Right to work — if the previous AT allowed it (for §18, the EU Blue Card (Blue Card), §19c — without restrictions)
Right to child benefit (Kindergeld) and social benefits — if you were entitled to them
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) is preserved
School and daycare (Kita) for children — without interruption
Travel within the Schengen area — usually possible with a valid passport and the Fiktionsbescheinigung, but without guarantees
Travel to third countries — risky: return may be difficult
Opening an account at a new bank — in practice often problematic
Applying for citizenship — residence under Abs. 4 counts as lawful

content.text: The most vulnerable point is leaving the EU. Despite §81 Abs. 4, airlines and border officers in third countries do not always interpret this status correctly. Before any trip outside the Schengen area, individual legal advice and coordination with the ABH are strongly recommended.
Not every ABH issues the certificate automatically: in large cities (Berlin, Munich) you often have to request it separately.

items: Step 1: file the application to extend the AT BEFORE it expires (online, by post or in person)
Step 2: obtain the Eingangsbestätigung — this already establishes that you filed in time
Step 3: book a Termin to be issued the Fiktionsbescheinigung through the city portal
Step 4: attend the ABH with your passport, the previous AT, the Eingangsbestätigung and the 13 € fee
Step 5: receive the certificate valid for 3–6 months
Step 6: extend the certificate if needed (a further Termin or via the portal)

If the ABH remains inactive for a long time, an action against the authority's inaction (Untätigkeitsklage) before the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht; §75 VwGO) is possible — usually after the prescribed waiting period

content.text: The fiction works reliably as long as you do nothing out of the ordinary: changing employer, travelling outside the Schengen area, taking out a mortgage. That is when it emerges that the bank, HR and border control interpret the status differently.

items: A new employer will not hire you on a fiction — show them §81 Abs. 4 and a copy of the previous AT with the right to work
The bank restricts your account — provide the Fiktionsbescheinigung and the registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung)
The foreigners' authority is slow to decide — an action against the authority's inaction is possible (§75 VwGO)
Detained at the border on return — show the certificate and the Eingangsbestätigung; if refused entry, contact the German mission
The fiction has expired and there is no decision — book another appointment and ask for an extension
Refused on the new AT — the fiction ends; you have the right to appeal (Widerspruch or Klage) subject to the prescribed deadlines

content.text: If the extension application is filed AFTER the previous AT has expired, the Fortgeltungsfiktion (§81 Abs. 4) does not apply and the right of residence is not preserved. In that situation the only route is to approach the ABH and file a new application; until a decision is made, only a deferral of deportation (Duldung) is possible. The difference is fundamental, so if you have missed the deadline, individual legal advice is recommended.

costs.label: Fiktionsbescheinigung (issue and extension)
costs.note: Under the AufenthV. The key is to file the application in time.

costs.label: Untätigkeitsklage (if the ABH is inactive)
costs.note: Court fees and costs depend on the case; if you win, the ABH may bear the costs.

costs.label: Certified translation of documents for the extension
costs.note: If circumstances have changed (a new marriage, the birth of a child), translations of the new documents are needed.

title: Foreign children: ius soli under §4 (3) StAG
tldr: A child born in Germany to foreign parents acquires German citizenship at birth under §4 Abs. 3 StAG if at least one parent, at the time of birth, has 5+ years of lawful residence in Germany and a permanent right of residence, unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht (permanent residence permit Niederlassungserlaubnis, EU long-term resident status, the EU citizens' right of free movement). The reform of 27.06.2024 lowered the threshold from 8 to 5 years and abolished the obligation to choose a citizenship (Optionspflicht) — the child now keeps both German and the parental citizenship and is not required to choose one of them. Entry in the birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) and the paperwork are handled by the registry office (Standesamt) immediately after birth, without a separate naturalisation procedure. From Germany's side, dual citizenship by ius soli is fully lawful; the rules of the parents' country of origin need to be checked separately.

steps.title: What ius soli under §4 (3) StAG is

content.text: Germany is a country governed primarily by ius sanguinis (citizenship by descent, §4 Abs. 1 StAG: the child of a German citizen is a German citizen). But since 2000, §4 Abs. 3 StAG has provided for a limited ius soli (right of the soil): a child born on German territory to foreign parents acquires German citizenship if the residence-period conditions for one of the parents are met.

The StAG reform that came into force on 27 June 2024 (Gesetz zur Modernisierung des Staatsangehörigkeitsrechts) lowered the parental residence threshold from 8 to 5 years and at the same time abolished the so-called Optionspflicht — the child's obligation to choose a single citizenship on reaching the age of majority. The child now keeps both passports.

items: §4 Abs. 3 Nr. 1 StAG: one of the parents has lawfully resided in Germany for 5 years
§4 Abs. 3 Nr. 2 StAG: that parent has an unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht at the time of birth

Permanent status (unbefristet): Niederlassungserlaubnis, EU long-term residence permit (Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt-EU), the EU citizens' right of free movement, and the permanent right of residence of Swiss nationals
A temporary residence permit (befristete Aufenthaltserlaubnis), for example under §§ 16b, 18, 19c AufenthG, does not grant the child ius soli
The child has to do nothing: citizenship arises at the moment of birth by operation of law (kraft Gesetzes)
The obligation to choose a citizenship (the former §29 StAG) was abolished on 27.06.2024

steps.title: How to register a German child

content.text: If both conditions of §4 Abs. 3 StAG are met, there is no need for an application (Antrag) or the 255€ fee that applies to naturalisation. The registry office for the place of birth enters the child in the birth certificate as a German citizen (deutscher Staatsangehöriger) at the same time as registering the birth.

items: Registration of the birth at the registry office — within a week of the birth (§18 PStG)
Documents: the Geburtsanzeige from the clinic, the parents' passports, the marriage certificate (apostille + translation)
The parent's Niederlassungserlaubnis or residence permit card (Aufenthaltstitel) — the original
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) — proving the parent's 5+ years of residence
The registry office checks the §4 Abs. 3 StAG conditions and enters the citizenship
The child's passport (Reisepass) or children's passport (Kinderreisepass) — ordered at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt)
Registration at the embassy or consulate of the country of the second citizenship — separately

content.text: If the registry office has doubts (for example, it is unclear whether the parent held a permanent status for 5 years), a separate certificate of citizenship (Staatsangehörigkeitsausweis) from the competent authority may be required — this takes several months. Until the document is issued the child is already legally German, but travel is difficult without the document.

Before the reform, under the former §29 StAG a child with two citizenships by ius soli had to declare, on reaching the age of majority, which citizenship they were keeping, or lose the German one. This rule (Optionspflicht) has been abolished.

items: Children born between 01.01.2000 and 26.06.2024 whose period for choosing a citizenship (Optionsfrist) had not yet expired are released from the choice
Anyone who previously lost German citizenship under the former §29 may, under certain conditions, regain it through a simplified procedure — check the details with the authority
Children born from 27.06.2024 keep dual citizenship
Multiple citizenship (Mehrstaatigkeit) is fully permitted from Germany's side for all new births
The parents' country of origin may have its own rules: some (Russia, Turkey, Iran) often allow dual citizenship, others (China, India) do not

content.text: Important: if the parents' country of origin does not allow dual citizenship (for example the PRC), this does not cancel the child's German citizenship under §4 Abs. 3 StAG, but it may mean that that country does not recognise the child as its national. Check with the consulate; in disputed cases individual legal advice is recommended.

costs.label: Geburtsurkunde mit Staatsangehörigkeit
costs.note: Standard Standesamt fee for a birth certificate; the citizenship is entered at no separate charge.

costs.label: Kinderreisepass / Reisepass
costs.note: Depends on the type of document and the age; check the exact rates at the Bürgeramt.

costs.label: Staatsangehörigkeitsausweis (if required)
costs.note: Confirmation of German citizenship if the Standesamt did not enter it automatically.

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung of the parents' documents
costs.note: Marriage certificate, apostille from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus — per page.

title: §10 StAG requirements: check yourself
tldr: Standard naturalisation is governed by §10 Abs. 1 StAG. The requirements are cumulative: 5 years of legal residence and an established identity (the opening sentence of Abs. 1); Nr. 1 — commitment (Bekenntnis) to the free democratic order and a declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung), including acknowledgement of historical responsibility (antisemitism and racism are a bar); Nr. 2 — a right of residence (Aufenthaltsrecht); Nr. 3 — means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) without basic income support (Bürgergeld) or social assistance (Sozialhilfe); Nr. 5 — no relevant criminal record; Nr. 6 — German at B1; Nr. 7 — the naturalisation test (Einbürgerungstest). The former requirement to renounce your previous citizenship (Nr. 4) has been abolished — dual citizenship is now allowed for everyone. The fast track after 3 years (former §10 Abs. 3) was abolished as of 30.10.2025 and is no longer available. The fee is 255€ / 51€ per child. Processing usually takes 6–24 months, longer in large cities.

content.text: §10 Abs. 1 StAG sets out a set of cumulative requirements — all of them must be met at the same time, both when you file the application and when the naturalisation certificate is handed over (Aushändigung der Einbürgerungsurkunde). The requirement to give up your previous citizenship (former §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 4) has been abolished — dual citizenship is now allowed for everyone.

items: 5 years of habitual residence (gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt) and an established identity — the opening sentence of §10 Abs. 1 (previously 8 years). The 3-year track (former §10 Abs. 3) was abolished as of 30.10.2025

§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 — a valid status: permanent settlement permit (NE), EU long-term resident status, a temporary residence permit (AE) under §§ 18, 19c, 25, 28 AufenthG, or an EU citizen's right of free movement
§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 6 — German at level B1 (per CEFR/GER)
§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 7 — a passed naturalisation test (33 questions, at least 17 correct)
§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 — means of subsistence without basic income support (SGB II) and without social assistance (SGB XII)
§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 5 — no relevant criminal record (minor penalties are disregarded under §12a StAG)

§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 — declaration of loyalty and acknowledgement of historical responsibility (antisemitism and racism are a bar; tightened by the 2024 reform). The former requirement to renounce your citizenship (Nr. 4) has been abolished

content.text: The means-of-subsistence requirement (Lebensunterhalt, Nr. 3) is one of the strictest after the 2024 reform. The former broad exception allowing benefits received "through no fault of your own" has been narrowed. Now receiving SGB II or SGB XII generally bars naturalisation, except in narrow cases (the guest-worker generation — Gastarbeiter, caring for children while in full-time work, and cases of particular hardship — Härtefälle). Housing benefit (Wohngeld), child benefit (Kindergeld) and BAföG usually do not bar it.

Habitual residence does not mean tourist trips, but registered residence with a residence registration (Anmeldung) under §17 BMG. Long interruptions abroad can interrupt or reset the count — the thresholds and consequences are assessed by the authority, so it is best to clear long absences with them in advance.

items: Time on a permission to stay during an asylum procedure (Aufenthaltsgestattung; §55 AsylG) and on a suspension of deportation (Duldung) is generally not counted
Time spent studying is counted (in full after the 2024 reform)
Humanitarian status under §24 AufenthG (including for Ukrainians) is counted from the date it is issued
Time on an EU Blue Card (Blue Card) is counted; under certain conditions the Blue Card speeds up obtaining an NE
Time of residence before reaching the age of majority is counted
The fast track after 3 years (former §10 Abs. 3 StAG) was abolished as of 30.10.2025 (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG) — it is now 5 years for everyone
Spouses of Germans: §9 StAG — usually 3 years of residence and at least 2 years of marriage

content.text: The Loyalitätserklärung (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1, supplemented by the requirement to acknowledge historical responsibility) is one of the main innovations of the 2024 reform. The applicant declares in writing their commitment to the free democratic basic order (freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung) of the constitution, condemns antisemitism and racism, and acknowledges the aus der deutschen Geschichte erwachsende besondere Verantwortung für die nationalsozialistische Unrechtsherrschaft und ihre Folgen, insbesondere für den Schutz jüdischen Lebens.

items: The declaration of loyalty is signed at the naturalisation authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) when you apply — this is mandatory
Refusing to sign leads to a refusal of naturalisation
Antisemitic or other incompatible public statements can be grounds for refusal
A query to the office for the protection of the constitution (Verfassungsschutzanfrage) is a standard check on applicants
B1 is proven with a telc, Goethe or ÖSD certificate or a German school or university qualification
The naturalisation test — 33 questions, at least 17 correct, fee 25€
The B1 certificate and the test result do not expire

content.text: The office for the protection of the constitution (Verfassungsschutz) screens applicants. Membership in banned or anti-constitutional organisations, support for terrorism, and public calls against the democratic order can lead to refusal under §11 StAG. If your profile is contentious, individual legal advice before applying is recommended.

If there is no entitlement to naturalisation under §10, the route of discretionary naturalisation (Ermessenseinbürgerung) under §8 StAG remains. Here the authority assesses whether there is a public interest (öffentliches Interesse). This is a rare route.

items: §8 StAG — there is no hard formal entitlement, but language and integration are taken into account
Criminal record: §12a StAG allows minor penalties to be disregarded (a daily fine rate, Tagessatz)
In case of illness or disability you can be exempted from the naturalisation test and B1 (§10 Abs. 6 StAG)
Older applicants may be granted concessions — assessed case by case
A refusal can be challenged through an objection (Widerspruch) and then before the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht)
In complex cases individual legal advice is recommended

costs.note: §38 Abs. 2 StAG. Paid when you apply or before the Urkunde is issued.

costs.label: Fee for a child included in a parent's Antrag
costs.note: A child's standalone naturalisation costs 255€.

costs.label: Einbürgerungstest
costs.note: At VHS and test centres; a retake is 25€ again.

costs.label: B1 certificate
costs.note: telc, Goethe or ÖSD; the price depends on the provider and city.

title: Discounts on the naturalization fee (Einbürgerung)
tldr: The standard naturalization fee is 255€ for an adult and 51€ for each child included in a parent's application (Antrag) (§38 Abs. 2 StAG). For low income, the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) can grant a reduction or a waiver of the fee "aus Gründen der Billigkeit oder des öffentlichen Interesses" under §38 Abs. 4 StAG; specific waiver cases are listed in §38 Abs. 3 StAG. Deferred payment (Stundung) is possible under the general rules on fees. Discounts are not granted automatically: you have to request them explicitly and attach proof of income (pay slips — Lohnabrechnungen, Bürgergeld-Bescheid, BAföG-Bescheid). The decision is made case by case at the authority's discretion, and practice varies between the federal states.

content.text: The naturalization fee is set out in §38 StAG. It is the same throughout Germany and does not depend on the federal state (Bundesland), unlike the fees of the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde).

items: §38 Abs. 2 StAG: 255€ — standard fee per adult
§38 Abs. 2 StAG: 51€ — for each minor child naturalized together with a parent (miteingebürgert)
A child naturalized on their own (without a parent): also 255€
The naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) is paid separately — 25€ (not included in the fee)
Certified translation (Beglaubigte Übersetzung) of documents — 30–80€ per page, not reimbursed
A passport (Reisepass) after naturalization is paid separately at the rates of the passport authority

content.text: The fee is usually paid before the certificate of naturalization (Einbürgerungsurkunde) is issued, sometimes when the application (Antrag) is filed. The StAG has no provision for an automatic partial refund of the fee. On the contrary, under §38 Abs. 2 StAG, if the application is withdrawn or denied after the substantive review has begun, a separate charge is levied (from 25€ up to the full fee amount). §39 StAG is a power to issue secondary legislation (Verordnungsermächtigung), not a refund rule. Check the practice of your specific authority (Behörde).

§38 Abs. 4 StAG allows a reduction of the fee (Ermäßigung) or a waiver of it (Befreiung) "aus Gründen der Billigkeit oder des öffentlichen Interesses". In addition, for minor children the fee is reduced to 51€ (§38 Abs. 2 StAG). Deferred payment (Stundung) is possible under the general rules on fees; check with the authority.

items: Deferred payment (Stundung) — suitable for a temporary financial burden
Fee reduction (Ermäßigung) — under §38 Abs. 4 StAG; for low-income earners and large families
Full waiver (Befreiung) — rare, in special circumstances
The request for a discount is filed as a separate application together with the naturalization application (Einbürgerungsantrag)
Proof: Bürgergeld-Bescheid, pay slips for the last 3 months, BAföG-Bescheid, bank statements (Kontoauszüge)
The decision is made by the naturalization authority; a refusal is formally challenged through an objection (Widerspruch)

content.text: Important: receiving basic income support (Bürgergeld) at the time of the decision is a ground for refusing naturalization under §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StAG, not a ground for a fee discount. A fee reduction is relevant, for example, for those who have already stopped receiving basic income support but whose own income remains low.

A family of two adults and two children pays 255 + 255 + 51 + 51 = 612€ for the fee alone, not counting tests, translations, and passports. A number of states apply a more generous practice of reducing the fee specifically for large families — check the exact conditions with your authority.

items: Large families: you can request a reduction of the fee per child under §38 Abs. 4 StAG
Students on BAföG: deferred payment until the end of their studies is possible
Trainees (Auszubildende) on a low income: a fee reduction is possible — at the authority's discretion
During insolvency proceedings the fee is often deferred
Legal advice assistance (Beratungshilfe) and advisory services (AWO, Caritas, Diakonie) help you draft the application
The states have their own administrative regulations (Verwaltungsvorschriften) on §38 StAG — ask at the naturalization authority

content.text: Don't confuse a fee reduction with a fee refund. If you have already paid the 255€ and then find a ground for a discount, the authority will usually refuse to refund it. You have to request the benefit BEFORE paying, when you file the application (Antrag).

costs.label: Standard fee (adult)
costs.note: §38 Abs. 2 StAG.

costs.label: Fee for a child with a parent
costs.note: §38 Abs. 2 StAG; an Ermäßigung under §38 Abs. 4 StAG is possible.

costs.label: Stundung — deferral
costs.note: Not a discount but deferred payment under the general rules on fees.

costs.label: Charge for a refusal or withdrawal of the application
costs.note: Under §38 Abs. 2 StAG, if the application is withdrawn or denied after the substantive review has begun, a charge from 25€ up to the full fee amount is levied.

title: C1 to avoid giving up your original citizenship? No
tldr: The myth that "C1 → you don't have to give up your previous citizenship" was always wrong: giving it up was governed by the former §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 4 StAG and the exceptions in §12 StAG, not by language level. After the reform of 27.06.2024 this condition was removed and §12 StAG was abolished — dual citizenship is allowed for everyone in standard naturalization with B1. Separately: the fast track to citizenship in 3 years with C1 (the former §10 Abs. 3 StAG) only applied from 27.06.2024 to 29.10.2025 and was abolished as of 30.10.2025 (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG) — C1 no longer shortens the naturalization period. A C1 certificate (telc, Goethe, TestDaF) costs 149–280€ and is still useful for work and study, but it is no longer required for naturalization.

steps.title: Where the myth about C1 and dual citizenship came from

content.text: Current as of 2026: the fast track in 3 years has been abolished. The former §10 Abs. 3 StAG (3 years with C1 and special integration achievements — besondere Integrationsleistungen) was abolished as of 30.10.2025 (Sechstes Gesetz zur Änderung des StAG). C1 no longer shortens the naturalization period; the standard is 5 years with B1. The part about giving up citizenship remains correct: no renunciation is required, dual citizenship is allowed for everyone.

Until 26 June 2024, the former §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 4 StAG stated: for naturalization you had to give up your previous citizenship (Aufgabe oder Verlust der bisherigen Staatsangehörigkeit). The exceptions were listed in §12 StAG — for EU and Swiss citizens, where renunciation is impossible, and where it would cause substantial disadvantages (erhebliche Nachteile).

A rule like "with C1 you can keep both passports" never existed in the StAG. The myth arose from conflating two different categories: highly qualified persons (hochqualifizierte Personen) within discretionary naturalization (Ermessenseinbürgerung) under §8 StAG and the general notion of public interest. Authorities sometimes mentioned a high language level as one of the integration factors, but not as an independent ground for keeping two passports.

items: Former §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 4 StAG: required giving up the previous citizenship — abolished 27.06.2024
Former §12 StAG: exceptions for the EU, Switzerland, where renunciation is impossible, and for substantial disadvantages — abolished
A rule "C1 = automatic right to two passports" never applied
2024 reform: multiple citizenship (Mehrstaatigkeit) is allowed for everyone without conditions
The fast track in 3 years (former §10 Abs. 3 StAG) abolished as of 30.10.2025

content.text: If in 2026 you see a website or a "consultant" claiming that C1 is needed for dual citizenship or that naturalization in 3 years is available, that is outdated or misleading information. Rely only on sources that reflect the version of the StAG after 30.10.2025.

steps.title: The real role of C1 after the reform

content.text: Fast-track naturalization in 3 years with C1 level (the former §10 Abs. 3 StAG) applied from 27.06.2024 to 29.10.2025 and was abolished as of 30.10.2025. Now B1 is enough for naturalization, and C1 gives no reduction in the period. C1 level is still valuable for the labour market, for studying, and for university admission.

items: Former §10 Abs. 3 StAG (3 years + C1 + special integration achievements) abolished as of 30.10.2025
B1 for the standard 5-year naturalization remains the mandatory minimum
C1 does not shorten the naturalization period but is useful for your career and studies
Recognized C1 certificates: telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule, Goethe-Zertifikat C1, ÖSD C1, TestDaF, DSH-2/3

steps.title: How to get C1 and what it costs

content.text: C1 is an advanced level: understanding complex texts, speaking fluently, writing structured texts. Many people at B1 level need about 6–18 months of classes to reach C1. Options for preparation: the adult education centre (Volkshochschule, VHS), the Goethe-Institut, private schools, self-study.

items: C1 courses at the VHS: roughly 250–450€ per module; you usually need several modules
Goethe-Institut, intensive C1 courses: considerably more expensive
telc Deutsch C1 certificate: 149–180€
Goethe-Zertifikat C1 certificate: 220–280€
TestDaF: roughly 200€
Study materials: "Aspekte neu C1" (Klett), "Erkundungen C1" (Schubert), DW Nicos Weg for listening
The certificate has no expiry date (like B1) — no need to retake it

content.text: If you completed higher education in German (for example, by passing DSH or TestDaF for admission), that document usually proves a high language level for work and study. For naturalization itself, again, B1 is now enough.

costs.label: B1 → C1 courses (VHS, several modules)
costs.note: The VHS is cheaper; the Goethe-Institut and private intensive courses are more expensive.

costs.label: telc Deutsch C1 certificate
costs.note: The most affordable recognized C1 certificate.

costs.label: Goethe-Zertifikat C1 certificate
costs.note: More expensive, widely recognized by authorities and universities.

costs.label: Einbürgerung (adult)
costs.note: State fee under §38 Abs. 2 StAG; does not depend on language level.

title: Declaration of loyalty (Loyalitätserklärung)
tldr: The declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung) is a mandatory part of naturalization, strengthened by the reform of §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG on 27 June 2024. It is a written commitment to the free democratic order of the Federal Republic, a condemnation of antisemitism and racism, and an explicit acknowledgement of Germany's special historical responsibility for National Socialism and its consequences and for "protecting Jewish life". It is signed in person at the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde). Refusing to sign leads to refusal of naturalization. As part of the procedure a check by the office for the protection of the constitution (Verfassungsschutz) is carried out; public support for organizations banned in the Federal Republic, calls for violence, and Holocaust denial are grounds for refusal under §11 StAG, and certain acts also carry criminal liability. If your profile is contentious, individual legal advice is recommended.

content.text: §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG, in its 2024 version, requires a commitment (Bekenntnis) to the free democratic order (freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung). The Federal Constitutional Court (BVerfG) defined this concept back in 1956 in its decision banning the KPD (BVerfGE 5, 85): respect for human dignity, popular sovereignty, separation of powers, accountability of the government, an independent judiciary, a multi-party system.

The 2024 reform broadened the wording by adding an explicit condemnation of antisemitism, racism, and other misanthropic ideologies, as well as an explicit acknowledgement of Germany's historical responsibility for National Socialism and its consequences — insbesondere für den Schutz jüdischen Lebens.

items: Acknowledgement of the Basic Law (Grundgesetz) and the democratic order
Renunciation of any violent seizure of power
Condemnation of antisemitism
Condemnation of racism and other misanthropic acts (menschenverachtende Handlungen)
Acknowledgement of the special historical responsibility for National Socialism and the Holocaust
Acknowledgement of the responsibility for protecting Jewish life in Germany

steps.title: Where and how it is signed

content.text: The declaration is signed in person at the naturalization authority — usually when the naturalization application (Einbürgerungsantrag) is filed, and in many cities again at the handover of the certificate of naturalization (Aushändigung der Einbürgerungsurkunde), sometimes with a public commitment to the constitution (Bekenntnis zur Verfassung) at the ceremony.

items: The text is standard under §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 StAG; the form is issued by the authority (Behörde)
The signature is personal, not through a representative
As part of the procedure the authority initiates a check by the office for the protection of the constitution
The review period varies; if the result is positive, the certificate (Urkunde) is issued

content.text: Don't try to sign "with reservations" (for example, by excluding the part about protecting Jewish life). A reservation is treated as a refusal to make the commitment and leads to refusal of naturalization. The text is accepted in full.

Authorities check whether the applicant is compatible with the declaration of loyalty and may take public statements into account, including on social media. A number of states have officially included such a check in the standard process. The aim is to identify signs of incompatibility with the free democratic order.

items: Public support for organizations banned in the Federal Republic — a ground for refusal
Calls for violence against people on the basis of nationality or religion — a ground for refusal
Holocaust denial (incitement to hatred, Volksverhetzung; §130 StGB) — a ground for refusal and a criminal case
Statements incompatible with the equality and dignity of people — a reason for a deeper review
Public support for a war of aggression may be treated as incompatibility with the declaration of loyalty
Participation in organizations under observation by the office for the protection of the constitution — a reason for refusal

content.text: If you have made contentious public statements in the past, individual legal advice (administrative law, citizenship law — Verwaltungsrecht/Staatsangehörigkeitsrecht) is recommended before filing the application (Antrag). Certain acts may lead not only to refusal but also to criminal liability (for example, §130 StGB).

If citizenship was obtained by deception (Täuschung), including a knowingly false commitment in the declaration of loyalty, it can be revoked under §35 StAG within the set time limits after the handover. This is allowed by case law where deception is proven; the specific conditions and time limits are assessed by the authority and the court.

items: §35 StAG — withdrawal of an unlawful naturalization (Rücknahme rechtswidriger Einbürgerung) in cases of deception
Ground: deception about material facts, including political ties
If the withdrawal would render the person stateless, constitutional limits apply (Art. 16 GG)
For people with two citizenships, the previous citizenship remains if the German one is withdrawn
Loss under §28 StAG is also possible — voluntary service in foreign armed forces without permission

costs.label: Loyalitätserklärung
costs.note: Signing itself is free — the text and the form are provided by the Behörde.

costs.label: Verfassungsschutz check
costs.note: Not charged separately; covered by the general fee of 255€.

costs.label: Legal advice (for a risky profile)
costs.note: Erstberatung on Verwaltungsrecht/Staatsangehörigkeitsrecht.

title: Russian citizens: naturalization in 2026
tldr: For Russian citizens in Germany in 2026, naturalization under §10 StAG follows the general rules: 5 years of legal residence, B1, the naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest), the declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung), and self-sufficiency. Since the reform of 27.06.2024, dual citizenship is allowed on the German side for everyone — you don't have to give up your Russian passport. On the Russian side, there is an obligation to notify the competent body of the Russian Ministry of the Interior about the acquisition of a foreign citizenship; as a general rule this applies to people who have a place of residence in Russia, and for those permanently living abroad and removed from the residence register the obligation usually does not arise. Russian law changes from time to time, so check the current requirements and deadlines with a specialist lawyer in Russian law; individual legal advice is recommended. As part of the German procedure a standard check by the office for the protection of the constitution (Verfassungsschutz) is carried out, so public statements matter.

steps.title: The general procedure for Russian citizens

content.text: Since 27 June 2024, the same rules of §10 StAG apply to Russian citizens as to citizens of other third countries: 5 years of ordinary residence (gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt), B1, the naturalization test, the declaration of loyalty, no basic income support (Bürgergeld), no relevant criminal record. The key change: giving up Russian citizenship is no longer required.

items: 5 years of legal residence (including studies, the EU Blue Card — Blue Card, status under §18a/§18b AufenthG)
A valid status: temporary residence permit (AE), permanent residence permit (NE), or EU long-term resident status
B1 — telc, Goethe, ÖSD, or a German school leaving certificate
Naturalization test — at least 17 out of 33, 25€
Means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) without basic income support (SGB II)
Filing the application (Antrag) at the naturalization authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) at your place of residence
Processing usually takes 6–24 months, longer in large cities
The Russian passport remains valid; you don't have to surrender it

content.text: Russian citizenship law provides for an obligation to notify the competent body of the Russian Ministry of the Interior about the acquisition of a foreign state's citizenship. As a general rule, this obligation is tied to having a place of residence in Russia; breaching it carries administrative and, in certain cases, criminal liability. The rules and penalties change from time to time, so check the specific deadlines and procedure with a specialist lawyer.

items: The notification is filed within the time limit set by law after acquiring the foreign citizenship
It is filed with the competent body of the Ministry of the Interior at the place of residence in Russia, or through a foreign mission if that is provided for
As a general rule, the obligation applies to people who have a place of residence in Russia
Removal from the residence register in Russia usually affects whether the obligation exists — check with a lawyer
The Russian passport remains valid until it expires
To enter Russia, a Russian citizen needs a Russian passport
A Russian passport is issued at the consular offices in the Federal Republic

content.text: Germany does not strip you of German citizenship because you hold a Russian one. The Russian side, as a general rule, does not strip you of citizenship for naturalizing in the Federal Republic; voluntary renunciation of Russian citizenship is a separate procedure. Since Russian rules change, agree on whether and how to notify with a specialist lawyer; individual legal advice is recommended.

As part of naturalization, a standard check by the office for the protection of the constitution is carried out. For some applicants, the authorities pay closer attention to possible links with state or propaganda structures and to support for a war of aggression. The aim is to make sure the applicant is compatible with the free democratic order.

items: Working for state propaganda media — a reason for a deeper review
Spreading propaganda narratives on social media — may become a reason for refusal
Public support for a war of aggression — incompatibility with the declaration of loyalty
Displaying symbols associated with support for the war — risky
Past military service in itself is not an automatic ground for refusal, but it may be checked
An anti-war, pro-democratic stance is usually assessed positively by the authority

content.text: Be honest in your application and in the interview with the authority. If you have made contentious public statements in the past, individual legal advice before filing the application is recommended, along with a readiness to explain how your views have evolved.

Russia is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention, so Russian documents are accepted in Germany with an apostille and a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung). The apostille for different types of documents is issued by different Russian bodies. Since 2022, obtaining an apostille from abroad has become more difficult but is still possible, including through a representative.

items: Birth certificate — apostille + translation (30–80€ per page)
Marriage or divorce certificate — apostille + translation
Certificate of no criminal record from Russia — apostille + translation (limited validity period)
Educational document — the apostille is issued by the competent body
Russian passport — copy + translation, if the authority requires it (Behörde)
Instead of a certificate from Russia, a German certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis) is often enough for long-term residents in the Federal Republic

content.text: Document requirements vary between authorities: some accept, instead of a certificate from Russia, a sworn statement (Eidesstattliche Versicherung) that you have no criminal record since you left. Check the policy of your specific naturalization authority in advance.

costs.label: Standard naturalization fee
costs.note: §38 Abs. 2 StAG.

costs.label: Apostille on a document from Russia
costs.note: Russian state fee plus the representative's service; more expensive through consular channels.

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung from Russian
costs.note: Per page; a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer).

costs.label: Russian passport at a consulate in the Federal Republic
costs.note: Needed to enter Russia; the issuing time depends on the consulate.

sources.title: §10 StAG — Anspruch auf Einbürgerung (Gesetze im Internet)

title: Ukrainian citizens: naturalization and §24
tldr: Most Ukrainians in Germany received temporary protection (vorübergehender Schutz) under §24 AufenthG (the EU Temporary Protection Directive — EU-Massenzustromrichtlinie 2001/55/EG) after 24.02.2022. This grants the right to work, basic income support (Bürgergeld), free courses, and healthcare, but not automatic inclusion in naturalization. Under §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 StAG you need a suitable residence permit; a permit under §24 AufenthG is generally accepted by the authorities as sufficient for naturalization (Einbürgerung), and the residence period under it counts in full from the date of issue (it is advisable to confirm the position of your naturalization authority — Einbürgerungsbehörde). By 2027, Ukrainians who arrived in 2022 will reach the 5-year threshold for standard naturalization under §10 StAG. Dual citizenship is allowed: after the reform Germany does not require renunciation, and Ukraine effectively does not take away its passport. An alternative is switching to §18 AufenthG (skilled worker — Fachkraft), §28 (marriage to a German citizen), or §25 Abs. 2 (refugee protection — Flüchtlingsschutz), each with its own conditions. Individual legal advice is recommended.

content.text: §24 AufenthG implements the EU Temporary Protection Directive 2001/55/EG, which was activated for the first time in EU history by Council Decision (EU) 2022/382 of 4 March 2022. Ukrainians receive a temporary residence permit (AE) under §24 for 1–3 years, with extension; in 2026 the EU Council extended it until March 2027.

items: §24 AufenthG — temporary protection; in force until 04.03.2027 (the latest EU Council decision)
Right to work from day one (without a priority check for local workers — Vorrangprüfung)
Access to basic income support since June 2022 (transition from the AsylbLG — Übergang)
Full access to statutory health insurance (Krankenversicherung GKV)
Right to the integration course (Integrationskurs) and the vocational language course (Berufssprachkurs) — free of charge
Time under §24 counts towards the 5 years for §10 StAG from day one
For those who arrived in February–March 2022, the right to apply (Antrag) arises in February–March 2027

content.text: Don't confuse §24 (temporary protection) and §25 Abs. 2 (refugee protection). The latter gives the right to a permanent residence permit (NE) after 3–5 years (§26 Abs. 3 AufenthG), whereas §24 leads to an extension (Verlängerung), not to NE. Many Ukrainians in 2024–2025 are switching to §25 Abs. 2 through refugee recognition by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF), or to §18a/c if they have a job.

steps.title: What a Ukrainian needs to check by 2027

content.text: By the time the naturalization application (Einbürgerungsantrag) is filed, all the conditions of §10 Abs. 1 StAG must be met (Nr. 4 has been removed from the list, so Nr. 1–3 and 5–7 apply). For Ukrainians with §24 it is important to check them in advance — some requirements take years of preparation.

items: 5 years of legal residence — yes, if you have had an AE under §24 since 2022
A valid residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel): §24 is accepted, but switching to §18 or §25 Abs. 2 is better
B1 — the integration course / language course (Sprachkurs) gets you to B1 in 12–18 months
Naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) 17/33 — 25€, prepare with the BAMF app
Means of subsistence (Lebensunterhalt) without basic income support at the time of the decision — critical!
Declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung) — no problem for most Ukrainians
Certificate of no criminal record from Ukraine — needed, with an apostille or through the embassy
Dual citizenship is allowed: Ukraine does not require renunciation (Art. 19 of the Law "On Citizenship")

content.text: The condition on means of subsistence (§10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StAG) is the hardest for Ukrainians. If you are receiving basic income support at the time the decision on your application is made, naturalization will usually be refused. The 2024 reform sharply narrowed the former "through no fault of your own" exception, so even unemployment in good faith now usually does not help. The strategy is to reach stable full-time employment in advance (several months without benefits before applying), or to check whether the narrow exception for full-time workers (Vollzeit) applies. For contentious cases, individual legal advice is recommended.
Over 2022–2026, many Ukrainians have found work, married German or EU citizens, or been recognized as refugees through BAMF. Each of these statuses has its own particularities for naturalization.

items: §28 AufenthG (marriage to a German citizen) → §9 StAG: 3 years of residence (Aufenthalt) + 2 years of marriage
§18 AufenthG (skilled worker) → standard §10 StAG, 5 years, B1
§25 Abs. 2 AufenthG (recognized as a refugee) → 5 years + NE after 3 years; naturalization under §10 StAG
EU Blue Card (Blue Card; §18g) → a fast track to NE (21–27 months), then 5 years to §10 StAG
University studies (Studium) → the time counts in full since the 2024 reform
Switching from §24 to §18 is possible if you find qualified work
Switching from §24 to §25 Abs. 2 requires an asylum application (Asylantrag) and recognition by BAMF — this reassesses your status

content.text: Important: there is NO longer fast-track naturalization after 3 years of residence. The former §10 Abs. 3 StAG (3 years with C1 and special integration achievements), introduced by the 2024 reform, was abolished by the sixth law amending the StAG, which came into force on 30 October 2025. Now the general 5-year period under §10 StAG applies to everyone; C1 level and volunteering can no longer speed up naturalization. Don't count on the three-year path — it doesn't exist.

steps.title: The Ukrainian side and dual citizenship

content.text: Under the law in force (the Law "On Citizenship of Ukraine" of 2001), Ukraine formally does not recognize dual citizenship, but in practice it does not take away a Ukrainian passport when a foreign citizenship is acquired. That is why many Ukrainians in the Federal Republic use both passports at the same time.

items: Law "On Citizenship of Ukraine", Art. 19 — grounds for loss of citizenship (not applied in practice)
Renunciation of Ukrainian citizenship by presidential decree — a voluntary procedure, not mandatory
A Ukrainian passport can be renewed at the Ukrainian consulates in the Federal Republic (Berlin, Munich, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Düsseldorf)
Ukraine's rules on military registration and mobilization for men change often and are not directly related to German citizenship
On questions of leaving/returning and military registration, check the current guidance of the Ukrainian consulate
Legalizing dual citizenship in Ukraine is being discussed at the level of draft laws; as of the publication date no single law has been adopted

content.text: After naturalizing in the Federal Republic, you can keep your Ukrainian citizenship — this is not a breach of German law (§10 StAG no longer requires renunciation). On the Ukrainian side the status legally remains, and in practice no consequences have been recorded. When entering Ukraine, use your Ukrainian passport.

costs.label: Naturalization fee
costs.note: §38 Abs. 2 StAG.

costs.label: Integrationskurs (B1) — for those granted §24
costs.note: Free under §44 Abs. 1 AufenthG for AE holders.

costs.label: Certificate of no criminal record from Ukraine
costs.note: Free through the "Diia" app, up to 50€ through a consulate in the Federal Republic.

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung from Ukrainian
costs.note: Finding a sworn translator for Ukrainian is harder than for Russian.

title: Naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest): 17 out of 33 — how to prepare
tldr: The naturalization test (Einbürgerungstest) is a mandatory test of knowledge about Germany required for naturalization under §10 (1) Nr. 7 StAG. It consists of 33 multiple-choice questions: 30 nationwide + 3 specific to your federal state (Bundesland). Time limit — 60 minutes. Passing score — 17 correct. The fee is 25€, and it is taken at centres accredited by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) (adult education centres — VHS, Volkshochschulen; private schools). The question pool — 310 general + 10 per state — is public and posted on bamf.de and einbuergerungstest-online.de. You can prepare for free with the official BAMF "Einbürgerungstest" app or by drilling the questions online. Most people pass on the first try with 10–20 hours of preparation. The certificate is valid indefinitely.

content.text: The naturalization test was introduced by §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 7 StAG and is governed by the naturalization test regulation (Einbürgerungstestverordnung, EinbTestV). The catalogue of 310 general questions plus 10 state questions for each of the 16 federal states is public and has not changed for years — the latest revision was 2019, with minimal edits after the 2024 reform.

items: 33 questions = 30 general (from 310) + 3 state questions (from the 10 for your federal state)
4 answer options, only 1 correct (Multiple Choice)
60 minutes for the whole test — plenty of time
Passing score: ≥17 out of 33 (≈52%)
If you fail — you can retake it an unlimited number of times, 25€ each time
The test is taken at accredited BAMF examination centres (Prüfstellen): VHS, IB, private schools
Topics: democracy (Demokratie), the rule of law (Rechtsstaat), history (Geschichte), federalism (Föderalismus), symbols (Symbole), rights/duties, basic geography

steps.title: How to prepare: apps and online

content.text: The question pool is public — which means preparation comes down to working through it. Most people with B1 and decent general knowledge pass on the first try after 10–20 hours of going through the pool.

items: The official "Einbürgerungstest" app from BAMF — iOS/Android, free, with an exam mode
einbuergerungstest-online.de — a free portal with a simple practice mode
The BAMF PDF with the full question catalogue — on bamf.de
The educational portal ZBE (Centre for Civic Engagement; Zentralstelle Bürgerschaftliches Engagement)
A preparation course at the VHS — usually 6–8 hours, ~50–80€
YouTube channels (Deutschstunde, Einbürgerung leicht gemacht) — in Russian and Ukrainian
A practice test with a timer and the real format — a must, one week before the exam

content.text: In the BAMF app and on bamf.de you can filter to show only the state questions for your federal state. This is handy — the 10 state questions take 15 minutes.
The questions seem easy, but 3 out of 33 hinge on details where it is easy to slip up. Especially: dates of historical events, exact numbers in the federal parliament (Bundestag), symbols.

items: Bundestag: the catalogue asks about the minimum number of seats — the answer is 598; under the 2023 electoral law reform (Wahlrechtsreform) the size of the Bundestag is capped at 630 seats starting with the 2025 election (on the test, stick to the wording of the BAMF catalogue)
The Federal Chancellor (Bundeskanzler) is elected by the Bundestag, while the Federal President (Bundespräsident) is elected by the Federal Convention (Bundesversammlung)
The term of office (Wahlperiode) of the Bundestag is 4 years, the Federal President is elected for 5 years, and the Federal Convention meets once every 5 years
Minimum age (Mindestalter): the right to vote and to stand in Bundestag elections — from age 18
Women's suffrage (Frauenwahlrecht) in Germany — 1918, not 1919
The BRD (Federal Republic of Germany) was founded on 23.05.1949 (Grundgesetz), the GDR on 07.10.1949
The fall of the Berlin Wall (Mauerfall) was on 09.11.1989, German reunification (Wiedervereinigung) on 03.10.1990
There are 16 federal states, of which 3 are city-states (Stadtstaaten: Berlin, Hamburg, Bremen)
Germany's EU membership — a founding member in 1957 (EEC, EWG), not 1992 (Maastricht)

content.text: The state questions (the last 3 of 33) often involve specific names of the state's premier (Ministerpräsident), coats of arms, and capitals. These are passive-recall questions — be sure to run through the 10 questions for your state at least 5 times.

steps.title: Who is exempt from the test

content.text: §10 Abs. 6 StAG provides an exemption from the naturalization test for certain categories — usually on medical grounds or for people with German schooling.

items: Minor children naturalized together with their parents (Miteinbürgerung) — exempt
People with a German school-leaving certificate (Schulabschluss: Hauptschule, Realschule, Abitur) — exempt
People with a physical, mental, or psychological illness — exempt with a medical certificate
Elderly people with age-related limitations (altersbedingten Einschränkungen) — assessed individually
An exemption does not waive B1: language is still checked separately
An exemption is requested in a separate application with supporting documents attached
Without an exemption — the test is mandatory, even for people with a German university degree

content.text: You register for the test via the examination centre's website (VHS, IB, BAMF partners). The waiting time is usually 2–6 weeks, in Berlin and Munich up to 3 months. Registration plus payment of 25€ online or on site.

items: Passport or residence permit card (Aufenthaltstitel) — without it you will not be admitted
Proof of the 25€ payment (if paid in advance)
A black or blue pen — pencil is not allowed
No phones, dictionaries, or cheat sheets — exclusion from the exam (Prüfungsausschluss)
The result — usually within 4–6 weeks by post (a certificate — Bescheinigung)
The certificate is an official document, attached to the naturalization application (Einbürgerungsantrag)
A duplicate certificate if lost — costs 25–50€

content.text: Arriving more than 15 minutes late = no admission and no refund of the fee. Come 20 minutes early and find the room. During the test you have 60 minutes — don't rush, read all 4 options carefully: there is usually one obviously correct answer, plus 1–2 that are close but wrong.

costs.label: Einbürgerungstest — fee
costs.note: Each attempt is 25€; a retake is another 25€.

costs.label: VHS preparation course
costs.note: 6–8 teaching hours, in a group.

costs.label: BAMF app and online portals
costs.note: Free; iOS/Android.

costs.label: Duplicate certificate
costs.note: Better to make copies right away — the Behörde accepts a Beglaubigung.

title: EHIC: the EU health insurance card
tldr: The EHIC (European Health Insurance Card, in German EHIC / Europäische Krankenversicherungskarte) is the reverse side of your German health insurance card (Gesundheitskarte). Any statutory health insurer (Krankenkasse) issues it FOR FREE, and it entitles you to medically necessary treatment in all EU/EEA countries, Switzerland and the UK at the rates and under the rules of the country you are in. The EHIC covers only that country's public system; it does not replace travel insurance and does not cover planned treatment or repatriation.

steps.title: What the EHIC is and where it works

content.text: The EHIC (Europäische Krankenversicherungskarte) is not a separate card but the printed reverse side of your electronic health insurance card (elektronische Gesundheitskarte, eGK). If you are insured with a German statutory insurer (GKV), you already have an EHIC — turn the card over and check that your details and the EHIC logo with the EU flag are printed there.

The EHIC entitles you to medically necessary treatment during a temporary stay (holiday, business trip, studies) on the same terms and at the same rates as people insured locally. The principle is benefits in kind (Sachleistungsprinzip): you receive care in the public facilities of the country you are in as if you were insured there.

items: Works: all 27 EU countries + Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway (EEA) + Switzerland
United Kingdom: since 2021 the GHIC applies instead of the EHIC, but the German EHIC is also accepted there
Coverage = the standard of the public system in the country you are in
In countries with co-payments (France, Spain) you pay the same share as locals
The EHIC is free and included in your GKV contribution — no separate payment needed
Privately insured people (PKV) are not issued an EHIC — they need separate foreign health insurance (Auslandskrankenversicherung)

steps.title: How to get and check your EHIC

content.text: The EHIC is printed automatically on every health insurance card a German insurer issues. If the card is old or damaged, or the EHIC side is blank, order a new card for free — it is your right as an insured person, and the insurer may not refuse or charge for it.

items: Turn over your health insurance card (Gesundheitskarte): the back should show your name, date of birth, card number and the insurer's code
The EHIC's validity matches the expiry date printed on the card
Order a new card through the insurer's app, the online account or by phone
Delivery of a new card usually takes 1–2 weeks by post
If you are travelling urgently and the card has not arrived, ask for a provisional replacement certificate (Provisorische Ersatzbescheinigung, PEB) as a PDF
The PEB works just like the EHIC and is issued by the insurer within a few days

content.text: Do not confuse the EHIC with travel insurance. The EHIC does NOT cover: repatriation (Rücktransport) to your home country when you are ill, planned treatment abroad, private clinics, or co-payments above the local standard. For a holiday you should still take out travel health insurance (Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung) — it costs 5–20 € a year and closes these gaps.

When you see a doctor or go to a hospital in an EU country, show your EHIC and passport. Ideally, go to a public facility (öffentliches Krankenhaus, or a doctor under contract with the local system). A private clinic may not accept the EHIC, and you will have to pay yourself.

items: Show the EHIC before treatment begins, not afterwards
Keep all receipts, prescriptions and invoices — you will need them for reimbursement
If you had to pay yourself, apply to your insurer for reimbursement after you return
In some countries the doctor charges you first and the insurer reimburses at local rates
Prescription medicines are bought at a local pharmacy and paid for under that country's rules
In an emergency, call 112 — the single ambulance number across the EU

content.text: The EHIC only applies during a temporary stay. If you move to another EU country permanently or for work, the EHIC is not enough — you have to re-register in that country's system. And remember: the EHIC is not for medical tourism — a trip taken specifically to get treatment abroad is not covered.

costs.label: Issuing the EHIC
costs.note: Free for everyone insured in the GKV; included in the normal contribution.

costs.label: New Gesundheitskarte with EHIC
costs.note: The insurer may not charge for replacing the card.

costs.label: Additional Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung (per year)
costs.note: Covers repatriation and private clinics; strongly recommended alongside the EHIC.

sources.title: krankenkassen.de — EHIC: Was leistet die Karte im Ausland

title: Family insurance (Familienversicherung): free cover for your family
tldr: Under §10 SGB V, a spouse and children can be insured FOR FREE as family members (Familienversicherung) with a statutory insurer (GKV) — at no separate contribution. The condition: their own income must not exceed the limit (2026 — 565 €/month in general; with a mini-job (Minijob) — up to 603 €/month from the side job). Children are covered up to 18, up to 23 if not working, and up to 25 if studying. The savings are huge: a family of four pays one contribution from the working parent instead of four. This exists only in the GKV — in private insurance (PKV) everyone pays for themselves.

steps.title: What Familienversicherung is under §10 SGB V

content.text: Familienversicherung is the mechanism under §10 SGB V whereby, in a statutory health insurer (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung, GKV), family members are insured together with the working policyholder at no separate contribution. One person pays their contribution, and the spouse and children get full insurance cover for free.

This is a unique feature of the German statutory system and one of the main reasons families choose the GKV. In private insurance (PKV) every family member, including every child, is insured separately and a contribution is paid for each one.

items: Covered: spouse, registered partner (Lebenspartner), children, sometimes grandchildren and stepchildren
A family member gets their own health insurance card (Gesundheitskarte) and the full range of GKV benefits
There is NO extra contribution for family members
The family member must have their habitual residence in Germany (gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt)
Works only if the main policyholder is themselves in the GKV, not the PKV
Legal basis — §10 Fünftes Buch Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB V)

content.text: The key condition for Familienversicherung is that the family member's own income must not exceed the set limit (Einkommensgrenze). For 2026 this is 565 €/month of ordinary income (one seventh of the monthly reference figure, Bezugsgröße). For a side job under the mini-employment scheme the limit equals the mini-job threshold (Minijob-Grenze) — for 2026 that is 603 €/month (tied to the minimum wage, Mindestlohn, of 13.90 €/hour).

items: Ordinary income limit 2026: 565 €/month (one seventh of the Bezugsgröße)
Limit for a mini-job 2026: 603 €/month (marginal employment threshold, Geringfügigkeitsgrenze)
If your spouse has a Minijob, Familienversicherung is kept
If income is even one euro above the limit, they need their own insurance
All regular income counts: salary, rent, interest, pension
Children usually have no income, so the limit is almost always met for them

content.text: The limits are tied to the Bezugsgröße and the Minijob-Grenze, which rise every year. For 2025 they were 535 € (ordinary) and 556 € (Minijob); for 2026 they are 565 € (ordinary) and 603 € (Minijob) — your insurer publishes the exact figure at the start of the year, so check the current value. If your spouse's income fluctuates around the threshold, always confirm with the insurer.

steps.title: Up to what age children are covered

content.text: For children, §10 SGB V sets out age tiers. The older the child, the more conditions apply for keeping the free insurance.

items: Up to 18 — always, with no further conditions
Up to 23 — if the child is not working (has no regular employment)
Up to 25 — if the child is studying (school, university, vocational training, Ausbildung)
No age limit — for children with a disability who cannot support themselves
The age-25 limit is extended for the duration of voluntary social service (Freiwilligendienst, FSJ/FÖJ) or military/civilian service
After finishing studies or turning 25, a student moves to their own student insurance

content.text: When a student child turns 25 or finishes their studies, Familienversicherung ends. Do not miss this moment: you need to arrange their own insurance in time (for students, the reduced student health insurance (studentische Krankenversicherung), ~120 €/month), otherwise a gap in cover and a contribution debt build up.

You apply for Familienversicherung through the main policyholder's insurer — there is no need to register separately with another insurer. The insurer checks that the conditions are met and issues a card for the family member.

items: Fill in the family insurance questionnaire (Fragebogen zur Familienversicherung; available in the online account or on request)
For a child: birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde)
For a spouse: marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) and income details
Proof of study (Immatrikulationsbescheinigung) for children aged 18–25
The insurer sends a separate health insurance card for each family member
Once a year the insurer may request up-to-date income data for a review

costs.label: Contribution for family members (Familienversicherung)
costs.note: Under §10 SGB V, spouse and children are insured for free provided the income limit is met.

costs.label: Family member income limit 2026 (ordinary)
costs.note: One seventh of the monthly Bezugsgröße (2026: 3 955 €/month); check the exact figure with your insurer at the start of the year.

costs.label: Limit with a Minijob 2026
costs.note: Equals the Geringfügigkeitsgrenze; tied to the Mindestlohn of 13.90 €/hour from 2026.

costs.label: Student insurance after losing Familienversicherung
costs.note: Reduced studentische KV; needed after age 25 or after finishing studies.

title: Statutory (GKV) vs private (PKV) health insurance: which to choose
tldr: Germany has two health insurance systems: statutory GKV (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) and private PKV (private Krankenversicherung). An employee can switch to the PKV only if their gross income exceeds the compulsory insurance threshold (Versicherungspflichtgrenze; 2026 — 77 400 €/year, or 6 450 €/month; in 2025 it was 73 800 €). The PKV offers faster appointments, a private room and better dental cover, but contributions rise with age and are paid separately for each family member. The MAIN trap: after age 55 it is almost impossible to return from the PKV to the GKV. For families and those planning to stay in Germany long-term, the GKV is usually the better deal.

content.text: The GKV (statutory insurer) works on the solidarity principle: the contribution is a percentage of income (14.6% + a supplementary contribution, Zusatzbeitrag), not of your health status. Everyone gets the same basic range of services, and family members are insured for free. The PKV (private insurance) calculates the contribution by individual risk — age, health status and the chosen tariff — and each person pays for themselves.

items: GKV: contribution = % of income, capped by the income ceiling for social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze)
GKV: family insurance (Familienversicherung) — spouse and children for free (§10 SGB V)
PKV: contribution depends on age and health at entry, not on income
PKV: every family member, including each child, pays a separate contribution
The GKV is open to everyone; the PKV only to certain groups
About 90% of residents in Germany are in the GKV, about 10% in the PKV

steps.title: Who can actually switch to the PKV

content.text: An employee must stay in the GKV (Versicherungspflicht) as long as their gross salary is below the compulsory insurance threshold (Versicherungspflichtgrenze, JAEG). Only once they exceed it does the employee gain the right to choose the PKV. The self-employed, freelancers, civil servants (Beamte) and students follow separate rules and can move to the PKV more freely.

items: Versicherungspflichtgrenze 2026: 77 400 €/year gross (6 450 €/month; in 2025 it was 73 800 €)
An employee must exceed this threshold to be able to choose the PKV
The self-employed and freelancers — can go into the PKV almost always
Civil servants (Beamte) — usually PKV + the state allowance Beihilfe (the state pays a share)
Students under 30 can choose the PKV, but it is then hard to return
The threshold rises every year; keep track of the current value

steps.title: Pros and cons of the PKV

content.text: The PKV appeals to young, healthy, well-paid singles: for them the contribution can be lower than in the GKV, and the service is noticeably better. But the picture changes with age and once a family arrives.

items: Plus: faster appointments with specialists (you are seen as a private patient, Privatpatient)
Plus: a private room in hospital, treatment by the head physician (Chefarztbehandlung)
Plus: better cover for dentistry, glasses and alternative medicine
Plus: for a young, healthy single the contribution can be lower than in the GKV
Minus: the contribution rises with age, and the PKV becomes expensive for older people
Minus: a separate contribution for each child and non-working spouse
Minus: with pre-existing conditions, surcharges apply or cover may be refused

steps.title: The PKV trap: a one-way street

content.text: The most important point when choosing the PKV is that it is almost a one-way ticket. The older you get, the harder it is to return to the statutory system. After age 55, returning from the PKV to the GKV is in practice closed off by law, with rare exceptions.

WARNING: returning from the PKV to the GKV after age 55 is practically impossible. Before 55 you can return only under certain conditions (for example, your income falls below the threshold and you become an employee). If you choose the PKV at 30, there is a high risk of staying in it for life — with contributions that in old age can reach 700–1000 €/month. Before leaving the GKV, calculate the long-term outlook three times over.

items: Before 55 you can return to the GKV only if your income falls below the threshold and you have employee status
After 55 a return to the GKV is practically blocked by law
In the PKV, age reserves (Altersrückstellungen) are built up that soften the rise in contributions, but not fully
If you change employer abroad or lose income, the PKV stays expensive
A family with children in the PKV often pays more than a single GKV contribution would have cost to cover everyone

content.text: The decision depends on your life situation, not just on today's contribution. Think 20–30 years ahead.

items: Planning a family and children — the GKV is usually the better deal (free Familienversicherung)
A young, healthy, high-earning single with no plans for children — the PKV may suit you
A Beamter with Beihilfe — the PKV is usually more logical
Not sure you will stay in Germany long-term — stay in the GKV
Before the PKV, consult an independent insurance adviser (Versicherungsberater; not an agent for one company)
Compare the contribution not for today, but projected to age 60–70

costs.note: Annual gross income (6 450 €/month); in 2025 it was 73 800 €, the threshold rises every year.

costs.note: Percentage of gross + Zusatzbeitrag; split 50/50 with the employer.

costs.note: Depends on age, tariff and health; can be higher in old age.

title: hkk: a cheap health insurer
tldr: All statutory insurers (GKV) provide the same basic set of services — this is fixed in SGB V. What differs between them is the supplementary contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) and their bonus programmes. hkk (Handelskrankenkasse) has for many years kept one of the lowest Zusatzbeitrag rates in Germany (historically around 0.98–1.5%, against a market average of 2.5–2.9%). Switching to hkk or another cheap insurer is free, done online, and needs no mandatory link to your employer — the contribution is deducted automatically. You can change insurer after 12 months of membership.

steps.title: Basic services are the same at every insurer

content.text: The key thing to understand about the GKV: about 95% of services (Leistungskatalog) are the same at every insurer, because they are fixed in SGB V and regulated by the state. The doctor, the hospital, medicines, operations — all the same everywhere. So there is usually no point in paying more for a more "well-known" insurer.

items: General contribution rate (allgemeiner Beitragssatz): 14.6% — the same for everyone
The difference lies only in each insurer's supplementary contribution
The basic catalogue of services is identical under SGB V
Only bonuses (Bonusprogramme), extra services and customer service differ
The contribution is split 50/50 between employee and employer
The lower the Zusatzbeitrag, the more stays in your pocket

content.text: hkk (Handelskrankenkasse), based in Bremen, is an insurer open to everyone that has for years kept one of the lowest Zusatzbeitrag rates in the country thanks to a lean structure. While the market-average Zusatzbeitrag is around 2.5–2.9%, hkk has historically held around 0.98–1.5%.

items: hkk is open to all residents of Germany, not only to retail workers
One of the lowest Zusatzbeitrag rates in Germany for many years
The full basic GKV catalogue of services, like any insurer
Has bonus programmes and top-ups for prevention
Online service and an app for electronic prescriptions (E-Rezept)
The savings on the contribution difference can come to hundreds of euros a year

content.text: The size of the Zusatzbeitrag is not fixed forever — insurers review it every year, and in 2025–2026 many raised it because of the system's deficit. Before switching, check the current Zusatzbeitrag of hkk and of several competitors on the insurers' websites or in the comparison at gesetzlichekrankenkassen.de. The cheapest insurer can change from year to year.

steps.title: How to switch to another insurer

content.text: Switching to another insurer is free, simple and done online. Since 2021 the minimum membership period has been cut to 12 months, and the switch itself has become almost automatic: the new insurer notifies the old one for you.

items: Look up the current Zusatzbeitrag of the insurers you want on their websites
Compare bonus programmes and extra services
Check whether the insurer has a convenient app and online service
Consider the service: some cheap insurers respond more slowly
Fill in the online application on the new insurer's website (Mitgliedsantrag)
The new insurer will notify the old one for you — you do not have to cancel yourself
The minimum membership period at your current insurer is 12 months
The notice period is 2 months to the end of the month
If the Zusatzbeitrag is raised, you have a right to early exit (Sonderkündigungsrecht)
You will receive a new health insurance card (Gesundheitskarte) by post

content.text: You do not have to notify your employer of the change of insurer by hand either — the new insurer passes on the data via electronic exchange, and the contribution is deducted automatically from your salary in favour of the new insurer from the day of the switch.

costs.note: The same at every insurer under SGB V; split 50/50 with the employer.
