title: Vaccinations: what is mandatory
tldr: Germany has no general mandatory vaccination for adults. Recommendations are issued by STIKO (Ständige Impfkommission at the Robert Koch Institute, RKI) — this is not law, but it is on the basis of STIKO that the public health funds (GKV) cover vaccinations for free. The only genuinely mandatory vaccination (Impfpflicht) is against measles (Masernschutzgesetz, in force since March 2020): it is mandatory for children in daycare (Kita) and school, as well as for medical and teaching staff. Vaccinations are given by your family doctor (Hausarzt) and recorded in a vaccination certificate (Impfpass, the yellow booklet).

content.text: In Germany vaccinations are mostly voluntary. The government body STIKO (Ständige Impfkommission) at the RKI (Robert Koch-Institut) publishes a calendar of recommended vaccinations (Impfkalender) every year. These recommendations are not law, but they determine which vaccinations the public health fund covers for free.

items: STIKO operates at the RKI (Robert Koch-Institut) — the federal public health institute
STIKO recommendations = the basis for free coverage of vaccinations by the GKV fund
For children: Tetanus, Diphtherie, Keuchhusten, Polio, Hib, Hepatitis B, Pneumokokken, Rotaviren, Masern-Mumps-Röteln (MMR), Windpocken
For adults: refresh Tetanus/Diphtherie every 10 years, plus flu, COVID, FSME (tick-borne) and Pneumokokken (60+) where indicated
For pregnant women STIKO recommends Keuchhusten (Pertussis) and flu
Vaccinations are recorded in the Impfpass — the yellow international booklet

content.text: The only truly mandatory vaccination in Germany is against measles (Masern). The Masernschutzgesetz has been in force since March 2020 and requires proof of immunity against measles for certain groups. For all other diseases there is no Impfpflicht in Germany.

items: The Masernschutzgesetz has been in force since 1 March 2020
Mandatory for children on admission to a Kita and school
Mandatory for staff of Kitas, schools, medical facilities and care homes
Proof is two MMR vaccinations or confirmed immunity (Titer)
Without proof a child may be refused admission to a Kita; staff may be banned from working
Fines of up to 2500 € are possible for non-compliance

content.text: If you are bringing a child to Germany for daycare or school, check the Impfpass in advance for two measles vaccinations (Masern or MMR). Without proof of immunity the public health office (Gesundheitsamt) may refuse admission to the facility. Vaccinations given in Russia/CIS are usually accepted — bring the original certificate, with a translation if needed.

steps.title: Where and how to get vaccinated

content.text: In Germany vaccinations are given first and foremost by your family doctor (Hausarzt), and for children by a paediatrician (Kinderarzt). For people insured under the GKV, the vaccinations recommended by STIKO are free.

items: Book an appointment with your family doctor or paediatrician for a vaccination (Impftermin)
Bring your Impfpass (yellow booklet) — the doctor will record the vaccination in it
If you have no Impfpass, the doctor will start a new one or issue a certificate
Vaccinations under STIKO are fully covered by the fund (GKV)
Flu and some other vaccinations are now also given in pharmacies (under new rules)
Travel vaccinations (yellow fever, hepatitis A) are often paid for privately — ask your fund

content.text: If you bring a vaccination certificate from another country, have the doctor translate or check it — they will transfer the data into the German Impfpass and prescribe any missing doses if needed. Keep the originals of all vaccination documents.

costs.label: Vaccinations recommended by STIKO (GKV)
costs.note: Fully covered by the public health fund; including the children's calendar.

costs.label: Travel vaccinations (not STIKO)
costs.note: Often paid; some funds reimburse part — check with them.

costs.label: Fine for violating the Masernschutzgesetz
costs.note: For lacking the required proof of immunity against measles.

title: Sick pay (Krankengeld): 70% of gross
tldr: If you are ill for longer than 6 weeks, the public health fund (GKV) pays a cash sickness benefit (Krankengeld) under §44 SGB V. For the first 6 weeks of illness your employer pays 100% of your salary (Entgeltfortzahlung). From day 43 the fund steps in: Krankengeld = 70% of gross, but no more than 90% of net. It is paid for a maximum of 78 weeks within 3 years for one and the same illness. Pension and unemployment contributions are deducted from Krankengeld, so the net amount you receive is less than 70%. You need continuous sick notes (AU-Bescheinigung) with no gaps.

content.text: Sick pay in Germany comes in two phases. For the first 6 weeks (42 days) of one and the same illness your employer keeps paying your full salary — this is Entgeltfortzahlung (Lohnfortzahlung) under the Entgeltfortzahlungsgesetz. From day 43 of illness the health fund takes over and pays Krankengeld under §44 SGB V.

items: Days 1–42 (6 weeks): the employer pays 100% of salary (Entgeltfortzahlung)
From day 43: the fund pays Krankengeld
Entitlement to Entgeltfortzahlung — after 4 weeks of work with the employer
The 6 weeks are counted afresh for each new illness
If you fall ill again with the same diagnosis, the periods may be added together
The legal basis for Krankengeld is §44 SGB V

steps.title: How much is paid: 70% of gross, capped at 90% of net

content.text: Under §47 SGB V Krankengeld is 70% of your gross income (Regelentgelt), but it cannot exceed 90% of your net income. In practice the amount falls somewhere between these two limits. Contributions to pension, unemployment and long-term care insurance are also deducted from Krankengeld, so the net amount you receive is lower still.

items: Basic formula: 70% of gross (Regelentgelt)
Ceiling: no more than 90% of net
Gross is counted up to the contribution ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze), so there is also an absolute cap — in 2026 around 135,63 € per day
Contributions to pension, unemployment and long-term care insurance (Renten-, Arbeitslosen- und Pflegeversicherung) are deducted from Krankengeld
Krankengeld itself is not subject to income tax, but it affects your tax rate (Progressionsvorbehalt)
The net amount you receive is less than the calculated figure — after contributions are deducted it is usually around 75–80% of your normal net pay

content.text: Krankengeld is not the same as your normal salary. After contributions are deducted, the net amount you receive is noticeably less than your previous net pay. On top of that, because of the Progressionsvorbehalt the benefit raises the tax rate on the rest of your annual income — this can lead to a tax back-payment in your annual return. Build up a financial cushion in case of a long illness.

steps.title: Duration: up to 78 weeks in 3 years

content.text: Under §48 SGB V, Krankengeld for one and the same illness is paid for a maximum of 78 weeks within three years. An important detail: the first 6 weeks of Entgeltfortzahlung count towards this 78-week period, so the pure Krankengeld from the fund works out to about 72 weeks.

items: Maximum of 78 weeks for one illness within 3 years (Blockfrist)
The 6 weeks of Entgeltfortzahlung count towards these 78 weeks
After Krankengeld is exhausted — a move to rehabilitation (Reha) or a reduced-earning-capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente)
For a new, unrelated illness the period starts again
The fund will warn you in advance as the end of the period approaches (Aussteuerung)

steps.title: How not to lose the payments

content.text: Krankengeld is paid only while your incapacity for work is confirmed. The main rule is that your sick note (Arbeitsunfähigkeitsbescheinigung, AU) must be continuous, without a single day's gap, otherwise your entitlement to payment can be interrupted.

items: Get a new AU from your doctor BEFORE the previous one ends, not after
Not a single day's gap between sick notes
These days the AU is transmitted by the doctor to the fund electronically (eAU), but check that it arrived
Report any changes to the fund and respond to its letters
The fund may refer you for review by the funds' medical service (Medizinischer Dienst, MD)
Cooperate on questions about rehabilitation — otherwise the payment may be suspended

content.text: A single day's gap between sick notes can cost you your Krankengeld. If the previous AU ends on a Friday, the new one must be issued no later than that same day or the next working day, depending on the fund's rules. Do not put off your visit to the doctor until the current sick note has expired.

costs.label: Krankengeld (share of gross)
costs.note: Percentage of gross (Regelentgelt) under §47 SGB V; capped at 90% of net.

costs.label: Employer's Entgeltfortzahlung (first 6 weeks)
costs.note: Percentage of full salary; paid by the employer, not the fund.

costs.label: Maximum duration of Krankengeld
costs.note: Weeks within 3 years for one illness (including the 6 weeks of Entgeltfortzahlung).

title: Additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) 2026: comparing health funds
tldr: The general GKV contribution rate (allgemeiner Beitragssatz) is 14.6% across all health funds. On top of that, each fund charges its own additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag). For 2026 the average (durchschnittlicher) Zusatzbeitrag is around 2.9%, with the spread between funds running roughly from 1.5% to 4.5%. That means: for the same set of benefits you can overpay or save hundreds of euros a year simply through your choice of fund. When a fund raises its Zusatzbeitrag, you gain the right to switch to another fund early (Sonderkündigungsrecht).

steps.title: How the GKV contribution is structured

content.text: The contribution to a statutory health fund has two parts. The first is the general rate (allgemeiner Beitragssatz) of 14.6% of gross income, the same for all funds by law. The second is the fund-specific additional contribution (kassenindividueller Zusatzbeitrag), which each fund sets itself. Both parts are split 50/50 between employee and employer.

items: Allgemeiner Beitragssatz: 14.6% — fixed by law for everyone
Zusatzbeitrag: individual to each fund
Full contribution = 14.6% + Zusatzbeitrag, of gross income
The contribution is split evenly: the employee pays half, the employer half
Calculated up to the income ceiling for contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze)
Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) is a separate contribution on top and is not included in these figures

content.text: For 2026 the average (durchschnittlicher) Zusatzbeitrag that the Federal Ministry of Health publishes as a benchmark is around 2.9%. But that is only an average: actual funds differ. Cheap ones stay around 1.5%, expensive ones reach 4.5% and above. Against the backdrop of the healthcare system's deficit in 2025–2026, many funds raised their Zusatzbeitrag.

items: Durchschnittlicher Zusatzbeitrag 2026: around 2.9% (Ministry of Health benchmark)
Spread across funds: roughly 1.5% – 4.5%
Cheap funds (for example hkk): historically at the lower end
Expensive large funds: closer to the upper end
A 2 percentage point difference on an income of 50 000 €/year is about 1000 €/year in total contribution (roughly 500 € as your share)
Funds publish their exact rates at the start of the year

content.text: The durchschnittlicher Zusatzbeitrag is only an averaged benchmark from the Ministry of Health, not your fund's actual rate. Your fund may charge noticeably more. Always check the kassenindividueller Zusatzbeitrag of your specific fund in its documents or member portal, not just the average figure from the news.

Since the basic set of benefits is identical, comparing funds comes down to price (Zusatzbeitrag) plus a few softer factors: bonus programmes, extra services, quality of service, and whether there is a convenient app.

items: Compare the current Zusatzbeitrag of several funds (fund websites, gesetzlichekrankenkassen.de)
Assess the bonus programmes (Bonusprogramm) — cashback for sport and prevention
Extra services beyond the mandatory ones: professional dental cleaning, osteopathy, travel vaccinations
Quality of service and availability by phone and online
Whether there is an app with electronic prescriptions (E-Rezept) and electronic sick notes (eAU)
Don't chase the lowest rate alone if the service is poor

content.text: If your fund raises its Zusatzbeitrag, you gain a special right to switch early — the Sonderkündigungsrecht. It applies even if you have not yet completed the minimum 12 months of membership.

items: When raising the Zusatzbeitrag, the fund is obliged to notify you
A Sonderkündigungsrecht arises — you can leave regardless of the 12-month term
You must apply to the new fund by the end of the month of the increase (per the rules)
The new fund notifies the old one for you — no need to cancel manually
Without an increase: a normal switch is possible after 12 months of membership, with a 2-month notice period
The contribution is automatically deducted by the employer in favour of the new fund

content.text: Don't ignore letters from your fund about a Zusatzbeitrag increase — they are exactly what opens the window for an early switch. The Sonderkündigungsrecht is time-limited, and if you delay you'll have to wait the usual 12 months. Once a year, check whether a fund has appeared with a noticeably lower contribution at the same level of service.

title: Registering with ELSTER
tldr: ELSTER (ELektronische STeuerERklärung) is the free official portal of the tax office (Finanzamt) for filing tax returns online. Since 2025 almost all mandatory returns (Einkommensteuer, Umsatzsteuer, Gewerbesteuer) can only be filed electronically. Registration at elster.de is free, but not quick: after you fill in the form, part of the data arrives by post (an Aktivierungs-ID by email, an Aktivierungs-Code by ordinary letter after ~14 days), and only then is access set up. Identification is via your tax identification number (Steuer-ID; 11 digits from a letter sent by the tax authority BZSt) or via your electronic ID card (Personalausweis) or electronic residence permit (eAT) with the eID function. At the end you get a "Mein ELSTER" account and a certificate for logging in. Without ELSTER you cannot file a return yourself and will depend on a tax advisor (Steuerberater; from 200 €).

steps.title: What ELSTER is and why you need it

content.text: ELSTER is Germany's electronic tax administration system, originally developed by the Bavarian tax authority and used throughout the country. The Mein ELSTER portal (elster.de) fully replaces paper forms: you use it to file your income tax return (Einkommensteuererklärung), the advance VAT return (Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung), applications for a tax class (Steuerklasse), for child allowances and dozens of other forms.

Since 2025, electronic filing through ELSTER has been mandatory for entrepreneurs, freelancers (Freiberufler) and business owners (Gewerbe) — the tax office no longer accepts paper for most forms. Employees often do not have to file a return at all, but through ELSTER it is free, whereas commercial services such as WISO or Taxfix charge 30-40 € a year.

items: Cost of registration and filing: 0 € (completely free)
Who is required to use it: the self-employed, members of the liberal professions, entrepreneurs and landlords (Selbständige, Freiberufler, Gewerbetreibende, Vermieter)
Who benefits: anyone who wants to recover an overpayment (on average ~1 095 € refunded per year)
What you need to start: a Steuer-ID (11 digits) OR a Personalausweis with eID
Time to activation: ~10-14 days (the letter with the Aktivierungs-Code comes by post)
Interface language: German only (there is officially no English)

content.text: ELSTER exists only in German. If your German is weak, keep DeepL or your browser's page translation handy, but do NOT machine-translate the forms themselves when submitting — a translator may distort numbers. It is better to learn many of the terms (Bescheid, Vorauszahlung, Festsetzung) in advance.

The main obstacle for newcomers is having a tax identification number (Steuer-Identifikationsnummer, Steuer-ID, IdNr). This is an 11-digit number that the BZSt (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern) sends by post automatically within 2-3 weeks after your first residence registration (Anmeldung). Without it, registration via the standard route is impossible.

items: Steuer-ID (11 digits) — from the BZSt letter after registration, or on your first payslip (Lohnabrechnung) from your employer
A working email address (the Aktivierungs-ID will be sent to it)
A current postal address in Germany (the Aktivierungs-Code will be sent to it)
Date of birth and full name as in your registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung)
For the eID route: an EU Personalausweis or an electronic residence permit (eAT) with the eID function activated + PIN + a smartphone with NFC and the AusweisApp

content.text: If your Steuer-ID has been lost or has not arrived yet, request it again for free at bzst.de (the "Mitteilung der IdNr" form) — it will arrive by post within 2-4 weeks at your registered address. Do not confuse the Steuer-ID (permanent, 11 digits) with the tax number (Steuernummer; issued by the local tax office, in a format like 12/345/67890, and changing when you move).
Registration happens in two stages, with a mandatory pause for postal delivery. Allow roughly 2 weeks from the start to your first login on the finished account.

items: Step 1: at elster.de click "Benutzerkonto erstellen" and choose the login "Für mich (z.B. Privatperson)"
Step 2: choose the login method — the recommended "Zertifikatsdatei" (certificate file) for most people
Step 3: select identification via Steuer-ID (the "Steuer-Identifikationsnummer" option) and enter the 11 digits
Step 4: enter your email, name and date of birth, and confirm your email via the link
Step 5: the Aktivierungs-ID arrives by email immediately, and the Aktivierungs-Code by ordinary letter (wait ~10-14 days)
Step 6: once the letter arrives, return to elster.de and enter both codes together
Step 7: the system generates and downloads a certificate file (.pfx) — save it and set a password
Step 8: log in to Mein ELSTER by uploading the .pfx file and entering the password

content.text: An alternative quick route is via the eID Personalausweis or electronic residence permit (eAT). Then no postal letter is needed: at the login-selection step you choose "Personalausweis", hold the card to your smartphone via the AusweisApp, enter the 6-digit eID-PIN, and the account is activated the same day. The downside is that for many eATs the eID function is not activated, or the PIN has been lost.

steps.title: First login and storing your access

content.text: After activation you land in your personal Mein ELSTER account. Here you have access to all forms (Formulare), the pre-fill feature "Belegabruf" (the tax office pulls in your data on salary, insurance and pension for you) and an archive of submitted returns.

items: Make a backup of the certificate file (.pfx) to the cloud and a USB stick
Write the certificate password down in a password manager — it cannot be recovered
Enable "Belegabruf" (Bescheinigungen abrufen) — it saves hours of manual entry
The certificate is valid for 3 years; ELSTER reminds you about renewal in advance
One account = one person; for spouses, create two accounts or file jointly through one

content.text: If you lose both the certificate file and its password, access cannot be recovered — you will have to register again and wait for the letter all over again. That is why many people prefer to log in via the eID Personalausweis or the ELSTERSecure app, where the device binding is easier to restore.

costs.label: Registering and using ELSTER
costs.note: The portal and the filing of all returns are completely free.

costs.label: Re-requesting the Steuer-ID from the BZSt
costs.note: Free via bzst.de, arrives by post within 2-4 weeks.

costs.label: Alternative: commercial software (WISO, Taxfix)
costs.note: Paid by those who want a Russian/English interface with prompts. ELSTER does the same thing for free.

title: ELSTER: zertifikatsdatei vs PIN
tldr: When registering with ELSTER you have to choose a login method (Login-Verfahren), and it determines how convenient and secure your filing will be for years. There are four main options: (1) a certificate file (Zertifikatsdatei) — a free .pfx with a password, the most common one, but the file is easy to lose; (2) ELSTERSecure — an app on your smartphone, bound to the device, convenient and file-free; (3) Sicherheitsstick / Signaturkarte — a hardware USB token or smart card (from ~50 €), for those who file often; (4) an electronic ID card (Personalausweis, eID) or residence permit (eAT) — login via your electronic passport with NFC and a PIN, with nothing to lose. All methods are free except the hardware stick. The certificate file is valid for 3 years, after which renewal is one click. The main risk with the file: lose the .pfx and password and it cannot be recovered.

content.text: ELSTER does not use an ordinary "login + password". Instead, each login is confirmed with a cryptographic certificate. You choose how this certificate is stored once, during registration (you can change it later, but it is a hassle). Understanding the differences up front will save you headaches.

items: Zertifikatsdatei — a .pfx file on your device + a password (free, the default)
ELSTERSecure — an app on your smartphone, like a bank's 2FA (free)
Sicherheitsstick — a USB token holding the certificate (hardware, ~50-70 € one-off)
Signaturkarte — a smart card with a reader (for business, more expensive)
Personalausweis / eAT (eID) — login via your electronic passport with NFC + PIN (free)

content.text: The certificate file (Zertifikatsdatei) is the default choice for ~80% of private users. On activation ELSTER generates a file with the .pfx extension; you download it and set a password. For each login you upload this file and enter the password — like a key to your house.

items: Pro: completely free, nothing to buy
Pro: works on any device you have copied the file to
Pro: does not depend on a phone or on NFC being available
Con: the file is easy to lose when reinstalling the system or if the disk fails
Con: the password CANNOT be recovered — forget the password and the account is lost
Con: store the file carelessly and an outsider could use it

content.text: Right after downloading the .pfx, make at least two copies (cloud + USB stick) and write the password down in a password manager. This is the most common failure for beginners: the return is due in April, but the file stayed on the old laptop, which has already been handed back or has broken.

steps.title: ELSTERSecure and eID: login without a file

content.text: If you do not want to deal with a file, there are two essentially "passwordless" routes. ELSTERSecure is the official ELSTER app for iOS/Android: the certificate is stored securely on the phone itself, and login is confirmed with your fingerprint or Face ID, just like in a banking app. Personalausweis/eAT (eID) is login by holding your electronic passport or residence permit to a smartphone with NFC and entering the 6-digit eID-PIN via the AusweisApp.

items: ELSTERSecure: free, bound to your smartphone, recovery via the ELSTER server is easier than with a file
ELSTERSecure: when changing phones you have to transfer/reactivate the certificate
eID Personalausweis: nothing gets lost, but you need the PIN (often forgotten) and an NFC smartphone
eID eAT (electronic residence permit for non-EU citizens): the eID function must be activated — check at the foreigners' office (ABH)
The eID-PIN can be reset for free at your district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) if it is lost

content.text: For many holders of an electronic residence permit (eAT, elektronischer Aufenthaltstitel) the eID function was deactivated on issue, or the PIN stayed in the sealed PIN letter (PIN-Brief) that was then lost. You can activate or reset the eID-PIN for free at the foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde) or your district citizens' office — without this, login via eID will not work.

steps.title: What to choose in your case

items: File 1 return a year, don't like phones → Zertifikatsdatei (but make a backup!)
Want maximum convenience, everything on your smartphone → ELSTERSecure
Already activated eID on your Personalausweis/eAT → login via eID, the most "loss-proof" option
Freelancer/business, filing VAT (Umsatzsteuer) monthly → Sicherheitsstick (more reliable for frequent work)
Don't trust storing a file at all → ELSTERSecure or eID

content.text: You can change the login method later: in Mein ELSTER → "Mein Benutzerkonto" → "Login-Verfahren wechseln". For example, you start with a file, then activate eID and switch to it. The old certificate is deactivated in the process.

The hardware Sicherheitsstick and Signaturkarte are the only paid options (the stick is ~50-70 € one-off, plus compatibility with specific models). A private individual almost never needs them: the free file/ELSTERSecure/eID options are enough.

costs.label: Zertifikatsdatei (certificate file)
costs.note: Free. Valid for 3 years, renewal in one click.

costs.label: ELSTERSecure (app)
costs.note: Free for iOS/Android.

costs.label: Login via Personalausweis / eAT (eID)
costs.note: Free. Requires an NFC smartphone and an activated eID-PIN.

costs.label: Sicherheitsstick (hardware token)
costs.note: A one-off purchase of a compatible USB token. Needed only for frequent filing (business).

costs.label: Resetting the eID-PIN at the Bürgeramt/ABH
costs.note: Free, if the PIN is lost and you need to activate eID.

title: Property purchase tax (Grunderwerbsteuer): 3.5-6.5%
tldr: The real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer, GrEStG) is a one-off tax on the purchase of property and land in Germany, paid by the buyer once at the transaction. Each federal state sets its own rate, so it varies from 3,5% (only Bayern) to 6,5% (NRW, Brandenburg, Schleswig-Holstein, Saarland). On an apartment costing 400 000 € in NRW that is 26 000 €, while in Bayern it is only 14 000 €: a difference of 12 000 € purely because of the state. The tax is calculated on the purchase price (Kaufpreis), and without it the notary will not transfer ownership: the tax office (Finanzamt) issues a clearance certificate (Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung) only after payment. Movable property (kitchen, furniture) can be listed separately in the contract to reduce the base. The tax is part of the incidental purchase costs (Kaufnebenkosten; ~10-15% on top of the price, together with the notary and the land register, Grundbuch).

steps.title: What this tax is and who pays it

content.text: The real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) is governed by the Grunderwerbsteuergesetz (GrEStG). It is charged on the purchase of land, a house or an apartment (and also of shares in companies that own property). It is paid by the buyer, once, after the notarial completion of the transaction. Do not confuse it with the annual property tax (Grundsteuer, a tax on ownership) — Grunderwerbsteuer is paid once, on the transfer of title.

The tax base is the purchase price (Kaufpreis) stated in the notarial contract (§8, §9 GrEStG). Since 2006 each state sets the rate (Steuersatz) itself, so an identical apartment is taxed differently depending on the federal state (Bundesland). The minimum base below which no tax is charged (Freigrenze) is 2 500 €.

items: Who pays: the buyer (Käufer)
When: once, after the notarial transaction (Beurkundung)
Base: the purchase price per the notarial contract
Freigrenze: transactions up to 2 500 € are not taxed
Without payment the tax office will not issue the clearance certificate (Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung) → no entry in the land register (Grundbuch)

content.text: The Grunderwerbsteuer rates current for 2026. Note: Thüringen lowered its rate from 6,5% to 5,0% on 1 January 2024, Sachsen raised its rate from 3,5% to 5,5% on 01.01.2023, and Bremen raised it from 5,0% to 5,5% on 01.07.2025 — so it is worth re-checking before a transaction.

items: Bayern — 3,5% (the lowest in the country)
Sachsen — 5,5% (raised from 3,5% on 01.01.2023)
Baden-Württemberg — 5,0%
Rheinland-Pfalz — 5,0%
Bremen — 5,5% (raised from 5,0% on 01.07.2025)
Niedersachsen — 5,0%
Sachsen-Anhalt — 5,0%
Thüringen — 5,0% (lowered from 6,5% on 01.01.2024)
Hamburg — 5,5%
Hessen — 6,0%
Berlin — 6,0%
Mecklenburg-Vorpommern — 6,0%
Nordrhein-Westfalen (NRW) — 6,5% (maximum)
Brandenburg — 6,5%
Schleswig-Holstein — 6,5%
Saarland — 6,5%

content.text: The rate is determined by where the property is located, not by where you are registered. If you live in Bayern (3,5%) but buy an apartment in Berlin (6,0%), you pay the Berlin rate. States change their rates from time to time for budgetary reasons, so before a transaction check the current value with your notary.
The calculation is straightforward: purchase price × the state's rate. But on large sums the difference between states is enormous.

items: Difference purely because of the state: 12 000 €

content.text: A trick for reducing the base: movable property is not subject to Grunderwerbsteuer. If the seller leaves a fitted kitchen, a sauna, a garden shed or furniture, list these separately in the contract (bewegliches Inventar). For example, a kitchen worth 15 000 € in NRW reduces the tax by 15 000 × 0,065 ≈ 975 €. The amount of inventory must be realistic (the tax office usually accepts up to ~15% of the price without issue), otherwise it may query it.

You do not need to calculate anything yourself. After certifying the contract, the notary (Notar) automatically notifies the tax office. The tax office then sends you a tax assessment (Grunderwerbsteuerbescheid) with the amount and a deadline (usually 1 month to pay).

items: Step 1: the notary certifies the purchase contract (Kaufvertrag) and notifies the tax office (sale notification, Veräußerungsanzeige)
Step 2: the tax office sends a tax assessment (Grunderwerbsteuerbescheid, the bill) to your address
Step 3: payment within ~1 month to the tax office's account
Step 4: the tax office issues a clearance certificate (Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung)
Step 5: with this certificate the notary submits the entry recording you in the land register (Grundbuch)
Only after the land-register entry do you become the legal owner

content.text: Grunderwerbsteuer is part of the incidental costs (Kaufnebenkosten), which together come to ~10-15% on top of the price: Grunderwerbsteuer 3,5-6,5% + notary ~1,5% + land register ~0,5% + (if applicable) an agent up to 3,57%. Banks usually do NOT finance these incidental costs (Nebenkosten) — this money has to be paid in cash (your own capital, Eigenkapital). For a purchase of 400 000 € in NRW, keep ~50-60 thousand € of your own funds just for the costs.

costs.label: Grunderwerbsteuer (minimum, only Bayern 3,5%)
costs.note: Example: 3,5% of 250 000-400 000 €. The 3,5% rate applies only in Bayern; paid once.

costs.label: Grunderwerbsteuer (maximum, NRW/Brandenburg/SH/Saarland 6,5%)
costs.note: Example: 6,5% of 250 000-400 000 €. The highest rate.

costs.label: Notary (Notarkosten)
costs.note: About 1,5% of the price, on the fixed GNotKG scale.

costs.label: Entry in the Grundbuch (Grundbucheintrag)
costs.note: About 0,5% of the price, mandatory for the transfer of ownership.

title: Property tax (Grundsteuer) 2025: the new reform
tldr: Property tax (Grundsteuer) is an annual tax on owning real estate, paid by all owners of land and houses (and, through operating costs / Nebenkosten, effectively by tenants too). A reform took effect on 1 January 2025: the old assessed values (Einheitswerte) from 1935/1964 were ruled unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court, and the tax has been recalculated under new rules. Most states apply the federal model (Bundesmodell, value-based), but 5 states introduced their own: Bayern uses a pure area-based Flächenmodell, Baden-Württemberg uses a Bodenwertmodell (land value only), and Hamburg, Hessen and Niedersachsen use area-based models with adjustments. Owners filed a revaluation return (Grundsteuererklärung) in 2022–2023, and the first new bills arrived in early 2025. The final amount = Grundsteuerwert × Steuermesszahl × the municipality's Hebesatz. For some the tax went up, for others down — it depends on the municipality.

content.text: Property tax (Grundsteuer) is governed by the Grundsteuergesetz (GrStG) and is paid annually by property owners to the municipality (Gemeinde). Before 2025 the tax base was calculated using assessed values (Einheitswerte) frozen as far back as 1935 (East) and 1964 (West). In 2018 the Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) ruled this unconstitutional: identical neighbouring houses were paying different amounts because of outdated valuations.

The court ordered the system to be reformed by 2025. That is why, in 2022–2023, all ~36 million owners had to file a revaluation return (Grundsteuererklärung) through the tax authority's ELSTER portal. Based on this data the tax office (Finanzamt) recalculated the base, and new bills have applied since 1 January 2025.

items: Who pays: the owner of the land/house/apartment
Paid to: the municipality (Gemeinde/Stadt), not the tax office directly
How often: annually (usually 4 payments a year)
Tenants: indirectly, via operating costs (Betriebskosten/Nebenkosten)
Old base: assessed values (Einheitswerte) from 1935/1964 — abolished as of 2025

content.text: The reform gave states the right to deviate from the federal model (Öffnungsklausel). As a result, different approaches now coexist. The majority (11 states) apply the federal model (Bundesmodell) — the value takes into account the cadastral land price, building type, area, year of construction and the local rent level (Mietniveaustufe). Five states introduced their own models.

items: Bundesmodell (value-based) — Berlin, Brandenburg, Bremen, MV, NRW, RLP, Saarland, Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt, SH, Thüringen
Bayern — area-based model (Flächenmodell): only land and building area, value is not considered (favourable for expensive areas)
Baden-Württemberg — land value model (Bodenwertmodell): only land value × area, the building itself is not considered
Hamburg — location-based model (Wohnlagenmodell): area + an adjustment for a "good/normal" location
Niedersachsen — area-location model (Flächen-Lage-Modell): area + a location factor
Hessen — area-factor method (Flächen-Faktor-Verfahren): area + a location factor

content.text: In value-based models (Bundesmodell, BW Bodenwert) the tax depends on the market price of the land — in expensive cities it rose more sharply. In purely area-based models (Bayern) two apartments of the same size pay the same, even if one is in central Munich and the other in a village. That is why the "fairness" of the reform is still being challenged in the courts.

steps.title: How the final amount is calculated

content.text: The formula is the same for all models; only the way the base value (Grundsteuerwert) is derived differs. Amount = Grundsteuerwert × Steuermesszahl × Hebesatz.

items: 1) Base value (Grundsteuerwert) — calculated by the tax office from your return (delivered in the Grundsteuerwertbescheid notice)
2) Tax base rate (Steuermesszahl) — a fixed factor (for residential property in the Bundesmodell ~0.031%, a reduced rate)
3) Base tax amount (Steuermessbetrag) = Grundsteuerwert × Steuermesszahl (delivered in the Grundsteuermessbescheid notice)
4) Municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) — a percentage set by the municipality ITSELF (from ~80% to 900%+)
5) Final figure = Steuermessbetrag × Hebesatz — in the Grundsteuerbescheid notice from the municipality

content.text: Simplified example: the base value (Grundsteuerwert) of an apartment = 200 000 €. Tax base rate (Steuermesszahl) 0,031% → base tax amount = 200 000 × 0,00031 = 62 €. Municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) 470% → annual tax = 62 × 4,7 = 291,40 €. In a city with a 900% multiplier the same apartment would cost 62 × 9 = 558 €. The Hebesatz is the main lever: the same apartment in neighbouring municipalities pays a different tax.

Many municipalities raised the multiplier (Hebesatz) in 2025 to keep the reform "aufkommensneutral" (revenue-neutral overall), but for an individual owner this meant either an increase or a decrease. If your bill jumped sharply, check the base value notice (Grundsteuerwertbescheid) for errors (area, year of construction) and file an objection (Einspruch) within 1 month.

steps.title: What an owner should do now

items: Make sure you filed the revaluation return (Grundsteuererklärung) — the deadline was in 2022–2023; if you did not, the tax office will assess you by estimate (Schätzung), usually to your disadvantage
Check the figures in the base value notice (Grundsteuerwertbescheid): plot area, living area, year of construction, building type
Received the 2025 tax notice (Grundsteuerbescheid) from the municipality — check the multiplier (Hebesatz) and the total
If there is an error, file an objection (Einspruch) within 1 month of the date of the notice (Bescheid), free of charge
New owners: when you buy after 2025, the transfer is handled automatically through the notary
The tax is usually split into 4 quarterly payments (15.02, 15.05, 15.08, 15.11)

content.text: Numerous test cases (Musterklagen) against the Bundesmodell have been filed across the country — especially by Haus & Grund and the Bund der Steuerzahler. If you think your assessment is too high, it can make sense to file an objection (Einspruch) referring to these proceedings (suspension of the case, Ruhen des Verfahrens) so as to preserve your right to a recalculation if the courts find the model unconstitutional.

costs.label: Grundsteuer for an apartment (typical range/year)
costs.note: Depends heavily on the municipality's Hebesatz and the land value. After the 2025 reform it went up for some and down for others.

costs.label: Grundsteuer for a house with a plot (typical range/year)
costs.note: Depends on the state model, the plot area and the Hebesatz.

costs.label: Filing the Grundsteuererklärung via ELSTER
costs.note: Free if you do it yourself. Via a Steuerberater — from 100–300 €.

costs.label: Einspruch against a Bescheid
costs.note: Filing an objection is free; deadline is 1 month from the date of the notice.

title: Tradesperson services (Handwerkerleistungen): 20% refund
tldr: Under §35a Abs. 3 EStG you can get back 20% of the cost of tradesperson services (Handwerker) directly off your income tax. This covers repairs, maintenance and modernisation in your home: plumber, electrician, painter, window installation, boiler repair, chimney cleaning, garden work. The key limitation: only 20% of the labour cost is refunded (Lohnkosten — labour, travel, machine time) — NOT the cost of materials. The maximum eligible expense is 6 000 € per year, i.e. the maximum tax credit is 1 200 € per year. Conditions: an invoice (Rechnung) showing labour (Lohn) and materials (Material) separately, and payment ONLY by bank transfer — cash is categorically not accepted. It also works for tenants (via their own service-charge statement, Nebenkostenabrechnung). This is not a deduction from income but a direct credit against tax (tax reduction, Steuerermäßigung).

content.text: §35a Abs. 3 EStG (the Income Tax Act, Einkommensteuergesetz) grants relief for "Handwerkerleistungen für Renovierungs-, Erhaltungs- und Modernisierungsmaßnahmen" — that is, any repair, maintenance and modernisation work by tradespeople in your household. The work must be carried out in your home (owned or rented) within the EU/EEA.

items: Plumbing: pipe repairs, replacing a mixer tap, installing a toilet
Electrical: new wiring, fitting sockets, repairing the fuse box
Painting and plastering, laying floors, tiling
Replacing/repairing windows, doors, roof, façade
Servicing and repairing heating, the boiler, the gas water heater (Therme)
Chimney sweep (Schornsteinfeger), air conditioning service
Garden work: tree pruning, paving paths, fencing
Repairing built-in appliances and a fitted kitchen (Einbauküche) on site

content.text: New construction (Neubau) does NOT count — the relief is only for existing housing. Work to create new living space from scratch does not qualify, but an extension/modernisation of an already existing house does.

This is the key point where people lose money. Only the labour cost (Arbeitskosten / Lohnkosten) counts — including the tradesperson's travel costs (Anfahrtskosten), machine time (Maschinenkosten) and consumables such as lubricant (Verbrauchsmittel). The cost of the material itself (tiles, paint, boiler, window) is NOT counted at all.

items: Counts: labour, travel, machine time, minor consumables
Does NOT count: materials (Material), spare parts, equipment
The invoice must separate labour (Lohn) and materials (Material) into separate lines
If the invoice shows a single lump sum, ask the tradesperson to issue a new one with a breakdown
VAT (Umsatzsteuer) on the labour portion also counts

content.text: Tip: when commissioning work, ask the tradesperson to break out the labour portion (Lohnanteil) in the quote in as much detail as possible. Sometimes you can legitimately structure the invoice so the labour share is shown correctly and in full — but you cannot inflate it artificially, as the tax office checks against typical norms.
The relief is a direct credit against tax (tax reduction, Steuerermäßigung), not a deduction from income. In other words it reduces your final income tax (Einkommensteuer) directly, euro for euro.

items: Rate: 20% of the eligible labour cost (Lohnkosten)
Maximum eligible labour cost: 6 000 € per year
Maximum credit: 6 000 × 20% = 1 200 € per year
The limit is shared per household (Haushalt), not per person
Any unused remainder does NOT carry over to the next year

content.text: Example: a painter painted the apartment. On the invoice the labour cost (Lohnkosten) = 2 500 €, materials (paint) = 800 €. Only the 2 500 € counts. Credit = 2 500 × 20% = 500 €, which is deducted directly from your tax. Second example: a full bathroom renovation, labour cost = 9 000 €. Only the 6 000 € ceiling counts, credit = the maximum 1 200 €. Tip: if there is a lot of work, spread it over two calendar years so you can use the 1 200 € limit twice.

steps.title: How to claim and pay correctly

items: Get an invoice (Rechnung) that lists labour (Lohn) and materials (Material) separately
Pay ONLY by bank transfer (Überweisung) — cash is not accepted
Keep the invoice and the bank statement (Kontoauszug) as proof
On your income tax return (Einkommensteuer) fill in the "Haushaltsnahe Aufwendungen" annex (household-related expenses), the Handwerkerleistungen field
Tenant: take the figures from your service-charge statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) / Hausgeldabrechnung — the management issues a §35a certificate
You don't have to attach the documents, but keep them in case the tax office asks

content.text: Paying in cash instantly costs you the entire relief — even a perfect invoice won't save it. §35a Abs. 5 EStG explicitly requires cashless payment into the provider's account. Never pay a tradesperson "off the books" if you want to get the 20% back.

costs.label: Maximum tax credit per year
costs.note: 20% of the 6 000 € Lohnkosten ceiling. Limit per household.

costs.label: Typical refund for an average repair
costs.note: 20% of Lohnkosten of 1 500–4 000 € (excluding materials).

costs.label: Self-filing via ELSTER
costs.note: Free. Filled in under Anlage Haushaltsnahe Aufwendungen.

sources.title: §35a EStG — Steuerermäßigung für haushaltsnahe Beschäftigungsverhältnisse und Handwerkerleistungen

title: Household services (Haushaltsdienstleistungen): 20% refund
tldr: Under §35a Abs. 2 EStG you get back 20% of the cost of household services in your home (haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen): cleaner, nanny, gardener, dog walking, elderly care, window cleaning. The limit here is more generous than for tradespeople: the maximum eligible expense is 20 000 € per year, i.e. the maximum tax credit is 4 000 € per year. A separate strand is a mini-job (Minijob) in the household (e.g. a cleaner at 603 €/month): for it the credit is 20%, but capped at 510 € per year. The conditions are the same as for §35a: an invoice + payment ONLY by bank transfer (for a Minijob — via the Haushaltsscheck procedure at the Minijob-Zentrale). Labour counts, not materials. This is a direct credit against tax, not a deduction from income. It also works for tenants via the service-charge statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung).

steps.title: What counts as a household service (haushaltsnahe Dienstleistung)

content.text: §35a EStG distinguishes three categories. Abs. 2 covers household services (haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen) — things residents would normally do themselves, but which someone performs for a fee in your home. The service must be provided in your home or on the adjacent property (EU/EEA).

items: Cleaning of the apartment/house by an external firm or a self-employed person
Window cleaning, carpet cleaning
Garden care: mowing the lawn, weeding, tending plants
Nanny (Babysitter), childcare at home
Care for the elderly and the sick at home (Pflege)
Walking and caring for pets on the property
Winter snow clearing in front of the house (Winterdienst)
Moving services (Umzugskosten) for a private move

content.text: Don't confuse this with §35a Abs. 3 (tradesperson services, Handwerkerleistungen — repair work, a separate limit of 1 200 €). Care/housekeeping services fall under Abs. 2 with their own limit of up to 4 000 €. These limits do NOT compete — you can use both in the same year.
For household services (haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen, through a firm or a self-employed person, not a mini-job) the limit is the largest of all the §35a strands.

items: Rate: 20% of eligible expenses (labour + travel, excluding materials)
Maximum eligible expenses: 20 000 € per year
Maximum credit: 20 000 × 20% = 4 000 € per year
Limit per household (not per person)
Direct credit against tax, not a deduction from income
Any unused remainder does not carry over to the next year

content.text: Example: a cleaner from a cleaning firm, paid 200 €/month = 2 400 €/year. Credit = 2 400 × 20% = 480 €, which directly reduces your tax. Example with care for an elderly relative at home: a care service (Pflegedienst) at 12 000 €/year. Credit = 12 000 × 20% = 2 400 €. To use the full 4 000 € limit you need 20 000 € of expenses a year.

steps.title: A mini-job (Minijob) in the household: 510 € limit

content.text: If you hire a household helper directly as a mini-job employee (Minijobber, e.g. a cleaner at 603 €/month), this is a separate sub-category, §35a Abs. 1, with its own, more modest limit. You must register such an employee via the Haushaltsscheck procedure at the Minijob-Zentrale.

items: Rate: 20% of the cost of a mini-job employee (Minijobber) in the household
Maximum credit: 510 € per year (this is the ceiling specifically for a household mini-job, Haushalts-Minijob)
Registration: via Haushaltsscheck at the Minijob-Zentrale (minijob-zentrale.de)
You pay the contributions as the employer, and they are also partly counted
Advantage of the Haushaltsscheck: a reduced, simplified contribution scheme (~14,8%)

content.text: Don't employ a household helper "off the books": without a Haushaltsscheck you not only lose your right to the credit but also break the law (illegal employment, Schwarzarbeit), and if the worker is injured you bear full liability. Registration via the Minijob-Zentrale is free and takes minutes.

items: For firms/self-employed: get an invoice (Rechnung) and pay by bank transfer (cash is not accepted)
For a mini-job: set up a Haushaltsscheck, and pay contributions and wages cashlessly
On your income tax return (Einkommensteuer) — the "Haushaltsnahe Aufwendungen" annex (household-related expenses)
The household-services field (haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen, Abs. 2) and/or household employment (Haushaltsnahe Beschäftigungsverhältnisse, mini-job)
Tenant: take your share from the service-charge statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) — the management lists the amounts that fall under §35a (stairwell cleaning, gardener, caretaker/Hausmeister)
Keep invoices and statements in case of a query

content.text: As everywhere in §35a (Abs. 5 EStG): payment must be cashless only. Even for cleaning done "neighbourly" in cash you will not get a cent back. And remember: materials (cleaning products, fertiliser) do not count — only labour and the associated services.

costs.label: Maximum credit for haushaltsnahe Dienstleistungen
costs.note: 20% of the 20 000 € ceiling. Limit per household.

costs.label: Maximum credit for a Haushalts-Minijob
costs.note: A separate §35a Abs. 1 ceiling for a Minijobber in the household.

costs.label: Typical refund for a cleaner
costs.note: 20% of 1 500–3 000 €/year paid to a cleaning firm.

costs.label: Haushaltsscheck registration at the Minijob-Zentrale
costs.note: Free. A reduced contribution rate of ~14,8% for households.

title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) without an appointment: emergency options
tldr: If there is no free appointment slot (Termin) and the 14-day deadline of §17 BMG is looming, there are several strategies that work: catch leftover slots (Restplätze) early in the morning on the city portal, travel to the citizens' offices (Bürgerämter) of suburbs and smaller districts where the queue is shorter, use morning walk-in hours (in some cities they accept walk-ins in the first hours of the day), and as a last resort a paid private booking service (Anmeldeservice; a legal grey area). The key thing: keep all the evidence of your attempts to book — it protects you from an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG) if the delay is not your fault.

content.text: Most cities release new and freed-up slots (Restplätze) in batches — usually early in the morning and when other people cancel. If you methodically refresh the portal at the right time, you can catch an appointment even where "everything is booked for months ahead".

items: Check the city's website at 6:00–8:00 — when the system releases new dates
Cancellations free up slots during the day — check several times
Monday and the start of the month are the peak for new appointments appearing
Don't limit yourself to the central office — look through all branches
Keep your details ready so you can book in seconds

content.text: A radical way to do without an appointment is the nationwide electronic registration portal wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de. If your city is connected to it (since 2023 this includes, for example, Hamburg and a number of others), residence registration (Anmeldung) is done online without a visit or an appointment. You need a national ID card (Personalausweis) or eID with the online function activated, plus the AusweisApp app.

Beware of bot sites and services that "book a Termin for you" automatically — many cities officially prohibit automatic scraping of appointments, and paying such a service does not guarantee a result. This is exactly the grey area (see the step on the booking service, Anmeldeservice).

In large cities appointments are snapped up instantly, but at the suburban citizens' offices (Bürgerämter) and small district offices the queue is often shorter. In many cities (Berlin, Hamburg, Munich) you can book at ANY office, not only the one for your area.

items: Check whether free choice of office applies in your city
Look for an appointment in outlying districts — Spandau instead of Mitte, Bergedorf instead of the centre
If you're ready to ride the S-Bahn for 30–40 minutes — that often solves the problem in days rather than weeks
There's usually no point looking for an appointment in neighbouring small towns — registration is only at your actual address

content.text: You can only register at the address where you actually live. Choosing "another office" concerns only the place of the appointment, not the address of registration. A fictitious registration at someone else's address (Scheinanmeldung) is an offence under §54 BMG: providing an address for a fictitious registration (§19 Abs. 6 BMG) is punishable by a fine of up to 50 000 € and risks criminal consequences.

In a number of cities walk-in hours survive (offene Sprechstunde / Spontantermine) — usually in the first morning hours and for a limited number of people. It's a lottery with an early queue, but a workable option when the deadline is looming.

items: Call 115 and ask about walk-in hours (offene Sprechstunde) / emergency appointments (Notfalltermine)
Arrive 30–60 minutes before the office opens
Bring ALL your documents — there may not be a second attempt the same day
Check the rules for handing out queue numbers on site with security/reception
Be prepared to wait several hours

content.text: The argument "my 14-day deadline is running out" often helps: some authorities treat such cases as an emergency (Notfall) and grant an appointment out of turn. Bring your tenancy agreement and the landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) with the move-in date as evidence.

steps.title: Strategy 4: a private booking service (Anmeldeservice; grey area)

content.text: There are commercial services that, for 20–100 €, promise to find or book an appointment, and sometimes to accompany you to the registration. Legally this is a grey area: the service of "finding an appointment" itself is not prohibited, but the automatic grabbing of slots is blocked by many cities, and there are no guarantees of a result.

items: The cost is usually 20–100 € to find/book an appointment
The service does not stand in for you — you still go to the registration (Anmeldung) in person
The service does not prepare your documents (passport, landlord's confirmation, Wohnungsgeberbestätigung)
No guarantees: the city may cancel "bot bookings"
Use it as a last resort, not the main route

content.text: Never pay for "registration at an address without living there" — that is a fictitious registration (Scheinanmeldung) and a direct violation of §54 BMG (providing an address under §19 Abs. 6 BMG — a fine of up to 50 000 €, and for organisers up to criminal liability). A legitimate booking service only helps with the appointment; it does not sell a fictitious address.

steps.title: How to protect yourself from a fine

content.text: The law requires you to register within 14 days (§17 BMG), but if cities physically cannot issue appointments, the authorities understand this. The key is to prove the delay was not your fault.

items: Take screenshots of "no free Termine available" with the date
Keep the appointment confirmation (Terminbestätigung) — it records the booking date
Keep your correspondence with the landlord about the landlord's confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung)
At the appointment, calmly explain that you tried to book right after moving in
The administrative fine (Bußgeld) under §54 BMG is a right, not an obligation of the authority; with proven attempts it is usually not imposed

costs.label: Anmeldung (officially)
costs.note: Registration at the authority is free in most cities.

costs.label: Private Anmeldeservice
costs.note: Commercial searching/booking of a Termin; the result is not guaranteed.

costs.label: Bußgeld for being late
costs.note: Under §54 BMG; with a proven shortage of Termine it is usually not charged.

sources.title: hamburg.de — Anmeldung der alleinigen Wohnung oder Hauptwohnung

title: Residence registration (Anmeldung) in Stuttgart
tldr: In Stuttgart, residence registration is handled by the district citizens' office (Bürgerbüro; the city's citizen-service offices, Bürgerbüros, in the city's districts). Appointments are booked online at stuttgart.de or by phone on 115. Under §17 BMG you must register within 14 days of moving in; a delay risks an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 1000 € (§54 BMG). Registration itself is free; a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) costs about 5–10 €. A passport and a landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung, §19 BMG) from the property owner are mandatory.

steps.title: The district citizens' office (Bürgerbüro) in Stuttgart

content.text: In Stuttgart, the registration of residents is handled by the district citizens' offices (Bürgerbüros). There is one in the centre (Bürgerbüro Mitte on Eberhardstraße) and others in the city's districts (for example Bad Cannstatt, Vaihingen, Zuffenhausen). You can book at any of them.

items: The office is called the Bürgerbüro (the city's citizen-service office)
The main office is Bürgerbüro Mitte, Eberhardstraße 39
Branches in the districts: Bad Cannstatt, Vaihingen, Zuffenhausen and others
Booking is possible at any Bürgerbüro in the city
Registration on site is free

content.text: An appointment (Termin) is booked online at stuttgart.de under Bürgerservice / Terminvereinbarung. Choose the service "Wohnung anmelden" (registration) or "An-/Ummeldung", then a convenient Bürgerbüro and an available date.

items: Open stuttgart.de → Bürgerservice → Termin vereinbaren (book an appointment)
Choose "Wohnung anmelden / ummelden" (registration / re-registration)
Compare dates across all the district Bürgerbüros
No online slots — call 115
Take your booking confirmation (Terminbestätigung)

content.text: Queues in Stuttgart are more moderate than in Munich, but in the centre an appointment can still be several weeks away. Take a slot at a district office (Vaihingen, Zuffenhausen) — there is usually more availability there, and the 14-day deadline under §17 BMG is critical.

items: Passport/ID for everyone being registered
A landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung, §19 BMG) — mandatory
The completed registration form (Anmeldung) — from stuttgart.de or on site
Marriage/children's birth certificates — for families
Your rental contract — as evidence (sometimes requested)

content.text: After registering you receive a free confirmation (Anmeldung). The official registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) costs about 5–10 € and is ordered separately — for the bank, your employer, the registry office, your driving licence and other authorities.

Moved from another city in Germany? A separate deregistration (Abmeldung) is not needed — a new registration in Stuttgart automatically closes your previous registration within the country. Deregistration is only required when leaving the country (§17 Abs. 2 BMG).

costs.label: Anmeldung
costs.note: Residence registration in Stuttgart is free.

costs.label: Meldebescheinigung
costs.note: A simple registration certificate.

costs.label: Bußgeld for a delay
costs.note: Under §54 BMG for violating the 14-day deadline.

sources.title: Stadt Stuttgart — Register residence as main residence

title: Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung): where you need it
tldr: The registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) is an official proof of registered address, issued by the authority at your place of residence (the district citizens' office, Bürgeramt / Kundenzentrum / KVR). You need it to open a bank account, get a driving licence, register a marriage at the registry office, start a job, enrol a child in daycare (Kita), get a library card, and obtain a resident parking permit. A simple certificate costs 5–16 € depending on the city. It is important to distinguish the paid registration certificate from the free confirmation of registration (Anmeldebestätigung), which is often accepted instead.

content.text: The registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) is official proof from the residents' register (Melderegister) that you are registered at a specific address. It is based on the data the authority entered during registration (Anmeldung). The certificate comes in a simple (einfache) form and an extended (erweiterte) form with additional details for certain authorities.

items: Simple certificate (einfache Meldebescheinigung) — name, date of birth, current address
Extended certificate (erweiterte Meldebescheinigung) — plus previous addresses, nationality, marital status, etc.
Issued by the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) / Kundenzentrum / KVR at your place of registration
You can order it in person, and in many cities online
Costs 5–16 € depending on the city (Hamburg is more expensive)

steps.title: Where the registration certificate is required

content.text: The list of situations where you may be asked for proof of registration is broad. Most often you need it for financial and official procedures.

items: Opening a current account (Girokonto) — the bank checks your address
Issuing and exchanging a driving licence (Führerschein)
Registering a marriage at the registry office (Standesamt)
Starting a job — the employer's HR may request it
Enrolling a child in daycare (Kita-Anmeldung)
Library card (Bibliotheksausweis)
Resident parking permit (Anwohnerparkausweis)
Applying for subsidies, allowances and social benefits

content.text: A parking permit and registering at the registry office almost always require the official registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung). Banks and employers, however, are often satisfied with the free confirmation of registration (Anmeldung).

When you register, the authority issues a confirmation of registration (Anmeldebestätigung) FREE of charge — proof that registration took place. This is not the same as the paid registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung), even though the address on both documents is the same.

items: Confirmation of registration (Anmeldebestätigung) — free, issued immediately when you register
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) — paid certificate (5–16 €), ordered separately
Many banks and employers accept the free confirmation
The registry office, parking and some authorities require the registration certificate specifically
Before paying, check with the requesting party which document is needed

content.text: Do not pay for a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) "just in case". First ask whether the free confirmation of registration (Anmeldung) will do — this saves both money and a trip to the authority. If you do need the certificate, in many cities you can order it online without an appointment.

items: In person at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) / Kundenzentrum / KVR — usually handed over on the spot
Online on the city portal (service.berlin.de, hamburg.de, stadt.muenchen.de, stuttgart.de) — sent by post or as a PDF
Bring your passport/ID; for online you need a BundID account (the single login for government services) or a city service account
The extended (erweiterte) certificate may cost slightly more than the simple one
Certified copy (beglaubigte Kopie) — surcharge of +5–10 € if you need an apostille/translation

content.text: You can obtain the certificate at any time after registration (Anmeldung) — you don't have to order it on the day you register. But keep in mind: some authorities require a "fresh" registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) no older than 3–6 months.

costs.label: einfache Meldebescheinigung
costs.note: Simple certificate; the price depends on the city (Hamburg ~10–16 €, others 5–12 €).

costs.label: Anmeldebestätigung
costs.note: Free confirmation, issued at Anmeldung; often accepted instead of the certificate.

costs.label: Beglaubigung / certified copy
costs.note: Surcharge for certification, if needed for an apostille or translation.

title: Second home (Zweitwohnsitz): a second residence and its tax
tldr: If you have two places of residence in Germany, you must declare one as your main home (main residence, Hauptwohnung) and the other as a secondary one (secondary residence, Nebenwohnung / Zweitwohnsitz) under §21–22 BMG. Your main home is the one you use predominantly. Many cities levy a second-home tax (Zweitwohnsitzsteuer) — a municipal tax, usually 5–20 % of the annual cold rent (Nettokaltmiete; München 18 %, Berlin 20 %, Hamburg 8 %, Köln/Frankfurt 10 % each). In a number of cities students are exempt or pay a reduced rate. Wrongly assigning the main and secondary residence (Haupt-/Nebenwohnung) is a breach of §54 BMG (fine of up to 1000 €), and trying to hide a second home to save on tax is risky.

content.text: Under §21 BMG, if a person has several residences in Germany, one of them is the main residence (Hauptwohnung) and the rest are secondary (Nebenwohnung). The main one is the residence you use predominantly (§22 BMG). When you register (Anmeldung), you must state the status of each address.

items: Main residence (Hauptwohnung) — the predominantly used home (§22 BMG)
Secondary residence (Nebenwohnung) / second home (Zweitwohnsitz) — any additional residence in Germany
For families: the main home is where the family lives (predominantly)
The status is stated when each address is registered
A change of predominant residence must be re-registered (re-registration of status, Ummeldung)

content.text: A typical case of a second home (Zweitwohnsitz) is working or studying in another city while keeping your main home (for example, with your parents or your family). The home at your place of work/study is then registered as secondary (Nebenwohnung).

The second-home tax (Zweitwohnsitzsteuer; the official term in city statutes is Zweitwohnungsteuer / Zweitwohnungssteuer) is a municipal consumption tax (örtliche Aufwandsteuer) that many, but not all, cities levy on a second home. The base is usually the annual cold rent without utilities (Nettokaltmiete), and the rate is set by the city's local statute (Satzung).

items: München — 18 % of the annual cold rent (since 2022)
Berlin — 20 % (since 1 January 2025; previously 15 %)
Hamburg — 8 %; Köln and Frankfurt am Main — 10 % each
Nationwide, rates range roughly from 5 to 20 %
Not all cities levy the tax — check the statute (Satzung) of the specific city
The base is the annual cold rent (Nettokaltmiete, excluding heating and utilities)

content.text: Both the rates and whether the tax applies at all depend on the city and are changed regularly by local statutes (Satzung). The percentages given are a guide; before calculating, check the current statute on the specific city's website. The tax is charged as soon as you register a secondary residence (Nebenwohnung) — and retroactively too.

Students are a frequent case of a second home (Zweitwohnsitz): their main home is with their parents, the secondary one is in the city where they study. The rules for them vary by city: in some places they are exempt, in others they pay like everyone else, and in others at a reduced rate.

items: In some cities students are exempt from the second-home tax (Zweitwohnsitzsteuer)
In others they pay the same as everyone — the tax on the secondary residence (Nebenwohnung)
The exemption often depends on income and who pays for the home
Solution: make the home in your city of study your main one (Hauptwohnung) — then there is no tax
Check the specific rules in the statute (Satzung) of your city

content.text: A tip for students and people working in a single city: if the home you study/work in is also your predominant place of residence, register it as your main one (Hauptwohnung). Then the second-home tax (Zweitwohnsitzsteuer) does not arise at all, since the tax applies only to a secondary residence (Nebenwohnung).

The temptation to "not register" a second home or to state the wrong status to save on tax is risky. Assigning the main and secondary residence (Haupt-/Nebenwohnung) is a legal obligation, and breaching it is punishable.

items: An incorrect main/secondary residence (Haupt-/Nebenwohnung) status — a breach of §54 BMG (fine of up to 1000 €)
An unregistered second home — also a breach of the registration obligation (Anmeldung)
The city can assess the second-home tax (Zweitwohnsitzsteuer) retroactively + penalties
Registering a fictitious main residence (Hauptwohnung) to avoid the tax is deceiving the authority
When your predominant residence changes, the status must be re-registered in time

content.text: The second-home tax (Zweitwohnsitzsteuer) is a real expense: at the München rate of ~18 % and a cold rent (Kaltmiete) of 600 €/month, the tax comes to more than 1200 € a year. Take this into account when deciding which home to make your main one (Hauptwohnung), and do not try to hide a secondary residence (Nebenwohnung) — cities cross-check register data and rental contracts.

costs.label: Anmeldung Nebenwohnung
costs.note: Registering a secondary residence itself is free.

costs.label: Zweitwohnsitzsteuer (per year)
costs.note: Depends on the city (München 18 %, Berlin 20 %, Hamburg 8 %, Köln/Frankfurt 10 % each); 5–20 % overall, not levied everywhere.

costs.label: Bußgeld for a breach
costs.note: Under §54 BMG for an incorrect status or failure to register.

title: Russian consulates in Germany: where they are and what they do
tldr: Since 2022 the Russian consular network in Germany has shrunk sharply. As of 2024–2026, citizens are received only by the consular section of the Russian Embassy in Berlin and the Consulate General in Bonn; the consulates general in Hamburg, Frankfurt am Main, Leipzig and München are closed until further notice following the mutual expulsion of diplomats. This has created huge queues: people wait months for a passport appointment. Consulates issue international passports, return certificates, notarial acts, powers of attorney, registration of birth/marriage, certificates, and registration on the consular roll. Appointments are made through the official portal germany.mid.ru (Berlin) and ruskonsulatbonn.de (Bonn). Never pay intermediaries for a "fast-track appointment" — it is illegal.

steps.title: Where Russian citizens are received in 2026

content.text: Until 2022, the Russian Embassy in Berlin and five consulates general operated in Germany. After the mutual reduction of diplomatic staff, the situation changed radically. According to official data from the German Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt) and the Russian missions, for 2024–2026 consular services to citizens are provided by only two locations.

items: Russian Embassy, consular section — Unter den Linden 63–65, 10117 Berlin (germany.mid.ru)
Russian Consulate General — Waldstraße 42, 53177 Bonn (ruskonsulatbonn.de)
The consulates general in Hamburg, Frankfurt am Main, Leipzig, München — CLOSED until further notice
Do not use the former honorary consulates (including Nürnberg) for current consular services — their status is unstable, check on germany.mid.ru
Service districts have changed: check on the embassy's website which location you are assigned to based on your federal state of residence

content.text: The closure of four consulates general has shifted the entire load onto Berlin and Bonn. This means real queues and trips across the whole country. Plan ahead: passport appointments may open once every few weeks and be snapped up within minutes.

The range of services is defined by the Consular Charter of the Russian Federation and the Foreign Ministry's administrative regulations. The basic list has been preserved, but processing times have grown due to the load.

items: International passport (biometric, 10 years / old-style, 5 years) — the main queue
Return certificate (SNV) — if your passport is lost/expired, for a one-time trip to Russia
Notarial acts: powers of attorney, consents, certification of copies and signatures
Registration of a child's birth, registration/dissolution of marriage
Registration on the consular roll (recommended but not mandatory)
Certificates (of marital status, of citizenship), retrieval of documents from Russia
Renunciation of Russian citizenship — filed here, decided by the President of Russia, takes 1–2 years
Consulates do NOT issue the Russian internal passport — only through the Ministry of Internal Affairs in Russia

content.text: Appointments are made only through the official websites. No "paid hotlines" or paid bots — these are either fraud or a violation that can get your appointment cancelled.

items: Berlin: appointment through the system on germany.mid.ru (consular section page)
Bonn: appointment through ruskonsulatbonn.de
Passport slots open in batches — check regularly and seize the moment
Come to the appointment with ALL documents: old international passport, Russian internal passport, photos to spec, completed application form
Payment of the consular fee is on site, by card/cash according to the location's rules
Being late or having an incomplete set = a new appointment and waiting all over again

content.text: If your Russian international passport is expiring and there have been no appointments for months — check whether what you primarily need is a valid German residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel). An expired international passport does not in itself strip you of your legal status in Germany if you hold a residence card; but for travel and renewing your residence permit you usually need a valid passport.

costs.label: Russian international passport (consular fee)
costs.note: The fee is set by the Russian Foreign Ministry; the biometric passport costs more than the old-style one. Check the exact amount on the location's website.

costs.label: Notarial act (power of attorney)
costs.note: Per document; depends on the type of act under the consular fee schedule.

costs.label: Return certificate
costs.note: Issued when a passport is lost/expired for a one-time trip to Russia.
