title: Exchanging a Russian driving licence for a German one
tldr: A Russian driving licence is exchanged in Germany under §29 FeV — but Russia is NOT in Anlage 11 FeV (the list of states with a simplified exchange without an exam). This means: to swap a Russian licence for a German one you have to pass both the theory and the practical exam in Germany. The window is simple: after moving your main place of residence (Wohnsitz) you may drive on your Russian licence for another 6 months (§29 Abs. 1 FeV); for the exchange itself the law allows up to 3 years. What you need: an application to the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle), a certified translation/classification of the licence (via the ADAC motoring club or a sworn translator), an eye-test certificate, a first-aid course, theory (25,80€) and practical (~167€) at TÜV/DEKRA, plus a driving school for preparation. The bottom line in money — roughly 350–600€.

content.text: The exchange (Umschreibung) of a foreign licence is governed by §28–§31 FeV. States in Anlage 11 FeV exchange licences without an exam or with a simplified exam — for example, many US states, Canada, Japan, Switzerland, South Korea. Russia is NOT listed in Anlage 11 FeV. Therefore a Russian licence is exchanged only after passing the full exam — theory and practical.

items: Anlage 11 FeV — a closed list; Russia is not in it
Consequence: §29 FeV allows driving on a Russian licence only for 6 months after registering your place of residence (Wohnsitz) in Germany
After 6 months a Russian licence is invalid in Germany — driving without an exchange = driving without a driving entitlement (Fahren ohne Fahrerlaubnis, §21 StVG, fine/criminal liability)
For the exchange procedure itself the law allows up to 3 years from the time of the move
Category B (passenger car) — the standard case; C/D have separate requirements
Tourists/short-term visitors do not need an exchange — for them the licence + translation applies

content.text: The six months count from establishing your place of residence (Wohnsitz; residence registration, Anmeldung), not from the date of entry. Miss the window and you cannot drive until you obtain a German licence. This is a common, costly mistake made by people arriving from Russia.
The application is filed with the driving-licence authority (Führerscheinstelle / Fahrerlaubnisbehörde) at your place of residence. The office checks your licence and refers you to the exams.

items: Russian driving licence (original)
Certified translation / classification of the licence — via the ADAC, ACE motoring club or a sworn translator (öffentlich bestellter Übersetzer)
International passport + residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) / residence registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Biometric photo (35×45 mm)
Eye test (Sehtest) — a certificate from an optician/doctor
First-aid course (Erste-Hilfe-Kurs) — 9 teaching hours
Confirmation of passing the theory and practical exam (Prüfbescheinigung TÜV/DEKRA)

content.text: Since Russia is not in Anlage 11, there is no way around the exams. The theory and practical exams are taken at TÜV/DEKRA, usually through a driving school (Fahrschule), which arranges the admission.

items: Theory: 30 questions (category B), a Russian-language test is available at TÜV/DEKRA — you can take it in Russian
Practical: ~45 minutes with an examiner; a route in the city/on the road
Driving school (Fahrschule): a full "from-scratch" course is formally not mandatory if you hold a foreign licence, but a school is needed for admission to the practical and to rent a training car
Many people take a few practice lessons (Übungsstunden) to get used to German rules (right of way/Vorfahrt, roundabouts/Kreisverkehr, environmental zone/Umweltzone)
Be ready for strictness: the German practical is tougher than the Russian one, and a failed exam is retaken for a fee
After you pass, the driving-licence authority issues the German licence; the Russian one is usually withdrawn (returned to Russia through the consulate on request)

content.text: The translation/classification of the licence via the ADAC motoring club is an almost mandatory step: the office needs to understand which categories you hold and from which year. Without the classification, your application will stall.

costs.label: Theorieprüfung (TÜV/DEKRA)
costs.note: About 25,80€ for the category B theory exam (GebOSt schedule).

costs.label: Praktische Prüfung
costs.note: About 167€ for the category B practical exam; a retake is paid for again.

costs.label: Übersetzung/Klassifizierung of the licence (ADAC)
costs.note: Classification of the foreign licence; a sworn translation is separate.

costs.label: Fahrschule (preparation + admission)
costs.note: Practice hours and arranging admission; depends on the number of lessons and the city.

costs.label: Gebühr Umschreibung (Führerscheinstelle)
costs.note: Administrative fee for issuing the German licence.

title: Evading Russian mobilization: asylum in Germany
tldr: Evading mobilization and deserting from the Russian army can be grounds for protection in Germany under §3 AsylG (refugee status) or §4 AsylG (subsidiary protection), but not automatically. The legal basis is Art. 9(2)(e) of EU Directive 2011/95 (Qualifikationsrichtlinie): persecution for refusing service, where that service would mean taking part in war crimes, counts as an act of persecution. The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) assesses each case individually (Einzelfallprüfung). In practice, deserters with a call-up or mobilization order have markedly better chances than draft evaders without a summons: the former find it easier to prove a concrete risk of persecution. According to the federal authorities' position, where desertion is credibly established, persecution on return to Russia is generally presumed. Applying for asylum is free; the key is the evidence base.

steps.title: Grounds: §3, §4 AsylG and the EU Directive

content.text: Germany grants protection on several levels: refugee status (§3 AsylG, implementing the Geneva Convention and Directive 2011/95) and subsidiary protection (§4 AsylG — serious harm: the death penalty, torture, a threat to life in armed conflict). Refusing service is not in itself equivalent to grounds for protection, but if that service would mean taking part in acts contrary to Art. 9(2)(e) of Directive 2011/95 (war crimes), such a refusal can become grounds for persecution.

items: §3 AsylG — refugee status: persecution on a protected ground (race, religion, nationality, political opinion, social group)
Art. 9(2)(e) of Directive 2011/95: persecution for refusing service in a conflict linked to war crimes = an act of persecution (Verfolgungshandlung)
§4 AsylG — subsidiary protection: serious harm on return (torture, threat to life)
A deserter has already received a call-up or been drafted and fled; a draft evader avoids conscription before any summons
The ECtHR (Bayatyan v. Armenia, Grand Chamber, 2011) recognized conscientious objection as a human right under Art. 9 ECHR
The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) carries out an individual assessment of each case (Einzelfallprüfung)

content.text: The statistics are harsh. Despite political statements, in the first years of the war most Russian draft evaders were refused. The decisive factor is being able to prove a concrete threat specifically to you.

items: According to the federal authorities' position: where desertion is credibly established, persecution on return is generally presumed
Deserters with a call-up or mobilization order have better chances: there is concrete proof of risk
Draft evaders without a summons are in a weaker position: BAMF often points to the low statistical probability of being conscripted
A public anti-war stance (posts, taking part in protests, persecution in Russia) strengthens a §3 AsylG case
Evidence: call-up paper, mobilization order, messages from the recruitment office, screenshots, witness statements, publications about you
A BAMF refusal can be appealed at the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht); the appeal deadline depends on the type of refusal

content.text: Do not destroy documents from the recruitment office — they are your main evidence. And do not enter on false grounds: lying in the BAMF interview (Anhörung) almost guarantees a refusal and undermines trust in your entire case. Every case is individual; for your specific situation, consult a specialist lawyer for migration law (Fachanwalt für Migrationsrecht).

The application is submitted in person; it cannot be filed by post. The procedure is free; while it is being processed you receive a permit to stay for the duration of the asylum proceedings (Aufenthaltsgestattung, §55 AsylG).

items: Declare your intention (Asylgesuch) — at an initial reception centre (Erstaufnahmeeinrichtung), the police, or the foreigners authority (Ausländerbehörde)
Registration, fingerprinting, issue of an arrival certificate (Ankunftsnachweis)
Formal asylum application (Förmlicher Asylantrag) — filed at a BAMF branch
Personal interview (Anhörung): the key moment, where you set out your story and present evidence
BAMF decision: §3 (refugee), §4 (subsidiary protection), §60(5)/(7) (deportation ban) or refusal
If refused — file a court action (Klage) at the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht); the appeal deadline depends on the type of refusal (often 1–2 weeks)
A migration-law lawyer and counselling are recommended (Caritas, Diakonie, PRO ASYL)

content.text: Time spent on a permit to stay for the duration of asylum proceedings (Aufenthaltsgestattung) and on a deportation deferral (Duldung) does not count towards the period of residence required for naturalization. If you have an alternative legal route (work visa, EU Blue Card/Blue Card, studies), it is often more practical and faster than asylum. Weigh both options.

costs.note: Filing the application and the BAMF assessment are free.

costs.label: Migration-law lawyer
costs.note: Rough cost for handling the case or an appeal; on a low income, Beratungshilfe and Prozesskostenhilfe may be available.

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung of evidence
costs.note: Call-up paper, mobilization order, documents — per page.

title: Russian international passport in Germany: getting an appointment
tldr: A Russian international passport can only be issued and renewed through Russian consular missions. After 2022 only two remain in Germany: the consular section of the Russian Embassy in Berlin and the Consulate General in Bonn (Hamburg, Frankfurt, Leipzig and Munich are closed). Because of this, getting an appointment is the main problem: the wait for a biometric-passport slot often runs to months. You can apply for a new-format biometric passport (10 years, with fingerprints — only at the consulate) or an old-format passport (5 years, sometimes faster). Appointments go strictly through the official portals (germany.mid.ru and the Bonn consulate site); avoid paid "expediters". The consular fee is set by the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs; check the exact amount on the mission's website. A Russian internal passport is not issued in Germany.

steps.title: Where and which passport to apply for

content.text: A Russian international passport is issued only by consular missions. After the network was cut back in 2022–2024, two locations operate in Germany: Berlin (the embassy's consular section) and Bonn (the Consulate General). Choose the one for your consular district as listed on the embassy website.

items: New-format biometric passport — valid 10 years, with a fingerprint scan; issued only at the consulate in person
Old-format passport — valid 5 years, without fingerprints; sometimes more slots available
Children under 14 — usually an old-format passport
An internal (Russian) passport is not issued at the consulate — only through the Interior Ministry in Russia
Check the districts on germany.mid.ru: you are assigned to Berlin or Bonn by your federal state of residence
Renewal on expiry, loss, change of name, or pages running out are separate grounds

content.text: A biometric passport cannot be obtained by proxy — you must appear in person to have your fingerprints taken. This is part of the queue and there is no way around it.
The appointment is the main barrier. Slots appear in batches and are taken quickly, so patience and regular checking matter most.

items: Berlin: booking system at germany.mid.ru (consular section page)
Bonn: booking through the Consulate General website
Check the site regularly — slots open up at irregular times
Prepare your document package in advance so you can book the moment a slot appears
Do not pay intermediaries for a "guaranteed appointment" — this is fraud or a violation, and the appointment may be cancelled
If your passport is expiring soon and there is no slot, consider an old-format passport as a faster option

steps.title: Documents and details of your status in Germany

content.text: Come to the appointment with a complete set: an incomplete package means a new appointment and waiting all over again.

items: Valid or expired international passport (if you have one)
Russian internal passport
Completed application form in the consulate's format
Photo meeting the requirements (for the old format); for biometrics the photo is taken on site
Documents on a change of name (marriage, name change), if applicable
Payment of the consular fee — on site according to the mission's rules
For children — birth certificate, parents' passports, consents

content.text: An expired Russian international passport does not affect your legal status in Germany if you hold a valid residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — a residence card or settlement permit. But a valid international passport is usually required to renew your German residence permit and to travel. If no appointment is available, it makes sense to notify the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) in advance and to keep a record of your booking attempts — this will be useful as proof of good faith.

costs.label: Biometric international passport (10 years)
costs.note: The consular fee is set by the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs; paid in euros at the mission's exchange rate. Check the exact amount on the website.

costs.label: Old-format international passport (5 years)
costs.note: Usually cheaper than the biometric one; a separate rate applies for children.

costs.label: Photo and travel to Berlin or Bonn
costs.note: The trip to one of the two locations can be long — budget for transport.

title: US citizens: visa, taxes, FATCA
tldr: US citizens enjoy visa-free entry to the Schengen area for up to 90 days within a 180-day period (tourism or a visit), but to live and work you need a national D visa and a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel). There is a special privilege: US citizens (like those of Canada, Australia, Japan and several other countries under §41 AufenthV) can enter without a visa and apply for a residence permit from within Germany, at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde). The main difficulty for Americans is taxes: the US taxes its citizens on the basis of citizenship (citizenship-based taxation), so an IRS return, the FBAR report (FinCEN 114) and Form 8938 (FATCA) must be filed even while living in Germany. Double taxation is avoided through the double taxation agreement (DBA) between the US and Germany, as well as via the FEIE or the Foreign Tax Credit. Because of FATCA, German banks are sometimes reluctant to open accounts for people with US person status.

steps.title: Entry and visa for US citizens

content.text: The US is on the Annex II list of EU Regulation 2018/1806 — visa-free entry for short stays (up to 90 days out of 180). To live and work you need a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel). The privilege for US citizens: under §41 AufenthV you can enter without a visa and apply for a residence permit from within Germany.

items: Visa-free entry of up to 90 days out of 180 for tourism or a visit (no right to work)
§41 AufenthV: citizens of the US, Canada, Australia, Israel, Japan, Korea, New Zealand and the UK can apply for a residence permit from inside Germany
In practice: visa-free entry → residence registration (Anmeldung) → appointment at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) → application for a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel)
Residence-permit routes: §18a/§18b (work), §18g (EU Blue Card, Blue Card), §21 (self-employment and the liberal professions, Freiberufler), §16b (study)
ETIAS — an electronic authorisation for visa-free tourist entry, not a visa (check the date it starts to apply)
If entering for work, it is better to obtain a D visa in advance or to apply for a residence permit straight away at the foreigners' authority

content.text: Visa-free entry does not grant the right to work. If the purpose is work, you must obtain a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) before starting employment. §41 AufenthV lets you file the application in Germany, but you may only work once the permit has been issued.

The key difference for Americans is that the US taxes its citizens by citizenship, not by residence. Even while living and paying taxes in Germany, a US citizen must file a federal return with the IRS (Form 1040) every year, plus a number of reports.

items: Form 1040 — the annual federal return to the IRS, mandatory for all US citizens regardless of country of residence
FBAR (FinCEN Form 114) — a report on foreign accounts if their combined balance exceeded 10 000 USD at any point in the year
Form 8938 (FATCA, Statement of Specified Foreign Financial Assets) — when asset thresholds are exceeded (the thresholds are higher for those living abroad)
Filing deadline for those abroad — an automatic extension to June 15 (and further on request)
FEIE (Form 2555) — exclusion of income earned abroad (Foreign Earned Income Exclusion)
Foreign Tax Credit (Form 1116) — a credit for taxes paid in Germany
Failing to meet the FBAR requirements risks heavy IRS penalties — this is the most common pitfall

steps.title: US–Germany DBA and the FATCA problem

content.text: To keep the same income from being taxed twice, the double taxation agreement (DBA, Doppelbesteuerungsabkommen) between the US and Germany applies. But FATCA creates everyday difficulties when opening accounts.

items: The US–Germany double taxation agreement (DBA) is in force and allocates taxing rights between the two countries
Germany taxes the worldwide income of tax residents (§1 EStG, unbeschränkte Steuerpflicht)
Double taxation is removed via the DBA, as well as the FEIE or the Foreign Tax Credit on the US side
FATCA requires German banks to report to the IRS the accounts of people with US person status — so the bank will ask about US citizenship
Some German banks and brokers are reluctant to open accounts for Americans because of the FATCA reporting
A tax adviser (Steuerberater plus a US tax preparer) is recommended to coordinate the two systems
Renouncing US citizenship (renunciation) is a last resort with its own Exit Tax; not something to do on advice from the internet

content.text: Your tax obligations to the IRS do not disappear when you move to Germany. Ignoring the FBAR and Form 8938 can lead to serious penalties. Coordinate your German and US returns through a specialist, especially if you have investments, real estate or self-employment.

costs.label: Nationales Visum D (if obtained in advance)
costs.note: If a D visa is requested before entry; under §41 AufenthV many apply for a residence permit once in Germany.

costs.label: Aufenthaltstitel (card issuance)
costs.note: Fee for the residence card at the Ausländerbehörde; for a Blue Card or work — around 100€.

costs.label: US tax preparer and Steuerberater (coordination)
costs.note: Preparing the US return and reconciling it with the German one — an annual guide figure.

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung of US documents
costs.note: Per page; diplomas and certificates for the residence permit and qualification recognition.

title: Cold rent (Kaltmiete) vs warm rent (Warmmiete): what's included
tldr: In a German apartment listing you'll see two figures. Rent without utilities (Kaltmiete, "cold") is the charge for the square metres only, without utility services. Rent with utilities (Warmmiete, "warm") = Kaltmiete + utility and operating costs (Nebenkosten/Betriebskosten): heating, water, rubbish collection, building cleaning, the caretaker, etc. Electricity (Strom) and internet are almost always SEPARATE contracts and are NOT included in the Warmmiete. All the important amounts (the rent itself, the deposit = a maximum of 3 Kaltmieten) are calculated from the cold rent — so always check which figure is shown.

content.text: In Germany the cost of rent is almost always shown on two lines. Rent without utilities (Kaltmiete; also Grundmiete, Nettokaltmiete) is the "bare" charge for using the home, calculated by area (€/m²). Rent with utilities (Warmmiete) is the total you actually transfer to the landlord each month: the Kaltmiete plus operating costs (Betriebskosten, colloquially called Nebenkosten, NK).

Important: the utility costs (Nebenkosten) within the Warmmiete are an advance payment (Nebenkostenvorauszahlung), not a fixed charge. Once a year the landlord sends a utility statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) — a comparison against the actual costs. If you paid less in advance than the real costs, there will be a back-payment (Nachzahlung); if more, a refund (Guthaben).

items: Kaltmiete = area only, €/m²
Warmmiete = Kaltmiete + operating costs (Betriebskosten): water, heating, rubbish, building
The Nebenkosten within the Warmmiete are an advance, reconciled once a year
All the key amounts (the deposit Kaution, the rent cap Mietpreisbremse) are calculated from the Kaltmiete
Sometimes a "Pauschalmiete" is stated — a single sum with no reconciliation (rare)

steps.title: What is included in the Nebenkosten and what isn't

content.text: The list of what the landlord may pass on to the tenant (umlagefähige Kosten) is strictly limited by law — by the operating costs ordinance (Betriebskostenverordnung, BetrKV). If a cost is not in this catalogue, it cannot be included in the utility costs (Nebenkosten).

items: Heating (Heizung) — often the largest item
Hot and cold water, sewage (Warm- und Kaltwasser)
Rubbish collection (Müllabfuhr)
Building cleaning and the caretaker (Hausreinigung und Hausmeister)
Garden, stairwell lighting (Gartenpflege, Beleuchtung)
Property tax (Grundsteuer) — paid by the tenant via the NK
Building insurance and the chimney sweep (Gebäudeversicherung, Schornsteinfeger)
Electricity (Strom): you sign your own contract with a provider
Internet/phone (Internet/Telefon) — unless a cable connection (Kabelanschluss) is listed separately in the NK
Insurance for your own belongings (Hausratversicherung) — voluntary
Public broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) — ~18,36 €/month per household
Repairs and maintenance of the building itself (this is the owner's responsibility)
Building management costs (Verwaltungskosten) — cannot be passed on

steps.title: How to calculate your real budget

content.text: Don't look only at the Kaltmiete — that is what the landlord uses to screen applicants. The real burden on your wallet = Warmmiete + electricity (Strom) + internet + broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag). Typical utility costs (Nebenkosten) run 2–4 €/m² per month: for a 60 m² apartment that's roughly 120–240 € on top of the Kaltmiete.

Too low a utility advance (Nebenkosten) is a common trap. The landlord can understate the advance (Vorauszahlung) so the Warmmiete in the listing looks attractive, and a year later you get a large back-payment (Nachzahlung). Compare the stated advance against the 2–4 €/m² norm and ask for last year's statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung).

When screening tenants, applicants often have to prove an income of three times the Kaltmiete (a credit-bureau report from Schufa + salary slips, Gehaltsnachweise). But in practice you will pay the Warmmiete plus electricity — factor in this gap so you don't overestimate what you can afford.

costs.label: Typical Nebenkosten (Betriebskosten)
costs.note: Per square metre per month; for 60 m² that's ~120–240 € on top of the Kaltmiete.

costs.label: Rundfunkbeitrag (broadcasting fee)
costs.note: 18,36 €/month per household; paid separately, not included in the Warmmiete.

costs.label: Strom (electricity) for 1 person
costs.note: A separate contract with a provider; not included in the Warmmiete.

title: Rental deposit (Kaution): 3 Kaltmieten, return
tldr: The rental deposit (Mietkaution) in Germany is governed by § 551 BGB: a maximum of 3 Kaltmieten (without utilities, Nebenkosten), and you are entitled to pay it in three equal monthly instalments. The landlord must keep your deposit separate from their own money — in a dedicated deposit account (Mietkautionskonto) earning interest that belongs to you. After move-out the deposit is returned, as a rule within 3–6 months, less any justified claims; part of it may be withheld until the final utility statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung). An alternative to a cash deposit is a deposit guarantee (Mietkautionsbürgschaft), but it costs around 5% per year.

content.text: The rental deposit (Mietkaution) is security against unpaid rent, damage or unmet obligations. § 551 BGB sets strict limits: the amount may not exceed 3 Kaltmieten (Nettokaltmiete, without the utilities Nebenkosten and without heating). Anything above this is unlawful — you can demand the excess back.

items: Maximum — 3 Kaltmieten (without NK)
You are entitled to pay in three equal parts: the first at the start of the tenancy, the rest over the next 2 months
The landlord may NOT demand the full amount before move-in
The deposit is held separately from the landlord's assets (protected in bankruptcy, insolvenzfest)
The interest on the account belongs to you and adds to the deposit

content.text: The right to pay in three parts is enshrined in law and cannot be overridden by contract. If the contract says "the whole deposit (Kaution) before signing", that clause is invalid insofar as it limits your right to instalments. You may pay at once if you wish, but no one can compel you to.

steps.title: Where the deposit and interest are held

content.text: A cash deposit must be placed by the landlord in a separate bank account, kept apart from their own assets (getrennt von seinem Vermögen) — so the money is protected if the landlord goes bankrupt. Interest accrues in your favour. In practice, with professional landlords this is a deposit account (Mietkautionskonto) or a deposit savings book (Kautionssparbuch) in your name with a deposit notation.

items: A deposit account (Mietkautionskonto) is opened — often free or up to ~5 €/year
The money is frozen: neither you nor the landlord withdraws it during the tenancy
Interest is added to the deposit
Ask for confirmation of which account the deposit is held in
A bank or insurer vouches for you instead of a cash deposit
No need to tie up cash — convenient when moving
Costs about 5% of the deposit (Kaution) per year (an ongoing expense)
The landlord is not obliged to agree to this option

content.text: After you hand back the apartment, the landlord must return the deposit within a reasonable period. The law gives no exact figure, but in practice it is 3–6 months: they need to check the condition of the home and wait for the final utility statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung). For that they may temporarily withhold a proportionate part (usually 3–4 monthly NK advances) and return the rest right away.

items: Make a handover protocol (Übergabeprotokoll) with photos at move-out
Record the meter readings and the absence of damage
Deductions are only allowed for justified claims (debts, damage beyond normal wear)
Normal wear and tear (normaler Verschleiß) may NOT be deducted
Part may be held until the annual utility statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) — this is lawful
Demand the return in writing if more than 6 months have passed

content.text: Deductions for "repairs" are often disputed. Normal wear (worn flooring, faded walls, picture-hook holes) the landlord must accept without deductions — these are their costs. They may only withhold for actual damage beyond normal use. If they deduct without justification and without a breakdown, demand a written itemisation, and in a dispute turn to a tenants' association (Mieterverein).

costs.label: Mietkaution (deposit)
costs.note: Up to 3 Kaltmieten under § 551 BGB; depends on the size of the cold rent.

costs.label: Mietkautionskonto (account upkeep)
costs.note: Per year; free at many banks.

costs.label: Kautionsbürgschaft (guarantee)
costs.note: About 5% of the deposit per year; an ongoing expense instead of tying up cash.

title: Nebenkostenabrechnung: how to check it
tldr: Once a year the landlord sends a utility statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) — a reconciliation of the actual operating costs against your advance payments (§ 556 BGB). The deadlines are strict: the landlord must deliver the statement within 12 months after the end of the accounting period — miss it, and they can no longer recover a back-payment from you. You also have 12 months from the moment you receive it to file a written objection (Einwendungen). ONLY the costs from the BetrKV catalogue may be passed on to the tenant; management costs and building repairs cannot. Check the allocation key, the period, the area, and your right to demand the underlying documents (Belegeinsicht).

content.text: The utility statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) is an annual report: how much the operating costs (Betriebskosten) actually were for the period and how they compare with your monthly advance payments. Under § 556 BGB there are two key deadlines, and both work in your favour if you know them.

items: The landlord must deliver the statement within 12 months after the end of the accounting period
Late with the statement → loses the right to claim a back-payment (Nachzahlung) for that year
But a refund (Guthaben) must still be returned to you
You have 12 months from receipt to file a written objection (Einwendungen)
Miss your objection deadline → the statement is deemed accepted

content.text: Missing the 12-month objection deadline is risky: after it, you effectively accept the statement even if it contains errors. When you receive the utility statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung), mark the deadline in your calendar right away and check the document — do not pay a back-payment (Nachzahlung) blindly before checking it.

steps.title: What to check in the statement

content.text: Many utility statements (Nebenkostenabrechnungen) contain errors — from an incorrect area to inadmissible items. Only costs from the catalogue of the operating-costs ordinance (Betriebskostenverordnung, BetrKV) may be passed on to the tenant. Building management (Verwaltungskosten), repairs and maintenance of the building, and reserves may NOT be passed on (umlagefähig).

items: Accounting period (Abrechnungszeitraum) — exactly 12 months, with no gaps or overlaps
Your time share, if you did not live there the whole year
Living area (Wohnfläche) — of your flat and of the whole building (used for allocation)
Allocation key (Verteilerschlüssel) — by area, by number of occupants, by meters
Advance payments (Vorauszahlungen) — whether all your advances for the period are counted
Each item — whether it is in the BetrKV catalogue
Heating costs (Heizkosten) — at least 50–70% allocated by actual consumption (the heating-costs ordinance, Heizkostenverordnung)

content.text: Inadmissible items are a common problem. If the statement includes management costs (Verwaltungskosten), building repairs (Instandhaltung/Reparaturen), the landlord's bank charges (Bankgebühren) or a reserve fund — these may NOT be passed on to the tenant. Strike out such items in your objection, citing § 556 BGB and the BetrKV.

steps.title: Right to documents and to object

content.text: If the figures raise doubts, you have the right to inspect the underlying documents (Belegeinsicht) — supplier invoices, contracts, building calculations. The landlord must provide them; until then you may withhold the disputed back-payment.

items: Ask in writing to see the original invoices and calculations
You may take photos or copies of the documents
You can temporarily withhold the disputed back-payment (Nachzahlung) until you have checked it
Compare the invoice amounts with what was allocated to you
List the specific items with errors, citing the BetrKV / § 556 BGB
Send it within 12 months of receipt, ideally with proof of dispatch
Keep a copy of the letter and evidence of the date
In a complicated case — to a tenants' association (Mieterverein), where they will check the statement line by line

costs.label: Typical Nebenkosten (basis for advances)
costs.note: Per m² per month; this is exactly what is reconciled in the Nebenkostenabrechnung.

costs.label: Checking the statement via Mieterverein
costs.note: Annual membership; includes a line-by-line check of the Nebenkostenabrechnung.

costs.label: Mietrechtsschutzversicherung
costs.note: Per year; covers the dispute if it goes to court.

title: Stepped rent (Staffelmiete) vs index-linked rent (Indexmiete)
tldr: These are two ways of agreeing in advance on rent increases. Rent with stepped increases (Staffelmiete, § 557a BGB) is a tiered rent: the contract sets out specific amounts and dates for the increases (for example, +30 € a year). Index rent (Indexmiete, § 557b BGB) is tied to the consumer price index (Verbraucherpreisindex, VPI, from Destatis). Both share a common feature — with them the landlord CANNOT additionally raise the rent up to the local comparative rent (Vergleichsmiete); ordinary increases are ruled out. Each step or adjustment must hold for at least 12 months. The rent brake Mietpreisbremse applies to the starting rent and to each step.

content.text: With rent that has stepped increases (Staffelmiete), the future increases are already fixed in the contract: it states either the new amounts or the exact increment for each step and the date it takes effect. The advantage is predictability: you know in advance how much you will be paying in a year or two.

items: Specific amounts or increments and dates are written into the contract
Each step must apply for at least 12 months
During a Staffelmiete, ordinary increases up to the comparative rent (Vergleichsmiete) are ruled out
The amount must be stated in euros, not as a vague formula
The rent brake (Mietpreisbremse, extended to 31 December 2029, § 556d BGB) applies to both the starting rent and each step in the zones where it is in force

steps.title: Indexmiete: tied to the VPI under § 557b BGB

content.text: With index rent (Indexmiete), the rent is tied to the consumer price index (Verbraucherpreisindex, VPI) for Germany, published by the Federal Statistical Office (Statistisches Bundesamt, Destatis). When the index rises, the landlord can adjust the rent proportionally. The logic is "as prices rise across the country, so does the rent".

items: The basis is the official VPI from Destatis, not the landlord's wishes
An adjustment is possible no more than once every 12 months
The change is made in writing (Textform), stating the old and new index and the new rent
It rises when the index actually changes — and can also fall in a deflation
With Indexmiete too, ordinary increases up to the comparative rent (Vergleichsmiete) are ruled out

content.text: In periods of high inflation, index rent (Indexmiete) can rise faster than a Staffelmiete with fixed amounts. Before signing, look at the VPI trend: when high inflation is expected, a predictable Staffelmiete is sometimes more favourable, and vice versa.

steps.title: What to choose and what to look at

items: Staffelmiete: add up the total rent over the whole period you plan to live there
Indexmiete: assess the inflation trend and the past VPI figures
Check that each step or adjustment applies for at least 12 months
In a rent-brake (Mietpreisbremse) zone, make sure the start does not exceed the comparative rent (Vergleichsmiete) + 10%
Staffelmiete: pay according to the schedule automatically — no separate letter is required
Indexmiete: an increase takes effect only after a written notice with the index-based calculation
Check that the index references are correct at each adjustment
Doubts about the calculation — to a tenants' association (Mieterverein)

content.text: With both forms, the landlord cannot "additionally" raise the rent up to the local comparative rent — this protects you from a double increase. But increases after modernisation (Modernisierungsumlage) are in some cases still possible: check the wording of the contract.

costs.label: Typical annual Staffelmiete step
costs.note: Depends on the contract; stated in euros for each step.

costs.label: Indexmiete increase per year
costs.note: Depends on the change in the VPI; in years of high inflation it can be substantial.

costs.label: Checking an increase via Mieterverein
costs.note: Annual membership; they will check that the step or index is correct.

sources.title: Verbraucherzentrale — Staffelmiete und Indexmiete im Vergleich

title: Subletting (Untermiete): rent out a room legally
tldr: Subletting (Untermiete): as a tenant you rent out part of your apartment (a room) to a third party. Under § 553 BGB you have a RIGHT to do this: if a legitimate interest arose after you signed the lease (financial, a flatmate, a partner), the landlord cannot unreasonably refuse to allow you to sublet PART of the home. Subletting the entire apartment is a separate case and requires explicit consent (§ 540 BGB). You must always request permission in writing BEFORE the subtenant moves in; without it you risk a formal warning (Abmahnung) and even termination. Income from subletting is taxable.

steps.title: Your right to rent out part of the apartment

content.text: The law distinguishes between subletting PART of a home and subletting the whole apartment. For a part (for example, a single room), § 553 BGB gives the tenant a strong right: if a legitimate interest (berechtigtes Interesse) arose after you signed the lease — for example, your costs went up, you want a flatmate, or a partner is moving in — the landlord may not unreasonably refuse permission to sublet a part.

items: Subletting PART (a room): a right under § 553 BGB, given a legitimate interest
The landlord cannot unreasonably refuse a partial sublet
Subletting the entire apartment: explicit consent is required (§ 540 BGB)
The legitimate interest (berechtigtes Interesse) must have arisen after the lease was signed
The landlord may ask for a small sublet surcharge (Untermietzuschlag) if it is reasonable in their case

content.text: Never let a subtenant move in without written permission. Unauthorised subletting breaches the lease: the landlord may issue a formal warning (Abmahnung) and, if you persist, terminate the lease. First the request and the permission, then the move-in.

Request permission in writing and in advance. In your request, state exactly who is moving in, which part of the apartment they will occupy, for how long, and the reason (your legitimate interest). The landlord must respond; refusing a partial sublet without good reason when a legitimate interest (berechtigtes Interesse) exists is unlawful.

items.title: 1. Write a request to the landlord

items: Name and details of the future subtenant
Which part of the apartment is being sublet (the room) and for how long
The reason — your legitimate interest (berechtigtes Interesse): finances, flatmate, partner
A request to grant written permission by a specific date
Send it so that you keep proof (registered letter Einschreiben / email)
A sublet agreement (Untermietvertrag) in writing: room, term, rent, deposit
Do not mark up your own rent to an unreasonable degree
Record the condition of the room (photos, a handover protocol)
The subtenant does their residence registration (Anmeldung) at this address — for that you give them a landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung)
Remember: you are responsible to the landlord for everything, not the subtenant

content.text: Income from subletting is rental income (Einkünfte aus Vermietung und Verpachtung), and as a rule you must declare it in your tax return (Steuererklärung). Expenses relating to that part can be deducted. Simplifications apply to very small and short-term cases, but check your own situation.

items: Sublet income is declared on the tax return (the Anlage V attachment)
Your expenses for the sublet part can be deducted
Short-term rental to tourists (Airbnb) often requires a permit for the change of use of housing (Zweckentfremdungsgenehmigung) — separate municipal rules apply
You remain the main tenant: debts or damage caused by the subtenant are your responsibility
If you are unsure about the taxes — see a tax adviser (Steuerberater) or an income-tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein)

content.text: Short-term per-night rental (Airbnb) is NOT ordinary subletting (Untermiete): many cities have a ban on the change of use of housing (Zweckentfremdungsverbot), and without a permit you face heavy fines. This rule usually does not apply to a permanent flatmate, but renting to tourists is a different story.

costs.label: Untermietzuschlag (sublet surcharge)
costs.note: The landlord may ask for a reasonable surcharge; the exact amount depends on the case.

costs.label: Tax on sublet income
costs.note: Taxed as rental income; the rate depends on your total income.

costs.label: Consultation at a Mieterverein
costs.note: Annual membership; they will help with the request and the sublet agreement.
