title: Vehicle registration (KFZ-Zulassung)
tldr: Vehicle registration (Kfz-Zulassung) in Germany takes place at the vehicle registration office (Zulassungsstelle, often inside the Straßenverkehrsamt). The main things you must not forget are the electronic insurance confirmation number (eVB-Nummer, from your insurer) and a direct-debit authorization (SEPA-Lastschriftmandat) for collecting the vehicle tax (Kfz-Steuer). You need to bring a national ID card (Personalausweis) or a passport with a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung), the Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil II (the old Fahrzeugbrief) and Teil I, and a valid TÜV inspection (HU). Registration costs roughly 30–60 €, plus license plates (Kennzeichen) at 20–40 €. Since 2023 some steps are available online via i-Kfz.

steps.title: Where to go and what the eVB-Nummer is

content.text: Vehicle registration in Germany is handled by the vehicle registration office (Zulassungsstelle, the motor vehicle registration department), usually part of the Straßenverkehrsamt or the district citizens' service (Bürgeramt) of your district (Kreis/kreisfreie Stadt). As a rule you must book an appointment (Termin) online in advance — in many cities you will not be seen without one.

The most important thing, and the one most often forgotten, is the electronic insurance confirmation number (eVB-Nummer, elektronische Versicherungsbestätigung). This is a 7-digit code from the insurance company confirming that the car is covered by at least third-party liability insurance (Haftpflicht). Without the eVB-Nummer registration is impossible: by law insurance is mandatory before a car may be on the roads.

items: The authority is called the Zulassungsstelle (often part of the Straßenverkehrsamt)
Book an appointment (Termin) online in advance — slots are limited
Get an eVB-Nummer from your insurer BEFORE the visit (often issued within minutes online)
The eVB covers at least the Haftpflicht; partial or full comprehensive cover (Teil-/Vollkasko) can be added separately
Registration is tied to your residence registration address (Anmeldung)

content.text: Which documents you need depends on whether you are registering a new car, a used one keeping the same plate, or a change of address. The basic set for registering a vehicle is below.

items: National ID card (Personalausweis) or a passport + a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
eVB-Nummer from the insurance company
Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil II (the old Fahrzeugbrief) — the main owner document
Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil I (the old Fahrzeugschein), if the car was already registered
A direct-debit authorization (SEPA-Lastschriftmandat) for collecting the vehicle tax (Kfz-Steuer) — mandatory
A valid roadworthiness inspection report HU/TÜV (Hauptuntersuchung)
Old license plates (Kennzeichen), if the car was already registered
A power of attorney (Vollmacht) + the owner's ID, if you are registering a car that is not yours

content.text: A direct-debit authorization (SEPA-Lastschriftmandat) is now mandatory: the vehicle tax (Kfz-Steuer) is collected by customs (Zoll/Hauptzollamt), and without a valid authorization to debit your bank account the registration will not be completed.

steps.title: TÜV (HU), plates and the green badge

content.text: Before you register a used car there must be a valid roadworthiness inspection (Hauptuntersuchung, HU), carried out by TÜV, Dekra, GTÜ and others. Without a valid HU the car either will not be registered or you will be required to undergo the inspection immediately.

items: Plates are made at a plate-embossing shop (Schilderprägestelle, often right next to the Zulassungsstelle building)
You can reserve a desired plate (Wunschkennzeichen) online in advance
After the Zulassungsbescheinigung is issued, registration seals (Plaketten) are stuck onto the plates

content.text: To enter the environmental zones (Umweltzonen) of most cities you need a green environmental sticker (Umweltplakette). You can get it right away at registration, at TÜV/Dekra, or at a garage — see the separate guide on the Umweltplakette.

steps.title: Online via i-Kfz and the cost

content.text: Since 2023 the i-Kfz system has been expanded: online you can register a new or used car, re-register, deregister and change the plate. For online registration you need a national ID card (Personalausweis) with the online function activated (eID) and a card reader or the AusweisApp, plus the access codes from the car's documents.

items: i-Kfz runs on the portal of your region or city (links at kba.de and on the state websites)
You need: an eID (the Personalausweis online function), an eVB-Nummer, an IBAN for the vehicle tax (Kfz-Steuer)
After online registration the documents and stickers arrive by post
If the eID is not activated or the car is from another region — it is easier to go in person

content.text: A car without valid insurance and registration must not be driven on public roads. Driving without third-party liability insurance (Haftpflicht) is a criminal offense (§6 PflVG), not just a fine.

costs.label: KFZ-Zulassung (registration)
costs.note: Basic government fee for registering a vehicle; depends on the region and the type of transaction.

costs.label: Kennzeichen (license plates)
costs.note: Making a pair of plates at a Schilderprägestelle; a Wunschkennzeichen costs more.

costs.label: Umweltplakette (green sticker)
costs.note: The green badge for entering Umweltzonen; often issued right away at registration.

sources.title: Bundesministerium für Digitales und Verkehr — i-Kfz (internetbasierte Fahrzeugzulassung)
ADAC — Auto anmelden: Kfz-Zulassung Schritt für Schritt

title: KFZ-Steuer: the vehicle tax
tldr: The vehicle tax (Kraftfahrzeugsteuer, Kfz-Steuer) in Germany is collected not by the tax office (Finanzamt) but by customs — Zoll / Hauptzollamt (since 2014). For passenger cars the calculation base under §8–9 KraftStG is made up of the engine displacement (Hubraum, per each started 100 cm³) and CO2 emissions (a surcharge for grams above the tax-free threshold). For example, a 1.6 l petrol car usually comes to roughly 100–150 € per year. The tax is debited once a year in advance via SEPA direct debit (SEPA-Lastschrift), which you set up at registration. Electric vehicles are exempt from the tax: the exemption has been extended — it applies to cars first registered up to 31.12.2030 and applies for no longer than until 31.12.2035 (previously until the end of 2025 / the end of 2030; the 8th law amending the KraftStG). Check that this is still current.

steps.title: Who collects the tax and how it is calculated

content.text: Many newcomers look for the vehicle tax (Kfz-Steuer) at the tax office (Finanzamt) — and do not find it. Since 1 July 2014 the vehicle tax has been administered by customs: Zoll and the regional customs offices (Hauptzollämter). It is a federal tax (Bundessteuer).

You do not need to file anything separately: when you register at the vehicle registration office (Zulassungsstelle) you give a direct-debit authorization (SEPA-Lastschriftmandat), and Zoll debits the tax a year in advance (or for the period of ownership if the car is registered or deregistered mid-year).

items: The authority is Zoll / Hauptzollamt, NOT the Finanzamt
The debit is taken by SEPA direct debit (SEPA-Lastschrift) from the account given at registration
The tax is paid a year in advance; when you deregister, any overpayment is refunded
The tax assessment (Steuerbescheid) arrives by post after registration

steps.title: How the amount is calculated (§8–9 KraftStG)

content.text: For ordinary passenger cars (Pkw) with a combustion engine, the basis is §8 and §9 KraftStG. Two parts are added together: the tax on the engine displacement (Hubraum) and a surcharge for CO2 emissions above the tax-free threshold.

items: Calculated per each started 100 cm³ of displacement
Petrol engines: roughly 2 € per 100 cm³
Diesel engines: considerably higher — roughly 9.50 € per 100 cm³
That is why a diesel of the same displacement is taxed more heavily than a petrol car
Grams of CO2/km above the tax-free threshold are taxed (for most new cars — 95 g/km)
The rate is progressive: the higher the emissions, the more each additional gram costs
For older cars (by date of first registration) different transitional rules apply
The exact CO2 and engine displacement (Hubraum) figures are stated in the Zulassungsbescheinigung

content.text: Example: a petrol car with an engine of about 1.6 l usually comes to roughly 100–150 € per year depending on CO2 emissions. A diesel of the same displacement is noticeably more expensive. For an exact figure it is convenient to use the vehicle tax calculator (Kfz-Steuer-Rechner) on the website of the Federal Ministry of Finance (Bundesfinanzministerium).

Purely electric cars (BEV) are exempt from the vehicle tax (Kfz-Steuer) for a limited period. Under the current version of §3d KraftStG the exemption applies to cars first registered up to 31 December 2030 and lasts no more than 10 years, but at most until 31 December 2035. Once the relief ends, electric vehicles (EV) are taxed at a reduced rate (by weight — with a 50 % discount relative to combustion engines).

items: BEV (fully electric) — a temporary exemption; recheck the deadlines on zoll.de
Hybrids (Plug-in/Hybrid) are usually taxed like combustion engines, by engine displacement (Hubraum) + CO2
There are exemptions for vehicles of people with disabilities (severe disability, Schwerbehinderung) — §3a KraftStG
Classic cars (Oldtimer) with a historic plate (H-Kennzeichen) pay a flat rate (around 191 € for passenger cars)

content.text: The deadlines for the electric-vehicle relief have changed several times. Before counting on the exemption, check the current rules on zoll.de and the text of §3d KraftStG: the relief is tied to the first-registration window (up to 31.12.2030) and is capped at 31.12.2035.

costs.label: KFZ-Steuer for a passenger car (per year)
costs.note: Depends on engine displacement, fuel type and CO2 emissions; a 1.6 l petrol car is usually ~100–150 €/year.

costs.label: KFZ-Steuer for an electric car (BEV)
costs.note: A temporary exemption within the set first-registration window; then a reduced rate by weight.

costs.label: Oldtimer with an H-Kennzeichen
costs.note: A flat annual rate for passenger classic cars (motorcycles are cheaper).

sources.title: ADAC — Kfz-Steuer: So wird sie berechnet

title: KFZ-Versicherung: SF classes
tldr: Third-party liability insurance (Haftpflicht) in Germany is mandatory by law (§1 PflVG) — without it your car will not be registered. The cost is largely determined by the no-claims class — the Schadenfreiheitsklasse (SF-Klasse). You usually start at SF0 or class S (for new drivers), and for each claim-free year the class rises (up to SF35 and beyond) while the percentage you pay (Beitragssatz) falls. A foreign no-claims history is sometimes credited if the insurer in your former country confirms it in a letter. Besides the mandatory Haftpflicht there are voluntary partial comprehensive cover (Teilkasko) and full comprehensive cover (Vollkasko).

content.text: Germany has three levels of car insurance. Only the first is mandatory by law.

items: Car liability insurance (Kfz-Haftpflicht) — mandatory (§1 PflVG): covers the damage you cause to others
Partial comprehensive cover (Teilkasko) — voluntary: theft, glass, natural events, animals, fire
Full comprehensive cover (Vollkasko) — voluntary: everything from Teilkasko + damage to your own car, including when you are at fault
For registration the Haftpflicht is enough — it is what gives you the eVB-Nummer (the electronic insurance confirmation number)

content.text: Driving without valid third-party liability insurance (Haftpflicht) is not a fine but a criminal offense under §6 PflVG (up to one year in prison or a monetary fine). A car without insurance is automatically deregistered on the insurer's notification.
No-claims class (Schadenfreiheitsklasse, SF-Klasse): the longer you drive without reported claims, the higher the class and the lower the percentage of the base tariff (Beitragssatz) you pay.

items: Beginners often start at class S (Sonderklasse) or SF0 — the highest percentage (often 100–230%)
After the first full year without claims, SF1 is usually assigned
After that the class rises by 1 for each claim-free year

items.title: 2. Class growth and a lower premium

items: The scale runs to about SF35 and beyond, depending on the insurer
High classes give a payment percentage (Beitragssatz) of around 20–30% of the base
After a claim you are downgraded by several classes (Rückstufung)
Many offer a discount protection (Rabattschutz): for an extra fee, one claim a year does not lower your class

content.text: When relocating, many drivers already have years without claims abroad. German insurers sometimes credit this history and do not place you in the most expensive class S, but they do so voluntarily and by their own rules.

items: Ask your previous insurer for written confirmation of your claim-free years (preferably in German or English)
The document should show the insurance period and the absence of payouts
Within the EU/EEA crediting is common; for countries outside the EU it depends on the specific company
Without crediting you will start at a high percentage — compare offers from several insurers
You can compare tariffs via Check24, Verivox or directly with the insurers

content.text: The no-claims class (SF class) is tied to the driver and to a specific type of insurance (separately for a car, separately for a motorcycle). When you switch insurers, the previous one passes your class to the new one — do not lose your accumulated years by signing up "from scratch" without need.

costs.label: Kfz-Haftpflicht (per year, as a guide)
costs.note: Strongly depends on the SF class, region (Regionalklasse), model and mileage; beginners pay several times more.

costs.label: Extra for Teilkasko (per year)
costs.note: Added to the Haftpflicht; depends on the deductible (Selbstbeteiligung) and the value of the car.

costs.label: Extra for Vollkasko (per year)
costs.note: Full comprehensive cover; usually worth it for new and expensive cars or when financed/leased.

sources.title: Verbraucherzentrale — Kfz-Versicherung: Haftpflicht, Teil- und Vollkasko

title: Exchanging an EU licence: no test
tldr: A driving licence issued in any EU/EEA country is valid directly in Germany without any exchange and without any test (§28 FeV). If you become a resident, the licence stays valid until its expiry date. You only need to exchange (Umschreibung) it for a German one in specific cases — for example, to renew an expired licence, to replace a lost one, or if you simply want a German document. The exchange procedure for an EU licence is straightforward: an application to the driving licence authority (Fahrerlaubnisbehörde), a photo, ID, sometimes a translation; no tests are taken. The cost is roughly 35–45 €.

steps.title: An EU licence is valid directly (§28 FeV)

content.text: The main rule for holders of an EU/EEA licence: your driving licence is recognised directly in Germany. Under §28 FeV you may drive on your national EU licence for as long as it is valid, even after becoming a resident of Germany. There is no mandatory exchange and no tests.

items: An EU/EEA licence is valid in Germany within its categories and validity periods
Moving and residence registration (Anmeldung) do not cancel the validity of an EU licence
Tests (theory/practical) are NOT required
Exchanging it for a German document is optional, or done upon expiry/loss

steps.title: When an exchange (Umschreibung) is needed after all

content.text: Although exchanging an EU licence is not mandatory simply because you live here, there are situations where an exchange (Umschreibung) is convenient or necessary.

items: The licence is expiring — renewing it as a German document is easier
The licence is lost or damaged
Categories on the EU licence have a limited validity (for example, lorry/bus C/D), and a German entitlement is needed
You want a single German document for convenience
The authorities have found a breach of recognition (for example, the licence was obtained by circumventing the rule on permanent residence)

content.text: Recognition of an EU licence does not apply if it was obtained by circumventing the principle of normal residence (Wohnsitzprinzip) — that is, 'licence tourism' to another EU country without actually living there may not be recognised by Germany.

The exchange is handled by the driving licence authority (Fahrerlaubnisbehörde), often part of the road traffic authority (Straßenverkehrsamt) or the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt). Book an appointment and submit an application for the exchange (Umschreibung).

items: Application for the exchange (Antrag auf Umschreibung) to the driving licence authority
National ID card (Personalausweis)/passport + a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
The original EU licence (it is surrendered in exchange for the German one)
A biometric photo (35×45 mm)
Sometimes a translation/extract, if the data on the licence is illegible for the authority
No theory or practical test is required for an EU licence

content.text: After you apply, the German licence usually takes a few weeks to produce; a temporary confirmation may be issued for that period. The surrendered original EU licence is, as a rule, returned to the issuing country.

costs.label: Umschreibung of an EU licence into a German one
costs.note: Official fee for issuing the German Führerschein; the photo is paid for separately.

costs.label: Biometric photo
costs.note: At a photo studio or photo booth; requirements follow the biometric standard.

sources.title: Bundesministerium für Digitales und Verkehr — Führerschein aus EU/EWR

title: Exchanging a non-EU licence: Anlage 11 FeV
tldr: A licence from a country outside the EU/EEA can only be used in Germany for the first 6 months after you move (from the moment your normal residence is established, Begründung des ordentlichen Wohnsitzes) — after that you need a German entitlement (§29 FeV for visitors, an exchange under §30–31 FeV for residents). The scope of the requirements is set by the annex Anlage 11 to the FeV: for some countries it is a full exchange with no tests, for others a theory test only, for others theory and practical. For Russia, Belarus and Ukraine there is NO full test-free exchange — tests must be taken (always check the current scope against Anlage 11). During the first 6 months an official translation of the document (Übersetzung) or an international driving permit will come in handy.

steps.title: The 6-month window: the most important deadline

content.text: If you have moved to Germany from a country outside the EU/EEA and established permanent residence, your foreign licence is only valid here for 6 months (under §29 FeV). After that you may no longer drive on it — you need a German entitlement (an exchange, Umschreibung, or a new licence).

items: The 6 months count from the moment your normal residence (ordentlicher Wohnsitz) is established, usually from registration/moving in
During these 6 months the licence is valid for the relevant categories
Many authorities require an official translation (Übersetzung) of the licence or an international permit
Translations are done by ADAC, sworn translators or consular services
In exceptional cases the 6 months are extended to 12 (for example, if it is clear in advance that the stay will be ≤12 months)

content.text: Once the 6 months expire, driving on a non-EU licence counts as driving without a licence (Fahren ohne Fahrerlaubnis) — that is a criminal offence (§21 StVG), not a fine. Start the exchange procedure early; do not wait until the deadline runs out.

steps.title: Anlage 11 FeV: three categories of countries

content.text: The scope of the requirements when exchanging depends on the country that issued the licence and is set by the annex Anlage 11 to the FeV. Countries are divided into groups.

For a number of countries (for example, Switzerland, Japan, South Korea, certain US states and Canadian provinces) the exchange happens with no theory or practical — the licence is exchanged directly.
For some countries you only need to pass the theory test (Theorieprüfung); the practical is not required.

For countries not listed in Anlage 11 with concessions, both a theory test and a practical driving test (praktische Prüfung) are required. Russia, Belarus and Ukraine generally fall into this group — there is NO full test-free exchange for them, tests are required. Always check the exact scope for your specific country and category against the current Anlage 11.

Anlage 11 changes periodically (countries and conditions are reviewed). Before you start, be sure to check the current version on gesetze-im-internet.de and confirm with your driving licence authority (Fahrerlaubnisbehörde) — for your country and category the requirements may differ from the general expectation.

The exchange (Umschreibung) is submitted to the driving licence authority (Fahrerlaubnisbehörde). If tests are required, the authority issues a permit to sit them, and the theory/practical are administered by TÜV/Dekra; you usually take a few lessons at a driving school (Fahrschule) before the practical.

items: Application for the exchange (Umschreibung) to the driving licence authority + an appointment booking
Passport/residence permit + a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
The original foreign licence + an official translation (Übersetzung), e.g. from ADAC
A biometric photo (35×45 mm)
An eye test (Sehtest) at an optician/doctor
A first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe-Kurs), if required
If needed — a theory test (Theorieprüfung) and/or practical test via TÜV/Dekra

costs.label: Umschreibung (official fee)
costs.note: For issuing the German Führerschein at the exchange.

costs.label: Tests (theory + practical, if required)
costs.note: TÜV/Dekra fees + the minimum lessons at a Fahrschule; depends on the number of attempts and lessons.

costs.label: Licence translation, Sehtest, Erste-Hilfe, photo
costs.note: Übersetzung (ADAC/sworn translator) + eye test + first-aid course + biometric photo.

sources.title: Bundesministerium für Digitales und Verkehr — Umschreibung ausländischer Fahrerlaubnisse (Nicht-EU)

title: Getting a licence from scratch: Fahrschule
tldr: If you get a licence from scratch, you need to enrol at a driving school (Fahrschule). For the passenger-car category B the path is standard: an eye test (Sehtest), a first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe-Kurs), a biometric photo, an application to the driving licence authority (Fahrerlaubnisbehörde), then mandatory theory and practical lessons, after which you sit the theory test (Theorieprüfung) and the practical driving test (praktische Prüfung) at TÜV/Dekra. The total cost has been rising and now usually comes to 2500–4500 €, sometimes higher in big cities. You can get category B from age 17 under accompanied driving (Begleitetes Fahren, BF17).

steps.title: Preliminary steps before the driving school

content.text: Before getting behind the wheel with an instructor, you need to put together a basic set of documents and submit an application for the entitlement (Antrag auf Erteilung der Fahrerlaubnis) to the driving licence authority (Fahrerlaubnisbehörde). The driving school (Fahrschule) itself often helps prepare the paperwork.

items: An eye test (Sehtest) at an optician or doctor (valid for a limited time)
A first-aid course (Erste-Hilfe-Kurs) — usually 9 teaching units, one day
A biometric photo (35×45 mm)
National ID card (Personalausweis)/passport + proof of registration
An application to the driving licence authority (can be done via the driving school)
The minimum age for category B is 17 (BF17) or 18

content.text: Training for category B is tightly regulated: there is a mandatory minimum number of theory hours and mandatory special drives (Sonderfahrten) that cannot be skipped.

items: Mandatory minimum: 12 double lessons of basic theory + 2 for category B (basic and additional material, Grund- und Zusatzstoff)
In parallel you study the questions for the theory test (Theorieprüfung), and you can practise in apps
The theory test is taken on a computer at TÜV/Dekra; versions are available in various languages
Regular driving lessons — the number is individual, until you are ready
Mandatory special drives (Sonderfahrten): 5 overland (Überland), 4 on the motorway (Autobahn), 3 at night (Nachtfahrten) — 12 in total
Without the completed special drives you will not be admitted to the practical driving test (praktische Prüfung)

content.text: First you take the theory test (Theorieprüfung), then the practical driving test (praktische Prüfung) with a TÜV/Dekra examiner. Once you pass, you receive a German driving licence (Führerschein).

items: The theory test is taken on a computer; if you fail, you retake it for an additional fee
The practical test is a drive with an examiner (about 55 minutes for B)
The total cost depends heavily on the number of driving lessons and attempts
BF17 (accompanied driving, Begleitetes Fahren ab 17): you can get the licence at 17 and drive only with a registered accompanying person until you turn 18

content.text: Driving-school prices have risen noticeably: a budget of 2500–4500 € is a rough guide, and in big cities (Munich, Hamburg, Berlin) the final figure is often higher. The main factor is the number of practical lessons, so realistically set aside a buffer above the minimum estimate.

costs.label: Full category B course (Fahrschule)
costs.note: Includes the school's base fee, lessons and preparation; can be higher in big cities.

costs.label: Sehtest + Erste-Hilfe-Kurs + biometric photo
costs.note: Eye test (~6–10 €), first-aid course (~30–50 €), photo (~10–15 €).

costs.label: Test fees (TÜV/Dekra) + official fee
costs.note: Theory and practical separately; retakes are paid for again. Usually included in the overall estimate.

sources.title: ADAC — Führerschein machen: Ablauf, Kosten, Dauer
Bundesministerium für Digitales und Verkehr — Fahrerlaubnis und Führerschein

title: Umweltplakette: the green zone
tldr: Many German cities have low-emission zones (Umweltzonen) that you can only enter with a valid emissions sticker — the Umweltplakette (Feinstaubplakette). In practice a green (grüne) sticker is required almost everywhere — that is group 4, the cleanest. The sticker is fixed to the windscreen and tied to a specific number plate. You can get it at TÜV, Dekra, GTÜ, at the vehicle registration authority (Zulassungsstelle) or at many garages. It costs roughly 6–20 €. Entering a low-emission zone without a sticker, or with the wrong one, means a fine (Bußgeld) of 100 €.

steps.title: What the Umweltplakette and the zones are

content.text: The emissions sticker (Umweltplakette, officially Feinstaubplakette) is a round sticker on the windscreen that shows the car's emissions class. The colour depends on the group: red (2), yellow (3) and green (4). Green is the cleanest and practically the only one that currently grants entry to active low-emission zones (Umweltzonen).

items: Low-emission zones are marked with an 'Umwelt ZONE' road sign showing the permitted colours
Almost all active zones require the green (grüne) sticker specifically
The class is determined by emissions standards (Schadstoffgruppe) from the car's papers
Most modern petrol and diesel cars (Euro 4+ / with a filter) qualify for the green one
The sticker is tied to a specific number plate (Kennzeichen) and is not transferable to another car

steps.title: Where and how to get it

content.text: Getting the emissions sticker is quick and easy — all you need is the car's papers. A physical inspection is usually not required, since the class is already recorded in the registration certificate (Zulassungsbescheinigung).

items: Where to get it: TÜV, Dekra, GTÜ, the vehicle registration authority (Zulassungsstelle), many garages (Werkstätten) and petrol stations
All you need is the vehicle document (Fahrzeugschein) / registration certificate (Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil I)
You can order it online (sent by post) from TÜV/Dekra and other services
The cost is usually 6–20 € depending on where you get it
The sticker is applied to the inside of the windscreen, with the number plate written on it

content.text: Enforcement is based on the sticker: entering a low-emission zone without a suitable sticker carries a fixed fine.

items: An administrative fine (Bußgeld) for entering a low-emission zone without a valid green sticker — 100 €
The fine is the same for local and foreign cars — foreigners also need a sticker
If the car does not reach the green class, exemptions/permits (Ausnahmegenehmigung) may be available from the city
The sticker must not be forged or displayed with someone else's number plate — that is a separate offence

content.text: Foreign tourists and newcomers often think the zones do not apply to them — they do. A low-emission zone applies to everyone; entering without a green sticker is punished with a 100 € fine in Germany.

costs.label: Green Umweltplakette
costs.note: A one-off purchase; the price depends on where you get it (TÜV/Dekra/garage/online).

costs.label: Bußgeld for entering without a sticker
costs.note: A fixed fine for breaching the Umweltzone rules.

sources.title: ADAC — Umweltplakette und Umweltzonen: Regeln und Bußgelder

title: Winter tyres: situative Winterreifenpflicht
tldr: Germany has no rigid calendar rule of 'winter tyres from this date to that date'. A situational winter-tyre obligation (situative Winterreifenpflicht) applies under §2 (3a) StVO: in winter road conditions — black ice (Glatteis), packed snow (Schneeglätte), slush (Schneematsch), icy or frost-induced slipperiness — you may only drive on tyres suitable for winter. The recognised marking is the snowflake-on-a-mountain symbol (Alpine-Symbol, 3PMSF); the old M+S marking is only valid for tyres produced before the end of 2017, as a transitional rule. The popular rule of thumb is 'O bis O' (von Oktober bis Ostern). A breach means an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of 60–120 € and points in Flensburg.

content.text: The key difference between Germany and many other countries: the winter-tyre obligation is not calendar-based but situational. Under §2 (3a) StVO winter tyres are needed not 'by date' but whenever the road is in winter conditions.

items: Winter tyres are mandatory in: black ice (Glatteis)
Packed snow (Schneeglätte)
Slush (Schneematsch)
Icy slipperiness (Eisglätte)
Frost-induced slipperiness (Reifglätte)
If none of these conditions are present — you may formally drive on summer tyres too, but the weather changes quickly

content.text: Since there is no calendar ban, drivers follow the popular rule 'O bis O' — von Oktober bis Ostern (from October to Easter), keeping winter tyres on. This is not a law but a practical habit under the situational rule.

steps.title: Which tyres count as winter tyres

content.text: Not just any tyre with a label will do. The law requires specifically winter-capable tyres with the correct marking.

items: The main sign is the snowflake-on-a-mountain symbol (Alpine-Symbol / 3PMSF / Bergpiktogramm)
The old M+S marking was only recognised as a transitional rule for tyres produced before 31.12.2017; they could only be used until 30.09.2024 — that deadline has passed
Winter and all-season tyres with the 3PMSF symbol are suitable
Tread depth: the legal minimum is 1,6 mm, but for winter at least 4 mm is recommended
Studs (Spikes) are mostly banned in Germany, except for border-area exceptions

content.text: M+S marking without the snowflake is no longer enough on new tyres — the transitional rule for M+S tyres has ended. Check the sidewall for the snowflake-on-a-mountain symbol (Alpine-Symbol, 3PMSF).
Breaching the situational obligation is punishable, and the amounts depend on whether you caused an obstruction or a hazard.

items: Driving without winter tyres in winter conditions — an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of 60 €
If you obstructed traffic (Behinderung) — 80 €
If you created a hazard (Gefährdung) — 100 €, or with an accident/crash — 120 €
In all 'aggravated' cases — 1 point in Flensburg (the driver fitness register, Fahreignungsregister)
The vehicle's owner (Halter) who allowed such driving of their car can also be fined (75 €)

content.text: Beyond the fine there is an insurance risk: in an accident in winter conditions on summer tyres, comprehensive insurance (Kasko) may cut the payout for gross negligence (grobe Fahrlässigkeit), and part of the blame may be placed on you.

costs.label: Set of winter tyres (4 pcs.)
costs.note: Depends on size and brand; tyres on rims and premium brands cost more.

costs.label: Bußgeld for a breach (range)
costs.note: 60 € base; up to 100–120 € if you create a hazard/accident, plus 1 point in Flensburg.

sources.title: Bundesministerium für Digitales und Verkehr — Winterreifen und Alpine-Symbol

title: Open a current account (Girokonto): step by step
tldr: A current account (Girokonto) is the main account without which, in Germany, you cannot be paid a salary, sign a lease or set up SEPA debits (insurance, phone, electricity). You can open an account two ways: at a classic bank (Sparkasse, Volksbank, Deutsche Bank) or at a neobank/online bank (N26, ING, DKB, C24). To open one you need a passport or a national ID card (Personalausweis), usually a residence registration (Anmeldung) and a tax identification number (Steuer-ID); some neobanks do not require a registered address. Identification is done via PostIdent (at the post office) or VideoIdent (a video call from your smartphone). Almost all banks run a SCHUFA query (the largest credit bureau) — except the basic account (Basiskonto), which they are obliged to open for everyone. A basic Girokonto costs from 0 to 10 € a month.

steps.title: Why you need a Girokonto and which to choose

content.text: A current account (Girokonto, from the Italian giro — circulation) is a checking account for everyday transactions: receiving your salary, paying rent, and setting up regular debits via SEPA-Lastschrift and SEPA-Überweisung transfers. Without it you effectively cannot function normally in Germany: an employer transfers your salary only to an account, the landlord and insurance companies collect payments via direct debit (Lastschrift), and many services stopped accepting cash long ago.

The fundamental choice is between a classic bank with branches (Filialbank: branches and a personal advisor, but a monthly fee of 5-10 €/month) and an online bank/neobank (Direktbank: everything in the app, often 0 €/month). For newcomers neobanks are more convenient: N26 and C24 open in 10-15 minutes via the app, sometimes even without a residence registration (Anmeldung). ING and DKB are large online banks with a free account under certain conditions (for example, a monthly salary deposit).

items: Cost: from 0 €/month (neobanks, ING/DKB with an incoming salary) to 10 €/month (a bank with branches)
Time to open: 10-30 minutes online (neobank) or 1-3 days at a branch
What you get: an IBAN (DExx...), a German debit Girocard (the former EC-Karte) and/or a debit Visa/Mastercard
Whether you need a registered address: usually yes; N26 and some neobanks open without a registration (Anmeldung)
SCHUFA query: almost always (the exception is the basic account, Basiskonto)

content.text: A debit Girocard and a credit card are not the same thing. Many neobanks issue only a debit Visa/Mastercard by default, with no classic German Girocard. Some landlords, doctors' practices and machines (for example, in car parks) accept the Girocard only. If you need it, check this before opening the account.

The minimum set barely varies from bank to bank. The main obstacle for newcomers is the tax identification number (Steuer-ID) and the residence registration (Anmeldung): the first arrives by letter after your first registration, the second is done at the district citizens' service (Bürgeramt). Without them some banks will not open an account or will limit its functions (for example, they will not let you invest).

items: A valid passport OR an EU national ID card (Personalausweis) (for VideoIdent — mandatory with a machine-readable zone)
Confirmation of registration (Anmeldebestätigung) — required by most banks
Tax identification number (Steuer-Identifikationsnummer, 11 digits) — the bank is obliged to report interest data to the tax office (Finanzamt)
A German phone number and email — for SMS-TAN and access
For students/some tariffs: a university certificate or proof of income

content.text: If your tax identification number has not arrived yet, many banks let you open an account and submit the number later, but without it they may not run a church tax (Kirchensteuer) check or apply a tax exemption on interest (Freistellungsauftrag). Do not open an account on a tourist visa intending to stay illegally — the bank checks your residence status, and false information leads to the account being blocked.
Under the German anti-money-laundering law (Geldwäschegesetz, GwG) the bank is obliged to identify the customer in person. There are two methods, and you usually choose during the application.

items: A video call with an agent right from the bank's app (5-10 minutes)
You need a passport/national ID card (Personalausweis) and good lighting
The agent will ask you to turn the document, and will check the holograms and a code read aloud
Usually available from 8:00 to 22:00, in German and often English
The account is activated immediately after a successful check

items.title: 2. PostIdent — via a Deutsche Post branch

items: The bank sends a PostIdent-Coupon (on paper or as a QR code in the app)
You go to any Deutsche Post branch with your passport
The clerk checks the document and sends confirmation to the bank
Free for the customer; the account is activated within 1-3 business days
Convenient if you have poor internet or no smartphone with a camera

content.text: For VideoIdent the document must be internationally recognised and undamaged. With some kinds of residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel card) VideoIdent may not go through — in that case choose PostIdent or the eID on a national ID card (Personalausweis). Never go through "identification" via links in emails supposedly from the bank: that is phishing.

steps.title: After opening: what to set up

content.text: Once you have the IBAN, give it to your employer (for your salary) straight away and switch your regular payments to the new account. Many banks offer an account-switching service (Kontowechselservice) — automatic transfer of all direct debits (Lastschrift) and incoming payments from the old account.

items: Give the IBAN to your employer, landlord and insurers (a direct-debit mandate, Lastschrift-Mandat)
Order a Girocard if you need it (often paid/optional)
Set card limits and push notifications for debits
Submit a tax exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) of 1 000 € (the tax-free allowance for savers, Sparerpauschbetrag) if you will hold savings/investments
Save your access credentials and enable two-factor authentication (pushTAN/photoTAN)

content.text: Check the conditions for a fee-free tariff: at ING, DKB and a number of banks the account is free only with a monthly income deposit (for example, from 700 € of deposits, Geldeingang). If there are no deposits, a monthly fee will appear from the following month. Read the price and services list (Preis- und Leistungsverzeichnis) carefully before signing.

costs.label: Girokonto at a neobank / online bank
costs.note: N26 Standard, C24, ING and DKB are free (sometimes with an income deposit); premium tariffs cost more.

costs.label: Girokonto at a Filialbank (Sparkasse, Volksbank)
costs.note: Monthly fee for branches and a personal advisor.

costs.label: PostIdent / VideoIdent
costs.note: Identification is free for the customer; the bank pays.

costs.label: Girocard (physical card)
costs.note: At some neobanks it is issued for an extra fee; at a Filialbank it is usually included in the tariff.

title: Basiskonto: the right to an account for everyone
tldr: A basic account (Basiskonto) is the right — enshrined in § 31 Zahlungskontengesetz (ZKG) — of anyone legally residing in the EU to a payment account. Every bank that offers ordinary current accounts (Girokonto) to private individuals is obliged to open a basic account for everyone — including people without permanent housing (obdachlos), asylum seekers (Asylsuchende), people with temporary status, and even those with a poor SCHUFA. It is an account with basic functions: transfers, direct debit (Lastschrift), a card, cash withdrawals — but usually without an overdraft (Dispo). The bank may not refuse without a lawful reason; an unjustified refusal can be reported to BaFin. The fee must be "reasonable" (angemessen) — in practice around 3-7 €/month. The application is submitted on a special form, and the bank must respond within 10 business days.

content.text: Since 2016, Germany has had a payment accounts act (Zahlungskontengesetz, ZKG), implementing the European Payment Accounts Directive. §31 ZKG states directly: every consumer legally residing in the EU has the right to a basic payment account (Basiskonto). The law also covers people with no fixed address, asylum seekers, and people with a deportation deferral (Duldung) — in some cases even without a valid passport.

The key difference from an ordinary current account (Girokonto): the bank cannot refuse on the grounds of a poor credit history or lack of income. A SCHUFA query (the largest credit bureau) for a basic account generally does not block the opening — the account must be opened even with negative entries. It is a "basic payment account contract" (Basiskontovertrag), and every bank that serves private individuals is obliged to offer it.

items: Legal basis: §§31-38 ZKG (Zahlungskontengesetz)
Who is entitled: anyone legally present in the EU, including refugees and the homeless
Functions: SEPA transfers, direct debit (Lastschrift), a debit card, cash withdrawal/deposit, online banking
What is usually not included: an overdraft (Dispokredit) and a credit card
Bank's response time: a maximum of 10 business days after a complete application

content.text: There is an official standard form for the basic account — Antrag auf Abschluss eines Basiskontovertrags. You can download it from the bank's website or from BaFin. It is important to submit exactly this form (not an ordinary current-account application, Girokonto), so that the bank handles the request under the ZKG and cannot quietly refuse.

items: Download, or pick up at the bank, the "Antrag auf ein Basiskonto" form
Attach an identity document (passport, a substitute ID Ausweisersatz, an arrival certificate Ankunftsnachweis for refugees)
If you have no permanent address — give a contact address (e.g. of a social service, a shelter, c/o)
Submit it at a branch or online; record the date of submission
Wait for a decision within 10 business days (in writing)

content.text: The bank may refuse only on lawful grounds under §§35–37 ZKG: for example, if you already have a suitable account in Germany (§35 ZKG), or in cases of proven criminal conduct/threats to staff or breaches of anti-money-laundering rules (§36 ZKG). A "poor SCHUFA" or lack of income are NOT lawful grounds. Insist that any verbal refusal be put in writing, stating the reason.

The ZKG requires the fee for a basic account to be "reasonable" (angemessen) and to take into account the market level and the customer's behaviour. In practice, after several rulings by the Federal Court of Justice (Bundesgerichtshof, BGH), banks have cut their rates: the typical price today is roughly 3-7 €/month. Excessive fees (for example, 0.99 € for each transfer on top of the monthly fee) have been ruled inadmissible for a basic account.

items: Monthly fee: on average 3-7 € (banks vary — compare them)
Transfers and direct debit (Lastschrift) are included in the basic functionality
Cash withdrawals at your own network's ATMs at no extra charge
An overdraft (Dispo) is usually unavailable — the account cannot go into the negative
A debit card (Girocard or Visa/Mastercard Debit) is provided

content.text: Before opening one, compare the basic-account rates of different banks — the spread is large. Verbraucherzentrale regularly publishes overviews. If a bank charges a clearly excessive fee or imposes penalties for each transaction, you can challenge this by citing the BGH rulings on the "reasonableness" of the fee.

steps.title: If the bank refuses: a complaint to BaFin

content.text: An unjustified refusal or delay is grounds for a free complaint to BaFin (the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority, Bundesanstalt für Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht). BaFin runs a special administrative procedure (Verwaltungsverfahren): the authority reviews the refusal and can order the bank to open the account. In parallel, you can go to court (the conciliation body Schlichtungsstelle or the civil court Zivilgericht).

items: Collect the bank's written refusal (or prove that the bank is not responding within the 10-day deadline)
Fill in on bafin.de the form "Antrag auf Durchführung eines Verwaltungsverfahrens Basiskonto"
Attach a copy of your application and documents
Submit it online or by letter — the procedure is free
BaFin will issue a decision; the bank must comply with it

content.text: Do not stay silent if you are refused: many people mistakenly think that a "poor SCHUFA" deprives them of the right to an account. That is not so — §31 ZKG protects exactly these people. Keep all correspondence with the bank; you will need it for the complaint to BaFin.

costs.label: Basiskonto — monthly fee
costs.note: The law requires a "reasonable" (angemessen) fee — § 41 ZKG. Banks' rates vary, so compare them.

costs.label: Application and the Antrag auf Basiskonto form
costs.note: Submitting the application is free; the form is provided by the bank or BaFin.

costs.label: Complaint to BaFin in case of refusal
costs.note: BaFin's administrative procedure is free for the consumer.

sources.title: Gesetze im Internet — Zahlungskontengesetz (ZKG), §31 Anspruch auf Basiskonto
BaFin — Basiskonto: Recht auf ein Konto für jedermann

title: Trade Republic, Scalable: brokers
tldr: Trade Republic and Scalable Capital are the two largest German neobank brokers for investing in stocks, ETFs and crypto straight from your phone. Trade Republic charges a flat 1 € per trade (a flat third-party cost fee, Fremdkostenpauschale) and runs regular savings plans (Sparpläne) for free; it holds its own German banking licence. Scalable Capital works on two models: FREE Broker (1 € per trade) and the paid PRIME subscription (from ~4.99 €/month) with free trading. Both are regulated by BaFin, and clients' money is protected by the deposit guarantee scheme (Einlagensicherung, up to 100,000 € per partner bank), while securities are segregated assets (Sondervermögen), kept separate from the broker's own assets. This is an easy, cheap and legal way for a beginner to start investing.

steps.title: What these brokers are and how they differ

content.text: Trade Republic and Scalable Capital are so-called next-generation brokers (Neobroker): brokers with no branches, where everything happens in the app. They are radically cheaper than classic bank securities accounts (where a trade could cost 10-25 €). This has made investing accessible to anyone who puts aside 25-50 € a month.

items: Flat third-party cost fee (Fremdkostenpauschale) of 1 € for each buy/sell
ETF and stock savings plans (Sparpläne) — free
Its own German banking licence (a full bank, Vollbank)
Interest on your cash balance (varies with the ECB rate)
Trading via the LS Exchange / partners
FREE Broker: 1 € per trade, no subscription fee
PRIME subscription (from ~4.99 €/month): commission-free trades subject to conditions
Wide choice of ETF savings plans (Sparpläne), including free ones
Also offers a robo-advisor (managed portfolio) separately
Securities institution licence (Wertpapierinstitut), with partner banks holding the cash

content.text: For a beginner with small amounts and regular contributions, Trade Republic or Scalable FREE Broker (no subscription fee) is usually the better deal. Scalable's PRIME subscription only pays off if you trade large amounts frequently.

steps.title: Regulation and the safety of your money

content.text: Both brokers are regulated by BaFin (the German financial supervisor) and the Bundesbank (the German central bank). This means that clients' money and the custody of securities are subject to strict rules. Understanding the two protection mechanisms matters for a beginner's peace of mind.

items: Deposit guarantee scheme (Einlagensicherung): cash is insured up to 100,000 € per client at each partner bank
Securities (stocks, ETFs) are segregated assets (Sondervermögen): if the broker goes bankrupt they remain yours and are not part of the insolvency estate
The broker cannot "spend" your shares — it merely holds them at a custodian
BaFin supervision: brokers file reports and undergo audits
Access is protected by PIN/biometrics and confirmation of transactions

content.text: The deposit guarantee scheme (Einlagensicherung) covers only cash, not a drop in the value of your investments. If an ETF loses value, that is market risk, and no insurance compensates for it. Also keep in mind: "crypto" at these brokers is often not real coins in your wallet but a derivative product — read the description.

steps.title: How to open a securities account

content.text: Opening a brokerage account (Wertpapierdepot) is technically similar to opening a current account (Girokonto): everything is in the app, with identification via VideoIdent or eID. You will need your tax identification number (Steuer-ID), because the broker automatically withholds capital gains tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) and reports to the tax office (Finanzamt).

items: Download the app (Trade Republic / Scalable Capital) and complete registration
Have your passport/national ID card (Personalausweis), tax identification number (Steuer-ID) and a German IBAN for funding ready
Complete VideoIdent or eID identification
Submit an exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) for 1,000 € (the saver's allowance, Sparerpauschbetrag) so that profit up to that amount is tax-free
Fund the account by SEPA transfer and make your first purchase or set up a savings plan (Sparplan)

content.text: Be sure to give the broker an exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) — up to 1,000 € per person, 2,000 € for married couples filing jointly. Without it the broker will withhold 25% withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) plus the solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) from the very first euro of profit you earn, and you would have to reclaim the overpayment through your tax return. Do not invest money you will need in the next 1-2 years.

costs.label: Trade Republic — per trade
costs.note: Flat Fremdkostenpauschale per buy/sell; Sparpläne are free.

costs.label: Scalable Capital — FREE Broker trade
costs.note: No subscription fee; 1 € per trade, many Sparpläne are free.

costs.label: Scalable Capital — PRIME subscription
costs.note: About 4.99 €/month; commission-free trades when the conditions are met. Pays off with frequent trading.

costs.label: Opening and maintaining a securities account
costs.note: The securities account itself is free at both brokers.

sources.title: Trade Republic — official website (Gebühren und Lizenz)
Scalable Capital — Broker Preise und PRIME
