title: ETF-Sparplan: investing for beginners
tldr: An ETF-Sparplan is a plan for regular, automatic investing into an exchange-traded index fund (ETF), for example the MSCI World, which with a single instrument spreads your money across ~1,500 companies worldwide. You set up a debit of 1-25 € a month, and the broker buys fund units for you — this is the most popular way for beginners in Germany to build wealth over the long term. The key point about taxes: profit (price gains, Kursgewinne, and dividends) is subject to withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% + the solidarity surcharge (Soli), but a saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag) applies — 1,000 € of profit per year is tax-free (set up an exemption order, Freistellungsauftrag). An important German peculiarity is the advance lump-sum tax (Vorabpauschale): tax may be charged on the fund's "assumed" return even before you sell. There is a distinction between reinvesting (thesaurierend) and dividend-paying (ausschüttend) ETFs.

content.text: An ETF (Exchange Traded Fund) is a fund that replicates the composition of a stock index. By buying a single ETF unit tracking the MSCI World index, you are effectively investing in the shares of ~1,500 of the largest companies in developed countries all at once. A savings plan (Sparplan) is the automation: you set the amount (for example, 50 €) and the day of the month once, and each time the broker buys ETF units for you, including fractional ones.

The principle is powerful for two reasons. The first is diversification: the risk of one company falling is spread across thousands. The second is the cost-averaging effect (Cost-Average-Effekt): by buying regularly, you pick up units both when prices are high and when they are low, averaging out your entry price. Over a horizon of 10-15+ years this has historically been one of the most reliable ways to grow capital, accessible even with small amounts.

items: Minimum contribution: from 1 € (Trade Republic) up to 25 € a month at various brokers
Popular ETFs for a core holding: MSCI World, FTSE All-World, MSCI ACWI
Execution fee: 0% (free savings plans) up to ~1.5% per debit
Horizon: at least 10 years is recommended, to ride out drawdowns
What you need: a brokerage account (securities account) + tax identification number (Steuer-ID)

content.text: By how they handle dividends, ETFs fall into two types, and the choice affects taxes and convenience.

items: Dividends are automatically reinvested back into the fund
Convenient for long-term saving — compounding works on its own
No need to reinvest payouts manually
The advance lump-sum tax (Vorabpauschale) most often applies to this type
Dividends arrive in your account as cash (for example, quarterly)
Convenient if you want a passive cash flow
Payouts help you "use up" the annual saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag) of 1,000 €
You have to reinvest the payouts manually (or via a new savings plan, Sparplan)

content.text: For pure long-term saving, many people choose the reinvesting type (thesaurierend) — fewer moving parts. To use up the tax allowance every year, the distributing type (ausschüttend) is more convenient. The type has little effect on the final return — the main thing is to start at all and not interrupt the plan.

Capital gains (capital income, Kapitalerträge) in Germany are subject to withholding tax on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% + the solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag, 5.5% of the tax) + church tax (Kirchensteuer) where applicable. This is governed by §20 EStG. But there are two things a beginner needs to understand first.

items: Saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag): the first 1,000 € of profit per year per person (2,000 € for married couples) is tax-free
For the allowance to work automatically, give the broker an exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) for 1,000 €
Without an exemption order the broker withholds tax from the first euro, and you can only reclaim it via your tax return
The tax is withheld automatically (withholding tax, Quellensteuer) — the broker sends it to the tax office (Finanzamt) itself
Legal basis: §20 EStG (Einkünfte aus Kapitalvermögen)

content.text: The advance lump-sum tax (Vorabpauschale) is a frequent surprise for beginners. It is an "advance" tax on a notional minimum return of the fund (the base rate Basiszins set by the Bundesbank), which can be debited at the start of the year BEFORE you actually sell any units. If there is no free cash in your account at the broker, the broker may debit the advance lump-sum tax and your cash balance goes "into the red". Keep a small cash balance in your brokerage account in January to avoid trouble. The advance lump-sum tax you pay is later credited when you sell.

An ETF-Sparplan is an investment, not savings: its value can fall. Do not invest money you will need in the next 1-2 years, and do not panic during drawdowns — selling at the bottom locks in your loss. This is not financial advice; for large amounts, consult an independent fee-based advisor (Honorarberater).

costs.label: Minimum monthly contribution
costs.note: From 1 € at Trade Republic up to 25 € at some banks; there is no upper limit.

costs.label: Sparplan execution fee
costs.note: 0% at neobanks (free plans) up to ~1.5% of the debited amount at some banks.

costs.label: Tax on profit above the allowance
costs.note: Abgeltungsteuer 25% + Soli applies to profit above the 1,000 € Sparerpauschbetrag (§20 EStG).

sources.title: Gesetze im Internet — EStG §20 (Einkünfte aus Kapitalvermögen)

title: Transfers abroad: Wise, Revolut
tldr: For international transfers out of Germany, a classic bank SWIFT transfer is almost always a bad deal: the bank hides 3-5% in a poor exchange rate, plus fixed fees and correspondent-bank charges. Wise (formerly TransferWise) and Revolut exchange currency at the real interbank rate (mid-market rate) and charge a transparent fee of ~0.4-1% of the amount — several times cheaper. Wise is a multi-currency account with local account details in dozens of countries; Revolut operates on a banking licence in Lithuania (EEA), which provides European deposit protection. Both are regulated by financial supervisors: Wise's services in the EEA are provided by Wise Europe SA, licensed as a payment institution by the National Bank of Belgium (NBB); in the UK, Wise is regulated by the FCA. Revolut in the EU operates through its bank in Lithuania (supervised by the Bank of Lithuania). They are well suited for freelancer salaries, transfers to family and paying abroad.

steps.title: Why a bank SWIFT transfer is expensive

content.text: When you make an international transfer through an ordinary German bank, the visible fee (say, 15-25 €) is only part of the cost. The main loss is hidden in the exchange rate: the bank sets a rate with a 2-4% markup over the real market rate. On a transfer of 1,000 € that is 30-40 € you lose, which is easy to overlook at first glance.

items: Hidden markup on the exchange rate (Wechselkursaufschlag): usually 2-4% at banks
Fixed SWIFT transfer fee: 10-25 €
Correspondent-bank charges: sometimes an extra 10-30 € along the way
Time: 1-5 business days
Total real cost: often 3-5% of the transferred amount

steps.title: Wise and Revolut: how they differ

items: Exchange at the real interbank rate (mid-market rate)
Transparent fee of ~0.4-1% of the amount, shown in advance
Local account details (IBAN, account number) in dozens of currencies
You can hold and convert 40+ currencies
In the EEA — Wise Europe SA (payment institution licence, supervised by NBB Belgium); in the UK — FCA
Banking licence in Lithuania — deposit protection within the EEA (up to 100,000 €)
Free exchange limit on weekdays, with a markup on weekends/above the limit
Paid plans (Premium/Metal) raise the limits
Card, virtual cards, budgets, crypto (as a product)
Convenient for frequent travel and paying abroad

content.text: For a one-off large transfer (for example, to family or to buy property), Wise is usually the better deal: a transparent percentage and local account details in the recipient's country. Revolut is more convenient as an everyday multi-currency card while travelling. Many people use both: Wise for transfers, Revolut for spending.

steps.title: How to make a transfer and what to keep in mind

content.text: Signing up with Wise/Revolut is like signing up with a neobank: app, passport, VideoIdent. The transfer takes minutes: you fund the account by SEPA transfer from your current account (Girokonto), choose the recipient's currency, and see the final amount and fee in advance.

items: Register and complete identification (passport/national ID card, Personalausweis)
Fund the account by SEPA transfer from a German IBAN (cheaper than by card)
Enter the recipient's details and check the rate + fee BEFORE confirming
Compare the total with your bank — usually the savings are several times over
Keep the transfer confirmation (for your records, if it is income)

content.text: Large or regular transfers (especially outside the EU) may come under review under the anti-money-laundering law (Geldwäschegesetz) — the service is entitled to ask about the origin of the funds. This is normal: have your documents ready (contract, payslip). Wise is a payment institution, not a classic bank: the money is held separately (safeguarding) but is not covered everywhere by a deposit guarantee scheme (Einlagensicherung) the way it is at a bank; for Revolut in the EU the Lithuanian deposit protection scheme applies. Do not keep large amounts in payment accounts as you would on a deposit.

costs.label: Wise — transfer fee
costs.note: About 0.4-1% of the amount at the mid-market rate; the exact fee is shown in advance.

costs.label: Revolut — currency exchange
costs.note: Free on weekdays within the limit; a markup on weekends and above the limit/plan.

costs.label: Classic bank SWIFT (for comparison)
costs.note: Plus a hidden 2-4% markup on the rate: the total cost is often 3-5% of the amount.

title: Schufa: free data copy (Datenkopie)
tldr: Under Article 15 GDPR (DSGVO), everyone has the right to find out free of charge what data the SCHUFA credit bureau holds about them. This free report is called the data copy (Datenkopie, formerly «Datenkopie nach Art. 15 DSGVO», and before that the self-disclosure, Selbstauskunft). Don't confuse it with the paid creditworthiness report (BonitätsAuskunft) for 29,95 € — that one is a document to show your landlord. You request the data copy for free at meineschufa.de; it arrives online or by post and lists all your records and your score (from 17 March 2026 onward on the new 100–999 scale, instead of the old base score Basisscore of 0–100%). It's worth checking at least once a year: a third of files contain errors that lower your score and can cost you a rental or a loan. You have the right to dispute any inaccuracies for free — SCHUFA is required to check and correct them.

content.text: SCHUFA offers several products, and it's easy to overpay by mistake. The key is to tell the free right apart from the paid service.

items: A right under Article 15 GDPR: free of charge
Contains all stored data + your score (new 100–999 scale from 17.03.2026) + the sources of inquiries
For your own review and for correcting errors
NOT intended as a document for your landlord
Can be requested regularly (at least once a year for free)
A paid document (about 29,95 €)
Nicely formatted — to show your landlord (Vermieter) when renting
Contains only positive/neutral data for presentation
Needed when a landlord specifically demands a rental report

content.text: On the SCHUFA website the paid products are more prominent than the free data copy, whose link sometimes takes some searching to find. To check your own data, what you need is precisely the free data copy (Datenkopie), not the paid creditworthiness report. Only pay if a landlord explicitly demands a rental report.

steps.title: How to request the free data copy (Datenkopie)

content.text: You submit the request online at meineschufa.de or by post. To verify your identity, SCHUFA will ask for a copy of an identity document. After the check, the report arrives in your online account or by post.

items: Go to meineschufa.de and find «Datenkopie (nach Art. 15 DSGVO)»
Fill in the form: name, date of birth, current and previous addresses
Attach a copy of your passport or national ID card (Personalausweis) to confirm your identity
Choose to receive it online (faster) or by post
Wait for the report — usually anywhere from a few days to a couple of weeks

content.text: List all your previous addresses from recent years — otherwise SCHUFA may fail to match some of the records. Don't pay anything at this step: requesting the data copy under Art. 15 DSGVO is free. Beware of third-party sites that imitate SCHUFA and charge for a «free» report.

Once you receive the report, check every line. Common errors: a long-paid debt still marked as open; someone else's record matched to you by name; an old address with strangers' data attached to it; contracts you closed long ago.

items: Cross-check the list of contracts and loans — are they all yours and up to date
Check whether paid-off debts are marked as «erledigt»
Make sure there are no records tied to other addresses or people
If you find an error, send a written objection to SCHUFA with proof
SCHUFA is required to review and correct or delete incorrect data free of charge

content.text: The right under Art. 15 DSGVO only gives you information; to correct an error, use the right to rectification (Art. 16 DSGVO) and attach supporting documents (for example, a payment receipt). If SCHUFA doesn't respond, you can complain to the data protection supervisory authority (Datenschutzbehörde) — that's free too.

costs.label: Datenkopie (Art. 15 DSGVO)
costs.note: Free under the right of access to your data; at least once a year.

costs.label: Correcting errors (Art. 16 DSGVO)
costs.note: Objecting to and correcting incorrect records is free.

costs.label: BonitätsAuskunft (document for renting)
costs.note: Paid report to show your landlord; not needed for your own review.

title: Sparkasse vs Direktbank
tldr: The main choice when opening an account in Germany is a savings bank (Sparkasse) or a cooperative bank (Volksbank) versus a direct bank (Direktbank) or a neobank. A Sparkasse is a regional public-law bank with a dense network of branches and ATMs, a personal advisor and on-the-spot support, but it charges a monthly fee of ~5-10 €/month and higher transaction costs. Direct banks (Direktbank: ING, DKB, Comdirect) and neobanks (N26, C24) operate online only: the account is often free (0 €/month, sometimes only if income is paid in) and everything happens in the app, but there are no branches and no personal advisor. Your money is protected either way: a Sparkasse has its own institutional protection (Institutssicherung), while private banks have deposit insurance (Einlagensicherung) up to 100 000 €. The choice comes down to what matters more to you: in-person service and cash on site, or saving money and a convenient app.

content.text: The German banking market is split into three «pillars»: public-law (savings banks, Sparkassen), cooperative (Volksbanken/Raiffeisenbanken) and private commercial banks (including direct banks, Direktbanken, and neobanks). For a new resident the choice usually comes down to a Sparkasse (the classic option with branches) versus a direct bank or neobank (everything online).

items.title: Sparkasse / Volksbank (a bank with branches, Filialbank)

items: A regional network of branches and ATMs — cash and help nearby
A personal advisor (Berater), in-person discussion of loans and mortgages
Monthly fee ~5-10 €/month, higher transaction charges
Handy for dealing in cash, for older people and for complex matters
Protection through the institutional guarantee (Institutssicherung) of the Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe association
Everything in the app/online, no branches
Account often 0 €/month (sometimes only if income is paid in)
Quick to open, handy push notifications, free withdrawals within partner networks
Support by chat or phone, often in English
Protection through deposit insurance (Einlagensicherung) up to 100 000 €

content.text: There's no universal answer — the choice depends on your habits and your circumstances. Think about how you actually use money in Germany.

items: Often need cash or need to deposit cash into your account → Sparkasse (ATMs and tellers nearby)
Value saving money and do everything on your phone → direct bank or neobank (0 €/month)
Planning a mortgage and want a personal advisor → Sparkasse/Volksbank
Weak German, need English-language support → some neobanks (N26)
Need a classic German debit card (Girocard) for machines and medical practices → check first: neobanks often don't offer one

content.text: The «free» condition at direct banks often applies only if income is paid in every month (Geldeingang, for example from 700 €). If you have no regular incoming payments (a student, or a freelancer with irregular income), the account can become chargeable — read the schedule of prices and services (Preis- und Leistungsverzeichnis) carefully.

steps.title: Safety of your money and switching banks

content.text: Your money is protected in both models, but the mechanisms differ. Private banks have deposit insurance (Einlagensicherung) — by law up to 100 000 € per customer per bank (many private banks additionally belong to a voluntary fund with higher coverage). Sparkassen and Volksbanken use an institutional guarantee (Institutssicherung): the association keeps the bank itself from going bankrupt, which in practice also protects deposits.

items: Private banks: statutory deposit insurance (Einlagensicherung) up to 100 000 € per customer per bank
Sparkassen/Volksbanken: institutional guarantee (Institutssicherung) — protection of the institution itself
For amounts over 100 000 €, spread them across different banks
Switching banks: use the account-switching service (Kontowechselservice) — it transfers direct debits (Lastschrift) and incoming payments for you
Switching banks often is harmless in itself, but many new account-opening inquiries can slightly affect your SCHUFA

content.text: Many newcomers open a neobank account for speed, then run into the fact that they need a German debit card (Girocard) or cash deposits, which a neobank doesn't offer. A sensible strategy is to have a main free online account and, if needed, a simple Sparkasse account for cash. Before closing your old account, make sure all direct debits (Lastschrift) and your salary have already been switched to the new IBAN.

costs.label: Sparkasse / Volksbank Girokonto
costs.note: Monthly fee for branches and an advisor; there are discounts for students and young people.

costs.label: Direktbank / neobank Girokonto
costs.note: Often 0 €/month (sometimes only if income is paid in); premium plans cost more.

costs.label: Kontowechselservice (switching banks)
costs.note: Transferring payments when switching banks is usually free.

title: GmbH vs UG: founding
tldr: The limited liability company GmbH and the mini-LLC UG (haftungsbeschränkt) are both forms of limited liability company under the GmbHG. A GmbH requires a minimum share capital (Stammkapital) of 25 000 € (at founding it's enough to pay in half — 12 500 €), notary services and an entry in the commercial register (Handelsregister); founding costs roughly 600–1000 € plus the capital itself. The UG is a «mini-GmbH»: minimum capital from 1 €, cheaper to found (300–600 €), but under §5a GmbHG it is REQUIRED to set aside 25% of annual profit into a reserve until it accumulates 25 000 € and converts into a full GmbH. Both forms cap liability at the share capital, both go through a notary and the commercial register, and both must keep double-entry bookkeeping and publish their accounts.

content.text: Both forms are governed by the Limited Liability Companies Act (Gesetz betreffend die Gesellschaften mit beschränkter Haftung, GmbHG) and offer one main advantage — capping personal liability at the share capital. The difference lies in the starting capital and the obligation to build it up.

items: GmbH: share capital (Stammkapital) of at least 25 000 €, with at least 12 500 € paid in at founding (§7 GmbHG)
UG (haftungsbeschränkt): capital from 1 €, under §5a GmbHG (often called a Mini-GmbH)
The UG must set aside 25% of annual profit into a reserve until it reaches 25 000 €
Both require a notary and an entry in the commercial register (Handelsregister, Abteilung B)
A GmbH looks more solid to banks and partners; a UG starts up faster and cheaper

content.text: The practical choice: if you have 12 500 € to pay in and image matters, start straight away as a GmbH. If you don't have the money but need limited liability, go with a UG, which gradually «grows» into a GmbH through the mandatory reserve.

steps.title: Notary and commercial register (Handelsregister): mandatory steps

content.text: Unlike a sole proprietorship (Einzelunternehmen) or a trade (Gewerbe), corporate forms come into being only before a notary. The notary certifies the articles of association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) or the model protocol (Musterprotokoll), attests the appointment of the managing director and files the application with the commercial register.

items: Prepare the articles of association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) or use the model protocol (Musterprotokoll) — cheaper for simple cases
Notarial certification of the articles (notarielle Beurkundung) is mandatory under §2 GmbHG
Appointment of the managing director (Geschäftsführer)
Passports of all founders; for non-EU citizens, a residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel)
An interpreter is sometimes required if a founder doesn't speak German

items.title: 2. Paying in capital and the bank account

items: Open a business account (Geschäftskonto) in the name of «GmbH/UG in Gründung»
Pay in the capital: GmbH — at least 12 500 €, UG — the declared capital in full
Get the bank's confirmation of payment (Einzahlungsbestätigung)
With this confirmation the notary completes the filing with the commercial register
Registration is done electronically via handelsregister.de
The company legally comes into existence at the moment of the entry (Eintragung)
Before the entry, the founders bear personal liability for transactions
After the entry — publication and assignment of an HRB number

steps.title: The UG's special rule: a mandatory 25% reserve

content.text: The main «price» of the UG's cheap start is §5a Abs. 3 GmbHG. Every year a UG is required to set aside at least a quarter of its annual profit (after deducting prior years' losses) into a statutory reserve. This reserve cannot be distributed to the founders — it accumulates until it reaches 25 000 €.

items: 25% of annual profit goes into the reserve — it can't be paid out to yourself as dividends
The reserve accumulates until the capital reaches 25 000 €
Once accumulated, the UG can be converted into a regular GmbH (via a notary)
The conversion isn't mandatory, but it removes the «haftungsbeschränkt» suffix
The UG's name MUST contain «UG (haftungsbeschränkt)» in full

content.text: You can't «forget» about the UG's reserve: distributing profit in circumvention of §5a GmbHG makes the payout void, and the managing director (Geschäftsführer) risks personal liability. A UG with 1 € of capital also slips into the red almost immediately because of founding and bookkeeping costs — budget for realistic starting capital (at least a couple of thousand euros) so you don't end up technically insolvent (Überschuldung).

A corporate form means not just limited liability but also a serious reporting burden. Before choosing a GmbH/UG over a sole proprietorship (Einzelunternehmen), weigh up the annual cost of an accountant.

items: Double-entry bookkeeping (doppelte Buchführung) and annual financial statements (Jahresabschluss)
Publication of accounts in the Bundesanzeiger
Corporate income tax (Körperschaftsteuer, 15%) + solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) + trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) at company level
The managing director's salary is taxed like an employee's (wage tax Lohnsteuer, social contributions)
A tax advisor (Steuerberater) usually costs substantially more than for a sole trader (Einzelunternehmer)

content.text: A GmbH/UG makes sense when there are real liability risks or outside investors. For a solo freelancer with low turnover, the overhead (notary, balance sheet, publication, tax advisor, double taxation of profit and dividends) often outweighs the benefit of limited liability. Run the numbers before founding.

costs.label: Founding a GmbH (notary + Handelsregister)
costs.note: Excluding the capital itself; plus at least 12 500 € of Stammkapital to be paid in.

costs.label: Founding a UG (notary + Handelsregister)
costs.note: Cheaper when using the Musterprotokoll; capital from 1 €.

costs.label: Minimum Stammkapital
costs.note: For a GmbH; at founding it's enough to pay in 12 500 €. For a UG — from 1 €.

costs.label: Bookkeeping / Jahresabschluss (per year)
costs.note: Double-entry bookkeeping and a balance sheet are substantially more expensive than a freelancer's EÜR.

sources.title: GmbHG §7 — paying in capital at founding

title: Small business owner (Kleinunternehmer) §19 UStG
tldr: The small-business-owner scheme (Kleinunternehmer) under §19 UStG exempts small entrepreneurs from charging turnover tax (VAT, Umsatzsteuer). Under the reform that applies from 1 January 2025, the limits have been raised: you can use the scheme if the previous year's turnover did NOT exceed 25 000 € AND the current year's turnover doesn't exceed 100 000 €. The upside: you don't add VAT to your invoices and don't file a preliminary VAT return (USt-Voranmeldung). The downside: you CANNOT deduct input VAT (Vorsteuer) on your purchases. You choose the scheme in the tax registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung). Be careful: if you exceed the limit during the year your status falls away, and it's important to start issuing invoices with VAT in time — otherwise you'll have to pay it out of your own pocket.

steps.title: What the small-business-owner (Kleinunternehmer) status gives you

content.text: §19 UStG is a simplification for small entrepreneurs. If you stay within the limits, you don't charge turnover tax (VAT, Umsatzsteuer) to clients, don't file a preliminary VAT return (USt-Voranmeldung) and generally simplify your reporting considerably. This is handy for those who work with private individuals (B2C), who have no need for input VAT.

items: You don't add 19% (or 7%) VAT to your invoices
No need to file a monthly or quarterly preliminary VAT return (USt-Voranmeldung)
The invoice must carry a note that §19 UStG applies (without stating VAT)
You still have to pay income tax (Einkommensteuer)
You choose the status in the tax registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung) via the tax authority's ELSTER portal

content.text: From 1 January 2025, the reform raised the §19 UStG thresholds. Previously they were 22 000 € (previous year) and 50 000 € (current year). Now two conditions apply at the same time.

items: Previous calendar year's turnover: NO more than 25 000 €
Current calendar year's turnover: NO more than 100 000 €
Both conditions must be met at the same time
In your first year of business you go by the projected turnover (no more than 25 000 €)
When starting mid-year, turnover is no longer pro-rated to a full year the way it used to be under the new rules — check with a tax advisor (Steuerberater)

content.text: The main trap of the 2025 reform: now, if you exceed the 100 000 € limit DURING the year, the small-business-owner status ends immediately from the moment you exceed it, not from the following year. All invoices issued after the threshold is crossed must include VAT. If you keep issuing invoices without VAT, the tax will be charged anyway — and you'll have to pay it retroactively out of your own pocket.

steps.title: The flip side: you can't deduct input VAT (Vorsteuer)

content.text: The VAT exemption cuts both ways. Since you don't charge clients VAT, you also have no right to deduct input VAT (Vorsteuer) on your purchases — equipment, hardware, services. For a business with large purchases this can be a disadvantage.

items: Bought a laptop for 1190 € (1000 € + 190 € VAT)? You can't get that 190 € back
If you have large start-up investments, standard taxation (Regelbesteuerung) may be more favourable
Work with business clients (B2B)? VAT doesn't bother them — they deduct it themselves
You can VOLUNTARILY waive §19 (switch to standard taxation, Option zur Regelbesteuerung)
Waiving it voluntarily binds you for 5 years (§19 Abs. 2 UStG) — think it through in advance

content.text: Waiving small-business-owner status in favour of standard taxation binds you for at least 5 calendar years. Don't waive it on impulse for the sake of one large deduction — work out whether it pays off, taking into account the monthly preliminary VAT return and the cost of an accountant over all five years.

steps.title: How to issue invoices as a small business owner (Kleinunternehmer)

content.text: A small business owner's invoices contain no VAT, but they must carry an explicit note about the basis for the exemption. Without it the invoice is formally incorrect.

items: Do NOT state the VAT rate and amount on the invoice
Add the wording: «Gemäß §19 UStG wird keine Umsatzsteuer berechnet»
The other invoice details (name, address, date, number, description) are mandatory as usual
State your tax number (Steuernummer); as a small business owner you usually don't need a VAT identification number (USt-IdNr)
Keep invoices and receipts for your annual return

costs.label: Choosing Kleinunternehmer status
costs.note: Indicated for free in the Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung (ELSTER).

costs.label: Savings on the USt-Voranmeldung
costs.note: No need to file preliminary VAT returns — saving time and accountant costs.

costs.label: Non-refundable Vorsteuer on purchases
costs.note: A hidden «cost»: input VAT on purchases can't be reclaimed. The amount depends on your expenses.

title: KSK: social insurance for creatives
tldr: The Artists' Social Insurance Fund (Künstlersozialkasse, KSK) is a unique mechanism through which self-employed artists and publicists (Künstler und Publizisten) get social insurance almost like employees. The idea: the KSK covers roughly half of the contributions (the "employer" share), while the insured person pays the other half — at employee rates into health insurance (Krankenversicherung), long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) and pension insurance (Rentenversicherung). This is a serious saving compared with paying everything yourself. But you can't simply "join" the KSK — you have to APPLY and pass a review: you must pursue artistic or publicistic activity professionally and as your main source of income. Painters, musicians, designers, photographers, journalists, writers and literary translators are typical candidates.

steps.title: What the KSK is and why you need it

content.text: An ordinary self-employed person pays all of their social insurance themselves — and health insurance as a private individual can be expensive. The KSK was created so that creative professions are not left without social protection: the fund pays roughly half of the contributions, as an employer would.

items: The KSK covers ~50% of contributions to health insurance (KV), long-term care (PV) and pension (RV)
The insured person pays the other half — at the employee rate
This is significantly cheaper than paying for insurance entirely on your own
The KSK is not an insurer but an intermediary: the actual insurance stays with your health insurance fund and pension fund
It is financed through the contributions of the insured, the artists' social contribution levy on clients (Künstlersozialabgabe) and a state subsidy

steps.title: Who can get into the KSK

content.text: Eligibility for the KSK is set by the Artists' Social Insurance Act (Künstlersozialversicherungsgesetz, KSVG). The activity must be artistic or publicistic, carried out independently (selbständig) and professionally (for income, not as a hobby).

items: Artists (Künstler): musicians, painters, actors, dancers, designers, fine-art photographers
Publicists (Publizisten): journalists, writers, editors, translators, lecturers
The activity is your main income, not a side hobby
Minimum annual income from creative work — at least 3900 € (the minimum threshold, Mindestgrenze, §3 KSVG; the professionalism threshold)
Purely craft-based or commercial work (with no creative component) does not qualify

content.text: The KSK reviews applications carefully and re-checks members periodically. If your creative income drops below the professionalism threshold for more than a short period, or your activity shifts into a purely commercial sphere, your membership can be terminated. Report your income honestly: understating your turnover to lower your contributions is a violation that comes to light during reviews.
The application is submitted directly to the Künstlersozialkasse. Be prepared to prove the nature of your activity — portfolio, contracts, invoices, publications. A decision can take weeks or months.

items: Download the questionnaire (Fragebogen) at kuenstlersozialkasse.de
Describe the type of artistic or publicistic activity
State your projected annual income from this activity
Attach evidence: contracts, invoices, links to your work, portfolio
The KSK checks that you meet the KSVG criteria
It may request additional documents
On a positive decision, you pay a contribution based on your declared income
Income can be adjusted annually (updating the forecast)

steps.title: How much to pay and how the contribution is calculated

content.text: The contribution is calculated from your projected annual creative income. You pay the employee's share of health, pension and long-term care insurance, and the KSK adds the other half.

items: The basis is your declared annual income from creative work (Arbeitseinkommen)
You pay ~half the rates for health insurance + long-term care + pension (like an employee)
The KSK takes on the other half — that is the main benefit
It is important to keep your income forecast realistic — large discrepancies will trigger a recalculation
The artists' social contribution levy (Künstlersozialabgabe) is paid by your clients (companies), not by you personally

content.text: Do not confuse a KSK member's contribution with the artists' social contribution levy (Künstlersozialabgabe). The latter is paid by companies that commission creative services (even if the contractor is not in the KSK). If you, as an entrepreneur, regularly hire artists, designers or copywriters, you yourself may be liable to pay this levy — check, or a review will assess it retroactively.

costs.label: Applying to the KSK
costs.note: The application is free; it takes time and documents to prove your activity.

costs.label: KSK member's contribution
costs.note: Depends on income: you pay roughly half of the usual social insurance rates, the KSK pays the other half.

costs.label: Künstlersozialabgabe (for clients)
costs.note: A percentage of payments to creative contractors; paid by the commissioning companies, with the rate reviewed annually.

sources.title: BMWK Existenzgründer — social insurance for the self-employed

title: Invoice (Rechnung): mandatory details
tldr: An invoice (Rechnung) in Germany is not just a slip of paper with an amount: §14 UStG prescribes a mandatory set of details, without which the client cannot deduct VAT and you risk objections from the tax office (Finanzamt). Mandatory are: the full name and address of both parties, your tax number (Steuernummer) OR VAT identification number (USt-IdNr), the invoice date, a unique sequential number (Rechnungsnummer), a description of the service or goods (Leistungsbeschreibung), the delivery or service date (Leistungsdatum), the net amount, and the VAT rate and amount. For small invoices up to 250 € a simplified format applies — the small-amount invoice (Kleinbetragsrechnung, §33 UStDV) with a reduced set of fields. A small business (Kleinunternehmer) under §19 UStG does NOT show VAT but must add a note about the exemption.

content.text: §14 Abs. 4 UStG lists the details that every full invoice must contain. Their absence is a frequent reason for the tax office (Finanzamt) to deny the client the input VAT deduction (Vorsteuer) and to raise objections against you.

items: Full name and address of the supplier (you) and the recipient (the client)
Your tax number (Steuernummer) OR VAT identification number (USt-IdNr)
Invoice issue date (Ausstellungsdatum)
Unique sequential invoice number (fortlaufende Rechnungsnummer)
Quantity and description of the goods or service (Menge + Leistungsbeschreibung)
Delivery or service date (Leistungsdatum / Lieferdatum)
Net amount, VAT rate (7% or 19%) and VAT amount shown separately

content.text: The invoice number must be unique and must not be repeated. The law does not require strictly gapless numbering, but the numbers must unambiguously identify each invoice. In practice it is more convenient to keep continuous or structured numbering.

items: Each number is used only once
Acceptable schemes: 2026-001, 2026-002 or RE-0001, and so on
You can split by year, project or client type — the key thing is uniqueness
Never issue two invoices with the same number
Keep the numbering logic sequential to make audits easier

content.text: Do not "reuse" or duplicate invoice numbers — during an audit the tax office (Finanzamt) will treat this as a sign of revenue manipulation. If you made a mistake on an invoice, do not quietly delete it: issue a correcting document (Storno / correction), keeping the original number in the record.

steps.title: Small-amount invoice (Kleinbetragsrechnung): a simplified invoice up to 250 €

content.text: For invoices with a total amount (gross) up to 250 €, a simplified format applies under §33 UStDV. It is a lifesaver in retail and for small services — you don't need to state the recipient's details or a separate VAT amount.

items: Limit — 250 € including VAT (Bruttobetrag)
Enough: the SUPPLIER's name and address, the date, a description, the amount and the VAT rate
The recipient's details and a separate VAT calculation do NOT have to be stated
Applies to cash register receipts, small services, retail
Above 250 € — the full set of §14 UStG details is required

steps.title: Special cases: §19 UStG and reverse charge

content.text: Not all invoices contain VAT. A small business (Kleinunternehmer) doesn't charge it, and for B2B transactions within the EU or under the reverse-charge mechanism the recipient pays the tax. These cases require specific notes.

items: Small business: the note "Gemäß §19 UStG wird keine Umsatzsteuer berechnet"
Reverse charge (B2B within the EU): the note "Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers"
Under reverse charge, state both USt-IdNr (yours and the client's)
Keeping invoices — by law for at least 8 years (§14b UStG; the period was reduced from 10 to 8 years by the BEG IV law, in force from 2025)
Electronic invoices (E-Rechnung) are becoming mandatory in B2B — take the format into account

content.text: From 2025, the mandatory electronic invoice (E-Rechnung) in a structured format (for example, XRechnung/ZUGFeRD) is being phased in for B2B trade in Germany. A PDF by email no longer counts as a full electronic invoice for B2B. Check whether your invoicing tools are ready for the new format, so that your invoices are not rejected.

costs.label: Issuing invoices manually / from a template
costs.note: You can keep them in a spreadsheet or text template for free as long as you comply with §14 UStG.

costs.label: Invoicing service (per month)
costs.note: Paid tools help with numbering and the E-Rechnung; there are free plans.

costs.label: Keeping invoices for 8 years
costs.note: An obligation under §14b UStG; no cost, but you need a reliable archive.

title: USt-Voranmeldung: monthly
tldr: The advance VAT return (USt-Voranmeldung) is a preliminary return for value-added tax (VAT, Umsatzsteuer) that most entrepreneurs (except small businesses under §19 UStG) are required to file regularly through the tax authority's ELSTER portal. The default period is the quarter; those whose VAT payable (Zahllast) for the previous year exceeded 7500 € file monthly. The former rule that "new businesses always file monthly for the first two years" is suspended until the end of 2026, so newcomers currently file quarterly by default. The deadline is the 10th of the month following the reporting period. You can obtain a permanent deadline extension (Dauerfristverlängerung) of one more month (monthly filers need a special advance payment, the Sondervorauszahlung). In the return you show the VAT charged minus the deductible input VAT (Vorsteuer) and pay the difference (or receive a refund). Filing is electronic only, through ELSTER. A tax advisor (Steuerberater) charges roughly 50–200 € per month to handle it.

steps.title: How often to file: monthly or quarterly

content.text: The frequency depends on the amount of VAT payable (Zahllast) for the previous year. By default the period is the quarter; monthly filing is mandatory only if last year's VAT exceeded 7500 €. For newcomers, the former rule of "always monthly in the first two years" is suspended and does not apply until the end of 2026.

items: By default (including for new businesses until the end of 2026): quarterly
Last year's VAT above 7500 € — monthly
Projected VAT above 7500 € in the year of founding — monthly from the very first year
Last year's VAT no more than 1000 € — the tax office (Finanzamt) may exempt you from the advance return (annual only)
Small businesses under §19 UStG do not file an advance return at all

content.text: Don't assume monthly filing is automatic: until the end of 2026 the suspension means that newcomers file quarterly by default, and monthly only if VAT exceeded 7500 € for the previous year. From 2027 the former rule for new businesses may return — check the current regime. Missing the deadline leads to a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag) and interest, and if you fail to file at all, the tax office will estimate the VAT itself (Schätzung) — usually not in your favour.

You must submit the return and the payment by the 10th of the month following the reporting period. For January — by 10 February; for Q1 — by 10 April. If the 10th falls on a weekend, the deadline shifts to the next business day.

items: Monthly: by the 10th of the following month
Quarterly: by the 10th after the end of the quarter
The amount due is debited or transferred by the same deadline
It is convenient to set up SEPA direct debit (SEPA-Lastschrift), so that the tax office debits the VAT itself
A late filing means a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag) + a late-payment penalty (Säumniszuschlag)

steps.title: Permanent deadline extension (Dauerfristverlängerung): +1 month to the deadline

content.text: If the 10th is too tight a deadline, apply for a permanent deadline extension (Dauerfristverlängerung) through ELSTER. It grants a permanent one-month extension for all future periods.

items: The application is submitted once through ELSTER (form USt 1 H)
The filing deadline shifts forward by 1 month (for example, for January — to 10 March)
MONTHLY filers need a special advance payment (Sondervorauszahlung) of ~1/11 of last year's VAT
This advance payment is credited in the December return
Quarterly filers do not need the advance payment

steps.title: Filing through ELSTER and calculating the amount

content.text: The advance VAT return is filed exclusively electronically through ELSTER. In the return you state the VAT charged on sales and the deductible input VAT (Vorsteuer) on purchases; you pay (or are refunded) the difference.

items: Add up the VAT on all issued invoices (turnover tax, Umsatzsteuer)
Add up the input VAT on purchases (Vorsteuer)
VAT payable (Zahllast) = Umsatzsteuer − Vorsteuer
If Vorsteuer is greater — the tax office will refund the overpayment (Erstattung)
Log in to Mein ELSTER with your certificate
Select "Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung" for the period you need
Enter the amounts, check them, and submit
Save the confirmation (Übertragungsprotokoll)

costs.label: Filing through ELSTER
costs.note: The portal and filing all returns are free.

costs.label: Steuerberater for handling the USt-Voranmeldung
costs.note: Per month; depends on the volume of transactions and the frequency.

costs.label: Verspätungszuschlag for a late filing
costs.note: A late-filing surcharge plus interest (Säumniszuschlag) — the amounts grow over time.

title: USt-IdNr: for trading within the EU
tldr: The VAT identification number (USt-IdNr, Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer) is a number for transactions within the EU. It is issued FREE of charge by the Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern, BZSt). You need it for intra-Community supplies (innergemeinschaftliche Lieferungen) — supplies of goods or services to business customers (B2B) in other EU countries — as well as for the reverse-charge mechanism, where VAT is paid by the recipient. Important: the USt-IdNr is NOT the same as the tax number (Steuernummer); the two exist in parallel. The tax number is used within Germany with the tax office (Finanzamt), while the USt-IdNr is for cross-border transactions within the EU. You can request it during registration in the tax registration questionnaire (Fragebogen) or later online at bzst.de. The validity of an EU counterparty's number is checked through the VIES system.

steps.title: VAT identification number (USt-IdNr) versus tax number (Steuernummer)

content.text: Newcomers are often confused by having two different numbers. The tax number (Steuernummer) is assigned by your local tax office (Finanzamt) — it is for domestic German correspondence and returns. The USt-IdNr is issued by the federal BZSt — it is for VAT transactions within the EU. These are two different numbers that exist at the same time.

items: Tax number (Steuernummer) — local, from the tax office, for domestic matters
USt-IdNr — federal, from the BZSt, for B2B trade within the EU
USt-IdNr format: DE + 9 digits
Both numbers can appear on invoices (for EU transactions, specifically the USt-IdNr)
A small business owner (Kleinunternehmer) under §19 usually doesn't need a USt-IdNr, but may request one for purchases within the EU

content.text: The main reason to get a USt-IdNr is cross-border transactions within the EU. Without it, you can't correctly process VAT-exempt supplies to business customers in other EU countries.

items: Intra-Community supplies (innergemeinschaftliche Lieferungen) — B2B supplies of goods to EU countries
Services to business customers in the EU under the reverse-charge mechanism
Purchases from suppliers in other EU countries (intra-Community acquisition, innergemeinschaftlicher Erwerb)
Working with marketplaces and platforms that require a VAT ID
Filing the recapitulative statement (Zusammenfassende Meldung, ZM) on EU transactions through the BZSt

content.text: With reverse-charge, the invoice must include BOTH USt-IdNr numbers — yours and the client's — and the note "Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers". Before a VAT-exempt supply, verify the client's USt-IdNr through the VIES system (EU validation): if the number is invalid, the exemption may not be recognized and the VAT may be charged back to you.

The number is issued free of charge. The simplest route is to request it right at registration, in the tax registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung). If you didn't do it then, you can submit a request later online at bzst.de.

items: In the tax registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung), tick the box to request a USt-IdNr
The BZSt will send the number by letter once it has processed the request
This is the most convenient moment if you are planning EU transactions
Submit an online request at bzst.de (USt-IdNr section)
You will need your tax number (Steuernummer) and your tax office details
The number usually arrives by letter within 2-4 weeks
The request is completely free

steps.title: Using the number and the recapitulative statement (Zusammenfassende Meldung)

content.text: Once you have a USt-IdNr, you don't just put it on invoices for EU transactions — you also take on an additional reporting obligation. Cross-border transactions within the EU must be reported to the BZSt through the recapitulative statement (Zusammenfassende Meldung, ZM).

items: Put the USt-IdNr (not the tax number) on invoices for B2B EU transactions
File the recapitulative statement (Zusammenfassende Meldung, ZM) on EU transactions through the BZSt/ELSTER
The recapitulative statement shows turnover with EU clients by their USt-IdNr
The statement's deadlines depend on the volume of EU transactions (usually monthly or quarterly)
A mismatch between the recapitulative statement and the preliminary VAT return triggers queries from the tax office

content.text: Don't forget about the recapitulative statement: the VAT exemption for an intra-Community supply (innergemeinschaftliche Lieferung) only works with a correct and timely recapitulative statement (Zusammenfassende Meldung) carrying the client's valid USt-IdNr. Missing or erroneous statements are a common reason for the tax office to deny the exemption and charge VAT retroactively.

costs.label: Obtaining a USt-IdNr from the BZSt
costs.note: Completely free, both at registration and via an online request.

costs.label: Checking a counterparty's number (VIES)
costs.note: Free online validation of EU numbers through the VIES system / BZSt confirmation.
