title: Returning to work after parental leave (Elternzeit)
tldr: After parental leave (Elternzeit), under §15 BEEG you have the right to return to your previous position or an equivalent one at the same salary level. During this leave, special protection against dismissal under §18 BEEG applies: it is nearly impossible to dismiss you. You can work part-time (Teilzeit) up to 32 hours per week right during parental leave (the right to part-time work, Teilzeitanspruch), and afterwards you can request a reduced schedule under §8 TzBfG. Submit the notice ending your leave or requesting part-time work in writing and well in advance, otherwise the employer will have grounds to drag things out.

steps.title: What rights you have when returning

content.text: Parental leave (Elternzeit) is unpaid leave until the child turns three (part of it can be carried over to the ages of 3–8). The employment contract does not end, it merely "sleeps": the duty to work and the duty to pay salary are suspended, but your position is kept for you.

Under §15 BEEG, once parental leave ends you return to the same position or an equivalent (gleichwertige) one. The employer isn't required to give back literally the same desk, but the new position must be comparable in content, responsibility and pay. Demoting you or cutting your salary "because you were away for a long time" is not allowed.

items: The contract remains in force for the entire parental leave; you don't need to resign for this
You return to your previous position or an equivalent one at the same pay level
Your length of service at the company (Betriebszugehörigkeit) keeps accruing for calculating deadlines and rights
The employer may reduce vacation days for the time on parental leave proportionally under §17 BEEG
Leave accrued before parental leave does not expire — you can take it after returning

steps.title: Part-time work (Teilzeit) during and after parental leave

content.text: Right during parental leave you can work part-time up to 32 hours per week — this is part-time work during parental leave (Teilzeit in Elternzeit) under §15 (4)–(7) BEEG. At companies with more than 15 employees there is a legal right (Anspruch) to such a schedule, provided you have worked more than 6 months and gave notice of it in time.

items.title: 1. Part-time work right during parental leave (Teilzeit in Elternzeit, §15 BEEG)

items: The company has more than 15 employees
Your length of service at the start of part-time work is more than 6 months
The desired volume — from the minimum up to 32 hours per week
The application is filed at least 7 weeks (child under 3) or 13 weeks (ages 3–8) before the start
The application states the start, the volume and, ideally, the distribution of hours

items.title: 2. Part-time work after parental leave (§8 TzBfG)

content.text: If you want to stay on a reduced schedule after parental leave has ended, this is a separate right under §8 of the Act on Part-Time Work and Fixed-Term Employment Contracts (Teilzeit- und Befristungsgesetz, TzBfG): it is available at companies with more than 15 employees to those with more than 6 months of service. The application is filed at least 3 months before the desired start; the employer can refuse only on substantial operational grounds (betriebliche Gründe).

Part-time work during parental leave and part-time work under §8 TzBfG are two different legal regimes with different application deadlines. Don't confuse them: an application to "return to part-time permanently" under the parental-leave rules is not automatically extended once parental leave ends.

During parental leave, enhanced protection against dismissal under §18 BEEG applies. The protection begins as early as 8 weeks before the start of parental leave (or 14 weeks if it is planned for the ages of 3–8) and lasts until it ends. During this period the employer essentially cannot dismiss you.

An exception is possible only with the consent of the state's highest occupational-safety authority (oberste Landesbehörde für Arbeitsschutz) — for example, in the case of a complete shutdown of the company. In practice such permissions are rare, so a dismissal during parental leave is almost always invalid.

Even under the protection of §18 BEEG: if you do receive a termination of contract (Kündigung), you have only 3 weeks to file a claim with the labour court (Arbeitsgericht) under §4 KSchG. Miss the deadline and the dismissal is considered valid, even if it was unlawful. Don't wait for parental leave to end before challenging it.

steps.title: Returning in practice: what to do

items: Inform the employer in writing of your exact return date (if parental leave ends before the planned date, agree on the early ending in advance)
3 months before returning, file an application for part-time work under §8 TzBfG if you want a reduced schedule
Clarify how much accrued and unused leave remains
Check the offered position for equivalence: content, grade, salary
If you are offered a demotion or reduced pay, get it in writing and take advice before signing

content.text: If the employer refuses to give back an equivalent position or pushes for a "voluntary" resignation, this is a dispute under §15 BEEG. Free initial advice is offered by your trade union (Gewerkschaft) if you are a member, and by women's and family counselling services; for a fee, by a specialist employment lawyer (Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht).

costs.label: Returning to work and the Teilzeit application
costs.note: The applications themselves and the return are free; everything is handled through letters to the employer.

costs.label: Consultation with a Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht (for a dispute)
costs.note: Erstberatung; with trade-union membership — free through Rechtsschutz.

title: Kündigungsfristen: notice periods for dismissal
tldr: Notice periods for dismissal (Kündigungsfristen) in Germany are set by §622 BGB. For an employee, the standard period is 4 weeks to the 15th or to the end of the calendar month. For the employer, the period grows with length of service: from 4 weeks (less than 2 years of service) up to 7 months to the end of the month at 20+ years of service. During the probationary period (Probezeit) the period is shortened to 2 weeks. A contract or a collective (sectoral) agreement (Tarifvertrag) may change the periods, but it cannot put the employee in a worse position than the statutory minimum relative to the employer.

content.text: The notice period for dismissal (Kündigungsfrist) is the period between submitting the notice of termination and the actual ending of the employment relationship. During this period the contract is in force: you work and receive your salary, unless the parties have agreed on a release from work (Freistellung). The basic periods are set by §622 BGB.

Under §622 (1) BGB, the standard period for both parties is 4 weeks to the 15th of the month or to the end of the calendar month. "4 weeks" is exactly 28 days, not "a month": count the exact dates, don't round.

items: The period is counted from the day the other party receives the written termination of contract (Kündigung), not from the date on the letter
The termination of contract must be in writing with an original signature — §623 BGB; email, WhatsApp and SMS are invalid
"To the 15th or to the end of the month" — dismissal can only take effect on these two dates
If you gave notice too late for the nearest date, the period shifts to the next permissible one

steps.title: The periods for the employer grow with length of service

content.text: Under §622 (2) BGB, the longer an employee has been at the company, the longer the period the employer must observe when dismissing them. All these extended periods end only at the end of the calendar month (not at the 15th).

items: Less than 2 years of service — 4 weeks to the 15th or to the end of the month (the basic period)
From 2 years — 1 month to the end of the month
From 5 years — 2 months to the end of the month
From 8 years — 3 months to the end of the month
From 10 years — 4 months to the end of the month
From 12 years — 5 months to the end of the month
From 15 years — 6 months to the end of the month
From 20 years — 7 months to the end of the month

content.text: Important: by law, these extended periods protect the employee. An employee who resigns of their own accord stays on the basic 4 weeks by default — unless the contract provides otherwise. So there is no "mirroring": with length of service, only the period on the employer's side grows longer.

During an agreed probationary period (Probezeit), which lasts a maximum of 6 months, a shortened period of 2 weeks applies under §622 (3) BGB — with no tie to the 15th or the end of the month. A dismissal during the probationary period does not have to be justified with the usual reasons.

An employment contract or a collective (sectoral) agreement (Tarifvertrag) may set different periods. Under §622 (5)–(6) BGB, the contractual period for dismissal by the employee may not be longer than the period for the employer. A collective agreement may deviate more widely, including by shortening the periods.

Don't confuse the notice period for dismissal (Kündigungsfrist) with protection against dismissal (Kündigungsschutz). Observing the period does not make the dismissal "lawful on the merits": at large companies the employer still needs socially justified reasons. If you received a termination of contract, you have 3 weeks to file a claim under §4 KSchG, regardless of the length of the notice period.

steps.title: How to calculate and serve your own notice period

items: Work out the date when the other party will receive the letter
Add your period (for example, 4 weeks = 28 days)
Find the nearest permissible date: the 15th or the end of the month
If you can't make it, shift to the next permissible date

items.title: 2. Deliver the termination of contract (Kündigung) correctly

content.text: Submit it in writing with a signature, ideally in person against an acknowledgment of receipt (Empfangsbestätigung) or by registered mail with proof of delivery to the mailbox (Einwurf-Einschreiben). This is needed so you can later prove the date of receipt, from which the period is counted.

costs.label: Submitting your own Kündigung
costs.note: The only cost is the registered letter (Einschreiben), about 3–5 €.

costs.label: Having a disputed period checked by a lawyer
costs.note: Erstberatung Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht; free through the trade union with membership.

sources.title: Bundesagentur für Arbeit — Arbeitslosengeld und Sperrzeit

title: CV (Lebenslauf): the German format
tldr: A CV (Lebenslauf) is a tabular (tabellarisch) résumé of 1–2 pages in reverse chronological order: most recent experience first. It lists personal data, work experience, education, skills and languages. A photo is optional (under the AGG an employer may not require one), but in Germany it is still common. When you submit online, a signature is not required. The CV comes with a cover letter (Anschreiben) and attachments — references and certificates (Zeugnisse). What matters most is a clear structure, no gaps in the dates, and honesty: fake certificates come to light during verification.

content.text: A German CV (Lebenslauf) is not running text but a table of blocks. The standard is reverse chronological order (rückwärtschronologisch): the most recent job or studies at the top. Keep it to 1–2 pages, use a neutral font, and keep the layout tidy and consistent.

items: Personal data (Persönliche Daten) — name, address, phone, email; date of birth and nationality are optional
Work experience (Berufserfahrung): period, employer, position, key tasks
Education and qualifications (Bildung / Ausbildung) with dates
Skills (Kenntnisse): IT, professional competencies
Languages (Sprachen) with level (for example, Deutsch B2, Englisch C1)
Optionally: further training (Weiterbildungen), certificates, volunteering, hobbies (briefly)

content.text: The General Equal Treatment Act (AGG, Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz) prohibits discrimination in hiring, so a photo, date of birth, marital status and religion are formally optional details: their absence cannot be grounds for rejection. Whether or not to include them is the candidate's choice.

items: Photo — optional, but in German practice still often expected; if you add one, use a professional application photo (Bewerbungsfoto)
Date of birth, marital status, nationality — optional, may be omitted
When submitting online (PDF, portal) a signature is not required
If you submit a paper folder — a signature with place and date at the bottom is acceptable

content.text: Do not leave unexplained gaps (Lücken) in the dates. HR staff in Germany look closely at the chronology: it is better to label breaks honestly (for example, parental leave (Elternzeit), further training (Weiterbildung), job search (Jobsuche)) than to leave a "hole". Invented or embellished experience is grounds for dismissal and even for challenging the contract (Anfechtung) once it comes to light.
A CV is rarely sent on its own. A standard application package (Bewerbungsunterlagen) includes several documents, usually as a single PDF.

A separate page: why you, why this company and position. Specific and targeted, not copy-pasted onto every vacancy. In German culture the cover letter (Anschreiben) is still valued, although some IT companies have dropped it.

items: References from previous jobs (Arbeitszeugnisse) — in Germany this is a formal document
Diplomas and educational certificates
Recognition of a foreign qualification (Anerkennung), if relevant to the profession
Tailor the CV to each vacancy: highlight the relevant experience
Send it as a single PDF file with a clear name (Lebenslauf_Familienname.pdf)
State your language levels honestly: B2/C1 will be tested at the interview
Free templates are available on the Make it in Germany portal and from the employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit)
Paid help — an application-preparation service (Bewerbungsservice, 50–200 €) — is optional; for a basic CV it is not necessary

costs.label: Writing the Lebenslauf yourself
costs.note: Free templates on Make it in Germany and from the Agentur für Arbeit.

costs.label: Bewerbungsfoto at a photographer
costs.note: Optional; an application photo is not required under the AGG.

costs.label: Professional Bewerbungsservice
costs.note: Optional — proofreading and formatting of the CV and Anschreiben.

sources.title: Make it in Germany — Bewerbung und Lebenslauf
Bundesagentur für Arbeit — Bewerbung und Lebenslauf

title: Payslip (Lohnabrechnung): how to read it
tldr: A payslip (Lohnabrechnung, Gehaltsabrechnung) shows the path from gross (Brutto) to net take-home pay (Netto). From the gross amount, taxes are deducted — wage tax (Lohnsteuer), church tax (Kirchensteuer, if you are in a church), the solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag, abolished for most low and middle incomes since 2021) — along with social security contributions (Sozialversicherung): health insurance KV, long-term care insurance PV, pension insurance RV, unemployment insurance AV. Exactly what is withheld depends on your tax class (Steuerklasse), whether church tax applies, and your health fund's contribution. Net is the bottom line. Check your tax class and health fund — mistakes here are real.

steps.title: From Brutto to Netto: the general logic

content.text: Every payslip (Lohnabrechnung) follows the same scheme: at the top the gross salary earned (Bruttolohn, everything earned before deductions), then two kinds of deductions — taxes and social security contributions, and at the bottom the net salary (Nettolohn), which actually lands in your account.

items: Gross salary (Bruttogehalt) — the agreed salary before deductions
Minus taxes (Steuern): wage tax (Lohnsteuer), and where applicable church tax (Kirchensteuer) and the solidarity surcharge (Soli)
Minus social security contributions (Sozialversicherungsbeiträge) — the employee's share
Result = net salary (Nettogehalt, Auszahlungsbetrag) — the take-home amount
On top of this the employer pays its own share of contributions (Arbeitgeberanteil), which is not visible in the net pay

content.text: A prepaid income tax that the employer withholds and transfers to the tax office (Finanzamt). Its amount depends heavily on your tax class (Steuerklasse, 1–6). After the year you can file a tax return (Steuererklärung) and often get the overpayment back.

The solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag). Since 2021 it has effectively been abolished for the vast majority of employees on low and middle incomes — the line will show 0. Only high incomes still pay it.

8–9 % of the wage tax (Lohnsteuer), withheld only if you are officially a member of a taxable church. If you are not a church member, the line should be empty. You can leave the church through a declaration of leaving (Kirchenaustritt), after which the tax disappears.

These are the four mandatory branches of social insurance. Contributions are generally split in half between employee and employer (with some nuances for the supplementary fund contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) and long-term care insurance). Below are the approximate employee-share rates for 2026: these are a guide; the exact figures depend on your fund and federal state.

items: Health insurance (KV, Krankenversicherung): ~7,3 % + half of your fund's supplementary contribution (Zusatzbeitrag)
Long-term care insurance (PV, Pflegeversicherung): the share depends on whether you have children; childless people over 23 pay a surcharge
Pension insurance (RV, Rentenversicherung): ~9,3 % employee share
Unemployment insurance (AV, Arbeitslosenversicherung): ~1,3 % employee share
Contributions are calculated up to a ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze); above it the rate does not rise

content.text: On the payslip the social security contributions are usually grouped separately from the taxes. The employer's share (Arbeitgeberanteil) is often printed alongside for reference: this is money the employer pays for you on top of your salary.

steps.title: What to check and where errors hide

items: Tax class (Steuerklasse) — does it match your family situation (the wrong class = overpaid tax)
Church tax (Kirchensteuer) — is there a line for it even though you are not a church member (a mistake made during residence registration, Anmeldung)
The name of the health fund and its supplementary contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) — does it match your actual fund
Social security number (Sozialversicherungsnummer) and tax ID (Steuer-ID) are stated correctly
Gross = the contractual salary plus allowances; check there are no extra or missing components

content.text: If the payslip shows the wrong tax class (Steuerklasse) or church tax (Kirchensteuer) is withheld even though you are not in a church, contact your employer's payroll department (Lohnbuchhaltung) in writing. An overpayment of wage tax (Lohnsteuer) will be returned by the annual tax return (Steuererklärung), but an erroneous church-tax component is easier to fix straight away. Keep all your payslips (Lohnabrechnungen): you will need them for renting, loans and calculating your pension. For complicated or disputed deductions, advice can be given by an income-tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein), a tax adviser (Steuerberater) or a specialist employment lawyer (Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht).

costs.label: Receiving a Lohnabrechnung
costs.note: The employer is obliged to issue a payslip under §108 GewO — free of charge.

costs.label: Steuererklärung via a Lohnsteuerhilfeverein
costs.note: Annual membership fee based on income; the refund of overpaid Lohnsteuer often exceeds the cost.

sources.title: GKV-Spitzenverband — Zahlen, Grafiken und Rechengrößen der Sozialversicherung

title: Mini-job (Minijob): the 603€ threshold in 2026
tldr: A mini-job (Minijob, geringfügige Beschäftigung) in 2026 is a sideline with a limit of 603 € per month. The threshold is tied to the minimum wage (Mindestlohn) and is calculated as 13,90 € × about 43,4 hours. For the employee the pay is free of income tax and the usual social security contributions — the employer pays those as a flat rate (pauschal). For pension insurance (RV) the employee contributes a small share by default, but can apply for an exemption. The main risk is exceeding the limit: a regular overshoot turns the work into a normal job, subject to social security contributions (sozialversicherungspflichtig) with all the contributions.

steps.title: What a Minijob is and the 603 € limit

content.text: A mini-job (Minijob) is low-paid employment (geringfügig entlohnte Beschäftigung): a sideline with limited earnings. From 2026 the monthly limit is 603 € (the marginal-earnings threshold, Geringfügigkeitsgrenze). This threshold is dynamic: it is tied to the minimum wage (Mindestlohn) and is calculated as 13,90 € × about 43,4 working hours per month.

items: The limit is 603 € per month (on average up to 7 236 € a year if earnings are even)
Hours per week — about 10 at the minimum rate
Registered by the employer through the mini-job clearing house (Minijob-Zentrale)
One person can hold one mini-job plus a main job without losing the benefits
Several mini-jobs are added together — total earnings above 603 € remove the privileged status

steps.title: Taxes and contributions: who pays what

content.text: The main appeal of a mini-job for the employee is the near-zero burden. No income tax or the usual social security contributions are withheld from the employee's pay: the employer takes those on as a flat rate (pauschal) and transfers them to the mini-job clearing house (Minijob-Zentrale).

items: Wage tax (Lohnsteuer) — as a rule not withheld (the employer pays it at a flat rate or via the wage-tax card, Lohnsteuerkarte)
Health, long-term care and unemployment insurance (KV, PV, AV) — no contributions from the employee
Pension insurance (RV) — by default a small employee share is mandatory
You can be exempted from the pension-insurance share by application (exemption from compulsory pension insurance, Befreiung von der Rentenversicherungspflicht)

items.title: 2. Paying into the RV or not

content.text: If you keep paying contributions into pension insurance (RV), you build up full pension periods and rights (for example, to rehabilitation). If you apply for an exemption (Befreiung), you get a little more in hand, but your pension rights for this period do not grow. The decision depends on your situation.

steps.title: The risk of exceeding the limit

content.text: The main risk of a mini-job (Minijob) is overshooting 603 €. If you regularly earn more, the work loses its mini-job status and becomes a normal job subject to social security contributions (sozialversicherungspflichtig): full contributions for health, long-term care, pension and unemployment (KV, PV, RV, AV) and tax kick in. Accidental overshoots are allowed only in exceptional, unforeseeable cases and for a limited number of months per year.

items: The average earnings over the year are counted, not just a single month
An unforeseen overshoot is allowed only to a limited extent (as a rule, up to 2 months a year)
A planned overshoot immediately turns the work into a transition-zone job (Midijob) / normal employment
Several mini-jobs add up — keep an eye on the total

content.text: A mini-job (Minijob) is a full employment relationship: you are entitled to paid leave (like everyone, in proportion to your hours), to continued pay during illness (Entgeltfortzahlung) and to a wage not below the minimum wage (Mindestlohn) of 13,90 €/hour.

items: A written employment contract and time records are mandatory
The right to leave and sick pay is retained
Earnings not below the minimum wage (Mindestlohn) for the actual hours worked
Registration by the employer with the mini-job clearing house (Minijob-Zentrale) is mandatory — without it this is illegal employment
The mini-job clearing house explains all questions about status and contributions free of charge

costs.label: Employee taxes and contributions for a Minijob
costs.note: Neither income tax nor most contributions are withheld from the employee's pay; the employer pays a flat rate.

costs.label: Employee share in Rentenversicherung
costs.note: The employee RV share is 3,6% of earnings (~22 € at 603 €); you can apply for a Befreiung and pay 0.

title: Urlaub: vacation days and the rules
tldr: The minimum paid leave is set by the Federal Leave Act (BUrlG): §3 guarantees 24 working days for a 6-day working week, which equals 20 days for a 5-day week. Many collective (sectoral) agreements (Tarifverträge) and employment contracts give more — 28–30 days. In the first year leave accrues pro rata, and the full entitlement arises after 6 months of work. By default, unused leave must be taken before the end of the year; carrying it over to the next year is possible only to a limited extent and usually only until 31 March for compelling reasons.

content.text: The Federal Leave Act (BUrlG) sets the mandatory minimum of paid leave for all employees. Under §3 BUrlG this is 24 working days (Werktage) for a 6-day working week. Working days (Werktage) here are all days except Sundays and public holidays, so Saturday also counts as a working day.

items: 6-day week — a minimum of 24 working days
5-day week — a minimum of 20 working days (24 ÷ 6 × 5)
For part-time work the days are recalculated in proportion to the number of working days per week
This is precisely the minimum: an employment contract or a collective (sectoral) agreement (Tarifvertrag) often gives 28–30 days
Leave is paid at your average earnings (holiday pay, Urlaubsentgelt)

steps.title: The first year and the Wartezeit

content.text: The full entitlement to annual leave arises under §4 BUrlG after 6 months of work (the waiting period, Wartezeit). Before that, and also if you joined or left mid-year, leave accrues pro rata (pro rata temporis) — at 1/12 of the annual leave for each full month worked.

items: The first 6 months — leave accumulates, the full entitlement after the waiting period (Wartezeit)
On joining/leaving mid-year — in proportion to the months
On termination, unused leave is compensated in money (leave compensation, Urlaubsabgeltung)
Leave cannot be "sold" during employment — only on termination of the contract

content.text: Under §7 Abs. 3 BUrlG leave must, as a general rule, be used within the current calendar year. Carrying it over to the next year is possible only for compelling reasons (urgent operational or personal ones), and then the carried-over leave must be taken by 31 March of the following year — otherwise it lapses by default.

An important clarification from case law (EuGH/BAG): leave does not lapse automatically. The employer is obliged to notify you in advance and explicitly about unused days and the risk that they will lapse. If the employer has not done so, the leave may not be lost and can carry over to later periods. During a long illness, unused leave is preserved longer — up to 15 months after the end of the year.

items: By default, leave is taken in the current year
Carry-over — only for compelling reasons, to be used by 31 March
Lapsing requires the employer's prior notification (case law)
During illness, leave is preserved up to 15 months after the end of the year

steps.title: How to request leave and what to consider

content.text: You propose the dates of your leave, but the employer approves them taking into account operational needs and the wishes of other employees (§7 Abs. 1 BUrlG). The employer may refuse for compelling reasons, but is generally obliged to take your wishes into account, especially family ones (for example, your children's school holidays).

items: Submit a leave request (Urlaubsantrag) in advance and in writing
Wait for the approval (Genehmigung) — taking leave without permission is grounds for dismissal
If you fall ill during your leave and provide a sick note — those days do not count as leave (§9 BUrlG)
Check your remaining days at the start and end of the year so you do not lose the carry-over

costs.label: Arranging leave
costs.note: Leave is paid by the employer; there are no arrangement costs.

costs.label: Advice on a leave dispute
costs.note: A lawyer's initial consultation (Erstberatung); free through a union if you are a member.

title: Daycare voucher (Kita-Gutschein)
tldr: In some federal states (especially Hamburg and Berlin) a daycare place is paid for through a voucher system — the daycare voucher (Kita-Gutschein). First you get a voucher from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) confirming a state-recognized need for childcare and the required number of hours, and then you "redeem" it at the daycare you choose. The daycare gets the money from the city, and you pay only your own share. In Berlin daycare (Kita) has been free (Gebührenfreiheit) since 2018 — parents pay only for meals, about 23 €/month. The voucher does not guarantee a specific daycare: you still have to find a place yourself.

content.text: A daycare voucher (Kita-Gutschein) is a document the city issues to a parent confirming that your child has a right to childcare and a recognized number of hours. The voucher itself contains no money — it is a "promise of payment". You find a daycare, hand it the voucher, and the daycare receives funding directly from the city. This model applies primarily in Hamburg and Berlin.

items: Step 1 — get the voucher (Gutschein) from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) / district office (Bezirksamt)
Step 2 — find a daycare willing to take the child (you have to search yourself)
Step 3 — "redeem" the voucher at the daycare, sign a contract
The city pays the daycare, the parent pays only their own share (if any)
The number of hours in the voucher depends on the need (parents' work, studies)

content.text: In states WITHOUT a voucher system, parents apply directly to daycares or through a common portal, and the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) only coordinates the places. Check the model in your particular city — the procedure is fundamentally different.

steps.title: Number of hours and the need

content.text: How many hours of care per day the voucher will cover depends on the recognized need (childcare need, Betreuungsbedarf). Every child is entitled to a basic amount, while an extended one (full day) applies if both parents work, study or are looking for work.

items: Basic care (Grundbetreuung) — every child is entitled to it
5, 7, 9 or 12 hours per day — depending on the need
A full day requires proof of employment/studies from both parents
For single parents — based on their employment
The number of hours is stated right in the voucher and carried over into the daycare contract

content.text: In Berlin, daycare (Kita) has been completely free (beitragsfrei) for all children since August 2018 — from nursery to school, regardless of income or the number of hours. Parents pay only a fixed contribution for meals of about 23 € a month, and low-income families are exempt even from that.

items: Care is free for all ages up to school
Meals (Verpflegung) — a fixed contribution of about 23 €/month
Low-income families are exempt even from the meal contribution
You still have to get the daycare voucher (Kita-Gutschein) from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt)
Being free does not remove the waiting list — you still have to find the place yourself

content.text: Free daycare in Berlin does not mean a place is easy to find. The shortage of places in Berlin is severe: having a voucher in hand does not guarantee a daycare. Apply to several daycares well in advance and keep your right to demand a place under § 24 SGB VIII.

The voucher is requested from the youth welfare office (in Berlin — from your district office (Bezirk), in Hamburg — from the district office (Bezirksamt)). It is worth applying in advance — the voucher is usually issued no earlier than a few months before the required date, but the exact deadlines depend on the city.

items: Application for cost coverage / daycare voucher (Antrag auf Kostenübernahme / Kita-Gutschein) at the youth welfare office (Jugendamt)
Attach proof of residence registration (Anmeldung), birth certificate, proof of measles vaccination (Masernschutznachweis)
Proof of the parents' employment/studies for extended hours
The youth welfare office (Jugendamt) sends the voucher (Gutschein) stating the number of hours and the validity period
Check that the required hours and period are stated
The voucher is valid for a limited time — redeem it on time
Find a daycare willing to take the child
Hand over the voucher, sign a childcare contract (Betreuungsvertrag)
The daycare arranges the funding from the city directly

costs.label: Care at a Kita (Berlin)
costs.note: Free for all children since 2018.

costs.label: Meals in Berlin (per month)
costs.note: A fixed contribution; low-income families are exempt.

costs.label: Parent's co-payment (Hamburg/others)
costs.note: Depends on hours and income; basic hours are often free.

costs.label: Getting the voucher
costs.note: Issuing the Kita-Gutschein at the Jugendamt is free.

title: University admission: Uni-Assist
tldr: For foreigners with a foreign school-leaving certificate or degree, admission to a German university most often goes through uni-assist — a centralized service for checking foreign educational documents. It assesses whether your certificate is recognized and forwards the application to the university. Cost: 75 € for the first application to one university per semester + 30 € for each further one. For subjects with a nationwide cap on places (an admission grade, NC — Medizin, Pharmazie) the application goes through the hochschulstart.de portal. If your certificate is not equivalent to a German one, you need a preparatory college attached to a university (Studienkolleg) and an entrance qualification exam (Feststellungsprüfung). The language barrier is covered by the university German exam DSH or the German exam for admission TestDaF.

content.text: In Germany there is no single admission system for everyone — the route depends on your qualification and the subject you choose. First work out which of the three routes is yours.

items: If you have a foreign school-leaving certificate/degree
uni-assist checks the documents and forwards them to the university or universities
Suitable for most bachelor's and master's programs
For the nationwide admission grade (Numerus Clausus): Medizin, Zahnmedizin, Pharmazie, Tiermedizin
Centralized allocation of places across the whole country
Some applications still go through uni-assist (certificate check)
Some universities accept foreign applications themselves, without uni-assist
EU citizens or holders of a German school-leaving certificate often have a direct route
Always check the requirements of the specific university on its website

content.text: uni-assist (Arbeits- und Servicestelle für internationale Studienbewerbungen) is the organization through which more than 170 German universities accept applications from foreign applicants. You create an online account, upload documents, send certified copies by post, and uni-assist checks the formal eligibility of the certificate and calculates your average grade on the German scale.

items: Registration in a personal account at uni-assist.de
Choosing universities and programs from the catalog
Uploading scans + sending certified copies and translations by post
uni-assist checks recognition of the certificate and converts the grades
The result is a preliminary review document (Vorprüfungsdokumentation, VPD) or forwarding to the university
The admission decision is made by the university itself, not by uni-assist

content.text: uni-assist checks only the FORMAL eligibility of the documents and forwards them — it does NOT make the admission decision. A positive uni-assist result does not equal admission; the final decision always rests with the university.
uni-assist charges a processing fee. The rate depends on the number of universities and semesters you apply for.

items: The first application to one university for one semester — 75 €
Each additional application in the same semester — 30 €
When applying to several universities, the amounts add up
Payment online by card or bank transfer
The application is processed only after the payment arrives

content.text: Allow time: the check through uni-assist takes several weeks, especially during peak application periods. Send your documents in advance, before the university's deadline (usually 15 July for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer one).

steps.title: Studienkolleg: if your certificate is not recognized

content.text: If your school-leaving certificate is not equivalent to the German certificate of completed secondary education (Abitur; which is often the case for school graduates from CIS countries), you will not be admitted directly to a bachelor's program. First you need to complete a preparatory college attached to a university (Studienkolleg) — a preparatory year — and pass the final entrance qualification exam (Feststellungsprüfung), which grants the right to admission.

items: A preparatory college attached to a university (Studienkolleg) — a preparatory course of about 1 year
Courses by track: T (technical), W (economics), M (medicine), G (humanities) and others
Concludes with an entrance qualification exam (Feststellungsprüfung, FSP)
A passed FSP grants the right to apply for programs in the corresponding track
State preparatory colleges (Studienkolleg) are usually free, private ones charge fees
Check recognition of the certificate in the anabin database (a database on the recognition of foreign qualifications) or through uni-assist

content.text: Whether your certificate is recognized directly can be checked in advance in the anabin database (Datenbank zur Anerkennung ausländischer Bildungsabschlüsse) run by the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education (Kultusministerkonferenz). This will save time and money before you apply.

For German-language programs you must prove your level of German. The two main exams are the university German exam DSH (Deutsche Sprachprüfung für den Hochschulzugang, taken at the university) and the German exam for admission TestDaF (Test Deutsch als Fremdsprache, taken at centers worldwide). For English-language programs, IELTS/TOEFL is required instead.

items: DSH-2 or TestDaF (usually level TDN 4 in all parts) — the standard for German-language programs
DSH is taken at the university, TestDaF — at accredited centers (possible abroad)
For English-language programs — IELTS or TOEFL instead of German
The level must be proven BEFORE enrollment, sometimes already at the application stage
Some universities recognize telc C1 Hochschule or the Goethe-Zertifikat C2

content.text: A language certificate is a separate requirement, and its absence blocks enrollment even if your certificate is perfect. Start learning the language and planning the exam long before applying: places for DSH/TestDaF are booked up in advance.

costs.label: uni-assist: first application (1 university / semester)
costs.note: The basic processing rate.

costs.label: uni-assist: each additional application
costs.note: In the same semester.

costs.label: Studienkolleg (state)
costs.note: Usually free; private courses charge fees.

costs.label: Semester fee (Semesterbeitrag)
costs.note: Paid to the university per semester; often includes a transit pass.

title: Childminder (Tagesmutter)
tldr: A childminder (Tagesmutter, or Tagesvater) is a licensed home-based carer who looks after a small group of children in their own home or in a special facility. It is a full alternative to a daycare and part of the home-based childcare system (Kindertagespflege) under § 43 SGB VIII. A childminder must hold a childcare permit (Pflegeerlaubnis) from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt), complete training, and may look after up to 5 children at a time. The service is subsidized by the municipality just like a daycare: the parent pays only their income-based share, and a place with a childminder also counts toward the legal right to childcare from age 1.

steps.title: What a Tagesmutter and Kindertagespflege are

content.text: A childminder (Tagesmutter, literally "day mother") is a professional carer who takes a small group of children into their care. Legally this is called home-based childcare (Kindertagespflege) and is governed by § 43 SGB VIII. Unlike a private nanny who looks after your child in your home without a license, a childminder holds an official permit from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) and works as part of the state childcare system.

items: Governed by § 43 SGB VIII (home-based childcare, Kindertagespflege)
Care is usually in the childminder's home or in a rented facility
A small group — up to 5 children at a time with one carer
Especially popular for toddlers under 3 (U3)
An alternative to a daycare (Kita) and counts toward the right to a place from age 1

content.text: A childminder is often chosen precisely for the youngest children: a home setting, a small group and individual attention suit children under 3 better than a large daycare. It also helps where there are simply no daycare (Kita) places available.

A childminder is not "just a neighbor who loves children". To look after other people's children for payment on a regular basis, you legally need a childcare permit (Pflegeerlaubnis) — a permit from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt). It is issued after a check and training.

items: A childcare permit (Pflegeerlaubnis) from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) — mandatory (§ 43 SGB VIII)
A basic training course (a minimum of ~160 hours under the DJI/QHB standard)
An extended certificate of good conduct (Erweitertes Führungszeugnis)
A check of the facility for safety and suitability
First aid for children and proof of health
Regular further training and support from the youth welfare office (Jugendamt)

content.text: Make sure your childminder has a valid childcare permit (Pflegeerlaubnis). Only a licensed carer is part of the state system — which means the service is subsidized by the municipality and you pay only your share. An illegal nanny without a permit is not subsidized and does not count toward the right to childcare.

steps.title: How to find and arrange one

content.text: The search for a childminder goes through the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) or specialized home-based childcare services (Kindertagespflege) — for example a childminder exchange (Tagespflegebörse) or a placement service (Vermittlungsstelle). They keep lists of licensed carers with vacancies and help you find a suitable one.

items: Contact the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) or the specialist home-based childcare service (Fachdienst Kindertagespflege)
Ask for a list of licensed childminders (Tagesmütter) with vacancies
Get to know them, view the facility, discuss hours and meals
Sign a childcare contract (Betreuungsvertrag) with the carer
Submit a funding application to the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) (cost coverage, Kostenübernahme)
Attach proof of employment and a certificate of income
The youth welfare office (Jugendamt) pays the carer the main part (a cash benefit, Geldleistung)
You pay only your share (the cost contribution, Kostenbeitrag) based on income
At a low income the share may be zero

steps.title: How much it costs the parent

content.text: The financial logic is the same as for a daycare (Kita): the municipality pays the childminder the main remuneration from the budget (an ongoing cash benefit, laufende Geldleistung under § 23 SGB VIII), and the parent pays a socially graded share (the cost contribution, Kostenbeitrag) depending on income, the number of children and the hours.

items: The parent pays only their share (the cost contribution, Kostenbeitrag), not the full rate
The share is calculated by the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) based on income — as for a daycare (Kita)
Low-income families and recipients of Bürgergeld/KiZ are often exempt
Meals may be paid for separately
A place with a childminder fulfills the legal right (Rechtsanspruch) under § 24 SGB VIII

costs.label: Parent's share (Kostenbeitrag, per month)
costs.note: Depends on income; calculated by the Jugendamt as for a Kita.

costs.label: Tagesmutter's remuneration
costs.note: The main part is paid by the municipality directly to the carer (§ 23 SGB VIII).

costs.label: Meals
costs.note: Sometimes paid for separately by arrangement.

Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB) Achtes Buch § 23 — Förderung in Kindertagespflege

title: Dual vocational training (Ausbildung)
tldr: Vocational training (Ausbildung) is dual vocational training, a hallmark of the German system: you work at a company and study at a vocational school (Berufsschule) at the same time. It lasts 2–3.5 years and ends with a recognized profession (anerkannter Ausbildungsberuf) and a state qualification. The key difference from studying is that you ARE PAID: the training salary (Ausbildungsvergütung) rises year by year and cannot be below the legal minimum (in 2026 — 724 € per month in the first year), and in sectors with collective agreements it is noticeably higher. It is a popular path into a profession for young people and a good way into the labor market for newcomers. Job databases are run by the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit), the Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training (BIBB) and the planet-beruf.de portal.

content.text: Vocational training (Ausbildung; more precisely — dual vocational education, duale Berufsausbildung) is a system in which you train for a profession in two places at once: for most of the week you work and train at a company (Betrieb), and 1–2 days a week or in blocks you attend a vocational school (Berufsschule), where you get the theory. Hence the name "dual" — two places of training.

items: Practice at a company + theory at a vocational school (Berufsschule)
Duration — usually 2–3.5 years depending on the profession
More than 320 recognized professions (anerkannte Ausbildungsberufe)
Concludes with an exam at the chamber of industry and commerce (IHK) or the chamber of skilled crafts (HWK) and a state qualification
Governed by the Vocational Training Act (BBiG)

content.text: A recognized profession (anerkannter Ausbildungsberuf) is a state-standard qualification that is valued throughout Germany and is often recognized in the EU. The list of professions and the standards are maintained by the Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training (BIBB, Bundesinstitut für Berufsbildung).

The key difference between vocational training (Ausbildung) and ordinary studies: you are paid from the first day. The training salary (Ausbildungsvergütung) is the pay the company provides. It rises with each year of training and cannot fall below the legal minimum (the minimum training salary, Mindestausbildungsvergütung) under § 17 BBiG, and in sectors with collective bargaining (a collective (sectoral) agreement, Tarifvertrag) it is noticeably higher.

items: The legal minimum in the 1st year in 2026 is 724 €/month (higher in sectors with collective agreements)
The minimum rises by year of training: +18 % in the 2nd, +35 % in the 3rd, +40 % in the 4th
The minimum floor (the minimum training salary, Mindestausbildungsvergütung, § 17 BBiG) is updated annually
In sectors with a collective (sectoral) agreement (Tarifvertrag) the rates are noticeably above the minimum
Contributions are paid from the salary — you are automatically in the social security system

content.text: The amounts depend heavily on the sector, region and the presence of a collective agreement. Do not rely on a single figure: check the specific offer and compare it with the current year's minimum rate in the Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training's database (Datenbank Ausbildungsvergütungen). The legal first-year minimum is set anew every calendar year.

steps.title: How to find an Ausbildung place

content.text: To start vocational training (Ausbildung), you first need to find a company willing to take you on (a training place, Ausbildungsplatz) and sign a contract with it. The vocational school (Berufsschule) is added automatically once you are employed. The search is conducted like a job search.

items: Explore the professions on planet-beruf.de and in BERUFENET
Take career-orientation tests (Check-U from the employment agency, Arbeitsagentur)
Go to careers fairs and open days
The training-places database (Ausbildungsstellen) of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit)
Company websites, the IHK apprenticeship exchange (IHK-Lehrstellenbörse), the chamber of skilled crafts (HWK)
Submit applications (Bewerbung) with a CV and a cover letter in advance
Sign a vocational training contract (Ausbildungsvertrag) with the company
The contract is registered with the chamber of industry and commerce (IHK) or the chamber of skilled crafts (HWK)
The company enrolls you in the corresponding vocational school (Berufsschule)

steps.title: Ausbildung for newcomers and the visa

content.text: Vocational training (Ausbildung) is an excellent entry into the German labor market for foreigners. For third-country nationals there is a separate residence permit for vocational training (Aufenthaltserlaubnis zur Berufsausbildung, § 16a AufenthG). It requires a confirmed training place and, as a rule, German at a level of about B1.

items: EU/EEA/Switzerland citizens — without visa restrictions
Third countries — § 16a AufenthG (residence permit for vocational training)
You need a confirmed training place and usually German at ~B1
After the training — a simplified transition to work in the profession
Recognition of a foreign certificate (Anerkennung) — through the anabin database (a database on the recognition of foreign qualifications)

content.text: After successfully completing vocational training (Ausbildung), a graduate from a third country can usually obtain a residence permit to work in the profession they have acquired, and over time also a more stable status. This is one of the most reliable ways to establish yourself in Germany.

If the training salary is not enough to live on, there is state support. The main tool is the vocational training allowance (Berufsausbildungsbeihilfe, BAB) from the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) for those who do not live with their parents.

items: Vocational training allowance (Berufsausbildungsbeihilfe, BAB) — a living-cost supplement during dual training
Application to the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit), the amount depends on income
Child benefit (Kindergeld) continues to be paid during training (up to age 25)
Housing benefit (Wohngeld) — possible at a low income
Assisted training (Assistierte Ausbildung) / study support (abH) — support in case of difficulties

title: Marriage at the registry office (Standesamt): documents
tldr: A legal marriage in Germany is concluded only at the registry office (Standesamt) — a church ceremony has no legal force. Foreigners almost always need a certificate of no impediment to marriage (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis) or an exemption from it through the higher regional court (OLG). We break down the document package, certified translations, fees of 40–90 € and the typical mistakes that push the wedding date back by months.

steps.title: Where and how a marriage is concluded

content.text: In Germany a legally valid marriage is concluded exclusively at a state registry office (Standesamt). This is laid down in § 1310 BGB: a marriage comes into being at the moment both partners declare, in person, simultaneously and in the presence of a registrar (Standesbeamter), their wish to marry. A religious (church) ceremony in Germany produces no legal consequences — it can be held after the civil registration, but that is purely the couple's private matter.

The process itself begins not with the wedding but with the declaration of intent to marry — the notice of marriage (Anmeldung der Eheschließung, formerly called Aufgebot). Both partners submit it at the registry office at the place of residence (Wohnsitz) of at least one of them. After accepting the documents, the registry office checks for any impediments to marriage; if everything is in order, you are given a ceremony date. Several weeks usually pass between submitting the notice (Anmeldung) and the wedding itself.

items: A legal marriage — only at the registry office (§ 1310 BGB)
First the notice of marriage (Anmeldung der Eheschließung), then the ceremony itself
Submit it at the place of residence of one of the partners
A church wedding — without legal force, optional after the registry office
Same-sex marriages (Ehe für alle) have been concluded the same way since 2017

steps.title: The basic document package for both

content.text: A minimum set is required from each partner regardless of nationality. Documents from abroad almost always need an apostille/legalization and a certified translation into German (beglaubigte Übersetzung) from a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer). It is best to check the exact list in advance — each registry office has its own quirks, especially by country of origin.

items: A valid passport or national identity card (Personalausweis)
A certified extract from the birth register (Beglaubigte Abschrift aus dem Geburtenregister) / a recent certified birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde)
An extended residence registration certificate (Erweiterte Meldebescheinigung) — obtained from the residents' registration office (Einwohnermeldeamt) / district citizens' office (Bürgeramt)
Proof of marital status (that you are not married) — a certificate of single status (Ledigkeitsbescheinigung)
For the divorced — a court divorce decree with a note of legal force (Scheidungsurteil mit Rechtskraftvermerk)
For widowers — the spouse's death certificate
If you have children together — their birth certificates

content.text: Many documents have a "shelf life": registry offices often require the birth certificate and the registration certificate to have been issued no earlier than 6 months before submission. Old documents will need to be renewed — allow time for this.

The key document for a foreigner is the certificate of no impediment to marriage (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis). This is a document from your country of citizenship confirming that, under the laws of your homeland, nothing prevents you from marrying (you are of age, not married, etc.). It is issued by the registry authorities or another authorized body of the country of origin; the document is needed with an apostille and a certified translation.

The problem is that a whole range of countries — including Russia, Ukraine and a number of CIS countries — do not issue such a certificate at all or issue it in a form that the German registry office does not recognize. In that case you need an exemption from presenting the certificate — an exemption from the obligation to present a certificate of no impediment to marriage (Befreiung von der Beibringung des Ehefähigkeitszeugnisses), issued by the president of the higher regional court (Oberlandesgericht, OLG). The application for an exemption (Befreiung) is submitted through the same registry office; the OLG decision is usually valid for about 6 months.

items: You obtain the certificate of no impediment to marriage (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis) in your homeland (or via a consulate)
You add an apostille / legalization
You get a certified translation into German
The certificate is valid for a limited time — usually 6 months

items.title: 2. Your country does NOT issue the certificate

items: Through the registry office you apply for an exemption (Befreiung) via the higher regional court (OLG)
You prepare an extended package: on marital status, birth, registration
The OLG checks your documents instead of the certificate
The fee for the exemption (Befreiung) depends on income — it can be substantial
The OLG decision is valid for a limited time — plan the wedding date around it

content.text: The exemption procedure through the regional court (OLG-Befreiung) is the biggest bottleneck in terms of time. Several months can pass from submission to the decision, especially if the documents are from a country with complex legalization. Start gathering documents as early as possible and do not set a "firm" wedding date until the OLG decision is in.

Once both partners have submitted the notice of marriage (Anmeldung) and handed in the full package, the registry office checks for the absence of impediments and sets a ceremony date. The notice (Anmeldung) is valid for a limited time (usually 6 months) — if you have not managed to marry within that period, the submission has to be repeated. For the ceremony itself you may invite witnesses (not obligatory), and also arrange a ceremonial hall or an off-site ceremony (for an extra fee).

items: The fee for the notice/check (Anmeldung/Prüfung) without a foreign element — usually ~40–50 €
If foreign law is involved (a foreign partner) — higher, ~70–90 €
A certificate of no impediment to marriage (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis) from abroad — ~20–50 € + apostille
A certified translation of each document — ~30–70 € per document
An exemption through the regional court (OLG-Befreiung) — the fee depends on income, can be significant
A ceremonial hall/Saturday/off-site ceremony — a separate extra fee

content.text: After the wedding you receive a marriage certificate (Eheurkunde). Do not forget to update your records everywhere: a name change (if you chose a common married name, Ehename) entails replacing documents — the national identity card (Personalausweis)/passport, driving license, insurance cards, and for foreigners — updating the data at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) and, if necessary, changing the basis of residence (marriage to an EU/German citizen may grant a right to a residence permit).

costs.note: The basic fee for accepting and checking the notice without a foreign element.

costs.label: Anmeldung with a foreign partner
costs.note: Higher because of checking foreign law.

costs.label: Ehefähigkeitszeugnis (from the country of citizenship)
costs.note: Plus apostille/legalization; in some countries it is not issued at all.

costs.label: Certified translation of a document
costs.note: Per document; a sworn translator.

costs.label: OLG-Befreiung (exemption from the certificate)
costs.note: The fee is calculated on the applicants' income; needed if the country does not issue an Ehefähigkeitszeugnis.

title: Housing benefit (Wohngeld) 2026
tldr: Housing benefit (Wohngeld) is a state supplement toward rent (a rent subsidy, Mietzuschuss) or toward the costs of owner-occupied housing (a burden subsidy, Lastenzuschuss) for people on a low income who do NOT receive Bürgergeld. After the Wohngeld-Plus reform (2023), millions of new households became eligible, and after the scheduled indexation (Fortschreibung) from January 2026 the average payment rose to about 435 €/month. We break down who is eligible, how it is calculated and where to apply at the housing benefit office (Wohngeldstelle).

steps.title: What Wohngeld is and who is eligible

content.text: Housing benefit (Wohngeld) is a state subsidy toward housing, regulated by the Housing Benefit Act (WoGG). It is NOT Bürgergeld and NOT social assistance: housing benefit is intended for people who earn an income themselves but whose income is not enough to fully cover the cost of housing. There are two forms: a rent subsidy (Mietzuschuss) — a supplement for tenants, and a burden subsidy (Lastenzuschuss) — a supplement for owners who live in their own housing.

An important rule of demarcation: housing benefit (Wohngeld) and Bürgergeld cannot be received at the same time for the same costs. If you receive Bürgergeld (SGB II) or basic income support (Grundsicherung, SGB XII), the cost of housing is already covered by those benefits, and housing benefit is not available to you. Housing benefit is precisely an "in-between" support for workers, pensioners and students with their own income.

items: A rent subsidy (Mietzuschuss) — for tenants; a burden subsidy (Lastenzuschuss) — for owner-occupiers
For those who do NOT receive Bürgergeld/basic income support (Grundsicherung)
Eligibility depends on income, household size and the amount of rent
The legal basis is the Housing Benefit Act (WoGG)
Submitted to the local housing benefit office (at the city/district)

steps.title: The Wohngeld-Plus reform and who benefited

content.text: Since 1 January 2023 the largest reform — Wohngeld-Plus — has been in force. It pursued three goals: to raise the payments themselves, to expand the pool of recipients, and to build into the calculation a permanent component for heating and climate (the heating and climate component, Heizkosten- und Klimakomponente). As a result, the number of households eligible for housing benefit (Wohngeld) grew several times over — the subsidy became available to many families who previously "fell short" of Bürgergeld but also could not manage the rent.

items: Wohngeld-Plus has been in force since 01.01.2023; the rules are regularly indexed (the latest indexation (Fortschreibung) — from 01.01.2026)
A permanent heating component (Heizkostenkomponente) is built into the calculation
A climate component (Klimakomponente) has been added — a surcharge accounting for the rise in energy costs
The average payment in 2026 is around 435 €/month (depends on the case)
Many who were previously refused are now eligible — it is worth recalculating

content.text: The main practical takeaway: if you were refused housing benefit (Wohngeld) before 2023, it makes sense to apply again. The reform shifted the thresholds substantially, and a significant share of people on a salary just above the subsistence level, as well as pensioners on a small pension, now meet the criteria.

The amount of housing benefit (Wohngeld) is not fixed — it is calculated individually using the formula from the WoGG and depends on three parameters: (1) the total income of all household members, (2) the amount of countable rent/burden (within the upper limits) and (3) the number of household members. The rent limits are affected by the rent level (Mietstufe) in your city (from I to VII): the more expensive the region, the higher the rent ceiling taken into account.

items: The combined income of everyone living together is counted
Flat-rate deductions (for taxes, social security contributions) are subtracted from the gross income
The lower the net countable income, the higher the housing benefit (Wohngeld)
If your income is too high, eligibility for housing benefit disappears
The "cold" rent + allowable costs are counted (without heating — that goes via the component)
The rent level (Mietstufe) I–VII determines the upper limit of countable rent
In expensive cities (Mietstufe VI–VII) the ceiling is higher
Rent above the limit is counted only up to the ceiling
The more people, the higher the limits and the higher the payment
All family members living together are counted
Children and dependents increase eligibility for the subsidy

content.text: The application is submitted to the housing benefit office (Wohngeldstelle) — a department at your city or district administration (Stadt/Landkreis). Many cities already accept online applications. Housing benefit is granted, as a rule, for 12 months (the approval period, Bewilligungszeitraum), after which you have to apply again (a continuation application, Weiterleistungsantrag). The payment starts from the month of application — housing benefit is usually not paid "retroactively" for past months, so apply as soon as you realize you are eligible.

items: A rental contract (Mietvertrag) and proof of the rent amount
Income certificates for all household members (payslips, Lohnabrechnungen, pension, etc.)
A residence registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) / proof of registration
Documents for children and dependents, if any
Bank details (IBAN) for the payment
A completed housing benefit application form (Wohngeldantrag; on the city's website or at the housing benefit office)

content.text: Housing benefit (Wohngeld) is paid only from the month of application and going forward, not retroactively. If your situation has changed (the rent went up, your income dropped), apply straight away — every month of delay is money lost. And remember: you cannot receive housing benefit and Bürgergeld at the same time — first check which is more advantageous for you.

costs.note: The application and its processing are free.

costs.note: On average about 435 €/month (2026); depends on income, rent and family composition.

title: Child support (Unterhalt): the Düsseldorf Table (Düsseldorfer Tabelle)
tldr: The amount of child support (Kindesunterhalt) in Germany is set by the Düsseldorf Table (Düsseldorfer Tabelle) — a chart that ties the amount to the payer's net income and the child's age. As of 1 January 2026 the minimum support went up: 486 € (ages 0–5), 558 € (6–11), 653 € (12–17) in the first income group. The payer is guaranteed an untouchable minimum (Selbstbehalt) — 1450 € while employed. We explain how to read the table and where the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) comes in.

steps.title: What the Düsseldorf Table (Düsseldorfer Tabelle) is

content.text: The Düsseldorf Table (Düsseldorfer Tabelle) is not a law but a guideline chart (Leitlinie) drawn up by the Higher Regional Court of Düsseldorf (Oberlandesgericht Düsseldorf) together with other regional courts and updated, as a rule, on 1 January each year. Courts all over Germany use it to calculate the amount of child support (Kindesunterhalt) consistently. The legal duty to support a child follows from § 1601 ff. BGB; the table merely translates that duty into concrete figures.

The logic of the table is simple: the support amount rises with (1) the payer's net income (Bereinigtes Nettoeinkommen, broken down into income groups) and (2) the child's age (4 age brackets: 0–5, 6–11, 12–17, 18 and over). The higher the paying parent's income and the older the child, the larger the amount. The first income group sets the minimum support (Mindestunterhalt).

items: The Düsseldorf Table is usually updated on 1 January each year
The basis of the duty is § 1601 ff. BGB (support among relatives)
The amount depends on the payer's net income and the child's age
It is a guideline for courts, not the law itself

content.text: As of 1 January 2026 the minimum support (Mindestunterhalt) in the first income group went up again. These are the base amounts below which support for a minor child usually does not fall.

items: Ages 0–5: 486 € per month (1st income group, 2026)
Ages 6–11: 558 € per month
Ages 12–17: 653 € per month
From age 18: calculated separately, usually taking both parents into account
As the payer's income rises, amounts go above the base figures (higher groups of the table)

content.text: An important detail: half of the child benefit (Kindergeld) is credited against these amounts. For a minor child, half of the child benefit is deducted from the table figure (the so-called amount actually paid out, the Zahlbetrag, which is lower than the table figure). This is because child benefit legally counts as support from both parents, and the share attributable to the paying parent is credited against their support.

items: 1st group — net income up to roughly 2100 €/month (minimum rates)
The higher the income group, the higher the percentage of the minimum support (Mindestunterhalt)
The top groups give substantially larger amounts than the minimum
Work-related expenses and certain debts are deducted from income (Bereinigung)
The table amount (Tabellenbetrag) — for example, 486 € for ages 0–5
Half of the child benefit (Kindergeld) is deducted from it
The amount actually transferred (Zahlbetrag) — what is really paid out
So the actual payment is lower than the figure in the table

steps.title: The untouchable minimum (Selbstbehalt): what the payer keeps

content.text: A support payer cannot be "squeezed dry": the law and the table guarantee them an untouchable minimum (Selbstbehalt, own need — Eigenbedarf) — an amount that must remain for them to live on. The levels of the untouchable minimum in 2026 in respect of minor and privileged adult children stayed unchanged.

items: The untouchable minimum for a working payer is 1450 €/month (2026)
For a non-working payer it is 1200 €/month
If income is not enough to cover the minimum for all children, this is a shortfall case (Mangelfall)
In a shortfall case the court distributes the available amount among the children proportionally
The receiving parent has their own subsistence-minimum thresholds

content.text: The untouchable minimum in respect of minor children is lower than in respect of other relatives. Minimum support for children takes priority: if money is tight, minor children are provided for first, rather than, say, a former spouse or the payer's parents.

steps.title: How to arrange it through the youth welfare office (Jugendamt): advisory support (Beistandschaft)

content.text: The parent the child lives with does not have to hire a lawyer to obtain support. You can turn to the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) free of charge and set up advisory support (Beistandschaft; §§ 1712–1717 BGB, § 18 SGB VIII): a staff member of the office helps establish paternity (Vaterschaft), calculate and collect support, including drawing up an official enforceable document (Jugendamtsurkunde) under which a debt can be collected without going to court.

items: Advisory support (Beistandschaft) at the youth welfare office — free and voluntary for the receiving parent
They help establish paternity (Vaterschaftsfeststellung)
They calculate support according to the Düsseldorf Table
They draw up an official enforceable document (Jugendamtsurkunde) — an enforcement title without a court
If payments are missed — help with collection; a state advance on support (Unterhaltsvorschuss) may be possible

content.text: If the other parent does not pay support, there is a state advance on support (Unterhaltsvorschuss, under the Unterhaltsvorschussgesetz) that is paid to the child up to a certain age, with the state later recovering the money from the debtor. This is a lifeline for single parents left without payments. The application for the advance is filed with the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) or the relevant department (Unterhaltsvorschussstelle).

costs.note: 1st income group; before deducting half of Kindergeld.

costs.label: Minimum support ages 6–11 (2026)
costs.note: 1st income group of the Düsseldorfer Tabelle.

costs.label: Minimum support ages 12–17 (2026)
costs.note: 1st income group; the highest age bracket for minors.

costs.label: Beistandschaft through the Jugendamt
costs.note: Help with establishing paternity and collecting support — free of charge.

title: Care level (Pflegegrad): levels 1-5
tldr: The care level (Pflegegrad) is the key to all care benefits in Germany. A level from 1 to 5 is assigned by the medical service (Medizinischer Dienst, MD) using a points system across 6 modules (mobility, cognition, self-care, etc.). The care level determines the amount of the care allowance (Pflegegeld): in 2026 that is 347 € (PG2), 599 € (PG3), 800 € (PG4), 990 € (PG5). We explain how the assessment works and how to apply.

content.text: The care level (Pflegegrad) is the officially determined degree of a person's need for care. The system is governed by the Eleventh Book of the Social Code — SGB XI. Since 2017, instead of the old three "care stages" (Pflegestufen), there are five care levels (Pflegegrade, from 1 to 5), which cover not only physical frailty but also cognitive impairments (such as dementia). The higher the care level, the greater the need for help — and the higher the payments and services from the care fund (Pflegekasse).

items: Care level 1 — minor impairment of independence
Care level 2 — significant impairment
Care level 3 — severe impairment
Care level 4 — most severe impairment
Care level 5 — most severe impairment with special care requirements
Legal basis — SGB XI (Soziale Pflegeversicherung, social long-term care insurance)

steps.title: How the medical service (Medizinischer Dienst) assesses: 6 modules

content.text: The level is determined not by the family doctor but by an independent assessor — the medical service (Medizinischer Dienst, MD) for people in statutory insurance (or MEDICPROOF for private insurance). The assessor comes to the home and rates the person's independence using a points system (the new assessment method — Neues Begutachtungsassessment, NBA). 6 modules are assessed, each with its own weighting; the resulting total of weighted points (0–100) determines the care level.

items: Module 1 — mobility, getting around (Mobilität)
Module 2 — cognition, communication (Kognitive und kommunikative Fähigkeiten)
Module 3 — behaviour, mental state (Verhaltensweisen und psychische Problemlagen)
Module 4 — self-care: eating, hygiene (Selbstversorgung)
Module 5 — treatment, taking medication (Bewältigung von krankheits-/therapiebedingten Anforderungen)
Module 6 — organising daily life and social contacts (Gestaltung des Alltagslebens)
Modules 2 and 3 are counted by the higher of the two (not added together)
The result is a weighted points total from 0 to 100
from 12.5 points — care level 1
from 27 points — care level 2
from 47.5 points — care level 3
from 70 points — care level 4; from 90 — care level 5

content.text: You need to prepare for the medical service assessor's visit: keep a care diary (Pflegetagebuch) for 1–2 weeks, gather all medical reports, and don't play down the situation out of pride. A common mistake is that on the day of the visit the person "pulls themselves together" and presents better than usual, which results in an understated care level. Describe the worst days, not the best.

The main cash payment is the care allowance (Pflegegeld): it is paid if the person is cared for at home by relatives/informal helpers (rather than a professional service). The money is transferred to the care recipient themselves, who uses it for the benefit of whoever cares for them. As of 1 January 2025 the care allowance was raised by 4.5 %, and these amounts continue to apply in 2026 (the next scheduled adjustment is only from 1 January 2028).

items: Care level 1: no care allowance is paid (only the relief amount — Entlastungsbetrag)
Care level 2: 347 €/month (2026)
Care level 3: 599 €/month (2026)
Care level 4: 800 €/month (2026)
Care level 5: 990 €/month (2026)
An alternative to cash is care service benefits (Pflegesachleistungen), with higher amounts

content.text: At care level 1, no cash care allowance is paid out, but a relief amount is available (Entlastungsbetrag, around 131 €/month) — an earmarked amount for relief services (cleaning, accompaniment, day care). You can also combine the care allowance and care service benefits (combination benefit — Kombinationsleistung) if part of the care is taken on by a professional service.

The application is filed with the care fund (Pflegekasse) — it sits within your health insurance fund (Krankenkasse). It is enough to call or write informally, "Ich beantrage Leistungen aus der Pflegeversicherung" — the date of the request fixes the start of possible payments. After that, the fund sends a questionnaire and then schedules a visit by the medical service assessor. Payments run from the month the application is filed (if the decision is positive), even if the assessment took place later.

items: Step 1 — file the application with the care fund (Pflegekasse; in writing/by phone), the date matters
Step 2 — fill in the fund's questionnaire
Step 3 — home visit by the medical service assessor (MD)/MEDICPROOF
Step 4 — the decision on the care level arrives by letter
Step 5 — if you disagree, file an objection (Widerspruch) within 1 month
Payments — from the month the application is filed

content.text: If the assigned care level is lower than expected, don't give up: file an objection (Widerspruch) within one month. Request a copy of the assessor's report (Gutachten) from the fund and challenge the module points point by point. The success rate of care objections is fairly high, especially with dementia, which is underestimated at the first visit.

costs.note: For care by relatives at home; the rate applies from 01.01.2025.

costs.label: Pflegegeld Pflegegrad 3 (2026)
