title: Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung)
tldr: Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) is mandatory insurance against the need for care, the fifth pillar of the German social insurance system (SGB XI). The contribution in 2026 is 3.6 % of income (split with the employer) plus a 0.6 % surcharge for the childless (Kinderlosenzuschlag). It is this fund that finances the care allowance (Pflegegeld) and care services according to your care level (Pflegegrad). We explain who is insured, how the contribution is calculated, and what the insurance covers.

steps.title: What it is and who is insured

content.text: Social long-term care insurance (Soziale Pflegeversicherung) is mandatory social insurance for the case where a person becomes in need of care (pflegebedürftig). It is the "fifth pillar" of the German social insurance system alongside health, pension, unemployment and accident insurance. The legal basis is SGB XI. The principle "care insurance follows health insurance" (Pflegeversicherung folgt Krankenversicherung) applies: you are automatically covered for care wherever you are covered for health — in a statutory (gesetzlich) or private (privat) fund.

items: Mandatory for practically all residents of Germany
Governed by SGB XI
Follows your health insurance: statutory (soziale PV) or private (private PV)
Administered by the care fund (Pflegekasse) at your health insurance fund (Krankenkasse)
Finances care payments and services once you have a care level (Pflegegrad)

content.text: The contribution to social long-term care insurance in 2026 is 3.6 % of contributory income (beitragspflichtiges Einkommen), up to the contribution assessment ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze). For employees the contribution is split roughly in half with the employer. For childless insured persons aged 23 and over, a childless surcharge (Kinderlosenzuschlag) of 0.6 % applies, so their rate is 4.2 %; this surcharge is paid by the employee alone, without the employer's involvement.

items: Base rate 2026: 3.6 % (stable compared with 2025)
Split between employee and employer (roughly evenly)
Childless from age 23: +0.6 % surcharge → 4.2 % in total
The childless surcharge is paid by the employee alone
With 2 or more children — discounts for each child (up to the 5th)

content.text: Since July 2023 the childless surcharge and the discounts for children have been differentiated: for the second through fifth child (while each is under 25), the rate drops by 0.25 % per child. In other words, families with several children pay less, and the childless pay more. When the youngest child turns 25, the discounts end, but the base "family" rate without the childless surcharge stays for life (the fact of having children does not "expire").

Long-term care insurance is partial-coverage insurance (the partial-coverage principle — Teilkaskoprinzip): it does NOT pay all care costs but only pays fixed amounts depending on the care level (Pflegegrad). The difference (especially with inpatient care) is topped up by the person themselves or, if their means are insufficient, by the social welfare office (Sozialamt) through care assistance (Hilfe zur Pflege). It is important to understand this in advance, so you don't count on the fund covering the full cost of a nursing home.

items: Care allowance (Pflegegeld) — cash for care by relatives (347–990 €/month by care level)
Care service benefits (Pflegesachleistungen) — payment for a professional service (Pflegedienst)
Combination benefit (Kombinationsleistung) — a mix of cash and services
Relief amount (Entlastungsbetrag, ~131 €/month) — for relief services
Substitute care (Verhinderungspflege) — when the relative is on holiday/ill
Short-term inpatient care (Kurzzeitpflege)
Day/night care (Tages-/Nachtpflege, teilstationär)
Care consumables (Pflegehilfsmittel) — gloves, incontinence pads — and assistive devices
Measures to improve the living environment (Wohnumfeldverbessernde Maßnahmen) — a subsidy for adapting the home (up to 4000 €)

content.text: Don't confuse long-term care insurance with health insurance: treatment, medication and hospital are health insurance (Krankenversicherung). Long-term care insurance kicks in only when a person has been assigned a care level (Pflegegrad) and needs help specifically with everyday life. Without a registered care level the care fund pays nothing, even if you have paid contributions for decades.

steps.title: Private insurance, migrants and the fine print

content.text: If you are insured with a private health fund (PKV), you will also have private mandatory long-term care insurance (private Pflegepflichtversicherung) — it too is mandatory by law, and you cannot opt out of it. In terms of benefit scope, private care insurance is obliged to provide no less than the statutory system. For newcomers the rule is simple: as soon as you take out health insurance (for example when you start a job), care insurance is added automatically — there is no need to arrange it separately.

items: PKV → private mandatory long-term care insurance (private Pflegepflichtversicherung; also mandatory)
The protection scope of private care insurance is no lower than the statutory one
For newcomers, care insurance is added automatically together with health insurance
Pensioners pay the contribution from their pension (the pension fund covers part)
Family insurance (Familienversicherung) — children/a non-working spouse free of charge in a statutory fund

content.text: When moving to Germany, the key thing is to have health insurance at all — without it there is no care insurance either. If you work without registered insurance or in a "grey" zone, you risk ending up with no entitlement to the care allowance (Pflegegeld) in the future. Make sure contributions are actually being paid (they are visible on your pay slip — Lohnabrechnung).

costs.label: Pflegeversicherung contribution 2026 (base)
costs.note: Percentage of income; split with the employer (the value in "euros" = the % rate).

costs.label: Childless surcharge (Kinderlosenzuschlag)
costs.note: On top of the base rate → 4.2 % for the childless aged 23 and over; paid by the employee.

costs.label: Subsidy for adapting the home
costs.note: Wohnumfeldverbessernde Maßnahmen — up to 4000 € per measure if you have a Pflegegrad.

title: The youth welfare office (Jugendamt): how it helps and how it can be dangerous
tldr: The youth welfare office (Jugendamt) is a two-faced institution: on one hand it helps families free of charge (daycare — Kita, counselling, child support via advisory support — Beistandschaft, parenting help — Hilfen zur Erziehung); on the other, it has the power to step in and, where a child is at risk, take the child away (temporary protective custody — Inobhutnahme, § 42 SGB VIII). For migrant families it is a frequent source of anxiety. We explain the balance: when the office is an ally and when you should be on guard and call a lawyer.

steps.title: What the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) is

content.text: The youth welfare office (Jugendamt) is a municipal authority for child protection and family support, operating on the basis of the Eighth Book of the Social Code (Achtes Buch Sozialgesetzbuch, SGB VIII) — the law on child and youth services (Kinder- und Jugendhilfe). Its dual task is reflected in the law itself: on one hand, to support parents in raising children (§ 1 SGB VIII), on the other, to safeguard the child's well-being (Kindeswohl), up to and including intervention when parents cannot manage it. It is precisely this duality that makes the office both a helper and a supervisory body.

items: A municipal authority, operating under SGB VIII
The law's main yardstick is the child's well-being (Kindeswohl)
It supports families AND monitors children's safety
Most contacts are voluntary and free of charge
Intervention against the parents' will is a last resort, under judicial oversight

steps.title: How the youth welfare office actually helps

content.text: For most families the youth welfare office is a free support resource, not a threat. You can come here for parenting advice, help in a crisis, arranging a daycare place (Kita), and support for single parents. Parenting help services (Hilfen zur Erziehung, §§ 27 ff. SGB VIII) include a family helper (Familienhilfe), educational support and counselling — all of it provided at the parents' own request.

items.title: 1. Advisory support (Beistandschaft) — help with child support and paternity

items: Free help establishing paternity (Vaterschaft)
Calculating and collecting child support (Unterhalt) without a lawyer
Drawing up an official enforceable document (Jugendamtsurkunde) — an enforcement title
Especially valuable for single parents
Parenting counselling (Erziehungsberatung)
An in-home family helper (Sozialpädagogische Familienhilfe)
Support with conflicts, divorce, difficulties with a teenager
Provided at the parents' request (voluntarily)
Help getting a daycare place (a voucher — Kita-Gutschein)
Information about benefits and family services
Support in difficult life situations
Early help for young parents (Frühe Hilfen)

steps.title: When the office steps in: temporary protective custody (Inobhutnahme)

content.text: The most painful topic for migrant families is the youth welfare office's power to take a child temporarily into protective custody (Inobhutnahme, § 42 SGB VIII). This is not arbitrary: the law allows removal only in case of serious danger to the child (dringende Gefahr für das Wohl des Kindes) — for example, violence, severe neglect, a threat to health. Temporary protective custody is an emergency measure; if the parents object, the office must immediately (by the next working day) turn to the family court (Familiengericht), and it is the court that decides whether continuation is justified.

items: Temporary protective custody (Inobhutnahme, § 42 SGB VIII) — a temporary protective measure, not a punishment
Permissible only in case of a real danger to the child
If the parents object, the case is referred straight to the family court (Familiengericht)
The decision to restrict parental rights is made by the COURT, not the office
A teenage child can ask for protection themselves (Selbstmelder)

content.text: There is a real risk of misunderstanding for migrants: cultural differences in parenting, the language barrier and stress can be interpreted against you. If the youth welfare office shows up to check on you — stay calm, ask for an interpreter, don't sign documents you don't understand, and in a serious conflict consult a family law (Familienrecht) lawyer right away. You have the right to a defence and to appeal in court.

The sober view is this: for the vast majority of families the youth welfare office is a source of free help, not out to take children away. Rumours about "taking children away over poverty" are greatly exaggerated: poverty in itself is not grounds for protective custody — on the contrary, in case of material hardship the office is supposed to offer support. Being afraid to ask for help because of these rumours is a mistake that deprives the family of real resources.

That said, reasonable caution is in order: put agreements in writing, keep an interpreter with you at important meetings, and at any mention of protective custody (Inobhutnahme) or the family court (Familiengericht), bring in a lawyer. Knowing your rights turns the youth welfare office from a bogeyman into a resource you can use — and one you can, if necessary, defend yourself against in court.

items: Poverty is NOT grounds to take a child; it is a reason to offer help
Most services are voluntary and initiated by the parents themselves
Put agreements in writing, ask for an interpreter
If removal is threatened — a family law (Familienrecht) lawyer immediately
Decisions on parental rights are overseen by an independent court

title: Legal guardianship (Rechtliche Betreuung): care for adults
tldr: Legal guardianship (Rechtliche Betreuung) is a form of legal representation for adults who, due to illness or disability, cannot manage their own affairs. After the 2023 reform (§ 1814 BGB and following), the focus shifted to self-determination: the guardian (Betreuer) only supports, rather than "giving orders". Guardianship is appointed by the guardianship court (Betreuungsgericht) and only in those areas where it is genuinely necessary. We explain how it differs from a power of attorney (Vollmacht) and how to avoid unnecessary guardianship.

content.text: Legal guardianship (Rechtliche Betreuung) is a form of legal support for an adult who, due to illness or disability (mental, physical or intellectual), is wholly or partly unable to manage their own legal and everyday affairs. With the reform of guardianship law that took effect on 1 January 2023, the central provision is § 1814 BGB. The old concept of wardship (Vormundschaft) for adults no longer exists: for adults there is only guardianship (Betreuung), and wardship remains only for minors.

The key idea of the reform is self-determination (Selbstbestimmung). The guardian (Betreuer) is not the ward's "boss": they must act according to the person's wishes (Wünsche des Betreuten), support them rather than replace them where the person can manage on their own. Guardianship is appointed only for specific tasks (areas of responsibility — Aufgabenbereiche) — for example, financial affairs, health, housing — and does not automatically strip the person of legal capacity.

items: For adults unable to manage their affairs themselves
The central provision is § 1814 BGB (reform from 01.01.2023)
Wardship (Vormundschaft) for adults has been abolished — only guardianship (Betreuung)
The principle is self-determination and support, not control
Appointed only for the necessary areas (Aufgabenbereiche)

steps.title: When guardianship is needed and when it isn't

content.text: Guardianship is a last resort (the necessity principle — Erforderlichkeitsgrundsatz, § 1814 Abs. 3 BGB): the court may not appoint it if the person's affairs can be helped in another way. If, while still legally competent, the person set up a power of attorney for the event of incapacity (Vorsorgevollmacht) in favour of a trusted person, guardianship is usually not needed at all — the trusted person acts on the basis of the power of attorney. So the best protection against unnecessary guardianship is a timely power of attorney for the event of incapacity (Vorsorgevollmacht).

items.title: 1. Power of attorney for incapacity (Vorsorgevollmacht) — better than guardianship

items: Set up in advance, while the person is still competent
You appoint the trusted person yourself (not the court)
Usually makes court guardianship unnecessary
Can be registered in the Central Register of Powers of Attorney (Zentrales Vorsorgeregister)
A living will (Patientenverfügung) — instructions about treatment
A care directive (Betreuungsverfügung) — your wish as to WHO the court should appoint as guardian, if guardianship is needed after all
Taken into account by courts and doctors
They supplement, but do not replace, a power of attorney

content.text: A common misconception: "I'm the spouse, so I can automatically decide for my partner." That is not so — there is no general automatic representation between spouses in financial matters. There is only a narrow emergency right of representation between spouses (Notvertretungsrecht) in urgent medical matters (§ 1358 BGB) for up to 6 months. For everything else you need either a power of attorney (Vollmacht) or guardianship (Betreuung).

Guardianship is appointed by the guardianship court (Betreuungsgericht — a division of the local court, Amtsgericht). It can be initiated by the person themselves, a relative, a doctor, a hospital or a social service. The court is required to hear the person in person, orders a medical assessment (an expert opinion — Sachverständigengutachten) on whether guardianship is necessary and, as a rule, brings in a procedural representative (Verfahrenspfleger) — an independent person representing the ward's interests in the proceedings. The court prefers a close person as guardian; if there is none, a professional guardian (Berufsbetreuer) is appointed.

items: The decision is made by the guardianship court (Betreuungsgericht) at the local court (Amtsgericht)
A personal interview between the judge and the person and a medical assessment are mandatory
Appointed only for specific areas (property, health, housing)
Priority goes to a close person; otherwise a professional guardian (Berufsbetreuer)
For major decisions (selling the home, an operation) court approval is needed
Guardianship is periodically reviewed for necessity

content.text: The guardian must report to the court annually (on finances and on the ward's condition) and must obtain the guardianship court's approval for especially important steps — for example, placement in a closed facility or serious medical intervention. This is a system of checks: even an appointed guardian does not have unlimited power and is under the court's supervision.

steps.title: The ward's rights and ending guardianship

content.text: The 2023 reform strengthened the ward's own rights. In most cases guardianship does NOT strip the person of legal capacity: they can still vote in elections, marry and carry out everyday transactions. Only in particular severe cases does the court impose a requirement of the guardian's consent for certain transactions (Einwilligungsvorbehalt) — but this is the exception, not the rule, and it too is limited to specific areas.

items: Guardianship in itself does not strip a person of legal capacity
The right to vote and the right to marry are retained
A requirement of the guardian's consent (Einwilligungsvorbehalt, § 1825 BGB) — only in exceptional cases
The ward has the right to appeal decisions and to request a change of guardian
Guardianship is lifted as soon as it is no longer necessary

content.text: Guardianship is not a "life sentence". The court must periodically check whether it is still needed and must lift or narrow it if the person is once again able to manage part of their affairs themselves. If you or your relative believe guardianship is no longer needed or has been imposed too broadly, you can file an application for review with the guardianship court (Betreuungsgericht).

costs.note: Depends on the scope and assets; a simple one can be done without a notary, and certifying the signature is cheaper.

costs.label: Registration in the Zentrales Vorsorgeregister
costs.note: A one-off fee for entering the power of attorney in the central register.

costs.label: Berufsbetreuer (professional guardian)
costs.note: Remuneration at fixed rates; if the ward has no means, the state covers it.

title: Basic income support (Grundsicherung): help for the elderly
tldr: Basic income support in old age and on reduced earning capacity (Grundsicherung im Alter und bei Erwerbsminderung, SGB XII) is basic support for pensioners and people with disabilities whose income (often a small pension) is not enough to live on. In essence it is "basic allowance (Bürgergeld) for those who can no longer work". The standard rate in 2026 is 563 €/month for a single person, plus housing and heating costs. It is filed with the social welfare office (Sozialamt). We explain who is entitled, what is included, and why many pensioners fail to claim it for no good reason.

steps.title: What basic income support in old age (Grundsicherung im Alter) is

content.text: Basic income support in old age and on reduced earning capacity (Grundsicherung im Alter und bei Erwerbsminderung) is basic state support under the Twelfth Book of the Social Code (SGB XII, §§ 41 ff.). It is intended for two groups: (1) people who have reached retirement age (the general retirement age — Regelaltersgrenze), and (2) people over 18 with a permanent full reduction in earning capacity (dauerhaft voll erwerbsgemindert) — if their own income and assets are not enough to live on. In essence it is the equivalent of the basic allowance (Bürgergeld), but for those who are no longer expected to take up work. Note: the basic allowance under SGB II itself is being gradually renamed to "new basic income support" (Grundsicherung; reform adopted in 2026) from 1 July 2026; this renaming does not directly affect basic income support in old age under SGB XII, but the names may differ across sources.

items: Governed by SGB XII (§§ 41 ff.)
For pensioners by age and for the fully unable to work
Condition — a lack of one's own income and assets
In essence "basic allowance (Bürgergeld) for those unable to work"
The application is filed with the social welfare office (Sozialamt), not the job centre (Jobcenter)

content.text: The amount of basic income support is made up of the standard rate (the basic need — Regelbedarf) plus the actual costs of housing and heating (Kosten der Unterkunft und Heizung) within reasonable limits, plus possible supplements (additional needs — Mehrbedarfe). The standard rates did not rise in 2026 — a so-called zero round of adjustment (Nullrunde) applies: the calculated amount came out below the previous one, but the protective clause (Besitzschutz, § 28a SGB XII) does not allow the rate to be lowered, so the values that have applied since 2024 remain.

items: The basic need (Regelbedarf) for a single person (Stufe 1): 563 €/month (2026)
For each of spouses/partners (Stufe 2): 506 €/month
ON TOP OF the rate — payment for housing and heating (rent — Miete + heating — Heizung)
Additional needs (Mehrbedarfe) — supplements (disability, special diet, etc.)
Assets and income (including pension) are counted and reduce the payment

content.text: An important feature of basic income support in old age compared with ordinary social assistance: with it, as a rule, there is NO recourse to support (Unterhaltsrückgriff) against children on ordinary incomes. In the past, the elderly were afraid to claim help so that the social welfare office would not demand money from their children. Since 2020 such recourse is possible only if the child's annual income exceeds 100 000 € — for most families this threshold is not reached, and you can apply for help with peace of mind.

steps.title: How to apply and what to keep in mind

content.text: The application is filed with the social welfare office (Sozialamt) for your place of residence (unlike the basic allowance — Bürgergeld, which is applied for at the job centre — Jobcenter). The entitlement arises from the first day of the month in which the application is filed. You will need documents on income (first and foremost the pension notice — Rentenbescheid), on assets, your tenancy agreement and housing bills.

items: Pension notice (Rentenbescheid, the pension amount) or confirmation of reduced earning capacity (Erwerbsminderung)
Information on income and assets (accounts, savings)
Tenancy agreement (Mietvertrag) and heating/utility bills
ID / residence permit, registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Bank details (IBAN)
There is protected property (Schonvermögen) that is not touched
Modest savings and adequate owner-occupied housing usually don't get in the way
Too large an asset — you first have to "spend it down"
Income (pension, annuity) is deducted from the payment

content.text: A huge problem is hidden poverty in old age (verdeckte Altersarmut): by estimates, a significant share of the elderly entitled to basic income support (Grundsicherung) do NOT claim it — out of shame, lack of knowledge or fear of "burdening the children". This is lost money. The entitlement to basic income support is not charity but a guarantee of a dignified minimum enshrined in SGB XII. If the pension is not enough — turn to the social welfare office (Sozialamt), if needed through a social advice service (Sozialberatung) or the Verbraucherzentrale (consumer advice centre).

steps.title: What else comes with basic income support (Grundsicherung)

content.text: Basic income support is not just a monthly payment: along with it comes access to a range of additional benefits and one-off expenses that recipients often don't know about. In addition, it is important to understand the link with the pension: basic income support can be received as a top-up to a small pension (aufstockend), not only instead of one.

items: A supplement for disability with the G/aG mark in the disability ID card (Schwerbehindertenausweis)
A supplement (Mehrbedarf) for a costly therapeutic diet (on a medical certificate)
A supplement for single parents (if applicable)
One-off needs (Einmalige Bedarfe) — furniture, household appliances, pregnancy
Full coverage of contributions to health and long-term care insurance (Pflege)
Exemption from the broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag, the TV/radio levy) — on application
Discounts on transport, museums, swimming pools under local rules (via the social welfare office)
An entitlement to a housing benefit (Wohngeld) does NOT arise alongside this (housing is already covered by basic income support)

content.text: If you are refused or granted less than you expected, you have one month to object (Widerspruch) to the social welfare office's decision. For elderly migrants there is a separate point to bear in mind: for basic income support by age you generally need ordinary (permanent) residence in Germany (gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt) and a corresponding residence status — it's best to clarify this in advance with a social advice service.

costs.label: Regelbedarf single person (2026)
costs.note: Stufe 1; in 2026 — Nullrunde, the amount is kept at the 2024 level (protective clause § 28a SGB XII).

costs.label: Regelbedarf per partner (2026)
costs.note: Stufe 2; for each of the spouses/partners living together.

costs.label: Housing and heating costs
costs.note: Paid ON TOP OF the rate at the actual reasonable costs; the amounts are individual.

costs.label: Filing the application at the Sozialamt
costs.note: The application and its processing are free of charge.

title: Emergency numbers: 110, 112, 116117
tldr: In Germany, 110 is the police, 112 is the fire brigade and ambulance (works across the whole EU, including with a blocked SIM). 116117 is the medical on-call service (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst), an on-call doctor for non-serious cases in the evening and at weekends, when the regular practice is closed but it is not an emergency. For women who have experienced violence, there is the free 116 016 (the helpline — Hilfetelefon, 24/7, interpreters in 18 languages). All these numbers are free and operate around the clock.

content.text: Germany has no single number for every situation. The main rule: 110 is the police (Polizei), 112 is the fire brigade and rescue services with the ambulance (Feuerwehr + Rettungsdienst). Both numbers are free, operate 24/7 nationwide and are reachable even with no credit on your account and a blocked SIM card.

items: 110 — a crime, a threat, theft, assault, a road accident with casualties, aggressive behaviour
112 — fire, respiratory arrest, heart attack, stroke, serious injury, loss of consciousness, heavy bleeding
112 is uniform across the whole EU (112.eu) — it works in any country of the European Union
116117 — you need a doctor, but it is NOT life-threatening (high fever, pain, prescription) outside practice hours
116 016 — the helpline (Hilfetelefon) for women who have experienced violence, free and anonymous 24/7
116 006 — the hotline of the victim support organisation Weisser Ring (White Ring)

content.text: If you're unsure between 112 and 116117 — call 112. It is better to overestimate the situation than to underestimate a heart attack or stroke. The 112 dispatcher will decide whether an ambulance is needed or an on-call doctor is enough. Only a deliberately fabricated call counts as a false alarm, not an honest mistake in judging severity.

The 110 and 112 dispatcher will walk you through the questions — you don't need to know a formula in advance, just answer clearly and don't hang up until you're told to. Many dispatch centres in large cities can connect an interpreter, but a few basic words in German will speed things up.

items: Wo? — where it happened: street, house number, town, landmarks
Was? — what happened: fire, road accident, an unconscious person
Wie viele? — how many casualties
Welche Verletzungen? — what injuries or symptoms
Warten auf Rückfragen — wait for follow-up questions and don't hang up first
Ich brauche einen Krankenwagen — I need an ambulance
Es brennt — there's a fire
Eine Person ist bewusstlos — a person is unconscious
Sprechen Sie Englisch? — do you speak English?
Ich spreche kein Deutsch — I don't speak German

content.text: 116117 is the medical on-call service of statutory healthcare (ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst). It is for cases where you need a doctor but your regular practice is closed (at night, on weekends, on holidays) and the situation is not life-threatening. The call is free, available 24/7; the website 116117.de has an online symptom check and a search for on-call practices.

items: High fever, flu, pain — but with no threat to life
You need a prescription or a sick note (AU) outside practice hours
Advice on whether to go to the emergency department (Notaufnahme) or wait until morning
Through 116117 you can also book appointments with specialists (the appointment service — Terminservicestelle)

content.text: 116 016 is the helpline for women who have experienced violence (Hilfetelefon "Gewalt gegen Frauen"). Free, anonymous, around the clock, with interpreters in 18 languages and support for the deaf. It is suitable for domestic, sexual or psychological violence, stalking, forced marriage. Counsellors will help you draw up a safety plan and point you to the nearest women's shelter (Frauenhaus).

Do not use 116117 if you suspect a heart attack, stroke, severe allergy or heavy bleeding — every minute counts, dial 112 right away. Signs of a stroke (the FAST test): a drooping face, weakness in an arm, slurred speech — call 112 immediately.

costs.label: Call to 110 / 112
costs.note: Free, including with no credit and a blocked SIM.

costs.label: Call to 116117
costs.note: Free from any network; the medical care itself is covered by insurance.

costs.label: Call to 116 016 / 116 006
costs.note: Free support hotlines; anonymous.

sources.title: 112 — the single European emergency number (Europäische Kommission)

title: Fire: what to do, the smoke detector (Rauchmelder)
tldr: In a fire the rule is: get people out, close the door behind you, call 112, don't use the lift. Smoke detectors (Rauchmelder) are mandatory in all 16 federal states in bedrooms, children's rooms and hallways leading to the exit. As a rule, the owner pays for installation, while keeping them operational (Betriebsbereitschaft) is the tenant's responsibility — but in some states maintenance is also on the owner. A single detector costs 10-30 €.

steps.title: What to do in a fire

content.text: In a fire the priority is lives, not property. Remember the order: warn and get people out, close the door of the burning room behind you (this holds back the fire and smoke), leave the building via the stairs and call 112. Never open a door if it is hot to the touch — there may be fire behind it.

items: Loudly warn the neighbours and lead everyone to the exit
Close the door of the burning room behind you, but don't lock it
Go down the stairs — NEVER use the lift
If the hallway is full of smoke — move crouched down, the air is cleaner near the floor
If there is dense smoke in the stairwell, stay in the flat, close the door, plug the gaps with wet cloth and signal from a window
State the address, what is burning and whether there are people in the building
Gather at the agreed assembly point (Sammelplatz)
Don't go back into the building for belongings
Meet the firefighters and tell them whether anyone is still inside

content.text: The main danger in a fire is the smoke, not the flames: most victims die from inhaling combustion products within a matter of minutes. Smoke spreads faster and is often opaque. That is why a working smoke detector (Rauchmelder) saves lives — it wakes you in your sleep, when your sense of smell is switched off.

steps.title: The duty to install detectors (Rauchmelderpflicht): where and how many

content.text: The duty to install smoke detectors (Rauchmelderpflicht) has been introduced in all 16 federal states through their state building codes (Landesbauordnung). The specific deadlines and details vary by state, but the basic minimum is common: detectors must be in bedrooms, children's rooms and in the hallways/corridors that serve as an escape route (Rettungsweg).

items: Mandatory: bedrooms (Schlafräume)
Mandatory: children's rooms (Kinderzimmer)
Mandatory: hallways (Flure) leading to the exit of the flat
Recommended in addition: the living room and other living rooms
Kitchen and bathroom — usually NOT fitted with a smoke detector (false alarms from steam/smoke); for the kitchen there are heat detectors (Hitzemelder)
Use devices certified to DIN EN 14604, ideally with the 'Q' mark

content.text: Who is responsible for what (the general rule in most states): the owner (the landlord/owner — Vermieter/Eigentümer) is responsible for installing (Einbau) the detectors. For keeping them operational (Sicherstellung der Betriebsbereitschaft) — that is, checking and replacing batteries — the tenant is responsible, UNLESS the owner has expressly taken on this duty themselves. In a number of states (for example Berlin) maintenance is placed on the owner. Check the exact breakdown in the building code of your state.

If your flat has no detectors or they don't work, the insurer may cut the payout in a fire due to a breach of duties. Do not remove the smoke detector (Rauchmelder) or take out the battery for some peace and quiet — instead, ask the owner to replace the device. False alarms are solved by repositioning or replacing the detector, not by switching it off.
A smoke detector only works if it is looked after. Check it regularly and don't cover it over. Modern models have a built-in 10-year battery, after which the whole device is replaced.

items: Once a month, press the test button — a signal should sound
Don't paint over or cover the detector
A periodic chirp = a low battery, replace the battery or the device
The device's service life is usually 10 years, the date is marked on the casing
If the owner does the maintenance, the costs may be included in the utility costs (Nebenkosten/Betriebskosten)
Don't install above the stove or shower — false alarms

costs.label: Smoke detector (Rauchmelder), per unit
costs.note: Certified to DIN EN 14604; models with a 10-year battery cost more.

costs.label: Heat detector for the kitchen (Hitzemelder)
costs.note: Optional; does not react to steam and kitchen smoke.

costs.label: Call to 112 in a fire
costs.note: Free and around the clock.

title: Disputes with the landlord: where to go
tldr: In a conflict with the landlord (Vermieter) — a rent increase, withholding the deposit, claims over utilities (Nebenkosten), demanding repairs, terminating the contract — your cheapest and fastest tool is membership in a local tenants' association (Mieterverein, ~70-100 €/year) belonging to the federal tenants' association (Deutscher Mieterbund). There they give legal advice and write letters. If that doesn't help — a conciliation body (Schlichtungsstelle, out-of-court settlement), and as a last resort — a lawsuit at the local court (Amtsgericht) for the location of the housing. Put everything in writing and meet the deadlines.

content.text: German tenancy law (Mietrecht, §§535 ff. BGB) strongly protects the tenant. Most conflicts are resolved by correspondence if you know your rights and put everything in writing. Don't pay disputed amounts 'to avoid a quarrel' — it can be taken as agreement; instead, pay under reservation (unter Vorbehalt).

items: Rent increase (Mieterhöhung) — without legal grounds or above the rent index (Mietspiegel)
Deposit (Kaution) — withholding or non-return of the deposit (the review period is usually up to ~6 months)
Utility statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) — incorrect or inflated
Defects (Mängel) — mould, heating, leaks: the right to a rent reduction (Mietminderung)
Termination (Kündigung) — unlawful, or the owner's personal need (Eigenbedarf) being in doubt
Cosmetic repairs (Schönheitsreparaturen) — disputed clauses on moving out

content.text: Meet the deadlines. An objection to the utility statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) is filed within 12 months of receiving it. An objection to a rent increase based on the rent index (Mietspiegel) — by the end of the second month after receiving the demand. A missed deadline often = loss of the right. Send all letters with proof of delivery (registered letter — Einschreiben or Einwurf-Einschreiben).

steps.title: The tenants' association (Mieterverein): the first line of defence

content.text: The most practical step is to join a local tenants' association (Mieterverein), affiliated with the federal tenants' association (Deutscher Mieterbund, mieterbund.de). For a membership fee of roughly 70-100 € a year you get unlimited advice on your contract, checking of documents and help with correspondence with the landlord. This is many times cheaper than a lawyer.

items: Fee ~70-100 €/year, sometimes plus a one-off joining fee (Aufnahmebeitrag)
A lawyer will check your contract, utility statements (Nebenkosten) and the landlord's letters
The association will draw up a reasoned objection or claim on your behalf
Tenancy legal protection insurance (Mietrechtsschutz) is often included in membership
Find the nearest association: mieterbund.de → search by town/postcode

content.text: Important: the insurance/legal protection within membership usually does NOT cover disputes that are already underway or already brewing at the time of joining (pre-contractual nature — Vorvertraglichkeit / waiting period — Wartezeit). Join in advance, before the conflict. If the dispute has already started, the association will still give advice, but you'll have to bear the court costs yourself or seek a court costs subsidy (Prozesskostenhilfe).

steps.title: Escalation: conciliation (Schlichtung) and the local court (Amtsgericht)

content.text: If correspondence hasn't helped, there are out-of-court and judicial routes. First it's worth trying conciliation (Schlichtung), then court. In tenancy disputes the court of first instance is almost always the local court (Amtsgericht) for the location of the housing, and here, unlike at higher instances, a lawyer is not formally required.

items: A neutral mediator helps reach an agreement without going to court
Cheaper and faster than court proceedings
In some states conciliation is mandatory for small disputes before filing a lawsuit
The tenants' association will tell you whether there is a suitable conciliation body (Schlichtungsstelle)
Filed at the local court (Amtsgericht) for the address of the disputed housing
In the first instance for tenancy a lawyer is not required (mandatory representation by a lawyer — Anwaltszwang — only from the regional court — Landgericht)
Court costs depend on the amount in dispute (Streitwert)
On a low income, file an application for a court costs subsidy (Prozesskostenhilfe)
Gather evidence: the contract, correspondence, photos of defects, handover protocols

content.text: Document defects: the date, photos, a written notice of defects (Mängelanzeige) with a reasonable deadline for remedy. For a rent reduction (Mietminderung) it is important to officially report the defect and not miss the notification — reducing the rent on your own without notice is risky.

costs.label: Membership in a Mieterverein (per year)
costs.note: Includes advice; often with Mietrechtsschutz within membership.

costs.label: Schlichtungsstelle
costs.note: Often free or a token fee; depends on the state and the body.

costs.label: Court costs at the Amtsgericht
costs.note: Depend on the Streitwert; on a low income Prozesskostenhilfe may be available.

title: Reporting a crime (Anzeige): how to file with the police
tldr: A criminal complaint (Strafanzeige) is a report of a crime to the police: you can file it at any station (Polizeidienststelle), and in many states online through the online police station (Online-Wache). Distinguish between a criminal complaint (Strafanzeige, simply reporting a fact) and a request to prosecute (Strafantrag, a demand to initiate prosecution, mandatory for so-called offences prosecuted on request — Antragsdelikte, with a 3-month deadline). You can file a complaint even anonymously. As a victim you have rights: an interpreter, a copy of the complaint, information on the progress of the case, support from the victim support organisation Weisser Ring (White Ring). Filing is free.

steps.title: Criminal complaint (Strafanzeige) and request to prosecute (Strafantrag) — the difference

content.text: The legal basis is §158 StPO (the Code of Criminal Procedure — Strafprozessordnung). A criminal complaint (Strafanzeige) is a report of a suspected crime: anyone can report it, and the police and the public prosecutor's office (Staatsanwaltschaft) are obliged to investigate. A request to prosecute (Strafantrag) is a separate declaration of will by the victim that they demand criminal prosecution; it is mandatory for so-called offences prosecuted on request (Antragsdelikte).

items: Criminal complaint (Strafanzeige, §158 StPO) — to report the fact of a crime, done by anyone
Request to prosecute (Strafantrag) — needed for offences prosecuted on request (Antragsdelikte): insult (Beleidigung), trespass (Hausfriedensbruch), minor damage
The deadline for the request to prosecute is 3 months from the moment you learned of the offence and the offender (§77b StGB)
Offences subject to public prosecution (Offizialdelikte — serious ones: robbery, violence) are prosecuted even without your request
A complaint can be filed anonymously — but this will hamper contact and the investigation

content.text: Don't miss the 3-month deadline for the request to prosecute (Strafantrag) for offences prosecuted on request (for example, insult). After it expires, prosecution for such offences is generally impossible. If you're unsure whether an offence is one of these, file the complaint as soon as possible anyway and state explicitly that you demand prosecution.

You can file a criminal complaint (Strafanzeige) in several ways, and all of them are free. For a serious or ongoing crime, call 110. For cases that have already happened, choose a station or online filing.

items.title: In person at a police station (Polizeidienststelle)

items: Go to any police station — not necessarily where the crime took place
Bring your passport/ID and all evidence (photos, receipts, correspondence, names of witnesses)
You have the right to an interpreter if you don't speak German (§185 GVG)
Ask for a copy or a case number (Aktenzeichen / Tagebuchnummer)

items.title: Online through the online police station (Online-Wache)

items: Each state has its own online police station (Online-Wache; links via polizei.de)
Convenient for theft, fraud, cybercrime with no urgency
NOT for emergencies — for those, call 110
Save the confirmation of submission and the assigned number

content.text: As a victim (Verletzte/r) you are not just a witness — you have rights enshrined in the StPO. Knowing them helps you take part in the case and get protection.

items: The right to a free interpreter during questioning and in correspondence
The right to information on the progress and outcome of the case (Verfahrensausgang) on request
The right to bring a trusted person (Beistand) to the questioning
The right to a victim's lawyer (Opferanwalt / private accessory prosecution — Nebenklage) — free of charge in serious cases
The right to psychosocial support (psychosoziale Prozessbegleitung)
Support from the victim support organisation Weisser Ring (White Ring, tel. 116 006) — free and independent of the police

content.text: If you have become a victim of violence — first ensure safety and medical help (112), then where possible have your injuries documented by a doctor (this is evidence). Don't delete correspondence or remove recordings: digital evidence often decides the outcome of a case. File the criminal complaint (Anzeige) as soon as possible, while the evidence is fresh.

costs.label: Filing a Strafanzeige / Strafantrag
costs.note: Always free — in person, online or in writing.

costs.label: Interpreter at the police
costs.note: Provided free of charge to the victim/witness.

costs.label: Victim's lawyer (Nebenklage)
costs.note: In serious crimes a free appointment is possible (Opferanwalt); otherwise paid or via PKH.

sources.title: Weisser Ring — Hilfe für Opfer von Straftaten

title: Weisser Ring: support for crime victims
tldr: Weisser Ring is Germany's largest independent NGO for victims of crime and their relatives. Help is free and does not depend on the police, your citizenship, or whether you filed a police report (Anzeige). The 24/7 hotline is 116 006. They accompany you to court and to the authorities, provide emotional support, and issue Hilfescheck vouchers for a free initial legal or psychological consultation. It is there for victims of violence, theft, fraud, and domestic abuse, and for the bereaved.

content.text: Weisser Ring e.V. is a non-profit association (Verein) with local branches all over Germany that helps people affected by crime and their relatives. Help is completely free and confidential. Importantly, it does not depend on whether you have German citizenship, on your legal status, or on whether you filed a police report.

items: Help is free and independent of the police and the public prosecutor
Available to all victims, including foreigners and refugees
Does not require you to file a criminal complaint (Strafanzeige)
24/7 victim hotline: 116 006
Local volunteer staff in almost every region
Support also for witnesses and the bereaved

content.text: Weisser Ring bridges the gap between the official authorities and a victim's real needs: it helps you understand your rights, gives you emotional support, and takes the first steps toward specialists on your behalf.

items: Personal support and emotional care after a crime
Accompaniment to the police, to a lawyer, and to court (Begleitung zu Terminen)
Hilfescheck vouchers for a free first consultation with a lawyer or psychologist
Help applying for state compensation for victims (OEG/SGB XIV)
In urgent cases, one-off financial support (Soforthilfe)
Information about the rights of the injured party in criminal proceedings

content.text: The Hilfescheck is a practical tool: you receive a voucher, visit a lawyer or psychotherapist from the network, and Weisser Ring pays for the first consultation. This lets you get a professional assessment of your situation without spending money and without any obligation.

items: Free, 24/7, and anonymous if you wish
Briefly explain what happened — there will be no judgement
You will be connected with a local branch for in-person help
The website weisser-ring.de also has an online chat and a contact form
A staff member will meet you and discuss your needs
If needed, they will issue a Hilfescheck voucher for a lawyer or psychologist
They will help you apply for compensation (OEG/SGB XIV)
They will accompany you to an interview or court hearing if needed

content.text: Weisser Ring helps you cope with the aftermath, but if there is an acute threat to life or ongoing violence, call 110 (police) or 112 (ambulance) first. For women experiencing violence there is a separate 24/7 helpline, 116 016 (Hilfetelefon), with interpreters. Weisser Ring steps in alongside it or afterward.

costs.label: Weisser Ring support
costs.note: Completely free for victims and their relatives.

costs.label: Call to 116 006
costs.note: Free from any network, 24/7.

costs.label: Hilfescheck (first legal/psychological consultation)
costs.note: Paid by Weisser Ring; free for the victim.
