The function is free and switched on by default in new documents
To use it you need a PIN and a device with NFC

items.title: 1. A document with eID switched on

content.text: Since 2017 the online function is switched on by default. If you have an old card where the eID was switched off, you can activate it for free at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) on presenting the document.

When the document is issued you receive a letter with a PIN (PIN-Brief) containing a five-digit transport PIN. Before first use, replace it with your own 6-digit PIN via the AusweisApp. If the letter is lost or the PIN is blocked, a new PIN can be set at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) or a reset can be ordered.

items.title: 3. A smartphone with NFC or a card reader

items: A smartphone with NFC (most modern Android phones and iPhones) — hold the card against the phone
Alternative: a computer + a USB card reader that supports eID
Official app: AusweisApp (formerly AusweisApp2), free
BundID / id.bund.de — a single account for federal and state government services
Mein ELSTER — registration and login without a letter-code
Opening a bank account online at some banks
i-Kfz — online vehicle registration and de-registration
Requesting statements, certificates, submitting applications in the states' digital portals
Electronic signing and access to some insurance and pension services

content.text: The logic is always the same: on the service's site you choose login "mit dem Personalausweis / Online-Ausweis", the AusweisApp opens, you hold the card against the phone, enter your PIN — and your identity is verified.

After three wrong PIN entries the function is blocked and will require the PUK (from the PIN letter, PIN-Brief), and after several blocks — a visit to the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) for a reset. Never tell anyone your PIN: not "support", not websites — real services ask for your PIN only inside the AusweisApp, not on a web page. If the PIN-Brief is lost, order a new PIN at the Bürgeramt in advance, not at the last minute before an important online operation.

costs.label: Activating and using the eID
costs.note: The online function and the AusweisApp are free.

costs.label: Issuing a new Personalausweis (adults aged 24+)
costs.note: From 07.02.2026 the fee for a new ID is 46 € (under 24 — 27,60 €); the eID itself is included free.

costs.label: Setting/resetting the PIN at the Bürgeramt
costs.note: Setting the PIN at the office is usually free.

costs.label: USB card reader (optional)
costs.note: Only needed if your smartphone/computer has no NFC.

title: ePA: the electronic health record 2025
tldr: From January 2025 the electronic health record (elektronische Patientenakte, ePA) switched to an opt-out model: everyone insured under statutory health insurance (GKV) gets one set up automatically unless they actively decline. The ePA stores diagnoses, prescriptions, lab results, the medication plan and documents from doctors. Access is via your health insurer's (Krankenkasse) app with identity verification (eID or a postal code). The guide explains what goes into the ePA, how to manage it, how to limit doctors' access and how to decline (objection, Widerspruch) if you don't want to take part.

steps.title: What the ePA is and the opt-out model

content.text: The electronic health record (elektronische Patientenakte, ePA) is a secure digital store of your medical data, shared across all the doctors you see. The idea is that a new doctor can immediately see your history — diagnoses, medications, lab tests — and not duplicate examinations.

The key change of 2025: the model switched from opt-in to opt-out. Previously you had to set up the ePA yourself. Now it's set up automatically for everyone insured under statutory health insurance (GKV) — it's created by default unless you have declared an objection. If you don't want an ePA, you have to actively file an objection (Widerspruch) with your health insurer (Krankenkasse).

steps.title: What is stored in the ePA

items: Diagnoses and medical histories
Prescribed medications and the unified medication plan (eMP)
Results of laboratory tests and investigations
Doctors' letters, hospital discharge summaries (Arztbriefe)
Vaccination data and, if you wish, an electronic vaccination record
Documents you upload yourself (for example, old examinations)

content.text: From 2025, data on issued prescriptions (via E-Rezept) and automatic filling of the record during doctor visits are gradually being connected. From 1 October 2025 the use of the ePA became mandatory for medical practices, pharmacies and hospitals across Germany. For practices, from 1 January 2026 there are penalties for non-use (a reduction in fees and a cut in the TI surcharge); hospitals have a longer transition period — the TI surcharge is cut if the ePA is not used by April 2026. You remain the owner of the data: you see who accessed your record and when.

items: Download the ePA app of your insurer (TK, AOK, Barmer, etc.)
Verify your identity: most often the eID of your national identity card (Personalausweis) + PIN or a postal code
In the app you see the record's contents and the access log
You can upload and delete documents, and manage visibility

content.text: When you present your health card (eGK) at a practice, the doctor by default gets access to the ePA for a limited period (usually up to 90 days). You can hide individual documents from specific doctors or fully restrict access to sensitive information via the app.

items: The objection is filed with your health insurer (Krankenkasse) — via the app, your account, a letter or the office
You can decline the creation of the ePA entirely
You can decline partially: for example, block certain data or access by specific people
Declining and consenting again are possible at any time — the decision is not final

content.text: If you do nothing, the ePA is created and filled automatically — that's the whole point of opt-out. Those worried about the privacy of their medical data should make a conscious decision: keep the ePA (and configure access restrictions) or file an objection (Widerspruch). Don't ignore letters from your insurer about the ePA — they explain the deadlines and the procedure for declining.

costs.label: ePA for those insured under GKV
costs.note: Included in statutory insurance, no separate charge.

costs.label: Krankenkasse ePA app
costs.note: Free app from your health insurer.

costs.label: Filing a Widerspruch (objection)
costs.note: Declining the ePA is free and possible at any time.

title: Digital licences and documents on your phone
tldr: Many people come from countries where their licence and documents already live on their phone, and expect the same in Germany. The reality in 2025–2026: Germany still has no official digital driving licence (Führerschein) in a phone wallet that replaces the plastic card during a police check. The main digital document is the eID online function in the national identity card (Personalausweis). The EU is preparing a pan-European digital identity wallet (EU Digital Identity Wallet, EUDI Wallet), to which driving licences and other documents will be added later; EU countries must provide at least one wallet by the end of 2026, and the German national wallet is planned for early 2027. This guide honestly explains what already works digitally, what's in pilots, and what you should still carry only as plastic.

steps.title: There's no digital licence "in a wallet" yet

content.text: Unlike in some countries, Germany has no official digital driving licence (Führerschein) that you can show the police instead of the plastic card. At a roadside check you are still required to present the physical Führerschein. A photo of your licence on your phone is not legally a valid document.

Don't rely on a screenshot or photo of your driving licence: at a roadside check it does not replace the original. Driving without the document on you can result in a fine (Verwarnungsgeld), although the right to drive itself remains. Carry your plastic driving licence (Führerschein) with you.

items: The eID in the national identity card (Personalausweis) — the main digital proof of identity for online government services
BundID — a single digital account for submitting applications to the authorities
Mein ELSTER — tax matters fully online
i-Kfz — vehicle registration online (but this is not "a licence on your phone")
E-Rezept and ePA — prescriptions and the health record in digital form

content.text: In other words, digitalisation in Germany runs through identification (eID) and service portals, not through storing document cards on a smartphone. This is an important conceptual difference.

steps.title: EU Digital Identity Wallet: what's coming

content.text: The pan-European digital identity wallet (EU Digital Identity Wallet, EUDI Wallet) is a Europe-wide wallet app to which, over time, you'll be able to add your ID card, driving licence, diplomas and other documents. Under the eIDAS 2.0 regulation, EU countries are required to provide citizens with at least one such wallet by 31.12.2026, and Germany plans to launch its national wallet in early 2027 (around January 2027).

items: 2026+ — phased launch of national EUDI wallets in EU countries
Digital licences (mDL) will be added gradually, not all at once
Recognition by the police as a replacement for plastic will come even later
For now, follow official announcements from the BMDV and the states' digital ministries

steps.title: What to do in practice now

items: Activate the eID in your national identity card (Personalausweis) — it covers online government services already today
Install the AusweisApp and create a BundID
Carry the original driving licence (Führerschein) and (if needed) the vehicle registration certificate, part I (Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil I) in the car
Don't throw away your plastic documents in anticipation of digital ones — the transition will take years

costs.label: eID and AusweisApp
costs.note: Digital identification is free.

costs.label: EUDI Wallet (in future)
costs.note: Planned as a free government service.

costs.label: Fine for driving without the document on you
costs.note: Verwarnungsgeld of roughly 10 €; the right to drive remains.

sources.title: Europäische Kommission — EU Digital Identity Wallet

title: i-Kfz: re-registering a car online
tldr: Through the i-Kfz portal, since 2023 (stage 4) you can fully online register a new or used car, re-register it to yourself, de-register it and change details — without going to the vehicle registration office (Zulassungsstelle). For this you need: the eID online function in your national identity card (Personalausweis) with a PIN, a smartphone/card reader with NFC, and the hidden security codes (Sicherheitscodes) on the registration certificate (Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil I and II) and on the licence-plate stickers (Plaketten). Online is usually cheaper than at the office. This guide breaks down the requirements, the steps and the typical pitfalls.

steps.title: What you can do via i-Kfz

content.text: i-Kfz is the federal online portal for vehicle registration. Since 2023, in full scope (Stufe 4), the main vehicle actions are available fully remotely, including situations involving someone from another region or a change of owner.

items: Neuzulassung — first registration of a new car
Umschreibung / Ummeldung — re-registration to yourself (including on moving to another district)
Wiederzulassung — re-registering a previously de-registered car
Außerbetriebsetzung (Abmeldung) — de-registration
Changing details (for example, when keeping the plate number)
A national identity card (Personalausweis) with the eID online function active and a 6-digit PIN
A smartphone with NFC + the AusweisApp (or a PC with a card reader)
For foreigners — the electronic residence permit card (eAT) with eID, if supported by the portal
A valid residence registration (Anmeldung)

content.text: The requirement people most often trip over: online operations need hidden security codes. They are concealed under a protective layer that you have to scratch off carefully.

items: The code in the Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil I (the certificate you carry in the car)
The code in the Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil II (the owner's document)
The codes under the stickers (Plaketten) on the licence plates — for de-registration/re-registration
These codes only exist on documents issued in the new format (since 2015)

content.text: If the car or documents are of the old format without security codes, the online operation is impossible — you'll have to go to the Zulassungsstelle in person. Also, when buying a used car, make sure the seller has handed over both Teil and that the codes haven't already been "scratched off" and used.

items.title: 1. Logging in to the portal and identifying yourself

items: Go to your district's i-Kfz portal (links via kba.de / your state)
Authenticate via eID (AusweisApp, NFC, PIN)
Select the action you need (for example, re-registration, Umschreibung)
Enter the security codes from Teil I, Teil II and from the Plaketten
Provide the eVB number of your insurance (from the insurer)
Confirm the holder and address details
Pay the fee online (card/bank transfer)

content.text: Once the check is complete you can drive legally straight away (in some cases — with a preliminary confirmation), and the official documents and, if needed, new stickers arrive by post. On de-registration the status is updated, and you cancel the stickers as instructed.

items: Online fees are usually lower than at the office thanks to a digital discount
Get the eVB number from your insurer in advance — without it registration won't go through
Check your eID PIN beforehand: a blocked PIN will stop the process
Keep both Teil and your insurance details to hand before you start

content.text: Don't put off re-registration when buying/selling: while the car is on the old owner, the tax and liability fall on them. The seller should make sure the buyer has actually re-registered the car, otherwise fines and tax will come for a car that's already been sold.

costs.label: i-Kfz online registration/re-registration
costs.note: Depends on the action and the district; usually cheaper than in person.

costs.label: De-registration (Abmeldung) online
costs.note: Often cheaper than the in-person procedure.

costs.label: Licence plates (if new ones are needed)
costs.note: Making the physical plates is paid for separately.

title: Mein ELSTER: what the account can do
tldr: Mein ELSTER (elster.de) is the free official online portal of the German tax authority. Through it, individuals and entrepreneurs file returns, complete the questionnaire for tax registration (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung) when registering as self-employed, submit the advance VAT return (USt-Voranmeldung), receive and download tax assessments (Bescheid), upload documents and correspond with the tax office (Finanzamt). Registration requires identity verification (by a postal code or instantly via eID). The guide shows what the account can really do, how to register and how to use pre-filling with your data (vorausgefüllte Steuererklärung).

content.text: Mein ELSTER is a single point for all online dealings with the tax office (Finanzamt). It works for both ordinary employees who file a return once a year and the self-employed/entrepreneurs who file regularly.

items: Filing the annual tax return (Einkommensteuererklärung)
The questionnaire for tax registration (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung) — registering as self-employed and getting a tax number (Steuernummer)
The advance VAT return (USt-Voranmeldung) and the annual VAT return (Umsatzsteuererklärung) for businesses
Receiving and downloading tax assessments (Steuerbescheid)
Uploading documents (Belege) and messages to the tax office (Finanzamt)
Simplified income-and-expenditure accounting (EÜR, Einnahmenüberschussrechnung) and other forms for entrepreneurs
On elster.de select "Benutzerkonto erstellen"
Provide your Steuer-ID and e-mail
Receive an activation code by post (the letter takes ~1–2 weeks)
Download the certificate file (.pfx) — this is your "key" for logging in
Keep the certificate file and password safe — without them you can't log in

content.text: If you have the online function of your national identity card (Personalausweis, eID) activated and the AusweisApp, you can register and log in without waiting for the code letter — your identity is verified instantly via NFC and PIN. This is the fastest route for newcomers.

The ELSTER certificate file is easy to lose when you change computers. Make a backup in a safe place and remember the password. If you lose it you'll have to register again and wait for the code letter once more, which will delay filing your return before the deadline.

items: Vorausgefüllte Steuererklärung — the tax authority already knows your salary and contributions, and will fill them into the form
Importing last year's data to reuse it
Error checking and an estimate of your expected refund before submitting
Receiving the Bescheid electronically is faster than on paper
Notifications in the account about the processing status

content.text: Pre-filling (vorausgefüllte Steuererklärung) speeds the process up a lot: you activate the service, confirm it, and the return automatically pulls in the data on salary, health insurance and pension contributions reported by your employer and insurers.

items: The return is filed for the past year; standard deadlines depend on whether you are required to file
If you are required to file, the deadline is usually 31 July of the following year (extended in certain years)
With a tax adviser (Steuerberater) the deadline is extended
A tax assessment (Bescheid) can be objected to (Einspruch) within 1 month of receipt

content.text: Don't leave registering on ELSTER until the last day before the deadline: getting the activation-code letter takes time. If you want to file straight away, register via eID. For a late mandatory return, the tax office (Finanzamt) can charge a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag).

costs.label: Registering and using Mein ELSTER
costs.note: The tax authority's official portal is completely free.

costs.label: Verspätungszuschlag (late-filing surcharge)
costs.note: From 25 € for each month started late; the total depends on the amount of tax.

title: City apps and portals
tldr: Besides the federal services, every major city has its own portal and often an app for booking appointments (Termin) and submitting applications. Berlin — service.berlin.de and the BerlinApp; Munich — muenchen.de; Hamburg — hamburg.de. Many services are being digitalised thanks to the law on online access to government services (Onlinezugangsgesetz, OZG), which obliges the authorities to bring administrative services online. This guide shows which tasks can actually be handled through city portals, how to use them, and why it's worth creating a BundID to log in to most services.

content.text: In Germany a great deal is handled at city and state level, so the municipal portals are your main tool for everyday bureaucracy: appointment booking, residence registration, applications and certificates.

items: Berlin: service.berlin.de — appointments and services; the BerlinApp
Munich: muenchen.de / stadt.muenchen.de — the district citizens' office (Bürgerbüro) and online services
Hamburg: hamburg.de — Online-Dienste and appointment booking
Other cities: search "[city] + Bürgeramt / Online-Dienste"
Booking an appointment (Termin) at the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt) and other authorities
Requesting certificates: registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung), certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis)
Submitting certain applications (for example, renewing documents, registering a car via i-Kfz)
Applications for the housing benefit (Wohngeld), parking permits, dog registration (dog tax, Hundesteuer) — depends on the city
Paying some fees online

content.text: The range of online services varies greatly by city and is constantly expanding. If a service isn't available online, the portal is still useful — it lists the documents, fees and addresses of the authorities you need.

steps.title: OZG and single sign-on via BundID

content.text: The law on online access to government services (Onlinezugangsgesetz, OZG) is a law that obliges federal, state and municipal authorities to provide administrative services in digital form. It's because of it that cities are rolling out online forms en masse. Implementation is uneven, so the level of digitalisation depends on the region.

items: Create an account on id.bund.de (BundID)
Connect the eID of your national identity card (Personalausweis) for the highest level of trust
With BundID you log in to many state and city services with a single login
This saves you from creating a separate account on every portal
Always start from the city's official site (the domain ends in .de and belongs to the city)
Create a BundID + activate the eID in advance — this will unlock the maximum number of functions
Install the city app if there is one: notifications about appointments are handier
Compare branches right in the portal — dates vary a lot

content.text: Beware of copycat sites and paid "intermediaries" that pose as official portals and charge money for free government services or appointment booking. Official city services are free (you only pay the set fee for the service itself). Check the site address and don't enter your eID PIN anywhere except the AusweisApp.

costs.label: City portals and apps
costs.note: Access to the portals and apps is free.

costs.label: BundID
costs.note: The single government account is free.

costs.label: Fees for specific services
costs.note: Depends on the service (for example, certificates); the portal itself charges no surcharge.

title: Exemption from the broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag)
tldr: The public broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) is a mandatory contribution of 18,36€/month per dwelling. Recipients of basic income support (Bürgergeld), the BAföG grant, social assistance (Sozialhilfe) and basic security benefits (Grundsicherung) can get a full exemption under §4 RBStV; people with disabilities who hold the RF mark pay one third. The exemption is not automatic — you must file an application with the contribution service (Beitragsservice) and supply proof.

steps.title: What the broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) is and who pays it

content.text: The broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag; formerly called GEZ) is a mandatory contribution that funds public broadcasting (ARD, ZDF, Deutschlandradio). Since 2013 it has been tied not to owning a TV or radio but to the dwelling (Wohnung): every household pays, regardless of whether it owns any equipment.

items: Amount of the fee: 18,36€ per month (220,32€ per year); an increase to 18,64€ is planned (a Federal Constitutional Court (BVerfG) decision is pending, with a hearing on 23 June 2026)
Paid per dwelling, not per person
In a family or shared flat (WG) a single payer for the whole dwelling is enough
The fee is collected by the contribution service (Beitragsservice von ARD, ZDF und Deutschlandradio)
Registration happens automatically after residence registration (Anmeldung) — the contribution service gets your data from the residents' registration office (Einwohnermeldeamt)

content.text: After residence registration (Anmeldung), the contribution service will send you a payment demand on its own initiative — even if you never contacted anyone. You cannot ignore the letters: the debt builds up and is later collected by force through enforcement proceedings (Vollstreckung).

It is important to understand the logic: an exemption (Befreiung) is not "not paying because I have no TV." Owning equipment is irrelevant. An exemption is granted only on the social grounds set out in §4 RBStV.

steps.title: Who is entitled to an exemption under §4 RBStV

content.text: A full exemption from the fee (Befreiung) is available to recipients of certain social benefits. The legal basis is §4 Abs. 1 Rundfunkbeitragsstaatsvertrag (RBStV). The list is closed: if you are not on it, you cannot be exempted on the basis of income, but there is a separate "hardship case" route (see below).

items: Basic income support (Bürgergeld; formerly Arbeitslosengeld II / Hartz IV) under SGB II
Social assistance (Sozialhilfe — Hilfe zum Lebensunterhalt) under SGB XII
Basic security benefits in old age and in case of reduced earning capacity (Grundsicherung im Alter und bei Erwerbsminderung, SGB XII)
The BAföG grant (students and pupils who do NOT live with their parents)
Vocational training allowance (Berufsausbildungsbeihilfe, BAB) and Ausbildungsgeld
Recipients of asylum seeker benefits (Asylbewerberleistungen) under AsylbLG
Recipients of the blind person's allowance (Blindenhilfe) and a number of other benefits for people with disabilities

content.text: Separately: people with severe disabilities whose disability card (Schwerbehindertenausweis) carries the "RF" mark pay a reduced fee — one third, that is 6,12€ per month instead of 18,36€. Deafblind people and recipients of the blind person's allowance (Blindenhilfe) are fully exempt.

The BAföG grant exempts you only if the student lives apart from their parents. If you are registered in your parents' flat, the fee is already covered by their household, and a personal grant does not provide a separate exemption "for the parental flat."

steps.title: How to apply for an exemption (Befreiung)

content.text: The exemption is NOT granted automatically when you receive a benefit. You must file an application for exemption (Antrag auf Befreiung) with the contribution service yourself and attach proof of eligibility. Until the application is approved, you are formally required to pay.

The fastest route is to fill out the application on the official portal rundfunkbeitrag.de under "Befreiung / Ermäßigung beantragen." You will need your contribution number (Beitragsnummer) from the contribution service's letter, if you already have one.

items: A current official decision (Bescheid) granting the benefit (for example, the Bürgergeld-Bescheid from the job centre (Jobcenter))
For the BAföG grant — the BAföG-Bescheid stating the period
For a disability — a copy of the disability card (Schwerbehindertenausweis) with the RF mark
The document must show the current validity period of the benefit

content.text: The exemption is granted for the validity period of the benefit (usually 1 year, after which you have to reapply). The application can take effect retroactively — as a rule, up to 3 years back, if you can prove that you were entitled to the exemption throughout that time. Fees already paid for that period are refunded.

The exemption is not open-ended! It is tied to the benefit period. When the official decision (Bescheid) expires, the exemption ends and the contribution service starts charging the fee again. File a new application in advance, with a new Bescheid.

If your income is slightly above the threshold for social benefits (for example, you were denied basic income support over just a few euros), you can apply for an exemption on the grounds of a special hardship case (besonderer Härtefall) under §4 Abs. 6 RBStV. You must prove that your income does not exceed the benefit amount plus the amount of the fee itself.

items: Shared flat (WG): only ONE person pays for the whole dwelling — do not register every flatmate separately
Moving house: when you change flats, update the address so you do not pay twice for two dwellings
Second home (Zweitwohnung): since 2018 you can get an exemption for a second address if you already pay for the main one
Foreign exchange students get an exemption under the same rules as German ones — the main thing is to confirm the status

content.text: Never ignore letters from the contribution service (Beitragsservice), even if you are sure you are entitled to an exemption. The debt builds up until the application is approved. If you do not pay, the case is handed over for enforced collection (Vollstreckung) via a bailiff (Gerichtsvollzieher), and the amount grows because of the added fees.

If you have moved to Germany and are not yet entitled to an exemption but money is tight — the fee is still mandatory. There is no option to "opt out": it is a public-law contribution, not a subscription to a service.

costs.label: Rundfunkbeitrag (standard)
costs.note: 18,36€ per month = 220,32€ per year per dwelling regardless of whether you own equipment.

costs.label: Befreiung (full exemption)
costs.note: 0€ for recipients of Bürgergeld, BAföG, Sozialhilfe, Grundsicherung under §4 RBStV.

costs.label: Reduced fee (RF mark)
costs.note: 6,12€ per month (one third) for people with severe disabilities with the RF mark on their card.

sources.title: Beitragsservice von ARD, ZDF und Deutschlandradio

title: Streaming: Netflix, Sky, DAZN, WOW
tldr: In Germany you have access to Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime, Sky/WOW, DAZN and Paramount+. Prices range from 5€ for basic Netflix to ~35€ for sports-focused DAZN. Content is geo-locked: the German catalogue differs from the one in your home country. ARD/ZDF Mediathek and the public channels are free (but funded by the broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag)).

steps.title: Which services exist and what they cost

content.text: The streaming market in Germany works much like in other countries, but with local specifics: prices, catalogue and the availability of individual shows differ because of licensing. Most services are billed monthly, with the option to cancel at any time.

items: Netflix — films and series, plans with and without ads (~5–20€/month)
Disney+ — Disney, Marvel, Star Wars, Star (~6–12€/month)
Amazon Prime Video — included in the Prime subscription (~9€/month or paid annually)
Sky / WOW — film, HBO series, sports; WOW is the streaming version of Sky
DAZN — sports (football, Bundesliga, boxing), expensive (~35€/month)
Paramount+, Apple TV+, MagentaTV (from Telekom) and others

content.text: A separate category is public broadcasting: ARD Mediathek, ZDF Mediathek, Arte. They are free for the viewer (formally paid for through the broadcasting fee) and offer films, documentaries, news and sports. A good free starting point for practising German with subtitles.

steps.title: Geo-locked content: what you watch in Germany

content.text: The same service shows a different catalogue in different countries. After moving to Germany, you will see the German Netflix catalogue — some shows from your home country may be missing, but new ones will appear. Most content has a German dub plus the original audio track with subtitles.

items: The account is tied to the country of payment/residence, not to citizenship
Many services let you change the interface language and the audio track
ARD/ZDF Mediathek are accessible only from Germany (geo-block)
Sports rights (Bundesliga, Champions League) are split between DAZN, Sky and Amazon — there is no single service that covers all football

content.text: Using a VPN to bypass the geo-block usually violates the service's terms of use (AGB) — the account can be blocked, and the platforms actively detect VPNs. It is not a criminal offence, but the risk of losing access is real.

steps.title: How to save money and avoid overpaying

content.text: Netflix, Disney+ and Amazon have introduced cheap plans with ads. If ads do not bother you, this is the most budget-friendly legal option. In Germany in 2026, Netflix Standard with ads costs around 4,99€, Standard without ads — 13,99€, Premium 4K — 19,99€ (check that these are current, as prices rise periodically).

Netflix has tightened the rules on password sharing between households and charges extra for an additional user outside the home. Within a single dwelling (shared flat WG, family) sharing is allowed. Amazon Prime can be shared via Amazon Household.

items: Turn on DAZN/Sky only for the season of the tournament you want and cancel afterwards
WOW offers flexible monthly packages — Entertainment / Cinema / Live-Sport separately
Watch for promotions (Black Friday, annual discounts)
Free trial periods exist, but require cancellation before you are charged

content.text: DAZN and Sky/WOW have historically offered subscriptions with a minimum term (12 months) — read carefully whether the plan is monthly (cancellable each month, Monatlich kündbar) or an annual contract. The annual one is cheaper per month, but you cannot cancel early.

costs.label: Netflix
costs.note: DE 2026: with ads ~4,99€, Standard 13,99€, Premium 4K 19,99€. Prices rise periodically — check that they are current.

costs.label: Disney+ / Amazon Prime Video
costs.note: Disney+ ~6–12€; Amazon Prime ~9€/month or cheaper when paid annually.

costs.label: DAZN (sports)
costs.note: ~35€/month and up — the most expensive because of sports rights to the Bundesliga and others.

costs.label: WOW / Sky
costs.note: Flexible packages Entertainment / Cinema / Sport, the price depends on the bundle.

costs.label: ARD / ZDF Mediathek
costs.note: Free for the viewer, funded through the Rundfunkbeitrag.

title: Transferring your internet when you move
tldr: When you move house, you can transfer (Mitnahme) your internet contract to the new address or, if the provider cannot serve the new address, terminate it early under the special right in §60 TKG. You need to notify the provider about six weeks in advance. Be prepared for a possible downtime of several days or weeks without internet.

content.text: Internet contracts (DSL, cable, fibre) in Germany are usually signed for 24 months. When you move, you are NOT automatically released from the contract — but you have two lawful routes, depending on whether the provider can serve the new address.

items: Scenario A — transfer (Mitnahme): the provider serves the new address → the contract moves there on the same terms
Scenario B — early termination (Sonderkündigung): the provider CANNOT serve the new address → the right to early termination under §60 TKG
Notice period for the provider: aim for ~6 weeks before the move
The decision rests with the provider: whether it offers the service at the new address

content.text: The logic of the law: you should not have to pay for a service that cannot be delivered, but you also should not be able to drop a contract simply because you moved if the provider is ready to connect you at the new place.

If the provider serves the new address, it moves your contract there. Technically this is a new connection, so there may be a gap without internet between the disconnection at the old flat and the activation at the new one.
Contact the provider as early as possible (4–6 weeks ahead) and give the new address and the moving date. This gives time to check technical availability and to plan the connection.

items: The provider will check whether its line is available at the new address (availability check, Verfügbarkeitsprüfung)
The technology may change (for example, it was DSL — now it is cable)
They may offer a new plan/speed at the new address
Confirm the activation date and any possible downtime

items.title: 3. Your rights if the terms get worse

content.text: If at the new address the provider can only offer worse terms (lower speed, higher price), you also gain the right to early termination, because the service is essentially changing. Clarify this during the call.
Do not cancel the old contract yourself "just in case," and do not sign a new parallel contract until the transfer is sorted out — you risk paying for two connections at once.

steps.title: Scenario B: early termination under §60 TKG

content.text: If the provider CANNOT deliver the service at the new address, §60 Telekommunikationsgesetz (TKG 2021) gives you the right to early termination (Sonderkündigungsrecht). The termination period is, as a rule, three months, but the provider may not demand payment until the end of the minimum term (24 months) if delivering the service at the new address is impossible.

items: Submit a written termination of the contract (Kündigung) stating the reason "Umzug, Leistung am neuen Wohnort nicht verfügbar"
Attach proof of the move (for example, a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) or rental contract (Mietvertrag))
The termination takes effect at the end of the month after the three-month period — but only if a transfer is impossible
Return the equipment (router) on time to avoid extra charges

content.text: Important: §60 TKG protects precisely the case where the service is unavailable. If the provider is ready to connect you at the new address and you simply want to switch providers, that is not grounds for early termination — you will have to wait for the contract to run out or pay.

Do not end up without internet by chance: connecting a new provider at the new address also takes time (often 2–4 weeks). Order the new connection in advance and consider mobile internet (a prepaid SIM with a data package, or a router) as a temporary solution.

costs.label: DSL/cable internet
costs.note: Typical monthly plan 20–50€ depending on speed and provider.

costs.label: Connection transfer (Umzugspauschale)
costs.note: Some providers charge a one-off fee for activation at the new address.

costs.label: Temporary mobile internet
costs.note: Prepaid SIM or LTE router with a data package for the downtime period.

sources.title: Bundesnetzagentur — consumer rights for telecom contracts

title: Contract vs Prepaid: which to choose
tldr: A mobile contract (Handyvertrag; 24-month) gives you a subsidised phone and a monthly bill, but requires a credit check at the Schufa bureau, a German bank account and a registered address. A prepaid card (Prepaid) requires neither Schufa nor a contract — you top up as needed. For newcomers without residence registration (Anmeldung) and a credit history, Prepaid is almost always the best start.

steps.title: What is the difference between a contract (Vertrag) and prepaid (Prepaid)

content.text: In Germany there are two fundamentally different ways to use mobile service: a postpaid mobile contract (Handyvertrag / Postpaid) and a prepaid card (Prepaid). The choice depends heavily on how long you have been in the country and whether you have a registered address, a bank account and a credit history at the Schufa bureau.

items: Mobile contract (Handyvertrag): usually for 24 months, a bill once a month, often with a phone in instalments
Prepaid (Prepaid): no contract, you pay in advance, top up your balance (Aufladen), and can cancel at any time
A contract requires a check at the Schufa bureau, a German IBAN and often residence registration (Anmeldung)
Prepaid does NOT require Schufa and usually does not require a bank account

content.text: The major networks are Telekom (D1), Vodafone (D2) and O2 (Telefónica). Besides them there are many discounters (Aldi Talk, congstar, Lidl Connect, winSIM, Lebara) that rent capacity from the big operators and cost less.

steps.title: Why prepaid (Prepaid) is better for newcomers

content.text: If you have just arrived, you most likely do not yet have residence registration (Anmeldung) or a German bank account, let alone a credit history at the Schufa bureau. A contract usually requires all of this — and a newcomer simply will not pass the Schufa check, because there is no data about you in the system.

items: Prepaid SIMs (Prepaid) are sold in supermarkets, kiosks and at discounters (Aldi Talk, Lidl Connect)
SIM registration is mandatory by law — you need a passport/ID to activate (PostIdent or Video-Ident)
You can start using mobile service on your very first day in the country
A data package (for example, 10–20€ for a few GB) is enough to get started
Later, once you have residence registration and an account, you can switch to a contract

content.text: Since 2017 all prepaid SIMs in Germany are registered to an ID (§172 TKG) — you cannot buy an anonymous card. When buying, you will need a passport or ID and identity verification (in the shop or online via Video-Ident).

steps.title: How to choose and what to look out for

items: You are staying long-term and want a stable plan
You need a new phone in instalments without a large one-off spend
You have residence registration (Anmeldung), a German account and a clean credit history at the Schufa bureau
Large data packages at a fixed price matter to you
You are new to the country or your status is temporary
You have no credit history at the Schufa bureau, no German account or no registered address
You want full control over spending, with no surprises in the bill
You use the service little and do not need a new phone

content.text: Check whether EU roaming is included (usually yes), whether the package auto-renews (Automatische Verlängerung), which actual network is behind the discounter, and whether there is a hidden minimum term. For a contract, look at the term (Laufzeit) and the cancellation notice period (Kündigungsfrist).

A contract involves a check at the Schufa bureau: the operator may refuse you or demand prepayment/a deposit if your credit history is weak. Do not sign a contract "to try it out" — getting out of a 24-month contract early is almost impossible.

costs.label: Handyvertrag (contract)
costs.note: 20–50€/month depending on data and whether a phone is included in instalments; the term is usually 24 months.

costs.label: Prepaid (pay-as-you-go)
costs.note: 8–20€ for a data package; you pay only when you top up, with no commitment.

costs.label: Prepaid starter pack
costs.note: A one-off purchase of a SIM with an initial balance in a supermarket/kiosk.

sources.title: Bundesnetzagentur — mobile service and subscriber rights

title: Landline (Festnetz): do you need it
tldr: A landline phone (Festnetz) in Germany almost always comes bundled with DSL internet — a standalone "bare" phone line is now a rarity. VoIP technology has become the standard, and the phone works through the router. Many people use only mobile service, but a landline number is still useful for official contacts and is sometimes required for registrations.

content.text: A landline (Festnetz) is a fixed telephone number. It used to run over a separate copper line, but today telephony in Germany has almost entirely moved to VoIP (Voice over IP): calls go over the internet connection, and the phone plugs into your router (for example, a FritzBox).

items: A landline is almost always sold as a bundle with internet (DSL/cable/fibre)
A standalone "phone only" line (Nur-Telefon-Anschluss) is now rare and uneconomical
Calls within Germany to landline numbers are often included as unlimited (Flatrate)
The phone plugs into the router, so a separate TAE socket is no longer required

content.text: In a typical internet plan the phone line comes "for free" as part of the bundle — there is usually no separate line item for it.

Many people in Germany (especially younger people and recent arrivals) use only mobile service and do not set up a landline at all. But in a number of situations a landline number is still convenient or expected.

items: For official contacts, contracts and doctors — a landline number looks "more solid" and more stable
At home, stable call quality through the router, not dependent on mobile coverage
Unlimited calls within Germany included in the plan
Sometimes a registration form asks for "Telefon" — a mobile works too, but a landline number fits well

items.title: When you can do without it

items: You mostly call via WhatsApp or your mobile
You move often — a mobile number is easier to carry over
You do not want extra equipment and setup
No mandatory registration requires a landline from you

content.text: With VoIP the phone works through the router and depends on electricity and the internet: during a power or internet outage the landline phone is dead. For emergency calls (112/110) rely primarily on your mobile.

steps.title: How to set it up and the fine points

content.text: There is usually no point in ordering a "bare" landline separately — get an internet plan with telephony included. The provider gives you a phone number, which you set up in the router. An old analogue phone will work too — via an adapter.

items: Order an internet plan with the telephony option (Telefon; almost all DSL packages include it)
Connect the phone (a DECT handset or an analogue one) to the router
When you move, the landline number can usually be carried over (number porting, Rufnummernmitnahme)
Porting your mobile and landline number when switching provider is your legal right (§59 TKG)

content.text: Do not pay for a separate, expensive "phone only" service if you need the internet anyway — a DSL+Telefon bundle is almost always cheaper and more convenient.

costs.label: Festnetz in a DSL bundle
costs.note: Usually included in the internet plan at no separate charge.

costs.label: Internet+phone (bundle)
costs.note: The combined price of a DSL package with telephony is 20–50€/month.

costs.label: Number porting (Rufnummernmitnahme)
costs.note: May be free or carry a small one-off fee when switching provider.

title: Roaming outside the EU: how not to go broke
tldr: The EU "Roam like at home" rule applies only within the EU/EEA. Outside it (USA, UK, Turkey, Russia, Asia, etc.) roaming is NOT included and can cost from 1 to 20€ per megabyte without a package — bills reach hundreds of euros. Solutions: a daily package from your provider (Travel & Surf and similar), a local SIM or eSIM, or simply turning off mobile data.

steps.title: EU roaming versus the rest of the world

content.text: Within the EU/EEA the "Roam like at home" rule applies (EU Regulation 2022/612): in these countries you pay the same as at home, and your data package and minutes work without surcharges (subject to a Fair Use caveat). But as soon as you travel outside the EU/EEA, this rule stops working entirely.

items: EU/EEA (including Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway): roaming as at home
Outside the EU (USA, UK, Turkey, Switzerland, Russia, Asia, Africa and others): ordinary paid roaming
Without a package, the price for data outside the EU can reach 1–20€ per MB
Calls and SMS outside the EU are also charged separately and expensively

content.text: The United Kingdom and Switzerland are NOT part of EU roaming. Turkey — a popular destination — is also outside the zone. Do not assume that "close to Europe = free": check the country in advance.
The main danger is background data use (app updates, syncing, maps) while roaming is on outside the EU. A few minutes of navigation or an auto-update can cost tens of euros. Act pre-emptively.

items: Ask your provider whether the destination country is part of EU roaming
Ask about a daily/weekly package for that country
Set a roaming spending limit with your operator (Kostenlimit), if available
Download offline maps and the content you need in advance over home Wi-Fi
Turn off mobile data roaming (Datenroaming) in the settings if you have no package
Use the Wi-Fi in your hotel/café for messengers and navigation
Turn on mobile data only when you need it
Watch for operator notifications about exceeding limits

content.text: German operators send an SMS when you enter a non-EU country, listing the rates, and usually impose a protective spending limit (around 60€), after which data is cut off. But do NOT rely on this blindly — in some countries/plans the limit does not trigger, and the bill can run into hundreds of euros.

steps.title: Daily packages, local SIMs and eSIMs

content.text: There are three practical ways to stay connected outside the EU without going broke. The choice depends on the length of the trip and how much you need your German number.

items: A daily package from your provider (for example, Telekom Travel & Surf, Vodafone ReisePaket): 5–10€/day for a data limit — handy for short trips
A local SIM card in the destination country: cheap for long trips, but the number changes
eSIM services (Airalo, Holafly and similar): you buy a data package online before departure, set it up as a second profile, and your German number stays active for calls/SMS
Fully turning off data + Wi-Fi only: free if you rarely need a connection

content.text: An eSIM is the most convenient modern option for a traveller: it activates in minutes, you do not need to hunt for a shop in a foreign country, and your main German number stays in the phone in case of an important call.

Check whether your phone supports eSIM and two SIMs at once (Dual SIM). Older models may not. And remember: when you use local/eSIM data, incoming calls to your German number can still be charged as roaming if the German SIM is active.

costs.label: Roaming outside the EU without a package
costs.note: 1–20€ per MB of data — risk of a bill in the hundreds of euros if you are careless.

costs.label: Daily package from your provider
costs.note: 5–10€ per day for a data limit in the destination country (Travel & Surf and similar).

costs.label: eSIM / local SIM
costs.note: A data package for the trip via Airalo/Holafly or a local SIM — usually cheaper than daily packages on a long trip.

sources.title: Europäische Kommission — Roaming in the EU
Verbraucherzentrale — roaming outside the EU and protection from bills
Telekom Travel & Surf — packages for abroad
Verordnung (EU) 2022/612 über das Roaming (Roam like at home)

title: Spam calls: blocking, Bundesnetzagentur
tldr: Unsolicited telephone advertising (unerlaubte Telefonwerbung) is banned in Germany under §7 UWG. You can file a complaint with the Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur), which fines violators. Block numbers on your phone, use apps (Clever Dialer, Hiya), and NEVER confirm contracts over the phone — scammers record a spoken "yes" and pass it off as consent.

content.text: Cold advertising calls without your prior consent are illegal in Germany. This is directly prohibited by §7 Gesetz gegen den unlauteren Wettbewerb (UWG): an advertising call to a private individual is permitted only with the subscriber's explicit prior consent (Einwilligung).

items: Advertising by phone without consent = an unreasonable nuisance (unzumutbare Belästigung) under §7 UWG
This applies to energy sales, insurance, lotteries, telecom plans and the like
Hiding or spoofing the number on such calls is also prohibited
A violator faces an administrative fine (Bußgeld) of up to 300 000€, imposed by the Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur)

content.text: A common scam is calls supposedly from Microsoft, a bank, the police (Europol), a "grandchild in trouble" (the grandchild trick, Enkeltrick) or about a "prize." The goal is to extract money or data. Real banks and authorities NEVER ask over the phone for passwords, a TAN, card details or a money transfer.

steps.title: How to protect yourself during the call

content.text: The main rule: do not give scammers anything that can be recorded and used. Many schemes are built on getting a spoken "yes" or personal data out of you.

items: If the call is unexpected and an advertising one — hang up without explanation
Do not give out personal data, account details, passwords or a TAN
If in doubt, call the organisation back on its official number from its website
Note down the number and the time for a possible complaint
Do not say "Ja" in response to odd questions — a spoken consent can be faked into a contract
Do not confirm or conclude contracts over the phone
Do not call back unknown expensive numbers (trap calls, Ping-Anrufe)
Do not let on that you are home alone or going away for a long time

content.text: A contract "concluded" over the phone without your real consent is, as a rule, invalid. If you receive a bill or confirmation for a phone "deal" you did not agree to, dispute it in writing (objection, Widerspruch) and do not pay.

steps.title: Complaint to the Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur) and blocking

content.text: The Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur) is the federal regulator that accepts complaints about illegal telephone advertising, spam and number spoofing, and fines violators. The more complaints about a number, the higher the chance of an investigation.

items: Go to bundesnetzagentur.de, to the section for complaints about telephone advertising/number misuse (Telefonwerbung/Rufnummernmissbrauch)
State the caller's number, the date/time and the gist (what they offered)
If possible — the name of the company on whose behalf they called
The complaint is free and submitted online
Block individual numbers right on the phone (the "Block caller" function)
Use caller-ID apps: Clever Dialer, Hiya and similar flag spam numbers
On the router (for example, a FritzBox) you can set up block lists for the Festnetz
Turn on the "silence unknown callers" filter on your smartphone

content.text: Caller-ID apps process data about your calls and contacts — choose reliable ones and check their privacy policy (data protection, Datenschutz). Do not install dubious "blockers" from untrusted sources.

costs.label: Complaint to the Bundesnetzagentur
costs.note: Free — submitted online.

costs.label: Caller-ID apps (basic)
costs.note: Clever Dialer, Hiya and others have free versions; premium features are paid.

costs.label: Fine for the violator
costs.note: Up to 300 000€ Bußgeld for illegal telephone advertising under §7 UWG (paid by the violator, not you).

sources.title: Verbraucherzentrale — illegal advertising calls and fraud

title: Public Wi-Fi (WLAN): where and safety
tldr: Free public Wi-Fi (WLAN) is available in cafés, on German railways (Deutsche Bahn; WIFIonICE), in city hotspots and libraries. Since 2017 the network operator's liability (Störerhaftung) has been abolished — owners of open networks are no longer liable for users' actions, so there are now more open networks. For safety, use a VPN, stick to HTTPS, and do not enter sensitive data on open networks.

content.text: Public wireless internet (in Germany people more often say WLAN than Wi-Fi) is available in many places. After the so-called network operator's liability (Störerhaftung) was abolished in 2017, it became safer for businesses to offer open networks, so there are noticeably more of them.

items: Cafés, restaurants, shopping centres — often free guest Wi-Fi (WLAN)
German railways (Deutsche Bahn): WIFIonICE on ICE trains and at major stations
City hotspots (Freifunk — a community initiative of open networks)
Public libraries and universities (for students — eduroam)
Airports and many hotels

content.text: Freifunk is a non-commercial network run by enthusiasts: open access points without registration all over Germany. Handy, but like any public Wi-Fi it calls for caution with your data.

Previously, the owner of an open Wi-Fi could be held liable for offences committed by network users (for example, illegal downloading) — this was called the network operator's liability (Störerhaftung) and held back the spread of open networks. In 2017 the law (then the Telemediengesetz, TMG) was changed, and this liability for operators of open Wi-Fi was effectively abolished. As of 14 May 2024 the TMG has been replaced by the Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz (DDG), and the protection of WLAN operators has been preserved and is now enshrined in §7 DDG.

items: The operator of a free Wi-Fi is no longer liable for users' offences
This removed the main legal risk for cafés, hotels and private individuals
The result — more open networks across the country
For you as a user, this does not remove your personal liability for your own actions

content.text: Abolishing the network operator's liability (Störerhaftung) protects the OWNER of the network, not you. If you do something illegal yourself over public Wi-Fi, you are the one who will be held liable. And a public network is still technically insecure — that is a separate matter.

Open Wi-Fi is convenient but insecure: traffic can be intercepted, and attackers sometimes set up fake access points with similar names (Evil Twin) to get at your data. A few simple rules sharply reduce the risk.

items: Use a VPN — it encrypts all your traffic on an untrusted network
Make sure sites open over HTTPS (the padlock in the address bar)
Turn off automatic connection to open networks
Keep your system and apps updated
Do not log into online banking or enter card details on open Wi-Fi without a VPN
Do not trust networks with strange or duplicate names
Do not leave file sharing (File Sharing) turned on
When in doubt, use mobile internet instead of public Wi-Fi

content.text: Fake access points (Evil Twin) disguise themselves as legitimate ones ("Free WiFi", "Cafe_Gast"). Confirm the exact network name with staff, and for anything sensitive (banking, purchases) prefer mobile data or a VPN.

costs.label: Public WLAN
costs.note: Free in cafés, on ICE trains (WIFIonICE), city hotspots and libraries.

costs.label: VPN service
costs.note: Reliable VPNs cost ~3–12€/month; there are limited free options.

costs.label: Mobile internet as an alternative
costs.note: Using your own data package instead of public WLAN — within your plan.

sources.title: §7 DDG — Beschränkte Verantwortlichkeit (abolition of Störerhaftung, WLAN)

title: Check your university in Anabin before moving
tldr: Anabin (anabin.kmk.org) is a free official database of the Conference of Ministers of Education (KMK) where, BEFORE moving, you can find out how Germany rates your degree. Your university gets the status H+ (recognised as a higher education institution), H+/- (disputed) or H- (not recognised), and the programme gets a rating of how it compares with a German degree. This directly affects the visa, recognition of qualifications and eligibility for the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU). If your university or programme is not in Anabin, you will need an individual official assessment of the foreign degree (Zeugnisbewertung) from the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB), about 200 €. It is best to do the check before applying for the visa: H+ status speeds up everything that follows.

content.text: Anabin (anabin.kmk.org) is the official information database of the Central Office for Foreign Education (Zentralstelle für ausländisches Bildungswesen, ZAB) at the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education of the federal states (KMK). It collects assessments of foreign universities and degrees for use in Germany. Access is free and requires no registration.

The main reason to check the status in advance: it determines whether your degree is recognised as higher education. That, in turn, decides whether you can apply for the EU Blue Card (Blaue Karte EU) and recognition of qualifications (Anerkennung), and which documents the German embassy will request when you apply for a visa. Finding this out before you buy tickets is far cheaper than sorting it out once you are there.

items: Anabin is free and open without registration
The university (Institution) and the degree (Abschluss) are checked separately
The status affects the visa, the Blue Card and recognition of qualifications
If the university is not in the database — you will need an individual assessment from the ZAB office
Do the check while still in your country of departure, before applying for the visa

steps.title: What the statuses H+, H+/- and H- mean

content.text: In Anabin a university is given one of three statuses. They describe whether Germany recognises the institution as a full higher education institution by the standards of the country where it is located.

items: The institution is recognised as a higher education institution
The best case: it simplifies the visa, recognition and the Blue Card
For the Blue Card, H+ is usually exactly what is required
Also check that your specific programme is in the degree database

items.title: H+/- — the status is disputed or limited

items: Recognition is partial or depends on conditions
An additional ZAB assessment is often required
Budget time and money for an individual assessment
Clarify with the embassy how this status is interpreted

items.title: H- — the university is not recognised

items: The institution is not recognised as a higher education institution
The degree most likely will not work for a visa or recognition
Consider an alternative route (for example, the Chancenkarte based on experience)
Get advice before moving so you do not lose money and time

content.text: The university's status and the degree's status are DIFFERENT records. It can happen that the university has H+, but the specific programme (Abschluss) is not in the database or is rated differently. For the EU Blue Card a match matters: both the university H+ and a degree assessed as corresponding to a German one (equivalent, gleichwertig / entspricht).

steps.title: How to check the university and the degree step by step

content.text: Anabin is split into two parts: "Institutionen" (educational institutions) and "Hochschulabschlüsse" (degrees). You need to check both.

items: Open anabin.kmk.org → the "Institutionen" section
Select the country (Land) where the university is located
Find your university by name (mind the spelling variants)
Note the status: H+, H+/- or H-
Take a screenshot of the university record with the date — useful for the embassy
Go to the "Hochschulabschlüsse" section
Select the country and find your programme or degree
See which German degree it corresponds to
Save the degree record with a screenshot
Match them up: university H+ + degree "entspricht" = a strong position for the visa

content.text: University names are often transliterated differently. If you cannot find your university, try alternative spellings, the former name (universities get renamed) and a search by city. Absence from the database does not mean H-, only that there is no assessment yet — in that case you need the ZAB.

steps.title: If the university is not in Anabin: a degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) from the ZAB office

content.text: If your university or degree is not in Anabin, or the status is disputed (H+/-), order an individual official assessment of the foreign degree (Zeugnisbewertung) from the ZAB office. This is an official document that explains to German authorities what your education corresponds to. It is accepted by embassies, employers and authorities.

items: The application is submitted online through the KMK/ZAB
You will need the degree certificate, the transcript and translations
The standard fee is about 200 € (there are reductions for certain categories)
Processing usually takes several months, so budget time for it
The official degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) is precisely an assessment, not recognition of a profession

content.text: Do not confuse two things: Anabin and the official degree assessment (Zeugnisbewertung) assess the academic level of the degree, whereas professional recognition of qualifications (Anerkennung) for regulated professions — doctor, teacher, lawyer — goes through a separate process via the relevant authority. For academic professions, H+ in Anabin is often enough; in disputed cases individual legal advice is recommended.

costs.label: Check in Anabin
costs.note: The database is free, no registration required.

costs.label: ZAB Zeugnisbewertung (individual assessment)
costs.note: The standard KMK/ZAB fee; reductions are possible for certain categories.

costs.label: Certified translations of documents
costs.note: Per page; a degree certificate with its transcript runs to several pages.

sources.title: Anabin — ZAB/KMK database on foreign education
