title: Retiring at 63, 65, 67
tldr: The standard old-age pension (Regelaltersrente) for those born in 1964 and later starts at age 67 — this is the standard age with no deductions. The "pension for the especially long-term insured" (Rente für besonders langjährig Versicherte, 45 years of insurance) lets you retire without deductions (Abschläge) earlier: the age rises gradually from 63 to 65 depending on your year of birth. The "pension for the long-term insured" (Rente für langjährig Versicherte, 35 years of insurance) allows retirement from 63, but with a deduction of 0.3% for each month of early retirement (max ~14.4%), and the deduction stays for life. You can keep working past the standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze) and earn supplements (Zuschläge) of 0.5%/month. A flexible partial pension (Teilrente) lets you combine a partial pension with work. Calculate the deductions in advance — they can be offset by voluntary contributions under §187a SGB VI.

content.text: The standard old-age pension (Regelaltersrente) is an old-age pension with no deductions (§35 SGB VI). For insured people born in 1964 and later, the standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze) is 67. For those born 1947–1963 the threshold rose in stages from 65 to 67.

items: The minimum insurance period (qualifying period, Wartezeit) for the standard old-age pension is 5 years (60 months)
Born in 1964 and later: 67 years — a full pension with no deductions
Once you reach the standard retirement age, you can earn on the side without limit and without your pension being cut
The application is submitted about 3 months before the desired start of payments

content.text: The size of the pension depends on the pension points you've accumulated (Entgeltpunkte, Rentenpunkte). A year with an average income gives 1 point; the value of a point (current pension value, aktueller Rentenwert) is indexed annually on 1 July.

steps.title: "Pension at 63": 45 years of insurance with no deductions

content.text: The so-called "pension at 63" (Rente mit 63) is the pension for the especially long-term insured (Rente für besonders langjährig Versicherte, §38, §236b SGB VI). It is available without deductions (Abschläge) to those with 45 years (540 months) of insurance. The name itself is outdated: the no-deduction age is rising.

items: 45 years (540 months) of the qualifying period (Wartezeit) are required — work, children, care, and partly unemployment count
Born before 1953: possible at 63 with no deductions
After that the age rises by about 2 months per year of birth
Born in 1964 and later: no deductions from age 65
Periods of unemployment benefit I (Arbeitslosengeld I) in the last 2 years before retirement usually do NOT count (to stop unemployment being used as a bridge into early retirement)

content.text: Don't confuse the pension for the especially long-term insured (Rente für besonders langjährig Versicherte, 45 years, no deductions) with the pension for the long-term insured (Rente für langjährig Versicherte, 35 years, with deductions). These are two different types of pension with different conditions.

The pension for the long-term insured (Rente für langjährig Versicherte, §36 SGB VI) with 35 years of insurance lets you retire as early as 63, but with a permanent deduction. The deduction (Abschlag) is 0.3% for each month of early retirement relative to your individual standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze).

0.3% × the number of months of early retirement. For example, retiring 4 years (48 months) early = 48 × 0.3% = 14.4% permanent reduction of the pension. This deduction applies for life, including after you reach the standard age.

From age 50 you can make compensation payments (Ausgleichszahlungen) under §187a SGB VI to fully or partly offset the future deduction (Abschlag). These contributions are additionally tax-deductible as retirement provision expenses (Altersvorsorgeaufwendungen) — a double benefit. The German Pension Insurance (DRV) calculates the amount in a special statement (Auskunft).

items.title: 3. Earning on the side before the standard retirement age (Regelaltersgrenze)

content.text: Since 2023 the additional earnings limit (Hinzuverdienstgrenze) for old-age pensions has been abolished: even with an early pension you can earn without your payments being cut. But social contributions and tax still apply.

The deduction (Abschlag) permanently reduces not only your pension but also the future survivor's pension (Witwen-/Witwerrente) for your spouse. When calculating early retirement, take into account the long-term consequences for the whole family.

steps.title: Partial pension (Teilrente), late retirement and flexible models

items: Partial pension (Teilrente): you can take the pension partly (e.g. 50%) and keep working — a balance between income and free time
Deferral (Aufschub) / late retirement: for each month after the standard retirement age the pension grows by 0.5% (a supplement, Zuschlag), plus you accrue new pension points (Entgeltpunkte)
Flexible pension (Flexirente): a combination of a partial pension + additional earnings (Hinzuverdienst) + additional contributions
Pension for severely disabled people (Rente für schwerbehinderte Menschen, §37 SGB VI): with a degree of disability (GdB) of 50+, earlier retirement with smaller deductions is possible
Request a free pension statement (Rentenauskunft) / pension consultation (Rentenberatung) from the German Pension Insurance (DRV) before deciding

content.text: Deciding when to retire is a trade-off between the size of the pension, life expectancy, health and the desire to keep working. Advisers at the German Pension Insurance (DRV-Berater) will calculate several scenarios for you free of charge, with specific figures.
Submit your pension application in advance (about 3 months ahead). If you're retiring from another country, check the exportability and taxation — that's a separate topic, especially if you move.

costs.label: Abschlag for early retirement
costs.note: Not money, but a 0.3% reduction of the pension for each month of early retirement, max ~14.4% over 4 years. Applies for life.

costs.label: Zuschlag for late retirement
costs.note: A 0.5% bonus to the pension for each month worked after the Regelaltersgrenze, plus new Entgeltpunkte.

costs.label: Rentenauskunft / Rentenberatung DRV
costs.note: Free consultation and scenario calculation at the Deutsche Rentenversicherung.

title: Witwenrente: survivor's pension
tldr: The survivor's pension — for a widow or widower (Witwen- / Witwerrente, §46 SGB VI) — is a pension for the surviving spouse or registered partner of a deceased insured person. There are two forms: the large widow's/widower's pension (große Witwenrente, 55% of the deceased's pension under the new law) and the small one (kleine Witwenrente, 25%). The large one is granted if the widow/widower is 47+, or there is a minor child or a child needing care, or there is reduced earning capacity (Erwerbsminderung); otherwise the small one (limited to 24 months under the new law). Condition: the marriage lasted at least 1 year (a safeguard against a marriage entered into just to secure the pension, Versorgungsehe). For the first 3 months — the "death quarter" (Sterbevierteljahr) — 100% of the deceased's pension is paid with no offsetting of income. After that, the widow's/widower's own income above the tax-free threshold (Freibetrag) reduces the payment by 40%. Apply to the German Pension Insurance (DRV); pension splitting (Rentensplitting) is an alternative.

content.text: The widow's and widower's pension (Witwen- und Witwerrente) is governed by §46 SGB VI. It is a pension for the surviving spouse or registered partner (eingetragener Lebenspartner). The law distinguishes two forms by amount and conditions.

items: Large widow's/widower's pension (große Witwenrente): 55% of the deceased's pension (under the new law); it used to be 60%
Conditions for the large one: age 47+ OR raising a minor child or a child needing care OR your own reduced earning capacity (Erwerbsminderung)
Small widow's/widower's pension (kleine Witwenrente): 25% of the deceased's pension
Under the new law (marriage/death from 2002) the small pension is limited to 24 months
Under the old law (altes Recht: marriage before 2002 and one spouse born before 1962) — a higher share and no time limit

content.text: The age threshold of 47 for the large pension was raised in stages from 45 and is fixed at 47 for deaths from 2029 onward (for deaths before then it is lower, per the table in §242a).

items: The deceased completed the general qualifying period (allgemeine Wartezeit) of 5 years (60 months) of insurance
The marriage or registered partnership (eingetragene Lebenspartnerschaft) lasted at least 1 year — otherwise a marriage for the pension (Versorgungsehe) is assumed and the pension is refused
Exception to the 1-year rule: death due to an accident or other unforeseeable circumstances
The widow/widower must not have entered into a new marriage (a new marriage ends the entitlement but gives a one-off marriage settlement, Rentenabfindung)
The application is submitted to the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung)

content.text: Marriage for the pension (Versorgungsehe): if the marriage was entered into less than a year before the death, the German Pension Insurance (DRV) by default assumes the aim was to secure the pension, and refuses. You can prove otherwise (for example, that the wedding had been planned long in advance), but it is a contested and difficult procedure.

steps.title: The death quarter (Sterbevierteljahr) and offsetting of income

items.title: 1. The death quarter (Sterbevierteljahr) — the first 3 months

content.text: In the first three calendar months after the spouse's death (the death quarter, Sterbevierteljahr) 100% of the deceased's pension is paid, with NO offsetting of the widow's/widower's own income. This is a period of financial breathing space. The German Pension Insurance (DRV) can pay an advance (Vorschuss) quickly on request.

After the death quarter, your own income is offset. There is a tax-free threshold (Freibetrag) that is indexed annually and tied to the current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert). Income ABOVE the threshold reduces the widow's/widower's pension by 40% of the amount exceeding it.

items: Earned income (Erwerbseinkommen: salary, self-employment income)
Your own pension (old-age pension, Altersrente; reduced-earning-capacity pension, EM-Rente)
Capital and rental income — counted under the new law
For each child the tax-free threshold (Freibetrag) is raised
Basic income support (Bürgergeld) and some other benefits are not counted

content.text: Offsetting of income is a frequent source of unpleasant surprises: if you earn well, the small or even the large widow's/widower's pension can shrink almost to zero. The German Pension Insurance (DRV) recalculates annually and, if your income changes, may demand repayment of overpayments (Rückforderung). Report changes in income on time.

steps.title: How to apply and pension splitting (Rentensplitting)

items: Submit the survivor's pension application (Hinterbliebenenrente-Antrag) to the German Pension Insurance (DRV; form R0500 and annexes)
Attach the death certificate (Sterbeurkunde), the marriage/partnership certificate (Heiratsurkunde/Lebenspartnerschaftsurkunde), and income documents
If needed, request an advance (Vorschuss) for the death quarter (a quick partial payment)
Check entitlement to an orphan's pension (Waisenrente) for children (§48 SGB VI) — a separate pension
Consider pension splitting (Rentensplitting, §120a SGB VI) as an alternative — spouses split the accumulated pension entitlements in half

content.text: Pension splitting (Rentensplitting) can be more advantageous than the classic widow's/widower's pension for couples where both have similar pension entitlements, because with splitting your own income is not offset. But the decision is generally irreversible — calculate both options at the German Pension Insurance (DRV).

On remarriage the entitlement to the widow's/widower's pension ends, but a one-off marriage settlement (Rentenabfindung) of 24 average monthly pensions is paid. If the new marriage breaks down, you can apply for the revival (Wiederaufleben) of the former widow's/widower's pension.

costs.label: Große Witwenrente
costs.note: 55% of the deceased's pension (neues Recht), plus a Zuschlag for children; depends on the widow's/widower's income.

costs.label: Kleine Witwenrente
costs.note: 25% of the deceased's pension; under the new law limited to 24 months.

costs.label: Hinterbliebenenrente application to the DRV
costs.note: Free; the consultation and calculation are also free.

sources.title: §97 SGB VI — Einkommensanrechnung auf Renten wegen Todes

title: Rechtsschutzversicherung: legal expenses insurance
tldr: Legal expenses insurance (Rechtsschutzversicherung) covers the costs of legal disputes: lawyers' fees, court costs, expert reports, and the other side's costs if you lose. The policy is built from modules: private legal protection (Privat-), traffic legal protection (Verkehrs-), professional (Berufs-), housing/tenancy legal protection (Wohnungs-/Mietrechtsschutz). It costs roughly 150–400€/year depending on the set of modules and the deductible (Selbstbeteiligung). There is almost always a waiting period (Wartezeit) of ~3 months (for employment and tenancy law), while traffic accidents and criminal cases are often without a waiting period. A key limitation: disputes that already exist or were known at the time the policy was taken out are not covered, along with a number of exclusions (family law — often only an initial consultation, Erstberatung; building your own house, etc.). For foreigners, tenancy legal protection (Mietrechtsschutz) and employment legal protection (Arbeitsrechtsschutz) are especially useful.

steps.title: What it covers and why you need it

content.text: Legal expenses insurance (Rechtsschutzversicherung) takes on the financial risk of a legal conflict. In Germany the principle applies that the losing party pays both its own and the other side's costs (§91 ZPO), and these can quickly run into thousands of euros. The insurance removes the fear of "not being able to afford a lawyer".

items: Lawyer's costs (Anwaltskosten) — your lawyer's fee under the RVG
Court costs (Gerichtskosten) — court fees
The other side's costs (Kosten der Gegenseite) if you lose
Experts / reports (Sachverständige / Gutachten) — expert assessments
Witness fees (Zeugengelder), mediation (Mediation), and sometimes criminal bail (Strafkaution) on a trip abroad
Telephone legal advice (telefonische Rechtsberatung) — a hotline for quick questions

content.text: For foreigners this is especially valuable in disputes with a landlord (tenancy law, Mietrecht), with an employer (employment law, Arbeitsrecht) and in traffic cases. Legal language and procedures are complex, and without insurance a lawyer charges you up front.

items: Private legal protection (Privatrechtsschutz): contracts, purchases, disputes with companies and neighbours, consumer rights
Traffic legal protection (Verkehrsrechtsschutz): traffic accidents, disputes with insurers, fines, licence withdrawal — often taken on its own even without other modules
Professional / employment legal protection (Berufsrechtsschutz / Arbeitsrecht): disputes with an employer, dismissal, formal warning (Abmahnung), reference (Zeugnis)

Housing and tenancy legal protection (Wohnungs- und Mietrechtsschutz): disputes with a landlord (Vermieter) — utility costs (Nebenkosten), termination of the contract (Kündigung), defects (Mängel), deposit (Kaution)
Optional: tax legal protection (Steuerrechtsschutz, disputes with the tax office, Finanzamt), social legal protection (Sozialrechtsschutz: job centre, Jobcenter; authorities, Behörden)

content.text: "Private + professional + traffic + housing" packages (Privat + Beruf + Verkehr + Wohnen) are the most common set for a family. A deductible (Selbstbeteiligung, usually 150–300€ per case) lowers the premium: the higher the deductible, the cheaper the policy.

Tenancy legal protection (Mietrechtsschutz) and employment legal protection (Arbeitsrechtsschutz) are often sold only in combination or as an add-on. If your main goal is protection for tenancy or work, make sure those specific modules are included, not just private legal protection (Privat).

steps.title: Waiting period (Wartezeit) and what is NOT covered

content.text: Most modules have a waiting period (Wartezeit) of about 3 months: the insured event must arise after it ends. Traffic legal protection (Verkehrsrechtsschutz) and criminal legal protection often work immediately, with no waiting period. The point of the waiting period is to stop you taking out insurance when a conflict is already on the horizon.

The insurance does NOT cover conflicts whose cause arose before the contract was concluded or during the waiting period (Wartezeit), nor those you already knew about. You can't take out a policy "retroactively" for a brewing dispute.

items: Family and inheritance law (Familien- und Erbrecht) — usually only an initial consultation (Erstberatung), not court
Building and buying (Bau und Kauf) your own house/flat (construction risk, Baurisiko) — generally excluded
Investments and speculative transactions — often excluded or limited
Intentional crimes (vorsätzliche Straftaten) are not covered
Disputes between people insured under the same policy (for example, spouses against each other)

content.text: Before filing a claim, request a confirmation of cover (Deckungszusage) from the insurer. The lawyer usually does this for you. If cover is refused, you can turn to an independent assessment (Stichentscheid) or the insurance ombudsman (Versicherungsombudsmann).

costs.label: Annual Rechtsschutzversicherung premium
costs.note: Per year depending on the set of modules (Privat/Verkehr/Beruf/Wohnen) and the size of the Selbstbeteiligung.

costs.label: Selbstbeteiligung per case
costs.note: The deductible; a higher one lowers the annual premium.

costs.label: Erstberatung with a lawyer without insurance
costs.note: Capped by law at a maximum of ~190€ net (≈226€ gross) for an initial consultation for a private individual.

title: Accident insurance (Unfallversicherung)
tldr: Private accident insurance (private Unfallversicherung) covers the consequences of accidents 24 hours a day, worldwide — unlike statutory accident insurance (gesetzliche Unfallversicherung, under SGB VII), which pays only for accidents at work and on the way to/from work. The main benefit is a one-off disability payout (Invaliditätsleistung) in the event of permanent damage to health, calculated using the disability scale (Gliedertaxe) and the sum insured with a progression (Progression). It costs ~50–200€/year. It is especially useful for the self-employed, homemakers, children, the non-working and pensioners who are not covered by statutory insurance. It's important to understand: illnesses (unlike injuries) are not covered — to protect your income you need occupational disability insurance (BU). Accidents cause only 1–2% of cases of lost earning capacity, so it is a supplement, not a replacement.

content.text: Statutory accident insurance (gesetzliche Unfallversicherung, §§1 ff. SGB VII) automatically covers employees, but only accidents at work (Arbeitsunfälle, at the workplace), commuting accidents (Wegeunfälle, on the way to/from work) and occupational diseases (Berufskrankheiten). In your free time — at home, doing sport, on holiday — it does NOT apply. Most accidents happen precisely at home and during leisure.

items: Statutory (gesetzlich): only work + the commute to work; the employer pays the contributions
Private (privat): 24/7 worldwide — at home, sport, holiday, hobbies
Private is especially important for those whom statutory insurance does not cover at all
Children at daycare (Kita)/school are covered by statutory insurance only during lessons and the journey
Private insurance does not depend on fault or on where the injury occurred

content.text: The self-employed, members of the liberal professions (Freiberufler), homemakers, the non-working and pensioners are usually NOT covered by statutory insurance. For them, private accident insurance (Unfallversicherung) is often the only protection against the financial consequences of a serious injury.

steps.title: What it covers and how the payout is calculated

content.text: The central benefit is the disability payout (Invaliditätsleistung): a one-off sum in the event of lasting (permanent) damage to health after an accident. Its size depends on the sum insured (Versicherungssumme), the degree of disability per the disability scale (Gliedertaxe) and the chosen progression (Progression).

items: Disability payout (Invaliditätsleistung): the main benefit; the disability scale (Gliedertaxe) sets the % for loss of function of a specific body part (arm, leg, eye, etc.)
Progression (Progression, 225%/350%/500%): sharply increases the payout at high degrees of disability
Disability pension (Unfallrente): optional — a monthly pension for disability from a certain threshold (for example 50%)
Death benefit (Todesfallleistung): a payout to relatives in the event of death from an accident
Rescue costs (Bergungskosten), cosmetic surgery, a daily hospital allowance (Krankenhaustagegeld) — additional options

content.text: Tip: choose a high sum insured with a progression (Progression) rather than a low sum — serious disability is expensive, and the premium doesn't rise proportionally. For children there are often separate cheap tariffs with high sums.

steps.title: Limitations and where it fits among other insurances

content.text: Accident insurance (Unfallversicherung) pays only in the event of an accident (Unfall) — a sudden external event. Illnesses (cancer, heart attack, mental disorders), which cause the overwhelming majority of cases of lost earning capacity, are NOT covered. This is the key limitation.

items.title: 2. Not a replacement for occupational disability insurance (BU)

content.text: Accidents account for only ~1–2% of all cases of occupational disability (Berufsunfähigkeit). If your goal is to protect your income against being unable to work, the main tool is occupational disability insurance (Berufsunfähigkeitsversicherung; see the separate guide), and accident insurance is only a supplement.

items.title: 3. What to look at in the terms

items: The deadline for reporting disability (Invalidität) — usually it must be established within 12–15 months of the accident
The contribution of illnesses/infirmities (Mitwirkung von Krankheiten/Gebrechen): the insurer can cut the payout if a pre-existing condition contributed
Exclusions: some extreme sports, alcohol/drugs, aviation sports
Disability scale (Gliedertaxe): compare the percentages across insurers — they differ

content.text: Don't buy accident insurance (Unfallversicherung) as a "cheap replacement" for income protection. A healthy employee whose priority is protecting their earnings should first take out occupational disability insurance (BU), and add accident insurance as a second layer. For the non-working and for children, on the other hand, accident insurance is a sensible basic choice.

costs.label: Annual premium for private Unfallversicherung
costs.note: Per year; depends on the sum insured, the Progression, occupation/hobbies and the set of options.

costs.label: Tariff for a child
costs.note: Per year; usually cheaper than for an adult at a high sum insured.

costs.label: Gesetzliche Unfallversicherung
costs.note: Free for an employee — the employer pays the contributions in full to the Berufsgenossenschaft.

title: Voluntary contributions to pension insurance (Rentenversicherung)
tldr: Voluntary contributions (freiwillige Beiträge) to the state pension insurance (gesetzliche Rentenversicherung, §§7, 232 SGB VI) let those who are not required to be insured (the self-employed, the non-working, those living abroad) pay contributions voluntarily. The main goals: top up missing months for the qualifying period (Wartezeit) (for example 60 months for a minimum pension or for the reduced-earning-capacity pension, Erwerbsminderungsrente), keep your entitlement to that pension (EM-Rente), or simply increase your future pension. You choose the contribution amount yourself: from the minimum contribution (Mindestbeitrag, 112.16€/month in 2026) to the maximum (Höchstbeitrag, 1 571.70€/month in 2026), tied to the income ceiling for calculating social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze). Contributions can be paid retroactively until 31 March of the following year. Setup and calculation are done through the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung); before starting, request a free account clarification (Kontenklärung) and a consultation.

content.text: Voluntary insurance (freiwillige Versicherung, §7 SGB VI) is open to those who are not subject to compulsory pension insurance: the self-employed who are not subject to an insurance obligation (Versicherungspflicht), the non-working, homemakers, and citizens living outside Germany. It is a way to build or keep entitlements in the state pension insurance (gesetzliche Rentenversicherung) on your own.

items: Top up the qualifying period (Wartezeit): for example 60 months — the minimum insurance period for the standard old-age pension
Keep your entitlement to the reduced-earning-capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente): for this, recent compulsory or voluntary months in the run-up matter
Increase your future pension: each contribution adds pension points (Entgeltpunkte)
Meet the conditions for early types of pension (for example 35/45 years of insurance)
Available from age 16 to those who are not otherwise compulsorily insured

content.text: Especially important for the reduced-earning-capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente): entitlement to it generally requires at least 36 months of compulsory or (in some cases) voluntary contributions (Pflicht- oder freiwillige Beiträge) in the last 5 years. Missing payments can quietly deprive you of this protection — check the details with the German Pension Insurance (DRV).

You choose the monthly contribution amount yourself, between the minimum contribution (Mindestbeitrag) and the maximum (Höchstbeitrag). The minimum contribution is tied to the minimum assessment base (Mindestbemessungsgrundlage) and is 112.16€/month in 2026; the maximum contribution is calculated from the income ceiling for social contributions (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) and in 2026 is 1 571.70€/month.

items: The contribution rate to the state pension insurance (Beitragssatz gesetzliche RV) is 18.6% of the chosen base
The minimum contribution (Mindestbeitrag) is 112.16€/month in 2026 (base ~603€)
The maximum contribution (Höchstbeitrag) is 1 571.70€/month in 2026 (18.6% of the income ceiling BBG 8 450€)
You can change the amount every month — flexible to fit your budget
Contributions for a past year can be paid retroactively until 31 March of the following year

content.text: The more you pay in, the more pension points (Entgeltpunkte) you get and the higher your future pension. But for the goal of "just topping up the qualifying period", the minimum contribution (Mindestbeitrag) is usually enough — there's no need to overpay just for the qualifying period.

steps.title: How to set it up through the German Pension Insurance (DRV)

content.text: First, request an account clarification (Kontenklärung) and a pension statement (Rentenauskunft) from the German Pension Insurance (DRV): you'll see how many months of insurance are already counted and how many are missing for the required qualifying period (Wartezeit). Without this you won't know how much to pay or why.

items.title: 2. Application for voluntary insurance (Antrag auf freiwillige Versicherung)

content.text: Submit an application for voluntary insurance (Antrag auf freiwillige Versicherung, form V0060) to the German Pension Insurance (Deutsche Rentenversicherung). You can do it online, by post or through a consultation office (Beratungsstelle). The DRV will confirm your entitlement and give you the payment details.

items: Pay using the German Pension Insurance (DRV) bank details; you can set up a regular transfer
Make sure the contributions for the year arrive by 31 March of the following year
Keep the confirmations — the contributions are partly tax-deductible as retirement provision expenses (Altersvorsorgeaufwendungen)
Once a year, check the updated pension information (Renteninformation)

content.text: The consultation and calculation at the German Pension Insurance (DRV) are free. Before you start, be sure to go to a pension consultation (Rentenberatung) — a specialist will advise whether, in your case, voluntary contributions (freiwillige Beiträge), a compensation payment (Ausgleichszahlung) to offset deductions (Abschläge), or another tool is more advantageous.

Voluntary contributions (freiwillige Beiträge) cannot be refunded if you later change your mind. Also important: they affect the calculation of entitlement to the reduced-earning-capacity pension (EM-Rente) and the export of the pension abroad. If you plan to return to another country, first check how these contributions will be counted and taxed.

costs.label: Mindestbeitrag freiwillige RV
costs.note: Per month; 112.16€ in 2026 (18.6% of the minimum assessment base). Indexed annually.

costs.label: Höchstbeitrag freiwillige RV
costs.note: Per month; 1 571.70€ in 2026 (18.6% of the BBG 8 450€/month).

costs.label: Kontenklärung and Rentenberatung DRV
costs.note: Free at the Deutsche Rentenversicherung.

title: Student visa §16b
tldr: §16b AufenthG is the national visa and residence permit for full-time study at a German university. The basic condition is admission (Zulassung/Immatrikulation) to a recognised university (Hochschule). Financial proof is a blocked account (Sperrkonto) of ~11 904 € per year (the BAföG requirement of ~992 €/month × 12). You can work 140 full or 280 half days per year without a separate permit; student jobs at the university (HiWi) don't count toward the limit. The residence permit is issued for the duration of the studies, with extensions. Fees: national visa 75 € + residence permit 100 €. After graduation — §20 for up to 18 months to look for a job in your field.

steps.title: What §16b gives you and who it suits

content.text: §16b AufenthG (study, Studium) is the main provision for non-EU students entering a full academic programme (Bachelor, Master, Staatsexamen, doctorate) at a recognised German university (Hochschule). The residence permit covers the period of study and is extended as long as you remain enrolled (immatrikuliert) and are passing exams.

Citizens of Russia, Belarus, Ukraine and most third countries first get a national D visa at the diplomatic mission, and in Germany exchange it for an electronic residence permit card (eAT) at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde). Citizens of a number of countries (USA, Canada, Australia, Japan, the Republic of Korea, etc.) are allowed to enter without a visa and arrange the §16b residence permit on the spot.

items: Who: non-EU students admitted to a full-time programme at a German university
Basic condition: admission (Zulassung) and subsequent enrolment at the university (Immatrikulation)
Finances: a blocked account (Sperrkonto) of ~11 904 € per year or other proof
Work: 140 full / 280 half days per year without the consent of the Federal Employment Agency (BA)
Duration: for the period of study, usually with extensions
After graduation: §20 for up to 18 months to look for a job in your field
The study period is partly counted toward later periods for permanent residence

content.text: §16b is specifically a status for studying at a university. The preparatory stage (a preparatory college attached to a university, Studienkolleg; a study-preparatory language course, studienvorbereitender Sprachkurs) also falls under §16b (a study purpose), but it is a separate sub-category; a pure language course with no aim of enrolment is arranged under §16f with stricter conditions. Don't confuse the grounds: an error in the choice of provision leads to refusal.

steps.title: Admission (Zulassung) and enrolment at the university

content.text: The key document for §16b is the admission notice (Zulassungsbescheid) from a German university. Without it the consulate won't issue the visa. Documents are submitted directly to the university or via the uni-assist platform, which checks the recognition of your diploma or school certificate and converts the grades into the German system.

items.title: 1. Check the recognition of your school certificate or diploma via anabin

items: anabin.kmk.org → the Schulabschlüsse / Hochschulabschlüsse sections
A Russian school certificate after 11 grades usually doesn't give direct access — you need 1–2 years of university or a preparatory college (Studienkolleg)
A Russian bachelor's diploma generally opens access to a Master's programme
If the university is marked H+, the documents are recognised more easily

items.title: 2. Apply via uni-assist or directly to the university

items: Register at my.uni-assist.de, upload scans of your school certificate or diploma with a certified translation
uni-assist fee: 75 € for the first application plus 30 € for each subsequent one in the same semester
Processing time 4–6 weeks — apply in advance
Language certificate: TestDaF or DSH (for German-taught programmes), IELTS or TOEFL (for English-taught ones)
After admission (Zulassung) you pay the semester fee (Semesterbeitrag, often 150–350 €, frequently includes a transport pass)
Enrolment at the university (Immatrikulation) confirms your student status and is needed to extend the residence permit
Student health insurance is mandatory for enrolment

content.text: For §16b you need to prove your means of subsistence (Lebensunterhaltssicherung) for a year. The amount is tied to the BAföG rate and for 2026 is ~11 904 € (992 €/month × 12). The most common method is a blocked account (Sperrkonto), from which a fixed limit is available to you each month.

items: Blocked account (Sperrkonto) providers: Fintiba, Expatrio, Coracle — online opening with a Russian passport
The full amount of ~11 904 € is deposited, with ~992 €/month available for withdrawal
Alternative: a declaration of commitment to cover costs (Verpflichtungserklärung) from a sponsor in Germany
A scholarship from a recognised foundation (DAAD, Erasmus+) is accepted
Due to SWIFT restrictions, a transfer from Russia usually goes through banks not under sanctions or an account in a third country

content.text: Since 2022, direct SWIFT transfers from most Russian banks to Germany have been unavailable. A practical route is an account in a third country (for example Armenia, Kazakhstan, Georgia) and a transfer from there to the blocked account (Sperrkonto). Check the current list of source countries in the provider's FAQ — it changes.

Under §16b students can work without separate consent from the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) within a limit of 140 full or 280 half days per year (a half day is up to 4 hours). The limit applies to any work except student positions at the university itself (student/research assistant, studentische/wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft, HiWi), which don't count toward the limit.

items: 140 full days (more than 4 h) OR 280 half days (up to 4 h) per calendar year
A student assistant (HiWi) or tutor at the university — with no limit on days
Self-employment and freelancing require a separate permit from the foreigners' authority (ABH)
A mini-job (Minijob) is a popular format; check the current mini-job ceiling for the year in question
During a mandatory internship in your curriculum (Pflichtpraktikum) the limit does not apply

content.text: Exceeding the 140/280-day limit breaches the conditions of the residence permit and can be a ground for refusing an extension or for revocation. Keep a record of the days worked. Studying must remain the main purpose of your stay.

After finishing university you can stay in Germany: §16b lets you apply for a §20 residence permit (job search, Arbeitsplatzsuche) for up to 18 months to look for a job in your field. During this period work is allowed without restrictions. Once you find a position matching your qualification, you move to §18b (including the EU Blue Card, Blue Card) without leaving the country.

items: §20 after graduation: up to 18 months to look for a job, with unlimited work
A job in your field → moving to §18b or the EU Blue Card (Blue Card)
A permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) under §18c is possible once the conditions are met (work, language, contributions)
The study period is partly counted toward the period for citizenship
Family reunification is possible with proof of income and housing

costs.label: National D visa for studying
costs.note: Paid at the diplomatic mission when applying, non-refundable if refused.

costs.label: Issuance of the §16b residence permit card (eAT)
costs.note: Paid at the Ausländerbehörde after arrival.

costs.label: Sperrkonto: deposit
costs.note: ~992 €/month available for withdrawal. Provider servicing — 5–9 €/month.

costs.label: Application via uni-assist
costs.note: 75 € for the first application plus 30 € for each additional one in the semester.

costs.label: Certified translation of school certificate or diploma
costs.note: With a sworn translator (beeidigter Übersetzer) — 50–80 €/page; cheaper in Russia.

costs.label: Student health insurance
costs.note: Roughly ~120 €/month, mandatory for enrolment.

title: Study preparation visa §16b
tldr: Study preparation (foundation college at a university (Studienkolleg), studienvorbereitender Sprachkurs, sitting entrance exams) falls under the purpose of "study" per §16b AufenthG, not §16a (which governs vocational training (Berufsausbildung)). Colloquially this is the Studienbewerbervisum (prospective-student visa). You need a conditional admission (bedingte Zulassung) or a place at a foundation college (Studienkolleg) / on a preparatory course. Finances: a blocked account (Sperrkonto) of ~11 904 € per year. Work during the preparatory phase is restricted more tightly than for regular students. Preparation usually lasts up to 2 years; you then switch to §16b for the studies themselves. Fees: D-visa 75 € + residence permit 100 €.

content.text: Not every foreign school certificate gives direct access to a German university. A Russian certificate after 11 years of school is generally not recognised as a higher-education entrance qualification (Hochschulzugangsberechtigung) — you either need to complete 1–2 years of university at home, or go through a foundation college (Studienkolleg) and sit the final qualifying exam (Feststellungsprüfung). German-taught programmes require German at DSH-2 level (university German exam) or TestDaF (German exam for university admission), which many people reach on intensive courses once they are already in Germany.

All these preparatory measures (foundation college (Studienkolleg), studienvorbereitender Sprachkurs) legally fall under the purpose of "study" under §16b AufenthG. Important: §16a governs vocational training (Berufsausbildung), not university preparation. Colloquially the preparatory visa is called the Studienbewerbervisum (prospective-student visa). It does not let you start a Bachelor's straight away — it is a stage after which you continue your studies under §16b.

items: Who: prospective students who need preparation before admission
Forms: foundation college (Studienkolleg), language course aimed at admission, sitting entrance exams
Basic condition: conditional admission (bedingte Zulassung) or a place at a college (Kolleg) / on a course
Finances: blocked account (Sperrkonto) ~11 904 € per year
Work: during the preparatory phase more restricted than for §16b students
Duration: usually up to 2 years for all preparation
Next: switch to §16b for the university studies themselves

content.text: A purely language course with no prospect of admission is handled under §16f (not the purpose of "study"), where conditions are stricter and work is usually prohibited. The preparatory residence permit is granted when a concrete goal is visible — admission to a university. State clearly in your motivation letter which programme you are aiming for.

The foundation college (Studienkolleg) is a college attached to a university or a university of applied sciences. Over 1–2 semesters it brings your German and your subject knowledge up to the required standard, after which you sit the qualifying exam (Feststellungsprüfung), which grants access to the relevant group of degree subjects (Schwerpunktkurs: T-Kurs for technical, W-Kurs for economics, M-Kurs for medical, G-Kurs for humanities, S-Kurs for languages).

items: Admission to the college (Kolleg) — via an entrance exam (Aufnahmeprüfung) with German at B1–B2 level
State foundation colleges (Studienkolleg) are free (you pay only the semester fee (Semesterbeitrag))
Private foundation colleges charge fees: roughly 5000–12 000 € per course
Your choice of Schwerpunktkurs determines which subjects are open to you
The qualifying entrance exam is recognised by universities in the state (and often nationally)

content.text: Places at state foundation colleges are few and competition is high. For the preparatory visa you need confirmation of admission or at least registration for the entrance exam (Aufnahmeprüfung). Without a confirmed preparatory programme the consulate will not issue the visa — the intention to "come and get admitted once I'm there" is not enough.

The financial requirement is the same as for a student visa: ~11 904 € for the year via a blocked account (Sperrkonto), a sponsorship undertaking or a scholarship. The difference in the preparatory phase is the work rules: at this stage employment is more strictly limited than for §16b students and usually requires the explicit consent of the foreigners' authority (ABH).

items: Blocked account (Sperrkonto) ~11 904 € (992 €/month × 12) — Fintiba, Expatrio, Coracle
Work during the preparatory phase is restricted; check the amount and conditions with the foreigners' authority (ABH)
During a language course employment may be restricted more tightly
Student or private health insurance is mandatory
Transferring money from Russia — via banks outside sanctions or an account in a third country

content.text: Preparation is a temporary stage. Once you have passed the qualifying entrance exam (Feststellungsprüfung) or reached the required language level and obtained admission (Zulassung), you apply to the foreigners' authority (ABH) for a §16b residence permit for university study — without leaving Germany. This is a routine procedure provided you stayed within the preparation period (usually up to 2 years) and did not breach the conditions.

items: You receive admission (Zulassung) → apply for §16b (study) at the foreigners' authority (ABH)
Change of stay purpose without returning for a new visa
You need: enrolment, current health insurance, proof of finances
After the switch the §16b work rules apply (140/280 days)
If preparation is not completed in time, an extension is generally not granted

content.text: The preparatory phase is time-limited (generally up to 2 years for the entire path of preparation and finding a place). Plan your foundation college (Studienkolleg) and your language exam so that you can apply for §16b before the preparatory residence permit expires.

costs.label: National D-visa (Studienbewerber)
costs.note: Paid at the diplomatic mission when you apply; non-refundable if refused.

costs.label: Issue of the residence-permit card (study preparation)
costs.note: Paid at the Ausländerbehörde after arrival.

costs.label: Sperrkonto: deposit
costs.note: Available to withdraw ~992 €/month. Provider servicing fees — 5–9 €/month.

costs.label: Private Studienkolleg (if no place at a state one)
costs.note: State Studienkolleg are free, but places are scarce.

costs.label: Certified translation of the school certificate
costs.note: From a sworn translator — 50–80 €/page.

title: Vocational training visa (Ausbildung) §16a
tldr: §16a AufenthG (Berufsausbildung) — visa and residence permit for qualified vocational training (Ausbildung). You need a signed training contract (Ausbildungsvertrag) in a recognised occupation. German is usually required at B1 level; for care and medicine often B2. The trainee receives a trainee wage (Ausbildungsvergütung; roughly 1000–1200 €/month in the first year), so a blocked account (Sperrkonto) is often not required. Side jobs beyond the training are limited. After completion — a residence permit to look for work in your field (up to 12 months) and a switch to §18a. Fees: D-visa 75 € + residence permit 100 €.

steps.title: What Ausbildung is and the §16a visa

content.text: Vocational training (Ausbildung) is German qualified training, most often dual: you work at a company and study at a vocational school (Berufsschule) at the same time, learning a specific occupation (nurse, electrician, IT Fachinformatiker, cook, logistician and hundreds of others). It usually lasts 2–3.5 years, and unlike university study you are paid a trainee wage (Ausbildungsvergütung).

For non-EU foreigners, entry for vocational training is handled under §16a AufenthG (qualifizierte Berufsausbildung). It is an attractive route for citizens of Russia, Belarus and Ukraine: the entry threshold is lower than for university visas, there is a wage, and on completion you can stay and work with good prospects for permanent residence.

items: Who: those wanting to learn an occupation in the dual system
Basic condition: a signed training contract (Ausbildungsvertrag) in a recognised occupation
Language: usually B1, for care and medicine often B2
Wage: trainee wage (Ausbildungsvergütung) roughly 1000–1200 €/month in the first year
Blocked account (Sperrkonto) often not needed if the wage covers the subsistence minimum
Side jobs beyond the training are limited
After: residence permit to look for work in your field (up to 12 months) → §18a

steps.title: Finding a place and the Ausbildungsvertrag

content.text: The main and hardest part is finding an employer willing to sign a training contract (Ausbildungsvertrag) with you. Without this contract the §16a visa cannot be issued. Positions are found through the portal of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit), specialised platforms, and directly with employers in shortage sectors (care, hospitality, crafts, logistics).

items.title: 1. Where to look for a training place (Ausbildungsplatz)

items: Jobbörse of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit, arbeitsagentur.de)
Make it in Germany — vocational-training (Ausbildung) section and job portal
IHK-Lehrstellenbörse (the Chamber of Industry and Commerce's apprenticeship exchange) and HWK (Chamber of Crafts) for craft occupations
Company websites and care (Pflege) networks
German certificate at B1 (Goethe, telc, ÖSD) — the minimum for most occupations
For care (Pflege) and medicine, B2 is often required
The vocational school (Berufsschule) is taught in German — without the language you cannot keep up
The contract is registered with the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) or the Chamber of Crafts (HWK) (for a recognised occupation)
The contract states the occupation, the duration and the trainee wage (Ausbildungsvergütung)
This document is the basis of the visa package

content.text: The occupation must be state-recognised (staatlich anerkannt); the list is maintained by the Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training (BIBB). Informal internships and "training" with a private individual not registered with the Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK) or the Chamber of Crafts (HWK) do not qualify for the §16a visa. Make sure it really is a training contract (Ausbildungsvertrag) and not an ordinary employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag).

The advantage of vocational training over ordinary study is that you get paid. The trainee wage (Ausbildungsvergütung) in the first year is usually 1000–1200 €/month and rises with each subsequent year. If the wage covers the subsistence minimum, a blocked account (Sperrkonto) is generally not required. If the wage is low, the foreigners' authority (ABH) may request additional security.

items: Trainee wage (Ausbildungsvergütung): roughly 1000–1200 € in the first year, higher in later ones
If the wage covers the subsistence minimum — a blocked account is often not needed
If the wage is low — a partial blocked account or a sponsorship undertaking
Health insurance is mandatory (usually through the employer)
Support via BAB (Berufsausbildungsbeihilfe — vocational-training allowance) may be possible — check your eligibility separately

steps.title: After Ausbildung: work and permanent residence

content.text: Once you have completed the training and received your completion document (Gesellenbrief / Abschlusszeugnis), you can stay: §16a grants the right to a residence permit to look for work in your field for up to 12 months. Once you have found a job in the occupation you trained for, you switch to §18a (Fachkraft mit Berufsausbildung). This is a direct path to a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis).

items: After graduating: residence permit to look for work for up to 12 months
Work in your field → §18a (Fachkraft mit Berufsausbildung)
A permanent residence permit per §18c is possible once the conditions are met (length of employment, language, contributions)
Good chances in shortage occupations (care, crafts, technical fields)
Time spent in vocational training partly counts towards the residence period for citizenship

content.text: During vocational training, side jobs are limited and must not interfere with the main training. Interrupting or failing the training is grounds for refusing to extend the residence permit. Be sure to notify the foreigners' authority (ABH) of any change of employer or occupation.

costs.label: National D-visa for Ausbildung
costs.note: Paid at the diplomatic mission when you apply; non-refundable if refused.

costs.label: Issue of the §16a residence-permit card
costs.note: Paid at the Ausländerbehörde after arrival.

costs.label: German courses and exam up to B1/B2
costs.note: Depends on your starting level; the telc/Goethe exam costs around 150–250 €.

costs.label: Certified translation of documents
costs.note: From a sworn translator — 50–80 €/page.

costs.label: Partial Sperrkonto (if the wage is low)
costs.note: Not needed if the Ausbildungsvergütung covers the subsistence minimum.

title: Au pair: visa and conditions
tldr: Au pair — living with a German family helping around the house and caring for children in exchange for accommodation, meals and pocket money. The legal basis for work access is §12 BeschV. Age 18–26, basic German A1; EU/EEA citizens need no visa. Duration — a maximum of 1 year, with no extension. Pocket money ~280 €/month plus free room and board and the family paying for a language course. Workload up to 30 hrs/week, no more than 6 hrs/day. Fees: D-visa 75 € + residence permit (for au pairs often at a reduced rate). The host family must have at least one child and speak German at home.

steps.title: What au pair is and who it suits

content.text: Au pair is a form of cultural exchange: a young person lives with a host German family, helps with the children and light housework, and in return receives free accommodation, meals, pocket money and the chance to learn the language. It is not work in the classic sense, but a programme for getting to know the country's culture and language.

The legal basis for work access is §12 BeschV (Beschäftigungsverordnung — Employment Ordinance); the visa is issued as a national D-visa. For citizens of Russia, Belarus and Ukraine (non-EU) a visa is mandatory; EU/EEA citizens need no visa.

items: Age: 18–26 at the time of application
Language: basic German A1 (certificate)
Citizenship: outside the EU/EEA (otherwise no visa needed)
Duration: a maximum of 1 year, with no extension
Pocket money: ~280 €/month
Room and board — free from the family
The family must have at least one child and speak German at home

content.text: Au pair is generally a one-off programme of at most a year: it is neither extended nor repeated. By itself it does not lead to long-term residence: to stay, you need to switch within the year to study (§16b), vocational training (Ausbildung, §16a) or another status. Plan your next step in advance.

steps.title: The host family and the conditions

content.text: You can find a family yourself or through recognised agencies (for example, members of the Gütegemeinschaft Au-pair carrying the RAL quality mark). An au-pair contract (Au-pair-Vertrag) is signed between the au pair and the family, setting out duties, working hours, days off, pocket money and payment for a language course. This contract is the key document for the visa.

items: Workload: up to 30 hours a week, no more than 6 hours a day
At least one day off a week and several free evenings
Pocket money of ~280 €/month is paid by the family
The family pays for a language course and provides a separate room
The family arranges health insurance and accident insurance
Paid holiday (in proportion to the length of stay)

content.text: If the family demands more than 30 hrs/week, uses the au pair as a full-time nanny or housekeeper with no days off, or fails to pay for insurance and the course — this breaches §12 BeschV. The au pair has the right to terminate the contract; turn to the agency or a migrant advice service. Do not agree to "grey" conditions.

You apply for the national D-visa for au pairs at the German diplomatic mission. The main documents are the signed au-pair contract (Au-pair-Vertrag), the German A1 certificate, proof of insurance from the family and a motivation letter. The visa fee is 75 €. After arrival you obtain a residence-permit card (residence permit) from the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde).

items: Fill in the national-visa application form and book an appointment at the consulate
Documents: passport, au-pair contract (Au-pair-Vertrag), A1 certificate, photo, insurance
D-visa fee: 75 €
After entry: residence registration (Anmeldung) at the family's address and a residence-permit card (residence permit) at the foreigners' authority (ABH) (for au pairs often at a reduced rate)
Sign up for a language course (paid for by the family)

steps.title: What to do after the au-pair year

content.text: The au-pair year ends, and it cannot be extended. To stay legally, you need to switch to another status in good time: university study (§16b), study preparation (§16b, studienvorbereitend), vocational training (Ausbildung, §16a) or, if you have an offer and the qualifications, a work residence permit. Many use the au-pair year as a stepping stone: they raise their German from A1 to B1/B2 and enrol in vocational training or a foundation college (Studienkolleg).

items: Switch to §16b (university study) if you have a Zulassung
Switch to §16a (vocational training, Ausbildung) with a signed training contract (Ausbildungsvertrag)
Study preparation (§16b), if your language or school certificate is not yet enough
The change of status is done at the foreigners' authority (ABH) without leaving the country
Use the year to bring your German up from A1 to B1/B2

content.text: Start looking for your next status several months before the year ends: finding a training place (Ausbildungsplatz), getting admitted and processing documents all take time. If the au-pair residence permit expires without a switch to a new status, you will have to leave. Don't leave this to the final weeks.

costs.label: National D-visa for au pair
costs.note: Paid at the diplomatic mission when you apply; non-refundable if refused.

costs.label: Issue of the residence-permit card after arrival
costs.note: Paid at the Ausländerbehörde; for au pairs often at a reduced rate.

costs.label: German course and exam up to A1
costs.note: An A1 certificate is needed before applying; the Goethe/telc exam costs around 80–150 €.

costs.label: Certified translation of documents
costs.note: Translation of certificates and records for the visa package.

costs.label: Pocket money (income, not an expense)
costs.note: ~280 €/month is paid by the family; room and board are free.

title: Researcher visa §18d
tldr: §18d AufenthG (Forschung) — residence permit for research staff. The key document is a hosting agreement (Aufnahmevereinbarung; hosting agreement) or an employment contract with a recognised research institution. The process is fast, with no labour-market test by the Federal Employment Agency (BA). Pluses: simplified family reunification, the spouse's right to work immediately, EU mobility, time counting towards later permanent residence. Suits postdocs, professors, researchers at institutes (Max Planck, Fraunhofer, Helmholtz, Leibniz, universities). Fees: D-visa 75 € + residence permit 100 €.

steps.title: What §18d offers and who it suits

content.text: §18d AufenthG (Forschung) is a special, fast and advantageous residence permit for scientists and researchers, implementing the European directive on researchers. It is intended for those coming to carry out research at a recognised research institution in Germany: a university, a Max-Planck-Institut, Fraunhofer, Helmholtz, the Leibniz-Gemeinschaft and others.

The main advantages of §18d are the absence of a labour-market test (the consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) is not required), simplified family reunification and the spouse's right to work without restrictions from day one. It is one of the most convenient statuses for qualified moves in academia.

items: Who: postdocs, professors, research staff, researchers
Basic condition: a hosting agreement (Aufnahmevereinbarung) or an employment contract with a research institution
No labour-market test (BA) — the process is fast
The spouse may work immediately without restrictions
Simplified family reunification
EU mobility: short-term (up to 180 days within 360) and long-term (§18e)
Time counts towards the residence period for a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis)

content.text: The basis of the §18d visa is a hosting agreement (Aufnahmevereinbarung) between you and an institution recognised by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) as a research institution (Forschungseinrichtung). It records the research project, the duration and the funding. The alternative is an ordinary employment contract for a research position at the same institution.

items: The institution must be on the register of recognised research institutions (Forschungseinrichtungen) of BAMF
The hosting agreement describes the project, the duration, the salary or stipend
The institution confirms the financial security — a blocked account (Sperrkonto) is usually not needed
Both permanent positions and temporary grants and stipends are permitted
The qualification is, as a rule, at the level of a doctorate or equivalent

content.text: The institution must hold a valid recognition (Anerkennung) from BAMF to host researchers under §18d. If your future institute is not on the register, it can apply for recognition, or you can apply on another basis (for example, §18b / the EU Blue Card (Blue Card EU)). Clarify this with the HR department or the Welcome Center before applying for the visa.

§18d is especially valuable for family moves. The researcher's spouse receives a residence permit with the right to work immediately — with no separate permit and no requirement to know German at the outset. Children join under simplified conditions. The researcher status grants mobility within the EU: part of the research can be carried out in other Union countries.

items: Spouse: residence permit and the right to work without restrictions from day one
Children: reunification under simplified conditions
Short-term EU mobility: research for up to 180 days within 360
Long-term mobility (§18e) — for lengthy projects in another EU country
For reunification of a researcher's spouse the B1 requirement does not apply

steps.title: The process and the path to permanent residence

content.text: You apply at the diplomatic mission for a national D-visa with the hosting agreement (Aufnahmevereinbarung). Since no labour-market test is needed, processing is usually faster than for standard work visas. After arrival you obtain a residence-permit card (residence permit) at the foreigners' authority (ABH). Time under §18d counts towards a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis).

items: Apply for the D-visa with the hosting agreement (Aufnahmevereinbarung), fee 75 €
Fast processing: the consent of the BA is not required
After entry: residence registration (Anmeldung) and a residence-permit card (residence permit) at the foreigners' authority (ABH) (~100 €)
Time counts towards the residence period for a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis)
For highly qualified specialists and researchers, accelerated timelines to permanent residence are possible (once the §18c conditions are met)

content.text: If the research project ends early or you change institution, notify the foreigners' authority (ABH) and conclude a new hosting agreement (Aufnahmevereinbarung): §18d status is tied to a specific research agreement. Without a valid agreement, the right of residence under §18d ends.

costs.label: National D-visa for researchers
costs.note: Paid at the diplomatic mission when you apply; non-refundable if refused.

costs.label: Issue of the §18d residence-permit card
costs.note: Paid at the Ausländerbehörde after arrival.

costs.label: Certified translation of a diploma or doctoral document
costs.note: From a sworn translator — 50–80 €/page.

costs.label: Apostille on academic documents (Russia)
costs.note: Arranged through the relevant authority; takes up to 45 days.

costs.label: Financial security
costs.note: Usually covered by salary or a grant under the Aufnahmevereinbarung; a Sperrkonto is not required.

title: ICT-Karte: intra-corporate transfer
tldr: ICT-Karte (§19 AufenthG, Intra-Corporate Transfer) — residence permit for transferring an employee within an international group from a unit outside the EU to a German unit. Categories: manager (Manager), specialist (Spezialist), graduate trainee (Trainee). Conditions: prior employment in the group of companies (usually at least 6 months; for a Trainee — a valid employment contract), the transfer is initiated by the receiving/parent company. Duration: up to 3 years (Manager/Spezialist), up to 1 year (Trainee). The Mobile-ICT-Karte allows you to work at units in other EU countries. Fees: D-visa 75 € + ICT-Karte from 100 €.

content.text: The ICT-Karte (Intra-Corporate Transfer, §19 AufenthG) is a residence permit for employees of international companies who are transferred from a unit outside the EU to a German unit of the same group. The card implements the European ICT Directive and is intended not for changing employers, but for an intra-corporate transfer within a single group of companies.

For employees of international corporations from Russia, Belarus and Ukraine, this is one of the most direct routes to Germany: you do not need to find a new employer — it is enough for the company to arrange a transfer to its German office.

items: Who: employees of international groups being transferred to a German unit
Three categories: Manager, Spezialist (specialist), Trainee (graduate trainee)
The transfer is initiated by the company, not the employee
Duration: up to 3 years (Manager/Spezialist), up to 1 year (Trainee)
Mobile-ICT-Karte — for working at units in other EU countries
This is not a route to changing employers: the status is tied to the group

content.text: An ICT-Karte usually requires prior employment within the group of companies immediately before the transfer (generally at least 6 months; for a Trainee a valid employment contract and a completed higher education are enough). Working conditions and pay in Germany must be no worse than those of comparable local workers.

items: A management position in the German unit
ICT-Karte duration: up to 3 years
Employment in the group: usually at least 6 months before the transfer
Specialist knowledge important for the unit
ICT-Karte duration: up to 3 years
Employment in the group: usually at least 6 months before the transfer
A university graduate undergoing training or rotation within the group
ICT-Karte duration: up to 1 year
A valid employment contract and a training plan are required

content.text: An ICT-Karte is not issued if your company is not part of the same group as the German unit, or if the transfer is in fact disguising an ordinary hire. It is also unsuitable if you are already in Germany on another status and merely want to change category — the ICT-Karte is designed precisely for entry as a transfer from outside the EU.

steps.title: Mobile-ICT and working across the EU

content.text: If you obtained an ICT permit in another EU country and carry out part of your work in Germany, you need a Mobile-ICT-Karte. It lets you work legally at the group's German unit while holding ICT status from another Union country. This is convenient for projects spanning several European offices.

items: Mobile-ICT-Karte — for ICT holders from another EU country working in Germany
Short-term mobility (up to 90 days within 180) is often handled by notification, without a separate card
Long-term mobility — a Mobile-ICT-Karte at the German ABH
Working conditions and pay — no worse than comparable local workers
Involvement of the Federal Employment Agency (BA) is required in standard cases

content.text: The application is usually prepared by the German unit and the parent company. The employee outside the EU applies for a national D-visa and, after arrival, obtains the ICT-Karte at the foreigners' authority (ABH). The card fee is from 100 €. In most cases the consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) is required, which is requested as part of the procedure.

items: The transfer is initiated by the company; a transfer letter and working conditions are prepared
The employee applies for a national D-visa at the diplomatic mission
After entry: residence registration (Anmeldung) and the ICT-Karte at the foreigners' authority (ABH) (fee from 100 €)
The consent of the BA is requested during the procedure
When the ICT ends, a switch to §18b / the EU Blue Card (Blue Card) is possible if hired by a German employer

content.text: The ICT-Karte has a hard ceiling on duration (up to 3 years for Manager/Spezialist) and is not extended beyond it in the same role. Time under the ICT-Karte generally counts less favourably towards the residence period for permanent residence than standard work statuses. If your goal is long-term residence, plan in advance to switch to §18b or the EU Blue Card (Blue Card EU) through a direct employment contract with a German company. Individual legal advice is recommended.

costs.label: National D-visa (ICT)
costs.note: Paid at the diplomatic mission when you apply; non-refundable if refused.

costs.label: Issue of the ICT-Karte / Mobile-ICT-Karte
costs.note: Paid at the Ausländerbehörde; the exact amount depends on the state and the duration.

costs.label: Certified translation of employment documents
costs.note: Employment contract, transfer letter, diploma — from a sworn translator.

costs.label: Relocation support (often paid by the employer)
costs.note: Relocation agencies and lawyers; in corporate groups usually at the company's expense.

title: Westbalkanregelung §26 BeschV
tldr: Westbalkanregelung (§26 Abs. 2 BeschV) — a special channel for citizens of six Western Balkan countries: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia. What makes it unique: ANY job is open (not only skilled work), provided you have a concrete offer and the consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit). There is an annual quota (about 50 000 permits), and the rule has been made permanent. You need: an offer, BA consent, an appointment at the diplomatic mission (often a long queue). Fees: D-visa 75 € + residence permit 100 €. It does not apply to citizens of Russia, Belarus and Ukraine.

content.text: The Westbalkanregelung is a special rule, §26 Abs. 2 BeschV, that opens up the German labour market to citizens of six Balkan countries for any job, not only skilled work. This is a rare exception: a work visa usually requires a recognised qualification, whereas here a firm job offer and the consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) are enough.

items: Who: citizens of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia
Unique: ANY job is allowed, not only skilled work
Basic condition: a concrete offer from a German employer
Mandatory: the consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit; Zustimmung)
Quota: about 50 000 permits per year
The rule has been made permanent (entfristet)

content.text: The Westbalkanregelung applies ONLY to citizens of the six Western Balkan countries listed. Citizens of Russia, Belarus and Ukraine do not fall under it — for them other channels apply (the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) §20a, §18a/§18b, the EU Blue Card (Blue Card EU)). This guide is useful for understanding the system and for those who hold Balkan citizenship.

The key elements are a concrete offer (verbindliches Arbeitsplatzangebot) from a German employer and the consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit). The BA checks that working conditions are no worse than those of comparable local workers and, in some cases, carries out a priority check for local workers (Vorrangprüfung). A recognised qualification is not required for this channel — this is the main difference from §18a/§18b.

items: A concrete offer (verbindliches Arbeitsplatzangebot) with a job description
The consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Zustimmung der Bundesagentur für Arbeit) — mandatory BA consent
Working conditions no worse than those of comparable local workers
A recognised qualification is not required
Shortly before applying you must not have received certain social benefits in Germany

steps.title: The quota and the application process

content.text: The channel is capped by an annual quota of about 50 000 permits (the quota was increased and the rule made permanent). In practice the bottleneck is the appointment for submission at the diplomatic mission: queues stretch out over months. The order is: get an offer → request BA consent → book an appointment and apply for a national D-visa.

items: A specific employer and position, conditions no worse than local
Unskilled work is allowed (construction, hospitality, logistics)

items.title: 2. Consent of the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit)

items: The BA checks the working conditions; a priority check for local workers (Vorrangprüfung) is possible
Accelerated procedure (beschleunigtes Fachkräfteverfahren) — via the employer
An appointment at the diplomatic mission — the main bottleneck (long queue)
Visa fee 75 €; the application counts towards the annual quota
After entry — a residence-permit card (residence permit) at the foreigners' authority (ABH)

content.text: Because of the quota and the queues, the process can take many months. Applications count towards the annual cap of about 50 000; once it is exhausted you will have to wait until the next year. Start with a solid offer and an official request for BA consent — "grey" arrangements will not get you a visa.

The Westbalkanregelung grants the right to work, but in itself it is not a status for settling immediately. After entry and Anmeldung you receive a residence permit tied to your employment. Once you have obtained a recognised qualification or moved to a skilled position, it makes sense to switch to §18a/§18b — these count better towards the residence period for a permanent residence permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) and give the family more rights.

items: After entry: residence registration (Anmeldung) and a residence-permit card (residence permit) at the foreigners' authority (ABH)
The residence permit is tied to employment — clear any change of employer with the foreigners' authority (ABH)
Recognition of your qualification (anabin — the database on the recognition of foreign diplomas / ZAB — the Central Office for Foreign Education) opens up a switch to §18a/§18b
A permanent residence permit — under the general rules after several years of employment
Family reunification is possible with sufficient income and housing

content.text: Because §26 BeschV permits unskilled employment, time under this status counts less favourably towards the residence period for permanent residence than under skilled work visas. For long-term plans, consider having your qualification recognised and switching to §18a/§18b at the first opportunity.

costs.label: National D-visa
costs.note: Paid at the diplomatic mission when you apply; non-refundable if refused.

costs.label: Issue of the residence-permit card after arrival
costs.note: Paid at the Ausländerbehörde after entry.

costs.label: Consent of the Bundesagentur für Arbeit
costs.note: The BA consent itself is free; the accelerated procedure via the employer carries a fee of ~411 €, usually paid by the employer.

costs.label: Certified translation of documents
costs.note: Employment contract and personal documents from a sworn translator.
