title: UK citizens after Brexit: status in Germany
tldr: After Brexit, the status of UK citizens in Germany is split into two groups. Those who were legally resident in Germany before the end of the transition period (31 December 2020) are protected by the Withdrawal Agreement: they keep rights close to freedom of movement and receive a special document — a residence document under Article 18(4) WA (Aufenthaltsdokument-GB; a declaratory system in Germany). These rights also extend to their family members. Those who come to Germany after 1 January 2021 are treated as third-country nationals (Drittstaatsangehörige): they no longer have freedom of movement and need a visa or residence permit under the general rules of the Residence Act (Aufenthaltsgesetz) — Blue Card §18g, skilled employment §18a/§18b, study §16b, etc. A nice detail: UK citizens (like citizens of the USA, Canada, Australia and a number of other countries) can enter Germany without a visa and apply for a residence permit on the spot, at the foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde), within the first 90 days. The fee for a residence permit or Blue Card is around 100€.

steps.title: Two groups of Britons: before and after 2021

content.text: Brexit split UK citizens in Germany into two fundamentally different categories. The cut-off is the end of the transition period, 31 December 2020. Those who were legally resident in Germany before this date are protected by the Withdrawal Agreement (WA). Those who arrive after 1 January 2021 are treated as third-country nationals (Drittstaatsangehöriger) under general migration law.

items: Residence before 31.12.2020 → Withdrawal Agreement protection → Aufenthaltsdokument-GB
Arrival from 01.01.2021 → third-country national status → visa or permit under AufenthG
EU freedom of movement for Britons has ended — new arrivals no longer have it
Family members of WA residents are also protected by the agreement

content.text: UK citizens who were legally resident in Germany before the end of 2020 keep the right to live and work, close to the former freedom of movement, on the basis of Article 18(4) of the Withdrawal Agreement. Germany applies a declaratory system: the rights exist regardless of the document, but to confirm them a special residence permit is issued — the Aufenthaltsdokument-GB. It is processed at the local foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde) and confirms the WA-protected status.

If you moved to Germany before 31.12.2020 but still have not obtained the Aufenthaltsdokument-GB, do it. Although the system is declaratory (the rights exist by virtue of residence), without the document it is extremely hard to prove your protected status when working, travelling and dealing with authorities.

Britons arriving from 2021 onward use the same channels as other third-country nationals under the Residence Act (Aufenthaltsgesetz). There is no freedom of movement — you need the appropriate residence permit matching the purpose of the stay.
For specialists with a university degree and a salary above the threshold; it offers a fast track to permanent residence and easier family reunification.
For people with vocational or university education, provided they have a job offer and recognition of their qualification.
Study, research and job-search routes — as for other third countries.

steps.title: Visa-free entry and applying on the spot

content.text: An important practical advantage: UK citizens (like those of the USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel) can enter Germany without a visa and apply for a residence permit while already in the country — at the local foreigners' authority (Ausländerbehörde), within the first 90 days of the stay. In other words, you do not have to arrange a D visa in London in advance: you can come, find a job or start studying, and apply for the permit on the spot. Nevertheless, you may not work until the permit is issued.

Visa-free entry lets you apply for a permit in Germany, but does not give you the right to start work before it is issued. Submit the application to the foreigners' authority within the 90 days, well before they run out, and do not start paid work until you have the permit.

costs.note: Issuing the document for WA-protected status; the fee is low or symbolic as part of implementing the WA.

costs.note: Not mandatory for Britons — you can apply on the spot, but sometimes it is more convenient in advance.

title: Anlage KAP: capital income
tldr: Anlage KAP is the attachment to the tax return for capital income: dividends, interest, gains from the sale of shares and funds. By default a bank in Germany itself withholds the flat tax at source on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% + the solidarity surcharge (Soli) of 5.5% + church tax (Kirchensteuer) where applicable (§32d EStG), and then you do not have to fill in Anlage KAP. It is worth filing it if you have not fully used the tax-free allowance for capital income (Sparerpauschbetrag; 1000€ per person, 2000€ per couple) across all banks, to check whether your personal rate is more favourable (Günstigerprüfung; if your personal rate is below 25%), or if you have foreign accounts and brokers where tax is not withheld automatically.

steps.title: What is taxed and whether you need Anlage KAP at all

content.text: Capital income (Kapitalerträge) under §20 EStG is taxed at a flat rate, the tax at source on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer), of 25%. On top of that comes the solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) of 5.5% of the tax and, if you are a church member, church tax (Kirchensteuer) of 8% (Bayern, Baden-Württemberg) or 9% (other states). The total burden is roughly 26.4–27.8%.

The main principle: a German bank or broker usually withholds the tax at source itself and transfers it to the tax office (Finanzamt). If you have only one German account and the tax has already been withheld, you are not legally required to declare your capital in Anlage KAP — the tax is considered paid (abgegolten, hence the name Abgeltungsteuer).

items: Dividends on German and foreign shares
Interest on deposits, Tagesgeld, Festgeld, bonds
Gains from the sale of shares, ETFs and funds (Aktiengewinne)
Distributions and the advance lump-sum income (Vorabpauschale) on investment funds
Income from crypto assets generally goes NOT in KAP but in Anlage SO (private transactions §23 EStG)

steps.title: When filing Anlage KAP is mandatory or worthwhile

content.text: It is worth filling in Anlage KAP in several situations. In some of them it is an obligation; in others, it is your chance to recover an overpayment.

items: The tax-free allowance for capital income (Sparerpauschbetrag) has not been fully used: the 1000€ (single) / 2000€ (joint return) was distributed between banks via an exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) sub-optimally, and somewhere tax was withheld unnecessarily

Check of the more favourable personal rate (Günstigerprüfung): your personal income tax rate is below 25% (low annual income, students, pensioners) — the tax office will recalculate the capital income at your rate if that is more favourable
Foreign accounts and brokers (for example, a foreign broker without a German tax agent): the tax is NOT withheld automatically — you have to declare the income yourself
Crediting of foreign tax at source (anrechenbare ausländische Quellensteuer) on dividends
Carrying over losses from the sale of shares (Verlustverrechnung), especially between different banks — the loss certificate (Verlustbescheinigung) must be requested from the bank by 15 December
Checking the correctness of the withheld church/solidarity surcharge

content.text: The tax-free allowance for capital income applies only if you have submitted an exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) to the bank in advance. Without an order the bank withholds tax from the first euro of interest, and you can recover it only via Anlage KAP in the annual return.

steps.title: How to fill it in: which lines and documents you need

content.text: From each German bank and broker, request the tax certificate (Steuerbescheinigung) for the tax year (often available in online banking in February–March). It already breaks the figures down line by line: capital income (Kapitalerträge), withheld tax on capital income (Kapitalertragsteuer), the solidarity surcharge (Soli), church tax (Kirchensteuer), the tax-free allowance used (Sparerpauschbetrag), losses and the credited tax at source (Quellensteuer).

items.title: 2. Transfer the amounts into Anlage KAP

items: The capital-income figures are transferred from the tax certificate almost one to one
Income without tax withheld (foreign accounts) is reported separately
Tick the box 'check of the more favourable rate' (Antrag auf Günstigerprüfung) if you want a recalculation at your personal rate — the tax office will apply it only if it is in your favour
To offset losses between banks, attach the loss certificate (Verlustbescheinigung)
To credit foreign tax, fill in the relevant lines for the creditable tax at source (anrechenbare Quellensteuer)

content.text: Anlage KAP can be filed for free via the tax authority's online portal ELSTER or via tax software (WISO, Taxfix), which fills in the lines itself by importing the tax certificate. The software is especially helpful with the check of the more favourable personal rate — it works out for you whether this is worthwhile.

costs.label: Filing Anlage KAP via ELSTER
costs.note: The official portal is free; only the tax software or an adviser may be paid.

costs.label: Possible savings via Günstigerprüfung / Sparerpauschbetrag
costs.note: Depends on the amount of capital and your personal rate; the point of filing is to recover an overpayment, not to pay extra.

title: Anlage Vorsorgeaufwand: insurance contributions
tldr: Anlage Vorsorgeaufwand is the attachment to the tax return where you claim insurance contributions as a deduction (§10 EStG): pension insurance (Rentenversicherung), health insurance (Krankenversicherung), long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung), unemployment insurance (Arbeitslosenversicherung), as well as personal liability insurance (Haftpflicht). Basic health and long-term care insurance (Basisabsicherung) is fully deductible. Contributions to retirement provision (Altersvorsorge) are deductible up to a cap — around 27 566€ per person in 2026 (double for a joint return). This is one of the largest deductions available to an employee.

content.text: Special deductible expenses (Sonderausgaben) under §10 EStG are personal expenses that the state allows you to deduct from your taxable income. Insurance contributions (Vorsorgeaufwendungen) fall into two groups: retirement provision (Altersvorsorge) and other contributions (sonstige Vorsorgeaufwendungen — health, care, liability, etc.).

items: Statutory pension insurance (gesetzliche Rentenversicherung) — mandatory retirement provision (Altersvorsorge)
The Rürup basic pension (Rürup-Rente, Basisrente) and comparable products — retirement provision
Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) — statutory or private
Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung)
Unemployment insurance (Arbeitslosenversicherung)
Personal liability insurance (Haftpflichtversicherung) — private liability cover

Occupational disability insurance (Berufsunfähigkeitsversicherung), accident insurance (Unfallversicherung), partly term life insurance (Risikolebensversicherung) — within the limit for other contributions (sonstige Vorsorge)

steps.title: How much is actually deductible in 2026

content.text: Since 2023, contributions to basic retirement provision are counted at 100% up to the maximum deduction. In 2026 the cap for retirement provision (Altersvorsorge) is roughly 27 566€ per person (double for jointly assessed spouses). The employer's share of pension insurance (Rentenversicherung) is also subtracted from this amount — tax software and ELSTER calculate this automatically.

items: Basic health insurance (Basisabsicherung KV) and long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) are fully deductible — this is the most valuable part for employees
Top-up health insurance for extra comfort (treatment by the head physician — Chefarzt, a single room, additional services — Zusatzleistungen) does NOT count as basic cover (Basisabsicherung)

Other insurance (personal liability — Haftpflicht, unemployment — Arbeitslosen, accident — Unfall) falls under a separate limit for other contributions (sonstige Vorsorge) — for employees this is often already used up by health insurance
Important for newcomers: contributions to mandatory German health insurance are fully deductible — this reduces your tax in the very first year

content.text: If basic health insurance and long-term care insurance (KV/PV) already exceed the limit for other contributions (sonstige Vorsorge), additional insurance (personal liability — Haftpflicht, accident — Unfall, etc.) will have practically no effect on the tax. This is not an error — that is how the §10 EStG mechanism works. Do not give up useful insurance just for the sake of a deduction.

steps.title: How to fill it in and where to get the figures

content.text: For an employee, most of the figures are already in the annual wage and tax statement (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung) from the employer: contributions to pension, health, long-term care and unemployment insurance (Renten-, Kranken-, Pflege- und Arbeitslosenversicherung) appear on separate lines. Some of the data is sent to the Finanzamt directly by the insurers (elektronische Übermittlung).

items: For private insurance, request the annual contribution certificate (Beitragsbescheinigung) from the insurer
Personal liability (Haftpflicht) — enter the annual contribution amount
For private health insurance (PKV) the insurer will separately state the basic-cover share (Basisabsicherung)
Rürup basic pension (Rürup/Basisrente) — the contribution certificate from the provider

content.text: In the tax authority's online portal ELSTER, many fields of Anlage Vorsorgeaufwand are pre-filled from the transmitted data (pre-filled return — vorausgefüllte Steuererklärung). Tax software fills them in automatically and itself allocates the amounts between retirement provision (Altersvorsorge) and other contributions (sonstige Vorsorge).

costs.label: Filing Anlage Vorsorgeaufwand via ELSTER
costs.note: Free; the contribution data is mostly already transmitted to the Finanzamt electronically.

costs.label: Tax software (optional)
costs.note: WISO Steuer around 36€, Taxfix around 40€; automatically allocates contributions by category.

title: Church tax (Kirchensteuer): how to leave the church
tldr: Church tax (Kirchensteuer) is 8% (Bayern, Baden-Württemberg) or 9% (other states) of your income tax on salary (Lohnsteuer). It is withheld automatically if German records list you as a member of a church (this often surfaces during residence registration — Anmeldung — or because of a baptism in another country). To stop paying, you have to officially leave the church (Kirchenaustritt) — via the civil registry office (Standesamt) or the local district court (Amtsgericht) at your place of residence; the fee is around 30€ (depends on the state). The tax usually stops from the month after you leave. The act of leaving itself does not affect your migration or tax status.

steps.title: Why Kirchensteuer is being withheld from you at all

content.text: In Germany the state collects church tax for recognised religious communities (above all the Catholic and Protestant churches). If you are officially listed as a member of such a church, the tax is calculated as 8% (Bayern, Baden-Württemberg) or 9% (all other states) of your income tax — not of your income, but specifically of your income tax on salary (Lohnsteuer/Einkommensteuer).

items: During residence registration (Anmeldung) the form often has a field for religion (Religionszugehörigkeit)
If you stated a Catholic/Protestant denomination, you are registered as a member and the withholding is switched on
The tax is withheld by the employer together with the income tax on salary (Lohnsteuer) and is visible on the payslip (the KiSt / Kirchensteuer line)
For high earners this easily runs to hundreds of euros a year
Many newcomers only learn about the tax from their first payslip

content.text: A membership record can appear even if you were baptised long ago in another country — the data is sometimes matched during registration. If there is a Kirchensteuer line on your payslip but you do not consider yourself a church member, this can be stopped only by officially leaving the church (Kirchenaustritt).

Leaving the church is a civil administrative procedure, not a religious one. You do it in person at the civil registry office (Standesamt) or the local district court (Amtsgericht) — which body is responsible depends on the state. The declaration is filed at your place of residence.

items.title: 1. Find the right office and book an appointment

content.text: On your city's website, find the page about leaving the church (Kirchenaustritt). In most states this is the civil registry office (Standesamt), in some it is the local district court (Amtsgericht). An appointment (Termin) is often required in advance. Check whether an appointment is needed and what documents to bring.

items: A valid passport or national ID card (Personalausweis)
Registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) / proof of address (may be requested)
If available — a baptism certificate (usually not required)
Money for the fee — around 30€ (the exact amount depends on the state; in some states, for example Bremen, it is free)

content.text: You declare your departure in person (declaration of leaving the church — Kirchenaustrittserklärung), pay the fee and receive confirmation (certificate of departure — Austrittsbescheinigung). Keep this document — it proves the date of leaving.

steps.title: When the withholding stops and what else to consider

content.text: Withholding of church tax usually stops from the next calendar month after you complete your departure (the exact rules and the transition month depend on the state). The office transmits the information to the register, and the employer stops withholding the tax. If too much was withheld during the transition period, this is corrected in the annual return.

items: Keep the certificate of departure (Austrittsbescheinigung) — it will be useful if the line on your payslip does not disappear in time
Check your next payslip: the Kirchensteuer line should drop to zero
Leaving also stops the withholding of church tax on capital income at the bank
Leaving the church does not affect your residence permit, citizenship, tax residency or social insurance
Consider the personal consequences of membership (church rites, working in church organisations) — that is no longer a tax matter

content.text: Leaving only takes effect going forward. Tax withheld before the date of leaving the church (Kirchenaustritt) is not refunded. The sooner you complete your departure, the less is withheld for the current year.

costs.label: Fee for the Kirchenaustritt
costs.note: Around 30€ in most states; depends on the Land (free in some states).

costs.label: Savings on Kirchensteuer after leaving
costs.note: 8–9% of your income tax each year — for middle and high incomes this is hundreds of euros a year.

sources.title: Berlin.de — Kirchenaustritt (example of a city page and the fee)

title: Freelancer taxes: quarterly payments
tldr: A freelancer or self-employed person in Germany does not pay tax as a single lump sum at the end of the year, but in advance instalments throughout the year. Advance payments on income tax (Einkommensteuer-Vorauszahlungen, §37 EStG) are quarterly advances (due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September, 10 December) that the tax office (Finanzamt) sets after estimating your income. In parallel runs the advance VAT return (Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung) — reporting and paying VAT, monthly or quarterly depending on turnover. Set aside tax from every payment received, do not spend the gross amount as if it were net income.

steps.title: Two streams of payments: income tax and VAT

content.text: For a freelancer in Germany, taxes run in two independent streams. Do not confuse them: these are different taxes, different deadlines and different forms. Many beginners spend the whole fee they receive, forgetting that part of it is VAT and future income tax that they will have to hand over to the state.

items: Income tax (Einkommensteuer) on your profit (income minus expenses) is paid in advance instalments quarterly
Value-added tax (Umsatzsteuer, USt / VAT) — the tax you add to clients' invoices and transfer to the tax office (Finanzamt)
Income tax depends on profit; VAT depends on turnover
If you are a small business under the special regime (Kleinunternehmer, §19 UStG), you do not charge VAT — but you still pay income tax
The solidarity surcharge (Soli) is only paid by freelancers with high incomes (see the separate guide on Soli)

content.text: Under §37 EStG the tax office sets advance payments on income tax based on the expected profit (usually from the previous return). You receive a notice of advance payments (Vorauszahlungsbescheid) with the amounts. The payments fall due four times a year.

items: Deadlines for the quarterly advances: 10 March, 10 June, 10 September, 10 December
The amount is set by the tax office in the notice of advance payments on the basis of an income estimate
In your first year of work there may be no advances — the tax is assessed on your first return, and then a large back-payment for the previous year plus the new advances can fall due at once
If your income has dropped, you can apply to reduce the advances (Antrag auf Anpassung der Vorauszahlungen)
If your income has risen, it is sensible to ask to raise the advances in advance, so as not to get a big bill at the end

content.text: The classic first-year trap: the assessment comes later, and the tax office at the same time demands a back-payment for the previous year AND the first advances for the current one. This can be a double burden in a single quarter. Keep a tax reserve from the very start.

If you are not a small business (Kleinunternehmer), you regularly file an advance VAT return (Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung) via the tax authority's online portal ELSTER: you declare the VAT collected from clients, deduct the input VAT paid to suppliers (Vorsteuer), and transfer the difference. The frequency depends on the amount of VAT in the previous year.

items: New entrepreneurs often report monthly in the first years
With moderate VAT they later move to quarterly reporting
With very small amounts the tax office may exempt you from the advance return (Voranmeldung)
The filing and payment deadline is usually by the 10th after the period (with the option of a permanent extension — Dauerfristverlängerung — by one month)

content.text: The advance return is filed electronically via ELSTER (or accounting software with an ELSTER interface). At the end of the year you also file an annual VAT return (Umsatzsteuererklärung), which reconciles all the advance reports.

items.title: 3. Set aside tax from every payment received

content.text: A freelancer's survival habit: from every payment you receive, immediately set aside the VAT (it does not belong to you) and a reserve for income tax in a separate account. Then the quarterly deadlines will not become a problem.

costs.label: Filing via ELSTER
costs.note: Vorauszahlungen and Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung are filed and paid without a separate fee.

costs.label: Late payment / report
costs.note: Verspätungszuschlag — 0.25% per month of the tax, a minimum of around 25€ per month; plus late-payment surcharges, Säumniszuschläge.

costs.label: Accountant / Steuerberater (optional)
costs.note: Depends on the volume; many freelancers do the USt-Voranmeldung themselves in software.

sources.title: Bundesministerium der Finanzen — Steuern für Selbstständige

title: Soli: who still pays in 2026
tldr: The solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag, Soli) is 5.5% of income tax. Since 2021 it has effectively been abolished for the vast majority: thanks to a high threshold (Freigrenze), it is only paid by roughly the top ~10% of earners. For single people in 2026 the surcharge starts when income tax on salary (Lohnsteuer) exceeds around 19 950€ a year (roughly an income of about 73 000€ and up), for couples it is twice as much. An important exception: on capital income (Kapitalerträge) the surcharge is always withheld together with the tax at source on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer), regardless of your total income.

steps.title: What Soli is and why it was almost abolished

content.text: The solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) was historically introduced to finance German reunification. It is 5.5% not of income but of the amount of your income tax (Lohnsteuer/Einkommensteuer). The legal basis is the Solidaritätszuschlaggesetz 1995 (SolzG).

Since 2021 a reform raised the threshold (Freigrenze) so that for most taxpayers the surcharge has dropped to zero. By most estimates, it is still paid only by roughly the top 10% of earners. If you are an employee on an average salary, the Soli line on your payslip is most likely zero.

items: Single people: the surcharge starts when the annual income tax exceeds the threshold (Freigrenze) of around 19 950€ (that is roughly an income from ~73 000€ and up — it depends on deductions)
Joint return (Zusammenveranlagung): the threshold is roughly twice as high
Above the threshold there is a gradual phase-in zone (Milderungszone), then the full 5.5%
Capital income: on the tax at source on capital income (Abgeltungsteuer) the surcharge is ALWAYS withheld, regardless of total income
Corporate tax (Körperschaftsteuer) at a limited liability company (GmbH) is also subject to the surcharge with no relief threshold

content.text: The main exception: on capital income the surcharge always applies. Even if your Soli on salary is zero, the bank still withholds the 5.5% surcharge on dividends and interest together with the 25% tax at source (Abgeltungsteuer). There is no separate threshold (Freigrenze) for capital.

steps.title: How to check and what to do

content.text: Check your payslip and your tax assessment. The Solidaritätszuschlag line will show whether you pay it at all. For most employees it will be zero — this is normal and fully in line with the law, so no separate action is needed.

items: An employee on an average salary — the Soli on salary is almost certainly 0, nothing needs to be done

High income — the surcharge is calculated automatically by the employer and the tax office (Finanzamt); you can reduce it only by reducing your taxable income (deductions, insurance contributions — Vorsorge)

You have capital — note that the surcharge on dividends/interest is still deducted; you can recover it at a low rate via the check of the more favourable personal rate (Günstigerprüfung) in Anlage KAP
Doubts about the amount — check your tax assessment (Steuerbescheid); errors in calculating the surcharge are rare but possible

costs.label: Soli for most employees
costs.note: After the 2021 reform the surcharge is zero for roughly 90% of taxpayers.

costs.label: Soli for high incomes and capital
costs.note: 5.5% of income tax above the Freigrenze; on capital income — always 5.5% of the Abgeltungsteuer.

title: Tax return deadlines 2026
tldr: For the 2025 tax year, the return must be filed by 31 July 2026 if you do it yourself. If a tax adviser (Steuerberater) or an income-tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein) prepares the return, the deadline is extended to around the end of April 2027 (check the exact date for the year 2025 — after the COVID-era extensions the deadlines are normalising). If you file voluntarily (return on application — Antragsveranlagung, usually for a refund), you have much more time — up to 4 years afterwards. Missing the deadline for a mandatory return risks a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag): 0.25% of the tax per month, a minimum of around 25€ per month.

steps.title: First understand: mandatory or voluntary return

content.text: The deadline depends on whether you are required to file a return (mandatory return — Pflichtveranlagung) or are filing voluntarily for a refund (return on application — Antragsveranlagung). This determines both the deadline and the risk of a penalty.

items: You are required to file if you had the tax-class combination III/V or IV with a factor, income without tax withheld over 410€ (side income — Nebeneinkünfte), parallel employers (class VI), wage-replacement benefits (Lohnersatzleistungen — parental, sickness, unemployment benefit — Eltern-, Kranken-, Arbeitslosengeld) above the threshold, freelance/business income, etc.
You file voluntarily if you usually have a single employer and tax class I/IV with no special cases — the return most often results in a refund
If in doubt — assume that the return is mandatory, so as not to miss the deadline
Self-filing (mandatory) for 2025 — by 31 July 2026

With the help of a tax adviser (Steuerberater) / income-tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein) — extension to around the end of April 2027 (check the exact date for the year 2025 with your adviser/in the source)
Voluntary return (return on application — Antragsveranlagung) — up to 4 years back, i.e. for 2025 roughly until the end of 2029
If 31 July is a non-working day, the deadline shifts to the next working day

content.text: After the pandemic-era extensions, the deadlines are gradually returning to the standard 31 July for self-filers. To be safe, always check the final date for the specific year in a current source from the Federal Ministry of Finance (BMF) or on the tax authority's portal ELSTER before filing.

Do not confuse them: the voluntary return has 4 years in reserve, but the mandatory one has a hard deadline of 31 July of the following year. If you are required to file and miss the date, a late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag) is charged, even if you are ultimately due a refund.

steps.title: Lateness, penalties and how to get an extension

content.text: The late-filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag) for a mandatory return is 0.25% of the assessed tax for each month started of lateness, a minimum of around 25€ per month. With a large tax bill and a long delay, the amount grows. In addition, interest and late-payment surcharges (Säumniszuschläge) are possible if the tax itself is not paid.

items.title: 2. How to ask for an extension

items: Before the deadline expires, submit to the tax office (Finanzamt) an application for an extension (Antrag auf Fristverlängerung) with a justification

The most reliable way to stretch the deadline is to entrust the return to a tax adviser (Steuerberater) or an income-tax assistance association (Lohnsteuerhilfeverein): the extended deadline then applies automatically
Do not go quiet after the deadline — it is better to contact the tax office than to ignore the problem

items.title: 3. Better to file early via ELSTER/software

content.text: Filing via the tax authority's online portal ELSTER is free, and tax software (WISO, Taxfix) speeds up the filling-in and checks for errors. If you are expecting a refund — file as early as possible, the money will come back sooner.

costs.label: Filing via ELSTER
costs.note: The official portal is free.

costs.label: Verspätungszuschlag for lateness
costs.note: 0.25% of the tax for each month started, a minimum of around 25€ per month.

costs.label: Steuerberater (for the extended deadline)
costs.note: More expensive than self-filing, but gives an automatic extension of the deadline.

sources.title: Bundesministerium der Finanzen — Abgabefristen der Steuererklärung

title: Tax software: WISO, Taxfix, ELSTER
tldr: You can file a return in Germany in three ways. ELSTER is the official portal of the tax office (Finanzamt), completely free, but with no prompts or explanations: it suits those who already understand the forms. WISO Steuer (around 36€) is the best balance of price, features and prompts, supports data import and complex cases (capital, freelancer). Taxfix (around 40€ or a percentage of the refund) is a question-and-answer app, as simple as possible for a typical salary, but weaker for complex situations. For most newcomers earning a salary, WISO or Taxfix pay for themselves through the refund.

steps.title: Three options and who each suits

content.text: Any method ultimately sends the data through the interface of the tax authority's portal ELSTER to your tax office (Finanzamt) — the difference is in convenience, prompts and price. The choice depends on how complex your situation is and on how willing you are to get to grips with German terms.

items: ELSTER — free, official, but with no explanations or optimisation: for confident users
WISO Steuer — around 36€, the best price/features ratio, prompts and error checking
Taxfix — around 40€ (or a % of the refund), interview format, the simplest for a typical salary
Smartsteuer and other online services — alternatives in a similar price range
Price: 0€
Pros: the official portal, pre-filled return (vorausgefüllte Steuererklärung — pre-filling from employer and insurer data), no intermediary
Cons: the interface is dry, no prompts on what to deduct, easy to miss deductions, terms only in German
For whom: those who already understand Anlage N, KAP, Vorsorge and do not want to pay for software
Price: around 36€ (desktop/online/app)
Pros: guides you step by step with prompts, looks for missed deductions, data import, handles complex cases (capital, freelancer, rental), compares with the previous year
Cons: the interface is dense, German language, a one-off purchase for the year
For whom: most people — the best price/features ratio
Price: around 40€ per filing (or a model with a percentage of the refund)
Pros: question-and-answer format, very beginner-friendly, mobile app, partly more accessible by language
Cons: more expensive than WISO, weaker for complex cases (large capital, business), less fine-tuning
For whom: those with a simple situation (one salary) who want minimum effort

steps.title: What to choose and what to watch out for

content.text: Practical takeaway: if your situation is simple and ease matters most — Taxfix; if you want the best price/features ratio and are not put off by a dense interface — WISO Steuer; if you understand the forms confidently and do not want to pay — ELSTER. The cost of the software (around 36–40€) usually deducts itself as tax-advice expenses (Steuerberatungskosten) in the next return, for the part relating to income.

items: Complex income (capital on several accounts, freelancing, rental, foreign income) — go with WISO or an adviser
Only salary and standard deductions — Taxfix or WISO will both handle it equally well
You want 0€ and are ready to figure it out — ELSTER
Check the current price before buying — versions are released every year for a specific tax year

content.text: ELSTER being free is deceptive if, for lack of guidance, you miss deductions worth hundreds of euros. For most newcomers, paid software pays for itself through the refund in the very first year.

costs.label: ELSTER
costs.note: The official free portal of the Finanzamt.

costs.label: WISO Steuer
costs.note: Approximate price for the version for one tax year; the best price/features ratio.

costs.label: Taxfix
costs.note: Around 40€ per filing or a model with a percentage of the refund; question-and-answer format.

sources.title: ELSTER — official portal of the Finanzverwaltung

title: Work-related expenses (Werbungskosten): what to deduct
tldr: Work-related expenses (Werbungskosten, §9 EStG) reduce an employee's taxable income. The tax office (Finanzamt) automatically deducts the standard allowance for employees (Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag) of 1230€ a year without any receipts. Itemising specific expenses only makes sense if together they exceed 1230€. The main items: the commuting allowance (Pendlerpauschale), home office (Homeoffice-Pauschale), work equipment (Arbeitsmittel), professional development (Fortbildung), job-application costs (Bewerbungskosten), work clothing, a work-related move and a second household (doppelte Haushaltsführung).

content.text: Work-related expenses (Werbungskosten) under §9 EStG are an employee's professional expenses. The state automatically grants the standard allowance for employees (Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag) of 1230€ a year: this amount is deducted from income with no receipts and no claim. Collecting and claiming specific expenses only makes sense if their total for the year exceeds 1230€.

items: Up to 1230€ — you do not need to prove anything, the allowance is already counted
Above 1230€ — claim the actual expenses (individual proof — Einzelnachweis) in Anlage N with supporting documents
Add up all the items together — often it is the commute to work that pushes you over the threshold
Keep receipts and supporting documents all year, even if you are not sure you will exceed the threshold

content.text: The most common and largest item. The distance from home to work one way is counted (the distance allowance — Entfernungspauschale), for each working day, regardless of the means of transport. For long commutes, this alone easily adds up to more than 1230€ a year.

items: The home office allowance (Homeoffice-Pauschale) — for days working from home (check the current daily rate and annual cap for the current year)
Work equipment (Arbeitsmittel) — laptop, monitor, desk, professional literature, software (expensive items are written off over time through depreciation)
Phone/internet — the work-related share of the costs

items.title: Training, job search, work clothing and moving

items: Professional development (Fortbildung) — courses, seminars in your current profession
Job-application costs (Bewerbungskosten) — applications, photos, travel to interviews
Work clothing (Berufskleidung) — typical work/protective clothing (not ordinary clothes)
A move for work reasons (Umzug aus beruflichem Anlass) — a work-related relocation
A second household (doppelte Haushaltsführung) — a second home near the workplace while keeping the main home
Contributions to professional associations and a trade union (Beiträge zu Berufsverbänden / Gewerkschaft) — membership fees of trade unions and professional associations

steps.title: How to claim and not miss anything

content.text: All work-related expenses are claimed in Anlage N (for employees). In the tax authority's online portal ELSTER you have to enter the amounts manually; tax software (WISO, Taxfix) walks you through the categories and points out the ones many people forget.

items: Set up a folder (paper or digital) and put receipts in it throughout the year
Multiply the commuting allowance (Pendlerpauschale) × working days — often this is already more than 1230€
Do not throw supporting documents away straight away — the tax office may request them on a spot-check basis
Split partly personal expenses (phone, internet, laptop) into a work and a personal share
If the expenses are less than 1230€ — just rely on the automatic allowance (Pauschbetrag), there is no need to claim anything

content.text: Work-related expenses reduce your taxable income, not the tax itself directly — the real benefit equals your marginal rate applied to the claimed amount. And remember: claiming only makes sense above 1230€, otherwise you are merely repeating what the tax office has already counted as a flat allowance.

costs.label: Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag (automatic)
costs.note: Deducted with no receipts; it is only worth claiming actual expenses above this amount.

costs.label: Filing via ELSTER
costs.note: Anlage N is filed for free via the official portal.

costs.label: Tax software (optional)
costs.note: WISO around 36€, Taxfix around 40€; helps you not miss deductions.

sources.title: ELSTER — Anlage N (Einkünfte aus nichtselbständiger Arbeit)
Bundesministerium der Finanzen — Werbungskosten und Pauschbeträge

title: Income for citizenship: without basic income support (Bürgergeld)
tldr: §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StAG requires that you support yourself and your dependants without relying on basic income support (Bürgergeld, SGB II) or social assistance (Sozialhilfe, SGB XII). The StAG reform of 27.06.2024 sharply tightened this rule: the former broad exceptions for people not at fault for receiving benefits have been almost entirely abolished — now even a partial top-up to a low income (aufstockendes Bürgergeld) while working full-time blocks naturalisation, except in narrow cases of severe hardship (Härtefall) and for special groups (the guest-worker generation — Gastarbeiter, workers with childcare duties). Both your current and your projected ability to support your family count: salary, self-employment, pension, spouse's income. A housing benefit (Wohngeld), child benefit (Kindergeld) or BAföG does NOT block it — these are not social benefits (Sozialleistungen) within the meaning of §10. Evidence: payslips (Lohnabrechnungen) for 3–12 months, a tax assessment (Steuerbescheid), an employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag), and for the self-employed — a business activity report (BWA) and a certificate from a tax advisor (Steuerberater-Bescheinigung).

content.text: The condition in §10 Abs. 1 Satz 1 Nr. 3 StAG reads as follows: you must be able to support yourself and the family members who are dependent on you (unterhaltsberechtigte Familienangehörige) without relying on payments under SGB II (basic income support, Bürgergeld) or SGB XII (social assistance, Sozialhilfe). The authority (Behörde) assesses not only the present moment but also the outlook — whether your financial situation is stable.

The reform — the Act on the Modernisation of Citizenship Law (Gesetz zur Modernisierung des Staatsangehörigkeitsrechts), which came into force on 27 June 2024 — deliberately tightened this rule. Before the reform, §10 Abs. 1 Satz 3 StAG (old version) exempted from the requirement anyone who received benefits nicht zu vertreten — through no fault of their own (for example, a job-seeker acting in good faith). The reform almost entirely removed this general clause: now, under the new version of §10 Abs. 1 Satz 3 StAG, exceptions exist only for a strictly defined list of groups.

items: Blocks naturalisation: basic income support (Bürgergeld, SGB II), social assistance / basic subsistence support (Sozialhilfe / Grundsicherung, SGB XII)

Does NOT block: child benefit (Kindergeld), parental allowance (Elterngeld), housing benefit (Wohngeld), BAföG, short-time work allowance (Kurzarbeitergeld), unemployment benefit ALG I (insurance-based, not SGB II)
Counts as income: net/gross salary (netto/brutto), self-employment, pension, spouse's income, maintenance payments
Community of need (Bedarfsgemeinschaft): if even one family member receives basic income support (Bürgergeld), this usually blocks the whole application (Antrag)
The outlook must be positive: temporary work for 3 months is not enough

steps.title: Why the 2024 reform made the rule stricter

content.text: The paradox of the 2024 reform: it cut the required residence period from 8 to 5 years and allowed dual citizenship, yet the income requirement itself became stricter. The legislator stated explicitly that, as a general rule, naturalisation is not possible while you are receiving SGB II/XII payments, and narrowed the range of exceptions — so as to tie naturalisation to the applicant's own contribution.

This is especially painful for those who work full-time but, because of a low salary and a large family, receive a top-up to basic income support (aufstockendes Bürgergeld) from the job centre (Jobcenter). Previously, such people often qualified under the "through no fault of their own" clause. After 27.06.2024 even this top-up generally blocks naturalisation — except for the narrow exceptions below. Check the current practice of your naturalisation authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde).

items: Remaining exceptions under §10 Abs. 1 Satz 3 StAG (new version):
The guest-worker generation (Gastarbeiter) — those who came under inter-state labour recruitment agreements before 1974 (West Germany) or contract workers of the GDR
Their spouses who joined them
Persons working full-time (Vollzeit) for at least 20 of the last 24 months
The spouse of such a worker, where they live together and there is a minor child in the community of need (Bedarfsgemeinschaft)
Hardship case (Härtefall) — a separate individual clause for severe life situations

content.text: The authority wants to see that your income is stable and covers the assessed needs of your family (the standard need — Regelbedarf, under SGB II plus housing costs). For an employee, the key documents are an open-ended employment contract (or one with a long term) and payslips. For a self-employed person — proof of profit over a full year.

items: Employees: payslips (Lohn-/Gehaltsabrechnungen) for the last 3–12 months
Employees: a valid employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag; an open-ended one — unbefristet — is valued more highly)
Everyone: the latest income tax assessment (Einkommensteuerbescheid) from the tax office (Finanzamt)
Self-employed: a business activity report (BWA, betriebswirtschaftliche Auswertung) + a certificate (Bescheinigung) from a tax advisor (Steuerberater) on profit (Gewinn)
Self-employed: business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) or proof of liberal-profession status (Freiberufler-Nachweis)
Pensioners: a pension notice (Rentenbescheid) from the German pension fund (Deutsche Rentenversicherung)
Proof that you do NOT receive SGB II/XII payments: a certificate from the job centre (Jobcenter) confirming their absence (Negativbescheinigung), if requested
Housing: a tenancy agreement (Mietvertrag) + proof of payment, to assess living costs

content.text: If your income is borderline, do the maths yourself: take the standard need (Regelbedarf) of your community of need (Bedarfsgemeinschaft; a single adult in 2026 — about 563€/month of the basic rate — Regelsatz) plus your actual rent including utilities (Warmmiete). If your family's net income (netto) is above that sum, you are outside the SGB II zone, even if you never actually claimed benefits. The authority looks precisely at the hypothetical entitlement (Anspruch).

steps.title: What to do if your income is borderline

content.text: If you receive a top-up to basic income support (aufstockendes Bürgergeld), or your income fluctuates around the threshold, do not apply and hope for the best — strengthen your position first. A few months of stable full-time employment often settle the matter, and for the groups in §10 Abs. 1 Satz 3 StAG (full-time — Vollzeit — 20 of 24 months) the reform explicitly left a path open.

items: Check whether you fall under the "full-time (Vollzeit) 20 of 24 months" exception
Increase your hours to full-time (Vollzeit) if you work part-time (Teilzeit) — this both removes the top-up and opens the exception
Gather payslips (Lohnabrechnungen) for a continuous period without basic income support (Bürgergeld) before applying
Take your spouse's income into account: the combined income of the community of need (Bedarfsgemeinschaft) may cover the need
In a severe life situation, ask for a hardship case (Härtefall; a separate clause) to be considered
A consultation at a migration advice service (Migrationsberatung) before applying saves months of waiting and a rejection

content.text: A rejection under §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 is not for life: you can reapply once your income stabilises. But reapplying means a new fee and a new queue. It is better to apply once, already having a stable income and evidence covering a sufficient period.

costs.label: Einbürgerung (adult)
costs.note: State fee for the naturalisation of an adult under §38 Abs. 2 StAG; it does not depend on the level of income and is paid upon a positive decision.

costs.label: Bescheinigung Steuerberater (self-employed)
costs.note: Proof of profit/BWA for the Einbürgerungsbehörde, if there is no annual Steuerbescheid.

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung of income documents from abroad
costs.note: Per page; needed if part of your income or pension comes from your country of origin.

title: Processing times for naturalisation (Einbürgerung)
tldr: The law sets no official deadline for processing a naturalisation application, but §75 VwGO gives a benchmark: after 3 months of inaction by the authority (Behörde) without good reason, you are entitled to file an action for failure to act (Untätigkeitsklage) at the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht). In practice, times range from 6 to 24+ months and vary sharply by federal state (Bundesland) and city: Berlin is notorious for queues of 2–3 years, while small districts decide within half a year. The 2024 reform triggered a surge in applications, which lengthened the queues. Digital portals (for example, the berlin.de Einbürgerungsportal, bund.de) speed up intake, but not the decision itself. You can speed things up with a complete, flawless package, a status request (Sachstandsanfrage) every 2–3 months, and, if it drags on, an action for failure to act (Untätigkeitsklage; a court fee, a chance to force the authority to decide).

steps.title: Real timelines by state and city

content.text: The StAG names no maximum processing time. Everything depends on the workload of the specific naturalisation authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) and on how complete your package is. After the reform of 27.06.2024, the number of applications rose noticeably: the 5-year period and permitted dual citizenship expanded the pool of those entitled to naturalisation, so queues in large cities have lengthened.

items: Average range nationwide: 6–24 months
Berlin (the immigration authority — LEA / the naturalisation authority): historically 2–3 years, partly relieved via the digital portal
Hamburg, Munich, Cologne: 12–24 months
Small Landkreise: sometimes 4–8 months
The clock often starts not from submission but from the moment the package is deemed complete (vollständig)
An incomplete package is the main cause of delays: one missing translation pushes the case back by months

content.text: In 2023–2024 Berlin launched a digital naturalisation portal (Einbürgerungsportal) and a centralised state naturalisation centre (Landeseinbürgerungszentrum) to relieve the district citizens' offices (Bürgerämter). Submission has become faster and more transparent (you can see the status online), but the decision itself can still take more than a year in complex cases.

items: Submit a perfectly complete package: one missing document means months of idle time
Have all foreign records ready in advance with an apostille (Apostille) and a certified translation (beglaubigte Übersetzung)
Pass B1 and the naturalisation test (Einbürgerungstest) BEFORE applying and attach the certificates right away
Every 2–3 months, send a written status request (Sachstandsanfrage) quoting your case number
Keep the confirmation of receipt of documents (Eingangsbestätigung) — it records the date the count starts
Respond to the authority's requests within the set deadline, otherwise the case goes to the back of the queue
Via the digital portal (where available), the status and documents are visible without a visit

content.text: Do not pay intermediaries who promise to jump the queue — there is no lawful "paid fast-tracking" in naturalisation. The only real lever when it drags on is an action for failure to act (Untätigkeitsklage; see below).

steps.title: Action for failure to act (Untätigkeitsklage) — against the authority's inaction

content.text: If the authority stays silent for longer than a reasonable period, §75 VwGO (the Administrative Court Procedure Code — Verwaltungsgerichtsordnung) lets you file an action for failure to act (Untätigkeitsklage) at the administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht). The rule: at least 3 months after submitting the application with no decision and no good reason for the delay. The aim of the action is not to win citizenship immediately, but to compel the authority to make a decision.

items: §75 VwGO: an action is possible if über den Antrag ohne zureichenden Grund nicht entschieden
The minimum benchmark is 3 months of inaction, but in naturalisation cases courts often wait for a real delay (a year or more)
It is filed at the administrative court for your place of residence
The court may stay the case (aussetzen) for a reasonable period, giving the authority time to decide
Often the mere fact of the action prompts the authority to take up the case
If you win, the authority partly reimburses your costs (court costs — Gerichtskosten — plus a lawyer's fee if one is involved)

content.text: An action for failure to act can technically be filed without a lawyer (representation is not mandatory at first instance before the administrative court), but a lawyer specialising in migration law (Migrationsrecht) improves your chances and frames the claim correctly. Before filing, be sure to send a written reminder / status request (Mahnung/Sachstandsanfrage) — it is proof that you gave the authority a chance.

The speed depends not only on the authority (Behörde) but also on the complexity of your particular case. Simple cases (a single applicant, an EU country of origin, a clean package) move faster than cases with children, foreign records and checks across several authorities.

items: The completeness of the package at submission — the number-one factor
The number of family members in the application: each child adds checks
The need for enquiries to other authorities (the office for the protection of the constitution — Verfassungsschutz, the police — Polizei) lengthens the timeline
A complex residence history (changes of status, gaps) requires additional checks
The workload of the specific authority and the wave of applications after the 2024 reform
Timely responses to the authority's requests keep the case from sliding to the back of the queue

content.text: Do not quit your job or change your residence status during processing without need: any change of circumstances (income, address, marital status) forces the authority to re-check the conditions of §10 StAG and resets the progress on your case.

costs.label: Gerichtskosten Untätigkeitsklage
costs.note: Depends on the Streitwert (for naturalisation usually a fixed Auffangstreitwert of ~5000€); reimbursed by the Behörde if you win.

costs.label: Anwalt Migrationsrecht (optional)
costs.note: Fee under the RVG for handling an Untätigkeitsklage; costs may be reimbursed if you win.

costs.label: Sachstandsanfrage / correspondence
costs.note: Free by e-mail or via the portal; a registered postal letter costs a couple of euros.

title: The full document package for citizenship
tldr: The full package for standard naturalisation under §10 StAG includes: a passport, a valid residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel), a B1 certificate (or equivalent), a naturalisation test certificate (Einbürgerungstest), proof of income (payslips — Lohnabrechnungen / tax assessment — Steuerbescheid / employment contract — Arbeitsvertrag), a pension insurance statement (Rentenversicherung), a tenancy agreement (Mietvertrag), birth and marriage certificates (with an apostille — Apostille — and a certified translation — beglaubigte Übersetzung), a biometric photo, a CV (résumé — Lebenslauf) and a declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung; written, as part of the commitment — Bekenntnis — under §10 Abs. 1 Satz 1 Nr. 1 StAG — expanded by the 2024 reform). Foreign civil-status records almost always require legalisation/apostille and a sworn translation. One missing or untranslated document is the main cause of delays of months. Gather everything BEFORE booking your submission appointment.

steps.title: The core package: what everyone needs

content.text: Your naturalisation authority (Einbürgerungsbehörde) issues the exact list (it varies slightly by state), but the core is the same across Germany and rests on the conditions of §10 Abs. 1 StAG. Prepare originals plus copies; biometric records — with an apostille (Apostille) and a sworn translation.

items: A completed naturalisation application (Einbürgerungsantrag; your authority's — Behörde — form / online portal)
A valid national passport (Reisepass) + a copy of all pages with stamps
A valid residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel): a settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis), EU long-term residence (Daueraufenthalt-EU) or a suitable temporary residence permit (AE; eAT card)
A German B1 certificate (Zertifikat Deutsch / telc / Goethe / DTZ B1)
A naturalisation test certificate (a pass certificate — Bestehensbescheinigung, 17+ out of 33)
Aktuelle biometrische Passfotos (35×45 mm)
A registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) / proof of residence (Aufenthaltsnachweis) for 5 years of residence (the standard period under §10 StAG)

A declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung) — part of the commitment (Bekenntnis) under §10 Abs. 1 Satz 1 Nr. 1 StAG (signed in person; the written form was enshrined by the reform of 27.06.2024)
Proof of income: payslips (Lohn-/Gehaltsabrechnungen) for 3–12 months OR a tax assessment (Steuerbescheid)
An employment contract (Arbeitsvertrag; for employees) / a business activity report (BWA) + a tax advisor's certificate (Steuerberater-Bescheinigung; for the self-employed)

An insurance record statement (Versicherungsverlauf) from the German pension fund (Deutsche Rentenversicherung; pension insurance number — Rentenversicherungsnummer) — confirms employment/contributions
A tenancy agreement (Mietvertrag) + proof of rent payment (to assess housing costs)
A tabular CV (tabellarischer Lebenslauf; covering education, work, residence)
For a spouse/children — proof of health insurance (Krankenversicherungsnachweis) for the family
A job centre certificate of non-receipt of benefits (Negativbescheinigung Jobcenter) — that you do NOT receive basic income support (Bürgergeld; if requested)

content.text: The insurance record statement (Versicherungsverlauf) from the German pension fund can be ordered free of charge online or by letter — it answers two questions at once: it confirms your actual employment over your years of residence and helps prove §10 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 (self-sufficiency).

Certificates of birth, marriage, divorce and change of name from your country of origin almost always need to be (1) legalised — an apostille (Apostille) under the 1961 Hague Convention, or consular legalisation for countries outside the convention — and (2) translated by a sworn translator (beeidigter Übersetzer) recognised by a German court.

items: Birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) — original + apostille (Apostille) + sworn translation
Marriage certificate (Heiratsurkunde) — if married
Divorce decree (Scheidungsurteil) — if there was a divorce
Change-of-name certificate (Namensänderungsurkunde) — if you changed your name in your country of origin
For Russia/Ukraine/Belarus/Kazakhstan — the apostille is affixed by the competent authority of the issuing country
Only a sworn / officially appointed translator (beeidigter/öffentlich bestellter Übersetzer) in Germany (or a recognised one) may do the translation

content.text: Do not order the translation before the apostille (Apostille) is affixed: the apostille is also translated, otherwise you will have to translate the document twice. First the apostille in the issuing country — then a single sworn translation of the whole package. The documents must be recent: many authorities (Behörden) require statements no older than 6 months.

steps.title: Declaration of loyalty to the constitution (Loyalitätserklärung) — a new condition in 2024

content.text: The reform of 27.06.2024 expanded the commitment to the free democratic basic order (Bekenntnis zur freiheitlichen demokratischen Grundordnung; §10 Abs. 1 Satz 1 Nr. 1 StAG) and enshrined a written declaration of loyalty (Loyalitätserklärung). You confirm that you recognise the free democratic order and the equality of the sexes, and that you have not committed antisemitic, racist or other acts directed against human dignity. A knowingly false statement may later become grounds for the withdrawal (Rücknahme) of citizenship under §35 StAG.

items: The authority (Behörde) issues the loyalty declaration (Loyalitätserklärung) form — it is signed in person at submission
It contains recognition of the democratic order (demokratische Grundordnung) and a rejection of antisemitism/racism
Confirmation that you are not in several marriages at once (polygamy — Mehrehe)
False information is grounds for a subsequent withdrawal of naturalisation (Rücknahme der Einbürgerung; §35 StAG)

costs.note: State fee under §38 StAG for the naturalisation of an adult.

costs.note: Sworn translation of certificates; the total depends on the number of documents and pages.

costs.label: Apostille in the country of origin
costs.note: The rate depends on the issuing country; for Russia/Ukraine/Kazakhstan it is affixed by the competent authority.

costs.label: Biometrische Passfotos
costs.note: Standard biometric photos, 35×45 mm.

title: Changing your name on naturalisation
tldr: After acquiring German citizenship, Art. 47 EGBGB lets you adapt your name to the German legal order — this is called bringing the name into line / Germanising the name (Angleichung / Eindeutschung). You can: adopt a German form of your first name or surname (Александр → Alexander), drop the patronymic (Vatersname), which German law does not recognise, remove the gendered surname ending (Иванова → Iwanow), choose a single first name and surname from a chain of names, or take a new name if yours has no German form. The declaration to bring the name into line (Angleichungserklärung) is filed at the registry office (Standesamt) — usually together with naturalisation or right after; it is done once and is irreversible. The new name is then carried over to your national ID card (Personalausweis) / passport (Reisepass). If you change nothing, your name stays as in your passport. The declaration under Art. 47 EGBGB is comparatively cheap (usually around 30€ for certification at the registry office — Standesamt) and does not require proving an important reason (wichtiger Grund), unlike a later change under the NamÄndG. Individual advice at the registry office is recommended.

steps.title: What you can change on naturalisation

content.text: A German name consists of a first name (Vorname) and a surname (Familienname) — without a patronymic and without gendered endings. That is why the law gives anyone who has acquired German citizenship the right to a declaration to bring the name into line (Angleichungserklärung) — a declaration to adapt the name to the German legal order. The basis is Art. 47 EGBGB (it applies when a person's name first comes under German law). A separate provision, §94 BVFG, applies only to late repatriates (Spätaussiedler) and does not relate to ordinary naturalisation.

items: Germanising (Eindeutschung) the form of the first name: Алексей → Alexej/Alexander, Дмитрий → Dimitri
Germanising the surname: a Germanised written form
Dropping the patronymic (Vatersname) — German law does not provide for it
Removing the gendered surname ending: Петрова → Petrow, Kowalska → Kowalski (to the family form)
Choosing a new first name (Vorname) from the German cultural sphere, if the previous one is untranslatable
Simplifying the transliteration (removing diacritics, bringing it to the Latin alphabet per ISO/German rules)
Keeping the name unchanged — also an option (by default it stays as in the passport)

steps.title: How to declare a name change

content.text: The declaration to bring the name into line (Angleichungserklärung) under Art. 47 EGBGB is filed at the registry office (Standesamt). In practice, many naturalisation authorities (Einbürgerungsbehörden) accept it together with naturalisation and forward it to the registry office, but legally it is the registry office that records the name (the naturalisation certificate — Einbürgerungsurkunde — states the name as at the time of naturalisation). Check with your authority (Behörde) and registry office how this step works for them. Once the new name is registered, it is carried over to all your German documents.

items: Declare bringing the name into line (Angleichung) under Art. 47 EGBGB at naturalisation or right after it
Attach your birth/marriage certificate with a sworn translation — the basis for the original name
The name under Art. 47 EGBGB is registered by the registry office; the declaration is made once and is irreversible
After naturalisation, go to the district citizens' office (Bürgeramt): a new national ID card (Personalausweis) and passport (Reisepass) in the German name
Update your details: bank, insurers, employer, tax office (Finanzamt; the tax ID — Steuer-ID — stays), pension insurance (Rentenversicherung)
The declaration under Art. 47 EGBGB is cheaper and simpler than a later change under the NamÄndG (which requires an important reason — wichtiger Grund)

content.text: Note: if you miss the moment of naturalisation, a later name change goes through the Name Change Act (Namensänderungsgesetz, NamÄndG) via the registry office / authority (Standesamt/Behörde), requires an important reason (wichtiger Grund) and a separate fee (often 2.50–1022€ depending on the state and the complexity). So settle the name question RIGHT AWAY when applying for citizenship — this window is cheaper and simpler.

steps.title: Consequences for documents and your country of origin

content.text: The German name applies in all your German documents. But your old passport from your country of origin stays in the previous name — and since the 2024 reform allows dual citizenship, many people keep both passports. This creates a situation where you have two different spellings of your name in two passports.

items: German national ID card and passport (Personalausweis/Reisepass) — in the new (Germanised) name
The foreign passport stays in the old name until you change it in that country
If you keep dual citizenship, carry both passports when travelling to avoid questions at the border
Diplomas and old documents can be accompanied by a certificate of identity of names (Namensbescheinigung)
To change the name in the foreign passport — a separate procedure at the consulate of your country of origin

content.text: Tip: if you plan to travel often to your country of origin and use its passport, weigh up whether you need radical Germanisation (Eindeutschung). Minimal adaptation (just dropping the patronymic and bringing the surname to a single form) is often more convenient than a full name change, which desynchronises the two passports.

steps.title: How to decide whether to change your name

content.text: The name decision is personal and is uniquely advantageous at the moment of naturalisation. Before you choose, work through the practical consequences: documents, diplomas, travel, recognition in your profession.

items: Do you want a single spelling across all your EU documents — then Germanisation (Eindeutschung) helps
Do you often travel to your country of origin on its passport — then be careful with a mismatch of names
Are diplomas/publications/your business tied to the old spelling — an abrupt change will complicate recognition
Do you need to drop the patronymic — almost always convenient, German systems do not accommodate it
Decide at naturalisation: the declaration under Art. 47 EGBGB is cheap and without an important reason (wichtiger Grund), a later change under the NamÄndG is expensive and harder
If in doubt, take minimal adaptation rather than a full name replacement

content.text: The declaration to bring the name into line (Angleichungserklärung) under Art. 47 EGBGB is made once and is irreversible. After it, reversing the change goes through the NamÄndG — with an important reason (wichtiger Grund) and a separate fee. So do not rush to sign the declaration at the appointment: think the choice through in advance and come with a decision ready.

costs.label: Angleichungserklärung under Art. 47 EGBGB (Standesamt)
costs.note: Declaration to bring the name into line with German law; certification at the Standesamt is usually around 30€, the exact fee depends on the state.

costs.label: Later name change under the NamÄndG (if the window is missed)
costs.note: Via the Standesamt/Behörde, requires a wichtiger Grund; the rate depends on the state and complexity.

costs.label: A new Reisepass in the German name
costs.note: 37.50€ under 24, 70€+ for an adult; more for express production.

costs.label: Beglaubigte Übersetzung of certificates
costs.note: Per page; needed to confirm the original name.
